Description: Time seems to have stood still in this beautiful restaurant occupying a neo-Classical residence from the mid 1800s, where the delightful patio, contemporary decorative features and 19C spirit come as a pleasant surprise. Here, the focus is on updated Greek cuisine presented in two menus (both with 5- or 6-course options): one entitled Earth & Sea, the other, the vegetarian-based Garden & Nature.

Name: Alessandro Borghese - Il lusso della semplicità
Address: Calle Seconda del Cristo 2040, Venice, 30121, Italy
Description: This restaurant is situated in the Casinò di Venezia, or to be more precise, Palazzo Ca’ Vendramin Calergi, a 16C building overlooking the Grand Canal which boasts a beautiful garden in which meals are served on warm summer evenings. Chef Alessandro Borghese serves modern and attractive cuisine which is full of enticing flavours. There are two tasting menus available, with the option of adding the chef’s signature dishes to either of these.

Name: Alessandro Feo
Address: Via Angelo Lista 24, Marina di Casal Velino, 84040, Italy
Description: In a beautiful stone-vaulted building (an old 17C monastery) on the town’s seafront promenade, young owner-chef Alessandro Feo has made his mark in this region that perhaps has fewer gourmet restaurants than many places elsewhere. Here, he creates dishes that combine traditional influences and classic favourites from Campania with his own individual flair and creativity. His focus is on local, seasonal ingredients, including produce from his two kitchen gardens and fish sourced from local fishermen as well as from his own ventures out to sea.

Name: Alessandro Maino
Address: Rei En Jaume 5, Castelló de la Plana, 12001, Spain
Description: In this centrally located restaurant, with its contemporary ambience, you'll find an interesting international approach, with nods to the countries where the chef trained (his native Italy, France, Switzerland and Spain) before settling, for love, in this city. They offer à la carte service (we particularly liked the prawns in different textures) and balanced menus, a lunch menu that varies according to the number of starters and a tasting menu (it has 11 dishes explained in detail) that must be booked in advance.

Name: Alessandro Mecca al Castello di Grinzane Cavour
Description: There’s no shortage of classic Piedmontese ingredients (such as anchovies, peppers and veal) on the menu at this restaurant, where traditional recipes are reinterpreted with a personalised and contemporary touch. Dishes from outside the region, including various fish-based options, also feature, while the restaurant aims to avoid food waste by using every single part of its ingredients where possible. The location in a splendid castle with 11C origins, once the home of Camillo Benso, count of Cavour, adds to the appeal.

Name: Alex
Description: A real gem! The restaurant of the elegant Alex Lake Zurich hotel is laid out over two levels, right by Lake Zurich – the setting is modern and lively, with large windows affording unobstructed views of the water. It goes without saying that the terrace is also wonderful. Fine Mediterranean cooking is the order of the day, with an appealing set menu available at lunchtime.

Name: Alex
Address: Via Versilia 157/159, Marina di Pietrasanta, 55045, Italy
Description: This elegant yet relaxed restaurant does not overlook the sea directly, but is situated on a trendy roadside, adorned with tribal motifs, wicker chairs and dark wood marquetry tables. Here, guests can enjoy a menu predominantly based on seafood, featuring modern touches and imaginative interpretations that make the most of the ingredients without compromising their identity. The menu also features some of the restaurant’s great classics, such as the unmissable steamed langoustines and prawns, served with crisp vegetables and mayonnaise in a perfect example of flavour, balance and technique.A high-quality wine cellar completes the experience with a wide and international selection of wines, perfect for accompanying dishes that, while Mediterranean in style, offer a broader, more cosmopolitan perspective.

Name: Alex Cool Club
Address: Juan Ramón Jiménez 46, Miranda de Ebro, 09200, Spain
Description: This restaurant with its urban and industrial atmosphere, dominated by the pink and grey tones of concrete, should be seen as the low-cost version of the award-winning Alejandro Serrano restaurant. Its kitchen, which integrates exposed steel into the décor as it is completely open to the dining room, offers a fun and informal proposal, reinterpreting the dishes of its big brother in a more casual way. The menu, with dishes such as ceviche-style prawn carpaccio and an open-face omelette with cod kokotxas, is rounded out with an economical daily set menu.

Name: Alexandre
Description: This 18C doctor’s home, set in the picturesque village of Herzele and a well-kept secret among discerning foodies, is depicted by a snug interior, a superb terrace and Tamara’s attentive service. Tim Ritserveldt deploys his virtuoso culinary skills, rustling up a set menu overflowing in creativity. Hearty, gutsy flavours are his hallmark, such as feta, watermelon sorbet and guacamole cream which enhance the character and depth of thinly sliced Duroc ham. Full-bodied, spot-on food that enjoys straying from conventional culinary paths.

Name: Alexperience
Description: Set beside a lake and boasting a magnificent view of Mont Blanc, this chalet has a resolutely understated decor. On the menu, traditional cuisine is given free rein, in dishes such as slow-cooked egg, lentils, smoked diot (pork sausages from the regional repertoire) and a bacon emulsion, or beef bourguignon. In fact, the chef won a competition with his pâté en croûte.

Name: Aleño Brassafina
Description: Considered the informal little brother to Ancestral, which can be found on the upper floor and boasting a MICHELIN Star, everything here is designed for sharing (among the starters, don't miss the pickled mussels), with the grill at its core. The ‘Viandas y chacinas’ (Prepared dishes and charcuterie) section stands out, as well as its selection of meats, with select cuts (Wagyu beef tomahawk, Angus sirloin, black angus entrails...) and maturities to suit all tastes. The accompaniments are served separately!

Name: Alfonsina
Address: C. García Vigil 183, San Juan Bautista La Raya, Oaxaca, 71232, Mexico
Description: At several points en route to this hidden restaurant, you will wonder if you’re lost. But hold steady: A half hour’s drive south of Oaxaca city and down several bumpy dirt roads, this humble, reservation-only destination is as close of an invitation into someone’s home as you’re going to get. Chef Jorge León and his mother Doña Elvia run this idyllic, breezy backyard with tables set under a canopy of trees. The tasting menu is by no means formal or lengthy. Rather, expect a leisurely procession of traditional, comforting dishes like a tamal filled with spiced green beans or grilled local fish with molé estofado rich with fruit and warm spice notes, complemented by tortillas hot off the comal.

Name: Alford Arms
Description: Wind your way down a series of twisty country lanes and you will be rewarded with a visit to this attractive Victorian inn beside the village green. The charming interior comes with bags of character and a warming fire, while the summer months are best spent on the covered terrace, with cosy, sheepskin-lined benches on hand for when the sun sets. The cooking is unashamedly traditional and executed with a minimum of fuss but plenty of skill, resulting in hearty, robustly flavoured dishes like ox liver with mash and bacon. The friendly team will happily guide you through the menu.

Name: Alfredo
Description: If you are in the mood for authentic Italian cuisine in Cologne, Roberto Carturan is your man. His father, Alfredo, laid the foundations for upscale Italian cuisine in 1973, and the second generation of the Carturan family has cultivated a straightforward and minimalist style of cooking. Without a doubt, the house classic is the pappardelle with braised duck. The charming chef-patron is on hand and will talk you through the menu in person. The atmosphere is relaxed – the focus is on pleasure. You can feel that the whole team is genuinely invested in your experience. Besides cooking, Roberto Carturan has another talent: he is a trained singer – on Friday evenings there's the "musical culinary soirée": a six-course set menu with a performance by him as the finale! One practical tip: Parking is available in the Opern Passagen shopping centre located behind the restaurant. You might also take the opportunity to see the original 4711 store with its famous carillon.

Name: Alhambra
Description: This restaurant, the younger sibling of the award-winning Europa, bears the quality stamp and DNA of the Idoate family, where the brother-and-sister team of Iñaki and Esther run the dining room. It also happens to be one of Pamplona’s classic dining addresses – the reason why it is often full with its regular and loyal customers. The à la carte (with the option of ordering “raciones” so that you can try different dishes) is complemented by two tasting menus. One of its most typical dishes is the cod “ajoarriero” with lobster.

Name: Ali Nasi Lemak Daun Pisang
Address: Sri Weld Food Court, 19 Lebuh Pantai, George Town, 10300, Malaysia
Description: This halal stall only sells nasi lemak: the national dish of coconut milk rice wrapped in banana leaf, topped with sambal and one of the six toppings. Try anchovies with a hard-boiled egg. And go easy on the fiery sambal.

Name: Alice B.
Address: 1122 E. Tahquitz Canyon Way, Palm Springs, CA, 92262, USA
Description: Alice B., from Chefs Sue Feniger and Mary Sue Milliken, is an inviting restaurant located within the Living Out community in Palm Springs. The dining room, tucked away from the bar serving its own bites, is a warm and inviting space set with flickering candles, stone tables and comfortably cushioned seating. Meanwhile, the menu features Californian cuisine threaded with Mediterranean influences, as in appetizers like tender, smoky grilled black tiger prawns with saffron red pepper aioli and entrees like skillfully hand rolled ricotta cavatelli with vibrant kale pesto. Don't skip dessert, especially the brownie topped with vanilla ice cream, salted caramel and crushed walnuts.

Name: Alice Hawthorn Inn
Address: The Green, Nun Monkton, YO26 8EW, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This smartly modernised dining pub sits on a large village green where, as well as a duck pond, you’ll find the country’s tallest maypole. Guests are spread across multiple rooms that are all packed with charm, character and the obligatory exposed brickwork and beams. The hearty, well-presented dishes showcase some garden produce and know no borders, meaning you could find dynamite shrimp and sea bass ceviche alongside fish & chips and leek & potato soup. Welcoming service and smart, slightly Scandic-style bedrooms complete the picture.

Name: Aliro
Description: In the historical heart of the city, near the covered market of Les Halles Castellane, this restaurant has the look and feel of a loft, with plants, soothing colours and soft music. Chef Jean Gary-Bobo serves his surprise set menu, which can be adapted to suit your wishes, at lunch and dinner. Local ingredients (fish from local fish markets, meat from the neighbouring butcher, fruit and vegetables from the Hérault). Wine pairings with regional wines are also served by the glass.

Name: Alivetu
Description: This little "olive grove" (alivetu in Corsican) is a haven for foodies in the Saint Victor neighbourhood, abutting the Colline de la Garde. Diners can tuck into the chef's Mediterranean cuisine in the downstairs dining room with a polished concrete floor or on the mezzanine. Think braised endive, flame-seared oranges, roast squash and gorgonzola. The market-fresh lunchtime score is chalked up on a board; surprise menu in the evening.

Name: Alkimista Kulináris Műhely
Description: Its name means ‘Culinary Workshop’ but that feels like doing it an injustice, as this is a beautiful, elegant spot. It's hidden away behind locked gates in a city centre courtyard and everyone is greeted at 7pm by the infectiously enthusiastic chef-owner. Seasonal ingredients feature on a highly personalised tasting menu which cleverly blends the old and the new. Flavours are memorable, sauces are a highlight and the chef describes every dish with heartfelt passion. The price also includes a carefully curated selection of drinks featuring many local biodynamic and organic wines.

Name: All Day Darling
Description: This eatery in historic Montford is a quintessential neighborhood gathering place. Packed with colorful chairs and tables, it's a casual, come-as-you-are spot that's just right for picking up to-go orders as it is for settling in for a meal with friends. Chef Jacob Sessoms leans into the cozy, market-focused vibe with a menu built around breakfast and lunch favorites. It all begins with “The Wake Up” section full of egg sandwiches, frittatas and shakshuka, before transitioning to “Open and Closed” with picks like burgers, biscuit fried chicken sandwiches and avocado toast. Sides include everything from lentil fritters to gloriously crisp tater tots, and there’s a chalkboard near the register announcing the daily specials.

Name: All Spice
Address: 1602 S. El Camino Real, San Mateo, CA, 94402, USA
Description: Like a bracelet glittering with different jewels, All Spice is home to a bevy of vibrant dining rooms, made extra colorful with artwork and sparkling chandeliers. It’s a delightful blend of old-school charm and contemporary verve that appeals to a sophisticated crowd. They’re usually here to catch up with friends or celebrate a birthday. This kitchen offers a variety of creative selections on the three, four and five-course menus, which spin to highlight the seasons. Chilled butternut squash soup in a shot glass makes a soigné amuse-bouche and is a delicious way to start a meal. Then a brick-shaped, perfectly cooked strip loin is accompanied by baby zucchini, pearl onions, confit mushrooms and smoked kale sauce for added enrichment.

Name: All'Olivo
Description: In one of the characteristic squares of the beautiful old town, four dining rooms, the central one lined with bottles of wine, while the others are embellished with numerous drawings by artists who have taken part in the legendary Lucca Comics festival. The menu is of regional inspiration, offering both meat and fish dishes. Be sure to try the traditional Lucca tortelli served with meat sauce. The extensive wine list also offers a good selection of wines by the glass. Delightful alfresco service in summer.

Name: All'Osteria Bottega
Description: Beneath the porticoes of a somewhat hidden side street in the city centre lies a trattoria that celebrates authentic Emilian cooking, prepared according to tradition, without diversions or reinterpretations, but showcased in its most typical recipes. From the exceptional selection of cured meats and cheeses to the fresh pasta dishes, from the meat dishes to the wines – largely local – everything speaks the forthright and comforting language of this land. It is worth, therefore, leaving a little room for the zuppa inglese, served with alchermes ring cake and chocolate shavings: a great classic that concludes the meal in the most indulgent fashion. The setting is small and welcoming, and it comes as no surprise that the restaurant is fully booked every day: reserving a table is strongly advised.

Name: Alla Corte Lombarda
Description: Housed in a restored hay barn on the edge of the village, this charming rustic restaurant offers traditional cuisine with a modern twist, a good selection of wine and an excellent choice of beer. Every week, the menu features five records which played a major role in the history of music or which represent an important moment in time for the restaurant owner.

Name: Alla Fassa
Address: Via Nascimbeni 11, Castelletto di Brenzone, 37010, Italy
Description: Although the beautiful views of the lake (with only a cycle path between the restaurant and the water) and mountains on the opposite shore can be admired from the dining room, in fine weather it’s a race for the outdoor tables just a few metres from the water. The cuisine is as impressive as the setting, with a fine balance of classic and modern dishes featuring fish from the lake (such as the “il lago in un piatto” – the lake in a dish – starter) and the sea. A few guestrooms with views of the lake are also available.

Name: Alla Laguna - Vedova Raddi
Description: Situated in a charming small town criss-crossed by canals, this restaurant serves traditionally inspired fish-based dishes. The restaurant stands on the port facing the fish market, so it’s no surprise that the fish served here is of the freshest quality.

Name: Alla Lanterna
Description: On the Adriatic coast road south of Fano, run by the same family since 1976, the year it opened, this restaurant is a must for seafood lovers. The dishes are essentially inspired by the seafaring traditions of the Marche region.

Name: Alla Locanda
Description: A colourful, contemporary-style restaurant within the Locanda degli Artisti Art Hotel, a new address that is striking for its large art collection displayed throughout its various rooms. The cuisine here focuses on seasonal ingredients which are used to create personalised and imaginative dishes showcased on tasting menus and an à la carte. Interesting wine list, with a special emphasis on labels from the Trentino-Alto Adige region.

Name: Alla Vita
Address: 564 W. Randolph St., Chicago, IL, 60661, USA
Description: The Boka Restaurant Group is no stranger to quality, which you’ll find in spades in this gorgeous room decorated with crystal pendants, hand-painted tile floors, and an amber-tinted sculpture floating overhead. Freshly made pasta, puffy-edged pizzas, and shareable entrées satisfy a range of cravings. There’s the crowd favorite rigatoni alla vodka—at once sweet, creamy, and toothsome—as well as a confident half chicken, roasted and served with grilled lemon. Come lunch time, a long, rustic stone bar is a prime perch where fellow diners happily dig into some of the most satisfying sandwiches in town. You can linger over a bottle of wine or dash in and out for a quick bite. The professional staff will keep everything sailing smoothly either way.

Name: Allard
Description: In the heart of bustling Saint Germain des Près, this authentic Parisian bistro, dripping in charm and now part of the Ducasse empire, has changed very little since it opened in 1932. The culinary score wavers between bistro fare and heroic brasserie staples. Attractive lunchtime menu.

Name: Allauddin's Briyani
Description: The family has been selling its famous biryani since the 1950s. The set comes with yellow basmati rice enhanced by a spice mix; mutton, chicken or fish curry; and papadums. The mutton sambal is tender and tasty.

Name: Alle Ciaspole
Address: Località Plazze 4, Frazione Tret, Fondo, 38013, Italy
Description: This beautiful Alpine house surrounded by the low mountains of the Val di Non is home to husband-and-wife team Ivano and Antonella, who have run this restaurant with enthusiasm and professionalism for many years. She offers a warm welcome front of house, while he is at the helm in the kitchen, where he prepares dishes from top-quality ingredients (mostly local, such as the Alpine beef, char, cheese and game) with skill and precision. A few seasonal ingredients from outside the region also make it on to the menu, as do a couple of fish-based dishes.

Name: Alle Codole
Address: Via XX Agosto 27, Canale d'Agordo, 32020, Italy
Description: ‘Codole’ is the nickname of the family that runs this restaurant and whose ancestors once worked in the copper mines in the area. Today, the family has exchanged mining for cooking, offering guests specialities such as ricotta and black truffle ravioli with a lamb ragù, and loin of venison in a porcini mushroom crust.

Name: Alle Corone
Address: Campo della Fava, Sestiere Castello 5527, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: Modern Mediterranean and Venetian cuisine served in three elegant dining rooms or – on request – in the wine bar surrounded by bottles of wine. Through the windows, enjoy the spectacle of gondolas passing by along the small canal outside.

Name: Allegar
Description: Briones is one of Spain’s most beautiful medieval villages and is also home to the superb Vivanco bodega-museum. Named after a local Rioja word that means ‘to scrape the plate clean’, ‘allegar’ is the perfect way to define the approach to food at this restaurant inside the Santa María Briones hotel, where the culinary focus is on an updated take on Rioja cooking, featuring intense flavours and even the occasional hint of trompe-l’oeil. They propose a unique ‘Journey through La Rioja’, which can be experienced in the form of three set menus: À la carte tasting menu (a sort of fixed-price menu, every day for dinner), the Short Trip (El Viaje Corto) and the Long Trip (El Viaje Largo), with these last two only available from Thursday to Sunday. The restaurant is also home to an old and typical wine cellar, known locally as a ‘calado’.

Name: Allegria !
Address: Les Petites Maisons - Hameau des Baux, 285 chemin de Bourgeac, Paradou, 13520, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In this luxury hamlet surrounded by olive and almond trees, tables are set out in the inviting dining room or on the terrace in the shade of the plane trees, with the song of the cicadas in the background. Chef Julie Chaix, who has worked in Anne-Sophie Pic and Alain Ducasse's restaurants, prepares a lovely market-fresh menu inspired by the ingredients and traditions of Provence. Diners can indulge themselves with dishes such as aubergine tian with pistou, Mediterranean rock octopus in stuffed ravioli, or apricots roasted in Alpilles honey. Excellent value for money at lunchtime.

Name: Allemansgeest
Description: The Vliet canal provides the stunning backdrop to this stylishly decorated yet cosy farmhouse. The waterfront terrace (with mooring facilities) and the sight of the passing boats captures everyone's heart. This is a magical setting in which to discover a modern approach to French cuisine with occasional subtle exotic nuances. Savour classic lobster soup with crayfish and Cognac crème, or tuck into a medium-rare beef fillet with a bold red wine jus. Deciding whether to go à la carte or opt for the set menu (vegetarian version available) will be difficult!

Name: Alleudium
Description: Keiichi Shinohara, a Japanese chef with solid credentials (including a stint at Le Violon d'Ingres during the Christian Constant era), is at the helm of this restaurant with refined contemporary decor. Customer satisfaction is the goal here, in particular when it comes to the food, which is modern and inspired, with the odd nod to Japan.

Name: Allium
Description: Some chefs tout their use of local products, but Chefs Adolfo Galnares and María Ortega are truly committed at their restaurant, Allium, where nearly 100% of their ingredients are Mexican. A rooftop garden provides hyperlocal produce, while Nayarit seafood is the star of the show. Sit indoors or out and enjoy dishes like the tiradito de pina, a fish of the day layered with charred pineapple and finely diced chiles in a soy marinade. Main dishes like crisp-skinned, pan-seared pescado with a tomatillo pistachio mole verde never disappoint. Neither does their dulce de leche panna cotta with guava compote and house-made ice cream.

Name: Allium
Description: Arthur and Gideon first met while working in a kitchen and promised that one day they would open a restaurant together. Years later, with a wealth of experience behind them, they have realised that ambition by setting up this resolutely contemporary yet wonderfully intimate restaurant. It is clear from the enticing menu how much pleasure the chefs take in what they do. They remain true to their classical foundations while enlivening their dishes with exotic influences and vibrant flavours - just enough vadouvan to lend finesse and depth to a bisque sauce, or a delicately balanced combination of jalapeño and fermented tomato to give fish an extra kick: this is confident cooking. A fine addition to Haarlem's culinary landscape!

Name: Allora
Description: Modern and convivial, Allora offers neighborhood charm with a sense of elevated style. The Cal-Italian kitchen focuses on sustainable seasonal ingredients, with West Coast seafood a particular highlight, seen in dishes like balsamic-glazed octopus with Calabrian chili and potato gnocchi. House-made pastas are a draw in their own right, as in silky tajarin with duck confit and porcini cream. The menu is offered in three, four, or five courses, with an impressive list of Italian-focused wines overseen by owner and beverage director Elizabeth-Rose Mandalou for pairings. Come dessert, a simple-but-excellent affogato with house pistachio gelato is a winner, or opt for a more elaborate “barra di cioccolato” with hazelnut mousse and amarena cherry.

Name: Alloro
Description: In the baroque heart of the city, this small restaurant – comprising two dining rooms, one overlooking the bell tower of the Basilica Collegiata dei Santi Apostoli Pietro e Paolo, the other more intimate – welcomes guests with a contemporary style and cozy atmosphere. The cooking takes a modern and bold approach, offered either à la carte or through two tasting menus that trace journeys of travel and inspiration by way of forthright and intriguing flavours. To then end the meal with a touch of lightness thanks to the playful ‘tiratisù’. Here, you are not simply clients, but guests.

Name: Allt Yr Afon
Address: Wolfscastle Country Hotel, Wolf's Castle, SA62 5LZ, United Kingdom
Description: Down in Wales’ far southwest corner, Wolfscastle Country Hotel may be best known as a boutique wedding venue, but it also harbours this six-table restaurant that’s worth a visit in its own right. The concise à la carte is influenced by the seasons and locality, with the kitchen team pouring obvious care and understanding into each dish. The pistachio soufflé, for example, is beautifully risen and nicely balanced by chocolate ice cream and sharp raspberry purée. Attentive service is delivered with palpable pride.

Name: Alluma
Description: Former Balagan chef Liran Tal has tastefully revamped this establishment with immaculate white walls. He crafts delicious Mediterranean cuisine with Israeli influences: delicious msabbaha hummus, yellowtail crudo with figs and spices, lamb sirloin and an apricot-miso condiment. Choice of organic and biodynamic wines, most notably from Italy, Spain and Armenia.

Name: Allégorie
Address: Bretón de los Herreros, 39, Madrid, 28003, Spain
Description: If you enjoy dining in restaurants that showcase French cuisine, Allégorie is definitely an option for you in the heart of the city’s Chamberí distrct. Here, you can discover the full virtues of Gallic cooking courtesy of young French chef Romain Lascarides, whose mantra is ‘eating nourishes the spirit, thoughts and the faculty of judgement.’ His cuisine varies with the seasons thanks to his total respect for the seasonality of ingredients and their producers. It features a bar at the entrance (serving wines, cocktails and champagne) and the dining room on the upper floor, where you can discover the tempting set menus: Prelude (Tuesday to Thursday), Adagio and Sinfonia.

Name: Alma
Address: 130 Quay Street, Britomart, Auckland Central, Auckland, 1010, New Zealand
Description: Andalusian cuisine, with its wide-ranging influences from across cultures, is the attraction at this very likeable and sunny corner restaurant. Sit yourself at the counter if you want to watch how the team expertly use the open wood fire, which is the centrepiece of the kitchen. The appealing menu is divided into three sections: fish, veg, and meat and if you’re one who doesn’t like sharing then know that most dishes are available in half sizes. Sherry lovers will be happy and, like the food, the wine list is an appealing mix of New Zealand and Spain.

Name: Alma Bodega
Description: The more down-to-earth little brother of MICHELIN-starred Alma has its own personality. Chic marble and stylish design give this laid-back restaurant flair. You can drop in any time of day to indulge in a fresh take on familiar flavours. The menu features a variety of dishes that will tempt your taste buds, including gyoza, köfte, pâté en croûte, perfectly done entrecôte with a delicious veal jus, rum baba and more. The skilfully prepared and generously flavoured dishes never fail to impress. The wine list always includes some exciting finds. Be sure to make your reservation in good time to avoid disappointment!

Name: Almacita
Description: This restaurant in Valence is the brainchild of Louis Chabran, who serves South American cuisine prepared by bona fide Latin-American chefs. The menu opens with a selection of tapas – from pimientos to tacos de pollo, croquetas de chorizo – to whet the appetite, followed by dishes with bold flavours, such as sea bream ceviche with leche de tigre or grilled swordfish served with a cream of sun-dried tomatoes, flaked almonds and smoked aubergine caviar. Spices and exotic flavours are introduced with a delicate touch. A selection of cocktails and mocktails completes the experience in a relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Almanaque Casa de Comidas
Address: Plaza de España 5 duplicado, Cadiz, 11006, Spain
Description: A small, charming restaurant occupying a historic building in the old quarter of Cádiz, next to the Plaza de España park, the latter home to the monument to the 1812 constitution. Juan Carlos Borrell, for several years a pupil of award-winning Valencian chef Ricard Camarena from whom it is said he learnt how to cook rice to absolute perfection, showcases cuisine that avoids unnecessary frills to concentrate on safeguarding traditional Cádiz recipes and maximising flavour. On the concise à la carte, which works with the seasons, make sure you try the typical Poleá dessert.

Name: Almarge
Description: An informal, centrally located restaurant on two floors, run by a couple with an inviting warmth. The traditional cuisine with a contemporary touch seeks to offer something different and the chef is not exempt from risks, but always under control, when combining ingredients. They have dishes to share and offer a tasting menu that evolves with the seasonality of the product!

Name: Almazen
Description: Amid the surprising landscapes of the Valle Salado de Añana, overlooking its salt pans that date back millennia, you’ll find this rustic-style former salt warehouse that now features the kitchen at its very heart with a bar counter arranged around it. Head chef Beatriz Pascual shows off her skills in front of us, using locally sourced organic fruits and vegetables to create honest and regionally inspired cuisine. She presents a singular tasting menu that evolves with the season and, weather permitting, begins with the first appetisers at a table that overlooks the ancient salt mines. We were surprised by both the coffee course, with honey provided directly by the beekeeper, and a homemade ‘Baileys’ made with toasted cereal and fermented bread. She tends to work a lot with the ‘muera’, the salt of the earth, an exclusive product!

Name: Almeja
Description: It’s housed in a building that used to be a traditional coffee and tea shop on the outskirts of Bolhão (the place that gives its name to one of its executive menus). Chef João Cura, after gaining experience in prestigious restaurants in Spain, decided to embark on his own project alongside his wife, Sofia Amaral — who runs the dining room. The concept is grounded in seasonal cuisine and, before designing the menu, the freshest products are selected from local producers. Originality and flavour abound in the chef’s signature creations, which can be enjoyed as a 10-course tasting menu, the Bolhão and Trindade menus (available only on weekdays), or à la carte options. Enjoy the experience in the garden — it’s charming!

Name: Almer Schlossmühle
Description: The old mill next to the palace, Schloss Alme, has been lovingly restored and is an appealing restaurant that abounds with rustic charm. Diners are invited to discover cuisine at the crossroads where "Sauerland meets Austria", courtesy of a menu that features seasonal dishes from the regional repertoire as well as classic fare from the chef's native Austria. The menu features dishes such as "Almer trout meunière" and Viennese fried breaded chicken with potato and cucumber salad. Head for the lovely terrace in fine weather. There are also guestrooms for an overnight stay.

Name: Almocadén
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: This restaurant takes its name from the old family farmhouse! Run by chef Tomás Rueda, it offers contemporary cuisine and a pleasant patio-terrace. Here you will find a traditional menu brought right up to date, with some Asian flourishes, complemented by good recommendations of the day, dishes that change with the seasons, a set lunch menu and a more extensive tasting menu (this one requires a reservation a minimum of 24 hours in advance). What to order? Don't miss the Tartare of matured picaña, with peppers and pistachios, or the Cod confit with honey aioli.

Name: Almondo Trattoria
Address: Piazza Gran Madre di Dio 2/l, Turin, 10131, Italy
Description: This simple yet charming restaurant located just a few metres from the Gran Madre church serves a fine array of regional Italian dishes. Although specialities from Piedmont understandably take pride of place, the menu takes guests on a culinary journey throughout Italy and the changing seasons, featuring dishes such as scialatielli pasta with seafood, Puglian stuffed meat rolls, and zabaglione with traditional hazelnut cake from the Langhe. There’s also a good selection of gluten-free options.

Name: Almoraduz
Address: Benito Juárez 11 & 12, Rinconada, Puerto Escondido, 71983, Mexico
Description: This ambitious restaurant has for years set the standard for serious cooking in sunny Puerto Escondido. Open since 2013 by a husband-and-wife team, Almoraduz is Oaxacan at its core but pulls inspiration from all over. The corn tostada with confit pork jowl, creamy refried beans, guacamole and grasshoppers is a worthy order, as is the catch of the day topped with chimichurri, spinach and grapefruit segments. Whether you order a la carte or trust the kitchen with the signature tasting menu, expect attractive presentations and bold flavors. The space is equally inviting with its handsome wood tables, comfy dining chairs, and pleasant greenery. Service is ace as well thanks to friendly servers with a strong attention to detail.

Name: Almú
Address: Progreso S/N, Carr. San Martín Tilcajete, Oaxaca, 71506, Mexico
Description: For an adventure off the beaten path, make the trek to this rustic countryside kitchen south of Oaxaca City. More than once, you will wonder if you’re headed in the right direction, up until you find an expansive shed with an open-air dining room surrounded by plants, trees, and pottery. Sweet smoke wafts from the kitchen, which is powered by burning logs that cooks move around with their hands. The offerings are traditional: Crispy memelas, hearty enmoladas enrobed in mole, and sizeable tlayudas stuffed with local cheese. Excellent tableside salsas enliven everything they touch. It goes without saying that this outdoor experience has plenty of charm and also assumes that guests don’t mind dining with the elements.

Name: Alobar Yorkville
Description: The warm and flattering lighting, the low ceiling, and the curved banquettes all make you think you’ve walked into a cocktail bar rather than a destination restaurant. But that noisy buzz of contentment you hear on arrival is a testament to the food, which hits the spot just as well as the skillfully made cocktails. Seafood is a big deal here, whether scallops or bream, but meats too, such as Creekstone striploin and Iberico pork chop, demonstrate that the kitchen knows its way around a charcoal grill. Those familiar with the Alo Food Group’s other restaurants will recognize classics like the wedge salad, Dover sole, and the banana cream pie holding court in this dining room as well. A second location downtown offers a near identical menu.

Name: Aloette
Description: Open since 2017, this stylish bistro remains one of the coolest reservations in town. Chef Patrick Kriss and his well-oiled restaurant group again demonstrate that they have the Midas touch. With the tasting menu-only ALO just upstairs, the team here is impressively polished in this diner setting. No wider than a train car, the cozy space offers satisfying, approachable dishes that look and taste far better than imagined. Iceberg wedges dressed in chive cream arrive under a mountain of puffed wild rice. A complimentary loaf of cheddar brioche wouldn’t be out of place on white tablecloth. Everyone wants the burger. And for dessert, there must be pie. The signature lemon meringue is a towering finale that will have you rolling out the door.

Name: Alois-Anton Kaminrestaurant
Description: A good alternative to the fine dining restaurant of the Park-Hotel Egerner Höfe. The choice is yours: dine in the cosy Bavarian-style dining rooms dubbed "Alois" and "Anton" or in the more upmarket Kaminrestaurant. Just as charming is the terrace, which is sheltered from the wind and has a view of the pastures and mountains. Either way, you can enjoy cordial service and regional and seasonal dishes in a pleasantly laid-back atmosphere.

Name: Alpenkönig - Esslust
Description: Diners take their seats in a lovely, upscale dining space comprising areas that range in style from traditional charm to modern chic. A cordial and professional front-of-house team serves fresh regional cuisine that draws on the seasons and Mediterranean influences. You can go à la carte or choose dishes for the three or four courses of your own set menu. There is also an appealing wine list. The restaurant is located in the attractive Alpenkönig hotel, which has inviting guestrooms and modern wellness facilities, set in the gorgeous Allgäu landscape.

Name: Alpenrose
Address: Via delle Sette Chiese 1, Loc. Pinzago, Brixen, 39042, Italy
Description: Situated in a beautiful panoramic location a few kilometres outside Bressanone, this restaurant combines regional traditions with a modern approach thanks to its classic techniques and the use of Mediterranean ingredients in some dishes. There are also elegant apartments available, plus a private wellness space, for anyone wishing to extend their stay.

Name: Alpes
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A warm and welcoming setting, where hospitality stands out for its authenticity and attention to detail. The kitchen, under the direction of chef Matthias Kirchler, presents creative, refined dishes designed for those who love to experiment and be surprised. The gastronomic offering has been recently refreshed and now unfolds in two distinct journeys: “Alpes 1988” and “Alpes – Locanda” for culinary experiences that narrate the territory with contemporary flair.

Name: AlpiNN by Norbert Niederkofler
Address: Plan de Corones, alt. 2275, Brunico, 39031, Italy
Description: Situated at an altitude of 2 000m in the Plan de Corones ski area, this restaurant is accessed via the cable-car from Riscone and then, in winter, by walking (or skiing) for around 150m through the snow. This impressive project by famous chef Norbert Niederkofler showcases his “Cook the Mountain” philosophy, where a modern approach and Alpine traditions combine to create perfect dishes full of flavour, all inspired by the seasons with a focus on using the whole ingredient with no food waste. The five tables with the best views are reserved for guests who choose the tasting menu, which has to be booked ahead of time. NB: the last cable-car leaves at 5pm!

Name: Alquimia
Address: 6 rue de la Table-Ronde, Vienne, 38200, France
Description: Not far from the banks of the Rhône, this historic building (parts of which are 18C) ticks all the boxes: high ceilings, exposed stone and brick walls and, at the helm, a young Franco-Paraguayan couple with bags of personality. Chef Horacio Zàrate Franco, who has a flair for presentation, composes creative cuisine with South American notes. At lunchtime, diners can compose their own menu, while in the evening the chef is given carte blanche. A buzzy vibe reigns, thanks to the people skills of the hostess.

Name: Alta
Address: 9 Kingly Court, Carnaby Street, Soho, London, W1B 5PW, United Kingdom
Description: Split over two floors of Soho’s Kingly Court gastro-haven, Alta ticks all the boxes for the modern London restaurant: dishes cooked over fire, a menu designed for sharing and even some wines on tap. Spanish influences, especially from the northern Navarra region, can be found across the menu of flame-centric dishes, which show off prime British produce like Middlewhite pork chop alongside humbler but equally delicious ingredients such as slow-cooked white beetroot with a charred finish. The knowledgeable and approachable team will help guide you through the menu.

Name: Alta Adams
Address: 5359 W. Adams Blvd., Los Angeles, CA, 90016, USA
Description: This is the kind of homey and comforting spot that anyone would be glad to have in their neighborhood, but would just as happily drive to find. Generous portions make it a favorite for family-style and group dining. The lovely back patio is draped with string lights and vines, fashioning a perfect backdrop for evenings alfresco. The cooking is soulful and comforting, starting with a plate of golden-fried black-eyed pea fritters with a garlicky green herb sauce for dipping. Their fried chicken is decadent, served juicy with a wickedly spicy hot sauce and caramelized sweet potatoes. Buttery coconut cake for dessert is pure, old-fashioned bliss.

Name: Altatto
Description: A taste of the big city in Milan’s southwest inner periphery: Altatto brings a fully vegetarian cuisine built on contemporary ideas, modern techniques, and flavors that alternate between bright citrus accents and softer, more captivating tones. A prime example is the mascarpone risotto with celeriac base and walnuts, intense and perfectly balanced. The space, minimal and clean-lined, finds warmth in an informal, jovial service that makes the overall experience all the more welcoming.

Name: Altdeutsches Restaurant
Description: Florian Kellerbauer's kitchen philosophy centres on quality ingredients, with a strong commitment to regional and seasonal sourcing. Diners can opt for a set menu – either with meat or vegetarian – comprising four, five or six courses. You can also order à la carte. The service is friendly, attentive and professional. The restaurant occupies a prime spot in the historical centre – Kirche St Georg just opposite is well worth a visit. For overnight stays, there is Hotel Deutsches Haus, a patrician house dating from 1440, or in the Ehemalige Sparkasse, both just 50m away.

Name: Alte Mühle
Description: This friendly, well-run restaurant with its appealingly pared-back style adjoins the historical building of a grain mill, which has been converted into guest accommodation. Service is provided by attentive and professional staff, as you tuck into Mediterranean, regional and seasonal cuisine. In addition to à la carte dishes, a set menu is also available.

Name: Alte Mühle Thomas Höreth
Description: With this individual and thoroughly charming establishment the Höreth family have created a wonderful retreat. The guest lounges are lovingly decorated and the inner courtyard is idyllic. This is a real gem of a place, which also has its own wine estate. Slightly higher up, charming rooms are available for guests to stay the night.

Name: Alter Torkel - Huus vum Bündner Wii
Description: Even from the outside, Alte Torkel, which is located right on the road through the vineyards, is liable to turn heads! The old stone house at a remove from even its closest neighbours has maintained its regional charm while incorporating modern touches; the wine theme is omnipresent. In keeping with its "Fine Wineing" motto, the menu is characterised by a regularly changing selection of wines by the glass. A contemporary influence makes itself felt in the seasonal, regional cuisine. The hosts are cordial and dedicated. In summer, the terrace with a view of the valley is a real boon!

Name: Alter Wirt
Description: This inn has a long-standing tradition of hospitality. A relaxed atmosphere reigns in the delightful interior, which combines modern elements with rustic charm. Outside, the lovely terrace is shaded by chestnut trees. With an emphasis on organic and locally sourced ingredients, the menu features regional fare and takes its cue from the seasons. Daily specials are also available. For overnight stays, there are well-appointed guestrooms furnished with natural materials and designed with sustainability in mind.

Name: Alternative
Description: Alt-rock is rock music that doesn’t fit any particular category or is born of a spirit of breaking down established concepts. Noting the free rein Gallic cuisine enjoyed during his sojourn in France, the chef named his restaurant ‘Alternative’ to signal his determination to create new value. He lays the foundations of classic French theory and technique before adding elements from Japanese and Chinese culinary traditions. The venue, the former premises of a neighbourhood workshop, also expresses the chef’s individualism.

Name: Altes Gericht
Description: The building itself is really quite something. Dating back to the 13C, this former courthouse – also known as the Schmiedhaus – has retained its original charm both on the outside and in its five dining areas, which feature plenty of old wood and historical details. A cosy atmosphere prevails throughout. Diners are served cuisine in a classical vein that draws on high-quality ingredients. Think variations of scallop – carpaccio au gratin and crispy scallop on a bed of mango and avocado salad. In summer, the garden planted with chestnut trees makes for a romantic setting.

Name: Altes Rathaus by What the Food
Description: A truly delightful example of casual, down-to-earth dining that brings pleasure and joy! This restaurant is housed in a picturesque half-timbered house in the pedestrian area. The interior is modern and minimalist, and outside there is a charming terrace overlooking the forecourt. Chef-patron Patrick Schubert cooks up dishes that are creative and full of flavour – opt for his ambitious signature set menu ("Da kommsch rum") or choose from the somewhat simpler à la carte selection. Options are more limited at lunchtime. Friendly and competent service comes courtesy of maître d' Anne Henrichs. Good to know: they have a food truck that can be booked for special occasions.

Name: Alteño
Address: Clayton Hotel & Members Club, 249 Clayton St., Denver, CO, 80206, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Slightly moody with statement lighting and a vibe-y ambience, Chef Johnny Curiel's vibrant spot taps into his roots in the Jalisco Highlands of Mexico. Inspired by the rustic dishes of his upbringing and the regional flavors of Los Altos, Alteño offers a fresh, thoughtful take on traditional Mexican cooking—think bold flavors and a clear respect for regional ingredients. The menu moves from bright seafood and raw plates into soulful appetizers, tacos and larger-format entrees meant for sharing. You’ll find everything from aguachile and carne apache to roasted sweet potatoes, tacos packed with personality and hearty mains like carne asada and bone-in chuleta. Some of the can't-miss dishes include oysters on the half shell, kanpachi tostada with Santa Barbara uni, and a braised, bone-in Colorado lamb shank for DIY tacos.

Name: Altriménti
Description: A bistro with a contemporary soul, where the informal atmosphere mingles with a subtle elegance that captivates without ostentation. The scents that waft out from the kitchen reveal the seasonality of the ingredients: fresh, carefully selected from small producers, transformed into dishes that speak Italian, with a harmony between sea and land. Every course is an invitation to discover something new, every detail a sign of attention. When it comes to wine, let the owner guide you: his enthusiasm will steer you towards pairings that enhance every nuance of flavour.

Name: Altro Paradiso
Address: 234 Spring St., New York, NY, 10013, USA
Description: Often packed and quintessentially SoHo, this beloved charmer from Chef Ignacio Mattos is as welcoming as ever. The setting is comfortably stylish with its high ceilings, amber hues, and handsome woodwork accented with wine bottles all over. Far from predictable, the menu is a thoughtful, creative curation based on the seasons and on regional specialties. Pastas like the strozzapreti with Meyer lemon or the capellini with tuna and Calabrian chili are made in-house and rotate frequently. Entrees like the roasted half chicken or bronzed Milanese feed groups with ease. Another house specialty? The salads. From winter citrus topped with Formaggio di Fossa to abundant chicories spiked with a sharp vinaigrette, they are worthy complements to any meal.

Name: Altrokè
Description: Located in the pedestrianised historic centre of Ljubljana, Altrokè occupies an ancient building of authentic charm, with exposed stone walls and brick vaulted ceilings, alongside a small terrace looking onto a narrow cobbled street. The kitchen, inspired by Istria and the Mediterranean, distinguishes itself through the use of produce from the family estate at Plavje, near Koper: grapes, olives, figs and aromatic herbs, together with house-made oil and vinegars, elevate well-executed and flavourful dishes of land and sea tradition, accompanied by a carefully curated wine selection.

Name: Alumni Kitchen Table
Address: Glenaree, Feighcullen, Rathangan, R51 RH90, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Pets not allowed
Description: There’s something charming about this personally run rural restaurant with a contemporary feel. Stay the night in one of their four rooms to make a proper occasion of your visit and dine either around the eight-seater communal table or at the small open kitchen island. The balanced tasting menu is quite an immersive experience, featuring a range of inventive, adventurous dishes using some prime Irish ingredients. Well-crafted artisan crockery, locally made leather items, fine cutlery and a well-chosen wine pairing all enhance the experience.

Name: Am Osterfeuer
Description: First opened as a bakery 100 years ago, this family-run establishment is now in its fourth generation. Hans-Jörg Dunker and his team have long been synonymous with quality and Westphalian cuisine with an international twist. The restaurant interior is attractive and cheerful, having been given a skilful modern makeover, but care has been taken to leave the traditional character of the building intact. One of the chef's specialities is the wonderful fish and shellfish soup with aioli, bread and Parmesan. A gorgeous terrace for summer. There is also a charming hall available for festivities.

Name: Ama
Description: This engaging restaurant in the heart of the spa resort is helmed by chef Adrien Layssac who rolls out seasonal market cuisine made with local produce: txangurro à la donostiarra; Basque lamb, squash and sweet chestnut gnocchi. Colourful, flavoursome fare that hits the spot every time.

Name: Ama.zo - Cozinha Peruana
Description: This restaurant occupies the charming garden of an old property known as the Casa da Don'Anna, a 20C house with a strong coffee legacy. The ambience here is delightful, protected by the vagaries of the weather by an almost invisible roof, and features large jabuticabeira trees, tables laid out in the garden, and a semi-open kitchen to the rear. Here, Peruvian chef Enrique Paredes conjures up Andean cuisine that is reinterpreted through the use of local ingredients, strong flavours, pleasant textures and subtle nuances from the Amazon region. Among the starters, the fresh oysters with a Japanese ponzu sauce, physalis and black massago stands out, followed, perhaps, by a main of ossobuco cooked at low temperature with an Arequipeño sauce, and accompanied by a cassava millefeuille. Lovers of cacao will adore the intense and absolutely delicious chocolate x 4!

Name: Ama.zo - Pátio Higienópolis
Description: Located outside of the Pátio Higienópolis shopping mall, it features an attractive room with lots of natural light and an open-air terrace decorated with plants and Peruvian works of art. Here, the Lima-born chef Enrique Paredes, whose philosophy is “Cooking with freedom”, is at the helm of his second venture, where he combines Peruvian flavours and techniques with local ingredients to showcase the flavours of the Amazon, without losing sight of the region’s roots. On the menu you’ll find dishes such as langoustine carpaccio, the traditional Lima dish “causa limeña”, along with various types of ceviche, rice dishes and vegetarian and vegan options. One dessert that you won’t want to pass up is the “Suspiro Limeño” made with delicious Peruvian “dulce de leche”, a dehydrated quinoa and togarashi meringue, praline and chocolate sorbet – a true delight for the tastebuds!

Name: Amadeus
Address: Rua Haddock Lobo 807, São Paulo, 01420-002, Brazil
Description: No description of Amadeus can be made without mentioning the Masano family, along with their passion, enthusiasm and dreams. Thanks to rave reviews of their cooking from friends, they decided to open a restaurant known as “fish corner” in São Paulo. Today, the kitchen is overseen by chef Bella Masano, the owners’ daughter, who embellishes the menu with her innovative culinary creations alongside classic dishes which have been given a contemporary makeover. Her cooking is showcased on an à la carte and tasting menu which includes options such as fresh oysters from the family’s own beds in Florianópolis. Amadeus’ signature dishes include the shrimp “à paulista”, prepared with olive oil and garlic, which is full of flavour and perfect for sharing, and the “moqueca Amadeus”, a stew with fish and shrimp, served with plantain and onion farofa – an exquisite combination!

Name: Amai by Viktor
Address: 4 Harry Street, Dublin City, D02 CX24, Ireland
Description: Describing itself as ‘Brazilian Roots in Irish Soil’, this hidden-away restaurant offers something different to the Dublin dining scene. Set on the first floor of a former shoe shop, you ring the doorbell by the plain black door to enter, before being whisked up into the dining room. Foliage hangs from the ceiling, while a drawing of a favela pays homage to where Chef Viktor Silva grew up; the restaurant’s name, Amai, is a tribute to the women who raised him. The tasting menu fuses Irish produce with South American flavours in dishes that are packed with interesting flavours and textures.

Name: Amajia
Address: 189 Huanggang Road, Jinshan District, New Taipei, Taiwan
Description: In 2020, this red-brick house perched on a slope was turned into a restaurant that serves the freshest catch from the nearby Huanggang port, plus other home-style favourites. Its name is the transliteration of "grandma's home" in Mandarin, and the seasoned chef strives to foster a sense of comfort and warmth – and to deliver the familiar taste of grandma's cooking. Tender and tasty, the braised pork belly exudes the aromas of dried bamboo shoot.

Name: Amal
Address: 131 Bloor St. W., Toronto, M5S 1R1, Canada
Description: Looking for a bite to eat in between shopping and sightseeing? Amal, with a sexy, sleek, mod Middle Eastern look and ambient vibe, is just the place. Tables are always in demand here, but the smartly dressed service team handles it all seamlessly. Weekends are especially buzzy thanks to entertainment ranging from belly dancers to DJs spinning tunes. Expect modern presentations of classic Lebanese and Middle Eastern dishes on this halal menu, all prepared with authenticity, heart and refinement. Order a few mezze to start - perhaps the seared halloumi or the spinach fatayer. Then, opt for one of their delicious skewers or grilled octopus, which are worthy choices. For dessert, save room for the delightful kanafeh.

Name: Amalie
Description: A charming 18C townhouse by Amalienborg Palace - its two tiny, cosy rooms are decorated with antique prints. The menu offers a large choice of traditional Danish dishes, including herring prepared in various ways; pickled, fried and marinated in curry or port are some of the options available for lovers of the fish. Salmon, salads and smørrebrød are also available, in satisfyingly tasty versions of tried-and-tested classics.

Name: Amandus
Address: Via Statale 125, Mandello del Lario, 23826, Italy
Description: Situated in the Villa Lario Resort, this restaurant directly overlooks the lake and boasts fine views which extend as far as the promontory of Bellagio. The excellent cuisine features a few freshwater fish dishes, as well as plenty of meat and seafood options, on a menu that combines classic recipes with a few more creative specialities.

Name: Amandus
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Interesting wine list
Description: Located a short walk from the Old Town, Amandus brings with it a dose of history and a relaxed, bohemian vibe. Guests arrive all together at 7pm, whereupon owner Deivydas Praspaliauskas greets them personally – and further interaction comes when the chefs present their own dishes at the table. The surprise tasting menu draws its inspiration from historical recipes and flavours, which are brought together, updated and presented in a modern way. For something a little more intimate, book the artistically curving table in Epotheca, set within an old pharmacy repository.

Name: Amano
Description: This pleasant establishment that serves excellent cuisine is located on the edge of the old town. An interior with exposed brick and concrete walls, vintage-style furnishings and decorative wine racks creates a charming atmosphere. The open kitchen at the end of the dining area turns out modern Italian specialities. The dishes cooked on the open grill, which change every day, are highly recommended; be sure to try the pasta and risotto as well, and the all-year truffle specialities. In addition to an à la carte menu, there is a four-, seven- or ten-course set menu. A fine selection of wines is also available.

Name: Amanõ
Description: The tilde accent over the “o” in the name of this restaurant is a subtle allusion to the sea that lies between Campania (the chef’s native region) and Sardinia (his adopted home). With just a few tables and an open-view kitchen, the dining room here is adorned with hand-made decorations, hence the name of the restaurant (“a mano” means “by hand”). The chef makes full use of Sardinian ingredients in his elaborate and creative cuisine, so this is a good choice for anyone seeking a change from traditional fare.

Name: Amapola
Address: Banyan Tree Hotel, Veya, Camino Vecinal #179, Ejido El Porvenir, Valle de Guadalupe, Ensenada, 22755, Mexico
Description: Dinner at the Banyan Tree Veya resort begins with an adventure. Guests race up the mountainside in a rugged courtesy vehicle and ascend to the highest peak. The stylish hotel enjoys expansive views of the valley, and the intimate, quiet setting borders on sacred. Off to the side, find a room where a large U-shaped counter encircles a kitchen team busy at work preparing a contemporary Mexican tasting menu that features quality, locally sourced seafood. Pristine oysters, clams, tuna, abalone and crab are prepared with panache and often with international influences. A generous wine pairing works well with the elaborate menu.

Name: Amapola Kitchen
Description: The premium location at the foot of Pont Vieux, overlooking the historic town and cathedral, is eminently Instagram worthy. The savvily revamped dinky bistro is run by a former art historian, whose healthy, colourful, well-crafted dishes hit the spot. This unorthodox, fine food DJ mixes South American, Italian and Comorian influences, with a scattering of lacto-fermented ingredients and a preference for organic sources. First-class organic and natural wines.

Name: Amar Barcelona
Address: Gran Via de les Corts Catalanes 668, Barcelona, 08010, Spain
Description: The Palace Barcelona’s in-house restaurant, overseen by chef Rafa Zafra, has a very strong attachment to both the Mediterranean and the city. On the menu you’ll find excellent oysters and caviar, superb fish priced by weight and perfect for sharing, traditional Catalan recipes, as well as the hotel’s signature dishes that pay homage to the Ritz, and a tasting menu (Amar Lentamente) that gives centre stage to the sea and the full bounty of its ingredients.

Name: Amarante
Description: This bistro wedged between Bastille and Lyon railway station serves a bighearted, no-nonsense score rich in nostalgic flavours. The ingredients, such as ‘triple zero’ jumbo shrimps from Nantes, Kintoa pork or monkfish caught by small fishing boats, are allowed to shout their name. The interior is equally simple and authentic: tiled floor, red imitation leather benches and wooden tables. Bags of substance and atmosphere!

Name: Amari
Address: 15 Baker Street, Brighton and Hove, BN1 4JN, United Kingdom
Description: Look out for the bright-red exterior that draws you like a beacon to this Spanish-inspired restaurant tucked down a busy side street in the north of the city. The simply decorated setting keeps the focus on the food, with a menu full of dishes that deliver on their promise: the croquetas are creamy, the crudo is refreshing and the suckling pig is prepared with skill. The wine list is expectedly Spanish in its focus, while the selection of sherries is the ideal way to kick off the evening.

Name: Amarines by Mauro Colagreco
Address: Villa Miraé, 770 chemin de la Garoupe, Antibes, 06160, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Part of a luxurious boutique hotel on the Cap d'Antibes peninsula, this creative fine dining establishment is helmed by renowned chef Mauro Colagreco. The restaurant occupies a charming pavilion set within the hotel gardens. Its dining room, which boasts a decor inspired by the sea and the natural world, opens onto a terrace planted with mulberry plane trees. Expect refined interpretations of Mediterranean cuisine: gamberoni prawn carpaccio with citrus and basil oil; wild-caught Mediterranean fish, sauce vierge with Taggiasca olives, preserved lemon, capers and fennel; floating island calisson-style, lavender-infused crème anglaise.

Name: Amaru by Claudia Canessa
Description: A taste of Peru in the heart of the Upper Engadine. At the restaurant housed in the elegant Kulm Hotel St. Moritz, the charming, attentive and professional front-of-house team welcomes you in a tastefully decorated and cheerful space with a handsome vaulted ceiling. In the kitchen, Claudia Canessa and her team bring Peruvian cuisine in all its diversity to the plate, cooking up modern-inspired dishes using excellent ingredients. Intriguing options include "El Choclo y sus Gambas" (grilled corn cake, red prawns, pickled onions, ocopa) and "Tuna Chicano" (aka ceviche).

Name: Amarylis
Address: Queen Boutique Hotel, ul. Józefa Dietla 60, Kraków, 31-039, Poland
Description: Global and Polish influences are effectively integrated at this basement restaurant inside the Queen Hotel, close to Kraków Old Town. Choose to sit in either a traditional brick-built room or a more modern space furnished in black and white, then sit back and enjoy the attractively presented modern dishes. There’s a good degree of detail in the cooking, which showcases precision and effective flavour contrasts throughout.

Name: Amazónico
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Spread over three floors, the flamboyant and animated Amazónico comes with a greenery-filled, tropical rainforest themed interior, an open kitchen and a lively bar. The Latin American menus reflect the varied communities of the Amazon by offering everything from sushi and sharing plates to grilled meats and fish; all the dishes are colourful, vibrant and full of flavour. Be sure to book a table on the first floor for prime views of the chefs in action in the open kitchen, then head to the panoramic terrace for a Latin-inspired aperitif.

Name: Amazónico
Address: 10 Berkeley Square, Mayfair, London, W1J 6BR, United Kingdom
Description: There is a tremendous sense of flair to this sexy, stylish restaurant with a party atmosphere. The glowing, flaming grills are an immediate eye-catcher, as is the jungle-inspired décor that combines with live music to make this the perfect place not just for a meal, but for a proper night out. Quality ingredients power the roster of South American dishes from tiraditos to tequeños. There's a small sushi selection available too, from the playfully named 'Japazonico' menu.

Name: Ambeis
Description: Sharing is the name of the game at this small restaurant near Place de la Canourgue, so let's partake in the pleasure of lovely creative dishes made with high-quality, environmentally friendly Occitan ingredients – fish soup, rouille, cucumber, celery; veal, purple beans, basil, hazelnuts, served cold carpaccio-style; figs, ricotta and honey for dessert. At this pleasant eatery, even the sourdough bread is made in-house.

Name: Amber Garden
Address: Van Heuven Goedhartlaan 15, Amstelveen, 1181 LE, Netherlands
Description: Amber Garden is the most stylish of Chinese restaurants. The arched doorway, koi and Chinese calligraphy all reflect a seamless harmony between feng shui and modern comfort. The chef also strikes a balance between authenticity and the demands of today's discerning diners. The extensive menu brings together specialties from Chengdu Sichuan, Guangdōng Cantonese, Shanghai and Beijing cuisines. The Peking duck ranks among the finest in the Benelux, the sauces are bursting with nuances of umami, the house-made noodles are divine, and then that delicate interplay of sweet and sour… This is Chinese food that packs a punch!

Name: Ambiente
Description: Few would suspect that such a stylish restaurant could be found on this rather unremarkable industrial estate. In summer, a lovely terrace adds to the appeal. The friendly proprietress provides highly attentive service while the chef-patron transforms top-quality ingredients into freshly prepared classic dishes such as venison saddle with nut crust, savoy cabbage, gnocchi and juniper jus. Three set menus are available (one of them vegetarian), and dishes may also be ordered à la carte.

Name: Ambiente Italiano
Description: Dating from 1902, this inviting villa entices guests with its scenic location and excellent cuisine that caters to all tastes. In the trattoria, the menu features Italian classics, pasta made in-house or freshly caught fish, as well as a selection of pizzas. Ristorante Ambiente Italiano, meanwhile, serves more sophisticated dishes that draw on Italian influences. The terrace with its stunning views of the Main River is a summer highlight! The service is friendly and attentive. Good to know: There is a car park directly in front of the building.

Name: Ambos
Description: Overlooking the Senate (upper house of the French parliament) and Luxembourg gardens, this friendly bistro in tune with its era sports an open kitchen and a small counter. ‘Ambos’ (‘both’ in Spanish) refers to Pierre Chomet and his Venezuelan wife, Cristina. Their culinary adventures have taken them from Bangkok to London and Paris, and a Top Chef TV season for Pierre. Together they lovingly concoct a light-hearted, personal and vibrant tapestry of flavours that draws on a wide variety of influences – European (monkfish from Le Guilvinec, butternut, tapioca and shellfish) and Thai (tom kha kai-style langoustine tartar,) as well as South American (Castilian beef, sweetcorn, cachapa and mole seasoning).

Name: Ambra
Description: A restaurant within a restaurant, Ambra is an intimate experience built around a single communal table in the dining room or four cozy seats in the kitchen. Chef Chris D'Ambro engages guests during this leisurely tasting menu that can take upwards of three hours. What’s the rush, anyway? House-made pasta and gnocchi, warm focaccia and the likes of sweetbreads and lamb draw on Italian inspiration and reflect the team’s own commitment to the changing seasons. Dishes are attractively presented, and free-flowing beverage pairings are required.

Name: Ambre.
Address: 2860 chemin des Quatre-Bourgeois, Québec, G1V 1Y3, Canada
Description: Located in Sainte-Foy, at a remove from the historical centre, this restaurant wins you over with its laid-back and inviting atmosphere. The setting is simple, but the welcome is warm. The restaurant showcases ingredients from Quebec's terroir. The indulgent, meticulously prepared cuisine can be enjoyed in the form of a tasting menu consisting of a dozen small plates to share: Gaspé Peninsula lobster ravioli and cauliflower with a fragrant bisque, house-made beer sausages and Migneron de Charlevoix cheese aligot, or Paris-Brest made according to time-honoured tradition. A 100% Quebec wine list rounds off this gourmet experience.

Name: Ambrozijn
Description: Previously a church, Irenekerk (1891) is now a restaurant. Here, design reigns supreme, with a stylish blend of soft and raw materials. The newly built roof truss immediately catches the eye, as do the rugged black walls. Downstairs, the chef's table encircles the completely open kitchen; on the upper floor, there is a magnificent bar built in the shape of an organ. This place is all the more exceptional because of the way Sven Nijenhuis draws on French cooking styles and innovative techniques. With exquisite sauces and precisely judged seasonings, he makes his mark. Think slow-cooked pork cheeks with glazed aubergine, mayonnaise finished with Thai basil, subtly spicy baba ganoush and a veal jus elevated with fenugreek. Simply divine!

Name: Amen
Description: Two-star chef Pascal Devalkeneer (Le Chalet de la Forêt) has a knack for picking the best produce. From the contemporary dishes and intense flavours to the range of textures, his dishes are masterpieces of culinary art. Amen!

Name: Amfora
Description: There’s a stylishly stripped-back look to this passionately run restaurant where the moody colour scheme and lighting set the scene for a globetrotting meal. The menu is inspired by the chef’s travels and features flavours from around the world, including several from the Middle East, and each dish is as generous in size as it is in flavour. The thoughtfully curated wine list includes a strong natural selection and plenty of choice by the glass.

Name: Amici
Description: It is as if the sun never sets over this characterful, whitewashed street corner building on the Instagram-perfect village square of Sint-Martens-Latem. As its name suggests, it is just the spot to feast on lashings of joyful Italian cuisine with friends and family. Vitello tonnato, al dente fettuccine with ragù and parmesan, house-made tiramisu: familiar family favourites that deliver the goods every time! The menu is comforting yet interesting and is backed up by a sensibly-priced list of well-curated Italian wines. An absolute treat.

Name: Amico BJ
Address: Shop 109, 1F, Pacific Century Place, 2A Gongrentiyuchang North Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
Description: The faux-industrial space with bare concrete and exposed bricks is livened up by the generous use of plants. The food is basically Italian with Japanese influences – the chef spent years in Italy, where he met his Japanese wife. Local ingredients are juxtaposed creatively and some items, like bread and sauces, are made from scratch. Check out the wine list with good Italian labels. Book ahead for a seat at the counter overlooking the open kitchen.

Name: Ammazzacaffè
Description: This quintessential Italian gem on Grand Street is bound to surprise the moment you enter. The large and welcoming space draws you in thanks to an impressive wood bar, sleek dining tables and a handsome penny-tiled floor. Both the tables and light olive-tinged walls are dressed minimally—the former with wildflowers and the latter with beautifully framed photos. The garden outside will transport you to a trattoria in Umbria—on a dime. The well-edited menu spins to the season but start with a spiedini (skewer) or dish for the table to share. Do not miss their expertly prepared pasta dishes like ondine, with shrimp in a kicky tomato sauce, then follow it up with an entree like the grilled branzino with cauliflower pieces, roasted grapes, wilted spinach, almond puree, and verjus. Tiramisu is a classic send-off.

Name: Ammākase
Description: In case you're curious about the name (or perhaps you guessed), this place serves a 6- to 10-course omakase-style tasting menu, showcasing diverse flavours from across India. Chef Robin champions a refined take on Indian cuisine, using solid French techniques and ingredients from West Bengal, Gujarat and Sri Lanka. Elegant smaller dishes are meticulously prepared for a balance of flavours. Perfectly paired with their Indian-inspired cocktails.

Name: Amo Bistrot
Description: Traditional features such as exposed stone walls and wooden ceilings provide a pleasant contrast to the contemporary-style furnishings at this restaurant housed in the charming Palazzo Forti, while the attractive cloister with its old walls and soft lighting is highly recommended in the hot summer months. The cuisine combines traditional meat and fish dishes with Asian fare, including the option of sharing small dishes such as tapas or bao (steamed buns). There’s also an excellent brunch on Sundays.

Name: Amore, Pasta e Gioia
Address: Rue de la Crêche 11, Ixelles, 1050, Belgium
Description: The name of this family-run osteria rather says it all! In the company of Giuseppe and Karina in the kitchen and Kevin in the dining room, you know you are in the hands of a team you can trust. Start with an array of flavoursome antipasti, like beef carpaccio and shavings of parmesan laced in a tangy dressing, followed by a dish of house-made pasta, like al dente tagliatelle in a gutsy meat sauce. Next what about a succulent Angus rib steak alla tagliata? Each dish is packed in indulgent Italian scents and flavours and rather than fussy frills, you can expect familiar, heartwarming flavours. Go there your eyes closed!

Name: Amour Blanc
Address: Fleur de Loire, 26 quai Villebois-Mareuil, Blois, 41000, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Christophe Hay's second restaurant is named after a species of carp. It is located on the first floor of a modern extension slightly set back from the original building. This inviting wood-panelled and light-filled interior, with its large bay windows looking out over the Loire, immediately works its magic. The chef of Fleur de Loire gives free rein to his passion for Loire ingredients (local cheeses, géline de Touraine heirloom poultry, fried small fish and mullet from the River Loire, lamb and caviar from the Sologne), but also Wagyu beef from his own farm. In short, fine ingredients treated with care to create dishes that tend towards the classical.

Name: Amparito Roca
Description: One of those restaurants that never fails to impress and feels as though it has been a long-standing fixture on the Madrid dining scene, establishing a hugely loyal following in the city in a short space of time, especially amongst its business community. Named after a famous pasodoble, it focuses on well-prepared honest and traditional cuisine on an à la carte featuring copious dishes that always includes one or two game-based escabeches. The decorative detail here comes as an added surprise!

Name: Amphitryon
Address: 26 rue de la Boucherie, Limoges, 87000, France
Description: This pretty half-timbered house in the heart of the picturesque village of Les Bouchers is the domain of chef Olivier Polla. His modern cuisine lets the ingredients do the talking (foie gras, scallops, calf sweetbreads, female Muscovy duck etc), prepared according to his inspiration. A real treat for the taste buds.

Name: Amu
Description: A stone’s throw from the main square, the Amu Food and Wine Bar sports a marriage of elegant and intimate that is both romantic and sexy. In this intriguing setting, chef Marjanne Moonen rustles up genuine delicacies. Her surprise menu, composed of fascinating dishes based on just a few ingredients, is both free of fancy frills and always spot on. Her distinctive culinary signature is a patchwork of Mediterranean influences, spices and fermentation techniques from the Middle East. Examples include her yoghurt and tahini sauce that adds a kick to a dish of sweet potatoes and carrots, suavely blending depth and balance. The affordable wine list is sourced from all over the world.

Name: Amuse by Kevin Dalgleish
Address: 1 Queen's Terrace, Aberdeen City, AB10 1XL, United Kingdom
Description: Kevin Dalgleish is a well-known chef in Aberdeen and his restaurant occupies the spacious basement of a granite townhouse, in a quiet residential neighbourhood yet just minutes from the city centre. Kick off with a drink in the bar or by the wood burning stove. The kitchen use prime Scottish ingredients blended with French techniques to create good-looking dishes that deliver on flavour.

Name: Amused Food & Wine
Description: On one side is Next wine bar, which is a stylish and trendy spot in which to sample vinologist Corine Vink's latest finds, served with freshly prepared bar snacks. Then there is the elegant restaurant with its chic decor, where Chiel de Groot incorporates his creative ideas into a surprise menu and beautifully presented plates of food. He likes to use produce from his own vegetable garden to bring his creations to life. Intensity is his guiding principle: a grilled sandwich filled with game stew, for instance, makes for an original accompaniment to a medium-rare roe fillet, an exquisite game jus and a cream sauce with chanterelles. Prepare to be surprised with every bite!

Name: Amélys
Description: This bright, airy brasserie, which is a hit with everyone, serves tasty, scrumptious food all day long, and yummy brunches on Sundays. The varied menu features classical fare, of the likes of steak tartare, vol-au-vent and chicken cordon bleu, and more modern dishes, always with the chef’s international signature. Examples range from a tempura of anchovy to seabass in a herby crust and a delicious medley of veggies with citrus fruits and herbs.

Name: Amí Bistro
