Description: On the ground floor of the Winckley Stays Hotel, you’ll find this sweet restaurant where an open fire greets you on arrival in the colder months. There’s a cosy feel to the room, which is minimally decorated but enlivened by some bright artwork on the walls. The cooking takes the form of a seasonal tasting menu, with dishes like duck leg suet pudding delivering intense flavours. Friendly, efficient service enhances the experience, as does the choice between two wine flights and even a beer pairing.

Name: Avenida
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The old saying “talent runs in the family” is particularly apt in this case! Dutch chef Roeland Klein’s passion for cooking was born from his father’s example, a chef of a Michelin‑starred restaurant in his home country. At the Lagos Avenida hotel’s restaurant, a few steps from the beach with a view over Lagos marina, you can choose to sit at the counter of the attractive open kitchen and watch the dishes being prepared, or enjoy the meal in the cosy glass‑walled dining room. With tasting menus — shorter at lunch and fuller at dinner — and à la carte options, the offering combines maritime flavours, such as grilled mackerel served with oysters, mussels and salmon roe, with outstanding meats, such as rib‑eye aged for 12 weeks, from José Gordon–El Capricho, considered a benchmark in the field. An ideal experience to share as a couple or among a group of friends!

Name: Avista
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: It is located in the fabulous Cliff Bay hotel! This restaurant, like its older “sibling” — the two‑Michelin‑starred Il Gallo d’Oro — enjoys truly spectacular views, with the immensity of the coast and the Atlantic as its backdrop. The menus, signed by chef Benoît Sinthon, are prepared daily by chef João Luz and, among a wide offer, include two tasting menus (Innovation and Vegetarian Innovation), à la carte options, vegetarian dishes, petiscos (Portuguese small plates) and even a children’s menu. The focus is seasonal Mediterranean cuisine and the concept of comfort food based on local ingredients (above all from the PortoBay kitchen garden), where dishes shine such as Black Angus tartare with balsamic vinegar, Pommery mustard, confit egg yolk and cep ice cream, Atlantic squid with cuttlefish sauce, ginger and smoked Spanish paprika, or 100% acorn‑fed Iberian pork fillet, sweet potato, pineapple and mustard jus.

Name: Avista Ásia
Description: It completes the culinary offering of the luxurious Cliff Bay hotel! This restaurant, located on the upper floor of Avista, firmly backs Asian fusion cuisine with Japanese, Chinese and Korean influences, always with robust flavours to which are added touches from the Mediterranean and the Madeira archipelago. Chef Rui Pinto’s background, acquired in renowned restaurants at home and abroad, takes him on a unique sensorial journey, with singular views over Funchal and the Atlantic. His proposal, based on four distinct menus: Omakase (chef’s choice), Descoberta (3 courses), Nómada (5 courses) and Premium (7 courses) offer you dishes such as scallop tartare, which brings jalapeño together with kalamansi sauce and fig leaf, eel donburi of smoked eel with trout roe and uruchimai (Japanese short‑grain rice) and the dessert Do Funchal a Tokyo, which blends the tropical flavour of passion fruit and Madeiran mango with a touch of ginger and yuzu.

Name: Avize
Address: 956 Brady Ave. NW, Atlanta, GA, 30318, USA
Description: Boho and rustic vibes create the sense of being in a cozy cabin at Chef Karl Gorline's Avize, while the menu leans modern, with a contemporary take on traditional alpine cuisine that incorporates the culinary traditions of France, Italy, Germany and Switzerland. Decadent dining begins with an array of starters such as frog legs, venison tartare and foie gras parfait, to a caviar service featuring berliners filled with elderflower crème fraîche. Main dishes include duck, fermented carrot Bolognese and American wagyu; the Milanese schnitzel is set over a green goddess sauce and topped with mizuna salad with Caesar dressing and furikake breadcrumbs. Black sesame tiramisu is a tempting dessert.

Name: Avli BY TASHAS
Address: Unit C01, Gate Village 9, DIFC, Dubai
Description: Expectations are exceeded at this bright, dapper-looking restaurant in the DIFC. Its owner is of Greek heritage, and the extensive menu offers authentic, carefully cooked Greek dishes made from quality ingredients. Enjoy mezze, salads and seafood alongside classics such as feta saganaki and lamb youvetsi.

Name: Avlu Restaurant
Address: Cankurtaran, Tevkifhane Sokak No:1, Fatih, Istanbul, 34122, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Brunch,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Once a prison, the Four Seasons Hotel Sultanahmet now exudes luxury down to every last detail. Nestled in the inner courtyard, Avlu has a casual feel, a Mediterranean oasis in which you can escape the bustle of the city. Your meal starts with some delicious bread from the wood-fired oven and continues with this fresh take on indulgent Turkish fare. The chef prepares turbot both pan-fried to a succulent finish and folded into dumplings with cauliflower and spinach, rounding off the dish with the fine contrast of a rich sauce and a fresh salad. Between the wide-ranging à la carte selection of Anatolian classics and the tempting set menu (also available in a vegetarian version), making up your mind is the hardest part.

Name: Awabi
Address: 63 Halkett Place, Saint Helier, JE2 4WG, United Kingdom
Description: Owner and self-taught chef, Stephen, takes inspiration from his travels and discoveries across Asia when compiling the immensely appealing menu at this cute neighbourhood spot, which resembles something between a little bistro and an izakaya. There are lots of local ingredients, the bao buns are delicious, and be sure to end with the Japanese French toast.

Name: Awasi - Mendoza
Description: This restaurant, nestled among vineyards, is luxury and distinction in its purest form. With a Spanish colonial design, the Awasi Mendoza hotel (with fewer than 20 exclusive rooms) surprises with its picturesque outdoor areas and breathtaking views of the Andes. The restaurant, intimately lit by candlelight, is run by Samanta Lugo, a chef forged in the kitchen of Awasi Iguazú. Revolving around a single tasting menu called Tradicional Asado Argentino, the proposal seeks to reinterpret the flavours of the national and regional cuisine, always with high culinary standards. There is also a vegetarian option available. You can't miss the empanadas with choice cuts of meat, chorizo, black pudding, pork matambrito (flank steak), ribeye steak, barbecued ribs or the grilled vegetables and salads, which are usually based on products from their own vegetable garden.

Name: Aya Japanese Cuisine
Address: Avenida Pedroso de Morais 141, São Paulo, 05419-000, Brazil
Description: This attractive property with a contemporary ambience and minimalist decor has a good location in a busy part of the city, just a few metres from the famous Avenida Rebouças. It is under the baton of sushi chef Juraci Pereira (better known as “Jura”) who, after working as Jun Sakamoto’s right-hand man for 11 years, decided to open his own venture in collaboration with his business partner Beto Ganme. Downstairs, where guests can sit at the counter to watch the expert hands of the chefs in action, the atmosphere is more intimate, while the upstairs is more modern and cosy. The cuisine includes a special Aya omakase menu, various types of sashimi, sushi (à la carte and combos), makimonos and hot dish options.

Name: Ayantar
Address: Paseo de San Francisco de Sales 41, Madrid, 28003, Spain
Description: In the district of Vallehermoso, next to the sports and leisure centre known as the Parque del Tercer Depósito, you’ll find this restaurant in which the enticing and traditionally focused tasting menu has an unashamed focus on classic recipes, stews and slow-cooked dishes (veal tripe, cod with a pil-pil sauce, oxtail in red wine with a celeriac purée, truffled pigs’ trotters etc), a few grilled meat dishes, and excellent dishes of the day that don’t appear on the menu. Half-portion options are also available for the majority of the dishes here.

Name: Ayara Thai
Address: 6245 W. 87th St., Los Angeles, CA, 90045, USA
Description: Vanda Asapahu has taken on the role of chef in this family-owned and operated restaurant started by her parents. Wood tables and chairs decorate the interior, and a patio also welcomes diners.The menu is packed with everything from tried-and-true pleasures to more inventive items, and the kitchen caters to your spice preferences. Start with their classic papaya salad with a bold and flavorful kick and make sure to get a curry, perhaps the green curry that's made with a fresh chili curry paste and coconut and your choice of protein. Don't ignore their pastries, which incorporate a bit of French technique. The Thai tea flan with bitter caramel and ripe, fresh berries on top is a perfect choice.

Name: Ayutthayarom
Address: 1/1 Mu 7, Ban Pom, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Situated in a pleasant, cool, and shady location, the riverside offers seating in small Thai pavilions and boasts views of a golden pagoda. The space is decorated in traditional Thai style, in keeping with the cuisine, which features intense local flavours. Try the sour soup with fresh chilli and squid, and the aromatic, flavoursome fried river fish in chu chi curry. Round off your meal with classic Thai desserts made with fresh coconut milk.

Name: Ayà
Address: 7F, The Balmori Suites, Hidalgo Drive, Rockwell Centre, Makati - Metro Manila, The Philippines
Description: In a stylish glass-walled lounge on the mezzanine of Hapag is Ayà. This sister restaurant's à la carte menu features an original yet respectful take on Filipino classics: kinilaw or warek-warek (small plates) and Binondo steak or beef short rib kare-kare (mains) pair with a calamansi or coconut house-made cocktails for a modern Filipino experience. Open for lunch and dinner, Ayà is true to its name, derived from "anyaya", an invitation to gather and enjoy.

Name: Azabu
Address: 2F, Hôtel du Parc, 84 Tran Nhan Tong Street, Hai Ba Trung Ward, Hanoi, 113000, Vietnam
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Located on the 2nd floor of Hôtel du Parc, bask in the elegant main dining room or watch the sushi chefs at work from the blonde wooden counter. The menu covers all the bases and is great value for money at lunchtime. The extensive à la carte menu offers a fine range of Kaiseki options. Don't overlook the house specialities, including the knockout sushi and sashimi. A smooth, professional operation run by a smart, friendly team. Sushi omakase, crafted by Chef Toshihide Terado, is served only on Tuesday to Saturday evenings and requires advance reservation.

Name: Azalina’s
Address: 499 Ellis St., San Francisco, CA, 94102, USA
Description: Chef Azalina Eusope continues to make her mark as an ambassador for Malaysian cuisine in this cleverly designed space that calls to mind a tropical hideaway ensconced in the rough-and-tumble Tenderloin.The menu is a frequently changing seasonal prix fixe with dishes that offer her own interpretation of flavors she grew up with— think California meets Penang. Quality ingredients and creativity are hallmarks, seen in a dish of "economy noodles" with fermented chili paste, topped with barbecued quail and toasted hazelnuts, or steelhead trout baked in banana leaves. Her pastry training is evident in a complex dessert of pandan custard with water chestnut and coconut granita, served with a take on kuih kasturi, a mung bean fritter filled with jackfruit and sweet red bean.

Name: Azalée
Description: The Von Siebenthal family welcomes you with dedication and genuine hospitality – both at the stylish Boutique-Hotel Alpenrose and in the restaurant. In an elegant traditional setting, diners tuck into classic cuisine with a contemporary twist. You can choose between a vegetarian or a conventional tasting menu, with the option to order individual dishes à la carte – such as porcini ravioli with Alpine cheese, shallots and sun-dried tomatoes, or perch fillet in rice paper with green asparagus, verjuice, sorrel and gnocchi. In summer, a pared-down version of the menu from Sammy's Grill Restaurant & Bar, which is only open in winter, is also available. Exceptionally warm service is provided by the proprietress and her daughter. Stunning terrace overlooking the mountains!

Name: Azerole
Description: Originally from Northern China, Xin Meng runs this delightful French-Asian fusion place with a simple neo-bistro decor (stone walls, dark wood tables and chairs). Single-handed in the kitchen, the chef skilfully combines spices, tofu and kimchi with high-quality seasonal French ingredients, to compose dishes such as rack of pork, chimichurri, courgette cream and green curry, accompanied by a dash of creamy hummus and multi-coloured carrot ribbons tossed in an orange vinaigrette – delicious!

Name: Azimut
Description: This wine bar/cave à manger serves locavore cuisine whose flavours are drawn from locally sourced and, often, organic ingredients (including free-range poultry, snails from Eyrieu, lentils, fish from a fish farm near Châtillon-en-Diois, olives from Nyons). At lunchtime, there is a short and very reasonably priced set menu. To be washed down with organic or sulphur-free wines from a terrific selection – and the recommendations are on point!

Name: Aziza
Address: 5800 Geary Blvd., San Francisco, CA, 94121, USA
Description: Chef Mourad Lahlou made his name at the original Aziza, but this triumphant second act offers the same magic. Dressed up with pale hues and a colorful bar, this remarkable menu offers a fresh take on the chef's signature Moroccan fare. Chef Lahlou is famous for weaving California staples into dishes with stunning results. Loyalists will be happy to know the iconic specialty, basteeya with golden phyllo wrapped around a delicious mix of shredded chicken and spiced almonds, remains. Other specialties, like mussels with vadouvan butter and marash pepper, or grilled octopus with hand-rolled couscous, preserved apricot and merguez vinaigrette, are every bit as appealing. Compelling cocktails and warm service seal the deal.

Name: Azotea
Description: In the very heart of the city, with a small terrace that sets the mood, the interior reveals deliberately aged walls in soft shades of green, enriched by climbing plants that evoke a corner of South American jungle. It is the ideal setting for Nikkei cooking that looks directly to Peru, the chef’s native land, and expresses itself through a range of beautifully fresh offerings available both à la carte and within carefully considered tasting menus. The philosophy is clear: to celebrate one of the most vibrant and contemporary gastronomic traditions, with a hand attuned to contrasts and the clarity of flavours. Among the distinctive features of the house, which also operates as a well-stocked cocktail bar, the sip pairing stands out: a sequence of small cocktail tastings crafted with ingredients typical of Nikkei cuisine, conceived to accompany the dishes without overpowering them. Not to be missed is the yuzu Americano, pleasingly citrus-forward, with a hint of sharpness that invites the next sip.

Name: Azul Mariscos + Muelle
Address: 1177 N. Elston Ave., Chicago, IL, 60642, USA
Description: The surrounds are industrial and rather bleak, but get up close only to discover this veritable mirage of a spot. Settled on a bright corner, it is a pulsating retreat that virtually lures you in with hospitality. If that's not irresistible, the interior features a series of intriguing murals by street artist, Senkoe; aqua-blue chairs, cement floors, and a DJ booth complete the festive look.Diners are attended to by a small army of smiling servers. Pan-Mexican dishes are on the menu, with such popular plates as a whole-grilled pineapple stuffed with tender octopus, chipotle-cream sauce, and Chihuahua cheese; or a spicy and smoky seafood paella. This is food that's clearly well-rounded in its flavors, impressive to look at it, and captivating to taste.

Name: Azul Mediterráneo
Address: Paseo del Arco de Ladrillo 48, Valladolid, 47008, Spain
Description: Located opposite the Ciudad de la Comunicación park and aesthetically consistent with its name, the yellow and blue tones here make us think of the sand and the sea. The highlights of its menu are the rice dishes, all delicious and prepared at a counter in full view of the diner, but you should also try some of their creative pinchos (Principino, Michemar, Lechazus Deliciosus, and more), as they have been awarded prizes in different regional competitions. If you prefer to let yourself be guided, the Brisa menu is an excellent choice!

Name: Azura
Description: This ambitious Danforth Avenue restaurant brings a new standard of hospitality to the neighborhood. Just across from the favored music hall, enjoy a generous, leisurely tasting menu that plays with Mediterranean flavors and rolls with the seasons. Start to finish, Chef Adam Ryan displays his creativity and eye for presentation. From the striking assortment of canapés to an inventive short rib tagine, ingredients are often locally foraged and always arranged with style. The space itself is one of ease, featuring a busy bar anchoring the center, warm honeyed lighting, and a comfy tufted banquette. Esoteric wines and cocktails, like the gin-based Olive Branch, tell their own thoughtful stories and should be explored liberally.

Name: Azurite
Description: When a passionate craftsman and veteran of the Dutch culinary scene like Mario Ridder shares his most personal vision, every foodie knows it's time to pay attention. In the heart of Delft, Azurite immerses diners in a tasteful setting featuring glass, concrete and wood. Raw, natural and yet warm, with select provisions showcased as visual highlights (the upper floor is home to a wine loft holding hundreds of bottles and a vintage whisky and digestif bar). The service is equally elegant – unobtrusive yet attentive – with a sommelier who curates outstanding pairings. The stage is set; now the chef lets his expertise in classic cuisine and passion for Dutch produce do the talking.There is a choice of three set menus (vegetarian, signature and caviar) that encapsulate his distinguished career with finesse. Picture a room-temperature bluefin tuna fillet served with a simple artichoke cream, then topped with a fine sliver of aged beef, drizzled with a full-bodied olive oil and finished with a subtly vibrant kohlrabi vinaigrette. Simply exquisite! Mario Ridder bares himself bare in the kitchen, and that promises the diner an extraordinary experience.

Name: AÜC
Description: Excellent chicken croquettes, tripe with calf’s head boasting a wonderful spicy touch, a tasty special section dedicated to macaroni (just like mama used to make)... This cosy restaurant in the heart of the Sant Gervasi neighbourhood is run by experienced catering professionals and champions traditional Catalan cuisine that takes diners back to the flavours of home, reflecting a mother or grandmother’s cuisine, while not shying away from some modern touches in some dishes. Here, above all, humble and local cuisine can be rediscovered.

Name: AŞEKA
Address: Müeyyedzade Mahallesi, Arap Oğlan Sokak No:6, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34425, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Tucked away in a side street in the Karaköy neighbourhood, this somewhat inconspicuous historical building reveals a tastefully decorated interior featuring intimate lighting, a palette of dark brown hues, and regularly changing artwork. Diners can choose from a tempting à la carte selection or opt for one of the creative set menus. The dishes are not unnecessarily complicated but are bursting with flavour – it is the seasoning and robust sauces that set them apart. Take, for instance, the succulent agnolotti del plin, filled with slow-cooked oxtail and served with a Parmesan cream and fine breadcrumbs. Be sure to stop by the handsome bar to sample one of the cocktails.

Name: B-Restaurant
Description: Atop the InterContinental Hotel, the broad windows offer a 180-degree view over Ljubljana and its castle, particularly captivating as evening falls. In a space of contemporary design with an open kitchen, B-Restaurant offers a cuisine that reflects the openness of the panorama: alongside reinterpreted Slovenian dishes, creations of international scope find their place. Drawing on tradition and working with high-quality ingredients, the chef transforms them with technique and creativity in a modern spirit, guided by a philosophy of simplicity and taste. Before or after dinner, the B-Bar next door is well worth a visit for a drink with a view.

Name: B7
Description: Be sure to book ahead at this homely neighbourhood restaurant,which has an experienced chef at its helm. The room has a pleasingly simple rusticity, and the atmosphere and service have a laid-back feel, with the owner both cooking for and serving the guests himself. Pick from around 16 dishes – sharing 4 between two diners is a great way to sample a range of flavours – or simply choose the tasting menu. The flavoursome modern cuisine takes its influences from around the globe, ranging from Cantabrian anchovies to salmon ceviche; desserts are a highlight and the wine list offers great value.

Name: BABO
Description: BABO is currently something of a lesser-known gem. Set up by a pair of experienced restaurateurs, it’s split between two rooms and a smart terrace. One of the owners hails from Georgia and it’s this that informs the menu. Delicious breads are cooked in the pizza oven and the charcoal grill adds a lovely flavour to the various meats and fish. Order two dishes each and share – maybe beef and pork khinkali (dumplings), salmon in bazhe (walnut) sauce or chicken tabaka with salt and lemon. The superb wine list showcases a unique mix of classic and modern Georgian wines, which they import directly.

Name: BAHR
Address: Praça Luís De Camões 2, Lisbon, 1200-243, Portugal
Description: Located on the top floor of the Bairro Alto Hotel (hence the origin of its name) and featuring a kitchen that opens onto the dining room, BAHR describes itself as a “bohemian and irreverent space”. At lunchtime it offers a much more informal market-inspired “executive menu”, with more elaborate, exclusively à la carte dishes in the evening, but all featuring the very best ingredients.

Name: BAK
Description: Take the stairs to the third floor of this unobtrusive warehouse (you'll need to ring the bell in the evening) to discover this rather rugged yet inviting restaurant with its splendid view over the IJ River. Benny Blisto sets great store by the origin of his ingredients, be it a carrot or ray wing. Locally sourced, seasonal produce is the inspiration behind his creativity. For instance, with slightly tart rhubarb and an exquisite beetroot sauce, he elevates a venison fillet to new heights. An exciting dining experience is guaranteed!

Name: BALOCI
Address: 18 Highfield Road, Birmingham, B15 3DU, United Kingdom
Description: An elegant Georgian townhouse has been given a bold and blingy makeover for this opulent restaurant, where the décor blends rich, plush furnishings with flashes of shiny gilt. The cooking is self-described as ‘Indo-Persian’ and indeed the menu is an enticing melting pot of influences, including those from Afghanistan, Turkey and Balochistan. The tasting menu will allow you to try a broader range of cuisines, but if you’re going à la carte then keep an eye out for the Sultani lamb chops, which melt in the mouth and are enhanced by their subtle spicing.

Name: BAMBAKUN
Description: Two people known only as ‘Bamba-kun’ and ‘Bamba-chan’ offer an interlude of fun at this charming patisserie. To heighten the deliciousness of the prix fixe dessert menu, the sweets are preceded by a light, slightly salty meal of soup, salad and sandwiches. French dessert recipes are interpreted through fruits in season and Japanese ingredients. Baked sweets are misted with awamori, wreathing the creation in a sake aroma.

Name: BANCAL
Description: A unique restaurant in every sense of the word, occupying the old Villa Thiebaut, an aristocratic property in the city’s embassy district that is now home to delightful dining rooms full of history (there’s also a more modern private space in what was once the chapel). The property is also home to the MOM Culinary Institute and has its own small city garden. The restaurant’s identity and cooking, under the baton of chef Miguel Vidal, have their focus on contemporary cuisine that always champions the best seasonal ingredients and classic techniques. These are showcased in outstanding dishes such as the prawn croquettes “al ajillo” with a prawn tartare. On the table you’ll also find a glass dome under which fresh sourdough is presented before being taken to the oven to be baked!

Name: BAR TATAR in der Schreiberei
Description: In the heart of the city, just a stone's throw from Marienplatz, this restaurant is on the ground floor of Munich's heritage-protected chancery (Schreiberei), where the city's history has been recorded since 1552. The attractive interior has a certain brasserie feel and, in good weather, the quiet sheltered courtyard terrace is especially inviting. Made with select ingredients, such as the veal cheeks with truffle polenta, the food is bursting with flavour. The tartare – there are many different variations, including meat, fish and vegetarian options – is a must. Be sure to try one of the delicious desserts, too. The varied à la carte selection is also ideal for sharing. When it comes to the excellent wine list, ask for a recommendation for a glass or bottle to accompany your meal.

Name: BASK
Description: BASK is depicted by a mix of untreated vintage details and a buzzy, rock’n roll vibe. The refrigerated counter is piled high with seafood treats, which are then cooked over a wood-fired asador grill. The chefs have perfected the art of BBQ and craft a lineup of dishes to share of Basque inspiration, loaded with creative touches. Nibble on a few pintxos with your aperitif, before sampling delicacies like grilled turbot or juicy tender breasts of aged guinea fowl flanked by a rich gravy made from the neck. A festival of fascinating and felicitous flavours and delicate sauces. Should you have forgotten to book, there is generally space at the bar around the kitchen for a snack (or two)…

Name: BECKER'S
Description: Matching the architecturally striking design hotel of the same name, this upscale fine dining restaurant impresses with its chic, minimalist style. The interior boasts leather shell chairs, elegant hardwood floors and grey panelling on the walls – a lovely setting in which to enjoy a modern menu made with selected ingredients, to the sound of contemporary background music – choose four- to six courses. Incidentally, chef-patron Wolfgang Becker is not only a cook – as the son of a winegrowing family (now in its fifth generation), he has also trained as a winemaker. He shares his passion for fine wines with his wife Christine Becker, herself a winemaker and sommelier, who oversees the vineyard. Naturally, wines from their own estate are among the options to accompany the excellent food.

Name: BECKER'S Weinhaus
Description: The original building, which houses this, the second Becker's restaurant, stands in contrast to the modern new hotel building. The abundance of pale woodwork makes it nice and cosy in this space, which leads into an adjoining vaulted brick cellar. Choose between a three- or four-course set menu and à la carte options. The "business lunch" deal and the "quick lunch" daily special are popular. Pretty terrace.

Name: BECKERS
Description: The atmosphere in this attractive historical corner-plot building is pleasingly casual. Featuring high ceilings, warm wood panelling, cosy booths and large arched windows, the pretty dining space has the feel of a classic bistro. There is also a bar, and in summer a terrace is set up out front, giving onto the street. The menu includes flavoursome dishes such as oysters, beef tartare, fine fish dishes and premium steaks. Tempting options on the shorter lunch menu include veal meatballs with carrots and mashed potatoes.

Name: BEES Restaurant
Address: Am Rottland 6, Rüdesheim am Rhein, 65385, Germany
Description: This attractive restaurant serving appealing seasonal cuisine is housed in the premises of a former Asbach Uralt brandy distillery. The set menu includes a minimum of four courses, but you can also order à la carte. Sit back to savour your meal and enjoy friendly service in this chic setting with a partially visible kitchen. Tables are set up to create a pleasant terrace in summer. Tip for motorists: there is also a public car park near the train station and the Rhine.

Name: BELLIES
Description: A former factory plays host to this unique restaurant, which brings together exposed brick walls, modern asymmetric tables and designer furnishings. Another unusual feature is the completely plant-based cuisine, which celebrates some often overlooked ingredients. The Italian chef draws on his heritage to inspire the tasting menu, while also adding Asian flavours (such as Sichuan pepper or ssamjang) as well as some Nordic influences (via a range of fermented and preserved components) in order to create original, sometimes playful dishes, like pumpkin, sea buckthorn, gochujang and bergamot ravioli.

Name: BELLY
Address: 157 Kentish Town Road, Kentish Town, London, NW1 8PD, United Kingdom
Description: Your belly will certainly be full after visiting this warm and welcoming Filipino bistro where the flavour-packed cooking will quickly have you planning your return. The concise menu is full of originality and appeal, making choosing the hardest thing you’ll do all day. Do you go for the signature cod pandesal or the fabulous scallops ‘Bicol Express’? Wagyu picanha or seafood calderata? Whatever you opt for, the terrific flavours will shine through. Finish with the unusual-sounding but utterly joyous frozen custard profiterole with salty fish sauce caramel.

Name: BIRD LAND
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: BIRD LAND enchants guests with its wonderfully distinctive yakitori. With supple imagination and a wealth of experience, Toshihiro Wada crafts a new world of possibilities for the humble skewer. Included among the skewers in his set menus are liver paté, chicken grilled in pepper and oyakodon (chicken and egg on rice). Always attentive to customers’ voices, he reveals the value of rare cuts such as chicken oyster. Determined to pass on his skills, he often works the grill with apprentices at his side.

Name: BON CHEMIN
Description: The name, which means ‘good road’, reflects Ryo Hanazawa’s determination to tread the path of the culinary artist with sincerity. His theme is universal flavour and his methods are based on the recipes of the legendary restaurateur Auguste Escoffier. Sardine and vegetable soup, and pigeon and duck roti with offal sauce are long-time favourites in which he takes special pride. Japanese ingredients give a unique twist to his dishes as they bring back the aroma of the good old days of French cuisine.

Name: BORD
Description: You’re guaranteed a warm welcome at this sweetly run bohemian bistro. A communal table is at the heart of proceedings, but there are a few smaller tables and some counter seating available too. Starters merge into mains on the daily menu of unfussy, pared-back dishes, where skilful Mediterranean-inspired cooking keeps the focus firmly on the top-quality ingredients. They make their own ricotta on-site and the wood-fired oven is used to great effect, from baking bread in the morning to gratinating langoustines in the evening. Dinner is the main event, but they also open on Saturdays for lunch.

Name: BOU4
Description: First things first: be sure to book, because the Bouvier family's small restaurant has just four tables (hence the name "BOU4"). Junior manager and maître d' Julian Bouvier attentively hosts a maximum of 14 diners. Chef Christoph Gschwendtner also joins in front of house, proud to personally present his creations at the table. His cooking leans towards classic French cuisine, with Asian or Levantine accents adding variety. The dishes are elaborate and technical, as you will see from the get-go with the array of appetisers. Diners can opt for a four- or six-course format of the set menu, the dishes in which change weekly. The meal starts for all diners at 6pm. The curved black wooden tables make for a distinctive feature in the pared-back, modern interior. The restaurant is on the premises of Hotel Jägerhof.

Name: BRASSERIE Schwarzenstein
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: In this chic brasserie in a glass-paned pavilion at Burg Schwarzenstein, you can savour a wonderful view (also magnificent from the terrace!) and market-fresh French cuisine – from starters such as "escargots de vigne en cocotte" to meat and fish dishes such as "choucroute Schwarzenstein" or sole meunière, and, for dessert, île flottante. You also have the option of oysters and caviar. The well-stocked wine list homes in on German and French labels. Tip: For the optimum experience, consider staying overnight – there are lovely individually styled guestrooms distributed across the Parkresidenz, Burghotel and Guesthouse.

Name: BRIKZ
Description: At this restaurant in the heart of Charlottenburg – which used to be a jazz café – Arne Anker and his team serve up cuisine that is inspired by the seasons. Choose the five- to seven-course set menu (water included) or go à la carte; you can also put together your own menu from the à la carte selection, and it is possible to make this vegan. The wafer-thin slices of tender entrecôte and spicy guanciale served on wooden skewers are excellent – described by the chef himself with a wink as "our version of a Berlin kebab". The restaurant is happy to cater for food intolerances – it is best to let them know in advance. The alcohol-free drinks are also fabulous, with house-made kombucha, kefir, syrup, tea etc. The ambience is characterised by striking exposed brick walls and decorative art. The service is friendly and well organised, the atmosphere relaxed and informal – even the chef sometimes comes to diners at their tables. Pleasant pavement terrace.

Name: BROTO
Address: Largo Rafael Bordalo Pinheiro 20A, Lisbon, 1200-445, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: In the heart of Chiado, a Lisbon neighbourhood truly appealing for its abundance of theatres, bookshops and dining options, this relaxed restaurant emerged (hence the name) with the intention of exalting Portuguese culinary roots, always with honesty and a clearly contemporary vision. Chef Pedro Pena Bastos, well known to the wider public for sitting on the judging panel of MasterChef Portugal, presents an extensive menu with a charcutaria (charcuterie) section, small hand-held snacks (we particularly enjoyed Barriga de atum rabilho (bluefin tuna belly), a little gem lettuce, tempura de algas (seaweed tempura), lima caviar (finger lime), dishes designed for sharing, a daily main course that changes every day… all of which celebrate the quality of local produce and give vegetables a very special starring role.

Name: BUTCHER BOY
Address: 2F, Alabang West Parade, Daang Hari Road, Makati - Metro Manila, 1750, The Philippines
Description: This slick restaurant located in a high-rise in Salcedo Village has a long, narrow layout with an open kitchen and glass lamps. High tables, counter seating and leather banquettes make for a relaxed vibe. Quiet at lunchtime, the restaurant draws a crowd in the evenings. The menu impresses with flavourful fare, such as the laksa dumpling and fried bun with chilli crab sauce. Creative cocktails round off the experience at this stylish, modern spot in Makati.

Name: Ba Restaurant
Description: This restaurant combines Chinese traditions with contemporary, fashionable design in a dining room where large red lamps and small lanterns on the tables create an intimate and relaxing feel, accompanied by lounge music as a backdrop. The modern twist added to the classic Chinese dishes gives the cuisine an interesting flavour, from the carefully chosen ingredients and quality of their Dim Sum to our inspector’s favourite dish, namely the scallops with XO sauce, asparagus, foie gras salsa and cured ham chips.

Name: Baan Chik Pork Noodles
Address: 89/3-4 Naresoun Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
Description: This eatery has thrived in a traditional shophouse for over 30 years. Choose between the original flavour and tasty tom yum with its fresh lime and roasted peanut aroma, served with or without soup.

Name: Baan Landai (Phra Pok Klao Road)
Address: 252/13 Phra Pok Klao Road, Si Phum, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
Description: Don’t let the slightly unkempt exterior keep you from visiting Chef Landai’s restaurant. The interior exudes charm with its eclectic décor and a window into the kitchen, where chefs whip up pan-Thai dishes like flavourful pork ribs with red wine sauce. The portions are suitable for sharing with friends, and don’t forget to save room for their traditional Thai desserts.

Name: Baan Nam Ngiew Wieng Kao
Address: 99/4 Mu 5, Nong Pa Khrang, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50000, Thailand
Description: This laid-back shop in a shady spot is known for its traditional Chiang Rai-style nam ngiao. Generous bowls of rich, tangy broth made with fresh coconut milk come with pork or beef, tomato and herbs. Sides and vegetables are also available. Busy at lunchtime, so be ready to wait.

Name: Baan Pomphet
Address: 13/5 U Thong Road, Ho Rattanachai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This Thai restaurant next to Pom Phet (Diamond Fortress) is in the distinctive-looking boutique hotel of the same name. Inside, the stylish dining room is fitted with large windows that frame a view of the restaurant’s deck and the Chao Phraya. Sourcing ingredients from the river and local farms, the chef creates flavourful dishes like standouts grilled river prawns and boiled freshwater snails in red curry soup. Book ahead for a riverside table at dinner.

Name: Baan Rearn Mai
Address: 37/18 Mu 4, Khok Kloi, Takua Thung, Phang-Nga, 82140, Thailand
Description: Operating for 25 years, this small eatery offers an à la carte menu focused on seafood. The freshly prepared meals are light, allowing the natural umami of the seafood to shine. In addition to their signature yellow curry crab, the steamed sea bass with soy sauce is a must-try.

Name: Baan Suan Mae Rim
Address: 261 Mu 2, Chiang Mai-Fang Road, San Pong, Mae Rim, Chiang Mai, 50180, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This popular spot has been serving Northern Thai dishes in Mae Rim district since 2004. The menu is simple, typical Thai fare that leans towards meat and freshwater fish – the owner-chef will gladly recommend the freshest dishes of the day. Start with the deep-fried chilli minced pork – bold, salty and spicy – followed by tom yam fish. Arrive before sunset for a terrace table or opt for the comfort of the air-conditioned room overlooking the tranquil pond.

Name: Baan Suriyasai (Bangrak)
Address: 174 Surawong Road, Si Phraya, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: Located in a restored 100-year-old mansion in the heart of the city, Baan Suriyasai evokes early 20C Thai elegance with time-tested dishes and old-world hospitality. The menu is drawn from royal recipes from the Rama V era and bygone family favourites, including the five-spice stew with boiled eggs, and the stir-fried crispy pork belly, fish flakes and dried shrimp with seasoned paste. Head to the classic Thai cocktail bar upstairs for an after-dinner drink.

Name: Baan Ton Sai
Address: 189/49 Mu 8, Pratu Chai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: The restaurant's vibrant colours stand out from afar. In the backyard, a banyan tree provides pleasant shade. The menu features straightforward and unpretentious seafood, pork and chicken dishes. Expect large servings of seafood that make the mouth water at wallet-friendly prices. We recommend trying their rat na noodles. Closing times may vary, so it's best to arrive early.

Name: Baannok Bangkok (Langsuan Road)
Address: 2F, VIVRE Building, 34/3 Lang Suan Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Baannok serves authentic Khorat-style Thai food, in which the sweetness that is typical to the region is toned down for broader tastes. To awaken the palate, try the sweet and sour Khorat sausage salad. The signature Phat Mi Khorat with a giant river prawn is expertly wok-fried with duck egg and accompanied by a smooth sweet sauce. For something comforting, take the Kaeng Liang Kam Thale So, a spicy vegetable soup, fragrant with herbs and spices commonly used in Isan cooking. Advance reservation is a must.

Name: Babbo Osteria
Address: Rua Barão Da Torre, 632, Rio de Janeiro, 22411 002, Brazil
Description: An outstanding property in a quiet residential section of Ipanema, whose Italian name (“babbo” is a colloquial Italian word for “dad”) provides an insight into the cuisine served here, a fusion of Italian and “carioca” dishes conjured up by chef Elia Schramm. One of the most popular eateries in the area, Babbo Osteria pays homage to the chef's father, and brings childhood memories and family influences to the cooking on offer. One of the dining rooms, decorated with ornaments reminiscent of a traditional Italian “osteria”, provides the backdrop for handmade pasta dishes such as Uova Pepenara (tagliolini served with small cubes of bacon and a creamy soft egg) – the chef's version of the classic carbonara. Main courses include the “filetto”, a medallion served with a delicious pepper sauce and golden gnocchi, as well as desserts in the purest Italian style, such as tiramisù and a perfect combination of pistachio and lime!

Name: Babette
Description: Situated just beyond the centre of Albenga in a beautiful location right on the beach (with only a small private beach club separating it from the sea), this restaurant has been in business for over 20 years (10 years on this site, and 10 in the town centre before that). It is renowned for its excellent, modern cuisine that focuses on top-quality, fresh and seasonal fish. A lighter (yet equally excellent) menu is also available at lunchtime.

Name: Babinicz
Address: Resort Dworzysko, aleja Spacerowa 22, Szczawno-Zdrój, 58-310, Poland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: As you enter this restaurant at the heart of the sprawling Dworzysko estate, it very quickly sets out its stall. A fridge filled with prime meats, along with animal heads lining the walls, add to the feel of an old-school hunting lodge, and indeed Polish meats are at the core of the menu. Steaks of various shapes and sizes are a feature, aged in-house and delivering plenty of flavour. The delightful team are genuinely eager to please and do their bit to enhance the experience.

Name: Babiččina zahrada
Description: This restaurant in a quiet suburb of Prague has bags of charm. The interior is done out in a country-house style complete with lovingly chosen decorations. Outside, the terrace laid out in a gorgeous garden is inviting. The kitchen, which can be seen from the front section of the dining area, serves seasonal, regional and traditional dishes; a favourite is the beef broth with liver dumplings, vegetables and noodles, which is served in a pot to scoop yourself. And the steak tartare is prepared at your table. Friendly service. The hotel has cosy, attractive guestrooms, and the charging station for electric vehicles is a handy amenity. By the way, the name of the restaurant means "grandma's garden".

Name: Baccanti
Description: Facing Matera’s picturesque cave churches in one of the most charming parts of the old town, this restaurant is housed in a complex of old caves. Despite being inspired by local traditions, the cuisine is modern and creative in style and always of the highest quality.

Name: Bacchus
Address: Wedgewood Hotel, 845 Hornby St., Vancouver, V6Z 1V1, Canada
Description: Bacchus is very special indeed. Cocooned inside the Wedgewood Hotel & Spa, this elegant restaurant is the kind of place where quotidian concerns immediately disappear. Just off the intimate lobby, where stunning flower arrangements, a glittering chandelier and marble reception area exude tasteful luxury, Bacchus transports guests to a more refined era. There's even a grand piano to boot. Of course, it's not all style and no substance; Chef Stefan Hartmann turns out classic but memorable dishes. A terrine of foie gras mousse might be paired with roasted plum chutney and caramelized endive, while a dish of prawn and scallop tagliarini is sauced with lobster bisque. Desserts by Chef Samson Iza-Fellows will surprise and delight.

Name: Bacchus
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A hotel restaurant with solid management, cheerful and welcoming. While lunch offers a very simple selection (including club sandwiches and hamburgers), as well as service, it’s in the evening that a beautiful menu based on Sardinian and Mediterranean cuisine is presented, with land-based dishes and especially seafood. When the weather permits, choose a table on the veranda overlooking the pool.

Name: Bacco
Description: Nestled within the historic centre, you’ll find classic and charming Apulian stone environments of a fourteenth-century building, while the kitchen sends forth predominantly fish dishes, along with some meat offerings, in classic Italian tradition recipes with a few modern twists.

Name: BaceLo
Description: BaceLo is located along a central pedestrian street in the heart of the Magdalena district and boasts an informal, rustic-contemporary ambience. The attentive couple in charge (Alex and Mar, both of whom are cooks), showcase cuisine with a contemporary flair through which they enjoy combining Galician-inspired dishes with others from further afield, but always based around local ingredients. Examples include the tom yum crab croquettes with peanut satay, conger eel cannelloni with chipotle au gratin, and pork ribs cooked at low temperature with chestnuts, bulghur wheat, walnuts and curry.

Name: Bachmaier
Description: Ulrike and Otto Bachmaier have been running their restaurant for many years. The modern decor is delightful and you can watch the river traffic on the Neckar through the floor-to-ceiling windows, as well as from the terrace. Friendly and adept service comes courtesy of the lady of the house while the chef-patron delivers seasonal dishes such as Obsiblue prawn soup with ginger, or braised shoulder of locally hunted venison, glazed in the pan, with Swede, palm tree kale and celeriac. A vegetarian set menu is available by prior arrangement. Good wine pairings. Tip: Book well in advance.

Name: Bachtekerke
Description: Bachtekerke is undeniably smart, but its pride and joy is a blissful summer terrace on the banks of the Leie, whose secluded, idyllic setting makes you feel as if you are on an island! Even better, the chef has no equal for wholehearted cuisine, oozing in flavour and variety. From dim sum to share, crunchy, piping hot shrimp fritters and melt-in-the-mouth steak tartare to a bona fide patriotic Belgian dish – vol-au-vent, it finds favour with everyone, from gourmet gluttons to discerning foodies…

Name: Bachten De Leie
Description: Burnished copper saucepans and a striking colour scheme set the stylish scene in this welcoming restaurant. The youthful chef, Louis Wauters, is a butcher’s son and proud of it. You will sample perfectly cooked rib of beef with a silky béarnaise sauce and French fries, but the chef is also keen to pamper fish and seafood amateurs. Flavour and generosity are the watchwords here.

Name: Backmulde
Description: This is just the sort of restaurant you would like to have in your neighbourhood. At this lovely location in the Old Town, in the cosy atmosphere of a charming centuries-old half-timbered house, you can look forward to great food and select wines and expert recommendations. The ambitious food is rooted in classic French cuisine and courts modern trends. In addition to the seasonal menu, daily specials feature on the blackboard. The service is attentive and seamless – and the presence of the chef brings a personal touch. Tip: Take a look around the wine shop opposite.

Name: Backstage
Address: GF, Capella Hanoi, 11 Le Phung Hieu Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Your inner celebrity will revel in this opera-themed restaurant, whose open kitchen takes front stage. Signature dishes like Capella Pho and Bun Cha Hanoi respect their northern heritage, whilst featuring modern techniques with European touches that will leave your tastebuds singing an aria of delight. The impressive cocktail list offers some intriguing mixes. The theatrical setting showcases stunning costumes from the world’s greatest operas.

Name: Bacon
Description: Your host, an enthusiastic champion of natural and organic wines, was a butcher in a former life. In the company of his partner, they have embarked on a new adventure in the shape of a cosy, trendy eatery. She woos diners with fresh cuisine, jazzed up with international seasonings and brimming with flavour in dishes – with or without meat! If you opt for the surprise menu, you will be delighted by her knack for playing with contrasts. An example: lamb cooked two ways – one spicy in pita bread, the other with lamb’s tongues cooked slowly in a tomato coulis and a madeira-laced gravy. Crisp, understated interior with a sober colour scheme and a fondness for plants.

Name: Bacon & Butter
Description: If the name doesn't have you salivating yet, the plates being ferried through the bustling dining room certainly will. Bacon & Butter draws a steady stream of diners — queues often stretch late into the morning — thanks to its promise of hearty American breakfast and brunch done with care.The menu covers the classics, from flapjacks and French toast to omelets and oversized breakfast burritos. Portions are generous and ingredients noticeably fresh, whether you're digging into a stack of pancakes or a simple plate of eggs. A bar adds to the fun with mimosas, cocktails and even playful shots for those leaning into the brunch spirit. Everything here is big enough for two, but who wants to share when it's this good?

Name: Bacucco d'Oro
Description: From the coast, you take a winding road uphill to this family-run trattoria which boasts sea views from its terrace. Apart from the salted cod, the menu only features meat dishes, with a focus on simple, traditional Abruzzo specialties. These include arrosticini (skewered grilled meat), fragrant mushrooms, barbecued meat and delicious “pizza dogge”, the latter a type of layered dessert with sponge cake, custard, confectioner’s cream and Alkermes liqueur. The concise wine list also focuses on the Abruzzo.

Name: Bacán
Address: Lake Nona Wave Hotel, 6100 Wave Hotel Dr., Orlando, FL, 32827, USA
Description: Set in the Lake Nona Wave Hotel, Bacán isn't your typical dining room. Full of energy and personality, the dramatic space dons warm wood, vivid colors, impossibly high ceilings and a luxurious banquette that runs down the middle. On the food side of things, there's a contemporary menu that spans Central and South America, with a good dose of tropical influence. An expo robot that assists with service fits in nicely with the modern aesthetic.Diners may sample small plates like pork belly and lobster tacos; or larger, signature dishes like the market fish with a grapefruit mojo. Dessert is worth saving room for, especially with such options as a banana tart finished with gold leaf or chocolate cake encased in a chocolate sphere that's melted tableside.

Name: Bad Ass Lamb Hot Pot (Maizidian West Street)
Address: 39 Maizidian West Street, Chaoyang, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: The restaurant offers a smorgasbord of 15 cuts of lamb, and despite its name, dishes offered here are anything but "bad". While you may see hand-sliced lamb on almost every table, lamb shin tastes less greasy and more velvety after being swished for seconds in a broth of your choice. The blanched head is also a nice surprise with thin slices of juicy meat seasoned with cumin. Malabar spinach and kelp are delicious and provide a healthy dose of dietary fibre.

Name: Bad Idea
Description: Renovating a church sanctuary to house a wine bar and restaurant certainly doesn't sound like a Bad Idea to us. That is the premise behind this striking East Nashville spot, where Alex Burch leads a robust wine program with more than 100 selections housed in a custom wine cellar. Featuring a massive bar anchoring the center of the room and expansive seating all around, the restaurant is primed for groups out for a good time. The kitchen prepares a host of playful dishes like whipped pimento cheese or a riff on chicken nuggets, as well as hearty entrees like charcoal grilled steak and quail stuffed with spinach.

Name: Bad Schauenburg
Description: Whether you're seated in the Basler Stübli, the Gaststube or the Veranda, the fine dining restaurant of Hotel Bad Schauenburg serves classic French cuisine that takes its cue from the seasons in all its lovely rooms. Some of the produce comes from the hotel's own garden. The highlight in summer is of course the delightful terrace!

Name: Badageoni
Address: 26 E. Main St., Mount Kisco, NY, 10549, USA
Description: Mount Kisco locals pack this impossibly delicious Georgian "kitchen" as well as the new culinary dialect that accompanies it. This is a simple, welcoming dining room with a trestle-like ceiling, soft Edison light bulbs and dark wood bar. There are a few must-orders, including the khachapuri, a boat-shaped bread loaded with melted cheese and a raw egg yolk in the center that's mixed together for a sinfully good treat. Another go-to includes the ground lamb kebabs wrapped in lavash sided by house-made French fries.

Name: Badalamenti Cucina e Bottega
Description: A historic address, established in the 1950s as a delicatessen selling charcuterie, cheeses and wines, it is now in its third generation and has been given a contemporary makeover. It is still “the shop” where you can buy local delicacies, but it also offers a restaurant service: traditional dishes from land and sea, revisited with taste and personality. The inspector's favourite dish? Cuttlefish ink arancina with red prawn tartare, pea cream and cheese fondue.

Name: Badalucci
Description: A historic restaurant whose roots are firmly embedded in Italian tradition. Originally from the island of Procida in southern Italy, the chef focuses mainly on fish and seafood, although the lineup also features succulent meat dishes together with vegetarian options for each course. Whatever you order, seasonal ingredients take the limelight in this sleek eatery slightly out of the centre and just the ticket for anyone in search of authenticity off the beaten track. Some of the establishment’s signature dishes include an exquisitely balanced and refreshing tartare of seabass with cold spaghetti. The meticulously sourced olive oil is truly first class. The wine list reveals a passion for champagne and features vintages from prestigious wineries and characterful small-scale producers.

Name: Badessa
Description: This restaurant has a surprising location in a 19C cheese factory which once produced parmesan. Although the purpose of the building has changed, the love of the region remains the same – the chef goes out of his way to source local ingredients and search out old recipes, serving traditional Emilian dishes often with a modern twist. The fresh pasta and other ingredients are produced by the restaurant, while the carefully chosen wine list focuses on natural labels in particular.

Name: Badi
Description: Midway between Umag and Novigrad, in the fishing village of Lovrečica, stands Badi, a restaurant opened in 1986 and managed ever since by the Badurina-Badi family. Its reputation rests above all on fish: the protagonist of classic, simple dishes that celebrate the quality of the catch. Among the specialities, the langoustines, brodetto Badi, sea bass in a bread crust and preparations “alla busara” are the highlights. The wine list offers Istrian labels alongside a selection of Italian wines.

Name: Baduzzi
Address: 10/26 Jellicoe Street, North Wharf, Auckland Central, Auckland, 1010, New Zealand
Description: There’s nothing more reassuring than walking into a restaurant and being instantly hit with the sound of contented customers. But however busy this North Wharf spot gets, there’s a well-oiled service team on hand and they cope effortlessly well. The owner pays homage to his Italian-American roots, so start with some meatballs – the crayfish versions are very good. Pasta is homemade and there’s plenty of wood-fired bistecca. Add in an almost exclusively Italian wine list and you have all the ingredients for a fun time.

Name: Baffo
Description: Originally from southern Tuscany, Fabien Zannier pays tribute to the flavours of his childhood in this small, colourful trattoria that packs a tasty punch. Fresh organic ingredients, often sourced directly from the producer: arborio rice, Colonnata bacon, artisanal pasta from Pitigliano and Italian wines.

Name: Bagatto
Description: Hidden down an alleyway in the town centre, this friendly trattoria boasts an attractive ceiling with exposed brickwork. An excellent address for fans of Ligurian cuisine, fish and seafood. House desserts include sour orange semifreddo.

Name: Bahia
Address: De Paule Avenue, San Anton, Balzan, BZN 9023, Malta
Description: Set within an intimate dining room on the first floor of the elegant Corinthia Palace Hotel, this restaurant – named after a local variety of orange – offers two tasting menus, “The Villages Journey” and “Plant-Based”, alongside an à la carte selection. There is also the “Inħalli f’idejk” (“I leave it in your hands”) menu, designed for guests who wish to be surprised and fully trust the chef's creativity. The culinary concept draws inspiration from Maltese culture, taking guests on a sensory journey through the island’s different villages, with each dish accompanied by a note indicating its specific origin. Rooted in tradition yet forward-looking in spirit, the cuisine stands out for its precision and complexity, appealing to diners who appreciate thoughtfully composed dishes and creative flavor combinations.

Name: Bahnhöfle
Description: Run by Thierry and Elisabeth Falconnier, this charming restaurant is a real institution in the Freiburg area. Set in a little house by Gundelfingen's railway station, the place has a cheerful, easygoing feel. Inside, watercolours by the owners' daughter adorn the walls; outside, the cosy terrace is lovely in summer. True to his roots, the chef-patron serves up French cuisine – pleasingly pared down, brimming with flavour and made from excellent ingredients. Fish is the speciality here: think salmon carpaccio, monkfish with porcini or grilled sea bass. Meat lovers are also well catered for, with highlights such as Ibérico pork chop or braised beef cheeks.

Name: Baho (Da'an)
Address: 4, Lane 102, Section 1, Anhe Road, Da'an District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: This barbecue restaurant buys whole Omi Sawai hime cows to offer over 30 Shimofuri and Akami Wagyu cuts that are aged separately and prepared in a variety of ways, including tartare, sushi, soup and seared steak. In addition to typical steaks for two to four people to share, thickly sliced pieces in smaller portions are also available for smaller parties. Rare cuts such as top round and inside skirt tend to run out but can be pre-ordered.

Name: Bai Rong
Address: 1F, N2 Building, The Bund Finance Centre, 558 Zhongshan Dong Er Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: Bai Rong – peony – is the floral emblem of Shandong Province. Naturally, this modern restaurant generously adorned with lush greenery focuses on Shandong cuisine, especially live seafood shipped from Jiaodong Peninsula. Order the Jiaodong cold seafood platter to sample sea cucumber, jellyfish, abalone and octopus all at once. Rustic recipes from rural Shandong, such as sautéed Linyi chicken with fish maw, are hard to find elsewhere.

Name: Baia del Silenzio
Description: In a beautiful position inside the bay, the restaurant serves dishes with a contemporary twist that enhance the local products and the good ingredients. The offer is divided between the bistrot for lunch, the gourmet dinner and the wine bar. In summer you can dine alfresco on the outdoor terrace or directly on the beach.

Name: Bailara
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Bailara’s contemporary ambience in a rural hotel in the heart of nature definitely strikes a chord! The modern-inspired cuisine on offer here is centred around a single surprise tasting menu that showcases seasonal dishes and is based around ingredients sourced from local producers (asparagus, teardrop peas, artichokes, cep mushrooms etc) and meat from local breeders. We particularly enjoyed the charcoal-grilled beef tacos!

Name: Baillotte
Description: Perhaps chef Satoshi Amitsu (ex Georges Blanc) is just being modest when he uses the term "semi-gourmet" cuisine on his website, because this bistro with an alluring red frontage more than holds its own on the restaurant scene. Deploying the precision for which the Japanese are renowned, the chef delights diners with pedigree Gallic cuisine replete with colours and contrasts, backed up by meticulous jus and sauces: smoked seabream, kohlrabi, fresh goat’s cheese, trout roe, fermented apricot dressing; caramelised upside-down apple pie, cinnamon-laced shortbread, cream cheese and rum-raisin ice cream. Insightful selection of wines by the glass that outstrips your average offer, with expert advice from the waiting staff.

Name: Bairoz
Description: Just a stone's throw from the River Loire, this charming, modern restaurant sports a striking decor with pendant lights, wood panelling and exposed stonework. At the helm are chef Estelle Méheust and pastry chef Jérôme Berdelou, both of whom are active in the kitchen as well as the dining room: one starts the service while the starters and main courses are being made, the other taking over when it comes to the desserts. This charming, discreet couple won us over with their market-fresh fare at lunchtime, and their more high-level cuisine at dinner: scallops, onion cream, marjoram fumet; pigeon fillet, squash and granola.

Name: Baita Fraina
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Warm little bar rooms, reminiscent of the German wine bars or "Stube", a summer terrace and well - prepared regional dishes: for those who want to escape the mundane life of Cortina for the silence of an isolated "baita" [mountain hut]. Delightful rooms, colourfully furnished in warm tones so you can better enjoy the silence and scents of the mountains.

Name: Baiweiyuan Dumpling (Tuanjiehu Road)
Address: 52 Tuanjiehu Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
Description: For over a decade, this shop has been serving dumpling soup, steamed dumplings and potstickers that are stuffed and cooked à la minute – so expect slower service than at your average dumpling joint. Signature Baiwei dumplings come with meat, shrimp and veggie fillings; ovo-vegetarians may opt for the egg-and-tomato variety. Try the cold appetisers such as thinly sliced soy-braised pork trotter with the perfect ratio of skin, fat and lean meat.

Name: Bajel
Address: Sofitel Mexico City Reforma, Av. Paseo De La Reforma, 297, Cuauhtémoc, 06500, Mexico
Description: Nestled inside the Sofitel, Bajel boasts a prime location with stunning views. It's a French brand so they may whisper bonsoir, but one look at the menu and it's clear they're firmly planted here. Inside this sophisticated setting, the fully open kitchen demands your attention. There are two tasting menus on offer; the "clarity and depth menu," with meat and fish, and a vegetarian-minded "purity and refinement" menu. Those who choose the former may experience the likes of a deconstructed Caesar salad, trout in a leek sauce and their signature white mole with 25 ingredients (they even present a card detailing all 25).

Name: Bak Kut Pan
Address: 22 Bao'an Street, Xindian District, New Taipei, Taiwan
Description: This cheerful joint near an MRT station specialises in bak kut teh. On top of the typical braised pork in Chinese herbal soup, the menu also rolls out a ‘dry’ version – fall-off-the-bone pork is sautéed with aromatic herbs and seasoning in a claypot. The broth here boasts mellow herbal instead of peppery aromas. You can specify the cut you prefer, such as spareribs, leg or trotter; optional add-ons include tripe, intestines, tofu puffs and mushrooms.

Name: Bala Baya
Address: Arch 25, Old Union Yard Arches, 229 Union Street, Southwark, London, SE1 0LR, United Kingdom
Description: The atmosphere is loud and lively at this infectiously fun restaurant that celebrates the Tunisian and Syrian heritage of its passionate chef-owner, as well as his global travels. The bright, modern interior is inspired by Bauhaus architecture, with the counter being the best place to sit if you want to feel the buzz and watch the chefs as they cook. Dishes are fresh, vibrant and designed for sharing, with the signatures including prawn baklava and 'aubergine mess'.

Name: Balafenn
Description: In a small village, this discreet old house that has been turned into a cosy restaurant also has a terrace giving onto a bucolic garden. The butterfly (balafenn in Breton) – the emblem of this restaurant and its cuisine – appears everywhere, from the decor to the flower beds. The chef's culinary signature is carefully crafted modern cuisine that showcases seasonal Breton produce. The monkfish with peas, carrots and cherry pickles is a perfect example: precisely cooked, well-balanced flavours and beautifully presented. The chef's wife extends a warm welcome.

Name: Balarés
Description: Found inside the boutique hotel of the same name, which in turn takes its name from the nearby Balarés beach, one of the most beautiful and unspoilt beaches on the Costa da Morte. In the restaurant, with its elegant rustic atmosphere, you will find traditional cuisine based on a fixed-price menu and another tasting menu, always using local seasonal produce and modern techniques. Interesting facts: The menu often mentions some of their suppliers, as their motto is ‘Territory & Proximity & Commitment’.

Name: Baldio
Address: Antonio Solá 26, Colonia Condesa, Cuauhtémoc, 06140, Mexico
Description: Taking inspiration from London's Silo, where Chef Max MacLean previously worked, Baldio is zeroing in on zero waste. It's all about a holistic approach to sustainability, going beyond the locally caught freshwater fish and vegetables from chinampas farms to include in-house water purification and recycled corn husk paper for printing. Green practices aside, this restaurant doesn't pull any punches when it comes to cooking, available à la carte or as a tasting menu. Dishes like fluke crudo, shingled with slices of jicama, star fruit and avocado in a leche de tigre, or the heirloom tomato medley with ginger-pickled chayote over sikil pak (a Yucatán dip made from toasted pepitas, charred tomatoes, habanero, cilantro and onion) display this kitchen's skill.

Name: Balera
Description: Thin and crispy pizzas packed with flavor rarely disappoint at Balera, where vinyl records, retro accents and a shimmering disco ball set a playful tone. Not sure which one to pick? The Diavola is spot-on, arriving with an impressive aroma of Pecorino cheese, golden slices of Calabrian soppressata and Italian basil with hot honey, but this restaurant delivers more than just (really good) pizza. Watch the team at work making pasta and focaccia in the open kitchen while snacking on fritto misto with shrimp, calamari, red onion and pineapple with sumac mayonnaise. The Italian-focused wine list runs deep, with two pages dedicated to sparkling wines alone.

Name: Bali Hai Seafood Market
Description: Bali Hai has been feeding seafood lovers with the freshest critters and best quality fish for over ten years. Pick your own catch at the live fish tank by the entrance. Specify the way you want them cooked – in Teochew, Nyonya or even Thai style. The must-try “cereal prawns” are tossed in butter and milky oat powder that forms a crispy crust. Stir-fried crab with salted egg yolks that strikes a balance between umami and saltiness is not to be missed.

Name: Balin Sestri Levante
Description: An intimate restaurant on the seafront with a tiny dining room and small veranda, and a young, contemporary ambience. The Mediterranean-style cuisine is modern and creative with a focus on Ligurian ingredients to which the chef adds the occasional Asian twist, often in the sauces. Booking ahead is recommended given the limited number of tables here!

Name: Ballato
Address: 55 E. Houston St., New York, NY, 10012, USA
Description: This beloved Houston St. standard is an unsung hero, even if many walk past the gold- and red-etched window and write it off as some run-of-the-mill red-sauce joint. Step inside the narrow, weathered space where the team of this family-run operation offers guests a gracious and genuine Italian-American experience. The menu is filled with pasta classics like Roman cacio e pepe, tossed with sharp pecorino and freshly ground black pepper. Signature specialties include pollo Emilio, a delicately breaded chicken cutlet draped in lemon-caper sauce; and clams oreganata speckled with garlicky breadcrumbs. Crisp cannoli shells filled with vanilla- and cinnamon-tinged ricotta cream rival any other version found from Palermo to Siracusa.

Name: Balm - La Pistache
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At the elegant restaurant of Hotel Balm both the service and Beat Stofer's cuisine have a classical feel. He cooks unpretentious fare using excellent ingredients. Choose between the three- to five-course "Amuse Bouche Menu" or order from the à la carte selection. Highlights include classics such as "Chateaubriand in two courses" (served for two or more) or Swiss Black Angus simmered beef terrine with apple, mustard and horseradish. There is also a well-curated wine list. In good weather, the terrace is a fabulous spot from which to enjoy the mountain views. This place is always busy, so be sure to book well in advance! Inviting guestrooms.

Name: Balmumu Dükkan Lokanta
Address: Alsancak, Kültür Mah, 1388. Sokak No:5 D:C, Konak, Izmir, 35220, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Venture down this side street on the edge of the Konak district to savour traditional Aegean cuisine as the locals do. The chefs work with fresh ingredients purchased at the market that very morning and showcase their offerings in the display counter, from mezze to the side dishes you choose with your main course. Vine leaves are stuffed with boldly seasoned rice, lamb is slowly cooked to retain its succulence and accompanied by a buckwheat ragout; pumpkin is cooked with cinnamon, cardamom and bay leaf and finished with a sweet caramel sauce. These are dishes with soul, prepared with personality.

Name: Balon
Description: This contemporary bistro, recently renovated but with over twenty years of history, is located on the outskirts of the capital in a green and peaceful area, offering a spacious outdoor area perfect for the warmer months. The cuisine highlights the local territory with classic recipes reinterpreted in a modern style, enriched by a Mediterranean touch, especially in the seafood offerings. The inspectors’ favorite dish: Shredded lamb, artichoke cream, cinnamon demi-glace, and baked radicchio.

Name: Balos Estiatorio
Address: 1940 N St. NW, Washington, DC, 20036, USA
Description: With two large rooms dotted with olive trees and decorated with wall hangings and fine pottery, you might just convince yourself that you've left DC for this restaurant's namesake— an idyllic location on Crete. This impressive spot from three friends offers a roll call of Greek favorites (think spanakopita and citrus-toned avgolemono). Choose meats from the grill or regional fish grilled with ladolemono and capers flown in from Greece. There's always the classic chicken souvlaki with wonderful, salty pita bread and creamy tzatziki, but it's those Greek fries that win your heart every time. Of course, when dessert comes around, it's no question: baklava with iced Greek yogurt for the win. Greek wines round out the experience.

Name: Balıkçı Kahraman
Address: Rumeli Kavağı Mahallesi, İskele Caddesi No:15/1, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34450, Türkiye
Description: Be sure to try the fish kokoreç, a traditional dish made with grilled fish offal; the perfectly grilled turbot, which is the house speciality, is also a must; and let's not forget the dried mackerel, nor the buttery-soft tuna lakerda prepared with house-made olive oil. A word to the wise: The best way to experience Kahraman Altun's cosy fish restaurant is to bring friends and sample as many of his traditionally prepared delicacies as possible. Afterwards, you should definitely take the time to explore the surrounding fishing village of Rumeli Kavağı (also known for its figs). This peaceful corner of Istanbul is sure to enchant you.

Name: Ban Lan
Address: 3F, Podium, Building No.8, One Sino Finance Plaza, 6 Lingyan Road, Huqiu, Suzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: Here, traditional Fujian recipes get an update with an emphasis on lighter seasoning and natural flavours. Both the owner and the chef hail from Fujian, and only the best produce in season, mostly shipped straight from their home province, makes it onto the table. There are a number of set menus to choose from and they may feature signatures such as ginger duck stew, or peanut sweet soup with taro paste and bird's nest.

Name: Ban Ting Jia Yan (Suzhou Industrial Park)
Address: 1F, Tonino Lamborghini Hotel, 168 Xinggang Street, Suzhou Industrial Park, Suzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: This restaurant on the shore of Jinji Lake affords stunning views. Live Pingtan and Kunqu performances are a nod to Suzhou culture, but the theatrics continue offstage: The fried sheefish with shrimp roe served in a metre-long plate is quite a spectacle. The flesh is tender and finely textured, in stark contrast with the thin, crispy scales. Fox nut sweet porridge or square cakes with red date filling make for a perfect sweet finale.

Name: Bandiat
Description: The story begins as you enter this vast estate on the edge of the Périgord-Limousin Regional Nature Park, here in the heart of Périgord Vert. Winding its way through the grounds is the Bandiat, the small river after which this restaurant is named. Housed in a large building featuring a brand new timber roof, it is bathed in soft light and imbued with a country house atmosphere. The chef concocts a surprise menu using seasonal ingredients supplied by small-scale local producers – as well as mushrooms and herbs picked on site (sometimes by the chef himself).

Name: Bang Dean
Address: 16/10 Mu 1, Phet Kasem Road, Bang Nai Si, Takua Pa, Phang-Nga, 82110, Thailand
Description: A local favourite in Takua Pa, popular for its flavoursome halal breakfast and beautifully aromatic and rich slow-cooked beef and goat curries. The clear beef soup made to order arrives piping hot. Dishes also come in smaller portions – perfect for sampling a variety of options.

Name: Bang Por Seafood Takho
Description: Bang Por boasts an experienced kitchen team composed of local chefs who have worked here for many years. This simple beach-front restaurant is depicted by holiday vibes and Southern Thai seafood fare. The spicy stir-fried squid with herbs is cooked in a spicy curry paste and the grilled fish is sprinkled with mixed Thai herbs. The house shrimp paste is packed with aromatic plants and coconut chili and grilled before serving, hence the pungent aroma.

Name: Bangkok Bold (Pathum Wan)
Address: LGF, Central Embassy, 1031 Phloen Chit Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Word-of-mouth inspired Chef Nhoi to take the leap from cooking studio in the old town to opening a restaurant in the city centre. Her aim is to preserve the heritage of Thai taste that’s ‘basic and bold’ with creative twists. Check out the unique stir-fried pork and shrimp, hummingbird flowers, fish sauce and scrambled eggs. And the spicy salted beef in coconut cream is tender with balanced flavours, enlivened by fresh shallots and bird's eye chillies.

Name: Bangkok Supper Club
Address: 641 Hudson St., New York, NY, 10014, USA
Description: This spot with Chef Max Wittawat at the helm is very chic and on trend with a contemporary Thai menu pulling from family recipes while adding a touch of refinement. The product quality and execution are exacting, and even dishes that seem simple, as in the fiery scallop ceviche with watermelon chili granita, are impactful and play on dramatic contrasts. The deep-fried pork cheeks served sliced over savory garlic-baked rice are highly recommended. Loaded with flavor, each bite alternates between the sweet-tender pork and the savory-delicious rice. For dessert, cubes of a coconut chiffon cake topped with a pandan custard are nestled inside a young coconut. A creative cocktail menu showcases as much care as the food.

Name: Banrimbung
Address: 372/21 Mu 2, Nong Din Daeng, Mueang Nakhon Pathom, Nakhon Pathom, 73000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted
