Description: The national historical site in the heart of the city faithfully replicates details of a Lingnan-style Chinese garden. Inside, diners are wowed by 14 gilded redwood vases with elaborate carvings on all sides. Opened in 1928, it is famed not only for its palatial decor but also for such Cantonese home-style dishes as Huadiao drunken chicken and its exquisitely made dim sum – try char siu puff pastry, and steamed chicken with fish maw.

Name: Bel Ami
Description: This 19C palazzo renovated in modern style serves fish and seafood, including raw dishes, with fish displayed in a cabinet in the dining room. Among the desserts, the vanilla ice-cream is a classic favourite!

Name: Beletage Zum Schwarzen Kameel
Description: Just what is it that makes this place so appealing? For one thing, there's the central location; for another, the extremely inviting Jugendstil building, which dates back to 1901 and contributes to a very particular atmosphere here on the first floor. The decor is elegant yet cosy, and the professional, pleasingly laid-back team provides seamless classical service. Then, of course, there's the fantastic food: a celebration of Viennese classics, complemented by seasonal creations. There is a well-curated à la carte menu with a set menu option – dishes such as "'Radlberg' char, cucumber, rhubarb & elderflower" and "lamb loin, harissa, preserved lemon & polenta" are sure to whet your appetite.

Name: Belga Queen
Address: Rue du Fossé aux Loups 32, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
Description: Following a superlative makeover, the Belga Queen, an iconic culinary landmark of Brussels, is ready to write a new chapter of its story. This majestic edifice, which started out as a bank in the 18C, is famous for its remarkable architecture, boasting dome-shaped windows and imposing columns. Brasserie classics rub shoulders with more up-to-the-minute dishes on the menu, while the seafood bar reflects the chef’s passion. His North Sea waterzooi is made with seabass and plaice, together with crunchy veggies, a subtle velvety fish soup and briny touches of mussels and shrimp. Finish your meal in style with a Brussels waffle, made from scratch on demand. The Belga Queen is back!

Name: Belimbing
Description: Belimbing refers to "starfruit", a versatile ingredient in Asian cooking. The bustling open kitchen is set against sage green walls and wood trims that impart serenity. The menu features traditional Singaporean fare with creative twists. Corn salat is a nod to kueh salat, reimagined with sweet corn and brown butter for nutty, toasty sweetness. Paired with assam pedas and white pepper sauce, the silky clam custard boasts layers of flavour.

Name: Bell
Address: The Square, Ramsbury, SN8 2PE, United Kingdom
Description: The Bell is not just a pub but a true village hub. A charming 300-year-old building, it comprises a bar, a restaurant, bedrooms and even a café to make itself useful no matter when you're visiting. The carefully executed cooking ensures the flavours of the high-quality ingredients shine through, be that in lighter dishes such as scallop ceviche with fennel or pub classics like beer-battered haddock and chips. The surrounding 19,000-acre Ramsbury Estate provides not just a picturesque setting but also much of the seasonal produce that powers the menu.

Name: Bell-Lloc
Address: Carretera Sant Feliu a Girona, Santa Cristina d'Aro, 17246, Spain
Description: Bell-Lloc occupies an old farmhouse with a marked rustic ambience, the origins of which date back to the 17C. Traditional Catalan cooking that is simple yet delicious, including dishes cooked on the grill.

Name: Bella Aurora
Description: This sister concept from the same people behind Rosetta and Lardo is a comforting spot for all-day dining in Roma Norte. From its pink exterior to its greenery-filled interior, Bella Aurora is cute and chic without a whisper of pretension. Come for breakfast, where the bakery items are the ones to beat, while at lunch and dinner the focus is on contemporary Italian fare. It's all good, executed with an attention to detail and great care. Begin with their pulpo, lightly pickled and tossed with potato for an enjoyable first course. Pasta is always a winner, especially the conchiglie tossed with tuna ragout with chili and Kalamata olives. Main dishes and pizza are also on offer, but with tiramisu to a cheese course with herb and blueberry focaccia, do save room for dessert.

Name: Bellanger
Address: 9 Islington Green, Islington, London, N1 2XH, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: With awnings stretching over the pavement and walls festooned with classic posters, Bellanger has the feel of a Parisian grand café. The cooking, however, speaks with more of a southern French accent, its Mediterranean inspirations sitting alongside the ubiquitous French classics like coq au vin or beef Bourguignon. Open from day to night, it's the kind of neighbourhood spot where you could drop in for anything from brunch to an aperitif at the large cocktail bar. Structured, well-drilled service enhances the experience.

Name: Belle Parti
Description: In a charming arcaded alley in the pedestrian centre, on the first floor of the historic Palazzo Prosdocimi, the warm and welcoming romance of the room will convince you that you are in the right place. Paintings, mirrors, and woodwork rival the beautiful ceiling of exposed beams, while the à la carte proposal is in tune with the seasons, offering a review of tasty and classic mostly seafood dishes (but some customisation is there, as in the case of Belle Parti's spaghetti alla chitarra, a cacio e pepe embellished with scampi), mostly regionally sourced, with good meat alternatives. Reception and service genteelly tuned to the feminine.

Name: Belle Vue
Description: To make the most of the simply stunning mountain views, opt for a table near the large glass-planed front – or on the delightful terrace! Complementing the wonderful scenery, the interior of the Bellevue Parkhotel & Spa restaurant boasts a sleek design that provides the backdrop for the fine dining menu: classic dishes such as roast duck breast with potato galettes are served in the evening, and a simpler à la carte selection is available at lunchtime. Choose an accompaniment from the exquisite wine list.

Name: Bellini
Description: The Parkhotel in Gütersloh not only has attractive, individually designed guestrooms and suites and its own private garden, but also boasts an impressive range of dining options. Among its various restaurants, Bellini deserves special mention. Here, in truly refined surroundings, attentive and accomplished service complements cuisine that is firmly rooted in classical technique yet interpreted with a modern sensibility and subtle Japanese accents. A four-, six- or seven-course set menu is to be had – notable highlights include "Turbot, teardrop peas, romaine lettuce, brown shrimp koji beurre blanc" and "Wagyu beef, potato, morel, caper leaf". A vegetarian alternative is also available on request at the time of booking.

Name: Bello Visto
Description: Gassin, which comes from the expression Guardia Sinus, meaning guardian of the gulf, is a former Sarrazin village occupied by the Moors until the 10C. After finding the house on Place des Barri, take a seat on the superb terrace and gape at the view over the Gulf of Saint-Tropez and the Maures mountains. Among the house specialities are rock octopus casserole; tartlet of red mullet; roast seabass with Sicilian-style fennel. This Mediterranean score is crafted by an enthusiastic veteran chef and local lad, whose grandmother used to live in the village! Food that throbs with flavour and a few rooms for overnight stays.

Name: Bello by Sandro Nardone
Address: 1200 Bison Ave., Ste. C2, Newport Beach, CA, 92660, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Originally from Atina and boasting a lineage of chefs and farmers, Chef/co-owner Sandro Nardone brings his experience with Italian cuisine and wood-fire cooking to Newport Beach. Low lighting and large paintings set a chic tone in the dining room, while the open kitchen keeps all eyes focused on the food. It is an idyllic setting for a gastronomic retreat; and the contemporary cooking never disappoints. Get one of their skillfully made pizzas, perhaps one topped with mushrooms and green onions or tuck into a plate of pasta amatriciana, a house-made rigatoni in a guanciale and pomodoro sauce with some pepperoncino for a touch of heat. To finish, an affogato or tiramisu seal the deal.

Name: Bellota
Address: 43 Churchgate Street, Bury St Edmunds, IP33 1RG, United Kingdom
Description: Those who like to see chefs at work will find their paradise at this 20-seater counter in the heart of Bury St Edmunds. A chef-led operation, where the kitchen team both cook and serve their dishes, it’s the brainchild of Spanish chef Ruben Aquilar Bel and his Hungarian-born wife Gabi, who makes the desserts and the excellent bread. Sharing plates are an option at lunch, while only a tasting menu is served for dinner, showcasing Spanish flavours with a degree of restrained creativity. "Yaya Bel’s Iberian Ham Croqueta" is a lovely snack to start, paying homage to Ruben’s grandmother.

Name: Belotti Ristorante e Bottega
Description: This petite, casual restaurant-turned-enoteca is set on a busy but bucolic stretch of Rockridge’s main artery. Boasting an impressive round of regulars who frequently park at the bar to chat with the owner in Italian between bites, Belotti dabbles in the traditional cuisine of Piemonte. Envision such hearty dishes as brasato, or braised beef with mushrooms served over polenta and finished with a nebbiolo reduction. House-made pastas are also a major attraction here, including the heirloom grain spaghettini in a tomato sauce with creamy burrata. More unexpected dishes excel as well: try the delicious butter lettuce salad with lemon and pine nuts, or the decadent tortino, a spinach flan with egg yolk and truffle. Silky panna cotta with raspberry coulis is the perfect finish.

Name: Beloved BBQ at Love, Makoto
Address: 200 Massachusetts Ave. NW, Ste.150, Washington, DC, 20001, USA
Description: Located in the Capitol Crossing, this steakhouse is undeniably striking with dark walls, a neon hallway and large tables with central circular grills. The style here is distinctly Japanese. Icy cold oysters with chili koji are an ideal opener before tucking in to dishes like A5 Wagyu fried rice with soft egg, served in a steaming hot pot and folded together by the server to ensure each kernel is coated in the lush ingredients. Naturally, meat plays the starring role here. Some of the flavorful selections include prime short rib with sudachi, sea salt and black pepper; Wagyu New York strip with lime and wasabi; and aged beef tongue with excellent gamey notes.

Name: Beluga
Address: Plaza de las Flores 3, Malaga, 29005, Spain
Description: Nestled in a central square, run by a couple who are committed to what they call 'meridian cuisine', representing the southern Mediterranean culture, with dishes of great delicacy and flavour with no shortage of technical details. The menu, with a tasty and comprehensive selection of rice dishes (Shell-free rice with monkfish and white prawns, Alicante-style rice cooked in fish stock, served with wild-caught fish, Rice with Angus beef cheek and chickpeas...) which can be enjoyed individually, is rounded out with two tasting menus (Meridiano Cero and Virazón). We recommend booking, especially if you want to eat on their pleasant terrace!

Name: Belvedere
Address: Via Monti di Mola 39, Porto Cervo, 07021, Italy
Description: Over the years, this family restaurant has become one of the most popular along this coastline. An informal dining room provides the backdrop for the decidedly Mediterranean cuisine served here, where the focus is the fish display cabinet that changes daily and from which guests can make their choice. The friendly and professional approach of the two brothers that run the restaurant has contributed to its success, while the brand-new terrace-lounge, with its stunning view, is the perfect spot for an aperitif or after-dinner drink.

Name: Belvedere
Description: The culinary flagship of the A-ROSA Strandidyll Heringsdorf hotel. From your table in the fourth-floor dining area, which with its glass dome has an elegant modern feel , you can take in the wonderful view over the hotel grounds all the way to the Baltic Sea. The cuisine is classic in its foundations and partly based on regional produce. You are free to put together your own set menu. Friendly and well-drilled waitstaff. Tip: Your aperitif is best enjoyed on the gorgeous terrace.

Name: Belvédère
Address: Hôtel Belesso, 34 avenue des Baux, Fontvieille, 13990, France
Description: Japanese chef Kohei Ohata skilfully harnesses the flavours of the Mediterranean fare that abounds in the surrounding markets to produce really appealing dishes. His talented wife brings her skills to bear on the pastry section. It is all fresh, fragrant and charged at a fair price. This excellent establishment is a little hidden away in the Hotel Belesso – reserved for those in the know, and all the better for it.

Name: Belzan
Address: 371 Smithdown Road, Liverpool, L15 3JJ, United Kingdom
Description: Situated in a buzzing suburb that's popular with students, there's a relaxed, unpretentious appeal to this cosy modern bistro. The chatty, attentive service puts all guests at ease, before the generous, flavoursome cooking arrives and puts smiles on faces. To start, it's hard to resist the signature Guinness rarebit potato, followed by carefully executed larger dishes such as steamed salmon with wild garlic vichyssoise and shrimp sauce vierge. On Sundays, the chefs turn their attention to a classic roast lunch.

Name: Belé
Description: The name says it all – in Milanese dialect, “belé” means beautiful and the word is an apt description of this restaurant. Belé is charmingly lit by an old-fashioned chandelier on which the pieces of crystal create a play of light resembling an intricate and shifting lace-like pattern. The dining rooms are decorated in attractive contemporary colours, with comfortable armchairs and acoustics perfect for conversation, while the cuisine is Italian with a modern twist.

Name: Belén by Paulo Airaudo
Address: 2F, Intercontinental Chiang Mai The Mae Ping, 153 Room 2A, Sridonchai Road, Chang Khlan, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50100, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: This confident new face on Chiang Mai's dining scene brings a refined energy to the table. Local ingredients play a central role – fruit, vegetables, tea, even cheese – and are elevated by sharp European cuisine technique. The experience begins with an aperitif in a playful, book-lined lounge, then you move into the intimate 18-seat dining room anchored by a chamchuri wood counter. Don't miss the goat's cheese flan paired with seasonal fruits: it's smooth and effortlessly moreish.

Name: Benares
Description: Following in the footsteps of its London namesake, Benares’ major selling points are its modern take on classic Indian cuisine and its pleasant terrace-garden with a soothing patio pool.

Name: Bencotto
Address: 6F, Mandarin Oriental Hotel, 158 Dunhua North Road, Songshan District, Taipei, 105, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: With its lofty, airy room, this long-standing hotel restaurant is a favourite among locals craving traditional Italian fare. The Italian head chef, who honed his skills in various countries, adapts his menu as the seasons change. Ask the servers about specials not on the menu, such as handmade tagliatelle alfredo with winter truffles and parmesan aged for six months – the bouncy noodles go down a treat with the rich, hearty sauce.

Name: Benders
Description: This chic and modern restaurant has found the perfect home within the pretty half-timbered building of the long-established Birkenfelder Hof. It is an ideal setting for "casual dining". The atmosphere is also suitably relaxed, the waitstaff are experienced and friendly, and the delicious seasonal modern cuisine, which draws on French, Mediterranean and regional influences, incorporates the occasional Asian touch. The successful synthesis of different culinary styles is evident in dishes such as "Breton monkfish, dashi beurre blanc, pak choi, Sardinian pasta, tomato and pine nut vinaigrette". Classics such as roast beef, burgers (Tue-Wed only) and Wiener schnitzel (Thu only) are also tempting. It is pleasant to dine al fresco on the beautifully landscaped terrace. Well-maintained guestrooms available for overnight stays.

Name: Benedicts
Address: 9 St Benedicts Street, Norwich, NR2 4PE, United Kingdom
Description: Situated in a bohemian part of the city, the modern bistro vibe perfectly suits this simply decorated restaurant that carries its unfussy ethos through into the cooking. Chef-Owner Richard Bainbridge is proud of his Norfolk roots and an ambassador for the region’s larder, and his understated dishes rely on top quality ingredients to lead the way. They serve a range of menus, varying in length and with vegetarian and, on request, vegan options available. For those looking for a lighter bite, sit outside and order small plates from the Alfresco menu.

Name: Benedikto
Address: Via Eremo delle Carceri 1/a, Assisi, 06081, Italy
Description: On the edge of Assisi’s historic centre, within the refined setting of the Nun hotel, Benedikto offers a selection of classic Umbrian products, but the gastronomic proposal is principally creative and of a high order. In fine weather, dining on the terrace with its view over the Rocca di Assisi takes on a particularly romantic quality.

Name: Benet
Address: Plaza del 1 de Octubre 21-23, Les Borges Blanques, 25400, Spain
Description: This family-run restaurant occupies a building with plenty of history behind it as it once served as a mill and the town hall. Here, you’ll find an updated take on Catalan cuisine, with the date on which each dish was created listed alongside the name. Examples includes the carpaccio of marinated tomatoes and wild mushrooms (2021) and the cod confit with “samfaina” (2025). The paired “Maridaje+Art” menu includes a tasting of different olive oils.

Name: Benjamin
Description: Ten seats are set around a horseshoe counter, chefs interact with guests, presenting carefully executed, boldly flavoured dishes, which are inspired by the Czech cuisine using only local products. The tasting experience starts at a fixed time in the evening, beginning with an introduction to the region's seasonal products staged in eight courses. Wine pairings are offered to match. It is also worth mentioning the great decorative touches, which contribute to the welcoming atmosphere. Please note: Booking is essential.

Name: Benjamin Schmitt Restaurant
Description: This restaurant in Pigalle pays tribute to the land and those who work it. The youthful chef cultivates culinary eclecticism, seamlessly segueing from one style of cuisine to another and from traditional to modern fare. The enticing names of the dishes live up to their promise: duck, foie gras and pork pâté en croûte; farm-raised guinea fowl cooked two ways with herby aubergine and cherries in red wine vinegar; Tanzanian dark chocolate mousse with coffee-hazelnut praline and coffee ice cream. Wallet-friendly lunch set menu; tasting menu and à la carte in the evening.

Name: Benjarong
Address: GF, Dusit Thani Makati, Ayala Centre, Makati - Metro Manila, 1223, The Philippines
Description: The Dusit Thani Hotel's signature Thai restaurant is true to its name – a "benjarong" is a vessel for serving treasured dishes... and here those are inspired by Royal Thai cuisine. Highlights include yam woon sen – glass noodle salad with fresh seafood – as well as whole fried sea bass and velvety green curry. A contemporary tasting course puts a modern spin on classic flavours, for a balanced introduction to this elevated culinary approach.

Name: Benno
Address: Hotel San Cristóbal, Carr. Federal No. 19KM 54+800, Playa Punta Lobos, Todos Santos, 23300, Mexico
Description: This dining room of the Hotel San Cristóbal in Todos Santos feels a bit in the middle of nowhere but commands a prized perch along the Baja coast. Benno embraces an easy-breezy indoor/outdoor vibe. The patio area faces the pool and the beach; time it right and you get a stunning view of the sunset.Breakfast is offered, and evening fare incudes simple, straightforward cooking in preparations like ceviche, grilled local cheese, roasted chicken and house-made pasta. The pesca en mole verde, or catch of the day, may be yellowtail; it is served with a smooth textured, mild, herb and pumpkin seed sauce and very fresh vegetables. The churros are cleverly done as bite-sized pieces, accompanied by house-made dulce de leche and warm chocolate sauce for dipping.

Name: Benoit
Address: 10F, La Porte Aoyama, 5-51-8 Jingumae, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo, 150-0001, Japan
Description: The Tokyo outpost of Benoit, which was founded in Paris in 1912. The cuisine of this bistro that co-stars French and Japanese influences is overseen by Alain Ducasse. The menu is prix fixe, but diners can choose items to their liking. Dishes bequeathed by the Paris flagship, such as oven-baked escargot and terrine, stand alongside regional fare made with ingredients from across Japan. Antique-accented décor and attentive service convey an unmistakeably French esprit.

Name: Benoit
Address: 60 W. 55th St., New York, NY, 10019, USA
Description: This Alain Ducasse bistro, housed in the venerable La Côte Basque space, may have been renovated in recent years, but it remains decidedly Old World in look, feel and taste. The setting remains a sight to behold, with its abundant framed mirrors, red velvet banquettes and oak paneled walls. In the front salon, two red wingback chairs are tilted in to face a working fireplace and make an idyllic spot for nibbling madeleines at the end of your meal.The unabashedly French menu is stacked with comfortable, familiar bistro dishes that feature the likes of cassoulet, pâté en croûte and foie de veau. Traditional desserts are a highlight, especially the rum baba with its fluffy brioche served with lightly sweetened whipped cream and a generous pour of rum.

Name: Benoit
Address: Area 1, King Abdullah Financial District, Al Aquiq, Riyadh, 13519, Saudi Arabia
Description: Overlooking the Financial Plaza in KAFD is this branch of Alain Ducasse’s Benoit. This classic French bistro de luxe is a restaurant on the ground level and a café on the first floor. Bright red banquettes and vintage chandeliers hanging from the ceiling add a classic touch to the otherwise modern and futuristic architecture of the district. It’s like being in a tiny corner of France as the vocals Édith Piaff and Charles Aznavour play in the background, while the menu offers escargot, pâté en croûte and soufflé au chocolat. Some subtle Middle Eastern influences are evident too, like the Camel Rossini and lamb kafta.

Name: Benoit
Description: This genuine Parisian bistro still boasts its period Belle Époque interior (woodwork, copper pots, mirrors, velvet banquettes) and everything down to the plates bears the B monogram, further adding to the authentic vibe. Proudly and heartily traditional, the recipes star country produce: pâté en croûte, calf’s head with ravigote sauce, cassoulet, millefeuille pastry!

Name: Benoit
Address: The Hotel Seiryu Kyoto Kiyomizu, 2-204-2 Kiyomizu, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, 605-0862, Japan
Description: Curated by Alain Ducasse, the Benoit chain spreads the bistro charm beloved of Parisians to locations that span the globe, anchored by its flagship in Paris. A soaring glass wall commands views of Yasaka Pagoda. The modern interior, appointed with antique silverware and furniture, is a harmonious fusion of old and new. Prix fixe is the rule here; classic French cuisine prepared with a modern sensibility from appetiser to dessert.

Name: Benoli
Address: 5 Orford Street, Norwich, NR1 3LE, United Kingdom
Description: ‘Benoli’ might have an Italian ring to it but this three-floored restaurant near Norwich Castle is actually named after the chef-owner's brother, Ben, and himself, Oliver – although Italy is still very much their inspiration. Start with a drink at the marble-topped cocktail bar – a negroni or an Aperol Spritz, perhaps – before enjoying highlights including homemade pasta and deliciously indulgent desserts, such as tiramisu with hot chocolate mousse and mascarpone gelato. The atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming, enhanced by a confident and personable team.

Name: Benso
Description: Situated in a small garden in the historic centre, this modern bistro has a light, airy feel thanks to its large windows and its outdoor tables perfect for alfresco dining in summer. The menu features contemporary-style, personalised meat and fish dishes which are full of flavour, while at lunchtime, the lighter “Pranzetto” menu is a good option. The restaurant also offers an excellent selection of cocktails for an evening aperitif, plus an impressive choice of digestifs to enjoy after your dinner.

Name: Bentōteca
Description: Top-quality Japanese cuisine with heavy Mediterranean influences takes pride of place at this restaurant, where talented chef Toku Yoji Tokuyoshi creates dishes such as horsemeat tataki with a pizzaiola sauce, and barbecued fish neck with friggitello pepper. If you opt for a seat on the large bench facing the kitchen, you’ll be able to watch the chefs at work and admire the precision required to prepare different types of sushi. Modern, understated decor.

Name: Berchtesgadener Esszimmer
Description: This long-established inn run by Maximilian and Roxana Kühbeck with great dedication has bags of character. As the charming couple work alone, service can occasionally take a little longer, but this only enhances the pleasingly warm atmosphere. Their seasonal dishes are made with carefully selected ingredients from the immediate area – herbs, for instance, are foraged, or harvested from their own organic garden. There are two set menus, one of which is vegetarian, plus an à la carte selection. In addition to the cosy little dining space with its vaulted ceiling, there are two very popular "Kitchen Tables" for those who wish to see the chefs at work.

Name: Bergara
Address: General Artetxe 8, Donostia / San Sebastián, 20002, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: A popular eatery in the Gros district of the city which has won various awards for its miniature take on haute cuisine! In its colourful and delightful bar you’ll find a vast array of innovative tapas and pinchos, both hot and cold, such as Txalupa (a gratin of mushrooms with prawns), Itxaso (monkfish with a seafood cream), Udaberri (courgette with a crayfish cream), plus the delicious foie gras with port-braised grapes. If you're on your own... be prepared to share a table!

Name: Bergergut
Description: This tasteful restaurant in the charming hotel of the same name promises elegant modern decor and a pleasingly quiet, almost intimate atmosphere, as well as attentive and proficient service, and – last but not least – really good food based on carefully selected ingredients. Quality and craftsmanship shine through in dishes such as creamy ragout of Mühlviertel milk-fed veal lights with Serviettenknödel (bread dumplings). Brunch is served Mon-Sat, Wirtshauskuchl (traditional hearty Austrian fare) at lunchtime, and fine dining in the evening. Sundays feature a "gourmet brunch" with live music, and classic tavern cuisine is served for lunch.

Name: Bergfriedel
Description: This establishment has been run by the same family with great dedication for years! The welcoming team serves delicious, fresh food that diners can enjoy as they take in the views over the Bühlertal. They follow a philosophy that is close to nature - and their own chickens in the garden fit in nicely. The wide-ranging menu includes traditional cuisine from Baden, vegetarian/vegan dishes and gourmet specialities. Add to that an extensive wine list. The chic restaurant extension is done out in a modern take on regional style. Pleasant overnight accommodation is available – the rooms and suites ("Natur-Zimmer" and "Natur-Suiten") are done out in locally sourced materials and are contemporary in their design.

Name: Berghofstüble
Description: This restaurant enjoys a stunning location up above the town. The interior has a pleasing design and there is an attractive conservatory with a pretty terrace outside offering impressive views. The cuisine is based on good, fresh produce with appetising dishes such as Skrei cod on leaf spinach in beurre blanc.

Name: Berghotel Wiedener Eck
Description: Marie and Lorenz Wissler represent the fourth generation of their family to run Berghotel Wiedener Eck, which enjoys an idyllic location at over 1 000m above sea level – the view of the valley is stunning! For overnight stays, there are attractive, cosy guestrooms, and the restaurant is brimming with traditional Black Forest charm, interspersed with modern touches. In the restaurant, you can look forward to friendly and courteous service, as well as regional cuisine and dishes that draw on the culinary traditions of France and the Mediterranean, all made from fresh high-quality ingredients – the chef even hunts his own game. In the evenings, there is a set menu that changes every day, plus the seasonal "Wiedener Eck Menü". You can also order the individual courses of both à la carte. Tip: The surrounding forests and meadows make this hotel a perfect starting point for hikes!

Name: Berghuus Radons
Description: The magnificent location alone – against a stunning mountain backdrop – makes it worth coming to Berghuus. The interior decor is just as charming: carefully restored, the historical timber house oozes charm with its upscale aesthetic combining rustic style and modern touches. The cuisine features regional ingredients, the provenance of which is stated on the menu. In the evening, choose from six dishes, half of which are vegetarian, to put together a three-course meal. There is also a small à la carte menu featuring traditional regional classics. And be sure to take a look at the wine list, which includes some well-known names. The cosy guestrooms are in keeping with the inviting feel of the whole place – making an overnight stay an appealing option. N.B. You will need a permit to drive to the property, which is accessible via narrow roads – please enquire in advance!

Name: Bergwelt - BG's Grill Restaurant
Description: Modern chic with an Alpine touch: Done out in warm tones, with lovely hardwood floors, striking designer lamps and an open kitchen complete with an impressive charcoal grill, this restaurant – part of the equally attractive Bergwelt Grindelwald hotel – has a truly unique atmosphere. The cuisine, inspired by the region, is also very appealing. For meat lovers, the fragrant, golden-brown Wiener schnitzel is sure to whet the appetite, and the same goes for the top-quality signature cuts from the barbecue. Vegetarian options are also available. The well-curated wine list predominantly features Swiss and French labels.

Name: Bernhardhof
Description: This delightfully chic and modern restaurant is to be found at the foot of the hill on which Andechs's famous abbey stands. The Holzinger family used to run a farm here, but nowadays they welcome diners with warmth and dedication. While the father handles the service, the son runs the kitchen with his mother's assistance, preparing delicious dishes using fresh ingredients and drawing on regional and international influences. Think sous-vide neck of Bavarian free-range pork with mashed potatoes, Dijon mustard, onion and pork jus, or roasted root chervil, peanut curry crunch, black cumin mayonnaise and orange yoghurt. You can also stay overnight here in one of the really comfortable and spacious maisonettes or suites.

Name: Bern’s Steak House
Address: 1208 S. Howard Ave., Tampa, FL, 33606, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: For decades, this stately steakhouse has been a local favorite for special occasions of all stripes, and its popularity shows no signs of shrinking. Diners dress to impress amid the garish vintage opulence, which is matched by a slickly ceremonious suit-clad service team and colossal wine collection.A meal might start with oysters, or one of the many caviar options, but savvy diners save ample space for a curated selection of prime steaks, many dry-aged extensively in house before getting a char treatment on the kitchen’s massive grill. Don’t fill up on the assorted sides—at the end of the meal, guests are whisked to the posh upstairs dessert room, where bananas Foster or baked Alaska can be enjoyed with house-roasted coffee and live piano music.

Name: Berso
Description: Berso occupies a tastefully renovated house with a striking contemporary interior design, featuring walls embellished with colourful canvases and decorative details that relate to the town’s renowned music band. The chef at the helm, Martín Mantilla, has created an updated traditional menu that works with the seasons and ingredients that he sources locally. The pleasant patio-terrace is an added bonus.

Name: Berta
Description: Berta would be very proud of her grandson, chef Assaf Granit, who has named this appealing restaurant after her. The energy of the chefs in the open kitchen, nestled behind the counter, is infectious, as they fill the colourful dining space with a vibrant and convivial atmosphere. A lively scenario, for which the menu is a perfect match: it is a veritable celebration of family recipes from Jerusalem infused with the modern spirit of Berlin. The "Frenavon" bread with tahini and tomatoes served beforehand is downright addictive. It is practically impossible to resist the charm of this restaurant!

Name: Bertas im weissen Rössl
Description: Susi and Josef are your young hosts at this charming little restaurant. The stylishly modern interior is wonderfully inviting, with large windows framing spectacular mountain views, which can also be enjoyed from the balcony terrace in summer. The atmosphere is pleasantly relaxed, not least thanks to the friendly proprietress overseeing the service. Inspired by the changing seasons and the culinary traditions of the region, the chef-patron cooks up modern and visually appealing dishes. Options such as free-range chicken from Rietz with cauliflower mash and florets, almonds and raisins, or creamy goulash made with veal from Hanselerhof farm and served with Topfenspätzle (Austrian curd noodles) and Brussels sprouts are served à la carte. The thoughtfully curated wine list emphasises Austrian picks. Private parking available. The restaurant itself is named after Susi's grandmother, whose influence led her into the world of gastronomy.

Name: Bessie
Address: 178 St Asaph Street, Christchurch Central City, Christchurch, 8011, New Zealand
Description: Long tables, booths and plenty of tables for two mean this darkly atmospheric, ersatz industrial looking room caters to all group sizes. It’s a steakhouse featuring dry-aged beef, largely Canterbury grass-fed meat, all cooked in the Spanish charcoal oven. Check out the ageing room, which has pride of place next to the kitchen. There are plenty of imaginative side dishes, along with assorted sauces from the traditional to the more creative. If you’re not a meat lover, go for the Akaroa King salmon.

Name: Best BBQ
Address: 5000 Buford Hwy. NE, Chamblee, GA, 30341, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted
Description: Don't let the name fool you: Best BBQ isn't your typical Southern barbecue spot. Instead, this casual eatery is located inside Chamblee's Ba Hue Market. It's simple and straightforward, with ducks and roast meat on display and walls lined with large photos of the food, making it easy to order by number at the counter. Come hungry or with a crowd, as the portions are large and shareable (though you might want to keep those leftovers all to yourself). The casual Cantonese cooking includes dim sum, barbecue, roast duck, noodles and fried rice with standout dishes including quarter roast duck, honey barbecue roast pork and shrimp congee.

Name: Besta
Description: A casual “neo-bistro” run by chef Manu Núñez, well known after his time on the programme Top Chef. A native of A Coruña, he manages to fuse his Galician origins with Catalan flavours, goes through a constant renewal process, also bringing to his offer some Nordic touches learned during his time working in award-winning restaurants in Sweden. The proposal, typical of a market cuisine that makes constant nods to both the Atlantic and the Mediterranean, takes the form of a small à la carte and two set menus: Degustación and Festival (9 and 12 courses). The Mariscada course, made up of several appetisers that pay tribute to Galician seafood from a modern perspective, really caught our attention. They also have what they call the Chef’s Table, a bar where you can eat while you watch some dishes being finished.

Name: Bestia
Address: 2121 E. 7th Pl., Los Angeles, CA, 90021, USA
Description: As cool and convivial as ever, this is the kind of place where both diners and staff seem perpetually at bliss. Inside, it all feels like a labor of love thanks to husband-and-wife team Ori Menashe and Genevieve Gergis, whose dining rooms across the city are perpetually packed. The space itself is warehouse-sized and rustic, with a copper bar, tulip-shaped pendant lights, booths that appear virtually suspended and a flaming red domed oven. However, it is the cooking that truly calls these crowds. Grilled prawns with serrano pesto, blistered pizzas dressed with Sichuan peppercorn and wildflower honey, and rich pastas showered in truffles strike all the right chords. Desserts are equally enticing,

Name: Betong
Description: ‘Betong’ translates as ‘concrete’ in English, which explains the bare walls at this buzzy, simply decorated restaurant. Dishes like the Chef's signature ‘Cold Curry’ (available as an added extra to the tasting menu) showcase his creative heart, but the kitchen's classical technique shines through in highlight dishes like butter-poached skrei cod with pak choi. Dining here is a fun experience, in a space bursting with energy and filled with pumping music; but it might not be the best spot for an intimate romantic date.

Name: Betton Fils
Description: This small restaurant in the city centre sits neatly in a corner building sporting the characteristic grey stone of Saint-Malo. At the helm is chef Victor Betton, once a fencing champion, who deftly dishes up generous cuisine. A devotee of fine food, he searches out the best ingredients within a 50km radius. At lunchtime, the reasonably priced menu would disarm any adversary: fillet of pollack cooked golden, creamy potato purée, flavoursome shellfish foam; roasted figs, rosemary oil, shiso and herbaceous granita. In the evening, the menu focuses on more premium ingredients (hand-dived scallops, line-caught John Dory).

Name: Between
Description: This top-quality restaurant occupies just one simple, minimalist-style dining room, where the young female chef serves a happy combination of Piedmontese ingredients and more creative dishes acquired during her time working abroad.

Name: Beulings
Description: This warm, intimate restaurant is nestled in a quaint little street in the capital city. Bas cooks solo in the open kitchen while Lisja charms diners with her charisma and outstanding wine recommendations. The set menu showcases the chef's wealth of experience through elegant compositions and harmonious flavours. French foundations meet Cantonese influences in dishes such as beautifully seared Ibérico secreto accompanied by subtly smoked king trumpet mushrooms, a cashew cream, dumplings with a creamy minced pork filling and a peppered pork sauce. For foodies, Beulings is a home from home.

Name: Beurre Noisette
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the heart of Lucenay, a village built of Beaujolais golden limestone, this restaurant occupies a converted village school. Pauline Fleuret, along with her partner, front of house, keeps things simple in this inviting space. Her market-fresh cuisine is fresh and healthy, designed for maximum flavour: Comté croquettes, saucisse de Morteau and beetroot ketchup; chicken blanquette with tarragon and candied lemon, polenta gratin; lemon and sesame cake, mascarpone cream and meringue pieces. Reasonable prices. Booking is essential.

Name: Bevir by Lopesan
Description: After enjoying such resounding success in the capital of Gran Canaria, this restaurant is embarking on a new venture in the luxurious Lopesan Costa Meloneras Resort & Spa hotel. The goal? To offer diners an even more hedonistic culinary experience. The restaurant is found in an interior courtyard with large windows overlooking it, opting for a minimalist aesthetic and with chef José Luis Espino at the helm, a man loyal to Canarian produce who tries to define his cuisine under the concept ‘Where the vegetable garden meets the sea’, always paying homage to local flavours and the importance of making the most of natural ingredients. You will find two tasting menus, with a modern twist, which seek to pay tribute to Benito Pérez Galdós's most famous characters and celebrate this distinguished Canarian writer: Fortunata (11 courses) and Jacinta (14 courses). The standout dish? We loved the beetroot with beurre blanc and dill oil for its excellent combination of flavours and textures.

Name: Beyti
Address: Şenlikköy Mahallesi, Orman Sokak No:6, Florya/Bakırköy, Istanbul, 34153, Türkiye
Description: Beyti Güler is a living legend in Istanbul. Since the 1980s, Istanbulites have been coming to dine in this stylish building, a fine example of nostalgic Turkish charm, with its little fountains at the entrance and sculptures in the garden. And this historical establishment boasts no fewer than 12 dining rooms! The charcoal grill is at the centre of the kitchen, where the experienced chefs cook all kinds of meat to perfection. Take the imam bayildi, for example: meltingly tender braised aubergine topped with tomatoes, bell peppers and onions, cooked just long enough to bring out all their flavours. And be sure to try one of the kebabs, too. Traditional Turkish fare just as it should be.

Name: Bez Gwiazdek
Description: Located just minutes from The Royal Castle in Warsaw, this cosy restaurant has a real neighbourhood feel. The menu changes monthly, with each version focusing on cooking inspired by one of Poland's 16 regions. The chefs take traditional recipes and modernise them using contemporary techniques and sometimes a creative edge. Service comes from a wonderfully enthusiastic team who show considerable pride in their work. The great wine recommendations favour biodynamic choices from smaller producers.

Name: Beç
Address: Copríncep François Mitterrand 2, Escaldes-Engordany, AD700, Andorra
Description: If you’re looking for a spectacular setting in which to eat near the Caldea spa, this restaurant in a shopping district just two minutes’ walk away could be the place. To a welcoming contemporary backdrop featuring a profusion of wood and an open-view kitchen, enjoy an updated take on traditional cuisine. Standout dishes include aged beef loin tartare, pigs’ trotters stuffed with prawns from Sant Carles and several seasonal specialities such as Maresme peas with wild mushrooms and white prawns.

Name: Bhoomi
Description: Solid wood furniture, rattan pendant lamps and wagon wheel chandeliers impart modern boho chic in this bright, cosy space with two levels. The chef recounts his memories and personal story through a menu that encompasses meat dishes, as well as vegetarian, gluten-free and vegan options. Inspired by Indian street food, the signature Indori beetroot tikki is big on flavours with a hint of sweetness from the corn.

Name: Bhoomi Kitchen
Address: 52 Suffolk Road, Cheltenham, GL50 2AQ, United Kingdom
Description: You’ll receive a warm welcome at this sumptuous restaurant, run by the third generation of a family who settled here from India 50 years ago. The menu is mostly southern Indian, with a particular focus on recipes from Kerala, and the dishes prove to be bright and authentic. Options like the 'Chilli Chicken', combining succulent chicken breast with a rich tomato, chilli and garlic sauce, showcase skill and flavour aplenty. If you're celebrating or simply feeling indecisive, the 'Banquet' and 'Feast' menus are a great way to go.

Name: BiBi
Address: 42 North Audley Street, Mayfair, London, W1K 6ZP, United Kingdom
Description: Chef Chet Sharma’s buzzy Mayfair restaurant is named after his grandmothers (bibis), Kamal and Ranjana, and there’s often a family story behind each creation on the evening set menu, which offers around 10 courses. A seat at the counter is therefore a must, to watch Sharma and his team prepare and explain the history of each detailed dish. The menu starts with intriguing and varied snacks like Kala Channa and Oxford Blue Malai Kofta; other standouts from the experience include Sharmaji's Lahori Chicken and Ajwaini Scallops.

Name: BiBo Budapest
Address: Dorothea Hotel, Apáczai Csere János utca 11, 7th Floor, Budapest, 1051, Hungary
Description: Take the dedicated lift up to the seventh floor of the Dorothea Hotel and you’ll be warmly greeted with magical views across the river towards Budapest Castle. Start with one of their signature cocktails on the terrace to take it all in, then choose from a menu that fuses Hungary and Spain with aplomb. From rock prawn tempura to their signature ‘Garcia’ burgers or chicken stuffed with morels – as well as dishes to share – everything is generously proportioned and expertly delivered. Providing a perfect match is a wine list that favours, you may have guessed it, Hungary and Spain.

Name: BiBo Madrid
Address: Paseo de la Castellana 52, Madrid, 28046, Spain
Description: If you are keen to embark on a culinary journey to explore a magical gastronomic world of cosmopolitan cuisine at its finest, you don’t even need to leave Spain’s capital! This restaurant, decorated by the famous interior designer Lázaro Rosa-Violán, will surprise all and sundry with its fun aesthetic, dominated by some 7 000 light bulbs (that take us on a journey to the brilliance of the Málaga fair) and even an aerostatic globe! From a purely gourmet viewpoint, the contemporary, globally inspired cuisine (but with its roots in Andalucia), bears the hallmark of award-winning Marbella chef Dani García. The food here is very much designed for sharing in an informal atmosphere as a couple or with friends, and includes dishes such as foie gras and goat’s cheese millefeuille, almadraba-caught tuna tartare, fried hake, and 100% acorn-fed Iberian pork “pluma”. The à la carte also includes a small section dedicated to the chef’s signature dishes.

Name: Bianca by Giovi
Description: This welcoming restaurant in the heart of Arrowtown sports a cosy dining room, a relaxing patio and a Vespa oozing vintage Italian charm. The menu offers handmade pasta and pizzas that stay true to their roots. The ravioli, filled with ricotta and spinach or Angus beef, and served in basilico or butter and sage sauce, is always blissful. Round off with limoncello and cantucci biscotti in true Italian style.

Name: Bianca sul Lago
Description: Overlooking the evocative Lake Annone, the restaurant at Bianca Relais captivates from the very first glance thanks to its expansive panoramic windows, which frame sunsets of rare beauty as the sun slips slowly behind the gentle outline of the surrounding hills. An elegant and refined setting, ideal for an emotionally resonant gastronomic experience. At the helm of the kitchen is chef Filippo Oggioni, previously awarded a Michelin Star at Vecchio Ristoro in Aosta, who presents a creative and refined proposal articulated across three “blind” tasting menus: one dedicated to the plant world, one centred on freshwater fish, and a third that follows the inspiration and seasonality of the market. Completing the journey is a young, well-trained and attentive front-of-house team. For a more informal approach, the Drop Restaurant & Lounge Bar offers a versatile and contemporary alternative, with an all-day menu served continuously from midday to ten in the evening, perfect for any moment of the day.

Name: Bianchi
Description: A slice of la dolce vita! Located right by the Limmat River, this ristorante boasts a bright and modern interior where excellent service comes courtesy of a cheerful and adept front-of-house team. Made with top-notch produce, the Mediterranean-style fish and seafood dishes here are in high demand. Gorgeous little terrace.

Name: Biao Xia
Address: 3F, The Ritz-Carlton, 369 Guangji South Road, Gusu, Suzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The room inspired by classical Suzhou gardens serves refined Huai Yang and Jiangzhe cuisine. This cuisine has no secrets for chef Tian, whose father and grandfather were both Huai Yang chefs. Seasonal produce, freshwater fish and seafood are crafted into culinary gems depicted by light, umami flavours. His braised glass noodles with river shrimp, tomalley and roe are a nod to the classic shrimp trio noodles, with mild heat and acidity to cut through the richness.

Name: Bibi Ji
Address: 1213 State St., Ste. B, Santa Barbara, CA, 93101, USA
Description: With their name emblazoned in pink, this trendy Indian from co-owners Alejandro Medina and noted sommelier Rajat Parr makes quite the splash. Inside, the space is small but well appointed, with vaulted ceilings and chandeliers; the patio outside is a verdant, summertime delight. Harnessing the best of land and sea, these dishes are born for sharing. Behold such inventive bites as crispy cauliflower tossed with chili-garlic sauce and finished with sesame. Barra kebab highlights intensely spiced tandoor lamb chops with mint chutney; while vegetables like baingan bharta (eggplant with ginger) are a heady treat. The cooking is strong and flavors well executed. No wonder, dessert is an afterthought.A list of natural wines merely augments the focused carte.

Name: Bichopalo
Description: The Pozuelo brothers (Daniel in the kitchen; Guillermo front of house) continue to showcase their “uninhibited haute cuisine” that is part of their DNA. In this small restaurant in the Ríos Rosas district, a much more comfortable setting than their previous eatery in the Barceló market, they have kept their dining counter as a sign of their identity as well as to retain the informal ambience. The cuisine here, contemporary in style and featuring innovative flavours and Mediterranean and Asian touches, is based around a single surprise tasting menu on which dishes add a completely new dimension to traditional day-to-day recipes!

Name: Bick Stuff
Description: A family-run establishment where you will instantly feel at home. Bick is a local word which literally means ‘beak’ in English but loosely translates as ‘food’. Owners Virginie and Denis Laissy have the same goal: to serve good food in a relaxed atmosphere. Chef Denis rustles up reassuringly classical recipes, adding his own distinctive touch. We recommend the set menu.

Name: Bicol Korean Cuisine
Address: Rua José Getúlio 422, São Paulo, 01509-000, Brazil
Description: Bicol is a must if you’re keen to try Korean barbecue-style cuisine. This classic address in the Liberdade district of the city has been run by a South Korean family for three generations. In this spacious restaurant, the tables have their own grills so that guests can cook meat (usually cut super-fine) to their individual taste. Dishes for sharing are the mainstay here, including the Burgogui, Garbi and Samguiopsar combos, as well as cuts of pure national Wagyu beef, always accompanied by Banchan (small side dishes of the day). The Bibimbap (a typical rice dish), soups, or classic dishes such as Topokki and Korean fried chicken are other interesting options on the menu, not forgetting the delicious kimchi, of course. Why not pair your food with the traditional soju, a typical Korean beverage with differing strengths of alcohol?

Name: Bicyclette Cookshop
Address: 819 Vanderbilt Beach Rd., Naples, FL, 34108, USA
Description: At this neighborhood favorite in North Naples, find sincerity and creativity in ample supply. A warm front of house team treats everyone like a regular, while the kitchen prepares a playful, inspired menu that is endlessly tempting. Where does one begin? Caviar with bugles and crème fraiche? Chorizo potatoes with chipotle hollandaise? The signature vanilla soft serve doused with olive oil from the owner’s own vineyard in Italy is a sweet, honest reflection of the restaurant itself. A tastefully designed dining room makes this a sharp pick both for lunch and dinner.

Name: Bidaia
Description: In the heart of Badajoz, on the ground floor of a corner building next to the cathedral, lies a simple bistro with the soul of a gastronomic bar, which surprises with its culinary offerings. Under the Basque name of Bidaia, a term that could be translated as ‘journey’, the young couple at the helm, Elena Ruiz and Álvaro Serrano, champion a small market à la carte and two set menus, which are closely linked to the season and hark back the traditional roots drinking from memories and personal experiences, mainly in the north of Spain. We loved the all-natural prawn tartare and its mellow Iberian cheek a la royale!

Name: Bido
Address: Marcial del Adalid 2, A Coruña, 15005, Spain
Description: Well-prepared dishes, high-quality products and delicate presentation lie at the very heart of this restaurant. Not far from the fish market, this establishment surprises in both substance and form, offering contemporary local cuisine in a designer setting. The menu, with the option of half portions for all dishes, is complemented by two set menus: 'Gastronómico' and 'Degustación' (both with wine pairing options). What to order? We were particularly impressed by the successful combination of flavours in the grilled lamb loin and braised neck, 'Queso do Cebreiro', avocado and pea guacamole.

Name: Bidou
Address: 9 Jalan Setiakasih 5, Bukit Damansara, Kuala Lumpur, 50490, Malaysia
Description: Unlike Dewakan that focuses on innovation, chef Darren Teoh opened Bidou to revisit the nouvelle cuisine movement. The 3- or 4-course set menu offers a choice of dishes, which may include threadfin and scallop mousse baked en croûte, in a nod to the recipe of culinary pioneer, Paul Bocuse. The pastry crust is shaped like a fish and a tangy Choron sauce complements the juicy flesh. Also check out the wine list with over 30 by-the-glass choices.

Name: Bieberbau
Description: For those who appreciate not only good food but also a wonderful atmosphere, this is just the place! Dating back to 1894, the beautifully restored, heritage-listed dining room features truly spectacular stucco work by Richard Bieber. Within this unique setting, guests are warmly attended to by the friendly and capable service team led by hostess and sommelier Anne Garkisch, while chef-patron Stephan Garkisch cooks up modern dishes at the Molteni stove. There is a choice of two set menus (one of which is vegetarian) of at least three courses, in which herbs and spices are given star billing – much of the produce comes from the restaurant's own garden. Good value for money.

Name: Bienheureux
Address: 35 avenue de la Marne, Wasquehal, 59290, France
Description: In a red-brick manor house turned into a hub combining co-working spaces, offices and a garden, Lucas Grabowski (who after a stint at NESO in Paris went on to run Gabo) cooks up precise and creative seasonal cuisine: ballotine of sole with seaweed and roasted buckwheat; confit egg yolk with peas and herb broth. There is a simpler set menu at lunchtime, and an extensive à la carte menu in the evening.

Name: Bienvenue
Description: John van Leerzem is a fan of tradition and of the ingredient before all else. This institution on the main square of Maaseik does far more than showcase time-honoured classics. The chef happily subverts traditional recipes, particularly thanks to carefully devised side dishes, such as a terrine of veal cheek and tongue that he subtly contrasts with sweet-sour chutney. His stamp can also be tasted in the tournedos and stroganoff sauce that strikes a perfect balance of flavours. A feast for foodies!

Name: Big Ray's Fish Camp
Description: Far from the trendy neighborhoods, this seafood shack that could be mistaken for a bait and tackle shop flies slightly under the radar but is a total find. Order from the menu displayed behind the counter, then find a seat at one of a few wooden tables set with metal chairs inside, or head outdoors to a tent-covered picnic table. Owner Raymond "Nick" Cruz doles out a typical dressed-down, seafood shack-style menu with starters like smoked fish dip, peel and eat shrimp, and a basket loaded with blackened shrimp and Cuban-style yucca. Then, a smattering of sandwiches includes their house classic fried grouper alongside creative riffs like a lobster tail corn dog sided by fries or coleslaw. To finish, nothing beats a wedge of key lime pie with graham cracker crust.

Name: Bij Hammingh
Description: It is impossible to resist the authentic charm of this former ferry house, from the terrace of which you can fully appreciate the lovely views across the canal and drawbridge. Inside, you can sense the building’s rich heritage, where the chef focuses on regional delicacies that showcase modern techniques and natural finesse.

Name: Bij Sidney
Address: Kerkstraat 5, Loenen aan de Vecht, 3632 EL, Netherlands
Description: Chef Sidney Heinze and maître d' Dennis Bitter are united by their passion for traditional gastronomy. Having established themselves in Loenen aan de Vecht, they have infused their intimate restaurant with the charm of the village. The number of diners is intentionally restricted to ensure a personal experience – the chef likes to introduce himself at each table. The enticing menu is a genuine tribute to French-Belgian cuisine. Drawing on a wealth of experience, chef Heinze puts his own stamp on dishes such as frog's legs à la meunière, tournedos Rossini and oven-baked turbot accompanied by a lobster Béarnaise. A nose for top-quality ingredients, a mastery of intense sauces and the ability to make seemingly straightforward dishes shine with their classical depth: craftsmanship is the hallmark here.

Name: Bilanx
Description: Located in an old townhouse midway between the Széchenyi Chain Bridge and St. Stephen's Basilica, Bilanx takes a fresh, modern approach to dining out. Its interior is sparsely decorated, with varnished wooden chairs set at white-tile-topped tables, while neon light strips create glowing archways above and pop music plays through the speakers. The chef offers a tasting menu which combines his two loves – Hungarian produce and classical French techniques, so you’ll find dishes like Mangalitsa pork with choron sauce and parsley root cream. There’s also an interesting three-course menu available at lunch.

Name: Billy's
Description: Billy’s, established in the original century-old homestead of the Ayrburn dining precinct, features several rooms, each with a different tale. A glazed conservatory lets guests dine under the Otago sky year-round, as creative, refined Chinese fare takes centre stage. Crystal prawn har gow boasts smooth skin and a generous filling, as coriander adds aromas and fish roe offers a burst of flavour. Chinese themed cocktails are well worth trying.

Name: Bina Bar
Address: José Cádiz Salvatierra 7D, Jerez de la Frontera, 11405, Spain
Description: Behind the term Bina, which is a reference to the viticultural work to oxygenate the soil of the vineyards and rid them of weeds, is chef Juanlu Fernández’s more informal dining space, the man at the head of the two-star LÚ Cocina y Alma. Here, in the area known as the Torres de Córdoba (about 10 minutes from the centre), you will find a modern restaurant that oozes the essence of Jerez, with many dishes inherited from the old gastronomic restaurant, a good selection of stews and dishes that reinterpret both Andalusian cuisine and recipes from further afield (especially Colombia, a nod to his business partner and romantic partner, Dolce Nilda Suarez). Don't miss the Huelva prawn salad or the delicious steamed almadraba tuna mollete with kimchi mayonnaise.

Name: BingSheng Pin Wei (Dongxiao Road)
Address: 33 Dongxiao Road, Haizhu, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: The group first made its name with sashimi and, at this branch, diners may choose from sea perch, grass carp, amberjack and a myriad of live prawns. It also prides itself highly on the unmissable 'four beauties' – crispy char siu (pork belly crusted with breadcrumbs and sugar), soy-marinated pork trotters, pork tripe and goose intestines. Large parties may also try their jumbo-sized pineapple buns, to be ordered by the half dozen.

Name: Bink
Description: If you’re looking for good food in a warm romantic-cum-characterful bistro vibe, head towards the former Brepols printing works, where an open kitchen sets the tone in this feel-good establishment. You can choose between a primarily classical lineup or a more modern repertory, strewn with Asian influences. Top-drawer, consummately crafted ingredients, like lobster and black truffles on a bed of duxelles cèpe mushrooms and crunchy brioche bread, flanked by a mushroom garum and a subtle choron sauce. Classy minimalism, fresh ingredients cooked from scratch and authentic hospitality.

Name: Bino
Description: Situated in the historic centre near the ceramic museum (some of its pieces are also on display in the restaurant), Bino Ricchebuono boasts an attractive outdoor space in a charming small square. Michelin-starred chef Ricchebuono from Noli is the brains behind this restaurant, which serves fish and meat dishes prepared with a touch of creativity.

Name: Biondi
Description: Near the Cirque d’Hiver, this gifted chef named his buzzy restaurant after a famous Argentinean clown, Pepe Biondi. South America also takes pride of place on the lineup which stars a fine selection of meats cooked over embers and desserts of the likes of a caramel flan with a dulce de leche mousse – to die for! Fine selection of Argentinean wines.

Name: Bird & Buffalo
Description: Picnic tables gift-wrapped with colorful plastic tablecloths and unhurried, nonchalant service readily evoke the casual roadside restaurants scattered throughout Thailand—and happily, so do the multifaceted, punchy flavors. The menu encompasses Northeastern specialties like redolent grilled meats and zingy, crunchy green papaya somtum (pick from Thai or Lao style, with the addition of fish paste and salted crab), but you’ll also find more cosmopolitan staples like Kao Soi curry noodles and a variety of curries. When it comes to spice level, ask and ye shall receive—you won’t regret having an ice-cold Singha on hand. After a meal of boldly seasoned dishes, lusciously ripe mango over sweet-salty coconut sticky rice makes for a pleasingly gentle finish.

Name: Birdie's
Description: This East Austin darling from Chef Tracy Malechek-Ezekiel and partner Arjav Ezekiel looks and feels like the quintessential neighborhood place but one glance at the line out the door and it's clear Birdie's is also a destination for visitors. Be prepared for a wait to order at their counter, then find a seat indoors or out on the shaded patio.Everyone is here for a taste of their unfussy but well-executed, regional European cooking. Each month, a set menu focuses on a different location, with France and Italy often appearing as the firm favorites. Homemade pasta is always a highlight, while soft serve ice cream is a reliable treat.

Name: Birds Of Paradise (Katong)
Description: A mesmerising array of top-quality gelato and sorbet is served in house-made thyme-scented waffle cones. Sea salt hojicha, white chrysanthemum, and raspberry lychee are some of its outstanding offerings.

Name: Birinci Kordon Balık Restoran
Address: Alsancak, Atatürk Caddesi No:196/A, Konak, Izmir, 35220, Türkiye
Description: Fish, fish and more fish – that's what you can expect at this rather simple restaurant. The refrigerated display counter immediately catches the eye as the charcoal grill works overtime in the kitchen. After some freshly prepared mezze, for example, allow the chef to delight you with succulent barbecued calamari rings in a chilli crust, or just as expertly flame-grilled sea bass. Such incredible flavours! No frills here: the focus lies squarely on unadulterated top-quality produce. A gem among the many restaurants on the quayside.

Name: Birrieria y Taqueria Cortez
Address: 2108 E. Rosedale St., Fort Worth, TX, 76104, USA
Description: Rogelio Cortez Jr. first earned a steady following with a food truck before opening this brick-and-mortar location where music keeps things lively, and the vibe is casual and inviting. The name says it all, as their specialty lies in their wonderfully tender and flavorful birria. It's not just the highlight—it's the only protein offered—but it's served in a number of tempting ways from tacos and flautas to tortas, burritos, and quesadillas. Order their corn tortilla tacos, stuffed with a generous amount of birria and accompanied by onion, cilantro, and lime, or choose their quesatacos, or two corn tortillas filled with mozzarella cheese and birria meat that is crisped at the edges.

Name: Birriería "David"
Address: C. Joaquin Angulo 188 E, Centro Barranquitas, Guadalajara, 44280, Mexico
Description: There are only eight stools lined up against a stainless-steel counter at this spot, located on the second floor of the Mercardo Alcalde, so you should expect a bit of a wait. It's worth your time, though, as this laidback eatery has perfected the art of birria, with three generations honing their craft over the last 60 years. Today, the son and grandson of the founder share their skills with diners who choose between a small or large plate as well as a choice of cuts (surtida or carnaza). It's slightly different here than what you may expect, as the meat is left in pieces, but it has that perfect blend of a crispy, golden-brown exterior with moist, tender meat. To top it off, you'll get a pour of their birria consommé, as well as some warmed tortillas.

Name: Birriería las 9 Esquinas
Address: C. Colón 384, Zona Centro, Guadalajara, 44100, Mexico
Description: From the tile floors and tile-lined walls to walls hung with pots and pottery, Birriería las 9 Esquinas has simple, rustic charm down pat. If the name didn't offer a hint, this longstanding restaurant is all about birria, specifically goat birria (the stained-glass goat's head enhancing one side of the kitchen is another clue). It is offered in a variety of ways here, with a standard order, a small order and an order of three tacos in freshly made corn tortillas. Their tortillas are skillfully made and cooked to order, and the birria is accompanied by a variety of salsas, as well as diced onion and lime for an enjoyable, casual meal you won't soon forget.

Name: Bis Osteria Italiana Contemporanea
Address: Via 20 Settembre 50, Colle di Val d'Elsa, 53034, Italy
Description: In the glorious premises of the old Arnolfo restaurant in the old town, this restaurant is run by the same management as previously, although with a new young chef at the helm in the kitchen. The delicious yet concise menu features “Italian specialities” (the name given to all the main courses) with a focus on meat and fish, accompanied by excellent bread options (you can even order “scarpetta” dipping bread for mopping up the remains of a Cinta Senese pork sauce). The house speciality is a delicious pigeon dish. In fine weather, guests can dine on the beautiful, tranquil terrace.

Name: Biscotte
Description: Pauline and Maximilien, two alumni of the most prestigious establishments (Le Bristol, Lasserre, Arpège), have set up their own place near Porte de Versailles. Convivial bistro interior, large atelier windows separating the kitchen, tasty and studied dishes: all the ingredients are in place for an enjoyable experience.

Name: Bislakko
Address: Via Thaon de Revel 87, Vercelli, 13100, Italy
Description: They’ve played with words here, because “bislacco” (quirky) applies only to the name. This restaurant will win you over with its cuisine: meat dishes, fish, and vegetarian options coexist harmoniously, without forgetting the ever‑present risottos, available à la carte or in tasting menus. Among these, Chocolate Passion stands out, where chocolate – expertly dosed – appears in every course. After all, they call themselves a “cioccoristoreria” (a playful portmanteau of chocolate and restaurant).

Name: Bisou
Address: 68 Soi Langsuan 9, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Valet parking
Description: Chef Antoine Darquin and sommelier Théo Lavergne bring a fresh, fashionable Parisian flair to Bangkok's dining scene. Bisou delivers sexy simplicity through modern French cuisine, prioritising premium ingredients. The stylish yet relaxed space features enchanting lights, a spiral staircase and wall art. The dishes and rare wines contribute to a unique local experience influenced by the latest trends from Paris.

Name: Bisque
Description: At Bisque, everything is perfectly balanced: the understated luxury of the interior, the precision of the cuisine and the warmth of Sabrina, who welcomes every guest with ease. At the back, chef Niels Schievink runs his kitchen with a steady hand. Understated in style, precise in execution. A dish featuring langoustine immediately reveals his signature style: a perfectly cooked tail combined with carrot, yuzu and a soft bisque with subtle citrus nuances. And whether you finish with a classic soufflé or his own interpretation of tiramisu, this less-is-more approach to French cuisine and celebration of beautiful produce will stay with you.

Name: Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Bistro is housed in Parkhotel Quellenhof, the flagship of Aachen's hotel scene – the marble lobby and the fireplace and tearoom with its exquisite wood panelling are well worth seeing. Classic cuisine with Mediterranean influences is served in a stylish, minimalist-style dining space. The appealing evening menu features dishes such as Black Angus beef tartare with brioche, lobster foam soup with lobster ravioli and tarragon, and Wiener schnitzel with potato and cucumber salad, as well as vegetarian options. There is a smaller selection of dishes available at lunchtime and a snack menu in the afternoon. The terrace overlooking the park is a delightful spot.

Name: Bistro
Description: The bistro at the exclusive Gut Lärchenhof golf club on the outskirts of Cologne offers a somewhat simpler alternative to the eponymous fine dining restaurant, but you are just as assured of flavour and freshness – at both lunch and dinner. They serve dishes ranging from Currywurst to Königsberger Klopse (meatballs) and caviar. Needless to say, the terrace overlooking the green is delightful!

Name: Bistro 9:45
Description: Nestled in the natural surroundings of Bovec, this small bistro offers an informal, welcoming atmosphere ideal for sampling modern, imaginative dishes of land and sea, executed with simplicity and attention to detail. Standout offerings include trout sashimi and roast beef. A panoramic veranda with splendid forest views completes the experience at this pleasant destination.

Name: Bistro B
Description: This friendly neo-bistro in Lyon's 6th arrondissement offers a traditional menu in the zeitgeist with the odd globetrotting influence: tataki of beef and miso, celeriac marinated in walnut vinegar; leg of guinea fowl, truffle-flavoured mashed potatoes and mushrooms; hake with bok choy cabbage, seasonal veg and curry sauce.

Name: Bistro BT
Description: This casual yet charming outpost arrives on the scene courtesy of celebrated local restaurateur, BT Nguyen. It is friendly and atmospheric with gracious servers merely augmenting the inviting feel. Over in the kitchen, the team cooks up a homey combination of French and Vietnamese dishes, ranging from beloved standbys to bolder bistro fare. The Vietnamese plates are a cut above, though, and include the likes of crispy spring rolls faithfully packed with ground pork, glass noodles and wood ear mushroom; followed by deeply aromatic pho bobbing with springy noodles and generous amounts of meltingly soft tenderloin.A handful of carefully curated wines along with a small assortment of thoughtfully crafted iced teas are sure to quench your thirst in style.

Name: Bistro Bardot
Description: Exposed brick and pipework give this two-roomed brasserie a rustic, slightly retro feel that chimes perfectly with its buoyant atmosphere. It’s a deservedly busy place, named after actress Brigitte Bardot and taking a similarly French outlook on culinary matters too. The extensive à la carte offers all manner of classic brasserie staples, from steak au poivre to tarte Tatin, while the 'menu du jour' provides a simpler, good value selection. The wine list has some appealing French favourites and the friendly team serve the large numbers with ease.

Name: Bistro Berto
Description: Zulte-Waregem football club has hired a new striker! In the southern stand, David Bertolozzi hits the bullseye every time with his generous dishes. Start with a range of snacks to share, like generous nuggets of plaice dipped in tartare sauce, before digging into a modern version of classical recipes, such as pheasant with winter side dishes or a heart-warming vol-au-vent. Attractive lunchtime menu.

Name: Bistro Boca
Description: With moorings just a few metres away, this bistro is of course popular with yachties, as well as to anyone seeking an authentic French dining experience with sea views. A Parisian-style décor sets the lively stage for a crisp, deftly crafted menu including moules frites, steak tartare, cassoulet de canard and the classic sole meunière in a festival of traditional flavours courtesy of premium ingredients. We recommend starting with a knockout cocktail - the bartender excels at timeless classics. Inspector’s tip: make the most of the small beach just below after lunch or before dinner.

Name: Bistro Bord'o
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: The moment you enter this welcoming restaurant, the emphasis on French and European wines is unmistakable. So, an aperitif is definitely in order before settling down to the food, which is rooted in French culinary tradition and includes occasional international influences. No fancy foams here, just top-notch ingredients. Think rare ribeye accompanied by a full-bodied bordelaise sauce, or sea bass ceviche marinated in calamansi and red chilli, seasoned with pezo and served alongside fresh snow crab, coastal vegetables and fennel prepared with a crisp, acidic dressing. This is a chance to savour a wealth of flavours in a laid-back setting – in summer, you can even do it on a boat!

Name: Bistro Ego
Description: Earthy colours set the tone at this relaxed neighbourhood spot, where a huge modern painting takes centre stage and plush cushions and potted plants are dotted about the place. If it’s a more intimate feel you’re after, however, head down the spiral staircase to the cellar, where you’ll be greeted by exposed brickwork and moody lighting. The menus certainly offers something a little different for Helsinki, with French bistro classics given a Japanese makeover; you might find pike quenelles with togarashi spiced lobster cream or yuzu parfait with Japanese rose syrup and caramelised buckwheat.

Name: Bistro Fatal
Description: It would be a shame (perhaps even a fatal mistake) not to get to know Alexandre and Sarah Bourgeuil's pleasantly unpretentious bistro, where savoir-vivre is the order of the day. The classic French menu is enticing, featuring staples such as beef tartare, chocolate soufflé and – of course – oysters. The food here is excellent. You can pick dishes to make up your own three-course "Toi & Moi" set menu – vegetarian options are also available. In summer, a terrace is set up on the pavement in front of the building. N.B. Finding a parking space nearby is not easy.

Name: Bistro Glass
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Bistro Glass is elegant and cosy – make a beeline for the terrace on Vlaamse Kaai if you really want to soak up the hip atmosphere of the Zuid neighbourhood. Sally, who presides front-of-house, consistently proves that she is a hostess at heart, while chef Alain showcases his versatility. His cuisine is intricate and draws inspiration from both Eastern and Western culinary traditions. Think house-made pasta stuffed with potato and truffle, paired with ginger and five-spice chicken, Chinese cabbage, a creamy truffle sauce and foie gras. He balances rich flavours with a sure touch, creating ingredient-led cuisine that is truly captivating.

Name: Bistro Gourmand
Description: Behind the characteristic stone façade of the Wave Distillery, this bistro more than embodies its name (gourmand)! Matthieu Chalmagne adds a new spin to pedigree Gallic classics in a high-flying bistronomic vein and imbues a certain delicacy to his dishes, without losing sight of their hunger-satisfying goal. His personal take on a family favourite, veal stew, is a case in point: fluffy rice with carrots and celery, on top of which are placed two slices of Melba toast which are, in turn, smothered in melt-in-the-mouth, fork-tender veal stew, while a dollop of Madras curry-spiked creamy gravy adds the final flourish. While the chef freely admits to adding playful touches to his work, he nonetheless ensures that the à la carte lineup remains on a reassuringly classical keel.

Name: Bistro LOF
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Chicory (lof in Dutch) grows in the kitchen garden that surrounds this laid-back restaurant, which is modern with a raw edge. Set in a converted farmhouse on the Parc Broekhuizen estate, where diners sit beneath the handsome timber roof trusses, the design brings nature indoors, creating a soothing, zen-like atmosphere. The chef cooks in step with the harvest, showcasing Dutch produce and using spices to add verve. A dish might feature cherry tomatoes plucked straight from the garden and herbs folded into a mayonnaise to accompany briny mussels, chopped watermelon and a complex mussel jus with yellow curry.
