Her cooking is sophisticated and indulgent. In this bistro, you can both see and taste how the seasons enrich the land.

Name: Bistro Luux
Description: No need to wonder whether Bistro Luux is open: this upscale bistro welcomes diners every day, both at lunchtime and in the evening – and whenever you decide to come, the mood inside is wonderfully relaxed. The terrace on the market square is also inviting. In the open kitchen to the rear, you can see seasoned chef Ron Lemmens at work. He closed his previous restaurant (Flavours) in order to pursue a more accessible cooking style, more akin to French cuisine. From his lavish bouillabaisse with impeccably fresh fish to a vol-au-vent enriched by a rich velouté and crisp vegetables, or even a whole lobster Bellevue, he brings tradition to life with generosity and a commitment to quality. The broad menu will undoubtedly make choosing difficult. You could happily make this a daily habit.

Name: Bistro Là-Haut
Description: Thanks to the hilltop location on Mont Valérien, this loft-style restaurant commands a superb view of Paris. The à la carte menu boasts a tempting range of contemporary dishes, such as hay-smoked poultry, vegetable tian au gratin with aged parmesan and a reduced jus. For dinnertime, booking is strongly recommended.

Name: Bistro Madeleine
Description: As typical as the name sounds, this place is far from being your average bistro. Rather than a stuffy decor, you can expect a 21C take on the standard bistro setting. The chef conjures up the same impression on the plate. Upon entering, you are greeted by the delicious aroma of fresh bread. Here, simplicity is synonymous with robust flavours. The modern touches he brings to the dishes add a surprising twist. Think ray wing with a roasted pepper sauce vierge, creamed celeriac and a frothy tarragon sauce. The carefully curated wine list is second to none. An atypical bistro!

Name: Bistro Margaux
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Djailany van de Laarschot’s ambition is clear: to celebrate life à la française, and to bring his vision to life he has transformed a former estaminet into this charming, ever-buzzing bistro. The extensive menu embraces French culinary tradition – think foie gras pâté with brioche to start, followed by juicy rotisserie poussin and, finally, an indulgent crêpe Suzette. Traditional flavours are served up with abundant generosity in a heartwarming feast for any foodie.

Name: Bistro Mathilda
Description: A modern bistro on Leopold II Laan. The enthusiastic owners shine the spotlight on North Sea delicacies sourced from local boats, together with brasserie dishes and a set menu with choices in a more contemporary vein. The chefs may craft rye cheeks à la meunière, flanking them with a buttermilk puree for a tangy fresh note, fresh fennel and a subtle buttery sauce. Big-boned flavours packed in varying nuances. A safe bet every time for a slap-up meal in Ostend.

Name: Bistro Ocho
Description: The hustle and bustle of Calle Ocho quickly fades once inside this beautiful space that glows a gorgeous amber and features colorful floors, a dramatic ceiling and modern light fixtures. A finely stocked bar anchors the dining room, where guests enjoy contemporary Mexican cuisine prepared with the occasional Floridian spin. Think house-made brioche topped with king crab salad and finished with ikura. The classics are carefully handled here too: Lamb barbacoa tossed in a three-chili salsa arrives with house-made corn tortillas, while warm chalupas feature fiery salsa verde. A doughnut filled with vanilla cream, rolled in sugar and topped with shaved black truffles makes for a delightful, sweet finale.

Name: Bistro Pinot
Description: Are you in Friesland and dreaming of a getaway to Paris? Then make your way through the lovely streets of Grou to this delightful bistro. The nostalgic wall tiles, the marble counter and wooden stools, the French music pouring out of the speakers… This place has real character! Bistro classics are prepared in time-honoured tradition here: succulent foie gras on brioche, zesty canard à l'orange, a crispy and wonderfully fresh macaroon tart. The surprise menu transports you to those iconic bistros of the Parisian Left Bank.

Name: Bistro R
Description: Roland Debuyst is inspired by top-quality Belgian produce, but also by his globetrotting background. He focuses on bistro fare with a hint of modernity. Gyosa and ceviche are naturally combined with a dish of game, such as wild boar. This seasoned chef cannot be faulted when it comes to intelligently marrying flavours. The contemporary interior adorned with handsome works of art adds the final flourish to this enticing portrait.

Name: Bistro Refter
Description: Roelfien Steen and Cor Klevering's cosy bistro is a firm favourite. Don't expect creative excesses here, just authentic classic fare cooked up by an experienced chef; he draws much of his inspiration from French cuisine but also likes to express his love for Mediterranean flavours. This is the kind of place where you can feast on an intense bouillabaisse and a choice cut of meat with a bearnaise sauce prepared in time-honoured tradition.

Name: Bistro Rombaux
Description: Pieter-Jan Rombaux and his wife, Tineke, do everything themselves and the focus is clearly home-made. She nurtures the cheerful, unstuffy vibe, while he rustles up dishes that seek to enhance the ingredient’s pure flavours with perfect seasonings. Take a seat on the secluded terrace to admire the chef at work in the kitchen. Rather than gimmicky surprises, you can look forward to heart-warming dishes such as foie gras with brioche or hanger steak with a red-wine sauce to die for.

Name: Bistro S
Description: S like secret, savoury, sapid or Spinoza, not the philosopher but the owner who lovingly watches over this discreet Parisian establishment, and who is also a numismatist specialising in antique Greek coins and a genuine wine connoisseur. The talented Japanese chef Shimpei Oié crafts a fresh, healthy, balanced set menu backed up by his flawless culinary technique. Don’t miss the gilthead seabream: expertly fire-roasted and accompanied by white grapes and a kiwi juice. S like Super!

Name: Bistro SEENSUCHT
Description: The fantastic lakeside location – right by Wörthersee – means the terrace is a popular spot in summer, but sitting inside is also pleasant: the atmosphere is chic and nicely laid-back, and the tables by the windows boast a wonderful view of the lake. Attentive, seasoned staff serve up the delicious seasonal cuisine incorporating many regional ingredients. Be sure to try the handmade cheese and meat noodles. The fish of the day is also highly recommended. And for dessert, perhaps some apricot dumplings? The restaurant is located in the aenea hotel.

Name: Bistro Saint-Jean
Address: 132 boulevard de la Rochelle, Bar-le-Duc, 55000, France
Description: This ex-grocer’s shop is now a contemporary bistro, rich in flavour and colour, that hits the spot every time. The owner, son of a pastry chef, rustles up market-fresh cuisine in tune with the seasons, like this slow-cooked pork belly with baby onions and braising juices. Respect for the ingredients is the motto. Efficient, unobtrusive staff.

Name: Bistro Sophie
Description: Don't let the name fool you; this is an upscale restaurant with a stylish interior that features vintage decor and natural materials. Working in an open kitchen, Dejan Gavric is clearly keeping up with the times. He is a chef who likes to incorporate Mediterranean influences and techniques. This is evident in the dish comprising pan-fried sea bass fillet with mussels and sea lavender and featuring a variety of garnishes. The wine list, while not too extensive, is international, well curated and great value for money.

Name: Bistro Strong (Chaoyanggongyuan Road)
Address: M175, SOLANA, 6 Chaoyanggongyuan Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
Description: This bistro serves a small menu of Inner Mongolian beef and lamb cuts aged in-house. The lamb is prepared in myriad ways: mini lamb pie is made with porcini, truffle oil and parmesan in a vol-au-vent; the lamb skewer alternates dry-aged hind leg meat with fat. Made to order, the Hohhot lamb shaomai seduces with its meaty flavours and interesting textures. The signature cocktails that call for air-dried lamb or lamb ricotta are also ingenious!

Name: Bistro T-bone
Description: Everything revolves around the charcoal grill in this atmospheric establishment pleasantly situated in a quintessential old Dutch building. Whether he's barbecuing T-bone steak, a rack of lamb or sole, the chef bends the flames to his will with a sure touch. The results are dishes that are generous and brimming with typically robust flavours and character. The jovial owner will be happy to guide you through the menu, which also includes classics such as snails and onion soup – there are plenty of mouth-watering options.

Name: Bistro Toost
Description: Toost is a welcoming and vibrant bistro – the dried leaves hanging from the ceiling lend the setting a distinctively Mediterranean feel. Opting for a seat at the long bar is always a good idea. Diners order à la carte, choosing from a variety of typical dishes in smaller portions. Crab remoulade with crispy toast, crunchy vegetables and a mustard vinaigrette, or hand-cut steak tartare seasoned with capers and served with fresh chips and mayonnaise – these familiar dishes, with the occasional Asian twist, are the secret to the success of this charming bistro. Don't forget to make a reservation!

Name: Bistro Tribunal "Chez Yf"
Description: Have you ever heard of a meat sommelier? Well, in this traditional bistro, one such will help you make your choice among the fine cuts of meat supplied by the prestigious Rondou butchers. A refrigerated meat display counter and a lobster tank catch the eye. Rather than prissy, complex preparations, you can expect spot-on cooking, freshly prepared sauces and regular refills of hot, crunchy French fries. The wine list (splendid selection of Bordeaux wines) is at bargain prices.

Name: Bistro Villa Merton
Address: Am Leonhardsbrunn 12, Frankfurt on the Main, 60487, Germany
Description: Located just outside Frankfurt, north of the Palmengarten, Bistro Villa Merton is a lovely alternative to the fine dining restaurant. While the latter welcomes diners in the evening, the bistro is only open at lunchtime. In the spruce villa built in neo-Baroque style, you can take a seat in an inviting decor done out with an elegant touch to enjoy high-quality regional and international cuisine infused with seasonal influences. An appealing lunchtime set menu is on offer, as well as several à la carte options. The appetising dishes include breast and leg of guinea fowl and classics such as Wiener schnitzel made with veal. Excellent wine recommendations are to be had from the friendly and knowledgeable front-of-house team. Tip: There is a fantastic selection of champagnes. The terrace is also a pleasant place to sit. Good to know: Regular events are also held here.

Name: Bistro YEBISU
Description: The key to happiness here is the blackboard menu. Sea urchin with new onions, whitebait quiche, veal cutlets and other offerings are chalked simply on the board. The chef is a fount of knowledge; ask about the fare and conversation flows, heightening anticipation of the meal to come. The bistro is run by a couple whose concept is a restaurant that makes people happy. Spend a warm and comfortable time in this casual scene.

Name: Bistro de Holterberg
Description: Experience the charms of each season in this cosy bistro, whether it's winter by the large open fireplace or summer on the stunning terrace, offering an awe-inspiring vista of the Salland Ridge National Park. The extensive set menu features authentic French dishes that each showcase one or two bold flavours. Crispy fried sea bass fillet, langoustine sauce and boiled fresh vegetables: unadulterated flavours at their best.

Name: Bistro de Montcaud
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Château de Montcaud's chic bistro serves wholehearted cuisine with Mediterranean overtones as chef Mathieu Hervé shines the spotlight on local, often organic ingredients: Gubernat duck pâté en croûte and foie gras, mustard espuma; tataki of tuna and basil-laced humus; breast of Blaches guinea fowl, spelt risotto, green peas and St George’s mushrooms. A blissful shaded terrace overlooking the grounds, a warm welcome and cordial service add the final touches to this hospitable portrait.

Name: Bistro oma & enkel
Description: oma & enkel ("grandma & grandchild") is the culinary concept at this bistro in the long-established Posthotel. The name symbolises a bridging of the gap between the generations, from the traditional to the modern. Recipes of yesteryear are brought up to date and classics of Franconian cuisine are given a contemporary twist. In a pleasingly laid-back atmosphere, choose between "Franconian tapas", the "Signature Menu" or the "Duck Menu". Don't miss out on the Franconian bouillabaisse or the apricot dumplings.

Name: Bistro Štorja
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: The central location, in the small town that is home to some of the largest caves in Europe, makes this venue ideal both for a business lunch, aided by a well-priced menu of the day, and for a more leisurely visit. The kitchen offers dishes of regional inspiration reinterpreted with a modern touch, such as marinated trout served with wild asparagus, strawberry coulis and horseradish, or succulent oxtail with seasonal vegetables. The intimate interior dining room is complemented by a pleasant outdoor space, particularly agreeable in fine weather. The wine list is also worthy of attention, surprising in its breadth and depth: particularly notable is the vertical of Marjan Simčič’s Rebula Opoka.

Name: Bistro' 50
Address: 50 avenue de la Plage, Gujan-Mestras, 33470, France
Description: Just 100m from the beach and the port of La Hume, this modern, attractively done out bistro is the ideal place to share a handful of starters with friends or family, or to indulge in classic dishes given a lovely twist by chef Nicolas Vallois: poultry, duck and prune pâté en croûte; egg verjuice mayo, celeriac, baby gem and Granny Smith remoulade, salted egg yolks; pork confit cromesquis etc. The cellar features a good selection of organic and natural wines, as well as a fine selection of wines by the glass. When the weather permits, plump for a table on the large, pleasant, shaded wooden terrace and settle in for a relaxed meal.

Name: Bistronome
Description: In this chic bistro, chef Hospital imparts a daily lesson in bistronomy, giving popular dishes and flavours a gourmet spin. The food is as exquisite to behold as it is to taste. Throw in the occasional creative twist and a liberal sprinkling of generosity and the scene is set. In addition to dishes that have been revamped with seasonings from around the globe, the menu also features classics such as meatballs in tomato sauce or rib steak with a silky bearnaise sauce and hand-cut fresh fries. Making your choice from the set and à la carte lineups is always a challenge!

Name: Bistronoom
Description: Bistronoom is an elegant Normandy-inspired villa in the heart of the Flemish Ardennes. The appetising repertory draws on the best of French and Flemish traditions. The menu is deliciously familiar, the flavours are wholehearted and recognisable and the produce is seasonal. Examples include crispy sweetbread in a creamy cognac sauce with chives and fresh fries, unless you wouldn’t prefer a sole meunière or a gutsy osso bucco that explodes with flavour. The extensive menu is just one of the reasons that Bistronoom has earned itself such a loyal crowd of regulars.

Name: Bistronómika
Description: Part of the Bulbiza (Bulevar de Ibiza) gastronomic project, Bistronómika offers a traditional “No Carta” menu featuring touches of contemporary detail. The specialities here are the top-quality fish and seafood (the catch is displayed here every day to whet our appetite) cooked with minimum intervention, mainly on the open grill. Make sure you try the Gilda kebab-style appetiser, prepared with red tuna from the Mediterranean.

Name: Bistrot
Description: Overlooking a delightful, quiet little square, this romantic, welcoming restaurant serves traditional local specialities, often with an individual flavour. The menu includes some fish dishes, although the house speciality is the maltagliati pasta served with ‘Bistrot’ sauce.

Name: Bistrot 1936 - Domaine du Limonay
Description: The latest addition to the Maison Tirel-Guérin stable (established back in 1936) is this bistro firmly rooted in the current century, with its lovely choice of materials (light-coloured wood and exposed beams) and its bay windows that invite the light to flood in. The menu, overseen by the chef of the fine dining restaurant, features mouthwatering top-quality ingredients, such as poularde, foie gras and spider crab. The delicious farm-reared pork – grilled belly and a wafer-thin slice of andouille – was a particular hit with its delicious Roscoff onion jus.

Name: Bistrot 64
Description: The classic-style dining room in this restaurant situated in the Flaminio district belies the gourmet discoveries that await here, with echoes of traditions from Lazio that act as inspiration for creative, top-quality dishes with the occasional Asian twist.

Name: Bistrot André
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The Pic family’s André bistro unveils a dialogue between tradition and modernity depicted by a spot-on score and bolstered by a truly outstanding wine cellar, courtesy of the gastronomic parent establishment, and high-flying sakes. The family’s heritage is celebrated with Jacques's mosaic of red mullet and foie gras and his orange-laced iced soufflé. Local trout gravlax is dotted with veggie and spicy touches, half-way between a vibrant tribute and fresh new start.

Name: Bistrot August
Description: A stone's throw from rue Gabriel Péri, two young chefs have transformed an old wine cellar into an intimate bistro. Trained with the Ducasse group, Léopold Gillen is to be found in the kitchen, while Maxime Renvaze provides cordial and attentive service, as well as recommendations from a wine cellar composed of some 100 carefully selected labels. This seasonal, technical and flavourful cuisine features perfectly balanced seasoning and carefully crafted details: pâté en croûte with foie gras, pork, duck and venison; hay-smoked duck, squash and juniper juice. Great-value lunch set menu and short evening menu.

Name: Bistrot Coco
Description: Set in Strasbourg's old town, this contemporary restaurant with industrial-style decor is run by Constant Meyer, a young chef who earned his stripes at Le Crocodile and Le Relais de la Poste in La Wantzenau. He cooks up refined contemporary cuisine in a multi-course "carte-blanche" format (omnivore or vegetarian). Expect bold flavours and a friendly atmosphere.

Name: Bistrot Constant
Description: This spruce lock gatehouse, on the banks of a side canal of the Garonne River, is home to a bistro run by a meticulous chef. In a refurbished interior, Christophe Marque continues to champion wholesome bistro cuisine, courtesy of time-honoured classics faultlessly executed in keeping with culinary tradition – Bon appétit!

Name: Bistrot Cul Sec
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: This tiny bistro on the Place du Palais is run by a chef-sommelier duo with experience in MICHELIN-starred establishments. The concise, regularly updated menu features clean, unpretentious combinations that hit the mark: grilled green asparagus, pistachio foam and praline; pork loin, peppercorn jus, potato foam, roasted turnips; a baba drenched in macerated rum, vanilla chantilly. With a blend of bistro and industrial style, the decor fosters a convivial atmosphere; the long, narrow dining room with an open kitchen leads out onto a terrace that gives onto the square. Some real gems for all budgets are stocked in the extensive wine cellar.

Name: Bistrot Donatella
Description: This restaurant in a small village dominated by a bell tower boasts a charming inner courtyard which provides a romantic setting for a meal in fine weather. The Piedmontese cuisine served here is prepared using top-quality ingredients. A friendly welcome completes the picture, making this an enjoyable dining experience.

Name: Bistrot Francis
Description: When you name your bistro after your dog, it immediately wins people over! Here in the heart of the village, Antoine James and Sarah Mottay welcome diners into a space that exudes character, with terracotta-tiled floors, stone walls and a beamed ceiling. The chef rustles up enticing cuisine centred on local produce, with a Mediterranean lilt, but also other influences from around the world, for example Latin American: tiradito of yellowtail with lime and ginger, perfectly paired with a yellow pepper coulis. Laid-back service, welcoming little terrace.

Name: Bistrot Gros
Address: 18 rue de la Source, Nancy, 54000, France
Description: A youthful globetrotting chef runs this down-to-earth, laidback bistro in a cobbled street near St Epvre Basilica in the historic town. The bistro fare keeps step with the seasons and market availability, rolling out generous, appetising dishes, depicted by fried artichokes, frothy cantal cheese and confit egg yolk, or a fillet of trout with potato rosti, chermoula of cauliflower and an emulsion of Granny Smith apples. Natural wines dominate the wine list.

Name: Bistrot Ha
Address: 137 Eldridge St., New York, NY, 10002, USA
Description: Busy, cramped, and bursting with personality, this Vietnamese-inspired bistro from Chefs Sadie Mae Burns and Anthony Ha is the place to be. Getting in requires planning: Arrive before doors open to join the waitlist. Such is the reality of this rambunctious hotspot where Vietnamese and French ideas swirl about on a single plate. Think leeks vinaigrette with marinated mussels, fried whiting with tamarind powder, or a dazzling, celebratory, vol-au-vent loaded with pristine seafood flecked with fiery chilis. There’s plenty to drink too: A surprisingly lengthy list of natural wines tempts, but have you ever tried a fish sauce martini or a shiso margarita bolstered with lemongrass liqueur? There’s a first time for everything.

Name: Bistrot Instinct
Description: This pocket handkerchief contemporary bistro is in the hands of chef Maximilian Wollek and his enthusiastic youthful team. A market-fresh culinary score and updated classics with bistronomic overtones. Everything is homemade, even the cordials used in the unusual cocktails.

Name: Bistrot L'îlot
Description: A Parisian vibe mixed with industrial and minimalist details sets the welcoming scene. “What you see is what you get” is their motto! The chef intertwines international inspirations and punchy flavours as he orchestrates a mouth-watering score. He gives flawlessly steamed halibut a playful edge by flanking it with a range of mushroom textures and an expressive buttermilk crème. Rather than fussy frills, you can expect dishes in the zeitgeist and a splendid selection of (mainly French) wines.

Name: Bistrot La Perla
Address: Strada Col Alt 105, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Interesting wine list
Description: The venue unfolds around a large wooden bar, where the bartenders are constantly at work making excellent cocktails that complement an impressive wine list. We are in the bistro of the famous La Perla hotel: a tribute to mountain life, expressed through charming and cheerful décor that creates a lively and welcoming atmosphere. The menu invites you to indulge in mouth-watering dishes inspired by the classic flavours of Italian tradition, while live music plays in the background.The venue is open practically all day: a café in the morning, a bistro at lunchtime, a more informal menu from 2 pm to 4 pm, and then it’s time for aperitifs, with cocktails and snacks, before moving on to dinner.

Name: Bistrot Loiseau du Morvan
Address: Hostellerie de la Tour d’Auxois, 5 avenue Bernard-Loiseau, Saulieu, 21210, France
Description: Opposite the Loiseau family’s legendary Côte d’Or restaurant, this handsome 17C edifice is both a supremely comfortable traditional hostelry and a bistro, offering an appetising more casual alternative to its fine dining parent establishment. Here, local and regional recipes take pride of place, such as eggs in a red wine sauce or chicken à la Gaston Gérard. The rotunda dining room, which leads onto a terrace, is the epitome of country chic with old terracotta tiled flooring and a glorious timber ceiling, all of which in an unabashed, full-on Burgundy style.

Name: Bistrot Marloe
Description: In this upscale neighbourhood on a street corner, Marloe sports a stylish, buzzy bistro vibe: parquet floors, wainscoting, mirrors, green bench seating and a red Berkel meat slicer in the centre, ready to prepare aperitif boards. Deft and fresh depicts the menu: carpaccio of seabream with summer fruits or cod with Mediterranean accents. The "black truffle" menu (in season) is a must. On-the-ball, cheerful service.

Name: Bistrot Miraux
Description: Located on the edge of the Old Town, this charming little bistro is decorated with vintage French posters and photographs of famous actors. It’s a resolutely classic setting for an unashamedly traditional and proudly French restaurant, where the menu offers the likes of frog’s legs, duck confit, cordon bleu and crêpes Suzette to finish. This hearty cooking combines perfectly with friendly service to create a warm and comforting experience.

Name: Bistrot Paul Bert
Description: A bona fide Parisian institution for over 30 years, this bustling, vintage bistro serves honest, wholesome nosh to locals and tourists alike seated elbow-to-elbow at tightly packed tables. Examples include their legendary melt-in-the-mouth fillet steak whose pepper sauce more than lives up to its reputation. Slick, seamless service and a sensibly priced set lunchtime menu add the final flourishes to this local landmark that has been going strong for over three decades.

Name: Bistrot Racines
Description: Eugène Viollet-le-Duc found Chartres's Gothic cathedral to be the most beautiful in France. The owner of Le Grand Monarque Hotel had the inspired idea of opening this friendly bistro and wine bar with a terrace overlooking the imposing edifice. Locals, pilgrims and tourists dig into good traditional fare that showcases local farmers and market gardeners: pâté en croûte; veal belly, coffee reduction and fluffy dauphine potatoes; floating island served with a ladle, a French childhood classic. Savvy choice of wines from small-scale winegrowers.

Name: Bistrot Royal
Description: Inside the refined Grand Hotel Royal e Golf, the Bistrot offers the opportunity to savor the delicious flavors of Valle d’Aosta in a refined and lighter interpretation. In recipes where the quality of the raw ingredients takes center stage, you’ll be pampered by excellent service while comfortably seated in spaces that interpret Alpine style with personal touches.

Name: Bistrot Saint-Jean
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This bistro shares its grounds and chef, Olivier Valade, with Château Saint Jean’s other restaurant. The single set menu is the quintessence of creative bistro nosh: fillet of smoked mackerel, seaweed dressing and crunchy onion rings; tartare of veal, roast figs, red onion pickles, a crisp wafer-thin biscuit and shavings of smoked meat. The kitchen overlooks a long dining room and terrace.

Name: Bistrot Vérité
Address: 7 Liverpool Road, Birkdale, Southport, PR8 4AR, United Kingdom
Description: A friendly, bustling neighbourhood bistro, serving gutsy French dishes with a classic base, punchy flavours and the occasional international touch. It’s a family affair with Mum Michaela, Dad Marc and their sons all involved, either in the kitchen or front of house. Pop into their next-door bar, Petite Vérité, for pre or post-dinner drinks.

Name: Bistrot at Wild Honey
Address: Sofitel Hotel, 8 Pall Mall, St James’s, London, SW1Y 5NG, United Kingdom
Description: Occupying the ground floor of a Grade II listed former banking hall inside the Sofitel hotel, this restaurant aims to provide a more relaxed and keenly priced alternative to the adjoining Wild Honey St James. The team are undoubtedly succeeding in their mission, with lashings of flavour packed into every deceptively simple dish. Sit at the counter or in one of the dramatically red banquettes, which add to the French bistro feel. The menu incorporates a fair few Mediterranean influences alongside the Gallic staples, and the ‘prix fixe’ is an absolute steal.

Name: Bistrot de Paris
Description: This romantic, welcoming spot, hidden at the end of the corridor of the charming Villa San Pietro on Rua Augusta, gives you the delicious feeling of stepping into an authentic Parisian bistro. Led by renowned French chef Alain Poletto, the restaurant serves classic French cuisine based on traditional recipes and top-quality ingredients. Among the tempting starters are Charcuterias dos Alpes Caseiras, house-made Alpine charcuterie, Foie Gras and Patê de Campagne, all prepared in-house. The main course, Beef Wellington carved at the table, served with a fine golden crust, perfectly cooked meat and an irresistible Port-wine reduction with truffles, and the dessert, Riz au Lait with sea-salt caramel and caramelised cashews, deliver that Paris-in-São-Paulo moment. The drinks available to accompany the meal only enrich the experience further!

Name: Bistrot de Venise
Address: Calle dei Fabbri 4685, Sestiere San Marco, Venice, 30124, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: In the heart of the city, just a few steps from St. Mark's Square and Rialto, the fine restaurant Bistrot de Venise will surprise you with Venetian cuisine that combines tradition and innovation. Both past and current dishes are reinterpreted with a contemporary twist, offering a unique dining experience. Wine lovers will be delighted by the selection of Italian rarities, perfect to accompany each course.

Name: Bistrot de Yountville
Description: Bistrot de Yountville brings classic French-bistro charm to the city, evoking the warmth of the French countryside. The cuisine reflects the chef duo's dedication to the fundamentals of French cooking, infused with meticulous care and unwavering effort. The restaurant’s name pays homage to Yountville, the home of The French Laundry in California, where the chefs were inspired to recreate its unforgettable experiences for diners. The thoughtfully prepared dishes and cosy ambience here offer a delightful escape from the hustle and bustle of city life.

Name: Bistrot de la Place
Description: In the heart of the village where Chabrol filmed Le Boucher (1970). Old stonework, beams and tasty country cuisine including andouillette and confit de canard.

Name: Bistrot des Falaises
Address: Place de la Mairie, Saint-Romain, 21190, France
Description: In a picturesque wine-growing Côte de Beaune village, this countrified bistro is piloted by a talented chef. The enticing score, which delves freely and regularly into the bounteous local produce, is as inspired and modern in style as it is exciting: flame-seared confit trout, Brussel sprouts, unpasteurised cream and dill-laced oil; barbecued squid, glazed turnips, umeboshi ‘plums’ and beef-dashi stock… Bouncy, cheerful front-of-house team and a weakness for natural wines.

Name: Bistrot des Hauts de Loire
Description: In the outbuildings of the estate, a picturesque Sologne building with exposed timber beams and oak floorboards sets the scene. On the terrace, facing the kitchen garden, you can tuck into simple bistro dishes (matured meat, spit-roasts) or the chef’s more imaginative creations. Scrumptious!

Name: Bistrot du Boeuf Rouge
Description: This restaurant is well known in the local area for its simple yet gourmet Lyonnaise specialities: rosette sausage, hot saucisson, pike quenelles, etc. The Farina family's culinary skill is demonstrated on a daily basis, to a backdrop of attractive old-fashioned decor.

Name: Bistrot du Bord de l'Eau
Address: Hostellerie de Levernois, 15 rue du Golf, Levernois, 21200, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A delightful rustic dining room with exposed stonework, beams and a fireplace serves as the setting for the traditional cuisine and dishes fêting the terroir made with vegetables from the adjoining kitchen garden. Dishes such as snails in a mild garlic broth, grilled trout and lamb navarin can be enjoyed by the fireside or on the riverside terrace. Open every day of the week, this convivial and generous restaurant is a real favourite!

Name: Bistrot École
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Courgette stuffed with einkorn and fresh goat's cheese; confit of Sainte-Victoire pork belly, mashed potato: a masterclass in culinary natural history, courtesy of a wealth of local ingredients, served up in an old schoolhouse. Located in the heart of this hilltop winegrowing village, with a terrace protected by mulberry trees, this small bistro is the brainchild of Grégory Brousse, formerly chef at Le Mas de Peint, and Alima Louange, his partner. As well as offering a full set menu that won't break the bank, the restaurant is also on point with its selection of local ingredients and wines (to accompany your meal here or to take away).

Name: Bistrotel 't Amsterdammertje
Description: Brimming with character, this building by the Vecht River is enchanting, but just wait until you're sitting on the terrace… At Bistrotel, you can truly escape the hustle and bustle for a while! Before you retire to your comfortable guestroom, be sure to pop into the spacious bistro downstairs. André Gerrits has assembled a team here who know their way around bistro classics and flavours from all over the world. With options on the menu such as steak tartare, spicy rendang or farmhouse chicken from the spit; this is the kind of place where anything goes.

Name: Bistrónomo
Description: A simple bistro that defines its cooking as haute-cuisine from the “barrio”! Contemporary-style tapas and raciones featuring Asian fusions, vegetables, tripe etc, alongside a more seasonally inspired menu.

Name: Bistrô Severo
Address: Rua De Ricardo Severo 141, Porto, 4050-515, Portugal
Description: If you are seeking a small oasis of tranquillity in the city for a meal, there is an excellent option at Palacete Severo, a welcoming boutique hotel that houses both this restaurant and the gastronomic Éon. Taken together, it reflects chef Tiago Bonito’s more informal proposal, set in a pleasant interior courtyard with a panoramic glass roof, walls beautifully decorated with Portuguese tiles and a lovely fountain to one side. The proposal, which champions traditional cooking with dishes such as Amêijoas à “Bulhão Pato” (clams in a garlic-and-coriander sauce) or Paletilha de cordeiro de leite (suckling lamb shank), is complemented by an enticing executive lunch menu (you may choose between 2 or 3 courses).

Name: Bistrô by Vila Foz
Description: An informal venture from the prestigious Vila Foz, in collaboration with the renowned chef Arnaldo Azevedo. Located in the Matosinhos Municipal Market, the place exudes authenticity, with a counter facing the stoves and tables spread out on the terrace, in the midst of the market hustle and bustle. The idea here is to offer simple, honest cooking, where the raw ingredients take centre stage and preparation involves minimal intervention to preserve the quality and freshness of the produce that arrives straight from the wholesale fish market. Diners can choose to buy fish or seafood at the market stalls and bring it to be prepared in the restaurant (chargrilled, fried, grilled, etc.), or select from the menu options. An interesting detail? The chef used to come here as a child to buy fish with his father for the family restaurant.

Name: Bistrôt Le Ciel
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Terrace
Description: The sky is visible through the glazed roof and tropical plants and contemporary artwork set the singular scene indoors, while the terrace is taken by storm in fine weather. The food features a pageant of polished French fare with the occasional Italian twist, illustrated by terrine of foie gras or venison in a Grand Veneur sauce. Consummate craftsmanship and a reverent respect for culinary tradition.

Name: Bistrôt Le Nord
Description: Combining rustic charm and contemporary comfort, this authentic 1885 farmhouse provides the perfect backdrop for experiencing Grégory Nicole's refined cooking. The way he pays tribute to his homeland of France, including a fondness for cheeses from the north of the country, demonstrates real culinary know-how. Original flourishes bring excitement to the cooking without unnecessary frills . The crunchy tuna pizza with vibrant wasabi cream, a homage to the chef's mentor Joop Braakhekke, is one of the restaurant's signature dishes. At the same time, he can delight diners with a generous vol-au-vent combining crispy veal sweetbreads, delicate smoked eel and a mushroom cream. Choosing from the menu is no easy task; the lunch menu is equally deserving of attention.

Name: Bite N Eat Dindigul Biriyani
Description: Since 2014, this shop has been serving authentic Indian fare from all over the country. Its namesake signature biriyani is a must-try - pair with kongu nadu kozhi fry, or spicy dry-fried chicken with grated coconut, a Southern Indian speciality rich in tangy flavours. Also check the blackboard at the door for daily specials. Round off with house-made sweets or masala tea. Certain items are only served after 4 pm.

Name: Bites
Description: The cuisine at this tiny, simply furnished restaurant includes barbecued dishes and fermented ingredients, all of which feature on a tasting menu. Guests can also choose à la carte: the small portions (as the restaurant name suggests) make it possible to taste several dishes at a reasonable cost. Booking is essential in the evening and also advisable at lunchtime.

Name: Bitterroot
Address: 4463 Commons Dr. W., Destin, FL, 32541, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Credit cards not accepted
Description: It may be tucked away in an everyday shopping center in Destin, but this casual farm to table restaurant offers so much more than expected. Concrete floors, a wood-beamed ceiling and marble-topped tables lend a contemporary country appeal to this appealing space. It's the kind of place where you can pop in any time of day for a bevy of Southern-leaning casual, comforting dishes like the house-made, charred biscuit smothered in a bone marrow and black pepper gravy. Main dishes like Gulf shrimp and grits as well as sweet tea pork chop tempt at dinner, but no meal is quite complete without a wedge of house-made pecan pie sided by a scoop of brown butter ice cream.

Name: Bium
Description: Chef Dae-chun Kim's Bium showcases his deep understanding of Korean temple cuisine. Diners find a serene escape here, savouring calm, refined flavours away from the bustle of everyday life. Made with seasonal local vegetables, his dishes reflect the four Buddhist elements: earth, water, fire, and air. Chef Kim elevates Korean temple cuisine with premium produce, traditional jang, and refined techniques—offering wholesome, sophisticated flavours in every dish.

Name: Bizi Ona
Description: Chef Romain Lorenzon, whose good cheer is palpable right off the bat, chose to set up shop in this peaceful village. The premises have retained their authentic character thanks to their worn counter, exposed stonework and bistro-style conviviality. Armed with a long career in multi-MICHELIN-starred kitchens, not least Hôtel de Tourrel, he is now putting this experience to good use in a more free-spirited cuisine, uninhibited by convention and true to his beliefs: authenticity, simple pleasures and sharing. Hare à la royale, mallard duck pie with the glazed legs in a tarragon jus, palombe au capucin (wood pigeon flambéed with an Armagnac jus using a traditional cast-iron cone), Grand Marnier soufflé – his are comforting dishes to share with friends, especially seasonal game, a passion of the chef's.

Name: Bizie Lizie
Description: At Bizie Lizie you can choose from a modern brasserie dotted with vintage details or a swish, bordering on Baroque interior. However, those who find it difficult to make up their mind, may well find the amazing choice on the menu somewhat daunting! The menu that will find favour with lovers of nostalgic nosh features heart-warming brasserie fare, such as shrimp fritters, calf’s tongue in Madeira sauce or eels in sorrel.

Name: Black & Green
Address: 49 Hewell Road, Barnt Green, B45 8LT, United Kingdom
Description: A bijou neighbourhood restaurant with stools set at tall tables and a black and green colour scheme. The short, sensibly priced tasting menu moves with the seasons, using prime ingredients to deliver layers of texture and flavour in imaginative dishes. All guests are served at the same time and most go for the wine pairings. Add in the cheese course for a satisfying meal.

Name: Black Bass
Address: Black Bass Hotel, 921 route d'Albertville, à Sevrier, Annecy, 74320, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A smart trendy vibe, a hip interior design and a sweeping view of the lake set the scene for bistronomic dining. Fish from local farms play the lead role in a concise culinary score strewn with creative flair.

Name: Black Bear Inn
Address: Clytha Road, Bettws Newydd, NP15 1JN, United Kingdom
Description: There's a charmingly rustic feel to this smartly run rural inn close to the Victorian market town of Usk. A white-washed exterior, log-burning stove and wooden beams all add to the appeal, while the chefs do their part with a concise menu of well-executed, classically based cuisine. The fish cookery is a particular highlight, as evidenced by dishes like hake with a terrific butter sauce and capers. Everything is made in-house, including the ice creams and sorbets for dessert.

Name: Black Milk Gastro Bar
Description: This intimate restaurant offers great cooking and a fun night out, thanks to its moody lighting, pumping soundtrack and lively cocktail bar. Influenced by South America, Asia and Europe, the creative dishes deliver vibrant flavours and well-judged spicing, while using plenty of modern techniques. Expect to see some luxury ingredients, like Oscietra caviar and Périgord truffles, alongside an enjoyable dose of theatricality, with dishes ranging from courgette flower with cime di rapa, salsa verde and urfa pepper to homemade salted coconut and yuzu gelato topped with Oscietra.

Name: Black Radish
Address: The Coles Shop, 12 Watermill Way, Merton Abbey Mills, Merton, London, SW19 2RD, United Kingdom
Description: Situated in the Merton Abbey Mills development – which was once a 12th-century priory, then spent time as a mill and is now a thriving cultural quarter – Black Radish is an intimate, well-run restaurant with space for just 12 diners. A chef’s table for two is ideal if you want a ringside seat. The cosy atmosphere provides a backdrop for cooking that’s grounded in top-drawer ingredients – be that Orkney scallops with yuzu kosho, XO and finger lime or terrific Silver Hill duck with complementary quince and salsify.

Name: Black Radish
Address: 1304 N. Monroe St., Unit B, Tallahassee, FL, 32303, USA
Description: Located in the heart of Tallahassee, and part of the Seven Hills Hospitality Group, this contemporary styled space with an industrial chic feel focuses on seasonality and shared plates. It's first come, first serve at this popular spot where Chef/co-owner Matthew Swezey dishes up plates like creamy bubble potato spheres encased in a crispy shell, served with a house-made spicy mayo. Many of the pastas are made in house and are served in half portions should you want to sample several. Don't skip the scarpinocc, or clog-shaped pasta, filled with a flavorful sweet potato purée with parmesan and ricotta in a brown butter sage sauce. To finish, try the apple butter sundae with a swirl of miso caramel and candied pecan granola.

Name: Black Rooster Taqueria
Address: 1323 N. Mills Ave., Orlando, FL, 32803, USA
Description: This Mills area dining den is brought to you by husband and wife team, John and Juliana Calloway. The space is compact and industrial with a smattering of local artwork and refurbished furniture, including sleek tables crafted by the chef himself. Colorful booths and a striking black rooster painted on the wall put patrons in the mood for correspondingly vibrant and eclectic taqueria food.Farm to taco is their ethos, and every item packs a wallop of flavor peppered with creativity. A recent favorite included the slow-roasted pork achiote taco, crowned with pickled onion, cilantro and spicy habanero salsa. The smoked greens taco—with ricotta, shiitake mushrooms and crispy onions—has vegetarians coming in droves.

Name: Black Sheep
Description: The fine dining restaurant of Bergland hotel boasts a chic interior with a stylish dark colour scheme. The cuisine is entirely dedicated to the Alpine region. Ingredients are sourced within a 200km radius, with Austria and South Tyrol being the main suppliers. Much of the produce comes from the immediate vicinity, including herbs from the restaurant's own garden. They even raise their own sheep. The cooking style is very contemporary and incorporates subtle Japanese influences. For example, the six-course set menu includes dishes such as Alpine prawn katsuobushi with tomato and yuzu bisque, or Tyrolean catfish and broad beans.

Name: Black Smoke
Description: Black Smoke packs a distinctly American punch. The dimly lit, unpolished, rough and rugged interior is steeped in the smoky aroma of BBQ. The pitmasters have perfected the art of grilled meat in true Texan fashion. Traditional techniques, Latino influences and local produce for meals rich in big-boned, heart-warming flavours. Examples include lamb tacos jazzed up with a spicy za’atar, jalapeno pepper and fresh lemon. Or how about a cut of premium beef from the De Laet & Van Haver butcher’s shop? The drinks menu is practically as long as the food menu, while the ‘Bonanza Experience’ is billed as the ultimate sharing experience! So, let’s crank up the heat!

Name: Black-faced Spoonbill Canteen
Address: 17-18, Haipu, Shihfen Village, Cigu District, Tainan, 724, Taiwan
Description: A must for birdwatchers and seafood lovers, the restaurant is one of the best places to see endangered black-faced spoonbills in Taiwan. From September to May, these migratory birds fly here and feed on the fish in the restaurant owner's pond. Try the sustainably farmed milkfish and clams straight from his fish farm. To reduce food waste, the servers suggest the right portion for your party. Reservations are mandatory on holidays.

Name: BlackSalt
Description: It may be part market, but there’s nothing remotely pedestrian about BlackSalt. This lively restaurant’s menu manages to be both approachable and interesting, with sublime shellfish and a concise selection trawling coast to continent for inspiration. Begin with Addie’s mussels bathed in a well-balanced broth—you’ll be sopping up every last drop. Then move on to the ever-warming, saffron-tinged Provençal market stew bobbing with the day’s finest catch, which may include juicy mussels, tender shrimp and flaky swordfish, among others. Finish this aquatic feast with a slice of their tart key lime pie. Served with blueberry compote and freshly whipped cream along with a sesame seed tuille, it is a rich and delicious way to clinch the meal.

Name: Blackbelly Market & Restaurant
Address: 1606 Conestoga St., Ste. 1, Boulder, CO, 80301, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef/owner Hosea Rosenberg is a familiar name in these parts, and Blackbelly Market is just one of the reasons why. There are plenty of spots to sip and snack here, whether at the counter facing the open kitchen, the well-stocked bar area, or the polished, dark wood tables. Take a peek at the refrigerated, glassed-in butchery room, where you may see Head Butcher Kelly Kawachi holding court. You'll taste her handiwork across the menu, and in the charcuterie boards showcasing duck rillette, pork terrine, headcheese and saucisson. Koji-cured pork is supremely flavorful, while agnolotti made of caramelized onion dough in a fragrant mushroom "brodo" is an inventive twist. For the win, order the donuts, especially the chocolate hazelnut cream with hazelnut caramel and milk chocolate-hazelnut topping.

Name: Blackbird
Address: Nielson Tower, Ayala Triangle, Makati Avenue, Makati - Metro Manila, The Philippines
Description: Once Manila's first commercial airport, this striking site – formerly Nielson Tower – has taken flight again, this time as Blackbird, a sleek restaurant steeped in aviation lore. The chef presents a fittingly international menu, serving global classics from West to East. Off-menu dishes add intrigue: let the team guide you to Wagyu croquettes or spicy mussaman curry. A globe-trotting restaurant, where history and hospitality meet.

Name: Blackbird
Address: Hotel Californian, 36 State St., Santa Barbara, CA, 93101, USA
Description: Blackbird, tucked inside the waterfront Hotel Californian, is as polished as its surroundings. The dining room blends art deco and midcentury influences with an old-club atmosphere, while arched doors and a long bar keep the space feeling breezy and relaxed. Creative cocktails remain a focus, but the kitchen keeps one foot firmly planted in coastal California cooking. Seafood leads the menu with dishes like yellowtail crudo brightened with lilikoi aguachile, kiwi and cucumber, as well as Santa Barbara cioppino loaded with crab claws, mussels, clams, shrimp and local fish. Larger plates range from Chinese steamed fish with Dungeness crab hash and bok choy to seared day boat scallops paired with black garlic and delicata squash. Desserts maintain a seasonal bent, including pear and cardamom crème brûlée with rosé-poached pear and pomegranate sauce.

Name: Blackitch
Address: 27/1 Nimmanahaeminda Soi 7 Road, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
Description: This intimate 16-seat restaurant serves a seasonal tasting menu comprising over 10 courses made with ingredients from across Thailand. Some items such as soybean, are fermented or aged in-house by chef Phanuphol Bulsuwan, who was trained by his grandmother. The harmonious marriage of Nan black pig guanciale with pumpkin gnocchi, SyamIsBlue cheese and tomato-Sichuan pepper balsamic, is a highlight. Ask about the selection of house-fermented drinks.

Name: Blacklinen
Address: Level 9, The Millen, 55 Jalan Sultan Ahmad Shah, George Town, 10050, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: Supervised by chef Benny Yeoh, Blacklinen serves expertly chargrilled food in a design-forward luxury hotel. At the door, the dry-aging fridge, where the premium meat is displayed, greets diners. The menu features dry- and wet-aged beef cuts, lamb and duck breast, rub shoulders with seafood, chicken and other steakhouse favourites. If in doubt, ask the attentive staff for suggestions. Be sure to save room for the tiramisu!

Name: Blackthorn
Address: The Twelve Hotel, Bearna, H91 Y3KA, Ireland
Description: On the first floor of the personally run The Twelve Hotel, named after the nearby Twelve Bens mountain peaks, Blackthorn is a bright, airy spot with a Nordic influence. The dining room provides the ideal backdrop to a menu focused on grilling seasonal ingredients over charcoal, filling the air with wonderful smoky aromas. Whether it’s lamb with herb salsa, pheasant with cavolo nero or whole black sole with brown butter and capers, the ingredients are given a lick of fire in generous, carefully executed dishes.

Name: Blaise
Description: Housed in the historic Maternidade Filomena Matarazzo building, this restaurant draws its inspiration from Blaise Cendrars — the Franco-Swiss writer and passionate lover of Brazil. The interior evokes a cabin, reminiscent of the one in which the writer is said to have lived, decorated with volcanic crystal stones set amongst wood, in a rustic atmosphere warmed by the soft glow of lampshades that light the space. Here, chef Fernando Bouzan presents a French-inspired cuisine crafted exclusively from Brazilian ingredients, with a firm emphasis on seasonal produce and regional provenance. Our suggestion? The flavourful Fish Crudo served with cashew nuts, lírio do brejo — a native Brazilian marsh flower — and shiokara, a cured seafood condiment; the succulent Black Angus short rib with arracacha, mustard leaf and a natural jus; and, to finish, a Jabuticaba sorbet — made from the distinctive Brazilian berry that grows straight from the tree trunk — accompanied by a compote, jelly and pearls of the same fruit nestled in a delicate crème diplomate. The full offering is available either as a tasting menu called Experiência, or à la carte!

Name: Blanc
Address: Macalister Mansion, 228 Jalan Macalister, George Town, 10400, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: This fine dining restaurant in an 18C castle-turned heritage boutique hotel boasts graceful architecture and a stunning dining room done up in a colonial style with royal blue walls, white window shutters and a giant faux white tree in the centre. The 8-course tasting menu cannot be faulted and á la carte options are also plentiful. Each dish incorporates a variety of Asian ingredients and is intelligently devised and balanced. Make sure you save room for the desserts that are too good to miss!

Name: Blanco
Description: David and Celine describe Blanco as “highly Instagrammable” and the trendy interior definitely ticks all the boxes: fashionable, airy and buzzy! After a refreshing cocktail or a glass of natural wine, you will sample dishes of Mexican inspiration with a scattering of European touches. Tangy ceviche of gambero rosso with bloody oranges and leche de tigre, tacos stuffed with slowly cooked pork, pineapple and a pico de gallo sauce, or subtly spicy chipotle, ajo blanco (white gazpacho) and super fresh fish from the North Sea. A meal at Blanco is a genuine culinary adventure best shared… Unsurprisingly, it is already a hit with the locals!

Name: Blanco Osteria da Fabio
Description: Just steps from the waterfront, yet conveniently close to the city center, this venue captivates with its warm, welcoming atmosphere. The front-of-house is gracious and smiling, while the kitchen delivers a menu steeped in the sea and tradition: concise, yet brimming with authentic flavors. Our advice? Don’t miss the housemade fresh pasta: the scialatielli with shrimp and stracciatella is a celebration of indulgence, while the maccheroncini showcase simplicity elevated to excellence. Completing the experience, fragrant bread served with a light and rustic artisanal oil that speaks of authenticity.

Name: Blanqueries
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: This bright, modern and cosmopolitan restaurant is easy to find as it’s situated just 100m from the monumental Torres de Serranos, one of the historical gateways to the wonderful city of Valencia. Boasting its own distinctive character, the restaurant is run by two talented chefs who work together to create traditional cuisine with a more up-to-date feel. The philosophy here is clear – to offer reasonably priced, high-quality cuisine made from seasonal ingredients wherever possible. The restaurant focuses mainly on set menus, with cheaper options available at lunchtime and a higher-priced menu in the evening.

Name: Blas
Address: Twr y Felin Hotel, Ffordd Caerfai, St Davids, SA62 6QT, United Kingdom
Description: Originally built in 1806 as a working windmill, the Twr y Felin Hotel features contemporary artwork and is decorated in an understated, modern style. Its restaurant, Blas, is named after the Welsh word for 'taste’ and offers appealing menus which showcase seasonal Pembrokeshire produce from Solva crab and lobster to Welsh lamb rump in pared-back, modern dishes often cooked over the grill. On Sundays, expect a traditional roast dinner. The friendly team run the place with pride, enhancing the overall experience.

Name: Blaue Ente by Alex
Description: Historical industrial architecture outside and a trendy, lively atmosphere inside – the old machinery really draws the eye! The relaxed yet efficient front-of-house team contributes to a pleasingly casual vibe. Select ingredients are at the heart of the contemporary, seasonally inspired dishes. The menu features, for example, "fillet of smoked organic trout from the Glauser family, beetroot and shiitake mushroom tartare and horseradish" or "cordon bleu of Toggenburg veal with Graubünden mountain cheese, pommes alumettes and root spinach". A good selection of wines. The terrace is very popular. At lunchtime, there are also simpler, constantly changing daily specials.

Name: Blaue Quelle
Description: Behind the doors of this place that looks like something straight out of a picture book, dine in the pretty, wood-panelled space that oozes rustic charm – or on the gorgeous terrace. Gaby and Alexander Struth are the third generation to take the helm of this family business: she oversees the friendly service; he takes care of the cooking. The menu ranges from Austrian classics including Wiener schnitzel, Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) and Schlutzkrapfen (mezzelune pasta) to fresh pasta dishes and Asian specialities such as spicy Thai soup and Indian butter chicken. Then there is the freshly caught fish from nearby waters! You can also spend the night in one of their well-kept guestrooms.

Name: Blaue Traube
Description: Young yet already remarkably mature, Christoph Huber brings fresh energy to the Blue Grape (Blaue Traube), a historic establishment with roots reaching back to the seventeenth century. His is a contemporary cuisine that engages with South Tyrolean tradition without nostalgia, but with an informed and cultured perspective: rigorously selected local products, techniques such as fermentation to lend depth, and a precise vision that weaves together terroir and modern sensitivity. Hospitality is calibrated with, never excessive, care in perfect harmony with a setting that preserves the charm of history without forsaking present-day comfort. In the evening, the gastronomic experience unfolds through a shared tasting menu, conceived as a singular narrative. At lunch, the approach becomes more nimble and informal, while maintaining the same dedication to flavour and ingredient quality.

Name: Blauer Bock
Description: A cornerstone of the fine dining scene for years, this restaurant is housed in the spruce hotel of the same name, nestled in the centre of Munich – a stone's throw from the Viktualienmarkt and the city museum. The decor is tasteful, sleek and contemporary in style, with striking pictures adorning the walls. The cuisine is classic with a modern twist, and the menu includes mouthwatering options such as braised veal shoulder or sole for two. Outside, the tables overlooking the pedestrian area are in high demand.

Name: Bleue Bar Bistro
Description: Rather inconspicuously located on Grote Markt, there is a distinctly Parisian feel to this bistro with a predominantly green colour scheme. The long bar with ceramic tiles and open kitchen with green panelling make for an inviting setting. As you might expect, the menu features French bistro fare with the odd fresh twist – for instance, the chef incorporates kumquat into the rich duck jus that accompanies pan-fried duck breast and orange compote, without compromising the dish's signature flavours. The house-made pâté en croûte is certainly tempting. Full flavours guaranteed!

Name: Bleuet
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Time seems to have stopped still at Bleuet, which is confirmed by the view over the rolling hillsides of the Flemish Ardennes from the exquisite terrace and the cosy interior of this cosy cottage. Pieter-Jan is in the kitchen, while Yoran makes sure the dining room never gets too crowded to ensure optimum quality. Yoran can be relied upon to open a bottle of wine for you to taste, which is something of a rarity these days. The chef plays with familiar flavours and international accents, as his seabass fillets in a miso and champagne sauce with a risotto of wheat and crunchy veg demonstrates. Food that throbs with flavour and a felicitous feast of unexpected associations.

Name: Bloempot
Description: Tucked away in a red-brick courtyard of old Lille, Bloempot proudly flies the flag of locally sourced produce. In a former carpenter’s workshop, parquet floors, glass ceilings and dried flower arrangements set the quirky scene. Chefs Florent Ladeyn and Florence Grave sign a highly distinctive culinary score focused on regional ingredients and unusual combinations: trout and grilled apricots, pollock paired with velvety courgettes and a buckwheat and sunflower ganache with malt ice cream. Big-boned, yet polished food, spot-on yet casual service and excellent value-for-pleasure at lunchtime. No telephone, so reservations are made through the website or in person.

Name: Bloom
Description: Bloom is an apt name for a restaurant whose Mexican chef, Christian Ventura, crafts vegetarian sushi! Breaded crispy rice, delicately dressed in vinegar with finely diced shiitake, oyster mushroom and avocado, futomaki and pesto sauce or vegetable gyoza in a kimchi sauce. The chef, a staunch defender of our natural resources, has risen to the challenge thanks to a lineup of vibrant and succulent vegan dishes. The interior sports a wood vibe rich in textures.

Name: Bloom Garden
Address: Bloom House, 23 rue du Château-Landon, Paris, 75010, France
Description: This restaurant channels the spirit of the Mediterranean generously, from the hardwood floors covered with Berber rugs to the wicker hanging baskets and zellige-tiled walls. On sunny days, tables are set out on the pleasant patio by the pool. The chef cooks up sun-kissed dishes using carefully selected ingredients.

Name: Bloom in the Park
Description: Be sure to arrive early for an aperitif on the terrace of this charming lakeside lodge before heading through to the modern, minimalist restaurant. In an unusual twist, both the menu and the matching wine pairings are a complete surprise! You submit your allergies and dislikes in advance, with the components of the dishes only revealed at the end of the meal when you are given a QR code to scan. Combinations could include halibut with satsuma, endive and crab bisque or seared roe deer with pumpkin and forest mushrooms. This element of the unknown stimulates both the mind and the palate through your meal.

Name: Blossom
Address: 79 Upper St Giles Street, Norwich, NR2 1AB,, United Kingdom
Description: Launched by friends who used to work together at The Wildebeest in Stoke Holy Cross, this intimate restaurant in the heart of Norwich combines the cosiness of a neighbourhood spot with a more formal feel. Seasonal produce from local asparagus to Norfolk Black chicken leads the way and the fixed-price menu has an ambitious streak. At dinner, it moves from three courses to four, with the added ‘primo piatto’ showcasing the chef’s Italian roots through the likes of brown crab risotto or an open raviolo of lamb sweetbread. Friendly service completes the picture.

Name: Blossom Bistrot
Description: From its location on the banks of the Seine, this restaurant overlooks the limestone cliffs of Giverny and the passing barges. A welcoming atmosphere awaits you in a pleasant interior with polished concrete floors, whitewashed walls and vintage bistro furniture. Gabin Rodes, a young chef from Vernon who trained at Éric Guérin's La Mare aux Oiseaux, revisits bistro classics without compromising their character, a case in point being leeks in vinaigrette tweaked with coriander and black garlic. A strong commitment to using local produce means ingredients are sourced from within a 100km radius. The lunchtime menu is a simpler affair.

Name: Blu
Description: Overlooking the delightful Piazzetta del Popolo, this restaurant delights guests with its views of the lake and the Rocca d’Angera, which can be enjoyed from the bright, relaxing dining rooms as well as from the shaded outdoor terrace. Chef Roberta, the soul of the restaurant, describes herself as a “home-style cook” who creates authentic dishes that are unfussy and full of flavour. Her “dal fondale alla superficie” fried fish recipe (literally, “from the depths to the surface”) is a triumph of flavours and includes zander, whitefish, trout, alborella and seasonal vegetables. Front of house, Carlo is at hand to recommend wines and pairings with style and elegance.

Name: Bludorn
Description: Chef Aaron Bludorn and his wife Victoria are the minds behind this buzzy dining room fitted with cushy, royal blue booths, handsome wood chairs, and a gleaming open kitchen. There is something for everyone on this broad menu that pulls inspiration from all corners, swinging from seafood towers to cioppino with branzino, blue crab, and shrimp. Order the oysters, including some from Texas, and grab a counter seat to watch them being cooked. Bludorn follows the seasons closely, and his servers follow their guests even closer. Dinner must close with a sizeable baked Alaska, made with a range of sorbets and ice creams like pistachio, raspberry, and gianduja all covered in meringue and lit on fire. It is as entertaining as it is satisfying.

Name: Blue Duck Tavern
Address: Park Hyatt Hotel,1201 24th St. NW, Washington, DC, 20037, USA
Description: Set within the Park Hyatt hotel, this upscale American tavern boasts a sleek, urbane and dreamily sprawling interior, with soaring windows, walnut wood seating and highly coveted glass-enclosed booths. Whether dining in the plush room or expansive lounge, the gorgeous space and its well-to-do crowd are the epitome of casual sophistication. Similarly, the product-driven menu has an all-American sensibility, highlighting farms and purveyors. At the center of the open kitchen sits a behemoth wood-burning oven that turns out such classics as whole-roasted fish or the popular duck leg confit. Don't forget to peruse their dessert station and impressive tea list with nearly 30 teas of different levels, including the rare 1985 Emperor's Masterpiece.

Name: Blue Flamingo
Description: All aboard! Built entirely of wood, glass, steel and aluminium, this floating restaurant, akin to a 21C barge, stands at the edge of the Presqu'île André-Malraux. The bright, waterside space commands a view of the kitchen to the rear. The roof terrace has an appealing open-air guinguette vibe. As for the food, the chef rustles up modern cuisine packed with international flavours and bursting with colour and freshness.

Name: Blue Heaven
Address: 729 Thomas St., Key West, FL, 33040, USA
Description: Blue Heaven is a Key West classic. It's long been a fixture on the local scene, and it's always packed with a crowd who comes here for its reliable, all-day dining and lively atmosphere. Waiting for a table is par for the course but well worth it. The menu presents a blend of Caribbean flavors with a seafood focus. Come in the morning to enjoy their signature fluffy pecan pancakes studded with toasted nuts. Another breakfast favorite is the Key West shrimp benny, with poached eggs, sweet pink local shrimp and finished with a lime Hollandaise. Order what strikes your fancy but know that no visit to this standby is complete without a slice of their signature Key lime pie, topped with a towering baked meringue.

Name: Bluebells Restaurant
Address: London Road, Ascot, SL5 0PU, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: There’s a degree of opulence to this popular restaurant housed inside a whitewashed building. The striking dark green interior features glitzy rose gold panelling and distinctive tiling, ensuring the dining room feels a little bit special. Modern European dishes make use of effective, well-judged flavour combinations and there’s an assured level of technique in the cooking. Sit in the main room overlooking the fire pit or in the airy conservatory, while the smooth service team look after you with aplomb.

Name: Blum
Description: A magnificent location directly in a gazebo where you can count the waves breaking on the beach, but in case of bad weather, there’s also an equally intimate and elegant indoor dining room available. Pampered by attentive and exceptionally kind service, follow the chef’s creations along tasting journeys, including vegetarian options, or à la carte dishes from both land and sea, always served with great aesthetic taste, often built on local products crafted with contemporary and colorful sensibility. In short, enjoy the complete experience that two hours in this exclusive corner of Sicily will offer you!

Name: Blumé
Description: At Blumé, familiar ingredients are given an unexpected twist. For instance, Jerusalem artichoke is used to impart an earthy quality to a chocolate dessert; cardamom lends spicy depth to celeriac – unconventional ideas meet skilful preparation with exciting results. Head to this elegant restaurant on the edge of Groningen's city centre to discover the set menu for yourself!

Name: Bluu il Mare Dentro
Address: Piazza Luigi Guerritore 11, Nocera Inferiore, 84014, Italy
Description: The double “u” in this restaurant’s name is not a mistake but was added with the intention of evoking the flow and sound of water that can heard from afar. Here, chef Angelo Borghese demonstrates his passion for the sea through his delicious, precise and personalised recipes in which the highest quality fish takes centre stage. The escarole and anchovy pizza with colatura mayonnaise is excellent, as is the selection of raw and marinated fish dishes.

Name: Bo Home
Address: 183-1, Cingnian 1st Road, Lingya District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
Description: Now run by the third generation, Bo Home was opened in 1969 to feed nourishing comfort food to hungry workers away from home. The room is done out in warm wood overtones. The menu has expanded to include stir-fries and blanched side dishes. But ever since day one, the main event has been their signature braised pork rice. The sauce is slow-cooked for three hours to make the pork gelatinous. The sea bass soup pairs perfectly with the rice.

Name: Bo-tannique
Description: These attractive premises (with a contemporary interior and exposed Bordeaux stonework) are located on a charming cobbled pedestrian square. The fresh cuisine is full of contrasts and draws on influences from far and wide: grilled sardines with burnt miso and Lebanese-style tomato tabbouleh. The fine wine list features mostly organic and natural wines. Friendly service... A recipe for success!

Name: Boat aux Saveurs - La Table d'Annabelle
Description: This contemporary villa set away from the bustle of the town centre is run by a mother and daughter team. Foodies adore the lovingly prepared dishes fully in tune with the times. The chef makes a point of honour of sourcing ingredients from local producers and most of the veggies come from their own vegetable garden.

Name: Bob & Thoms
Description: Owner Oliver Körber, who treats diners to authentic Berlin-style hospitality, and chef Ruben Pahl cook up a pleasingly unaffected gastro concept as a two-man operation. Located in a quiet side street between the small Viktoria-Luise-Platz, laid out in 1899, and the department store KaDeWe, the restaurant delivers a five-course set menu, plus two dishes as an optional extra. Just a handful of components go into the fantastic, classically based dishes. Delicious examples include the flavoursome lobster soup with vanilla radish or the perfectly cooked saddle of venison with a robust venison jus and Brussels sprouts. The attractive interior is quite minimalist, with interesting photographs of Berlin and New York (taken by Oliver Körber's daughter) adding a decorative element. There are only a few spots up for grabs each evening, so be sure to book in good time! In summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous little terrace!

Name: Bob Bob Ricard City
Address: Level 3, 122 Leadenhall Street, City of London, London, EC3V 4AB, United Kingdom
Description: A younger yet bigger sibling to the iconic Soho original, this enthusiastically run brasserie with bling sits on the third floor of the financial district's 'Cheesegrater' building. Ostentatious in all the best ways, it's a room dressed to impress with a menu ideal for splashing out and celebrating. An assortment of caviar and oysters sets the tone, before a wide choice of classically luxurious dishes from chicken and champagne pie to a range of steaks cooked on the Josper grill. And don't worry, just like the original, there's a 'Press for Champagne' button here too.

Name: Bob Bob Ricard Soho
Address: 1-3 Upper James Street, Soho, London, W1F 9DF, United Kingdom
Description: Any restaurant known for its tableside 'Press for Champagne' buttons is bound to exude a certain glamorous exclusivity. So it is with Bob Bob Ricard, a compact yet nevertheless grand restaurant that's classic to its core and all the more appealing for it; this is the place to come if you're looking to impress a date in the old-school manner. The menu opens with vodka shots at -18° along with a choice of caviars – a clue as to the owner’s nationality – then moves on to a roll-call of well-loved dishes from sole meunière to beef Wellington to share.

Name: Boban
Description: In the heart of the historic center, this locale features a small outdoor area overlooking a charming pedestrian walkway – highly coveted, so advance reservations are advised. A true city “must,” renowned and frequented for its excellent Mediterranean cuisine with Italian influences, offering both meat and fish dishes. Inside, a convivial atmosphere prevails, complemented by elegant furnishings and beautiful vaulted ceilings. A carefully curated cocktail selection, ideal for pairing with courses, completes the experience.

Name: Bocca di Bacco
Description: On the outside, a smart historical façade, on the inside an attractively modern and elegant restaurant complete with bar and lounge. Visible through its glass panes, the kitchen turns out Italian cooking. Needless to say, the pasta is home-made. To be paired with one of their great Tuscan wines.

Name: Bocca di Lupo
Address: 12 Archer Street, Soho, London, WID 7BB, United Kingdom
Description: Longevity in this part of town is a mighty achievement, but it's easy to see why Bocca di Lupo has remained popular for so long. Besides the switched-on service and buzzing atmosphere, the cooking itself provides the classic Italian techniques that everyone loves. The extensive menu takes you on a journey around Italy, with the region of origin listed beside each dish; share some fritti Romani while you make your decision. The marble counter is the place to sit and, for the sweet-toothed, the team also run an ice cream shop, Gelupo, across the road.

Name: BoccaLupo
Address: 753 Edgewood Ave. NE, Atlanta, GA, 30307, USA
Description: What's not to love about a place that doesn't take itself too seriously yet cares deeply about their food? Chef/owner Bruce Logue is at the helm of this endearing and casual spot where smart cooking and modern takes on Italian-American classics lure a steady stream of regulars. It's comfort food at its best (think Southern fried chicken parm with pasta and creamy collards). Order a la carte or tuck in to a four-course tasting menu, with pasta tagging along on the savory courses. Adam's focaccia is worth the ask, brushed with honey and served with house made butter and a top notch balsamic. For those who like a bit of spice, try their signature black squid ink spaghetti with hot Calabrese sausage, rock shrimp and scallions. Quirky cocktails, such as the handshake cordial are conversation starters.

Name: Boccaccio 70
Description: This eatery, in the premises occupied in its early days by the La Fábrica restaurant, brings a new dining concept to our palates via award-winning chef Ricardo Temiño, who combines Italian cooking with the essence of Castilian cuisine. In its attractive dining room, featuring a striking look dominated by tones of red, choose between the à la carte and two menus (Fellini and Sophia Loren). Dishes appearing on these include artichoke with “anticarbonara” and smoked eel; cod with a pilpil sauce; and caramelised panettone “torrija”.

Name: Boccadoro
Description: Situated on the outskirts of Padova, this classically elegant restaurant is very popular with locals – and for good reason! The menu includes skilfully prepared dishes influenced by the traditions of the Veneto (from bigoli pasta to dried cod and liver Venetian-style) as well as a selection of grilled options.

Name: Boccafine
Address: Place de la Fontaine et des Platanes, Nonza, 20217, France
Description: A small, listed village on the Cap Corse road is home to this demure restaurant, hidden by a curtain of Virginia Creeper and tall plane trees. The chef unveils his know-how as he crafts painstakingly sourced, local and seasonal ingredients, illustrated by ultra-fresh croaker, pancetta and pork jus in a surf and turf recipe of wondrous harmony. Love at first bite.

Name: Boccatti
Description: A family-run restaurant that has been keeping its customers happy since 1978! Maritime-inspired cuisine that is particularly renowned for its wild-caught fish and seafood. Booking recommended.

Name: Boccon DiVino
Address: Via Traversa dei Monti 201, località Colombaio Tozzi, Montalcino, 53024, Italy
Description: At the edge of the town, a skilfully restored farmhouse welcomes guests into an atmosphere of refined simplicity: from the carefully appointed rustic dining room to the bright glazed terrace, pleasant even in winter.The kitchen celebrates the flavours of the territory, reinterpreted in a measured contemporary key, without forgoing certain great classics such as peposo and onion soup.The wine list favours the local reds, with particular attention to Brunello and to labels of mature vintages.
