In the dining room, a warm welcome and assured knowledge of wine contribute to making the experience all the more rewarding.

Name: Bockem
Description: Good food and warm hospitality await in this 1905 townhouse located near the Vltava River and Kinský Garden. The enthusiasm of the team is palpable. The cosy, somewhat shabby-chic decor and the extremely dedicated, friendly and courteous front-of-house team make for a wonderful atmosphere. The food is cooked with respect for tradition, but also with a modern twist. In the morning, everything revolves around breakfast, but in the evening, the five-course set menu takes centre stage – think mouthwatering dishes such as beef cheeks with rose hip, cranberry and truffle, or the classic Bohemian sour soup.

Name: Bodega Noi
Description: A really attractive restaurant: sleek, modern, spacious and – thanks to the large glass frontage – pleasingly bright, not to mention the view of the beautiful countryside. The leafy terrace with its shady chestnut tree is also very inviting. On the menu: flavourful cuisine prepared using excellent ingredients and drawing on Mediterranean and regional influences. Lunchtime options are more limited and more moderately priced.

Name: Bodega del Riojano
Address: Rio de la Pila 5, Santander, 39003, Spain
Description: A restaurant with an abundance of character, history and authenticity, plus a unique museum (Museo Redondo) teeming with works of art. This business, which first started out in the 1930s selling agricultural items and wines, is nowadays a classic address in the city. The traditional menu features dishes such as the popular Rioja-style braised snails, as well as hake with a velouté cream and peppers. We recommend booking a table in advance and enjoying an aperitif in the bar before moving on to the dining room.

Name: Bodegón Alejandro
Address: Fermín Calbetón 4, Donostia / San Sebastián, 20003, Spain
Description: If you’re looking for somewhere to eat in the old town that epitomises Basque values and traditional cooking, the Bodegón Alejandro is the place for you, thanks to its focus on authentic local cuisine. In the simply furnished, rustic yet contemporary interior, choose between a varied à la carte of seasonal dishes (fried anchovies, Donostia-style supreme of cod with pil-pil and crab, Iberian pork loin with mashed potatoes etc) and an impressive tasting menu. Make sure you leave space for dessert as the warm pistachio soufflé with lemon sorbet is absolutely delicious!

Name: Boen Gård
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: Just a few kilometres from the rocky mountains of Sørlandet, on the banks of the Tovdal River, you’ll find this magical estate where peace and quiet reign and time almost seems to stand still. The elegant restaurant is housed in a lovingly restored 19th-century property at its centre, and the surrounding gardens, meadows and river provide the vegetables, fruits, berries, herbs and fish – while meat comes from small organic producers located nearby. Two tasting menus offer classic French recipes that have been given a modern overhaul, and an impressive wine cellar tops off the experience.

Name: Bog
Description: "New Nordic Restaurant" is a term that sparks the imagination. The sleek, rather understated decor of Bøg is certainly in line with what one would expect. Diners can choose between a vegetarian and fish/meat set menu, both equally creative and appealing. The finest ingredients, often locally sourced, are balanced with a minimalist approach and a sure touch. Pork, for example, is barbecued and served with al dente vegetables, a tart touch of cassis, a spicy sauce and a chilli-infused jus. Subtlety meets exuberant flavours in this fabulous restaurant.

Name: Bohème
Address: 47 avenue du Moulin de la Croix, Mougins, 06250, France
Description: In this smart, trendy establishment with a decor of premium and untreated materials, the food is an ode to the very best breeds of beef cattle, aged and prepared by the famous butcher Alexandre Polmard in his unique way. Peruvian chef Manuel Rondan is in a class of his own when it comes to cooking over hot coals and wild-fish ceviche, as well as some lovely Mediterranean dishes. There is a drop-dead view from the terrace.

Name: Bolboreta
Description: The first thing to strike you in this unpretentious bistro in the Lavapiés district, just a few steps from the Antón Martín market, is the close working relationship between the couple at the helm, namely Patricia in the dining room and British-born chef Aaron in the kitchen. The latter showcases his market-inspired cuisine with the occasional nod to his homeland (e.g. the “Hash Brown”, chorizo; salmon, ajoblanco, spicy radish, etc), on a concise menu that changes every three months. “Bolboreta” is the Galician word for “butterfly”, and is a reference to the chef’s grandmother, who loved these particular insects.

Name: Bolea
Description: In this 17C bistro, Léa Lestage (also at the helm of a.lea in the 18th arrondissement) crafts an intelligent bistro menu, weaving delicious modern notes into her unpretentious traditional food. The chef takes great care with the presentation of her plates and uses carefully sourced ingredients to deliver precise and flavourful dishes: langoustine bisque spiced with citrus and a fiery aioli; trout prepared two ways, with a sorrel cream sauce; chocolate mousse dusted with fleur de sel and drizzled with fruity olive oil.

Name: Bolivian Llama Party
Description: Bolivian Llama Party began as a passion project from Bolivian-American brothers who first started selling food at street fairs before building a devoted following in Queens. Today, the tiny Sunnyside counter remains lively and distinctly personal, blasting Bolivian pop music while serving approachable takes on traditional specialties and street-food favorites. Saltenas are a standout, their carefully crimped pastry shells holding rich, soupy fillings of chicken or beef alongside hard-boiled egg and spicy llajua salsa. The creamy sopa de mani, a traditional peanut soup enriched with beef broth and potatoes, offers comforting depth, while sandwiches like the brisket chola and fiery Diablada Bros’ter fried chicken showcase the kitchen’s talent for balancing bold flavors with fresh toppings and excellent bread.

Name: Bolle
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: We are in the Agnelli showroom, a well-known manufacturer of cookware for professional kitchens. The modern shop is located on the ground floor, while the first floor hosts the restaurant with its elegant tables in a refined minimalist and contemporary environment. On the menu, dishes with an impressive balance of ingredients, including occasionally exotic choices.

Name: Bombance
Description: Pressé de bœuf (beef terrine), kale mayonnaise; roast mallard, glazed mini beetroots, confit legs; peanut chocolate, chocolate quenelle, ice cream and peanut praline: chef Guillaume Campion, like the pro he his, having worked in some of the best restaurants in the world, is embracing his role. With a sure hand, he delights diners with his lively bistro-inspired cuisine. In addition to the tables along the banquette, there are also larger tables, ideal for feasting with friends.

Name: Bombay Bustle
Address: 29 Maddox Street, Mayfair, London, W1S 2PA, United Kingdom
Description: A charming train theme runs through this Indian restaurant, where the ground floor is the livelier area and downstairs is more ‘first class’. Mumbai is known for its chaat so – before a prawn curry, chicken biryani or succulent lamb chops from the tandoor – order some to share, like their wonderfully crisp and colourful Raj Kachori. And they make a fine rice pudding for dessert.

Name: Bomfim 1896
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: It is located in Quinta do Bomfim, an estate run by the Symington family since 1896. This cosy restaurant on the banks of the River Douro, it boasts a classic and sophisticated ambience, plus a completely open dining room with a view of the kitchen, and superb vistas through the large picture windows. The fireplace and wood-fired oven take centre stage here, alongside cuisine that revisits the flavours of the Douro Valley’s time-honoured kitchens, albeit with a more contemporary vision.

Name: Bon Kushikatsu
Description: This restaurant will whisk you off to Osaka to discover the city's culinary speciality of kushikatsu (meat, vegetables or seafood skewers, coated in breadcrumbs and deep fried). A low-key setting provides the perfect foil to the chef’s virtuoso performance: shiitake stuffed with ginger-laced chicken, foie gras flambéed in Japanese whisky and wasabi or brochette of wagyu beef. Bold flavours depict the evening omakase menu, while the score is simpler at lunchtime. The quintessence of Japan depicted by dishes ranging from beef sancho to spicy caramelised stew, a gracious welcome and courteous service.

Name: Bon Wei
Description: China on a plate! This attractive restaurant with an intriguing decor combining elegance, modern style and Asian influences serves a wide selection of Chinese specialities. Dishes include appetisers, dumplings, noodles and meat options, as well as a huge array of specialities from eight different regions, from the spicy dishes of Szechuan to the delicate flavours of Zhejiang.

Name: Bon appétit Meshiagare
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Shoes must be removed
Description: The chef honed his skills in Paris and other parts of France and uses Nara ingredients to prepare local dishes using traditional techniques he learned there. Seasonal vegetables and fruits come from Gojo City and Soni Village, and he also uses wild game caught in Tsuge. The main appetisers are homemade-style charcuterie, and the main meat dishes are roast and stew. He also incorporates ingredients like ayu and tilefish, sometimes giving the dishes a Japanese touch.

Name: Bong
Description: This tiny, high-energy Cambodian restaurant in Crown Heights is already a neighborhood fixture. Reservations disappear quickly, so arrive early in order to jockey for a spot at their counter. From the ambience to the shared plates-style menu, this is the kind of place that begs for a group to best sample standouts like plea satch ko, a Cambodian beef salad with razor-thin meat that melts in your mouth in a delightfully funky, spicy sauce. Don't miss the crispy whole fish sided by green mango sauce. Set over chilled vermicelli noodles and accompanied by all of the fixings for packing lettuce wraps, it's a fun and flavorful dish.

Name: Bongmilga
Description: Run by a chef with a deep passion for buckwheat noodles, Bongmilga embraces meticulous preparations and strict standards for ingredients. The house-made pear vinegar, mustard sauce, daily-prepared radish kimchi, and slightly thick hand-cut buckwheat noodles set it apart from typical naengmyeon shops. The clear broth, simmered for about five hours with Korean beef and medicinal herbs, offers a clean, consommé-like flavour. Guests can enhance their experience by adding pear vinegar and mustard to the noodles and enjoying them with boiled pork. The menu offers a wider range of choices, including also Pyongyang-style noodles with minari and a comforting gomtang.

Name: Bonheur Simple
Description: It is the little things that make us happy. Such as an attractive table setting in a contemporary restaurant, a peaceful atmosphere, and authentic Thai flavours in the creative cooking. Simplicity really is good.

Name: Bonhomme
Description: The trio who founded this lively bistro in the Faubourg Poissonnière are certainly not short on bonhomie! In this trendy, distressed-decor setting (stripped walls, marble-topped tables, glass-fronted cellar), the chef creates tasty modern dishes like trout raviolo, butternut, coriander, peanut and beurre blanc; Gâtinais chicken, parsley, glazed baby carrots, black garlic and jus, or chocolate mousse with salted butter caramel... Great atmosphere guaranteed.

Name: Bonifas
Description: Bonifas is steeped in the charm of a country inn with welcoming staff and a warm contemporary ambience. Chef Grégory Duranton is an unabashed fan of Gallic cuisine. You can expect rich dishes that star ingredients such as suave foie gras, intense truffle-flavoured pasta and a cut of Limousin beef crafted with textbook perfection and served with a béarnaise sauce of such depth that it will knock your socks off. The lunchtime and set menus are very popular.

Name: Bonjour Vietnam Bistro
Description: With looks somewhere between a tropical greenhouse and a nightclub, plus a cool, clubby atmosphere, this lively, colorful boîte could just as well be in West Hollywood as Vancouver. Some of the plant life is artificial, but rest assured the homey Vietnamese fare is the real deal. A hip, fashion-forward clientele is drawn in by the cooking, but the energetic vibe and disarmingly sweet service can’t hurt. You might start with grilled skewers, like a pork sausage shaped around a lemongrass stalk, or a pepper-crusted beef carpaccio topped with fragrant herbs, crispy garlic and shallot—but save room for the soul-warming bowls of pho (a short rib version is noteworthy) and bun bo hue. Each item has a vegetarian counterpart, so there’s no shortage of options.

Name: Bonnetti’s
Description: Mark Bonneu unveils a culinary score whose Spanish heritage is mixed with international overtones. The extensive menu rolls out an enticing selection of dishes to share, snacks and more high-flying creations. He might pair scallops and turnips with miso, for example. Texels lamb is jazzed up with a rosemary-flavoured gravy, a cream of chickpeas and carrots, unless you wouldn’t prefer an empanada of pork cheeks or a pan con tomate? The imposing edifice, which sports a pleasing light colour scheme, sings an ode to throbbing flavours and mouthwatering aromas. Even better, you can leave with a bottle of wine and/or a few delicacies to nibble at home.

Name: Bonnotte
Description: A 10min walk from the Albert Kahn Museum, Manon Negretti-Guichard and Antoine Guichard's restaurant has a simple, warm aesthetic. The pair of chefs have a solid track record to their names and pay homage to the Île de Noirmoutier and its famous bonnotte potato, a painting of which hangs on the wall. Manon runs the kitchen; Antoine also takes care of diners during service. The bistronomy cuisine gives pride of place to fresh produce and vegetable flavours: grilled courgette with feta and black olives; roast chicken leg (poulet jaune des Landes) with potato purée and a fragrant jus; apple crumble.

Name: Boompjes Restaurant
Description: As you enter, you pass the brasserie, where you can enjoy a casual lunch or snack. The space at the rear of the restaurant is like an oasis, with trees, plants and wood setting the tone. The terrace seamlessly merges with chef Jaap Volman's kitchen garden. An ambassador of Dutch cuisine, his cooking style is very much French-inspired, but his creative use of vegetables and fruit adds lightness and freshness . The velvety consommé with its subtle acidity accompanying the succulent pork cheeks was just as delightful as the vibrant medley of garden-fresh vegetables and herbs. What a way to showcase Dutch produce!

Name: Boon & De Koot
Description: A charming vintage bistro with tables set close together for a cosy feel, an irresistible menu filled with accessible yet flavoursome dishes, and a broad European wine selection put together with real expertise. What a delightful place this is! The chef enjoys working with vegetables and embraces the power of simplicity. A briefly deep-fried egg with Jerusalem artichoke cream and a medley of crispy potato skins and wild mushrooms finished with chives is a perfect example. With just a few components, he conjures up rich, playful dishes – all at moderate prices that are sure to win you over.

Name: Boon Keng Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Description: Come here for fish head noodle soup, and choose between Spanish mackerel, red grouper and regular grouper. The fish is fresh and the broth is flavoursome. The version with poached or fried sliced fish is also worth trying.

Name: Boon Nam
Description: A fun, intimate restaurant in the basement of the Hotel St George; the perfect place for a night out with friends. The fragrant dishes cover all the regions of Thailand and are good for sharing. Unsure what to order? Then go for one of the set menus, which also include good vegetarian options. A range of cocktails will help to keep you in the party mood, including some specially made to go with dessert.

Name: Boon Tong Kee Kway Chap‧Braised Duck
Address: Zion Riverside Food Centre, #024, 70 Zion Road, 247792, Singapore
Description: Boon Tong Kee prides itself on its spiced soy marinade made with aromatic Chinese herbs. With its springy skin and tasty meat, the signature braised duck is a hit. The braised pork trotter and taro rice are also popular.

Name: Boonville Hotel & Restaurant
Description: Unless you’re already staying at the hotel, dinner here means driving along the lonely, hairpin-turning, and mountainous course of Highway 128 until you reach the quaint town of Boonville. But what a happy place it is, thanks to the talents of Chef Perry Hoffman, who prepares simple but arresting plates highlighting product sourced from their own vegetable garden and local farms. A recent menu showcased roasted sunchokes tossed with a rosemary vinaigrette; butter-poached chicken breast with green garlic, ricotta gnudi, chives and preserved lemon sauce; as well as a decadent chocolate brownie with cardamom ice cream. This is food that’s easy to eat—again and again. Opening hours change with the season and the menu daily, so check the website before making the drive.

Name: Bootshaus
Description: The beachside location is simply idyllic – you can't get much closer to the Baltic Sea! In this restaurant at the Weissenhaus Private Nature Luxury Resort, diners are shown to their tables in a modern interior with a glazed façade that affords fantastic views. But it is of course the terrace that is the top attraction! The food is a fresh blend of Mediterranean fare – somewhat simpler at lunchtime, more sophisticated in the evening, from classic dishes to elegant culinary compositions. Service runs from 12:00 to 17:00, and in the evening (by reservation) from 18:00 to 21:30.

Name: Bootshaus Bar & Grill
Description: Bootshaus is located in the heart of Hamburg's HafenCity. From the comfortable "Boot" (boat) dining area, watch the action in the open kitchen or look out over the marina (Grasbrookhafen) from the light and airy bar area. In summer the waterfront terrace beckons. The Josper grill takes centre stage, with cuts such as New York strip, rib-eye and porterhouse cooked to perfection! There is also a large selection of side dishes and delicious sauces. Keep an eye out for the seafood specials and the "Chef's Choice" deal. The early opening times (from 5.30pm) make this an ideal spot for dinner before a concert at the nearby Elbphilharmonie – or perhaps a drink at the bar afterwards.

Name: Boozehounds
Address: 2080 N. Palm Canyon Dr., Palm Springs, CA, 92262, USA
Description: What's in a name? In this case, at least, there’s a tongue-in-cheek précis: a dog-friendly cocktail bar. Diners and their canine confrères can enter a spacious enclosed patio area through a separate "doggy door," which offers access to an additional menu of bowls and treats for Fido and Spot. The stylish indoor space remains a humans-only domain, where the focus shifts to a top shelf drinks menu (replete with dog-themed nomenclature, naturally), as well as an appealingly eclectic bar menu that spans both snacks and more substantial fare. Standbys like truffled parmesan fried and blistered shishitos are nothing to sniff at, but less expected items like Japanese-inflected tuna tataki, Filipino adobo or Korean rice cakes offer an exciting change of pace.

Name: Bord' Eau by Nicolas Isnard
Address: Level 3, Lobby Level, Shangri-La Qaryat Al Beri Hotel, Abu Dhabi
Description: This outpost of French chef Nicolas Isnard, from Auberge de Charme in the Côte-d'Or in France, champions inventive French classics and dishes inspired by his travels. It's a spacious and high-ceilinged room, decorated with contemporary chandeliers and large tables. Choose between an à la carte or one of two tasting menus: 'French classics' or 'Travels around the world', which takes its influence from the chef’s global adventures. The generously sized dishes use first class ingredients, are boldly flavoured and combine classic recipes with a modern flare. Try the Modern Onion Soup and the delicious Belle Hélène pear in 70% Grand Cru dark chocolate.

Name: Bord'eau
Address: 17 rue de la Poissonnerie, Colmar, 68000, France
Description: In the heart of Little Venice, this handsome regional edifice on the banks of the Lauch belongs to chef Jean-Yves Schillinger. A tasteful contemporary decor sets the stage for a culinary cast drawn from near and far: cassolette of prawns and Thai veggies; red mullet, baby artichokes and a rouille sauce with Alsace saffron; wafer-thin apple pie, butterscotch and vanilla ice cream…

Name: Bordo Mavi
Address: Jumeirah Fishing Harbour, Al Urouba St, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,No alcohol served,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Valet parking
Description: There’s no better place to open a seafood restaurant than in the Jumeirah Fishing Harbour. The owners behind 3Fils have partnered with Turkish fisherman Ersan Yilmaz to create this rustic eatery overlooking the harbour. As you enter, take a moment to admire the fresh fish displayed on ice before you start your meal. Take your pick from Norwegian salmon, tuna, turbot and, if you’re lucky, locally caught hamour. We recommend starting with a ceviche or tartare and a salad before diving into the main fish dish and finishing off with a tahini baklava.

Name: Boreczna
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Hidden away among the Owl Mountains, you’ll find this rural oasis on a former farm. The eye-catching dining room has a slightly glitzy feel, with chandeliers and large candlelit tables. The cooking packs in plenty of flavour and shows off the kitchen’s technical skill with dishes like loin of veal with a meaty, multi-layered sauce. The service team are eager to please and, if you want to stay overnight, there are cosy bedrooms and even lodges in the grounds.

Name: Boreumsae
Description: Boreumsae is the only place in Seoul that serves heukwoo, or native Jeju black cattle raised on a farm the restaurant runs on the island. Heukwoo is much firmer in texture, as it is leaner and nuttier in flavor. The robust, savory flavor fills the palate with only a simple sprinkling of salt. The restaurant takes exceptional pride in the quality of their meat, which is flown in fresh directly from Jeju. Boeumsae is the place to visit if you seek lean, clean flavored beef in Seoul.

Name: Borg, Raíces y Alas
Address: Juan de la Cierva 31, El Campello, 03560, Spain
Description: Located near the beach and under a name that at first makes you think of legendary tennis player Björn Borg, we find Swedish-Spanish chef Carl Borg Medina who was born in Madrid and, from a culinary perspective, trained in Barcelona. His restaurant, with à la carte service (which changes three times a year) and the option of three set menus (an economical one at lunchtime and two tasting menus: Raíces and Alas, with 7 and 10 courses, respectively), combines Mediterranean and regional flavours with his Nordic roots. Recommendations? Everything is well priced, so start with the Gravadlax, a salmon tenderloin with fresh dill and a touch of mustard based on the family recipe book.

Name: Borgo Agnese
Description: You'll feel as if you've been whisked away to the Mediterranean! The menu features tempting dishes such as "shrimp confit, potato, saffron aioli, radish", "gnocchi, mushrooms, pine nuts, beetroot, goat cheese, herbs" or "boar, cream, cranberries, semolina". Simply order à la carte, or opt for one of the tasting menus compiled from the same options. The delicious food can be accompanied by something from the extensive wine list, which features European labels, including some big names. Furthermore, diners enjoy attentive and adept service in a bright and classically elegant setting – a unique detail of the decor is the excavated historical church wall, protected by glass.

Name: Borgo Cala Creta-Giardino Arabo
Description: In the elegant resort of Dammusi di Borgo Cala Creta, surrounded by lush Mediterranean scrub, the “Giardino Arabo” is their beautiful restaurant, with tables elegantly arranged around a spectacular olive tree. Outdoors, you can enjoy a rich seafood cuisine with a modern and imaginative touch, featuring traditional recipes, including an unmissable “Seafood Caponata” enriched with unsweetened cocoa and pistachio.

Name: Borgo Hannam
Description: Once up the tiny set of stairs of Borgo Hannam, you will be greeted with homemade dishes and liqueurs befitting the cosy space. From the bread freshly baked in the morning to pastas and desserts, everything is handmade by Chef Stefano Di Salvo. The kitchen's signature Caldaro soup, inspired by the fisherman’s soup in Tuscany, has a rich, spicy flavour with the chef’s own twist. With a friendly atmosphere, this is a great spot for enjoying heartwarming Italian food from various regions.

Name: Borgo Mooca
Address: Rua Barão De Tatuí, 302, São Paulo, 01226-030, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Counter dining,Valet parking
Description: This laid-back gastronomic retreat, nestled in the Santa Cecília neighbourhood, sets itself apart with its bold concept of "Punk Italian" — rooted in traditional Italian cooking, yet reinterpreted with creativity and a liberating sense of freedom. Founded by chef Bianca Giacomelli, the restaurant has made a name for itself through its seasonal cooking, combining classical techniques with a contemporary, experimental, and boldly disruptive approach. The atmosphere is further enriched by a counter overlooking the open kitchen, and a décor featuring original photographs by Neapolitan photographer Ciro Pipoli, capturing the everyday life of Naples. Not-to-be-missed dishes? The Tuna Akami Mille-feuille with parrilla-roasted beetroot and sour cream, the Gnocchi Fritti served with baby squid and Santa Catarina bottarga, and the house classic, Beef Wellington accompanied by mashed potato and demi-glace.

Name: Born & Raised
Address: 1909 India St., San Diego, CA, 92101, USA
Description: No expense was spared making this wildly polished, upscale steakhouse that resembles a midcentury, art deco dream lined with black-and-white photos of old-school rap legends. There is a glassed-in meat cutting room in the back; and a lovely, open-air rooftop bar overlooking Little Italy. Waiters dressed in tuxedos and Converse shoes drift between tables, pushing nostalgic tableside carts where they whip up starters on the spot or pour Manhattans and martinis to order. Certainly, you’re here for the impeccably cooked steaks, but don’t miss the tartare, prepared tableside with quail egg, capers and cornichons (to name just a few embellishments) and served with herbed aïoli.

Name: Born and Bred
Address: B1F Paradise Hotel, 296 Haeundaehaebyeon-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48099, South Korea
Description: Premium-grade hanwoo is now served in Busan. Only top-grade female cattle (1++BMS9 grade) are hand-picked daily by highly experienced staff, aged and trimmed to a perfect thickness to create a multi-faceted flavor profile. Born and Bred also offers an omakase-style experience where diners can taste 15 to 19 different cuts of charcoal-grilled beef. The menu is filled with creative dishes like beef sashimi and beef tacos. Make sure you arrive ready to indulge yourself.

Name: Born and Bred
Description: Born and Bred showcases top-grade hanwoo sourced from Majang-dong, curated by an owner truly “born and bred” there. Spanning four floors, each with its own concept, the restaurant offers a wide range—from signature burgers and steaks to Korean-style grilling cuts and specialty selections by weight. One floor serves a set tasting menu, while another presents a chef’s choice menu that best reflects the restaurant’s identity, so it’s worth choosing your floor in advance.

Name: Borona Bistró
Description: A small, centrally located restaurant that takes its name from the famous corn bread traditionally eaten in the north of Spain, particularly in Galicia and Asturias. The couple at the helm, Víctor Corchado and Rocío Rey, with him manning the cooker and her front of house, present a detailed cuisine that seeks to respect the traditions of Extremadura and its flavours, updating the dishes both in terms of techniques and presentation. The menu, which includes various individual sampling options, is complemented by a tasting menu called Algarabía (with two wine pairing options: A tour of the region and A journey around the peninsula). One dish we liked? Fried suckling pig's ear and white prawn with lime (it is always on the menu or on one of the set menus, although the accompaniment usually changes depending on the season).

Name: Borsa Restaurant
Address: Vaniköy Caddesi No:12, Adile Sultan Sarayı, Üsküdar, Istanbul, 34684, Türkiye
Description: The Adile Sultan Palace is an events venue that is as spectacular as its name suggests. A stroll through the building will give you a sense of its grandeur and splendour – characteristics that Borsa is fortunate to share. To dine against a breathtaking backdrop of the Bosporus, head to the terrace. This upmarket restaurant showcases traditional Turkish cuisine on an à la carte basis. In his dish featuring medium-rare lamb ribs, spinach and roast potatoes, the chef allows the distinctive flavours of the ingredients to shine through. Less is more at Borsa. Make sure you leave room for dessert – the classic katmer (crispy filo pastry filled with pistachio) is very tempting!

Name: Bosq
Description: The name of this restaurant is inspired by the Spanish word bosque ("forest"). This warm and welcoming spot stands on the edge of the National Park, affording stunning views of the lush landscape – the terrace is a real highlight! Robin Koenen combines finest local produce from Texel with Mediterranean flair and Asian nuances. His penchant for umami and barbecue notes shines through in dishes such as succulent pan-seared turbot with briny shellfish from the Wadden Sea, sweet tomatoes and a beurre blanc made with fish fumet and a judicious splash of soy sauce. His cuisine packs a punch and, thanks to the smaller-sized portions, you can sample it extensively.

Name: Bosque FeVi
Description: If your tastebuds start to tingle at the idea of biting into a “croquetas de jamón” and a “crema catalana” with a hint of citrus fruit, then book a table straight away in this exquisite restaurant, depicted by a striking “undulating” wooden wall-cum-artwork. Fernando Andreu conjures up a Mediterranean score with a dash of modernity by delving into his Spanish roots and the odd international influence like kimchi or tikka masala. If you’re in the mood for tapas, make a beeline for FeVi Gaudium, under the same roof of the Seven Hotel.

Name: Bossi
Address: 10 Commerce Street, Auckland Central, Auckland, 1010, New Zealand
Description: Olive green velvet banquettes contrast nicely with the dark wood panelling. Full length picture windows fill the space with natural light, while a double-height wine cabinet catches the eye. Italian classics define the menu. Start with their baked-to-order garlic bread. For primo, try house-made pasta like Bolognese Bianca – cavatelli in a rich, creamy white wine meat sauce. And there’s no better way to end a meal here than an iconic tiramisu.

Name: Botanica
Address: Hotel Botanica, Nyárfa utca 57, Dánszentmiklós, 2735, Hungary
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Lovely gardens surround this delightful, family-owned country house, which comes with bespoke designer bedrooms and charming service. Start with a drink in one of the comfortable lounges before heading through to the elegant restaurant, where a spot on the terrace is a must in summer. The multi-course menu showcases refined, modern creations in dishes which pay tribute to the locality, as well as the chef’s Swabian roots. Both wine and non-alcoholic drinks pairings are on offer, along with fermented beverages crafted from local fruits and vegetables.

Name: Botanist
Address: Fairmont Pacific Rim,1038 Canada Pl., Vancouver, V6C 0B9, Canada
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Glide through the elegant lobby and up the sweeping staircase of the Fairmont Pacific Rim to arrive at Botanist, where dressing up is de rigueur. The kitchen takes great pride in sourcing the best local product, whether it's wild, locally caught seafood or produce from the Fraser Valley.Every dish on this modern Canadian menu is delightful, but some of the standouts include hand-cut tagliatelle bathed in a mushroom sauce and crowned with wild mushroom ragout. Pan-seared striploin is perfectly cooked, resting alongside a tender cabbage roulade stuffed with lush beef tongue, Chinese broccoli and spicy XO sauce. To finish, desserts are impressive; especially when faced with the refreshing lemon syrup-soaked cake dressed with Meyer lemon curd and bay leaf ice cream.

Name: Botswana Butchery
Description: Nestled in the historic Archer's Cottage on the Queenstown lakefront, this restaurant serves up steakhouse classics and lovely vistas of Lake Wakatipu. The premises, from the door handle to the logo, are dotted with cleavers, underscoring the meat-centric menu dominated by various cuts of New Zealand beef and lamb. But it is worth considering the oysters, market fish of the day and seasonal vegetables. The food pairs perfectly with Central Otago wines.

Name: Bottega
Address: 2240 Highland Ave. S., Birmingham, AL, 35205, USA
Description: There is a good reason why reservations are sparse at Frank and Pardis Stitt’s long-standing Bottega. The historic, neo-classical Beaux-Arts building stands out in Birmingham's Southside neighborhood, and eager, sharply dressed guests wait outside for doors to open. Some find seats at the bar; others settle into an elegantly cut dining room fit with dark wood walls and high ceilings. Prepared with confidence, the menu paints broad strokes with its Italian-Mediterranean bent. Think parmesan souffle, wobbly and just set, or sweet potato gnocchi with rock shrimp. Wherever you sit, warm, polished servers ensure a welcoming experience.

Name: Bottega Aleotti
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the splendid Santa Croce church, this charming restaurant should not be missed. The cuisine combines Emilian traditions with fresh, local ingredients, and includes dishes with a more contemporary touch. The excellent bread and home-made pastries add to the overall dining experience.

Name: Bottega Caruso
Address: 2-4 Broad Street, Margate, CT9 1EW, United Kingdom
Description: A former pub plays host to this sweet little osteria offering southern Italian fare, often using ingredients from the chef-owner's home region of Campania. There's a homespun charm to the place, so it's only right the hand-made pastas form the core of the menu. The rest of the simple, rustic cooking consists of small plates and snacks; look out for the 'polpette di pane al sugo', where bread has been used to fashion a 'meatball' of sorts. The same team run a deli a few doors down, which transforms into a wine bar at weekends that's ideal for a drink before or after dinner.

Name: Bottega Culinaria
Address: Contrada Pontoni 72, San Vito Chietino, 66038, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Nestled amid a charming landscape of olive groves, this restaurant is not particularly easy to find, so make sure that you use a satnav or ask for directions when booking. A simple, minimalist-style dining room provides the backdrop for imaginative cuisine which includes plenty of vegetables and is full of contrasting flavours and reinterpreted regional influences.

Name: Bottega Lucia
Description: A charming bistro-style establishment, with exposed wood and brick creating a warm, informal atmosphere, offering immediate and flavorful Italian cuisine – the spaghetti alla chitarra cacio e pepe with black truffle is emblematic – alongside forays into the nearby Iberian Peninsula and playful international influences. Among these, the steamed bao with pulled pork and coleslaw and the celebrated Milanese-style gyoza stand out, the latter filled with ossobuco and served with saffron cream. Meat and fish appear in equal measure, in a menu designed to satisfy diverse tastes without losing coherence. Just steps away is Casa Lucia, a more informal iteration of the same establishment, ideal for simple dishes and good pizza.

Name: Bottega Vannini
Description: This lively bottega doubles as a delicatessen, so you tuck into your meal surrounded by shelves of Italian delicacies (be sure to stop by the counter afterwards). Expect no frills here, just unadulterated Mediterranean flavours. Their take on beloved classics like vitello tonnato and saltimbocca alla romana showcases the full potential of these dishes. Or how about perfectly al dente cavatelli pasta with succulent sausage meat and crunchy niebé beans? Accompanied by interesting wines (corkage fee €15). Irresistibly authentic!

Name: Bottega del Re
Address: Via Francesco Domenico Guerrazzi 66r, Genoa, 16146, Italy
Description: In the tranquil heart of Albaro’s residential quarter, a cool summer courtyard welcomes guests with the scent of flowers and the gentle rustle of leaves. Inside, warm spaces blend rustic charm with elegant touches, creating a comforting, refined atmosphere. The cuisine is a journey between land and sea, where tradition meets seasonality: each dish reveals the authentic flavors of ingredients carefully sourced by young, talented Chef Orlandi. Not to be missed: the “quaglia della bottega,” quail stuffed with a giardiniera of crunchy, aromatic vegetables, releasing intense aromas with every bite. Our advice: save room for dessert, true masterpieces of sweetness that bring the meal to a close with velvety, surprising notes.

Name: Botánico
Address: Alfonso Reyes 217, Colonia Condesa, Cuauhtémoc, 06100, Mexico
Description: Upon first glance, it may not look like much, but the exterior belies the oasis found within. Tall cacti, a lake stocked with fish and a convivial atmosphere make this a natural choice for date night, but this laidback spot is equally well suited to families and groups too. Everyone enjoys being here as they connect over plates like serrano and pistachio aguachile topped with shrimp or cavatelli tossed with blue crab and finished with an anchovy breadcrumb. Crème brûlée delivers a strange-sounding surprise with the addition of Kalamata olive, but it's a convincing finale.

Name: Boubou's
Address: Rua do Monte Olivete 32 A, Lisbon, 1200-280, Portugal
Description: Located beside the National Museum of Natural History and Science, this welcoming restaurant has reinvented itself and now embraces the identity of a ‘contemporary French bistro’. At its helm is chef André Lança Cordeiro, a well-known figure on Lisbon’s gastronomic scene thanks to his restaurant Essencial (recommended in the MICHELIN Guide) and his strong affinity with French techniques. Here, he invites diners on a sensory journey through the classic, essential flavours of French cuisine. Served exclusively à la carte and available only at dinner, the offering includes specialities such as Tarte Pissaladière, Toulouse-style Pâté en croûte, bistro Steak tartare and the True Cordon bleu. An experience combining an informal yet elegant atmosphere with impeccable flavours!

Name: Boucan
Description: Chef Kevin Barata and Lucile Prévost (partners in business and in life), already owners of Au Koning Van Peene, are now also at the helm of the restaurant of La Barcarolle theatre. Neon lights and zesty colours make for a delightfully pop decor. The cuisine is straightforward and generous (especially the sauces!) and draws on emblematic produce from this northernmost part of France.

Name: Bouchon
Description: This may be quaint Yountville, but Thomas Keller's French bistro paints a scene that is straight out of Paris. Red velvet booths, marble tables, polished brass and a tiled floor make for a buzzy scene. The next-door bakery is equally busy with its own lines often stretching out the front door. True to form, the cooking is righteously, unapologetically indulgent. Salade Lyonnaise studded with bacon lardons, flat iron steak with French fries, mussels steamed with white wine, boudin blanc with potato puree — the classics are well accounted for. Finish strong with profiteroles matched with vanilla ice cream and chocolate sauce.

Name: Bouchon Racine
Address: 66 Cowcross Street, Clerkenwell, London, EC1M 6BP, United Kingdom
Description: Just a few steps from Farringdon station, tucked away above the Three Compasses pub, you'll find Chef Henry Harris' take on the classic French bistro. Simply set tables, old French wine bottles and vintage posters tick all the decorative boxes, while the menu is a rollcall of classic Gallic fare. Think escargots, duck confit and steak tartare, along with sharing dishes like côte de boeuf with béarnaise sauce or roast Basque chicken with morels. The well-chosen French wine list puts the final touch on a comforting Francophone experience.

Name: Bouchot
Description: The charm of Bouchot brings out the warmth of this stylish building dating back to 1934. Smiling sommelier and hostess Tessa provides excellent wine recommendations; meanwhile, in the kitchen, Bram expresses his love for Zeeland and classic French cuisine. On retro tableware, he serves up œufs meurette – soft-poached eggs in a sweet and intense red wine sauce with bacon and mushrooms – and crispy veal sweetbreads with hazelnuts and a sauce enriched with balsamic vinegar and spices. Quality ingredients speak for themselves in all their simplicity, thanks to the expertly made sauces. A new favourite spot for Brabant's bon vivants!

Name: Bouffard
Description: Bouffard has two different dining spaces to suit different moods: a snug lounge area at the front and a more vibrant room adorned with colourful artworks. Thomas Dockx is very selective when it comes to his ingredients, and he takes a less-is-more approach to preparing them. Eschewing any unnecessary frills, he allows the natural flavours to shine through with the help of robust sauces. In one of his exuberant dishes, he combines golden-brown pan-fried scallops, tender pork cheek and a creamed cheek broth. This chef understands how to create a well-rounded set menu that keeps you engaged from beginning to end!

Name: Bouillon Baron
Description: Jérémie Baron, the former chef-patron of Autour d'un Cep, has set up shop in this building dating back to 1895. In a simple setting with a buzzing atmosphere, he regales a packed house of enthusiastic diners with traditional and popular recipes, such as terrine de campagne with pickles; œuf mimosa (devilled eggs), beetroot and vinaigrette; saucisse de Toulouse; calf's head with ravigote sauce; and chocolat choux craquelin (cream puffs) with pecans for dessert. The lunch menu, featured on the blackboard, is unbeatable value. A selection of organic and biodynamic wines principally from the Loire Valley.

Name: Bouillon Bilk
Address: 22 rue Sainte-Catherine Est, Montréal, H2X 2W5, Canada
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Right in the heart of the Quartier des Spectacles, a stone's throw from Place des Arts, Bouillon Bilk blends seamlessly into the bustling rue Sainte-Catherine. Behind the restaurant's plain façade, Chef François Nadon crafts cuisine imbued with influences from around the world, served in a refined setting. Celery root fried in panko is accompanied by a raw pear coulis and a miso sauce, with raw enoki and pan-fried shiitake. The just-seared scallops are set on a hazelnut butter and different textures of zucchini. For dessert, pastry chef Léa Godin Beauchemin creates a lovely combination of pear sorbet, pumpkin purée, oat crumble, and buttermilk granita. The wine list, selected by Minh Doan, is remarkable.

Name: Boulcott Street Bistro
Address: 99 Boulcott Street, Wellington Central, Wellington, 6011, New Zealand
Description: A firm favourite among locals for over 30 years, this classic bistro in a charming Victorian cottage is the perfect spot for casual lunches and formal dinners. The menu rolls out time-honoured bistro staples built on solid techniques and honest flavours, ranging from French onion soup and crumbed calamari to aged beef fillet in sauce béarnaise and a crème brûlée that never disappoints... Reservations only accepted for lunch and early dinner up to 6pm.

Name: Boulder Dushanbe Tea House
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This hand-built gift from Dushanbe, Boulder's sister city in Tajikistan, offers a respite from quotidian life. Walk through the front garden and you'll be instantly transported to a zen-filled, magical space. If the bucolic setting doesn't lower your blood pressure, the stunning interior that transports you to a faraway culture will. As the name suggests, tea is the raison d'être here, and the selection is comprehensive. From apple strudel and samosas to feijoada and plov (a buttery rice dish studded with chickpeas, dried fruit and grilled beef), the menu reads like a world explorer's diary. Naturally, tea time and afternoon tea are reason alone to visit, and the dessert selection is particularly tempting.

Name: Boulevard
Description: The welcome is warm, the room elegant, and the food heartening and eminently satisfying. The passion and experience of the two chef-owners is evident in all areas of this likeable restaurant. The quality of the fish and shellfish really comes through, thanks to the classic techniques used by the kitchen.

Name: Boulevard Kitchen & Oyster Bar
Address: Sutton Place Hotel, 845 Burrard St., Vancouver, V6Z 2K6, Canada
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: It's large, with several dining spaces bearing distinctive styles, but Boulevard Kitchen & Oyster Bar ties it all together with chic, modern ease. Whether it's the imported hand-painted tile floors and marble-topped bars, the romantic lighting or the buttery leather seating, luxurious details abound. The versatile menu is as instantly likeable as the setting. Discover classics like baked oysters with creamed spinach, garlic bread crumbs and wild oregano. House-made pasta is tucked with a bevy of seafood, including Pacific white prawns, Humboldt squid, clams and mussels, while Calabrian chili bread crumbs deliver an enjoyable kick of heat. Whole cauliflower, roasted in curry leaves with green chutney and coconut turmeric sauce, is a veritable celebration of the vegetable.

Name: Bouquet de France
Description: “The countryside is the foundation of French cuisine”, says Hidetoshi Imoto. He pours his labours into the flavours of rural France, such as cassoulet, a stew from Languedoc, and baeckeoffe, an Alsatian casserole. The charcuterie of pork pâtés and sausages is indispensable in expressing its home culture. Proprietress Yoko Harada’s amiable service relaxes guests with a cheerful, homelike atmosphere.

Name: Bourgeon
Description: In a converted cooperage in this fabled little wine-growing town, a young duo who were previously at La Rôtisserie du Chambertin have opened this contemporary restaurant with a personal touch. Chef Maxime Strassel and maître d' and sommelier Alexis Rappe treat diners to a minimalist dining room with an open kitchen and a few counter seats. The chef presents his contemporary cuisine, often plant-forward (foraging, preservation), in different tasting menus. Carefully selected ingredients star in precise and balanced dishes, underpinned by confident technical skills.

Name: Boutary
Description: This is just the spot to discover or brush up on your caviar know-how (osetra, sterlet and baeri), as the owners have been raising sturgeon in southern Bulgaria for several generations. A plush smart interior serves as a backdrop to the chef’s “carte blanche” menus and a very popular traditional caviar tasting session, served on the back of the hand. Former pastry chef of Ledoyen, the latter signs an outstanding delicate, low-sugar dessert lineup, illustrated by a coffee and caramel delight. The front-of-house team bends over backwards to satisfy and please.

Name: Bowleys at The Plough
Address: The Plough Inn, Taylor's Lane, Trottiscliffe, ME19 5DR, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Tucked away down a narrow street, The Plough proudly declares that it is 'community owned, family run'. The community in question is the people of Trottiscliffe, who rallied round to buy and refurbish their local pub when property developers were circling. Among their number was the Yates family, who now look after this small restaurant offering a concise menu of carefully crafted, ambitious and classically based dishes. Local produce, some of it their own, informs the menus – even the butter is homemade.

Name: Box Tree
Address: 35-37 Church Street, Ilkley, LS29 9DR, United Kingdom
Description: Set within two charming, 18th-century sandstone cottages, this iconic Yorkshire restaurant was established back in 1962 and continues to draw in diners over six decades later. Today, the kitchen is in the care of Chef Brayden Davies, who was born in Western Australia to British parents – a background which is reflected across his tasting menu, from the barbecued 'Damper Bread' to the 'Paddle Pop' ice cream and the Jarrah honey. The service has a formal touch, but with plenty of personality from the engaging team.

Name: Boys Hall
Address: Boys Hall Road, Willesborough, Ashford, TN24 0LA, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Built in 1616 for the Boys family, this charming old house has been sympathetically converted into a hotel with eye-catching features at every turn, plus lovely gardens and land. The restaurant sits in an extension to the main house and serves high-quality Kentish produce, in flavourful dishes such as hake with roasted cauliflower, caviar and butter sauce. Great wines, also from Kent, are available to pair with your food and, should you wish to grab a drink before dining, the grounds also house a pub with a terrace.

Name: Boîte
Description: What a pity we don’t live down the road from this amusing "box"! “Taste the world, Share the food” is their baseline! The seasoned chef curates her own version of world cuisine, steeped in variety, harmony and exoticism… For example, deftly crafted spicy Lebanese toast, generous tajine, sweet and sour noodles, etc. Even better, diners can choose their own vegetable side dishes and are invited to share the main course with the rest of the table. Perfect for a casual dining experience!

Name: Brabo
Description: If you consider yourself an avid carnivore, don't miss this simple, contemporary steakhouse – an attractive “sanctuary of fire” where grilled meats are the undeniable stars of the show. Despite this, you’ll also find top-quality grilled fish and vegetables. The menu, created by the duo of chefs Rafa Panatieri and Jorge Sastre (they also run a popular gourmet pizzeria), usually starts with homemade sausages (wild boar mortadella, matured beef loin, country pâté, etc) is designed to be enjoyed with others (the Friesian beef T-bone steak is perfect for sharing), and is complemented by different side dishes. Interestingly, they enjoy working with the Gascón breed of pig (these are black, like Iberian pigs, but of French origin and few in number). The Experiencia Brabo tasting menu is also an option here.

Name: Brabohoeve
Description: Brabohoeve is a villa-restaurant whose smart, modern interior is adorned in arty photos. The terrace overlooking the surrounding meadows is a must when the weather is fine. Franco-Belgian classics take the leading role in the culinary repertory with family favourites like shrimp fritters and vol-au-vent of free-range chicken in star positions, crafted with flawless technique and flanked by a succulent selection of seasonal specials. Examples include fresh, juicy brill garnished with mushrooms and gnocchi, or saddle of hare in season. Expect to find it difficult to make up your mind, such is the range tempting and enticing…

Name: Brach
Description: In the luxurious setting of this former postal sorting office, redesigned and decorated by Philippe Starck, diners peruse a menu of Mediterranean-inspired dishes; these are executed with finesse and precision by chef Adam Benthala, who has an impressive CV to his name. The healthy and balanced fare embraces indulgence when it comes to sharing a round of kémia – small plates rife with aromas, spices and textures.

Name: Braise
Description: Wood furnishings, brick walls and soft lighting set the scene in this casual, lively bistro for meat-centric, flame-licked cooking. Against a backdrop of ageing display cases, diners sample simple recipes that revolve around the Japanese binchotan barbecue: perfectly grilled Baltic Black Beef rib eye, melt-in-the-mouth pâté en croûte or bona fide crème caramel.

Name: Bramble & Hare
Description: It's a farmhouse-meets-lodge vibe at Jill and Chef Eric Skokan's Bramble & Hare, where wood paneled walls and wood floors keep things rustic, and chairs and loveseats are draped with fur throws for an extra dose of charm. The couple's own farm supplies most of the inspiration for the dishes on this American menu—even down to the prosciutto they age in-house from their own pigs. Those impressive ingredients aren't gussied up in this kitchen, where a smart but straightforward cooking style allows them to truly shine. Many items are married in new and creative ways. Case in point? The salted turnips served with a pistachio purée, pickled onions and that fantastic house-cured prosciutto, delivering a fantastic surprise in a well-balanced, bright dish.

Name: Bramea
Address: Viale Villa d'Errico 10, Palazzo San Gervasio, 85026, Italy
Description: Bramea, whose name is inspired by a rare butterfly native to the Vulture area, comes to life within a skilfully restored ancient ruin. The restaurant, characterised by a modern and contemporary style, presents a cuisine that expresses itself through several tasting menus, set alongside a concise and well-calibrated à la carte menu. Lucanian ingredients form the point of departure for every journey and make their impression from the very first amuse-bouches: the fried lampascione and the taste of gnummareddo both stand out as particularly accomplished, immediately arousing the curiosity of the palate.

Name: Bramley
Address: 10 Main Street, Knockamoe, Abbeyleix, R32 D8C0, Ireland
Description: There’s an endearing quality to this characterful restaurant run by a young, friendly team and set inside a former garage and shop. The cooking champions the County Laois larder and other Irish produce, in satisfying dishes with tried-and-tested flavour combinations. At dinner, choose from the concise à la carte or sample the kitchen’s full range of talents with the 7 course tasting menu. Lunchtime is a slightly simpler affair and features daily specials.

Name: Brandal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: At this restaurant, nestled inside the Hotel Scala although with its own entrance, they like to say that here you can go ‘to enjoy the best flavours of Galicia at your leisure’. In its bright dining room, with a minimalist atmosphere, you can sample cuisine based on Galician recipes, with contemporary starters with a traditional taste (we were blown away by the bluefin tuna belly sandwich), select meats, good seafood and large fish of the day. Their grilled dishes are particularly noteworthy!

Name: Brasería Sansibar
Description: Located close to Praia da Lanzada, a popular local beach. In this family-owned restaurant run by a friendly couple who live on the floor upstairs, everything revolves around the open grill and top-quality ingredients, from the best cuts of Galician meat to fish from the local auction and a variety of seafood. We can definitely recommend the daily specials that do not feature on the menu.

Name: Brasserie
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: If you don’t fancy the gourmet cuisine on offer at Meierei, you can enjoy fresh, international fare or just a slice of home-made cake in the less formal atmosphere of the Brasserie.

Name: Brasserie 1809
Description: The restaurant is done out in a modern Alpine style, with an interior that is upscale, sleek and at the same time inviting. As for the food great store is set by regional produce. Select ingredients go into creating tasty seasonal dishes. It is pleasant to eat on the lovely terrace, and not only in summer! The Capra hotel has wonderful inviting guestrooms.

Name: Brasserie 1893
Address: 1F, Waldorf Astoria Hotel, 5-15 Jinyu Hutong, Dongcheng, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
Description: Calling itself a brasserie is just being humble. The elegant space features exquisite artwork and an attractive display kitchen. The à la carte menu changes regularly to include sharing plates that are great for families; the "Deluxe Degustation" tasting menu embodies the chef's culinary vision. Tea-smoked pigeon is one of his proud creations: he marinates then smokes young birds from Shiqi, uniting Chinese flavours with French techniques.

Name: Brasserie Astoria
Address: Victoria Concert Hall, #01-01, 11 Empress Place, 179558, Singapore
Description: An outpost of its namesake in Stockholm, this is the brainchild of the Swedish owner-chef Björn Frantzén. Nestled in the historical Victoria Concert Hall (1800s), its retro glamour complements the chef's new spin on brasserie classics, some with trolley or tableside service. Try the råraka, a Swedish potato cake topped with vendace roe, crème fraîche, chives and red onion. Toast Astoria with prawn, king crab and wasabi aioli is also unmissable.

Name: Brasserie Astoria
Description: The former Astoria Cinema, which dates from the 1870s, has been carefully restored and now boasts a bustling brasserie with all the glamour and opulence of yesteryear. Sit at the counter to watch the chefs at work; quality produce is used to create flavoursome modern brasserie classics with the odd Asian influence.

Name: Brasserie Benjamin
Address: Four Seasons Resort Megève, 373 chemin des Follières, Megève, 74120, France
Description: At the foot of Mont d'Arbois, this elegant brasserie within the prestigious Rothschild family hotel tempts skiers, hikers and trail runners with its mouthwatering menu. Sole meunière, Rossini-style beef fillet, Norwegian omelette to share or millefeuille feature alongside linguine with cockles and house-made bottarga, risotto and even vegetarian dishes. Spacious and cosy dining room, attentive service and superb wine list.

Name: Brasserie Blanche
Description: A cosy French restaurant housed in an 18C building which was originally a stable and later spent time as a garage and an interior furnishings store. It has a small front terrace, a bar decorated with wine boxes and a wall made of corks. The chef is a Francophile and creates flavoursome classic French dishes.

Name: Brasserie Boulevard
Description: Brasserie Boulevard pulls out all the stops when it comes to wooing discerning diners. Classy understated luxury meets cosy comfort, with an open fire crackling invitingly in winter and an exquisite terrace outside come summertime. Bouncy Thomas, in charge of the front of house, embodies the venue’s spontaneous, cheerful character. The appealing menu is of the same ilk, blending variety with sensible prices. Begin with appetisers to share: crisp fish fingers with tartare sauce — or an Ostend‑style egg that will take you straight to the coast, followed by a wonderfully comforting vol‑au‑vent. The chefs honour familiar flavours while adding a dash of contemporary inspiration and lashings of infectious enthusiasm.

Name: Brasserie Boulud
Address: Sofitel Dubai The Obelisk, Sheikh Rashid Road - Wafi City, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Creating a little piece of France in Sofitel Dubai The Obelisk is this classically styled brasserie deluxe with its marble flooring, red leather banquettes and art deco touches. In a spacious setting inspired by acclaimed chef Daniel Boulud, the restaurant’s appealing menu offers all the French classics from escargots and canard rôti to tarte Tatin and crêpes Suzette. It also has a good value business lunch.

Name: Brasserie Brixton
Address: 3701 N. Williams St., Denver, CO, 80205, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: The owners of this cozy spot in North Denver drew its inspiration from their love of the casual bistros and wine bars of Montreal, resulting in a certain approachable charm that makes it a neighborhood restaurant par excellence. It also comes through both in the rustic aesthetic, and moreover in the small menu of staples like steak frites with creamy pepper sauce, rib-sticking chicken fricassee with Boursin pomme purée, and comforting French onion soup, alongside more inventive items like blood sausage fried wontons with tamari vinaigrette. There's also an excellent burger. Well-crafted cocktails and a compact but thoughtful list of thirst-quenching natural wines round out the roster.

Name: Brasserie Brugg
Description: In this modern brasserie near the train station, the setting is inviting, sleek and accented with Art Deco touches. Large floor-to-ceiling windows flood the room with light and enhance the welcoming atmosphere. The terrace is lovely too. The cuisine is predominantly French-inspired – modern in its interpretation, precisely executed and packed with flavour. Subtle Asian influences appear here and there. The menu features dishes such as beef tartare with ponzu vinaigrette, or lobster bisque with lemongrass and vanilla, as well as classic and regional specialities such as braised beef cheeks, truffle ravioli, Brussels sprout leaves and pickled beetroot, or Chateaubriand and Tomahawk steak for two or more diners.

Name: Brasserie Bruis
Description: At Bruis, located in the centre of Haarlem, Jozua Jaring of MICHELIN-starred Ratatouille gives the floor to the next generation of culinary talent. Out front, the pavement terrace is all set; inside, the lighting underscores the intimate character of this cosy establishment. The chefs invite you to compose your own set menu from an enticing selection of French-inspired dishes with a contemporary twist. Expect dishes such as pan-seared sea bass with pancetta and a delicately zesty antiboise sauce with fresh herbs. A fitting finale comes in the form of a Paris-Brest featuring silky buttercream, caramel ice cream; a sprinkling of coarse salt rounds off this generous dessert. Get ready to savour indulgent flavours in a relaxed setting.

Name: Brasserie Chavant
Address: 15 chemin de la Croix-de-Montfleury, Corenc, 38700, France
Description: Set in a peaceful park, this third Brasserie Chavant has a large terrace shaded by a 300-year-old cedar tree, facing the tennis courts. The decor, echoing a tennis club vibe, features a green and terracotta checkered carpet, old Roland-Garros posters, vintage rackets and large bay windows. The kitchen brings a contemporary touch to brasserie classics and also serves the same signature dishes as the other restaurants – beef tartare, langoustine ravioli with foie gras and truffles, Angus rib steak with sauce béarnaise.

Name: Brasserie Chavant
Description: Located in a handsome mansion near the Chartreuse cellars, this tastefully redecorated brasserie, which sports a striking white staircase leading up to the first floor, offers a patriotic line-up of Gallic fare, such as velvety Dubarry soup and curry; Mille Pas pâté en croûte; Dauphiné ravioles, among others. Tributes to the bountiful Voiron region abound, hence the melt-in-the-mouth slow-cooked pork belly à la Chartreuse and a decadent iced dessert, also perfumed with green Chartreuse. Delightful welcome and service.

Name: Brasserie Chavant
Description: This establishment bang in the heart of the city impresses with its chic baroque decor. On offer is a lineup of Gallic brasserie favourites (eggs mayonnaise, creamy mushroom soup, beef tartare, Argentinean Angus rib steak, magret of duck in a sauce à l’orange, fish with a beurre blanc and others), together with a selection of more high-flying ingredients such as the house signature: ravioles of langoustine, foie gras and truffles. Chavant was the name of the owner's ancestors, restaurateurs since 1852.

Name: Brasserie Colette Tim Raue
Description: This is MICHELIN-starred chef Tim Raue's take on a French brasserie. The restaurant mirrors the Colette brasseries in Berlin and Munich with an interesting modern dining concept: Diners can order à la carte or compose their own four-course set menu, which can also be vegan. Classics such as beef Wellington (served for two) are available too, as are seasonal dishes. The highlight here is the first-floor terrace overlooking the pedestrian area – but seating is limited, so you'd be well advised to book!

Name: Brasserie Colette Tim Raue
Description: With this concept, Tim Raue has tapped into the zeitgeist. The ambiance feels like that of a French brasserie – stylish yet cosy. Service is well-organised, friendly and attentive, and the delicious food is prepared using select ingredients. Diners can order à la carte or compose their own four-course set menu, which can also be vegan. Classics such as beef Wellington (served for two) are available too, as well as seasonal dishes.

Name: Brasserie Colette Tim Raue
Description: A big name on the fine dining scene, Tim Raue has created a pleasingly down-to-earth brasserie of the sort you might expect to find in Paris. This place has a modern feel tempered by a slight touch of nostalgia. The excellent food comes in the form of an interesting contemporary concept: diners can choose à la carte or put together their own four-course meal – a vegan version is also possible. The menu features classics such as beef Wellington for two and seasonal dishes.

Name: Brasserie Constance
Address: Level 1, Fulham Pier, Stevenage Road, London, SW6 6HH, United Kingdom
Description: It’s not just supporters of Fulham FC that should welcome this sparkling brasserie situated within one of the stands at their Craven Cottage stadium. Part of the wider Fulham Pier development, the terrace has Thames views and there’s a subtle glitz to the design thanks to mirrored walls and Murano chandeliers. The extensive menu ranges from simple omelettes to large sharing plates such as whole butterflied sea bass, while the kitchen excels with classic dishes like pie and mash. Whatever you choose, the cooking uses quality produce that brings plenty of flavour.

Name: Brasserie Constance - Abbaye de Villeneuve
Description: The brasserie of this hotel that has been tastefully refurbished from top to bottom, is set up in a space that is flooded with light through a beautiful glass roof and bay windows overlooking the swimming pool and grounds. The chef presents a menu that combines traditional dishes (e.g. pâté en croûte, egg mayonnaise, fish with beurre blanc sauce, Loire fish quenelle with crayfish bisque) with more modern recipes. We also like the attractive wine list with (very) reasonable prices, especially for the wines from the region.

Name: Brasserie Cuvilliés
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Brasserie fare inspired by Bavarian-Alpine cuisine is the order of the day at the restaurant of the Rosewood Munich hotel. Classic, modern and traditional elements come together here. In the evening, dishes such as bouillabaisse or chicken from Landshut with corn, spinach and a pepper foam grace the menu; at lunchtime, tempting options include "Cuvilliés Burger" or quark pizokel. Wiener schnitzel is a mainstay on the menu. The daily-changing lunch menu with a choice of dishes is also worth perusing. The space has a chic brasserie feel and an open kitchen that can be seen from the dining area. Qu'ils mangent de la Brioche by ceramic artist Angelika Maria Stiegler also draws the eye. In addition, there is the inviting Bar Montez, the winter garden for afternoon tea and the Palaishof terrace. The central location, not far from the Feldherrnhalle and opera house, is perfect for a stroll along the exclusive Theatinerstraße.

Name: Brasserie Côté Cour
Description: This nostalgic brasserie enjoys an idyllic location in the courtyard of Bourglinster Castle, together with a terrace on the ramparts commanding knockout views. The warm welcome is perfectly emblematic of the establishment’s sincerity and hospitality. The food is mostly plant based, but there is also a separate menu including generous fish and meat dishes. The rich velvety cauliflower risotto paired with smoked salmon and crushed hazelnuts is a shining example of this bold, no-holds barred cuisine, which is inspired by the surrounding countryside.

Name: Brasserie Daefnis
Description: It isn’t easy to nab a table in this luxury brasserie, which is always a sign of top-notch quality. Daefnis specialises in first-rate produce: North Sea sole, lamb shoulder and Hereford côte à l'os are just a few of the delicacies that are showcased on the up-to-date brasserie menu. Familiar flavours are nonetheless respected, albeit with judicious nuances.

Name: Brasserie David
Description: The name of David Dewaele’s stylish friendly brasserie doesn’t just refer to his own patronym, but also to his love of David Bowie, whose music can often be heard on the sound system. In his entirely open-plan kitchen, the chef showcases traditional seafood delicacies and a lineup of brasserie classics. The side dishes are creatively crafted and add an extra whoomph to outstanding ingredients of the likes of sole, seabass and shrimp. An example: open fish lasagne of juicy ling in a gutsy bisque sauce with grilled langoustine, Swiss chard and leeks. The market menu is just the ticket to sample Belgian favourites with a sprinkling of originality.

Name: Brasserie Ehrlich
Description: A French-style brasserie par excellence. Stephan Fröhlich and his wife Nadine run their small restaurant with a personal touch – he is the head chef and she is the sommelier. In this cosy setting, diners can look forward to friendly service and good seasonal cuisine in the form of two set menus. Given the popularity of the place, it is advisable to book in advance. In summer the gorgeous terrace beckons. Tip: Delicatessen goods can be purchased to take home. Overnight accommodation available.

Name: Brasserie Fiston
Description: Fiston is a swanky brasserie depicted by a friendly, buzzy vibe. Chef Seynaeve rustles up text-book classics according to best practices. Geert Van Hecke’s pupil sources the best ingredients that he incorporates into home-made recipes. His shrimp fritters, turbot with a signature mousseline sauce and dame blanche dessert hit the spot every time. The suggestions reveal a more modern facet of the chef’s culinary score. Knock-out wine list!

Name: Brasserie Frantzén
Address: Atlantis The Palm Jumeirah, Crescent Road, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This elegant restaurant boasts a dreamy Japanese vibe complemented by an intimate setting on the lower floor of Atlantis The Palm. Moody lighting and deep, comfortable seating adorn the space, with the bar offering light bites and cocktails. The experienced kitchen marry cuisines from Japan, France and Scandinavia, in dishes packed with flavours. Prime ingredients are cleverly enriched by precise seasoning, like complex Scandinavian sushi or a Dover sole with truffle dashi and white soy. Have dessert in the 'Candy Room,' where pastries, candies and homemade sweets are offered.

Name: Brasserie Goeie Louisa
Description: This brasserie is part of the upscale Karel V hotel and shares its medieval charm. Once a monastery, the property has retained its original character, with Delft blue details and tiled floors reinforcing its rustic appeal. The cooking taps into that sense of tradition, with an emphasis on quality produce, classical techniques and carefully considered vegetable accompaniments. A standout example is the vol-au-vent of crisp sweetbreads, generously topped with black truffle and served with aromatic veal broth, flaky puff pastry and leaves of chicory and red endive brightened by a citrus vinaigrette. This is the kind of traditional generosity that food lovers find irresistible. The kitchen remains true to its foundations while retaining just enough vitality to keep things interesting.

Name: Brasserie Hansken
Description: The historic Kvadraturen quarter plays host to many 16th- and 17th-century buildings, as well as this traditional, French-inspired restaurant with a dark-hued terrace overlooking the City Hall Square. Inside, it has a vintage brasserie feel courtesy of parquet flooring, banquette seating, globe lamps and a marble-topped bar – and the cooking follows suit. Classic Gallic dishes such as oysters, French onion soup and côte de bœuf lead the way, complemented by some Nordic elements such as bleak roe, beef tartare and pickled herring. Seafood is a speciality and the wine list is worth exploring.

Name: Brasserie Juste
Description: Back-to-basics brasserie cuisine, fresh ingredients and a chef who adds his own personal touch. “Juste” what it takes to satisfy good food lovers. Even better, the chef is a fan of wood fired Josper ovens. Hand chopped beef tartare with crunchy fries, hearty helpings of vol-au-vent and a made-to-order dame blanche with vanilla ice cream and smothered in chocolate sauce: every dish is a model of culinary generosity. A suitably tasteful trendy interior and an alfresco area overlooking the fields and the vegetable garden.

Name: Brasserie Lamazère
Description: Ready for a dose of French savoir-vivre in Berlin? You almost feel like you are in France here in the heart of Charlottenburg at Brasserie Lamazère thanks to its charming, down-to-earth and lively atmosphere. The regularly changing seasonal dishes are chalked up on the blackboard. You can put together your menu (starter, main, dessert) from a fine selection. They will be happy to recommend a good French wine pairing to accompany your food – the appealing and reasonably priced wine list is proprietor Régis Lamazère's passion.

Name: Brasserie Latem
Description: There is more to this stylish brasserie on the busy Kortrijksesteenweg than you might expect. Chef Van den Bossche's love of Asia is evident throughout the restaurant, from the decor of the izakaya to the lounge-like terrace and the cigar lounge. Although you will find sashimi options and a bento box on the menu, it is dominated by classic fare. Think sumptuous vol-au-vent, onglet à l'échalote and pan-fried ray wing – prepared the way it should be: generously and using the finest ingredients. The extensive wine list is definitely worth exploring!

Name: Brasserie Leonis
Description: Housed in Löwen Hotel Montafon, this brasserie exudes elegance. Warm wood brings an Alpine touch to the clean lines, premium materials, tasteful colour scheme and bold floral decorations. You can also dine at high tables in the bar area, and the terrace is delightful in summer. The menu features classics such as Wiener schnitzel, as well as steaks from the Japanese Yakiniku charcoal grill, plus recommendations from chef Janine Wieland, such as quail coq au vin. The friendly and well-trained front-of-house team is led by sommelier Fabienne Hammer, who gladly assists with wine recommendations – the well-curated wine list is dominated by Austrian labels.

Name: Brasserie Les Deux
Description: If you like a lively, modern bistro, you’ll enjoy the seasonal, international dishes (such as gnocchi with asparagus and black tiger prawns) served here on the ground floor of Les Deux. Alternatively, try one of the “old” or “new” classics such as mini burgers or beef tartare with imperial caviar.

Name: Brasserie Les Trois Rois
Description: In the left wing of hotel Les Trois Rois, this classic, elegant brasserie has tasteful and sophisticated interior decor, with a wonderful view of the Rhine. The food expresses its French and Swiss influences in classic dishes from the cannon, such as beef tartare and sole meunière, but more modern dishes, for instance "loup de mer, green tomato, young artichoke, lemon, verbena", also feature on the menu. The terrific wine selection, too, has a penchant for Switzerland and France. The service is friendly and attentive. Brunch is served on Sundays. Tip: You can look into the kitchen through a window in the corridor leading to reception.

Name: Brasserie Lutetia
Description: Tartare of wild sea bass, sole meunière, Burgundy snails with parsley butter: the famous Brasserie Lutetia proudly serves the classics that have made its reputation, as well as some more contemporary creations. Purists and regulars alike can't get enough of the easy-going refined Art Deco atmosphere. Conservatory, mezzanine or patio: take your pick!

Name: Brasserie Nieuwpoort
Description: This is light years from your run-of-the-mill seaside brasserie! The opulent décor will bowl you over, as will the mixologist who rustles up intriguing cocktails behind the bar. Each dish overflows with generosity and is crafted by gifted, veteran chefs who work with the best ingredients. A range of dishes to share and wholesome brasserie fare. Why not start with a fresh, spicy, acidic ceviche of seabass, before pursuing with a royal vol-au-vent served with piping hot crunchy French fries? THE landmark brasserie of Nieuwpoort!

Name: Brasserie Rongese
Description: This characterful eatery is established in a former cafe in Runskt, a district that was once called Rongese. The owner, Peter Merken, is always on hand with excellent wine and beer tips to pair with the wonderful array of wholesome fare chalked up on the slate.
