Juicy rare entrecote steak with piping hot fries and al dente veggies followed by a Belle Hélène pear with vanilla ice cream and smothered in hot chocolate sauce: you can’t get more traditional than this brasserie score.

Name: Brasserie Roseaux
Description: With this brasserie, Tabata and Ludovic Mey (whose other restaurant, Ombellule, is next door) prove that they have more than one string to their bow. Sit down to classic, bourgeois French cuisine: beef fillet with sauce périgourdine, chicken and veal sweetbread vol-au-vent, turbot with sauce bonne femme, savarin, millefeuille for two, cut and plated tableside… A tempting lunch set menu comes in at a lower price point to complement the high-calibre à la carte menu. The establishment serves the same wine list (around 600 wines) as the fine dining restaurant.

Name: Brasserie RÉGINE
Address: 1F, The St. Regis Osaka, 3-6-12 Hommachi, Chuo-ku, Osaka, 541-0053, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: Casual French dining in St. Regis Hotel Osaka, where prix fixe menus change with the seasons. Supervising the cuisine is the chef from Ryuzu in Tokyo. Classic techniques meet a simple, modern décor and a deep respect for French tradition is reflected in the emphasis on quality ingredients. The house features a spacious interior, mosaic floor and outdoor terrace—de rigueur for a brasserie.

Name: Brasserie Stadthaus
Description: This attractive brasserie with its striking high coffered ceiling and pretty interior courtyard promises a genuine French dining experience. Try the tourte de queue de boeuf (oxtail pie) or the seafood platter followed by the tarte au citron. All the wines are French.

Name: Brasserie Sture 1912
Description: Sture has been an icon of Malmö since 1912, and it’s now been reborn as a classic brasserie with décor to match; think mosaic flooring, closely set tables, a long bar and black-and-white photos of celebrities adorning the walls. A large pavement terrace and bustling atmosphere only add to its appeal, as does an extensive menu mixing Swedish dishes with traditional Western European fare like confit rabbit or salad Niçoise. The lengthy wine list has a similar ‘Old World’ focus.

Name: Brasserie Tafern
Description: Elegant yet accessible – a concept designed with your comfort and well-being in mind, and a wonderful alternative to Epicures, the fine dining restaurant here at the Boutique Hotel Residenz Winkler. Executive Chef Daniel Pape is the man responsible for both kitchens, and the classic and Mediterranean cuisine impresses with its finesse and lightness. It can be sampled from an appealing à la carte selection (eg "artichoke consommé, tomato concassé" or " Senfrostbraten (pork roast with mustard, rainbow vegetables, red onion"), which is complemented by seasonal daily specials. In fine weather, diners can enjoy the view of the Chiemgau Alps from the magnificent terrace (Bergterrasse). Good to know: It opens at 3pm, and at noon on Sundays. Fun fact: The name "Tafern" is a throwback to the establishment's roots – as far back as the early 15C there was a tavern on this site.

Name: Brasserie Taste
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Taste is worthy of its name alone for its spacious, stylish interior, whose picture windows invite nature indoors. This characterful brasserie oozes classy luxury from every pore. Chef Van Hoecke unveils a passion for traditional cuisine and top-notch produce. The score is familiar yet scattered with unexpected international influences as it seamlessly slaloms between crispy shrimp fritters, royal vol-au-vent, fresh tangy ceviche and grilled duck packed in Asian notes. The plating is emblematic of this attention to detail and sense of refinement. There is something for everyone at Taste!

Name: Brasserie Zédel
Address: 20 Sherwood Street, Soho, London, W1F 7ED, United Kingdom
Description: With all its art deco flourishes and distinctively French glamour, Zédel is a restaurant that still delivers a certain expectant excitement as you descend the stairs towards the grand basement brasserie. Expect a roll-call of classic French dishes on the extensive menu, from snails to coq au vin, duck confit to profiteroles. It’s a permanently bustling place with live music and plenty of atmosphere, plus both a cocktail bar and cabaret venue attached.

Name: Brasserie de la Patinoire
Description: A grandiose Normandy-inspired edifice sets the scene for this characterful luxurious brasserie at the entrance to Bois de la Cambre, which can be admired from the spacious terrace. The chef favours nostalgic recipes, with the occasional more modern touch. A patriotic line-up of Belgian brasserie classics takes the limelight on the menu, including shrimp fritters, sole meunière and vol-au-vent. The shellfish bar, open all year round, is heaven for seafood lovers.

Name: Brasserie des Jardins
Description: If only we lived next-door to this modern brasserie… Slick, seamless service, a peaceful patio and a traditional culinary register crafted by expert hands. Gloriously thick fish soup, calf’s kidneys, cooked medium rare, paired with a mustard sauce and crispy fries, or wickedly enticing chocolate ice cream served with fresh cream – to die for! The chef clearly knows his stuff as the varied feast of à la carte delicacies confirms. The knockout wine list further confirms the establishment’s commitment to fine produce.

Name: Brasserie des Jardins - Domaine du Liziec
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: The second dining option at the Domaine du Liziec, this brasserie with bags of character wins diners over with its warm and authentic ambience and generous traditional cuisine. In addition to the weekday set menu, the thoughtfully curated à la carte menu showcases timeless classics such as house foie gras, lamb navarin, kidneys in mustard sauce, sole meunière. Meticulously prepared and bursting with flavour, the dishes are served in a light-filled dining room overlooking the gardens. And if you have to narrow it down to one dessert, the kouign-amann, baked to order until crispy, caramelised and meltingly soft, is pure indulgence.

Name: Brasserie du Château
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: The brasserie is a wonderful addition to the gourmet restaurant ‘Louis’ on the magnificent historic castle estate. Here you can enjoy French brasserie cuisine made from fresh produce, from ‘Beef tartare classique’ and ‘Moules marnière’ to ‘Veal ragout Blanquette de Veau’ or dishes for two, such as ‘Chateaubriand’, in a classic ambience for lunch and dinner. The well-stocked and extensive wine list is the same as that of the ‘Louis’. In summer, the terrace facing the moat under shady old plane trees is an idyllic spot.

Name: Brasserie du Louvre
Description: Take a seat in the sleek, spacious dining hall framed by floor-to-ceiling windows and revel in the quintessential view over Paris: Comédie-Française, Conseil d’Etat, Louvre… The enticing menu cleverly slaloms between hearty victuals of unabashed Lyonnais parentage (hot pistachio sausage in a soft bread roll, pike quenelle and nantua sauce) and timeless brasserie staples (snails in garlic and parsley butter, sole meunière, etc.). The terrace beneath the arcades of this emblematic Haussmannian edifice is sheer bliss in fine weather.

Name: Brasserie du Poisson
Description: This contemporary brasserie close to the lake offers unpretentious cuisine. Fish has the starring role (tuna tartare, perch fillets), as well as hearty traditional recipes such as croûte aux morilles (with morel mushrooms) and veal cutlets. A real treat for the taste buds, particularly as everything (including the bread and ice cream) is homemade.

Name: Brasserie du Quai
Description: The Meuse River is the star of this contemporary establishment, as the splendid view reveals. Take a seat on the terrace or near the floor-to-ceiling windows and treat yourself to traditional brasserie fare crafted by a veteran team. We suggest crunchy shrimp fritters to start, followed by a textbook perfect vol-au-vent, unless you wouldn’t prefer a piece of white cod in a whipped mousseline sauce? Next are the desserts which are equally classical and decadent. The extensive à la carte bill of fare of the Brasserie du Quai is nothing short of irresistible!

Name: Brasserie van Baerle
Description: There is no getting around it: wine is part of the core business of this elegant, ever-inviting luxury brasserie. The impressive selection of wines by the glass and extensive drinks menu will impress even the most seasoned connoisseur. Classics from the brasserie repertoire are served up here with great attention to detail and a sense of generosity. The steak tartare is a real crowd pleaser.

Name: Brasserie à 4 Temps
Description: A modern brasserie extended by a shady terrace, where you can enjoy classics that have been given a new spin by Franck Putelat's former sous-chef. House pâté en croûte, beef tartare, vol-au-vent or cassoulet… Rustic, wholesome fare throbbing with flavour. Book ahead to be sure of a table.

Name: Brassica Restaurant
Address: 4 The Square, Beaminster, DT8 3AS, United Kingdom
Description: A pretty 16th-century house plays host to this sweetly run restaurant, situated in a prime spot overlooking the small square of this characterful Dorset town. Inside, the bright, colourful décor adds to the endearing feel, with its countryside shabby-chic style. The concise, Mediterranean-inflected menu moves with the seasons to show off excellent produce, delivered with a palpable simplicity and textbook technique by the confident kitchen team. If you want to go all-in on the Brassica brand, visit their homewares store, Brassica Mercantile, across the road.

Name: Bratwursthäusle
Description: A trip to Nuremberg wouldn't be complete without trying the city's famous Rostbratwürste! Look no further than this little old stone house on Marktplatz next to Sebalduskirche. Sausages have been sold here since 1312. The interior is rustic and charming, the beechwood barbecue being the centrepiece. Their wonderful sausages are made fresh every morning in their on-site butchery. They are served with sauerkraut and/or potato salad – simply delicious! For the full experience, wash it down with a draught beer. If you're not in the mood for sausages, the menu includes alternatives such as pork shoulder, offal dishes and other snacks. In the summer, the delightful terrace is a popular spot.

Name: Brauereigasthof Aying
Description: The restaurant is part of the picture-perfect Brauereigasthof Hotel Aying is a family-run establishment steeped in tradition and now run by the seventh generation. Diners are treated to warm hospitality in an upscale yet cosy setting. The terrace to the rear of the building is delightful in summer. The menu features exquisite regional and seasonal dishes, crafted from carefully selected produce of the highest quality – the restaurant has its own herd of Pinzgau beef cattle, as well as a hunter, who provides the game. In addition to the selection of fine wines, there are of course Ayinger beer specialities. Good event facilities. Comfortable and tastefully decorated guestrooms available for overnight stays.

Name: Bravo
Description: This buzzy neighborhood spot has no shortage of admirers, and it's not hard to see why, between the friendly, down-to-earth service, thoughtful bar program, and satisfying, lively cooking. The small menu of seafood-centric offerings changes frequently, but bold, punchy flavors are a consistent element. Guests are liable to start with raw items like oysters on the half shell, paired with fermented hot sauce made from red jalapeño, or hiramasa, dry aged in house and served with a passionfruit aguachile and cantaloupe. More substantial options might include seared Hokkaido scallops with coconut, fregola, and kuri squash, or house-made pasta like tagliolini with a Humboldt squid "bolognese," herbed ricotta, and Taggiasca olives.

Name: Bravo
Description: Bravo was opened at the end of 2022 by a young couple on their first venture – and their enthusiasm and friendliness infuse this sweet little restaurant in a converted house. The menu is refreshingly concise and chef-owner Daniel, from his open kitchen, concentrates on clean, seasonal flavours using local ingredients.

Name: Brawn
Address: 49 Columbia Road, Bethnal Green, London, E2 7RG, United Kingdom
Description: Offering a warm welcome and robust, flavour-packed cooking, this is the kind of place everyone needs in their neighbourhood. The passionate team run it with a relaxed, upbeat vibe – sit in the back room to enjoy the buzz from the kitchen – and serve reliably tasty food that evolves with the seasons. The interesting wine list includes a number of organic options, as well as smaller producers and a good choice of orange wines.

Name: Breakers Beach House
Address: Koningin Astrid Boulevard 5, Noordwijk aan Zee, 2202 BK, Netherlands
Description: Welcome to the "Dutch Riviera", where dining with your toes in the sand is sure to give you that holiday feeling. The relaxed terrace affords a wonderful view of the sea, or you can enjoy the trendy brasserie ambience inside. This is the place to come for a plate of ultra-fresh oysters and seafood, followed by classically prepared dishes in which the produce (mainly fish, of course) steals the show. Simple and delicious!

Name: Breakwater Barbecue
Address: 10151 N. Cabrillo Hwy., El Granada, CA, 94018, USA
Description: Just about ten minutes north of Half Moon Bay in the charming seaside town of El Granada, Breakwater Barbecue is an all-American spot tucked inside a historic railroad station. Inside, you'll find a "coastal cowboy" aesthetic, with a friendly, laid-back vibe to match. A signature burger has many admirers, but if you're here with a group, the family-style platters are the way to go, The Texas Trinity serves as the crowning culinary achievement here: an assortment of lovingly slow-smoked brisket, pork ribs and spicy sausage links (made with pork and beef), served with pickles, thick-cut bread and a choice of sides. To accompany, Merle's potato salad and beans and greens are good choices, but a sausage-and-brisket chili braised in smoked pork stock offers its own appeal, especially matched with a miniature cornbread loaf.

Name: Breg
Description: In the heart of Ljubljana’s historic centre, overlooking the Ljubljanica river, Breg welcomes guests in a modern and carefully appointed setting, with light-filled spaces and a pleasant terrace ideal in the warmer months. The gastronomic proposal unites Slovenian roots with international influences, handling ingredients with technique and creativity. It is well worth leaving room for the delectable desserts, among which the plum dumplings with hazelnut mousse are not to be missed.

Name: Bresca
Description: Located close to the marina, this restaurant with a minimalist, contemporary feel has been serving customers now for over two decades (this strong work ethic is to an extent encapsulated by its name which is the Spanish word for “honeycomb”). The couple in charge, Xavier and Alba, conjure up an updated take on traditional cuisine on an à la carte and three menus: the daily “El del día” (available for lunch midweek), Arròs, and Bresca. We particularly enjoyed the crispy pigs’ trotters with black botifarra sausage.

Name: Brett
Address: 321 Great Western Road, Glasgow City, G4 9HR, United Kingdom
Description: Located along Glasgow's thriving Great Western Road is this small, long-standing restaurant with a compact terrace. The dining room features a large counter wrapped around the kitchen where chefs are busy cooking on the open grills. The menu aims to showcase the breadth of Scotland’s larder, in dishes such as barbecued squid with cockles, asparagus, black garlic and sorrel. If you get the chance, the mushroom XO linguine is a must. Natural wines accompany, and there's a relaxed, welcoming feel to the place.

Name: Brewery Bhavana
Address: 218 S. Blount St., Raleigh, NC, 27601, USA
Description: As the name suggests, beer does indeed figure largely here, but don't assume this Raleigh spot is just another pub. There are a number of beers to choose from, including seasonal supplements, but there's nary a burger in sight at this bistro-style restaurant. Instead, expect Chinese cuisine with a selection of dim sum that's perfect for lunch or as appetizers before a feast of their larger plates designed for sharing. Some dishes pack a little more heat than others. Peruse the flowers, local crafts and second-hand books for sale before or after your meal. There is a second location in nearby Fenton.

Name: Brezza fish and chill
Description: An alternative eatery amid the Abruzzo dining options, situated on the beautiful seafront promenade at Soverato. The idea is simple: fish takes centre stage, served in rolls, on "broast" and “friselle” bread, as well as raw or fried, although generous salads and delicious desserts are also available. The ingredients, full of flavour and always simply prepared, result in copious and colourful dishes. Good quality wine is available by the glass, plus a fine choice of cocktails which is enhanced in the evening by the addition of creative home-made options. Friendly female staff, plus excellent background music. A pleasant address serving quality food at very reasonable prices!

Name: Brichs
Description: South of Falset, just behind the beautiful building that houses the town's Cooperative Winery, this restaurant has taken a new direction under the leadership of chef Rafel Muria, who is flying high with his proposal at the award-winning Quatre Molins (in nearby Cornudella de Montsant, about 23 km (15 miles) away). In the dining room, sober yet elegant and with good views of the regional castle-museum that today delves into the history of El Priorat, you will find an à la carte service, a daily set lunch menu and three more tasting menus. We loved the scarlet prawn with potato parmentier ‘Robuchon’!

Name: Bridges
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Fish reigns supreme at this sleek restaurant, which also offers a beautiful view of the canals. Salted delicacies take centre stage in dishes that are distinctly contemporary in style. The chef combines classic sauces with the occasional Asian twist to showcase the fresh flavours of his ingredients.

Name: Brigadiers
Address: 1-5 Bloomberg Arcade, City of London, London, EC4N 8AR, United Kingdom
Description: The army mess clubs of India provide the theme for this large restaurant spread across several rooms on the ground floor of the Bloomberg building. The cooking has a strong live fire element, blending street food dishes and those cooked on the barbecue, like the delicious goat tikki bun kebab. 'Feast' menus are available if you're in a big group and there's a decent selection of beers and whiskies too. It's a perennially busy place and they have several screens for showing sport, so the atmosphere is predictably loud and lively.

Name: Brindo
Description: The service is characterized by a cohesive and friendly team in welcoming guests to their small home. Brindo is an informal reality, where the cuisine is fun, engaging and more than simply territorial: raw foods, tartar and fish of the day are at the top!

Name: Brio
Address: Armenta y López 300, Centro, Oaxaca, 68000, Mexico
Description: With its terraced setting overlooking a church in the center of the city, Brio looks and feels very Oaxacan. It's fitting, then, that the menu echoes the tribute to the region with its focus on local dishes and ingredients given a hint of Mediterranean flair. The wood-fired grill is the centerpiece, with all proteins kissed by the flames. Begin with an appetizer such as the roasted beet salad set atop chile de agua cream sauce and chamomile honey alongside sliced tomatoes and apples. Then, bone-in pork chop benefits from the wood fire, but the peanut mole is the last word. Crème brûlée is given a twist here, infused with poleo for a brightness not often seen.

Name: Brion
Description: With an enviable CV (including Pierre Gagnaire and Jérôme Banctel) under his belt, chef Geoffrey Lengagne has opened this pared-back eatery (polished concrete floor, pale wooden furniture, open kitchen). A champion of seasonal cooking, he uses the freshest ingredients to deliver veggie-, fish- and seafood-centric fare. His modern signature is embodied by marinated cèpe tartlet with figs and cocoa, poultry breast in port wine or agnolotti of squid and braised cod, kohlrabi, pleurotes and a purée of Camus artichokes. The lunch set menu is a bargain - more elaborate lineup in the evening.

Name: Brioude
Description: This endearing family inn has been serving well-crafted food, in which local producers take pride of place, since 1887! The elegant dining room which overlooks the countryside of southern Ardèche provides the perfect foil to sample Claude Brioude’s “Discovery” menu: a new spin on the omelette with Ardèche watercress, gravlax of trout and leeks, trilogy of lamb with a veggie pie…

Name: Brisket & Rice
Description: Chef Hong Tran originally cooked brisket as a backyard hobby but now finds himself running this bustling restaurant with his family in the greater Houston area. Long lines move quickly through this well-oiled operation, which previously shared a parking lot with a gas station just down the road. Practically everyone is here for the same thing, and Tran’s signature dish is a reflection of his Lone Star upbringing and Vietnamese roots: Jasmine fried rice tossed with fried egg and Chinese sausage packs proper wok flavor, and each order can come with two prime, melting slabs of brisket. No need to bother with the sides when you can fill up on the pork ribs, which are beautifully tender and delicately smoked.

Name: Bristol
Description: This bright, spacious brasserie on the seafront has been a landmark of Knokke-Heist for aeons. Expertly prepared Belgian classics are the specialities of the house. Think crispy shrimp croquettes (said to be the best around!) and pan-seared sole with a tartar sauce prepared à la minute. The chef loves working with North Sea fish, but also has a passion for meat dishes and seasonal specialties, such as hop shoots with mousseline sauce. These timeless brasserie classics are simply irresistible!

Name: Bristol Lido
Address: Oakfield Place, City of Bristol, BS8 2BJ, United Kingdom
Description: This unique restaurant boasts a charming and highly enviable location, directly overlooking a restored Victorian lido. Snack on small plates in the poolside bar, or head up to the first-floor former viewing gallery, where the retractable floor-to-ceiling doors and Mediterranean-inspired cooking will have you feeling like you're on holiday. Dishes such as St Ives Bay crab tagliatelle with lobster butter, pangritata and chives look simple but are full of bright, fresh flavours thanks to the quality of the ingredients and the skill of the chefs.

Name: Brisé
Address: 8 Lane 92, Section 1, Jianguo North Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: With a rich background in French cuisine, the chef weaves Western cooking techniques with Asian ingredients, crafting dishes that are simple in appearance yet meticulous in detail. The menu changes every three months and reflects the seasons well. In winter, for instance, the lamb main course is marinated with spices such as cardamom and cinnamon, imparting unforgettable, rich flavours. For lunch on weekdays, a shorter set menu is available with optional add-ons. The room is modern with an open kitchen, so diners can watch the cooking unfold.

Name: Bro's
Address: 36 rue de la Foulerie, Blois, 41000, France
Description: This eatery in the historic town just a stone’s throw from the banks of the Loire, which has quickly been taken by storm by the locals, is the brainchild of two enthusiastic cooks and inseparable pals. The scene upstairs sports a stylish rustic interior with contemporary touches, providing the perfect foil to a bistronomic score that shines the spotlight on locally sourced, seasonal ingredients, naturally washed down with Loire wines. Tapas inspired by the produce of south-west France and Spain are also available (evenings only and without reservations) in the ground-floor room.

Name: Broadway
Address: Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental Hotel, West Corniche Road, Al Ras Al Akhdar, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Counter dining,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This modern, American brasserie located in the Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental hotel is perfect for a lively evening in a Broadway-inspired setting. Combined with a DJ, live music on Saturday night, sharp service by a well-drilled team and a concise menu delivering a roll call of classics, you’ve got the ingredients for a glamourous night out with friends. The experienced chef delivers comforting dishes such as omelette Arnold Bennett, lobster bisque and their signature beef Wellington to share. Don’t miss steaks cooked to perfection and the glorious tart Tatin. They also offer a brunch on Saturday and a traditional roast on Sunday.

Name: Brodeto
Address: 2201 Iron Works Dr., Ste. 137, Raleigh, NC, 27604, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Brodeto occupies the ground floor of the former Raleigh Iron Works (RIW), now home to a hub of eateries, retail outlets and offices. The name, a nod to a fish stew found along the Adriatic coast, is the first hint that this restaurant takes its inspiration from the cuisines of Italy and Croatia. From crudo and must-have pasta dishes to wood-fired fish and meat to peka, a Croatian slow-cooked, fire-grilled dish with octopus and potatoes, and of course, the namesake brodeto, this menu is packed with appealing choices. You won't go wrong with any of the selections, but be sure to consult the wine list, where no region of Italy is neglected and special growers and vintages are highlighted.

Name: Broederenklooster
Description: The authenticity of this former monastery (1293) has been preserved in every detail. Where once the friars used to take their meals, you can now enjoy a luxurious dining experience in a historical setting. The ultra-modern open kitchen immediately catches the eye. Niels van Dooijeweert brings a penchant for bold flavours and contemporary techniques to French dishes. Succulent pan-seared sea bream with a brunoise of tomato, papaya, onion and pak choi, in a curry sauce finished with lemon oil – this is the kind of cooking that draws so many diners; exceptional ingredients take the spotlight. The lovely guestrooms are perfect for a good night's rest.

Name: Broeding
Description: This lively restaurant is an institution in Neuhausen. In an outwardly unassuming-looking building on a residential street, diners tuck into delicious, pared-back dishes made with excellent ingredients (mostly organic or Demeter-certified) sourced in the Alpine and pre-Alpine regions. From Mon-Thu, diners can opt for a three- to five-course version of the set menu; Fri-Sat, there is just the one five-course variant – or if you arrive at 6pm, you can go for the three-course early evening set menu. The pleasingly laid-back atmosphere is in no small part down to the friendly, attentive and unpretentious service, which comes complete with expert guidance when it comes to the terrific wine list, which focuses on Austrian wine-growing regions. In summer, the secluded inner courtyard terrace beckons. Tip: From 3pm onwards, Austrian wines can be purchased from the well-stocked wine shop to enjoy at home.

Name: Broken Spanish Comedor
Address: 12565 Washington Blvd., Los Angeles, CA, 90066, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Valet parking
Description: Who doesn't love a good comeback story? Chef/owner Ray Garcia's Broken Spanish Comedor is a reincarnation of his former restaurant, resurrecting signature favorites alongside a menu of nostalgic-yet-elevated Mexican cooking with bold flavors. The menu isn't huge, but it has plenty of hits, as evidenced by the crowds that flock here (definitely make reservations). Start the meal with botanas like kanpachi ceviche or their aguachile negro with bay scallops before moving into starters like the roasted mushroom, spinach and honeynut squash tamal en cazuela. Don't even think about skipping their signature dish — crispy pork belly chicharron in a garlic mojo sauce is a must.

Name: Brook
Description: International, German and classical influences are at play here, e.g. loin of lamb with string beans and Parmesan potatoes or venison with Brussels sprouts and chestnuts. In the evening, the beautifully illuminated Speicherstadt opposite is a sight to behold!

Name: Bros'
Address: SS172, zona G, 59, Martina Franca, 74015, Italy
Description: Overlooking the town square since 1968, this venue is now under new management, which has refreshed its direction while remaining faithful to its original character. The offering remains steadfastly anchored to a classic, clear and fragrant seafood cuisine, built upon superior-quality ingredients – with especial attention to raw preparations – and executed with meticulous care and precision. The experience is enhanced by several distinct advantages: private parking, a prime location just beyond the bustling town centre yet directly by the sea, a charming front garden and a spacious veranda-style dining room, fully openable and roof-retractable in fine weather. Throughout, one theme prevails: the constant call of the sea salt air.

Name: Brown Bear
Address: Two Mile House, Kildare, W91 PWH5, Ireland
Description: The village may seem appealingly sleepy, but this is an area renowned for the breeding and training of some top racehorses. The building sits on what was once part of the owner’s family dairy farm, with a lively locals’ bar on one side and a smart bistro on the other. The menu offers a mix of classical dishes and those displaying subtle international flavours, and there is a reassuring confidence to the service.

Name: Browns Bonds Hill
Address: 1 Bonds Hill, Waterside, Londonderry, BT47 6DW, United Kingdom
Description: The flagship of the Browns group sits on the east bank of the River Foyle and comes with a plush lounge and an intimate, art deco style dining room. The artful modern cooking is elaborate in its techniques and combinations and represents good value for money.

Name: Brugarol Barcelona
Description: Brugarol is tucked away in one of the narrow streets of the Gothic Quarter, a district with lots of culinary competition. This small but interesting dining space defines itself as a “tapas bar with the soul of an izakaya”, where chef Angelo Scirocco's cuisine combines Japanese techniques with Mediterranean ingredients (many of these, such as cheese, sobrasada and even wine, are sourced from his own farm in Palamós). Discover their tasting menus at the bar, where you can watch each dish being prepared!

Name: Brugmann
Description: If you fancy a slap-up meal in southwest Brussels, make a beeline for this fancy brasserie adorned with modern art and boasting a lovely alfresco space at the rear. Brugmann offers an extensive choice of pedigree Gallic dishes at lunchtime and in the evening. Traditional recipes are treated to modern, particularly Asian, interpretations, such as langoustine in a tempura of crunchy walnuts with a sweet and sour bisque sauce.

Name: Bruma Wine Garden
Address: Bruma Wine Resort, Valle de Guadalupe, Carr. Avinicola La Cetto, Fraccionamiento, A-B, P74, Francisco Zarco, Ensenada, 22760, Mexico
Description: Run by Chef David Castro Hussong, this spot is located on the Bruma winery property. Entirely outside, the lovely tree-covered space welcomes guests to take a seat at the oversized communal table or a few smaller tables flanking the sides. A contemporary menu echoes the casual setting. Starters like ceviche or cauliflower with mole are followed up by hearty main dishes like short rib with shiitake and noodles. The pizzas are a popular choice, and though far from traditional Italian, the Mexican spin (think tender beef birria with chile morita) are very successful. Don't sleep on dessert, especially the flaky banana tart that delivers on flavor and, like many other dishes, is sized for sharing.

Name: Brunelli's
Address: Bencomo 42, Puerto de la Cruz, 38400, Spain
Description: A splendid steakhouse located close to the entrance to the Loro Parque zoo. This family-run restaurant is a must on the island for meat-lovers given its choice of top-quality meat, with the advantage of many being aged on the premises. Make sure you try Brunelli's steak tartare, its signature speciality, or one of its superb cuts of grilled meat (Uruguayan beef entrecôte, Nebraskas Black Angus T-Bone, German Simmental ribeye, Chateaubriand and Spanish Tomahawk), many of which are sold by weight and designed for two people to share. The particularly impressive picture window here overlooks the sea.

Name: Brunnauer
Description: In the lovely historical setting of Villa Ceconi, Sybille and Richard Brunnauer's restaurant is the place to experience fantastic Austrian-style hospitality and cuisine. The dishes draw on French and international influences but give pride of place to the region and the seasons. Shining examples are the Styrian Alpine prawns with Marchfeld asparagus and creamed peas, or Tauern lamb with potato and leek mash and wild cauliflower. There are also vegan options. Everything is freshly prepared using premium ingredients. The themed speciality weeks are worth seeking out – from "Veal Offal Specialities" and "Fish & Shellfish" to "Truffle Specialities", seasonal classics take centre stage. Well-curated wine list. Tip: reasonably priced lunch set menu. The stylish modern interior is also attractive and the view of the fortress from the terrace is fabulous!

Name: Brunnenstuben
Description: Don’t be put off by the somewhat unprepossessing exterior at Brunnenstuben because the food is excellent! Petra and Thorsten Beyer – she running the kitchen, he managing the friendly and professional front-of-house team – serve flavoursome Swabian fare including an excellent Zwiebelrostbraten (roast beef with onions).

Name: Bruno Oteiza
Description: A restaurant with the feel of a speakeasy? Curiously, this one is hidden inside another one (it's in the basement of the Gatxupa), so in a way it gives off that aura of mystery and secrecy. In this modern space, with a large kitchen open to the dining room, chef Bruno Oteiza seeks a mestizo gastronomic experience based on a fusion of contemporary Basque and Mexican cuisine, mainly based on high-quality local produce. The tasting menu is complemented by a larger version called Amakase (a nod to the idea of omakase menus but playing on the word ‘ama’, which recalls a mother’s cooking).

Name: Brustin
Address: No. 301, 3F, Building 21, Art Park, No.111, Section 1, North Third Ring Road, Jinniu, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
Description: Chefs Bruce and his partner Justin opened Brustin in 2023 in a design-forward space in line with the artistic flair of the Tianfu Art Park complex that houses it. The dinner prix-fixes have 12 to 15 courses, re-interpreting Sichuan cuisine with Western techniques and an emphasis on seasonality. Diners can take home the paper menu, which features illustrations by local artists. Exquisite food is matched by the professional service of the servers and sommelier.

Name: Brut maison de cuisine
Description: This tasty bistro with a contemporary feel has an open kitchen, shelves filled with jars of fermented vegetables and books… and just a handful of tables, so it's best to book. The chef, who has a solid track record, devises a short menu that changes regularly. The three pillars of his cooking are seasonality, local ingredients (such as Racan poultry) and modern, often bold cuisine, for example his dessert that combines a naturally sweet Jerusalem artichoke cream and a coffee ice cream with a pronounced flavour. Short list of natural and organic wines.

Name: Brut, Table de saison
Description: On a narrow pedestrian street that gently slopes down to the beach, this discreet place holds its cards close to its chest. Front of house, Justine is from Le Touquet; in the kitchen is Alexis, who learned the ropes in Lille (Le Cerisier, La Laiterie). Together, they craft vibrant cuisine that is rooted in the Basque terroir and dotted with surf and turf references: a crispy cylinder of black pudding and langoustine, beef tartare and fried baby squid, red mullet accompanied by superb cecina from León. The desserts are just as accomplished!

Name: Brutal
Description: On a peaceful street corner in Lyon's Presqu'île neighbourhood, this neo-bistro has stylish credentials: a counter with a few seats, raw concrete pillars, an open kitchen behind an industrial-style glass partition, dim lighting, and electronic music playing softly. Chef Alban Joriot (Têtedoie, Le Neuvième Art, L'Établi) turns out seasonal dishes featuring clever flavour combinations, executed with precision and bags of character. Think white radish marinated in chilli, house-made pita, tempura vegetables; stone bass stuffed with wild garlic, braised sucrine lettuce, smoked tarama. There is a simpler set menu at lunchtime; more ambitious cuisine in the evening. A top-quality restaurant with a laid-back, trendy vibe: brutal by name, refined by nature!

Name: Brutal
Address: Avenida General Belgrano 1129, Mendoza, M5500, Argentina
Description: This centrally located restaurant draws attention to itself right from the outset thanks to the designer decor of large branches on the façade, a theme repeated on the ceilings of its meticulously appointed interior. The concept is the brainchild of Leonardo Hoffman, the executive chef, who, through a multi-course tasting menu, who promises an experience that is 'wild and primitive' (including a huge rib of beef to be eaten with your hands, hence the provision of gloves and a bib!). Although the majority of dishes here are cooked on the grill, you’ll still find plenty of creativity and technique, something that is especially evident in the intense sauces on offer. Interestingly, they work closely with local producers, age their own products using the Japanese shio koji fermentation technique, and incorporate smoke into the dining experience through direct interaction between the grill and the diner.

Name: Bruun
Description: The cuisine of brothers Ruben and Pieter is as elegant as the decor of their restaurant, whose entirely open-plan kitchen cannot fail but catch the eye. They have a knack for melding French technique with a modern, minimalist vision. Food that is free of fussy frills and in which every detail demonstrates a focus on gutsy flavours, like the scallops arranged like flower petals with radish, green apple and a natural apple and shiso dressing. At noon, the chefs roll out a lunchtime menu, while the evening score is more ambitious.

Name: Bruut
FacilitiesAndServices: Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: The initial impression of romanticism conjured up by the wisteria-clad historic edifice in which Bruut is located, quickly gives way to a rough, graffiti-adorned, almost brutal interior that is emblematic of its high-profile chef. Bruno Timperman sources most of his produce within a 30km radius of the restaurant to craft a single surprise menu that elegantly showcases his unconventional creativity and technical ingenuity. A few examples include a pizza meets tartlet dish that blends characteristic Mediterranean flavours of the likes of tomato and burrata with the strong distinctive taste of venison, cooked medium rare, and a gutsy gravy. An unorthodox chef and score, backed by a fine cellar of organic and natural wines.

Name: Bryghuset Vendia - Gourmet
Description: A microbrewery plays host to a stylish brasserie and this tiny gourmet restaurant, which consists of just three tables. It serves an 11 course themed surprise menu of creative, elaborately presented dishes designed to stimulate the taste buds.

Name: Bryn Williams at Porth Eirias
Address: The Promenade, Colwyn Bay, LL29 8HH, United Kingdom
Description: If it's a stunning setting you're after, this striking beachside brasserie delivers in spades. Providing gorgeous views over the water, the dining room is in an enviable spot, and is decorated with a faux-industrial style and blue leather banquettes. The eponymous chef oversees a menu of unfussy dishes utilising plenty of local seafood, such as the fish fingers made using the daily catch. The service is efficient and the atmosphere is relaxed and friendly, with the restaurant's popularity lending it a welcome buzz.

Name: Bryn Williams at Theatr Clwyd
Address: Raikes Lane, Mold, CH7 1YA, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Another success from the eponymous restaurateur, this modern British brasserie sits on the first floor of the Theatr Clwyd performing arts centre, with floor-to-ceiling windows that offer wonderful views of the Clwydian Range mountains. Welsh produce is the bedrock of the sensibly priced menu, including Williams’ own pedigree Welsh Black beef, which you could find in both crisp, flavoursome croquettes and a beef, onion and mushroom pie to share. The friendly service team run the place smoothly with a welcoming charm.

Name: Brücke
Description: The superb location on the River Aare is a big draw here, and it goes without saying that a spot on the terrace is highly prized! The food is fresh and aromatic, with emphasis laid squarely on the quality and seasonality of the produce. The "Tavolata" set menu, which also has a vegetarian counterpart, includes starters to share, a palate cleanser and a choice of different main courses. There is also an à la carte menu, reprising, for example, the starter selection from the set menu.

Name: Buabok
Address: Amanpuri Resort 118, 1 Si Sunthon Road, Pansea Beach, Choeng Thale, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
Description: Buabok is set in a tranquil resort that features reflective pools and swaying palms, creating the perfect backdrop for dining. Enjoy aromatic Thai cuisine beneath the pitched roof of an elegant wooden villa. From Thai salads to smooth curries, the menu is crafted from fresh local produce. Arrive before sunset to embrace the gentle pace of nature and stunning views of the Andaman Sea. Don't miss their rich, flavourful Panaeng Nuea, an Angus beef red curry.

Name: Bubala
Address: 65 Commercial Street, Spitalfields, London, E1 6BD, United Kingdom
Description: The Bubala brand may now have spread out to other sites in the city, but this compact Spitalfields spot is where the journey started. It's a simple, rustic place inside – with a green-tiled bar that nods to East London traditions – while the kitchen has a similarly straightforward approach in its flavoursome sharing plates of vegetarian Middle Eastern cuisine. Dips and flatbreads, falafel, potato latkes and the signature oyster mushroom skewers can be found on a menu elevated by the chefs' delicate spicing. At dinner, the à la carte gives way to a 'Bubala Knows Best' set menu.

Name: Buca di Sant'Antonio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Just a stone’s throw from Piazza San Michele, in the heart of the beautiful historic centre of Lucca, the Buca di Sant'Antonio dates back over 200 years and is one of the city’s oldest restaurants. Here, the old copper pots and pans that hang from the ceiling add to the warm, romantic atmosphere, while the cuisine unsurprisingly showcases traditional Tuscan specialities including meat dishes and home-made pasta.

Name: Bucado
Description: Brazilian chef Danielle Barbosa (winner of MasterChef Brazil 2020) is now alone at the helm of Bucado, in the location that used to be home to Būbo. To be enjoyed in an interior decorated with a colourful fresco inspired by South American flora, her dishes have a distinct character combining modern techniques (lacto-fermentation, fish maturation) and Brazilian influences (condiments and spices, cassava, tapioca etc). One of the set menus is vegetarian; classic cocktails. Attentive service with a smile immediately puts you at ease!

Name: Bucha
Address: 26/156 Chao Fah Tawan Ok Road, Chalong, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: Southern Thai soul surges through this gallery-like space, its wooden tables framed by soft light and glinting ranks of Buddha images and Luang Pu Thuat amulets. House-made curry pastes drive dishes that roar with the spicy and mildly sour hallmarks of the South. Highlights include yellow curry, fresh herb salads and crisp local fish draped in pungent budu sauce. As portions are generous and meant for sharing, gather your friends and taste a variety of dishes.

Name: Budnamujip
Description: Since 1977, this family-style restaurant has garnered an appreciative following of barbecue lovers, often seeing three generations of loyal patrons from one family frequenting the shop. A popular locality for residents south of the river, it specializes in various cuts of meat exclusively from the cow including ribs, sirloin and tripe. The rich flavors of the exceptionally tender meat is enhanced simply with quality bay salt.

Name: Buerehiesel
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This picturesque, half-timbered 17C farmhouse was reconstructed stone by stone in the Orangerie Park, next-door to the Council of Europe. The conservatory dining room and patio command a bucolic view of this leafy haven. The menu features some of the house signature dishes, such as frog’s legs sautéed in chervil or free-range pullet roasted in a casserole dish (backeoffe), together with more contemporary seasonal recipes.

Name: Buff On
Description: Start with a drink in the adjacent bar, then move on to this elegant space where comfy leather chairs, black tables and black walls create a cool, contemporary vibe; for larger groups ask for one of the appealingly intimate round booths. Meat is the cornerstone of the menu, with the steaks primarily sourced from the USA, but you can also expect the likes of lamb chops, duck breast and veal. Equal care goes into side dishes such as the roasted baby potatoes with beetroot cream or the grilled vegetables that include padrón peppers and meaty mushrooms.

Name: Buffet de la Gare
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: An old-fashioned restaurant of the type that is quite hard to find these days. It has Art Deco-style wood panelling, enamel plaques and coloured windows, as well as a terrace overlooking the surrounding greenery. There is also a traditional feel to the menu, which includes perch from Lake Geneva.

Name: Bugenvila
Address: Put dr. Ante Starčevića 9, Cavtat, 20210, Croatia
Description: A delightful establishment situated in the picturesque bay opposite the harbour of Cavtat, distinguished by a splendid terrace entirely covered in jasmine and bougainvillea. The menu is rich and varied: offerings range across meat, fish, and vegetarian options, all prepared with excellent local produce. At lunch, a generous selection of colourful and appealing salads is also on offer. Booking is decidedly advisable.

Name: Buitenplaats Slangevegt
Description: The River Vecht is the star of the show at this warm and welcoming restaurant – the spacious riverside terrace alone is reason enough to book a table! Further enhancing the charm is the attentive service. The cuisine is playful and creative – classic combinations are revamped with inventive ideas and refined textures. The chef serves cold veal, for example, with a vibrant ensemble of sweet-and-sour accompaniments such as marinated vegetables, tempeh manis and grated coconut. He likes to create contrasts, for instance by introducing a spicy note into his sauces.

Name: Buko Nero
Description: Diners flock to this small neighbourhood joint and it’s easy to understand why: the bubbly, charming hostess works seamlessly with her husband chef from Veneto, who in turn delivers simple, delicious Italian fare with subtle Asian twists. Try his tau kwa tower – an appetising mix of sautéed Italian-style greens and Singaporean dried tofu salad in a tangy Asian dressing. Hand-made pasta is another highlight, as are the weekly specials.

Name: Bull & Last
Address: 168 Highgate Road, Dartmouth Park, London, NW5 1QS, United Kingdom
Description: Hearty British dishes which are big on flavour are the order of the day at this sympathetically refurbished Victorian pub. The ground floor bar has a lively buzz and the more sedate first floor dining room opens later in the week. The terrific mushroom tempura is a prime example of what this kitchen does well: straightforward, moreish dishes that come in generous portions. Lovely bedrooms and a friendly, attentive team complete the picture.

Name: Bulle
Description: Chef Guy Lassausaie masterminded the stylish top to toe refurbishment of this restaurant in a former Jesuit seminary (1853). You enter through a bar which boasts a jaw-dropping panoramic terrace, before heading downstairs into the restaurant, passing by the building’s Gallo-Roman foundations on the way! A swish, historic interior (crystal lighting, parquet floors and a view of the kitchen) sets the scene for colourful seasonal food, such as brook trout, fennel and seasonal mushrooms…

Name: Bullerei
Description: The interior of the heritage-listed cattle hall of the former abattoir in Hamburg's Schanzenviertel is quite unique – exposed concrete and brick walls, visible ventilation pipes, stylish, comfortable chairs and benches set around wooden tables, and all manner of decorative details, such as comic-book figurines, pictures and lamps, combine in the airy, high-ceilinged space to create a truly individual blend of industrial architecture and trendy, high-grade style. Diners can also sit on bar stools at the large counter. The modern cuisine makes a strong case for itself, not least with its various grilled cuts of meat. At lunchtime, the front section of the restaurant operates as "Deli", with a shorter, simpler menu.

Name: Bunch of Grapes
Address: 14 Silver Street, Bradford-on-Avon, BA15 1JY, United Kingdom
Description: The Bunch of Grapes might be the oldest pub in this historic town but it now comes with an appealing modern edge and a deli selling tempting treats. Downstairs has a pubby feel, while upstairs has more of a restaurant vibe, and you can have anything from a burger to an ambitious tasting menu.

Name: Burdell
Description: Chef Geoff Davis named this nostalgic, homy Temescal spot after his grandmother, whose cooking informs his own fresh personal take on soul food. The small menu is a blend of staples like collard greens and fried chicken (though these are tweaked with the addition of berbere and pickle brine, respectively), novelties like an appetizer of chicken liver mousse with cornmeal waffle, and more broadly contemporary, Southern-inflected fare like a halibut crudo with buttermilk and grapefruit, or dry-aged duck with cherry "drippings" and dirty rice. Desserts follow a similar style, like strawberry shortcake with strawberry rhubarb jam and sorghum whipped cream. A particularly thoughtful wine list offers a wealth of options for afficionados, and who doesn’t love fried chicken with champagne?

Name: Burg Nideggen - Brockel Schlimbach
Description: What is it that makes this place stand out? For one thing, the location in a 12C castle above Nideggen in the middle of the Eifel National Park. For another, the attractive interior: a small period dining room in which plenty of beautiful woodwork as well as modern design details make for a truly unique setting. Last but not least comes the cuisine of owner Herbert Brockel and Tobias Schlimbach, whose names the restaurant bears. Their dishes are inspired by classical and Mediterranean cooking and based on carefully selected, mostly regional ingredients chosen according to the seasons. The set menu is available in four to six courses. The friendly waitstaff also gladly recommend the perfect wine match.

Name: Burg Nideggen - Kaiserblick
Description: This eatery is a good alternative to the Brockel Schlimbach restaurant at Nideggen's centuries-old castle, Burg Nideggen. They serve market-based cuisine in the form of regional dishes, prepared from fresh seasonal ingredients mainly sourced from suppliers and producers in the region. The interior decor is modern and the front-of-house team is very friendly and obliging. Weather permitting, you can dine on the pretty terrace in the castle courtyard.

Name: Buri Omakase
Description: Behind the term ‘buri’, which could be translated as ‘lemon fish’, hides one of the most interesting Japanese restaurants in Palermo Hollywood! Anyone familiar with Japan and with the challenges faced when setting up a restaurant will appreciate the complexities posed by Buri Omakase, where you have to ring the bell to property 002 in a small office block, and are then escorted by lift up to the authentically decorated dining room with seating for just 6 guests and an exclusive bar, where the bartender prepares both classic and signature cocktails. Chef Marcello Elefoso is inspired more by the traditions of Kyoto than Edomae, hence the prevalence of dishes prior to the nigiri courses, including an excellent miso soup and a creamy chawanmushi (savoury egg custard). For the nigiri, this chef uses high-quality local fish caught by trusted fishermen, most of them aged for a more powerful flavour. They work in two shifts, so try to be on time!

Name: Buriani dal 1967
Address: Via Matteotti 66, Pieve di Cento, 40066, Italy
Description: A family-run restaurant in the province of Bologna with an excellent reputation for good food. Whether you choose one of the fish-based recipes or meat dishes, you’ll enjoy cuisine with a balance of classic flavours and modern influences, including a few regional specialities.

Name: Burmatown
Address: 18 Tamalpais Dr., Corte Madera, CA, 94925, USA
Description: Head straight for the authentic Burmese dishes at this out-of-the-way spot. A nutty, crunchy and flavorful tea leaf salad with cabbage, dried shrimp, peanuts and fish sauce is the perfect answer to a hot summer day, while hearty spiced potato-stuffed samosas and fresh, springy egg noodles tossed with barbecue pork and fried garlic chips will warm your soul in the cooler months. Given the high quality of its food, it’s no surprise that Burmatown is Corte Madera’s most popular neighbor: it’s big with local families from the surrounding residences who pack every single table, attended to by warm servers. If you’re willing to make a special trip to this charming bright-orange bungalow, the laid-back vibe will have you feeling right at home.

Name: Burro
Address: 2 Floral Court, Floral Street, Covent Garden, London, WC2E 9FB, United Kingdom
Description: Fans of Trullo in Islington will be pleased to know that chef and co-owner Conor Gadd has opened his own Italian restaurant, this time in the more central and tourist-centric surroundings of Covent Garden. This space is bigger and more elegant, with high ceilings and a terrace that makes the most of the secluded courtyard in which it’s located. ‘Burro’ means butter – and plenty of it is used to cook the lovely crisp vitello. Fried artichoke with bottarga is a great way to start; fettucine with duck and porcini ragu is the pick of the pasta; and it’s hard to see beyond the tiramisu doughnuts for dessert.

Name: Busarin Cuisine
Address: 133 Rattanakosin Road, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
Description: Dining here feels like being welcomed into Chef Noi’s home. With its high ceilings, collection of fine chinaware, and green leather sofa booths set against light pink walls, the space feels both warm and elegant. The menu offers northern Thai dishes based on family recipes, with noodles and roti taking the place of rice. The standout is streaky pork, braised in hang le curry for two days, releasing an enticing aroma of ginger and spices. A delightful selection of authentic Thai desserts rounds off a truly memorable dining experience.

Name: Butcher & Still
Address: Four Seasons Al Maryah Island Hotel, 2 Global Market Street, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Those who like a classic steakhouse will find this one at the luxurious Four Seasons ticks all the boxes. Leather banquettes? Check. Prime American beef? Check. Great cocktails? Check. Start with the generously proportioned crab cake before diving into a steak – there are plenty on offer, from ribeye to porterhouse. To finish, there’s New York cheesecake of course, but the more adventurous should take on the challenge of the Tribune Tower chocolate cake.

Name: Butcher's Block
Address: Raffles Arcade, #02-02, 328 North Bridge Road, 188719, Singapore
Description: Wood-fire cooking is the speciality of this dark and handsome restaurant within Raffles hotel. Head straight to the tasting menu if you want to experience a variety of top-quality fish and meat dishes, all expertly prepared using American wood and supplemented with Asian flavours. The moodily lit room ensures your gaze never wanders too far from the open kitchen. A restaurant to appeal to the hunter-gatherer in all of us.

Name: Butcher's Dining
Description: The cosy restaurant of butcher shop De Laet & Van Haver is a veritable paradise for carnivores. Faced with such an array of delectable options, from Secreto 07 and entrecôtes of aged meat to traditional stews and offal, you'll be spoilt for choice. The carefully considered trimmings are a testament to the butcher's commitment to quality and craftsmanship. Think beautifully marbled cut of Simmental beef, simply seasoned with coarse salt and rosemary, and served with a tomato salad and a lightly whipped béarnaise sauce. What a feast!

Name: Butchery & Wine
Description: The name of this busy modern bistro says it all; the emphasis is on steaks, which are dry-aged for a minimum of 28 days in their glass-fronted ageing fridges. The cuts are then skilfully cooked in the Bertha oven, where temperatures can reach up to 500°C. Try a Polish cut or one imported from further afield, accompanied by a glass of red wine. Non-steak dishes might include spring rolls, homemade black pudding or grilled squid.

Name: Butchery & Wine
Description: Sister to the long-standing Warsaw operation and following the same tried-and-tested mantra, this well-run restaurant does what it says on the tin. Order a bottle from the wine list and take your pick of the local meats, from terrific homemade black pudding to a range of steaks cooked on the grill; the fish cookery is equally adept, meaning there’s plenty of choice. If you’re on a budget, the lunch menu offers brilliant value for money.

Name: Buxbaum
Description: This lovingly run restaurant is tucked away in the Heiligenkreuzerhof, a Cistercian monastery dating back to the 12C, and its assortment of pretty dining rooms creates a genuinely cosy, welcoming atmosphere. The lovely tranquil courtyard terrace is also not to be overlooked, and the charming service is the icing on the cake. On the menu: internationally inspired dishes and Austrian classics – think wild red prawn with rhubarb, nasturtium and sweet potato, or Wiener schnitzel served with potato and lamb's lettuce salad, lingonberries and lemon. Tip: wines from selected Austrian vintners.

Name: Bu’ul
Address: Chablé Maroma, Carr. Federal Cancún - Tulum, Punta Maroma Km. 51, Playa del Carmen, 77710, Mexico
Description: A journey through the jungle, past the private villas that make up the Chablé Maroma, will bring you to this enclave, serving singular cuisine that celebrates native ingredients and flavors. To that effect, sophisticated permutations of corn, beans, and chiles are threaded through the menu, as in a pickled Venison with crispy potato straws and a tableside pour of recado rojo. A main course of luxurious creamy rice — enriched with Ocosingo cheese and accented with nutty, herbaceous pipián verde alongside earthy venison longaniza — offers an unapologetically Mexican answer to risotto. Finish with a wonderfully intense molten cake of Oaxacan chocolate, ideally paired with a sip of mezcal.

Name: By Taste
Description: The village of Eys is sometimes referred to as the Tuscany of Limburg and, sitting on the tree-shaded terrace, looking out across the undulating countryside with a drink in hand, you can see why! Inside, this charming farmhouse has been elegantly refurbished without losing its authentic character. Chef Pluymaekers occasionally makes use of exotic seasonings and has an eye for presentation, but his cooking remains rooted in tradition. The lamb and asparagus are locally sourced – their superb quality is immediately apparent – and elevated by a refined lamb jus. He knows the importance of deep sauces and moves effortlessly from a tournedos Rossini to a lobster Thermidor. The freedom to choose between the set menu and à la carte dishes only adds to the hospitable vibe at By Taste.

Name: Byblos Beach
Description: On the Plage de Pampelonne, this elegant beachside retreat was designed with sustainability in mind. Boasting a decor of bleached wood and cotton sun shades, it draws a chic, laid-back crowd. On the menu: delicious fish, meat from the wood-fired grill and highly popular pasta dishes – best enjoyed with your toes in the sand, gazing out at the sea and basking in the sun. At lunchtime, there is even a tender service, which brings diners ashore directly from their boats.

Name: Byblos Sur Mer
Address: InterContinental Abu Dhabi, King Abdullah bin Abdul Aziz Al Saud Street, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,No alcohol served,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Start your visit on the wonderful terrace and spend time admiring, or indeed coveting, the boats bobbing in the marina that it overlooks. Sharing is everything at this two-level restaurant, where the service is affable and organised. The Lebanese menu offers bags of choice – the grilled section is a good place to head to, where lamb-lovers should look no further than machawi mchakaleh. Friday and Saturday evenings see live music and entertainment.

Name: BÒME
Description: Located in the lively and densely populated Trstenik neighborhood, this small, well-kept restaurant stands out for its colorful, elegant furnishings, as well as a pleasant covered terrace for dining during the warmer months. In the kitchen, chef and owner Mario Omrčen offers a modern Mediterranean cuisine, characterized by well-balanced flavors and textures that play a fundamental role. In the dining room, the young, dynamic Franciska will make you feel at home, providing a precise and attentive service. The wine list is also very interesting, featuring a selection of small Croatian producers.

Name: BÚN
Description: Leave the madding crowd far behind and relax in the hip casual vibe of this trendy Vietnamese eatery. You can expect to sample a fine dining version of characteristic Vietnamese sweet and sour, fermented and spicy flavours. The chef favours local organic produce, an ethos that is reflected in the attractive wine list, rich in natural vintages. The Little Bún noodle shop rustles up gutsy, full-bodied Vietnamese street food.

Name: Bà Cô Lốc Cốc
Address: 40A Tran Cao Van Street, Xuan Hoa Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 722700, Vietnam
Description: Known for premium seafood and a great selection of snails cooked in multiple ways, Bà Cô Lốc Cốc is a shellfish lover's delight. Highlights include snails in coconut soup, curry and steamed with fresh peppercorn. Another signature dish is apple snail with ginger and lemongrass. Each dish is complemented by fresh herb-infused sauces. The menu, available in Vietnamese, English and with pictures, is easy to navigate, and staff are happy to help with recommendations.

Name: Bà Diệu (Tran Tong Street)
Address: 17 Tran Tong Street, Thanh Khe Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: This simple shop specialises in bún bò, or rice noodle soup with assorted cuts of beef – thinly sliced, shin, tongue, tendon... Alternatively, the noodles can be paired with pork balls or pork trotters. The broth boasts a robust meaty flavour with natural sweetness and mild heat; the meat is cooked to perfection and the seasoning is spot on. Their signature thập cẩm noodle dish allows diners to sample the beef and the pork at the same time.

Name: Bàrbar
Description: In the heart of Palma’s old quarter, just a few metres from the Convento de la Concepció after which the street is named, you’ll come across this rustic-style eatery with lots of character, thanks mainly to its restored natural stone walls. It features two distinct dining spaces: one overlooking the kitchen for a more authentic experience, plus the pleasant main dining room. The à la carte dining format here is based around the Mediterranean with the occasional global touch, ably supported by seasonal suggestions and fish of the day options. Having tried the grilled wild turbot we can safely confirm that the quality of the fish is truly outstanding.

Name: Bánh Canh Yến (Hải Châu)
Address: 253 Nguyen Hoang Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: Come here for bánh canh – thick, chewy noodles made with tapioca starch and rice flour in a snakehead fish and pork broth. Choose toppings like fishcake, quail egg or crabcake. Order fried dough sticks for added crunch.

Name: Bánh Cuốn Bà Hoành
Address: 66 To Hien Thanh Street, Bui Thi Xuan Ward, Hanoi, 112300, Vietnam
Description: This is among the busiest shops in the area because of its steamed rice rolls known as bánh cuốn. Rice noodle sheets are steamed to order and then wrapped around minced shiitake and pork. They also sell bún chả, or grilled pork noodles.

Name: Bánh Cuốn Bà Xuân
Address: 16 Hoe Nhai Street, Ba Dinh Ward, Hanoi, 11115, Vietnam
Description: The chef crafts delectable bánh cuốn, Vietnamese steamed rolls with minced pork and black fungus. She also serves an option with a soft poached egg. Order the pork meatloaf and sausage, and season with fresh herbs, chilli, lime or garlic at will for a great breakfast or snack.

Name: Bánh Mì Nếm (Wan Chai)
Address: GF, 247-249 Queen's Road East, Wan Chai, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: This takeout-only shop specialises in Vietnamese sandwiches, alongside rice noodles and coffee. The signature bánh mì dặc biệt features Vietnamese char siu, sausage and pâté in a baguette. Pickled radish and chilli add extra zing.

Name: Bánh Xèo Bà Dưỡng
Address: 280/23 Hoang Dieu Street, Hoa Cuong Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: This 30+-year-old no-frills shop at the very end of an alley serves a concise menu of crispy pancakes known as bánh xèo, alongside skewered pork, grilled meat and noodles. Everything comes with fresh herbs, pickled papaya, cucumber and strips of eggplant. Feel free to customise your own rice paper pancake with meat to order and condiments on the table. The minced pork peanut sauce dip is a must.

Name: Bâoli
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This lively space located in J1 Beach is a restaurant, bar, and beach club all in one. The main eatery, with its more relaxed atmosphere, offers an extensive menu that blends Asian and European cuisines. Dishes are designed for sharing and range from salads to sashimi, robata grilled skewers to pastas, with steaks being the real highlight. We recommend taking the team’s advice on what to choose as some portions are made for two or more people. Pair your meal with one of many cocktails as either an aperitif, or to simply enjoy into the early hours after dinner.

Name: Bär & Schaf Wirtschaft
Description: What started as a pop-up has now become a permanent fixture in the historical Gasthaus zum Prinz Johann. The proprietor duo, Martin Nuart and Philipp Medved, offer their guests a very personal dining experience. Philipp manages things front-of-house with delightful ease, friendliness, and proficiency, while Martin heads up the regional cuisine. His intriguing plant-forward set menu showcases select seasonal ingredients from his family's own farm or neighbouring agricultural producers. In terms of wine, Austria takes centre stage, and is accompanied by offerings from Slovenia and Italy. The setting is wonderfully inviting – with lovely old floorboards, simple wooden benches and chairs and decorative contemporary artwork, the historical charm of the centuries-old inn has been retained with style.

Name: Bären
Description: Culinary passion is alive and well in this charming 17C inn! Owner Christian Mutschler is always on hand, advising and serving, but also sharing stories about the eventful history of the place. The no-frills food is tasty, and most of the ingredients come from the region. The game dishes are definitely worth trying – made with game hunted by the owner, they could hardly be fresher or more seasonal. The lunch menu is more limited, but depending on the number of reservations you may still be able to order from the regular menu. The wine list is also dominated by Swiss labels, and there are plenty of good bottles to choose from. Be sure to make the most of the terrace and the great view it offers!

Name: Bärenwirt
Description: Claudia and Manuel Ressi bring warmth and dedication to the running of this charming restaurant on the main square. The cuisine showcases select regional ingredients, which are presented in a kind of hybrid concept. On the one hand, there are the Austrian "Wirtshaus-Klassiker" à la carte (including Wiener schnitzel, Tafelspitz, Gailtaler Ripperl, and Backhendl), and then there is the four- to eight-course "Bärenwanderung" set menu with creative, modern dishes such as "Hühnerhof – organic chicken, beans, wild mushrooms, savory, buckwheat". You can also choose individual dishes from the set menu. The extremely friendly and attentive manager is happy to explain the provenance of the ingredients, giving guests an insight into the regional philosophy. The restaurant has two dining areas: one distinctly traditional small space and a more modern area, plus a nice terrace in front of the building. Der Kleine Bär located directly opposite has three inviting, nicely done out guestrooms. They also put on cookery courses and have an online shop – some of the produce available is made in-house.

Name: Bé Mặn
Address: Lot 9, Vo Nguyen Giap Street, Son Tra Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: One of the most famous seafood restaurants on My Khe Beach, Bé Mặn knows how to bring out the best in every ingredient. Start by picking your own live seafood from the rows of tanks and then specify how you want it cooked. From crabs and lobsters to geoduck and snails, whether deep-fried, stir-fried or steamed, everything tastes as good as it looks. Try the steamed squid with ginger and onion, dipping it in the spicy sour sauce for an extra zing.

Name: Béo Ơi
Address: 15/20 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: Off from the main drag, this simple shop is run by the owner-chef, affectionately known as béo ơi or "fat boy" by regulars, who come in droves during lunch hours. The menu features generous portions of Hanoian home-style cooking, including bún riêu cua, a flavoursome tomato crab soup topped with crispy deep-fried tofu. Order a couple of sides for a complete meal. Or go with friends and opt for a hot pot dinner with the tasty soup as a base.

Name: Béus
Description: Maria and Michel welcome guests to their gourmet establishment as if they were old friends of the family. Maria tends to your every need in the dining room, while Michel crafts what appears to be classical fare, yet with a subtle modern spin. Examples range from old-school grilled white pudding and traditional sole meunière with fresh fries to scallops served with curry-flavoured beurre blanc. Soul-warming food that has kept up with the times. At Béus, which loosely translates as “our home” in the local lingo, flavour is the overriding goal every time.

Name: Bún Bò Huế Cô Như
Address: 274/29 Vo Van Tan Street, Ban Co Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 722700, Vietnam
Description: This family-run shop is tucked away in a narrow alley. It takes a little effort to find, but you’ll well be rewarded by tasty beef noodle soups. First-timers may go for bún bò thập cẩm (mixed beef noodle soup), a great way to sample all four toppings of beef and pork, boasting robust meaty flavours. The sweet broth with great depth is made from beef meat and bones alongside herbs like lemongrass. Add a dollop of chilli sauce for added whoomph.

Name: Bún Chả Cá Bà Hoa
Address: 27 Le Hong Phong Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: Since 2009, this simple shop has attracted a loyal fan base with only one item on the menu – bún chả cá – rice noodles in a tangy tomato and pumpkin broth with fresh fishcakes, made in house daily using a variety of fish. Almost 300 bowls are sold every day and customised to order with fishcake only or a combo of fishcake and a chunk of mackerel or tuna. Try it with pickles or a dab of shrimp paste for extra flavour.

Name: Bún Chả Hương Liên
Address: 24 Le Van Huu Street, Hai Ba Trung Ward, Hanoi, 113000, Vietnam
Description: Playing on their claim to fame, this joint displays photos of its celebrity guests alongside the glass-encased “president table.” Ordering is straightforward, with most guests opting for the “Obama Combo”, which includes a fried seafood roll, a bowl of the special bún chả and a bia hà nội. The bún chả itself delivers a satisfying blend of rustic flavours, with smoky pork, meat patties, fragrant herbs and fresh salad leaves. Payment is made in cash at the entrance on departure.

Name: Bún Chả Đắc Kim (Hang Manh Street)
Address: 1 Hang Manh Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 11015, Vietnam
Description: Located in the Old Quarter since 1966, this no-frills shop reflects its long history. Nước chấm – sweet chilli fish sauce with finely sliced pickled green mango – is the perfect condiment for the vermicelli noodles which come with shredded smoky pork and plump pork patties. It’s a win-win combination of meat with sweetness and refreshing acidity. Queues are common, so be prepared to wait patiently and perhaps share a table.

Name: Bún Riêu Cua 39
Address: 39 Le Hong Phong Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: Set beneath a large tree and only open in the morning, they focus on rice noodles with crab meat in a family-recipe soup that’s rich in umami with a tangy note. Try the Tô Riêu Đặc Biệt, with crab and three types of fish cake. The pork sausage wrapped in banana leaves is also tasty.

Name: Bún Thịt Nướng Hoàng Văn
Address: 137 Chan Hung Street, Tan Hoa Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 736090, Vietnam
Description: At this family-run spot, the modest interior is neat and orderly. The one dish on the menu is bún thịt nướng: with cold rice noodles, grilled pork, meatballs and crisp spring rolls, lifted by a light yet flavourful, tangy dressing, it is an antidote to the city's humid climate.

Name: Bürestubel
Description: This half-timbered farmhouse is brimming with Alsatian charm! Pretty regional decor and (very) local specialities: bibalaskas with smoked ham, bacon, garlic and parsley ; veal fleischnacka with mushrooms and cream ; sourdough tartes flammées…and the unmissable “real crème caramel like my grandmother used to make”.

Name: Bütgenbacher Hof
Description: The second generation has further enhanced the already well-known reputation of this family-run establishment. Diners are welcomed like old friends into a chalet-like interior that provides the perfect foil for a classical lineup with a regional twist packed in generosity, as the chef adds a highly personal spin to all-time family favourites. Examples include an upside-down tart of sweet red onions with a sorbet of red cabbage and cream cheese and chives. The varied à la carte score and set menu that changes daily leave diners spoiled for choice. Go there your eyes closed – possibly booking a room so you can explore the surrounding unspoilt countryside at a more leisurely pace.

Name: Bākkō
Description: Located just a stone's throw from Paseo de la Castellana, in an area with plenty to see and do, this restaurant serves informal Japanese cuisine with a global twist, featuring charcoal-grilled dishes and interesting nods to Basque cuisine in some of its creations. The menu, which includes exclusive sections dedicated to nigiri, oysters and hot dishes (we particularly enjoyed their gyoza with cured egg yolk), is complemented by two Omakase menus (short and long), so you can indulge and let yourself be guided. They also offer a wide variety of sakes and a menu called Nigiris, which can only be ordered at the bar!

Name: BİZ İstanbul
Address: Atatürk Kültür Merkezi, Gümüşsuyu Mahallesi, Mete Caddesi No:2, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34337, Türkiye
Description: Head to the world-famous Taksim Square and take the lift to this spacious restaurant on the seventh floor of the Atatürk Cultural Centre. The interior is elegant and modern, complete with a stylish bar, but nothing compares to the terrace and its stunning views of the city and the Bosphorus. The menu celebrates the diversity of Turkish cuisine through contemporary interpretations of traditional dishes. For instance, a combination of subtly smoky aubergine purée, braised lamb, walnuts and a creamy lamb jus makes for a deeply layered main course. The chefs have an eye for detail, but it is the rich flavours that truly steal the show.

Name: Bōl
Address: 15 Jalan Sin Chew Kee, Bukit Bintang, Kuala Lumpur, 50150, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Having cooked together since they were young, Singaporean chef-owner and hotel designer, Kian Liew, and partner, Patrick, opened their brainchild in 2022 and have already earned the support of many regulars. Only set menus are available, including one that is entirely seasonal and one for vegans. The focus is on Nyonya style cuisine with Singaporean and Malaysian twists, using a healthy mix of herbs and spices to create a succulent range of flavours.

Name: Bếp Cuốn
Address: 31-33 Tran Bach Dang Street, An Hai Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: With both indoor and outdoor seating, diners can enjoy Da Nang’s warm seasons al fresco at this cosy restaurant. The space features greenery, lanterns, and bamboo accents in a charming Vietnamese style. Ideal for first-time tourists, the extensive menu showcases authentic dishes from both the north and south.
