Large tables suit groups, while solo diners can enjoy platters and combo dishes. The Mẹt Bếp Cuốn platter includes four snacks served with tangy fish and tamarind sauces.

Name: Bếp Hên
Address: 47 Le Hong Phong Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 840236, Vietnam
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted
Description: Step back in time and immerse yourself in the room’s vintage circa 1990s decor and memorabilia. The family business has been in operation since 2015 and the kitchen is helmed by mum. The extensive menu, which covers all of Vietnam, might seem overwhelming, but rest assured that all the sharing plates are authentic, hearty and comforting. When unsure, check out the section known as ‘mum’s favourites’, for items like fried garlic prawn, or stir-fried morning glory with garlic.

Name: Bếp Người Hội An
Address: 22 Tran Quoc Toan Street, Xuan Hoa Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 72408, Vietnam
Description: The decor is unmistakably Hội An in style – yellow walls, lanterns and wooden furniture. The menu is easy to navigate, with mì quảng noodles and cơm gà chicken rice being the main events. Trouble choosing? Try the mì quảng đặc biệt topped with shrimp, pork, quail egg, ham, fermented pork roll and peanut spring roll. Cơm gà xé comprises silky shredded chicken, onion and laksa leaves on a bed of chicken fat rice, with chicken offal sauce on the side.

Name: Bếp Prime
Address: 12 Hang Dieu Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 111202, Vietnam
Description: Tucked away in a quaint historic edifice, c. 1932, Bếp Prime specialises in traditional delicacies from Hanoi and the rest of Vietnam. Having travelled widely, the owner-chef returned to his hometown to open the restaurant and realise his culinary dream. For a Hanoian classic, order pigeon and mushroom hot pot – veggies, pigeon meat and offal are served in a bird cage to be blanched in a herbal broth or glutinous rice porridge. The crispy rice dish with the chef’s dip, made from pork jus, dried shrimps, chilli and pepper that packs umami and a spicy kick, is also recommended.

Name: Bếp Việt
Description: On premises that once housed a brasserie, this restaurant specialises in Vietnamese cuisine that is entirely vegetarian, often vegan, down to the broths and sauces free of any animal products – a rare find in Paris. Summer rolls with tofu and lemongrass, rice pancakes with mushrooms, and banana blossom salad with tamarind… these are generous, aromatic dishes, in which animal proteins are skilfully replaced by a variety of different textured plant-based ingredients.

Name: Bờm
Address: 24 Nguyen Thi Nghia Street, Ben Thanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 71009, Vietnam
Description: Bờm's ambience and cuisine conjure up a fairy tale-like nostalgia for Vietnamese diners. In a chic, low-lit venue combining traditional bamboo with minimalist cement elements, the modern, refined Vietnamese cuisine ticks all the boxes. Try the bò kho tart – tender braised beef encased in flaky puff pastry – and the signature Bờm Set, comprising bite-size shrimp fritters, snail cakes and fishcakes. Mè đen, a mochi with a black sesame filling, provides a sweet finale.

Name: C'Yusha
Description: Modern cuisine that makes full use of herbs and spices, created by a chef who works single - handedly in full view of the diners. Minimalist and intimately scaled (numbers are deliberately limited) in a resolutely contemporary setting.

Name: C'est la vie
Description: This restaurant is dedicated to the French way of life. As you sit comfortably at your table in the stylish modern interior, looking out through the floor-to-ceiling windows, the dedicated team busy themselves in the open kitchen, cooking up modern interpretations of dishes such as sea bass with root vegetables and potato croissant or Bresse chicken with morels, shimeji mushrooms and vin jaune. The creations are organised into two set menus – one vegetarian, one with meat – and accompanied by exclusively French wine, which are charmingly and skilfully presented at your table with the aid of a map. The wines can also be purchased in the shop. Tip: There is parking in the garage right next door.

Name: C.M.Y. Satay
Address: Chinatown Complex Market & Food Centre, #02-168, 335 Smith Street, 050335, Singapore
Description: Two shops share the same venue, so be sure you order from the right one. The grilled-to-order satay comes in pork, chicken and lamb varieties (or an assortment). The nutty, tangy sauce is tasty and you can order rice on top.

Name: CAAA by Pietro Catalano
Description: The location right next to an art gallery could not be more fitting, as creativity is very much at the heart of this restaurant too. The chic, modern interior is all curved lines, with the creatively designed ceiling as its centrepiece. Pale tones and the sleek design of the tables and chairs lend the space a Nordic feel. In the kitchen, which is completely open to view, bold modern dishes with Italian and regional influences are prepared using carefully selected premium ingredients. The agnolotti with braising jus and brown butter foam are simply superb. A tasting menu is served in the evening – choose how many courses you would like when making your reservation. The welcoming atmosphere owes much to the proprietress, the head chef's sister, who runs the dining room with effortless grace. A bar is also part of the concept, with cocktails and mocktails playing an integral role in the culinary experience. Tip: Take your aperitif with you as you wander through the art gallery, which is directly connected to the restaurant. During the summer months, the intimate courtyard terrace is especially inviting.

Name: CAMPHOR
Address: 923 E. 3rd St., Ste. 109, Los Angeles, CA, 90013, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: This popular spot hums with activity from eager diners and a bustling open kitchen. Headed by the talented Chef Max Boonthanakit and team, Camphor plates seriously good French fare with a sprinkling of creative flair. Inventive cocktails, including the refreshing Rue de Baci, complete the experience. Sea bream crudo with green apple ice and horseradish cream offers a fresh, aromatic opener before a main course like scallop demi-lune pasta in truffle-chive beurre blanc. Bistro classics like steak au poivre with Cognac cream (best accompanied by golden brown frites) remain central to the menu. A dessert of marzipan sorbet with a finely shaved Meyer lemon ice offers a feather-light finish.

Name: CAMPO Modern Grill
Description: There’s a real comforting quality to the cooking at this smart modern brasserie in the heart of the city. Share a couple of small plates to start, before moving on to the main event: steaks. A variety of cuts of top-quality Argentinian beef are cooked over charcoal in the Josper oven, then served with traditional adornments like chips and béarnaise sauce. The desserts have a similarly classic approach, with satisfying options like chocolate fondant with Chantilly cream.

Name: CARALEON
Description: This tastefully designed restaurant is housed in the small boutique hotel of the same name, which enjoys a fabulous location in the Wasserburger Bucht and boasts stunning lake views. It specialises in modern European cuisine infused with authentic Peruvian influences. There is a small selection of à la carte options as well as a five-course set menu (by advance booking only) – the chefs themselves serve the dishes, adding a distinctive personal touch. The 300 labels on offer showcase wines from Bordeaux to Slovakia. Alternatively, there is a good range of non-alcoholic drinks to accompany your food. Every Sunday from 12pm to 6.30pm is "Family & Friends", when à la carte classics are served, such as parihuela (Peruvian bouillabaisse), Wiener schnitzel or Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancakes). Tip: Head to the Sunset Lounge for a nightcap by the lake.

Name: CARBÓNCABRÓN
Address: Boulevard Cerro Colorado, México 1 Kilómetro 24.5, 23400, San José del Cabo, 23400, Mexico
Description: Chef Poncho Cadena is in charge at this moody space where it will take your eyes a minute to adjust to the darkness. Library-style stacks of mesquite wood serve as a dramatic design theme but also as a not-so-subtle hint at the live fire concept. The menu is divided into vegetables, seafood and "black market" meats including tongue, sweetbread and more. These plates are ideal for sharing, though a chef's tasting menu is on hand for those who want to sample it all. Nuanced cooking is seen in dishes like the onion petals filled with habanero aïoli, coated in charcoal tempura batter, and fried. Served simply in a bowl, guests are encouraged to use their hands to scoop up these delights. Tail-on shrimp over a thick slice of pork belly leans sweet but satisfying.

Name: CARLS Brasserie an der Elbphilharmonie
Description: As you take in the view of the Elbe River and the Elbphilharmonie concert hall, you can soak up the lively and casual yet elegant brasserie atmosphere and enjoy sophisticated North German cuisine such as fish stew or whole sole. The unique location means that window seats are in demand. And in summer, diners make a beeline for the terrace. The bistro next door serves bowls and tartines. A wine bar is also part of the premises.

Name: CARTE BLANCHE
Description: Housed within SO/ Berlin Das Stue hotel, on the edge of the Großer Tiergarten and right next to the Spanish Embassy, this restaurant is not to be missed. The modern, elegant and cosy design fosters a relaxed atmosphere that puts diners in mind of an upscale living room. The French-influenced cuisine includes classics such as beef tartare, grilled entrecôte or moules marinières. You can also sip on an aperitif or digestif in Stue Bar, which is right next to the restaurant. In fine weather, the quiet, leafy courtyard terrace is a lovely spot – exclusive access for hotel patrons to the Zoo Berlin is a real highlight of staying here! Tip: An attractively priced set menu is served at lunchtime.

Name: CARUSO Pastabar
Description: Neapolitan-born Anna and Marcello Caruso, working with Emanuele Barbaro, have come up with a cool concept: a flavoursome, relaxed and lively dining experience, played out in a chic atmosphere. Service comes courtesy of a relaxed, attentive team under the tutelage of the charming proprietress. They serve a three-course set menu, which you can put together yourself and add to as you wish – the main course is flavoursome house-made pasta! N.B. You should allow about two hours for three courses. There are two seatings: 6pm and 8.30pm. Trendy drinks at the bar.

Name: CASA LEO
Address: 4500 Los Feliz Blvd., Ste. C, Los Angeles, CA, 90027, USA
Description: CASA LEO, from Chef/owner Joshua Whigham, is a Spanish-inspired restaurant offering a variety of tapas-style plates, easy to order alone or as a variety to share with the table. Start with "shots" of bay scallop ceviche with tender scallops in a vibrant leche de tigre, served atop halved lime wedges. Choose between a variety of their Iberian flatbreads, including the lardons coca with caramelized onion puree, queso picon and a drizzle of fresh passionfruit topping. Proteins like their rabo de toro are a must; a decadent, tender wine-braised oxtail stew, topped with house-made potato chips for the right amount of crunch. Finish your meal with a delicious slice of Helen's cheesecake.

Name: CEO 1950
Address: 24, Lane 62, Section 3, Xinsheng North Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: The residence of Taiwan Central Bank's first CEO (1950s) now houses a European restaurant on the ground floor, plus an exhibition space upstairs. The airy dining room is lavishly furnished, its modern light fixtures complementing the exposed wooden beams. The head chef has years of experience in French cooking; in the 10-course dinner tasting menu and three-course lunch set, he imbues the classics with his original touch and the unique flavours of each season.

Name: CHECKin by Leonel Pereira
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This charming restaurant occupies a former cereal and wine storehouse which has been completely remodelled in Faro’s historic centre. The cooking of chef Leonel Pereira, a native of the Algarve, is based around seasonal ingredients with a strong focus on creativity and flavour. The menu is divided into different sections: Check-in, Cozinhados no Tacho, Momentos Especiais and Check-out. Make sure you try the cheesecake with strawberries, lime, meringue and tangerine peel ice-cream.

Name: CIRPAS
Description: The restaurant’s name stems from ‘Circulation’—the flow of guests, producers, and food culture—and ‘Passion,’ the driving force behind it. One dish features crab and caviar. The presentation of seasonal vegetables changes throughout the year, with geometric cuts and striking colours that highlight each ingredient while maintaining perfect harmony. At its core, the cuisine remains classic French, yet it embraces new sensibilities, bridging the past and the present.

Name: COCO
Address: 2F, Mactan Seaport Village, Punta Engaño Road, Lapu-Lapu, Cebu, 6015, The Philippines
Description: Opened in mid-2024, this easy-to-miss gem on the second floor of an old building blends tropical charm with rustic bamboo decor, stone-accented walls and a laid-back, vacation-like vibe. The Korean owner and young, local kitchen team deliver a menu that mixes Filipino and Thai flavours with creative flair. The highlight is sisig with egg – a flavoursome stir-fry of assorted pork offal and aromatic spices. Cool down with a fresh fruit shake on sunny afternoons.

Name: COMAL Restaurante
Address: Av. Miramar 666 Local 17, Plaza Santo Tomás, Ensenada, 22890, Mexico
Description: This all-day restaurant is located in the heart of trendy Plaza Santo Tomás. Under the soaring warehouse ceilings, high-top bar seating wraps around a small open kitchen where chefs regularly press and griddle tortillas on a small comal. From casual lunches to heartier dinners, regional inspiration is far-ranging, though Oaxaca is a frequent focus (think assorted moles, crispy tlayudas and warm tetelas). Chocolate flan with salted toffee caramel makes for a lovingly sweet, light finale. Service is notably friendly and accommodating.

Name: COMME À LA MAISON
Description: Yuji Wakui faithfully recreates the cuisine of southwestern France, taught to him by a chef from Landes. From pâté de campagne to terrine de foie gras and duck confit, all are prepared with heartfelt affection. But Wakui reserves a special fondness for soupe de garbure, a simmered mélange of ham, duck, white kidney beans and other ingredients that spreads the flavours of Landes to a ready audience in Tokyo. Unwavering faithfulness to tradition wordlessly expresses Wakui’s gratitude to his mentor.

Name: COOK HOUSE
Address: Foundry Lane Studios, Foundry Lane, Newcastle Upon Tyne, NE6 1LH, United Kingdom
Description: After opening a shipping container café, local food blogger Anna Hedworth crowdfunded this stripped-back, industrial-style restaurant with a pleasant terrace and a relaxed feel. Dinner is the main event, with many of the vibrant, fiercely seasonal dishes cooked on the hibachi barbeque.

Name: COPPIE
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed
Description: The aproned staff greet arriving guests as if welcoming friends into their home. The nostalgic interior of this old Japanese-style house oozes serenity. The concept is fare that complements sake and wine. The chef, not binding himself to any genre, serves up an imaginative medley of Japanese, Chinese, Western and ethnic influences. Using fermentation to impart flavour and tartness is the chef’s forte. Enjoy pairing innovative cuisine with compatible sakes.

Name: CR21
Description: In the heart of the old town, among narrow streets steeped in history, lies a modern bistro that exudes energy with its bright colours and open kitchen. Here, chef Di Bartolo creates contemporary dishes that evoke Mediterranean flavours, interpreted with skill and imagination. Every creation is an invitation to discover authentic flavours with an innovative twist, in an atmosphere that combines elegance and friendliness. Highlights include the crispy cannolo, red prawns and burrata with red fruit coulis, as well as chive mayonnaise.

Name: CRATAIN
Address: 306 Changsheng Road, Gushan District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
Description: Cratain is a portmanteau of Tasmania’s Cradle Mountain, which the owner once climbed. He draws a parallel between his restaurant and mountaineering, using the pristine white space as a blank canvas for dishes finessed with well-honed European techniques. He offers a set menu with a choice of mains, alongside optional seasonal specialities. Meat, chargrilled or pan-seared, is the main event, but the pasta is also a highlight.

Name: CREATERNA
Description: The chef prizes freedom in his cooking. He sharpened his creative sensibility by working across a range of culinary styles throughout Europe. His cuisine rests on three pillars: imagination, refinement and artistry. Ingredient combinations are kept simple, while plating is elegant, carefully considering negative space as well. The restaurant’s name fuses the Latin words ‘creatio’ (creation) and ‘aeterna’ (eternity). The chef continues to craft recipes with an eye to the future.

Name: CRKL
Description: CRKL may look like an upmarket concrete villa from the outside, but once indoors, you will find yourself in a romantic setting done up in soft pastel shades. Take a seat on the patio and sip an aperitif, as you get ready to sample the chef’s handiwork in which pedigree Belgian produce rubs shoulders with Asian and Mediterranean influences. Examples: Piedmont veal with goat’s cheese and lavender oil or fabulously fresh haddock paired with a creamy sauce based on fish stock and perfumed with miso. You can expect truly fragrant dishes packed in character. Finally, the establishment demonstrates a distinct preference for Belgian wines and olive oil, further squaring the circle in this distinctive venue.

Name: CULTURE
Address: Custom House Quay, 38b Arwenack Street, Falmouth, TR11 3JF, United Kingdom
Description: The open kitchen takes centre stage at this old quayside warehouse where provenance and seasonality are of utmost important to the chefs. Each dish on the set menu is named after the inspiration behind it, be it a local farmer or place – such as 'William's Grains' or 'Terras Farm' – while foraged ingredients also play their part. Don’t be surprised to see the occasional South African influence too, as the chef-owner is from Cape Town. The pared-back room has a natural feel, and it’s worth checking out the glass-walled wine cellar.

Name: CUT
Address: Beverly Wilshire, A Four Seasons Hotel, 9500 Wilshire Blvd., Beverly Hills, CA, 90212, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Tucked inside the sleek Four Seasons Hotel, this steakhouse from Wolfgang Puck isn't pulling any punches when it comes to luxury. Offering the finest cuts of beef from Australia and America to Japan, this is a place for a deep-pocketed crowd, and the elegant dining room with banquette seating is the ideal setting for a power meal. Chilled prawns or oysters on the half shell are classic openers, and it may prove difficult to stop nibbling on the sundried tomato Parker house rolls and the house-knotted pretzels, served with roasted pepper and walnut dip. Creekstone filet mignon with Armagnac green peppercorn bearnaise sauce is a sure bet, but it's those wagyu tallow French fries that you'll be thinking about later.

Name: Ca Aleix
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: What is most striking is its location in the Art al Camp, a natural-artistic outdoor space with a series of charming palm trees, olive trees and large wrought iron figures, the works of local sculptor Toni Marí and Juan Ripollés; in fact, visible from the road, we are welcomed by Antonia, a sculpture measuring more than 30 metres... in the shape of a whale! In the bright, contemporary restaurant, chef Alejandro Crespo adopts a Mediterranean-inspired cuisine that stands out for its modern take on tapas (such as Nuestro mejillón tigre (stuffed mussels)), the extensive Cocas de La Marina section and, above all, its delicious rice dishes (make sure to try the Prawn and pumpkin meloso or the Figatell and chickpea fideuá). Reservations are recommended, especially in summer to eat on the terrace!

Name: Ca Na Toneta
Description: This restaurant, whose name pays a small tribute to grandmother Toneta, is well run by two sisters and surprises by dividing the experience between two houses (in the first, they even have a small shop selling select local products). The proposal, which reflects authenticity and genuine devotion to seasonal Mallorcan cuisine, revolves around a single tasting menu that changes according to the season (we particularly liked one of the starters, their pumpkin flower, tender leaves, cherries and almonds). Don't miss the charming main terrace, partially covered with vines and featuring beautiful handmade murals that tell us stories of conscious gastronomy on the island!

Name: Ca l'Esteve
Description: A fourth-generation, family-run restaurant occupying a large stone house. The traditional Catalan menu is enhanced by several daily specials. Impressive choice of rice and grilled dishes.

Name: Ca na Pilar
Address: Avenida de la Mar 1, Es Migjorn Gran, 07749, Spain
Description: This restaurant occupies a typical 200-year-old house on the approach to Es Migjorn Gran in the centre of the island. It features an interior with a rustic-contemporary feel, plus an attractive patio-terrace that can only be booked for dinner. Here, the culinary focus is on simple, honest cooking with interesting French-inspired touches and dishes based around the best market-fresh local ingredients. They have a starter that's almost always on the menu and is absolutely delicious: smoked pâté de campagne.

Name: Ca' 7
Address: Via Cunizza da Romano 4, Bassano del Grappa, 36061, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in a charming 18C villa, this elegant restaurant overlooks its attractive garden in a magical setting which is typical of the Veneto. The cuisine also has a regional focus, with classic recipes featuring on the menu alongside more creative dishes (fish appears more often than meat).

Name: Ca' Apollonio Gourmet
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: Ca’ Apollonio Gourmet offers a contemporary cuisine deeply rooted in the territory of the Venetian foothills, where nature, seasonality, and research coexist in refined equilibrium. Within a historic villa set in the landscape of Monte Grappa, executive chef Alessio Longhini constructs tasting menus that celebrate local and organic ingredients sourced from a carefully selected short supply chain, many of them grown in the property’s own kitchen gardens according to principles of regenerative agriculture.The proposal develops through menus that weave together gastronomic memory, technique, and contemporary sensitivity, following the rhythm of the seasons and offering an evolving reading of the territory. Completing the experience is a cellar of over a thousand labels – spanning small producers and great houses – with a particular focus on PIWI grape varieties, curated by sommelier Michele Griggio. In an intimate and elegant setting, animated by the masterful front-of-house direction of maître Lorenzo Palma, every detail is considered with a view to creating an experience that is harmonious and immersive.

Name: Ca' Mia
Description: This welcoming restaurant in the hills surrounding Lake Alserio makes guests feel completely at home. The two young chefs with plenty of experience behind them create modern dishes with a preference for quick cooking methods and a focus on a wood-fired oven and barbecue, as well as fermented ingredients.

Name: Ca' del Profeta
Description: Situated in a beautiful location in the Asti countryside overlooking rolling hills and the estate’s own vineyards, Ca' del Profeta lies just a few kilometres from the provincial capital. A modern dining room and panoramic terrace provide the backdrop for decidedly innovative Piedmontese cuisine, which is inspired by traditional recipes and seasonal ingredients and then transformed by the chef into personalised dishes. Ingredients from further afield, such as root vegetables (black salsify, celeriac and beetroot) also make an appearance in three creative recipes inspired by the Orient. The service is friendly yet professional, plus a few modern guestrooms are also available. A panoramic swimming pool completes the picture.

Name: Ca'Suso
Description: A welcoming bistro-style eatery with a rustic-contemporary feel, enthusiastically run by two brothers (Vicente and Iván) who humbly refer to their restaurant as a canteen-like “casa de comidas”. Their more modern take on traditional, Asturian-based cooking includes an à la carte (don’t miss the famous liquid La Peral cheese croquettes or the spider crab ravioli with fennel) and two enticing menus. Some half-plate options are also available.

Name: Ca's Milà
Address: Playa de Cala Tarida, Sant Josep de sa Talaia, 07829, Spain
Location: Sant Josep de sa Talaia, Spain
Description: A restaurant in which to savour the flavours, aromas and sea views to the full. Along with its simplicity, Ca's Milà stands out for its homely atmosphere, attentive service and its location right by the beach, practically clinging to the cliff, along with charming terraces and romantic views. Its traditional Ibizan cuisine specialises in fish (mainly cooked à la plancha or on the grill) and rice dishes.

Name: Cabanas
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Ever heard of Cocido de Lalín? Cabanas, located in the city centre and boasting a warm atmosphere, is one of the best places to try this iconic dish, which is based on Galician pork products. They offer a traditional à la carte menu with seasonal dishes and excellent options for fish and seafood of the day, as well as a successful three-course menu called 'Cocido de Lalín'. The extensive and carefully selected wine list deserves a special mention, with more than 1,500 labels. In fact, Carlota, the owners' daughter, works as a sommelier, demonstrating her extensive knowledge and great professionalism.

Name: Cabaret l'Enfer
Description: This restaurant in Le Plateau is inspired by the legendary Cabaret de l'Enfer in Montmartre, Paris. Inside, diners are immersed in an ambience where rock 'n' roll meets industrial. The large, elongated space, waxed concrete floor, black walls, and central counter with stools, is reminiscent of a retro London club. Posters and rock music played at full volume add to the underground atmosphere. Italian-born chef Massimo Piedimonte serves up a flurry of meticulously prepared bites, the sophisticated plating of which is on a par with the culinary skill that has gone into them: scallops seared on the barbecue, served with a saffron condiment; lasagna-style zucchini strips braised on the barbecue, cold zucchini coulis, mushroom jus, and egg yolk fudge. It's certainly more heaven than hell here.

Name: Cabaña Las Lilas
Address: Avenida Alicia Moreau de Justo 516, Buenos Aires, C1107AAL, Argentina
Description: When you ask for advice on the best steakhouse for grilled Argentinian meat in Buenos Aires, this large-scale restaurant in Puerto Madero, featuring lots of private spaces and an open-view grill, is always mentioned. In this pleasant eatery with an elegant air overlooking the river, the undisputed star of the menu is its grilled meat (veal chitterlings, mixed offal, ribeye, Summus Rubaiyat picanha etc) from different breeds of cattle, although it also offers a good choice of cold plates, salads, fish of the day, and an impressive array of side dishes. The restaurant is located just a few metres from the century-old Corbeta ARA Uruguay museum ship and its renown is such that it is not unusual to see famous personalities dining here – past customers have included the likes of tennis player Roger Federer and French President Emmanuel Macron. The extensive wine cellar and the option of ordering half plates for most dishes complete the picture here.

Name: Cabo Vidio
Description: This attractive family-run restaurant, featuring a pleasantly surprising rustic-style dining room overlooking a charming landscaped terrace, is run in a friendly spirit and with great professionalism by chef Jairo López (who is in charge of both the kitchen and dining room). His traditional Asturian cooking, including dishes such as broad beans with cod cheek, spider crab cake, and the loin of sea bream with cider, always champions ingredients sourced from the local area. Although many of the dishes here are for two people, it is also possible to order individual portions.

Name: Cabotte
Address: 48 Gresham Street, City of London, London, EC2V 7AY, United Kingdom
Description: Classic French cooking yields plenty of flavour at this appealing bistro de luxe with distressed décor and plenty of rustic charm. Despite some seasonal Mediterranean touches, the Gallic influence is clear to see on the menu, so look out for dishes like pâté-en-croûte. Quality produce is key to the ingredient-led cooking, to which the chefs bring an assured, accomplished hand. It’s owned by two master sommeliers who share a passion for the wines of Burgundy, so the stunning wine list understandably offers a top-notch selection.

Name: Cacciani
Description: Run by the Cacciani family for over 100 years, this is one of the most famous restaurants in the Castelli Romani region. Demonstrating a real passion for regional traditions and eschewing modern trends, the menu continues to offer a tempting selection of delicious classic dishes from Lazio, including a couple of fish and seafood options. The focaccia, which is served with the bread, is superb and well worth a mention. The dining room evokes the long history of the restaurant, while the panoramic terrace is a firm favourite with guests.

Name: Cachet
Description: Lars Scharp is known for the MICHELIN-starred Lars Amsterdam, and now also for Cachet, where he is putting his own spin on the brasserie concept. You see the approach reflected in both the timeless interior decor, which is a contemporary take on traditional elegance, and the extensive menu, which caters for breakfast, lunch and dinner. A spicy prawn cocktail and foie gras terrine make an enticing start, followed by succulent poussin with pommes allumettes, and the pavlova provides a memorable finale that will have you planning your next visit. There is also an excellent selection of premium ingredients such as caviar and lobster. This is a lively restaurant where anything goes - and where lovers of good food feel right at home.

Name: Cadence by Dan Bark
Address: 225 Soi Pridi Banomyong 25, Khlong Tan, Khlong Toei, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Valet parking
Description: Drawing on his Korean-American heritage and experience in some of Chicago's top restaurants, chef Dan Bark uses a clever array of components to craft progressive American cuisine. The elegant space sets the stage for an artful marriage of Western and Asian flavours. The restaurant's commitment to excellence goes beyond the food, with an impressive wine selection, astutely curated cocktail pairings and charming service from a smartly turned-out team.

Name: Cadet
Description: Between the Villa Majorelle and the Musée de l'École de Nancy, this restaurant, which seats no more than 16, is housed in a historic former hairdressing salon! In a suitably uncluttered Scandinavian-style interior, chef Theo Mareschal rolls out simple, accessible cuisine in the zeitgeist, presented in “surprise menus”.

Name: Cafe Bau
Address: GF, FWD House 1881 Main Building, 1881 Heritage, 2A Canton Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: This dining concept by 'Demon Chef' Alvin Leung, is styled like a vintage brasserie dripping in retro glam. Sit at the bar and watch the bartender concoct exquisite beverages. On to the food, order the 8-course tasting extravaganza to experience the chef's vision in full glory. Or try the 3-course abridged version with a choice of starter, main and dessert. Home-grown produce like Ping Yuen chicken, rice and veggies is used to good effect.

Name: Cafe Cecilia
Address: Canal Place, 32 Andrews Road, Dalston, London, E8 4FX, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Pets not allowed
Description: It may be located beneath a modern apartment block, but the quasi-industrial look and warm service give this bright and airy restaurant added personality. The appealing menu is supplemented by some blackboard specials, such as delicious pork and rabbit rillettes. The cooking is pleasingly understated, allowing the ingredients room to shine, while the chef-owner’s Irish heritage is evident in the excellent Guinness bread and subsequent Guinness bread ice cream, which has become something of a signature.

Name: Cafe Commerce
Address: 964 Lexington Ave., New York, NY, 10021, USA
Description: If the name sounds familiar, that's because it is. Cafe Commerce, a beloved West Village spot that closed a decade ago, is back, though now with a new location on the Upper East Side. Chef/owner Harold Moore whips up contemporary American dishes with French and Italian influences. In addition to dishes like sea scallops, beef carpaccio, and steak Diane, expect a few fan favorites from the previous iteration (the fantastic sweet potato tortellini, for one), as well as daily specials like fried chicken and rack of lamb. It's the kind of menu where there's always something for everyone, and the vibe makes it a classic weeknight outing. Don't even think of skipping the coconut cake, which has earned a loyal fan base. It's four layers of pure delight.

Name: Cafe Kandl
Description: This restaurant is popular and it's not easy to get a table as a walk-in, so be sure to book. Why all the hype? In addition to cool drinks at the bar and a wine list curated by the team to feature their top picks, there's the lively and sleek urban vibe, not to mention the fantastic modern and creative food made with top-notch ingredients. The exciting dishes include charcoal-grilled saddle of venison and cevapcici made from venison with wild boar leg served with smoky beetroot ajvar, house-made sheep's milk kaymak, game jus and herby flatbread for dipping. If you can't decide, it's best to choose the surprise menu, which gives a good overview of the cuisine over six courses.

Name: Cafe La Trova
Description: Of Jewish and Latin descent but born and raised in Miami, Chef Michelle Bernstein is intrinsic to the city's culinary scene. For this concept in Little Havana, she teams up with cocktail guru, Julio Cabrera, and the result is extraordinary. It's a vivacious place that hums with live music and a décor that transports guests through decades of history—from Cuba to the Cuban experience in Southern Florida.The menu features such classics as lechon with steamed yuca and tangerine mojo. Specials may deviate from the norm but are exquisite in their sweet and savory blend—think seared foie gras paired with Spanish French toast, maduros and maple syrup. Digestifs, like the Hotel Nacional with pineapple rum and apricot liqueur, are a fine way to quench the affair.

Name: Cafe Mado
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: At first glance, it may seem like your typical neighborhood all-day café, but there’s more than meets the eye at Café Mado. This Prospect Heights café bustles with a coffee shop up front and a skylit atrium with a small bar and dining room. It is here where they sell house-baked bread, breakfast sandwiches, elegant small plates, and handmade pasta by day before shifting to a refined dinner of small plates. Begin with pissaladière, a warm, round loaf topped with anchovies, caramelized red onions, and olive spread or kick things off with a seasonal small plate like summer melon with lime granita and habanada before tucking into a plate of pasta, like pici with pesto Genovese.

Name: Cafe Milano
Address: Four Seasons Hotel, The Galleria Level 1, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Powerbrokers, movers and shakers in Washington DC will be familiar with the original Café Milano. This elegant sibling is in the Four Seasons – and if you want to be seen enjoying la dolce vita, then start with an aperitivo in the bar. The Italian chef and his team confidently prepare authentic Italian dishes; the homemade pastas are a highlight. There’s also a great terrace.

Name: Cafe Reyes
Address: 11101 Hwy. 1, Point Reyes Station, CA, 94956, USA
Description: Cafe Reyes remains an essential stop in Point Reyes Station, where the rustic, barn-like dining room and duo of wood-fired ovens continue to draw day-trippers and locals alike. Pizza is still the main attraction, with a compact lineup of crisp, beautifully blistered pies named after nearby coastal landmarks. Favorites include the Farallon, layered with pepperoni, mushrooms and roasted garlic, as well as simpler combinations like the Limantour with cherry tomatoes and fresh mozzarella or the Palomarin with boquerones and mushrooms. Beyond the pizzas, the kitchen also highlights local ingredients with offerings like fresh Tomales Bay oysters, organic greens finished with Point Reyes blue cheese and wood-fired herb bread topped with roasted garlic and mozzarella. The atmosphere remains relaxed, unfussy and perfectly suited to lingering after a day on the coast.

Name: Cafe Roze
Description: All-day restaurants are sometimes overlooked, but don't count out East Nashville's Cafe Roze; it's more than meets the eye. Whether you come for coffee or breakfast, swing by for an afternoon glass of wine or stop by on your way home for dinner, this welcoming spot hits all the right notes. The menu leans lighter with vegetable-forward small plates and oysters that seem simple but have unexpected depth. Grilled long beans atop hummus with green nasturtium zhoug is deeply savory and watermelon radish tossed in an urfu vinaigrette with greens is refreshing, while pork schnitzel with brown butter-chili sauce and a zesty slaw offers a fresh take on a classic. For dessert, you'll never go wrong with the creamy chocolate mousse.

Name: Cafe Sabarsky
Address: 1048 Fifth Ave., New York, NY, 10028, USA
Description: This Museum Mile kaffeehaus is so authentic it may as well be set along Vienna’s Ringstrasse. Instead, find it in a Beaux Arts mansion—home to the Neue Galerie, replete with 20th-century Austrian-and-German art and design. This gorgeous ground-floor den is clad in dark-stained wood with diners seated along a banquette covered in Otto Wagner fabric. Order one of the traditional specialties, including the city’s best wiener schnitzel or hearty Hungarian beef goulash, but it's the cakes and pastries that are the stuff of dreams. Linzer torte and Sachertorte are as classic as they are extraordinary. Feuilletine may be described as a chocolate mousse cake but it is anything but simple with its luscious, well-executed layers.

Name: Cafe Tempo
Description: An old car workshop in the artsy Telliskivi Creative City plays host to Café Tempo, which boasts a particularly appealing concept: during the day, it operates as a bakery and café, while at night it comes alive as a buzzy bistro. The high-ceilinged room with its bold chequerboard floor and zinc ducting is dominated by an open kitchen, where a chargrill takes centre stage, and it’s here that the highlight dishes are created, from Savoy cabbage to tender deer. Many of the appealing Mediterranean plates are designed for sharing, but thankfully not the delicious saffron cake with pistachio ice cream!

Name: CafeZique
Address: Rua das Bicas Velhas 5, Loulé, 8100 551, Portugal
Description: Within the walls of Loulé’s medieval castle, CaféZïque appears in a charming two-storey house overlooking the cobbled streets, with views over the Algarve hills. In a relaxed yet sophisticated atmosphere, the duo Leandro Araújo (chef) and João Valadas (sommelier) offers author-driven cuisine with a Portuguese soul and international influences, based on regional produce and showing a strong bond with the sea. Presented in two tasting menus and à la carte options, the experience begins on the rooftop with a welcome cocktail and continues with dishes such as Choco grelhado (grilled cuttlefish) with coriander and loquats, Sarrajão (Algarve-style fish dish) with red pepper and bread crumble, or the delicious Arroz de enchidos (rice with sausages), Zambujal pork and hollandaise sauce. The dessert of Bolo de alfarroba (carob cake) with green olives and olive oil — reveals a sweet finale with an unmistakable Algarve accent.

Name: Cafeína
Description: This is the first restaurant of the Cafeína Group, boasting 30 years of operation. Set on a corner between Rua do Padrão and Rua Gondarém, it occupies an old villa that retains its façade of tiles, still in pristine condition. Upon entering, you’ll find a classy, refined setting, marked by dark woods and warm hues, along with a traditionally styled bar. The bistronomie concept that defines it is clearly influenced by French cuisine, while also revisiting Portuguese dishes with a contemporary twist. Although the menu is packed with appealing options, ranging from puff pastry lobster soup to duck rice, be sure to save room for the “Cafeína classic”, the Crepe queimado (Crepe flambée), prepared with surprising flavours and textures.

Name: Caffè Cosi - La trattoria de Bruno Caironi
Description: Of Italian and Mediterranean inspiration, this bright, modern trattoria, housed in a former art gallery, overlooks a cobbled courtyard. We fell head over heels with the roasted artichokes in a pesto and parmesan jus. Before leaving, pop into the gourmet delicatessen store and stock up on top-of-the-range Italian goodies.

Name: Caffè Grande - Osteria del Centro
Description: Almost all the main dishes at this restaurant are grilled (mostly meat but there are also fish options), plus there’s a good choice of appetisers, including substantial options such as tripe and sweetbreads, with tasting menus that combine starters and main courses. The à la carte features a generous selection of classic, well-prepared dishes made from top-quality ingredients. The restaurant occupies the premises of a historic café that has experienced closures and problems in the past but has now been courageously reopened by three young business partners.

Name: Caffè Meletti
Address: via del Trivio 56 (piazza del Popolo), Ascoli Piceno, 63100, Italy
Description: Housed on the first floor of the historic café where the aniseed liqueur of the same name was created, this restaurant serves simple yet creative, regional and maritime - inspired cuisine. Don’t miss the terrace with views of Piazza del Popolo. Faster options available at lunchtime.

Name: Caffè Rojano
Address: 9 Mill Square, Padstow, PL28 8AE, United Kingdom
Description: Along with Rick Stein, Paul Ainsworth has come to define the Padstow food scene. This is his take on a lively Italian brasserie, where you'll find a good buzz from the contented holidaymakers. Well-executed pizzas and pastas form the core of the menu, but you'll also find Mediterranean-inspired fare such as Cornish cod with a pancetta and chorizo Tuscan bean stew. For dessert, opt for the intriguingly named signature 'Whoopsy Splunker'. The glass-enclosed terrace is a great spot on a sunny summer's day.

Name: Caffè delle Rose Bistrot
Description: Occupying an early 20C building in the heart of Pallanza’s picturesque historic centre, this authentic bistro now has a young and contemporary feel. Run by Massimiliano Celeste, a talented chef who is very well known in the region, the restaurant specialises in Mediterranean cuisine prepared with a touch of imagination. There’s a small chef’s table in front of the kitchen, plus an old ice-house (now a small wine cellar housing some excellent wines) which is well worth visiting.

Name: Caffé César L'initial
Description: A large patio and a spacious, modern interior with an open-plan kitchen set the scene for spot-on, bistronomic cuisine, steeped in the aromas and flavours of Provence and the Mediterranean. Tartlet of rockfish and artichoke with sumac; dentex with parsnips and a lemon-cardamon sauce; chocolate opéra cake. A cheerful, friendly vibe with wines by the glass from a magnum bottle…

Name: Café Alaia
Description: Looking for a truly warm and expansive spot serving special Italian cuisine? Come to this rustic-chic café, prettified with double-height ceilings, exposed wooden beams, and an ample bar. There are two rooms, each long and narrow but wonderfully comfortable and always abuzz. Thoughtfully arranged tables may be cradled with such impressively rich plates as tortellini en brodo, where house-made pasta bathes in a rich savory chicken broth, and pan-seared salmon with a mustard-based sauce, fingerling potatoes, and market carrots.

Name: Café Bohème
Address: 21-23 Windmill Brae, Aberdeen City, AB11 6HU, United Kingdom
Description: Tucked away in a city centre side street is this restaurant run by a friendly team with a genuine desire to please. Given the name, it's unsurprising to find a French bistro style to the décor, including simple wooden tables and wood panelling on the walls. The menu has a similarly Gallic influence, with time-honoured classics like pommes anna and crème brûlée to be found on the à la carte – yet there is a modernity and creativity in the cooking too, alongside technical skill from the kitchen team.

Name: Café Boulud
Address: Ground Floor, Four Seasons Hotel Riyadh, Kingdom Centre, Olaya Street, Al Olaya, Riyadh, 11321, Saudi Arabia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,No alcohol served,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Daniel Boulud brings his Café Boulud to the Four Seasons Hotel at the Kingdom Center. A series of elegant pastel decorated rooms including a bar, lounge and orangery make up the space. The all-encompassing menu blends creative French classics with subtle tastes of the Middle East in refined and eye-catching creations. Turophiles will appreciate the fine selection of French cheeses – they even have a cheese chef who will help you with your choices. On weekdays, make use of their good value business lunch menu, while Fridays offer a brunch menu.

Name: Café Bras
Description: The Café Bras, established in the heart of the Soulages Museum, pays tribute to Averyron produce. Two possibilities: order a snack or picnic basket from the counter or take a seat in the restaurant… The kitchen team crafts crisp, aromatic, light dishes, rich in generosity, colour and scents, like a tartare of tuna marinated in calamansi and Greek-style cucurbits or breast of roast duckling, acidic jus, new potatoes, cone cabbage and tiger courgettes with a sauce vierge. The attention lavished on flavour is second to none, as are the welcome and interior décor. Fully worthy of its ongoing success.

Name: Café Brunet
Address: 18 place Gabriel-Fauré - à Annecy-le-Vieux, Annecy, 74940, France
Description: This café dating back to 1875 is a real haven. It has managed to keep intact its soul of an authentic and convivial bistro (terrace, boules). As time meanders by, enjoy a good hearty meal or tasty little dishes.

Name: Café Café
Address: 175 Jalan Maharajalela, Kampung Attap, Kuala Lumpur, 50150, Malaysia
Description: Founded by two local chefs who plied their trade in France, Café Café is tucked away in a quiet part of the city. The interior, dripping in contemporary Parisian chic and traditional French grandeur, is ideal for a romantic dinner. The à la carte and set menus include classic dishes such as foie gras, escargots and duck confit. The carefully crafted food is perfectly poised between knockout texture and spot-on seasoning. The leg of duck confit has a crispy, delicious skin and succulent meat.

Name: Café Carducci
Description: Those with a passion for retro and nostalgic atmospheres will find inspiration in this establishment opened in 1928. Since then, generations have succeeded one another, but always within the same family. Today, you enter through the bar before passing into the dining room, a space so enchanting with its books, paintings, and bottles that you’ll never want to leave. Alongside a vast selection of cured meats and cheeses (predominantly French), exquisite meat and fish dishes await, complemented by a legendary cellar boasting some two thousand labels.

Name: Café Carmellini
Address: The Fifth Avenue Hotel, 250 Fifth Ave., New York, NY, 10001, USA
Description: Andrew Carmellini's return to fine dining is housed in the Fifth Avenue Hotel, a former Gilded Age gem now recast as an elegant NoMad stomping ground. The dining room bears a sumptuous throwback ambience with wood plank flooring, curved sapphire-blue velvet booths and caramel leather seating. The open kitchen turns out dishes that whiff of the Mediterranean, as in the crab mille-feuille, a neatly arranged tower of delicate wafers and sweet crabmeat in a golden-yellow Meyer lemon sauce. Scallops Cardoz is a heartwarming composition dedicated to the late Chef Floyd Cardoz and features beautifully seared bivalves with a turmeric-tinted and warmly spiced coconut milk sauce. The squab en croûte pairs rich and rosy breast meat and seared foie gras in a thin layer of pastry.

Name: Café Caron
Description: Vichyssoise, bouillabaisse, boudin blanc, pithivier – just hearing the names of these classics quickens the pulse of bistro aficionados, all the more so when they know that the kitchen is led by none other than celebrated chef and TV personality Alain Caron. The team respect the characteristic generosity of traditional French cuisine, but welcome modern spins and updates. The atmosphere is très française at this lively establishment, where the masterful "Caron touch" delights palates.

Name: Café Compagnon
Description: After Richer and 52 Faubourg, Charles Compagnon, restaurant owner, sommelier and coffee roaster, strikes again! This cafe offers an extensive menu ranging from nibbles to share to home-made ices. The original, deftly crafted recipes feature a modern bistro slant, depicted by market-fresh starters and succulent loin of pork. Heart-warming, authentic comfort food.

Name: Café Cracco
Address: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, Milan, 20121, Italy
Description: This café run by the famous chef of the same name (his gourmet restaurant is on the first floor of the same building) is the bar-pasticceria par excellence in Milan. It is also a good place to eat, with a menu that moves easily from Milanese specialities reinterpreted with a modern twist to international dishes, including pizza. The café offers tables arranged outdoors in the extraordinary Galleria and is open seven days a week but does not take bookings.

Name: Café César
Description: In a quiet little street, opposite a park, Café César is a modern bistro with a colourful, light-filled interior (red bricks, some painted white, blue zellige tiled counter, polished concrete flooring). From morning to night, people come and go, for coffee, lunch or dinner, the common thread being the precise and carefully prepared cuisine. The sauces and gravies, prepared to exacting standards, give layers of flavour to the dishes – crabmeat enhanced with curry, scallops served with a creamy fish roe sauce, or hot chocolate tartlet. Everything served here is house-made, the service is relaxed and, at lunchtime, the bill is more than reasonable. As Henry Miller would say, "Quiet Days in Clichy"!

Name: Café Deco
Address: 43 Store Street, Fitzrovia, London, WC1E 7DB, United Kingdom
Description: There is something refreshingly straightforward about this little neighbourhood restaurant, just around the corner from the British Museum. Its look is clean and simple, its service team are friendly and attentive, and its ambience is that of a buzzing little bistro. The regularly changing menu focuses on what’s in season and the cooking is honest, fresh and uncomplicated. The daily blackboard special is also worth considering or you can start with some nibbles, like anchovy buttered soldiers, then go for something like pork & veal goulash or some roast sea bass.

Name: Café Imperial
Description: A truly magnificent setting! The restaurant of the Art Deco Imperial Hotel, a time-honoured establishment, occupies a stylish high-ceilinged room in which gorgeous historical ceramic detailing on the ceiling, walls and striking columns draws the eye. The atmosphere is lively without being hectic, and the service is well organised and professional. Featured on the classic-leaning menu is a good selection of dishes, including Czech favourites. As the place is worth seeing and attracts many guests, it's wise to book! Also open for breakfast, brunch, coffee and cake.

Name: Café Kestrel
Address: 293 Van Brunt St., Brooklyn, NY, 11231, USA
Description: Café Kestrel occupies a diminutive space in Brooklyn's Red Hook neighborhood, but what is lacks in size it more than makes up for with thoughtful culinary executions and warm, refined service. At once casual and elegant, the tightly edited menu sports French leaning, pan-European selections with small bites like baguettes and chilled shrimp to larger terrines, salads and a broad list of entrées. Many dishes become instant favorites, as in the sage-infused fried halloumi served over honey Main dishes include duck leg confit with rich, creamy rutabaga puree and candied kumquats or a seafood terrine with crème fraîche and crispy, golden gaufrettes. Dessert is non-negotiable, especially the apricot cake with caramel sauce.

Name: Café Les Paillotes
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This old acquaintance of the Michelin Guide now has a new chef at the helm! Although the decor and furnishings remain the same with a slightly old-fashioned feel, the cuisine is modern yet with no unnecessary frills and has a fresh and generous flavour. Highlights on the menu include the new raw fish options, which have an entire tasting menu to themselves. The well-stocked wine cellar is home to around 500 labels which offer good value for money.

Name: Café Medina
Address: L'Hermitage Vancouver,780 Richards St., Vancouver, V6B 3A4, Canada
Description: The clink of glasses, the hissing steam of the cappuccino maker, even the shuffling back and forth to the counter by loyal patrons...Café Medina hums with activity all day long. This casual spot attracts locals who flock here for hearty Mediterranean-style fare. Mornings are especially great here—it's when egg dishes take center stage. The heady smell of freshly made Belgian waffles may have you trying to jump the (long) line outside, but ask nicely and they'll share a few of the hand-sized waffles while you wait. Once seated, don't waste any time deciding, as the paella is a must order. Inspired by the Spanish classic, their version is made with orzo flecked with cubes of smoky, spicy chorizo, roasted vegetables, avocado and a textbook-perfect fried egg.

Name: Café Quinson
Description: The Café Quinson has reopened! In this rustic yet elegant “mountain restaurant”, the whole family makes guests feel welcome, serving a selection of regional dishes with an imaginative and contemporary touch. Excellent choice of wines, almost all of which are available by the glass.

Name: Café Rapp
Description: A visit to this delightful village is definitely worthwhile! Originally a bakery and café, this family-run establishment has evolved into a restaurant serving flavoursome, meticulously prepared dishes that take their cue from the changing seasons. As well as à la carte options, there is a choice of set menus. The upscale setting has a classic aesthetic. Attentive service comes courtesy of a well-organised and adept front-of-house team. A must in the afternoon: the delicious freshly baked cakes! Pretty guestrooms.

Name: Café Riggs
Address: 900 F St. NW, Washington, DC, 20004, USA
Description: Inspired by the bustling brasseries of Europe, Cafe Riggs offers grace and modernity in a very polished setting. The historic dining room and bar, kitted out with gleaming brass and marble and velvet-covered Art deco booths, are not short on ambience. The sharp waitstaff makes this a prime business lunch or dinner destination, as well as an ideal post-work watering hole. Classic dishes with quality products shine, as in the delicate Wagyu beef tartare with creamy mustard sauce, tart capers and cornichons. Prawn risotto with saffron, peas and pickled ramps is a vibrant yet delicate, sea-forward course with a surprising refinement. Finally, nothing says goodbye quite like a chocolate soufflé, served here with Grand Marnier caramel sauce.

Name: Café Roma
Address: 4 rue des Escaliers Sainte-Anne, Avignon, 84000, France
Description: Italia Palladino's second restaurant (the other being Italie Là-Bas), Café Roma boasts a prime location in the historical centre, at the foot of one of the towers of the Palais des Papes – admire the view from the terrace. The colourful interior decor with large golden mirrors adds to the charm. The dishes showcase the generous and fragrant flavours of the Mediterranean, incorporating the occasional Asian influence: grilled prawns glazed with ginger and soy sauce, Thai-style black rice served with swordfish and caponata.

Name: Café Savoy
Description: Located in the same building as the iconic Restaurant Savoy, on the city’s central esplanade, this well-run brasserie is spacious, airy and deservedly busy. The cooking is classical with a southern French influence, so expect to find the likes of salade Niçoise and ratatouille on the menu. The chefs prepare their good quality ingredients with care, resulting in authentic and flavoursome dishes.

Name: Café Terroir
Description: Established near the Célestins Theatre, under the auspices of Jean-François Têtedoie (son of legendary Christian!), this house upholds the art of good food. The menu reads like a culinary bible of Lyon’s specialties: signature dishes like homemade terrine and gâteau lyonnais rub shoulders with rotisserie joints, to be shared and carved in front of you (Bresse poultry, rib of beef), without forgetting a lineup of bistro classics such as calf’s sweetbread vol-au-vent or Monts du Lyonnais snails with girolle mushrooms and cress. The wine cellar boasts over 1,500 references at temptingly reasonable prices.

Name: Café Terroir Chez Saint-Cyr
Description: The twin of the Lyon Café Terroir, this restaurant is located in the grounds of Domaine Saint-Cyr, the wine estate in Anse, on the edge of the Beaujolais area. A new take on Lyon specialities, excellent roast meats for sharing and an extensive wine list, on which the estate takes centre stage alongside vintages from Beaujolais and other terroirs, all from independent winegrowers. The place has a rustic and welcoming bistro feel and a terrace looking out onto the surrounding countryside.

Name: Café Xander
Address: Hotel Haffner Resort & Spa, ul. Jana Jerzego Haffnera 59, Sopot, 81-715, Poland
Description: Housed inside a hotel but with a separate entrance and a feel all its own, this elegant restaurant is worth the short walk out from the city centre. Start with a cocktail while you study the concise à la carte, where the Polish cooking comes with a Mediterranean influence that's noticeable in the occasional pasta or risotto. Top produce is clearly a priority, with the quality of the ingredients evident across the dishes. Attractive presentation and a touch of formality in the service enhance the experience.

Name: Café de Paris
Address: Place du Casino, Monaco, 98000, Principality of Monaco
Description: This refurbishment project is the first by renowned British architects, David Collins Studio, in Monaco and the result is spectacular! The firm has intelligently and respectfully preserved the pared-back Art deco spirit so dear to the Café de Paris’ regulars, thus creating an exquisite setting of wrought iron, mosaics and stained glass for chef Victor Marion’s new twist on brasserie classics. Egg mayonnaise with caviar, pâté en croûte, sole meunière and the iconic Crêpe Suzette (which was invented here!), flambéed at the table and served with orange zests in syrup for added decadence… Open morning ‘til night 7 days a week.

Name: Café de la Fontaine
Address: 4 avenue du Général-de-Gaulle, La Turbie, 06320, France
Description: Taken over by a duo of young professionals, Café de la Fontaine has been given a new lease of life without losing the nostalgic charm of a village café. The menu revolves around nicely crafted bistro classics: house-made country terrine seasoned with five-peppercorn mix, stuffed cabbage, onglet steak with marchand de vin sauce, pearly cod loin and petits pois à la parisienne, seasonal clafoutis.

Name: Café des Banques
Description: In the heart of Geneva, this chic bistro is the lair of Yoann Caloué who draws upon seasonal ingredients and high-flying technique to craft contemporary French cuisine. The classy yet cosily chummy setting provides the perfect foil to dishes of the likes of carpaccio of scallops enhanced by a sea urchin mayonnaise or free-range chicken served with a truffle-flavoured gravy. Wine buffs will be enchanted by the cellar, which stars mostly French wineries, with the odd international gem. The desserts are also meticulously crafted, illustrated by two signatures: soufflé à la chartreuse and lemon tart with a limoncello sabayon. This smart venue manages to combine fine dining with a friendly buzzy vibe.

Name: Café des Ministères
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: This neighbourhood cafe-inspired bistro is a firm favourite with fans of authentic French cuisine (especially from the south-west) and knockout sauces. Vol-au-vent with sweetbread, poultry and truffle jus, as well as stuffed Pontoise cabbage (French champion in 2022) are among its signature dishes. Now add a fine selection of wines from all over France, painstakingly curated by Roxane, the chef’s wine-buff wife, who can be relied upon for her inspired insights. Bookings highly recommended.

Name: Caia
Address: 46 Golborne Road, Notting Hill, London, W10 5PR, United Kingdom
Description: ‘Fire, wine, vinyl’ it says outside this cool Notting Hill spot – and that pretty much sums it up. It's the kind of place you come with friends for a fun night out, with the intimate basement room housing a diverse album library as well as a DJ spinning records most nights. Start with one of the snacks and a cocktail from the creative list, then choose from sharing plates that often feature a lick of fire. Ikejime trout meunière is the kind of classically based dish you can expect, while the moreish leek and comté gratin is a must-order when it's on the menu.

Name: Caillou
Description: Caillou is a hip, modern restaurant, strewn with passing nods to ‘pebbles’ (its namesake). The kitchen team prepares the food on a central table that sets the scene for their culinary show. The performance continues in the plate, with an appetising blend of flavours and textures and enticing veggie dishes. The chef doesn’t hesitate to spice up traditional recipes, flanking lobster and turbot, for example, with deftly crafted side dishes such as asparagus flan, a gutsy lobster béarnaise and a poivrade of fried artichokes. The sommelier may suggest an elegant mineral wine, echoing the establishment’s name, to pair with your food.

Name: Cais
Description: A relaxed restaurant with a lively atmosphere and good food, so it’s not surprising that it’s always full. Occupying a charming small house in the Vila Madalena neighbourhood of the city, Cais features tables outdoors next to the window, seats at the counter by the kitchen, as well more traditional tables. Run by Adriano de Laurentiis in the kitchen and chef Catarina Ferraz, its cuisine is centred around fresh fish and seafood. The concise menu is constantly updated in line with the availability and freshness of seasonal ingredients. Having savoured the delicious appetisers on offer here, we particularly recommend the week’s selection of fish and seafood, followed by the creamy and delicate cheesecake served with a milk sorbet.

Name: Cais da Villa
Address: Rua Monsenhor Jerónimo do Amaral, Vila Real, 5000-570, Portugal
Description: One of this establishment’s most striking features is its privileged setting: a century-old former warehouse located beside the city’s railway station. This charming, fully renovated space, regarded as one of the region’s tourist attractions, serves cuisine grounded in tradition and local roots, with pride of place given to seasonal produce and native breeds. The result is dishes such as PDO Maronesa veal rib and Bísaro pork secreto, while the dessert selection is headed by the traditional Pão-de-Ló à Caisdavilla, firm on the outside and creamy within, releasing a delicious egg custard when cut. The offering includes à la carte options, a five-course tasting menu guided by the chef’s inspiration, and a set lunch menu (available on weekdays); if you do not have time for a full meal, you can opt for a generous brunch.

Name: Caja de Cerillas
Description: The name (the Spanish for “matchbox”) is the perfect fit given the small size of this well-run restaurant with a pleasant bistro-style ambience. On his à la carte, owner-chef Enrique Valentí, focuses on risk-free, quality cuisine including several sharing options. His clam stew with white beans is outstanding, as is the finely textured dessert called “the flan you didn't eat in your childhood”. We also recommend booking a table in advance here.

Name: Cal Marquès
Description: Cal Marquès is located in the historic centre of Camprodon, one of the prettiest towns in the Ripollès region. Here, on the ground floor of Hostal La Placeta, you will find a traditional Catalan-inspired menu with its roots firmly within the surrounding area, as well as a tasting menu (Simbiosi) that showcases the best high-altitude cuisine. The dishes featuring lamb from Ripollès, raised on the family farm, are the stars of the show!

Name: Cal Pere del Maset
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: A family-run restaurant established over half a century ago where you can enjoy cooking with a traditional flavour, including renowned dishes such as baked cannelloni and pigs’ trotters with plums.

Name: Cal Travé
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: This impressively run family restaurant boasts a delightful decorative backdrop of antique objects (large wall clocks, wind instruments, coffee grinders etc) plus an open grill at the far end of the dining room. The traditionally focused Catalan cuisine on offer here features excellent stews, aged meats and plenty of grilled options (we particularly enjoyed the grilled duck breast). A selection of the restaurant’s own still and sparkling wines are also sold here.

Name: Cal Viva
Address: Gutemberg 20, Morón de la Frontera, 41530, Spain
Description: This restaurant, surprising both for its pleasant decor and its location on an industrial estate, takes its name from the Spanish word for “quicklime”, highlighting the historical importance of this artisanal product on the local economy. Here, chef Leonardo Ramos conjures up an updated take on traditional cuisine, based around locally sourced seasonal ingredients and showcased on two tasting menus (Omakase Andaluz and Homenaje Omakase) that change daily and on which the chef chooses dishes for his guests. You’ll also find options that don’t feature on any of the menus, including soups, stews and rice dishes.

Name: Cala
Address: José Luís Pérez Pujadas 7, Granada, 18006, Spain
Description: Located in the area known as the Forum, near the Parque de Las Ciencias, this restaurant is definitely worth a visit as it is intimate (just four tables) and boasts a meticulously contemporary interior. The cuisine here is an updated take on tradition that always pays homage to French (the chef, Samuel Hernández, is of French origin), Portuguese (because of his mother) and Spanish (because of his father) recipes. The concept revolves around a single tasting menu, with wine pairing options, which changes with each season and prioritises the use of seasonal and locally sourced produce, as well as a series of suggestions not included on the menu.

Name: Cala Luna
Address: Via Angela di Francesca 1, Cefalu, 90015, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Refined fine dining at the boutique hotel "Le Calette." In the summertime, Cala Luna is hosted in a splendid garden surrounded by plants and flowers, with breathtaking views of the bay, the Caldura sea stacks, and the Rocca. The dishes are a technical and creative expression of Chef Dario Pandolfo’s experiences, who applies what he has learned working in prestigious restaurants in Italy and abroad to Sicilian ingredients and traditions. The result is a vibrant and colorful cuisine, sometimes with strong flavors, always creative and deeply Mediterranean. "Green" notes are evident not only in the "Fiori di Luna" menu, dedicated to Sicilian vegetables, herbs, and flowers, but also in the sustainable approach to using raw materials, enhancing every part of them, and focusing on reducing waste without ever compromising quality.

Name: Cala del Tanit
Address: Rua Pais De Araújo, 147, São Paulo, 04531-090, Brazil
Description: A new culinary venture courtesy of chef Oscar Bosch, who has been on the rise in São Paulo's food scene since he opened the successful Tanit in the Jardins district of the city. Located in Itaim Bibi, in one of the typical three-storey houses in this neighbourhood, Cala del Tanit boasts a terrace at the entrance and a contemporary interior with a predominance of wood, an open-view kitchen and a counter where cocktails are also prepared for guests. The menu retains the essence of Mediterranean cuisine, with Spanish dishes such as tomato gazpacho and delicious rice dishes (Paella Marinera and duck rice socarrat, with grilled octopus and aioli), although the culinary repertoire here also includes an array of pasta dishes and a few Asian touches. A space for small private events, called Sala X, is also available.

Name: Caladh
Address: Church Road, Greystones, A63 TW18, Ireland
Description: A welcome addition to this residential seaside town just south of Dublin, Caladh sits inside a double-fronted Georgian property painted in a fresh light green colour that permeates inside, giving a cool, calming vibe to the brasserie-style dining room. The chefs aren’t trying to reinvent the wheel here, and therein lies the appeal. Classic dishes like confit duck leg and grilled pork chop are ingredient-led and lean on the abundant natural flavours of the produce. A sensibly priced wine list adds to the already considerable attraction.

Name: Calcifer
Description: Forget fire demons and infernos – here it's all about the art of wood-fired cooking, with mouth-watering dishes prepared in plain sight in the open kitchen of this neo-vintage bistro. In the lively atmosphere of the dining room with delightfully retro mosaic tiling, or in the privacy of a booth, tuck into superb whole cuts (eg turbot, matured Galician sirloin steak or Burgos suckling pig) served simply on stainless steel platters for sharing, accompanied by smoked lettuce or grilled seasonal vegetables. A warm welcome.

Name: Caleña
Description: A unique restaurant located alongside the city walls (the name Caleña is a reference to the type of stone used in its construction) and part of the La Casa del Presidente hotel, which was once the home of Adolfo Suárez (the first elected president of the Spanish government in its modern democratic era).This elegant eatery, occupying a rustic, glass-fronted annexe in the garden area of the hotel, has its own independent access and is run by young chef Diego Sanz, who aims to create an experience that takes guests on a journey across the roots of Castilian cuisine, albeit from a modern perspective. On his tasting menu, Tresbolillo, offering an immersive journey involving strong technique and interesting reflections on the environment (there are combinations as surprising as prawn-pine-pine nut), you will discover its approach to produce from the vegetable garden, marinades, delicious stews and fantastic grilled dishes. The finishing touches to many of the dishes here are added on a stand in front of the table.

Name: Calice
Description: The team from Baillote strikes again! Located in a narrow, picturesque little street, this convivial restaurant boasts a dining area done out in ochre tones and with leather banquette seating, an open kitchen with a counter and a back room with a skylight. Chef Louis Fedide (who has worked at Le Gavroche in London) is winning over diners with modern cuisine that combines French ingredients with the flavours of Japan – the influence of co-owner Kazuma Chikuda makes itself felt here. He cooks his pork tenderloin, cherry jus, pommes Anna and pak choi, for example, over binchotan charcoal. Delicious lunchtime menu-carte; in the evening, enticing small plates and fine cuts of meat and fish to share.

Name: Calipso Fish
Address: Küçükyalı Sahil, Cumhuriyet Caddesi No:2, Küçükyalı/Maltepe, Istanbul, 34840, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Istanbul residents come to this sun-drenched upscale restaurant to escape the hustle and bustle of the city. The waiters give expert advice on the wide selection of mezze in the display fridge – the salads are beautifully aromatic! And that's just the beginning, because the traditional preparation methods accentuate the rich flavours of super-fresh fish and seafood. Whatever you choose from the menu, the chef will cook it according to your wishes: sea bass, for example, grilled to juicy perfection and served with al dente vegetables. No unnecessary frills; just ingredient-led cuisine that never fails to impress. A reliable favourite!

Name: Calvi Ristorante
Description: This welcoming, contemporary-style restaurant with a large open-view kitchen serves two different types of cuisine – one regional and Mediterranean in style, the other more creative allowing the chef’s culinary skills to take centre stage. The black rice tacos with roasted eel, green beans, soya bean sprouts and spicy hummus mayo are truly delicious – definitely to be eaten with the hands!

Name: Camana Veglia
Description: Situated on the first floor of the hotel of the same name, this restaurant is run by professional and welcoming staff who immediately make you feel pleasantly at home in the warm, Stube-style dining room. The menu features local specialties alongside more creative options for guests keen for a change from traditional cuisine.

Name: Cambium Pirineos
Address: Plaza del Valle de Tena 7, Sallent de Gállego, 22640, Spain
Description: Located in the centre of the village, Cambium, which is Latin for “change” and is also the word to describe one of the outer layers of a tree trunk, is keen for guests to discover the flavours of the Aragonese Pyrenees from a different perspective. In its pleasant, rustic-style dining rooms, featuring a profusion of wood and views of both the village and its impressive surrounding mountains, choose between an à la carte option or two seasonal menus on request (Olla Tensina y Summum) with dishes such as marinated Oliván trout and IGP Aragón veal, which connect us with the culinary traditions of this part of the Alto Gállego region. An impressive array of D.O. Somontano wines completes the picture!

Name: Camille
Address: 2-3 Stoney Street, Borough Market, Southwark, London, SE1 9AA, United Kingdom
Description: Situated at the entrance to the foodie wonderland that is Borough Market, this intimate French bistro is rooted in an ethos of unpretentious, pared-back cooking that perfectly suits its rustic interior design. The blackboard-written menu is regularly changing, and you can expect straightforward yet eminently satisfying dishes like pâté-en-croûte or whole mackerel with café de Paris butter. A friendly welcome and cheery service ensure you’ll be dining with a smile on your face.

Name: Camilo
Description: This building was the backdrop to one of the most emblematic novels of Portuguese literature, as it was here that the writer Camilo Castelo Branco would meet his beloved Ana Plácido. In this establishment, spread over two storeys and with an open kitchen visible from the entrance, chef Diogo Coimbra presents contemporary cuisine with international influences, devised from national produce and placing fire and embers centre stage. The offering is divided into two concepts: the first is rooted in Portuguese cuisine, featuring an à la carte menu inspired by the love story between the writer and his beloved; the second, a tasting menu, explores the relationship between Ana Plácido and her husband, drawing on techniques and influences from different parts of the world. Alongside each dish on the menu, you will find a wine suggestion to pair with your choice!

Name: Camino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: The concept is hometown cooking from all twenty of Italy’s regions, spreading the word about the traditional dishes of each. Running the gamut from north to south, the prix fixe menu criss-crosses the Italian peninsula. Many ingredients are imported from Italy, keeping flavours as true to their roots as possible. The house makes its own pasta, demonstrating consummate skill. Like the menu, the wine list covers the whole of Italy. Wines from native cultivars are on offer, offering harmonious companions to dishes from the same region.

Name: Campagne, Vignes et Gourmandises
Address: 629 chemin des Terres, route de Suze-la-Rousse, Sainte-Cécile-les-Vignes, 84290, France
Description: With its atmosphere blending rustic charm (exposed stones, painted wooden furniture) and modern touches (contemporary paintings), this restaurant has bags of character. In the kitchen, chef Sylvain Fernandes prepares fresh ingredients in a subtle celebration of the flavours of the South of France. Extremely courteous service provided by Sylvia, the chef's wife!

Name: Campamac
