Address: 80 Guangming 1st Road, Zhubei City, Hsinchu County, Taiwan
Description: This yakiniku restaurant, prized for its Japanese Wagyu menu, is just the ticket for beef lovers. The well-curated set menus are ideal to sample a range of different cuts, including rare morsels like chateaubriand and zabuton. Everything is grilled to perfection at your table, and served with condiments like wasabi and garlic chips to complement the buttery notes. Wagyu sausage is another must-try. There is also a non-beef menu with seafood, pork and lamb.

Name: Chuan Kitchen
Address: 50/666 Mu 6, Soi Mu Ban Mueang Thong Thani, Ban Mai, Pak Kret, Nonthaburi, 11120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: With Singaporean chicken rice, Indonesian laksa and Malaysian Bak Kut Teh the highlights, Chuan Kitchen is the only restaurant in Nonthaburi offering this mix of national cuisine. Its stylish design is welcoming, with a high wooden ceiling, and floor-to-ceiling windows, accentuated by black stainless-steel frames and lighting. The nasi lemak and char kway teow are well executed, delivering a complete balance of flavours.

Name: Chuan Mu Yuan
Address: 120, Section 2, Chengde Road, Datong District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: Since moving here in 2024, the queues in front of this eatery have far from dwindled. In a cheerful, cosy interior, the regulars, who used to enjoy watching the chefs making dim sum behind a glazed partition, can still do so thanks to the semi-open kitchen. Crispy pancake roll filled with beef, scallion and sweet soybean sauce remains the hottest choice on the menu. Those who don’t eat beef, can order the dried small fish instead.

Name: Chuan Tai Hao Milkfish Ball
Address: 222, Section 1, Datong Road, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
Description: The owner worked in a milkfish ball shop for over 30 years before opening his own eatery in the 2010s. The stall sells soups with milkfish, fishballs and meatballs – customise the components to your liking. The springy milkfish balls are the highlight, but the fish skin is also worth trying – a thin layer of minced milkfish is spread on cooked fish skin for lovely textures. The aromatic diced pork rice with coriander makes for a hearty meal.

Name: Chuan Yu
Description: This Pacific Renaissance Plaza spot is a restaurant within a restaurant. Set on the second floor, it shares acreage with Sakura as well as the patio that overlooks downtown Oakland. The room is simple, with a host stand greeting diners. A long bar resides on the left; white booth seating on the right; and black tables run down the middle. A striking wall display of bottles puts diners in the mood for a sip before they sup. Service can be spotty, but all is forgiven when the Sichuan menu, complete with the classics, is presented. Portions are hefty, so bring a buddy and indulge in such refreshing starters as a lotus root salad with ginger and garlic sauce. This may be tailed by the likes of fiery mapo tofu or chongqing chicken for a tongue-numbing finish.

Name: Chuan Yue Hai Tang (Changning)
Address: A01, 4F, Livat, 788 Jinzhong Road, Changning, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: Several famous chefs joined forces in this venture that offers traditional and creative Cantonese and Sichuanese fare under one roof. Flavours are nuanced and varied, making for a multi-faceted experience. Signatures include roast young duck with Sichuan pepper, a crossover between Cantonese barbecue and Sichuanese spice. Yellow croaker can be prepared in myriad ways – try it poached in claypot with aged dried radish.

Name: Chuanpu (Lihua Street)
Address: 1F, Huangcheng Jewelry Exchange Center, 39-1 Lihua Street, Jinjiang, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
Description: The entrance may be rather obscure, but it is well worth seeking out Chuanpu for its authentic Fujian cooking. There is no menu – take your pick from the live fish tank near the kitchen. Eel, whelks and razor clams are among the most popular choices. Servers recommend having the eel steamed in black bean sauce to accentuate its fattiness. Other Fujian specialities such as layered pork intestine, and lor mee also live up to their reputation.

Name: Chubby Castor
Address: Fitzwilliam Arms, 34 Peterborough Road, Castor, PE5 7AX, United Kingdom
Description: There are few more inviting sights in Britain than a proper thatched pub. The Chubby Castor is a fine example, a 400-year-old village inn whose chocolate-box exterior belies its more modern, bright and somewhat glitzy interior design that stretches from a smart lounge into the intimate, linen-laid dining room. The cooking, overseen by experienced chef-owner Adebola Adeshina, is centred around time-honoured recipes that deliver on flavour. For dessert, look out for the wonderful Firetree chocolate with peanuts and caramel.

Name: Chubby Fish
Description: Ask any Charlestonian if they've been to Chubby Fish and they'll either rave or tell you they can't get in. Open since 2018, this walk-in only spot is easily recognized by the long line that forms outside. If you're lucky enough to get in, there's a hip look and feel with a communal table at the center, tall ceilings and an open kitchen where you can see the team at work. As the name suggests, it's all about the sea, and Chef/owner James London's menu comprises raw offerings, appetizers and entrees that change often (they're handwritten over the kitchen). North Carolina yellowtail tuna crudo or chilled local Steamboat Creek oysters with crab fat curry make for a good start, then share one of their entrees like smoked sheepshead curry that's served atop a bed of skillfully cooked rice.

Name: Chubby's Jamaican Kitchen
Description: The warm breezes of the Caribbean might be far away, but even in the dead of winter, stepping into this lively haven will bring a bit of island sunshine. Warm, easygoing hospitality is matched by homey, unpretentious cooking, with traditional dishes whose humble appearances belie surprising depth of flavor. "Likkle bites" like saltfish fritters are a fine starter, but don't let them distract you from exemplary versions of comforting classics like curry goat or oxtail stew (and take urgent note that the gravy from either can be ordered as a side). Perhaps best of all is the succulent jerk chicken, expertly cooked over a wood-burning grill to achieve an ethereal marriage of smoke, sweetness and spice—as good as any you’re likely to find this far from a beach.

Name: Chuen Kee Seafood (Hoi Pong Street)
Address: 53 Hoi Pong Street, Sai Kung, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Two family-run restaurants just a few minutes’ walk from each other have been in business since the 80s; choose the one by the quay for the rooftop terrace and harbour views. A wide array of seafood is available from adjacent fishmongers: cuttlefish, crab, lobster, molluscs, shrimps…Select your meal from the tank and ask the servers the best ways to cook it. Abalone and mantis shrimp in peppered salt are the smash hits not to be missed.

Name: Chugoku Hanten Fureika
Description: A fixture of Higashiazabu for a quarter of a century, Chugoku Hanten Fureika is an evangelist for the traditional cuisine of China, with the focus on Shanghai and Cantonese cuisine. The menu dazzles the eye with over 100 à la carte items, including roasted Jinhua pork fillet, grouper steamed whole and soup of shàngtāng premium soup stock. The wide selection includes cuisine from every region of China, all prepared with seasonal ingredients. Sharing single items as a group is a special pleasure of Chinese cuisine.

Name: Chugoku Hanten Kohakukyu (Amber Palace)
Address: 5F, Palace Hotel Tokyo, 1-1-1 Marunouchi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo, 100-0005, Japan
Description: The dining room incorporates traditional Chinese decorations into a modern, elegant space. An extensive menu ranges from dishes of various regions to creative cookery with the accent on seasonality. Char siu and Peking duck arrive courtesy of the roasting chef, while steamed meat dumplings and soup dumplings are tended by the dim sum chef. Seafood is offered with XO sauce, fermented black beans, chilli sauce or other preparations to suit each guest’s preference—an appealing feature of the menu. Explore the subtlety and depth of Chinese cuisine in all its splendid regional variety.

Name: Chugokusai HINA
Description: Counter-style Chinese committed to natural deliciousness. The husband, schooled in the kitchens of Yokohama and Shanghai, focuses on the cooking, while his wife serves guests. The inherent flavours of the ingredients are held paramount, interpreting the seasons of Japan through Chinese cuisine. Each dish is seasoned with restraint and elegance. In a novel twist, instead of Shaoxing wine, items are paired with well-aged Japanese sake or organic wine.

Name: Chugokusai KAKYU-BOU
Description: Huaqiu (read as Kakyu in Japanese) is the name of a holy mountain, mentioned in a Chinese book of philosophy, where many fruits grow. The name Kakyu-bou, ‘Kitchen of Mount Huaqiu’, captures the joy of cooking in a spirit of thanksgiving for the foods granted by the gods. As an apprentice, the chef learned that without the basics there can be no application. Accordingly, he searches for innovation while staying within the boundaries of orthodox Chinese cuisine. The appetiser assortment consists of bounty from sea and soil prepared with Chinese techniques. The joy of cooking creates the joy of eating.

Name: Chugokusai Kan
Description: Owner-chef, a Keio University graduate, became a chef from his dreams of being an artisan; a person who can accomplish one thing can do anything. Flame-broiled items finished in the massive oven are a gift acquired through many labours as a hotel chef. Fujii cuts a deft and poised figure in the kitchen, master of both theory and practice. He claims his mother vehemently opposed his choice of career, but when he beholds the joy of his guests, his face is the picture of happiness.

Name: Chulita
Description: With its mod Mexican good looks and its Venice location not far from the beach, Chulita is primed for sunny SoCal days. Tacos are served all day at this spot where Oaxacan-style, California-influenced fare rules. Slake your thirst with a tequila or mezcal, then tuck into a starter, such as the quesadilla de calabaza, made from dark masa, filled with Oaxacan queso and garnished with pipián de calabaza. Tender barbacoa takes it up a notch. Tortillas are made in house, and tacos are always a good idea. Order the tinga de pollo, filled with juicy chicken, or go straight for the steak taco with its slight char. You'll be satiated but go for the vegan churros with dulce de leche-style dipping sauce anyway.

Name: Chum (Saraphi)
Address: 1/1 Mu 7, Tha Wang Tan, Saraphi, Chiang Mai, 50140, Thailand
Description: Chum serves Northern Thai cuisine cooked from the recipes of the family's grandmother. The colourful restaurant is simply decorated with red and yellow walls and brightly coloured parasols of Northern Thai design hanging from the ceilings. The stir-fried pork and liver is well cooked, and packed with Thai herbs, wild pepper and coriander. The mixed Northern Thai starter uses a tasty young chili relish with the scent of green chili that isn’t too spicy.

Name: Chun Yu Garden
Address: 36 Quanzhoucuo, Tamsui District, New Taipei, Taiwan
Description: Opened in 2012, this Zen-inspired space at a remove from the city is an oasis. Wood details and pops of red add warmth to the bare concrete room overlooking a manicured garden. The husband-and-wife team, both avid gardeners and tea lovers, wanted to deliver creative, refined Chinese cooking in omakase style. Velvety and creamy, their chicken soup is thickened with brown rice gruel and exudes the deep aroma of scallops. Vegan menu available by arrangement.

Name: Chung Cheng
Address: Golden Mile Food Centre, #01-59, 505 Beach Road, 199583, Singapore
Description: Three options feature on the menu of this stall – chilli mee, prawn mee and laksa. Go for chilli mee: yellow egg noodles topped with tangy chilli sauce, pork ribs, prawns, hard-boiled egg, fish cake and tofu puffs.

Name: Church Street Tavern
Address: 3 Church Street, Colchester, CO1 1NF, United Kingdom
Description: Down a narrow city centre street, you'll find this attractive 18th-century building; a restaurant sits upstairs, while below is a trendy bar serving cocktails and light bites. The extensive menu ranges from bruschetta to quesadillas – plus a roast dinner on Sundays, of course – and the kitchen team ensure the dishes are as colourful and joyous as the décor and the atmosphere. The super-friendly, attentive service will really make you feel at home, as will bringing your own bottle on Wednesdays to take advantage of half-price corkage.

Name: Chutney Mary
Address: 73 St James's Street, St James’s, London, SW1A 1PH, United Kingdom
Description: This long-standing, popular Indian restaurant comes from the same stable as Veeraswamy and Amaya, and its stylish dining room may be the jewel in the group’s crown. A certain luxury is to be expected when Buckingham Palace is just a short walk away, but there’s a relaxed, fashionable feel to the surroundings here too. The appealing menu offers lots of choice and the well-judged, flavourful dishes (mostly from northern India) have been subtly updated, while still respecting the foundations of the cuisine.

Name: Chuí
Description: The four young owners of this vegetarian/vegan restaurant have taken full advantage of the potential of this empty piece of land next to the railway tracks. It occupies a huge semi-open industrial-style warehouse alongside a rustic garden that transforms the setting into an oasis in the heart of the city. If you look closely you’ll notice four main features: a cabinet for growing mushrooms, another to store preserves and pickles, plus a clay oven and a pizza oven in the huge open kitchen. Wild mushrooms pay a starring role on the menu in delicious dishes such as the oyster mushroom milanesa and the mushroom pâté. Chuí also usually offers four types of pizza – the female chef here is an expert at adding an extra fermented element or escabeche to give them an extra-special touch. The colourful desserts include a delicious cheesecake brûlée.

Name: Château Grand Barrail
Address: Route de Libourne D243, Saint-Emilion, 33330, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This neo-Romantic château built in 1902 lies in the heart of the Saint-Émilion vineyards. It blends a time-honoured setting with contemporary design and diners sit either in the Art Nouveau-inspired lounges or on the beautiful terrace that looks out over the grounds and a sea of vines. At lunchtime, bistronomy dishes such as crispy duck, finely puréed sweet potato and roasted hazelnuts are served. The dinner menu features more ambitious cuisine (roasted veal sweetbreads with Bordeaux butter, a medley of carrots and their tops, cardamom jus).

Name: Château Hochberg
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The restaurant within this majestic 19C residence boasts a contemporary decor dotted with creations by master glassmaker René Lalique (the Lalique Museum is just opposite). The chef concocts delicious seasonal cuisine inspired by the Alsace and Vosges terroir: goose foie gras terrine and sour cherry chutney, Sparsbach char confit, beef with béarnaise sauce and Macaire potatoes. Gorgeous terrace to the rear of the château overlooking the grounds.

Name: Château Royal
Description: The elegant hotel Château Royal stands near the Brandenburg Gate, behind a dapper historical façade. Combining classical elements, design highlights and contemporary art in its impressively high-ceilinged rooms, it also houses a stylish restaurant with a lovely bar. The atmosphere is pleasingly intimate, and the cuisine bears the hallmarks of both Mediterranean and classic influences – the freshly made pasta is particularly popular. At lunchtime, the reasonably priced lunch set menu is a winner.

Name: Château de Rochecotte
Description: Not far from the Bourgueil vineyards, this elegant château dating back to the Enlightenment is set in sumptuous grounds. In La Verrière with its contemporary decor and huge windows with views onto the greenery, or in the more classical dining area, enjoy fine dining-style cuisine, for instance, a fricassee of smoked eel in a Thai jus with lemongrass and coriander.

Name: Château du Bost
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A few minutes from Vichy, in peaceful grounds, this château with towers and a water-filled moat (15C-19C) offers a contemporary and cosy decor, complemented by a beautiful terrace and some comfortable guestrooms. The restaurant has a refined setting and serves tasty seasonal cuisine.

Name: Château du Mylord
Description: Martin and Nuria Simonart have breathed a new lease of life into this English-looking manor house (1861), a landmark for foodies for many years. Rich in period charm, you can expect a log-burning fire to greet you in winter. The food is high-flying, with a quest for perfection that occasionally borders on daring. Cream of Jerusalem artichoke with coffee-flavoured mushrooms and scallops, all of which jazzed up by a tangy mandarin jelly. Delicacy is what best defines this establishment.

Name: Chère Amie
Address: 5 avenue de la Marseillaise, Strasbourg, 67000, France
Description: In the Neustadt district, the former Hôtel des Postes – a monumental Prussian building – has undergone a complete renovation. The name ("Dear Friend") and decor of this spacious brasserie are inspired by letter writing… but rather a love note or a business letter? The choice is yours! Peruse the carefully devised menu of traditional dishes such as sauerkraut, beef tartare, bouchée à la reine, beef tenderloin with Bordelaise sauce, fish terrine and lobster bisque. A contemporary setting and good value for money – definitely something to write home about!

Name: Chả Cá Anh Vũ (Ô Chợ Dừa)
Address: 120-K1 Giang Vo Street, O Cho Dua Ward, Hanoi, 11511, Vietnam
Description: Having been in the city for over 20 years, this bouncy family-run operation offers slick service. The homely vibe is depicted by chequered tablecloths, patterned wallpaper and brightly painted murals. Chả cá, grilled catfish seasoned with turmeric, is the name of the game here; its tender, juicy flesh carries a delicate aroma. You can also add nem cá, fish spring rolls; canh cá, fish soup; and lòng cá, fish stomach, as extras. The fresh, tasty food delivers an explosion of flavours and textures.

Name: Ci Siamo
Address: 440 W. 33rd St., Ste. 100, New York, NY, 10001, USA
Description: Efficient, busy from the minute doors open and effortlessly likable, this Italian eatery hiding deep inside the Manhattan West development is everything we’ve come to expect—and enjoy—from restaurateur Danny Meyer. The space features a handsome bar, open kitchen, large windows and ample tilework—all of which will feel familiar to those acquainted with the Union Square Hospitality Group.Chef Hillary Sterling's food is equally inviting. The caramelized onion torta is enough to warrant a return, with melting onions packed into a delicate crust, buried under two kinds of pecorino and finished in the wood-burning oven. Generously rich pastas and hearty proteins are designed for sharing. A simple but arresting lemon torta with mascarpone and olive oil closes out the meal.

Name: CiPASSO
Description: A small restaurant which combines a contemporary feel with a hint of vintage style in its decor. The menu is inspired by Roman and regional traditions, with the occasional imaginative twist and other more Mediterranean-inspired dishes, all showing a strong focus on seasonal ingredients. The impressive wine list includes an excellent selection of regional wines, with a particular focus on wines by the glass. Friendly yet professional service from the young team completes the picture.

Name: Ciambra
Description: At the gates of the town and a few steps from the magnificent Cathedral of Monreale, this rustic yet elegant venue proves to be an intriguing destination for those wishing to explore refined seafood cookery, reinterpreted with a modern touch while never betraying the authenticity of the flavours. The Tonnarello fresco cacio e pepe con quenelle di gambero rosso (fresh tonnarello cacio e pepe with a red prawn quenelle) is a delightful pasta dish that well represents the chef’s hand, as do the impeccably fresh and expertly executed seafood crudo. Finally, the house desserts are not to be missed: the true stars of the end of the meal, leaving a deliciously lingering memory.

Name: Ciani Lugano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Located between the Palazzo dei Congressi and the Ciani Garden, this modern and cosmopolitan venue is a true gem. Renowned regional chef Dario Ranza focuses on Mediterranean cuisine, prepared with skill and precision to guarantee delicious flavors. Among his specialties: Lostallo salmon “Caini style,” a variety of risottos, sole meunière, and salt-crusted sea bass, filleted directly at the table. The selection of exclusive wines and Champagnes is truly remarkable.

Name: Ciao
Description: The 17C stately house on Poelaert Square belongs to TheMerode, a private club. Have no fear, though, everyone is welcome at Ciao. Our favourite in this edifice, oozing in character and elegance, was the dining room with a pretty bar. Authentic Italian flavours are treated to a sensitive modern makeover, illustrated by homemade tortellini with beef marinated in Chianti and a parmesan sauce subtly underscored by Campari. The chef avows a weakness for Tuscan recipes and delicately crafts succulent comfort food. Making your choice from the menu can be something of a challenge!

Name: Ciasa Mia
Description: In a side street near the Pantheon, this charming little restaurant with exposed stone walls and wooden furnishings has a rustic feel that calls to mind a chalet. At the helm is an Italian couple in their forties: he is in charge in the kitchen, she takes care of proceedings front of house, dressed in the traditional attire of the Dolomites. The food is presented in surprise set menus, in which an inventive spin is put on local ingredients and bitter flavours are subtly explored – a hallmark of refined Italian cuisine. A good selection of wines completes the experience.

Name: Cibrèo
Address: via A. Del Verrocchio 8r, Florence, 50122, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: A historic city institution and essential stop for anyone arriving in Florence, this establishment welcomes guests into an elegant dining room reminiscent of a private salon, where cordial, graciously measured service frames a cuisine of bold flavors. The menu features dishes that have become true house classics, capable of narrating the territory through recipes that time has rendered iconic: pork liver with lemon, tortellini timbale, squab stuffed with mostarda, rabbit roulade with sweet-and-sour borettane onions, and, to close, a cheese tart accompanied by marmalade.

Name: Cibus
Address: Plaza Primero de Mayo 13, Úbeda, 23400, Spain
Description: An unexpected surprise in the centre of Úbeda! The small restaurant, with an open kitchen by the entrance and a dining room with stone walls downstairs that dates back to the 16C, has a philosophy that it classifies as a "culinary renaissance”, which is showcased via dishes that are constantly evolving and change with every season. There’s no à la carte; instead, you’ll find two surprise tasting menus entitled Legado and Renacimiento (both are plant-based and come with a wine-pairing option). Extra virgin olive oil from Jaén is a constant presence in the dishes served here.

Name: Cibû
Address: Rua do Castelo 15, Leça da Palmeira, 4450-632, Portugal
Description: In a small alley next to the Forte de Leça da Palmeira stands Cibû, a charming restaurant that takes its name from a typical expression of the Trás-os-Montes region. The space shows Nordic influences, with stone walls and a predominance of wood in the ceilings and furniture, which define the character of the setting. In the kitchen is Chef Hugo Portela who, after working in renowned restaurants in Norway, Barcelona and Switzerland, decided to invest in his own team alongside his partner Sara Silva. The menu, designed for sharing, is inspired by traditional Portuguese dishes with touches from northern recipes, including delicacies such as Beef Tartare with Chaves bread, the Octopus açorda, and the Pork Neck with mashed potatoes and sugar snap peas — not to mention the desserts, which are more than reason enough to save a little space at the end of the meal!

Name: Ciccio Bistrot
Description: In the evocative vaulted dining room that once housed the celebrated Cavallino, Ciccio Bistrot now brings to the table a forthright, deeply local cuisine, faithful to tradition and free of unnecessary digressions – except in the playful titles that punctuate the menu. Among the offerings, the whimsically named “no name” deserves a taste: agnolotti del plin served with the sauce of your choosing, a small ritual of personalization that wins over regulars. Each day brings a few off-menu delicacies, while wine maintains the role tradition assigns it: a discreet yet essential companion, supported by a well-curated selection and the expert guidance of the owner, always ready to steer guests toward the most fitting pairing.

Name: Cicoria
Address: 5th Floor, Royal Opera House, Bow Street, Covent Garden, London, WC2E 9DD, United Kingdom
Description: Whether you’re here to see the tenors in action or not, it’s well worth stepping inside the stunning Royal Opera House for a meal at this chic Italian restaurant. Run under the auspices of Angela Hartnett, it’s perhaps no surprise that the classical cooking is bright, unfussy and full of flavour. Roasted cod with minestrone is a great example, an uncomplicated yet totally satisfying dish. The glass-enclosed terrace with views over Covent Garden and the city skyline beyond is a huge draw, as is the great value lunch menu.

Name: Ciel à Table
Description: On the church square in this village in the Toulouse Conurbation, this typical pink brick building has now been extended by a large room with a glass roof and a patio shaded by a chestnut tree and a lime tree. The light-filled restaurant room boasts contemporary decor and a large open kitchen. The cuisine reflects the style of the place, flirting with the zeitgeist, in dishes such as Mediterranean tuna bao with notes of sesame, or pigeon served two ways: the leg confit and the supreme cooked whole. Attentive and alert service.

Name: Cielo
Description: In the white city of limestone stairways, at the highest point of the village, a skillfully restored ancient residence houses a splendid relais that – fittingly – bears the name La Sommità. The gourmet restaurant Cielo welcomes guests with romantic summer dinners among the citrus trees of the small inner courtyard, or in the barrel-vaulted dining room, where the atmosphere is intimate and evocative. The menu offers a modern reinterpretation of Apulian cuisine: not to be missed are the stewed catalogna with grilled lamb offal and sweet-and-sour lampascioni, or the pasta cooked in spicy tomato water, served with raw red mullet and chervil. At aperitivo hour, it is worth ascending to the splendid terrace to take in the sunset, while at lunch the offering becomes simpler, designed for a lighter yet always refined experience.

Name: Cilantro
Address: MiCasa All Suite Hotel, 368B Jalan Tun Razak, Taman U Thant, Kuala Lumpur, 50400, Malaysia
Description: One of the city's favourite formal dining spots, Cilantro impresses with meticulous French fare that showcases first-rate Japanese ingredients. The food ranges from classic French to adventurous Japanese-French fusion. In addition to à la carte choices, the Japanese chef proposes various set menus and prix-fixes. Try his signature cold capellini with sauces and accompaniments that change with the seasons. They are open for lunch on Fridays only.

Name: Cinq
Description: The young and not so young come here to be spoiled rotten in this contemporary villa near the ring road of Brussels. Chef Verzele rustles up a varied menu in tune with the zeitgeist, adding a new spin to his classical background. Examples include perfectly poached fillets of sole, paired with fried prawns, a velvety saffron-flavoured risotto and a knockout fish sauce. Cinq is the sort of place that invites you to dig into meals steeped in gutsy, big-boned flavours whilst enjoying the casual buzzy vibe. Should you have cause for celebration, we can recommend the lobster menu.

Name: Cinque
Address: FIVE Palm Jumeirah - No 1 Palm Jumeirah, Dubai
Description: Fashionable, glamorous and full of energy, this buzzing Italian restaurant overlooks the trendy FIVE Palm Jumeirah’s swimming pool. Arched ceilings are complemented by warm lighting and a self-playing piano keeps everyone entertained. The menu offers up a mix of classic Italian favourites, such as parmigiana di melanzane and fassona tartare with white truffle, along with more modern interpretations, like their dessert version of a Bellini cocktail. The terrace is a great spot for alfresco dining during Dubai’s cooler weather.

Name: Cinque Foglie
Address: Via SS 18 Tirrenia Inferiore, 54, Battipaglia, 84091, Italy
Description: Cinque Foglie explores the roots of fine dining through the concept of “the evolution of ingredients”. Chef Roberto Allocca creates dishes that are regionally inspired, combing traditional flavours with an innovative touch. The ingredients, some of which come from the chef’s family farm in Piana del Sele, are showcased on three tasting menus, while the wine cellar is home to more than 1 000 labels, including some rare vintages.

Name: Cip's Club
Description: This is the most informal and intimate restaurant of the Hotel Cipriani and comes with a coveted panoramic terrace which looks out over the Giudecca Canal, St. Mark's Square and the Doge's Palace. It's a true institution in the city and the seasonal menu of Venetian dishes includes a whole page dedicated to its signature classics.

Name: Cipriani Dolci
Address: GL 7 & 8 Ground Floor - Haza Bin Zayed the 1st Street - Marina Mall, Abu Dhabi
Description: You can expect all the smart and elegant attributes found in Cipriani establishments, with a slight twist. This spot on the ground floor of Marina Mall is open for breakfast, brunch, lunch and small bites along with some daily specials and even pizza. They also have a fine selection of cakes, patisseries and some delicious house-made ice creams - perfect for a sweet treat when doing a little shopping.

Name: Circa
Address: 26 High Street, Totnes, TQ9 5RY, United Kingdom
Description: With stints as both a cobbler’s and a theatre for the Mayor of Totnes, this lovely 18th-century building has lived many lives over the years. Its latest incarnation is a friendly sharing plates restaurant with a bistro buzz, bringing a dose of welcoming hospitality to the charming Totnes High Street. The menu displays a modern outlook in its sharing plates format and incorporation of both fermented elements and open-flame cooking. The service has a genuine warmth to it, with the owners keen to ensure you’re having a good time.

Name: Circus
Description: A young couple from the region – Nino on the savoury side, Salomé handling desserts and service – cultivate a wine-bistro atmosphere in this former crêperie; a natural fit for this wine-growing town! Their cooking rooted in meticulously sourced produce is both fresh and indulgent: think Jura snails, charcoal-grilled oyster mushrooms and Brussels sprouts; house-made agnoletti, potatoes, Bleu de la Marre cheese in an oxidative wine sauce; bergamot, sweetcorn and yuzu sorbet… A lovely little spot.

Name: Cirkulo
Address: GF, Milky Way Building, 900 Arnaiz Avenue corner Paseo de Roxas, Makati - Metro Manila, 1200, The Philippines
Description: Cirkulo blends red tones, wooden accents and matador-inspired art for a vintage feel. The US-trained Filipino chef serves a diverse menu of classic Spanish fare. Tapas include ham, Basque-style elvers, and aromatic angulas a la vasca: fresh-tasting baby eels sautéed in garlic and olive oil. With different serving sizes of paella, there's plenty for larger groups to share. For those craving traditional Spanish food, this place has stood the test of time.

Name: Cisco - Cozinha Tradicional
Address: Rua do Matadouro Municipal 67, Almeirim, 2080-107, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Pets not allowed
Description: This restaurant is located in Almeirim, in a region renowned for its famous “sopa da Pedra”, a soup which understandably makes an appearance on the menu. However, you’ll also find lots of other options here, such as the “cozido à portuguesa” stew, the mouthwatering rice with veal cheek, the traditional “bacalhau à brás” and, for dessert, the classic “leite-creme”, and grandma Mariazinha’s almond pudding, both of which provide a fitting end to your meal. If you enjoy high-quality traditional and home-style cooking this is definitely the place, thanks to chef Alexandre Albergaria Diniz use of fresh ingredients to create authentic dishes without unnecessary frills, as well as daily specials, in a welcoming, traditional space run by an excellent team.

Name: Citrino da Yoshinaga Jinbo
Address: 2F, 18 On Lan Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: In 2024, Hong Kong’s CBD welcomed the arrival of Citrino, the brainchild of the Ryota Kappou Modern team and of chef Yoshinaga Jinbo. The decor overflows in Italian luxe, circa 1950s with rich, tactile finishes. On the menu, Italian dishes are given a Japanese spin, featuring many signatures from the chef’s flagship in Japan, such as smoked bagna cáuda with 30+ seasonal organic vegetables, as well as a pasta tasting menu with five primi choices.

Name: Citrus
Description: This restaurant in a traditional old building with a pretty patio to be enjoyed on sunny days has a small lemon-yellow dining area (echoing the name Citron) with exposed stone walls and modern bistro furniture. Éric Sampietro (previously chef at La Table des Cordeliers) concocts appealingly hearty fare, from vegetable broth with pork dumpling to roasted pear with ginger caramel, crumble and yoghurt ice cream.

Name: Citurna
Description: Can the flavours of the world be discovered all in one place? Here, in an environment of unique volcanic landscapes, they say they can, because they fuse their Latin American roots (chef Rubén Darío Rivera is from Colombia) with Canary Island products and make subtle culinary nods to other cultures. The menu, which always includes very interesting proposals (ask about the grilled local fish), is supported by two solid tasting menus: Ruta compartida and Experiencia Citurna.

Name: City Grocery
Description: In the heart of Oxford right on the town square, Chef John Currence’s flagship restaurant remains a shining culinary light for the region. Open since 1992, the historic dining room is wrapped in red brick, local art, and well-worn wood. The menu is a revolving door of ideas, but the style sticks to the seasons, sources quality product across the region, and largely celebrates Southern cuisine. Think salmon croquettes or a tower of fried green tomatoes with shrimp remoulade. Shrimp and grits is a house staple for good reason. Cap off the meal with a perfect slice of cake. Portions are generous and shareable, and lunch is a particularly good value.

Name: City Social
Address: 43rd Floor, Tower 2, Grosvenor House Hotel, Al Emreef Street, Dubai Marina, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Commanding views from its perch on the 43rd floor of the Grosvenor House hotel are not the only attraction of this branch of the Jason Atherton empire. The extensive menu offers something for everyone, including pasta dishes and a wide choice of dry-aged steaks which are cooked over charcoal. Kick off your experience with a cocktail on the intimate and elegant outside terrace.

Name: City Social
Address: Tower 42, 25 Old Broad Street, City of London, London, EC2N 1HQ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The buzz from the bar is the first thing you notice at Jason Atherton’s handsome restaurant on the 24th floor of Tower 42. Dark and moody, with a subtle art deco twist, it boasts impressive views of the City skyline. The menu of generous modern European dishes includes multiple cuts of Cumbrian beef cooked on the Josper grill, from rib-eye to sirloin. The wine list offers an appealing mixture of prices and styles, and there are noteworthy cocktails too.

Name: Cítricos
Address: Disney's Grand Floridian Resort & Spa, 4401 Floridian Way, Orlando, FL, 32830, USA
Description: Set on the second floor of the Grand Floridian Hotel, Citricos brings to life a gloriously contemporary vibe and décor elements that are a subtle nod to Mary Poppins. The menu is coastal American, as evidenced by the use of seafood, citrus and tropical fruit. The team has a refined cooking style, replete with balanced flavors and technical prowess.While the carte is seasonal, expect the likes of corn bisque whimsically arranged with pickled fennel and popcorn. Crispy smoked duck is finished with salt and gently set atop a tangle of tagliatelle with celeriac purée. Up next might be guava-braised short ribs with cheddar grits and poblano sauce, leaving you full to the brim. Save room for at least one exquisite dessert—like an orange blossom flan.

Name: Claire et Hugo
Address: 77 avenue du Général-Galliéni, à Sainte-Savine, Troyes, 10300, France
Description: An enthusiastic self-taught young couple runs this restaurant with a subdued decor composed of raw materials. The premises also house a bakery and delicatessen leading onto a lovely terrace and indoor garden (including a citrus tree greenhouse). The ingredients, which are 95% organic, make for healthy, tasty and balanced dishes.

Name: Clairefontaine
Description: Clairefontaine is the epitome of unostentatious luxury. This warm, stylish establishment, whose artistic dimension lends it a distinctive glamorous edge, is located bang in the heart of the city of Luxemburg, behind a majestic façade. Arnaud Magnier, a champion of fine goods from Bresse poultry to scallops from Dieppe, is a past-master when it comes to polished Gallic fare. An example: medium rare rack of lamb in a crispy parsley crust, paired with a velvety fritter of neck of lamb, a big-boned gravy and side dishes of the calibre of roasted artichoke and polenta gnocchi, all of which bear witness to the chef’s virtuoso skills as he orchestrates a symphony of flavours and textures. While remaining loyal to his classical training, he doesn’t shy away from bold inventive side dishes in a bid to stimulate, seduce and satiate our tastebuds.

Name: Clan BBQ
Address: Rua Dias Ferreira, 233 Loja B, Rio de Janeiro, 22431 050, Brazil
Description: To the backdrop of a neon sign “Não apague o meu fogo” (“Don’t put out my fire”) clearly visible above the door, chefs Pepo Figueiredo and Newton Rique showcase cuisine in which fire plays a key role here, enabling them to prepare fresh ingredients imbued with a special flavour. In this industrial-style ambience with a predominance of raw concrete, a sturdy tree takes centre stage in the middle of the dining room. There’s also the option of sitting at the counter by the grill to watch dishes and cocktails being prepared at close quarters. The menu is of course heavily focused on barbecued meats, although you’ll also find other options such as vegetables, fish and burgers. Dishes you won’t want to miss include the creamy oxtail croquettes and cubes of smoked tongue with aioli. The succulent French rack of lamb, served with chimichurri, is cooked to perfection.

Name: Clancy's
Address: 6100 Annunciation St., New Orleans, LA, 70118, USA
Description: Clancy's is a far cry from its former life as a beloved neighborhood po'boy shop from the 1940s. It's still a family affair, owned by former employee Brad Hollingsworth and run by his family, but that's where the similarities end. A man in a tuxedo will greet you upon arrival, welcoming you to an upscale setting complete with uniformed servers and white tablecloths. The kitchen delivers on its promise of refined Creole cuisine, and the menu is seafood focused with plenty of French and Cajun influences. Begin with their signature appetizer of fried oysters with brie, then move on to the chicken and andouille sausage gumbo. Fried, smoked softshell crab with meunière sauce is yet another Clancy's signature that impresses.

Name: Clandestino Susci Bar
Description: Built on stilts, the Clandestino is a unique restaurant with a simple yet trendy ambience, which overlooks a beautiful unspoilt beach with views of the sea from all the windows and a distinctly romantic feel at night. Here, Moreno Cedroni focuses on gourmet cuisine at lunchtime as well as in the evening. In addition to two tasting menus (Eros & Susci and Susci Memories), for lunch there’s a small à la carte.

Name: Clap
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Private lifts whisk you up to the 9th floor, where you enter this chic, modern restaurant with a sizeable cocktail bar and a buzzy vibe. The menu is a roll-call of Japanese classics, from sushi, sashimi and shrimp tempura to mains like miso cod. The rooftop terrace with its city views is the place to be.

Name: Clara
Address: 69 Soi Prasat Suk, Chong Nonsi, Yan Nawa, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Popular among both Thai and foreign foodies and housed in a Bauhaus-style villa surrounded by sculpture-filled gardens, Clara is an elegant Italian fine-dining restaurant from a seasoned Italian chef and his wife. The villa’s two-floor interior has a warm minimalist vibe. The set menu balances flavours and complex textures which are matched by the fine service. Pair with wine for a complete experience.

Name: Clarke's
Address: 124 Kensington Church Street, Kensington, London, W8 4BH, United Kingdom
Description: It's been over 40 years since Sally Clarke opened her eponymous restaurant, and the loyalty of her many regular diners is testament to the warmth of the place and her kind-hearted hospitality. The seasonal menu is a combination of British and Mediterranean influences, and the kitchen displays a light touch and a healthy respect for the quality ingredients, be it lemon sole or loin of fallow deer. If you want to take something home, check out her shop across the road.

Name: Claro
Address: 12 Waterloo Place, St James's, London, SW1Y 4AU, United Kingdom
Description: A former bank in the heart of busy St James’s provides a wonderfully bright and airy setting for this elegant restaurant with a distinctly Mediterranean slant. A large bar-counter provides a focal point for the room and presents the opportunity to sit in front of the semi-open kitchen and engage with the charming team, who are happy to chat and recommend dishes. The menu features Med-inspired options such as delicious short rib tortellini, alongside a host of influences stretching from North Africa into Asia – such as the yellowtail sashimi with freekeh tabbouleh.

Name: Clash
Description: Clash is a hip and vibrant restaurant with posters of celebrities providing an extra touch of cool. The lighting even gives the place a bit of a disco feel (be sure to check out the regular DJ nights). Classic dishes reign supreme on the menu, with aged meat being a big feature. No unnecessary frills, just straightforward, bold flavours. You might start with some crispy shrimp croquettes, then, during the game season, move on to pheasant roasted on the bone à la brabançonne. Be sure to leave room for the Brussels waffle, prepared to a time-honoured recipe. The extensive menu will leave you spoilt for choice.

Name: Claud
Address: 90 E. 10th St., New York, NY, 10003, USA
Description: Owned by Chase Sinzer, who pours the wine, and Chef Joshua Pinsky, who mans the stoves, Claud is a sleek and stylish place a few steps below street level. Inside, it's whitewashed brick meets dark charcoal tiled floors complete with snug seating and an open kitchen at the back. A shared plates style informs the menu, and the cooking is ingredient-focused and values substance over style. Begin with the red shrimp, which arrive sizzling with garlic and olive oil. Main dishes, like the pork chop with smoked onion jus and a classic roasted chicken, are hearty and especially satisfying. Complete your meal with a decadent six-layer Devil's food cake that says it's "for two" but we won't blame you if you eat the whole thing yourself. Reservations are often a challenge, but the bar is always a good option.

Name: Claudine
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Interesting wine list
Description: From chef Julien Royer of Odette fame comes this classic French brasserie, named after his mother. It's housed in a lovely converted 1930s chapel with an open kitchen at one end and a bar at the other. Those with a fondness for comforting French classics will find the roll call of favourites highly appealing, from foie gras terrine to vol-au-vents and soufflé. The wine list is thoughtfully curated and by-the-glass choices abound.

Name: Claudio Ristorante
Description: In the heart of the lower Padana valley, in the open countryside and in a lovely, specially restored farmhouse, Claudio prepares almost exclusively seafood cuisine of excellent quality, with a few southern accents, particularly from Puglia, his homeland. In summer, it is pleasant to sit at outdoor tables under the modern portico. The indoor dining room on the first floor has a contemporary feel.

Name: Clay
Description: Diners immediately feel at home in this establishment thanks to Zoë’s warm welcome. Unsurprisingly, given its name, earthenware plays a star role in the décor of this listed 17C presbytery dripping in warmth and elegance. You are invited to sample chef Roel’s set menu, depicted by razor-sharp craftsmanship and subtle marriages, which bear witness to the chef’s stints in prestigious establishments and also to his love of setting himself ever more creative challenges. He may offset the full-bodied character of a piece of beef with a spicy tarragon sauce and a kebab of lacquered calf’s tongue, teriyaki style. This establishment echoes the sincere and endearing enthusiasm of its owner couple.

Name: Clinton's
Description: Near the outskirts of Berlin, this restaurant is housed on the first floor of the European headquarters of the fashion company Clinton. The decor is up to the minute, as is the seasonally influenced cuisine – choose between a four- or six-course set menu and their à la carte "Signature" dishes, from "Berlin Blutwurst, sauerkraut, green back bacon, cassis, mustard" to "300g beef – roast beef, fillet, 16hr-cooked ox shoulder, truffle purée, teriyaki, vegetables from the farm". Fans of dry-aged steaks are also in for a treat. The service is attentive and the waitstaff professional. From some tables you can sneak a peek into the Clinton outlet.

Name: Clio
Address: 66 Chiltern Street, Marylebone, London, W1U 4EJ, United Kingdom
Description: Named after one of Zeus's daughters, this chic Marylebone spot is a celebration of classic and contemporary Greek cuisine. Situated below luxury apartments, the buzzing interior has a faux-rustic look with plenty of tasteful Hellenic touches. The fresh flavours of the Mediterranean abound in dishes ranging from a deconstructed take on red prawn ‘saganaki’ to luscious suckling pig with a vibrant salsa. The concise and fairly priced wine list pushes Greek bottles to the fore, while the service team are as warm and friendly as they are attentive.

Name: Clipstone
Address: 5 Clipstone Street, Fitzrovia, London, W1W 6BB, United Kingdom
Description: Sister to fellow neighbourhood spots Portland and 64 Goodge Street, this well-run restaurant provides a great all-round package. The young team are full of smiles, the wine list is cleverly conceived and there’s a pleasing buzz to the atmosphere. The cooking, for its part, showcases quality ingredients and an original touch in somewhat delicate dishes.

Name: Cloak & Petal
Address: 1953 India St., San Diego, CA, 92101, USA
Description: It’s in the heart of Little Italy, but you won’t hear any old crooners at this temple of Japanese haute cuisine. Instead, you'll find old-school rap on the soundtrack and graffiti art installations on the walls. And then there’s the bar, flanked by two faux-cherry trees in full bloom.The fresh-spirited menu brims with shareable plates such as blistered shishito peppers and crispy chicken karaage. Entrées include duck breast with golden tomato confit, miso-glazed black cod or even Wagyu grilled tableside on a yakitori. The sashimi is straight-up sublime, but it’s the envelope-pushing items that make the most impact. Contemporary maki are a hit among the hungry hordes, and include the Tokyo Gangster, with shrimp and beef in a spicy black garlic sauce.

Name: Clos Des Gourmets
Description: In his primary school graduation yearbook, the future chef wrote, “I want to be a chef”. He studied gastronomy in Paris, developing his most intimate relationships with a restaurant in the 7th arrondissement. The chef’s culinary philosophy, his restaurant’s name and his signature cuisine are all inherited from his mentor. One representative dish is tête de cochon, grilled cuts from a pig’s head. In this intimate eatery, guests are in close proximity with the chef, as if invited by a friend.

Name: Clos Maggiore
Address: 33 King Street, Covent Garden, London, WC2E 8JD, United Kingdom
Description: There's a comforting, bygone-era charm to Clos Maggiore, one of London's most distinctive and romantic restaurants that's bright and airy in summer and cosy in winter. The enchanting conservatory with its retractable roof is the prime place to sit, but love is in the air throughout thanks to the soft lighting and abundant indoor flora. Seasonal, French-inspired dishes are joined by a wine list of considerable depth. The lunchtime and pre/post-theatre menus are great value and are a hit with one and all.

Name: Clos d'Astorg
Description: "Cuisine au beurre" on the façade lets you know what to expect – butter is central to the recipes); "chou farci" reveals the house speciality: generously portioned, packed with a soft, light and fragrant farce, wrapped in a delicate green cabbage leaf. The interior is also done out in a bistro vein: mosaic and hardwood floors, exposed stone and brick walls, white tablecloths and light wood chairs. The confident cuisine focuses on the essentials, with leek vinaigrette, egg mayonnaise or green asparagus with mousseline sauce. Meat lovers are spoiled for choice: breaded veal sweetbreads "meunière", onglet steak with Bleu de Bresse cheese, boudin noir. And those with a sweet tooth are catered for with chocolate mousse, hazelnut and caramel riz au lait.

Name: Clos de Chacras
Description: The historic Clos de Chacras winery, built in 1921 by the Gargantini family and restored in 2003, is located 15 minutes from the city of Mendoza and is the ideal place to spend a quiet evening. In the restaurant, where a pleasant terrace or deck next to a pond filled with koi carp complements the charming dining room, you’ll find a fairly casual set menu—unpretentious but sensible, balanced, and carefully presented. Among the items on the menu, we especially liked the flavourful fried empanadas, filled with tender, hand-chopped meat and served with an ingenious smoked chimichurri, though the grilled ribeye steak with beetroot purée is also a great choice. For dessert, try their pear mille-feuille with carob crumble and white chocolate ganache with citrus. Wine pairing is included in the experience!

Name: Cloth
Address: 44 Cloth Fair, City of London, London, EC1A 7JQ, United Kingdom
Description: A hidden gem within the City of London, this sweetly run restaurant is just a stone’s throw from Smithfield Market, tucked down a narrow lane inside a period house which was once home to the poet Sir John Betjeman. It’s now under the watchful eye of Chef Tom Hurst and wine merchants Joe and Ben, who operate a tightly packed space filled to the brim with a convivial atmosphere. The cooking is pared-back and ingredient-led, with fine produce like Dorset crab and Somerset lamb given the space to shine. The wine list, as you’d expect, is extensive and full of interesting choices.

Name: Cloud Arise (Chenghua)
Address: 3-4F, Building Raidy Boer, 222 Shanbanqiao Road, Chenghua, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
Description: Although there are only six tables in the main dining room, there are private rooms with solariums, balconies and tea brewing rooms spread over two floors. A stylish, peaceful vibe reigns throughout the spacious, comfortable interior. The kitchen team crafts a menu of traditional Sichuanese fare such as fuqi feipian – sliced beef brisket and tripe in Sichuan pepper sauce. Their signature spicy pork belly, slow-cooked in an earthen jar over a wood fire, is rich and flavoursome.

Name: Clouds - Heaven's Bar & Kitchen
Description: Just 50 seconds in the lift and you are up on the 23rd floor, from which the view is simply magnificent. Modern cuisine is served in an urban-style interior: enquire about the extensive selection of meats; vegetarians are also catered for. In addition, there's a good bar serving a snack menu from 5pm. In summer, weather permitting, head to the 24th-floor Heaven's Nest for drinks and light bites.

Name: Clover
Address: 4F, Bellavita, 28 Songren Road, Xinyi District, Taipei, 110, Taiwan
Description: Renowned chef Jean-François Piège’s first venture outside France is a collaborative effort with the upmarket department store Bellavita. You will find the best sellers from chef Piège’s four French restaurants on the season-driven tasting menu and flexible set menu options. Thoughtfully crafted appetisers are served as a prelude to dishes that savvily showcase local ingredients. Finish on a high note with the wild raspberry soufflé with pistachio ice cream, a masterpiece of well-balanced sweet and tart notes.

Name: Clover Grill
Description: Mouthwatering dry - aged meats – Baltic black beef, Bavarian beef, Blonde d'Aquitaine, Black Angus – take pride of place in the window, drawing in diners keen to try them for themselves. From the starters to the desserts, everything is cooked over coals or roasted on a spit, giving the dining experience its own particular flavour. A great success.

Name: Clovis
Description: This bistro in the heart of a medieval village has a short menu with an original concept: several starter + main course pairings built around a flagship ingredient, such as a vegetable, Mediterranean fish or meat, often Parthenaise beef from the family farm in Vendée. We recommend starting with an aperitif and charcuterie. Warm welcome; excellent wine list. Adjacent to the restaurant is a wine bar, which serves delicious platters.

Name: Club Morera
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Nestled in Mediterranean scrub just beyond the hills overlooking the coast, this rustic farmhouse welcomes guests amid centuries-old olive trees and restorative quiet. Inside, exposed stone and beams frame a relaxed yet elegant setting, with a small garden terrace perfect for summer evenings. Chef-owner Vincenzo has realized his dream here: to offer genuine hospitality and regional cooking revisited with a contemporary taste. Don’t miss the candele pasta with knife-cut Cilento ragù and goat’s cacioricotta, or the tagliolini with four tomatoes, basil, and shrimp crudo. The cellar stocks 300-plus labels to pair thoughtfully with every dish.

Name: Clunie Dining Room
Address: Mar Road, Braemar, AB35 5YN, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Queen Victoria made this area fashionable when she started visiting Balmoral Castle in the 1840s, and this restaurant inside The Fife Arms hotel certainly has its own brand of eclectic chic. Murano chandeliers hang from the ceiling and a huge stag oversees proceedings, while the staff are dressed in tartan that matches the cubist painted walls. Come in winter and you'll be welcomed by the glowing embers of the fire. Prime Scottish ingredients from lobster to venison are presented in classical dishes that often incorporate the smoky aromas of a wood fire.

Name: Clutch
Description: In a setting emblematic of modern-day, trendy Eastern Paris (full-length picture windows, rough stone walls, bistro tables, an open kitchen and a few seats at the counter), the accent is on creative bistronomic fare, peppered with Asian notes. Casual, bouncy vibe.

Name: Clómada
Description: Fancy a distinctly-feminine international experience? Here you can have one, as the Ecuadorian chef Claudine Paulson, well accompanied by a team that is made up entirely of women, brings to the table the different flavours that she has come to know around the world during her time as a professional tennis player (she was the number one tennis player in Ecuador), a career that she combined with her hotel and catering studies. Within the proposal, with numerous international influences that evoke her nomadic lifestyle, dishes such as the fish ceviche or the crispy sea bass stand out. The logo and the striking lamps play with the symbolism of hot air balloons!

Name: Coalfire
Address: 1321 W. Grand Ave., Chicago, IL, 60622, USA
Description: Sure, you could come for a salad, but the focus here is on pizza—and yours should be, too. The dining room is cozy, showcasing an open kitchen where pie production is on full display for all to see. And in a playful bit of recycling, empty tomato sauce cans placed on each table become stands for sizzling pizzas churned straight from the 800-degree coal-fired oven.This hot spot has its ratio down to a fine art and knows not to burden its thin and crispy crust that’s blackened and blistered in all the right places. The mortadella is a delight, with chopped garlic and gossamer slices of peppercorn-flecked sausage. But if you wish to go your own way, build the perfect pie with toppings that run the gamut from decadent Gorgonzola to tangy goat cheese.

Name: Coarse
Address: Reform Place, North Road, Durham, DH1 4RZ, United Kingdom
Description: Hidden away in a small courtyard in the centre of Durham, this warm, cheerily run restaurant is the realisation of a dream for the three friends who crowdfunded its opening. The simple, rustic décor belies the quality of the cooking found within; the set menu of modern British small plates changes seasonally and the kitchen’s skill is clearly evident in the quality of the sauces.

Name: Coast
Address: 54F, Conrad Hotel, 186 Yanwu West Road, Siming, Xiamen, Chinese Mainland
Description: This upscale restaurant in a towering hotel commands breathtaking views of Gulangyu. Head to the romantic bar for a pre-dinner drink and watch the lights dim as the sun sets. Those craving the classics can order steak or seafood tower à la carte. If you're feeling adventurous, go for the tasting menu, which features innovative seasonal dishes – creations made with local catch such as yellowtail scad and fourfinger threadfin are especially impressive.

Name: Coastal Kitchen
Description: You'll have to weave your way through the Monterey Plaza Hotel and down a flight of stairs to find the entrance to this haven, but once you do, you'll be rewarded with a stunning view of the bay in a posh, elegant space. Thankfully, Chef Michael Rotondo’s tasting menu of colorful contemporary cuisine offers its own enticements to hold your attention. Highlighting local products while spanning global flavors, each dish provides a barrage of flavors, from a tart of local abalone featuring brown butter-cooked spinach and calamansi ponzu, to rich Iberico pork paired with matsutake and turnips, capped off with a soup dumpling filled with a savory oceanic broth. Diners looking for a less involved experience can opt for a three-course prix fixe and choose from a small selection of dishes.

Name: Coasterra
Address: 880 Harbor Island Dr., San Diego, CA, 92101, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Attention-grabbing views and attention-getting food go hand-in-hand at this modern Mexican eatery set on the tip of Harbor Island, which offers dramatic panoramas of downtown San Diego from across the water. The enormous patio, equipped with a sizable fire pit, is the best place to soak it all in, though the sleek, glassed-in dining room is an enjoyable second fiddle once the sun sets.Chef Deborah Scott nicely balances old-school and new-world takes on upscale Mexican fare. In the former, you’ll find delicious guacamole, made tableside; while in the latter, a smoked beet tartare tostada with king trumpet mushrooms and peanut salsa. Chicken enchiladas “divorciadas,” with a duo of sauces are a memorable indulgence, as are piping-hot churros for dessert.

Name: Cobo Tradición
Address: Plaza de la Libertad 9, Burgos, 09004, Spain
Description: Cobo Tradición is located in the medieval heart of the city, just a few metres from the emblematic 15C Casa del Cordón. Here, as part of a complex called Cobo Estratos, you’ll find an interior with an avant-garde design where the striking staircase and kitchens (also home to the award-winning Cobo Evolución) are the two standout features. The à la carte of traditional dishes has been brought impressively up to date and includes classics such as grilled and fried “morcilla de Burgos” (black pudding) with roasted peppers and sea salt, and the superb braised scallops with herb oil and Iberian pork cheek.

Name: Cobra City
Description: With its casual yet chic vibe, this lively establishment draws inspiration from the CoBrA art movement. A number of colourful pop art paintings command attention the moment you walk in. Behind the bar, the mixologist is at the ready. All manner of delicious dishes for sharing are served here from noon onwards. For example, you could start off with a lobster roll or pâté en croûte, then have Oedslach beef entrecôte as a main course and round off your meal with tarte Tatin. It's all possible here. No messing around, just simple, delicious flavours that will keep you coming back for more.

Name: Cocchi
Description: This restaurant adjoining the Daniel hotel is the town’s pride and joy. Here, two quiet, rustic-style dining rooms provide the backdrop for typical Parma specialities that change with the passing seasons – the “tortelli alle erbette” (tortelli pasta with herbs) with parmesan and melted butter is particularly delicious – all accompanied by an excellent choice of wines. Booking in advance is highly recommended as the restaurant is extremely popular with visitors and locals alike.

Name: Cocina Cabal
Address: Suárez de la Riva 5, Oviedo, 33007, Spain
Description: A restaurant that takes its name from chef Vicente Cabal and which features a kitchen visible from the dining room. Cabal is truly passionate about cooking and has had a long career working in leading restaurants across the country. On the à la carte, he conjures up creatively prepared Mediterranean cuisine with a balanced approach between tradition and innovation, which is complemented by a tasting menu named after the restaurant. In 2022, it won the award for the world’s best “fabada” stew!

Name: Cocotte
Description: Jan Mangelschots has clearly pondered and puzzled over every detail of the delightful Cocotte from the Art deco stained-glass, natural light and soothing colour scheme to its swish, uncluttered vibe and art-directed plating. Consummate yet subtle execution and intense sauces depict both the classical à la carte and the set menus. The chef has a flair for adding a sophisticated spin to a terrine of asparagus and squid served with a chilled asparagus soup and cream of smoked eel. Everything, from the food to the service, is bang-on confident and brimming in personality.

Name: Cocun Cellar Restaurant
Address: strada Prè de Vì 31, San Cassiano, 39036, Italy
Description: In the cellars of the Ciasa Salares hotel, you dine surrounded by bottles – after all, cocun in Ladin means cork, and not by chance the wine selection is vast. The chef creates dishes with ingredients and influences from every corner of the world and makes frequent use of the grill.

Name: Coda
Description: Classic elegance is the name of the game here. The restaurant is located in the hall of the Aria Hotel Prague – herringbone floorboards, chandeliers and interesting objets d'art contribute to the stylish atmosphere. With its magnificent view over Prague, the roof terrace is a huge draw in summer! The restaurant serves refined Czech cuisine, a signature dish being their kulajda – a mushroom soup with a poached egg.

Name: Codeso
Description: Behind this name, referring to a shrub endemic to the Canary Islands, this simple place with a contemporary atmosphere is surprising locals and visitors alike. Ronny Reina, a Colombian trained under the wing of award-winning chef Nandu Jubany, is unashamedly committed to the best local produce, combining the traditional dishes of the islands (such as its wonderful local fish in suquet of Canarian casserole with black potato) with delicious rice dishes a la llauna and other elaborations of a more international character (you will see the classic sirloin Wellington accompanied by Paris coffee sauce, microgreens and soufflé potatoes). The à la carte is supported by two suggestive tasting menus: Retama and Tajinaste!

Name: Coeur de Bois
Description: The name of this elegant restaurant was inspired by its wooden ceiling. Surrounded by spruce decor dating from the 18C, antique furniture and paintings, enjoy interesting traditional cuisine in this excellent gourmet restaurant, which is all the more attractive thanks to its location in the Gran Paradiso national park.

Name: Colbert
Description: In a modern brasserie setting, the chef rustles up traditional flavoursome food that spans the full gamut of classic French cuisine: eggs meurette, house smoked salmon, vol au vent and Simmental hanger steak with marrow bone… Given the quality of the food, it is hardly surprising that the restaurant is frequently fully booked.

Name: Colibri
Address: 14 rue de la Mittrie, Dinan, 22100, France
Description: In the heart of medieval Dinan, this modern bistro sports wood furnishings, oak parquet flooring, a fireplace and a view of the kitchen from the dinky dining room. Vibrant, often surf ‘n turf recipes set the culinary scene: lobster, green peas and strawberries, mullet, black pudding and figs; raspberries, red pepper sorbet and chiffon cake…

Name: Colita
Description: Located between Nice's port and the Colline du Château, this restaurant brings together the flavours of Colombia and Italy in bright and colourful fusion dishes cooked up by chefs Carlos and Daniele. Diners soak up the warm, relaxed atmosphere on the spacious terrace with orange seating or in the narrow indoor dining space done out in terracotta hues. In the visible kitchen, it is all about open-flame cooking – on plancha and parrilla grills. Grilled octopus, braised veal chop and sardines in a chimichurri sauce deliver intense flavours; a vibrant and well-balanced Peruvian ceviche combines white fish, red onion, crunchy sweetcorn and sweet potato. An authentic spot straddling two culinary cultures.

Name: Collina
Address: via Ca' Paler 5, Almenno San Bartolomeo, 24030, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Along the road leading to Roncola, a spacious and elegant restaurant whose main dining room opens – through a large glazed wall – onto an evocative Lombard panorama embracing the hills of Bergamo, seen from an unusual perspective. The cuisine of the chef-patron stands out for its solidity and imagination, with dishes built, wherever possible, from local ingredients and in strict respect of seasonality. Particular attention is devoted to freshwater fish, a true passion of the house, to which an entire tasting menu is dedicated, available on request.

Name: Collina am Berg
Description: This charming and trendy restaurant is located in the heart of Vienna's vibrant Spittelberg neighbourhood, known for its bars, restaurants and shops. The centrepiece is the large counter and open kitchen, where unfussy seasonal dishes are prepared. The ingredients are exclusively Austrian, mostly organic goods sourced from trusted suppliers. The house speciality is game, which the chefs also hunt themselves. Dishes include venison carpaccio with pickled celeriac and celeriac mayonnaise, and game schnitzel with potato salad and lemon. The exceptionally friendly and attentive team serves either a five-course tasting menu or individual dishes à la carte. During summer, the rain-protected pergola, with its open front of windows, provides a terrace-like setting. N.B. Parking in the immediate vicinity is difficult, but the nearest underground station, Volkstheater, is only a few minutes' walk away.

Name: Colline Emiliane
Description: A taste of the Emilia region in Rome. Ever since the 1960s, this friendly restaurant has been serving typical Emilian specialities such as delicious salumi, fresh homemade pasta made in the small kitchen visible near the entrance (tagliatelle with ragù, tagliolini with culatello ham, sometimes a superb green lasagne), and superbly cooked meat dishes, while the desserts are displayed in a large fridge to the rear. An extraordinary gastronomic voyage to a different Italian region while remaining in the country’s beautiful capital city.

Name: Collinsons
Address: 122-124 Brown Street, Broughty Ferry, DD5 1EN, United Kingdom
Description: You know what you're getting at Collinsons: an experienced chef showing his skill in delivering generous, consistently enjoyable dishes that are classic to the core. You're likely to find some of Chef-Owner Stephen Collinson's signatures recurring on the menu, like smoked haddock rarebit with leek or roasted venison with a port and cassis sauce. Whilst it may be tucked away down a quiet street, the restaurant itself is hard to miss thanks to its name etched across the floor-to-ceiling windows.

Name: Colmado 1917
Address: Doctor José Naveiras 38, Santa Cruz de Tenerife, 38004, Spain
Description: After its move to the Iberostar Heritage Grand Mencey, this intimate restaurant has taken a new direction, respecting the essence of its 19th-century grocery store origins and remaining faithful to its culinary philosophy of minimal intervention, in order to respect the raw ingredients and traditional techniques as much as possible. You can sit at the bar or the table, for six or four diners respectively, as you enjoy a menu that constantly revolves around Canarian produce, with salted fish, marinades, tartares, macerated dishes, cold cuts, cheeses, etc. There are no stoves here and the dishes are prepared to order!

Name: Colonel Fort Jaco
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An offshoot of Colonel, a temple of red meat, this stylish brasserie sports a tasteful colour scheme that is the epitome of suave urbanity. Diners are invited to choose one of the juicy cuts of meat from the butcher’s counter near the open-plan kitchen. The knife-edge precision offered by the Josper charcoal oven, the exquisite flavour of the cured meats, the made-to-order sauces and the crispy fries are indeed admirable, but that is not all. Side by side this traditional Belgian lineup, you will also find dishes like carpaccio or filet américain, and more nostalgic dishes like their excellent vol-au-vent. We recommend a seat at the counter to make the most of the show in the kitchen.

Name: Colonel Louise
Description: Red meat lovers fall head over heels with this swish brasserie on a street corner near Avenue Louise. As soon as you cross the threshold, you are struck by the array of cured meats on the counter. You must then decide whether you want Aubrac, Wagyu or Holstein beef, before you dig into impeccably cooked steak flanked by fresh sauces and fries cooked in beef tallow as tradition demands. The menu also features a host of other delicacies ranging from bone marrow to vitello tonnato and crispy sweetbread. Perfect for a single dish, lunch or a full-blown dinner – what’s not to like?

Name: Colony Club
Address: The Colony Palms Hotel and Bungalows, 572 N. Indian Canyon Dr., Palm Springs, CA, 92262, USA
Description: This Moroccan-style oasis at the plush Colony Palms Hotel has history and charm to spare, having once been the stomping ground of stars like Clark Gable and Humphrey Bogart. Whether you’re indoors admiring its elaborate floor tiles and wallpaper, or poolside watching guests take a dip in the turquoise waters, the glamour factor is undeniable and infectious. You might even spot a famous face on a jaunt from L.A. In keeping with the pool-party vibe, the menu is laid-back, from snacks like edamame hummus, to heftier fare like a grilled pork chop with cheesy polenta. Start with an appetizer, perhaps the scallop aguachile, before moving on to mains like chicken pot pie. To finish, the molten lava cake never disappoints.

Name: Coltivare
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The organic soul of the Brandini estate, which houses the restaurant, makes itself felt immediately upon arrival: from the vineyards managed with great respect for the environment to the small herb and spice garden, an invaluable support to the work of chef Zecchin in his continuous pursuit of new aromatic equilibria. A focused experimentation, serving to refine dishes of deeply Langhe character, underpinned by a solid grounding in the territory. Alongside the principal offering, a vegetarian menu is available for devotees of the kitchen garden, while from the carte particular attention is merited by the eel with an intense cream of pil and roasted lettuce, as well as the Fassona chuck, rendered all the more tender and harmonious by Pink Lady apple and a deep brown maize jus. The wine list reflects the same strong bond with Piedmont, without overlooking a carefully considered selection of Champagnes. By day, the spacious dining room affords a splendid view through the large windows that surround it, enriched by the dramatic presence of an imposing fireplace.

Name: Colvert
Description: This bistro in the picturesque Latin Quarter of Paris boasts a bubbly vibe, vintage charm and bold, deftly crafted cuisine whose hearty Gallic twang is treated to dollop of creative enthusiasm. Stellar technique and a quest for flavour are expressed in stuffed squid, roast Mallard duck and plum clafoutis illustrate the. Attentive service, nostalgic recipes with a twist and a bona fide Parisian bistro décor!

Name: Comal
Address: 116 Forsyth St., New York, NY, 10002, USA
Description: Welcome to Mexico City by way of the Lower East Side. Sporting wood tables, tile and a touch of greenery, this vintage room is where you’ll want to settle in and see where the night goes. Chef Gaz Herbert brings contemporary touches to a tight menu packed with flavor. Think al pastor but in skewer form and carefully charred. Mussel with corn custard, mil hojas potato, crab tostada with eggplant – the cooking is seasonally minded and smartly prepared. With a side of rice, the smoked half-chicken is a must-order and channels all the nostalgia of a backyard barbecue. To finish, soft serve ice cream is a cute, sweet send-off.

Name: Comal
Address: Chileno Bay Resort & Residences, Carr. Transpeninsular Km. 15, Cabo San Lucas, 23410, Mexico
Description: Walk through the lobby of the posh Chileno Bay Resort, down a small hill and along a dramatic walkway with swings and lounge furniture to arrive at this open-air restaurant with beautiful views of the water. The contemporary Mexican menu is inventive with a clear personality that spans the country's distinct regions while also pulling in influences from South America. Octopus kastakan is a ceviche-style dish made with thin coins of octopus tossed with crispy cubes of pork belly and crispy pork skin. Served with warm plantain tortillas with slightly sweet notes, it's a brightly flavored dish. Their variation on a Pavlova with strawberry-basil sorbet employs a variety of pastry techniques and is noteworthy.

Name: Come Daily Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee
Address: 127 Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-27, Blk 127, Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, 310127, Singapore
Description: The signature Hokkien prawn mee is made with yellow egg noodles, rice vermicelli and squid, topped with fried crispy lard that adds an extra layer of texture and flavours.

Name: Come in Corte Aurora
Description: At this restaurant, the two brothers (the owners) who work together front of house come from a family of farmers whose meat features on the menu, while two other brothers, originally from Rome but settled in the Veneto for many years, are at the helm in the kitchen. The original and colourful cuisine aims to please both the eyes and the palate, with dishes showcased on tasting menus and an à la carte – the quail served with a caponata of apricots, yucca and porcini mushroom mayonnaise was particularly memorable. Housed in the Villa Lussana, with its seven Art Nouveau-style guestrooms, the restaurant has been completely renovated by the new young owners. In summer, meals are served outdoors with views of the surrounding hills.

Name: Comedor
Description: Located in Austin's Central Business District, Comedor is a stunner with a carefully curated sense of cool. Inside, traditional and contemporary furnishings are combined with industrial but refined materials (think leather, polished woods, concrete, and glass), and when the weather permits, the courtyard is the place to be. No matter the time, Chef/owner Philip Speer's spot is nearly always packed, and they're here for more than the scene. Dishes such as bone marrow tacos with smoked butter and pecan gremolata play well with the more traditional tuna aguachile. Campechano de hongos is even better with a fiery salsa, while fish tacos are always spot on. For dessert, the tamal de chocolate with house-made ice cream is a rich and inventive Mexican treat.

Name: Comet
Address: 3 Joshua Lane, Dublin City, D02 C856, Ireland
