At lunchtime, a budget-friendly set menu makes this lovely urban spot even more irresistible.

Name: Cuichine
Description: House-made Peking duck with crispy skin, fresh veggies and pancakes ready to be stuffed, all of which flanked by a gutsy sweet and sour hoisin sauce. This signature dish embodies the philosophy of Cuichine: a modern version of old-school Chinese nosh, starring all our favourite Cantonese recipes. The interior of this eye-catching establishment is ideally suited to the trendy vibe and the restaurant also boasts a pleasant terrace.

Name: Cuina Sant Pau
Address: Nou 10, Sant Pol de Mar, 08395, Spain
Description: This iconic restaurant, which held three Michelin stars for many years, has adopted a new, much more informal bistro format featuring numerous images and mementoes that highlight the career of legendary chef Carme Ruscalleda. Her son Raül Balam Ruscalleda and Brazilian chef Murilo Rodrigues Alves are now in charge, offering a contemporary, Catalan-influenced menu that includes unpretentious dishes, Brazilian touches and a nod to the history of the restaurant.

Name: Cuisine & Nous
Description: Exclusive finishings endow this characterful edifice with elegance and the lush green garden is the ideal spot to bask in the establishment’s warm vibe. The inventive chef enjoys reworking textbook Gallic recipes, adding international influences as the inspiration takes him. Scallops are paired with different textures of endive, while a playful interpretation of vitello tonnato features several seafood versions. Deft craftsmanship and fascinating flavours are underscored by high-flying culinary expertise. Exemplary value for money!

Name: Cuisine Cuisine at The Mira
Address: 3F, The Mira, 118 Nathan Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The striking chandelier with hundreds of glowing glass globes is set nicely against the calming green colour scheme and verdant views. Cantonese classics underpinned by solid, traditional techniques are revitalised by creative use of ingredients and modern twists. On top of special dim sum such as crispy frog legs with peppered salt, try also Mrs. Song’s fish soup made with fresh grouper fillet. Wine pairings are thoughtfully matched.

Name: Cuisine de Garden
Address: 99 Mu 11, Nong Khwai, Hang Dong, Chiang Mai, 50230, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: Cuisine de Garden brings a Nordic-inspired approach to Thai ingredients in a rustic-chic setting with wooden finishes. The chef-owner's love for art and respect for nature show in his seasonal tasting menu, in which creativity meets mindful practices and waste reduction – byproducts from one course may star in another. Every element is local, thoughtfully used and artfully plated, making for an elegant fine dining experience.

Name: Cuisinez-Nous
Address: rue de la Gare 138, Bertrix, 6880, Belgium
Description: You can rely on Cuisinez-Nous to deliver the goods every time. Céline’s seamless, on-the-ball service sets the distinctive tone in this tasteful manor house dripping in charm and boasting a pretty rear terrace with a stately old beech tree. A glance at the menu unveils chef Alain’s devotion to pedigree Gallic recipes, albeit with the odd modern flourish. For example: lobster (a lobster tank takes pride of place in the dining room), lavishly prepared in a fascinating salad with a bisque espuma or hanger steak with freshly whisked, silky béarnaise sauce and hand‑cut, piping hot French fries. We wager it will be love at first bite/sight.

Name: Cuivre
Address: 1502 Middle Huaihai Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Echoing its name, this welcoming bistro in the French Concession amusingly features copper trimming on its walls and dinnerware. The kitchen excels in reinventing bistro classics with modern techniques and subtle Asian twists. L’agneau, or rack of lamb, is nicely charred on the outside and juicy on the inside. Round off with baba Zacapa. The wine list offers vintages from French small-batch wineries, alongside affordable new world choices.

Name: Culina Hortus
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: This vegetarian restaurant offers beautifully crafted dishes that are unabashedly creative in a set tasting menu (no choice) made with seasonal ingredients. In a sleek, yet snug interior of wood, concrete, adobe, the food is paired with an insightful selection of wines from the well-stocked cellar.

Name: Culinair
Description: The refined interior and gracious welcome are a foretaste of the exquisite culinary experience awaiting the diner. You will be able to observe the chef at work, wielding modern culinary techniques as he updates classical dishes. The same desire to pamper guests is palpable in the modern B&B of the Culinair.

Name: Culinarium
Description: This chic, pared-back restaurant with a lovely terrace area is located in the Weingut Matthias Dostert, a winery that also offers cosy guestrooms. Chef Walter Curman draws on his considerable craftsmanship to meticulously create flavoursome dishes. The classics on the menu hint at his Austrian origins – try the appetising Kaspressknödel (pressed cheese dumplings) or Alt Wiener Kaiserschmarrn (Viennese pancake)!

Name: Culinarium Alpinum
Description: With its tasteful blend of historical features and upscale minimalist modern design, this former Capuchin monastery provides a wonderful setting for the restaurant. In the open kitchen, the team champions ingredients from Central Switzerland, supplemented by produce from the Alpine region. The evening features an appealing à la carte selection alongside a four-course "Tavolata" for the whole table, available as a surprise menu or with a main course of your own choice. In summer, the secluded monastery terrace is especially lovely. Breakfast is also served, with a regional "monastery breakfast" available on Sunday mornings. In addition to the restaurant, the site includes charming guestrooms, a monastery shop, a wine shop, seminar rooms and a cookery studio. They also run guided tours. Don't miss the "Edible Landscape" monastery garden; it is open to the public and gives visitors the chance to sample ripe fruit directly from the source.

Name: Culto ao Bacalhau
Address: Rua Formosa 322 Loja R8 - Mercado do Bolhão, Porto, 4000 248, Portugal
Description: If you’re visiting the beautiful city of Porto and are planning on heading to the historic Bolhão market, make sure you jot down the name of this restaurant! It is located on the upper gallery of this legendary building and, as the name strongly suggests, it is almost completely focused on the world of cod, with bacalhau-related recipes from across Portugal (cod escabeche with mussels, “bacalhau à Brás”, rice with cod and oysters, etc), an influence that even extends to the desserts! One dessert that we particularly loved but which has nothing to do with cod was the spectacular “pão de ló” sponge cake with cream cheese from the Beiras region.

Name: Cultura
Address: Dolores St. btw 5th and 6th Ave. Su Vecino Courtyard, Carmel-by-the-Sea, CA, 93921, USA
Description: Cultura’s cooking is inspired by the cuisine of Mexico, with particular attention paid to the region of Oaxaca. It might not be the right place to take abuela for an authentic taste of home, but the food is very good. Tucked among shops in a courtyard away from the street, this dining room resembles a Mexican taberna, lined with deep red booths, coffered ceilings and wrought-iron accents. On fair nights, dine alfresco around the courtyard’s fire pits. Sip a seasonal cocktail, perhaps the Letters to Oaxaca with mezcal, sparkling rosé and honey, then tuck into the house-made Cultura mole with smoked pork, which arrives as a feast of freshly made tortillas and lightly pickled vegetable slaw for assemble-your-own tacos. Save room for desserts like the dense and dark Oaxacan chocolate brownie with a touch of chili and cinnamon cloaked in ganache.

Name: Cuoco di Bordo
Description: An attractively furnished restaurant on the seafront with a small dining room and a veranda offering partial views of the sea. Fish takes pride of place on the menu, which focuses on raw fish dishes and classic recipes. The wine list is excellent, especially the whites (although the reds also include some impressive options) with many different vintages of the same wine available.

Name: Cuq en Terrasses
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Perched high in the village, this charming 18C house is a haven of calm, whose unusual, terraced grounds showcase the produce of the kitchen garden. The restaurant is helmed by two young professionals with stints in starred establishments in Toulouse under their belt, who concoct delicate seasonal cuisine: gratin of artichoke with aromatic herbs and a chorizo emulsion; river trout from Condax fish farm and almond stuffing. The view of the Lauragais plain and the Pyrenees from the conservatory and terrace is breathtaking. Extend the experience in this tranquil setting in one of the charming guestrooms.

Name: Cura Cucina Contemporanea
Address: Via Risorgimento 6/8, Marina di Davoli, 88060, Italy
Description: A single tasting menu invites guests to explore the culinary vision of Chef Massimo: a journey through authentic flavors of land and sea, enhanced by creative, personal touches. Delightful contrasts unfold around the onion, enveloped in a velvety cheese cream, while the “sottobosco” dish evokes autumn with the earthy aroma of porcini and tart hints of red berries. All this is embraced by the warm atmosphere of a converted former stable, where dry stone walls whisper tales of times past.

Name: Curios-City
Description: You need to look hard to find this place – there is no sign and the exterior looks barren. The stunning, moody interior is furnished in wabi-sabi style with lots of greenery, giving it a cosy and stylish ambience. The chef creates dishes underpinned by European techniques and punctuated by Malaysian twists. He offers three set menus that change every two months. Try the seven-course set to experience his vision in full glory.

Name: Curiosa by Jean-Georges
Address: Four Seasons Hotel, The Corniche, Doha, Qatar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The eponymous Jean-Georges is none other than the world-famous Vongerichten, who has brought a sassy Latino vibe to the elegant Four Seasons Hotel. Ask for a table in the bar for the Gulf views, and then sit back and wait for the band to start playing as you enjoy a sparkling selection of Latin and globally influenced dishes. That could mean a classic ceviche, tacos and tortillas, sizzling shrimp or crispy fried chicken. End with the ‘Salted Impossible Flan’ or the vast passion fruit sundae and you’ll be gliding out happy.

Name: Curioso
Description: It is said that “those who search, will find” and based on this mantra, the young couple at Curioso appear to have found their own paradise! This restaurant, close to the famous Plaza del Coso, offers an attractive market-inspired à la carte featuring an updated take on traditional dishes. This is complemented by the Curioso tasting menu, on which you can savour dishes such as lamb trotter gyoza, venison bolognaise with fresh pasta, and croissant with oxtail and a bearnaise sauce.

Name: Curnonsky
Description: Chef Benjamin Capelier is back at the helm of this restaurant that he already ran once before. Renamed Curnonsky in homage to the famous food critic and his first restaurant in Lyon, the establishment remains true to its original spirit: a wallet-friendly single set menu for lunch and a multi-course tasting experience at dinner. In a very simple and convivial setting, this discreet and focused chef delivers delicious modern cuisine, with each dish reflecting meticulous attention to texture and flavour. He is passionate about wine (an understatement) and recommends the perfect pairings himself from an exceptional wine list at wine merchant prices.

Name: Current Charcoal Grill
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Could these ceilings be any higher? In this expansive warehouse, find dark hardwood floors, oversized booths and banquettes, and near-endless counter seating looking straight into the kitchen. This serious, larger-than-life operation by Chefs Adam Evans and Luke Joseph pulls inspiration from across Asia and prepares its best dishes on the hot grill. Find Thai, Korean and Chinese flavors in the likes of shrimp and chicken wontons, red snapper with charred sticky rice, Iberico pork with nam prik and crushed peanuts, and short rib bo ssam. Cocktails pull from a similar range of flavors. Portions are generous so you’ll need friends if you have any intention of making it to dessert.

Name: Customshop
Description: Befitting its status as a fixture of the charming Elizabeth neighborhood, Customshop offers a lively, convivial atmosphere. Chef Andrés Kaifer oversees a modern menu that blends together Latin and Italian influences with seasonal North Carolina produce in dishes that are both inventive and approachable. A hamachi crudo with parmesan leche de tigre illustrates the point beautifully with its blend of vibrant acidity and savory depth, and carefully crafted pastas like casarecce with chorizo, local mushrooms and sungold tomato broth put any doubts to rest. Eminently quaffable cocktails and a thoughtful, food-friendly wine list certainly are a bonus, especially when combined with the friendly, helpful service.

Name: Cut
Description: Situated right in the heart of the Bergamo plain in the small town of Caravaggio, famous for the painter of the same name and for a much-visited pilgrim shrine, this welcoming restaurant boasts a modern decor and vintage furnishings. At lunchtime, it serves a good, competitively priced business menu, while in the evening the more elaborate à la carte features contemporary-style meat and fish dishes (mostly the latter).

Name: Cut & Barrel
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Set away from the city centre in the old Goldberger textile factory, this lovely warehouse conversion comprises a wine shop, an impressive bar, a large dining room with a terrace and a smaller anteroom offering counter dining. The stunning shop comes complete with an incredible selection of wines from around the country – including from the owner’s vineyard (Haraszthy Wines in Etyek) – as well as a Harley Davidson, a Porsche and a Rolls Royce. The food has a strong Latin American base but it’s their own charcuterie and succulent steaks from the Josper grill that lead the way.

Name: Cuubo
Address: 49 High Street, Harborne, Birmingham, B17 9NT, United Kingdom
Description: Adding to the growing food scene in the Birmingham suburb of Harborne is this Kickstarter-funded spot from a local chef. The space is small and stylish, with the feel of a contemporary bistro, while the contented diners and lively soundtrack combine to bring a pleasant buzz to the atmosphere. The menu is proudly British and fiercely seasonal, coming across in well-crafted dishes like a wonderful frozen rhubarb dessert with peanut brittle and vanilla ice cream. The cooking is all the better for its absence of unnecessary frippery.

Name: Cuzeo
Address: Rúa de los Francos 6, Zamora, 49001, Spain
Description: This restaurant, located along a busy pedestrian street in Zamora’s old quarter and surrounded by the town’s emblematic Romanesque buildings, provides guests with the perfect opportunity to try local and regional dishes that showcase “Zamoran” ingredients (such as the delicious chickpeas from Fuentesaúco) and a strong focus on game (partridge, wild boar, venison etc, mostly sourced from the Sierra de la Culebra). The backdrop here is rustic-modern in feel, with several small dining rooms in which the updated traditional à la carte is complemented by an excellent tasting menu. Make sure you try the highly popular kimchi croquettes or the stewed rib of wild boar with sweet potato and pickles, which we particularly enjoyed.

Name: Cynthia
Address: 32 Jones St., New York, NY, 10014, USA
Description: Personal and heartfelt, this intimate restaurant in the West Village is off to an impressive start. Named after the owner’s aunt, Cynthia delivers a refined experience that celebrates the seasons, works closely with farmers and walks the talk with a zero-waste philosophy. Vegetable trimmings are reworked into beautiful sauces, and scraps and ends are reimagined and incorporated into pastas and breads with house-made butter. French, Asian and Latin influences weave in and out of view on a menu that’s always on the move. One past highlight featured a superb, just-set egg custard boosted with corn dashi and black truffles. Supplemental courses are well worth the expense. Through it all, a warm service team keeps the evening flowing with ease.

Name: Czosnek i Oliwa
Description: On the outskirts of the Old Town, this vast restaurant offers a slick, buzzy dining experience in an industrial-style building arranged around a u-shaped courtyard. Diners are spread across two rooms: one with a bar and semi-open kitchen, the other large and airy with two mezzanines and floor-to-ceiling windows. The regularly changing menu is guided by the seasons and includes bright, generous dishes like beetroot carpaccio with goat’s cheese and pickled turnips.

Name: CÉ LA VI
Address: The Address Sky View Tower 2, Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Boulevard, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: The Dubai outpost of this fashionable restaurant group is set on the 54th floor of the Address Sky View Hotel. It comes with a party atmosphere and a bird’s eye view over the city from its super terrace, and service is friendly and professional. Contemporary dishes have influences ranging from a mix of Mediterranean, such as fried calamari, to Japanese classics, such as nigiri and beef kushiyaki.

Name: Cávala
Description: A contemporary restaurant that stands out for its open-view kitchen and striking wine cellar, with more than 1200 labels. The cuisine of Miguel Ángel Mayor, a Barcelona-born chef with Andalucian roots, is centred around two surprise tasting menus: Recuerdos (’Memories’, which seeks to put a modern spin on local dishes, with nods to his own childhood) and Influencias (’Influences’, which focuses more on highlighting the skills he acquired at the restaurants where he has worked and in kitchens around the world). We absolutely loved the tasting menu dedicated to rabbit, featuring several dishes and different preparations!

Name: Cèpes
Description: Hotel de Sterrenberg's restaurant draws on its natural surroundings. The interior is sleek yet warm, combining lots of wood with concrete, and a large wooden stag's head that draws the eye. The chef believes in sourcing his produce locally, using local suppliers such as Gert van Eldik and the Veluwe asparagus farm. Diners are served a surprise menu composed of intricate and beautifully presented dishes. Think venison from the region with carefully considered vegetable accompaniments and a game jus enhanced with vermouth. A proud ambassador for the Veluwe!

Name: Cécile
Description: In the lively, bustling Carmes neighbourhood, a close-knit young team welcomes you to this modern bistro with a wood-decked veranda, large open kitchen and contemporary decor. The short menu is inspired by a real mix of cultures: exotic touches are incorporated into dishes such as Thai duck tartare and farm-reared pork loin with mango and pomegranate.

Name: Cécile
Description: A pretty brick edifice in the heart of Pajottenland, a few stepts away from the church. This picture postcard image of Flanders sports a trendy, predominantly black and white interior and natural light. Sisters Judith and Astrid expertly manage the front of house, while chef Tom crafts fine cuisine, such as pheasant cooked whole with a fine champagne sauce. He enjoys jazzing up steak tartare with Asian notes, but is equally at home championing comforting family favourites.

Name: Céline
Description: The austere appearance of Fort Jutphaas is in marked contrast to the restaurant it houses, which boasts an intimate atmosphere with subdued lighting and cosy terrace. Chef Rick works principally with Dutch produce, such as Dutch yellowtail, which he likes to season with subtle Asian flavours. This is original and modern cuisine, in which vegetables take pride of place. In fact, why not opt for the appealing vegetarian set menu?

Name: Céma Passion
Description: Pauline’s infectious enthusiasm in the front of house and Cedric’s charismatic personality in the kitchen set the scene in this quintessentially laid-back establishment that pulls out all the stops to pamper youguests. You can expect premium produce (like black truffle brought back from France by Pauline’s brother-in-law) and the chef’s fascinating modern spin on Gallic recipes. Examples: truffles with steamed scallops, white wax beans with braised ham and a knockout beef consommé. Sincerity, generosity and commitment are the watchwords of Céma Passion.

Name: Céna
Description: Chef Clément Briand-Seurat has left the Pic Saint-Loup restaurant to open his own establishment (Cena means supper or dinner in Latin) beneath the ribbed vaults of a medieval edifice in the heart of historic Montpellier. A snug, romantic vibe, enhanced by centuries-old stonework and candle-lit rough oak tables, sets the scene. The chef signs a creative single set menu in which he endeavours to enhance the produce of local growers and breeders thanks to flawless craftsmanship (chutneys, oils, crumbles, crackers and whipped siphon concoctions). His knockout mushroom consommé and ‘stroll in the woods’ embodies this ethos.

Name: Cô Liêng
Address: 321 Vo Van Tan Street, Ban Co Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 72407, Vietnam
Description: For nearly 30 years, this humble spot has been serving authentic Southern Vietnamese flavours. The highlight is the charcoal-grilled bò lá lốt, minced beef wrapped in betel leaves, with its well-balanced savoury-sweet taste. A charcoal grill at the entrance sends smoky aromas into the street as each order is freshly prepared. The grilled meats can be enjoyed with fresh herbs and vegetables or with bánh hỏi, rice vermicelli bundles.

Name: Cômo
Description: Renato Favaro pays tribute to his roots in this buzzy trattoria depicted by a smart urban vibe and a sprinkling of amusing decorative details (like a bumper of the iconic cinquecento car). Old school family favourites set the culinary scene including pizzoccheri della valtellina and fettuccine al ragu, unless you wouldn’t rather sample paccheri al dente in a rich tomato sauce enhanced by shitake mushrooms, parsley, fennel-laced sausage and lashings of parmesan? Free of fancy frills, the focus is on authentic flavours and familiar family favourites. The cherry on the cake is chef Favaro’s fun-loving personality.

Name: Côté Jardin
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At Château de Beaulieu's contemporary brasserie, chef Christophe Dufossé devises cuisine that embraces both the traditional and the modern. It is a superb setting in which to enjoy meticulously prepared high-quality dishes: poached egg, fried portobello mushrooms and a mushroom cream; mackerel from the Côte d'Opale, red cabbage and smoked bacon; walnut tart, milk chocolate cream and walnut ice cream. Barbecue on the large terrace in summer, slow-cooked dishes in winter.

Name: Côté Jardin by Steve Moracchini
Description: In Le Petit Juas, a neighbourhood in the upper reaches of Cannes, Côté Jardin has been taken over by Steve Moracchini and transformed into a charming bistro. Previously pastry chef at La Passagère, he delivers a generous, no-nonsense menu rife with Mediterranean influences: confit leeks, hazelnut crumble and a delicate honey vinaigrette; tenderly braised feather blade of beef, a reduced jus and saffron-infused fregola sarda. Naturally, the dessert – caramelised mille-feuille with apples – reflects the chef's talent for sweets. Whether in the bright interior or out on the veranda or small terrace, the atmosphere is convivial. Prices are very reasonable for Cannes.

Name: Côté Mer
Description: Inhale the salty sea air of the picturesque port of Cancale lined with fishermen's houses. This stylish restaurant flanked by a handsome terrace overlooks the bay with the iconic Mont Saint Michel in the distance. The menu champions the region’s premium produce from local seafood (oysters, abalone, lobster) to tender saltmarsh lamb. The fish of the day is announced out loud. Only a few steps away, the owners have opened the Juste à Côté, offering simpler fare, ideal for a casual meal overlooking the seaside scenery.

Name: Côté Préféré
Description: Tim Versyck is a proud champion of his native western Flanders. Cherry-picked ingredients form the backbone of his mainly classical repertory, albeit with the odd international twist. Produce from the North Sea and the polders is what truly galvanises this virtuoso craftsman. He might flank North Sea crab (crafted into rémoulade) with Ostend seaweed, samphire and an astounding bisque packed in fascinating briny flavours. Cheerful Jolien extends a warm greeting in the dining room, which sports a bright contemporary vibe and is flanked by an elegant garden terrace.

Name: Côté Saisons
Address: 10 avenue de la Côte-Vermeille, Laroque-des-Albères, 66740, France
Description: Let's set the scene: a 19C building surrounded by greenery, with large bay windows, a flower-decked garden and a pretty terrace to cater to all seasons. On the menu are tasty, well-crafted dishes, eg warm calf's head with Charroux mustard, Cerdagne pig confit with honey-ginger, tender chuck of beef and pan-fried foie gras. In addition, the service is all smiles.

Name: Côté Sud
Description: You are bound to enjoy your time in this stone-built house with a garden and pleasant terrace. The chef whips up well-constructed dishes – the likes of crab meat with candied orange peel, shellfish jelly and buckwheat, or a roasted sea bream served with a variety of cauliflower and seaweed. The wine list gives pride of place to organic and biodynamic wines. Charming service.

Name: Côté Toqués
Description: Chef Julien Chabozy's aromatic, tasty food showcases the best of local produce, with lashings of personality to boot. Friendly and endearing depict the front of house vibe, supervised by his wife Marie. The establishment also boasts a delicatessen and a wine shop, La Cave des Toqués, next door… It was love at first bite.

Name: Côté Vigne
Description: In this quintessential Alsace village, this imposing 16C half-timbered house is the domain of a chef who crafts delicious modern cuisine peppered with influences from further afield. The lunch menu is simpler. To wash it all down, try one of the organic wines from the family estate. Very pleasant terrace in summer.

Name: Cúrate Bar de Tapas
Description: This Spanish-inspired tapas bar lives inside a renovated 1920s bus depot and serves up a menu rooted in tradition—think charcuterie, croquettes, patatas bravas and shareable large plates like mussels and grilled meats. They also have a "jamonarea" with around six different types of cured meats available. Cozy yet refined. this spot in downtown Asheville makes you want to order a bottle of wine and settle in while snacking on a tabla de quesos, a board with a selection of Spanish cheeses, and curate sobrasada, a pimenton-spiced, spreadable, cured sausage sided by goat cheese and honey with a baguette.

Name: Cơm Gà Lan
Address: 520 Trung Nu Vuong Street, Hoa Cuong Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: As the name suggests, there's only one thing on the menu – cơm gà, or chicken rice, but you can opt for the poultry roasted, steamed or shredded. Served with soup and pickles, the cơm gà xé bóp (shredded version), is especially popular. The lemongrass, coriander and onion lend the juicy chicken extra zing. Given the quality of the food and bargain prices, it's no surprise that this place is always jam-packed. Avoid peak hours.

Name: Cồ Đàm
Address: 68 Tran Hung Dao Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 11019, Vietnam
Description: Named after the Buddha, Cồ Đàm’s eye-catching architecture boasts an ornate exterior inspired by Buddhist and Champa culture and a striking arched entrance of terracotta bricks. Four floors are open for dining, but the ground floor stands out for its tranquil pond and terracotta Buddha. The restaurant offers two set menus only — Vietnam Namaste and Cham Namaste — each showcasing creative, modern interpretations of beautifully presented Vietnamese classics, layered with rich flavour combinations.

Name: D'Amore by Italo Bassi
Description: Located on Bonifacio marina, this place immediately appeals with its bright, colourful decor, every last detail of which has been carefully thought through. The menu comprises crudos, cold starters and hot dishes (risottos and pasta, all house-made and cooked to al dente perfection). From olive oil to local fish and Italian ingredients, this restaurant exudes quality and good taste.

Name: D'Berto
Description: At D’Berto, you’ll experience the full potential and expression of the local estuary’s produce. For those for whom scale is of little importance, this is definitely the place, where you can enjoy a truly surprising array of fish and seafood accompanied by excellent service. Perfectly cooked grilled dishes and stews are more important here than technique, though the latter is certainly not lacking. Options include an array of shellfish and several classic dishes such as the pan-fried lobster and the spider crab. Don't miss out on seasonal cockles!

Name: D'Leria
Description: In a traditional fishing community such as this one, famous for the quality of its clams, the quality of ingredients always takes centre stage. This simple family-run restaurant, which has breathed new life into a former bar, is run by a couple – two chefs with a focus on contemporary, seasonal cooking inspired by the sea. This is showcased on a concise à la carte and a tasting menu option (“where the sea takes me”). We particularly enjoyed the black monkfish with a pepitoria sauce.

Name: D'une Île
Address: Domaine de l'Aunay, lieu-dit l'Aunay, Rémalard-en-Perche, 61110, France
Description: The country annexe of Paris's Septime. Come to enjoy enduring, seasonal and rustic cuisine that is rooted in its surroundings, drawing solely on quality produce from the nearby markets (in Sarthe and Normandy) and, to a lesser extent, what is harvested in the farm's vegetable garden. The tastefully decorated dining room exudes rustic chic. In the same spirit, a few guestrooms extend an invitation to linger a little on this wooded hill in the Perche region, with its fruit trees, hives, and even a sauna overlooking the natural surroundings. A laudable initiative.

Name: DA COSTA
Address: Durslade Farm, Dropping Lane, Bruton, BA10 0NL, United Kingdom
Description: The stunning Art Farm development makes a fitting home for this equally gorgeous restaurant. As soon as you enter, you’re met with the enticing aroma of wood-fired cooking, emanating from the breathtakingly designed open kitchen. With pots, pans and even chairs hanging from the ceiling, plus an abundance of wooden furnishings, it’s like dining in a particularly chic country kitchen. The menu looks to all things Italian, with terrific hand-cut pasta and hearty, wholesome flavours across the board – bigoli with venison ragu is the epitome of the style.

Name: DA MÓ
Description: This new, restored restaurant in the upper part of the Sassi (yet still near the centre of Matera and its car parks) has a warm friendly ambience and boasts a small, charming outdoor space. Here, an entire family (father in the kitchen, mother and daughter front of house), who moved to Matera from Venosa (home of the Latin poet Horatio), serves regional cuisine with a contemporary twist and no little skill and professionalism. Various tasting menus are available, as well as an à la carte. An interesting wine list completes the picture.

Name: DA PEPI
Description: The ivy-draped façade arrests the eye. On the menu, one item after another professes the chef’s admiration for the cuisine of Tuscany. ‘Fumo’ is a dish of pasta in tomato sauce, learnt by the chef on his Tuscan sojourn. Aromas of olive oil and garlic wafting from the kitchen, tables set to encourage sharing from a single dish: it all recalls everyday life in Italy. Set menus are always an improvised surprise. DA PEPI is fun, like an invitation to dinner at a friend’s home.

Name: DAMES
Description: Once a transport café between Saint-Malo and Mont-Saint-Michel, this establishment has been transformed by Marine Hervouet (trained by Alain Passard and Bruno Verjus) and Pascaline Albicini (taught by Robuchon and Etchebest). The premises have been renovated in a bucolic style characterised by exposed stone and contemporary wooden furniture and exude the warmth of a family home. The menu, focused on carefully selected local produce, is exceedingly high calibre. With flambéed tomato compote and a tomato caramel sauce, the vegetable agnolotti impresses with its aromatic depth. The audacious desserts – crispy choux pastry puff garnished with smoked aubergine, sorrel ice cream and hot caramel – hit the mark.

Name: DAN
Description: Casual French dining by a chef with deep experience in gastronomy. The counter forms an arc around the kitchen, dissolving the barrier between host and guest. Traditional recipes cooked with Japanese ingredients highlight the affinity between the two. Risotto, for example, is a perennial favourite, being a rice dish. The intimate establishment and cheerful circle of guests make Dan a step up.

Name: DAS BERNHARDS
Description: The Bernhard family's centrally located restaurant is cosy in its rustic charm, attracting many regular guests who appreciate both the cordial, attentive service and the excellent food. The menu features regional and seasonal dishes alongside Swiss classics such as "Züri Gschnätzlets – veal strips, creamy mushroom sauce, cognac, authentic Swiss rösti", reflecting the family's Graubünden roots. The daily specials are especially popular at lunch. The terrace is lovely in summer.

Name: DAS GOLDSTEIN BY GOLLNER'S
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: It's quite unexpected to come across such a chic restaurant in a remote wooded area like this. But the journey is absolutely worth making. Set in the former rifle club house about 5km from the city centre, this establishment boasts a tastefully sleek and upscale interior. It serves freshly prepared, predominantly Austrian cuisine, but the menu also features international dishes, some with Asian influences. The walk-in wine cellar and extensive wine list are a draw in themselves.

Name: DAS MAXI - GENUSSREICH
Description: Das Maxi has proven to be a successful addition to Das Freiberg hotel and is an appealing dining option – and not only for hotel guests. The kitchen specialises in contemporary, mostly Mediterranean dishes with seasonal influences. In addition to the set menu, which changes daily, there is also a small à la carte selection. Food is served in tastefully designed dining areas, and there is additional garden seating available for the summer months. The wine list, featuring international labels, is second to none. The gorgeous guestrooms have magnificent views of the mountains.

Name: DEBRA
Description: (DEBRA temporarily moved to Zuidstationstraat 14 in Ghent) DEBRA has achieved a subtle balance of warmth and intimacy, flanked by hip designer details and a funky soundtrack, courtesy of a vintage turntable (the name is from a song by Beck). The playful, distinctive food is signed Jason Blanckaert and Gilles Bogaert, who slalom between classical recipes like whole roasts and internationally inspired sauces. Kick off with a few appetisers, like tartare of langoustine served with a stock of heads and roe on crunchy toast. Next, expect to be surprised by eel, lacquered in brown ale, then grilled and served with a light, spicy mojo salsa. The distinctive hallmark of this high-profile chefs is their ingredient-led highly personal vision of feelgood food.

Name: DEG Ristorante
Address: Via Gioacchino Rossini 29, Busto Arsizio, 21052, Italy
Description: In a tranquil quarter of the city, where parking presents no challenge, a self-taught chef of considerable experience has taken the helm of an intimate and thoughtfully appointed establishment. The contemporary interiors, enlivened by delicate pastel tones, help create an atmosphere that is both intimate and refreshingly informal in spirit. Here, cookery is a convivial gesture: the chef does not remain hidden behind the stoves, but often comes out into the dining room to speak with passion about his dishes, born of contemporary techniques and personal sensitivity. His signature lies in well-calibrated sapidity, achieved through targeted fermentations, measured touches of acidity and a selection of quality ingredients that converse with Oriental influences while never losing their connection to Italian roots. The emblematic example is his tuna osso buco with yuzu potato cream, tuna jus and sun-dried tomato garum: a successful crossover in which tradition and Asian influences interweave with natural ease.The gastronomic offering is both broad and structured: several tasting menus allow one to explore the chef’s philosophy with coherence, including a Chef’s Table experience that must be booked in advance, designed to experience the service at even closer quarters, almost overlooking his work. There is also a generous carte, conceived for those who prefer to construct their own flavour journey whilst maintaining complete freedom of choice.

Name: DEN KUSHI FLORI
Description: A collab between the two restaurants Den, with its creative Japanese food, and Florilège, offering modern French cuisine. ‘Den’ and ‘Flori’ are joined by ‘Kushi’, meaning ‘skewer’. Yet despite the name, this is not a skewer restaurant; rather, the name reflects the experience and friendship that joins the eatery’s two partners. The fare is Japanese-Western fusion: tempura with sherry, for example, or sweetfish in baked custard tart. Always evolving, never making the same dish twice, it shows the world that experimentation makes food more fun.

Name: DESACATO
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: A restaurant with a relaxed, informal feel and an industrial-style decor in Seville’s historic quarter, where sections on the menu entitled The Preliminaries, Sharing is Living, Carnal Temptations, and From the Cantabrian Sea to the Mediterranean set the scene for what is to come. The restaurant describes itself as committed to “irreverent cuisine” in which fusion influences and Andalucian and Basque flavours all play their part. You’ll also find constantly changing fish and seafood dishes that don’t feature on the menu.

Name: DIA
Description: You’ll be surprised how busy this formally laid restaurant in a residential spot can get, but the experienced team cope well with the numbers – among which there are many returning guests. It sits within a tardis-like building, which also houses meeting rooms, and is smartly decked out with fine glassware and crockery. The menu is one of the most eclectic around and offers everything from a burger to fine steaks, with the popular daily specials including the likes of freshly caught fish. There really is something for everyone here.

Name: DIELS
Description: Dietmar and Elsko's bustling "Restobar" is a cosy, laid-back place where anything goes and nothing is compulsory. Drop in for a casual drink or settle in for a sumptuous dinner. The host presents an excellent wine selection at appealing prices, complementing the chef's à la carte offerings and popular surprise menu. Expect dishes such as kingfish sashimi with a punchy passion fruit and tarragon vinaigrette, medium-rare lamb with a robust lamb jus. This chef has an eye for detail and a solid grasp of the classics, occasionally drawing inspiration from Asia. Good times guaranteed!

Name: DIP
Address: Sheraton Cebu Mactan Resort, Mactan Island, Punta Engaño Road, Lapu-Lapu, Cebu, 6015, The Philippines
Description: Within the grounds of the Sheraton Cebu Mactan Resort, DIP boasts ocean views and designer interiors that blend exotic flair and modern elegance. Herringbone parquet, mosaic walls and rattan chairs make for a refined yet unpretentious atmosphere. The Nikkei menu highlights dishes such as ceviche hiramasa & hotate tiradito and the 16 hour cochinillo lechal confit. Service is charming and professional; cocktails and a modest wine list round off the occasion.

Name: DIREKTE
Description: Just a few steps from the always busy Diagonal, this establishment has turned the bar into the main protagonist.Chef Arnau Muñío, a native of Cerdanyola del Vallès, always takes risks in his combinations and shows a special interest in both seafood and vegetables, successfully fusing Catalan roots and Mediterranean market products with flavours from Asian cuisine. The proposal only comes to life through three surprise tasting menus: Direkte, Boqueria and Eixample (the latter, the most complete with 12 savoury courses and 3 desserts, requires prior reservation). What did we like the most? The tuna spine esqueixada, served in two courses alongside tuna spine consommé with fermented pine blossom, and their wonderful roast chicken stock with prawns. A comprehensive wine list, featuring international options as well as local and low-intervention wines!

Name: DOLLI·S
Description: If the thought of enjoying a pleasant meal with an idyllic view appeals to you, then this could be the place. This restaurant is located on the fifth floor of the luxury The Dolli at Acropolis hotel, a historic mansion that has been completely remodelled and boasts picture-postcard views of the Acropolis. The menu here is a combination of Mediterranean cuisine with Asian options prepared by a chef who conjures up dishes within full view of guests in the dining room. Precise and meticulously presented, his dishes are always based around top-quality seasonal ingredients. The gourmet experience is more extensive in the evening and is complemented by the extensive array of wines, including labels from leading wine estates as well as artisanal vineyards.

Name: DOYY
Description: DOYY offers an intimate and relaxed atmosphere with a touch of Middle Eastern elegance, reflecting the Azerbaijani-Turkish heritage of owner Yavuz. Chef Daan van Lieshout knows his French classics, as evidenced in the à la carte selection, which includes dishes such as steak tartare and tournedos Rossini. However, he also likes to incorporate Asian and Middle Eastern influences into his cooking – it is his set menu that really showcases his creativity. Think salty-sweet langoustine tartare with citrus chiboust, confit tomatoes, crispy chicken skin and a frothy bisque jus. Brace yourself for bold flavours with a spicy kick!

Name: DUOO Gastro Theatre
Address: Rua Dr. João Vitorino Mealha, 10, Portimao, 8500-660, Portugal
Description: This small restaurant is run by the chef couple, Leandro Silva and Catarina Monteiro (she is usually more present in the dining room), who show genuine passion for the kitchen and an unconditional commitment to the project. Together they have created a fusion proposal which, rooted in both their professional paths and life experiences, combines influences from Portugal, Spain and all of Latin America, while always taking Portuguese produce as its base. The name says it all: “DUOO” in reference to themselves, and “Gastro Theatre” as an ode to presentation, since diners sit at a Japanese-inspired counter to watch, in detail, all the chefs’ work at the stoves. The experience revolves around two tasting menus (Muralha and Ria), as well as an à la carte service and an executive menu at lunchtime.

Name: DVISI
Description: DVISI boasts a unique location in the landscaped gardens of the striking Casa Vincke hotel. In the bright dining room, which overlooks the swimming pool through large picture windows and features an open annexe that acts as a terrace, enjoy contemporary-style cuisine on an à la carte with dishes designed for sharing and a tasting menu, both which feature influences from Asia and Latin America. Oysters make a triple appearance (raw with Bloody Mary; charcoal grilled, with yuzu, sake and mirin; or grilled with aguachile pearl).

Name: DYLANS
Address: Oude Zeeweg 63, Noordwijk aan Zee, 2202 CJ, Netherlands
Description: The founder of Alexander Hotel was born a butcher's son and can be proud of this restaurant for meat lovers. The trendy intimacy of the decor, the gold elements, the hip lounge and cocktail bar all make for a magnificent venue. Many of the modern dishes are prepared on the Josper charcoal oven, resulting in robust, pure flavours. A fine côte de boeuf, a salt-crusted tenderloin to share, a choice cut of Japanese Wagyu beef: a feast for carnivores!

Name: Da Annetta
Description: In an 18th Century building, a rustic yet elegant atmosphere with a particular attentiveness at the tables and in the cuisine, which has a traditional base, but also knows how to add imaginative variations.

Name: Da Antonio
Description: The Meschino family opened a pizzeria on the food-centric Vilnius Gatvė in 1996 and, over the years, it has evolved into this smart, formal spot. Two small dining rooms are elegantly decked out with mirrors, chandeliers and linen-clad tables; in summer though, head for the flower-decked terrace. The chef may be Lithuanian, but you’d never know, as he follows the Italian principles of good ingredients, simple preparation and maximum flavour. The homemade pastas are a highlight – such as red maltagliati with lamb ragout, boletus and cream sauce – and interesting Italian wines accompany.

Name: Da Bibe
Description: At the gates of Florence, at the precise point where the city dissolves into the green of the countryside, Bibe welcomes guests beneath the leafy canopy of its summer terrace and within the warm interiors of a trattoria safeguarding over one hundred and fifty years of history, now in the hands of the sixth generation. Here, Tuscan cuisine remains the absolute protagonist: artisanal cured meats, traditional crostini, pici al ragù, and iconic dishes such as beef peposo. Not to be missed are the fried or grilled chicken and, for devotees, a fiorentina that interprets the classic canons in the most authentic manner.

Name: Da Bob Cook Fish
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Working in partnership with the nearby fishmongers which supplies it with fresh fish and seafood, this restaurant occupies a building once used for storing oranges that dates back 400 years. Although there is a menu, given the restaurant’s close relationship with the fishmongers we recommend asking the serving staff about the catch of the day and taking a look in the glass cabinet where the fish are displayed. Dishes are classic and traditional, allowing the full flavour of the fresh fish to shine through.

Name: Da Carla
Address: via Necchi 3/5, fraz. Molino Isella, Gambolò, 27025, Italy
Description: Once a mill, this restaurant still stands next to its old canal which lends the setting a delightful bucolic ambience echoed in the warm, welcoming dining room. Highlights on the menu include risottos, frog’s legs, snails and goose - based dishes, as well as cured meats. Inviting guestrooms complete this delightfully rustic picture.

Name: Da Cecco
Address: piazza Belvedere Puccini 10/12, Torre del Lago Puccini, 55049, Italy
Description: A cosylittle restaurant at the beginning of the lakefront. Mainly seafood dishes, though in the winter there is also game. Rustic atmosphere.

Name: Da Cesare
Description: A restaurant with an ultra-classic character, founded as far back as 1921, offering a menu with the flavour of another era: one of those very long lists, rich in choice and able to range naturally between meat and seafood. The section devoted to grilled meats is extensive, as is that reserved for raw fish, which is always much in demand. In the evening, the offer widens further with the addition of the pizzeria.

Name: Da Ciacco
Address: via Dante Alighieri 30/a, San Quirico d'Orcia, 53027, Italy
Description: In the heart of the pedestrian historic center, this venue offers a warm welcome in a rustic dining room or at a few tables overlooking the paseo. Family-run, it serves authentic Tuscan flavors prepared traditionally. The handmade pici with cherry tomatoes, olives, and slightly spicy anchovies are an unmissable summer delight!

Name: Da Concettina ai Tre Santi
Address: via Arena alla Sanità 7 bis, Naples, 80137, Italy
Description: In the heart of the Sanità district: ancient, lively, popular, often chaotic. The Oliva family has managed this excellent venue for over 60 years, successfully updating it with a tasteful renovation while maintaining its traditional roots. Today, it also offers more imaginative and modern pizzas, like the Sott e’ Ngopp (“under and over,” describing the concept of the dish), along with fried items and a tasting menu. Shaded terrace available.

Name: Da Enzo
Address: Via Ai Grotti, Ponte Brolla, 6652, Switzerland
Description: This Ticino-style stone house boasts a sun-blessed, verdant setting and a beautiful garden-terrace. Take a seat at one of its typical granite tables, either crowned by stone vaulting or shaded by trees, where you can savour exquisite Mediterranean on several tasting menus (including vegetarian) and an à la carte that includes daily specials. Other features include a well-stocked wine cellar and two romantic rustic-style guestrooms. Open for over three decades, Dan Enzo is now run by the second generation of the family.

Name: Da Ercole
Description: Situated on Crotone’s seafront, Da Ercole is a culinary institution for anyone who loves fish, with the benefit of 40 years in the business behind it! The salty tang of the Ionian sea is celebrated on an extensive menu, although if you really want to enjoy yourself to the full, let owner-chef and old-school host Ercole guide you in your choice (including some excellent raw fish dishes).

Name: Da Fausto
Description: Situated in these premises since 2015, Fausto has become a local favourite thanks to the quality and style of its cuisine which combines classic flavours and regional influences. Two of the chef’s great passions (chocolate and ice cream) always feature on the dessert menu, while the cool outdoor space near the entrance adds to the appeal.

Name: Da Gelsomina
Description: Reached on foot or (with a prior telephone call) by shuttle, this is an authentic family-run trattoria; just a few metres from the restaurant are the breathtaking views of the Philosophers’ Park. Among the most popular dishes are the Caprese ravioli and the chicken cooked under a brick in the wood-fired oven.

Name: Da Giacomo
Description: Within the charming centre of a beautiful locality divided by the Adda River and encircled by ancient walls, is a venue merging rustic notes with contemporary elements, featuring a delightful outdoor area beneath the portico. They present regional cuisine (for instance, nougat espuma with melted chocolate) and Italian dishes (glazed suckling pig loin with Sicilian orange blossom honey), modernised and lightened. The fine selection of wines is constructed over the years with care and passion by the owner.

Name: Da Gianfranco
Address: via delle Orchidee 5, Alba Adriatica, 64011, Italy
Description: Gianfranco Verdecchia, restaurateur and heir to a family of butchers, has always cooked the food that sustained his people. After running a restaurant in Sant’Omero – a hill town known for its festival dedicated to baccalà (salt cod), a staple in the area’s cuisine – he returned to his hometown of Giulianova. Here, in a stylish, secluded space away from the sea, he has kept baccalà as the sole seafood option, devoting an entire menu to it alongside a wide selection of dishes highlighting his first love: meat.

Name: Da Gigetto
Description: A long-established restaurant with a renowned reputation thanks to the enthusiasm of the family at the helm and the excellent cuisine on offer. The carefully designed menu focuses mainly on classic regional dishes, yet also includes more contemporary options and even a few fish-based specialities, while the impressive wine list features more than 1 000 different labels, including some surprising names and various vertical wine-tasting options.

Name: Da Giovanni
Description: The 18C ceramic stove, bright, colourful decor (both period and vintage), long family tradition and excellent cuisine all contribute to making this restaurant which opened half a century ago a bastion of fine cuisine in Piacenza and the wider Po valley. Meat and fish both feature on the menu, although it is the latter that has become renowned as the restaurant’s speciality over the years. The excellent service is friendly and informal yet highly professional, while the extensive wine list also includes a good selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Da Guido
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The story of this restaurant began in 1967, when Guido and Giovanna Fasan, both of whom still work front of house, met in Germany. They then moved back to Italy, where they opened Da Guido in the early 1990s. White dominates in the elegant, contemporary-style dining room, while the cuisine features delicious seafood dishes with a focus on grilled specialities. In summer, there’s a welcoming bar in the garden, which boasts a romantic atmosphere. Together with other restaurant-owners from Venice, the Fasan family also have a kitchen garden on the Venetian island of Sant’Erasmo, where they focus on sustainable growing methods.

Name: Da Lorenzo – Al Giardino Segreto
Address: Fondamenta Madona de l'Orto, 3500, Venice, 30121, Italy
Description: Hidden within the elegant walls of the NH Collection Palazzo dei Dogi, far from the bustling tourist crowds, Da Lorenzo – Al Giardino Segreto is an oasis of taste created by Paulo Airaudo, a multi-starred Spanish chef, who is assisted in the kitchen by the young Salvatore Paladino. Every dish at this restaurant is a refined combination of culinary technique, elegance and local flavours, enhanced by sophisticated Japanese accents. To immerse themselves in his gastronomic vision, guests can choose between two evocative tasting menus: Emozioni and Sensazioni – two experiences that convey the soul of this restaurant with style.

Name: Da Luciano
Address: via Nazionale 11, Passignano sul Trasimeno, 06065, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Enjoy beautiful views of Lake Trasimeno from the outdoor terrace of this restaurant, where the menu focuses mainly on fish, alongside original ingredients such as beans and Umbrian truffles which are used in typical specialities such as tegamaccio (fish stew).

Name: Da Manuela
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: To step inside Da Manuela is to gift oneself a moment of genuine conviviality, especially precious on the grayest winter days, when the warm welcome and proudly regional cuisine have a way of lifting the spirits. At the entrance, Berkel slicers take pride of place, devoted to showcasing local cured meats of great character, while the table receives freshwater fish prepared with skill – as in the charcoal tagliatelle with coarse perch ragù and Arctic char roe – alongside game preparations. Not to be missed are the fried frogs’ legs, snails offered in multiple versions, and the risottos of the day. Reasons abound, in short, to discover this storied corner. Need more convincing? The truly abundant cheese trolley and a cellar attentive to small local producers, yet open to new horizons and Europe’s principal wine regions, will win over the undecided.

Name: Da Miky
Address: via Fegina 104, Monterosso al Mare, 19016, Italy
Description: Situated right on the seafront, Miky is one of the best restaurants for fish (including the famous Monterosso anchovies) in the region, serving cuisine which is more and more exciting and individual every year. There’s also a small shop selling local produce.

Name: Da Miro alla Lanterna
Description: Buoyed by a long tradition that has made it a true institution of the city over the years, this historic venue overlooking the tourist harbour continues to stand as a point of reference for seafood cookery. Today the selection of fish no longer takes place at a display buffet, yet the menu – broad and well-constructed – speaks with precision to the quality of the produce and the variety of what is on offer. Crustaceans, deep-water fish and catch of varying size are handled with respect and expertise, giving rise to dishes capable of conveying genuine Mediterranean emotion. Among the preparations not to be missed are the spaghetti alla Trabaccolara, a historic recipe of the Viareggio tradition, based on tomato and fish, here interpreted in faithful keeping with local memory. The setting is that of a classic and elegant dining room, with professional and attentive service, accompanied by a wine list that is both broad and well-judged in its value for money. A reassuring constant since 1954.

Name: Da Nando
Description: Proud champion of local cuisine, along with more classic dishes, with a unique touch: the menu is written in Friulian dialect as well as Italian. Aromas of the woods and sea hover around the tables, with succulent meats – including game – and the freshest fish. Don't miss the cjarsons ravioli, delicious little morsels available in both sweet and savoury versions. The restaurant boasts an extensive wine cellar, and the scent of truffles reigns supreme on a dedicated menu in season.

Name: Da Nicolo
Description: Located in an advantageous spot along the promenade, where there is a summer dining area, this restaurant is really patronized for the quality of its food. Serving seafood and Carlofortinian specialties.

Name: Da Nilo
Description: In the heart of Cetona's square, a well-tended outdoor area among hedges welcomes guests with warmth and smiles. The cuisine is authentically Tuscan and well-crafted. Don’t miss the selection of local cured meats and the classic pici all’aglione, a true must-try!

Name: Da Noemi
Description: The mother of the current owner opened this busy restaurant in a medieval alleyway in the historic centre, giving it her own name. The historic dishes here reflect the culinary traditions of Ferrara, with specialities such as salama da sugo (pork sausage) and pasticcio di maccheroni (a baked pasta dish) on the menu. A must for anyone looking to sample local dishes already famous during the time of the Este family.

Name: Da Noi
Description: Perched on a rocky outcrop looking out across Nonza's bay, this old stone building sits alongside the Genoese tower and commands views stretching as far as Saint-Florent. Below the Paoline tower, the terraced dining area enjoys spectacular panoramas of the sea. The chef cooks up traditional Corsican cuisine that draws on Italian influences but is firmly rooted in local Corsican produce: local fish from Centuri, lamb from a neighbouring farmer, olive oil from the village, and vegetables from the kitchen garden – in season, almost solely. An authentic restaurant that also has a reasonably priced set menu.

Name: Da Nonna Sceppa
Description: Founded in the 1960s by Grandma Giuseppa, the inn has today become a restaurant. The management has stayed within the hands of the same family: nephews and great - nephews are spread over dining room and kitchen. Local recipes on the menu, which changes daily.

Name: Da Odino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant has stood on this square for many years, having been built as a “casone” and previously used as a dance hall. Despite its large size, the atmosphere is pleasant and convivial, helped by the staff here who are friendly yet professional. Situated just a stone’s throw from the Park Hotel Junior, a modern hotel under the same ownership, the restaurant specialises in fish and seafood, although you’ll also find meat and vegetarian options on the menu.

Name: Da Orlando
Description: Simply arriving in Cusago near Milan, where the imposing castle dominates the attractive centre, puts you in a good mood. At Da Orlando, the menu is equally balanced between top-quality fish dishes such as the “bollita di mare” and meat-based dishes that will delight food-lovers, such as snails with trumpet mushrooms and duck breast with ginger. Two elegant dining rooms are the perfect setting for a romantic evening, while the attractive outdoor space comes into its own in summer. A good restaurant with over 40 years of history.

Name: Da Oscar
Description: Standing on the hills overlooking Lake Garda, this attractive, spacious restaurant has an elegant atmosphere. There is a delightful terrace for alfresco dining in summer.

Name: Da Passano
Description: Overlooking the port, this restaurant and wine bar revisits traditional Corsican fare in a modern, designer interior. Live guitar music on summer evenings on the shaded terrace.

Name: Da Peppe
Description: Situated in the historic centre of a small village in the Parco del Pollino, this long-established restaurant serves traditional and copious local dishes that are always expertly prepared. Guestrooms are also available in the family B&B of the same name.

Name: Da Po
Address: Golden Mile Food Centre, #B1-53, 505 Beach Road, 199583, Singapore
Description: This stall serves only curry chicken noodles and Hainanese chicken rice. The latter comes in three portion sizes. Choose between roast or steamed chicken. The steamed one boasts meaty flavour, springy skin and silky flesh.

Name: Da Poli alla Stazione
Address: viale della Repubblica 10, Castelnovo di Sotto, 42024, Italy
Description: In the centre of a town known for its carnival and many allegorical floats, this family-run restaurant housed in an old railway station dating from the early 20C serves traditional regional dishes. The house speciality is charcoal-grilled cuisine, with an equal emphasis on meat and fish options.

Name: Da Politano
Description: Just outside Cuneo, at Boves, Da Poliziano is a family-run establishment that combines the hospitality of a hotel with a table attended to in every detail. The kitchen follows a tightly focused menu built around seasonality, enriched by a contemporary touch from young Luca, who draws on experience gained beyond these walls. In winter – particularly between December and January – the Helix pomatia snail ravioli with its own ragù is a must-order: a signature dish of rare finesse, worth the trip on its own.

Name: Da Rinuccio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: On the slopes of "a muntagna," one of the respectful nicknames for the volcano in the area, just outside the town with ample private parking, you'll find a family-oriented setting offering predominantly meat dishes, fresh pasta, and mushrooms. The dishes are carefully prepared, with generous portions, and meals are always enjoyed in a lovely glass-enclosed veranda. The wine list focuses mainly on Sicilian and particularly Catanese selections.

Name: Da Severino il Vecchio - Di Luciano
Address: largo Abruzzi 2, ang. via Piemonte 23, Senorbì, 09040, Italy
Description: This historic restaurant now has new premises with a classic yet modern feel. Mediterranean cuisine with a traditional and regional influence.

Name: Da Tonino
Description: The chef at this restaurant serves decidedly contemporary cuisine with its roots in traditional recipes. His creative flair results in modern dishes in which each detail is carefully curated, with bold combinations that come as a surprise yet always feature a perfect balance of flavours and textures. The restaurant, situated in a quiet residential area away from the hustle and bustle of the small town, is the perfect choice for anyone looking for a relaxed and yet elegant dining experience.

Name: Da Valentino
Description: Although it is the beautiful terrace that first catches the eye at this restaurant, the friendly welcome and attentive service offered by Valentino in the kitchen and Sabine front of house add to the appeal. Mediterranean specialities and traditional classic dishes feature on the menu, while an open fireplace creates a warm ambience in winter.

Name: Da Vincenzo
Description: It's never easy to find the right balance between quality and quantity, especially in a town that is very much on the tourist trail. However, Da Vincenzo has succeeded in doing just this for years, ever since it was first opened by the family’s grandfather Vincenzo in 1958. Today, the founder’s grandson (who shares his grandfather’s name) is at the helm here, creating dishes which focus mainly on fish. Pleasant atmosphere, with a few small tables on the pavement of the street that runs through the centre of Positano. A choice of cocktails supplements the wine selection from lunchtime onwards.

Name: Da iumén
Address: Via Vittorio Emanuele II 26, Castelnuovo Belbo, 14043, Italy
Description: Since 1869, five generations have reinterpreted Piedmontese tradition through a modern lens. In an elegant, intimate setting, the restaurant serves dishes that fuse history and innovation – don’t miss the potato-and-hazelnut gnocchi with robiola cream. In the warmer months, reserve a table on the panoramic terrace: the view of the town hall and the hills of Castelnuovo Belbo is pure poetry.

Name: Da ö Vittorio
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Reassuring Ligurian cuisine in a classic interpretation and in a “Historical Restaurant of Italy”, where the same family always keeps up with the times, served in two separate rooms: one with a traditional tone, the other more modern. It is interesting to browse through the menu and wine list with historical notes and useful information on grape varieties. The many seafood dishes are accompanied by timeless local specialities, such as cima alla genovese. The focaccia with cheese is proverbial!

Name: DaV Mare
Description: The classic, wrought-iron outdoor dining space at this restaurant overlooks one of the most romantic little squares in Italy, while the view takes in the promontory dominated by its castle – a picture-postcard view that is famous around the world. The experienced Cerea family from the famous three-starred Michelin Da Vittoria restaurant in Bergamo are at the helm, serving consistently top-quality cuisine whether you’re here for a quick lunch or a gourmet dinner. It’s best to book ahead as the few tables are much in demand!

Name: DaV by Da Vittorio Louis Vuitton
Description: Situated in the heart of the central fashion district at the beginning of Via Montenapoleone, this new restaurant is the result of a collaboration between the renowned Cerea family and the equally prestigious fashion house Louis Vuitton, one of whose Milanese stores is located right behind it. The cuisine here is Italian to its core, albeit with a focus on dishes reinterpreted in a contemporary style that blends perfectly with the setting and the expectations of its guests. The decor is that of an elegant bistro, with the very busy dining room immediately after the entrance and reception, and a more intimate mezzanine accessible via stairs or a lift. The staff will quickly put you at ease and are on hand to offer recommendations from the à la carte or the chef’s tasting menu.

Name: Dabbanna
Address: Piazza Principe di Napoli 8/9, Modica, 97015, Italy
Description: It all began with the Cabbanna rotisserie, opened by grandfather Carmelo in 1971 and still going strong today, on his return from a time spent living in Venezuela. Fifty years later, his grandchildren are running a restaurant right opposite, in the central area of lower Modica, in a charming establishment with tasteful, welcoming interiors and several outdoor tables used in the summer. The menu is based on the island's ingredients and recipes, but also includes exotic influences — such as ceviche, known locally as “Ciauru ri mari” — reinterpreted with a contemporary twist. This results in colourful, beautifully presented dishes, excellent ingredients and delicate, attentive service provided by a female team.

Name: Dae Mon
Description: This chic and rather stylish restaurant is an interesting option. Dubbed "open-minded cuisine", the food sees techniques and flavours borrowed from different cultures and combined to create modern, innovative dishes. Of their two Asian-inspired eight-course set menus, one is vegetarian. You can also swap individual dishes in or out to put together your own menu. Tip: As an alternative to wine, they propose a beautifully curated cold Asian tea pairing – a real treat for all those who like to go alcohol-free.

Name: Dagon
Description: Dagon calls this prominent corner of Broadway home and is appealingly flanked by large windows. Inside, the room is open, spacious and easy-breezy, infused with shades of teal. Large glass light fixtures illuminate the off-center bar—ideal for solo diners—and the long counter, which is definitely the preferred perch among many a patron here.The menu is a clear and nuanced expression of Middle Eastern flavors. Fresh-baked breads, like kubaneh accompanied by creamy hummus, shouldn't be missed. Chicken liver mousse with mustard seeds and date syrup is a match made in culinary heaven; Agu's cigar, filled with a blend of ground lamb, potatoes, and spices, is even better with tahini dipping sauce; and shakshuka is always comforting.

Name: Dah Makan
Description: Cod marinated in miso and grilled on a robata, served with crunchy veg and lashings of frothy beurre blanc spiked with yuzu… Dishes to share such as these explain the success of this snug eatery. The culinary score, depicted by Asian flavours and western influences, demonstrates a clear preference for superior produce such as wagyu beef or crab from the North Sea, which are often finished on a robata grill or teppanyaki griddle. The menu is almost impossibly varied!

Name: Dai Pai Dong
Address: Rosewood Abu Dhabi Hotel, Zayed the First Street, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Cantonese is king and sharing the thing at Rosewood’s good-looking Chinese restaurant. Whether you enjoy roasted duck, braised brisket, crispy chicken or double-boiled soups, there’s plenty for you to enjoy here, and if you prefer something a little more fiery there are Sichuan dishes too. Weekend brunches are hugely popular too; while Wednesdays host ‘All You Can Grill’ nights.

Name: Daica
Description: In this attractive Mallorcan-style townhouse with two rustic-contemporary dining rooms plus an attractive patio, enjoy cooking with a traditional feel, enhanced by creative touches and a constant nod to ingredients sourced from around the island. This is exclusively showcased on two menus: Temporada and Festa (a cheese course can be added to each menu at an additional cost).

Name: Daikanyama Issai Kassai
Description: The warmly lit counter catches the eye through the glass walls – so Japanese in style, yet Western in mood. Having honed his craft in New York, the chef opened this izakaya to offer Japanese fare in a casual setting. The proprietress greets guests in kimono. Sashimi is served as a mixed platter. Potato salad and steamed shrimp siu mai dumplings are perennial favourites, as is the finisher of takikomi-gohan (rice dish with soy sauce and boiled with various ingredients). Every dish bursts with playful creativity.

Name: Daise by Tony Parkin
Address: 11 Rose Mount, Oxton, CH43 5SG, United Kingdom
Description: Named after Chef Tony Parkin’s daughter, this small and intimate restaurant sees him working as something of a one-man band in the kitchen, along with serving some of the dishes himself. His well-crafted tasting menu provides a showcase for Parkin’s skill and experience, boasting modern dishes infused with creativity and a variety of Asian influences. Thai-inspired hot and sour broth with squid is a prime example of his talents, while yuzu, white chocolate and Gariguette strawberries prove a winning combination for dessert.

Name: Dakar NOLA
Address: 937 Leonidas St., New Orleans, LA, 70118, USA
Description: With roots in Harlem and Senegal, Chef Serigne Mbaye cooks from the heart and draws on flavors from across West Africa. Once a pop-up supper club, the restaurant has found a home by the river levee in historic Uptown. A tasting menu tells the full story of this restaurant, and past highlights have included a spiced soup of okra, fish broth, and crab as well as Gulf fish with jollof rice, sauteed sweet potato greens, and a peppy tamarind broth. Local pottery and a host of farms supply the restaurant. Meanwhile, co-owner Dr. Afua Richardson is a steady presence and brings sincere warmth to the young service team.

Name: Dalchini
Address: Diplomatic Street, West Bay, Doha, Qatar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: With a palette of purple, cyan blue and orange, there’s a bright and colourful feeling to this restaurant situated within the Centara West Bay Hotel. The name is Hindi for cinnamon and the cooking is described as ‘Progressive Indian’, with all regions represented on the menu. Dishes are confidently made and neatly presented, with the chefs delivering an original touch and a well-judged balance of vibrant and subtle spicing.

Name: Dalida
Address: 101 Montgomery St., Ste. 100, San Francisco, CA, 94129, USA
Description: The lush seclusion of the Presidio seems at first an unlikely locale for a restaurant hotspot, but once the charisma and talent of married couple and co-chefs Laura and Sayat Ozyilmaz are factored in, the popularity here is a foregone conclusion. The menu is broadly Eastern Mediterranean, drawing inspiration from the melting pot of Istanbul, with a bounty of dishes—from flaky, cheesy borek to juicy short rib kebabs with sweetbreads—that are well-suited to sharing with a group.Whatever else you opt for, consider it all but mandatory to start your meal with “breaking bread,” an assortment of spreads, olives, and pickles, served with superlatively pillowy, toasty pita that is rolled and hearth-baked to order—you’re unlikely to find better in the Bay Area.

Name: Dallmayr Bar & Grill
Description: Located next to the delicatessen on the ground floor, this Dallmayr restaurant is steeped in tradition and offers a lively and relaxed, yet stylish dining experience. At closely spaced tables, diners enjoy prompt and adept service provided by a courteous and well-staffed front-of-house team in white uniforms. From oysters and caviar to seafood and Bavarian ribeye with balsamic pearl-glazed onions, the international menu certainly whets the appetite. Be sure to sample the beef tomato with feta, honey and sesame. The bar is another highlight, perfect for unwinding with a pre-dinner drink.

Name: Dallo Zio
Description: Just a short stroll from the Arch of Augustus, Dallo Zio is a restaurant that manages to be appealing without becoming luxurious, with a convivial and pleasantly informal atmosphere. The cuisine follows the same spirit: traditional recipes, generally not overly elaborate and largely seafood-based, with cooking methods that respect the catch, whether grilled over embers or baked, alongside the ever-tempting fried specialities.

Name: Dalmar
Address: Faro de punta mala, 2, San Roque, 11310, Spain
Description: Found inside the luxurious Fairmont La Hacienda Costa del Sol hotel, which like this restaurant exudes glamour and enjoys marvellous views of the Mediterranean. The proposal, supervised by award-winning chef Benito Gómez (Bardal, with two MICHELIN stars), is that of a market cuisine with touches of creativity, always based on truly select products. They only offer à la carte service (of what we have tried, we have loved the Espardeñas and their spectacular Coquelet, confit and roasted in a fricassee of mushrooms and summer truffle).

Name: Dama
Address: Via Mulino 2, località San Gaudenzio, Cervesina, 27050, Italy
Description: Situated just a few kilometres from Voghera in the Bassa Lomellina area, this gourmet restaurant run by a young chef occupies the old stables of the Castello di San Gaudenzio. Alongside local specialities such as baked onion and 24-month-old Grana Padano cheese, the menu also features more creative dishes based around authentic recipes. The wine list includes some particularly interesting labels from the Oltrepò region.

Name: Dama
Address: 612 E. 11th St., Los Angeles, CA, 90015, USA
Description: Folks flock to this breezy, Latin-inspired spot in downtown Los Angeles. Dama's feisty flavors play well off its chic old Havana-style dining room, with plush leather sofas, massive wicker fans spinning overhead and colorful tile underfoot. The front patio is filled with plenty of greenery, while the glam central bar busily blends tropical cocktails to order. As for the menu, there’s plenty to choose from. Think kanpachi aguachile with red pearl onions; shrimp tostadas with pickled chilies, and lamb chops with olive salsa verde. Paella, pork and grilled ribeyes are best for sharing.

Name: Dama Restaurant
Description: The cuisine served at this restaurant comes from a deep knowledge of the region, is inspired by tradition and yet constantly evolving. At Dama , guests will find creative cuisine with an equal balance of meat and fish dishes. Housed within Ca’ Bonfadini, the restaurant boasts an outstanding location overlooking Cannaregio canal, while the attractive dining room has just three elegant wooden tables that encourage sharing and can accommodate up to 10 guests.

Name: Damas
Address: 1209 avenue Van Horne, Outremont, Montréal, H2V 1K4, Canada
Description: This place exudes an infectious joie de vivre. Whether you're new to Syrian or pan-Ottoman cuisine or a connoisseur, the experienced and welcoming team will lay out a memorable feast for you.
