Regional cuisine skilfully reinterpreted with a modern twist takes pride of place on the menu, where the focus is on flavour and seasonal ingredients rather than a vast selection of dishes. House specialities include options such as boned caramelised rabbit served with its own jus (inspired by the better-known traditional Marche dish), while daily visits to the market usually result in one or two fish-based recipes.

Name: Del Fagioli
Description: A historic city landmark, this rustic and sincere trattoria welcomes guests with a simple, warm atmosphere, where the open kitchen at the entrance serves as an immediate calling card. The distinctly familial ambiance makes it beloved by many, so much so that reservations well in advance are required. The table sees straightforward, fragrant recipes: excellent Florentine steaks, pici with aglione sauce, pappa al pomodoro, twice-cooked beef with sautéed green beans, and to finish, house-made cantucci. A stop that celebrates the most authentic Tuscan tradition with genuine spirit.

Name: Del Mar
Address: 791 Wharf St. SW, Washington, DC, 20024, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Fabio Trabocchi celebrates the flavors of Spain in this stylish, resort-chic restaurant at the Wharf. With coastal blues and whites, polished brass fixtures and large windows overlooking the Potomac, the yawning space has room for everybody. The cooking, meanwhile, delivers in spades, bringing finesse and refinement to classics like Andalucian garlic shrimp studded with croutons, and Spanish tortilla lined with caramelized onions. Barely touched or simply prepared, beautifully presented fish are a highlight, alongside seasonal soups and hearty paellas. The beverage program is equally impressive, featuring an extensive vermouth selection as well as a superb wine list highlighting gems and superstars from across Spain.

Name: Delahunt
Address: 39 Camden Street Lower, Dublin City, D02 K277, Ireland
Description: Delahunt must surely be one of the most charming and characterful restaurants in Dublin. Exuding a sense of history throughout its quirky interiors, this old Victorian grocer's shop is mentioned in James Joyce’s ‘Ulysses’, and what was once the clerk’s snug is now a glass-enclosed private dining room. The cooking itself is a showcase for Irish produce, such as fine lamb from The Comeragh Mountains served with a punchy black olive ketchup. Either before or after dinner, 'The Sitting Room' makes a great place for a drink.

Name: Delara
Description: Chef Bardia Ilbeiggi helms this restaurant where natural lights pours in, bursts of blue calm and lattice screens and paintings by local Iranian artists mesmerize. Complex and elegant, Delara's dishes deliver the essence of fresh, flavorful Persian cooking — tartness from dried limes, yogurt and berries; freshness from herbs; richness from nuts and seeds; and aromas from spices. Served in a deep bowl, hearty aush bobs with barley and legumes. Served with bread, it could be a meal alone, but don't stop there. Beef short rib with tangy gheymeh fills the room with a heady scent. Finally, turmeric and orange cake is a burst of sunshine with strong citrus notes.

Name: Delaunay
Address: 55 Aldwych, Covent Garden, London, WC2B 4BB, United Kingdom
Description: Inspired by the grand cafés of Europe, this is the epitome of an all-day, every day restaurant. The menus take you from all manner of eggs at breakfast to top-quality schnitzels and sausages at dinner, via the timeless joy of afternoon tea. In looks, the panelled walls, green leather banquettes and marble floors give it a classically sophisticated yet buzzy feel. Fans of the nearby West End will be in dreamland here too, thanks to a well-priced pre-theatre menu and occasional 'The Delaunay Presents' dinners featuring interviews with beloved stars of stage and screen.

Name: Delbar
Address: 870 Inman Village Pkwy. NE, Ste. 1, Atlanta, GA, 30307, USA
Description: This Middle Eastern spot from Fares Kargar is all about bringing people together over flavorful and authentic food. There is a generous spirit here, where the name translates to "heart, captured." The menu, a nod to the dishes Kargar grew up with, is designed for sharing, with spreads and small bites to start, an entire section dedicated to tahdig, that festive Persian crispy rice dish, and meats. Add the dill labneh to the house bread opener, then go for the lamb neck that is falling-off-the-bone tender, and sabzi polo, a basmati rice dish flavored with scallions and herbs and topped with crispy onions. Conclude the evening with a decadent treat like baklava ice cream or pistachio lava cake with cardamom ice cream.

Name: Deli
Description: A love of cooking with its roots in tradition is behind the values of this restaurant with its impressive array of rice dishes, soups, stews, and specialities such as Segovia-style roast suckling pig. Now run by the third generation of the family, Deli always works with local producers to source its ingredients, focusing on the traditional cooking of inland Andalucia, with some recipes on the menu harking back to the region’s long period of Moorish rule. Specialities here include partridge mousse with an Oloroso sherry gelée, wild seasonal mushrooms, roast shoulder of suckling lamb and the always delicious creamy rice with partridge.

Name: Deli Boutique・Uncle De Abalone
Address: 909 Xingye Avenue, Nancun Town, Panyu, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: It's a bit out of the way, but the tasty abalone makes the trip here worthwhile. The founder's love affair with the gastropod spans 30+ years. Each one is painstakingly prepared then slow-cooked for 156 hours, resulting in concentrated seafood umami and abalone that, while tender, retains a lovely chewiness. His flavourful abalone sauce goes perfectly with steamed rice. Cantonese stir-fries, such as sautéed winged bean with minced pork, also stand out.

Name: Delia
Address: 306 Santiphap Road, Pom Prap, Pom Prap Sattru Phai, Bangkok, 10100, Thailand
Description: Delia, a fresh addition to Bangkok's food scene, gives authentic Mexican flavours a contemporary twist. Greeted with a cheerful "Hola!", diners experience traditional techniques fused with quality Thai ingredients. Handmade tortillas, house‐fermented elements and bold, flame‐cooked dishes such as tostada with roasted cauliflower cream and taco de pastor – celebrate both heritage and innovation. Their unique spin on tamal de piña y umeshu rounds off the meal perfectly.

Name: Delibong
Address: 3F, 4 Millak-ro 27 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 47560, South Korea
Description: Devotedly crafted charcuterie is the soul of Delibong. The chef incorporates it into flavourful, visually striking dishes as main elements or garnishes, and highlights the character of each ingredient by skilful pairing techniques. Guests seated at the counter can watch the open kitchen at work, as charcuterie in the ageing cabinet patiently awaits its moment at the table. Set in calm neighborhood, the bright, white‑toned dining space adds to the restaurant’s serene atmosphere.

Name: Delicato
Description: Situated in a picturesque medieval hilltop village in the province of Rieti on the border with Umbria, this restaurant serves cuisine that is influenced by different regions and traditions. Choose between the minimalist-style dining rooms with exposed stone walls and, in fine weather, a charming outdoor space at the foot of Contigliano’s church. Here, chef Carlotta Delicato brings out the best of local ingredients in dishes that are kept deliberately simple and unfussy yet are full of flavour. We highly recommend the “spaghettone mare e lago” with a light brunoise of courgettes. As the restaurant is situated in Lazio, guests can enjoy good local wines made by small-scale producers, such as the Cabernet Sauvignon Masseria Baroni, which is of medium intensity with broad and pronounced aromas. .

Name: Deliciosamarta
Address: Escritor Benito Pérez Galdós 33, Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, 35002, Spain
Location: Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Spain
Description: A restaurant with plenty of personality and an appealing decor along an attractive pedestrian street in the city’s Triana district. Its cuisine is equally impressive, featuring market-inspired cooking with a modern touch and influences from the Canary Islands that is only available à la carte. We recommend booking ahead.

Name: Delicja
Description: Dine in the shade of one of the oldest trees in the Wielkopolska region in the small enclosed garden of this romantic restaurant. The elegant dining room is filled with antiques and polished silver, bringing a fittingly old-fashioned feel to proceedings in a long-standing restaurant that has been run by the same family for decades. The formal and personable service is a good match for the surroundings, as is the roster of classic yet ambitious dishes.

Name: Delightful House
Address: 153 Hanxi Avenue Middle, Panyu, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant annexed to a B&B on the outskirts of Guangzhou feels like an oasis. Bamboo bushes cocoon the terrace dotted with patio tables shaded by parasols. Well-crafted dim sum are served at breakfast and lunch, and Cantonese classics at lunch and dinner time. The deep-fried pork medallions stuffed with crab and shrimp have a crispy texture and plenty of umami. River fish such as the topmouth culter from Lake Wanlu is another must-try.

Name: Deliri
Description: In this urban-industrial-style restaurant, chef David Morera’s contemporary Catalan cuisine is fun and full of personality, including an impressive choice of suggestions as well as game dishes in season (wild boar wrapped in cabbage leaves, hare royale, etc.). Everything is supported by a 10-course tasting menu, called Deliri. Be sure to try the delicious stuffed paccheri pasta (macarras de l’àvia)!

Name: Dell'arte
Description: Robbert Dellaert has transformed his childhood home, dating from 1878, into a restaurant with a romantic feel. This is an intimate space with a beautiful garden. Thanks to Julie's excellent service, you can just relax and delight in the love that the chef expresses for his terroir – Zeelandic Flanders. He treats local produce with reverence, and his well-thought-out combinations create a sense of depth. For instance, he enhances ultra-fresh soused herring with avocado ice cream, yuzu gel and sweet and sour daikon. A unique culinary adventure!

Name: Delphine Ronsyn
Description: Chef Delphine Ronsyn designed this spacious restaurant, less than a kilometre from her family farm, and whose picture windows and terrace command fantastic views of the surrounding fields and meadows. Naturally enough, Delphine is a champion of local produce and her region, courtesy of unfussy bistro fare that is deceptively simple and straightforward. She may serve lobster glazed in aromatic tomatoes, flanked by mozzarella cream, tender artichoke and rocket leaf salad. The chef frequently pops out to ask diners for their thoughts about her cuisine. A word of advice: bookings are highly advised as this establishment is almost always packed to bursting.

Name: Delys
Description: Delys is a haven of design depicted by a chic black colour scheme. Intimacy and mystery set the stage, while floor-to-ceiling windows seem to invite the countryside indoors. Be it for a quick lunch or a more leisurely dinner, chef Doucet’s modern approach always hits the spot. He avows a weakness for crisp, legible, contrasting flavours. For example, he may add an exuberant edge to lightly poached Atlantic cod courtesy of lemon zest and a subtly smoky mushroom stock. Doucet leaves his heroic, distinctive stamp on each dish thanks to sensitive nuances.

Name: Demera
Description: Demera has long been a favorite in Uptown for its warm hospitality and authentic Ethiopian cooking. The bright, inviting dining room encourages communal meals, where platters arrive on top of tangy, house-made injera that doubles as both plate and utensil. The extensive menu offers everything from richly spiced stews and grilled meats to an array of thoughtfully prepared vegetarian dishes, making it equally appealing to newcomers and regulars alike. Fresh ingredients, vibrant seasoning and generous portions define the cooking, and the traditional family-style service encourages sharing and sampling across the table.

Name: Demo
Address: Plaza de Hernández Amores 4, Murcia, 30001, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Located at the foot of the tower of the cathedral, Demo’s contemporary ambience comes as a pleasant surprise in this historic quarter of the city, thanks to its white decor and glass ceiling with wood beams that resemble the branches of a tree. Chef Pepe Morales’ cuisine is very much inspired by market availability and the traditional flavours of Murcia, as evidenced by dishes such as the hake salad, the torrezno (fried pork belly) with a sweet potato parmentier, Demo’s artichoke, and cod pilpil. The chef is also more than happy to provide advice on the best wine pairings for you.

Name: Demon Duck by Alvin Leung
Address: Banyan Tree Dubai, Bluewaters Island, Dubai
Description: The eponymous celebrity chef brings his fun, bold style of cooking to Banyan Tree Hotel, where service is sweet and attentive, and the generous dishes are ideal for sharing. The fun, extensive menu offers Chinese classics with an original twist. We suggest starting with their salt and pepper tofu, then try out their lobster with green onions and ginger and finish off with a chocolate matcha fondant with brown rice ice cream.

Name: Den Duyventooren
Description: The spruce, traditional façade of this ancestral castle-farmstead hides a vibrant modern interior adorned in warm colours. The peaceful terrace feels light years away from Bellem. The establishment has acquired a faithful cohort of regulars, lured back by Inge Herteleer’s enticing set and à la carte menus. Her seasonal cooking throbs with generosity and is dotted with contemporary touches to which she adds a Mediterranean twist come summertime. The shrimp fritters are stuffed to the brim, while a suave cognac sauce enhances pheasant and green peas and mint contrast with fresh prawns. Searingly good food prepared on the spot! Don’t forget to book!

Name: Den Silveren Harynck
Description: Mother Els welcomes guests into the stylishly elegant Van Landeghem family establishment. Floor to ceiling windows lead into the garden which is flanked by a patio. Son, Sam, can be found rustling up tasty, flavourful delicacies in the kitchen, combining classical training and creative touches, ranging from Rossini tournedos steak to a bouillabaisse jazzed up with subtle, Asian notes.

Name: Deo Gracias
Address: 12 11th Jamboree Street, Diliman, Quezon - Metro Manila, 1103, The Philippines
Description: Tucked away on a quiet street in the heart of Quezon, this Spanish restaurant has a green-tiled shopfront selling Spanish specialities and a few tables for casual dining. In a tasteful interior blending wood, patterned tiles and soft lighting for a relaxed yet polished feel, highlights include the ensaladilla de prawns and croquetas de jamón ibérico, best enjoyed with a glass of Spanish wine. The shaded terrace makes for an inviting spot in fair weather.

Name: DepTH brianza
Address: 2F, Azabudai Hills Residence A, 1-2-3 Azabudai, Minato-ku, Tokyo, 106-0041, Japan
Description: DepTH brianza explores concepts that broaden the possibilities of Italian cuisine. Chef Okuno’s latest culinary adventure is a taste test that takes Italian cuisine a little outside its comfort zone. While firmly grounded in tradition, Okuno enjoys reframing Japanese ingredients in creative ways. ‘DepTH’ is a play on his name: ‘okuyuki’ is ‘depth’ in Japanese. Like a wizard reworking ancient spells, Okuno dreams up imaginative cuisine you won’t find anywhere else.

Name: Der Dantler
Description: A tip to start with: reserve well in advance! Given the great value for money and the relaxed atmosphere, it's no surprise that they tend to get booked up. They call themselves the "Bavarian Deli". In the interior done out in a slick Alpine/country-style style, the service is personable and relaxed. At lunchtime you can order pasta, a pastrami sandwich, ramen or the fish dish of the day à la carte, or the three-course "business lunch". In the evening, creative modern cuisine is served in the form of a set menu – a vegetarian or pescetarian version is also available (request this when you book). There is also a wine bar next door.

Name: Der Engel
Description: The perfect example of a traditional Baden inn! This family-run establishment has been welcoming guests since 1764, offering a consistently enjoyable experience. Behind its old half-timbered walls, there are charming dining areas – some more traditional, others more modern. In a warm and welcoming atmosphere, diners tuck into delicious regional fare. Options include classic dishes, daily specials and set menus. Tip: There is a fantastic selection of digestifs. Overnight accommodation available.

Name: Der Kaiserhof
Description: Run by the same family for four generations, Kaiserhof has a surprisingly chic and fresh interior behind its deceptively traditional façade. The tastefully designed dining space is accessed via the open kitchen – diners can also watch the chefs at work. The concept here is a seasonally orientated "Culinary Journey" in six courses – for which you should allow plenty of time. Vegetarian dishes such as aubergine with pointed cabbage and Parmesan are just as enticing as the duck with Savoy cabbage and blackcurrant. Friendly and attentive front-of-house team. The chefs are involved in serving and talk you through the dishes. In summer, head for the terrace in the small courtyard. There are well-kept guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Der Luis
Description: Luis Thaller represents the sixth generation of his family to run this establishment, which has been going since 1875. Made primarily from locally sourced ingredients, the dishes served here are sophisticated and packed with flavour. These are presented in the form of an ambitious surprise menu comprising four to seven courses. The chef's signature dish is the farm-fresh egg with celeriac, greaves and pig's head. To complement your meal, there is a good selection of wines and non-alcoholic beverages. The restaurant is housed in Der Thaller hotel along with Wirtshaus, a more down-to-earth alternative.

Name: Der Löwe
Description: For years, the Sauters' well-kept establishment has been lauded for its delicious cuisine. Game from the region is one popular choice here, but their dishes with an international spin have also garnered favour with customers. Friendly, attentive service; tasteful setting. Tip: On Wednesday evenings, they serve a four-course surprise menu at an affordable price.

Name: Der Philosoph
Description: This welcoming restaurant established by a pair of chefs is set in the charming district of Neuenheim. Attractive decorative features such as large-format black-and-white photographs, bold red accents and the open-view kitchen all help to create an inviting atmosphere, complemented by exceptionally courteous service. There is a choice of three set menus, one of which is vegetarian, with the possibility to order dishes individually à la carte. The Chateaubriand set menu for two needs to be pre-ordered – the main course is presented with the classic béarnaise sauce and potato gratin. The restaurant takes its name from its location at the foot of the Philosophenweg, a well-known and much-loved walking path overlooking the Old Town and the castle across the Neckar River.

Name: Der Schrenk
Description: A long-established inn with a wonderful terrace set out in the courtyard and an interior reminiscent of a charming old-style tavern. The kitchen remains true to tradition, albeit it with a contemporary twist, resulting in fresh, carefully prepared and attractively presented dishes such as "paprika chicken, spaetzle, sour cream", "Schrenk pork cordon bleu, salami, Arzberg Stollenkäse (cheese)" or "house-made gnocchi, courgette, ricotta". The daily specials, which staff talk you through at your table, are also of interest. Select ingredients from the region are the stars of the show.

Name: Der Schützenwirt
Address: Schützenweg 3, Sankt Jakob am Thurn, 5412, Austria
Description: In 2020, following stints at top-flight establishments, Andrea and Robert Rübsam fulfilled their dream of opening their own restaurant, which is located in a picturesque and tranquil spot some 20min south of Salzburg. Their culinary approach is grounded in seasonality and local sourcing, with 25 regional producers supplying fresh top-notch ingredients. The dishes reflect Austrian tradition, elevated with imaginative twists and influences from around the globe. The menu is written up on a board, featuring options such as "Gazpacho andaluz, bell pepper, jalapeño, croutons", "Pickled trout, cucumber, sour cream, rapeseed" or "Braised beef roulade, mashed potato, kohlrabi". The outdoor garden is a particular source of pride – arguably one of the loveliest in the Salzburg area. Warm, attentive and professional service, led by the proprietress, is the icing on the cake.

Name: Der Unterwirt
Description: Occupying a private house, this restaurant boasts a couple of charming Stube-style dining rooms, one of which is highly romantic and dates back to the 13C – although the vintage wood looks as though it may have come from elsewhere, it has in fact been here for centuries. Owner-chef Thomas Haselwanter creates carefully thought-out dishes which combine precision and classic comfort with the occasional modern touch, harmoniously combining the flavours of the Alto Adige with Mediterranean influences, with a particular focus on fish. A welcoming outdoor terrace for summer dining and seven modern guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: Der Unterwirt
Description: This inn dates back to 1490. In cosy, charmingly decorated dining rooms with touches of elegance, or out on the wonderful garden terrace, diners are invited to savour creatively inspired cuisine with regional foundations. Dishes such as "clear mushroom consommé, chive oil, game ravioli", or "red catfish, cucumber, rhubarb" are accompanied by a fine selection of wines with a focus on Austrian winemakers. The guestrooms are a real home away from home.

Name: Deraliye
Address: Divanyolu Caddesi, Alemdar Mahallesi, Ticarethane Sokak No:10, Sultan Ahmet, Fatih, Istanbul, 34110, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Deraliye is a landmark of the historical Sultanahmet neighbourhood, where there is one tourist restaurant next to the other. The colourful, opulent decor immediately catches the eye and, like the cuisine, is a tribute to the Ottoman Empire. The extensive menu features an array of dishes devised for sharing and specialities such as mezze, barbecued offerings and kebabs. Tempting options include duck stew in filo pastry with fragrant spiced rice, or a lamb and tomato dish, slowly simmered in an earthenware pot to let the flavours meld. Here, you can savour sumptuous Ottoman cuisine, occasionally presented with a touch of showmanship. Good to know: Deraliye also organises cookery classes.

Name: Derby Grill
Description: Facing the Villa Reale, the dining room envelops guests in classic elegance with British undertones, reflecting the Hotel de la Ville that houses it, while select tables overlook a luminous, refined veranda. From the kitchen emerge two tasting journeys: Viaggio alle origini, which tells the story of the chef’s native Campania through Mediterranean aromas, and Il territorio… secondo me, where Lombard tradition meets creative touches. Dishes, which may be selected freely, showcase seasonal ingredients and fresh vegetables harvested from the restaurant’s own organic garden.

Name: Dereszla Bisztró
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: There are few places more relaxing to dine than on the stepped riverside terrace of this modern wood and glass building located in the heart of wine country. Szabó and his front-of-house team warmly welcome you in, while his brother Bém works behind the scenes in the kitchen preparing a concise menu of modern Hungarian dishes. Good quality produce comes from their carefully selected suppliers, whether that’s local Mangalitsa or trout from Lillafüred, which could arrive served ‘kárpáti’ style with a creamy fish bone sauce. Considering the location, a Tokaj wine is the natural accompaniment.

Name: Dergi Praha
Description: If you want to experience authentic Georgian cuisine, this restaurant in a commercial building just a few metres from the Vltava River is the place for you. Be sure to sample the classic khinkali, available with various fillings – they are second to none! The barbecued dishes, which are also packed with flavour, come accompanied by typical sauces. The setting is wonderfully spacious and cheerful: it features decorative elements such as traditional colourful pendant lamps and patterned fabrics. Live Georgian music adds to the atmosphere.

Name: Derrière
Address: 17 rue de la Chèvre, Metz, 57000, France
Description: In this dinky restaurant with the kitchen at the ‘front’ and the dining area in the ‘rear’ of the dining area, the chef whips up familiar dishes, blessedly free of fads and with the greatest respect for the ingredient. A few examples: juicy Black Angus steak and calf’s sweetbread with morels. Relaxed casual vibe.

Name: Des Balances
Description: This place boasts an enviable location in the old town and, in summer, the terrace overlooking the River Reuss beckons – the views are stunning! You will find a chic setting in both the restaurant and the Bar & Lounge. On the menu: specialities from the barbecue as well as French and Mediterranean dishes, all made with top-quality regional and seasonal ingredients. The restaurant is located in the gorgeous Hotel Des Balances, so why not stay the night?

Name: Des Petits Pois Sont Rouges
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: No need to be a guest at the Miramont Hotel to enjoy the chef's cuisine. He of course pays homage to Pyrenean culinary heritage but doesn't hesitate to make a few welcome innovations.

Name: Des Terres
Description: A buzzy casual vibe depicts this neighbourhood bistro in the 20th arrondissement of Paris. In the company of natural wines displayed on a bookshelf, you will joyfully do justice to the chef’s competently crafted fare: cauliflower in a herring, hazelnut and green oil sauce; roast beetroot, Colonnata pork and creamy goat’s cheese. Seasonal nosh and a bargain-priced lunch menu.

Name: Desborre
Description: Offering dishes such as soufflé crackling, chicken in citrus escabeche, and “green chromatic in different textures”, this restaurant in the Austrias district very close to the royal palace is the fiefdom of Rioja-born chef Lucía Grávalos. Here, she showcases her permanent commitment to the land, organic ingredients, free-grazing livestock and sustainable fishing... as well as her rekindling of memories of her grandmother Ana Mari’s recipes and her passion for vegetables, which are always sourced and prepared in strict alignment with her culinary focus. The rustic-contemporary ambience is that of a stylish bistro, with a surprising display counter of fermented products (kombuchas, kefirs, shrubs etc) by the entrance. The contemporary-inspired à la carte is complemented by two interesting tasting menus (Petit and Desborre).

Name: Deschevaliers
Description: Under the guidance of multi-starred chef Nino Di Costanzo, a fine dining destination takes shape along one of Italy’s most celebrated gourmet streets, set within the elegant spaces of an international hotel showcasing its most exclusive brand. The atmosphere exudes refined contemporary flair: soft lighting, minimalist décor, and works by local artists that engage with the space. At the table, Neapolitan identity is expressed through dishes bearing dialect names, dressed in a modern aesthetic: creations that evoke tradition yet come alive with contemporary details, in a harmony of colors and textures. The service, attentive and professional, discreetly guides an experience that bridges heritage and innovation, weaving together authentic flavors and signature inspirations.

Name: Desert Rose Café
Address: Ground Floor, National Museum of Qatar, Museum Park Street, Doha, Qatar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,No alcohol served,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Beaming smiles greet you from behind the counter at this easy-going and friendly spot tucked away in the National Museum of Qatar. When it comes to ordering, start off with their arancini or ‘Dynamite shrimps’ then go traditional with keema, khabees and Chef Noof’s madrouba that’s made using a special recipe – and no visit here will be complete without the date cake. A great strawberry mojito or a cup from their vast array of speciality coffees will set you up nicely for your museum visit.

Name: Dessance
Description: In a former private mansion in the Marais, this elegant restaurant calls to mind a winter garden with its high ceilings – a delightful space that oozes charm and style. The chef produces inspired seasonal cuisine, served in the form of two carte blanche menus, one devoted to surf and turf flavours, the other vegetarian. The wine list includes a selection of natural and biodynamic wines.

Name: Dessirier
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: A historical establishment founded in 1883 and run by the Rostang family since 1996, Le Dessirier is an elegant contemporary brasserie specialising in fish and seafood. Chef Olivier Fontaine cooks up precise and flavoursome cuisine, in which tradition meets modernity: minced scallops and truffles, bouillabaisse, cod aioli, or squid with Coco de Paimpol beans and seasonal mushrooms. Oysters and shellfish are the final flourish on the menu. For dessert, the chocolate soufflé is an ode to tradition. A buzzing, upscale venue firmly rooted in Paris.

Name: Deste
Description: Set back slightly from the port, this restaurant boasts stunning views from its terrace which is highly recommended in fine weather. The culinary focus here is on modern dishes with an interesting choice of meat and fish options. Tea and kombucha offer an alternative to wine, while the home-produced gin is definitely worth sampling.

Name: Destroyer
Address: 3578 Hayden Ave., Culver City, CA, 90232, USA
Description: The architecturally intriguing Hayden Tract district is the perfect backdrop for Jordan Kahn's adventurous Destroyer, located just across the street from sister restaurant, Vespertine. The minimalist interior keeps your attention on the food, where each plate is a complex composition of flavors that are bound to delight and surprise. Begin with such harmonious starters as avocado confit, a half avocado dusted with their onion ash and served with confit tomatoes and dressed arugula that is simple but impressive. Koshikari rice porridge delivers depth and a riot of textures, while the milk chocolate crémeux finished with almond streusel, praline and a dusting of frozen cucumber cream is a striking closer.

Name: Det Røde Pakhus
Description: Two experienced owners bring their knowledge together at this modern, wood-furnished restaurant set in the centre of Bornholm’s capital. The chef is passionate about good produce and skilfully prepares local ingredients to create refined, imaginative dishes that can be taken in an à la carte format or as part of a 12-course tasting menu. Desserts are a highlight.

Name: Detapaencepa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: This eatery is two businesses in one: a busy tapas bar, plus the restaurant itself. In both spaces, guests can order from the same updated traditional menu of tapas, raciones and a choice of more elaborate dishes such as the pigs’ trotters with a Carabinero prawn tartare, and the delicious wild boar stew with wild mushrooms and “Gnocchi Sarda” pasta. The à la carte is complemented by an “executive” menu (lunch from Monday to Friday), an impressive “menú de la casa”, plus several daily suggestions.

Name: Deux Bistrot de chefs
Address: 58 rue de la Fontaine-au-Roi, Paris, 75011, France
Description: Tiphaine Mollard, from Savoie, and Romain Casas, from Béarn, have teamed up, pooling their contagious good humour and respective terroirs in this bright, inviting space: an open kitchen, shelves packed with bottles, trinkets, photos and plants. Tarte Tatin with miso-glazed onions, Reblochon sauce and tarragon emulsion; vanilla Basque cheesecake with pomelo coulis and blood orange sorbet: the food is joyful and indulgent, down-to-earth and unpretentious. Reasonable prices.

Name: Dhabkwan
Address: Dhabkwan Resort, 178-184 Nonthaburi Road, Suan Yai, Mueang Nonthaburi, Nonthaburi, 11000, Thailand
Description: Located in a teak house in the middle of Dhabkwan Resort, this traditional Thai restaurant opens onto a tranquil lotus pond and inviting gardens. The atmosphere perfectly matches the authentic Thai menu, which includes hard-to-find dishes like Miang Kam with lotus petals and santol curry with roasted pork. Making it even more authentic, meals are served on Benjarong porcelain. Dhabkwan also offers Thai cookery classes and is available for events.

Name: Di Martino Sea Front Pasta Bar
Description: Situated opposite the Maschio Angioino (Castel Nuovo) in Naples, this restaurant was opened by a pasta producer from nearby Gragnano, making it the perfect choice for pasta-lovers. Sitting at a sushi bar-style counter, you can watch the chefs at work and choose from a menu that is dedicated entirely to pasta dishes (as well as desserts of course): 126 varieties, unusual combinations and almost endless possibilities, without, however, neglecting tradition and the great classics. When ordered à la carte, the dishes are generously portioned; however, for a more complete overview, opt for the tasting menu which includes more courses but in smaller quantities.

Name: Di Vino Rosso
Address: 807 Gervais St., Ste. 100, Columbia, SC, 29201, USA
Description: Exposed brick walls and tile floors hint at the building's former incarnation as a Ford dealership but this address has been home to Di Vino Rosso for more than two decades. This longstanding Italian restaurant is a Columbia favorite, known for its focused menu of Italian staples made with local ingredients (they even list their farmers on the back of the menu). Tuck into a bowl of meatballs resting in tomato sauce before a plate of pappardelle with a rich and flavorful wild boat and Italian sausage Bolognese sauce. While the savory dishes are certainly the highlight, end the meal with an espresso and tiramisu for a classic finish. ---

Name: Di Yi Ding
Address: 1, Lane 161, Section 2, Dongmen Road, East District, Tainan, Taiwan
Description: In this 1960s mansion that has been restored to its former glory, the chef serves omakase menus that are priced according to the ingredients, typically starting with sashimi and ending with a starch dish. Portions and ingredients can be tailored to preferences. For first-timers, crab or lobster is the natural choice of main. Seafood is sourced with particular care, drawing on fresh catches from partner fishing boats across Taiwan and select imports from Japan. The wine list stars mainly French vintages, but you are welcome to BYOB.

Name: Dialogues
Description: Two distinct spaces lie behind the cream-coloured façade: the fine dining restaurant upstairs and the cave à manger in the basement. The contemporary elegance of the decor is appealing, with custom-made solid wood tables, emerald-green banquettes, armchairs re-upholstered with vintage fabrics, a backlit white marble counter and a superb mural with natural-pigment swirls. At the helm, Adrien Zedda and Thomas Bouanich devise 100% vegetarian or veggie-seafood set menus – plants are always at the fore. Their signature dish is a puff pastry half-moon filled with celeriac roasted for 12hr, mushroom duxelles and caramelised onions, paired with a lovage and celeriac jus whipped with butter and a deep, robust meurette-style red wine and mushroom sauce – vegetarian, of course.

Name: Diam's
Description: This establishment is located inside the DiamAndes winery, where they say that ‘nothing exceptional can be achieved without an exceptional terroir.’ After this statement, which takes on new meaning when you see its splendid facilities, the commitment to the environment and the Mendoza region is even more understandable. In this regard, and among many other details, it is interesting to know that they are members of the famous Clos de los Siete and have a gravity winemaking system. The most striking feature of the restaurant, located on the first floor and with spectacular views of both the Andes Mountains and the vineyards, is chef Santiago Orozco Russo’s elaborate proposal, who has been able to create a gastronomic concept that mixes meaning, flavour and flashes of creativity. You will find a small à la carte (designed for a more informal meal) and two carefully selected tasting menus: Petit Grand Cru and Grand Cru, both of which include a visit to the winery.

Name: Diana's Place
Description: Facing the square in front of Termini station, this wine bar-cum-restaurant is striking for its fresh and creative approach to cuisine. Nearly all the top-quality ingredients are local and can be purchased from the food counter. The excellent staff are happy to help with your choice of wine, which is also available by the glass.

Name: Diavola
Description: Its home in downtown Geyserville has a Wild West appeal, and the interior, styled with vintage film posters and antique tools, has a playful yet smart vibe. Diavola is certainly one of the most popular spots for miles—within minutes of opening, it's always a full house.The crowds are here for pizzas, like the signature combo of spicy meatballs, red peppers, provolone, pine nuts and raisins or the smoked pork belly, goat cheese and scallion, perhaps. Top-notch house ingredients include salumi, lardo and cured olives. But, that’s not to count out their pastas, including linguine tossed with baby octopus, bone marrow, zucchini and bottarga. Finish with their chocolate pistachio semifreddo paired with a Blue Bottle espresso.

Name: Dida
Description: Housed in a century-old building set slightly back from the coastal road that runs along the Adriatic, in the warmer months the restaurant welcomes guests with a pleasant shaded outdoor area looking across to the island of Krk. The interiors are warm and welcoming, centred around an attractive dining room with a fireplace. The kitchen offers rich and colourful dishes built around numerous ingredients and inspired by local specialities, reinterpreted with contemporary taste and careful presentation. Some rooms are also available.

Name: Didier Galet
Address: rue du Grand Bru 27, Sprimont, 4140, Belgium
Description: Before you even sit down in this friendly joint done up in an inviting vein, you feel perfectly at home. Christine greets diners with a smile and chef Didier Galet waves a hi from the kitchen. Galet is a champion of his region and committed to working with local ingredients. From wood pigeon to fresh veggies, the chef sources everything locally, crafting each ingredient with infinite respect. His cooking draws on his classical training, jazzed up with expressive sauces. He is equally capable of rolling out a rich mushroom and truffle stock, a light frothy espuma of potatoes or a liberal grating of royal truffle. The alfresco terrace is perfect to sample this ode to Belgian produce and producers.

Name: Didier Méril
Description: In a cosy, contemporary interior, enjoying lunch with a magnificent view over the bay of Le Prieuré promises to be a memorable experience. As they drink in the open sea, gourmets will appreciate the creative cuisine of chef-owner Didier Méril. His top-notch seasonal produce comes mainly from the market and local fisheries (Jerusalem artichokes showcased in a variety of textures and shellfish marinière; mackerel, spaghetti squash and a fish head jus finished with butter; pear tartlet with almond crisp, Tonka bean vanilla cream and pear sorbet). Good value for money at lunchtime.

Name: Die Alte Brauerei
Description: This establishment started out in 1877 as Becker-Brauerei and the interior decor incorporates a combination of historical, rustic and modern elements. In today's iteration of the restaurant, Florian Dauphin, son of the friendly owners, Eric and Isabelle Dauphin, heads up the kitchen team. Lorena-Jil, his charming wife, manages the service with professionalism, care and attention. You will be treated to seasonally influenced French dishes – choose à la carte or go for one of the set menus: the four-course "Découverte" or six-course "Signature". During the week, they propose a reasonably priced lunch deal. The restaurant is accessed via the courtyard. The terrace is lovely. It is also possible to stay overnight in one of the six guestrooms, each individually designed by artist Margret Lafontaine.

Name: Die Alte Schule
Description: Torben Tönsing, scion of a well-known family of restaurateurs in Herford, took over this restaurant from his parents in 2017. He focuses on contemporary cuisine that draws on both regional and international influences. The 17C half-timbered building has a charming atmosphere – food is served on different levels, and in summer the secluded terrace comes into its own. Excellent wine selection – they even have their own wine shop.

Name: Die Bürgermeisterei 1728
Description: A location steeped in history in which to enjoy a meal! The lovingly restored building, which gives directly onto the market square, was once the mayor's residence and dates back to 1728. The elegant fusion of modern style and historical details lends the place atmosphere. The evening menu is ambitious, fresh and full of flavour, with appetising options such as beef bourgignon, dried fig crumble and potato-parsnip mash. The small selection of seasonal dishes is also proposed in the form of set menus, one of which is vegetarian. In summer, make the most of the secluded terrace.

Name: Die Gersberg Alm
Description: This restaurant overlooking Salzburg boasts a wonderful location and stunning views. The atmosphere in the pretty wood-panelled dining area is cosy. The cuisine is rooted in the region but also draws on international influences, with a house speciality of Zitronen-Rahm-Herz vom Milchkalb (milk-fed calf's heart in a creamy lemon sauce) featured alongside dishes such as venison yellow curry served with spiced rice. There are set menus, one of which is vegetarian, an à la carte menu and an additional afternoon snack menu – there really is something for everyone. This lovely spot, which is also a favourite among locals, is housed in the hotel of the same name.

Name: Die Halde
Description: At an elevation of 1 147m, this elegant restaurant effortlessly bridges the gap between the old and the new! In cosy traditional dining rooms, friendly and professional waitstaff serve dishes such as medium-rare topside of veal with coleslaw, pickled onions, chive cream and mustard gherkins, or pan-fried cod fillet with gremolata, asparagus, pea purée and gnocchi. The menu also features Zwiebelrostbraten (sirloin steak with crispy fried onions and gravy), schnitzel and other classics. The kitchen prioritises regional ingredients, and the water comes straight from the property's own mountain spring. The lovely guestrooms are done out in a modern, regional style.

Name: Die Klosterschänke
Description: Idyllically set a few kilometres from the city centre, this warm and welcoming family-run restaurant boasts a magnificent terrace affording splendid views of the Rhine plain. The chef cooks up regional and seasonal cuisine along with a selection of Italian dishes. The mouthwatering options include a classic cordon bleu with Black Forest ham and Alpine cheese, and saltimbocca alla romana from the chef's homeland.

Name: Die Kurfürstenstube
Description: A classic of Heidelberg's dining scene! In the restaurant of the stylish grand hotel Der Europäische Hof Heidelberg, with its individually designed guestrooms and suites, the mighty coffered ceiling and wall panelling with beautiful inlays preserve a piece of history. The cuisine is based on the classics, and only the very best ingredients are used in the ambitious dishes. Choose à la carte or go for the set menu, available in various lengths. The wine list, specialising in German, French and Italian labels, is also excellent. The highly friendly, professional and attentive service is in keeping with the style of the place. In the summer months, a slightly simpler menu is served in the "Sommerrestaurant", which has a terrace and a pleasant, airy atmosphere.

Name: Die Ratsstuben
Description: One draw of this restaurant is its beautiful location in the centre of the pretty old town on the Alb River, another is its chic, modern interior. The cuisine is based on high-quality ingredients and ranges from classics such as house-made maultaschen to international specialities such as barbecued octopus and burgers, and not forgetting the various tartare options. The waitstaff are friendly and well trained. In summer, the terrace overlooking the square is a delightful spot where you will be serenaded by the carillon music from the town hall tower.

Name: Die Reichsstadt
Description: This is the restaurant of the chic hotel of the same name, which provides the historical backdrop for your meal. The tasteful dining area is done out with high-end furnishings and a modern eye. Staff are friendly and professional as they set about serving you fine Baden classics, modernised French dishes, which you can choose à la carte or combine into a set menu – a vegetarian version is also available. The "Taste Menu" comprising six or seven small courses is also an excellent recommendation. In summer, the garden is magical!

Name: Die Scheuer
Description: Once known as the Hammelsche Scheune, this 17C barn converted into a pretty half-timbered building has bags of charm. This family business a stone's throw from the market square is run with great dedication, and attracts many regulars. In summer, there is a lovely terrace out front. The interior makes for a cosy setting in which to savour delicious food such as locally hunted game. The restaurant endeavours to source ingredients locally and knows its suppliers personally.

Name: Die Speiserei im Maier
Description: The restaurant at Hotel Maier (a family-run establishment since its founding as a café and guesthouse in 1936) serves cuisine that showcases fresh seasonal regional produce; it is also, for the most part, organic and sourced as locally as possible. Order à la carte or opt for a three- to five-course set menu. In the inviting space, the original traditional character has been preserved, but given an elegant update courtesy of discreet modern accents. There is also a spacious courtyard terrace for those who enjoy dining al fresco. Friendly and professional service.

Name: Die Traube
Description: In the centre of the village, this half-timbered house dating from 1647 is a real gem. It is home to this restaurant run by Anita and Stefan Schleier with great dedication since 2001. The cosy atmosphere and traditional decor are as compelling as the ambitious Mediterranean cuisine based on carefully selected seasonal produce. Mouthwatering dishes include salmon with wild garlic risotto and melted tomatoes or "variation of veal with peas and carrots". There is also a well-curated wine list. The terrace in front of the old barn is another lovely feature. Tip for motorists: Public car park just around the corner.

Name: Die Weinbank - Wirtshaus
Description: Gerhard Fuchs and Christian Zach opened this tavern as a counterpoint to their fine dining restaurant. Serving seasonal dishes made with regional produce, the concept has proven to be a hit. Gerhard Fuchs brings many years of culinary experience to the table, and the team led by passionate sommelier and host Christian Zach provides attentive service with Styrian charm. Flavoursome dishes such as Leutschach pata negra pork brisket with chanterelle mushrooms and gnocchi with herbs can be accompanied by wine – the list comprises over 4 000 labels – or beer. The interior design is a modern take on rustic style, and there is also a lovely vine-covered terrace. Tip: Due to the popularity of this place, reservations are recommended. Delicious food items and wines can be purchased to take home. The name "Weinbank" is apt: you can hire lockers in which to store your fine wine purchases.

Name: Die Windmühle
Description: This former grain mill makes for a truly charming setting with its distinctive character. Run by the Lemke family, this restaurant has two cosy indoor dining spaces – the Mühlenstube ("Mill Room") and the Kaminzimmer ("Fireplace Room") – plus a lovely terrace, where you can tuck into the seasonal and regional fare served up by Holger Lemke. Opt for one of two set menus ("Westfälisch Genießen-Menü" or "Unser Windmühlen-Menü") or go à la carte. The friendly and attentive front-of-house team are happy to talk diners through their selection of wines. Anna-Katharina Lemke, the resident sommelier, has compiled a wine list that caters to true enthusiasts: it focuses on Germany's wine-growing regions, each represented by several wineries and a range of grape varieties. Pairings are also available to go with the set menus.

Name: Diekmann
Description: In the mood for the charm of a typical bistro setting? At the front, amid decorative wine racks from an old colonial goods shop, the casual dining area has high tables positioned around a free-standing oyster bar. Alternatively, nab one of the small tables in the charming minimalist-style space at the back of the premises. The welcoming and attentive service also adds to the feel-good factor. In the evening, ambitious French and German dishes are served à la carte or as a tasting menu – cleverly integrated original twists give them a distinctively creative edge. Lunchtime options are more limited but reasonably priced – water, bread and espresso are included. The impressive oyster menu is available at both mealtimes.

Name: Diergardts Kühler Grund
Description: Established in 1904, this family-run restaurant is now in its fourth generation, with Philipp Diergardt now at the helm. He is passionate about cooking up traditional, seasonal cuisine that draws on locally sourced ingredients. The extensive menu is extremely appealing, making it difficult to choose. In addition to the fairly priced set menu ("Heimatmenü"), there are also classics such as bouillabaisse or Wiener schnitzel, as well as weekly specials that change with the seasons and dishes for two or more people. Wine connoisseurs will find plenty to enjoy here, and all reasonably priced. The fine selection of high-end German wines and French vintages is of particular note. Then there is the tasteful country house ambience, gorgeous terrace and attentive service.

Name: Dil Se
Description: Dil Se is set along the village's main thoroughfare in Toronto's "Roncy" neighborhood. Effort has gone into the decor here, with linen-draped tables and walls accented by colorful fabrics.Chef/owner Mani Panwar offers highly enjoyable, well-prepared northern Indian cuisine.Paneer lababdar, a "Chef's special," is a Mughlai-style specialty featuring soft cubes of fresh cow's milk cheese simmered in a creamy, highly flavorful, orange-hued sauce enriched with cashews. Neatly presented in a metal bowl, vegetable biryani is fluffy and hot with a bright flavor courtesy of chilies, herbs and dried spices. Among the tandoor offerings, choose the lamb seek kebab, which comes with a zesty red chutney that leans tart.

Name: Dilia
Description: This small-format restaurant opposite Notre-Dame-de-la-Croix, in the heart of the 20th arrondissement, has buckets of charm and a country house feel. Tuscan chef Michele Farnese has good international credentials, as well as experience in French establishments such as Saturne and Thoumieux. With the name Dilia, he pays tribute to his ancestors, Dino and Illia. With a joyous sense of freedom, the chef cooks up his Italian cuisine. Sage takes pride of place alongside pillowy beetroot gnocchi and raw scallop shavings; the pasta is prepared in time-honoured tradition and marries perfectly with the bottarga and garlic bread. While the lunch menu is a good deal, the multi-course dinner menu ups the ante, and is accompanied by an excellent selection of French and Italian wines. Friendly and smiling service is provided by the manager and sommelier. A well-kept secret to (re)discover as a matter of urgency.

Name: Dill
Description: Warm beige, wood tones and soft lighting make for a calm and soothing space. Similarly, dishes created by the Norwegian chef are simple and honest, with a touch of Nordic charm. At lunchtime, light meals such as toast, sandwiches and waffles are served. To experience his culinary vision in full, try his dinner set, which may include the unmissable "cod, kohlrabi, celeriac" – fresh, perfectly cooked fish finessed by solid technique.

Name: Dilsk
Address: 44 Marine Parade, Brighton and Hove, BN2 1PE, United Kingdom
Description: Visit this intimate and slightly moody spot inside the Drakes Hotel and you will likely be treated to some of the delicious, red-brown seaweed – more commonly known as dulse – after which the restaurant is named. Both the Short and Full tasting menus on offer include colourful dishes that are the epitome of modern British cuisine, like hogget with wild garlic and purple sprouting broccoli. The roster of well-chosen wines offers less-common choices that complement the food well.

Name: Dim Sum
Description: This restaurant with a partially open kitchen introduces its guests to the delicious specialities of Guangzhou and Southern China in rooms full of decorative details. The small dishes which characterise the culinary traditions of these regions have been refined with just a hint of contemporary flavour. A truly authentic Chinese dining experience.

Name: Dim Sum Duck
Address: 124 King's Cross Road, King’s Cross, London, WC1X 9DS, United Kingdom
Description: If you're thinking of eating at this small, family owned 'simple shop', do ensure you get here early as it doesn't take bookings and is deservedly popular. A one-hour wait is not unusual but the team manage the queue well and once you're sat either in the lively interior or under the pavement gazebo, you can dive into the wide-ranging Cantonese menu. The authentic dishes are carefully cooked using good quality ingredients, with bold and well-defined flavours present in options like the xiaolong bao and the cheung fun.

Name: Dim Tao
Description: Dim sum, a representative Cantonese dish, literally means “touch the heart,” implying that it’s not intended to fill your stomach, but is supposed to be a simple meal. Dim Tao focuses on the most famous dim sum dishes among its countless varieties, including juicy xiao long bao (soup dumplings); a dumpling filled with plump shrimp and chives; wonton soup; and barbeque pork buns. Traditionally, dim sum is served with tea. We recommend the pu’er and jasmine teas. A long line of customers outside makes this popular establishment in the Haeridan-gil area impossible to miss.

Name: Dimora Ulmo
Description: Three tasting journeys are on offer – Contaminazioni, Dimora Ulmo and A Mano Libera – conceived to accompany the guest in a continuous dialogue between modern cooking and local traditions; individual courses may also be selected à la carte from within the menus. All of this takes shape within an ancient palazzo sensitively restored, enriched by a summer terrace with a striking outlook over Sassi. Among the dishes tasted, the porchetta-style rabbit with Ligurian gravy and roasted pepper merits particular mention, a successful expression of technique and personality. The service, attentive and engaged, conveys both expertise and genuine passion, while the well-constructed wine selection does justice to the territory without forgoing an openness to the rest of Italy and to some interesting international labels.

Name: Dina
Description: A large wooden door dating from the late 19C leads into this restaurant, which makes a striking impression from the moment you step over the threshold. You come first of all into a dark-coloured reception area, which then leads into three dining rooms decorated with antique furniture, most of which dates from the 1950s. Two tasting menus are served here (one classic in style, the other more creative), showcasing chef Alberto Gipponi’s culinary skills to the full – one of the most interesting options is the guinea fowl with lemon and gentian, which has a perfect balance of softness and delicate acidity. Ask the talented sommelier for his wine recommendations – we particularly enjoyed an excellent Riesling from the nearby Val Brembana.

Name: Ding Te Le Zhou Mian Guan
Address: No. 22, Lane 494, Middle Huaihai Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: To the passer-by, this simple shop hidden in an alley on Huaihai Road looks pretty much like any other. What sets it apart, however, are the authentic noodles it serves. It is particularly famous for its shredded pork noodles with scallions, its yellow croaker noodles with pickled vegetables, and its deep-fried pork chops. You can also enjoy congee, rice and snacks – and it stays open 24 hours a day.

Name: Dingles Public House
Address: 333 Fulton St., San Francisco, CA, 94102, USA
Description: The memorable name of this handsome establishment, tucked away in the back of a boutique Hayes Valley hotel, comes from owners Anissa and George Dingle—natch. She manages the well-edited beverage program, from the expected draughts to wine and pleasingly simple cocktails, while he has the run of the kitchen, serving up classic, unfussy British pub fare with an edge of refinement. Beer-battered fish and chips, paired with classic mushy peas and curry sauce, hits its mark, as does a spot-on Scotch egg, with its jammy yolk and crunchy, panko-crusted exterior, and Welsh rarebit makes a concession to the States with Jasper Hill Farm cheddar from Vermont. Sticky toffee pudding with stout caramel and brown butter ice cream is no slouch, either.

Name: Dinho's
Description: Dinho's was opened by Fuad Zegaib (the creator of the strip steak) six decades ago. Nowadays, the restaurant is run by chef Paulo Zegaib, the founder’s son. Occupying a new home on the ground floor of the Hotel Qoya, in the Paraíso section of the city (there’s also a Dinho’s in the Jardins district), it features a spacious, classically furnished main dining room, which is entirely glass-fronted and enclosed by a beautiful vertical garden plus a colourful open kitchen to one side. Renowned for its longevity in this bustling capital city, the restaurant offers superb cuts of beef, as well as feijoada on Thursdays and Saturdays, a buffet of salads and desserts, plus a copious seafood buffet on Fridays.

Name: Dining Room
Address: 37F, Park Hyatt Hotel, 1366 Qianjiang Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking
Description: With exquisite glass lanterns, glass screens and panoramic windows that welcome in river views, the high-ceilinged room is perfect for banquets and business dinners. The menu is dominated by Zhejiang classics, alongside some Cantonese dishes. The poetically named "Sinking Fish, Falling Geese" consists of white fish balls stuffed with bird's nest. The classic braised pork belly is thinly sliced and styled into a pagoda. Reservations recommended.

Name: Dining Room
Address: 87F, Park Hyatt, 100 Century Avenue, Pudong, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: This high-ceilinged room with full-length windows affords panoramic river views, which create a superlative backdrop to an exquisite Jiangnan feast. The chef crafts a lineup of unique signature dishes that respect tradition while embracing creativity. With silky meat and bouncy skin, poached chicken in scallion and shallot oil is garnished with French chives for layered allium flavour. Steamed line-caught belt fish with red glutinous wine lees exudes deep aromas.

Name: DiningRuhm
Description: Housed in a corner plot building in an inconspicuous location in the 4th district, this restaurant serves an interesting mix of Nippon and Nikkei cuisine – ie Japanese- and Peruvian-inspired dishes are in the spotlight. This unpretentious cuisine also goes wonderfully well with the interior, which is decked out in warm colours and characterised by modern lines. The sushi bar is located in one of the three rooms. Try the delicious finger food, sushi (including lobster nigiri with a creamy spicy sauce) or main courses such as black cod yuzu miso. Attentive service from staff who also provide good wine recommendations from a selection that highlights Austrian labels. Unless you would prefer a sake…

Name: Dio Deka
Address: Hotel Los Gatos, 210 E. Main St., Los Gatos, CA, 95030, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Dio Deka may specialize in Greek food, but this is no typical taverna, as the stylish dining room (complete with a roaring fireplace) ably demonstrates. A wealthy, well-dressed Los Gatos crowd flocks to the front patio on warm evenings, dining and people-watching within the vine-covered walls of the Hotel Los Gatos. The bar also draws a brace of cheery regulars. Nothing beats a mesquite-grilled and oven-baked pita with olive oil and oregano to kick off the meal. Then, keep things Greek: think stuffed grape leaves with tender braised beef cheek or a bright pan-seared local salmon with roasted yellow peppers, potatoes and artichokes. The adventurous shouldn’t miss out on the fun offering of Greek wines, and sweet buffs should allow space for the crema me meli, a fantastic burnt-honey mousse with almond and lemon.

Name: Dio Mio
Description: Chefs/owners Spencer White and Alex Figura have a background in fine dining, but this popular fast-casual concept thrives on an accessible, laid-back format. Creativity and a clear understanding of flavor go hand in hand on a small, seasonal menu, with house-made forming the centerpiece of the operation (both literally and figuratively—a pasta production table is visible at the heart of the kitchen), from tradition-adjacent mafaldine cacio e pepe, boosted with pink peppercorn, to totally iconoclastic combinations like casarecce with shrimp, dill and toasted parmesan.

Name: Discada
Address: 1700 E. Cesar Chavez St., Austin, TX, 78702, USA
Description: Head to East Austin to find this stationary food truck where they only have one thing on their mind—discada. It may be the easiest order you've ever made, and the only decision you'll need to make is how many taquitos you want. As for the food, it's all in the name. Discada is a Northern Mexican style of cooking with different cuts of beef and pork cooked together with aromatic vegetables. Their version also adds bacon, onion, and roasted poblano peppers, all cooked down and served taquito style in single layers of yellow corn tortillas. Topped with a pulverized pineapple slaw and served with fresh salsa on the side, it's a delicious style not often seen. Elote and soft drinks round out the hyper-focused offerings.

Name: Disciples
Description: Chef Jean-Pierre Vigato has lost nothing of his passion for passing on his knowledge. Indeed, in this bright, contemporary dining space that is in keeping with the chic neighbourhood, he has dubbed Romain Dubuisson his "disciple". On the agenda, a short menu of generous and tasty cuisine, specials and fine pieces of meat for sharing (e.g. veal chop, farmhouse pork loin).

Name: Dishes
Address: 194 High Street, Prestatyn, LL19 9BW, United Kingdom
Description: Chef Andrew Sheridan has returned to his native north Wales to open this stylish restaurant occupying a former cloth shop on the High Street. Take a seat at the counter or a high-topped table and relish the opportunity to delve into a roll-call of terrific Welsh ingredients – be it meaty Menai oysters or caramelised mutton belly from just up the road. Order sharing plates from the à la carte or opt for the chef’s choice if you’re indecisive. A relaxed atmosphere pervades throughout, with both the service team and chefs adept at interacting with their guests.

Name: Dispensa Franciacorta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The decor at this restaurant features bottles of wine on the walls (there are around 700 labels on the wine list, with an unsurprising focus on sparkling wines from the local Franciacorta region), while the menu celebrates some of Italy’s best produce, as well as ingredients from further afield, with a focus on Mediterranean flavours. There’s also an excellent cheese selection which will delight cheese-lovers.

Name: Distrikt41
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: A restaurant with a modern decor and gastro-bar ambience run by two chefs originally from the Netherlands, Danny van Vliet and Joris Bruurs. Here, the contemporary à la carte and menu options (daily and seasonal) change every two months. Their cuisine, with specials such as the delicious Stroopwafel (a reinterpretation of a Dutch dessert), combines Central European, French and Spanish influences. Sauces are a prominent presence, while many dishes are given a finishing touch on the grill.

Name: Dit i Fet
Description: In the heart of Girona's Barri Vell, in a narrow street that runs parallel to the Onyar riverbed, this restaurant is a great option, surprising diners with its interior design, the kitchen open to the dining room and large stone arches that speak of the magnificent urban historical legacy. The couple at the helm, formed with the Roca brothers, champion traditional Catalan cuisine expertly brought up to date, constantly looking at the season and with interesting suggestions. Our recommendations? We especially liked both the scallop tartare, manzanilla olive and piparra sauce and the creamy Palamós shrimp omelette.

Name: Diuna
Description: With a name meaning ‘sand dunes’, it’s no surprise to find this restaurant overlooking the dunes with the white sandy beach and Baltic Sea beyond. In summer, a table on the terrace is a must; if the weather keeps you inside, the views are better from the upstairs room. When you’re this close to the water, it makes sense to have seafood, so keep an eye out for some terrific skrei cod when in season. The meat options include beef Wellington to share when ordered in advance.

Name: Divinis
Description: In this really lovely spot, guests sit at tables laid out in several areas on different levels, surrounded by appealingly disparate furnishings. An abundance of individual details make for a charming backdrop – beautiful old floorboards, mismatched tables and chairs, original figurines, numerous books and designer lamps. Refined Italian dishes - prepared in the open kitchen - impress with their elegance and, above all, their flavour. The chef's signature dish is braised veal cheeks with Marsala, spinach and mashed potato with truffle butter. The friendly waitstaff are happy to advise you on the food and your choice of wine from the Italian-centric selection.

Name: Divino Gusto
Address: Square des Nations Unies 4A, Nivelles, 1400, Belgium
Description: Despite the Italian name of this elegant restaurant, Marc Grislain’s style is far from restricted to the bel paese. He may be a fan of Mediterranean panache, but that doesn’t prevent him showcasing his mastery of classical techniques together with Asian notes. For example, he might flank a rare rib of steak with veggies such as cream of squash and ginger and a gutsy cooking gravy flavoured with smoky black tea. The sommelier and owner, Gaëtan Poels, can be relied upon to ply you with insightful wine tips to create the perfect pairing. Hats off to this establishment that is enjoying a new lease of life!

Name: Divino Steak House
Description: This restaurant, located in the old O Burgo train station, is run by two Argentine brothers with Galician roots. They work with selected local meats, displayed like authentic treasures in their ageing chambers. Here, the menu revolves around gorgeous ribeye steaks cooked over charcoal, with a small selection of starters (including seafood, steak tartare, cecina croquettes, etc.) and three types of prime cuts (veal, cow and selected beef), with different maturations. There is also some fish (only available on request)!

Name: Doc
Address: via Vittorio Veneto 1, Borgio Verezzi, 17022, Italy
Description: Quiet, well - kept restaurant located in an aristocratic, early twentieth - century villa surrounded by a pretty garden.

Name: Docket Restaurant
Address: 33 High Street, Whitchurch, SY13 1AZ, United Kingdom
Description: Stuart and Frances Collins spent many years working overseas before moving to this old Shropshire market town to open their popular neighbourhood restaurant, sandwiched between two shops on the high street. Their travels are reflected in Stuart's cooking, which comes in the form of a tasting menu and takes an imaginative approach while being underpinned by his strong classical technique. Frances runs the efficient service with a smile and her enthusiastic team follow suit.

Name: Dodici Fontane
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The scenery that you drive through to get to this restaurant on the slopes of Mt Etna is as breathtaking and impressive as the charming luxury Villa Neri hotel in which it is housed. In the modern dining room, the chef serves personalised cuisine with a focus on Sicilian ingredients, resulting in occasionally complex dishes (meat and fish) which are showcased on his tasting menus. Guests can also choose dishes à la carte style, while the wine list includes an excellent and highly recommended selection of local Etna labels, including the property’s own wine (they also produce their own extra-virgin olive oil).

Name: Dogma
Description: A small restaurant run by two young and passionate spouses, drawing on considerable previous experience: she in the dining room, he at the stove. Their cooking has a strongly defined personality and focuses above all on the sea, with dishes in which cooking over charcoal – or at least certain fundamental stages of it – takes centre stage, extending even into the desserts. The flavours are intense and convincing, with occasional foreign inflections, as in the Talo, a kind of Basque flatbread, made with white maize flour and filled with anchovies, broccoli and stracciatella: a preparation that showcases their mastery of this type of cooking. The setting is intimate and welcoming; booking is advisable, particularly in the evening, given the growing popularity of the venue.

Name: Dogstar
Address: 17 Portland Place, Leith, EH6 6LA, United Kingdom
Description: One of the newer restaurants in this Edinburgh enclave, Dogstar occupies a former pub that’s now a buzzy space run by an engaging team whose cheery service will enhance any experience. The seasonal menu can change weekly or even daily, but expect dishes suited to sharing that show off an array of prime produce (sometimes cooked over coals), including stand-outs like fresh, sweet local surf clams with sea laver, rosemary and fino sherry. The carefully curated wine list offers a good range without breaking the bank.

Name: Dokjard
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Set in a former warehouse by the picturesque Noorderhaven, this relaxed "brew-bistro" offers a delightful blend of pub atmosphere and attentive service. When you first enter, you will be greeted by the aroma of freshly brewed beer and the sight of towering brewing kettles. The kitchen team pushes the boundaries, effortlessly weaving between the classic and creative. From steak tartare with an Asian twist to melt-in-your-mouth pork cheeks with dukkah and sesame seeds, this cuisine is vibrant and imaginative. The house beers perfectly complement the dishes, adding a personal touch. What a place!

Name: Dolce Amaro
Description: As you admire the mural depicting Piazza del Campo in Sienna and the patio to the rear, you may almost forget you’re in Brussels’ Louise district. Dolce Amaro is a 100% authentic, bustling Italian trattoria. The food is equally genuine: orecchiette al dente in an aroma-packed tomato sauce and juicy chunks of pork or super-fresh seabass exquisitely paired with melt-in-the-mouth aubergine… Outstanding flavours that will knock the socks off your tastebuds. Let’s not forget the wine list, an Aladdin’s Cave of Italian tipples.

Name: Dolce Vita
Description: In this compact restaurant in the city centre, you feel a bit like you are on holiday when you taste the Mediterranean cuisine that leans into fish, seafood, house-made pasta and risotto (they do also serve meat). The ingredients take centre stage, with a focus on premium quality, and all of the fish is wild caught. Each dish boils down to just a few components, eg the excellent meagre is accompanied by grilled courgettes and fluffy mashed potatoes; the delicate gnocchi are harmoniously complemented by clams in a white wine broth. In the evening, an ambitious surprise menu comprising five, seven or nine courses is served; the lighter lunch menu is somewhat more limited - the dinner set menu is also available on request. The wine list includes a selection of orange and natural wines. There is a cosy "living room" atmosphere, and friendly service is also part of the deal.

Name: Dolia Gaeta
Description: This brand-new restaurant boasts an elegant, chic decor and a relaxed and informal ambience. The very young team here is overseen by a talented chef who prepares modern and creative dishes with a focus on fish from the local gulf, as well as elsewhere. The wine list is also particularly interesting, featuring a remarkable choice of champagnes and a special emphasis on labels from Lazio.

Name: Domaine d'Auriac
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: A magnificent 19C property steeped in history sets the elegant scene and provides the perfect foil for classical recipes, enhanced by the odd modern twist. When the weather allows, make a beeline for the terrace overlooking the grounds. The epitome of good taste in a quintessentially French country estate.

Name: Domaine de Baulieu
Description: In an elegant and modern interior with large bay windows overlooking the terrace and the surrounding nature, you can enjoy food cooked up by Maxime Deschamps. Their dishes are well crafted and make the most of local produce. A super dining experience.

Name: Domaine de Rochevilaine
Address: à la Pointe de Pen-Lan, Billiers, 56190, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: This smart restaurant is part of the family-owned Grand Hotel de Solesmes estate, which boasts a charming patchwork of traditional cottages, houses and manors, manicured grounds and a jaw-dropping ocean view. Chef Maxime Nouail, also a fisherman, consummately works with premium seafood and local country produce. Lobster is the house signature, but the rest of the enticing menu is equally first-class: carpaccio of langoustines, green peas, cockles; John Dory roasted in butter with artichokes prepared several ways. Deft craftsmanship, crisp forthright flavours, a splendid wine list and flawless service: just the ticket for a culinary maritime experience in a magical setting. Swanky guestrooms and a spa for a luxurious seaside stay!

Name: Domaine de Rymska
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Set in the countryside between Beaune and Chalon-sur-Saône, this charming restaurant and hotel sits in the middle of a vast estate with lakes, a stud farm, and a farm that supplies some high-quality produce, including Wagyu beef, eggs, poultry, fruit and vegetables. The chef's cuisine also draws on the finest ingredients, and sometimes finds inspiration further afield: sea bream ceviche with lime and coconut milk; scallops, mushroom gyoza and Noilly Prat sauce; mandarin, orange and Timut pepper. The beautiful space boasts exposed stone walls, a beamed ceiling and a fire crackling in the imposing hearth. Extraordinary wine list.

Name: Domenica
Description: Domenica is the place to come to experience the bustling Jordaan neighbourhood. Whether you are dining outside on the terrace or inside at the bar of this modern bistro, there is always a lively atmosphere here. Authentic Italian seasonal dishes are served up with great skill and a proper sense of generosity. Think octopus with crispy skin and tender meat served alongside robust bell pepper and broccoletti. Owner Flavio pays tribute to his heritage with every vibrant plate. Be sure to check out his French and Italian wine selections too.

Name: Dominic
Address: 54G, The Row, Jalan Doraisamy, Chow Kit, Kuala Lumpur, 50300, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: From the blue façade and a terrace reminiscent of pavement cafes, to the oversized painting celebrating joie de vivre, the restaurant formerly known as 2OX transports diners to a Parisian bistro with its relaxed, convivial vibe. Helmed by Chef Dominic, the kitchen creates modern, sophisticated dishes that are deeply rooted in the French traditions. Most ingredients are imported from Europe; the artisanal cheeses are especially worth trying.

Name: Domitia - Maison de Cuisinier
Description: Slices of Mediterranean dentex served raw, caraway, cauliflower and elderberry vinegar; Camargue bull, oyster tartare from the Étang de Thau and salicornia-pistachio pesto: there's no doubt that chef Jérôme Faure has a masterful understanding of gourmet cuisine. His subtly innovative take on fine dining is based on a rigorous selection of local ingredients. The same goes for the wines.

Name: Domschenke
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This family-run restaurant is now in its third generation. Whether you sit in the rustic-style dining area with its regulars' table or in the pleasant conservatory, you are assured of friendly service.
