The menu features home-style, regional and more sophisticated dishes. Order à la carte or opt for one of the daily specials on the blackboard. In summer, make a beeline for the outdoor seating area, which is shaded by old trees.

Name: Don Angie
Address: 103 Greenwich Ave., New York, NY, 10014, USA
Description: This darling of a dining room is designed with elegant blue-gray leather banquettes, bentwood chairs, and a dark checkerboard floor. Potted plants, moody lighting, and a rustic bar with brass accents make it a dream-worthy refuge for a romantic tête-à-tête. Married couple, Angie Rito and Scott Tacinelli, are the brains behind this venture, where the team takes risks that result in highly creative and enriching cuisine.While the menu feels like an American story as told through an Italian lens, Asian elements also make guest appearances as in the spicy pepperoni fried rice gussied-up with tender grilled calamari. Playful aptly describes the combination of spicy veal tartare and tuna carpaccio. Pastas are similarly prolific, like the paprika-tinted sorpresine with smoked mussels or sourdough pasta in a 'nduja sauce with mezcal-braised chicken. Pesce alla griglia in a clam broth and Sicilian scallop crudo speak of bold flavors and polished methods.Desserts, such as the fior di latte mochi with golden Taggiasca olive oil or black cocoa tiramisu garnished with feuilletine, are just the icing on the cake. Go for over-the-top glee with a sip of house-made root beer amaro.

Name: Don Antonio
Address: 309 W. 50th St., New York, NY, 10019, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The namesake outpost is located in Naples and has been running strong since 1901. Meanwhile in Midtown, Don Antonio by Starita has been slinging authentic Neapolitan-style, woodfired pizza since 2012, thanks to Don's daughter, Giorgia Caporuscio, who learned the family craft and took over the family business here. This kitchen's signature is the Montanara Starita—a lightly fried pizza laced with house-made tomato sauce, smoked mozzarella, and basil, then finished in the wood-fired oven. But really, who could stop there with treasures like the salsiccia e friarielli pizza with fennel sausage or the delicious frittatine, where chopped spaghetti pieces and ham are blended with Buffalo mozzarella, breaded, and fried to a golden crisp.

Name: Don Camillo
Description: A long-established restaurant, active since 1985, that continues to win over the palate with a cuisine inspired by Sicilian tradition, reinterpreted with a modern and personal touch by chef-patron Giovanni Guarnieri. In the heart of Ortigia, steps from the Metropolitan Cathedral of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary, the surroundings express an equally timeless elegance: fifteenth-century tufa stone walls, period wooden furnishings and evocative wrought-iron candelabras contribute to a warm and refined atmosphere. Our Inspector recommends saving room at the end of the meal for their excellent desserts.

Name: Don Carlos
Description: The tribute that the Grand Hotel dedicates to Giuseppe Verdi is accompanied, in the small historic rooms of the Don Carlos, by a tribute to Milanese and Italian cuisine, perhaps with a Mediterranean nuance introduced by multi-star Gennaro Esposito, here as a consultant, and carefully executed. In a succession of sketches, pictures and paintings dedicated to the world of opera, for music lovers the restaurant is a must-visit. Caruso Nuovo, on the other hand, with its bistro formula, can be an always inviting and less demanding alternative.

Name: Don Cesar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The restaurant of the Don Cesar Hotel is certainly not lacking in charm with its luxurious, refined interior and large bay windows giving onto the terrace. The meticulously prepared and flavoursome food lies at the crossroads of French and Italian cuisine, and gives seafood pride of place, but also serves a wide range of dishes based on pasta made on site!

Name: Don Fadrique
Address: Carretera de Salamanca, Alba de Tormes, 37800, Spain
Description: At Don Fadrique, there’s a commonsense approach to the cuisine that makes its way from the kitchen to the table. This is showcased on an à la carte (including half portions), with an updated take on traditional cooking and a focus on the seasons, and two tasting menus: “Sabor de la Memoria”, with its homage to tradition and top-quality ingredients (including grilled fish and meat), and Instinto, a more personal and modern option which gives free rein to the chef’s creativity (prior booking required). The chef also presents and serves many of the dishes himself.

Name: Don't Tell Dad
Address: 10-14 Lonsdale Road, Queen's Park, London, NW6 6RD, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: ‘For Lesley, By Daniel’ is the tagline of this endearing neighbourhood restaurant inspired by the owner’s late sister and named in honour of their childhood escapades that would always start with “don’t tell dad”. Situated in the heart of bustling Queen’s Park, there’s a lovely vintage feel to the place, which also operates as a bakery during the day. Start with snacks such as the moreish truffle and cheddar beignets, before considering hearty sharing mains such as wing rib of beef with bone marrow butter. Ensure you save room for the freshly baked madeleines to finish too.

Name: Donaji
Description: Donaji, from Chef Isai Cuevas, who first built a loyal following selling tamales at Bay Area farmers’ markets, remains a cheerful neighborhood spot centered around Oaxacan cooking and exceptional masa work. Named after a Zapotec princess in homage to the chef’s roots, the restaurant continues to showcase handmade tortillas, earthy moles and carefully prepared antojitos. Tamales remain a highlight, but dishes like crispy tacos dorados de pollo with black bean purée and crema, or enchiladas draped in a deep, complex 20-ingredient mole negro, reveal the kitchen’s attention to detail just as clearly. Larger plates, including pollo asado or short ribs with mole coloradito, further highlight the richness and depth of Oaxacan flavors. House-made aguas frescas remain the perfect accompaniment to the savory, earthy fare.

Name: Donatz
Description: Cornelia and René A Donatz run their business with great dedication. In an elegant rustic-style decor, they serve good fresh cuisine, including classic veal dishes, Angus beef "bestsellers", vegetarian fare and fish such as Graubünden salmon from Lostallo. They stock some 550 wines (20 available by the glass) – a passion of the owner. Donatz Wine Bar proposes a smaller menu. Hotel Donatz has appealingly modern and comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Dong Ping Chao
Address: 1 Dongping Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, 200031, Chinese Mainland
Description: This restaurant in a century-old heritage building reinterprets Chaozhou fare with refined touches and local twists. Quality ingredients, especially seafood, are shipped from Chaoshan region twice a day to ensure freshness. Menus are tailor-made at least one day ahead. The speciality crispy-skin braised sea cucumber provides a nice contrast of texture, with a subtle hint of peanut butter in the abalone sauce.

Name: Dongnae
Address: 5-7 Chandos Road, City of Bristol, BS6 6PG, United Kingdom
Description: Bristol’s lovers of Korean food have found their haven in this charmingly run restaurant in the trendy Redland neighbourhood. The authentic cooking can be sampled as either a set menu or an à la carte of sharing plates, where each dish is cooked with care and precision using high-quality produce. The dishes from the charcoal grill – such as 'eoynyang bulgogi' made using Wagyu beef – are particularly enjoyable, thanks to the superb accompanying condiments that are expertly spiced and fermented to bring extra layers of flavour to the central ingredients.

Name: Dongyin Fisherman
Address: 96-2, Section. 1, Xiangshang Road, West District, Taichung, Taiwan
Description: A professional angler opened this joint over 10 years ago, naming it after his favourite fishing spot. It serves a menu similar to other stir-fry restaurants, but with an emphasis on line-caught fish from offshore islands, plus some original creations and specialities from the Matsu Islands. Must-tries include steamed fish in a house-made winter melon sauce, or sautéed squid with pickled cabbage. If in doubt, ask the owner's wife for recommendations.

Name: Donostia
Address: 10 Seymour Place, Marylebone, London, W1H 7ND, United Kingdom
Description: Perch at the counter or sit at one of the tables in this fun, warmly run little spot and enjoy a selection of pintxos and tapas inspired by the food of San Sebastián. House specialities such as gilda, bacalao and txuleta are always worth ordering. Just one dessert is offered, but when it’s Basque cheesecake as wonderfully creamy as this, who would want anything else?

Name: Dons Bogam
Address: 17 E. 32nd St., New York, NY, 10016, USA
Description: At Dons Bogam, the food is fantastic and service indulgent. From the festive bar up front right down to those two-tops sporting blazing grills, every seat is filled, so reserve ahead. Make no mistake: this is no average K-town joint. Inside, a top-notch venting system lets diners enjoy a smoke-free evening of exceptional grilled meats. Start with fried pork mandu, which are on-point and divine. Pork belly marinated in red wine is smoky and supremely tender, but for the ultimate payoff, opt for the beef platter. It features thinly sliced maeun and yangnyeom galbi set beside meaty king trumpet mushrooms. In Midtown for meetings? Pop in for the BBQ lunch, a fun and interactive midday meal that is leaps above a quick grab-and-go salad, yet just as healthy.

Name: Doori
Description: Born and raised in Yongsan, the chef and his wife present inventive Korean dishes in a serene, minimalist space. The restaurant's menu evolves constantly, shaped by seasonal ingredients and a thoughtful zero-waste philosophy. A standout in the menu, 'All of Today’s Scraps', transforms leftovers of the day into a dish that is remarkably aromatic and deeply flavourful. It’s hard to imagine a finer expression of conscious, creative dining than the one Doori offers.

Name: Doppelgänger Bar
Description: A highly informal gourmet bar inside the Antón Martín market offering mouthwatering fusion cuisine with a nod to the Iberian Peninsula, Asia and South America.

Name: Doppio Gusto
Description: A short distance from the city centre and the embarkation points for the Aeolian Islands, the broad and carefully kept terrace – between outdoor seating and open-air spaces – invites guests to take a break dedicated to taste. On the table, a fragrant and contemporary Sicilian seafood cuisine, built on seafood of great quality and interpreted with a contemporary touch. The wine offering is also well structured, with interesting labels available by the glass.

Name: Dorangeville
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: A picturesque medieval village provides the backdrop for this attractive 14C building, which houses a restaurant boasting an elegant contemporary interior and a terrace overlooking the garden. Chef Quentin Dorangeville, who hails from France's Sarthe département, cooks up seasonal cuisine that is as meticulous as it is ambitious. Using fine ingredients, he creates balanced combinations, such as medallion of blue lobster, tomato, preserved lemon and courgette cream with ginger. Good food and service with a smile!

Name: Dorf-Chronik
Description: This attractive winegrower's house dating back to 1747 stands in the centre of the town. Stefan Püngeler and his wife Michela De Munno – well-known figures in the region – have taken over the reins here after a successful run at Restaurant Schneider in Dernbach. He is in charge of the kitchen, and she is responsible for the friendly service. On the menu: flavoursome Italian fare – the house-made pasta is a particular highlight. The tiramisu, presented on a dessert trolley and freshly portioned tableside, is truly delicious. Rump steak – practically a staple in the region – is also available. The wine list features moderately priced labels from the region. Sandstone and half-timbering create a cosy atmosphere, and the courtyard terrace is delightful in summer.

Name: Dorfhus Gupf
Description: Dorfstuba is the name of the restaurant at the design-led boutique hotel Dorfhus Gupf, which stands out right in the centre of the village with its striking appearance. Service is provided by a friendly and attentive team, and the charming setting has a modern, Alpine feel. A particular focal point is the open kitchen with its prominent asado grill, on which whole fish and special cuts of meat are prepared. However, the Wiener schnitzel, braised beef cheeks or fish curry are also well worth trying. Sommelier Johannes Fitz is on hand to recommend the perfect wine from the fantastic list, which comprises 1 300 international labels, including 520 large formats. The Magnothek houses 15 500 bottles, with fine wines available to take home; the on-site shop, Lädeli, stocks gourmet food items.

Name: Dorfstube
Description: It's no wonder people that love to eat here! In addition to its fine dining restaurant, Hotel Hirsch has its Dorfstube, which is a great option for fans of Swabian cuisine. In the cosy old dining space, completely done out in wood, you can tuck into specialities such as tripe, maultaschen and Zwiebelrostbraten (roast beef with onions). Vegetarian options are also on the menu. The delicious dishes are all made using regional produce. Friendly service. We highly recommend staying overnight. The guestrooms are really lovely and inviting.

Name: Dorset
Description: Kitty and Willem have been welcoming guests with open arms since 2000. The charming couple have created an intimate and trendy restaurant with a pleasant lounge atmosphere and verdant terrace. Chef Davy Roord has a passion for local produce but equally enjoys working with exotic seasonings. His cooking is exuberant, at times creative, and it always has a fresh edge. For example, he pairs lamb from the region with textures of beetroot, celeriac and mustard, creating earthy-sweet, grilled, spicy and tangy nuances. The accompanying jus is artfully finished with red wine. Diner satisfaction is the priority here, when it comes to both the food and the wine!

Name: Dorsia
Address: 396 rue Notre-Dame Ouest, Montréal, H2Y 1T9, Canada
Description: With its decor of marble and mirrors, this chic and elegant establishment creates the ideal atmosphere for an intimate dinner for two. The delightfully simple menu harmoniously unites French and Italian influences in dishes such as roasted sea bream with a root vegetable salad, agnolotti with beetroot and sheep's cheese, or a delicious crown of duck à l’orange.

Name: Dos Pebrots
Description: If you’re looking for somewhere that reflects the essence of Mediterranean cooking, this restaurant in the El Raval district, close to MACBA (Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona), is a superb option. In the open-view kitchen, with its signature Josper grill, the focus is on the evolution of gourmet cuisine and the variety of Mediterranean flavours which are showcased on an interesting à la carte (each dish is accompanied by information to explain its history) and three meticulously presented menus (Dos Pebrots, Tasting menu and Festival). Take a seat at the bar to enjoy the experience to the full.

Name: Doshincho Washoku Zui
Description: ‘Zui’ means ‘fresh and lively’, which applies equally well to both fare and chef. His cheerful personality and energetic expression reflect his passion for cuisine and service. As a restaurateur who studied in Kyoto, the chef makes Rishiri kombu and light-coloured dried bonito flakes the foundation on which he works. Each dish is restricted to just two ingredients, so each component leaves a strong impression. He is especially adept at pairing ingredients with their own dashi, as seen in the sea bream sashimi accompanied by a jellied broth of sea bream dashi.

Name: Doughroom
Description: Dedicated to making artisanal pasta from scratch, Doughroom is a keeper for all Italian food lovers. The dough room itself, where all the pastas are made fresh daily, is undoubtedly the heart of the restaurant. While offering authentic flavors of Italy, it also serves fusion dishes using ingredients familiar to the local palate — for example, their buckwheat cannelloni. Asking for the action-packed dough room table when making a reservation is highly recommended.

Name: Dove
Address: 31 Kensington Park Road, Notting Hill, London, W11 2EU, United Kingdom
Description: Providing everything you would expect from a Notting Hill neighbourhood restaurant, Dove is the latest project from chef-restaurateur Jackson Boxer, taking over the space he once ran as Orasay. Bright, relaxed and simply decorated, it specialises in seasonal and high-quality produce across a menu that’s ideal for sharing. Dishes vary in size, from whole grilled fish and half a roasted chicken to snacks like fried potato pizzette with bonito, burrata and mortadella. The wine list offers something for everyone, with almost every choice available by the glass.

Name: Dovetale
Address: 1 Dover Yard, Mayfair, London, W1J 8NE, United Kingdom
Description: Like the hotel in which it sits – 1 Hotel Mayfair – Dovetale makes good use of natural materials and plenty of plants to create a warm, bright environment. It also has a great terrace for the summer months and a welcoming atmosphere all round. The menu looks to Europe for its contemporary dishes, such as Cornish John Dory with silky olive oil mash and a Madeira jus with just the right amount of intensity to enhance rather than overpower the fish. Look out for sharing options like the roast corn-fed Basseri chicken too. If you’re after a bit of nostalgia, you can 'design your own' Knickerbocker Glory for dessert.

Name: Down Home
Description: Known for their time at Sumac & Salt, Chef Joel Gray and Hannah Harradine apply a heartfelt approach by welcoming diners into their own home in Grey County for a charming, intimate experience. Here, an interior kitchen and a barbecue are used to create a meal that spotlights excellent local products. Everything is lovingly presented by the team, with the chef offering explanations of many of the courses. Standouts include pieces of coal-roasted beets arranged with pickled pumpkin and dabs of creamy pumpkin seed purée. Trout brined with spruce tips is slow-smoked then quick-seared and presented with Ontario potatoes, fiddlehead ferns, and trout roe. Braised lamb neck stuffs a wild leek raviolo dressed with a preserved green tomato jus, giving a subtle hint of spice.

Name: Downunder by Justin Jennings
Description: If you’ve never eaten crocodile or kangaroo, now is your chance in this unpretentious restaurant run by a young Australian chef who fell in love with Lisbon and set up his own business here. His somewhat unusual cuisine, available on an à la carte and two set menus, shines a light on Australian cuisine and its exotic meats.

Name: Dr. Xu's Wellbeing Branch (Tianhe)
Address: 7F, Concord Center, 57 Linjiang Avenue, Zhujiang New Town, Tianhe, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: Founder Dr. Xu is a postdoc in Chinese medicine and the restaurant doubles as a museum showcasing his collection of antiques and rare herbs. Diners appreciate the tonic effects of double-boiled soups, such as the abalone liver soup with wild tangerine, which imparts citrus tartness. Most dishes combine natural health-boosters and seasonal ingredients from around the world, especially live seafood. Pre-order your favourites; ask for a table by the window.

Name: Dragonfly
Address: The Lana Promenade, Marasi Drive, Business Bay, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Notable sake list,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: A sister to the original Dragonfly in Kazakhstan, this Dubai outpost boasts a contemporary Japanese menu with hints of pan-Asian influences. Sushi, maki, noodles and dim sum are a just a few items that adorn the menu and are prepared with prime ingredients – their braised Wagyu short rib and signature crystal toast are must haves. Inside, you are surrounded by Asian elements, with a dark wood ceiling and a large red dragonfly above; the wall panels were installed by craftsmen who travelled from China. Go for lunch for a great value meal or dinner for a lively evening out with signature cocktails.

Name: Drapers Arms
Address: 44 Barnsbury Street, Islington, London, N1 1ER, United Kingdom
Description: A stalwart of London's pub dining scene, Islington continues to be well-served by this imposing neighbourhood local. Not much has changed over the years and it's all the better for it; rustic décor, eager-to-please staff and a relaxed, unpretentious approach ensure the perfect pub atmosphere. The cooking is as hearty and satisfying as ever, but these days the traditionally British (steak & ale pie) sits alongside French influences (braised rabbit leg), courtesy of a Breton-born Chef. The courtyard garden is a great place to enjoy a glass from the superb wine list.

Name: Drei Könige
Description: This restaurant has a charming bistro feel and serves delicious food expertly prepared with fresh, carefully selected ingredients. At lunchtime, there is a set menu with options, and the atmosphere is upbeat and lively. In the evening, the pace is a little slower, and the food even more sophisticated.

Name: Drexlers
Description: Since 2007, this bright, modern restaurant right next to Colombipark has been something of an institution in Freiburg. Service is friendly and adept and the atmosphere warm and welcoming. Showcasing regional produce, the ambitious seasonally inspired cuisine draws on French and Italian influences. The four- to six-course set menu comes in a "classic" or vegetarian version. On Mondays and Thursdays you can also order individual courses à la carte. Great selection of reasonably priced wines – courtesy of their own wine shop. Tip for motorists: Rotteck underground car park is within walking distance.

Name: Dreyfus
Description: No obvious signage, curtains drawn and the front door frosted top to bottom. What could this cozy French bistro be hiding? The answer is indulgence. Situated on the first floor of a narrow townhouse, Dreyfus is the kind of dinner you have before hibernation and after an annual physical. Rare (and sadly empty) trophy wines line the room’s perimeter, while servers explain that the fries are for the pâté and that the doughnuts are for the smoked trout dip garnished with roe. That Zach Kolomeir cooks with maximum impact shouldn’t be a shock given his tenure at Montreal’s famed Joe Beef. Sitting elbow to elbow, oenophiles looking for primo vino will have to ask for off-menu bottles, some of which sit in plain sight above the bar.

Name: Drouant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: This iconic, yet resolutely sprightly restaurant provides the smart, elegant stage where the Goncourt and Renaudot Book Prizes have been awarded respectively since 1914 and 1926! After learning the ropes with legends such as Cyril Lignac and Yannick Alléno, gifted chef Romain Van Thienen rolls out a pedigree lineup of French classics, from vol-au-vent and sole meunière to last-minute steak tartare and the famous "madeleine de Proust". As you take a seat in the plush interior you can expect to taste beautifully crafted, flavoursome dishes whose ingredients are nothing if not fresh, served by a front-of-house team that is both on the ball and cheerful. The wine cellar boasts nearly 2000 references and a very respectable range of wines by the glass.

Name: Drum Café
Description: Designed as a landmark and tribute to the region, architect Frank Gehry's LUMA Tower not only draws art lovers but is also a beacon for foodies. Constructed using recycled materials and natural resources such as Arles merino wool, the venue boasts impressive proportions. Pushing the boundaries, the indulgent dishes showcase fine seasonal produce: poultry pâté en croûte; seared pollock, fennel confit with orange and saffron; lemon cream and Buddha's hand, hazelnut praline. The wine list homes in on organic labels.

Name: Drunken Duck Inn
Description: This picture-postcard pub sits in the heart of the beautiful Lakeland countryside and must be one of the most desirable in the region. Inside, the extended inn is overflowing with charm and character, especially in the buzzing bar. The generous cooking includes the likes of celeriac and hazelnut Kiev or venison loin and pie with beetroot fondant, and they can be paired with ales brewed on-site. Relaxed, chatty service enhances the experience, as do the boutique bedrooms, some of which boast terraces with stunning fell views.

Name: Drunken Fish
Address: 1F, Wynn Hotel, Rua Cidade de Sintra, NAPE, Macau, Macau
Description: Curved glass aquariums provide visual cues as to the oceanic theme that also dominates the seafood-led menu. Another recurring concept is the Chinese liquor Moutai. The young Beijingese chef melds global influences in dishes like leopard coral grouper in Moutai and Guizhou sour soup, or drunken freshwater prawns blanched in Moutai. Even the house-made chilli sauce is laced with the prized liquor. Order Moutai cocktails to start or finish your meal.

Name: Dry Aged
Address: via Cesare Da Sesto 1/A, Milan, 20123, Italy
Description: Two partners with significant experience opened this lively venue: the rooms combine modern and classic styles in an industrial-New York style decorated with works by major street artists. At the entrance, the glass counter shows off meats of different breeds to be enjoyed even charcoal grilled, but there are also other specialties: appealing dishes with a modern preparation and homemade pastas.

Name: Dry Creek Kitchen
Address: Hotel Healdsburg, 317 Healdsburg Ave., Healdsburg, CA, 95448, USA
Description: Open since 2001, this veteran haunt by Chef Charlie Palmer is attached to the sleek Hotel Healdsburg. Airy and elegant, the vaulted room boasts white tablecloths as well as large windows overlooking the downtown square. The cooking, meanwhile, is contemporary in design, with farm-sourced ingredients prepared with style. Snack on oxtail dumplings before moving on to an electric kanpachi tiradito. Mains cover the gamut: Salmon, duck, lamb and pork chops. Finish with an indulgent “cookie butter mousse bomb.”

Name: Drómo
Address: Antonio Martínez Virel 2, 1ª Planta, Badajoz, 06011, Spain
Description: Found on the first floor of a small shopping centre called Reina Mercedes (in the modern neighbourhood of Valdepasillas) and under the name Drómo, which has been retained from the previous establishment, lies a subtle nod to the life of Juan Manuel Salgado, the chef-owner.His cuisine embraces ‘informal haute cuisine’ and seeks to create an intimate experience, something you can enjoy more intensely if you sit at the bar, where you can observe every detail of his work. The elegant offering, typical of contemporary cuisine that draws on traditional Extremaduran recipes and childhood memories (pringá, puchero, cachuela, and Iberian pork), is available exclusively through two surprise tasting menus (Drómo and Gran Viaje). A standout dish? We liked the combination of prawns and Maresme peas, as the two work perfectly together. When you eat here, they ask you to be punctual so that all diners can start the experience at the same time!

Name: Du Ji Mai Bing
Address: 288 Taizhoufu Road, Linhai, Taizhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: For more than two decades, customers have flocked here in droves for Taizhou-style wheat flour flatbread known as ‘mai bing’. With more than 10 different fillings on offer, ranging from ground pork and egg to mashed potato, there is something for everyone. Their fried-to-order flatbread is crisp and nicely browned on the outside, moist and tender on the inside. Pair the flatbread with bian shi dumplings or hand-rolled noodle soup.

Name: Du Moulin
Description: The wood-burning fire in the cosy sitting room is the epitome of an Ardennes inn. This nostalgic charm is enhanced by the classical cooking of Jean Goire, who brooks no concessions. He pays tribute to his region, working closely with carefully selected suppliers. His culinary expertise unveils a deep-rooted respect and steadfast commitment to flavours that are gutsy, rustic and traditional to the core.

Name: Du Théâtre
Description: A stone’s throw from the centre, within the Crochetan theatre precinct, this elegant restaurant sports an airy interior, an open kitchen and a small conservatory. The Italian-born chef conjures up a creative, deftly crafted score that slaloms between regional classics and Mediterranean favourites, but always with seasonal produce. The crisp balanced dishes showcase the occasional inspired imaginative spin, like his wondrous “Risotto of red Sicilian shrimps with blueberry powder and celery”. The talented sommelier is a font of wine knowledge and the shaded terrace is bliss in fine weather.

Name: Du Yên
Address: 26B Street 10, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 71000, Vietnam
Description: Nestled in a quiet neighbourhood in town, this place occupies two levels with its room exuding rustic chic. The eclectic menu presents Vietnamese dishes plus Western and Thai options. Gỏi cuốn hoa bướm are the photogenic rice paper rolls adorned with edible pansies. The sweet peanut dip works well with the crisp vegetables. Męt bánh Huế is the vegetarian version of the famous steamed rice cake wrapped in banana leaves with fish sauce on the side.

Name: Du-An (Lebuh Pantai)
Description: The faux cement wall works well with the warm wood furniture in this casual, relaxing restaurant, which is all about traditional Malaysian cooking: think nasi lemak, rendang beef, laksa, satay etc. Their skin-on mutton curry is a particular standout with its melty texture, big aromas and spot-on seasoning, hitting a sweet spot on the spice-o-meter. All ingredients are certified halal.

Name: DuKKAh
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only - lunch,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: A counter restaurant serving the cuisine of northern Spain. After spending considerable time in Galicia and the Basque Country, the chef drew inspiration from the guardians of those regions’ culture and food. Both regions face the Bay of Biscay, so their cuisines, blessed with bounties of sea and land, are delightfully varied. Overlaying these traditions with Japanese foods such as kudzu, soba and green pepper flower creates expressions of unique character. A marriage of Spanish local cuisine with Japanese ingredients.

Name: Duanima
Description: In a narrow and elongated dining room, amidst subdued lighting and modern furnishings, Chef Patron Luca Floris champions a truly convincing culinary line. Whether dealing with meat or fish, his recipes reflect contemporary trends whereby the harmonious blend of ingredients is easily and delightfully discernible. Occasionally, the touch is more creative, such as with raw tuna carpaccio drizzled with the renowned Japanese teriyaki sauce, wherein soya’s savoury essence shines, enhanced by sweet chutney of Sardinian camoni tomatoes; at times it’s more classic, as with the Saint-Pierre scalopp atop varying vegetable textures.

Name: Dubrovnik
Address: 721 Main St., New Rochelle, NY, 10801, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Nestled along New Rochelle's more commercial streets, Dubrovnik is a real find—with the added bonus of live Croatian music on certain nights. Diners come from near and far to feast on their items from the wood-burning oven. Equally appealing is the interior design. Next door to the owner’s cabinetry business, everything here is custom-made. Attention to detail isn’t just a hallmark of their décor though; the menu follows close at hand, offering the likes of shatteringly crisp spring rolls filled with tender beef and vegetables and served with a spiced tartar sauce. Or try something cooked on their wood-fired grill like branzino served with smoky vegetables and broccoli rabe risotto, before savoring palačinke (crêpes with peach jam).

Name: Dubrovnik
Description: In the heart of Dubrovnik's Old Town, a restaurant with elegant and refined tones that offers a unique dining experience. The chef uses only local products to create flavourful and fresh dishes, such as scallops with soft polenta, goat cheese, hazelnuts, and porcini mushrooms, or the mouthwatering dessert of puff pastry filled with figs cooked in Prošek (local sweet wine), vanilla cream, cinnamon and almonds. The intimate and quiet terrace is particularly beautiful. Located slightly above the bustling pedestrian area, it allows undisturbed enjoyment of the historic atmosphere and, in the summer months, creates the perfect setting for outdoor dining. You can order à la carte or, for a complete dining experience, you can opt for the 5- or 9-course "Chef's Choice Tasting Menu". Excellent selection of international wines.

Name: Ducasse Baccarat
Description: This private mansion acquired by Maison Baccarat was once the residence of patron of the arts, Marie-Laure de Noailles (1902-70). This exceptional location was showcased and embellished by the work of many avant-garde artists throughout the 20C. The restaurant room now resembles a library, with its shelves housing collections of crystal. Working alongside Christophe Saintagne, Alain Ducasse takes diners on a veritable culinary voyage, from his native South-West France to the Côte d'Azur, making numerous stops around the world. The kitchen draws on fresh, carefully sourced ingredients to deliver exceedingly refined dishes, such as their "Blue lobster, white, rose" or the deliciously indulgent range of desserts.

Name: Ducasse sur Seine
Description: Well, no one can say that Alain Ducasse lacks for boldness or ideas, as the Ducasse sur Seine once again proves. An electric boat, moored on the quayside of Port Debilly in the swanky 16th arrondissement, offers a gastronomic cruise that is both ecological and silent. At the same time as you discover Parisian monuments, you will taste up - to - the - minute cuisine, masterfully crafted by a kitchen team worthy of the best restaurants. Well done, mon capitaine!

Name: Duchy
Address: 18 Phipp Street, Shoreditch, London, EC2A 4NU, United Kingdom
Description: Two alumni of Leroy took over the restaurant's former premises in 2025 and reopened it as Duchy. The look is pretty much as was, even down to the great vinyl collection by the front door. The kitchen, which uses mostly British ingredients, is now more focused; the Duchy in question is Savoy, which occupied a vast area of southwest France and northwest Italy. That translates into dishes like grilled John Dory with mussels or spaghetti with sage and pecorino. Start with snacks like brown crab arancini, while you decide which dishes you want to share.

Name: Duck Noodle House
Address: 945 Soi Wanit 2, Talat Noi, Samphanthawong, Bangkok, 10100, Thailand
Description: Popular with locals in Talat Noi, this family-run eatery in its second generation specialises in braised duck and goose. The silky meat and aromatic broth pair perfectly with flat egg noodles topped with mixed offal – a must-try. Come before lunch, as the goose sells out fast.

Name: Dudockx Bar & Kitchen
Description: Architect Dudok is the designer behind this trendy 1930s pavilion. Each table overlooks the Hilversum Canal, which really is something to behold as you sit on the gorgeous terrace. The resolutely modern cuisine shows a preference for organic and local produce, yet remains down-to-earth. For a variety of fish dishes with Asian nuances or a perfectly cooked piece of meat with an exquisite sauce, this is the place to come. The daily specials never disappoint. The restaurant also rents out boats!

Name: Due Pini
Address: via Spinale 37/bis, Madonna di Campiglio, 38086, Italy
Description: Although recently restored, this restaurant has retained its strong Alpine character. The cuisine is regional in style and reinterpreted with an imaginative and contemporary twist.

Name: Duet by David Toutain
Address: 7F, The Ritz-Carlton, Bangkok, 189 Witthayu Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: In this elegant space, set within a serene glasshouse on the seventh floor of The Ritz-Carlton, lush greenery blends with a striking wooden ceiling carved with nature-inspired motifs. Chef David Toutain presents a seasonal tasting menu that is creative, delicate and distinctly plant-forward, with clever touches that balance land and sea. The zero-proof drink pairing is a smart choice, enhancing flavours without overwhelming the delicate nuances of the food.

Name: Duhau Restaurante & Vinoteca
Address: Avenida Alvear 1661, Buenos Aires, C1014AAD, Argentina
Description: The fully laden wine shelves and cheese room with its display cabinets exert a Pavlovian effect as you enter this restaurant in the Park Hyatt hotel. The best Argentinian products – the majority of which are cooked on the parrilla grill – are the main attraction here, accompanied by an impressive wine list featuring the country’s most acclaimed wines. There are lots of dishes for sharing, from the grilled rib chops and Atlantic fish to the slow-grilled shoulder of lamb. Everything is abundant here, both in terms of flavour and portions, but make sure you order a side of the delicious and buttery smoked potato purée! The restaurant is popular with a business clientele, no doubt attracted by the good-value-for-money menu, as well as by the more relaxed ambience in the evening. The dining room is elegantly appointed and the staff highly attentive, while the arched doors lead to a charming terrace with views of the garden. The perfect place if you’re looking for a gastronomic bolthole to escape the hustle and bustle of the city.

Name: Duke
Address: Doctor José Naveiras 38, Santa Cruz de Tenerife, 38001, Spain
Description: In the north of the city, inside a neo-Canarian style villa located in the gardens adjacent to the iconic Iberostar Heritage Grand Mencey, this restaurant surprises both for its elegant interior with a contemporary aesthetic and for its culinary offerings, focused on Japanese cuisine but with elements of fusion (on the menu you will find nigiri, maki, sashimi, robata specialities, etc.). In the bar area, several chefs prepare cold dishes live!

Name: Dulchemente
Description: A contemporary-style restaurant which serves modern dishes alongside simpler, more classic options, with a notable focus on fish. A splendid outdoor terrace for alfresco dining and friendly, professional staff complete the picture.

Name: Dulse
Address: 17 Queensferry Street, Edinburgh, EH2 4QW, United Kingdom
Description: In Edinburgh's bustling West End, this unpretentious spot offers an enticing combination of wine bar and seafood restaurant. Start in the ground-floor bar with a glass from the interesting international list, before heading upstairs to enjoy a celebration of Scottish fish and shellfish. The quality of the produce shines through, from Shetland mussels to Skye langoustines, sometimes enhanced by flavours from Jamaican jerk spice to harissa butter. Head to their sister branch in Leith to put your bib on and get stuck in to the 'seafood boil' experience featuring an array of shellfish.

Name: Dunav
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: At the foot of the old town of Ilok, the elegant Hotel Dunav (the Croatian word for the Danube) houses a bright dining room whose principal asset is the magnificent view over the river. From the summer terrace or through the generous picture windows, one may gaze upon the Danube while savouring dishes of local tradition reinterpreted in a modern key, with particular attention given to freshwater fish. To conclude, those with a sweet tooth may choose between taške, small pastry parcels filled with jam, or šnenokle, the Croatian version of the île flottante.

Name: Dunsmoor
Address: 3501 Eagle Rock Blvd., Los Angeles, CA, 90065, USA
Description: With embers glowing, flames snapping and smoke billowing, two ferocious ovens serve as the twin hearts and hearths of this Glassell Park hot spot. Much of the Southern-inspired menu must pass through them — oysters, cornbread, rib eyes and pork chops. Nearly everything here offers some kind of hearty, no-nonsense kind of comfort. Highlights include the excellent pork and green chili stew; grilled quail with pepper jelly; and braised greens that bubble away by the coals all evening. Long communal tables set with flickering wax candles hold the center of the room while prized counter seats offer front row views of a kitchen in constant motion. In the far back, find a calm, intimate wine bar serving a lighter, more limited slice of the dinner menu.

Name: Duo
Address: via Cavour 7, San Felice del Benaco, 25010, Italy
Description: Situated in the historic centre of the charming small village of San Felice del Benaco, Duo is the project of chefs Daniele Ghedini and Federico Pelizzari (the latter also oversees the front of house). Their personalised, modern cuisine is Mediterranean in style and features meat-based dishes, vegetarian options and fish recipes (salt- and freshwater), with a focus on matured fish which also has its own dedicated tasting menu. This colourful restaurant also boasts an outdoor space shaded by a pergola and surrounded by walnut trees.

Name: Duo
Description: In this restaurant housed in a historic palazzo in the centre of Chiavari, the owners have used the structural beauty of the building to showcase the skills of local artisans, resulting in a very attractive ambience. The modern cuisine is simple in style, allowing all the flavour of the ingredients to shine through.

Name: Duo Ristorante
Description: This elegant, intimate restaurant with subdued lighting is the perfect choice for a romantic gourmet dinner. Showcased on tasting menus and a concise à la carte, the excellent cuisine focuses on typical recipes and specialities from Puglia, often with an added personalised and creative twist.

Name: Duomo
Description: Bright and inviting is the dining room of this small resource aspiring towards contemporary culinary offerings—grounded in seasonal products—and numerous homemade preparations. The two siblings at the helm also unveil intriguing regional recipes with apt personal touches. For the wine lovers, an appropriate label awaits every need, whilst the setting further enhances the enjoyment: located in the town’s alleyways, just steps from the Cathedral.

Name: Duong's (Ngo Huyen Street)
Address: 27 Ngo Huyen Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 110211, Vietnam
Description: Doung's is low profile yet easy to find. Over two storeys, the setting is cosy with comfortable wooden furniture and intimate, soft lighting. The set menu is suitable for smaller parties, while the à la carte presents a selection of more substantial signature dishes from Hanoi. The traditional grilled La Vong-style fish is a treat for the eye, while the consommé of beef soup has a clear broth with layers of spices. The chef also offers cooking classes.

Name: Durham Ox
Description: For over 300 years this charming pub has stood in a sleepy Yorkshire hamlet. It's a loveable, eclectically decorated place with a thoroughly welcoming feel that extends to the cosy bedrooms. As at any good inn, the fire is roaring in the winter and a lovely courtyard is available for warmer days. The cooking echoes the surroundings in its comforting heartiness, with full-flavoured and uncomplicated dishes spread across an extensive menu and plenty of seasonal specials. Steak and seafood platters are ideal for celebrations.

Name: Dveri Pax
Description: Nestled in an idyllic setting, the restaurant is reached by crossing gently rolling hills until you discover a charming 16th-century building, once home to the Benedictine monks who started the winemaking business. Today, the winemaking tradition continues, accompanied by tasting itineraries in which the chef interprets ingredients from the surrounding hills in a contemporary key, all in the evocative setting of the antique brick-vaulted cellars.

Name: Dvor
Description: Few places in Split offer such comfortable and pleasant accommodation, both in terms of the quality of the food and the setting. On the shoreline, just outside the centre, this restaurant is distinguished by its charming tree-lined garden overlooking the sea, where shaded tables provide a very pleasant respite. The relaxed environment and attentive, welcoming family management contribute to a convivial and authentic atmosphere. The cuisine is Mediterranean, with a focus on the wood-fired grill, on which fish and shellfish are prepared. The catch of the day is displayed in a refrigerated counter at the entrance so guests can choose directly from the freshest offerings. The wine list is well curated, with an interesting selection and a professional advisory service in the dining room.

Name: Dvor Jezeršek
Address: Zgornji Brnik 63, Cerklje na Gorenjskem, 4207, Slovenia
Description: In the quiet, idyllic village of Cerklje na Gorenjskem, in the heart of the Kamnik-Savinja Alps, the Jezeršek family has converted several historic buildings featuring traditional architecture into a spacious hotel and gourmet restaurant. The outdoor tables offer a particularly pleasant dining experience, while small windows inside allow guests to watch the kitchen staff at work. A four-course or longer tasting menu is offered in the evening, and can be tailored to suit guests' preferences, with the option of choosing individual dishes from a short list. The cuisine places particular emphasis on freshwater fish and game.

Name: Dworek New Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: There’s a characterful industrial-meets-traditional feel to this restaurant housed on the lower floor of an imposing 19th-century manor house. Smartly dressed tables sit within a red-brick room with vaulted ceilings and exposed pipework, while modern artwork enlivens the walls and mature gardens surround the building. The dishes are equally impressive to look at and deliver on flavour too, with excellent produce at the heart. Their take on a tiramisu is a real winner.

Name: Dyletanci
Description: Tucked away in a quiet city centre mews, this smart restaurant is the brainchild of an experienced chef and wine importer. This background shines through in an impressive wine list with over 1,500 choices, including a brilliant selection of burgundies and grower champagnes, plus plenty of biodynamic and organic options. The cooking is pared-back and vibrant, utilising ingredients from their own farm and local producers. The friendly team enhance the experience and the lunch menu is a steal.

Name: Dynasty Seafood
Description: Elegant and traditional, well-appointed Dynasty Seafood should be on everyone's radar. As evidenced by the fish tanks, you'll find some of the freshest seafood on offer here, but there's also an array of dim sum delights and off-menu specials (be sure to ask for them). The menu is packed with choices, but regulars are rewarded by calling ahead to learn of special dishes requiring advance notice. From the classic dim sum selection (steamed watercress dumplings with shrimp and pork; shrimp dumplings), to the congee and soups (crab meat and fish maw soup with its intoxicating aroma, for one), to the sauteed bitter melon with minced pork and olive, all of the dishes served here show the strength of this kitchen team.

Name: Dámaso
Description: With his natural humility and technical expertise, chef Dámaso Vergara is the real epicentre of this restaurant, a feeling that comes to the fore when he sits down to curate a bespoke, market-inspired menu for you (including small-plate options). The setting is the tranquil La Galera country club on the outskirts of Valladolid, where the dining room overlooks the golf course’s 9th tee. Dámaso is particularly popular with a regular business clientele.

Name: Dáviro
Address: San Alonso de Orozco 40, Oropesa, 45560, Spain
Description: This simple family-run business, named after the initials of the owners (including their daughter), is a great place to eat if you are visiting the Álvarez de Toledo Castle, home to the first Parador located in a historic building. You'll find a traditional menu with innovative touches, carefully prepared and full of flavour. Our recommendations? The house classic: matured beef ravioli in wonton pasta and truffle cream.

Name: Dì Hoa (Hòa Cường)
Address: 62/2A Nui Thanh Street, Hoa Cuong Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: Run by a husband-and-wife team for over 30 years, Dì Hoa serves Da Nang-style rice paper snacks – khô and ướt – with various toppings. Their khô trứng, often described as "Vietnamese pizza", is a standout: thin yellow rice paper with quail eggs, pâté, pork floss and shallots is grilled until crisp. The appetising xoài mắm features green mango with fish sauce, sugar and chilli for a lively balance. A great port of call, complete with a helpful photo menu.

Name: Dôme Sur Mer
Description: You are well and truly in the Art nouveau district of Zurenborg, even if this fish bistro would be quite at home in a seaside resort. The produce is outstandingly fresh, embodied by seafood platters overflowing in briny odours, delicately flavoured langoustines, cooked to perfection on a teppanyaki or sautéed fillets of seabass garnished with a gutsy olive oil sauce… In their open-plan kitchen, the chefs demonstrate that such delicacies have no need of prissy details, courtesy of spot-on cooking and ultra fresh side dishes.

Name: Döllerers Wirtshaus
Address: Markt 56, Golling an der Salzach, 5440, Austria
Description: This place has a long culinary tradition to its name, dating back to 1909. The Döllerer family's inn is located in the town centre, not far from the parish church and the castle. The atmosphere is pleasantly lively and with a cosy, rustic charm. Food is served by friendly waitstaff in two dining spaces with historical vaulted ceilings or on the terrace to the rear of the building. The menu features mouthwatering dishes such as sturgeon with Piedmont hazelnuts or Rauris venison ragout, not forgetting the signature dessert Schwarzbeernock'n (blueberry dumplings) with sour cream ice cream. Delicatessen goods are also available for purchase, including meat products, cheese specialities and delicacies such as jams, Alpine spices, mustard etc. Overnight accommodation available at the adjoining Hotel Döllerer.

Name: Dùthchas
Address: 187 Great Junction Street, Leith, EH6 5LQ, United Kingdom
Description: Blink and you could easily miss this diminutive restaurant in an unassuming parade of shops. Given what a lovely restaurant it is, we therefore recommend walking through Leith with your eyes wide open. Inside, it’s a cosy six-table operation where the enthusiastic chefs deliver a set menu of satisfyingly original dishes. Sit back and relax as the team proudly walk you through seasonally changing creations, such as their clever take on prawn toast. Go for the wine pairing, which offers an enlightening selection of lesser-known bottles.

Name: Dún
Description: Nestled right in the dunes, a contemporary concrete building boasting striking design serves as the remarkable setting for Hotel Elements. Dún, on the second floor, mirrors this sleek aesthetic, offering splendid views across the dunes – the terrace is fabulous! The menu is devised by the chefs of Restaurant 212 in Amsterdam, and their influence is evident in the cosmopolitan combination of local ingredients and international inspirations. Delicacies such as cockles and sea buckthorn berries are paired with components like rigatoni, schnitzel and XO sauce. The superb prawn bisque, scented with curry and lime and served alongside dumplings filled with Dutch shrimps and black-legged chicken, are proof that versatility need not come at the expense of depth of flavour. Be sure to explore the tempting wine list and cocktail menu to bookend your dining experience perfectly.

Name: Dōgon
Address: Salamander Hotel,1330 Maryland Ave. SW, Washington, DC, 20024, USA
Description: Tucked inside the Salamander Hotel, Chef Kwame Onwuachi's restaurant named for the West African Dogon tribe offers a blend of African and Caribbean inspiration alongside nods to Washington, D.C. The tightly edited menu presents a selection of boldly flavored small and large plates intended for sharing. Each dish is presented with flair and nuance, as in the hoe crab, served in a shell with shredded crab and shito alongside plantain cakes with aji verde sauce. Braised cabbage is given a good char, then paired with a coconut vinegar sauce, while rum cake is far from traditional thanks to the surprise of charred gooseberries. A clever cocktail list is complemented by its N/A counterparts, and the wine list is especially thoughtful.

Name: DŪM
Address: C. Centenario S/N, Colonia Centro, Todos Santos, 23300, Mexico
Description: Look for the carved wood sign, then walk along the path through what looks a bit like a jungle to this oasis-like space. Husband and wife, Chef Aurelien Legeay and Paulina Noble, are at the helm of this kitchen where the menu changes every new moon and offers both à la carte and tasting menu options cleverly dubbed "new moon" and "full moon." The cooking is playful and delights in the unexpected, as in oxtail with a red wine reduction and a smoked carrot purée with roasted baby carrots and long carrot chips. Steamed potato ravioli covered in a creamy potato Dauphinoise-inspired sauce with crispy matchsticks, diced smoked mackerel and a sweet candy tuile is a perfect example of their out-of-the-box style that comes with plenty of heart.

Name: EGERN 51
Description: The location on the promenade is fabulous – in summer, tables on the terrace overlooking Egerner Bucht (Egern Bay) are in great demand! But you can also take in the vista from indoors – the window seats in this cosy modern restaurant are popular, too. The kitchen draws its inspiration from Euro-Asian cuisine. Featuring a diverse range of options, from classic favourites to Mediterranean and Asian-influenced dishes, the menu has something for everyone. Friendly and adept service.

Name: ELECTRIC SHEEP
Address: 4F The Warehouse, 867 Charoenkrung Road, Talat Noi, Samphanthawong, Bangkok, 10100, Thailand
Description: This fourth-floor hideaway with an edgy, industrial feel delivers serious cooking with a commitment to mindful gastronomy and zero waste. Even the decor and plates are made from recycled materials. Chefs Amerigo Tito Sesti and Yoan Martin craft a sharp Mediterranean-inspired menu, using only Thai ingredients, many grown on the rooftop. Dishes such as mackerel with smoked fermented chilli boast clever, clean flavours. Go à la carte or try the playful Chef's Cuts menu.

Name: ELEMENT
Description: Lively and very much on trend, this restaurant enjoys a very central location in the city. Beyond the bar by the entrance (ideal for a cocktail), the dining space has an urban, industrial feel and features an open kitchen. The modern dishes created here – such as "grilled pork belly, ginger spinach, fermented black bean sauce" and "zander filet, confit leek, bean purée, parsley, Jerusalem artichoke" – are visually appealing and impress with their quality and bold flavours.

Name: ELPIC
Description: ELPIC, once a famed grill house on Jeju Island, has found its new home in Seoul. Dry-aged, wet-aged, and beeswax-aged beef steaks are signature dishes at this steakhouse; its grilled fresh squid, caught in the waters off Jeju Island, is also a culinary delight. The method of grilling the steaks is unique: They are cooked over charcoal at a low temperature and cooled, with the process repeating for more than 30 minutes to maximise tenderness and juiciness. Pair the meat with wine for additional gastronomic indulgence.

Name: EMBERS
Address: 24, Lane 122, Section 4, Ren-Ai Road, Da'an District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: In the wood-rich room, a nest-like centrepiece above the bar is styled after indigenous hunting huts of old. The food, too, pays tribute to indigenous cultures, featuring native ingredients such as mock betel nut, fermented fish, millet and paper mulberry leaf. The tasting menu accentuates the terroir and seasonal ingredients while offering diners deeper insight into marine resources. Vegan menu available on reservation.

Name: EMOTIONS by Guy Ravet
Description: The classic elegance of the Grand Hôtel du Lac, designed by architect Ernest Burnat, is the perfect setting for Chef Guy Ravet's ambitious cuisine. The finest ingredients are used with mastery and skill, as in the case of the fillet of wild turbot, seared, with cauliflower mousseline, red onion and mustard seed condiment and beurre blanc with chives.

Name: EN
Description: Whether you opt for one of the seven seats up at the counter or for a regular table, there is no escaping EN's vibrancy. This energy is also reflected in the food. The set menus introduce you to creative Japanese dishes including an original take on tuna sashimi. The à la carte options, on the other hand, are more traditional. Whatever you choose, you can count on the characteristic finesse and richness for which this cuisine is world-renowned. The extensive sake selection is terrific.

Name: ERH
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed
Description: The initials E, R and H stand for water, rice and men (Eau, Riz and Hommes in French); a poetic name for an unusual venue that shares its premises with the Houses of Sake and Whisky. The conservatory style interior features a counter overlooking an open kitchen. Japanese chef, Ryuichi Utsumi, rolls out Franco-Japanese fare, depicted by a tokinokakera, a crispy golden flaky pastry pie, when he isn’t adding his own spin to the delicacies of Osaka, such as kushikatsu. Pastry chef Hazuki Okuno crafts pared-back, legible, exquisitely balanced desserts that revolve around the ingredient: pear poached in elderflower syrup; chocolate millefeuille with citrus fruit preserves. The splendid (and sensibly priced) sake list is flawlessly served by a competent young French sommelier.

Name: ES Cantina&Ristorante
Description: Situated within the Gianfranco Fino wine estate, this tuff building houses a restaurant on its first floor with large picture windows that look out at the vineyards and a spacious terrace offering views of the surrounding countryside. Here, chef Simone Profeta from Naples serves modern meat and fish dishes, often cooked using wines from the estate, such as in the deliciously tender braised veal cheeks served with a full-bodied ES reduction. There’s also a vegetarian menu that features organic vegetables grown in the estate’s own kitchen garden. The wine list showcases the winery’s own labels of different vintages.

Name: ESPRIT C. KEI GINZA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Chef Kei Kobayashi, renowned for his 3 Michelin Stars in Paris, moves onto the next stage with this harmonious blend of tradition and modernity in Ginza. Based on the concept of a ‘gourmet laboratory’, he offers à la carte dishes bursting with creativity. The C. in the restaurant name stands for both ‘cuisine’ and ‘creation’. The spirit of KEI breathes new life into French cuisine.

Name: ESSLIBRIS
Description: ESSLIBRIS offers a relaxed, elegant atmosphere with a fine view of the garden. The food on offer is a mix of Mediterranean and regional. Try the suckling calf fillet and ravioli with carrots, parsley root and shallots. The kitchen is pleased to meet personal requests.

Name: ESSperiment
Description: This restaurant serves up modern cuisine that combines influences from different countries and changes with the seasons. Dine à la carte or opt for a set menu comprising four or six courses. On Sunday evenings, a surprise menu is another appealing option. The clean-lined modern interior design and friendly service make for an inviting atmosphere. The terrace is particularly lovely in summer.

Name: ESTIMA by Catalana
Description: Located in the heart of the Old Town, not far from the cathedral, this tasteful little restaurant prepares Catalan-inspired dishes in an open kitchen. At the helm in the kitchen is Jürgen Birth, who skilfully weaves both Spanish and French elements into his modern set menu. For example, scallops with brandade are followed by his "Hamburgesa 2.0" with Bellota Ibérico pork cheeks. His penchant for patisserie is also evident in the wonderfully refreshing mandarin sorbet pre-dessert. Choose between a conventional and a vegetarian set menu option – a pescetarian variant is also possible. Furthermore, the "Kennenlern-Menü" serves as an introduction to the restaurant's cuisine, as well as the shorter "TAPAS menu". To accompany the food, there are select Spanish wines, which owner Jan-Hendrik Feldner takes pride in presenting – diners are spoiled with attentive, personal service.

Name: ETXOLA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: A restaurant of Basque cuisine and Spanish wines. Etxola is Basque for ‘mountain hut’, and with its stout beams and white walls, the interior plays the part. Basque-style woven tablecloths drape the tables. Etxola is renowned for its asado of char-grilled seafood or meat; bread shipped in from Spain accompanies your dish. The chef and owner-sommelier work in sync to bring you the gastronomic culture of the Basque region.

Name: EV
Description: In the suburbs of the city (not far from the École de Nancy Museum), this discreet restaurant is run by an industry professional. In a simple and welcoming setting, it strikes a chord with its unpretentious sincerity. Market-fresh ingredients are the cornerstone of this young chef's tasty, well-executed bistro cuisine: Swiss chard stuffed with goat's cheese, veal shank with black garlic, and a grape and walnut dessert. A charming, friendly little place offering good value for money.

Name: East
Address: 63-67 Nelson Street, Auckland Central, Auckland, 1010, New Zealand
Description: Warm wood tones and geometric floor tiles add visual interest to the spacious room with forest green walls, chairs and banquettes. The menu stars Asian-inspired vegan and vegetarian dishes from Cantonese dim sum and Thai som tam to Korean gochujang cauliflower and Malaysian Nyonya curry. For dim sum lunch, try "lo mai gai", or sticky rice with shiitake, dried tofu and bamboo shoots wrapped in a lotus leaf. Char kway teow is loaded with smoky wok hei.

Name: East Harbor Seafood Palace
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Wheelchair access
Description: Guests can barely get through this front door, where crowds pack in on weekends for dim sum. They wait patiently as an announcer shouts reservation numbers over a booming speaker—like a game of high-stakes bingo. Dim sum is a well-orchestrated affair, with steaming carts rolling by and waiters ferrying trays into the gold-accented dining room. Eyes can guide the ordering when it comes to the carts, stocked with authentic bites. Highlights include the siu mai, followed by rice noodles wrapped around shrimp and doused in a sweet soy sauce. Black bean spare ribs are flavorful, but don't skip the zongzi—tea leaf-wrapped sticky rice stuffed with pork and mushrooms.Things are more tame on weekdays, but that just means there's no need to fight the lines.

Name: East Room Restaurant
Address: Plassey House, Sreelane, Castletroy, Limerick, V94 68P7, Ireland
Description: Start with an aperitif in the drawing room of this whitewashed Palladian-style house, which sits within grounds of The University of Limerick. There's an old-fashioned feel to the place, with the grand dining room boasting ornate plasterwork, Corinthian pillars and an impressive art collection. Beautifully presented dishes have a sophisticated feel, courtesy of quality produce and a deft touch.

Name: Eastern Castle Noodles
Address: 235, Section 1, Dongmen Road, East District, Tainan, Taiwan
Description: On the bustling Dongmen Traffic Circle, this simple shop has been serving stir-fried eel since opening its doors in 1970. Diners can specify if they want their eel in a glaze or not. The ‘dry’ version highlights the natural flavour of the fish with smoky wok hei and sweet and sour seasoning. E-fu noodles with stir-fried eel is a must for most regulars. Other specialities include stir-fried cuttlefish, and pork kidney cooked in sesame oil. Dishes are cooked-to-order.

Name: Easy Bistro
Description: This beloved locals' haunt is tucked into downtown Chattanooga, and Easy Bistro is just that. Comfortable but unfussy, this spot from Erik and Amanda Niel has been around for more than two decades. They open early with oyster hour, and it's always a hit. The menu is American at heart, with oysters and small plates, pasta, meat and side dishes, all created with a seasonal mindset. Tagliatelle with Florida rock shrimp and bottarga in a lemon butter sauce is given a boost of texture courtesy of Appalachian rye breadcrumbs, while pot de creme or ricotta doughnuts are worthy desserts. .

Name: Eat Me
Address: 1/6 Soi Phiphat 2, Convent Road, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Though hidden in a side soi, Eat Me is hardly a secret. Since 1998, it has been known for carefully cooked dishes that join global influences with local flavours. The best meals here start with Thai food-inspired cocktails at the ground floor bar. They continue at the minimalist second-storey dining room or leafy balcony with the star of the menu—mixed clams served with nam, or fermented Thai sausage, and coriander lime broth—and one of the unmissable desserts.

Name: Eaust
Description: Alicia and Bram have left their restaurant in Plassendale to set up shop in a hip, youthful neighbourhood on the east bank of Ostend, opening this warm vibrant eatery decked in soft natural colours and materials. The culinary lineup, which slaloms between Belgian family favourites and traditional Gallic classics, errs towards local seafood, but also finds favour with meat eaters. Think crispy piping hot fritters, stuffed to the brim with creamy shrimp, or super fresh sole with a beurre noisette, fresh French fries and green salad… A feast of North Sea delicacies. We highly recommend the lunchtime menu!

Name: Ebanat
Description: Surrounded by vineyards, this modern restaurant boasts a beautiful location on the premises of Weingut Kopp, a Demeter winery complete with its own wine shop. As you savour classic seasonal cuisine that draws on international influences, you can take in the view of the vines and the plain, to which the name makes reference (the village of Ebenung used to be called "Ebanat", a derivation of the Old High German word for "plain"). Made with locally sourced ingredients wherever possible, the excellent food can be accompanied by the restaurant's own wines. Friendly and professional service.

Name: Ebisu
Description: As soon as you exit the lift on the seventh floor of the Square Nine Hotel, you will find yourself in this swish, yet snug restaurant (named after the Japanese goddess of Fortune). You can choose between a bar stool, the sleek glazed interior or the rooftop terrace that commands jaw-dropping views of the historic city. The score is 100% Japanese, including sushi, sashimi, maki (the tuna maki with jalapeno pepper is particularly delicious), tempura (soft-shell crab served with wasabi mayonnaise and pickled ginger), teppanyaki, at least one ramen, and much more besides. The desserts, on the other hand, are modern European in style. The adjacent bar also offers a menu of saketini-inspired cocktails.

Name: Ebisu by Kobos
Description: Chef José Kobos Cortés says that ‘we eat every day but to smile while we do so is something else altogether.’ Here, just a few metres from the Cebada market (in the La Latina district), he has created his Japanese-inspired cuisine (he spent a year working in Japan under the baton of culinary maestro Norihito Endo) around technique, produce, and the seasons. In this unpretentious restaurant, where everything revolves around a small sushi bar, he conjures up a single Omakase menu that normally starts with a green tea to welcome you (and which is refilled on request). Before starting the experience of tasting the food he prepares, the chef shows us the cuts of fish he will be working with and which he combines with his superb and perfectly balanced rice. Don't miss the hake Moshimono, steamed with sake and a hint of oil, or the fantastic eel nigiri, prepared in the traditional style and recognised by itamae Norihito Endo as his best dish.

Name: Echaurren Tradición
Description: The meticulously appointed dining room here can be considered a temple of traditional Rioja cooking thanks to its respect for flavour and dishes prepared with the minutest of detail. The extensive à la carte, featuring the signature dishes of both Francis Paniego and his mother, is complemented by a daily menu (midweek only) plus a tasting option. We can definitely recommend the famous soft and creamy croquettes, the prawn carpaccio, the lightly battered hake confit (cooked at 45°C), and the Cameros cheese on toast with apple.

Name: Eckel
Description: This family-run restaurant in Vienna's beautiful 19th district has its fair share of regulars who come for its range of classic, flavoursome Austrian specialities. The menu features familiar favourites such as Wiener schnitzel, seasonal dishes with game, but also seafood – the lobster soup is a highlight. The attentive waitstaff and cultivated atmosphere add to the appeal of this place. In summer, be sure to nab a table on the lovely garden terrace.

Name: Eckington Manor
Address: Manor Farm, Hammock Road, Eckington, WR10 3BJ, United Kingdom
Description: You’ll find this proudly run 13C manor house and its collection of characterfully converted barns located on a 300 acre farm. Attractive modern dishes showcase local ingredients in ambitious combinations – and for those who want to get hands-on there’s a cookery school. Bedrooms are stylish.

Name: Eclectic
Description: A centrally located restaurant with a difference, given that its interior design resembles that of a private house, with a small entrance hall, an access corridor and a pass-through kitchen overlooking the dining room where various works of contemporary art adorn the walls. One of the restaurant’s key features is its “culinary liberty”, with chefs Paco Chicón and Sergio Musso (the former in the kitchen and the latter front of house) choosing a different theme every year (Galician women, Countess Emilia Pardo Bazán, Origen, Tempus etc). This season has been built around the concept of "Déjà vu" —that sense of having experienced something before—, with dishes showcased on four interesting menus: Sementes (which focuses on the marine world); Pedras (land and sea); Augas (the sea, with seafood taking pride of place); and Froitos (the most comprehensive menu, which features all kinds of ingredients from the surrounding area). It’s worth noting that the restaurant is fully committed to sustainability through actions such as measuring their carbon footprint and making every effort to making it carbon neutral.

Name: Edda Brasserie
Description: With this tasteful brasserie in the city centre, Alina Meissner-Bebrout offers a delightful alternative to her restaurant bi:braud. The cuisine takes its cue from the changing seasons. In an inviting and laid-back setting, diners can savour the freshly prepared dishes of the day, including classics such as buffalo tartare and Wiener schnitzel. Options are somewhat more limited on Mondays. In summer, the terrace seating overlooking the pedestrianised zone is inviting.

Name: Eddy Vraie
Description: Chef Eddy’s last name (True) is indeed emblematic of his powerful, honest cooking, free of pointless frills or fuss. Generous helpings of good wholesome nosh await the hungry diner. Examples include melt-in-the-mouth terrine of rabbit, speck and foie gras and the house signatures are salmon smoked on the premises and seared foie gras. A restaurant with a soul, both in the plate and the decor, both of which exemplify the establishment’s commitment to authenticity.

Name: Eden
Description: Eden radiates modern elegance. Natural elements and hues, warm mood lighting and chic decorative features make this open space feel cosy and sophisticated. Dining here is an absolute joy. Chef Herman Cooijmans presents creative, dynamic cuisine that embraces bold contrasts, for instance, working a liquorice vinaigrette with marinated pouting, asparagus and capers into a chocolate dessert – he pushes boundaries, often with surprising results. Explore the expertly curated wine list for the perfect accompaniment.

Name: Eden - Belle Époque
Description: At the restaurant of the Hotel Eden Spiez, diners can savour classic cuisine that showcases regional and seasonal produce including homegrown fruit and berries. The hotel also has its own herb garden. Take in stunning views of Spiez Castle, Spiez Bay and the imposing mountains from the stylishly elegant interior or the covered terrace – both spaces are equally delightful. A shorter menu is available at lunchtime.

Name: Eder's Eichmühle
Description: A superb destination that fully deserves its popularity! One of its greatest assets is its picturesque hillside setting, complete with a beautiful garden and lake views – needless to say, the terrace is a big hit in summer. But the interior of the long-standing Eder family inn is every bit as charming; tables are laid out in cosy traditional parlours and the airy, modern conservatory. The service is friendly and professional with a personal touch. Top-notch ingredients go into sophisticated dishes that are served à la carte or as a set menu. The extensive and very well-curated wine list deserves special mention. The lunch options are just as appealing.

Name: Edie's
Address: 10 Beach Road, Carlyon Bay, St Austell, PL25 3PH, United Kingdom
Description: It's a family affair at this relaxed, friendly restaurant that’s sure to put a smile on your face. Nigel is at the stoves and his wife Kelly is out front, aided by their daughter, the eponymous Edie. Brightly coloured chairs stand out against whitewashed brick walls, the shelves are crammed with cookbooks and there’s a terrific buzz from the open kitchen. Nigel’s experience shows in the unfussy, well-crafted dishes, which deliver appealing and effective flavour combinations with notable clarity.

Name: Edinbane Lodge
Address: Old Dunvegan Road, Edinbane, Isle of Skye, IV51 9PW, United Kingdom
Description: Reputedly the oldest inn on the Isle of Skye, this characterful lodge dates back to 1543 – although it's had a subtle modernisation since then. The chef is a Skye native and as such likes to show off the best of island and Highland produce – as well as local crockery – across his imaginative multi-course tasting menu, where each dish is beautifully presented and carefully constructed. If you're looking to explore the local area, stay overnight in one of the bedrooms, which have a subtle Scottish theme.

Name: Edith
Description: In a quiet street near the Champs-Élysées, this restaurant is nestled behind the attractive red-brick and stone façade of the Hotel Padam, on the ground floor. The interior design is pitch perfect: herringbone flooring, green velvet upholstery, striped wallpaper… The flavoursome traditional cuisine – asparagus mimosa; roast chicken with broad beans and peas, or apple tarte fine with vanilla ice cream – is very reasonably priced, which is not to be sniffed at in one of the most expensive areas of Paris. A short menu at lunchtime, a little more choice in the evening. Pleasant, dynamic service.

Name: Edlingers Tempel
Description: This restaurant is somewhat tucked away in a courtyard, which boasts a charming terrace for pleasant weather. Both here and in the inviting interior – notable details include vaulted ceilings and distinctive prints hung on the wall – diners are treated to very friendly service and delicious regional cuisine. The seasonally oriented menu features items such as marinated fillet of Arctic char on beetroot tartare with a horseradish foam, alongside classics like Wiener schnitzel. The wine list is well curated and distinctly Austrian – expert guidance is available. Tip: Look out for their special seasonal set menus.

Name: Edoboy
Address: 728 N. Thornton Ave., Orlando, FL, 32803, USA
Description: From the same team behind Tori Tori and Domu, this casual concept delivers something sleek and simple—a standing sushi counter. It's not a gimmick, it's designed to be fast and fun, and it's a perfect place to bring friends. Be sure to arrive promptly, since you're given a set time slot and you'll be whisked into the space at the start of yours. Once there you'll select a dozen pieces from the selection of nigiri, seared nigiri and hand rolls. Some of the best bites include a sweet Hokkaido scallop finished with briny uni from Tasmania; seared sea bream with uni butter, lemon and sea salt; and spicy Faroe Island salmon with edo sauce, cucumber and fried garlic rolled in crispy nori. Dinner is rounded out with miso soup made in house from the bones and trimmings of the day.

Name: Edomae Shibahama
Description: A stylish eatery serving the popular fare of Edo. To discover the original dishes of the city, Hiroshi Kaibara dived deep into the literature. ‘Mukimi-kiriboshi’ (dried daikon strips in clam soup stock), a staple of the restaurant, was widely enjoyed during the late Edo period as a favourite to pair with rice. Shiba shrimp, so named because it was originally caught in Shiba inlet, is served in soup as a fishcake. Soup stock brewed from dried bonito flakes, without using kombu, is another traditional taste of Edo cuisine.

Name: Eea
Description: Named after the Ancient Greek name for Ponza, this restaurant is situated above the port and boasts fine views of the island’s picturesque houses and rugged coastline from its terrace. With an almost exclusive focus on fish and seafood, the menu features a balance of creative and more traditional dishes.

Name: Eel Sushi
Address: 118 Talbot Road, Notting Hill, London, W11 1JR, United Kingdom
Description: The owner of Dorian is behind this compact sushi bar where the Swiss pine interiors could convince you that you’re dining in a ski chalet rather than in the heart of Notting Hill.
