The dining room still embraces the classic steakhouse playbook, from dramatic dry-aged cuts on display to plush interiors and a menu layered with luxury touches like caviar, Champagne and Japanese wagyu. Seafood-driven starters continue to open the meal, including hamachi crudo with lime leaf and coconut dressing or spicy ahi tuna cigars topped with caviar and black garlic aioli. Steaks remain the centerpiece, from prime ribeye cap and filet mignon to an elaborate beef Wellington, while house-made pastas and rich sides like dauphinoise potatoes and miso bagna cauda broccolini round out the experience. Desserts keep the decadence going with options like sticky toffee pudding with brown butter ice cream or a towering chocolate soufflé finished with Grand Marnier anglaise.

Name: Fiamma
Address: Capella Hotel, 1 The Knolls, Sentosa Island, 098297, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant in an ultra-luxury beach resort boasts a rustic chic room, complete with an open kitchen, wood-fired oven (hence the name) and a terrace overlooking the pool and garden. Here, the chef offers a good range of Italian classics, embodying his personal history and childhood memories. His tiramisu, generous enough for two to share, is topped with a crispy caramelised sugar shell, a perfect finale to the refined dining experience.

Name: Fiamma Cremisi
Address: via De Gasperi 37, località Viadana, Calvisano, 25012, Italy
Description: Italian cuisine that strikes a balance on several fronts: while the chef’s dishes include nods to Brescia’s culinary tradition, they are also enlivened with creative touches. In summer, service extends outdoors beneath a gazebo; in the colder months, the main dining room is warmed by a fireplace. At lunchtime the menu is shorter, more affordable, and there is a business menu.

Name: Fico
Description: At Fico, Nadia Bruno pays tribute to Sicily and her mamma, Grazziella. The cosy ambience and vibrant, vintage-inspired decor make for the perfect setting in which to savour her sun-drenched cooking. The chalkboard displays a tempting array of authentic dishes. Think al dente fettuccine elevated with sea urchin, an intensely flavoursome semifreddo made with grappa, honey and saffron. Here, bold flavours meet Italian finesse, with no room for pretension. Don't forget to make a reservation!

Name: Fico
Description: When you’re a chef and you start to consider the idea of opening your own restaurant, you need to view it as a long-distance race and a dream that you can achieve either with the support of partners or by your own means, the latter option enabling you to achieve your goal in a much more special and liberated manner. This is definitely the case for Estefanía Maiorano and Martín Sclippa, the duo of chefs at the helm of Fico, a name chosen thanks to their Italian roots, “fico” (fig) being the name of their favourite ingredient in Italian, and a restaurant where they have won over locals with their cuisine in Villa Crespo. This dynamic pairing (with Estefanía taking primary care of the baking and pastry side of things) developed their culinary skills under celebrity chef Narda Lepes at the Narda Comedor restaurant. At Fico, they conjure up contemporary, market-inspired cuisine that usually starts with freshly baked sourdough bread and tasty canapés, followed by dishes such as grilled catch of the day, peas and fennel purée. The desserts here are always exquisite!

Name: Fig
Description: This Charleston favorite has been at it for more than two decades, but judging by the demand, you’d think they had just opened. Reservations are a hot ticket, and crowds hoping to grab a walk-in seat line up before the front door opens. Despite its age, the food feels anything but dated. This is a kitchen that knows itself, its position in the South and its place in the Lowcountry. Seafood is a strength, and the slow-baked red snapper is a good example of this; here plated with a classic sauce Américaine and wilted heirloom spinach. The chicken liver pâté is accompanied by turnip remoulade and pickled beets. End on a sweet note, say the Carolina Gold rice pudding with Johns Island strawberries.

Name: Filandón
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: If you’re looking for a restaurant in which to escape the stresses of daily life, Filandón guarantees a thoroughly tranquil experience on the edge of El Pardo, in the heart of the countryside but just a few minutes from the centre of the Spanish capital. In its pleasant, rustically inspired dining rooms, one of which stands on the terrace, savour traditional cuisine where the focus is always on the best-possible ingredients, ranging from superb fish sourced daily from the Pescaderías Coruñesas company to select cuts of meat and delicious rice. Many of the dishes here are cooked on the grill.

Name: Filemone
Description: The concept is an encounter between Italian home cooking and the seasons of Japan. Each dish combines Japan’s four seasons with the distinctive characters of Italy’s twenty regions. Ingredients come from Yamanashi and Nagasaki Prefectures, the home regions of the chef and service staff respectively, affording a surfeit of bounty from both mountain and sea. In the evening, the menu offers both the fun of choosing à la carte and generous portions; you can also order a number of single dishes and split them. Lunch is strictly set menus.

Name: Filia Ristorante
Description: In Borgo Trento, an elegant residential quarter just steps from the historic center, Filia plays the card of a modern, minimalist setting, where just five tables find their place. Tasting menus are served, with dishes also available à la carte. The cuisine is modern and creative, at times revisiting classics of the Italian tradition.

Name: Filipa 18
Address: Hotel Indigo Krakow - Old Town, ul. Św. Filipa 18, Kraków, 31-150, Poland
Description: This intimate, modern restaurant blends a small open kitchen with powder blue banquettes and walls decorated with bright artwork from The Polish Poster School. The modernised versions of classic Polish dishes deliver an appealing blend of textures, alongside a careful balancing of complementary flavours. Breads are baked in-house and local ingredients are sourced from the nearby Stary Kleparz market.

Name: Filippi
Description: Along the Old Town promenade, the open-air service overlooks the Pelješac channel and the islands of the Korčula archipelago, shaded by large Calabrian pines that add to the atmosphere. The cuisine, Mediterranean, classic and straightforward, is entrusted to chef Ivan Uglik who, with his commitment and knowledge of the craft, carries on the restaurant's usual high standard, focusing on high-quality regional and seasonal products. In addition to the classic five-course tasting menu, you can choose from a three- or four-course à la carte selection or opt for a five-course vegan menu. The small but carefully curated wine list focuses on the areas of Korčula, Hvar and Pelješac, with an emphasis on lesser-known producers. Excellent sea bass fillet with mashed peas, fennel and potatoes.

Name: Filippino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Opened in 1910, this historic restaurant with an attractive shaded outdoor pergola serves an extensive array of delicious local fish prepared in traditional recipes. Enjoy a selection of typical Sicilian specialities prepared by the Bernardi family, including the highly recommended “Nonno Filippino” fish soup.

Name: Filippo
Description: In this modern and elegant restaurant, Filippo chooses three products every day and creates a surprise meal for guests with these ingredients. An original idea which is certainly worth a try, but for less adventurous diners there is also a small menu.

Name: Fillets
Address: Unit 2323, 3F, The Storeys, 199 One Bangkok, Wireless Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Notable sake list
Description: Chef Chaichat "Randy" Noprapa's Kappo-style omakase goes beyond sushi, mixing cuts, grills and delicate bites. A semi-circular counter faces a kitchen bathed in warm white light. Set menus come with or without drinks pairings, and Japanese imports meet vivid ideas, including three kinds of vinegared rice matched to each type of fish. Experience the omakase menus, which range from 15 to 18 courses, for a comprehensive showcase of technical culinary skill.

Name: Filo
Description: From the splendid lakeside position, the view extends to the opposite shore, Comacina Island, and Villa Balbianello. An enchanting terrace overlooking Lake Como, surrounded by greenery with hills as a backdrop like a painting, is where you can savor Mediterranean-flavored dishes. Choose from three tasting menus ("Freestyle," "Classics," and "Vegetarian"). Or opt for the à la carte menu, with offerings such as purple prawns with goat cheese cream, berries, and bisque: an explosion of flavors!

Name: FinESSEN
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Wheelchair access
Description: Located at TAUERN SPA wellness hotel, this chic little contemporary-style restaurant is separate from the hotel but accessible from inside it. Seating is limited to 14 diners, who are served a six-course ingredient-led set menu. With his menu titled "Reise durch Salzburg" ("Journey through Salzburg"), ambitious chef Christof Schernthaner showcases regional and seasonal cuisine, highlighting exceptional ingredients such as home-grown woodruff, Lungau Eachtling potatoes and Alpine prawns. Wine pairings are available on request. The service is cordial – the chef serves and explains his dishes personally. N.B. Advance reservation is advised (before 11am on the day).

Name: Fine Dining by Phillip Probst
Description: Located in The Liberty hotel, this is a tastefully modern fine dining restaurant with floor-to-ceiling windows that afford a view of the small harbour. There is also a gorgeous terrace. Chef Phillip Probst and his team use excellent ingredients to create an interesting set menu comprising four to eight courses. The dishes are contemporary, yet classical in their foundations, and the wonderfully intense sauces deserve a mention. Shining examples are the cauliflower polonaise (served with an exquisite beurre blanc enhanced with Imperial caviar) and the beetroot with barbecued eel. The fairly priced wine list is another highlight. The well-drilled front-of-house team are friendly and attentive – they really pull out all the stops! Part of the same business, the restaurant next door, Mulberry Street, proposes a short menu of contemporary dishes.

Name: Fine Gueule
Description: In Nice's old town, opposite the town hall, this restaurant's newly refurbished interior is organised around an open kitchen and a counter where customers can sit to eat. But the real pleasure is to be found in the food, with traditional dishes chalked up on the board each day, including for starters the home-made pissaladière, devilled eggs or calamari a la plancha.

Name: Finger's Garden
Description: Firmly aimed at a trendier crowd, this restaurant has soft lighting and an Oriental feel. The chef here skilfully creates a range of dishes, including raw fish options and original fusion cuisine with a hint of Brazilian flavour. Gourmet diners will be happy to give full rein to the chef on his surprise menu.

Name: Fino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: The city’s Old Town plays host to this understated restaurant surrounded by attractive period buildings. The elegant interior benefits from modern art for sale on the walls and floral arrangements adding a pop of colour. An overtly seasonal menu means you might be treated to superb, full-flavoured deer when the time is right; but there’s a luxury edge to the offering all year round, with ingredients like Oscietra caviar utilised with skill by the chefs. The friendly service stands out for the enthusiasm and knowledge of the team.

Name: Finz
Address: Beach Rotana Hotel, 10th Street, Al Zahiyah, Abu Dhabi
Description: Eating seafood by the sea – there aren’t many things in life that can beat it. At Finz the fish and shellfish come in a variety of styles to suit all tastes, so if you want to feel you’re holidaying on the Med you can order fruits de mer or moules marinières, while those who prefer a more Asian theme can try the tempura roll or teriyaki salmon. The charming service is another delight here.

Name: Fiocchi
Description: Fiocchi means ‘snowflakes’ or ‘crystal’, an apt metaphor for that moment when great taste fills our mouths. Lamb wrapped in straw—a dish rooted in Waldensian communities of Piemonte—is served with potatoes baked in ash to draw out sweetness. The combination of ingredients from mountain and sea in one dish signifies the flow of nature that links forest with ocean. The true essence of Italian cuisine, offered to all in Setagaya’s Soshigaya district.

Name: Fiola Mare
Address: 3050 K St. NW, Ste. 101, Washington, DC, 20007, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Perched along the Potomac River, Chef Fabio Trabocchi's salute to seafood enjoys privileged views that never get old. With more than a decade of history behind it, this nautical dining room is built for crowds with private rooms and expansive patio space to boot. Still, the well-oiled kitchen keeps a firm grasp on its strengths, preparing high-quality seafood and pasta with care and class. Vibrant salads, zippy crudos and expertly grilled fish delight, alongside the signature lobster ravioli, a rich triumph that will never leave the menu. Such pleasures and views are not without expense, but rest assured there is substance to all this style.

Name: Fiorentina
Address: Balthazar Design Hotel , ul. Grodzka 63, Kraków, 31-044, Poland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: The beautiful vaulted, red-brick ceiling is a key attraction at this well-run and deservedly busy restaurant. An experienced chef takes traditional dishes and gives them a modern update, while using the best of the local larder and delivering plenty of flavour. Their house specialities include Dover sole cooked over a wood-fired grill and, as the name would suggest, Fiorentina steak, which is dry-aged for 30 days before being chargrilled and served with a choice of sauces.

Name: Fiorfiore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This restaurant occupying an elegant villa in a panoramic location with views of Todi and the surrounding countryside serves modern cuisine with its roots in Umbrian tradition. The extra-virgin olive oil comes from directly from the estate, as does some of the wine; there’s also an interesting selection of champagnes. Our inspector recommends the roast suckling pig accompanied by rosemary-flavoured potatoes, as well as the hazelnut cream, yoghurt sorbet and warm chocolate foam dessert. Quiet, comfortable guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: Fireside
Address: MIRA Earth Studios, Rancho Sordo Mudo Carr. Ensenada – Tecate Valle de Guadalupe Km. 75, Ensenada, 22880, Mexico
Description: Perched high up on the rocky mountainside, this chic restaurant in the MIRA Earth Studios is a total oasis built for bliss. A sleek pool anchors the space, which has cushy banquettes and daybeds positioned to enjoy sweeping views of the valley. More than a place to lounge and swim, the daytime restaurant offers a short but finely prepared menu of small plates that delivers in spades. Pristine seafood handled with care is a highlight. Queen clams with morita chili butter, grilled scallops with ginger and other lovely dips and bites match the leisurely vacation vibes. Another round of cocktails? Sure, why not? Be sure to ask about special events and chef collaborations during the week.

Name: Firewood
Address: 15 Jalan Masjid Kapitan Keling, George Town, 10200, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: The historic building with a lofty ceiling is furnished in faux industrial style, providing the perfect foil for the central open fire grill. Ask for counter seats to make the most of the smoky vibe and high flames. Both set and á la carte menus are available. Start with hay smoked seasonal mushrooms, followed by tiger prawn in sweet, tangy Nyonya sauce. Beef lovers cannot fail but find their favourite cuts here – consider pre-ordering the dry-aged steaks in advance.

Name: Firmamento
Description: Showcasing the allure of Japanese ingredients through Italian cuisine. Seeking to deepen his knowledge of fish and their preparation, the chef also worked at a traditional Japanese restaurant. That experience lives on in his charcoal-grilled sweetfish, hamo and eel. Meat dishes presented on white porcelain plates celebrate the elegance of simplicity. ‘Firmamento’ is Italian for the vast, cloudless blue sky.

Name: Firoo
Address: 66 Shengli 6th Street, Zhubei City, Hsinchu County, Taiwan
Description: Warm light, limewash walls, a wooden counter and an open kitchen make for a cosy space that encourages interaction with the two Taiwanese chefs, who met in Australia. Firoo specialises in wood-fire cooking, using different wood for different ingredients – Formosan koa, longan or lychee. The rotating menu leans towards seafood from the island's northeastern coast, which exudes smoky depth, served with fermented sauces and rare spices such as strawberry gum.

Name: First
Description: Somewhat tucked away, this delightful restaurant in the Zurich Oberland has plenty of regulars. One draw is the wonderful view – in good weather you can see Mt Säntis. The interior is an attractive blend of cosy and traditional, with more modern touches. In summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous terrace in front of the building. The menu changes with the seasons. Choose à la carte or take a punt on the four- or five-course surprise menu, which also comes in a vegetarian version. Friendly and dedicated front-of-house team.

Name: Firstborn
Address: 978 N. Broadway, Los Angeles, CA, 90012, USA
Description: Chef/owner Anthony Wang, a first-generation American at the name suggests, weaves in his own interpretations and influences at this Chinese American restaurant in Mandarin Plaza. The dining room is welcoming and comfortable, offering a view into the well-organized kitchen turning out dishes that are intended for sharing. Begin with a cocktail from their enticing lineup before tucking into dishes like tender tofu dumplings with sautéed shiitake mushrooms or duck sausage. While their main dishes rotate, if the aged duck breast with persimmon and parsnip is available, order it. Round out your meal with a slice of vanilla sponge cake with red bean, oolong and berry sauce.

Name: Fischer's
Address: 50 Marylebone High Street, Marylebone, London, W1U 5HN, United Kingdom
Description: The spirit of old Vienna is alive and well at this slick Austrian café and konditorei. It’s perennially packed too, particularly in the mornings as Marylebone locals pop in for their eggs and viennoiserie – or a slice of rich sachertorte in the afternoon. At lunch and dinner, the menu is a roll-call of Central European favourites, lead by the likes of stand-out schnitzels with perfectly crisp exteriors and succulent meaty inners – it's well worth adding the piquant Holstein garnish too. The friendly team run their busy restaurant with ease.

Name: Fischer's Baslow Hall
Address: Calver Road, Baslow, DE45 1RR, United Kingdom
Description: At the centre of impressive formal grounds sits this fine Edwardian manor house with charming bedrooms and a classic country house feel, which is now run by the second generation of the Fischer family. Diners are spread across two elegant rooms overseen by a formal service team, with the ‘Kitchen Bench’ experience available for those who really like to be part of the action. Local is key on the menu of classically based dishes, with Chatsworth Estate venison a must-order if you're here in game season.

Name: Fischereihafen Restaurant
Description: This is and remains an institution – something of a home from home for Hamburg's fish lovers, young and old! A constant stream of international customers comes and goes from lunchtime to evening. In an elegant setting boasting traditional Hanseatic decor and a view of the harbour, quality fish from the fish market is served at the height of freshness. Classic dishes include turbot or lobster in different variations, but the menu also includes Asian and Mediterranean-influenced options.

Name: Fisgón
Description: This restaurant, close to the Bernabéu stadium, is run by two young chefs with a great desire to perform (Néstor López and Carlos Monge, who alternate between the stove and the dining room). The proposal, with a notable traditional character, is not exempt from modern touches and embraces the national recipe book from end to end, both in terms of product and flavour. The most outstanding dishes? We were pleasantly surprised by the sea bass ‘titan’ and silky smoke, where textures are played with, and a trompe l'oeil, the Magnum castizo de madroños and pacharán for dessert.

Name: Fish & Forest
Address: 13 Grape Lane, York, YO1 7HU, United Kingdom
Description: The name is a clue as to this intimate restaurant’s focus, as well as to its sustainable ethos. Tucked down a narrow cobbled-street in York's pretty city centre, not far from the famous Shambles, its menu focuses on fish from small boats, meats reared putting husbandry first and game from local shoots. All parts of the ingredients are used too, so that the constantly evolving blackboard menu produces little waste. The self-taught chef's cooking has an ambitious edge, with dishes proving to be fresh and vibrant. The friendly team add to the appeal.

Name: Fish Club
Address: Andaz Pattaya Jomtien Beach, 345 Mu 3, Na Chom Thian, Sattahip, Chon Buri, 20250, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed
Description: Fish Club's location on a serene beach sets it apart from the typical Pattaya dining scene. With indoor and outdoor dining, the restaurant combines a pleasant view with a lively atmosphere. The menu reveals Western and Asian influences, and the chefs excel at grilling, controlling temperatures perfectly. The peanutty sriracha sauce pairs impeccably with your steamed or grilled seafood.

Name: Fish Market
Address: InterContinental Jeddah, Hussein Basalamah, Jeddah, 23212, Saudi Arabia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,No alcohol served,Wheelchair access
Description: The name says it all – take your pick of an array of fish and shellfish, locally sourced from the nearby Red Sea, all displayed on ice. While your fish is being prepared – fried or grilled as you like – start with a refreshing salad from the colourful salad bar or have the creamy fish soup. Finish off with a cracking crème brûlée while enjoying the views of the Jeddah Corniche and the magnificent King Fahd’s Fountain.

Name: Fish Shop
Address: 610 Water St. SW, Washington, DC, 20024, USA
Description: If the name isn't a clear sign and the location facing the waterfront doesn't give it away, one look at the sophisticated nautical decor will set you straight. The large space includes a semi-open kitchen but the patio with marina views is the place to be on warm days.The menu echoes their sister spot in Scotland with a clear focus on fish, though here it's given a Mid-Atlantic update. The Maryland crab crumpet perfectly illustrates that across-the-pond connection and is a perfect opener. The fish is sourced from the Chesapeake region and from a D.C. farming operation, and the menu presents plenty of interesting items, like sugar toads, or northern puffer fish, served whole and crispy fried. Order the Virginia peanut tiramisu for a twist on a classic.

Name: FishHouse
Address: Kimpton Kitalay Samui, 10/79 Mu 5, Bo Phut, Ko Samui, 84320, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Set inside the Kimpton Kitalay resort, FishHouse crafts à la carte European recipes using the freshest local ingredients. Take a seat on the deck overlooking the beach and enjoy the sea breeze and the lively atmosphere by the pool where sunbathers sip cocktails. Start with ceviche, bursting with fresh tropical passionfruit flavours and perfectly marinated diced seabass. The Black Paella with squid and squid ink is ideal to share.

Name: Fishball Man (To Kwa Wan)
Address: Shop B, GF, 183 Ma Tau Wai Road, To Kwa Wan, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Though local snacks such as shaomai and cheong fun are served, it's the house speciality that remains the main draw. Chilli oil or curry sauce – the owner makes all sauces from scratch – work magic with the springy white fish balls.

Name: Fisherman
Description: Just 300m from the beach and with a name like Fisherman, it’s no surprise that seafood is the focus of this cosy, candlelit restaurant, which also boasts an attractive terrace if you prefer to dine al fresco. Produce from trout to catfish is used in unfussy, flavoursome dishes – including a knockout paprikash – that are often adorned with sea herbs and hedgerow flowers foraged by the team. It sits within Villa Sentoza, so there’s rooms available if you want to stay the night.

Name: Fishing with Dynamite
Address: 1148 Manhattan Ave., Manhattan Beach, CA, 90266, USA
Description: This tight and warm seafood spot is located just down the block from the ocean. Inside, it has a decidedly beachy vibe, flooded with sunlight and colors that make it feel cozy even when it's loud and busy. Raw bar dishes comprise half the menu, and if the list of first-class oysters, clams, and lobsters seems overwhelming, the friendly staff will help make sense of it all. Dishes such as wild New Caledonian prawns with garlic butter and fragrant lemon jasmine rice or seared diver scallops with Japanese curry sweet potato coulis are indicative of the delicious, decidedly uncomplicated cooking available here.

Name: Fiskebar
Description: A Nordic enclave at the Ritz Carlton in Geneva, Fiskebar has made a name for itself thanks to its delightful fish- and seafood-based cuisine. The finest ingredients are sourced via short supply chains and skilfully prepared by an expert kitchen team. Diners are treated to fresh and healthy Scandinavian cuisine, enhanced with subtle Mediterranean touches – smoking and fermentation techniques are also put to good use. In a setting that tastefully combines rustic materials with more modern touches, diners take their seats at tables that look onto the open kitchen or afford a view of the lake. On top of that, the wine list abounds with pleasing discoveries, including a range of biodynamic wines.

Name: Fismuler
Description: Gastronomy meets interior design in this restaurant with an austere retro-industrial feel. Despite this, the service and ambience is relaxed, with a menu that features pleasantly updated traditional cuisine.

Name: Five Little Pigs
Address: 26 St Mary’s Street, Wallingford, OX10 0ET, United Kingdom
Description: Named after a novel by Agatha Christie, who lived at the nearby Winterbrook House, this neighbourhood restaurant is divided into three areas: the brightly coloured front resembles a modern bistro; a bar fits in the centre; and the rear sports an open kitchen pass and cosy booths. Sharing is encouraged, with larger plates such as roasted halibut and smaller ones like ‘spare bed tempura’ – using vegetables grown in the gardens of neighbours who have some space to spare. The wholesome cooking is joined by a range of local gins to keep enthusiasts happy.

Name: Five Olives
Address: 2/1 Pasak-Koktanod Road, Cherngtalay, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: The Thai chef-owner draws superb flavour from a wood-fired oven, turning out Neapolitan pies with puffy, char-flecked Canotto rims and airy bases. The menu ranges from homemade pasta and creamy risotto to prime grilled meats, seafood and crisp salads, including green bowls. The braised seabass with clams is light, fresh and aromatic. Dine in the cool, air-conditioned room or on the leafy terrace; both suit laid-back gatherings among friends or family.

Name: Fiz
Description: Malaysian owner-chef Hafizzul Hashim opened Fiz in 2023 to honour his native food culture. In addition to à la carte dishes and the vegetarian set, consider ordering his ‘full experience’ menu – an ode to his childhood with family recipes that pack a punch. The food is intricately crafted with Malaysian produce, and the main courses are served communal style to re-enact traditions. Also try the house cocktails and wine-food pairings.

Name: Flacon
Description: “Shall we get a bottle?” is something of a recurring theme when Pierre Guérin and his mates get together. This idea of a fine glass of wine in good company is the keystone of this friendly bistro, to which the chef adds uninhibited bistronomic cooking, presented in an excellent lunchtime menu and à la carte in the evening. Deftly crafted, respectful of the ingredient and spot on every time. For example, the chef might add a kick to pork, spinach and purslane in crispy puff pastry courtesy of a red wine and wholegrain mustard jus, a blend of spices and chickpeas. Rather than unnecessarily complex or fussy frills, you can expect to taste bold, reassuringly recognisable flavours.

Name: Flama
Address: Gran Vía del Marqués del Turia 63, Valencia, 46005, Spain
Description: The high-level cuisine at this contemporary restaurant close to the Mercado de Colón comes as an impressive surprise, thanks to its complete focus on fire, the grill and smoke – techniques which chef Eduardo Espejo manages in an almost primitive yet masterful way. As you look into the open-view kitchen it has a stage-like appearance (when they serve the last order the team closes the curtain to signify the end of the culinary performance), you catch sight of fish ready in their individual grill racks, as well as delicious meats and select vegetables that crackle over the embers. It is usually full every day so we recommend booking a table ahead of time.

Name: Flaming Mountain
Address: 13520 University Plaza St., Tampa, FL, 33613, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted
Description: Flaming Mountain's strip mall environs may be less than exciting but they save their sizzle for the food. The owners, husband-and-wife Hongfeng Li and Ling Wu, are originally from Shenyang in China's northeast, and the menu proudly displays their regional heritage alongside classic Sichuan cuisine and grilled skewers. Chef Wei Zhang sources quality ingredients for dishes that deliver bold flavor across the board. Portions are hearty, so arrive armed with an appetite for meals like Chungking spicy chicken, with a plate piled high with classic dry fried chicken studded with chilies and peppercorns. Cucumber salad tossed in a vinegar sauce balances the heady spice. Cumin-scented lamb done in a stir fry style is another standout.

Name: Flamme
Description: Flames and fire are central to this buzzy gourmet bistro. Entirely open, the kitchen provides a fascinating insight into how the food is smoked, roasted and grilled. The menu may be concise, but making your choice remains a challenge. Veggies take the star role in big-boned recipes. Slices of celeriac are roasted like shawarma, rubbed with pitta spices and flanked by a garlic sauce. Or would you prefer pleurote mushrooms cooked over the open fire with a tempura of enoki mushrooms and marinated vegetables? You can trust the wine tips of the smiling, spontaneous lady of the house with your eyes closed.

Name: Flaveurs - Domaine Mont-Riant
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: In the Jurançon hillsides, this handsome 19C white mansion with a slate roof and set in wooded grounds is enjoying a new lease of life in the hands of a locally-born couple, Basque chef Patxi and his Béarn wife, Marilyn. The couple has tastefully revamped the bourgeois interior, whose windows command knockout views of Pau below. The decor provides the perfect foil for the veteran chef’s talented craftsmanship which slaloms between tradition and modernity. All of which is anchored in a commitment to sustainable fishing and local producers, illustrated by cèpe ravioles served with a mouthwatering slab of premium foie gras.

Name: Flavors of China
Address: 3F, White Swan Hotel, 1 Shamian South Street, Liwan, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Generously adorned with glass work and art, this graceful restaurant befits the famous hotel in which it is nestled. All tables have gorgeous river views that jazz up the dining experience. The menu features the best from all over China, with an emphasis on Huaiyang and Sichuan specialities, such as sunflower seed-fed chicken in rice wine sauce and scalded shredded eel in oil. Oenophiles are bound to be thrilled by the varied wine selection.

Name: Flea St. Cafe
Address: 3607 Alameda de las Pulgas, Menlo Park, CA, 94025, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: This longtime café has been welcoming diners since 1980 and still feels comfortably like dining in someone’s home, with small rooms spread throughout the house and walls lined with eclectic artwork. A cozy front bar and relaxed atmosphere add to the intimate charm. The kitchen continues to focus on California’s farm-to-table ethos, building a seasonal menu around produce sourced from nearby farms and the coast. Dishes highlight fresh vegetables, simple preparations and familiar comforts, from fritto misto of market vegetables to creamy risottos and classic desserts. The approach is straightforward and ingredient-driven, emphasizing freshness above all.

Name: Fleher Hof
Description: A little out of the way, this traditional restaurant has a cosy interior, with all the charm of wood-panelled walls, old floorboards and wooden tables. Then there is the tasty cuisine, which includes flavoursome classics with a modern touch. Choose from the à la carte selection, or opt for one of the set menus ("Hof Menü", "Bistro Menü" or vegetarian). This pleasant restaurant is popular, so be sure to book in good time! N.B. Although finding a parking space may not be easy, it's definitely worth coming.

Name: Fletcher's Restaurant
Address: 27 Princess Street, Plymouth, PL1 2EX, United Kingdom
Description: It may be just around the corner from the Theatre Royal, but this warmly run restaurant is so much more than a convenient spot to eat in before curtain-up. From the good value lunch menu to the à la carte, the eponymous chef-owner, who is a local himself, knows how to cater for all tastes – and it’s clear that plenty of care and attention go into every dish.

Name: Fletchers
Address: Grantley Hall, Ripon, HG4 3ET, United Kingdom
Description: Tartan upholstery and woodpanelled walls lend a historic feel to this intimate restaurant inside the luxurious Grantley Hall hotel. The dining room boasts garden views and there’s a lovely terrace on which to enjoy an aperitif in the summer. The large menu is influenced by the local area and ticks all the boxes for unfussy, flavoursome food with dishes like cheese soufflé, beef Wellington for two and a choice of cuts from the Josper grill.

Name: Fleur de Neige
Description: Duck pâté en croûte with foie gras, calf's head with ravigote, pavlova with bilberries: this tasty and hearty traditional cuisine is served in a family atmosphere and – in summer – on the lovely panoramic terrace, with a view of the Chablais mountains.

Name: Fleur de Sel
Description: In this stylish eatery with a bar and an open kitchen, you’ll find the eponymous artisanal French salt on each table – but you won’t need it thanks to the owner-chef’s spot-on sense of seasoning. At this ‘bistro de luxe’ he delivers classical French cuisine with a light, modern spin – making it easy to save room for his signature Baba. Two set menus - we recommend the tasting menu for a global experience.

Name: Fleur de Sel
Address: 85 montée de la Bourgade, Cagnes-sur-Mer, 06800, France
Description: Fleur de Sel, taken over by a couple of young industry professionals, Alexis Cachat and Chloé Feuillet, has the requisite crunch, freshness and flavour. The promising pair met while plying their trade at a MICHELIN-starred restaurant in the Massif de l'Estérel, and are now delighting their own guests with meticulous Mediterranean cuisine. Taking their cue from the seasons, they offer good value for money: courgette flower stuffed with ricotta, olives, anchovies, fresh herbs, gazpacho and crunchy local courgette. Chloé not only provides cordial service, she is also in charge of desserts: think brownie with roasted hazelnuts, vanilla cream and candied apricots with rosemary.

Name: Fleur de Sel
Description: You will instantly feel at home in this minimalist venture, two steps from the French border and founded by self-taught chefs, Slava and Antoine. The irresistible duo bowls us over - his passion and food-wine pairings and her delicate culinary flair and generous helpings. Slava’s meticulous attention to detail results in balanced dishes that combine fresh, acidic, spicy and many other subtle flavours. The ingredient takes pride of place in each carefully thought-out dish, whether it be asparagus that is enhanced in a ceviche, or lamb fillets underscored by an emulsion of beer and meat juices.

Name: Fleur de Sel
Address: 581-1 Shizheng Road, Xitun District, Taichung, 407, Taiwan
Description: The chef worked in France and Italy for 30 years before opening her restaurant in 2003, relocating to this elegant space in 2017. She uses mostly local ingredients in seven- to nine-course prix fixe menus with a choice of mains. Thoughtfully composed and executed, the menus evolve with the seasons, distinguished by clarity of flavour, harmonious balance, and subtle visual appeal. Her signature use of wine, Asian spices and herbs lends her dishes exceptional depth and aromas.

Name: Fleur de Sel
Description: This restaurant in a residential area in Maintal-Dörnigheim brings a slice of France to the Rhine-Main area. You can look forward to experiencing French-Mediterranean flair, both in terms of the feel of the place and Patrick Theumer's seasonally influenced cuisine. The three set menus, one of which is vegetarian, are particularly appealing. Friendly service headed by host Yasemin Theumer. It is also pleasant to dine on the beautifully verdant terrace.

Name: Fleur de Sureau
Description: This “Elderflower” has taken root opposite the train station! Its gardener is a chef who trained under Jean-Georges Klein at the Arnsbourg and who rustles up food for today’s palate, based on fine seasonal produce : tuna tartare, smoked herring roe, green pepper and blackberry gel, or gently cooked suckling pork, pan-fried cauliflower and plum compote…

Name: Fleur des Pins
Description: Grégory Colantuono, formerly chef at Bistro' 50 in La Hume, has now opened his own restaurant in the town centre, not far from the Théâtre Olympia. Post-renovation, this typical Arcachon villa boasts a bright, modern interior, in which to enjoy a delicious, wallet-friendly lunch – diners can also opt for the wine of the week by the glass. The evening menu is more ambitious, with creative and masterful combinations of ingredients sourced in Gironde and more exotic influences: scallops, coffee emulsion, napa cabbage with mead vinegar and kimchi sesame; squab with red kuri squash, Swiss chard, pomegranate molasses and fermented black pepper. Booking essential.

Name: Fleurs d'Olargues
Description: It's a real family affair here at this attractive restaurant run by Danish chef Kasper and his wife Fé. The culinary programme comprises local ingredients, vegetables from the garden, foie gras and home-made bread (eg smørrebrød) and a scattering of subtle Nordic touches (salmon marinated in beetroot juice, hasselback potatoes). The bucolic terrace overlooks the 12C Pont du Diable ("Devil's Bridge") and the village, officially designated as one of the Plus Beaux Villages de France.

Name: Fliana Chef's Table
Description: The restaurant of the upscale Hotel Fliana draws in clients with its excellent cuisine, but it is also a paradise for wine lovers! It all starts with a strong first impression in the spectacular Wine Safe, where over 900 different labels from top wineries are stored, including fine wines from France, Italy and Austria, including a considerable number of large-format bottles. From here, you enter the elegant little Chef's Table restaurant, in which 12 diners can sit at a long stone table in an extremely high-quality and tastefully designed ambience. In the open kitchen, a six-course set menu draws on select ingredients to create dishes such as "mountain potatoes, spinach, truffles" or "Tyrolean beef, parsnips, wild broccoli". Chef Andreas Spitzer is also a cheese sommelier and will tell you all about the lovely little selection on the cheese trolley. The expertise of certified sommelier Thomas Huber, who is always on hand for diners, is on a par with the restaurant's passion for wine.

Name: Flocon
Description: In a lively neighbourhood, the Flocon brothers’ eatery is depicted by a warm welcome, a buzzy vibe and a Scandinavian-ish interior. The mouthwatering score is seasonal and often demonstrates a plant-based edge: burnt leeks, lardo di Colonnata, onion pickles and a vermouth dressing; cabbage stuffed with fish, pistachio beurre blanc, cockles and Brussel sprouts. Handsome cuts of meat to be shared set the scene in the evening menu: Normandy beef tomahawk steak. On top of all that, everything is sensibly priced, including the wines.

Name: Flor
Description: Set opposite bigger sister and Green Star awarded Natura, Flor (meaning flower), is a relaxed restaurant-cum-wine-bar built by local craftspeople using primarily Finnish wood and decorated using natural, compostable clay paint. Located on a busy pedestrianised street, it’s the perfect spot to escape the hustle and bustle thanks to its menu of appealing, freshly crafted dishes that are swiftly prepared. Choose from the à la carte or a surprise menu comprising bread, three starters to share, a main, a side and a dessert, with dishes including the likes of organic salmon with citrus-bouillabaisse sauce and honey pomelo.

Name: Flora
Address: Stableyard, Trelowarren Estate, Trelowarren, TR12 6AF, United Kingdom
Description: Arriving here feels like you’ve leapt into the pages of a fairy tale. Buried deep within the Trelowarren Estate (follow their online directions not your GPS), the period conversion draped in twinkling lights is overflowing with rustic charm. The roaring log fire welcomes you in and is matched by the warmth of the wonderful team. Produce from the Estate is at the heart of a menu that delivers a wonderful celebration of the seasons through dishes like roast lamb chop and slow-cooked shoulder. At lunchtimes, visit the simpler café and bakery across the courtyard.

Name: Flores
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Owner and sommelier Elroy Slijkhuis has transformed this family-run business into a cosy gastro bistro – the tables on the patio by the wine store are much in demand! He has a clear vision for this enterprise: The emphasis is on plant-forward cuisine, with a commitment to using home-grown/local produce and ensuring the welfare of all parties. Natural wines dominate the wine list. Chef Luuk Freriks's dishes tend to be daring – even unsettling at times. He painstakingly transforms vegetables such as carrots and beetroot into a remarkable "charcuterie" platter. Koji is a tool he frequently uses to create depth, for example drying beef heart in it and then shaving it over a cut of meat to imbue it with profound intensity. At Flores, nature's bounty is showcased in the most innovative of ways.

Name: Floriditas
Address: 161 Cuba Street, Te Aro, Wellington, 6011, New Zealand
Description: Occupying a large white building, Cuba Street's most famous – and most aptly named – eatery is hard to miss. The menu revolves around European dishes made using quality local ingredients. Come for brioche French toast, or green eggs 'n' ham for breakfast or brunch. For lunch or dinner, the 20-year-old classic Flo's fish pie, or Flo's classic beef burger made with house-ground Greenstone Creek beef are solid choices. Visit their website for booking details.

Name: Floris
Description: Chef Floris Panckoucke has forged close ties with local producers. Veg from a nearby market gardener and North Sea fish fresh off the boat are crafted according to patriotic Franco-Belgian tradition without fancy frills in a bid to let the ingredient shouts its name. Come springtime, warm asparagus is flanked by an addictive, velvety Flemish sauce (beer based), while in autumn, you can expect big-boned game served with a sauce that will knock your socks off. A maestro when it comes to cuts of meat cooked on the bone and whole fish and poultry, each dish showcases the chef’s savvily judged creativity curated to appeal to today’s tastebuds. A first-class eatery whose sleek interior is appointed with natural materials and a spot-on front-of-house team.

Name: Flour + Water
Address: 2401 Harrison St., San Francisco, CA, 94110, USA
Description: As the name implies, two ingredients create a world of possibilities at this always-packed Mission stalwart. Affable service, plus a space that’s both buzzy and approachable, partly explain the evergreen appeal of this humble space, but it’s really the kitchen’s vibrant blend of Californian and Italian cuisines that draws the crowds. An ever-changing array of expertly handmade pastas is the main event, with creative offerings like chitarra spaghetti made with sea lettuce, paired with manila clams, guanciale and crunchy pangrattato, or ginger-infused caramelle filled with creamy koginut squash, sauced with sage brown butter. The option of half portions helps to ease the difficulty of choosing only one, but for those seeking even more variety, a multicourse pasta tasting is a real treat.

Name: Flurin
Description: Flurin occupies an old medieval tower in Glorenza, a small hamlet in the Val Venosta which is surrounded by walls that also date back to the Middle Ages. Furnished in a modern style that contrasts with its old, vaulted ceiling, the restaurant serves contemporary cuisine that enthusiastic owner-chef Thomas Ortler prepares from carefully selected seasonal ingredients from the region. His creative and imaginative recipes include dishes such as duo of Wagyu beef (raised on the property) served with polenta, carrots and spring onions. There’s also a charming small outdoor space which must be booked well in advance in summer.

Name: Foc (Central)
Description: When Spanish chef Nandu Jubany opened Foc over 10 years ago, he aimed to imbue Catalonian flavours with a modern touch. After a recent move, the new space exudes the same fun, lively vibe, and the menu still features his signature tapas-style dishes, eg deliciously crispy smoked Cantabrian anchovies on charcoal brioche with salted caramel butter. Larger parties can try the sharing plates like seafood "Senyoret" paella with carabineros, scallops and squid.

Name: Focaccia Sandwich + Bakery
Address: 2300 Bee Ridge Rd., Unit 207, Sarasota, FL, 34239, USA
Description: The team rises before the crack of dawn every day to fire up the ovens and make trays of gorgeous, fluffy rounds of focaccia. From buffalo chicken with green goddess to prime rib with smoked horseradish cream, this bread serves as the base for satisfying, hulking sandwiches that are finely constructed and come in half portions for those with more petite appetites. The simple operation has a few outdoor tables along with counter seats at the edge of the kitchen, which also turns out fine soups and salads.

Name: Fogo de Chão
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The Fogo de Chão restaurant is much more than just a place to eat as it represents Brazil’s churrasco tradition that has won admirers in different parts of the world. The origins of this method for cooking meat date back to the gauchos who discovered that skewering pieces of meat on wooden sticks and placing them around a fire transformed a simple cut of meat into a true delicacy. Served as part of “rodizio” all-you-can-eat format, the extensive selection includes beef, lamb and pork, as well as the famous prime rib and dry-aged meats (only available on the à la carte). To accompany the superb choice of meat, there’s also an extensive buffet of salads, rice dishes, carpaccios, cheeses and sausages. In total, there are five Fogo de Chão restaurants in São Paulo, all of which boast a comprehensive wine list. The new addition at the Jardins restaurant is a space dedicated to cigar-lovers.

Name: Fogón Asado
Description: If the idea of a dining experience based around a traditional grill concept sounds appealing, this unusual, behind-closed-doors restaurant in Palermo Soho (another with the same philosophy and name can be found in Palermo Viejo) takes care of every detail. Beware that prior reservation is required and all food is served in one shift. Here, everything revolves around two tasting menus: one 9-course option, and a second much more exclusive menu designed for just 10 guests in a private space called the Chef's Counter and consisting of 14 courses (Provoleta cheese, Patagonian trout, chorizo, morcilla, pork belly, pine cone-smoked ‘ceja’, ribeye, and more). The two informative menus involve lots of constant interaction and communication between the grill chefs and guests. Everything the chefs do is explained in detail, from the provenance of the wood used, the feed used for the cattle, the best accompanying sauces, etc. All in all, a splendid and fun gastronomic journey lasting over two hours across Argentina’s most popular culinary art form!

Name: Fogón Cocina de Viñedo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Here, at the Lagarde winery in Luján de Cuyo, half an hour from Mendoza, there’s a total commitment on local cuisine to complement the wine experience. Between this restaurant and Zonda, which could be described as its elder sibling, there is a strong emphasis on history, the connection with the local area, and the setting in this stunning natural paradise. Access to Fogón is via the winery’s boutique, where guests can also enjoy a tasting of food as well as wine. In the dining room, with its high ceilings and a kitchen visible at one end, you can choose between two tasting menus, both with wine pairings from the estate, plus an à la carte with a clear penchant for superb grilled Argentinian meats (ribeye, tri-tip, T-bone etc), Italian recipes (we particularly enjoyed the al dente Cavatelli pasta with lamb) and creative cuisine. It’s also possible to arrange a scenic open-air lunch here with views of the vineyards.

Name: Folie Cuisine d'Émotions
Description: In a heritage edifice in the heart of historic Chambéry, next-door to the Château des Ducs de Savoie, this establishment occupies the courtyard of what is now a luxury hotel. In a suitably classy setting, the chef crafts a “carte blanche” menu inspired by the seasons and travel, together with a simpler lunchtime score. Depending on your mood, choose from the sun-drenched terrace shaded by stylish white parasols or an immersive experience overlooking the kitchen.

Name: Folie des Sens
Address: 36 rue de la Rollandie, Saint-Flour, 15100, France
Description: In the heart of Saint-Flour, a medieval village built of volcanic stone, this restaurant was opened by a local couple at just the right time! The concise set menu, with its three options (including a starter and a vegetarian dish) doesn't disappoint: everything served here is cooked from scratch. The simple menu with an eye for the zeitgeist favours local ingredients (while sometimes casting the net wider), such as lentilles blondes de Saint-Flour, which the chef prepares chilli style, adding a slow-cooked egg and a corn espuma. In fact, the chef has become a specialist in this particular lentil!

Name: Folium
Address: 8 Caroline Street, Birmingham, B3 1TW, United Kingdom
Description: Situated in the city's Jewellery Quarter, this smart restaurant is decked out in minimalist-chic style, with neutral tones and pot plants adding a soothing touch. It's run largely by a two-person team: Ben is in the kitchen and the warm, genial Lucy is out front. The cooking, like the interior design, is modern in its approach and allows Ben’s personality to shine through in the flavours and presentation. His short and long tasting menus change with the seasons and the lunchtime option offers value for money.

Name: Folk
Description: This East Nashville restaurant from Chef/owner Philip Krajeck is the more casual sibling of Rolf & Daughters. Warm wood paneled walls and plenty of light lend an inviting ambience to this dining room. Chef Krajeck's contemporary menu is driven by local, seasonal produce. Items shift often but you'll always discover simple-but-satisfying plates with items like stracciatella dressed with olive oil and topped with fresh peaches or main dishes like bluefin tartare or chicken Milanese. Naturally leavened pizzas topped seasonally minded items (perhaps a summery treat of fresh sweet corn) are always a good bet. Then, round it all out with something sweet like focaccia ice cream set with rhubarb jam and whey caramel.

Name: Folke
Description: Friends Colin Uyeda and Pricilla Deo have brought bright, delicious plant-based fare to Kitsilano with Folke. A wall of wine greets guests at the entrance to this small-but-sophisticated spot where deep blue walls are adorned with original seaweed pressings and dried grasses complement the tranquil, coastal ambience. The fully open kitchen turns out impressive items. Don't skip the irresistible bread served with kale "butter" sprinkled with sesame seeds. A main dish of tender yet crunchy cabbage resting in a silky mole made from potatoes has terrifically tangy and smoky notes. In addition to the selection on display, the Folke team features a small selection of natural wine and locally produced ciders, as well as non-alcoholic libations to pair with your meal.

Name: Follia
Address: Creu de Muntaner 17, Sant Joan Despí, 08970, Spain
Description: In this attractive stone property, featuring numerous designer details, the clear focus is on seasonal ingredients. These can be enjoyed in the glass-fronted dining room with views of the surrounding vineyards that produce the property’s own wine, and a small garden full of tomatoes, lettuce, fruit trees and aromatic plants. The cuisine here is centred around two seasonal menus (Rauxa and Follia). Our recommendation? We especially liked the Corazón de bosque, beef and cucumber vinaigrette, which is accompanied by three types of bread made in-house.

Name: Fon-Cé
Address: 15, Lane 233, Section 1, Dunhua South Road, Da'an District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: The warm-hued room sports rustic LATAM charm, depicted by cacti against a terracotta backdrop paired with vibrant, sensual touches. Named after the chef’s parents, Fon-Cé captures the varied culinary landscapes of LATAM with passion and delicacy. Inspired by buñuelo, a fried dough fritter enjoyed throughout the continent, the chickpea with chicken liver pâté and caramelised coconut sauce stands out with a bold, flavourful twist.

Name: Fonda
Address: 12 Heddon Street, Mayfair, London, W1B 4BZ, United Kingdom
Description: The foodie hotspot of Heddon Street, tucked away on the edge of Soho, is the setting for this busy Mexican restaurant from KOL founder Santiago Lastra. In Mexico, a ‘fonda’ is a family-owned spot usually with just a few tables – here they have supersized the concept, with diners spread across two floors of the bright, airy restaurant decorated with light wood, foliage and colourful ceramic tiles. Kick off with a cocktail from the extensive list before sharing dishes like slow-cooked carnitas with fresh tortillas. Santiago’s signature cheesecake is a great way to finish.

Name: Fonda Alcalá
Description: When you look at the renovated stone façade it may not seem like it, but this is a centenary business (opening in 1922) that now has the fourth generation in charge. The Alcalá brothers, with Ignacio behind the stove and Miguel in charge of the dining room, have updated the comfort and the proposal, which continues to champion a respect for the flavours of Teruel and the Matarraña region. Within the menu, well supported by the chef's suggestions and a tasting menu called Cuarta Generación (available upon prior reservation), you will see that traditional dishes such as the famous Fonda Alcalá-style local Beceite white beans or the slow-cooked Ternasco de Aragón coexist with other more modern dishes. An interesting fact: They still offer ‘Les perdius de Picasso’, half a wild partridge stewed with ceps and potato chips, a specialty that has gone down in history because it was prepared for the brilliant painter during his stay in the nearby Tarragona town of Horta de Sant Joan.

Name: Fonda San Francisco
Address: Gómez Morín 323, Santa Engracia, San Pedro Garza García, 66268, Mexico
Description: As the name indicates, this is a humble establishment, with an under-the-radar vibe that’s a bit at odds with Chef/owner Adrián Herrera’s outsized personal brand. But though it certainly isn’t the sort of place to expect fancy trappings or hoity-toity service, it’s just right for satisfying a hunger for hearty food and good drinks in a relaxed, friendly atmosphere. Accordingly, the cooking is rustic, celebrating the kind of homey dishes whose charms are irresistible even without elegant plating, from earthy, nutty encacahuatadas to empalmes filled with a supremely tender, juicy stewed goat.

Name: Fonda de la Confianza
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: If you’re looking for impeccably prepared traditional cuisine and a focus on quality service, this restaurant is a splendid option, in large part thanks to the presence of Paco Patón, whose awards range from a National Gastronomy Prize to Best Front of House Manager. His cuisine, which is built around time-honoured stews, a few offal-based dishes, delicious rice options and superb escabeches, is complemented by a good selection of daily fish and meat options, with ingredients sourced directly from the auction.

Name: Fong Kei
Description: A longstanding shop offering Chinese cakes and biscuits. The almond cakes and egg rolls stand out.

Name: Fong Sense
Address: 1F, West Entrance, Marriott Nanjing South Hotel, 1519 Shuanglong Avenue, Jiangning, Nanjing, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant on the shore of Baijia Lake is helmed by renowned chef Zhou who captures the quintessence of Huaiyang cuisine courtesy of modern French techniques and plating. His set menu mirrors the seasons and can include portabella consommé with crispy sesame twists and a tofu chrysanthemum that entails exquisite knife skills. The set menu comes with two or three cups of Chinese tea and wine pairing is also available.

Name: Fong Wei Wu
Address: 82 Banawe Street corner Samat Street, Quezon - Metro Manila, The Philippines
Description: This cosy family-run spot serves home-style Taiwanese food. It is managed by a Taiwanese female chef who specially selects Taiwanese condiments such as soy sauce to recreate authentic Taiwanese flavors. The daily-changing spread includes 15-20 dishes. Don't miss the fried bihon – rice noodles stir-fried with pork and cabbage are topped with flavoursome minced pork to create a harmony of soy umami and vegetable sweetness.

Name: Fontané
Address: Carrer Major, Sant Julià de Ramis, 17481, Spain
Description: Fontané is located on the summit of the Sants Metges mountain in a location that the restaurant describes as “between heaven and earth”. Here, the focus is on the traditional Catalan cuisine that the Roca brothers, in a tribute to their mother (Montserrat Fontané), conjure up at the Hotel Esperit Roca, in the Castillo de Sant Julià de Ramis. The dining room, with its wooden deck and impressive views, provides the setting for cuisine that evokes the delicious dishes that their mother used to make at the original Can Roca, and which they have recreated here with a modern twist. We were pleasantly surprised by the “suquet de cabracho”, with a tomato tartare base unlike the usual preparation of this typical fish stew.

Name: Food Leigh-On-Sea
Address: 92 Leigh Road, Leigh-on-Sea, SS9 1BU, United Kingdom
Description: In a charming little seaside town, tucked away among the shops, is this narrow restaurant with a rustic look, that's given a cosy vibe by the friendly, engaging manner in which it's run. The creative, eye-catching dishes are full of flavour and focus on wellbeing and ingredient provenance. The format changes depending on when you visit, with tasting menus in the evening, a 'menu du jour' at lunchtime and a roast lunch on Sundays. Vegan diners are catered for too, with plant-based options at all times.

Name: Food Street Fried Kway Teow Mee
Address: Chinatown Complex Market & Food Centre, #02-173, 335 Smith Street, 050335, Singapore
Description: Loaded with wok hei, their kway teow mee is ribbon rice noodles, egg noodles, bean sprouts and scrambled egg tossed in a secret sauce. For toppings, choose clams only, or a mix of seafood with fish, squid, shrimps and clams.

Name: Food Terminal
Description: Chef/owner Amy Wong's Food Terminal may have multiple locations, but the Buford Highway original will always stand out from the rest. Located within a cavernous space that sports a contemporary feel (think exposed ducts, charcoal-gray walls and metal chairs), it's designed to resemble a night market. As for the food, it's Malaysian at its core. The massive menu is matched only by the portions, perfect for enjoying family style. It's a celebration of the cultural mash-up that is Malaysia with dishes like garlic noodles, made in house and tossed in a garlic sauce with spinach and mushrooms. It's so good it's nearly impossible to put your chopsticks down. Fried curry chicken nasi lemak features their take on the classic dish.

Name: Food by Fire
Address: 27F, Ad Lib Hotel, 999 Sri Chant Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: With its striking tiger mural on a deep red wall and U-shaped counter around an open kitchen, this Isan grillhouse celebrates northeastern produce in bold, contemporary style. Fire and fermentation anchor a steak and grill menu that is packed with local flavours, thanks to close ties with farmers and home-grown herbs. We highly recommend the Khon Kaen chocolate-fed beef, served with a spicy red-wine sauce, house-made papaya kimchi and an eggplant dip.

Name: Fook Cheow Cafe
Description: Located on a street corner, the signage is inconspicuous, but its popularity with locals mean that it can’t be missed. This simple eatery has been open for some 30 years, but only in the mornings, which makes it just the ticket to sample the local breakfast. The signature dish, koay teow th'ng, is rice noodle soup with fish balls, deep-fried garlic, shredded chicken and lettuce. The tasty soup broth is made from hen and pork bones.

Name: Foong
Address: 53 Soi Thong Lo 19, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Foong is a trendy local spot serving seasonal Thai set menus that change monthly. The homely yet skilfully executed cuisine focuses on familiar flavours and quality ingredients. Each family-style dining experience features around 10 shared plates – from nam prik, spicy salads, stir-fried and deep-fried dishes, and curries to hearty soups – finishing with a simple Thai dessert. Bookings are by reservation only, with a minimum of four guests required.

Name: Forchetta
Address: 2F, 36 Huizhong 7th Street, Xitun District, Taichung, 407, Taiwan
Description: Forchetta is popular with those in the know, but it's easy for first-timers to miss the sign. A vet by training, the head chef has a real passion for food and gardening, as demonstrated by his East-meets-West creations and miniature garden. The single set menu includes a choice of two mains. With prior notice, the chef can prepare different mains for returning customers. His tasty house-made tagliolini works beautifully with the Taiwanese sauce.

Name: Forde
Address: 7 Town Street, Horsforth, LS18 5LJ, United Kingdom
Description: Experienced chef Matt Healy – a onetime 'MasterChef: The Professionals' contestant – has come home to Horsforth to open this rustic bistro and wine bar. His appealing menu features appetising small plates with Mediterranean influences; two or three per person works well, and there are some well-chosen wines, craft beers and cocktails too.

Name: Forellenhof
Description: The diversity of the Bareiss culinary empire knows no bounds! The historic and idyllically located Forellenhof has been transformed into a charming restaurant open to all-comers from 11:30 am to 5: 30 pm, Fridays from 11:30 am. to 10 pm. The emphasis here is on freshwater fish – from their own fish farm – but they also serve snacks. Tip: you can buy fresh fish in the Forellenlädle (9am-noon).

Name: Foresta
Address: Via Litoranea 2, Marina di Pisa, 56128, Italy
Description: Overlooking the Tyrrhenian Sea, all the tables at this restaurant offer sea views, whether you’re sitting in the winter dining room or on the outdoor summer terrace. The menu here focuses on top-quality fish dishes, which are classic in style, as is the background music and wine list, although the desserts have a more imaginative flavour.

Name: Forma
Description: Chic and sultry, this Södermalm spot delivers the look and vibe of a bar, with the added bonus of flavoursome small plates. The cooking is bang on-trend, blending Nordic and French influences with pan-Asian elements including Korean kimchi, Chinese wontons and a daily selection of Japanese mochi for dessert. If you’re an indecisive diner, go for the keenly priced tasting menu to appreciate the full breadth of the kitchen's talents. Well-versed, professional service is the icing on the cake.

Name: Forme Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Forme Restaurant is a modern, ever-evolving venue located outside the city center within the Atena educational complex, which also houses the Sottoforme bistrot. At the helm is Abruzzese chef Arianna Gatti: her cooking is a contemporary narrative, vivid in color and bold in flavor, rooted in Italian tradition yet reimagined with restraint and sensitivity. Her dishes evoke the comforts of home: the spice-scented ventricina, Navelli saffron butter that gently caresses the palate, and artisanal Abruzzese spaghettone celebrating authentic simplicity.

Name: Forno da Telha
Address: Estrada Penedo do Ouro Lote 18 A, Évora, 7005-001, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: At Évora’s northern exit, in an attractive rehabilitated building that once housed a roof-tile factory, this is one of those restaurants that, at first glance alone, invites you to step through its doors. The proposal, under the guidance of the award-winning chef Miguel Rocha Vieira, clearly revolves around Alentejo cuisine, reinterpreting it from a contemporary perspective based on the latest techniques. On the menu, complemented by an executive menu (weekdays), you will find dishes such as Bacalhau com grão (salt-cod with chickpeas), chouriço and estufadinho de línguas e samos (slow-stewed tongues and sprouts), or Porco Preto (black pork), presa marinada no alguidar (pork loin marinated in an earthenware bowl), “miguinhas” de batata (little potato crumbs) and grilled heart of lettuce. Did you know? It has a terrace, bar and its own pool, making it ideal for a longer, more informal outing.

Name: Forsthaus Ilkahöhe
Description: The idyllic hilltop location with its fantastic view across Tutzing to the lake is a huge draw of this restaurant – the terrace is fabulous! This converted forester's lodge has an attractive, upscale interior that combines modern style and regional touches. The menu features seasonal dishes made with select ingredients. Mediterranean and international influences are as prominent as the regional classics. While only a small selection of simpler dishes is served at lunchtime, things take a more ambitious turn in the evening. There is also a self-service beer garden.

Name: Forsythia
Description: For an unabashed, full-steam-ahead celebration of French cooking, look to Chef Christopher Kearse at this relaxed, modern bistro. Cute tile flooring, globe lights and simple tables set the stage for tempura frog legs with saffron aioli, escargot with Pernod-almond butter and yellow corn vichyssoise with crab. Some opt for a seat at the bar in the front for snacks and a drink or two. Open since 2019, the dining room further in offers clear views of the open kitchen, which shows a fine hand with the likes of dry-aged duck and halibut poached in olive oil. To finish, think chocolate mousse or peach and apricot mille-feuille.

Name: Forsythia
Address: 9 Stanton St., New York, NY, 10002, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Open since 2020, this intimate, Lower East Side nook is all about pasta. Set menus begin with warm, pillow-like slices of fresh-baked focaccia. Take a look around – just about everyone is after the longstanding fried cacio pepe risotto suppli made with buffalo mozzarella and pecorino. Seasonal preparations can be as satisfying as they are generously portioned, and past highlights include grilled octopus with jimmy nardello peppers. The main event is, of course, the pasta. Agnolotti packed with short rib and tossed in butter has few equals, and the carbonara never disappoints. The restaurant also offers cooking classes during the week for those looking to up their game at home.

Name: Fort Oak
Address: 1011 Fort Stockton Dr., San Diego, CA, 92103, USA
Description: Named for the majestic oaks of nearby Presidio Park, this Mission Hills eatery helmed by Chef Brad Wise is perfect for happy hour or an intimate "chef's experience" tasting. Just don't let the fire fool you—Fort Oak is no log cabin. This historic, former car dealership is bright and airy, complete with a glamorous horseshoe-shaped bar and sleek, mid-century vibe. Chef Wise's menu is one intended for sharing. Try a bit of everything, from raw seafood appetizers or towers to hot appetizers like their cinnamon heavy lamb merguez kefta with a pistachio muhammara. Heritage pork chop with roasted Brussels sprouts and potatoes shows off the kitchen's flair for the flame, while desserts like apple crisp served hot in an iron skillet are the epitome of comfort.

Name: Forte del 48
Address: Via Carlo Vizzotto 1, San Donà di Piave, 30027, Italy
Description: This pleasant restaurant started life in 1848 as a bastion used by the Habsburg army and was later transformed into an inn. Recognised as a “Locale Storico Veneto”, it’s now run by the third generation of the De Faveri family who serve traditional meat and fish dishes here. Comfortable guestrooms are also available for guests wishing to extend their stay.

Name: Forthuber in Gstaig
Description: This inviting restaurant is run by Christoph Forthuber, who brings experience from prestigious kitchens to the table. Since spring 2025, he has been serving up flavoursome seasonal dishes crafted from locally sourced ingredients. Diners can choose between two set menus – one hearty, one light – or go à la carte. The wallet-friendly lunch deal is a hit. Diners are treated to friendly and adept service in a cosy setting – the long table in front of the decorative wine cabinet is ideal for larger parties. In summer, tables are set up in the shade of trees in the lovely garden, where there is also a gazebo for special occasions or additional needs. Guestrooms are available nearby.

Name: Fortu
Address: The Ponce De Leon Hotel, 97 Central Ave., St. Petersburg, FL, 33701, USA
Description: This attractive, high-energy dining room in downtown St Petersburg is cool in all the right ways. Handsome wood finishes, sleek lighting, and large arched mirrors cut a sharp figure at the base of the Ponce de Leon Hotel. Most importantly, this Pan-Asian kitchen backs up all this style with proper substance. Skip the raw bar in favor of plump, spicy pork wontons showered with crispy garlic and chili crisp. Glazed carrots in kimchi butter are both satisfying and sophisticated. And though the restaurant isn’t technically a steakhouse, this might be the best place around to splurge on beef. Beautifully marbled cuts of Japanese A5 wagyu are seared and seasoned to exacting measure. Desserts, like walnut and apple torte, make for a sweet finale.

Name: Fortuin
Description: Huge vats of beer and a remarkable tree sculpture immediately catch the eye as you step foot in the Staminée. Continue on to the elegant brasserie, where a trendy playlist and hip décor set the cosmopolitan scene. The chef puts his own spin on classical recipes. Examples of Fortuin’s focus on gutsy, authentic flavour include house-made fritters stuffed with hand-shelled grey shrimp or fork-tender cutlets flanked by crispy, piping-hot French fries cooked in tallow. Parents may be interested to know that children are more than welcome (special menu) and that there is a playground almost next-door to the restaurant. Accessible and easy-going set the scene here.

Name: Fortune Garden
Address: 504-506, 5F, Phase 2, Star Avenue, 1766 Wentao Road, Binjiang, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: This modern, cosy restaurant sits on the top floor of a shopping mall. The menu showcases the best of Cantonese cooking with sophistication, astuteness and precision. Their dim sum lunch is a must, as are the barbecued meats. The honey-glazed cha siu pork, for instance, boasts the perfect ratio of fat and lean meat, as well as smoky and crispy charred edges. Plum sauce on the side cuts through the richness. Book ahead for private rooms.

Name: Fortune Long Beijing Bean Sauce Noodles (East Xinglong Street)
Address: 56 East Xinglong Street, Dongcheng, Beijing, 100062, Chinese Mainland
Description: Since 1994, this restaurant has been synonymous with authentic zhajiangmian. It moved to this three-storey location over ten years ago and is always jam-packed. Once you step in the shop, you can’t miss the two caldrons of rich and flavoursome soybean sauce made fresh every day, to be served on the side with house-made noodles. Beijing snacks such as fried pork balls, and blanched ox tripe in sesame sauce are other solid options.

Name: Fou du Goût
Description: Fou du Goût manages to be both chic and cosy and the conservatory is definitely the best spot in the house. Thomas Cocquyt has a penchant for giving familiar flavours an exotic twist – chicken cooked in a spicy masala sauce, or pan-fried plaice with smoked eel and a beurre blanc infused with a yuzu gel for a tangy citrus burst. But you will also find sole meunière with fresh fries and venison in Arlequin sauce. The chef is a past master in the art of balancing bold flavours with a touch of intrigue. A firm favourite in the Meetjesland region!

Name: Found Oyster
Address: 4880 Fountain Ave., Los Angeles, CA, 90029, USA
Description: There is no ocean in sight from this busy corner of East Hollywood, and yet, this no-frills bar trades in impeccably sourced and prepared seafood. Opened in 2019, the cozy restaurant is minimally decorated and has kept a full house since the very beginning. From sea urchin to razor clams to freshly harvested scallops from Maine, this team knows that such treasures need little more than a drizzle of olive oil or squeeze of lemon to sing. Lobster rolls, tostadas, trout dip — the temptations are endless, down to the oysters sourced from the general manager’s family oyster farm.

Name: Fouquet's
Address: Louvre Abu Dhabi, Saadiyat Cultural District 1, Al Saadiyat Island, Abu Dhabi
Description: As befits the remarkable Louvre Abu Dhabi, its restaurant is not only one with a famous name serving classic French cuisine, but is also one decidedly grander than its ‘brasserie’ moniker would suggest. The huge, laminated menu offers something for everyone, from glazed duck breast to chicken supreme; finishing with crêpes Suzette will set you up nicely for more gallery viewings.

Name: Four Flamingos, A Richard Blais Florida Kitchen
Address: Hyatt Regency Grand Cypress Resort, 1 Grand Cypress Blvd., Orlando, FL, 32836, USA
Description: This exciting concept from Chef Richard Blais is nestled in the Hyatt Regency Grand Cypress property. Follow the footpath that leads over a bridge and towards the bright pink entrance, fronted by a waterfall. This retreat radiates a calming, coastal vibe with design details like plentiful windows, warm wood and pops of color. Fittingly, the menu is contemporary Americana meets the tropics. The chef's focus is on seasonal, bold and creative flavors, as in savory-sweet smoked salmon croquetas with sweet plantain and red pepper relish in an Old Bay aioli. Big eaters know to save room for mains like swordfish, grouper and deliciously spiced mojo chicken.Couples rejoice, as this is a perfect place to splurge, celebrate and eat to your heart's content.

Name: Four Kings
Address: 710 Commercial St., San Francisco, CA, 94108, USA
Description: Restaurants don’t get much buzzier than this bustling Chinatown haunt, where Chefs Franky Ho and Michael Long are drawing crowds eager to sample their breezy contemporary take on Cantonese cuisine. Reservations evaporate almost immediately, but determined diners can line up for counter seating before doors open—though there’s no guarantee of getting in. Once inside, the favored few will find themselves packed into a lively room with quirky décor, where food takes center stage. From claypot rice with bacon and Chinese sausage to savory “fish fragrant” eggplant, the cooking taps into traditional flavors while offering a fresh perspective, a formula that seems to have struck gold.

Name: Four Seasons Pavilion · Rùn
