Address: 2F, 9 South Door, Hall 3, Liu Hua Exhibition and Trade Center, 117 Liuhua Road, Yuexiu, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: The dining room had a facelift in 2022 and now boasts modern décor with Beijingese motifs. For more privacy, consider booking one of their well-appointed individual rooms. Helmed by a Beijingese kitchen team, it prides itself on Peking duck — sliced tableside and served with an array of condiments and toppings. Besides traditional Beijingese cooking, novelty dishes that reinvent Cantonese flavours in unexpected manners are also worth trying.

Name: Four Twenty Five
Address: 425 Park Ave., New York, NY, 10022, USA
Description: Jonathan Benno and Jean-Georges Vongerichten are behind this elegant restaurant named for the address of the sleek building it occupies. Flooded with natural light, the soaring dining room is striking yet understated, offering a polished Midtown setting. The menu pulls influences from France, Italy, and Asia, pairing classical technique with contemporary flavors. Delicate kampachi with aji amarillo, lime and crushed corn nuts highlights the kitchen’s restrained touch, while beautifully handmade rabbit agnolotti showcases refined pasta-making. Main courses such as steamed black bass in a fragrant mushroom broth demonstrate careful technique, and desserts balance familiar flavors with modern presentation.

Name: Fox & Hounds
Address: 2 High Street, Hunsdon, SG12 8NH, United Kingdom
Description: There's a pleasantly rustic feel to this welcoming high street pub sporting low beams and wooden furnishings. Classical dishes form the basis of the extensive menu, with tried-and-tested combinations like asparagus with hollandaise sauce proving a success. There's also a Mediterranean influence to the hearty cooking, plus the option of rare breed beef cooked over the Josper grill.

Name: Foxy
Address: 1638 rue Notre-Dame Ouest, Montréal, H3J 1M1, Canada
Description: In what was once an industrial area that is now gentrified, this place brilliantly captures the art de vivre in today's Montreal: hand-picked eco-responsible ingredients, wood-fired cuisine designed for sharing, plus service from a motivated front-of-house staff who are both cool and professional. The bespoke decor combines simplicity and warmth with unpretentious elegance. Here, the focus is firmly on fire, the central element of this instinctive modern cuisine, in which local produce sets the tone. The dishes, often plant-based and with Mediterranean influences, lend themselves to sharing as in maitake mushrooms glazed with maple and black garlic, gently chargrilled Arctic char, and grass-fed Angus beef with shallots and aioli.

Name: Foša
Description: Situated at the foot of Zadar’s historic city walls, directly opposite the small harbour, the restaurant celebrates the produce of the sea through classic recipes reinterpreted in a modern key. Among the dishes we most appreciated for their simplicity and accomplished execution, the grilled turbot fillet stands out, served with savoy cabbage, cauliflower cream and potato croquettes. To accompany the meal, we found an interesting curated wine list: the selection is not extensive, but it is thoughtful and focused on Croatian and Dalmatian producers, without entirely forgoing a number of Italian and French labels.

Name: Frades La Terrazza
Address: SP94 - Località Abbiadori, Porto Cervo, 07021, Italy
Description: Situated in a panoramic location on Cala di Volpe bay, this trendy restaurant serves excellent cuisine with a focus on Sardinian specialities and other Mediterranean dishes. There’s a beautiful terrace for an aperitif, plus tapas options to share and a good selection of sparkling wines. Young and enthusiastic staff.

Name: Frades Porto Cervo
Description: This new Milan venture is the brainchild of three brothers who already run a restaurant and delicatessen in Porto Cervo. Elegant and extremely contemporary in style, the restaurant serves modern Sardinian cuisine, while a corner reminiscent of their delicatessen allows guests to taste the island’s hams and cheeses by the slice.

Name: Frances
Description: Stylish and always packed, this disarmingly personal restaurant from Chef/owner Melissa Perello remains a neighborhood favorite. It’s as perfect for a low-key date night as it is for dinner with the kids, and while reservations are difficult to score, its cozy setting and gracious staff justify planning ahead.The ultra-seasonal tasting menu, served family style, combines fantastic Californian produce with a Mediterranean bent, eschewing trendy powders and foams for appealingly rustic fare like Charentais melon with coriander capers and dill pollen. House-made pastas, like a lumache with wagyu ragu, pecorino romano and Sicilian chili flake, are eminently satisfying. The meal ends with a homey dessert like roasted strawberry shortcake, finished with a cloud of mascarpone Chantilly.

Name: Franceschetta 58
Description: Intimate and vibrant settings, where the smell of warm bread and the clinking of glasses convey the simple philosophy with which Massimo Bottura renews his love for Modena and Emilia. The menu, which includes both classic dishes and tasting menus, starts from the roots: the intense flavour of 36-month aged pancetta caressed by the sweetness of Campanina apple “mostarda”, or the velvety creaminess of “zuppa inglese”. Then the journey opens up to creativity, with unexpected touches such as grey mullet “alla cacciatora”, which releases aromas of herbs and the sea. The tortellini, made by the patient hands of Tortellante, where fresh pasta becomes both a therapeutic gesture and shared art, are an absolute must. The wine list is short, with carefully selected wines, while Lambrusco, in all its nuances, occupies a whole page, celebrating the deep-rooted connection with the region.

Name: Franchino
Description: Situated within the Onda Verda hotel on the road down to the delightful seaside town of Conca dei Marini, this attractive restaurant boasts a terrace overlooking the sea that is hard to resist. The menu here adds to the appeal, featuring traditional fresh fish dishes and local seafood recipes which combine to make this an exquisitely romantic experience. When you book, ask for one of the tables on the terrace or on the pedestrianised promenade.

Name: Francis Mallmann au Château La Coste
Address: 2750 route de la Cride, Le Puy-Sainte-Réparade, 13610, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Francis Mallmann, one of Argentina’s most emblematic chefs, is fanning the flames in the heart of this exclusive wine estate-cum-resort on a dinky Provençal-looking square near the art centre. Premium meat is grilled on the parilla, slow flame-roasted or smoked using traditional methods that the chef has been championing beyond his country’s frontiers: Mendoza beef empanadas, asado of beef ribs… The theatrical open kitchen pulls out all the stops, while the stylish, contemporary interior brings to mind an Argentinean hacienda. Wines from the estate and Argentina feature prominently and the vibe on the terrace is buzzy and vibrant.

Name: Franco Belge
Description: The trendy, cutting-edge establishment of Tomas Puype is a culinary treasure trove, enhanced by an alfresco dining space to the rear and a theatrically visible kitchen, where you can see the ingredients respectfully, generously and traditionally curated. The chef is a genuine craftsman with a keen eye for detail and a love of vegetables. Succulent breast of guinea fowl with crispy skin is served with al dente green asparagus, morel mushrooms and a subtle jus of guinea fowl and tarragon. Highly popular at lunchtime.

Name: Franco's
Address: 61 Jermyn Street, St James’s, London, SW1Y 6LX, United Kingdom
Description: One of London’s oldest Italian restaurants, this reliably enjoyable spot has benefitted from the years of practice. The kitchen focuses on an extensive menu of classically based dishes like veal and beef lasagne or linguine with lobster, with each one proving to be uncomplicated and well-executed. The many regulars come back time and again for their favourite dishes and the intimate, cosy atmosphere. The wine list is joyfully Italian, with some wonderful barolos among the choices.

Name: Frangipaani
Address: The Republik, Lot No.M.03, Mezzanine Floor, Jalan Medan Setia 1, Bukit Damansara, Kuala Lumpur, 50490, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: The softly lit interior, outfitted in warm wood and tan leather, sets a rustic mood, while the terrace is relaxing and cosy. Since 2019, the kitchen team has been delivering tasty traditional cuisine, tweaked to suit local tastebuds. Go for the vegetarian samosa chaat and the tandoori specialities. The raan dum biriyani, or whole lamb leg cooked in basmati rice, is great for sharing.

Name: Franka
Description: Tucked away in the alleys of the small Dalmatian town of Trogir, hidden very near the bridge connecting the island to the mainland, this delightful spot offers a distinctly Mediterranean cuisine in an authentic setting, characterized by typical Dalmatian stone. The food is flavorful and based on local seafood, with occasional nods to Italian flavors, such as truffle pasta or a fresh burrata appetizer. At lunch, three budget-friendly set menus are available, alongside a few à la carte entrées. In the evening, the atmosphere is particularly pleasant, especially in the small courtyard overlooking the passageway. To start your meal on the right note, we recommend a glass of Extra Brut Tomac. Some rooms are also available on the upper floors.

Name: Frankfurter Botschaft
Address: Westhafenplatz 6, Frankfurt on the Main, 60327, Germany
Description: A really cool location – the spot directly on the Westhafen makes the terrace a real highlight! The interior is just as attractive with its chic decor and wraparound glazing that ensures fine views of the water from every angle. Internationally inspired cuisine is served as a set menu – with meat/fish or vegan – or à la carte. Furthermore, valet parking is also available – it's preferable to put in your request when you make your reservation. Another point of interest is 23 Nord, the event space on the 23rd floor of the adjacent Westhafentower.

Name: Franziska
Address: Hainer Weg 72, Frankfurt on the Main, 60599, Germany
Description: It takes 40 seconds in the lift up to the top of the Henninger Turm. As well as its magnificent views over the Frankfurt skyline, this restaurant proposes "Progressive German Vintage Cuisine". The name is a tribute to the great-aunt of the Mook Group founder. Cocktails in the Barrel Bar. Terrace one floor down. Online bookings only.

Name: Frau Specht
Description: "Dinner is ready" is the slogan here. You ring the doorbell before being escorted into this somewhat hidden little restaurant with a modern, minimalist decor. You are shown to your table in a pleasantly intimate living room-style interior – with a small open kitchen and just a handful of tables, it makes for a private atmosphere. The service comes with a personal touch: your cordial hostess, Yvonne Specht, after whom the restaurant is named, will also recommend just the right wines from the extensive list of top-draw international labels. In the kitchen, head chef Dirk Brendel cooks up an ambitious seven-course surprise menu in the evening, further embellishing it with a variety of additional small dishes. The menu is devised based on the season and the availability of the ingredients. The cuisine is classic and Mediterranean, but also includes international flavours.

Name: Freemasons
Address: 8 Vicarage Fold, Wiswell, BB7 9DF, United Kingdom
Description: Tucked away down a narrow lane in the heart of the Ribble Valley, this delightful pub is as characterful inside as it is from the exterior. Cosy and welcoming, the whole place exudes a rustic charm thanks to an open fire and antique furnishings. The modern British dishes use the best of the local larder and deliver bold, well-judged flavours in adventurous, original creations like the 'Malteser' dessert. For the ultimate experience, book the "Chef's Bench", which consists of just four seats in the heart of the kitchen. Make a night of it and stay over in one of the bedrooms too.

Name: Freihardt
Description: Eating here is a real pleasure! The cuisine is international and seasonal, the highlight being the Bavarian beef steaks. They also serve burgers on Wednesdays and Thursdays. Head here on a Saturday for a three-course surprise lunch or on a Sunday for a traditional home-style roast. A friendly atmosphere reigns in the restaurant and its conservatory, and the terrace on the busy street is a place "to see and be seen". Right next door is the restaurant's own butcher's shop, which for many years has employed so-called humane slaughtering methods.

Name: Freihaus Brenner
Description: This lakeside inn overlooking Tegernsee is picture perfect; in summer, the terrace is nothing short of sensational! The interior is especially inviting, with cosy dining spaces done out in warm wood. The delicious food is inspired by the seasons and often showcases locally sourced ingredients. The menu features regional classics such as roast pork or duck as a speciality, alongside internationally influenced dishes. The charming front-of-house team work well together. This is also a wonderful venue for special occasions. Tip: For overnight stays, there is a gorgeous suite on the top floor.

Name: Freilager La Cucina Colaianni
Description: Celebrity chef Antonio Colaianni runs this stylishly designed fine dining restaurant in the Albisrieden neighbourhood with maître d' Marco Però, and it makes for a perfect complement to their Trattoria, which is housed in the same building. Born in Italy, he wows diners with Italian and French dishes, balancing tradition and innovation with finesse. This is beautifully showcased in his five-course menu featuring dishes such as "Tonno Rosso" – bluefin tuna and king crab, or "Tre Volte Manzo" – fillet, shoulder and essence of beef with Périgord truffle. Made by his mother Maria, the orecchiette warrant a special mention. He serves these with polpettine and tomato sauce. The chef makes a point of visiting tables personally and usually brings his dishes himself. Open Thu-Sat. Things get underway at 6.30pm with an aperitif, and dinner starts at 7.15pm. Motorists are advised to use the adjacent multi-storey car park (entrance at Flurstrasse 116).

Name: Freilinger Wirt
Description: This traditional Bavarian inn has been around since 1870 and today it boasts a lovely blend of clean, modern design and warm wood. The patron and chef is a master butcher and his experience working at renowned restaurants can be seen in his good seasonal dishes. The large terrace is popular.

Name: Freisinger Hof
Description: Dating back to 1875, this traditional inn enjoys an idyllic location in Munich's Bogenhausen district, not far from the Englischer Garten. With its stylish yet cosy decor, the dining room oozes charm. The staff pull out all the stops to ensure a warm and personal atmosphere – the large number of regulars speaks volumes. Dishes are freshly prepared and full of flavour. The menu alternates between Bavarian and Austrian specialities – boiled beef from a fattened ox is as popular as Backhendl (breaded fried chicken), farmhouse duck or brook char fillet. Surrounded by greenery, the terrace makes for a wonderfully tranquil setting in summer. Reservations are recommended, not only at weekends! Immaculate, comfortable guestrooms are available for overnight stays.

Name: French Grill​
Address: LF, JW Marriott Hanoi, 8 Do Duc Duc Road, Tu Liem Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list
Description: This elegant hotel restaurant boasts a sleek, spacious dining room oozing with special occasion indulgence. Counter seats offer a view of the huge open kitchen and create a connection between the chefs at work and the diners. The contemporary French culinary score is consummately executed with subtle Asian twists, flanked by equally immaculate, spot-on, courteous service. Private dining rooms are available for everything from date nights to business dinners.

Name: Frenchette
Description: Frenchette may look like a warm traditional bistro, but it is also so much more! This becomes obvious as you peruse the set menus, to be shared or not, which showcase an authentic bistronomic slant that can only be described as exuberant. Wild mushrooms, snails and toasted bread are savvily combined, perhaps followed by a pot-au-feu of wild boar in Kriek beer… Forthright flavours and first-class produce paint the culinary portrait. After a day out in the easy-going town of Ostend, this is the perfect place to finish your trip on a festive note.

Name: Frenchie Biarritz
Address: Hôtel Regina Experimental, 52 avenue de l'Impératrice, Biarritz, 64200, France
Description: This restaurant ensconced in a hotel looking down over the bay has been entrusted to Grégory Marchand (of Frenchie). Once past the vast atrium that serves as the bar (where you get a foretaste of all the details of the delightful 1920s-inspired decor), you come to a beautiful dining space and a terrace with sea views. The chef has created a menu inspired by the Basque region and added a few creative touches in a "chic brasserie" style: smoked aubergine, yuzu condiment, grapefruit and black garlic; meagre meunière, artichoke barigoule, tarragon hollandaise, shellfish bisque with vanilla. Extensive wine list (around 15 wines by the glass).

Name: Frenchie Pigalle
Description: Grégory Marchand has brought a tongue-in-cheek vibe to the ground-floor restaurant of this hotel in Paris’ sleazy yet romantic Pigalle. Dishes to share in a joyful canteen ambience that err between regional comfort food, bang-on Gallic classics and world food, including a splendid cheeseboard and a wine list with natural inclinations…

Name: Fresca Trattoria
Address: GF, The Grand Midori, Bolanos, Legazpi Village, Makati - Metro Manila, 1229, The Philippines
Description: Behind a smart façade in a quiet side street, this sleek, elongated bistro exudes understated elegance. Dark wood tables, tiled walls, a long bar and shelves stocked with wine set a refined yet informal tone. An area to the rear can be closed off to make a private space; air conditioning and moody lighting keep things comfortable. Expect elevated trattoria fare, e.g. fregola gamberi or tiramisu, served with flair, and a savvy wine selection.

Name: Freya
Description: Freya, the goddess of nature in Norse mythology, presides over the very vegetable-forward feast served at this compact restaurant in the Saint-Charles neighbourhood. At the helm is a couple with a wealth of professional experience and many trips around the globe under their belt. Chef Guillaume Chatillon doesn't shy away from using meat or fish (particularly the top-notch fish from Saint-Jean-de-Luz fish market), but focuses on vegetables, which are elevated in the same way as any other premium ingredient, with a host of indulgent preparations and occasionally daring combinations, such as his beautifully balanced cauliflower with seaweed. N.B. Guests at the same table are invited to share the same plate. Wine recommendations come, with a smile, from Margot – most are organic or natural, and all are available by the glass.

Name: Fried Banana Rama 5 (Bang Kruai - Sai Noi Road)
Address: 116 Bang Kruai - Sai Noi Road, Bang Si Thong, Bang Kruai, Nonthaburi, 11130, Thailand
Description: This spot is best known for its deep-fried bananas. Coated in crispy batter made from coconut and white sesame, they exude a rich coconut aroma. The sweet potato balls are another standout. Be prepared for queues during peak hours.

Name: Friend's Table
Address: 125 Mu 6, Hang Dong, Chiang Mai, 50230, Thailand
Description: Friend's Table follows a chef's table concept in the glass-enclosed dining wing of the owner's home. Diners can chat with the chefs at work in this stylish interior, dimly lit with a red hue. Collaborating on each dish, the duo of chefs strive for perfection: the food is refined, creatively presented, and packed with flavour, possessing an intensity that is true to the Asian palate. Be sure to be punctual; dinner will start at 7 pm.

Name: Friends Only
Address: 1501 California St., San Francisco, CA, 94109, USA
Description: Although reservations are now open to the public, an air of exclusivity still pervades this hot-ticket counter, not least of all because of the Olympian price point. What that pretty penny buys, however, is one of the most engaging and indulgent omakase experiences in town, replete with enough luxury to sate even the most committed of sybarites. Sip on delightfully unique cocktails with the likes of black truffle amaro or sesame orgeat and enjoy a parade of bites highlighting seafood of impeccable quality, much of it painstakingly dry-aged in house. Traditional nigiri and sashimi are served alongside cooked dishes, as in cherrywood-smoked unagi brightened with the prickle of sansho pepper, or bouillabaisse reimagined with dry-aged fish bone broth.

Name: Frierss Feines Haus
Description: The Frierss family are renowned for their sausages and other meat products. These wares are on site in their butcher's shop and well-stocked delicatessen, and are also to be found on the menu in this modern restaurant. Barbecued steaks feature among the mouth-watering specialities of the house, but there are fish and vegetarian options prepared in the open kitchen. Good selection of wines. A budget-friendly lunch deal is available, too. The staff are incredibly dedicated and friendly. Tip: You can also have breakfast here.

Name: Fris
Description: Just outside the city centre, beside Frederikspark, the team at Fris welcomes you to a spacious, contemporary restaurant. Their enthusiasm is infectious. Put yourself in the chef's hands with the 10-course tasting menu, which is also available in a shorter version. France and Asia come together in creative dishes that combine classical techniques, seasonings from around the globe and a clear sense of originality. The vegetarian gado gado illustrates this perfectly: cauliflower hummus is topped with an intense peanut mousse and accompanied by purple cauliflower, mild chilli and a sesame crisp for added crunch. A light peanut and chilli broth brings every element into perfect harmony. Excellent wine pairings give this highly personal cuisine an extra lift.

Name: Fronda Pasaje
Description: If vegetarian cuisine is your go-to, you have to go to El Born and try it at this restaurant, located just a stone’s throw from the famous basilica of Santa Maria del Mar. The proposal, with a choice of à la carte and two set menus, bears the signature of Argentinean chef-biologist Máximo Cabrera, who shows us how plant-based cuisine is not only healthy, but also tremendously tasty. The dishes, which in some cases are presented as a surprising trompe l'oeil, successfully combine science and creativity.

Name: Frosch Restaurant
Address: Via Santi Pietro e Paolo 1, Varena, 38030, Italy
Description: Situated in the centre of the small village of Varena (just outside the more famous Cavalese), this romantic and intimate restaurant with modern comforts and a mountain ambience is home to a talented female chef. Her contemporary recipes focus on local produce combined with Mediterranean flavours in some of the fish dishes and international ingredients such as foie gras.

Name: Frosio
Description: Housed in a 18C villa which was once a family inn, this restaurant is run by the dynamic and professional Frosio family who have over 30 years’ experience in the restaurant business. There’s nothing improvised about Frosio, where Camillo guarantees impeccable service front of house and Paolo is at the helm in the kitchen, creating carefully prepared dishes with a classic-modern feel and an equal emphasis on meat and fish, often made from traditionally “gourmet” ingredients such as scampi, lobster, foie gras, pigeon and caviar. The wine list continues to offer an excellent selection, with one section dedicated to Italy and another to the rest of the world. Decorated with austere elegance, the wine cellar in the 13C tower is home to more than 1,000 different labels. Attractive outdoor space for summer dining.

Name: Frédéric Carrion Cuisine Hôtel
Description: The elegant dining room combines the character of this former coaching inn (parquet, fireplace) with more plush and cosy touches. The chef uses fine regional produce to concoct wonderfully creative dishes. Your meal is accompanied by a delightful selection of wines, including a range of Viré - Clessé wines. The pleasant rooms and spa round off your stay in wine - growing country.

Name: Fu He Turtle Soup
Address: Berseh Food Centre, #02-40, 166 Jalan Besar, 208877, Singapore
Description: Cantonese soups of soft-shelled turtle or lamb dominate the menu. The broth is steeped in umami, sweetness and complex herbal aromas. Try their lamb ribs, slow-cooked until the meat falls off the bone.

Name: Fu Man Yuan (Xinyuanli)
Address: No. 102, 1F, Block 2, Kunsha Center, 16 Xinyuanli, Xindong Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
Description: A household name for traditional Beijing home cooking since 1994. This branch directly opposite the flagship has a glass façade and sleek architecture. In this contemporary setting, calligraphy of the Chinese character "fu" is a nod to tradition. The wallet-friendly dishes may not wow but they are skilfully made with fresh ingredients. The old Beijing vegetarian assortment presents varied textures and sweet soy aromas; the braised Zhoushan hairtail is also worth trying.

Name: Fu Qi Yu Yuan
Address: 81 Ma'anchi East Road, Lucheng, Wenzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: For 10-plus years, locals have been flocking to this shop, open round the clock, for its fish ball soup and sliced fish cake made with fresh brown croaker. Loaded with umami and rich in soft texture, the fish balls are oblong rather than round in shape. The clear, flavoursome broth is best enjoyed with a dash of white vinegar and pepper. For noodle soup, choose between rice vermicelli and wheat noodles for a satisfying meal.

Name: Fu Quan Shu Yuan
Address: 5F, Building A, Zijin Plaza, 701 Gudun Road, Xihu, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: After renovation, this hub dedicated to Chinese tea, art and all things Zen befits Hangzhou’s moniker as a cultural jewel. Its adjoining eatery still serves vegetarian food with Zhejiang twists; all-time favourites like soy-marinated walnuts, fresh tofu skin in thick broth and red braised stinky tofu are still on the menu. Thickly sliced lurid bolete sautéed with green chillies stands out with aroma and toothsome texture.

Name: Fucheng
Address: 16F, Waldorf Astoria Hotel, 18 Linyao Road, Pudong, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: The archway lined in porcelain art is the prelude to a sophisticated dining experience in a swish interior with the bonus of spectacular river views. In addition to Minnan classics, the menu also features some novelty recipes with creative twists. Crispy eel is air-dried before being deep-fried and dressed in honey with three types of lemons, imparting fruity and citrusy aromas. Round off with dimpled sticky rice balls in brown sugar syrup and sesame.

Name: Fuego
Address: 2F, The Taste Thonglor, Thong Lo Soi 11, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed
Description: Helmed by a Spanish chef with a passion for Japanese cuisine, Fuego boldly blends these two culinary traditions. From your seat in this intimate setting, watch premium-quality Spanish and Japanese ingredients being meticulously crafted in the open kitchen. Don't miss the signature paella. Another standout is the tapas, complemented by Japanese whisky and sake. The velvety, multidimensional miso cheesecake is the perfect ending.

Name: Fuentelgato
Description: Run by a young couple and... gaining more and more fans in the mountains of Cuenca every day! Here, always with a modern approach that makes the most of seasonal products, everything revolves around two menus, a fixed menu called Fuentelgato and another called Carta Blanca that varies in the number of dishes, ingredients and prices, since it is aimed, as they themselves say, at those who like to enjoy themselves the most.

Name: Fugu Club miyawaki Bettei
Description: The chef trained in Osaka, where fugu (puffer fish) is a familiar ingredient. Wanting to dispel the image of fugu as an expensive luxury, he opened a restaurant with reasonable prices and tries to come up with ways to overturn people’s ideas about fugu cuisine. Fugu with salt sauce is coated with sesame oil before grilling to retain its moisture. Serving fugu steamed with sake instead of as a hot pot is also the result of his research into the fish. His creative menus let diners enjoy the appeal of fugu.

Name: Fugue
Description: Not far from Gare de l'Est, this contemporary bistro is appealing with its sociable counter, exposed stone walls, weathered beams and walls lined with bottles. The decor is warm and welcoming – the perfect backdrop for Hitoshi Minatani's personal, precise and indulgent cuisine. Think duck gyoza, pigeon bisque; skate wing, spring vegetables, anchoïade and langoustine bisque; citrus vacherin. In the dining room, Victor Baraton-Dorat pairs each dish with carefully selected organic and biodynamic wines. At lunchtime, the affordable set menu serves as a wonderful introduction.

Name: Fuhrmann
Description: An exceptionally friendly restaurant that feels almost neighbourly with its inviting, cosy atmosphere and friendly service. As for Mike Feierabend's truly tasty Austrian cuisine, choose à la carte or go for the five-course set menu that changes every month. At lunchtime there is a cheaper three-course menu. Your hosts will be more than happy to recommend a local wine, but big names from Europe are also served, including some spanning numerous vintages. On that note, it would be remiss not to mention owner and sommelier Herman Botolen, whose genuine passion for wine is plain to see. Tip: be sure to book, as places are limited! In summer, make a beeline for the pleasant terrace in the courtyard.

Name: Fuje
Description: Fuje presents contemporary cuisine rooted in French cookery, crafted with seasonal ingredients and homegrown vegetables and herbs. The menu reflects the chef’s desire to create trustworthy dishes. One standout dish features lightly blanched geoduck served with rice cooked in a clam broth; the flavour of the broth perfectly accompanies the sweet aroma and the great texture of the geoduck. The subtle oak aroma from the grill further enhances the dining experience.

Name: Fujian Restaurant
Address: 6F, Xiamenair Jianianhua Hotel, 16 Lize Road, Fengtai, Beijing, 100073, Chinese Mainland
Description: From its decor to its dishes, this restaurant is a celebration of Fujian culture. Diners can book one of the 13 private rooms, where tea sommelier service is provided, and pre-order a set menu. For authenticity, the all-Fujianese kitchen team insists on most ingredients being flown in daily from their home province. Signatures include braised eel with red mushrooms, pork cheek braised with dried squid, and sliced clam blanched in chicken stock.

Name: Fujiichi
Description: The owner-chef trained under the heir to kinari cuisine. In textiles, ‘kinari’ refers to the natural texture and colour, so kinari cuisine means making the most of the ingredients' inherent qualities without overcomplicating them. Adjusting dashi and seasonings to seasonal ingredients, he spares no effort in what goes on behind the scenes. The deeply comforting flavours are gentle and nourishing, evoking an appreciation for his craftsmanship.

Name: Fujisushi
Description: Enjoy the nigiri sushi you like, in the order you like – this is a sushi shop as it’s meant to be, back to basics. In a testament to the chef’s uncompromising standard, the sushi rice is polished just before cooking. A selection of small dishes is available, and sake is also there to be enjoyed. It’s perfectly acceptable to drop in for just a single piece of sushi—a casualness that is much appreciated. Desiring to be admired even overseas, the shop takes the name of Japan’s greatest mountain, to spread the foothills of sushi ever wider.

Name: Fujiyama 55
Description: A Japanese DJ based in Lyon wanted to replicate a Japanese ramen institution in France. In this utilitarian-style space in the Guillotière neighbourhood, choose from a range of reasonably priced ramen dishes, accompanied by a fine sake selection to soothe any nostalgia for Japan.

Name: Fukagawa Ramen XBerg
Description: You would be well advised to book at this Kreuzberg ramen restaurant, as it gets very busy at both lunchtime and in the evening. The focus is on tasty Japanese ramen, such as "shoyu ramen – matured soy sauce, chashu chicken, dashi, handmade noodles, marinated egg, nori". Tip: The gyoza are a great starter! There is also an interesting selection of drinks, including sake, wines and cocktails. The decor is pared back, in a minimalist urban style, and the service is quick and friendly.

Name: Fukku
Address: 16-18 Smith Street, St Peter Port, GY1 2JQ, United Kingdom
Description: Thankfully pronounced ‘foo-koo’, this former post office is now a slick and lively izakaya filled with the buzz of contented diners feasting on its roll-call of Japanese favourites. Tempura, robata, ramen, sushi – you name it, they’ve got it here and it’s executed with both skill and care. The chicken yakitori, for instance, is tender and tasty, enhanced by a little caramelised glaze. The ‘sābisu sa sete itadakimasu’ (‘let us serve you’) chef’s counter experience offers something more immersive, while the selection of sake and highball cocktails adds to the fun.

Name: Fukunoya
Description: The lively mingling of guests and staff mirrors the bustle of Kitashinchi. The chef reads out the orders to his cooks, who rush to fulfil them. The packed menu promises the joy of many choices as only a kappo can. Pike conger in summer and pufferfish in winter are renowned fare. Eel, a popular standard, is served at lunchtime over rice in a lacquered box or in a bowl of rice topped with egg. The shop lives up to its founder’s motto: ‘Anyone, as they please, anytime’.

Name: Funaokayama Shimizu
Description: You’ll find this Japanese restaurant in a residential area close to Funaokayama Park. The chef draws his water from Daitokuji Temple, gets his vegetables from farmers in Takagamine, and buys ingredients from various regions at the Central Market. He chose this location so he could focus fully on his craft. To honestly convey the flavours of his painstakingly selected ingredients, the chef avoids reliance on garnishes. Stripped to the bare essentials, his fare speaks with its own clear voice.

Name: Funke
Address: 9388 S. Santa Monica Blvd., Beverly Hills, CA, 90210, USA
Description: Chef Evan Funke, who also runs Felix and Mother Wolf, is at it again with this eponymous restaurant. Set in a three-story 1930s art deco building, it's a stunning tribute to Italian cooking, with handmade pasta taking center stage (there's even a glassed-in room to watch them at work). Tall ceilings, red leather booths, and stone tables with brown leather/suede chairs set a stunning tone for a menu that pulls from their sister restaurants while remaining true to itself. Start with their pillowy focaccia, then savor a plate of tender South Pacific blue prawns in a garlicky salsa verde. Handmade agnolotti is delightful with a creamy filling of taleggio fonduta, finished with a meaty, buttery sugo di arrosto and parmigiano reggiano. Finally, torta di cioccolato is a wonderful finish.

Name: Funky Fisch
Description: Are you in the mood for fish of the uncomplicated and Asian-inspired variety? Then head to the trendy and lively Funky Fisch by The Duc Ngo. The centrepiece is the large fish counter, where you choose the fish you want to eat, which is then prepared in the open kitchen. A wide range of Asian food, from Chinese to Vietnamese, is served, with influences from all over the world.

Name: Fuori Rotta
Description: In the "upper" part of the town, just steps from the public parking and already in the pedestrian area, the cuisine leans more towards Ligurian traditions than seafood. We enjoyed the "Scherpada": a savory vegetable tart with melted cheese, prepared and served by a young team passionate also about wine, as evidenced by the excellent wine list and recommendations from the owner-sommelier. Reservations are essential, especially for those wishing to sit at the panoramic outdoor tables.

Name: Furna
Address: 6 New Road, Brighton and Hove, BN1 1UF, United Kingdom
Description: This stylish city centre restaurant is the first solo venture for Chef-Owner Dave Mothersill, who has been a fixture of the Brighton food scene for some time and brings an array of techniques to his precisely crafted dishes. The food is largely served by the proud chefs and focuses on seasonal British produce, with a few international influences and a creative edge. A chic mix of vintage and contemporary décor helps to enhance the experience, with counter seating available to make the most of the fully open kitchen.

Name: Furong
Address: 2F, The Wellington, 198 Wellington Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: For its second restaurant, the Xin Rong Ji Group picked this wood-clad space in the heart of Hong Kong's CBD. There is no à la carte menu; instead, diners book ahead and have a menu tailored to their budget and preferences, for example, you can request less oily dishes or specify how spicy and salty you would like them to be. Try the steamed pork belly with fermented black beans and chillies, and the golden braised fish.

Name: Futura
Description: Situated in the heart of the historic centre overlooking the monumental Piazza San Giustino, this restaurant has a traditional feel in keeping with its location, enhanced by typical brick walls in dining rooms arranged on two floors. In contrast, the predominantly meat-based cuisine is contemporary in style, with some interesting technical and creative twists.

Name: Fuumi
Description: In the centre of Fontainebleau, Fuumi is the teppanyaki outpost of starred chef Kunihisa Goto. Authentic Japanese fare, crafted directly in front of diners, particularly if you are lucky enough to nab one of the counter seats that command the best view of the culinary performance. The banquet of gyozas, ramen and okonomiyaki, the house specialty, illustrates the infinite care lavished on each dish. The attractively priced Bento lineup at lunchtime (teishoku menu), with a soup, small sides and a choice of main course, is just the ticket for a delicious snack. Friendly, buzzy vibe. Bookings highly advisable as it is inevitably packed to the seams.

Name: Fux
Description: This chic restaurant is very much at home in Lech. Behind the large glass-paned façade a tastefully designed space with a modern feel awaits. The open kitchen certainly plays its part – you can watch the chefs from almost anywhere. The cuisine is a fusion of Asian and European – a style to which they have been committed for years. The wine list absolutely deserves a mention, being one of the finest in the country – the Champagne and Burgundy selection leaves nothing to be desired. The bar area is also inviting – ideal for an aperitif or a nightcap.

Name: Fuyacho Nozaki
Description: Housed in a traditional old house at the end of an alleyway. Hoping to make his place part of people’s lives, the head chef showcases his ryotei-honed skills in à la carte dishes. Here, sashimi features kelp-cured and seared preparations, and seasonal vegetable takiawase can be enjoyed, highlighting the breadth of his many techniques. Dishes with a twist, such as cheese-flavoured shiraae and minced fish cutlets demonstrate his individuality. The lunchtime menu also features rice bowls.

Name: Fuyuan
Address: No.40, Huaqiao Xincun, Xierhuan North Road, Gulou, Fuzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Foreign credit cards not accepted,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This pink villa is a private-room-only restaurant specialising in the cuisine of Fuqing City, Fujian, with clear Putian-style culinary influences. Seafood like razor clam and shrimp is the house signature. The crispy Fuqing oyster fritter brims with cabbage, oysters, razor clams and pork. Pickled bamboo shoot gives razor clam soup a kick and the bivalves coated in sweet potato starch stay plump and juicy.

Name: Fuzzy Duck
Address: Ilmington Road, Armscote, CV37 8DD, United Kingdom
Description: Siblings Adrian and Tania – owners of toiletries company Baylis & Harding – preside over this immaculately kept pub. It was once a boarded-up boozer, but these days a loving touch and keen eye have seen it reestablished as a welcoming, fashionably attired inn with bedrooms to match. The cooking mixes timeless British pub fare, like a prawn cocktail or a Scotch egg, with more modern and playful options like the 'quack and chips' – confit duck leg with a spiced gravy and refreshing carrot and sesame salad.

Name: Fyr
Description: After many successful years as co-owner of Two-Michelin-Starred Gastrologik in Stockholm, Jacob Holmström returned to his birthplace with his wife Emelie and fell in love with this fantastic building on the Tylösand headland. Its design is chic and modern, and the atmosphere laid-back – and you’ll find it hard to decide whether to keep your eyes on the view, the open kitchen or the plate in front of you. The menu opens with snacks and ‘Canned Food’ (roe and caviar), before moving onto ‘Fish from the Cabinet’ and dishes showcasing other regional ingredients such as lamb with nettle purée and artichoke.

Name: FØRMA contemporary restaurant
Description: Situated in a secluded residential district that is part of L’Aquila’s historic centre, this intimate restaurant with an elegantly minimalist ambience is home to skilful owner-chef Simone Ciuffetelli. Having gained experience working abroad, Ciuffetelli showcases local ingredients in his creative, contemporary dishes, with the occasional use of fermented products and a frequent focus on just three ingredients. A good example is his dessert featuring cream and crunchy toasted hazelnuts generously coated with a white-chocolate mousse that is “disguised” as an Italian-style meringue thanks to a sprinkling of liquorice powder.

Name: Fàula
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Fàula – “fairytale” in Piedmontese – represents the gourmet offering of Casa Langa, a property that opens like an elegant amphitheatre overlooking the valley. In the kitchen, Francesco Clerico presents a cuisine that weaves Piedmontese tradition and modern interpretations with natural ease, always with a personal touch. The tasting menu dedicated to vegetables from the estate garden speaks to a sincere attention to product, while the à la carte selection moves with balance among meat dishes, fish, and vegetable offerings. A well-curated wine selection and the gracious professionalism of the service complete a harmonious, thoughtfully constructed experience.

Name: Fährhütte 14
Description: This restaurant, an offshoot of Überfahrt, enjoys an idyllic lakeside location. The modern decor has a touch of rustic maritime flair while the service is friendly and accomplished. International and seasonal dishes. You will also have the opportunity to rent a deckchair on the beach! N.B. the restaurant is not accessible by car – getting there involves a 300m walk.

Name: Fässle le Restaurant
Description: For years this has been a favourite in the city, drawing plenty of loyal regulars and newcomers alike. In his cosy restaurant in the Degerloch neighbourhood, Patrick Giboin presents his take on classic French cuisine both as a set menu and à la carte. Vegetarians are also well catered for, and children's menus are available, too. At lunchtime during the week, the prices are somewhat lower – the Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) is especially popular. Tables on the terrace are coveted in summer.

Name: Félicie
Description: In an artfully distressed, industrial-style decor of waxed concrete, bare bricks and square tables made out of unglazed iron and wood, a youthful, enthusiastic team runs this establishment in the suburbs of Lille. Deftly crafted, market-fresh cuisine at bargain prices and fish of flawless freshness seeing as it comes from their own fishing boat. Fresh produce and impressive culinary talent set the scene in Félicie’s felicitous establishment.

Name: Félix
Description: The trip out of Hamburg city centre to the well-to-do Hochkamp neighbourhood is well worth it, as the many locals who regularly dine here will confirm. Fitting seamlessly into the villa-studded neighbourhood, this elegant little bistro boasts an upscale modern interior. The service is warm and professional. From some tables, diners can see through the glass partition into the kitchen. Félix Bechtolf – after whom the establishment is named – and his team craft classic French dishes including plenty of fish and seafood. The quality of the ingredients and meticulous preparation never fail to impress. Order à la carte or opt for the three-course set menu, which changes every week. The well-curated wine list features premium French labels. Open for lunch on Saturdays. Tip: In fine weather, take a stroll along the Elbchaussee.

Name: Fūmu
Address: Marqués de San Esteban 5, Gijón, 33206, Spain
Description: This restaurant, just a stone's throw from the marina and the Fomentín dock, boasts a young atmosphere and has a good sushi bar (for eight diners), although it also has a few tables. The two chefs in charge, Álvaro Gragera and Carlos Fraguas, propose a cuisine with Japanese roots based on the excellent products of the Bay of Biscay and Mediterranean recipes, through a small menu of bite-size nibbles (here the nigiris stand out for their technique, size and flavour) and an Omakase menu designed for sharing. They age the fish themselves!

Name: GAIA - Manoir de la Mortière
Address: 1 rue Eugène-Nauleau, Les Sables d’Olonne, 85340, France
Description: This superb medieval stronghold, which was once a coaching inn and then a family home, now houses a fine dining establishment depicted by elegantly refurbished lounges whose solid parquet floors, lime-rendered walls and bare stone are contrasted by a subtle modern edge. The name "Gaia", goddess of the Earth, hints at the chef's ethos: fish and shellfish from the town's fish market are combined with vegetables, flowers and herbs from Beauregard farm to create polished cuisine, characterised by bold, spot-on flavours.

Name: GALLADA
Address: Kemankeş Karamustafa Paşa, Kemankeş Caddesi No:34, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34425, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Gallada is the epitome of luxury. Located on the fourth floor of The Peninsula hotel, this exclusive restaurant seats more than 200 guests! Diners are drawn in by the stunning views of the Bosporus, the upscale decor and delicious cocktails served at Topside Bar. But they mainly come for the captivating fusion of Turkish and Asian flavours over the course of a culinary journey along the Silk Road. The melt-in-your-mouth tuna is first marinated in soy sauce, yuzu and ginger then combined with a tahini and yoghurt cream. You should also definitely try the tandoori duck and the restaurant's own version of baklava. At Gallada, an extraordinary experience awaits you.

Name: GAMIN
Description: After a period of hopping from one time zone to another (Alain Passard, Corsica, Dan Barber's Blue Hill restaurant in the US), it somehow made sense for Charlotte and Bastien Guillochon to set up shop opposite a port! Their "culinary house" (as they call it) is open from breakfast through to dinner and has plenty of cosy corners. Each dish on the menu starts with the name of a vegetable or fruit: split peas, soupe corse and smoked sausage; Pontoise cabbage, green curry and horse mackerel. This modern cuisine is respectful of the environment and expertly crafted.

Name: GB Roof Garden
Address: 1A Vasileos Georgiou A street, Athens, 105 64, Greece
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: If you’re on the lookout for a restaurant that is a little bit special, this could be an excellent option on the 8th floor of the Hotel Grande Bretagne, thanks to its elegant setting and superb picture-postcard views of the Acropolis from both the delightful terrace and dining room. Despite not being overly extensive, the Mediterranean-inspired à la carte focuses specifically on fresh seasonal ingredients, with a special emphasis on Italian cooking, including a small section dedicated to pasta and risotto.

Name: GENMAIAN
Address: 1-3-24 Horyuji Higashi, Ikarugacho, Ikoma-gun, Nara, 636-0112, Japan
Description: The meals here are all based on unpolished rice. Vegetable dishes with no meat or fish are served in small pots with unpolished rice that’s been cooked in a wood-fired oven. The owner-chef calls himself a master of unpolished rice cake, his speciality being rice cake made with a mortar and pestle. He wants his customers to get to know tastes that are being lost in an age of plenty, so he seasons his dishes with soy sauce, miso and mirin made using traditional processes.

Name: GG's Chicken Shop
Address: 3325 N. Southport Ave., Chicago, IL, 60657, USA
Description: Bright and contemporary, this utterly charming spot from Chef Lee Wolen is named for his mother. It's casual, an order-at-the-counter-style spot, and as the name suggests, it's all about chicken. Rotisserie chicken is available by the quarter, half or whole, along with chicken sandwiches (fried and rotisserie) and sides like creamy broccoli slaw with golden raisins and crunchy almonds or chicken drippings smashed potatoes that will have you hoarding your portion. The comforting menu is rounded out with a few nostalgia-inducing desserts including oatmeal cream pies and a dirt cup topped with gummy worms that makes you feel like a kid again.Despite the downhome digs, the kind and caring staff are incredibly professional, elevating an already enjoyable experience.

Name: GINZA HABSBURG VEILCHEN
Description: Shingo Kanda is spreading Austrian culinary culture. Giving top billing to the cuisine of Vienna, Kanda serves traditional fare from each state of Austria. Wiener schnitzel and boiled ham are typical Viennese specialities. Kanda happily explains where he gets his recipes and tells anecdotes, explaining a cuisine unfamiliar to many of his diners. This dining experience is sure to spark your desire to visit Austria.

Name: GLACIER
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: What a great location right in front of the Eiger North Face! The fine dining restaurant of the chic boutique hotel (also called Glacier) makes the most of its surroundings with a floor-to-ceiling window front – and a wonderful terrace with a magical view. The dishes are based on select regional ingredients: you can either opt for the set menu or go à la carte, and sharing is also possible. The set menu is accompanied by harmonious wine pairings from the 320-year-old wine cellar, which is home to some 500 labels, over 200 of which are available by the glass. The enthusiastic sommelier provides astute recommendations.

Name: GRACE
Description: "The place to be" in Berlin! A really appealing and stylish restaurant that oozes glamour and counts Hollywood stars among its patrons. Dishes with Asian-Californian and European flavours are served. A must: after the meal, a cocktail in the rooftop bar lounge! The restaurant is located in the tasteful, high-quality designed "Hotel Zoo" in a great location directly on Kurfürstendamm.

Name: GRANDUKE
Description: Almost hidden at the end of the quiet Jorge Juan alley, full of luxury boutiques, there is a restaurant with an intimate atmosphere that feels free and claims to work without borders! The experienced chefs at the helm, Javi Cobo and Emiliano Celli (one from Madrid and the other from Rome), have forged a proposal that combines Spanish and Italian culinary tradition with coherence, creativity and technique, focusing on the best products and avoiding the excess. Within its relatively confined menu, you will find dishes such as the ‘Javi’ tripe stew with roe deer sausage, the Urta reposada (warm spinach and espelette gazpacho) or its Crème brûlée ice cream, hazelnut and corn.

Name: GRETA OTO Frankfurt
Address: Thurn-und-Taxis-Platz 2, Frankfurt on the Main, 60313, Germany
Description: Above the upscale bar on the ground floor of the JW Marriott Hotel Frankfurt in the city centre, you come to this stylish and elegantly designed restaurant on the first floor. The charming team serves up a slice of Latin America, from tacos and "ceviche GRETA OTO" (take your pick from salmon, sea bass or king prawns) to mushroom karaage, aji verde sauce and cashews. Pick your dishes à la carte – they are designed for sharing.

Name: GRETA OTO Hamburg
Description: This stylish contemporary restaurant showcases the flavours of Latin American, with a menu dedicated to Peruvian cuisine with Brazilian influences. The pleasingly accessible dishes are designed with sharing in mind. The very friendly, professional and attentive front-of-house team are happy to cater to guests' individual wishes. Tip: Do take the time to sip on a cocktail at the bar – a DJ adds to the fun vibe at the weekend. The restaurant is located within the upscale Conrad Hamburg hotel, which occupies part of the Levantehaus. Fun fact: GRETA OTO is named after the tropical butterfly (also known as the glasswing butterfly), whose lightness and vibrancy reflect the spirit of the concept here.

Name: GRETA OTO Munich
Description: For starters, the location right on the square known by locals as "Stachus" is nothing short of exclusive. GRETA OTO is housed within the luxurious and contemporary new Königshof hotel, on the ninth floor to be precise, affording fantastic views of the city of Munich and the Frauenkirche. The restaurant is no less chic and sophisticated than the hotel itself. Calm warm hues and dimmed lighting create an intimate atmosphere. The cuisine is Latin American with modern international influences, from Peruvian ceviche to Brazilian fillet steak and grilled octopus. The wine list to accompany the food is international. Tip: They have a private table – "La Mesa" – that you can book for special occasions. There is also a bar and a lounge terrace.

Name: GRILL
Description: In this restaurant housed in Hotel Vier Jahreszeiten by Hamburg's Inner Alster lake, Caucasian walnut wood, warm colours such as olive green and pigeon blue, along with a log fire create an elegant yet cosy setting that harmoniously blends traditional and modern elements. On the menu: seafood specialities such as oysters and lobster, along with classics such as steak tartare and special cuts of meat cooked in the Southbend infrared broiler.

Name: GUI
Description: It's a good idea to book, because this lively bistro in the middle of town has more than its fair share of regulars! The Mediterranean-inspired cuisine also has regional influences. The quality of the ingredients is first rate, from the fresh pasta with porcini to the cod and the tender venison fillet. The modern interior decor is pleasant – the floor-to-ceiling shelf with decorative wine bottles draws the eye, as does the open kitchen with one striking red wall. In summer, the terrace in the pedestrian area is very inviting. Incidentally, ĝui means "enjoy" in the international language of Esperanto.

Name: Gaar
Description: The world is Joachim Müller's culinary playground. Generous dishes such as Limburg pork terrine or crispy tortilla with Asian-style marinated tuna and wasabi give expression to the chef's sense of fun. The extensive and varied menu never disappoints, and diners will enjoy the interesting wine pairings. Chef Joachim and front-of-house manager Myrthe make it their mission to show guests a good time. The pops of turquoise in the decor are in keeping with the convivial spirit of this place.

Name: Gage & Tollner
Description: Vintage mirrors, cherry wood and brass chandeliers line the length of this historic restaurant, which first opened in 1892. With an amber glow and buzzing crowd, the room immediately charms, down to the no-nonsense all-classic cocktail list. There is plenty to eat here, as the team is not content to merely let history and looks stand in for substance. Seafood towers, big steaks, crab cakes and a superb platter of fried chicken with cornmeal fritters take their cues from the legendary Edna Lewis, who ran the kitchen in the late 80s and whose Southern cooking has inspired countless followers. Dessert is essential and all of them, from the coconut layer cake to the baked Alaska, will make for a fond farewell.

Name: Gaggan at Louis Vuitton
Address: 2F, Gaysorn Amarin, 502 Phloen Chit Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: In an upscale dining room centred around 10 striking Italian marble tables, Gaggan presents a seasonal eight-course menu in two acts. Act I, The Exploration, serves as a sensory introduction to the collaboration, featuring iconic Gaggan creations such as the famous Yoghurt Explosion, alongside the World Map, a dish that draws on a global palette of spices to reflect culinary influences from around the world. Act II, The Destination, moves on to more substantial seasonal plates, highlighting Thai ingredients with a French touch that pays homage to the Maison’s roots.

Name: Gagini
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In the vibrant heart of the city, between the Vucciria market and the Cala harbor, modern design and vivid colours bring a contemporary touch to the timeless charm of the ancient walls that house it: those of the 16th-century workshop of sculptor Antonello Gagini. In the kitchen, a new chef of Piedmontese origin weaves together the recipes of his native region and northern Italy with the freshness of the sea and the rich pleasures of Trinacria, drawing out their quality through original and well-considered pairings. Among the standout dishes are barbecued mussels with ‘nduja salmoriglio, Vietnamese bisque and crispy rapini, or tagliatelle made with 30 egg yolks, served with artichokes, citron and tuna bottarga: dishes that speak of a vibrant and contemporary gastronomic encounter.

Name: Gai by Darren Chin (Taman Tun Dr Ismail)
Address: 26A Lorong Datuk Sulaiman 1, Taman Tun Dr Ismail, Kuala Lumpur, 60000, Malaysia
Description: Gai (Thai for chicken) delivers tasty northern Thai food to the people of KL. The restaurant embodies the spirit of family and dishes are best shared for a group. Don’t miss Papa Suwit's tom saeb oxtail stew; a spicy-sour broth that boasts intense flavour from a mix of vegetables and herbs. The signature free-range chicken is grilled with a secret family recipe that emits a pleasant, chargrilled aroma. There are several seafood options too, including the flower crab.

Name: Gaijin
Address: 950 W. Lake St., Chicago, IL, 60607, USA
Description: Gaijin is Paul Virant's love letter to okonomiyaki. Okonomi in Japanese means "what you like” and accordingly guests here are encouraged to choose their own course. Thanks to his time in Japan, the chef displays ace skills and experience. Osaka and Hiroshima are the main styles on his menu, which also flaunts a custom brew from Moody Tongue. While Tuesdays bring a tonkatsu feast, steamed rice with furikake, miso soup, and tsukemono are eternal hits. Desserts, like shirokuma with pineapple-buttermilk sherbet and coconut syrup, are worth the splurge.The room resembles a veritable izakaya, with an okonomiyaki griddle dominating the space—and conversation. Brass accents, exposed brick, and concrete floors add a dash of rusticity to this otherwise premium den.

Name: Gaijin
Description: Gaijin comes with dark, contemporary décor, a buzzing atmosphere, attentive service and an emphasis on sharing. Its experienced owners offer boldly flavoured, skilfully presented modern takes on Japanese, Korean and Northern Chinese recipes. The tasting menus are a great way to sample the different cuisines.

Name: Gainn
Description: A change of management in January 2026 brought with it a new hand in the kitchen, without however altering the identity of Gainn, open since 2007 and a long-standing and dependable ambassador of Korean gastronomic culture. The cooking is lively and flavoursome, composed of colourful dishes revolving around rice, restorative soups, meat and fish, with generous space given to vegetables, soya and a well-judged balance between sweet-sour and spicy notes. The approach is avowedly convivial: generous portions and preparations conceived to be shared at the centre of the table. A single dessert features on the menu: those with a sweet tooth would do well to bear this in mind.

Name: Gaio
Address: Poza de Bar 2, Santiago de Compostela, 15705, Spain
Description: This welcoming restaurant with a contemporary feel and occupying what was once a shop stands out for its decidedly informal ambience, along with an open kitchen surrounded by a dining counter. The menu, with its heavy focus on sharing, features fusion dishes such as charcoal-grilled chicken with Chinese cabbage and a “Genoveva” dressing; millet and bull’s beef “tosta”; and mackerel with grapes and “gazpachuelo”), all of which offer a combination of Peruvian and Asian flavours, but always centred around seasonal Galician ingredients. Several recipes pay tribute to the chef’s grandmother and aunt, as it was these two family members who helped Andrés Medina develop his passion for cooking.

Name: Galatoire’s
Address: 209 Bourbon St., New Orleans, LA, 70130, USA
Description: At one of the city's oldest institutions, Friday lunch is a revelrous rite of passage. Pearls and suits file in right as doors open to a gold-accented dining room encased in mirrors and watched over by tuxedoes. Everyone is celebrating something and has the balloons, Champagne, and party hats to prove it. For more than a century, French-Creole classics have run up and down the menu. Go heavy on appetizers, like the Oysters Rockefeller, crabmeat maison with shrimp remoulade, or those superb, puffy soufflé potatoes dipped in a rich béarnaise. For entrees, find more seafood topped with all manner of crab, cream, and butter. There is nothing light, quick, or quiet about this meal. This is about leisure. Take your time. There’s nowhere else you need to be.

Name: Galaxia Cocina Pepehillo
Address: Avenida Miguel Celdrán Matute 6, Badajoz, 06005, Spain
Description: A long-standing restaurant (it opened its doors in 1982) that wows with its renovated and original interior design and its extensive menu brimming with traditional flavours, particularly mouthwatering when it comes to fish and seafood, but without neglecting Extremadura's meats and cold cuts. Unmissable dishes? The Revuelto Pepehillo, the Sevillian hake, the tasty oxtail stew...

Name: Galileo
Address: Via IV Novembre conc. 25, Civitanova Marche, 62012, Italy
Description: Boasting a dining room overlooking the beach, Galileo is a typical Adriatic restaurant serving fish and seafood dishes that are popular with many Italians. Options include seafood salad, a selection of antipasti, fish and seafood pastas, assorted small fried fish, and grilled recipes. In other words, delicious, traditional and unfussy cuisine in which fish takes centre stage.

Name: Gallaghers
Address: 228 W. 52nd St., New York, NY, 10019, USA
Description: Gallaghers is an icon. Walls covered with photos of horses and jockeys harken back to the seasoned stallion’s former proximity to the old Madison Square Garden. From the rolling carts of steaks and desserts to a bar scene that feels as alive as ever, this place hums with energy. The menu’s “other soup” is a sly reference held over from Prohibition days; and diners still walk past the window-fronted meat locker where slabs of USDA Prime beef are dry-aged.Gallagher’s fresh sparkle is exhibited by the display kitchen, set behind glass panes. The kitchen turns out classic dishes – steaks over hickory logs, creamed spinach and other faithful sides that are executed with care. The rib steak is a bone-in ribeye that arrives mouthwateringly tender with a side of warm and savory house sauce.

Name: Galleria
Description: This extremely pleasant establishment is an institution here in the city centre – the small restaurant near Marienplatz has been around since 1998. A friendly atmosphere is fostered by the modern decor, with pictures and wine racks adding a nice decorative touch – royal blue gives the whole place a maritime feel. They serve really good Italian cuisine, including classics such as vitello tonnato and house-made pasta. At lunchtime, diners appreciate the competitively priced lunch set menu. The extensive wine list featuring wines from Italy is on point. Staff are attentive and knowledgeable. In summer, a table on the small terrace is a tempting prospect.

Name: Gallery Bistrot Contemporaneo
Description: Modern cuisine, prepared with meticulous attention and enriched with carefully selected seasonal products. Tradition meets originality, as in the surprising risotto with clams, cauliflower and a dash of cocoa. Only twenty places in a spectacularly designed dining room: walls and ceilings clad in undulating light wood panels that weave together in a dynamic arch, creating an impression of movement that envelops the dining experience.

Name: Gallina
Description: A delightful bistro-restaurant that focuses on the quality of its cuisine as well as the connection between art and gastronomy. In this vibrant setting, featuring elegant marble tables and a completely open-view kitchen where you can observe the chefs at work, it offers a culinary experience that blends French and Greek traditions into elegant dishes with impressive textures. The menu features fish, seafood and a varied selection of meats (including an array of matured cuts). A particular highlight on the menu are the raw Greek red prawns from Koilada, served with a hint of freshness and a balanced combination of flavours. The impressive wine list with more than 800 labels from different countries provides the perfect complement to Gallina’s dishes, while a private room on the top floor is available for those seeking a more exclusive and intimate experience.

Name: Gallo Nero
Description: Just a short distance from Campo, at the boundary of the Leocorno contrada, the restaurant settles at the foot of a medieval tower: a thirteenth-century structure that once served as an armoury and which today, following a careful restoration, receives its guests in surroundings enriched by design furnishings from the 1950s and 1970s. It is here that the gastronomic offering of the Gallo Nero takes shape, with a cuisine that celebrates the Sienese tradition through meat dishes firmly rooted in the territory, set alongside vegetable creations and forays towards the sea. The cellar, nestled within an evocative Etruscan grotto carved from tufa, holds some 300 labels: a treasure conceived to accompany the journey through flavour.

Name: Gambero Rosso da Domenico
Description: Domenico Cannizzaro has been on a mission to showcase Italian cuisine in Franconia for well over 20 years, and has run this restaurant at the small marina with his wife, Teresa, since 2012. Here, they live and breathe hospitality, serving two set menus, "Domenico" and "Teresuzza", which each comprise three or four courses – it's also possible to mix and match. Astute wine recommendations come courtesy of the chef-patron himself. Gorgeous terrace overlooking the Main River.

Name: Gamberro
Description: At Gamberro, you’ll find a somewhat unusual punk-style decor and creative dishes that are only served as part of a surprise tasting menu. Make sure you arrive on time as the dining experiences starts at the same time for everyone.

Name: Ganbara
Address: San Jerónimo 21, Donostia / San Sebastián, 20003, Spain
Description: While the large staff has set the rhythm of service, the quality of its pintxos has taken it to the height of success. It is complemented by an intimate and quaint dining room in the cellar.

Name: Gandria
Description: Chef-patron Adriano Peroncini is originally from Puglia, but his years of travelling took him all over Italy and far beyond. Since 2016 he has had his own restaurant, here in Zurich's Seefeld district. In this delightfully cosy space, where an inviting atmosphere reigns, he introduces diners to his fresh southern Italian-inspired cuisine – highlights on the menu include the salted cod or Piedmontese Fassone beef and, of course, the delicious pasta dishes! Opt for the five-course "Degustazione Esperienza Italiana" or order à la carte. The wine list is predominantly Italian, but some French labels also feature. Diners can also look forward to "servizio alla maniera italiana" – authentic hospitality that will make you feel at home! There is a lovely little terrace in front of the building.

Name: GansFein
Description: Set in a historical building right on Stadtplatz, beside the city wall and Lederturm, this inviting restaurant was once a feather bedding shop, as the façade still proclaims. A ceiling with old wooden beams provides a striking contrast to the sleek, modern decor. Diners seeking a special experience can reserve seats at the chef's table in the kitchen. Chef-patron Kevin Stummer creates contemporary, pared-back dishes that blend Mediterranean and Japanese influences, while hostess Carmen Stummer provides warm, attentive and adept service.

Name: Ganter Restaurant Mohren
Description: Whether or not you are staying at the delightful Ganter Hotel Mohren, the restaurant is an inviting culinary destination. The menu is inspired by regional and seasonal produce and includes delicious dishes such as "roast beef with onions, red wine jus, Reichenau mixed vegetables, pan-fried Swabian egg noodles and fried onions" and "marinated white and green asparagus, mixed salad and baked egg". In addition to the mouthwatering à la carte selection, there is the "Schmackofatz" set menu (three or four courses). Service is cordial, the interior is contemporary; the charming guestrooms are distributed across the historical main building and the new wing.

Name: Garcia's Mexican Food
Address: 842 Fredericksburg Rd., San Antonio, TX, 78201, USA
Description: Open since 1962, this venerable institution from the Garcia family remains a vibrant, proud part of the city’s dining fabric. At all hours, the squat building has people waiting outside waiting for a table and ready to dig into classic Tex-Mex cooking. The menu is expansive, and one could spend weeks trying to cover it. There are those who come to order eggs over easy, douse them in salsa, and scoop them up in warm flour tortillas. And then there are heartier appetites who launch right into the deluxe dinner, which features enchiladas, a tamale, chili con carne, and a hard-shell taco. Should you also tack on a brisket taco? Of course you should. Adding to the convivial charm of the diner setting is a staff that’s all smiles.

Name: Garde Manger
Description: In Old Montreal, this friendly restaurant lies behind a discreet façade. With its paneled ceilings, leather banquettes, bistro chairs, and low lighting, the atmosphere calls to mind an elegant inn. The open kitchen separates two lively dining areas set to music from the 80s and 90s. On the menu you'll find seafood-forward dishes, with oysters, wild prawns, and razor clams served in their purest form. There are also plates designed for sharing, in which the chef's specialties are combined with the inspirations of the day. The eclectic wine list is well curated, encompassing French, American, Italian, orange, and organic wines.

Name: Garden-Restaurant
Description: With a fabulous light and high-ceilinged industrial-style conservatory by Belgian interior designer and art dealer Axel Vervoord, the restaurant in the luxurious Grand Hotel Bayerischer Hof is exceptionally chic. At the stove, Philipp Pfisterer certainly knows his craft. He and his team cook up classics such as beef tartare, as well as modern dishes such as "fillet of sturgeon from Lombardy with an almond crust & saffron cream" or "grilled flank steak with salsa verde". At lunchtime, the two- or three-course business lunch is a good deal. The very quiet location is also pleasant – and something of a rarity in such a central part of Munich.

Name: Gardenia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Even if you’re not a local, you’ll feel at home in this old property which offers a glimpse of the Piedmont of old. In this 19C building, with a typical balcony running along the inner courtyard, the atmosphere continues into the dining room and, of course, via the dishes on the menu. Here, regional cuisine is celebrated to the full, so you’ll find lots of meat (although some fish options are also available), accompanied by a carefully selected choice of vegetables, some grown in the restaurant’s own garden.

Name: Garenne
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: At the foot of the Brézème hills, this restaurant housed in a light-filled farmhouse on a winegrowing estate is a feast for the eyes and the taste buds. Chef Teddy Bidaux's modern and inspired cuisine is served in a dining room with picture windows giving onto the vineyards: glazed carabinero prawn with a full-bodied jus, sea bass fillet and veal marrow in an original surf 'n' turf dish, Fin Gras du Mézenc beef shoulder accompanied by puff potatoes. The excellent house-made breads are the perfect accompaniment to delicious food made with a personal touch and many local and organic ingredients.

Name: Garibaldi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Ossobuco, costoletta alla Milanese and tiramisu are some of the signature dishes here, at one of the city’s best known Italian restaurants. The affable owner, though, wants everyone to be able to find their favourite dish which is why he offers such a large, all-encompassing menu. The impressive wine list, featuring around 7000 labels, is another feature for which this cosy and contemporary-styled restaurant is celebrated.

Name: Garlic
Address: 44 Soi Chotiwat, Bang Sue, Bangkok, 10800, Thailand
Description: Head to this unassuming yet charming restaurant for Thai home-style cooking in Bang Sue district. For over 40 years, diners have been relishing the cosy ambience and a Thai menu that favours seafood over meat. The crispy pork pairs up with a distinctive apple sauce; the tom yum coconut soup is enriched by the flesh of young coconut for a flavour that is a delightful deviation from the norm. Call ahead to nab a table at this neighbourhood gem.

Name: Garrison
Address: 101 Red River St., Austin, TX, 78701, USA
Description: Though it's nestled inside the chic, contemporary Fairmont Austin, Garrison has an identity all its own, standing out from the pack with its large open kitchen and live fire cooking. There's plenty of grilling and smoking going on here, but the kitchen's dishes really shine. Start with a balance and bright kanpachi crudo with slightly seared avocado and Espelette pepper or chickpea panisse with lemon aioli and za'atar. A flaky leek tart accompanied by goat cheese and a quenelle of onion and bacon jam is another delicious opener before tucking into the main event—grilled meat like the Akaushi wagyu ribeye. Expertly seared and lush, it's even better sided by hasselback potatoes with saffron rouille, fine herbs, and Bearnaise sauce.

Name: Garrison
Address: 99-101 Bermondsey Street, Southwark, London, SE1 3XB, United Kingdom
Description: Something of a Bermondsey institution, this charming pub is known for its vintage look and relaxed, buzzy atmosphere. Get comfy in one of the cosy booths to enjoy contemporary British dishes made from good quality seasonal produce. Roasts are a big hit on Sundays and the daily changing menu makes a feature of the fresh fish specials, such as a fabulous John Dory to share. The friendly, organised service team have an eye for detail that further enhances the experience.

Name: Garum
Description: In a handsome wainscoted interior, Christophe Bocquillon signs a concise menu that stars fine ingredients to share with friends over a glass of something before dinner (oysters, charcuterie, fries in beef tallow), together with heartier traditional main courses (confit of pork belly, cabbage and a sauce to die for). The bistro’s namesake is a fermented sauce popular with the Romans, and used by the chef to season beef tartare, in particular.

Name: Garum 2.1
Description: Located along what is popularly known as the “Calle de la Feria” just a few steps from the El Rastro cross and the Miraflores bridge, this family-run restaurant continues to win new fans through its contemporary vision of Cordoban recipes, which has resulted in it winning several tapas awards and competitions. Choose between à la carte dishes and two tasting menus (Esencia and Homenaje) featuring surprising recipes such as oxtail on a bed of almonds with squid ink. The dining room here has preserved vestiges of the old walls of the city.

Name: Gary Danko
Address: 800 North Point St., San Francisco, CA, 94109, USA
Description: Opened in 1999, Chef Gary Danko's eponymous dining room is a San Francisco institution. Located in Fisherman's Wharf, the restaurant continues to be a busy beacon for colleagues on business dinners and celebratory couples. The cooking is rooted in classic French cuisine with a wandering sense of global inspiration. Diners select from a prix-fixe with ample options in each category of appetizer, seafood, meat and dessert. Those who aren’t in the mood to decide can hand over the reins with the five-course chef’s tasting menu. An extensive wine list, servers dressed in dark suits, and an impressively large cheese trolley round out the vintage experience.

Name: Gasthaus
Description: Like the gourmet restaurant, Gasthaus also combines modernity and tradition, from the decor down to the menu. While things are a bit more casual here, the cooking is also really good – the quality of the sauces alone will convince you of that! You can put together your own menu – and even make it vegetarian. Friendly service.

Name: Gasthaus Adler
Description: Savour classic Baden fare with French and international influences in these cosy, quintessentially "Black Forest" dining rooms.
