Reservations are highly recommended if you’re planning on having dinner here.

Name: Giuseppe Grill Leblon
Address: Avenida Bartolomeu Mitre 370, Rio de Janeiro, 22431-001, Brazil
Description: As the name clearly states, all the dishes (fish and meat) at this restaurant are cooked on the charcoal grill. The menu here includes dry-aged meat options (T-bone, prime rib, bone-in tenderloin etc). Other standout dishes include the Maminha (sirloin trip-tip), the Picanha supra sumo (supra sumo rump cap), the brand’s registered trademark, as well as the slow-cooked Uruguayan lamb shoulder served with its own jus. A number of fish and seafood options are also on display, which vary according to availability on the day. The decor here features exposed stone walls, wooden chairs and leather sofas, all of which combine to add a rustic-elegant touch. Not forgetting the extensive wine cellar in the basement, featuring over 400 labels from different countries.

Name: Giuseppi's
Address: Salini Resort, Salina Bay, Naxxar, NXR 9030, Malta
Description: Housed within the attractive Salini Resort Hotel overlooking the bay of the same name, this exquisite restaurant uses top-quality ingredients to craft a Mediterranean-led score, although modern trends are starting to make a fleeting appearance in some recipes. The lunchtime lineup is slightly simpler than that served in the evening.

Name: Già Sotto l'Arco
Description: A historic gourmet restaurant, with an equally historic setting on the first floor of a Baroque palazzo fronting an elegant piazza. A fine staircase leads up to the simple yet stylish dining room, which is skilfully run by a father and his offspring. In the kitchen, his wife Teresa prepares creative, regional cuisine, which is showcased on a surprise menu of four, six or eight courses and which features locally sourced meat and fish. If you’d like to book the delightful table on the small terrace for just two fortunate guests, make sure you do so well in advance!

Name: Gjelina
Address: 1429 Abbot Kinney Blvd., Venice, CA, 90291, USA
Description: In more than a decade, this buzzy restaurant has spawned a to-go counter, highly popular bakery and cookbook. The ambience is ceaselessly upbeat, resulting in a scene that is a major draw among pretty young things.Brick floors and creeping vines fashion a picturesque, garden-like setting that is an idyllic match for their simply prepared Mediterranean menu of pizzas and shared plates like saffron spaghetti with bottarga, confit tomato, and garlic or grilled hanger steak with a rhubarb chimichurri. Vegetables, many sourced locally, are an absolute must with winning options like Japanese sweet potato with jalapeno yogurt and scallion, or the umami-rich grilled oyster mushroom with tarragon butter.

Name: Glebe House
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: A heartfelt and heartwarming place, Glebe House feels like a sanctuary from our over-busy modern world. Chef-Owner Hugo Guest grew up in this former Georgian vicarage, before returning home and transforming it into a 15-acre smallholding and restaurant. Rustic charm oozes from every corner of the classic country house décor, while the surrounding farmland provides plenty of quality ingredients for the tasting menu – including home-cured meats from their own pigs. Each dish is unfussy and flavoursome, and explained with pride by the chefs.

Name: Glin Thai Bistro
Description: This charming spot just steps from Fort Greene Park has an inviting tropical ambience and an even more enticing menu. Showcasing dishes from northern and southern Thailand, Glin Thai Bistro is the real deal, with unique offerings using high quality ingredients, all with a distinctively Thai look and feel. Begin with an order of gui chai, or crispy, golden-fried chive pancakes that balance sweet and savory. Fried rice studded with crabmeat, egg, and vegetables is ramped up with cilantro chili lime sauce and chili fish sauce, while the kra pow nuer, or 24-hour braised short ribs, will linger in your memory for their caramelized crust and fork-tender meat.

Name: Gloria
Description: An informal restaurant where Manzano siblings Esther and Nacho showcase traditional cuisine perfect for sharing, including delicious tapas, “raciones”, a few contemporary dishes, plus two menus (one daily option, including wine, that is available for lunch midweek, and a second more extensive menu named after the restaurant, featuring Gloria’s signature dishes).

Name: Gloria
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: The name of this designer-inspired restaurant with a relaxed ambience pays tribute, along with the eatery they own in Oviedo, to the grandmother of the award-winning Manzano siblings. Here, they triumph with the more informal side of their cuisine, which is based around a traditional à la carte with hints of fusion that is particularly designed for sharing, alongside two menu choices (one daily option only available at lunchtime midweek, and a second more extensive tasting menu). We recommend ordering the delicious nems with pork cheek and prawns, the potato tortilla, and the legendary Casa Marcial ham croquettes. You can also eat at the bar counter, where you can watch your food being prepared.

Name: Glou Glou
Address: Morelos s/n, Brisas de Zicatela, Puerto Escondido, 70934, Mexico
Description: Glou Glou, located at Hotel Casa TO, is a stunning space. Walk the concrete stairs lit by candles at night to arrive at this dining room with a full counter, tables down the center and tiered steps lined with pillows for additional guest seating. The sexy setting is a perfect match for a menu that pulls from Mexican, European, Indian and Asian cuisines and features everything from aguachile, gorditas, roti, as well as fish and pork chops. The shrimp gordita is a perfect starting point before moving on to something from the grilled section, perhaps a Berkshire pork chop served with a salsa a la pimienta. Finally, an affogato with its rich espresso and vanilla ice cream, made with Oaxacan vanilla, is an appropriate ending.

Name: Gnocchetto
Description: This long-established family-run restaurant (opened in 1926) with an updated contemporary decor continues to serve cuisine that is classic and generous in style yet adapted to modern tastes. Individual dishes take pride of place on the menu at lunchtime, although you can also order from the À la carte if you wish. There’s also an outdoor space for summer dining.

Name: Go Ang Seafood
Address: 226 Mu 2, Phuket Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: From humble origins as a small shop with a zinc roof, it’s now one of the most popular seafood restaurants with a comfortable interior and Chinese décor. Chef-owner Go Ang cooks the entire southern Thai menu. The blue swimming crab, horseshoe crab and mantis shrimp are sourced daily from 5 markets. The steamed crab with tangy seafood dip and fried mantis shrimp with garlic are delightful, while the Southern Thai spicy sour soup with seabass is also a must-try.

Name: Go La
Address: 11 Kra Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: In its third generation of family ownership, this is one of Phuket’s best Hokkien-style fried noodle joints. Its charm is conjured up by a concoction of special flavours, the sounds of the wok and charcoal smells. Order the yellow hokkien noodles with an extra egg for a creamier texture.

Name: Gochiso nene
Description: The style here is an omakase set meal of tempura and items prepared in dashi stock. The owner-chef fries the tempura, and the proprietress intersperses it with takiawase and hand-made oden. Truly a duo in consummate synchrony. For dashi dishes, the couple trade ideas and prepare items together. In summer, tempura of pike conger with simmered onions is served; in winter, crab tempura comes with pureed soup of lily bulb. The harmony between husband and wife is as melodious as their restaurant’s name.

Name: Gocklwirt
Description: What is it that draws regulars and day trippers here in equal numbers? The richly decorated space is wonderfully rustic and the remarkable collection of farm machinery is well worth seeing. Classic international and regional dishes such as Böfflamott (beef in red wine), rooster burger and saddle of lamb in a herb crust are served, as well as a seasonal set menu. Three individually decorated double rooms can be booked for overnight stays in the building next door.

Name: Godai
Address: Vía de Circunvalación, Ciutadella de Menorca, 07769, Spain
Description: Located within the Suites del Lago hotel (Lago Resort Menorca), where award-winning chef Julián Mármol conjures up exquisite Japanese-Menorcan cuisine. The terrace and views of the marina add to its appeal.

Name: Godaille
Description: ‘Godaille’ in French slang means a feast and merrymaking among friends. This eatery run by a group of mates gives pride of place to spices and fresh herbs, such as fried chicken with tender meat in crispy golden breadcrumbs, flanked by a ginger-lemon sauce. The set lunchtime menu changes weekly and the evening repertory is more ambitious: mussels in a coconut-green curry and Thai herb sauce, or confit veal belly. Attractive, slightly retro interior and a fine list of natural and organic wines.

Name: Goesepitte 43
Description: Step into the picturesque Goezeputstraat 43 and be transported to a jungle paradise, complete with a living moss wall and monkeys! Chef Jan Supply likes to come to the table in person to serve his dishes. These are characterised by a deft use of the Mibrasa charcoal oven, rich sauces and intriguing vegetable creations. This is bistronomy with that little bit extra, as evidenced by the hand-whipped lobster béarnaise that elevates smoky filet pur to new heights. Be sure to try the crêpe normande, a house classic.

Name: Goh Thew Chik Hainan Chicken Rice
Description: This shop with over 70 years of history serves not just Hainan-style chicken but also grilled chicken with chicken oil rice. The tangy chilli sauce made in-house cuts through the richness of the silky, juicy meat.

Name: Goicolea
Description: Located next to the Plaza de Alonso Martínez, this restaurant brings its Basque-French signature cuisine to the Spanish capital! The elegant restaurant, which in a way revives the aesthetic classicism (the murals of the Bilbao artist Ignacio Goitia stand out), features chef Mikel Goikolea behind the stove, a man who treasures the experience of having worked in the kitchens of the three-starred Azurmendi. The proposal, with some off-menu options that are ‘sung’ at the table, brings these northern flavours to our palates and invites us to let ourselves go. Many of the products used here come from small, reliable producers!

Name: Gojo GENBEI
Description: Pride of place given to the many attractions of Gojo attest to the deep roots the chef has put down here. Produce of the Kinki region is the heart of the cuisine. As he visits producers, the chef dreams up menu items based on the vegetables he sees harvested. Among his creations are ohitashi and deep-fried dishes, vibrant and flavoursome from their fresh-picked ingredients. Beef and chicken are sourced directly from livestock farmers; sake, miso and soy sauce are the pride of the region. The location in Gojo Shinmachi, famous for its streetscapes of old buildings, proclaims both history and good taste.

Name: Goldader - Alpine Kulinarik
Description: Housed in a modern building in a rural setting, this is an interesting location. The interior is stylish and minimalist with a soothing colour scheme – don't miss your chance to take in the lovely view from the terrace. The dishes served here are a modern take on Austrian cuisine showcasing the finest local ingredients including game and fresh trout. There is a tasting menu with a flexible number of courses. Friendly and attentive service.

Name: Golden Hour
Address: The Radical Asheville, Tapestry Collection by Hilton, 95 Roberts St., Asheville, NC, 28801, USA
Description: Located at the Radical hotel in Asheville's River Arts District, this red brick structure was originally built in 1923 and was previously a breakfast cereal factory. The space is done up in dark painted exposed brick walls decorated with murals, large windows with views of the French Broad river, tall ceilings, exposed air ducts and an open kitchen.Wood-fired is the dominant feature of this kitchen. Small plates include smoked fish dip accompanied by crunchy seasonal vegetables and house-made matzo; North Carolina crab beignets with Old Bay-seasoned powdered sugar for dusting, or a "Girl's Dinner" board of cheeses, local meats and pickles. A wood-grilled half chicken or slow-roasted lamb with pita are tempting and comforting large plates.

Name: Golden Silk
Address: 1F, The Silk Lakehouse, Shangri-La Hangzhou, 78 Beishan Road, Xihu, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: A joint venture between two famous restaurants, Golden Silk sits on the lush green banks of West Lake. The modern Jiangnan interior is adorned in silk lanterns, ink paintings and bamboo plants. The menu melds the traditional flavours of Wenzhou, Ningbo and Taizhou, underpinned by solid technique. Seafood is their mainstay: try octopus in pork cartilage and salted cabbage soup or brown croaker steamed with shredded pork and shrimp roe.

Name: Goldene Sonne
Description: A quaint historical half-timbered building provides the setting where Heiner Bohnet and Constanza Piccolo welcome diners into their inviting dining space, which has retained its traditional charm. The pair approach their work with tremendous dedication and enthusiasm – she provides friendly and attentive service, and he creates a new vegetable-forward set menu every week, always guided by what is in season. Ingredients are sourced almost entirely from the local area (except for the responsibly line-caught fish from the coast of Brittany). The chef-patron is a member of a farming collective and grows his own vegetables. A great deal of fermenting, pickling and preserving is done in-house, plus they bake their own bread. Tip: They offer three lovely double rooms for overnight stays.

Name: Goldener Engel
Description: Steeped in tradition and brimming with regional charm, this establishment is staffed by a young and adept team who deliver pleasingly down-to-earth yet ambitious cuisine. While the friendly proprietress Emma Ambs, who hails from a family of restaurateurs in the next village, attentively manages the service, Simon Bantle (a veteran of various MICHELIN-starred kitchens) fuses hearty traditional fare with classic French recipes. The dishes are meticulously prepared, packed with flavour and delightfully unpretentious – think jellied veal tripe with fried potatoes, or braised ox cheeks with Ihringen pinot noir jus, served with creamed kohlrabi, kohlrabi purée and pommes dauphine. Featuring labels from the region, as well as elsewhere in Germany and beyond, the well-curated wine list is worth exploring. Modern guestrooms are available in the adjoining hotel of the same name.

Name: Goldener Karpfen
Description: In this historical house, seasonal international cuisine with classic regional roots is prepared from select fresh produce. Tip: the classic beef tartare. To be accompanied by a choice of international wines. The interior is elegant and cosy at the same time; in summer you can sit outside. For overnight stays there are comfortable guestrooms ranging from stylishly refined to modern chic.

Name: Goldmund
Address: Schöne Aussicht 2, Frankfurt on the Main, 60311, Germany
Description: The restaurant in the Literaturhaus, set on the banks of the Main, has an extremely stylish and upscale interior. Eye-catching features include the spacious bar area and the striking portraits of international artists. The cuisine is rooted in classical traditions and guided by the seasons – order dishes à la carte or opt for one of the two set menus (one is vegetarian), which comprise four to six courses. The adjoining Kaminzimmer ("fireplace room") is also very pleasant. Tip: There are plenty of parking spaces behind the restaurant. This is also a good venue for hosting events.

Name: Gom Ba Wie
Description: Grilled tripe and large intestines reign supreme at Gom Ba Wie, which has seen three decades of customers hooked on their buttery, pleasantly chewy goodness. The original location and the new location stand back to back, offering a glimpse of the restaurant’s past and present. If beef intestines aren't your cup of tea, the restaurant also offers other cuts like ribeye, short ribs and brisket. All meats are grilled over wood charcoal.

Name: Gong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: East meets West in a harmonious fusion of flavours at this restaurant, which takes its name from the imposing gongs dotted around the modern, elegant dining room. The attentive and thoughtful staff are always on hand to explain the different dishes, which are influenced by Chinese traditions yet often have an innovative feel. Beautiful presentation and carefully chosen ingredients typify the contemporary international flavour of this type of cuisine, with an extensive and varied selection of dishes on the à la carte and various tasting menus. One of the latter is dedicated to Peking duck, the restaurant’s signature dish.

Name: Gongxi Gongxi (Pudong)
Address: 2F, InterContinental Pudong Hotel, 777 Zhangyang Road, Pudong, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: With a combination of Jiangzhe motifs and modern sensibility, the space exudes understated luxury. The owner was a food supplier and is picky about freshness and quality. All dishes – à la carte, set menus or seasonal creations – centre on the freshest catch from the East China Sea and sustainable produce from Ningbo. Standouts are the deeply flavoursome swimmer crab with rice cake and the silky, umami-laden braised pomfret with fish roe.

Name: Goobok Mandu
Description: This small, family-run spot is operated by a Korean husband and his Chinese wife, blending a humble setting with a gentle touch of Chinese warmth. The menu is simple, offering just four kinds of dim sum, with the signature gubok kimchi dumplings drawing the most attention. Pan-fried to achieve a crisp exterior and pleasantly chewy wrapper, the dumplings are filled with pork and house-made kimchi, delivering a refreshing acidity and subtle heat. Diners who enjoy bolder flavours can enhance them with the chilli flakes and vinegar provided at the table.

Name: Good Alley
Address: 8450 E. Valley Blvd., #108, Rosemead, CA, 91770, USA
Description: This Rosemead restaurant may be slightly short on fuss, with a well-lit dining room with booths and banquette seating and ordering conducted via a tablet, but the Chinese menu with a variety of offerings is the real reason you're here anyway. Several items are musts, including the rou jia mo, a street food-style Chinese hamburger of sorts with your choice of a protein (order the Kurobuta pork that's slow cooked and sandwiched between a properly crispy flatbread). Other nonnegotiables include xiao long bao, or soup dumplings, and the braised beef noodles with tender and flavorful beef and springy noodles.

Name: Good Crab House
Address: 696 Jiangong Road, Sanmin District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
Description: For over three decades, the owner-chef has been flying in the best ingredients from his home island of Penghu twice a day to serve his customers. The famous salt-baked virgin crab burst with buttery roe, while the baby octopus in dark brown sugar sauce boast tender flesh and deep caramel flavour. Fried fish tail tossed in salt and pepper is also hard to resist. Don’t miss the Feng-ju tea made with an herb native to Penghu.

Name: Good Friend Cold Noodles
Address: Shilin Night Market, 31 Danan Road, Shilin District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: Noodles dressed in sesame sauce impart a hint of lemony fragrance, a perfect match for egg drop miso soup.

Name: Good Hot Fish
Description: Good Hot Fish, found in the South Slope District among a bevy of craft breweries, stands out with its dark exterior and a whimsical neon fish over the door. The small setting is mostly all business, but there are a number of seats along dining counters inside and out, and the team is a pleasant bunch.Chef Ashleigh Shanti's enticing vision of a traditional fish fry features product like North Carolina catfish and dayboat shrimp. The fish sandwich is a must — dredged in coarsely ground, locally milled cornmeal for an enticing crunch, tucked between slices of white bread and drizzled with spiced buttermilk tartar sauce. A concise range of seafood preparations are also on offer, as well as side dishes like baked mac and cheese and Sea Island red peas.

Name: Good Hunan Cuisine
Address: 203 Wufei Street, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
Description: Concrete walls and moody lighting may not immediately conjure up the image of Hunanese food but, rest assured, all dishes here are authentically prepared. You can specify your preferred level of spiciness, and certain items can even be made non-spicy. Their signature braised pork belly is slow cooked in a caramel soy sauce that imparts a sweetness that complements the mild heat. Nourishing sicklepod tea cleanly cuts through the richness.

Name: Good morning Hongkong
Address: 19 Seojeon-ro 47 beon-gil, Busanjin-gu, Busan, 47247, South Korea
Description: If you pine for Hong Kong cuisine and want to experience a uniquely Hong Kong vibe, this diner deserves your full attention as it is inspired by cha chaan teng, or a Hong Kong-style café. The owner says he opened this joint merely out of his love for Hong Kong. It serves less-than-authentic Hong Kong dishes, slightly modified to suit the Korean palate. Still, their flavors and visuals are no less spectacular than those of the local Hong Kong cuisine. Signatures include pleasantly spicy tomato noodle soup with plenty of tomato and ham; bread generously glazed with condensed milk and syrup; sweet nai cha (milk tea); and dong ning cha (iced lemon tea). The diner’s Hong Kong-style visuals are a plus!

Name: Goosefeather
Address: Tarrytown House Estate, 49 E. Sunnyside Ln., Tarrytown, NY, 10591, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: This destination-worthy dining room is coveted for its idyllic setting of sprawling estate grounds with a carriage house, cottage, and two historic, freshly minted mansions. Nestled within these luxurious surrounds is Goosefeather, where guests are greeted by well-appointed nooks, all blending old-fashioned charm with new-world elements.The menu is surprisingly unforgettable as conceived by Dale Talde. Known for his craft with Hong Kong-style food, the talented chef infuses these staples with a modern, seasonal twist. Kung pao chicken wings with a buttermilk dill ranch dip gives a familiar favorite a new lease on life. Bao, with a salty-sweet crispy shrimp filling mixed with cool daikon and cabbage, is an absolute must.

Name: Gordon Grill
Address: Goodwood Park Hotel, 22 Scotts Road, 228221, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: A feature of Goodwood Park hotel since 1963, the restaurant is famed for its meat trolley service which is wheeled over to each table. Along with the meat and plentiful supplies of seafood from the grill, you can expect French-inspired classic dishes like lobster bisque, braised beef cheek, or Crêpes Suzette flambéed tableside. It’s a good choice for a quiet business lunch, a romantic dinner or weekend family outings.

Name: Gordon Ramsay Bar & Grill
Address: 2F, Grand Wing, Newport World Resorts, Pasay - Metro Manila, The Philippines
Description: Near the airport, on the first floor of the Grand Wing Casino, amid gleaming boutiques and grand hotels, this elegant restaurant is a plush retreat from the bustle of Manila. Dark wood, designer seating, modern art and a chic bar exude warmth and energy; the open kitchen hints at culinary precision. Service is swift and polished; highlights include a decadent Beef Wellington, the Seafood Tower and a wine and cocktail list that is as smart as the setting.

Name: Gordon's
Address: Main Road, Inverkeilor, DD11 5RN, United Kingdom
Description: This long-standing, passionately run restaurant never stands still, always investing and evolving over time. It’s still very much a family concern, with Garry Watson alone in the kitchen and his mother Maria handling the service with aplomb. There’s a modern feel to both the décor and the cooking, with the latter proving colourful and technically accomplished. Dishes really shine in their use of the Scottish larder, like local lamb with seasonal girolles. An interesting wine list and five bedrooms complete the picture.

Name: Gorgoli
Address: Yılmaz Sokak No:10, Mustafapaşa, Ürgüp, 50400, Türkiye
Description: This simply appointed restaurant is nestled in the charming university town of Mustafapaşa. The Gorgoli Valley is just nearby, and for the chef it's a privileged source of all manner of produce. The extensive menu reflects his deep respect for his terroir and local culinary tradition. Aubergine and peppers are grilled just right for a rich smoky-sweet starter; lamb is slow-cooked to succulent perfection and served with a creamy wheat risotto. Nothing is overworked – every dish is a celebration of true flavour.

Name: Gorjan
Address: 161 Kra Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: If you're near Gorjan Bridge, consider this simple family-run eatery. Every dish is rife with rich flavours, and many are created from their own recipes. The owner is poised to cook your food to order, which ensures a personalised dining experience.

Name: Gostilna AS
Description: Just a few steps from the iconic Triple Bridge over the Ljubljanica River, you can choose between a dining room with a classic vaulted ceiling or, on milder days, a charming outdoor space surrounded by greenery, offering views of the castle. The menu stays true to tradition, featuring a wide selection of Slovenian meats − primarily grilled − along with fresh Adriatic fish and homemade pasta.

Name: Gostilna Krištof
Description: In the heart of the Gorenjska region, at Predoslje near Kranj, Gostilna Krištof embodies the long hospitality tradition of the Bolka family, updated with intelligence yet faithful to an atmosphere that is warm and genuine. The cuisine unites local roots with contemporary sensitivity, celebrating territorial ingredients such as Krškopolje pork, Carniolan sausage, and farmed trout. The recipes, inspired by tradition but reinterpreted through modern technique, change with the seasons. A rich wine list, with many Slovenian labels often available by the glass, completes the experience.

Name: Gostilna Repovž
Description: This welcoming countryside restaurant is rooted in a long family tradition: the Repovž family has owned the property for more than 500 years, while the restaurant itself dates back around three centuries. Today, kitchen and dining room work in harmony to offer tasting menus that showcase the flavours of the region through a balance of tradition and contemporary creativity. A signature appetiser provides a snapshot of the territory, featuring trout, vegetables from the kitchen garden, rabbit with plum cream and pork with horseradish mousse. The wine list is also of great interest, with Slovenia in absolute command: worth seeking out are the Laški Riesling from Slovenian Styria, a natural wine of broad structure and persistence, and the Frelih St. Rupert, a lightly macerated Sylvaner of finesse and expressiveness.

Name: Gostilna Vovko
Description: Bar, wine shop, restaurant, and hotel: Gostilna Vovko is a historic family-run establishment that has been welcoming guests with warmth since 1977. The interiors, furnished in traditional style and centred around a wood-burning stove, create an authentic and relaxed atmosphere. The kitchen, rooted in the tradition of the Dolenjska region, follows the rhythm of the seasons and celebrates local specialties, many of them handmade, including pasta, štruklji and svaljki. The trout is offered as a refined tartare with horseradish, trout caviar and pumpkin seed oil mayonnaise, while among the meat dishes the wild boar in game sauce with cheese štruklji, buckwheat, herbs and redcurrants stands out. The wine selection is carefully curated and firmly anchored in the territory.

Name: Gostilna na Gradu
Description: The most scenic way to reach Ljubljana castle, which overlooks the city from the top of a hill, is by funicular – or by foot, if you like walking uphill. However you choose to get here, you’ll find this restaurant in the castle’s spacious inner courtyard, where it serves an excellent and well-crafted cuisine. Among the dishes that we enjoyed most, our favourite was the veal and curly kale – a superb fillet of veal served with the perfect accompaniment of curly kale and a fragrant mushroom cream.

Name: Gostilnica Barba
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: A short and pleasant stroll from the village centre, the restaurant makes an immediately favourable impression with its agreeable outdoor area, while the interiors are distinguished by an informal and welcoming atmosphere. The kitchen is not looking for special effects, it wins over its guests through taste: the dishes may appear simple, yet they reveal good ingredients and solid technique. A case in point is the cappuccino di mare, with squid and prawns accompanied by a light potato foam that brings balance and delicacy to the dish. On the wine front, the selection is broad, and the sommelier’s guidance proves invaluable in navigating a list that is predominantly Slovenian, enriched by a number of interesting European labels.

Name: Gotzon Jatetxea
Description: This third-generation family business is located right on the seafront and has a long and storied history. Today it is run by the Longarai sisters, with Gotzone in the kitchen and Sorkunde overseeing the dining room. Here you’ll find Basque cuisine made with seasonal ingredients, high-quality meats, and fresh seafood, though we suggest asking for recommendations to find out the catch of the day. Try the pan-sautéed clams, their fantastic red mullet, or the delicious flan with salted caramel ice cream. Our tip: Reserve a table for dinner on the terrace—watching the sun go down is a real delight.

Name: Gourmand
Description: Guillaume Scheer's Bistrot de Plaisirs certainly lives up to the indulgent promise of its name. In a cosy decor with a laid-back atmosphere, diners tuck into mouthwatering traditional cuisine. Delicious, generous dishes – such as frogs' legs with parsley and garlic sauce, duck foie gras, sea bass à la grenobloise, entrecôte with Béarnaise sauce – are expertly prepared by the head chef. There is a quiet terrace to the rear.

Name: Gourmet Louis
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: This idyllic 13C water castle is a tranquil haven nestled just outside Basel. Surrounded by a moat, the property with its old trees can be accessed from two sides via wooden bridges. This establishment boasts two culinary concepts: a brasserie and this fine dining restaurant. Head chef Guy Wallyn, having already worked at the castle for several years, serves up classic French cuisine in the form of a four- to six-course set menu, which can be supplemented with cheeses from the trolley. To complement this, a selection of fine wines is available. Up to 20 guests can be accommodated in the lavishly renovated historical Steinsaal (or "stone hall") in the left wing of the castle – the 18C stuccowork is stunning. The small private dining space in the tower is ideal for groups. Tip: Enjoy an aperitif or coffee in the castle's courtyard.

Name: Gourmetfabrik
Description: This restaurant boasts a gorgeous location at Lake Schwerin. Inside, the atmosphere is pleasingly laid back; the decor is modern, and you can see into the open kitchen. Out on the terrace you can take in the view of the small harbour. The reasonably priced daily set menu, served at lunchtime, is a hit. In the evening, you can choose from a good variety of dishes, including steaks listed on the specials board. Only the finest regional and seasonal ingredients are used. Tip: They also hold cookery classes.

Name: Gourmetrestaurant Fuggerstube
Description: The historical Fuggerstube – dating back to the 15C – is a real gem of a place. The beautiful wood panelling and the old stove cultivate a cosy atmosphere and old-world charm. There are just four tables, at which diners tuck into a seasonal set menu packed with regional ingredients. The wine pairings recommended to go with each course are excellent, and the wine cellar has quite a few bottles from which to choose. The restaurant is located in Der Böglerhof, a wellness hotel that has expanded over the years.

Name: Gourmetstube Hochfirst
Description: In the small fine dining restaurant of the luxurious Hotel Hochfirst, which dates back to around 1934, you can expect an elegant yet relaxed atmosphere – an Alpine touch creates a cosy feel. The space accommodates up to 16 diners at beautifully set tables with large festive candelabras, and windows overlooking the ski slopes. Served in a single set menu with a flexible number of courses, the cuisine is contemporary with an international edge. The influences range from regional – eg fillet and sweetbreads from local calves – to Italian – think ravioli stuffed with pheasant – and even Japanese, for example hamachi marinated in sake and shiso. Service comes courtesy of attentive and adept waitstaff, who can also provide wine recommendations. The well-curated wine list emphasises selections from Austria, Germany, France and Italy.

Name: Goustut
Address: Quai de la Pêcherie, Capbreton, 40130, France
Description: Behind an understated façade on the harbour, guests are welcomed into a beautifully designed, contemporary dining space with a calm, relaxed atmosphere. The chef delivers his remarkable take on exceptionally fresh seafood cuisine in a menu composed according to the day's catch. His subtly flavoured dishes – three cold and three hot – brilliantly showcase lesser-known locally caught fish in vibrant pairings with flavourful vegetables. A truly inspired restaurant!

Name: Goxo
Address: V Corporate Centre, L.P. Leviste Street, Salcedo Village, Makati - Metro Manila, 1200, The Philippines
Description: The discreet entrance to this intimate 12-seat counter asador restaurant tucked away in Pintxos adds intrigue. The charcoal grill is central to the prix-fixe menu, which sees traditional dishes injected with subtle innovation and a Filipino soul, and features both local and Spanish ingredients. Subdued lighting, Spanish music played on an acoustic guitar and interactions with the chef make for a nostalgic yet original dining experience that is full of heart.

Name: Goxoki
Description: Goxoki means an "inviting place" in Basque, which is perfectly suited to this restaurant run by the Hourcastagnou family in the Petit Bayonne neighbourhood. In a timelessly elegant setting, the food shines a spotlight on local seasonal produce. Regulars come back often to tuck into the indulgent, generous dishes.

Name: Goya Gallery
Description: In a building that began its journey as a bar in 1950 and a historical spot in the city, and no wonder... the Mostra de València-Cinema film festival was first established here! It offers a traditional Mediterranean à la carte featuring an impressive choice of starters (don’t pass up the chance to try the amazing Mosquitos, small battered crayfish, or the GOYA cuttlefish with mayonnaise) as well as for its wonderful section of dry and honeyed rice dishes, the house speciality (rice dishes must be ordered before 12:00 noon the same day). We recommend booking ahead as it usually fills up with loyal local clientele!

Name: Goya Zushi
Address: Rua Artur Frazão, 37, São Paulo, 01423-030, Brazil
Description: Looking for a Japanese restaurant in the Jardim Paulista area? This one won't disappoint — it is the kind of place where everything revolves around a U-shaped counter seating eleven, and where a single, ever-evolving omakase menu takes centre stage, shaped entirely by whatever is in season. Chef Uilian Goya, ably supported by Lucas Ryu, does everything in his power to ensure guests feel at ease and can fully appreciate the craft behind each step — a craft rooted in kaiseki culinary philosophy, the Japanese tradition of a multi-course meal that follows the rhythm of the seasons. The highlight comes during the sushi course, where you will witness the meticulous preparation of the traditional rice: mixed in a wooden bowl, damp cloth at the ready, a paddle, a generous splash of red vinegar… and the final, airy result taking shape right before your eyes. Your menu will be waiting at your place, handwritten with the day's dishes and the name on your reservation. One word of advice, though — punctuality matters, so that everyone can begin together!

Name: Goyvaerts
Description: The Goyvaerts brothers welcome diners to the imposing Domusdela, a converted monastery church in the heart of Eindhoven. Steeped in history, this splendid setting is replete with Scandinavian accents; high ceilings and architecturally striking walls lend the space a sense of grandeur. The wine cabinet is an eye-catching feature. Characterised by bold flavours and refined details, the dishes pack a punch, and their presentation is always carefully considered and precise. Take, for example, the entrecôte and stewed Dutch beef, accompanied by both a parsnip purée and a parsnip sauce enhanced with coffee, souffléed potatoes, caper leaves and a herb cream. Elegance meets culinary ambition at Goyvaerts.

Name: Grad Štanjel Restaurant & Lounge Bar
Description: If you don’t have the opportunity to stay in Štanjel, we suggest arriving at this restaurant at least an hour before your meal in order to enjoy a stroll through the narrow streets to the Fabiani Gardens, which boast fine views of the surrounding mountains. You might like to start your meal with a local aperitif – a glass of Teran wine by the Jazbec winery would be the perfect choice. Whether you have lunch or dinner here, the cuisine is regional in flavour, featuring many ingredients from the Karst area. If it’s on the menu, don’t miss the restaurant’s own cured ham which is truly exceptional. The wine list is concise yet carefully chosen, with labels chosen according to the season. Memorable dishes here include the black gnocchi served with cuttlefish, a delicate herb cream and cherry tomatoes. The friendly and informal service adds to the enjoyment of the experience.

Name: Grains de Sel
Description: "Gilles Schnoering, well established in his restaurant near the Halle aux Houblons, treats his guests to a short seasonal menu; his fresh, well - made creations owe much to the quality of the ingredients used. Savvy food and wine pairings. "

Name: Gran Azul
Description: A spacious and modern restaurant just a few steps from the Plaza de Zaragoza that is full every day – a success based on its simple motto of “rice and grilled dishes”. Its interior, a mix of the rustic and contemporary, provides the backdrop for its famous rice dishes (for a minimum of two people) and grilled options ranging from fish fresh from the market and top-quality cuts of meat. The à la carte is complemented by an impressive array of specials, including a variety of stews and seafood options.

Name: Gran Sol
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: The restaurant is named after the legendary fishing grounds of the North Atlantic, an important aspect of the town’s fishing tradition. Make sure you try the pintxos here, including Jaizkibel, Hondarribia and Huevo Mollete.

Name: Grand Beirut
Address: Unit 12100-1201 (FB), Level 2, The Galleria Al Maryah Island, Adgm Square, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
Description: Under the same management as Beirut Sur Mer, this restaurant offers just the thing for refuelling after a gruelling day of shopping around Abu Dhabi. The colourful space is decorated with floral printed chairs, vibrant vines adorned with pink flowers, a massive Sakura tree in the centre and an inviting open kitchen to watch the chefs at work. Served with a heartfelt smile, the Lebanese dishes are designed for sharing and generously sized; they are full of flavour and founded upon quality ingredients. Be sure to leave room for their delicious kunafa.

Name: Grand Café Occitan
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In a Minervois wine village, this former café is now a bistro-cum-wine bar, owned by neighbouring Château Maris. With its terrace shaded by a reed canopy and its mismatched furniture, the place has all the makings of an arty guinguette. French-English chef Tristram Bowden and Ana Dias, his Lisbon-born sister in law, have devised a short menu featuring seasonal local ingredients, sometimes with a subtle British touch: beef tongue remoulade, pork loin confit with braised courgettes, almond and cherry tart etc. The wine list – Ana's domain – includes a selection of organic and biodynamic wines from the Languedoc region.

Name: Grand Chaopraya
Address: 42/1 Ban Run, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: Opened in 2009, this riverside restaurant serves Thai cuisine made with local ingredients, including fish sourced from the river. The dining room features high ceilings, spiral staircases and floor-to-ceiling windows, while the terrace offers scenic views and nightly live music. The menu is packed with recipes from the owner’s mother. Her grilled river prawns and grilled fish and shrimp in pineapple curry are a must. Book ahead for an outdoor table at dinner.

Name: Grand Cru
Description: Access to this elegant modern restaurant is via a cobbled courtyard. Inside, a warm colour scheme creates a pleasant atmosphere, and the front area features a light and airy winter garden. The classic cuisine with a Mediterranean touch is made with ingredients of the highest quality; example dishes include lobster soup or sea bass with white wine sauce. There are also different grilled dishes every day. Plus they have good wine recommendations up their sleeve.

Name: Grand Dragon (Xihu)
Address: 1F, The Dragon, 120 Shuguang Road, Xihu, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: This long-established hotel restaurant is famous for its gorgeous garden views, elegant vibe and upmarket menu. Authentic Zhejiang cooking takes centre stage, alongside new creations melding Cantonese cooking techniques. Classics such as sautéed river shrimps with Longjing tea, and crispy eel with shrimps are revisited, the latter as fried eel pieces stuffed with minced shrimp in a sweet and sour glaze. Private dining rooms of various sizes are available.

Name: Grand Hôtel de Solesmes
Description: White asparagus, hollandaise sauce; slow-cooked egg, artichoke emulsion; saddle of lamb, chickpea purée and, above all, the excellent Cointreau hot soufflé… A reliable family-run establishment that defies its age and serves delicate, classic cuisine that immediately wins diners over; no corners are cut when it comes to the quality of the ingredients. What's more, the welcome and service are charming and do justice to this former coaching inn, which, in the 19C, welcomed the monks of the nearby Benedictine abbey.

Name: Grand Kasprowy
Address: Bachleda Kasprowy Hotel, ul. Szymaszkowa 20, Zakopane, 34-500, Poland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: Nestled within the Bachleda hotel, this well-run restaurant provides the perfect restoration after a tiring day skiing on the nearby slopes. Go for a table by the window if you can, so you can make the most of the views of the Tatra Mountains, then order from the comfortingly classic menu that specialises in prime cuts cooked over charcoal. From a range of steaks to local lamb, it’s hearty, satisfying fare. Don’t miss the apple pie with cinnamon ice cream to finish.

Name: Grand Largue
Description: From the upper floor of this villa, diners enjoy fine views over the gulf of Morbihan and gastronomic seafood cuisine (lobster, sea bass, shellfish). On the ground floor, the P'tit Zeph is a bistro with a distinctly seafaring air.

Name: Grand Restaurant
Address: Via Johannes Badrutt 11, Saint Moritz, 7500, Switzerland
Description: This classically elegant restaurant, with its beautiful stuccoed ceiling and valley views, is a piece of the Carlton's heritage. Ticinese interior designer Carlo Rampazzi has used natural materials and warm lighting to create a welcoming ambience. This connection to nature is also reflected in the cuisine; prepared with premium regional ingredients, it is guided by holistic principles and the latest findings in nutritional science. In addition to a well-curated à la carte selection including options such as "pigeon, beetroot, chestnut cream, wild fruit jus" or intriguing dishes for two, such as "Swiss pike-perch Wellington with Albufera sauce", there is the plant-based set menu "Moving Mountains", which comprises five courses such as "onion cooked in mountain salt, pumpernickel crumble, green leek cream, rapeseed hollandaise, apple cider sauce". Tip: Arrive a little early and take an aperitif in the stylish Carlton Bar and Bel Etage by the fireplace with piano music.

Name: GrandCœur
Description: Take a seat in the warm, welcoming interior (exposed beams and stonework, marble table tops and velvet upholstery), or on the pleasant terrace in the picturesque, cobbled courtyard of the Marais Dance Centre. The brainchild of Mauro Colagreco, the purebred Gallic recipes come with an international, often Italian twist… Examples include roast leeks, black pudding and citrus-spiked olive oil sauce or Milanese cutlet of suckling calf – expertly curated culinary art!

Name: Grande Étoile
Description: This restaurant in the Carlstadt district is a masterclass in chic: shimmering gold, velvet, striking chandeliers and stylish Art Deco features create a trendy, elegant atmosphere. It serves up flavourful, well-executed dishes from a menu featuring French brasserie classics as well as Italian influences: beef bourguignon, beef tartare, pasta, vitello al limone... Service is professional and friendly. Head there in the evening for the cocktail bar and DJs, who underscore the Parisian club vibe.

Name: Grandir
Description: Meaning 'to grow' in French, Grandir was created by a chef who studied in Japan and a sommelier who honed his skills in France. The chef marries classic French cuisine with Japanese techniques to create distinct dishes with harmonious flavours, such as the sweet corn soup served with pork shoulder and a consommé gelée. Pair these dishes with a good bottle of wine and experience the heightened balance between the food and sauce.

Name: Grandrestaurant Pupp
Description: What could be better suited to this time-honoured setting than classic Czech cuisine? The lavish restaurant of the venerable Grand Hotel Pupp is housed in a magnificent space boasting high ceilings, an abundance of mouldings and stylish details such as fine chandeliers and mirrors, elegant fabrics and heavy curtains, all exuding a sense of history. An adept front-of-house team serves classically rooted cuisine with Czech and international influences. Both a set menu and à la carte options are available.

Name: Granit
Description: Between Carnac and Quiberon, this modern edifice, deep in the Brittany countryside, is a foodie’s paradise! Chef Charles Moreau has knocked around a bit from China to the Belgian kitchens of Sang Hoon Degeimbre (including the 2-star Air du Temps). He signs a spot-on, balanced score, dotted with iconic local delicacies and the odd creative note: Brittany whiskey, buckwheat, artichokes, oysters, gwell and Guéméné andouille. Concise, mainly organic and biodynamic wine list.

Name: Grano
Address: Unit 5 Norseman Court, Manor Street, Stoneybatter, Dublin City, D07 XD89, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: To the northwest of the city, you’ll find this lovely little Italian restaurant specialising in homemade pasta. Unfussy dishes like spinach balanzoni or cavatelli with venison ragu are expertly cooked and deliver great flavours thanks to their quality ingredients. It’s a friendly and passionately run place, with an owner and chef who hail from Calabria and regularly import produce from their home town for an authentic touch. The all-Italian wine list features some organic and biodynamic options.

Name: Granoturco Bistrot
Description: Although the external façade of this restaurant recalls its former life as a pub, the building is now home to a restaurant run by a young chef whose experience working abroad has done nothing to dim his love of the Piedmont. Here, he serves some of the best regional cuisine in the area, with a few more creative options also featuring on the menu.

Name: Grantley Arms
Description: The team from the nearby country manor Grantley Hall have taken on a decidedly smaller scale project with this restored 17th-century pub. All the boxes have been ticked for a classic country inn: a roaring fire for winter; a terrace for summer; flag-floored interiors filled with trinkets and treasures; and finally, hearty traditional British cooking. Whether it’s the excellent braised beef and ale pie or throwback desserts like sticky toffee pudding and trifle, everything is comfortingly familiar, big on flavour and executed with skill.

Name: Graspoort
Description: Graffiti on the walls and a homemade tropical tree hung with brightly coloured leaves set the scene in this fun, offbeat eatery. Thibault Van Stratum cooks instinctively and frequently finds his inspiration in Asia. Highly creative fusion cuisine brimming in influences, illustrated by croaker and marinated mussels jazzed up by smoked oil-perfumed dashi.

Name: Gratal
Address: Paseo de la Constitución 111, 50600, Ejea de los Caballeros, 50600, Spain
Description: While this restaurant may seem simple, behind the stove is David Fernández, a chef who, after working in large restaurants, decided to return to his origins to forge his own identity. The small à la carte, organised as if it were different routes through the Cinco Villas region or Aragon itself, is complemented by a good daily menu (some dishes have a supplement) and a tasting menu. You can find interesting signature courses, as the chef has won several tapas competitions and even participated in Madrid Fusion!

Name: Graze
Address: 95 Upland Road, Kelburn, Wellington, 6012, New Zealand
Description: The eco-conscious husband-and-wife team may have picked a former neighbourhood butcher’s shop for their wine bar, but their menu is entirely meat-free! While many come for the libations, their small plates made with responsibly-sourced plants and seafood are just as worthy of attention. Check out the blackboard menu for the day’s catch and foraged ingredients, which spins daily according to season and weather.

Name: Grazie Nonna
Description: Chef Gerald Addison and Casey Patten are behind this spot that's long on nostalgia and short on shortcuts. This is hearty food that uses quality ingredients while channeling the memories of Mr. Patten's nonna's cooking. Italian-American classics are leveled up in plates of clams casino, perfectly tender and briny with sweet bacon and crunchy breadcrumbs. A handful of pizza selections includes the classics, but creative ones make interesting detours (try Heather's pie with pickled banana peppers and rings of white onions). Macaroni is given the Sunday supper treatment, but it's not just red sauce—prosciutto and peas, tossed with garlic-spiked cream, is a good bet too. Chicken Vesuvio never disappoints, just like this experience, where a buzzy bar is always packed.

Name: Great Maple
Address: 1451 Washington St., San Diego, CA, 92103, USA
Description: Take the classic 50s diner, add a little swagger and you get Great Maple. It is one of four outlets statewide, but this particular location is always buzzing. Be warned though as parking and counter seats are coveted, so plan ahead.Three-course chef dinners on Mondays; burger and beer nights on Wednesdays; and prime rib Fridays are popular, but it’s also great at brunch. Fruity Pebbles pancakes, lolliwaffles on a stick and maple-bacon donuts are sweet-tooth satisfiers. Late night? Sip a Bloody Mary and tuck in to the brisket popover, a fluffy base with tender smoked meat, poached eggs and béarnaise that will cure what ails you. Seasonal dessert pies are all the rage—including the Valencia orange cream with a pistachio- and brown butter-shortbread crust.

Name: Green Island
Address: Saint Clement, Green Island, JE2 6LS, United Kingdom
Description: Friendly, personally run restaurant with a terrace and beachside kiosk; the southernmost restaurant in the British Isles. Mediterranean-influenced dishes and seafood specials showcase island produce. Flavours are bold and perfectly judged.

Name: GreenTable
Description: With its light wooden furniture and on-view kitchen, there’s a pleasantly bright, open feel to this contemporary bistro. As the buzz of the chefs at work fills the room, choose from a selection of modernised Polish classics, whether that’s venison pierogi to start or miodownick honey cake to finish. There are a few Nordic touches to the cooking too (look out for skrei cod) and across the board the ingredients are seasoned well and adeptly cooked, so the unfussy preparations can really shine.

Name: Greenroom
Description: Make a beeline for the terrace to make the most of the lush green countryside. If the weather is fickle, never mind, the interior is equally attractive. The Green Room doesn’t distinguish between starters and main courses, which gives you more freedom to compose your menu. A classic seafood béarnaise or Flemish-style asparagus with a modern twist – sea lavender and guanciale. The bargain-priced wine list (available to take home) adds the final flourish.

Name: Gregans Castle Restaurant
Address: Gregans Castle Hotel, Ballyvaughan, H91 CF60, Ireland
Description: An attractive country house nestled in The Burren, Gregan’s Castle is an enviable location for a restaurant. It’s a luxuriously appointed place, with open fires, cosy sitting rooms and a charming bar. The equally impressive dining room is the stage for a menu based on produce from their own gardens and the surrounding area, such as some of the finest lamb in Ireland. The quality ingredients are expertly cooked and showed off in well-balanced dishes. Ask for a seat by the window to make the most of the fabulous views.

Name: Greisslerei beim Taubenkobel
Description: Barbara Eselböck and Alain Weissgerber offer a delightful alternative to Taubenkobel restaurant with this charming eatery located in the adjacent building. The atmosphere is friendly, relaxed and completely unpretentious, and the food is simply delicious. Select ingredients go into flavoursome dishes such as Alsace-style snails, Wiener schnitzel and gnocchi with fresh truffles. The interior is wonderfully cosy and has a vintage feel to it, with charming decorative touches and shelves displaying house-made and Pannonian food items, as well as regional wines. By the entrance, there is a counter displaying desserts. A small terrace shaded by an old tree is just outside.

Name: Grenat
Description: At the front, a bistro with garnet-red walls, exposed stone and polished concrete; to the rear, a verdant courtyard planted with edible herbs and flowers: two distinct settings, both with the same stylish atmosphere. At the counter, solo diners can watch the chefs in action around the open fire in the visible kitchen. The garden exudes a relaxed bohemian charm. The kitchen is a riot of smoke and flame! A boldly seasoned, fire-driven cuisine built on short supply chains.

Name: Grenzhof
Description: At Grenzhof, chef Sebastian Andrée and his team are strongly influenced by the seasons and their produce in their modern cuisine, which is served as a three to six-course menu and an appealing à la carte selection. In nice weather, the Kastanienhof is absolutely idyllic; on less clement days and in winter, the Gutsstube with its rural-style decor is welcoming. At lunchtime, options are limited to a lunch buffet and a short lunch menu. They also rent out various spaces for private events. For overnight stays, they propose attractive and inviting country house-style and themed guestrooms.

Name: Gresca
Description: A reference for foodies, Gresca features an open kitchen that enables the bar area to be connected to the dining room. The cuisine here is exclusively based around an à la carte of delicious, contemporary-inspired small plates with options for sharing, although if you’re on your own you can also order half portions. There’s also a strong emphasis on game, offal and seasonal ingredients.

Name: Grey's
Address: Whatley Manor, Easton Grey, Malmesbury, SN16 0RB, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Sitting within the luxurious Whatley Manor Hotel & Spa, but with a feel all of its own, is this elegant grey-hued restaurant – ask for a booth or dine in the garden in the summer months. It presents a slightly less formal alternative to The Dining Room, serving a menu of globally influenced small plates that's divided into 'Earth', 'Land' and 'Sea', often featuring salad and vegetables from the kitchen garden. The cooking showcases well-defined flavours and careful craft, in dishes like prawn tortellini with coconut bisque. On Sundays, you can enjoy a traditional roast lunch.

Name: Greyhound Inn
Address: The Street, Pettistree, IP13 0HP, United Kingdom
Description: A trip to this enthusiastically run country pub feels a little like stepping back in time, in the best possible way. Serving the kind of menu where you could happily eat every dish, the kitchen favours a no-nonsense approach where big, hearty flavours and prime produce lead the way. Great use is made of cooking over fire, in dishes like wood-roasted quail served with a glossy sauce made from its roasting juices. It’s all simply joyous cooking, made even better by the welcoming team and idyllic location in the shadow of this tiny hamlet’s picturesque church.

Name: Greyhound on the Test
Address: 31 High Street, Stockbridge, SO20 6EY, United Kingdom
Description: The picturesque town of Stockbridge plays host to this striking mustard-coloured pub with low beams, elegant décor and a wood-burning stove. The chatty team deliver appealing modern British dishes crafted from local produce. Homely bedrooms and a mile of River Test fishing rights complete the picture.

Name: Gric
Description: Marie Gricourt's career has already taken her to the heights of Christophe Hay's La Table d'à Côté, where she was head chef. She has since opened her own restaurant, a convivial place in keeping with her personality. In this restaurant not far from the banks of the River Loire, the chef and her mainly female team (who provide service with a smile) put a new twist on bistro-style cuisine, simply and precisely: a surf and turf starter with scallops cradled in a sweet potato, bacon and prune purée; conchiglioni stuffed with beef chuck and porcini; and for dessert a delicious floating island with citrus fruit, honey and pollen.

Name: Grill Royal Hamburg
Description: Right on Ballindamm, with a view of the Binnenalster and its fountain, the restaurant boasts a superb location. Inside, the place has an appealingly relaxed yet stylish feel, and the service is friendly and professional. Top-notch ingredients are beautifully prepared to create attractively presented dishes – don't miss the steak cuts from the grill (eg Black Angus sirloin or a 900g porterhouse). There are also seasonal specials, and seafood such as oysters and grilled fish. Order sides and sauces of your choice to accompany the dishes – our top tip if you are having beef is the chimichurri! For fine weather, there is a small terrace on the pavement in front of the restaurant.

Name: Grok
Address: 14 Yolo Forest Community, Soi Somkid, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: The interior, decorated in elegant dark tones with wood-clad walls, creates a nostalgic ambiance. The menu offers a modern take on Ratchaburi cuisine, where the intense flavours and aromas of each dish pair well with Thai herbs. The duck confit with red curry and the stir-fried minced chicken thigh with Thai herbs and five peppercorns are recommended.

Name: Grotta Cucina
Address: Rua José Maria Lisboa, 257, São Paulo, 01423-001, Brazil
Description: Fancy visiting a restaurant inspired by an Italian setting? At Grotta Cucina, the setting is inspired by the Grotte di Castellana, the breathtaking caves located just a few kilometres from Bari. In this two-floor space — where the walls evoke the interior of a cave and candles mimic the limestone formations that have built up over centuries — authentic Italian dishes are served, with simple preparations that are nonetheless bursting with flavour. The menu features a range of antipasti, including focaccias, millefeuilles, and carpaccios, as well as main courses such as dried pastas, risottos… Our recommendation? The Sinfonia D'Anatra, pappardelle spirals filled with duck and rôti sauce, and the Parigi, gnocchi with parmigiano fonduta and white truffle butter.

Name: Grotto Tavern
Address: 9/10/12 St Pauls Square, Rabat, RBT 1232, Malta
Description: This cosy, stylish tavern, in the heart of the charming town of Rabat and just a short walk from the St. Paul’s Catacombs, is both romantic and mysterious. A few steps lead down from the street to the main dining areas: the colourful Garden Dining Room, a riot of lush ornamental plants, and The Cave, carved out of the rock, which offers its own tasting menu, the ‘Grotto Experience’, alongside the à la carte and tasting menus available in the main dining room. The repertory is rooted in local produce and traditions, which are reinterpreted in a modern, creative vein.

Name: Groven
Description: A small restaurant with a focus on simple local dishes. If you stop here for lunch on the terrace, you’ll find a different menu every day inspired by whatever ingredients are in season. There’s also a tempting selection of cheeses and game such as venison and wild boar during the hunting season, plus an interesting wine list.

Name: Gruber's Restaurant
Description: Austrian cuisine is served in this charming restaurant with its various tastefully decorated rooms and pretty terrace. Whether traditional (such as the excellent schnitzels and memorable Kaiserschmarrn – shredded pancakes) or modern (Carinthian cheese noodles, pointed cabbage and blueberries), the dishes are always made from carefully chosen ingredients. More limited options, plus a schnitzel menu at lunchtime.

Name: Gräfinthaler Hof
Description: In this somewhat more remote part of the Bliesgau region, you will feel most welcome in this gorgeous location that was once home to a monastery complex dating back to the 13C. Inside, an elegant atmosphere prevails; outside, there is a charming terrace shaded by trees. Ambitious dishes are created with terrific ingredients – the roast dry-aged pork chop (matured on the bone for 21 days), with sage, Serrano ham, market vegetables and potato fritters, for example, is a wonderful meat option. There are two set menus – one meat, one vegetarian – or you can dine à la carte.

Name: Grüne Bar
Description: The façade of the majestic Hotel Sacher alone is striking. Inside, luxury meets tradition and impeccable classic hospitality, and the establishment's fine dining restaurant is no exception. The interior is stylishly appointed in refined greens and fine wood, accented by historical Lobmeyr crystal chandeliers and original Anton Faistauer paintings. Diners enjoy attentive and pleasingly personal service at elegantly laid tables. The cuisine is characterised by classic, international and seasonal influences – a blend of tradition and modernity. The à la carte menu includes tempting options such as Alpine ox tartare with toasted seeds and Schmand (cultured sour cream). Alternatively, you can opt for a surprise tasting menu.

Name: Grünerhof
Description: Young chef Maximilian Grüner's cuisine stays close to nature – his dishes take their cue from what the region and the seasons have to offer, and are served à la carte and in the form of a four- to six-course set menu. Among his appetising dishes are a potato and wild garlic soup served with baked egg and Jerusalem artichokes, and Schlutzkrapfen>/i> (Tyrolean ravioli) with cranberries, Gruyère and beetroot. The owner and her friendly, attentive team run the show front of house. Located in the eponymous hotel, which boasts a central location close to the ski slopes and attractive, cosy guestrooms, the restaurant has a lovely modern decor with an Alpine touch.

Name: Gu Su Qiao (Diyi Tianmen)
Address: 12-14 Diyi Tianmen, Guanqian Street, Gusu, Suzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: Traditional Jiangnan motifs are updated and juxtaposed with modern calligraphy in this simple, elegant restaurant in the old town. The menu showcases Suzhou noodles, with almost 50 different toppings to choose from – try the crab roe noodles in autumn and winter. Those struggling to make up their mind can order one of the popular combos. The four-appetiser platter and dim sum such as xiao long bao and pan-fried pork buns are also well made.

Name: Gu Yuan
Address: Room 103, 665 Huacheng Avenue, Tianhe, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: Slatted wood panels, exquisite bonsai and a soundtrack of a flowing river set the zen-like scene. The young chef, from Shaanxi province, draws on his extensive experience of plant-based cooking. His single tasting menu features the season's best produce imbued with unique flavours from Northern China. The noodles tossed in scallion oil are topped with a droolworthy faux meat sauce that combines chopped potatoes, carrots and string beans.

Name: Guan Yan Liu Jin
Address: 3F, Section A, Hubin Yintai in77, 123 Pinghai Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: The theatrically lit main room is a picture of understated elegance, and the private rooms are equally stylish. The head chef, who hails from Chaoshan region, specialises in the cuisine of his hometown. Try the marinated meat platter to sample a few of his signature items and their layered flavours. Deep-fried cloth-wrapped tofu in premium stock boasts a crispy crust and velvety centre. The mild soybean flavour works well with the umami-laden broth.

Name: Guang Tang Noodles
Address: 18/15 Pimpasut Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: The history of this egg noodle soup spot stretches back more than 70 years to the owner’s grandfather. Today, it still satisfies — especially the noodle soup with wontons and barbecue pork (the noodles and wontons are homemade) and the deep-fried noodles with gravy and pork or beef.

Name: Guard and Grace
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Guard and Grace occupies an enviable location at the base of the 56-floor Brookfield Building in downtown Denver. Expectations at this restaurant in one of the city's tallest skyscrapers are deservedly high, as this ultra-sleek space delivers day and night. The vast space is stunning, with an oak fire roaring in the open kitchen, a floor-to ceiling wine room and a sophisticated blend of modernity and rusticity. Steaks are the obvious draw but a full seafood bar is a close second. Artichoke and spinach dip is a rich and flavorful starter before tucking in to filet mignon with lime smashed potatoes and chili butter. Chocolate Luxardo cherry cheesecake sided by a scoop of honey Bourbon ice cream is nothing short of indulgent.

Name: Guarda Val
Description: At the fine dining restaurant of the Maiensäss Hotel Guarda Val, which enjoys an idyllic location, the rustic charm of a 300-year-old cow byre meets sleek contemporary design. Exceedingly tasteful decor also lends warmth to the lovely lofty space, and the team provides friendly and adept service. The kitchen champions regional sourcing, relying almost entirely on Swiss ingredients for the two set menus (one vegetarian) and à la carte options such as "Lago Maggiore pike-perch with verjus and Jerusalem artichoke". Lunch is more streamlined, featuring a three-course set menu and an à la carte selection. Tip: Take an aperitif in the inviting bar on the floor below the restaurant. The terrace, with its magnificent panoramic views, is another highlight.

Name: Guay Jub Mr. Jo
Address: 86 Soi Chan 44, Wat Phraya Krai, Bang Kho Laem, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: From early morning until late afternoon, locals flock to the small room at the front and large dining area at the rear. Enjoy guay jub as an entrée or in a sweet, peppery rice noodle broth; rich layers of soft pork are encased in a crispy skin. Can be ordered with or without pork offal.

Name: Guay Jub Ubon
Address: 7 Phrommathep Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, Ubon Ratchathani, 34000, Thailand
Description: For over 70 years, this little gem has maintained strict quality control, carefully selecting offal from more than 10kg of offcuts each day. Their specialty is guay jub rice noodles with pork offal in a dark five-spice soup. They also serve delectable egg noodle and wonton soups.

Name: Guay Tiew Pet Tun Saraphi
Address: 80 Mu 3, Liap Thang Rotfai Road, Saraphi, Chiang Mai, 50140, Thailand
Description: Take a break and make tracks to this wallet-friendly shop that’s mastered braised duck. The duck noodles use the family’s secret blend of spices, while the roasted duck has succulent meat and crispy skin, moistened by the duck's own jus. Northern-Thai and other dishes are available.

Name: Gucci Osteria da Massimo Bottura
Description: Relocated in 2025 to Gangnam’s commercial district, this restaurant now occupies a stylish space defined by calming green tones, European tableware, and artful furnishings. Its vision is rooted in Italian gastronomy while deliberately moving beyond tradition. The Korean head chef, who trained in Italy for two years, skillfully integrates local and seasonal Korean ingredients into the menu, creating a modern Italian cuisine that reflects dynamic seasonal shifts. Offered as both à la carte and tasting menus, the meticulously crafted pastas are the undeniable highlight.

Name: Guefen
Address: 212 bis rue de Charenton, Paris, 75012, France
Description: Just next-door to the 12th district’s town hall, Guefen catches the eye courtesy of a glazed façade and tasteful contemporary interior. The chef crafts a single set menu, which keeps pace with the seasons and is rich in Middle Eastern influences and seafood. The bold but aptly named dishes bring the promise of virtuoso craftsmanship: tartlet of greater amberjack and puffed quinoa; gazpacho of cucumber with a coulis of spicy watermelon; red tuna lacquered in a veggie stock and jazzed up with a yuzu aioli and thyme-flavoured white carrots. Delightful on-the-ball service.

Name: Guelaguetza
Address: 3014 W. Olympic Blvd., Los Angeles, CA, 90006, USA
Description: This distinct Oaxacan eatery knows exactly what its culinary mission is—so much so that it is made abundantly clear in everything from its website address (ilovemole.com) to the orange façade that announces its presence from blocks away. Inside, pops of green, vinyl-covered tables and happy faces brighten the whimsical setting. A grill station fills the room with the scent of blistering peppers and more.The tlayudas, enchiladas and pozole are all delightful, but it is their negro and rojo moles that are absolute favorites. Mole estofado is so complex that it is nearly impossible to pick out the ingredients creating such a rich and dark sauce, slathered onto chicken or pork. Everyone gets a taste of mole coloradito, drizzled over gratis chips.

Name: Guesthouse
Description: After a decade cooking at Larkspur’s beloved Picco, Chef Jared Rogers has grown well-attuned to the tastes of the polished Marin crowd. His Kentfield eatery is a neighborhood gem, but for residents with million-dollar homes. The menu is appropriately packed with dressed-up crowd-pleasers—from grilled king salmon with chimichurri and summery succotash to decadent flourless chocolate cake piled with chocolate ice cream.Donning soft leather booths, eye-catching wallpaper and a tiled central bar, the room has the feel of a cavernous old barn transformed into a luxe vacation hideaway. This holiday vibe continues with hand-crafted cocktails, like the Royal Bermuda Yacht Club — a tropical rum concoction with lime and grapefruit.

Name: Gui
Address: 776 Eighth Ave., New York, NY, 10036, USA
Description: Dining in the heart of Times Square isn't always a good bet, but Gui Steakhouse changes the narrative. A natural choice for pre- or post-theater dining, it's also worth a trip without show tickets to experience their traditional steakhouse classics with Korean influences in a sleek setting. The menu includes raw bar items (Alaskan king crab leg) before shifting the focus to steaks with Japanese wagyu and USDA Prime meat. With a beautiful sear and deep grill marks, the aged steaks are finished simply with a sprinkling of Maldon salt. While steaks are indeed the raison d'être, the menu also features traditional American dishes like flounder and grilled chicken alongside Asian-inspired plates like dan dan noodles and wagyu fried rice.

Name: Gui Yu Jia Mian
Address: 74 Lower Manjuelong, Xihu, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: The space may not be huge, but the minimalist Zen-inspired decor is soothing. In contrast to traditional Hangzhou-style noodles with their firm texture, these are handmade to a softer consistency – all the better for soaking up the soup. The spring water beef shin noodles deliver plenty of umami and a hint of spiciness. Sides such as braised bamboo shoot are also worth trying. Round off your meal with ding sheng cake with red bean filling.

Name: Guildhall Tavern
Address: 15 Market Street, Poole, BH15 1NB, United Kingdom
Description: While its name and exterior might give the impression that this is a pub, once inside the smart interior you’ll quickly get a different idea. There’s a subtle, refined nautical theme to the décor, including in the teak-furnished Yacht Lounge upstairs that’s ideal for an aperitif. Situated so close to the quayside, seafood understandably plays a key role on the menu and the cooking of it is a real strength of the kitchen – be it sweet scallops or crispy cod. The wine list includes local producers whose wines pair well with the food.

Name: Guisados
Address: 2100 E. Cesar E. Chavez Ave., Los Angeles, CA, 90033, USA
Description: Set on a busy corner with an unassuming façade, this may be a humble storefront, but it’s all heart with an inimitable taste of home. This clean, airy and family-owned spot is open all day, so pop in when the mood strikes to sample their daily specials. Consult the chalkboards for the latest update, then snag a seat at one of the few tables with a view of the grill.It's all about their skillfully prepared tacos and expect to make a mess, as the sauce and juice drip while you're eating. Steak picado tacos with stewed flank steak served over black beans, or their cochinita pibil, with shredded pork braised with achiote and topped with pickled onions, are two favorites.

Name: Gunnen
Address: Rúa Juan Díaz Porlier, 15, A Coruña, 15009, Spain
Description: In this small restaurant, located in a residential neighbourhood in the south of the city, they like to experiment with taste, textures, and products under the constant premise of doing something different and personal. From the kitchen, completely open to the dining room, chef Chechu Rey heads up a technical-creative project that, in a bid to avoid resembling anything we have seen before, always tries to enhance the flavours from paths less travelled (there are even biological and chemical compositions). The cuisine is brought to life through two constantly evolving tasting menus: Impulso and Tempo - A highlight? We loved his Tear pea with white garlic base.

Name: Gunshow
Address: 924 Garrett St., Ste. C, Atlanta, GA, 30316, USA
Description: It's almost a decade in, but this spot from Top Chef contestant Chef Kevin Gillespie is firing on all cylinders. It's fun and lively, making it ideal for groups, while the multicourse menu served family-style gives the place a dinner party vibe. The cooking here is experimental and creative—you'll always discover something new.A mini tart filled with green garlic and strawberry, then topped with radicchio whipped cream and strawberry pop rocks shows off an ingenious sweet-savory blend and is proof positive that this meal is far from standard. Melting-off-the-bone pork ribs with a tamarind and rose glaze are tangy and tender, while a scoop of salted grapefruit sorbet on a Camembert cheese foam with parsnip olive oil cake is another inventive twist.

Name: Gunther's
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This owner-chef worked in some famous restaurants in his native Belgium and France before coming to Singapore. He describes his cooking as "simple, honest and down-to-earth", though a number of sumptuous dishes are to be had. Try his cold angel hair with a 6g quenelle of Oscietra caviar – one of his proudest creations, served since 2005. In addition to the timeless classics, check out seasonal offerings such as white asparagus.

Name: Gunè San Frediano
Address: Via del Drago d'Oro 1r, Florence, 50124, Italy
Description: The chef at this small gastronomic restaurant serves cuisine which acts as a bridge between Basilicata and Tuscany, the two most significant regions in his life, resulting in creative, delicate and beautifully presented dishes.

Name: Guo Fan Jia Yan
Address: 2F, 123 TangAn Road, Tianhe, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: A must-try for spicy food lovers. Named after famous statesman Zeng Guofan of Qing Dynasty, the room pays tribute to him with his literary and calligraphic works. The menu also focusses on dishes and seasonal ingredients from Hunan province, where Zeng hailed from.
