The original menu fuses East and West, with the dim sum a hit and the signature beef dishes cooked over charcoal a real highlight. The wine list features some fine growers and the whole place makes for a glamorous night out.

Name: Heaneys
Address: 6-10 Romilly Crescent, Cardiff, CF11 9NR, United Kingdom
Description: Arrive early for a cocktail in the bar of well-known Chef Tommy Heaney’s stylishly laid-back suburban restaurant. Dishes are seasonal and modern, with some sophisticated contrasts; the set lunch menu delivers good value while, at dinner, the tasting menu takes centre stage. Next door is Uisce – his no-reservations, small plates restaurant – which showcases herbs and vegetables from the pretty kitchen garden.

Name: Hearth
Address: 10.5 King Street, City of Kingston-upon-Hull, HU1 2JJ, United Kingdom
Description: Run by a pair of friends and located among some fine buildings in the old part of town, this buzzy spot operates over two levels. The ground floor houses a bar and bakery, while the upstairs is home to the rustic two-room restaurant. The menu fuses small plates with larger dishes, often coming from the grill – or ‘hearth’ – that takes centre stage in the open kitchen. Start with sourdough from the bakery, then make sure you check the boards for daily specials, as you might get to enjoy delicious seasonal produce like Yorkshire grouse.

Name: Hebelstube
Description: This establishment has been a familiar and beloved landmark for decades. Part of the long-established Hotel Alte Post, the restaurant serves seasonal cuisine made with regionally sourced ingredients, with dishes such as calf's head, risotto and chard, or Black Forest salmon trout and crayfish lasagne with spring vegetables, citrus-infused beurre blanc and verbena shellfish emulsion, available either as a set menu or à la carte. The wine list homes in on labels from the region. Add to that a friendly and charming atmosphere, and very attentive, solicitous service. The terrace is delightful in summer. Their contemporary-style guestrooms are ideal for an overnight stay.

Name: Hed 11
Address: Kimpton Hotel Enso, 1800 Sutter St., San Francisco, CA, 94115, USA
Description: Perched in a swanky space at the corner of the Kimpton Hotel Enso, this ambitious Thai project from Chef Piriya "Saint" Boonprasan and owner Naruephon "Billie" Wannajaro gives a hint to its concept right in the name: an 11-course menu that celebrates regional Thai flavors with a contemporary style. The price point doesn’t lend itself to dining on a budget, but despite its variety, the meal won’t over-tax your schedule, with most of the courses arriving together as a sort of miniature banquet for the main. Sweet and savory are blended throughout the menu, whether in bites like a coconut pancake with lime and caviar, a take on khanom jeen sao nam with seared scallop paired with chilled rice noodles, tangy pineapple, and garlic, or even a Thai-style cheesecake with crispy fried onions and passionfruit syrup.

Name: Hegel Eins
Description: Housed within the Linden Museum, Baden-Württemberg's museum of ethnology, this stylish restaurant serves modern dishes inspired by the seasons, such as "scallop, dill, yoghurt, parsnip, cucumber" or "veal loin, polenta, Swiss chard, brown butter". A five-course set menu is available, with an abbreviated three-course option on Tue-Thu. The vegetarian version needs to be pre-ordered.

Name: Heh
Address: 158 Yaowarat Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: ‘Heh’ is an expression of curiosity, according to the chef-owner who leads a youthful and creative kitchen. The aim is to bring Melbourne to the Andaman, combining quality ingredients from the Andaman Sea with Australian imports. The chef injects excitement into the unique menu without ever overcomplicating it. The menu is all about fresh ingredients and bold flavours, cooked to order. The place feels relaxed but still has a bit of style, ideal for anyone who enjoys a mix of Asian and Western ideas.

Name: Hei Fung Terrace
Address: 2F, The Peninsula Tokyo, 1-8-1 Yurakucho, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo, 100-0006, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The exotic atmosphere is suggestive of a Chinese garden. Being part of a Hong Kong group, the focus is on Cantonese cuisine. The dim sum master creates xiaolongbao and gyoza, while the grill master serves up chicken and pork baked in iron pots. From the cornucopia of ingredients, guests can decide the seasoning and cooking style, including stewed items in oyster sauce and stir-fried items with XO or black bean sauce. Ask to sit overlooking the outer garden of the Imperial Palace.

Name: Heiligenstein
Description: Come here to enjoy classic seasonal cuisine in an inviting, modern atmosphere. High-quality, fresh ingredients are prepared in an agreeably straightforward way that brings out their flavour. Choose between an à la carte menu and a three- or four-course set menu. Then there's the excellent wine list featuring over 400 selections. In summer, tables are laid out on a wonderful terrace. The hotel boasts a peaceful location and lovely cosy guestrooms – and the abundance of greenery and surrounding forest mean it is also a good starting point for hikes.

Name: Heim's Restaurant
Address: Moselstraße 27, Reil an der Mosel, 56861, Germany
Description: The food served in this 300-year-old restaurant is honest, fresh and full of flavour. Classic and regional cuisine is served throughout the day (kitchen opening hours: 12-8.30pm), taking the form of dishes such as cod à la grenobloise with spinach and mashed potatoes or "Original Wiener Schnitzel" with fried potatoes, salad and cranberries. You will be able to find just the right Moselle wine to accompany your meal. Service comes courtesy of a friendly and proficient team, the atmosphere is pleasant, and in summer, the wonderful terrace with a view of the vineyards and Moselle beckons. The Reiler Hof hotel has lovely guestrooms.

Name: Heimat
Description: This restaurant has a laid-back and refreshingly natural feel; its name reflects chef Niels van Zijl's deep emotional connection to his hometown (Heimat) of Utrecht. That sense of local pride also shines through on the menu, where vegetables are the undisputed stars and local suppliers play an important supporting role. Vegetarians are catered for with a fully vegetarian set/tasting menu, although you can opt for a main course with fish or meat. The cooking is playful, approachable and carefully crafted, but never loses sight of the ingredients themselves. Creamy ricotta is paired with blistered heritage carrots, a reduced carrot jus bound with butter, mustard seeds and kumquat to create a dish that is full of character. The alcohol-free pairings are another of the restaurant's strengths: inventive, vibrant and perfectly matched to the creative energy of this socially engaged establishment.

Name: Heimat
Address: 8F, 33 Wyndham Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Heimat is German for "homeland". After working in some prestigious kitchens, German chef-owner Peter Find reinterprets classics from his home country with sophistication, quality ingredients and dexterous care. The tasting menu takes diners on a journey across Germany with flavours from his childhood memories. Ask for the wine or juice pairing to accompany the food. And who can resist the gummy bear trolley at the end?

Name: Heimatbühne
Description: This alternative to the fine dining restaurant at Hotel Trofana Royal also serves culinary delights right next to the ski slope. In an inviting decor, diners can choose from an appealing à la carte selection of freshly prepared Tyrolean dishes. These are made with the finest regional produce, such as Paznaun Highland beef, Diasbach trout and traditional Alpine cheese. Open to the lobby and bar area, and with only a handful of tables, this restaurant is done out in lots of warm wood, creating a pleasantly cosy feel. Exceptionally courteous and friendly service.

Name: Heinzle
Address: Wachaustr. 280, Weißenkirchen in der Wachau, 3610, Austria
Description: The location right by the Danube is reason enough to stop by. The unobstructed view of the water and the greenery all around make the terrace a popular spot. Large windows ensure that diners indoors can enjoy the scenery as well. This family-run restaurant stands out for its honest, traditional cuisine built on regional ingredients, with an emphasis on fresh fish from local farms. Alongside salmon trout, pike-perch, char and more, the menu features specialities such as fried blood sausage slices with potato salad and pumpkin seed oil.

Name: Heinzler am See
Description: Whether you are in the mood for regional comfort food or something more international, the Heinzler brothers have got it covered. Their wide-ranging menu includes Swabian Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy), Arctic char and whitefish fillets, and yellowfin tuna sashimi. There is also an appealing selection of barbecue dishes with a choice of side dishes and sauces. You can choose to dine in the cosy Jagdstube ("hunting lounge") with its winning blend of traditional charm and modern design, or the lovely Panorama-Restaurant, whose large windows afford stunning views. Not forgetting the fabulous terrace almost touching the water! The waitstaff are personable and attentive – service is clearly a serious matter here. Tasteful and comfortable guestrooms available at the hotel, which also boasts a private beach area at the lake and a private jetty.

Name: Heldmann & Herzhaft
Description: Originally the home of an industrialist, this smart 19C villa is the perfect backdrop for the delicious cuisine of chef-patron Ulrich Heldmann. Diners choose from a varied seasonal menu and à la carte dishes based on fresh produce – and the "Menu Surprise" Wed-Thu. The setting is truly lovely, with its high ceilings, elegant hardwood floors and refined table settings; in summer, tables on the terrace are of course particularly coveted. And then there is the experienced, attentive and pleasingly laid-back service provided by a team under the management of hostess Petra Heldmann. The restaurant is also open for lunch Wed-Fri.

Name: Helen
Description: Chef Rob McDaniel and his wife Emily built this downtown Birmingham restaurant as an homage to Rob's maternal grandmother who gathered her family for meals that she cooked over her indoor grill. Here at Helen, many of the dishes feature grilled elements.The menu is concise and showcases plates with Southern and international flair. Warm angel biscuits served warm alongside a quenelle of whipped cane syrup butter will soothe your soul. Enjoy a bowl of comfort with braised Peruvian lima beans in a golden broth with coal-roasted rapini and garlic chili oil. Cobia is beautifully seared on the plancha for a simple-but-satisfying dish.

Name: Helen
Description: This stylish establishment in a well-heeled district of Paris is the haunt of a chef, who works only with wild fish sourced daily from small boats that he crafts simply and lovingly. Rather than fussy frills, the goal is to enhance natural seafood flavours (raw, grilled, plancha seared, steamed). The menu varies depending on the catch.

Name: Hello Beasty
Address: 95-97 Customs Street West, Auckland Central, Auckland, 1010, New Zealand
Description: In an area not exactly devoid of dining options, Hello Beasty stands out with its Asian-themed menu and vibrant atmosphere. The influences come from Japan, Korea and China so there’s something for everyone and everything is for sharing. Start with potstickers or the delicious brisket bao; pork belly with the crispiest skin is a must, while the prawn and crab toast comes with eye fillet and will satisfy any appetite. However busy it gets, the service team remain impressively unfazed and always make time to offer recommendations.

Name: Hello Sailor
Description: Hello Sailor, the younger sibling of nearby Kindred, occupies a prime position overlooking Lake Norman, and the two outdoor terraces are the place to be when the weather is nice (though inside by the wood-burning stove is certainly no consolation prize when winter arrives). While this neighborhood spot that works for all occasions could rest on its setting alone, the menu ticks all the boxes. Its lakeside location means you'll find plenty of seafood on the menu, and PEI mussels and oysters with a glass of wine or cocktail is never a bad idea. Friendly service completes the sunny picture.

Name: Hem
Address: 22 Market Place, Warwick, CV34 4SL, United Kingdom
Description: In the market square of this historic town, you’ll find a lovely little restaurant. Named Hem in reference to previous incarnation ‘Tailors’ – which before that was an actual tailor’s – it’s a simple and unpretentious place, where long-standing friends Dan and Seb run the show with a smile. Dan is the chef of the pair, cooking hearty and satisfying dishes that are classic in their origins but executed with refinement and a playful touch – such as venison haunch with pear, walnut ketchup and bacon jam. Go for one of the carefully curated wine flights.

Name: Hemel & Aarde
Description: Rene van der Weijden welcomes you to the majestic-looking building of Nox Hotel. Once a stately gentlemen's club, it is now also home to a restaurant with striking decor in soft shades of green. The high, sculpted ceilings are stunning. In the open kitchen, the chef creates inventive, occasionally daring dishes that always highlight the finest Dutch ingredients. Think raw kingfish rolled in herbs, accompanied by various textures of red cabbage, including an aromatic kombucha and a horseradish ice pearl. The presentation is elegant, the flavours often bold and the chef's ambition shines through in the thoughtful details and generous touches. Be sure to pay a visit to the adjacent wine to enjoy a select vintage and some bar snacks.

Name: Hemispheres Steak & Seafood Grill
Address: 2F, Sheraton Hotel, K5 Nghi Tam, 11 Xuan Dieu Road, Tay Ho Ward, Hanoi, 11207, Vietnam
Description: Embark on a culinary journey around the world with the freshest ingredients from the northern and southern hemispheres, as well as the east and the west. Tailor your itinerary across the continent, possibly with house-marinated Atlantic salmon from the north-west, or grilled New Zealand rack of lamb from the south-east. A fine selection of world-class premium beef steaks, complemented by assorted seafood, creates an appealing “surf and turf” feast. The views over West Lake offer a slice of tranquillity amidst the urban turmoil.

Name: Hen Mother Cookhouse
Address: 11705 Jones Bridge Rd., Ste. B 201, Johns Creek, GA, 30005, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted
Description: Hen Mother Cookhouse has a setting that befits its name. This Johns Creek charmer (there are two locations) has kitschy farmhouse down pat with blue walls, white-painted bench seating and wood tables, while Chef/owner Soraya Khoury's menu of breakfast and brunch favorites has exactly what you want. From avocado toast and quiche to Southern classics like sourdough waffles with fried chicken, if you want (and you most certainly do), mornings are met with a bevy of delicious choices, but it doesn't end there. Come lunch and BLTs, burgers, and baked goods are the perfect order. No matter your selection, it's all prepared with skill and care, and you'll have a hard time putting down your fork (though the portions are generous, and sides are shareable).

Name: Hendersons
Address: 7-13 Barclay Place, Edinburgh, EH10 4HW, United Kingdom
Description: In 1962, Janet Henderson opened one of Scotland's most famous vegetarian restaurants; decades later her grandson Barrie is running the show in a busy premises by Bruntsfield Links. The appealing, skilfully cooked selection of meat-free dishes are mostly vegan, with options like salt-baked celeriac and their take on classic haggis, neeps and tatties. Friendly service creates a lovely neighbourhood feel, while unfussy plant-based puddings are on hand to satisfy the most sweet-toothed of diners.

Name: Hendrik van Maurick
Description: A visit to this medieval castle (1257) is an experience in itself. The wooded surroundings, the drawbridge, the courtyard… This is a truly romantic setting, further elevated by a gorgeous terrace overlooking the moat. Inside, all that historical character meets with modern comfort. The imposing fireplace and the portrait of the knight Van Maurick holding a smartphone immediately catch the eye. The menu may seem classical at first glance, but it features inventive dishes in which Dutch produce is given a French twist. Think North Sea crab salad with cucumber sorbet and jus, celery oil, pickled daikon and wakame. This is sophisticated, vibrant and ambitious cuisine!

Name: Heng Gi Goose and Duck Rice
Description: The soya sauce duck is very popular.

Name: Heng Khao Moo Daeng
Address: 428/1 Namueang Road, Talat, Mueang Surat Thani, Surat Thani, 84000, Thailand
Description: This simple eatery is always bustling at lunchtime with queues for both dine-in and takeout. The owner's inviting and chatty demeanour sets the scene. His signature barbeque pork comes with crispy pork and sweet sausage inside and a large portion only costs 40 baht.

Name: Heng Long BBQ Chicken Rice
Address: Mei Ling Market & Food Centre, #02-42, 159 Mei Chin Road, 140159, Singapore
Description: The BBQ chicken rice is an absolute must, but the honey-glazed char siew and roast pork are also popular. Or opt for their brine-poached chicken – succulent, perfectly seasoned and with a wonderful velvety texture.

Name: Henri
Description: This laid-back bistro perfectly embodies the hip, urban vibe of Brussels’ Rue de Flandres and we warrant you will fall in love with its casual ambience, cobbled terrace and splendid choice of wines and Brussels’ beers. The dishes are free of frills, all the better to allow the ingredients to take front stage. Mussels in a pastis-flavoured sauce, beef tartare with a Thai slant or text-book perfect sole meunière: the chef enthusiastically navigates between influences with a fondness for fresh Mediterranean fare. Fine dining with a Brussels’ signature!

Name: Henri Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Having returned to his native Viareggio in 2021, Henri Prosperi, a gracious maître in the old-school tradition, will guide you with style and professionalism in choosing dishes that blend classic and modern approaches, with a penchant for some French influences. The menu, divided between meat and fish, always focuses on premium ingredients, the same character that distinguishes the wine cellar, rich with great national and international labels, from Sassicaia to Petrus, including the finest Italian and French sparkling wines. An open kitchen and outdoor seating!

Name: Henrich HÖER's Speisezimmer
Description: The 400-year-old half-timbered house, which houses Hotel Höerhof and this charming restaurant, makes you feel at home. The combination of historical surroundings and modern touches makes for a special atmosphere, to which the warm service provided by the owner also contributes. In summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous terrace in the secluded courtyard! The excellent cuisine comes à la carte ("Kleine Schlemmerkarte", Tue-Sat), as a seasonal set menu (Tue-Sat) and a fine dining set menu ("Genusswelten", Thu evening-Sat).

Name: Henriks
Description: This stylish restaurant is loved for its good food and attractive setting. The interior is chic; outside, there is a lovely terrace shaded by mature trees. Led by patron Claas-Henrik Anklam, the kitchen team combines Asian and Mediterranean influences with seasonal, regionally inspired cooking, including grilled dishes, lobster and caviar. The wide-ranging à la carte selection is complemented by a more budget-friendly lunch menu – ideal when time is short (takeaway is also possible). Beyond the impressive wine list, HENRIKS Bar beckons with long drinks, cocktails and more.

Name: Henriqueta
Address: Rua Aristides Espínola, 121, Rio de Janeiro, 22440-050, Brazil
Description: This “tasca” style restaurant in the southern part of Rio de Janeiro showcases the best of Portuguese cuisine in a bright environment with a glass façade, open kitchen and Portuguese ceramic decoration. The cuisine on offer dispenses with unnecessary frills, focusing on the quality of the ingredients and dishes designed for sharing, among which the “biff-anas açorianas”, a crispy bread sandwich filled with pork escalope marinated in wine and garlic, stands out. As a main course, we recommend the tender octopus “a lagareiro” roasted in oil, served with onion confit and mashed potatoes, followed by the “toucinho do céu” made with egg yolks, almonds and cinnamon, an authentic Portuguese dish if ever there was one!

Name: Henrock
Address: Linthwaite House, Crook Road, Bowness-on-Windermere, LA23 3JA, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets not allowed
Description: Named after a rocky outcrop on Lake Windermere, this elegant restaurant sits inside the charming Linthwaite House hotel and is part of Simon Rogan's ever-evolving empire. The décor is minimal yet cosy, with plain wooden tables and lovely artwork on the walls. Simon's sustainable ethos is evident on the menu, with many ingredients in the colourful dishes coming from his 'Our Farm' estate and other produce – like Cartmel Valley venison – sourced in the local area. Warm, friendly staff enhance the experience.

Name: Henry Robertson
Address: Palé Hall, Palé Estate, Bala, Llandderfel, LL23 7PS, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: Set within an impressive Victorian hotel, this elegant restaurant is named after the industrialist-cum-MP the property was built for. Take in lovely views over the garden as you enjoy attractively presented dishes from either the simpler lunch menu or more ambitious à la carte. Herbs, fruit and vegetables are grown on the estate, then crafted into seasonally minded plates that incorporate more produce from the local area. The wine list offers some interesting English and local Welsh wines.

Name: Henry's
Address: 922 Queen St. W., Toronto, M6J 1G6, Canada
Description: Of the city’s many, many wine bars, Henry’s is both the newest and one of the most accomplished. Globe lighting, forest green cushions and gold-trim tables lend a certain mid-century modern sleekness to this inviting, airy space, which includes a backyard patio and a retail wine shop just next door.The menu makes no commitments to any one cuisine, beyond working exceptionally well with the wines on hand. You could assemble dinner solely out of appetizers like beef tartare with smoked crème fraiche, shrimp toast and fried zucchini blossoms. But then you’d miss that superb skate wing set in a fiery curry. Some might choose wine for their dessert, but a recent ancho-chili and chocolate mousse made a compelling case for never skipping sweets here.

Name: Henry's Cuisine
Address: 301 E. Valley Blvd., Alhambra, CA, 91801, USA
Description: In an unremarkable building that nearly blends in with the rest of the street, Henry’s has quietly but confidently satisfied an ever-dwindling demand for homestyle Cantonese cooking since 2015. With a scarlet-red lobster as their logo, shells painted silver and gold and hung on the wall, and large groups huddled around platters of it, there isn’t much guessing as to what the signature is here. Come for dinner to unlock the menu’s full breadth of specialties. Highlights include delicately fried shrimp with salted egg as well as a striking deep-fried salted pig’s feet, its skin as crisp and crunchy as a chip. Vegetables are a must but ask what’s in season. We’re partial to the soothing, quiet bitterness of mustard greens with garlic.

Name: HerR
Address: Herrngasse 20, Rothenburg ob der Tauber, 91541, Germany
Description: The handsome herrnschlösschen hotel, located in the Old Town, is home to a delightful little restaurant whose stylish modern interior design seamlessly incorporates the building's historical architectural features – note the huge wooden beam dating back to 1526! Following the seasons, the five-course set menu features dishes such as "Norwegian skrei, celeriac, pak choi, sesame" or "Franconian lamb, Jerusalem artichoke, morels, Martini". The charming waitstaff will recommend the perfect wine accompaniment. Fabulous terrace in the baroque garden!

Name: Herb & Wood
Address: 2210 Kettner Blvd., San Diego, CA, 92101, USA
Description: This establishment enjoys a loyal following. The multilevel former warehouse could lean cavernous, but its barrel-vaulted ceilings and funky artwork exude a distinct Parisian bohemian warmth. The whole place is set aglow and everyone, including the staff, wants to be here. Its wide-ranging menu runs the gamut—from rustic, wood-fired dishes including grilled trumpet mushrooms and pizzas, to more refined plates like venison over buttermilk polenta. The PB&C, a chocolate-whiskey cake with peanut butter mousse and rich milk chocolate gelato, absolutely hits the spot.

Name: Herbsaint
Address: 701 St. Charles Ave., New Orleans, LA, 70130, USA
Description: More than two decades after opening, Herbsaint remains one of New Orleans’ most dependable dining destinations. Set along bustling St. Charles Avenue, the dining room hums with regulars, business lunches and visitors drawn by Chef Donald Link’s influential blend of French, Italian and Southern cooking. Signature dishes endure for good reason, including the rich house-made spaghetti with guanciale and fried egg and Muscovy duck leg confit served with dirty rice and citrus gastrique. Cornmeal-fried oysters showcase the kitchen’s lighter touch, while an excellent wine list and warm service reinforce the restaurant’s enduring appeal.

Name: Hercule Poireau
Address: 2 rue de la Nation, Périgueux, 24000, France
Description: At the foot of Cathédrale St Front, this restaurant that pays homage to the fictional detective occupies a 16C room with a pale stone vaulted ceiling. Thanks to his little grey cells, Poirot would no doubt have detected the sincerity behind the deliciously revamped recipes based on produce from the exceptional terroir of the Dordogne: terrine of semi-cooked foie gras and rhubarb pickles with Monbazillac; pan-fried magret de canard; tarte Tatin with salted butter caramel ice cream. A warm welcome and dynamic service.

Name: Herise İstanbul
Address: Reşitpaşa Mahallesi, Kongre Caddesi No:15/A, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34467, Türkiye
Description: Asude and Bahadir are ambassadors for Anatolian cuisine. She will gladly tell you all about their concept while providing attentive service and bringing refreshing mocktails to your table (no alcohol served here). He works to a single set menu that celebrates traditional flavours. Variations of tomato and pepper are a common theme in his diverse range of dishes, whether vegetarian or meat-based. His less-is-more approach is exemplified by the millefeuille of dry figs with Aegean olive oil, or the refined combination of rosewater, saffron, currants and rice. Herise Istanbul is one of a kind.

Name: Heritage Dulwich
Address: 101 Rosendale Road, Dulwich, London, SE21 8EZ, United Kingdom
Description: ‘Heritage’ is key to the cooking at this Indian restaurant in a smart suburban shopping parade, where skilfully prepared dishes are knowledgably balanced, well-spiced and packed with authentic flavours. Dayashankar Sharma – who has led many of London’s best Indian kitchens – cooks alongside his son Anmol.

Name: Hermann's Jagdstube
Description: The exclusive little restaurant in the luxe chalet hotel Bergwiesenglück promises a very special culinary experience. If you pre-order it, they serve a game-based set menu, comprising eight small courses made using meat solely from animals hunted by the chef himself – the unusual dishes include, for example, black grouse liver, chamois brain, deer bone marrow or deer tongue. The wine list includes regional and international classics. Optionally you can order the wine pairings devised to accompany the set menu. The friendly and laid-back service is infused with a personal touch. Warm wood and clean lines make for a chic and modern Alpine interior. There are just four tables. A floor-to-ceiling glass façade affords a view of the terrace and the mountains.

Name: Hermannshöhle
Description: Set in a former ferry house dating back to 1517, this establishment has been run by Wigbert Weck since 2007 and has a loyal following of regulars. The dishes created by the chef-patron are skillfully prepared from fresh ingredients with no unnecessary embellishments, and they are delicious! Tip: the surprise menu (only for the whole table). Complete with a glass-fronted wine refrigerator full of regional wines, the interior has the feel of a modern wine bar. Outside, the lovely terrace overlooks the Nahe River, which is just across the road. Two holiday flats can be booked for overnight stays.

Name: Herons
Address: The Umstead Hotel & Spa, 100 Woodland Pond Dr., Cary, NC, 27513, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Need a getaway but have limited time? Herons offers the experience of a country escape without the commute. Set within The Umstead Hotel and Spa on three acres of woodland, this restaurant is a showpiece for their nearby farm's produce. Try several dishes or opt for the chef's surprise five- course menu to relish fresh and vibrant plates crafted with care by Chef Steven Devereaux Greene. His South Carolina roots are best seen in dishes like shrimp and grits, and a tropical-inspired dessert that combines pineapple jam, rum whipped ganache and ginger sorbet is impressive. Be sure to consult the extensive, globally minded wine list. The restaurant has even developed several wines in close collaboration with the vineyards.

Name: Herrenhaus
Description: Herrenhaus is located in the centre of the picturesque old town. A cloister, where you will find a quaint little terrace during the summer, leads you to the restaurant on the first floor. The historical setting adds to the warm and welcoming atmosphere. The delicious food is prepared using select in-season regional produce. The dishes are served à la carte or in the form of a set menu. Tip: Inexpensive lunch deal. The genial and obliging waitstaff will be happy to advise you on your choices. There is also an attractively priced wine list dedicated to German, Austrian and Italian labels.

Name: Hertebos
Description: The walls of Yasmine and Yoshi's living room-style restaurant are adorned with photos that afford a glimpse into their past, while an open fireplace adds a snug cosiness. In both the set menu and the classical à la carte lineup, the freshness of the ingredients is paramount. The chefs are as creative with textures as they are with their knockout sauces. For instance, they coax out all the facets of raspberry and yoghurt in an extravagant cake soaked in Amaretto.

Name: Herzog von Burgund
Description: First you admire the attractive exterior of this stylish townhouse. Then, inside, the impressive, heritage-protected staircase. The two dining spaces (Erftzimmer and Gartenzimmer) form a classically elegant setting – the paintings by Düsseldorf artist Markus Tollmann draw the eye. The menu has a seasonal focus, and Wiener schnitzel is a house speciality. Friendly and experienced waitstaff. Delightful outdoor seating: The terrace is a verdant oasis in the heart of the city!

Name: Hestia
Address: 8 rue de la Huchette, Paris, 75005, France
Description: Hestia, goddess of the hearth, presides over this restaurant that absolutely oozes cachet, with its white beams, stone walls and mirrors. Normandy-born chef Loïc Dantec (previously at 114 Faubourg) devises a seasonal menu only, with dishes that hit the mark, such as Cantal pork entrecôte cooked over an open fire with sweet spices. All the meat is grilled to perfection on the barbecue, ready to be carved tableside. The chef cooks without showboating, making flavour the priority. His partner Filipe Fernandes competently and assiduously manages the restaurant floor.

Name: Het Binnenhof
Address: Bocht van Guinea 6, Goes, 4461 BC, Netherlands
Description: Het Binnenhof exudes all the charm of Goes's historic centre. A narrow alleyway leads you to this stylishly refurbished restaurant, which is tucked away in a courtyard and boasts an inviting terrace. The seafood comes directly from the Vismijn Colijnsplaat fish auction; the vegetables and meat are also locally sourced. Chef Arjen spoils you for choice with his à la carte and set menus, and it doesn't stop there! Generous and highly accomplished, he whips up the most fabulous sauces.

Name: Het Bosch
Description: Breathtaking – that's the word that comes to mind as the view over the Nieuwe Meer marina unfolds before you. This modern pavilion takes full advantage of its surroundings, and the terrace is the prime spot. The extensive menu features classic French brasserie fare elevated with inventive twists and includes steak tartare, vegetarian options and lobster dishes. Alternatively, you might like to try the poached salmon with a beurre blanc elevated by dashi and parsley oil – a feast for the eyes and the palate!

Name: Het Koetshuis
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The drive to this traditional house with a handsome thatched roof, deep in the woods, showcases the magnificent countryside of the Veluwe region. That same charm carries through to the terrace and the atmospheric interior. The cuisine is imaginative, built on playful textures and influences from around the globe. Picture Arctic char served with deep-fried kale and finely sliced green apple, as well as nasturtium, a cucumber pearl, tarragon ice cream and a herb-seasoned buttermilk sauce. The inspired wine recommendations hit the mark every time.

Name: Het Moment
Description: Nicolas Hauman’s former villa is steeped in an exquisite ambience that is quite unforgettable. Whether you opt for the classical à la carte lineup or the more modern menu, you know the ingredients will be first-rate. Lightly seared fillet of veal with a ratatouille and a mustard-spiked gravy or glazed whiting paired with crunchy asparagus, briny Limonium and vin jaune flavoured beurre blanc: a fine dining treat from the appetisers to the dessert, further enhanced by seamless, spot-on service.

Name: Het Nieuwe Palinghuis
Description: There is an authentic feel to the dining area of this charming seafood restaurant. Adorned with various nostalgic photos of maritime scenes, it harks back to its opening year: 1983! Over the years, Het Nieuwe Palinghuis has earned a reputation for its classic fish dishes. The menu features langoustine with an intense nantua sauce, sole Véronique in a full-bodied white wine sauce, as well as a distinctively herby eel in green sauce. The dishes here have always been big on flavour, steering clear of any unnecessary frills. A firm favourite!

Name: Het Oude Gemeentehuis
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Once the town hall, this is the ideal place for convivial dining. Original features provide a striking contrast with the modern design and warm colours. Indulgence is the name of the game when it comes to the food. Whether you opt for the rich lobster bisque, the sea bass with the rich beurre blanc or their contemporary take on tiramisu, you will be bowled over by the skill and charm of Niels Minkman and his team.

Name: Het Roode Koper
Address: Jhr. Dr. C.J. Sandbergweg 82, Leuvenum, 3852 PV, Netherlands
Description: At Het Roode Koper, diners are immersed in the fairytale setting of a romantic decor that exudes luxury and sophistication, set against fabulous English gardens and the forests of the Veluwe all around. Dennis van den Beld's cuisine is rather classical but in keeping with the times. This translates into fabulous sauces, an emphasis on the produce and creative garnishes. The excellent wine list offers both prestigious bottles and finds from small wineries.

Name: Het Seminar
Description: Het Seminar is an ode to nature that adopts "farm to fork" as its guiding principle. A former monastery, this upscale restaurant stands in its own grounds. From fruit and vegetables to livestock, everything is grown or reared on site – the focus is on sustainability. The chef invites you to create your own set menu from an array of classic-style dishes that showcase bold flavours and the freshest ingredients. For example, he expertly pan-fries duck breast to a rosy pink, elevating it with a lemongrass-infused duck jus; this is served with vegetable accompaniments such as broad beans and caramelised onion, which provides a touch of sweetness. At Het Seminar, the fertility of the Dutch soil speaks for itself.

Name: Het Sluishuys
Description: Hand-cut steak tartare with fine acidity, turbot à la meunière with a beurre blanc cooked in time-honoured tradition and ravioli stuffed with oxtail: these are the kind of classic dishes for which Erik Hendriksen is renowned. At this warm and welcoming restaurant, in an idyllic location by an old lock and close to a small harbour, familiar flavours are given the attention they deserve.

Name: Het Weeshuys
Description: Striking murals with a culinary theme give this orphanage chapel (1310) real individuality. The vibrant decor indoors is certainly a sight to behold, but there is also a courtyard terrace that is idyllic in fine weather. Opt for the lunch set menu or simply let the chef surprise you with inspired and delicate creations such as choucroute and prawns with an Asian twist, or a new take on wild boar terrine – a feast for the senses is guaranteed!

Name: Het land aan de Overkant
Description: Leuven’s urbanites don’t hesitate to desert their city centre in favour of a seat in this smart edifice. Natural light, artwork and a lovely terrace all combine to paint a pleasing portrait. First run your eye over the beverage menu and start with a refreshing glass of Gueuze beer, before moving on to peruse the wine list. The exquisitely presented dishes reveal unexpected combinations of ingredients, such as al dente confit of celeriac with cream of goat’s cheese and foie gras, smoked eel and chilled consommé of celeriac, eels and verjuice. At lunchtime, there is only a single set menu.

Name: Heugümper
Description: This venerable townhouse enjoys a fantastic location in the heart of Zurich – the small terrace is a lovely spot in the summer. With its elegant contemporary decor, the interior is also inviting, and the charming hostess provides attentive service. Prepared using select ingredients, the dishes draw on Mediterranean and Asian influences. Options on the menu range from veal cordon bleu with truffle Brie to tuna with sesame and a ginger and mango sauce. Shorter, simpler menu at lunchtime.

Name: Heunisch und Erben
Description: As a result of this place being both a wine bar and a restaurant, it has a remarkable wine list and around 120 wines by the glass to accompany the ambitious modern cuisine. From a lovely selection of dishes, diners choose four to nine courses to make up their meal. Relaxed, attentive and knowledgeable service is provided. On balmy summer evenings, tables on the terrace are highly sought-after. The name is a nod to Heunisch, a foundational progenitor grape (the parent of most grape varieties known and drunk today), and Erben, the "heirs", its descendants, which you'll find here on the wine list and the shelves.

Name: Hey Kiddo
Address: 4337 Tennyson St., Ste. 300, Denver, CO, 80212, USA
Description: Perched above Tennyson Street, Hey Kiddo stands out as the hippest of Denver powerhouse Chef Kelly Whitaker’s empire. The third-floor venue encompasses a rooftop bar area and a bespoke cocktail lounge in the back (referred to as “Ok Yeah”) but the restaurant is the heart of the operation. The playful menu centers around broadly Asian-inflected shareable plates like an exceptionally crunchy take on Korean fried chicken, or tender pork ribs with a salted plum barbecue sauce, accompanied by compelling sides like crispy potato pavé with a trout roe gravy, or an assortment of house-made pickles and kimchi. For a sweet finale, red miso ice cream can be customized with the likes of brûléed banana, broken cone or grappa whipped cream.

Name: Hibiki Seafood
Address: 356 Shizheng North 2nd Road, Xitun District, Taichung, 407, Taiwan
Description: The tables sport ultramarine glass screens in keeping with the maritime theme. There is no menu: guests pick something from the live fish tanks and the staff recommends how best to cook it. The local catch from Yilan and Penghu and imported seafood are prepared Taiwanese style, namely steamed or pan-fried with garlic to highlight their natural flavours. Those who prefer their fish as natural as possible can opt for sashimi.

Name: Hibinoryori Viola
Description: A mother-daughter team opened this restaurant out of a desire to spread Japanese culinary culture. The chef and author of the menu is the mother, herself the daughter of the head of a tea ceremony school. The guiding principle is to base the fare on daily Japanese home cooking. Soup stock is drawn with painstaking care from select seasonal ingredients. The salad of cooked vegetables in season is generously portioned, while steaming fresh-cooked rice is served with Japanese comfort food. Home-style fare infused with the spirit of kaiseki.

Name: Hidalgo
Description: Although fish dishes also feature on the menu, Hidalgo has long enjoyed a reputation for its excellent meat options thanks to its different cuts of steak and beef sourced from all around the world and cooked mainly (but not exclusively) on the barbecue grill. In a separate room(Aomi, a kind of restaurant within the restaurant), guests can choose from a menu dedicated uniquely (from antipasti to main courses) to Japanese Wagyubeef.

Name: Hidden Fish
Address: 4764 Convoy St., San Diego, CA, 92111, USA
Description: You’ll be on the clock at this tiny sushi spot, where the omakase is a 90-minute experience, but despite such punctuality, you will savor every bite here. In fact, you’ll find yourself slowing down to savor each and every creation from the talented chefs. However, seats here are hard to come by so be sure to reserve ahead of time or risk serious FOMO.Like other top tier sushiyas, they source both locally with San Diego uni and across the globe with Peruvian scallops and of course, plenty of Japanese species. A chalkboard menu keeps diners apprised of the current lineup, and for those who are still peckish after their tasting, there’s a bonus menu of handrolls and special seasonal nigiri for further sampling.

Name: Hidden Omakase
Address: 5353 W. Alabama St., Ste. 102, Houston, TX, 77056, USA
Description: Note: Temporarily closedTrue to its name, this dark, intimate space is sealed off from the strip mall outside—but when it comes to its reputation for a showy, immersive experience, the secret is certainly out. In the care of Chef Marcos Juarez, this 18-seat counter features a wide array of premium seafood prepared with a unique approach that bucks tradition. Chefs happily engage with diners, explaining each of the courses. Nigiri is at the heart of this meal, featuring fish aged in-house, and may include toro, uni and plump mussels. Come with high expectations and do bring liquor, if you're so inclined, as they don't have a license.

Name: Hidden Place
Address: 1F, Hidden Place Hotel, 57 Shengxing Road, Wuhou, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
Description: Once a protégé of the Sichuan culinary master, the young owner chose to open her first venture in a secluded, serene hotel. She aims to re-create ancient Sichuan recipes, using precise techniques and premium ingredients from around the world. Braised mandarin fish topped with chillies boasts tender flesh in an aromatic, spicy sauce. Guaiwei chicken is dressed in a blend of over 20 condiments for layered, complex flavours.

Name: Hide
Address: Concourse, Ritz-Carlton Residences, 105 Jalan Ampang, Kuala Lumpur, Kuala Lumpur, 50450, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Valet parking
Description: The entrance to Hide is tucked away in a secluded corner among some paintings. The interior has a trendy feel, with its U-shaped marble counter overlooking the open kitchen. The young head chef once worked in the US, and his season-driven tasting menu embodies the multicultural influences in Malaysian cuisine. Local produce and seafood are prominently used in dishes such as lobster mapo with Sichuan pepper oil, and puff pastry with kaya mousse.

Name: Hide & Seek
Description: If you like to dine in a lively, modern atmosphere, the restaurant of Hotel Giardino Mountain is for you. The interior design marries chic contemporary touches with rustic wood. Service is attentive and professional. Most importantly there is the Mediterranean and Swiss cuisine, which prioritises aroma and flavour and is made using fresh, often regional ingredients. At lunchtime, the menu is simpler than in the evening. The terrace is a lovely spot when the sun is out.

Name: Hide & Seek
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Ayurvedic philosophy inspires a special section of the menu, where Mediterranean cooking styles and ingredients merge with chef Francesco Leone’s colorful and joyful vision. His cuisine, not without international influences, finds its ideal setting in this refined restaurant inside the “Giardino” hotel. In the warmer months, dining on the magnificent terrace overlooking the garden with its pond and floating flowers is unmissable: a corner of priceless tranquility and beauty.

Name: High Street
Address: 101 S. 9th St. Door 1, Philadelphia, PA, 19107, USA
Description: The Franklin Building plays host to this modern American restaurant founded by Ellen Yin. It’s quite an operation, as besides the main restaurant there’s also a bakery next door if you want to take something home, along with a private dining space at the back for that big celebration. Furthermore, they hold classes for anyone who wants to learn how to bake or make pizza. Robustly flavored and generously sized dishes are the mainstay of the kitchen, which is visible through the glass walls. At lunch, most customers come in for a hoagie or a sandwich, while at dinner the menu expands to include a variety of pasta dishes and pizzas, all of which show a level of care, commitment and originality, so you can try a pizza with escargot and provolone, or black bucatini with braised squid. Service comes with a smile.

Name: Highwater
Address: 54 Cuba Street, Te Aro, Wellington, 6011, New Zealand
Description: Brick walls, a wooden counter and moody lighting set the easy-going, vibrant scene. The menu stars seasonal organic produce, sourced mainly from small nearby farms. The kitchen deploys nose-to-tail and roots-to-shoots concepts to reduce waste. Tender and flavoursome, charcoal roast Black Origin Wagyu paddle flank is served with a roast bone reduction, pine nuts and currants. The wine list demonstrates a soft spot for organic and biodynamic tipples.

Name: Highway4 (Hang Tre Street)
Address: 5 Hang Tre Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
Description: This Vietnamese tửu quán (tavern) has always been popular with the locals and tourists alike. Most diners take their time, enjoying the food and drink in good company. The inn serves Northern Vietnamese fare and we recommend the subtly flavoured appetisers, such as salads or spring rolls. The catfish spring roll is the tasty signature dish. The heart-warming main courses come in earthen pots. The deliciously tender oxtail stew with herbs is to die for!

Name: Hiis
Description: Head east towards the coast and you’ll find yourself in a rural setting that plays host to this old farmhouse on the Taju Estate. Hiis translates as ‘secret grove’ or ‘holy site’ and, along with the forest and garden, the restaurant operates as a collective dedicated to the health and wellbeing of others. Here, Daanius Aas offers a 15-course menu of ingredients foraged from the surrounding land, as well as lesser-used cuts of meat and fish, to just six tables. Creativity leads the way, with detailed techniques used to capture the best flavours and textures, and childhood memories also coming into play.

Name: Hijirizaka Wakei
Description: The restaurant stands on Hijirizaka, a road said to have been created by the Koya Hijiri, the wandering ascetics of Mt. Koya. The chef, a devotee of the tea ceremony, strives to embody the spirit advocated by tea master Sen–no-Rikyu: harmony, respect, purity and tranquillity. These profound words emphasise how people should treat one another, and the importance of mutual respect. To add an inventive touch to fare handed down over generations, continual innovation seeks new expressions of flavour while preserving the basics.

Name: Hijo
Address: 170, Section 2, Chang'an East Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: Here at Hijo, freshness is everything. Most seafood is shipped from Penghu, an outlying island known for its clean waters, which explains why the fish and shellfish taste better here. The kitchen keeps the cooking simple and seasoning light-handed. The space is divided into private rooms, and diners pick their seafood from the live fish tanks next door. Generous portion sizes make it the perfect spot for family dinners and get-togethers with friends.

Name: Hika by Roberto Ruiz
Description: Do you like wine tourism? If so, you can't miss this modern txacoli winery (also called Hika) and the restaurant inside, with large windows to enjoy the views of the vineyards and mountains. The chef Roberto Ruiz, who always covers his head with a typical txapela (beret), offers us through his menu and his tasting menu a traditional cuisine, with Basque roots, with specialities such as Tolosa beans, Stuffed baby squid in their own ink, José Juan Castillo style, Txangurro a la Donostiarra (spider crab)... Interesting facts: The appetizers exalt the products of his garden and the stews are prepared in an economical kitchen, with wood and charcoal.

Name: Hikari Japanese Roots
Address: Buenos Aires 16, Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, 35002, Spain
Location: Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Spain
Description: Located just a few minutes’ walk from the San Telmo park, this small Japanese-inspired eatery has a dining counter for just nine guests (the best option in our view) and several tables, where experienced chef David Rivero takes us by the hand on a journey across the best flavours found in Japanese cuisine. He does this via a single surprise Omakase menu (with an extra main course option available for a supplement) that he explains in detail to every guest at the same time, hence his requirement for customers to be punctual. Because of the restaurant’s success, we recommend booking in advance.

Name: Hikarimono
Description: Kan Sato, known affectionately as ‘Satokan-san’, loves hikarimono (literally ‘shining thing’: fish with silver skin, sliced with the skin left on), hence the shop’s name. The menu is composed with drinkers in mind, so this hikarimono is never left off. Sato’s offering of three courses—sushi and bar snacks, mainly nigiri, and bar snacks—as well as à la carte is pleasing. Hikarimaki of pilchard, shredded dried plum and bettarazuke (daikon pickled in salted rice malt) is famous. Sato’s aim is to offer a sushi shop where people drop in casually. The value for money truly shines.

Name: Hill Street Fried Kway Teow
Address: Pasar 16@Bedok (Bedok South Food Centre), #01-41, 16 Bedok South Road, 460016, Singapore
Description: This stall serves a single dish that is drop-dead perfect every time. Full-bodied wok hei, irresistible aromas and generous toppings like cockles, Chinese sausage, chives and bean sprouts justify the often hour-long wait.

Name: Hillenberg
Description: Perfectly pitched for busy Humlegårdsgatan is this stylish take on a classic brasserie. It has a smart, elegant feel and a hugely impressive wine cellar. Appealing Swedish classics are immensely satisfying yet exhibit a subtle modern touch and sense of finesse.

Name: Himitsu
Address: 1030 Torrey Pines Rd. G, La Jolla, CA, 92037, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Wheelchair access
Description: "Irasshaimase!" is the greeting commonly heard upon entering this cozy little sushiya. You’ll want to plan ahead to snag one of the eight coveted seats at the pristine counter, but it’s well worth the forethought, as these friendly chefs take great pride in discussing the quality of their fish and the techniques used to prepare your meal. It’s also a front row seat to their admirable knife skills.Such affability extends to the dining room, where servers flash big smiles and loads of greenery as well as natural wood come together to create a truly serene effect. Omakase is the way to go, but there are à la carte options as well—from appetizers, soups, sashimi and maki (sporting soft, well-seasoned rice) to specialty plates and daily fish specials.

Name: HimmerRiget
Address: HimmerLand, Lars Larsens Vej 1, Farsø, 9640, Denmark
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The impressive HimmerLand Resort sits in a rural spot but has everything you need, from lodges and a spa to bowling and minigolf, as well as this small, elegant restaurant. Both the décor and the cooking are modern, with the experienced chef creating a seasonal tasting menu that showcases a journey through Northern Jutland’s landmarks and ecosystems, from the fjords to the dunes to the forests. Dishes are intricate and well-presented, with a great understanding of balance and flavour, such as in the quenelle of monkfish with beurre blanc and vendace roe. The accompanying wine list is of the highest order.

Name: Hing Kee
Address: 1F, Bowa House, 180 Nathan Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: It started two generations ago in Causeway Bay but the family’s reputation for Boat People style cuisine was made in Tsim Sha Tsui. Elder sister heads the serving team; younger brother runs the kitchen. They are famous for their stir-fried crabs with black beans and chilli, roast duck and rice noodles in soup and congee. You can decide level of spiciness for some dishes. Guests aren’t seated until everyone in the party has arrived.

Name: Hinoki
Description: A bona fide Japanese restaurant in Brest! Hinoki is run by local lad, Xavier Pensec, a diehard fan of Japanese cuisine. Locally caught fish is handpicked with exquisite precision by the chef who reveals a genuine gift for the art of sushi and a deep-rooted understanding of the role of each ingredient. Sushi and maki are crafted in view of diners as the chef discreetly deploys his virtuoso talent in an experience that borders on ceremonial.

Name: Hinterding
Description: Dating back to 1904, this spruce urban villa has been known as a stylish culinary destination for aeons. Owners Klaus Weingartz (kitchen) and Elke Zeitner (front of house) have been running this establishment with great dedication since 2011. Ambitious classic cuisine made with select ingredients is served by charming waitstaff in comfortable and elegant dining rooms with high ceilings, or out on the gorgeous terrace. Set menus can even be pre-ordered to take home. Cookery classes and overnight accommodation are also available.

Name: Hippo
Address: 5916 1/2 Figueroa St., Los Angeles, CA, 90042, USA
Description: The name comes from the building’s former life as the Highland Park Post Office, but everything else here is Cal-Ital in spirit. The dining space is convivial and airy, with beamed ceilings and an open kitchen as its focal point. The vibe is as good for dates as it is for groups. Complimentary bread is rarely as satisfying as their focaccia, with its crispy, salty crust and soft interior. Begin with a sampling of small plates, like hamachi crudo topped with dollops of Meyer lemon relish. Then move on to freshly made pasta, like tortelloni with herbed ricotta in a lemon butter sauce before enjoying the chicken grilled over almond wood and served with a slightly spicy aji panca sauce and griddled potatoes.

Name: Hippocampus
Description: In the city's well-heeled Bogenhausen area, Hippocampus is no run-of-the-mill Italian restaurant; it is a ristorante with real character. The reins of this family business have now been passed on to the next generation, which is upholding the tradition of serving Italian cuisine. Order à la carte dishes or opt for the surprise menu. A two-course set lunch is available Wed-Fri. The impressive wine list features around 160 Italian labels. Expect attentive service, delivered with Italian charm. Add to this an attractive interior with stylish details such as half-wall panelling in walnut wood, marble floors and Art Nouveau lamps. The terrace is equally inviting.

Name: Hiroki
Address: 1355 N. Front St., Philadelphia, PA, 19122, USA
Description: Kyoto-born Executive Chef Hiroki Fujiyama was inspired by the machiya of his hometown when creating this stylish and discreet Fishtown spot. From the understated façade to the custom-designed furnishings, it feels authentic but also contemporary; just be sure to book a place at the 12-seat counter rather than at one of the tables. The omakase is also a blend of the modern and the traditional. You can expect over 20 courses, perhaps starting with an array of zensai, a bowlful of somen in pork and ginger broth, or grilled tilefish. The nigiri is sized quite small, with highlights that can include finely diced squid from Hokkaido and madai from Kagoshima. Be aware that it won’t always be Fujiyama-san behind the counter.

Name: Hirosawa
Description: The restaurant is a forum for his self-expression, so the chef named it after himself. Its modern Chinese fare incorporates elements of Japanese dishes and French techniques. Garlic is toned down to allow the aromas of ingredients to speak for themselves. Roasted pork fillet is cooked twice, sparing neither effort nor time. Hot pots, which layer the flavours of Chinese shinesāhi soup stock with seafood dashi, show imaginative flair. Plating Chinese food on Japanese vessels is a distinctive touch.

Name: Hirsch
Description: This upscale restaurant serves classic cuisine that draws on Baden's culinary tradition and is made predominantly with regional ingredients. Options such as braised veal cheeks or a tasty fish medley in beurre blanc are sure to whet the appetite. Abundant wood and decorative features provide a cosy backdrop. In summer, head for the lovely verdant terrace. Very friendly service. Given the proximity to Strasbourg, the Black Forest and Europa-Park, it is also worth considering staying in one of Hirsch's well-kept guestrooms or apartments.

Name: Hirsch Genusshandwerk
Description: This lovely village inn serves dishes with classical foundations and modern inspirations. The seasons call the shots, and there is a preference for quality produce sourced locally or even grown in the restaurant's own garden. Led by the proprietress, the cordial and competent front-of-house team helps create the welcoming atmosphere. The terrace is delightful in summer. They also have their own distillery.

Name: Hirschen
Description: Classic, seasonal and regional food is the name of the game here. Guests can enjoy fine dining and vegetarian options in the Zeitgeist restaurant, as well as house classics, including the signature dish: chateaubriand. Tip: The chocolate cake with coffee is sensational! Alternatively, you can order burgers, pasta etc in the cosy Hirschenstube. Popular terrace for summer meals, plus comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Hirschen
Description: The mindful concept shines through in Jonathan and Raphaela Burger's cuisine. Ingredients are sourced in the region, the fruit and vegetables are predominantly organic or grown by neighbouring farmers, and a nose-to-tail approach is applied to all produce. The latter philosophy is evident, for example, in a dish of grilled chicken hearts, pumpkin and Schupfnudeln (finger-shaped potato dumplings). They also enjoy cooking vegetarian fare, especially in winter when in-house fermentation plays a major role – for example, their "Vetterhof radish³, gochugaru, miso stock". The setting is gorgeous: authentic parlours, typical of the Bregenzerwald, or the turn-of-the-century ballroom in the Hirschen hotel, a hub of art and tradition dating back to 1755. The "Easy Lunch" menu features favourite dishes and classics. The tartlets and desserts by pastry chef Raphaela Burger are also tempting.

Name: Hirschen
Address: Breisgauer Straße 47, Freiburg im Breisgau, 79110, Germany
Description: One of Freiburg's culinary institutions, Hirschen draws diners to the peaceful neighbourhood of Lehen. An authentic and cosy Baden-style atmosphere awaits you in the dining area of this charming historic inn, which is run with dedication by the Baumgartner family. For years, the kitchen has been renowned for its masterful blend of regional fare and classic French cuisine. Dishes such as Baden lamb's lettuce with roasted goose liver and black truffle, and "winemaker's skrei" with cabbage braised in champagne, glazed grapes, bacon strips, butter croutons and mashed potatoes showcase the finest, freshest ingredients. The carefully curated wine list also highlights wines from Baden and France, including prestigious labels such as Romanée Conti. Service is friendly and attentive. The restaurant is part of the hotel of the same name.

Name: Hirschen
Description: A beloved fixture in the valley, this restaurant is part of the long-established hotel of the same name, located right in the heart of the village on the banks of Glotter River. In its rustic yet elegant interiors, diners are waited on by a friendly front-of-house team. For decades, the kitchen has showcased the best of Baden and French cuisine, with a pronounced emphasis on seasonality – be it game, mushrooms or asparagus. Both at lunchtime and in the evenings, the cooking is ambitious. Dishes such as grilled octopus served on a bed of curried lentils and vegetables, or veal loin in a cream sauce with chanterelles are available à la carte or in the set menu. The wine list is dominated by labels from the Baden region.

Name: Hiræth
Address: 587 Cowbridge Road East, Cardiff, CF5 1BE, United Kingdom
Description: The Welsh word ‘hiræth’ has no direct translation, but it broadly refers to the pride and longing the Welsh feel for their homeland. That ethos comes through at this likeable little restaurant, thanks to the use of regional produce including locally foraged ingredients and some from their own smallholding. The cooking comes in a tasting menu format, with dishes flying highest when emphasising the quality of their ingredients, like sous-vide skrei cod with a mussel and wild garlic velouté. The team show pride in their work and will ensure you are well looked after.

Name: Hisa Polonka
Description: In the centre of Kobarid, a lively and colourful establishment that perfectly reflects the personality of its owner, Valter: a passionate wine lover and a host of great warmth and charm. The surroundings are simple and rustic, with wooden tables, lit candles and a warm and informal atmosphere. The cooking is frankly regional, made of charcuterie, excellent cheeses from local shepherds and dishes of genuine, hearty character, brought to life by bold flavours and accompanied by a very interesting wine selection at notably fair prices. Not to be missed are the Žlikrofi alla Polonka, ravioli filled with herbs and potato, with a most appealing aromatic profile, served with a generous dressing of butter, chives and crispy guanciale. Upstairs, a number of comfortable rooms are available for those wishing to extend their stay. A word of advice: covers are limited, so arriving early is advisable to secure a table.

Name: Hispania
Description: Hispania is smart and contemporary, but down to earth, like the Spanish cooking it honours. Marcos Morán of the Michelin star restaurant, Casa Gerardo, in Prendes, Spain, continues to roll out a varied menu that will enable you to sample tapas, traditional rice dishes, together with more modern creations. The accent is on big-boned, punchy flavours. The memory of the Galician veal, cooked rare, served with foie gras and an espuma of potatoes and truffles lingers still with our inspectors. A lineup of authentic Hispanic flavours, designed to transport you straight to southern Europe.

Name: Historisches Gasthaus Sanct Peter Restaurant Weinkirche
Description: Having been renovated following the disastrous floods of 2021, this restaurant gives off an impression of classical elegance. A 13C church with a gallery forms the core of the establishment. There are also two other attractive dining spaces (called Alte Lay and Walporzheimer Himmelchen). The delightful terrace to the rear of the building offers a view of the greenery. The menu features dishes with regional, seasonal and international influences. Classics include braised ox cheeks in Ahr valley Burgundy sauce, and turbot in Ahr valley blanc de noir sauce. The selection of Broggsitter wines is impressive, and there is a well-stocked wine shop on site, too. From 2-6pm, you can order from the smaller menu, with options such as the platter of cold meats and cheeses. They also run Hotel Sanct Peter in the town.

Name: Hito
Address: 26 rue de la Fonderie, Toulouse, 31000, France
Description: Hitoshi Araki's restaurant is near Place des Salins. Working alone in the kitchen, the chef cooks up creative French cuisine enriched with passing references to Japan. His indisputably precise execution, remarkable cooking technique and bold flavours come through in dishes such as melt-in-the-mouth pork belly preserved in its own juices and lightly caramelised on the outside – delicious! The lunch menu is a steal.

Name: Hiu
Address: Avenida del Baix Camp 2, Cambrils, 43850, Spain
Description: ‘Hiu’, which can be translated from Thai as ‘to be hungry’, is the name of this restaurant which defines itself as ‘restless’ and brings the flavours of Bangkok to the centre of the gastronomic capital of the Costa Dorada. Chef Sergi Palacin, well supported in the dining room by his sister Judit, enjoys creating his own special mixes for his curries, as well as fermented products and kombucha vinegars. He also sources typical ingredients from the local area, such as sea fennel, which are rarely found on restaurant menus. This fusion-focused eatery offers an à la carte service (half portions are available) and two tasting menus and one dedicated to the classics of the house. We loved the Asian-style clams marinière!

Name: Hiyakawa Miami
Address: 2700 N. Miami Ave., #5, Miami, FL, 33127, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list
Description: Is there a dining room cooler than Hiyakawa Miami? Probably not. Modern art hangs throughout the space that is art itself, with the counter and tables under an arch of backlit, undulating wood slats. This intimate stage glows at the bottom of an apartment building in trendy Wynwood.Top-quality seafood flown in from Japan and beyond meets creative flourishes like cured egg yolk and Okinawa salt. A multicourse omakase is available at the counter and in the dining room, and the a la carte offers a range of items in addition to nigiri, sashimi, and maki. Don't sleep on the Sakana Kara Age, or fried fish fillets sprinkled with seaweed salt and resting in a fish broth, but it's the lamb chops, doubling as performance art thanks to a bed of burning rosemary, that make a lasting impression.

Name: Hiç Lokanta
Address: Yeni Mahallesi, Zafer Caddesi No:52, Urla, Izmir, 35430, Türkiye
Description: Housed in a former Greek theatre in the picturesque old town of Urla, this trendy establishment combines an industrial aesthetic with an inviting atmosphere. The restaurant's freshly pressed olive oil is a highlight of its modern cuisine, which is full of personality. Acidity and spice bring the dishes to life. Start, for example, with pickled sea bream with green apple and a splash of lime juice, then follow that up with melt-in-your-mouth charcoal-roasted lamb cutlets with parsley, olive oil and onion – straightforward and delicious. The ingredients speak for themselves.

Name: Hiély-Lucullus
Address: 5 rue de la République, Avignon, 84000, France
Description: ‘Pérouvence’, which is a porte-manteau of Peru, the homeland of the chef’s wife, Patricia, and Provence, chef Gérald Azoulay is from Avignon, is how the chef describes his culinary theme. Peruvian spices and a commitment to sustainable development guide Azoulay who takes us on a flavoursome globetrotting journey dominated by acidity, spices and embers: provençal stock, aji chuncho and smoked garlic; celeriac, green aji rocoto and a veggie reduction; Costières squab, ocopa, aji panca and gin. The interior sports a plush Belle Epoque edge and the wine list stars tipples from both countries.

Name: Hiša Raduha
Description: Every day, Martina Breznik, the fourth generation to run this restaurant, selects ingredients from her own garden, the nearby forest and a network of growers and farmers from the surrounding area. Early spring vegetables, cheeses and autumn mushrooms reflect the character of the Luče region throughout the year. The menu changes daily according to availability and showcases the ingredients used in the kitchen. Don’t miss the trout from the River Savinja served with vegetables from the kitchen garden. Young Filip will be happy to offer wine recommendations, including labels such as the delicate and rounded Meum Chardonnay 2019 from nearby Styria.

Name: Hiša Torkla
Description: The open grill at this restaurant is a regular feature, delighting guests with a wide array of top-quality meat dishes. From Tomahawk to chops, and fillets to picanha steak (the meat is sourced locally, as well as from further afield), the quality is excellent, while the service is quick yet friendly and discreet. The large picture windows boast fine views of the surrounding hills, giving guests the pleasant sensation of dining outdoors. There’s also a second dining room with a cosy, minimalist feel, which is perfect for winter evenings. Local, seasonal ingredients take centre stage here, such as asparagus, which is served with fuzi pasta and scampi or grilled as a side dish, and truffles, which feature in a number of dishes, including deliciously creamy mashed potatoes.

Name: Hiệu Lực Canh Cá Rô Hưng Yên (Hoàn Kiếm)
Address: 39 Hai Ba Trung Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 111000, Vietnam
Description: These speciality rice noodles from Hưng Yên Province are topped with crispy deep-fried climbing perch and bouncy fish cakes for umami; mustard greens and green onions add freshness. Diners choose between silky flat rice noodles and plump red grain noodles for a perfect bite.

Name: Ho Chu Yuan
Address: 63 Nanzhong Street, North District, Hsinchu City, Taiwan
Description: The decor may feel a little dated, but the room is clean and well maintained. Taiwanese classics are the strong suit here; traditional recipes with authentic local flavours keep diners coming back. Their sautéed beef with scallion stands out for its tender meat and spot-on seasoning. Prompt service keeps the wait time to a minimum. Note that the restaurant has irregular days off, so check their website before heading there.

Name: Ho Kee Dessert (To Kwa Wan)
Address: Shop 111 & 122, GF, I-Feng Mansions, 237A To Kwa Wan Road, To Kwa Wan, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: The staple in Mong Kok for over 30 years moved to this location in 2020. Rest assured their traditional sweet soups like black sesame paste, and glutinous rice balls in ginger syrup taste as good as ever.

Name: Ho Lee Fook
Address: 3-5 Elgin Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Walls covered in gilded maneki-neko, mahjong tiles, pop art and red Chinese floral motifs make this a bold, unorthodox spot for a fun night out. The 80s Canto-pop soundtrack is also a proud expression of its local DNA. The open kitchen on ground level is a spectacle to behold and its creative Cantonese cooking harnesses bold distinctive flavours and wok hei. Try the crispy three-yellow chicken with sand ginger dip, and other wok-fries. Check ahead for dishes that need pre-ordering.

Name: Hoa Túc (Sài Gòn)
Address: 74/7 Hai Ba Trung Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: Remodelled from an old opium refinery, Hoa Túc boasts an al fresco dining area steeped in an early 1900s circa Parisian vibe, while the Colonial-style interior pays homage to Vietnam’s history. On the menu, traditional Vietnamese dishes are updated thanks to fancy presentations. Start with refreshing pink pomelo salad with crabmeat and shrimps, followed by bò lá lốt bánh hỏi (grilled beef wrapped in betel leaves on a rice noodle nest).

Name: Hock Hai (Hong Lim) Curry Chicken Noodle
Address: Bedok Interchange Hawker Centre, #01-58, 208 New Upper Changi Road, 460208, Singapore
Description: The curry broth may be only mildly hot, but its flavours are deep. The chicken is tender; potato and tofu puffs soak up the sauces. Besides curry, there is satay chicken served on your choice from three varieties of noodles.

Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Address: Pasar 16@Bedok (Bedok South Food Centre), #01-50, 16 Bedok South Road, 460016, Singapore
Description: Fish balls are tender and rich. The al dente noodles marry well with the fresh broth.

Name: Hodan Yalıkavak
Address: Kudur Mevkii Sehit Engin Buyuksoylemez Caddesi No:9, Bodrum, 48890, Türkiye
Description: Çiğdem Seferoğlu invites you to the Avantgarde Refined Yalikavak Hotel, home to her open-air restaurant that boasts a magnificent view of the sea. More compelling still is her personal take on the region's culinary bounty. Her light and elegant cuisine highlights fish and seafood with a feminine touch. She confits gurnard in olive oil, which renders the texture wonderfully soft, and serves the fish with fennel seasoned with turmeric and coriander seeds, a blend of purslane and mint leaves with nectarine, and warm Turkish bread. The chef also prepares meticulous vegetarian dishes and proves that healthy food can indeed be profoundly flavoursome.

Name: Hoe Kee Kitchen
Address: Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre, #01-39, Blk 505, Jurong West Street 52, 640505, Singapore
Description: There is always a queue at this popular stall. Steamed chicken rice with tender meat and flavourful rice perfumed with chicken oil is the must-try. Char siew and roasted pork are also good – order a combo of either.

Name: Hof Grothues-Potthoff - Hasenklee
Description: A charming modern restaurant serving ambitious seasonal cuisine that is strongly influenced by the region and often incorporates home-grown fruit and vegetables. The set menu has four, six or eight courses; its vegetarian counterpart comes in a four- or five-course format. The service is friendly and the wine recommendations helpful. In the attractive courtyard, there is also a bakery, a farm shop and a farm café, as well as a hotel. Alternatively, Hasenpfeffer is open in the evenings for traditional dishes with modern influences.

Name: Hof Ter Doest
Description: A 17C monastic farmstead and its 13C barn depicts the picturesque setting of this country restaurant, run by the Dendooven family. You will taste delicious local turf (beef and poultry in particular) and surf (oysters and lobsters from the tank) produce. Hearty, wholesome cooking such as crispy shrimp fritters or Belgian Blanc Bleu beef roasted in a wood-fired oven. Luxurious guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Hof aan Zee
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Just 500m from the North Sea, Hof aan Zee is set in a historical Scandinavian farmhouse nestled in tranquil natural surroundings. The chef has developed his own Zeeland-inspired Nordic style – playful and expressive, with notes of fermentation, hints of smoke and a full appreciation for local produce such as Eastern Scheldt fish and seaweed. He adds punch to raw wild duck tartare with wild garlic capers, finely chopped shallot, a potato emulsion and blackcurrant powder for herbal vibrancy. This is a culinary journey defined by purity and a deep reverence for the local environment. Take the opportunity to stay in one of the guestrooms by the kitchen garden – an experience not to missed!

Name: Hof van Herstal
Description: What used to be the guesthouse of Lilbosch Abbey now exudes the charm of a classic fine dining restaurant. Built in 1890, this stately property is surrounded by a lovely garden perfect for al fresco dining on sunny days. Martin Bruggeman demonstrates time and again that he is a consummate craftsman. He relies largely on local ingredients, from game provided by hunters in his circle to fruit, vegetables and herbs grown in his own garden. Wild duck breast, full of character and cooked to a beautiful pink, is served with a rich duck jus à l'orange, red cabbage and sautéed girolles. The chef's sincere pride in his work is more than warranted.

Name: Hofgut Hohenkarpfen
Description: This restaurant enjoys a wonderful location in the middle Baden-Württemberg's oldest nature reserve and boasts stunning views – it's well worth booking a table on the terrace. In what was once the dairy of the over 300-year-old farmstead, diners are pampered with delicious food and attentive service. The modern cuisine incorporates classic and regional influences, as well as international, sometimes Asian touches. The former barn of the heritage-protected estate has been transformed into a hotel with attractive and cosy minimalist-style guestrooms. Tip: Take the time to look around the art museum.

Name: Hofmeisterei Hirtzberger
Address: Hauptstraße 74, Wösendorf in der Wachau, 3610, Austria
Description: This building has a long history. Built in 1320, it was originally part of a monastery – Stift St Florian. Today, it is home to a charming and elegant restaurant with a lovely vaulted ceiling. The kitchen serves a modern take on classic cuisine. In addition to two set menus with four to seven courses, there are daily specials. Standout dishes include "Irish rock oyster with a clear Bloody Mary and celery stick", sweetbreads with pimientos, chipotle and lime, and Wiener schnitzel with potato salad. Everything is prepared using select ingredients. To complement the food, there is a fantastic wine list comprising over 2 100 labels. The champagne and Veltliner selections are especially enticing.

Name: Hofstede Meerzigt
Description: Zoetermeer harbours a secret oasis that is waiting to be discovered.
