This enchanting estate boasts a chef’s table in a wine barn, a wedding venue in a converted stable, a terrace overlooking a lush garden, not to mention a stylish restaurant in a converted 17C farmhouse. The hospitality here is genuine, as is the kitchen team's appreciation of their ingredients. Alain Adriaanse shares his passion by delivering dishes that give familiar flavours the odd twist. With an Asian touch and fresh flavours, he elevates the sea bass tartare to new heights. He also puts a unique spin on steak tartare by adding playful textures. The extensive wine list is the icing on the cake.

Name: Hog Island Oyster Co.
Address: 1 Ferry Building, #11, San Francisco, CA, 94111, USA
Description: Can’t make the trip to Marin to shuck oysters on Hog Island’s docks? They’ll bring Tomales Bay’s finest to you at this buzzing cityside outpost in the Ferry Building, which draws long lines of tourists and locals for platters of some of the sweetest, freshest bivalves on the West Coast. You’ll receive all the accompaniments — lemon, Tabasco, mignonette — but they’re good enough to slurp solo. Once you’ve had your fill, sample other aquatic offerings: crudo featuring sustainably caught sea bass; a rustic seafood stew loaded with prawns, clams and mussels; as well as the exceptional Manila clam chowder. Throw in the expansive Bay views from the patio and dining room, and those lines come as no surprise.

Name: Hohenhaus Grill
Description: This is the second restaurant of the idyllically situated Hohenhaus hotel, a magnificent property steeped in history. The interior has a classic, rustic decor and a warm atmosphere – plus a lovely 18C tiled stove. The seasonal cuisine is based on premium ingredients, sourced from the region for the most part. Delicious options include barbecued wild game sausage made with meat hunted on site and served with Hohenhaus potato mash, or braised local mutton. It is a treat to sit on the terrace and take in the surrounding countryside.

Name: Hoi An Sense
Address: 6F, 12 Phan Ke Binh, Tan Dinh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: Exiting the lift onto the sixth-floor restaurant with a charming lotus pond and iconic lanterns feels like entering the ancient town of Hoi An. The Huế-style rolls with pork and pickled shrimp feature fresh vegetables, a hint of purple sweet potato and a tangy vinegar sauce. Another standout is the grilled sea bass wrapped in pork belly with lemongrass, complemented by pickled radish and shiso leaves. Private dining areas, separated by traditional screens, are available.

Name: Hokkien Huay Kuan
Address: 5F, Xintiandi Style I, 177 Madang Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: The interior is inspired by Fujian-style ink paintings, with water features dividing the room into zones. On the menu, premium produce from the province is deftly prepared by Fujian natives for the most authentic experience possible. Try the signature Shuizhu seafood trio – live prawns, razor clams and giant red squid are blanched in a mild mala broth over a bed of pickled broccoli stems, cucumber and bean sprouts for crunch and tartness.

Name: Hokkien Man Hokkien Mee
Address: Blk 19, Toa Payoh 7, #01-264, Kim Keat Palm, 310019, Singapore
Description: As its name suggests, this stall specialises in Hokkien fried noodles in a garlicky broth made with prawn heads. Besides the typical toppings of prawns and squid, you may order others, like egg or abalone, at an additional cost.

Name: Hokkien Street Bak Kut Teh
Address: Hong Lim Market and Food Centre, #01-66, Blk 531A, Upper Cross Street, 051531, Singapore
Description: The dark amber coloured bak kut teh from this stall is loaded in herbal goodness. Pair with pork knuckle, pork intestines, steamed fish, pork tail, pork kidney or pork liver on the side, as you prefer.

Name: Hokusaï
Address: Metropolitan Paris Tour Eiffel, 3 rue des Belles-Feuilles, Paris, 75016, France
Description: This hotel on Place de Mexico is introducing a new concept of Japanese cuisine with a South American twist. In a contemporary, minimalist setting, the menu combines signature rolls, sushi and teriyaki chicken with ceviche and Hispanic ingredients such as chimichurri sauce and jalapeño. Freshness and flavour are the order of the day.

Name: Hollow Bottom
Description: It doesn’t take long after you enter this welcoming pub before you notice how fiercely proud it is of its horseracing links. Don’t be surprised to see the day’s runners and riders on the TV in the memorabilia-filled bar, where you can settle in for a local ale and the ‘Nap of the Day’ lunch deal. For more substantial fare, head to the beamed dining room for classic pub dishes ranging from Scotch eggs to gammon chop. For dessert, the black treacle and date pudding provides a delightful sugar rush that will have you hurtling over the finish line.

Name: Holm
Address: 28 St James Street, South Petherton, TA13 5BW, United Kingdom
Description: Situated within a charming village, there's something special about this former bank, which has been impressively converted into a spacious restaurant with eye-catching architecture. Sit in the chic dining room with its distressed designer style, bag a spot at the kitchen counter or head to the lovely rear terrace when the sun is shining. Choose from a range of menus, all of which are underpinned by a commitment to seasonal ingredients. If you want to explore more of the Somerset countryside, there are seven bedrooms available to stay the night.

Name: Holsterhof
Description: With the hard work of hostess Lissa and chef Kaj, the restaurant at Holsterhof camping farm has gradually evolved into a sought-after culinary destination, set in a modern, light-filled space surrounded by lush greenery. The service is relaxed and friendly. The chef is an expert sauce maker who creates daring combinations on the plate, without making things overly complicated. His exquisite red curry with coconut milk adds depth of flavour to the tender quail leg with black lentils. Working with two set menus, he consistently surprises with subtle nuances.

Name: Holy Carrot
Address: 156 Portobello Road, Notting Hill, London, W11 2EB, United Kingdom
Description: London’s constantly expanding vegan food scene received another boost when this former pop-up and supper club opened up permanently on Portobello Road. It’s the ideal place for convincing your carnivorous friends of the virtues of plant-based cuisine, as each dish bursts with colour and creativity. The ‘small’ and ‘large’ plates are best shared to sample the broad range of cooking techniques, from barbecued carrot to coal-roasted leeks. The dining room itself – filled with polished concrete and light Mediterranean colours – provides a soothing backdrop that enhances the experience.

Name: Homa Central
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: It may be located in the historic Dorćol quarter, but Homa sports a thoroughly modern look and feel. Take a seat on the leafy terrace during the day, or in the softly lit restaurant come nightfall, to enjoy modern bistro cuisine with an emphasis on Mediterranean influences, in an informal atmosphere.

Name: Home Dishes
Address: 260, Section 1, Wenxing Road, Zhubei City, Hsinchu County, Taiwan
Description: Green wainscotting and seating provide visual continuity with the lush outdoor greenery, while splashes of orange add contrast. The kitchen team, who have experience in Cantonese, Taiwanese, Hakkanese and Sichuanese cooking, craft an eclectic Chinese menu that crosses geographical boundaries. Try their signature sautéed squid in salted egg yolk sauce, shredded beef with yellow chives, or fried crispy duck.

Name: Home Grown
Address: 968 Memorial Dr. SE, Atlanta, GA, 30316, USA
Description: Located in the Reynoldstown neighborhood in East Atlanta, Home Grown is a classic all-day breakfast and lunch spot complete with knotty pine paneling and booth seating. While it has a retro feel to it, don't assume you know everything on this menu. Instead, expect oodles of Southern charm and definitely ask about the daily specials, since you may come across items like house-made tamales, Gulf red snapper tacos, lasagna or even a pu pu platter with frog legs and crab claws. The focused menu stays largely local in both theme and sourcing, delivering country cooking that never disappoints. Case in point? That open-faced buttermilk biscuit layered with perfectly crisp chicken drowned in hearty pork sausage gravy, of course.

Name: Homer St. Cafe
Description: Nestled within a hip neighborhood, Homer St. Cafe entices with its inviting patio, but step inside and and you'll quickly see that this contemporary bistro is no slouch indoors, either. Equal parts trendy and quirky, with chairs doubling as wall hangings, Homer St. Cafe delivers on its promise of comfort food done really well. The rotisserie chicken is the draw, brined in their signature sauce overnight to render tender, flavorful meat. Order it half or whole and then tuck in to the crispy skin doused in gravy or buttermilk ranch. Sided by fluffy, buttery biscuits, it's a stick-to-your-ribs satisfying meal. If you have room, order the cheesecake with white chocolate-almond crumble resting over quince preserve.

Name: Homestead Kitchen
Address: Prudom House, Goathland, YO22 5AN, United Kingdom
Description: The North York Moors and their produce are the inspiration behind this charming little restaurant housed inside a rural, stone-built former farmhouse. Chef-Owner Peter Neville and his partner Cecily Fearnley show great pride as they enthuse about their environmental philosophies. Local produce – be it Moorland roe deer, Whitby crab or any number of ingredients from the kitchen garden – is used in hearty dishes that pack a punch when it comes to flavour. Sauces and accompaniments are a particular strength of the kitchen.

Name: Honey & Co
Address: 54 Lamb's Conduit Street, Bloomsbury, London, WC1N 3LW, United Kingdom
Description: There's a bright, pared-back style to this Middle Eastern restaurant consisting of several light and airy rooms; opt for a seat in the middle one, or on the pavement terrace in the summer months. Breakfast is served daily, offering the likes of shakshuka and bureka, while later on the menu includes a range of colourful sharing plates. Start with meze such as the creamy hummus with green chilli tatbila, followed by larger dishes such as sea bass and fennel tagine with a well-balanced white wine and orange sauce.

Name: Honeysuckle
Address: 631 N. Broad St., Philadelphia, PA, 19123, USA
Description: There is no exact right way to experience Omar and Cybille St. Aude-Tate’s darling restaurant on North Broad. You could post up at the big bar or hold court on a large communal table or ease into the couches. In this airy, industrial space, you have choices, just as you do with their wonderful, Afro-centric prix fixe. Hush puppies come crowned with country ham and paired with smoked bacon aioli. You’ve never seen a potato salad like this one or had fried fish with crème fraîche and chive-dill sauce. How about wagyu beef cheek and oxtail tamales? Course after course, find refinement and imagination, careful calibration and attractive presentation. Service is equally warm and attentive, and the whole thing comes together like a charm.

Name: Hong
Address: Ritz-Carlton Riyadh, AlHada Area, Mekkah Road, Riyadh, 11493, Saudi Arabia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,No alcohol served,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Luxury, elegance and Chinese cuisine come together on the second floor of The Ritz-Carlton Hotel, Riyadh at this restaurant overlooking the hotel’s leisure club pool. The extensive menu boasts a wide range of authentic and bespoke Chinese dishes such as tasty dim sum, classic Peking duck, spicy Sichuan beef and the ever-so-loved sweet and sour prawns. Come Saturday night for a special-priced menu showcasing their dim sum selection.

Name: Hong 0871
Address: Building 6, E9 Zone Innovation Works, Shuangshu North Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
Description: Nestled in an industrial park, Hong 0871 is a bit out of the way. But that doesn’t stop gastronomes from making a trip there for their refined Yunnanese food deeply rooted in traditions but updated with creative twists. Most ingredients are shipped from Yunnan and the menu changes regularly. But try stewed pig skin with red bean and preserved vegetable when it’s available: gelatinous pig skin soaking up the flavourful sauces is truly decadent.

Name: Hong 0871
Address: 5F, Shanghai Chengtou Holding, 130 Wusong Road, Hongkou, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: From the range of fresh Yunnanese produce displayed at the entrance, it's no surprise that this restaurant specialises in that province's cooking. Start with Nuodeng ham, cured for three years, with wafer-thin rushan (dry cheese), followed by steamed or deep-fried lard-layered buns with "winter melon" pork and bean sauce filling. The mushroom feast in summer is also a highlight. The Yunnan tea flight or Yunnan fruit drinks are the perfect accompaniment.

Name: Hong Khao Tom Pla
Address: 5 Kra Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: There is always a queue in front of this small shop. The mainstay on the menu is seafood. Dishes are carefully prepared by the owner, and the fresh prawns are a must. Check the whiteboard for the daily catch.

Name: Hong Kong Cuisine
Address: 1F, Elegance Court, 2-4 Tsoi Tak Street, Happy Valley, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: This upstairs restaurant is helmed by Chef Li, who started cooking professionally in the UK at the age of 16 and his dishes are rooted in Chinese traditions, but underpinned by modern French techniques and novel food combinations. He has an affinity for perfumed oils and the use of fried tofu and fried pork lard in caramelised sweet and sour Iberico pork is ingenious. His aromatic smoked soy sauce chicken is also unmissable.

Name: Hong Kong Food Street
Address: 23015 Colonial Pkwy., Ste. a101, Katy, TX, 77449, USA
Description: Congee with abalone and chicken. Pork and shrimp wontons in a clear, light broth. Portuguese egg tarts. In a non-descript shopping center in Katy, this family-owned restaurant brings a taste of Hong Kong to Houston. The modern dining room features sleek light fixtures and handsome private dining rooms fit with lazy susans. And unlike some restaurants that compile an endless book of options, the kitchen here keeps things tight with a relatively curated selection of classics. Nothing is rushed or thrown together, and food arrives piping hot. Beautifully fried shrimp with candied walnuts is an indulgent throwback. Shrimp and tofu fritters delight as well. On weekends, be sure to ask about any seafood specials.

Name: Hong Kong Old Restaurant (Wujin)
Address: 1F, Sheraton Changzhou Wujin Hotel, 1 Yanzheng West Avenue, Wujin, Changzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: The Hong Kong-based brand started in 1991 and this outpost was opened its doors in a majestic hotel in 2010. With over 20 years of experience, chefs from Hong Kong are well versed in iconic Cantonese fare from seafood dishes and Cantonese barbecue to dim sum and stir-fries. Try their famous roast goose with wafer-thin, crackling skin and tender, juicy meat. Some seafood and barbecue dishes need pre-ordering. The elegant room provides the perfect foil for a culinary feast.

Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Address: People's Park Complex Food Centre, #01-1064, 32 New Market Road, 050032, Singapore
Description: Offers xiao long bao, dumplings and hand-pulled noodles.

Name: Hong Wen Mutton Soup
Address: Beauty World Food Centre #04-20, 144 Upper Bukit Timah Road, 588177, Singapore
Description: In operation for over half a century, this stall is now run by the second-generation owner and his wife. Their signature soup comprises mutton, tripe or tendon in a garlicky and peppery broth with strong herbal accents.

Name: Hong Yu Fang
Address: B1-06, Mix 6, 686 South Xizang Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: A household name in Huangpu district, this place has been around for 10-plus years. Regulars keep flocking to its new shop since it moved into a shopping mall. Open in the morning only, it always attracts a queue of customers coming for a hearty meal. With their juicy, generous pork filling, Shanghai classic potstickers are a must-try. Cabbage rice with sausage and salted pork is another hit, each grain of rice enrobed in creamy lard.

Name: Hoog Holten
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Hoog Holten steals your heart before you have even taken your seat. The drive to this romantic spot introduces you to the splendour of the Salland countryside. Eating on the terrace, which has a hunting lodge ambiance, is highly recommended! Lunchtime features a simple à la carte selection, but in the evening, the chef takes classic dishes to new heights with innovative ideas, in a set menu that changes daily. For example, he serves duck breast with an orange-infused jus, and he adds candied kumquat to al dente vegetables for a tangy twist. Consider an overnight stay for a more immersive experience.

Name: Hook
Address: North Plantation, St Peter Port, GY1 2LQ, United Kingdom
Description: After admiring the view of the harbour opposite, enter into The Hook’s ground-floor Casbah bar, where you can sip a cocktail before dinner and perhaps be tempted by the enticing nibbles and flatbreads. Upstairs, the main event awaits, with an appealingly varied menu that ranges from small plates to whole fish and nose-to-tail cooking over the open fire. Clean, uncluttered dishes are the overriding theme, such as succulent scallops with punchy XO sauce or skate wing with caper butter. Ask for a table by the window for the best views, or in a booth for more privacy.

Name: Hool
Address: Rua de Santa Maria, Largo da Oliveira, Guimaraes, 4800-443, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Visiting Guimarães is like diving into Portugal’s history, a city revered for its historical importance in the country and acknowledged as “the birthplace of the Portuguese nation”. Located in the Hotel da Oliveira, right next to the impressive Church of Nossa Senhora da Oliveira, this venue boasts a classic décor, highlighted by stone walls and ceilings adorned with wooden beams. The culinary offering, designed by Chef Vítor Matos and overseen daily by Chef Liliana Moura, showcases a modern and creative cuisine with Mediterranean touches, taking traditional roots as its reference point. The menu, which includes some vegetarian dishes, is rounded out by two tasting menus (Raízes [“Roots”] and À Descoberta [“Discovery”]).

Name: Hop Yik Tai
Address: 121 Kweilin Street, Sham Shui Po, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: The menu at this always busy shop features Hong Kong-style snacks like fish balls, pork skin and braised radish. The hugely popular rice rolls are silky-smooth, with a hint of richness from the lard.

Name: Hope & Anchor
Address: Sluice Road, South Ferriby, DN18 6JQ, United Kingdom
Description: Don’t be put off by its location next to the cement works, as this rustic, nautically themed pub with Humber views is definitely worth the visit. Carefully prepared British dishes display touches of originality and are full of flavour, with top quality ingredients leading the way and fruit and veg from their own smallholding. Meats are aged in a glass-fronted drying cabinet and cooked in the Josper oven; some are designed for sharing and they even offer Wagyu. Bedrooms are modern and some have estuary views.

Name: Hopmanns Olive
Description: With great dedication, the Hopmanns have been running this friendly, sleek, modern restaurant for over 20 years – Ingo heads up the kitchen; Petra is in charge front of house. Based on classical foundations, the cuisine is seasonal and draws on Mediterranean inspirations. One of the classics is, for example, gently braised lamb shank. In summer, you can also take advantage of the gorgeous terrace. Tip: The adjoining historical engine shed is an ideal location to book for events.

Name: Hoppe's
Description: The atmosphere is welcoming and lively, and the food is great – it's no wonder that people come back again and again. The menu features dishes from Alsace and Baden, with mouthwatering options such as "coq au vin à la chef", beef sirloin served with roasted onions and spaetzle, or Baden-style pike dumplings. They also do Flammkuchen. There is outdoor seating to the front of the building.

Name: Hoppá! Bistro
Description: This contemporary eatery stands out amongst the myriad choices on vibrant Október Street, both for its smooth service and its modern, well-presented cooking – and it's certainly a popular spot. The menu sees traditional Hungarian recipes brought up-to-date, and there’s a range of daily specials and an excellent value lunch menu on offer too. You might find smoked catfish with onions and sesame seeds, followed by veal with bread dumplings and sage, then, for dessert, crème brûlée accompanied by seasonal fruit. Local beers and wines complete the picture.

Name: Hordago
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: High up on the Lizarrieta Pass on the French-Spanish border, at the end of a remote road, this typical Basque inn has a chequered history, including – legend has it – a stint as a smugglers' den. Now, thanks to chef Rémy Le Charpentier (previously at the restaurant Arraya, also in Sare) and his partner Mikela Luro, the place is definitively on the up. Local ingredients, herbs, condiments and mushrooms (picked by the chef) make for a pretty and flavoursome fiesta in dishes pepped up by creative touches: line-caught bigeye tuna, fregola sarda salad, lemon, ginger and candied tomato. Last but not least, the restaurant's terrace affords a lovely view.

Name: Horgonyzó Kisvendéglő
Description: Simplicity leads the way at this endearing restaurant set just a short stroll from the River Tisza. The room has an unfussy lodge style and there’s plenty of outdoor space courtesy of both a front and rear terrace. Cooking is fresh and well-executed, and offers something for everyone, from Hungarian classics to pizzas, burgers and street food. The wood-fired oven plays a key role, and everything is prepared with love and care.

Name: Hors-Champs
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Stefan Jacobs has metamorphosed the Ernage farmstead. This gifted chef has opened a B&B, a bakery and a tasteful restaurant that sports a rough, brutalist look. His sustainable ethos can be tasted in subtle dishes, rife in unorthodox and playful combinations. His devotion to the produce of his own cottage garden and that of local market gardeners is unwavering. He may use cucumbers in a myriad of ways, such as in a concoction of mussels, briny seaweed and fresh veggies. Or would you prefer a veggie burger stuffed with different textures of courgettes, radish and turnip and served with a veggie gravy that is reminiscent of a big-boned BBQ sauce? This light-hearted culinary ethos is paired with an unconventional wine list that has been savvily curated to enhance the food’s numerous nuances. A generous ode to the region!

Name: Horta
Description: This restaurant, also part of the PortoBay group, embraces a concept centred on healthy comfort food. The dining experience places great emphasis on local, locally sourced ingredients, with greens and vegetables taking centre stage. The bright interior features natural touches that harmonise perfectly with the wooden furniture and warm-toned lighting; outside, the discreet and pleasant terrace blends seamlessly into the surrounding greenery. The menu includes a variety of vegetarian and vegan dishes, such as Baba Ganoush Hummus served with pickled onion and sesame crisps, without overlooking fish and meat options, as well as an excellent selection of desserts made with fruits typical of Madeira.

Name: Horta
Description: The heart of Villa Crespo, a district that is becoming popular with foodies, is where the duo of Lucas Díaz and Clara Chavarría have set up shop, with the former in the kitchen and the latter front of house. Before opening their own eatery, this couple spent some time in the Algarve in Portugal (hence the name of the restaurant – “horta” is the Portuguese word for “vegetable or market garden”). They define their cuisine as “honest cooking” and this philosophy is clearly demonstrated in the dishes they create: “Every dish that we serve at Horta is an expression of our love for food and a homage to the bounty of nature and its wealth of flavours”. In this modern eatery, dominated by a white colour scheme and with a large round communal table on the small patio-terrace, the cuisine could be described as contemporary and built around micro-seasonal ingredients. The à la carte includes signature dishes such as tortellini with parmesan mousse, butter, sage and walnuts. The exquisite homemade desserts provide a fitting finale!

Name: Hortùs
Description: Hortùs means ‘garden’ in Latin and plants are at the heart of the cuisine of chef Clément Lessoud (former sous-chef to Ludovic Turac at the restaurant Une Table au Sud in Marseille). His creative, healthy and eco-minded cooking (i.e. organic ingredients and limited animal protein) is an ode to the South in the broadest sense, and more particularly to the flavours of the Mediterranean: pissaladière with creamy potatoes and capers; squid like a cacio and pepe carbonara with guanciale bacon; blackberry sorbet and a coffee ice cream cone.

Name: Hosiló
Description: The owners here appear to know all their customers and, such is the warm and laid-back atmosphere, you’ll find yourself wanting to become one of those regulars yourself. The name translates as ‘small room’, an apt description for this single-storey building sandwiched between two larger structures in a side street not far from the House of Collections. The market-led, weekly changing menu is appealingly concise, comprising a couple of starters and three main courses. Expect a daily catch and lots of heartening, flavour-packed dishes like peas on toast with shallots or Iberico secreto with peaches.

Name: Hospiz Alm
Address: St. Christoph 18, Sankt Anton am Arlberg, 6580, Austria
Description: Just so you know: This place is a haven for wine connoisseurs! The Gothic wine cellar is a real treasure trove, boasting a unique collection of large bottles that is world-famous, not least for its Bordeaux selection. Magnums, primats: you name it, they have it. Be sure to take a look at the impressive Wine Dome with its private dining table for exclusive tastings. In the restaurant itself, a typical ski hut feel prevails at lunchtime, but in the evening, it's all about fine dining in a lovely cosy setting brimming with Alpine charm.

Name: Hosszú Tányér
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: This romantic little restaurant sits in an attractive courtyard setting and is keenly run by its hands-on owner Franciska. Nothing is too much trouble for her when it comes to her guests, who she encourages to relax and fully appreciate the experience. The five-course tasting menu comes with plenty of little extras and the flavour-packed dishes are truly beautiful to look at – with flavours to match. In an all-encompassing experience, the contemporary artwork on the walls changes every two months along with the menu – and the ceramic dishes are specially designed by the chef himself.

Name: Host
Address: 33 rue des Dames, La Rochelle, 17000, France
Description: Alice Roger and her partner have set up shop just a stone's throw from the market, in a simple, contemporary location inspired by their first meeting in the United Kingdom. The warm, unpretentious welcome reflects the philosophy of the restaurant: getting to the heart of the matter. Organised into market-inspired lunch options and a more ambitious tasting menu featuring premium ingredients, the chef's cuisine exudes well-defined flavours. Dishes such as bluefin tuna with beetroot and sorrel, and a dessert bursting with colour and flavour – coffee, tonka bean, hazelnut and Peruvian chocolate – speak to her talent!

Name: Host
Address: 13 Ranelagh, Dublin City, D06 V0C1, Ireland
Description: A modern, simply-furnished neighbourhood restaurant with a buzzing atmosphere and a super-friendly team. Ingredient-led, Italian-influenced cooking means an abundance of natural flavours; the concise, daily changing menu features prime meats, homemade pasta and dishes designed for sharing.

Name: Hostaria Baccofurore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Patience is needed to get to this restaurant from the coast, as a result of the winding road which makes its way through small villages, but once here the view of the sea is breathtaking. The village of Furore is built alongside the road and is famous for the Marisa Cuomo winery situated opposite the restaurant. The cuisine is as impressive as the vista, with its focus on different local ingredients cooked with a mix of traditional influence and imagination. Comfortable guestrooms are also available, almost all of which have been recently renovated and boast impressive views.

Name: Hostaria alla Tavernetta
Address: Via Artico di Prampero 2, Udine, 33100, Italy
Description: A venue that welcomes warmly, thanks to a lively, family atmosphere. A lit fireplace fills the air with the scent of burning wood, while wooden furnishings and linen runners blend with background music to create a relaxing setting. At the table, authentic flavors: from Friulian frico with Montasio and potatoes to plum gnocchi cloaked in clarified butter and cinnamon, to succulent goose leg. Mediterranean forays also appear, such as the tuna tataki with anchovy sauce and bottarga. For those who wish, a carefully crafted vegan menu is also available.

Name: Hostaria da Franz
Address: Salizada Sant'Antonin, sestiere Castello 3499, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: Founded in a different venue by an Austrian soldier in the late 19C, this historic Venetian restaurant is now run by owner Maurizio, who oversees the front of house in a courteous yet friendly manner. He introduces guests to its variety of dishes, which aim to please rather than surprise. Fish specialities are to the fore here.

Name: Hostaria dai Musi
Description: Offering a limited à la carte that includes fish dishes (including raw options) which vary according to market availability, this restaurant serves what it describes as “typically modern cuisine”. The breaded and fried anchovies with a typical saor sauce and lemon gel are particularly good, plus the menu features a selection of typical regional specialities. The pleasant setting is enhanced by the backdrop of the large central square in a pedestrianised area on the edge of the old town. The drinks menu includes an excellent selection of wines, plus a good choice of local beers.

Name: Hostaria del Pavone
Description: A small gem for fish enthusiasts, this delightful restaurant situated amid the alleyways of the historic centre (just 2 minutes’ walk away) boasts a quiet ambience with a white colour scheme and minimalist decor chosen by the exuberant owner. Although the menu focuses on fish and seafood (the raw fish dishes are superb), the pasta dishes and main courses are also excellent. To round off a delightful dining experience, the wine list includes some surprising top-quality labels. A must!

Name: Hostaria del Teatro
Address: Via Ordanino 5b, Castiglione delle Stiviere, 46043, Italy
Description: In the heart of the small town, within a rustic building enriched by refined interiors and an atmosphere that is at once warm and homey, the cooking distinguishes itself through a carefully considered and territorially inspired offering, with one dish that is most certainly worth tasting: the unmissable duck agnolini with their jus and black truffle, an authentic signature of the house.

Name: Hostaria del Vicolo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in a central yet secluded location, this intimate and elegant restaurant serves typical Sicilian cuisine with a focus on fish, vegetables from the kitchen garden and delicious cheeses. A good wine selection completes the picture.

Name: Hostellerie De Biek
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: We wager that before you even set foot in this family-run eatery, you will have fallen in love with the authentic Flemish village. The immense windows of the former brewery overlook the village and a sheltered terrace, while the striking interior sports timber rafters and brick walls. Before relaxing in one of the comfortable guestrooms, treat yourself to something from the extensive menu. Brabançon-style pheasant or bouchot mussels served in a spicy nduja and red curry sauce: the chef adds a kick to Belgian classics thanks to playful, creative inventions. A knockout lineup of regional produce.

Name: Hostellerie Les Gorges de Pennafort
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The restaurant has an elegant, contemporary decor and a terrace beneath the plane trees. The setting is enticing, and the food even more so. Flowers, spices, herbs and the chef's personal touches bring together tradition and generosity.

Name: Hostellerie Stafelter
Description: This hostelry is emblematic of Tom Brosius and his outlook. The interior is warm and elegant, and the flavoursome food is free of fussy frills. He cherry-picks premium market-fresh produce and locally grown ingredients, concocting veggie-led recipes oozing in character. The repertory is rich in pedigree Belgian favourites like pot-au-feu made with fork-tender chuck beef and a delicious green veggie sauce. At lunchtime, choosing between the set and à la carte menus can be something of a conundrum. Comfortable guestrooms await you should you wish to extend your stay in this welcoming establishment.

Name: Hostellerie de l'Abbaye de la Celle
Address: 10 place du Général-de-Gaulle, La Celle, 83170, France
Description: Near Celle Abbey, this remote fine dining inn occupies a stunning 18C edifice. Part of the Ducasse Group, the restaurant boasts all the facilities one would expect of a luxury establishment, including a finely crafted Mediterranean score with a soft spot for veg, illustrated by stuffed Provençal vegetables overflowing with herbs and garlic. Unostentatious tradition.

Name: Hostellerie de la Mer
Description: The chef crafts cuisine in tune with the zeitgeist, wonderfully blending fish from the local catch and ingredients from Brittany's terroir, such as house-smoked salmon, tangy herb cream and buckwheat blini, or the blanquette of monkfish and Molène sausage, vegetables and steamed potatoes. The cooking is precise and accentuates the well-chosen ingredients!

Name: Hostellerie des Châteaux
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An elegant and intimate backdrop for modern cooking with good classical foundations : millefeuille of Rosheim snails with wild garlic and parsley, or fillet of turbot, champagne beurre blanc and black bean cream. Comfortable guestrooms that combine the contemporary with traditional Alsatian style.

Name: Hostellerie du Château des Fines Roches
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: On a hilltop in the heart of the prestigious Châteauneuf-du-Pape vineyards, this flamboyant miniature Palais des Papes commands superb views over the vineyards, the Alpilles, the Luberon and Mt Ventoux. The restaurant serves delicate cuisine inspired by Provence and the Mediterranean: line-caught pike-perch, courgette flower and ricotta, shellfish jus; Costières de Nîmes pigeon cooked whole, corn with black garlic and Albufera sauce. All washed down with wines from the estate.

Name: Hostellerie du Château des Monthairons
Address: 26 route de Verdun, Les Monthairons, 55320, France
Description: This family-run château restaurant serves meticulous cuisine, in which more contemporary touches meet classic foundations. As you might imagine, this 19C château in the Meuse Valley is a superb backdrop, with mouldings, old hardwood floors and plush drapes.

Name: Hostellerie du Grünewald
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Fresh, healthy food, but also deliciously generous. This very pleasant bistro with a fine terrace provides an opportunity to sample simple ingredients devoid of unnecessary frills. Save room for the scrumptious desserts. Elegant guestrooms ensure sweet dreams.

Name: Hostellerie du Prieuré
Description: This 18C sandstone former convent chants a pure-bred Gallic culinary litany based on regional produce (rack of lamb from the Moselle meadows, fillet of Lorraine beef) and seafood (brill, line-caught whiting, scallops). The portions are generous and the desserts are divinely decadent. Charming welcome.

Name: Hosteria Giusti
Description: Hidden away in the back room of the historic Giusti delicatessen, which has been famous for over four centuries, is a small dining room with just four tables. Simple and pleasantly retro, this is th perfct place to soak up the authentic spirit of Modena’s culinary tradition. The menu is a sincere tribute to Emilian cuisine: it begins with charcuterie, mostly from Mora Romagnola pigs reared in the wild, accompanied by the ever-present gnocco fritto and fragrant pasta fritters.This is followed by fresh pasta, the star of iconic dishes such as tortellini in capon broth and tagliolini with cheese and walnuts, before moving on to slow-cooked meats, including the outstanding beef stew with mashed potatoes and the traditional recipe for fried cotechino with Sorbara zabaione, a precious tribute from the Morandi family. The desserts are simple yet delicious and include panna cotta with saba (grape syrup), a perfect blend of tradition and simplicity.All that’s left is to wish you “buon appetito”.

Name: Hosteria La Cave Cantù
Description: Situated within the 18C Cantù monastery, now also home to a museum and library, this modern restaurant with a friendly ambience in its dining rooms and wine cellar also boasts an attractive outdoor space and a convenient car park. The menu features personalised cuisine with the occasional exotic influence prepared by the owner-chef (his wife, who works front of house and oversees the excellent wine list, is from Ecuador). The result is colourful, generous and beautifully presented cuisine which is full of flavour.

Name: Hosteria Toblino
Address: Via Garda 3, Sarche di Madruzzo, 38070, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The most welcoming section of the extensive Cantina Toblino complex is home to the large, contemporary and minimalist-style Hosteria. Here, a young chef serves simple reinterpretations of regional dishes with a focus on zero-mile produce with the occasional yet astute use of ingredients from further afield.

Name: Hosteria del Platano
Description: Situated on the main road overlooking the lake, this pleasant family-run restaurant serves excellent traditional cuisine with a focus on local fish. Atmospheric dining room with stone walls and vaulted ceilings, plus an attractive outdoor space, and friendly, attentive owners.

Name: Hostería de los Palmeros
Description: An impressive family-run restaurant occupying a building that was once a hospital for pilgrims along the Way of St James. To a backdrop of rustic-classic decor, choose from an extensive regionally focused à la carte complemented by three set menus (Bordón, Escarcela, and Compostela). The cuisine here has a very strong regional focus with an emphasis on locally sourced ingredients, including standout game options (partridge, pigeon, venison etc) and locally grown ingredients (alubia beans from Saldaña, vegetables from the province of Palencia etc).

Name: Hosun Nagashima
Description: Emmachi is where the chef was born and raised. He turned the family home into a restaurant, pledging to contribute to the town he loves. ‘Hosun’ means ‘a little square’ or ‘the space occupied by my heart’; the Japanese of old believed that the heart covered about 9 square centimetres, and the chef wants his shop to be a place where the hearts of guests and chef come together. Cuisine is focused on dashi, with harmony between ingredients and broth. The flavour of the seasoned first dashi in soup dishes derives from makombu seaweed. Char-grilled fish is paired with dashi paste.

Name: Hot and Hot Fish Club
Address: 2901 2nd Ave. S., Ste. 110, Birmingham, AL, 35233, USA
Description: With history dating back to 1994, Chris and Idie Hastings have cooked their way into the very fabric of the city’s culinary tapestry. Now located in trendy Pepper Place, the bustling space features a curved chef’s counter in the kitchen as well as ample bar and table seating. Their respect for the seasons means that the menu is constantly on the move. Come winter, look for hearty preparations like rabbit pappardelle with butternut squash or ancho-rubbed Iberico pork chop with apple chutney. In the summer, everyone comes for the tomato salad, which features a towering stack of heirloom tomatoes dressed up with lady peas, fried okra and a zippy balsamic vinaigrette. For dessert, chocolate souffle with crème anglaise is a lovely, sweet finale.

Name: Hotell Borgholm
Description: The beautiful island of Öland is famous for its wild herbs, and that’s reflected in the cooking at this historic hotel’s restaurant, where the chefs enhance their elaborate dishes with thyme, basil and a host of other flavours from the 100-variety-strong garden. The original, boldly flavoured cooking comes in a tasting menu format, marrying classical techniques with subtle modern ones in dishes such as pan-fried red kingfish with spring chlorophyll, pickled cloudberries, saffron butter sauce and bronze fennel. The accompanying wine list is a real treasure trove for oenophiles.

Name: Hotwoods (Xihu)
Address: 1F, Building 27, Xixi Yihao, Ziyun Street, Xihu, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: This bustling spot serves barbecue in Texan, Brazilian and Argentinian styles. With a wood-fired smokery and ovens on site, the place exudes intoxicating smells. Try slow-smoked beef brisket, either grain-fed from the U.S. or grass-fed from New Zealand: the former is richer, the latter leaner. Pronounced smoky notes complement the beef perfectly. Grilled pineapple in banana walnut sauce for dessert cuts through the richness. The wine list is worth exploring.

Name: Hougang Traditional Famous Wanton Noodle
Address: 51 Old Airport Road Food Centre, #01-35, 51 Old Airport Road, 390051, Singapore
Description: The traditional wanton here is generously filled with pork, either blanched and served in noodle soup or deep-fried. The noodles, cooked to order, boast bouncy texture. The yellow shrimp broth is loaded with flavour.

Name: House of Lechon
Address: Acacia and Tojong Street, Cebu, Cebu, 6000, The Philippines
Description: Immensely popular with locals and visitors alike, this place celebrates Cebu's iconic dish. With its crispy skin and tender, flavourful meat, lechon is a true cultural staple, to be savoured here along with other local favourites. For an accessible introduction to regional cuisine, it serves a variety of portion sizes in a comfortable, spacious setting – both indoors and out. A welcoming spot that captures the essence of Cebuano culinary heritage.

Name: Hozan
Description: Hozan’s allure lies in its menu’s exhaustive range of fish dishes. Having apprenticed at a seafood restaurant, the owner-chef is a master of fish preparation. Fresh and aged fish are handled differently, conveying all the depth and subtlety of their flavours. The meal begins with a seafood iimushi (mochi rice steamed with toppings). For soups, the dashi stock is drawn from the seafood, modulating the flavour. Keen that every guest should enjoy to their heart’s content, Hozan offers rice in earthenware pots as a choice of white rice or fish takikomi-gohan.

Name: Hu Ge Si Fang Cai
Description: Next to a cultural park, this restaurant stands in serene, lush nature. The interior, too, is pleasing, with its retro water town decor. On the menu, Hangzhou classics take centre stage; river fish stands out in particular. The slaughtered-to-order river eel is steamed with preserved mustard greens and has oily flesh and deep umami. The fresh local vegetables and traditional staples such as Hangzhou style tossed noodles and sticky rice cake are also worth trying.

Name: Hu Qing Yu Tang Yao Shan
Address: 98 Zhongshan South Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: Hu Qing Yu Tang is a renowned Chinese medicine shop and this restaurant is its culinary venture, specialising in medicinal cooking. The chef complements ingredients with the therapeutic properties of herbs to derive maximum benefits. Huang qi river shrimps, steamed fu ling dumplings, and black sticky rice cake with ginseng are all unique creations you won't find anywhere else. For optimum results, pair your food with medicinal wines or healthy drinks.

Name: HuThoPi
Description: Run by Hugo, Thomas and Pierre – aka HuThoPi – this compact restaurant a stone's throw from the Marché d'Aligre boasts a vibrant, unpolished decor with exposed stone walls, hardwood floors, jars of fermented vegetables and an open kitchen. Having worked at some top eateries, from luxury hotels to trendy restaurants (Le Meurice, Plaza Athénée, Oka, Cobéa, L'Ours etc), the three friends serve vegetable-forward, wholesome and balanced cuisine based on seasonal produce: Marmande tomatoes and piperade espuma, yellowtail crudo and ajoblanco, red mullet with saffron sabayon, Paimpol beans and lardo di Colonnata.

Name: Hua Chi 88
Address: 2F, Hyatt Regency, 88 Huachi Street, Suzhou Industrial Park, Suzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: The head chef is a Suzhou native with over 30 years of experience in Jiangsu cooking. Only the freshest local produce makes it into his repertoire, which boasts spot-on seasoning and exceptional wok hei. His signature braised boneless beef cubes melt in the mouth; the sticky, briny-sweet dark soy sauce is rich and mellow. The steamed sponge cake, freshly made daily, is a great way to round things off. The open kitchen makes for an engaging experience.

Name: Hua Xing Bak Kut Teh
Address: Yuhua Market & Hawker Centre, #01-171, Blk 347, Jurong East Avenue 1, Jurong East, 600347, Singapore
Description: Bak kut teh with a strong, peppery flavour and aromatic pork ribs. Add rice, pork organs, pork trotter, or vegetable soup for a complete meal.

Name: Huadao Art Of Life · Yu Shan Ge
Address: South Square, No.1-8, Building 16, Tiexiang Temple Riverfront, 88 Tiexiangsi Road, Wuhou, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
Description: The Taiwanese vegetarian restaurant chain chose a verdant location by the river for their first outpost in mainland China. The lofty interior is inspired by Japanese Zen Buddhism, imparting a calming vibe. Three set menus are offered, with thoughtfully named and meticulously plated courses inspired by kaiseki cuisine. Vegetables and mushrooms take pride of place on the menus; some dishes are given a Sichuanese twist with mala seasoning.

Name: Huai Xiang Guo Se
Address: L311-L312, 3F, CP Center, 20 Jinhe East Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: The interior is inspired by classical Jiangnan gardens; the menu is designed to re-enact the timeless beauty of Huaiyang culture. To ensure authenticity, the kitchen team from Jiangsu source produce from their home province. The sautéed river shrimps with chickpeas have incredibly deep flavours, and the slow-cooked lion's head pork meatballs are fluffy textured, with a hearty broth. Seasonal dishes and the chef's tasting menu are also worth trying.

Name: Huat Heng Fried Oyster
Address: Whampoa Makan Place, #01-26, 90/91 Whampoa Drive 90, 320091, Singapore
Description: The oyster omelette is fried to order until the crust is nicely browned, while the oysters remain plump and juicy. The house-made chilli sauce elevates the dish considerably. Various portion sizes are available.

Name: Huber
Description: Sandra and Michael Huber run their sleek, minimalist-style restaurant In an attractive residential area of Bogenhausen. Here, they serve flavoursome and ambitious contemporary cuisine that makes a pleasingly down-to-earth impression. There is a choice of two set menus (one of which is vegetarian), each comprising four or six courses, with dishes such as spinach with organic egg and Perigord truffle or skrei, beans and 'nduja. The wine list has a few gems in store, with plenty of appealing options for every budget.

Name: Huber's im Fischerwirt
Description: People have been flocking to Andrea and Harald Huber's Fischerwirt for years – and with good reason. This is hospitality at its finest. In the charming and elegant indoor area or out on the cosy little terrace, diners are attended to by a thoroughly affable team managed by your cordial hostess. And, of course, there is the delicious food – seasonal specialities from the region and traditional classics are served throughout the day. The extensive menu has something for everyone – from braised Borettana onion with crosne and charred leek to Backhenderl (breaded fried chicken) and Kalbsrahmbeuschel (veal lights ragout), every dish looks tempting. Be sure not to miss out on the wonderful desserts such as Topfenknödel (curd dumplings) or Heidelbeer-Datschi (blueberry cake). Tip: The four- to seven-course "Fischerwirts Chef Menü" comes with optional wine pairings. The well-curated wine list is dominated by Austrian labels and also includes a good selection of Champagnes. Plus there is a delicatessen selling chocolates, jam and spices etc.

Name: Hubertushof
Address: Arzheimer Straße 5, Ilbesheim bei Landau in der Pfalz, 76831, Germany
Location: Ilbesheim bei Landau in der Pfalz, Germany
Description: Remaining true to the Südliche Weinstraße, Sandra Bernhard and Jochen Sitter moved from Birkweiler to this 300 year-old former coaching house, which they run with great dedication and charm. The chef cooks traditional and modern, but above all, flavoursome fare. Dishes include classics such as pan-friend black pudding and Saumagen (stuffed pig’s stomach). The interior courtyard is gorgeous.

Name: Huen Jai Yong
Address: 65 Mu 4 Buak Kang, San Kamphaeng, Chiang Mai, 50130, Thailand
Description: Operating since 2002 in this traditional Thai house adorned with teak furnishings and local crafts, Huen Jai Yong is devoted to Northern Thai cuisine. From the sausage to the chilli dips, it all tastes unmistakably home-made. Order a few small sharing-sized dishes – the steamed chicken with herbs is tender and fragrant; the kaeng pak wan with ant eggs is light and naturally sweet. Gently spiced with typical Lanna seasoning, this is authentic, aromatic fare.

Name: Huen Lamphun
Address: 64/233 Mu 5, Suan Phak Road, Chimphli, Taling Chan, Bangkok, 10170, Thailand
Description: Northern Thai food has a special place in the hearts of locals, but finding good food like this outside the region can be tough. So Huen Lamphun is a gem of a find, to such an extent that large groups from the neighbourhood return in droves. Every dish uses organic vegetables grown onsite. The grilled, fermented northern Thai pork in banana leaf explodes with chilli and garlic. Another favourite is Makwan-marinated grilled chicken with a peppery flavour and herbal aroma.

Name: Hugenhof
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list
Description: Inside Hugenhof is every bit as attractive as its exterior suggests with its lovely high ceilings, cosy old beams and a roaring open fire in winter. Every evening brings a different 4-course menu, which chef Klaus Ditz will announce at your table. This is accompanied by expert wine selections from his fellow chef and sommelier. The rooms are simple but smart.

Name: Hugo
Address: Av. Veracruz 38, Roma Norte, Cuauhtémoc, 06700, Mexico
Description: With its terrace shaded by an awning and likable ambience, Hugo is the sort of place you'll want to return to time and again. While the wine list is indeed extensive, giving it its wine bar classification, it's not just about the bottles here; it's as equally well liked for its bistro-style menu. Quality products shine in dishes with pleasing presentations, while the contemporary cuisine remains faithful to traditional flavors.

Name: Hugo
Address: 1F, The Terrace, 126 Oxford Terrace, Christchurch Central City, Christchurch, 8011, New Zealand
Description: The elegant room, styled after a modern Parisian bistro, overlooks the bustling riverside. The French chef serves authentic cuisine from her home country, underpinned by solid, modern techniques and crafted with cherry-picked New Zealand ingredients. The menu changes with the seasons; it may include her signature flank steak and silky crème brûlée with crunchy caramelised topping. Also check out the predominantly French wine list.

Name: Hugo & Co
Description: This contemporary bistro opposite the Arènes de Lutèce, the Ancient Roman amphitheatre, bears the signature of talented chef Tomy Gousset (Tomy & Co). He has set the scene for a simple and convivial dining experience – open kitchens, wood and steel furniture, mason jars, bottles, books and pop art touches. The menu ranges from bluefin tuna with tomato and watermelon gazpacho to cod au gratin with miso and piperade, and rib of beef to share. The signature dish is fried gnocchi tailored to seasonal ingredients such as chanterelles, country ham and Parmesan. The presence of Constance and her team embodies the collective spirit of Hugo "& Co".

Name: Hugo’s Frog Bar & Fish House
Address: 1024 N. Rush St., Chicago, IL, 60611, USA
Description: Housed in a sprawling setting adjacent to big brother Gibson’s, Hugo’s always seems packed. The vast dining room sets white linen-topped tables amid dark polished wood and pale walls decorated with a mounted swordfish, fish prints, and model ships. Hugo’s bar draws its own crowd with abundant counter seating. The menu focuses on a selection of fish, steaks, and chops, supplemented by stone crab claws, oysters, crab cakes, chowders, and sautéed frog’s legs. Family-style sides—creamed spinach or roasted Brussels sprouts in Bourbon maple butter—are a worthy addition.With generous portions all around, you'll need a football team to share a slice of the Muddy Bottom Pie, or just a handful of pals to savor other decadent desserts like the apple pie.

Name: Hui Chung
Address: 69 Fuyuan Street, Xitun District, Taichung, Taiwan
Description: Managed by a Buddhist temple, this vegetarian restaurant has an earthy colour scheme with pops of turquoise and sage green. The experienced chef defies expectations with bold flavours, creative twists and a nod to Hong Kong-style dim sum traditions. Inspired by the classic wok-fried beef rice noodles, his version using basil, sweet pepper and assorted mushrooms in place of meat imparts remarkable soy aromas and wok hei. Book early during holidays.

Name: Hui Ji
Address: Villa 2, LJZ Financial Holdings Plaza, 1788 Century Avenue, Pudong, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: This imposing villa is home to Xin Rong Ji group's first Anhui restaurant, which is adorned with exquisite gilded wood reliefs. To ensure authenticity, most ingredients are shipped from Anhui. Made with 36-month-old birds from Wan Xi, the brine-marinated goose platter features various cuts of meat and offal – the intestine and head are especially enjoyable. The steamed wine-scented river eel with cured ham is packed with aromas and umami.

Name: Hui Lao Tang
Address: Meeting at the ticket gate, Luxiang Ancient Village, Dongshan Town, Wuzhong, Suzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: In a boutique hotel converted from a 500-year-old residence, this restaurant in Luxiang Ancient Village commands both lake and mountain views. It serves a grand chancellor feast that takes its cue from the season – wild greens in spring, lotus in summer, crab in autumn. Dongshan sliced lamb is sparingly seasoned to let its natural flavour shine. Duo Taihu shrimps are shelled and sautéed, or fried with the shells on for different textures. Reservation mandatory.

Name: Hui Wei Private Kitchen
Address: 15-1 Tongjiang Road, Cangshan, Fuzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: The spacious room has a live fish tank and display fridges at the entrance. The founder hails from Songxi County in northern Fujian, and the menu features specialities and snacks from there. The Lan Gu-style smoked yellow croaker impresses with its delicate flesh and subtle smokiness; chilli sauce further accentuates the umami. The traditional snack radish puff is crispy and golden, creating a stark contrast with the soft, juicy radish chilli filling.

Name: Huisje James
Description: Start your meal with an aperitif by the fireplace of this former workshop, after which you will be guided to the villa. The thatched roof, the intimate ambience and beautiful art give this restaurant a cosy feel. The surprise menu features classic favourites alongside contemporary surprises, all made from regional ingredients, including home-grown produce.

Name: Huit 100 Vingt
Description: In the heart of a farm in the Lanaudière region, this country restaurant delivers a full farm-to-plate experience. In a timber-built barn overlooking the countryside, Loïc Leperlier cooks instinctively with local produce: vegetables, herbs, free-range birds and house-made maple syrup. Made to order, the dishes on the single set menu faithfully follow the harvests and are dotted with nods to the chef's Réunion Island roots. Jessica Grégoire extends a warm welcome, adding a personal touch to the service.

Name: Huize Alberic
Description: From the ironwork and the restored fireplace to the wooden floors, the former home (1920s) of Alberic Plettinck, ironworker and artist, has been tastefully and respectfully refurbished in a stylish vein. After being welcomed by your gracious hostess, you will sample an updated version of classical recipes in which chef Bram demonstrates his flair for plating. His consummate craftsmanship shines through in the intense creamy gravy that flanks pheasant or in his modern spin on eels in sorrel.

Name: Huma
Description: Steak lovers need look no further than this smartly dressed restaurant from the same owners as Fiorentina and Kogel Mogel. An eye-catching parrilla grill is at the heart of the operation, used with great skill on prime steaks from Poland and the US, best enjoyed with a glass of red wine from the impressive list. Don’t overlook the other dishes too, such as the beef pretzel with a deliciously piquant gherkin and caper cream. Cheery, genuine service is the perfect finishing touch.

Name: Human
Description: In a quiet residential street behind the 17C Skansen Kronan fortress, you'll find this stylishly decorated restaurant decked out with neutral tones and vintage furniture. The first solo project for Martin Moses, it focuses on New Nordic cooking, which is executed with a skilful touch. In the evening you can sample the quality dishes from either a small or large tasting menu, with a four or five course set menu available at lunch.

Name: Humbachstube
Description: The Alpenhof Jäger hotel's restaurant may be small but what it lacks in size it makes up for in atmosphere! With plenty of wood, a tiled stove and pretty decorations, the cosy and homely Humbachstube is completely in keeping with the rustic charm of the 380-year-old regional-style building in which it is located. In the kitchen, Florian Jäger and his father Martin cook with market produce, creating dishes based on the classic repertoire, such as sirloin of local mountain lamb roasted with aromatics, fresh spinach leaves and potato and Parmesan gnocchi. The wine list is all about Austria's own production. Diners will enjoy friendly, attentive service with a real family touch.

Name: Huna Le Restaurant
Description: In a hamlet a few kilometres from Fouday, a couple who worked at Auberge du Bœuf (Sessenheim) have renovated this village house with a spruce green façade. With sincerity, passion and a lack of pretentiousness, Antoine Huguenin (kitchen) and Nadège Monna (restaurant floor) champion cuisine that is in touch with the seasons and draws extensively on the large vegetable garden that stretches out behind their restaurant. The restaurant boasts ultra-fresh vegetables, while fermentation, dehydration and salting help to get through the winter. The clarity of the explanations given by the lady of the house is also much appreciated.

Name: Hung Hom Pancake
Address: Shop 2, Polly Court, Taku Street, Hung Hom, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: For over 40 years, this neighbourhood shop has provided the childhood memories of many. Pancakes, waffles and egg waffles are all made to order. Tricolour egg waffles in plain, chocolate and matcha flavours particularly stand out.

Name: Hungry Thirsty
Description: Hungry Thirsty breathes new life into the space formerly occupied by the popular Ugly Baby and now draws lines of its own for its standout southern Thai cooking. From the bright yellow facade to the orange walls and blue-and-green bar, this place doesn't pull any punches when it comes to bold design, and the vibe is equally upbeat. And then there's the food, with a range of likeable dishes like salads, curries, stir-fries and sides turned out by Chef Prasert "Tee" Kanghae. Pla Kra Pong Tod Nam Pla is a beautiful, fried branzino served with dipping sauce that impresses with each bite, and thirteen eggs, a plate of soy sauce-marinated eggs, is a worthy accompaniment. For dessert, a coconut houses jelly with strips of sweetened coconut flesh for an intriguing ending.

Name: Hunters Room & Grill
Address: The Westin Hotel Doha, Salwa Road, Fereej Bin Mahmoud, Zone 23, Doha, Qatar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: To find this spacious restaurant and some of the best steaks in the city, look out for the huge statue of a stag at the heart of the Westin Doha Hotel. As the name suggests, it’s all about the grills here. Premium quality and full-flavoured Australian Black Onyx steaks, a nice piquant sea bass aguachile and even homemade bread flavoured with meat juices are all must-tries on the menu.

Name: Hup Hong Chicken Rice
Address: Yuhua Village Market and Food Centre, #01-51, Blk 254, Jurong East Street 24, 600254, Singapore
Description: The queue to get your roasted or boiled chicken rice may be long, but the wait is worthwhile for the silky-fleshed meat and the heady aromas of rice cooked in chicken stock and fat. Enjoy with char siew or roast pork.

Name: Hup Kee Fried Oyster Omelette
Address: Newton Food Centre, #01-73, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, 229495, Singapore
Description: This spot opened some 50 years ago as a street stall and has focused on just one item – fried oyster omelette. The lacy edges are nicely browned and crispy, in contrast with the plump, juicy oysters. The tangy chilli dip is a must.

Name: Hup Kee Teochew Fishball Mee
Address: Mei Ling Market & Food Centre, #02-38, 159 Mei Chin Road, 140159, Singapore
Description: This popular stall is always busy, even at off-peak times. There are different noodles to choose from, and these are topped with tasty fish balls, pork balls and fried fish cakes. A little of the hot sauce goes a long way!

Name: Hus Şarapçılık
Address: Kuşçular Mahallesi, 8018/1. Sokak No:39, Urla, Izmir, 35437, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: The terrace of this inviting restaurant is the best place to experience the charm of the Hus wine estate to the full. The sight of the vines and olive trees immediately has a calming effect. Be sure to sample the wines produced on site – your charming service team is on hand to offer expert guidance. These wines pair perfectly with the food, which is a contemporary take on Mediterranean cuisine prepared to order. Having started with the addictive house-made focaccia, for example, you could move on to the perfectly cooked medium-rare lamb saddle seasoned with rosemary, accompanied by a robust lamb jus and a roasted garlic cream to really bring out the characteristic flavour of the meat. Finish off with a Turkish coffee for a burst of intensity!

Name: Husar
Description: Charming dining rooms await behind the painted façade of this inn, which has stood for over 400 years. Here, diners are treated to attentive service as they tuck into classic cuisine. The dishes are packed with flavour and made with good-quality ingredients; attention is paid to seasonality, and a regional produce is given preferential treatment. Started in 1986, the Merget family business continues today, having resumed in 2004 after a brief hiatus.

Name: Husk
Description: Open since 2011, the enduring legacy of this Southern restaurant continues to draw in waves of diners. Reservations are scarce, and before doors open, crowds form on the sidewalk hoping to snag a table inside this historic, two-story house. But make no mistake, this kitchen isn’t resting on any laurels. The menu is full of Southern favorites prepared with notable care: pimento cheese with country ham and biscuits, cornbread, fried catfish. Pies, cakes and a generous dose of warm hospitality make for a complete experience at this Southern staple.

Name: Hutong
Address: Gate Building 6, Ground Floor DIFC, Al Sukook Street, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: The terrace is festooned with lanterns, while the focus of the interior is around a wishing tree wreathed in red ribbons. The menu tells the story of the Silk Road that ran from Europe to China, so along with specialities from Northern China are also ones from more westerly regions like Xinjiang; and as the chef is from Sichuan, expect fiery dishes from that province too. A more business orientated lunch leads into an altogether livelier dinner. For a special occasion, order the ‘Flaming whole Peking duck’.

Name: Huí Huí
Address: 155-4 Dongding Road, Ruifang District, New Taipei, Taiwan
Description: Opened in 2023, this cosy bistro in a quiet village by the sea sports a rustic yet refreshingly modern interior. A zero-waste ethos and locally sourced ingredients set the scene of the French menu which demonstrates strong Asian influences and changes frequently. It may include items like Shandong roast chicken with grilled pickled cucumber or fried lamb tripe with purple cabbage in coriander sauce. Also check out the well-curated selection of natural wines.

Name: Huître Brûlée
Description: Don’t worry, the oysters aren’t burnt - despite the name! Updated recipes, quality ingredients, locally sourced whenever possible (organic veg, fish from small boats) and a concise, seasonal menu. This friendly bolthole is run by an enthusiastic couple: local lad Paul Lacheray, in the kitchen, and his partner, Chloé Woestelandt, who runs the dining room.

Name: Hwaro
Description: Chef Sungchul Shim is no stranger to the New York restaurant scene, but this 22-seat counter located inside Gui Steakhouse is certainly one to watch. Begin with a cocktail before riding the elevator to discover this hidden-in-plain-sight spot. The space is stunning, though all eyes are drawn to the center where the chefs prepare a multicourse menu fusing Korean flavors with French techniques. The meal begins with a bowl of luscious brown butter miso soup before wild amberjack crudo with a tableside pour of buttermilk koji sauce. The shrimp toast sandwich reveals perfectly cooked abalone nestled at its center, though the white soy custard with Osetra caviar for spooning over top is reason alone for its guest favorite status. A sesame ice cream popsicle is a delightful finale.

Name: Hyde Park Garden
Address: 44 Hoi Pong Road Central, Lei Yue Mun, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: The owner also sells seafood from the opposite stall so diners can pick from a dazzling selection flown in daily. Ask servers for the best way to cook your meal; for instance, razor clams are typically stir-fried in chilli black bean sauce, and abalone with ginger and scallion in a claypot. The signature fish soup is simmered for hours with freshwater fish and tofu. Try also the deep-fried eggplant, and tofu skin sweet soup with pearl barley.

Name: Hyderabadi Zaiqa
Description: Don't come with a big group expecting a seat, as this tiny Theater District spot only has a few tables and counter seats, but Mohammad Tarique Khan and Jayesh Naik deliver food with a big personality. Service is a rare cross between attentive and efficient, and the food comes out just as quickly. This is Indian cooking with a focus on Hyderabad, though regional favorites from the north and south also make an appearance on the menu. First up is the unmissable samosa, that flaky, golden-brown pyramid filled with a comforting blend of potatoes, peas, and spices. Then, opt for the goat fry biryani with an oval silver tray piled high with rice studded with tender, stewed bone-in goat meat. Fragrant and flavorful, it's served with a side of raita.

Name: Hydra
Description: Situated in the picturesque historic centre of Salerno, this is one of the city’s best restaurants. The dining room here is almost minimalist in style, yet thanks to the soft lighting and beautiful background music it has a pleasing atmosphere; in fine weather, tables are set out in a charming inner courtyard. The cuisine is Mediterranean and contemporary, with a selection of light and creative meat, fish and vegetable dishes featuring on the menu.

Name: Hyun
Address: 10 E. 33rd St., New York, NY, 10016, USA
Description: Hyun is a luxurious take on Korean barbecue, focusing squarely on top-notch Japanese A5 Wagyu, butchered in-house and grilled tableside. Enter this temple of indulgent tranquility to discover sleek dark wood, cool slate surfaces, and private rooms.The Hyun-makase is the gateway into this one-of-a-kind meal which takes you on a journey of 12 different pieces of Japanese A5 Wagyu. Each piece is expertly prepared tableside and served alongside house-made fresh kimchi, green lettuce for wrapping, and a crispy scallion salad that balances the unctuous Wagyu. The tasting is complete when the bulgogi is prepared. Diners may also look forward to other indulgences like rice with uni and truffles, or thick noodles with cold beef broth.

Name: Hábitat Cigüeña Negra
Address: Carretera EX-205, Km. 24, Valverde del Fresno, 10890, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: This rural hotel for adults only shares the beauty of the Sierra de Gata with its guests. Taking its name from the black stork, a migratory bird which nests in several locations on an estate with over 220ha of holm oak and olive groves, it also features a gourmet boutique next to the bar’s lounge area, an organic olive oil mill and a hammam. In its asador-style restaurant, featuring a semi open-view kitchen and large windows through which guests can gaze out at its surrounding pastures, choose from a regionally inspired à la carte strong on grilled meats, especially those it rears itself, including goat, Iberian pork and RetWagyu beef (a cross between Retinto and Wagyu).

Name: Hám-Khàk
Address: 6F, Kaipuu Belfry, 2 East Street, Licheng, Quanzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: This restaurant stands in the heart of the old city, atop a hotel. Acclaimed for his home-style dishes made with local seafood and seasonal produce, the executive chef honours Fujian traditions while thinking outside the box with modern techniques and thoughtful plating. Pre-order his gourmet "Buddha jumps over the wall" without shark fin: the umami-rich brown broth is packed with hand-picked dried items such as abalone, sea cucumber and fish maw.

Name: Härg
Description: This lively all-day brasserie provides the perfect pick-me-up – particularly in the snowy months – thanks to its characterful stone walls, exposed ducting and striking copper chandeliers, while its courtyard is the place to be when the temperatures start to rise. Whatever the weather, you’ll always experience a warm welcome from the charming team. Modern dishes keep their focus on the local area, with the chargrill taking centre stage – the ‘Dirty Steak’, a rib-eye, is cooked directly on the charcoal itself. Portions are generous, so come hungry if you want to make it all the way through to dessert!

Name: Hærværk
Description: A group of friends run this laid-back restaurant, which has something of a bohemian feel thanks to its collection of cookery books, sheepskins and modern art. To say that the set surprise menu is seasonal would be an understatement. Top-quality local and organic ingredients set the tone, and the dishes feel pure, allowing said ingredients to take centre stage in their natural form. Expect delicious salad leaves and the likes of line-caught wolffish with green asparagus, followed by rhubarb tart with rhubarb sorbet and lemon verbena ice cream. Modern, natural wines make the perfect accompaniment.

Name: Héctor Oribe
Description: This restaurant, located in a winelover’s paradise and run by a friendly couple (Héctor Oribe in the kitchen and Patricia Ruiz as maître d’ and sommelier), is one of those places you don’t hesitate to recommend to a friend. Here, the traditional cuisine with a contemporary touch is built around seasonal ingredients and showcased on a single tasting menu (a shorter version of the same menu is also available). We particularly enjoyed: the artichokes in season, beef jerky, and asparagus; a fantastic dish of Angus beef cheeks; creamy mashed potatoes and truffle mayonnaise; apple pie, cinnamon ice cream, and quince paste. In this space, there is an ever-present feeling of warmth and familiarity!

Name: Hélicoptère
Address: 4255 rue Ontario Est, Montréal, H1V 1K4, Canada
Description: This restaurant at the entrance to Hochelaga wins diners over with its contemporary bistro vibe and fresh, well-balanced cuisine that is firmly rooted in the seasons. David Ollu, previously at Bouillon Bilk, composes clean and inspired dishes, such as textures of courgette elevated by an XO sauce, or house-made pappardelle topped with a lemon corn cream with lobster. A dessert featuring strawberries, raspberries and nasturtiums is an elegant conclusion to the meal. A warm welcome, a succinct and carefully selected drinks menu and real culinary personality. The café at the back, Hélico, serves light meals and quality coffees during the day.

Name: Héritage East
Address: 1F, Block 66, 1 Zhongguancun South Street, Haidian, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
Description: Exquisite artwork and elaborate wainscoting set the scene for a dining experience that is the epitome of stylish, even down to the hand-painted tableware. The restaurant prefers to customise menus to diners’ tastes ahead of time, but à la carte choices also abound. Top notch ingredients are deftly crafted with spot-on seasoning and outstanding wok hei. During the mushroom season, try the sautéed lurid bolete with wrinkly chillies.

Name: Héroine
Description: Housed in an industrial building, this restaurant has a unique feel on account of its decor incorporating retro features and modern design, as well as striking artwork on the walls. The surprise menu showcases exciting combinations, international influences and vegetables. The chef serves crispy breaded scallops, for instance, on a delicate passion fruit cream, finishing the dish with a butter sauce enhanced with coconut and dill. His bold and innovative creations will leave you craving more.

Name: Hôtel du Phare
Description: Belle-Île-en-Mer's emblematic Hôtel du Phare (1880) and its restaurant have been redesigned and revamped by a famous architect. The decor is original, juxtaposing bright colours with the black and white of the Breton flag. The menu focuses on marine flavours, with dishes such as spider crab in its shell, bisque, celeriac ravioli with spider crab; viennoise of sea bass cooked on a stone, artichoke fricassee with clams and black garlic. As much as he can, the chef uses quality ingredients, often from the island (eg lamb reared in Bangor, honey, organic vegetables and fish from a local fisherman). There is a lovely terrace overlooking the harbour, and further dining options at Le Bistrot.

Name: Hõlm
Description: Hotel Lydia welcomed its first guests in 2016, but its story stretches back to the 1800s – and it’s this heritage that inspired both the hotel’s name and that of its restaurant. Lydia Grünmann Hõlm, the founders’ beloved grandmother, is not just referenced here in name though, as it’s her recipes that shape the cuisine, taken from a cookbook she wrote in 1925. That’s not to say that this restaurant is traditional; in fact, it’s quite the opposite. This a smart, modern spot both in looks and style, where the cooking takes on an ambitious, contemporary approach that comprises many different elements.

Name: Höfli
Description: The charming Höfli blends seamlessly into the picturesque old town setting. The enchanting cobblestone courtyard invites you to dine under the summer sky, surrounded by historical walls and half-timbered buildings. The interior is just as pleasant with its sleek, contemporary feel. While maître d' Alexandra Killy ensures a warm welcome, her husband, Marco, prepares delicious and neatly crafted dishes. His classical training shines through in dishes such as foie gras tiramisu with mascarpone, quince, coffee and brioche, or John Dory with fregola sarda and a pointed pepper broth.

Name: Høst
Description: Not far from Nørreport station, Høst is a busy neighbourhood restaurant that offers an enjoyable atmosphere and good value cooking. Dishes are modern, boldly flavoured and visually impressive, and the set menus come with lots of extra surprises. Nordic fish and shellfish feature largely, while the vegetarian dishes – like celeriac with truffle and ´Vesterhavsost’ – are some of the highlights of the menu.

Name: Hēdonē
Description: Chef Davine grabs your attention right from the start with her open kitchen positioned bang in the heart of this cosy restaurant, stylishly decked in works of art.
