Meticulous Davine works with an equally spot on partner, Nicholas, in the front of house. The set menu (whose dishes are also available à la carte) is founded on premium produce and suave international twists. An example of her elegant, confident cooking: she jazzes up lobster by lacquering it with a boiled bisque paired with Timut pepper and a combava zest. Named after the goddess of pleasure and sensuality, Hēdonē bears the hallmark of an enthusiastic couple.

Name: Hōchō
Address: Ground Floor, VIA Riyadh, Al Hada, Riyadh, 12912, Saudi Arabia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,No alcohol served,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: It’s all about Kobe beef here. Located in the luxurious VIA Riyadh, this simple yet contemporary restaurant with a large open kitchen finds itself sitting pretty in the high-end shopping district. While Kobe beef-based dishes are the star of the menu, it also features some modern and well-crafted sushi that are worth exploring. Finish off with a date, walnut and Saudi coffee tart – a sweet delight.

Name: Hōra
Description: At Hōra and its elegant, understated dining room, Gilles Moreau has reinvented his universe, whilst retaining his knack for flavourful cuisine drawing on local produce: Aubrac beef, aligot and a red wine reduction with shallots; organic trout from the Monts d'Aubrac with a bacon foam, risotto with Vieux Rodez cheese; free-range guinea fowl with black trumpet mushrooms and ham-perfumed wheat. In fine weather, the terrace at the rear is blissfully quiet.

Name: I 5 Campanili
Address: Via Luigi Maino 18, Busto Arsizio, 21052, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Contemporary cooking with an emphasis on Mediterranean fare in tune with the seasons is to the fore in this elegant restaurant occupying a 20C building with an attractive veranda to the rear. Fish takes pride of place on the menu, with a particular focus on raw dishes and shellfish, but the splendid desserts are also worthy of note, such as cherries in sour cherry juice with fior di latte ice cream.

Name: I 5 Sensi
Description: The whole family (mother and four children) is involved in the running of this restaurant, both front of house and in the kitchen. If you’re looking for top-quality cuisine which focuses on local ingredients yet is also creative and innovative, then this is the place for you! Classic-style dining room with the occasional modern decorative touch, plus a well-stocked wine cellar offering a selection of 700 labels.

Name: I Banchi
Description: Housed in a palazzo full of history – the building was a synagogue before the 1693 earthquake and has retained its ritual bath in its charming room of mirrors – this restaurant bears the imprint of renowned chef Ciccio Sultano, holder of two Michelin stars at the nearby Duomo restaurant. The cuisine is eclectic yet with a Sicilian focus, plus the wine list is complemented by a choice of interesting cocktails.

Name: I Carracci
Description: Within the luxurious Grand Hotel Majestic, though with its own independent entrance, the restaurant welcomes guests into a dining room of great impact, presided over by a spectacular ceiling frescoed in the seventeenth century by the school of the Carracci. An ideal setting for special occasions, which finds further expression in the cuisine of chef Agostino Schettino. Originally from Castellammare di Stabia, the chef weaves Emilian and Neapolitan influences into his offering: emblematic in this regard is the tasting menu “La Dotta, La Grassa, La Rossa”, an homage to Bolognese tradition. More generally, his is a contemporary Mediterranean cuisine, balanced with confidence between sea – as in the sea bass with charred lettuce, almond, oyster and caviar – and land, with dishes such as the lamb accompanied by scorzonera and marinated red onion. For the pairings, alongside the expertise of the sommelier, a well-considered cocktail offering distinguishes itself as an original complement to the wine list.

Name: I Cavallini
Description: Chef Nick Curtola cooks with restraint and confidence at this regional Italian spot just across from sibling The Four Horsemen. The menu is rooted in tradition, handled cleanly and without excess. Begin with the nervetti and onion salad, where braised beef tendons are shaved thin and paired with crisp, acidic onions; a striking dish that signals the kitchen’s comfort with depth and simplicity. Handmade pastas and rustic mains follow with balance and control. Desserts are essential here: the tiramisu is feather-light, generously portioned and among the most satisfying in the city. Reservations may be hard to come by, but arrive early for a seat at the bar and a lovely way to experience the room and the cooking up close.

Name: I Due Cippi dal 1976
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Upon entering, guests are welcomed by an evocative crackling fireplace, beside which aged meat is cooked to perfection. The varieties offered come from the world’s finest regions and sustainable farms, including prized wagyu. Chianina naturally takes center stage, but the menu extends to game as well, offering a wide range of authentic flavors. The elegant dining rooms, which have gained charm and refinement over the years, are the result of management that began in the 1970s and is now more vibrant than ever. A warm atmosphere, attentive service, and a selection of prestigious labels complete the gastronomic experience. During the warmer months, outdoor seating is also available.

Name: I Giardini dei Rodo
Address: Via Bonomo Alto - Scauri, Pantelleria, 91017, Italy
Description: As its name suggests, this restaurant’s guests can enjoy their meal surrounded by verdant gardens, which are planted with palms, flowers and citrus trees. Regional flavours take centre-stage in the modern dishes in this romantic and original setting.

Name: I Lustri Lab
Description: After years working in Michelin-starred restaurants in Lazio, owner-chef Kerim Jlali has achieved his dream of opening his own restaurant here, along with his life-partner Chiara. In an informal and colourful setting, the chef demonstrates his passion for fish and seafood, transforming his ingredients into contemporary recipes using skilful techniques (he refers to his restaurant as a “lab”) . The end results are visually striking and full of colour.

Name: I Mori
Description: This is the classic spot to recommend to anyone who wants fish prepared simply and traditionally, with no frills, just top-quality seafood that the friendly owner personally sources. The menu is supplemented by spoken specials based on that day’s fish-market finds, but among the mains we suggest you don’t miss the charcoal-grilled dishes.

Name: I Pifferi
Description: This restaurant occupying an old post house that dates back to the time of Marie Louise, Duchess of Parma, lies amid the verdant landscapes of the Parco Regionale dei Boschi di Carrega, just a kilometre outside the village of Sala Baganza. This stunning setting is the backdrop for typical dishes from Parma, such as Nonna Lina’s herb tortelli served with melted butter and parmesan cheese. In summer, dine alfresco in the cool, shady garden.

Name: I Rodella
Address: strada esterna vicinale della Rocca 2, Deruta, 06053, Italy
Description: This complex, which also includes two junior suites and seven guestrooms, dates back to the early 17C and was commissioned by the Church as a stopping off point for travellers on their way to Rome. For many years now, the restaurant has been run by a Venetian family with twin brothers (both highly experienced) working in the kitchen and a third brother, a sommelier, at the helm in the dining room. The cuisine is inspired by local and Venetian traditions, with a modern approach to the combinations of flavours (including home-grown herbs) and to the presentation of its delicious, generous dishes. We recommend that you do as we did and follow Samuele’s advice when making your choice from the dishes prepared by Stefano and Andrea with great skill and passion.

Name: I Salotti
Address: Località Querce al Pino, SS 146, Chiusi, 53043, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In summer, the outdoor spaces at this restaurant, such as the garden gazebo, are the perfect setting for a candlelit dinner in total harmony with nature, while in winter, the elegant dining room with just a few tables (book well in advance) really comes into its own. Creative cuisine prepared using produce from the restaurant’s own farm, plus a long-established wine cellar that has been extended over the years so that it now boasts over two thousand different labels from the region and elsewhere in Italy, many of them of the highest quality.

Name: I Salti
Address: au golf du Reginu - Moulin de Salti, Speloncato, 20226, France
Description: In the Reginu valley, next to the golf course, this pretty little restaurant housed in a converted mill enjoys a bucolic setting and outdoor café garden vibe. The delicious menu is the culmination of the finest ingredients of the Balagne region (local fish, organic vegetables). The prawn arancini, cold bisque and snow peas is a particularly fond memory. A warm welcome and a really charming setting, far from all the hustle and bustle: a firm favourite.

Name: I Savi
Address: Via Spangaro 6, località Peseggia di Scorzè, Scorzè, 30037, Italy
Description: Situated in a small rural hamlet, this restaurant is one of the best in the Venetian hinterland for top-quality fish. Served in welcoming dining rooms, the fish and seafood dishes here are traditional and unfussy in style, and full of natural flavour.

Name: I Sette Consoli
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: In this simple restaurant boasting an attractive outdoor summer garden and splendid views of the Duomo, chef Anna Rita focuses on carefully selected ingredients from the region and beyond. Highlights include soft egg, pan-fried courgettes and spring onions, and pecorino crumble, as well as soft veal rump, Jerusalem artichoke sauce and home-made pickled vegetables. The wine and spirits selection is particularly appealing – as an example, the Orvieto Classico Superiore Doc “Vendemmia Tardiva” is the perfect pairing for your dessert.

Name: I Sodi
Address: 314 Bleecker St., New York, NY, 10014, USA
Description: Manhattan has no shortage of Italian restaurants, but surely Rita Sodi runs two of the most beloved ones. Just down the street from Via Carota, this cozy, buzzy hotspot remains a difficult reservation to score so consider planning on an early-hour walk-in. The kitchen watches the seasons closely in daily specials like grilled tomato and burrata, while also respecting that some signatures can never leave the menu. The perfectly layered lasagna is a must for first timers, and it contrasts wonderfully with a citrusy tangle of pappardelle al limon. Regardless of where you sit – bar, dining room, or further back – the neighborhood restaurant is a constant hive of activity, fueled in part by a busy bar that knows its way around a Negroni.

Name: I Tigli
Description: An iconic pizzeria which has brought Italy’s favourite street-food snack right up to date! With almost 30 years’ experience behind him, Simone Padoan knows how to make difficult things easy: he uses a mix of wholemeal flours and pays meticulous attention to natural leavening processes to create a dough which has a crispy crust yet soft interior. He also focuses on different types of toppings, including fish, meat and vegetables – whether your preference is for traditional or more imaginative pizzas, every option is of the highest quality. A choice of excellent desserts provides the perfect conclusion to your meal!

Name: I+T
Description: This restaurant, which describes itself as “freestyle with a Japanese soul” is located just a few minutes from Salamanca’s historic centre. The cuisine here is uncompromisingly focused on a fusion of Japanese techniques, international recipes, and Mediterranean flavours. Chef Taigoro Suzuki, who trained in Madrid but has experience working in kitchens in Bangkok and Tokyo, creates bold dishes but which feature a harmony of flavours and ingredients and impressive presentation. These are presented as part of a tasting menu that changes in line with the seasonal availability.

Name: I-SANG
Address: 2F, VIVRE Building, 34/3 Lang Suan Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: Taupe tones, natural light and clean lines lend this modern Korean restaurant a calm, minimalist charm. Chef Lee Sanggun channels global experience into a concise tasting menu that smartly fuses Korean roots with Thai produce – vegetables, seafood and Chiang Rai rice. Highlights include bright, colourful naengchae, comforting perilla oil guksu, and a flavour-packed crispy crab – his playful riff on Korean fried chicken. The pickles are made in-house.

Name: IAán
Description: This restaurant showcases bold contemporary flavours derived from classic French and Korean cuisine. The dish names are Korean, yet the sauces and plating are distinctly French. The chef's remarkable ability to balance sauces suggests even more promising work to come. Cosy carpets and minimalist tables create an atmosphere that is warm, calm, and refined, much like the food. This is a lovely, quiet place to unwind over good food and wine.

Name: IBAIA
Description: This bistro is sure to satisfy the cravings of carnivores, with French flame techniques that bring out the sizzle in meat dishes. Beef, pork, lamb and duck are cooked as hearty slabs. Their famous cutlet of beef tenderloin looks like a standard Japanese take on Western cuisine, but with a French twist: parsley and garlic are mixed in, a la lamb grilled in breadcrumbs. Here, you’ll find the thrill of savouring thick cuts of meat and the joy of opening a bottle of wine.

Name: ICHI
Description: If you are looking to experience Japanese cuisine in Kiel, this city-centre restaurant with a modern and minimalist design is just the place. Laid out over two levels and boasting floor-to-ceiling windows, it extends diners a very warm welcome. Authentic Japanese dishes including sushi and sashimi are conjured up in the partially visible kitchen. Order à la carte or opt for a set menu – vegan options are also available. The restaurant is conveniently located close to the pedestrian area and the harbour with its cruise terminals. Tip: Park your car in the Schlossgarage, which is just a 3min walk away.

Name: IJssel Restobar
Description: Part of the Pillows hotel, this stylish restaurant encapsulates the best of Deventer. Seating options include a lovely conservatory and a terrace overlooking the River IJssel – the perfect place from which to take in the city's skyline. Wouter van Leeuwen creates a menu that's simply irresistible. Timeless classics such as steak tartare are accompanied by contemporary creations that draw on international influences and feature playful textures. For instance, he serves a combination of North Sea crab, leek and carrot with an espuma and powdered tomato. Foodies are sure to be delighted by the wide range of options.

Name: IKON
Description: Set on a main street in the heart of the city, IKON stands out among the other eateries for its smart look, structured service and confident cooking. The chef spent time working in England and his dishes are an intriguing mix of reworked Hungarian classics and some British influences – go for something from the ‘Traditions Reborn’ section and be sure not to miss dessert. For a more immersive experience, book the chic Kitchen Table.

Name: IL GiOTTO
Description: In this white-walled detached house facing Komazawa-Koen Avenue, with its cosy, wood-lined interior, sounds of food preparation from the open kitchen, and the atmosphere of a shop run by a couple, guests feel invited into a home. Chef Naofumi Takahashi specializes in meat dishes, such as bruschetta with home-cured ham and simmered tripe. He takes special pride in his slow-aged, char-grilled meats. Beef, aged to enhance umami, is seasoned with salt and pepper.

Name: IL Sommelier
Description: Behind the unassuming façade of a modern building in the Trudering district, this is a real gem of a restaurant. In the chic, contemporary space, diners are served authentic, flavoursome, down-to-earth cucina italiana. The dishes on the menu are sophisticated but not pretentious, and include tortelli with a cheese and aubergine filling or beef cheek braised with sweet potato mash. The wine list features Italian wines exclusively. In summer, the quiet terrace to the rear of the property beckons.

Name: IMA
Address: 9669 S. Santa Monica Blvd., Los Angeles, CA, 90210, USA
Description: Few restaurants place such an emphasis on both sukiyaki and shabu-shabu as this classic-meets-contemporary retreat, where premium A5 Wagyu beef reigns supreme. Glass and blonde wood panels lend a cool and airy vibe; while floor tiles, ambient lighting, and custom bamboo blinds make things specially intimate.Inside, tables are outfitted with a conventional grill for cooking. Your meal may begin with such cold bites as arugula and spinach ohitashi with lobster or a shiso-infused vichyssoise. Diners may then go for the traditional, special, or à la carte sukiyaki, complete with an appetizer, unabashedly rich beef tongue, leafy veggies, and three cuts of Yazawa beef. Truffle-kissed zōsui (or ojiya) is a delicious, subtle, and crowning way to seal this feast.

Name: IMPERIAL TREASURE
Description: A Chinese restaurant from Singapore has landed in Ginza. The interior, with a focus on semi-private rooms, is an elegant and subdued space. The menu is extensive, refined with modern seasonings and presentations. Trademark dishes include Peking duck and suckling pig stuffed with sticky rice. Japanese ingredients such as tilefish and hair crab are also used, creating dishes unique to this restaurant.

Name: INDIA CLUB
Description: Authentic Indian cuisine is to be found in Berlin! At India Club, the self-styled "rustic cuisine" with its roots in North India includes delicious curries and original tandoori dishes, as well as numerous vegetarian and vegan options. In addition to the appealing à la carte menu, the three-course surprise menu is highly recommended, as it gives a good overview of this style of cuisine. Many ingredients are sourced from the restaurant's own organic farm (Gut Vorder Bollhagen) on the Baltic Sea. With its mahogany furniture, dark wood panelling, bright colours and traditional patterns, the elegant interior has an almost festive atmosphere and exudes Indian flair. The restaurant is located not far from the Brandenburg Gate, at the rear of the exclusive Hotel Adlon.

Name: INOS
Description: Located in York’s buzzing centre, this relaxed restaurant brings a sunny taste of Greece to the historic city. It’s a simple, cheerful place with an informal bistro vibe and friendly service. The cooking presents great value for money, especially at lunchtime, and offers well-executed versions of classic dishes: start with pita and dips, then share the likes of ‘keftedakia’ meatballs or moussaka, before ending on a sugary note with the ‘Portakalopia’, a Cretan cake with orange syrup. Greek wines and spirits add to the authenticity.

Name: ITO
Description: In this trendy Japanese restaurant in the Belgian Quarter, Kengo Nishimi uses top-notch ingredients to create clearly structured dishes in which traditional Japanese cuisine is laced with modern European influences. In the evening, Japanese classics such as tempura, sashimi and sushi can be ordered à la carte, plus there is an extensive omakase menu. At lunchtime, a moderately priced set menu is available. In the front part of the restaurant, you can watch the chef at work at the sushi counter.

Name: IU & ON
Description: This family business in the heart of Nuremberg has been around since 1972! Many regulars keep coming back, having been won over by the aromatic dishes, which include classics like laab and tom yum. Add to that a clean-lined, minimalist-style interior and friendly service. By the way, the restaurant takes its name from the sisters Iu and On who cook here.

Name: Iai
Address: GF, The Montane, 8th Avenue corner 35th Street, Bonifacio Global City, Taguig - Metro Manila, 1630, The Philippines
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list
Description: Chef Bruce Ricketts has designed a deeply personal restaurant where Japanese precision meets Filipino soul. Unfolding at the sweeping acacia counter, the omakase experience blends traditional sushi with inventive touches such as foie gras parfait with pineapple. In a thoughtfully composed menu, which includes home-smoked tuna, it's the classics that shine brightest. The curated wine pairings round off a refined journey that reflects the chef's passions.

Name: Ibai
Address: 90 Bartholomew Close, City of London, London, EC1A 7BN, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Large, airy and with an industrial-chic vibe that perfectly matches the buzz of its open kitchen, there’s something quite cool about Ibai. Backed by one of the co-owners of Donostia, it takes that restaurant's love of Basque cooking and leans it further towards the region’s French influences. The signature ‘Croque Ibai’ is a prime example and a delicious pintxo to start your meal with. Quality ingredients are used throughout, treated with care and often cooked over fire. Wine enthusiasts will be impressed by the well-stocked cellar.

Name: Ibidem
Address: Barrio Zoña 1 - Castillo de Siete Villas, Arnuero, 39193, Spain
Description: Ibidem occupies a manor house with a somewhat surprising interior featuring an elegant dining room with a designer feel and decorated in shades of white. The cooking here is centred around a single surprise tasting menu with a focus on contemporary cuisine and meticulous presentation.

Name: Ibn Albahr
Address: Club Vista Mare, Palm Jumeirah, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,No alcohol served,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: This Lebanese seafood restaurant features fishing paraphernalia like ropes, anchors and even a boat – as well as a beautiful terrace with a great view of the beach. Ask for a table on the sand for a beach day experience, then head to the fresh fish counter to choose what you’d like to eat; the simple yet classically cooked dishes let the ingredients speak for themselves, complemented by a blend of aromatic herbs and spices.

Name: Ichigo Ichie
Description: After working in a kappo restaurant in Tokyo and helming a famous sushiya in Singapore, Chef Eno has brought to life her own fine-dining concept. At this address since 2024, she serves two set menus that change with the seasons. Her signature somen with kuruma ebi and uni bursts with seafood umami – the briny and sweet prawn broth clings nicely to the silky noodles. Reservations recommended, especially for the sought-after counter seats.

Name: Ichikawa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Wheelchair access
Description: Ichikawa is one of the culinary masters who played a part in introducing Japanese cuisine to Italy. After decades in the country working in various restaurants, this chef has finally opened his own eatery, where he serves top-quality Japanese cuisine ranging from familiar favourites such as sushi and sashimi to other less-known family dishes and street food from the land of the Rising Sun. A good place to discover the joys of Japanese cuisine!

Name: Ichiu
Description: A door of cedar bark, roof tiles for a nameplate, and a rope curtain with the same diagonals as the ceiling. ‘Ichiu’ means ‘under one roof’, and the ceiling is shaped like a roof to emphasise this point. The menu is faithful to the spirit of Chef Koichi Hamano, a man experienced in Japanese cuisine, particularly sushi. The evening begins with a cup of sake; soup and steamed dishes are then served. After the sushi, takikomi gohan - rice with a variety of ingredients concludes the meal.

Name: Ikaitz
Address: Paseo Colón 21, Donostia / San Sebastián, 20002, Spain
Description: This pleasant family-run restaurant in a good location in the Gros district of the city focuses on traditional-regional cuisine and is almost always full, including with many foreign visitors who are attracted by cuisine with an authentic Basque flavour and generous portions. Ikaitz’s à la carte features delicious fish, premium meats and plenty of locally sourced ingredients. These are showcased in dishes such as grilled octopus with a creamy purée and paprika, and boneless oxtail in its own jus, served with vegetables and almonds.

Name: Ikigai Flor Baja
Description: Consistent, technically accomplished and high-quality cuisine in an informal setting, where the chef creates Japanese cooking that borders on the traditional while at the same time surprising guests with a fusion of French and Spanish influences. The à la carte (complemented by an Omakase menu option) features a good selection of starters, tasty temaki and nigiri (both classic and fusion-style). Highlights include white prawns with garlic, and spicy tuna with a marrow flan.

Name: Ikigai Velázquez
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed
Description: Ikigai's little brother! The restaurant, which can be reached by going down a flight of stairs, has a carefully designed interior, with details inspired by 1980s New York apartments, and a sushi bar that clearly takes centre stage as it can be seen from any point in the room. They offer a menu with a Japanese flavour (we liked their varied Sashimi, made with four different fish depending on the market) and a complete tasting menu, with dishes taken from the same (gyozas, tartares, classic and fusion nigiris, and more).

Name: Il Bacaro
Address: Campbell House, 106 Lebuh Campbell, George Town, 10100, Malaysia
Description: Photos from a by-gone era, retro ceiling fans and patterned tiles exude a nostalgic mood. This restaurant, run by a friendly Italian couple (who also own the hotel), has been serving classics from their home country for more than a decade. You can find most Italian classics on the menu, such as antipasto, pizzas, pastas and mains. Start with bruschetta tradizionale for a refreshing and appetising opener. Save some room for their homemade sweets.

Name: Il Baretto
Description: Il Baretto on the outskirts of Padova is a must for anyone who loves classic, traditional fish and seafood, thanks to its menu which includes a number of typical Venetian dishes. The top-quality fish is skilfully prepared to bring out its full flavour and distinctive characteristics, providing a real treat for the tastebuds in this inland temple to the sea.

Name: Il Baretto
Address: Discovery Boulevard, King Abdullah Financial District, Al Aquiq, Riyadh, 13519, Saudi Arabia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,No alcohol served,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Italian classics find themselves in the heart of KAFD. This elegant restaurant sits at the footsteps of one the many modern skyscrapers and comes dressed with velvet armchairs, large bouquets of fresh flowers and art pieces hung on the walls. The charming team is happy to guide you through the extensive menu which is packed with favourites like gnocchi alla Sorrentina, veal chop alla Milanese or the feather-light Amalfi lemon soufflé. If you’re working in the area, head over for the business lunch – it’s a steal.

Name: Il Barolino
Description: The Emilian authenticity of the Barolo brothers and their team fills the air with smiles and warmth, making every visit to this simple and welcoming restaurant a pleasure, the perfect place to enjoy the company of friends or colleagues. The menu is steeped in tradition: it is impossible to resist their pasta dishes, such as the creamy and satisfying “gramigna sporcafaccia” or tortellini covered in a velvety smooth Parmesan cream sauce. Desserts include a crunchy “sbrisolona” cake served with zabaglione made with passito wine, while the “zuppa inglese” trifle releases deliciously smooth notes to end the meal on a sweet note.

Name: Il Basilisco
Description: Situated in a peripheral residential area, this restaurant sports a vibrant and simple interior centred around splendid cuisine. Although many dishes adhere to the traditional national classic genre, local offerings particularly impressed us, such as the Risi e Bisi made with native peas cooked in pod broth. Nonetheless, room remains for certain fish offerings. A pleasant outdoors area is available for fair-weather enjoyment.

Name: Il Bikini
Address: SS 145 Sorrentina km 13,900, Vico Equense, 80069, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: For over 70 years, the elegant Il Bikini restaurant has been soaking up the sun in this superb location facing the spectacular Bay of Naples. Now home to a new and exuberant chef, the restaurant serves classic fish cuisine with a contemporary twist at lunchtime under the name Locanda di Mare, while in the evening the restaurant transforms into L’Atollo, a more elegant, fine-dining venue. Ever since the restaurant was opened in 1952, the panoramic terrace here has been one of the best places in the region in which to enjoy good food and spectacular sea views.

Name: Il Borgo
Description: This Italian restaurant has been a mainstay of Schwabing's culinary scene since 1989. The interior is modern and elegant yet cosy, with the current decor successfully incorporating the old wall tiles and original bar. The menu sticks close to the seasons. In addition to the five-course tasting menu, there is an à la carte selection – from delicious pasta dishes to branzino al sale (salt-baked sea bass) for two.

Name: Il Borro Tuscan Bistro Dubai
Address: Jumeirah Al Naseem Hotel, 906 Jumeirah Street, Umm Suqeim 3, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Set by the lovely Turtle Lagoon on the Jumeirah Al Naseem resort, this chic, well-dressed restaurant is understandably popular. Colourfully presented, traditional Italian dishes transport diners to the rolling Tuscan hills, while the interesting wine list offers a good selection of Italian, French and American names. The friendly yet formal service comes with old-fashioned Italian charm.

Name: Il Cairoli
Description: As is suggested by the use of the definite article before its name, Il Cairoli is a modern hotel restaurant with its own entrance. The menu here features classic Milanese specialities such as mondeghili meatballs, ossobucco risotto and veal cutlets, as well as other delicious and colourful dishes that are contemporary in style and based on the use of seasonal ingredients. There are also a few vegetarian options, as well as daily specials at midday, when a quicker and cheaper lunch option is available. An attractive dining room with large picture windows boasting views (albeit partial) of the Sforza castle adds to the appeal.

Name: Il Calandrino
Address: Via Liguria 1, loc. Sarmeola, Rubano, 35030, Italy
Description: Situated next to the three-Michelin-starred Le Calandre (and run by the same family), Il Calandrino is an elegant and eclectic restaurant which includes a bar-cum-pasticceria that is well worth visiting at any time of day. The cuisine here ranges from creative dishes such as scallops with toasted leek cream, sea urchins and cima di rapa, to classic house favourites such as Erminio’s legendary beef tartare with toasted bread and salad greens, and Rita’s pazientina (chocolate layer cake) served with zabaglione.

Name: Il Capestrano
Address: Via Gian Francesco Pizzi 14, Milan, 20141, Italy
Description: This restaurant takes its name from the warrior statue dating back to the 6C BC which was discovered in Capestrano (Aquila province) in 1934. The statue, carved from a single block of local stone, is one of the most mysterious finds in history. No such mystery surrounds the dishes served in this restaurant, which focuses on cuisine from the Abruzzo, including top-quality hams and cheeses produced by small-scale producers, as well as mutton, lamb, beef, barbecued lamb kebabs and other culinary delights.

Name: Il Capriolino
Address: Via Nazionale 108, Vodo di Cadore, 32040, Italy
Description: This elegant restaurant has been run by the same family for years and has a history dating back over two centuries. It serves regional yet creative cuisine and has a distinctly Middle European ambience with its hunting trophies, clocks and frescoes.

Name: Il Carpaccio
Description: This traditional family restaurant has been recently renovated to include an attractive veranda - style dining room overlooking the valley. Typical dishes from Calabria, fish specialities by prior arrangement, and a good wine list all add to the appeal.

Name: Il Cascinalenuovo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Having been under the watchful eye of chef Walter Ferretto for decades, Il Cascinalenuovo serves classic, seasonal cuisine which celebrates local traditions in a glorious array of Piedmontese dishes, such as the region’s famous plin (filled pasta) served in a napkin or with a roast meat sauce, tongue millefeuille and pigeon. The menu also includes more contemporary-style recipes such as the “artichoke and artichoke” dish or the lightly fried catch of the day, while the extensive and carefully curated wine list focuses largely on Piedmont. In fine weather, book a table in the attractive outdoor space overlooking the garden and swimming pool. The restaurant also offers romantic guestrooms, which are ideal for a relaxing stay.

Name: Il Cavallo Scosso
Description: A young and modern restaurant situated in a residential area about 2km from the centre, where owner-chef Enrico Pivieri offers a menu that is equally divided between traditional meat-based dishes from Piedmont (some, such as the plin pasta, are very traditional in style while others have a more reinterpreted feel) and more creative fish-based options. The chef gives full rein to his creativity in dishes such as the Mediterranean fish ceviche with avocado, passion fruit gel and sea-urchin mayonnaise.

Name: Il Chiosco di Bacco
Description: This restaurant boasts a rural location in the Montefeltro region, to which half the menu is dedicated (fresh home-made pastas, salumi, porchetta-style rabbit etc). The other half focuses on meat dishes, with an interesting selection of steaks and ribs from Italian and Scottish breeds (including more expensive beef that has been left to age for a month). You’ll find the perfect wine pairing on the excellent wine list.

Name: Il Cigno
Description: Adjacent to the historic center, this elegant and refined restaurant occupies an evocative sixteenth-century building that preserves a timeless charm. The talented and creative chef presents a contemporary cuisine that alternates meat and fish dishes with balance, playing with modern techniques and touches of imagination. The “amberjack sashimi with almond cream, raspberry, and puffed quinoa” is a small opening of pure finesse, while concluding with their excellent desserts is nearly obligatory. In fine weather, it is worth reserving a table on the evocative terrace, arranged around a captivating fifteenth-century well.

Name: Il Cipresso - Da Cioni
Address: Via Alcide De Gasperi 28, Loro Ciuffenna, 52024, Italy
Description: Standing on a round terrace, this restaurant with a fairly plain interior serves dishes made from some of the best produce of the region – cured hams, bread, pasta and famous Tuscan meats. The restaurant also offers simple, rustic - style guestrooms.

Name: Il Colmetto
Description: A true gourmet agriturismo, Il Colmetto changes its menu almost week by week in line with the changing seasons. Full of flavour, the ingredients here (many of which are produced on the property, while others are sourced locally) are cooked with precision, avoiding overly fussy and complicated techniques. Instead, the focus is on good, honest cuisine with its roots in peasant traditions, in which the aim is to create comforting dishes that will appeal to the palate. The barbecued specialities, such as the sweetbreads and the excellent Jerusalem artichokes, are particularly delicious, while the superb goats’ milk butter, served soft and fluffy as a cloud with bread and focaccia, is truly delicious – its only drawback is that it can be addictive!

Name: Il Convito della Venaria
Address: Via Andrea Mensa 37/g, Venaria Reale, 10078, Italy
Description: This restaurant is run by an enthusiastic couple, with Lucia front of house in the classic and welcoming dining room and Christian at the helm in the kitchen. The menu is lighter (and less expensive) at lunchtime with a wider choice of regional and Italian fare in the evening, plus a few more creative options, including fish dishes. Comfortable guestrooms are also available, two of which have views of the royal palace.

Name: Il Cortile
Description: You get to this restaurant, which is located in a pretty little courtyard in Erfurt's old town via Johannesstraße. In a cosy atmosphere, diners tuck into Mediterranean-inspired cuisine that draws on flavours from all over the world. The menu features dishes such as "Ricotta, truffle, pea, Serrano", "Salsiccia, capers, sugar snap pea" or "Fjord trout, grape, risotto, truffle".

Name: Il Cortiletto
Description: Standing on the Lake Garda road, this small, simple, yet far from ordinary restaurant serves Mediterranean dishes with the occasional inventive twist. Two words of advice – opt for alfresco dining in fine weather, and don’t miss the maccheroncini served with perch and lemon pesto sauce.

Name: Il Credenziere
Address: Via Quattro Strade 12, Annone Veneto, 30020, Italy
Description: Situated in a small country hamlet, this restaurant is run by a chef from Puglia, whose origins can be glimpsed here and there in his dishes. The influence of the Veneto, where the chef has been working for some time, is also evident in the local dishes which appear alongside more creative options on the menu.

Name: Il Cugnolo
Address: Contrada Cugnolo 19, Torre di Palme, 63900, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This gourmet restaurant housed in a restored period residence that once belonged to the counts of Adami is surrounded by the green maquis and hills of the Marche, with the sea visible in the distance just a few miles away. Here, the young Neapolitan chef creates cuisine that is surprising for its attractive, clean lines, providing a real explosion of flavours and a tribute to the region and the Mediterranean in general. The restaurant also owns a nearby agricultural estate which provides many of the wines and olive oils served during tastings.

Name: Il Doretto
Description: Housed in an attractive farmhouse, this restaurant serves seasonal cuisine that includes delicious fish and seafood (raw dishes as well as more elaborate options), alongside meat dishes, including some delicious game recipes.

Name: Il Faggio
Description: In the building that once housed the Workers’ Mutual Aid Society, there now unfolds an elegant dining room, with large windows and classic furnishings, wrapped in a comfortable atmosphere that feels almost suspended in time. While the setting evokes an elegance of another era, the kitchen moves along calmly modern lines, with a clearly recognisable Mediterranean imprint. The menu alternates with balance between seafood dishes – such as amberjack marinated with curry, coconut and beetroot – and meat-based proposals, among which the partridge cooked on the bone with smoked parsnip, a date stuffed with its livers and mustard sauce stands out: careful, readable preparations with real personality. Completing the experience is a particularly extensive wine list, with a solid Piedmontese presence alongside labels from across the Italian peninsula, as well as France and other interesting international forays.

Name: Il Favri
Address: Via Borgo Meduna 12, San Giorgio della Richinvelda, 33095, Italy
Description: This inn, which has been serving food since the early 19C, boasts a warm atmosphere with a rustic feel. The beautiful garden makes a delightful setting in fine weather, while the cuisine focuses on traditional dishes from Friuli, such as “frico” (potato, onion and cheese fritter) and cured ham.

Name: Il Fico trentacareghe
Description: Along one of the region's most scenic coastal routes, fronted by a charming olive garden, and within a petite hotel yet operating independently, the vista stands as a restaurant's focal strength, appreciated from some dining area tables and further still from the summer terrace. The cuisine, however, doesn’t fall short: two tasting menus and a seafood-focused menu rooted in local traditions with a flourish of creativity bear the kitchen’s signature.

Name: Il Fiorista
Address: 17 W. 26th St., New York, NY, 10010, USA
Description: Owners Alessandra and Mario De Benedetti's bright, airy dining room doubles as a flower shop, and its vivid, spring-like décor feels like stepping into a magazine cover. But these gorgeous blooms serve a third, even more exciting, role here, making their way into cocktails and dishes crafted with edible flowers like nasturtium blossoms and hibiscus petals. (They're also crafting a collection of spices, salts and sugars).The results are deliciously unique. Graze on a charcuterie plate or an assortment of small dishes like the thinly sliced and delicately fried lotus root dusted with pine pollen. Next, house-made pasta is a must, especially the campanelle tossed in a cream-based white Bolognese sauce, or opt for the broiled Alaskan salmon on a bed of tossed braised fennel and roasted cauliflower.

Name: Il Focarile
Address: Via Pontina al km 46,5, Aprilia, 04011, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The sumptuous entrance gives an elegant tone to a large bright dining room with well spaced out tables; a touch of Tuscany with a cuisine rich in tradition and also imagination. Now offers new, elegant rooms.

Name: Il Frantoio
Address: Via del Castello 40, Colle di Val d'Elsa, 53034, Italy
Description: The 19C millstone, press and cisterns can still be seen in the dining room at this restaurant, bearing witness to its past as an olive oil mill. Situated in spectacular Colle di Val d’Elsa, Il Frantoio boasts old stone and brick walls and vaulted ceilings, as well as tables set out in the piazza for summer dining. Although the setting suggests simple and rustic cuisine, the chef surprises guests with top-quality dishes which are technical and often highly creative, such as liver with sour cherries and pistachios, and smoked spaghetti with an anchovy sauce, capers and black garlic cream.

Name: Il Frate
Description: In 2025, this restaurant celebrates a century of existence, as a veritable treasure trove of history that has preserved its family soul intact. Today, the kitchen is run by Lorenza, heir to a tradition that smells of Emilia and Piacenza, the same tradition lovingly preserved by her mother. The dishes arrive at the table generous and steaming, with classic flavours that seduce the eye and the palate. The wine list, which is now digital, boasts around 350 labels: the treasures of Northern Italy prevail, but there are also international notes. For the perfect pairing, let yourself be guided by Giorgio, the fourth generation of the family in the dining room. With grace and expertise, he will transform every sip into a harmonious accompaniment to your dish.

Name: Il Funghetto
Address: Strada Litoranea 11412, località Borgo Grappa, Latina, 04010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Fish and seafood take pride of place on the menu at this restaurant just a few minutes’ drive from the beach. The owner-chef (the second generation since 1973) is happy to advise guests on food and wine choices alike, offering a wide choice of wines from all over Italy and around the world. Welcoming dining room and shady arbour. Gluten-free options available.

Name: Il Galeone
Description: In a bright, elegant and modern dining room inside the Elisabeth Due hotel, Galeone is one of the city's finest gastronomic destinations. The menu focuses on fish, with dishes that draw on local traditions, such as “brodetto alla fanese” fish soup (available by advance order), alongside more creative offerings.

Name: Il Gattopardo
Description: Il Gattopardo is a charismatic Italian restaurant that possesses a certain je-ne-sais-quoi. The chef personally comes to your table to present his signature Sicilian dishes, which he revamps with fresh twists. Familiar flavours are enriched with subtle influences from further afield. The comforting classic melanzane alla parmigiana, for example, is elevated with deep-fried shiso leaves and basil ice cream. The chef shows the same precision in crafting deeply flavoured sauces as he does in preparing a cannolo filled with airy ricotta and delicate notes of orange. Be sure to peruse the wine list, which features a fine selection of Italian labels.

Name: Il Gattopardo
Address: 27 Albemarle Street, Mayfair, London, W1S 4HZ, United Kingdom
Description: Given its name – which translates as ‘leopard’ – it’s not hard to guess that this chic Mayfair operation specialises in classic Italian cuisine. Thankfully, this is a leopard that won’t change its spots, serving time-honoured dishes cooked in the traditional Italian way, with quality ingredients and plenty of flavour. Sharing is encouraged and given the generosity of dishes like the veal Milanese, it’s probably a good idea. All of this comes wrapped up in elegant surroundings, whether you’re sat in the main room, on the light-filled terrace or by the crudo bar.

Name: Il Giardinetto
Address: Piazza Giuseppe Garibaldi 10, Mandello del Lario, 23826, Italy
Description: Looking out over the calm blue water, this classic restaurant serves traditional cuisine with the occasional imaginative twist. Fish from the lake feature on the menu, as do meat and seafood options with something for everyone. There’s also a small outdoor terrace where guests can enjoy a pre- or post-dinner drink.

Name: Il Giardino
Address: Hôtel Byblos, 20 avenue Paul-Signac, Saint-Tropez, 83990, France
Description: Behind the Place des Lices, the legendary Byblos hotel is home to this Italian gem, set opposite the swimming pool beneath a pergola covered in a profusion of greenery. The chef draws on the palace hotel's permaculture vegetable garden to create elegant Italian cuisine: flavoursome antipasti, house-made pasta, timeless classics (cotoletta milanese, paccheri carbonara) and refined creations such as saltimbocca of red mullet. The service is impeccable, thanks to unwavering attention to detail. The epitome of Saint-Tropez dolce farniente.

Name: Il Giardino "Da Felicin"
Description: A bastion of the most authentic Piedmontese tradition, the restaurant is located in a refined period building, enhanced by a panoramic terrace and a romantic garden that invites guests to dine al fresco in the summer months. The dining rooms reflect the same vocation for traditional, rich and welcoming elegance, which reaches its fullest expression in the dishes: impeccable interpretations of the region’s finest cuisine. The restaurant’s signature dish is the famous Tajarin di Felicin, handmade tagliatelle cut into very fine strands and served with a delicate Fassona beef sauce, a true declaration of love for local gastronomy. The property also comprises a scattered hotel, with rooms located both in the main building and in other parts of the village, including the charming Palazzo Boeri, which has a small spa accessible by reservation. The owners know the area intimately and are delighted to accompany guests on guided tours of the Langhe, organised by themselves or by local experts, making the stay a complete experience encompassing cuisine, hospitality and local culture.

Name: Il Giardino del Gusto
Description: In the most evocative heart of Ventimiglia, the restaurant looks out over a graceful pedestrian square where, in the warmer months, a small outdoor area welcomes guests to the slow rhythm of the old town. Inside, the intimate dining room, with its classic décor, exudes a discreet warmth, made up of traditional details and an atmosphere that invites guests to linger. The kitchen gives pride of place to the sea, interpreting local produce with respect and creativity, the undisputed star of the menu. Yet there is also a tasting menu dedicated to the vegetable garden, designed to showcase the freshness of Ligurian land, as well as a number of carefully prepared meat dishes that complete a balanced and contemporary gastronomic offering.

Name: Il Giardino delle Esperidi
Description: The ideal starting point for an exploration of the area. In summer one dines on the terrace located in the heart of the historic centre while drinks and cigars may be enjoyed in the lounge bar.

Name: Il Ginkgo
Description: A restaurant with modern, minimalist dining rooms that houses the creative and gourmet cuisine of young chef Lorenzo Barbieri. A native of Cremona, he serves in his splendid city elaborate and contemporary dishes, both of meat and fish, with few references to local traditions, yet these will appeal to those seeking novelty, echoes of international cuisine and occasionally unexpected flavour pairings.

Name: Il Giurista
Description: This restaurant is named after Bartolo da Sassoferrato (as is the street on which it stands), a distinguished 14C jurist. From the street, you head down a few steps to the welcoming dining rooms with their historic ambience and brick-vaulted ceilings that keep the temperature pleasantly cool. The cuisine, which focuses exclusively on meat, is traditional and regional in flavour – an entire section of the menu is dedicated to black truffles in season. Friendly and attentive service.

Name: Il Grano di Pepe
Description: While you’re trying to decide between the tasting menu and the à la carte at this restaurant, you can tuck into its excellent bread, including the “sfincione” – a type of tomato-flavoured focaccia from Palermo which makes the journey here worthwhile on its own! If fish is your preference, we recommend the “Palermo and Marseille” fish stew, an intense dish full of bold and delicious flavours. Minimalist decor and a friendly welcome from chef Rino Duca complete the picture.

Name: Il Grifone
Address: Via Ca' Masino 611/a - loc. Varignana, Castel San Pietro Terme, 40024, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: This fine-dining restaurant housed in the 18C Palazzo Bentivoglio Bargellini is part of the luxurious Palazzo di Varignana resort (with which it shares the Il Grifone symbol), the latter also home to a farm producing olive oil, wine and fruit. In the evening, choose between two tasting menus and an à la carte offering a selection of meat and fish dishes on which the modern recipes feature a careful balance of colours and flavours.

Name: Il Grottino
Address: Piazza Beato Ugolino 5, Gualdo Cattaneo, 06035, Italy
Description: Situated in the old medieval village of Gualdo Cattaneo, amid the gentle valleys not far from Foligno, Il Grottino is the perfect choice for anyone keen to sample the authentic flavours of Umbrian cuisine. Here, truffles and zero-km produce take pride of place on the menu, with a particular focus on meat which is carefully cooked on the open-view barbecue grill. Alongside locally sourced produce, you’ll also find a choice of carefully selected Prussian beef. Comfortable and welcoming guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: Il Gusto
Description: In the central area, chef Alessio Boldrin has reinvented the Venetian bàcaro tradition. Classic cicchetti here become samples served on one large plate, entertaining the palate. Not to be outdone is the à la carte menu, which offers a wide selection of mouth-watering and satisfying dishes, such as tagliolini cacio, pepe and scampi. The wine list features a good selection of Italian and French bubbly.

Name: Il Gusto di Xinge
Description: The dining room plays on warm brown tones reminiscent of a teapot, enlivened by touches of brilliant blue and modern leather chairs that lend a contemporary edge to the space. The Chinese chef presents authentic cuisine from her homeland – dim sum included – while drawing inspiration from Italian and French culinary traditions, all infused with a decidedly “pop” creative flair. To best begin the experience, consider an artisanal cocktail at nearby DrinX, the perfect prelude to dinner.

Name: Il Labirinto
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated on the outskirts of Brescia, this long-established restaurant has an elegant retro atmosphere. The cuisine is varied with a balance of fish and meat dishes, as well as some excellent home-made salumi.

Name: Il Liberty
Description: Nestled in an Art Nouveau palazzo just a short walk from the dynamic Porta Nuova district, the restaurant offers a warm and refined setting, comprising a bright main dining room, a romantic balcony, a small room with an open‑view kitchen and a convivial social table. Inspired by Mediterranean tradition, the menu weaves together seafood and meat dishes with fine balance: from the “cotto-crudo” veal and mortadella mondeghili with soft potato, light salsa verde and hazelnuts, to the sumptuous thick-cut veal cutlet Milanese, served with fresh potato crisps, homemade ketchup and a delicate honey mustard.

Name: Il Marchese - Osteria Mercato Liquori
Description: Boasting a sumptuous Art Deco setting that contrasts pleasingly with the traditional cuisine served here, this restaurant is the Milanese sibling of Il Marchese in Rome which pays tribute to the famous Italian film “Il Marchese del Grillo” starring Alberto Sordi (it is also the first bar in Europe to offer more than 600 “amaro” liqueurs). The culinary philosophy here is based on traditional Roman cuisine with a contemporary flavour, including delicious specialities such as pasta with carbonara, matriciana and gricia sauces, veal saltimbocca, pork belly and much more besides!

Name: Il Marchese - Osteria Mercato Liquori
Description: Convivial and informal with a touch of elegance, this restaurant is perfect for a night out with friends – and indeed for anyone in the mood for delicious cuisine brimming with flavours which are predominantly Roman in style. The carbonara and amatriciana are superb, while the antipasti (especially the croquettes and artichoke in season) should not be missed. An impressive selection of cocktails completes the picture. Booking is recommended, as it’s often full!

Name: Il Mecenate
Description: Occupying the premises of a historic local laundry along the city “moat”, this authentic trattoria has a friendly, convivial ambience. The menu showcases local dishes to the full, including specialities such as “tordelli lucchesi” (ravioli stuffed with different meats, thyme and nutmeg and always served with a meat ragù), tripe and bread pudding, the original recipe of which dates back to the 18C. A picturesque outdoor terrace facing San Francesco church and an excellent wine selection complete the picture.

Name: Il Melograno
Description: In the village centre and therefore not right by the sea, this successful, well - established restaurant is decorated in elegant contemporary style. The menu focuses on fish dishes reinterpreted with a touch of imagination.

Name: Il Merlo
Address: Viale Sergio Bernardini 660, Lido di Camaiore, 55041, Italy
Description: Situated right on the beach, Il Merlo boasts a welcoming dining room decorated in elegant, contemporary style. The owner is at the helm in the kitchen, where he creates dishes with a focus on fish and seafood, such as the raw seafood platter and the salt-baked catch of the day. A few delicious meat options, such as plin pasta and pigeon, are also available.

Name: Il Michelaccio
Description: A modern bistro in the heart of the city, just a short walk from the famous Via XX Settembre. Here, the chef and owner interprets fragrant, market-fresh cuisine that pays tribute to Ligurian tradition – such as potato cream with Genoese-style sea snails – and embraces Italian flavours, such as pappa al pomodoro with burratina. In addition to the menu, delicious dishes inspired by the market surprise guests every day. Don't miss the “Minestrone alla ligure” soup, served in a small pot: pure goodness! The warm and informal welcome makes everything special.

Name: Il Mirto
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: On arriving at the luxurious Hotel Botania, guests are accompanied to the restaurant through a park of over three hectares immersed in the most luxuriant Mediterranean vegetation: the finest possible introduction to the cuisine that awaits at Il Mirto. Here the experience unfolds across two extended tasting menus – with the option of reducing either to four freely chosen courses – one vegetarian and one vegan, with almost all the vegetables sourced from the property’s own kitchen gardens or from cultivation elsewhere on the island. Among the most representative dishes, the signature “Ris8” stands out, interpreting technique and creativity in a contemporary key. The service, too, is excellent – young and spontaneous – contributing to an evening that is a fully immersive experience in nature.

Name: Il Molo
Address: Via Falcone Borsellino 2, San Leone, 92100, Italy
Description: Situated on the seafront facing the small tourist harbour of San Leone, this elegant restaurant boasts an attractive summer terrace with a relaxed ambience. Here you can savour a selection of regional fish and meat dishes prepared by the owner-chef with ingredients of the highest quality.

Name: Il Molo
Address: Via Aganor Pompili 9, Passignano sul Trasimeno, 06065, Italy
Description: Situated in the historic centre of Passignano, where the village seems to jut out into Lake Trasimeno (some tables in the main dining room boast views of the lake – make sure you book in advance), Il Molo has been run by the Pellegrini family since 1978. The restaurant has become a popular choice for guests keen to try top-quality fish from the lake as well as excellent poultry dishes, with dishes showcased on an à la carte and three tasting menus. We highly recommend the herb bottoni pasta with sunfish and saffron butter. There’s also a good choice of sparkling wines and champagnes.

Name: Il Narciso
Description: Housed in the Polda baths near the marina, this recently opened small restaurant on the beach serves cuisine with a contemporary yet classic flavour. The restaurant boasts excellent bread, home-made pasta, traditionally cooked dishes such as chicken casserole and creative desserts. Highly recommended, especially the terrace with its fine sea views.

Name: Il Paguro
Address: Via Cala Capra, Capo d'Orso, Palau, 07020, Italy
Description: The small bay of Cala Capra is truly romantic and exclusive. Advance reservations are advised; without one, the barrier at the top of the road down to the marina won’t be raised. Hotel Capo d’Orso, which houses the Paguro restaurant, shares the same atmosphere: with a gorgeous Mediterranean-style terrace overlooking this little slice of paradise. The food suits the setting: classic, straightforward cooking built mostly around excellent local catch. A place that’s genuinely hard to leave.

Name: Il Pavone
Description: Situated in the heart of Alghero and with a beautiful veranda overlooking the sea, this restaurant has been in business for almost 50 years. Fish and seafood take centre stage here, served in classic dishes which are full of flavour and prepared using top-quality local ingredients. Specialities include fresh pan-fried and grilled fish, delicious bavettine pasta with scampi and fried mussels, and the island’s famous “seadas” served with Sardinian eucalyptus honey or home-made ice-cream.

Name: Il Pescatore
Address: Via Acqua Dolce 7, Cala Gonone, 08022, Italy
Description: This Mediterranean-style restaurant has the evocative feel of a seaside village with its beautiful photos of the coast on the walls. It’s best to book ahead if you want one of the tables on the small terrace overlooking the sea. To avoid confusion, note that the Il Pescatore that we recommend is situated at 7, via Acqua Dolce.

Name: Il Piraña
Description: A classic fish restaurant that opts for simply prepared dishes rather than fussy, inventive avant - garde cuisine. The perfect address for those in search of traditional fare.

Name: Il Poggio
Description: This simple yet welcoming family-run restaurant is situated on the wine route that wends its way through the hills behind Sondrio, less than 5km away. The dining room boasts a cheerful open fireplace (also used as a grill), while an attractive outdoor terrace offers fine views of the valley. The cuisine focuses mainly on local recipes and ingredients, with some main courses cooked over the grill.

Name: Il Ponte
Description: A short walk from the town centre, this restaurant with elegant tones welcomes you to a beautiful veranda room with refined furnishings that play on shades of yellow and blue. The kitchen interprets the flavours and traditions of the Mediterranean with modern techniques and creative cues, and in the summer, the open-fire grill takes centre stage – a spectacle that allows you to watch the chefs at work, especially in the preparation of fish and seafood. Along with à la carte choices, you can enjoy a three-course menu or a five-course tasting menu, also available with wine pairings – a highly recommended option. Desserts, mouthwatering and well-executed, close the meal with satisfaction.

Name: Il Portico
Description: Chef Lopriore returns to his native region with this new restaurant which offers an original format – the lunchtime menu focuses on single course options, while in the evening the tasting menus comprise an interesting combination of imaginative fish, meat and vegetable dishes which can be combined as you wish. Cuisine with an emphasis on seasonal market ingredients where locally sourced produce takes pride of place.

Name: Il Portolano
Address: Via Molara 11, Porto San Paolo, 07020, Italy
Description: Right on the seafront in front of Tavolara Island, a simple restaurant run by an experienced couple. The kitchen exalts the best fish in the area with a modern taste, offered with a wide selection including some raw (such as red tuna tartare with cucumber and raspberries) and the catch of the day grilled, baked or in salt. In the summer, reservations are highly recommended because the scenic outdoor seating area, although large, is extremely popular!

Name: Il Posticino
Description: A tiny gem in the historic center, just steps from the San Michele towers. A very intimate setting, with a refined yet informal atmosphere. The cuisine? Seafood with a seasonal twist, including standouts such as the surprising Brandapolenta: creamy baccala, crispy polenta, taggiasca olive pâté. Reserving a table – especially for outdoor seating – is a must!

Name: Il Pozzo
Description: This restaurant is housed in a historic palazzo. It has a traditional dining room, as well as an area that was once home to a wine bar (vaulted ceilings and more convivial atmosphere). A full range of Italian specialities are served.

Name: Il Presidente
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: In the heart of the historic centre, just a short distance from the Cathedral of Lucera, this restaurant lies in an ancient alleyway where the stables of a noble palazzo once stood. Today the dining room is arranged across several interconnecting spaces, framed by elegant stone vaulting; at its centre, two glass panels allow a glimpse of the cellar, which houses over 300 labels. The cooking is Mediterranean, modern and vivid in colour: among the dishes, octopus with almonds, fusillone with pumpkin cream and scampi, and a fillet of fish – sea bream, sea bass or dentex according to the market – accompanied by seasonal vegetables, to give some sense of the style. The focaccia di mare is not to be missed. This is not so much cooking of technical virtuosity as a homage to the ingredient itself: flavour, here, remains the true protagonist.

Name: Il Principe
Address: Via Colle San Bartolomeo 4, Pompei, 80045, Italy
Description: This restaurant focuses on a skilful and creative reinterpretation of Campanian specialities, serving the type of cuisine that you’d be happy to eat every day. Although the dishes are inspired by the chef’s childhood memories and his grandmother’s cooking, he adds his own contemporary touch and careful presentation. Both meat and fish feature, showcasing all the colour and imagination of the best regional cuisine.

Name: Il Riccio
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Situated just a few metres from the Blue Grotto and perched right above the water, Il Riccio is the quintessential Mediterranean fine-dining restaurant thanks to its tasteful and elegant decor. Undoubtedly one of Capri’s iconic addresses, it focuses uniquely on fish and seafood dishes. Whether you have a sweet tooth or not, a visit to the tempting dessert buffet to admire its array of delicacies is a must!

Name: Il Ridotto
Address: Campo S.S. Filippo e Giacomo, sestiere Castello 4509, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: Just a few steps from St. Mark's Square and the Bridge of Sighs, in a small square, Il Ridotto welcomes you with a colourful and warm atmosphere. The cuisine, based on territoriality and seasonality of products, will win you over. Not to be missed is the mouthwatering and fresh white chocolate dessert of bergamot, citrus and grapefruit.

Name: Il Ristorante - Niko Romito
Address: Via Privata Fratelli Gabba 7/b, Milan, 20121, Italy
Description: Housed within the Bulgari hotel, a secluded haven of elegance right in the heart of the most exclusive district in Milan, this restaurant alternates the trusted chefs at its helm, all of whom continue to serve light, contemporary Italian cuisine in dishes that focus more on substance than form. Choose between tasting menus and a generous à la carte selection featuring meat and fish dishes alike, including classic local favourites such as risotto and vitello alla Milanese (breaded veal cutlet).

Name: Il Ristorante - Niko Romito
Description: Situated on the fifth floor of the Hotel Bulgari with views of the Mausoleum of Augustus, this restaurant boasts a spacious terrace and an elegant, welcoming dining room with mahogany walls adorned with works of art. To reach the dining room, you pass through the lively bar, where we recommend starting your evening with an aperitif. Once at your table, the menu offers a concrete expression of three-Michelin-star chef Niko Romito’s culinary approach which focuses on lighter, elegant versions of traditional Italian dishes in a sequence of courses that take guests on a culinary tour around Italy. Spaghetti in tomato sauce, artichoke soup, saffron risotto and Piedmontese “bonet” dessert all feature on the menu.

Name: Il Ristorante - Niko Romito
Address: Hôtel Bulgari, 30 avenue George-V, Paris, 75008, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Niko Romito, a chef from Abruzzo with three Michelin stars to his name, updates the classics of Italian cooking in a menu that really homes in on the produce and dares to go light (easy on the fat, limited sauces, steamed ingredients, rice starch for the breadcrumb coating etc). The saffron risotto with parmesan is subtle and does not weigh on the stomach, as is the magnificent veal cutlet alla Milanese, to be savoured in this elegantly sleek dining area that opens onto the interior garden.

Name: Il Ristorante Alain Ducasse Roma
Description: A few steps from Piazza del Popolo, a 17th-century palazzo houses the Romeo hotel and, within it, the restaurant bearing the name of the world’s most-starred chef. The dining room – like the entire hotel, designed by Zaha Hadid – is a triumph of precious materials: ebony on the walls, marble for the open kitchen, an aesthetic that unites luxury, exclusivity and futuristic lines in every detail. Leading the kitchen is a young chef who honed his technique in the kitchens of Alain Ducasse, between Monaco and Paris. Here he selects ingredients of great quality and works them into compositions that are never complicated, characterised by clear, readable flavours, often punctuated by Mediterranean accents. Cooking that finds its most convincing expression in the elegance of the raw materials and the precision of the cooking, perfectly in harmony with the striking surroundings.

Name: Il Ritorno
Address: 449 Central Ave. N., #101, St. Petersburg, FL, 33701, USA
Description: For more than a decade, Chef David Benstock has led this fine dining Italian stalwart from the heart of downtown St. Petersburg. High ceilings, exposed red brick, and easy-going servers set a relaxed tone for a team that’s full of ideas and keen to present them in attractive ways. How often do you see duck tortellini with shaved foie gras or a salad of radishes presented as a garden bed with soil and fences? Creative pastas are at the heart of this menu, alongside serious cuts of steak and lamb sourced from their butcher shop next door. Though some dishes can feel busy, there is boldness and flavor in spades. Luxury comes in the form of caviar doughnuts, Japanese wagyu, and a special tasting menu available only at the chef’s counter.

Name: Il Rivale al Lago
Address: Via Marconi 93, Padenghe sul Garda, 25080, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the lake, this multi-faceted restaurant serves classic Italian dishes, often with a creative twist, alongside top-quality international ingredients such as Cantabrian anchovies and Japanese Wagyu beef. Grilled meats and vegetable dishes also make an appearance on the menu.

Name: Il Rivale in Città
Description: Situated in a beautiful 18C palazzo right in the centre of Brescia, this elegant restaurant consists of several small dining rooms of different colours, fabrics and furnishings yet all with the same historic atmosphere – the room with just one table is truly intimate! The cuisine features substantial recipes with a contemporary Italian flavour including top-quality options such as potato puff pastry, scampi, caviar and hazelnut cream, while one of the highlights of the new formula is the wooden dessert trolley on which a selection of tempting home-made delicacies is presented. The wine list (easily consulted on a tablet) is also impressive, with a particular focus on labels from nearby Franciacorta.

Name: Il Salotto Atelier Gourmet
Description: The small, classic Rosabianca hotel on the seafront in Rapallo has begun to improve its facilities, starting with its restaurant where large windows (which can be opened in summer) overlook the promenade, and its intimate, elegant interior with subtle lighting and a relaxing ambience. The cuisine focuses on fish and seafood which are skilfully prepared so that the quality of the superb ingredients shines through, while the service ensures that guests are looked after with discretion and professionalism.

Name: Il Sanlorenzo
Description: A historic palazzo built over the foundations of the Teatro Pompeo is home to this atmospheric restaurant, which brings together history and contemporary art. However, the real star is the fish on the menu, most of which comes from the island of Ponza, and is served either raw or cooked very simply in a modern style.

Name: Il Santo Bevitore
Address: Via Santo Spirito 64/66 r, Florence, 50125, Italy
Description: The atmosphere is simple and convivial, with the authentic feel of a typical Tuscan trattoria. It is from this tradition that the cooking takes its cue, offering a number of regional classics: from the selection of cured meats to ribollita, from roast pigeon served with fettunta and zolfini beans to cantucci with Vin Santo. There are also occasional seafood dishes, such as cuttlefish and artichoke stew. These are generous, full-flavoured dishes, faithful to a style of cooking that expresses Tuscan identity to the full, sometimes refreshed through more contemporary interpretations, yet always recognisable and reassuring.

Name: Il Saturnino
Description: It was a love story between an American and a local girl from Forio that led, in 1949, to the opening of this restaurant overlooking the port, with its attractive veranda boasting fine sea views. The current management team have made this one of the most interesting restaurants in the region for anyone keen to sample traditional cuisine from Ischia and Campania. Don’t miss the pasta served with local (and very rare) zampognaro beans, mussels and squid, or the Ischian-style rabbit presented in an attractive terracotta dish. A good choice of fish dishes is also available.

Name: Il Sole di Ranco
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: An elegant residence with gardens sloping down to the lake. The charming terrace, where meals are served in summer, offers superb views of the lake, while the cuisine combines the traditional and the modern, including imaginative flavours with a focus on locally sourced ingredients.

Name: Il Sommelier
Description: This small, intimate restaurant next to the elegant Palazzo Roccabruna in the historic centre is slightly off the beaten track despite its central location. Recently opened by the Poletti brothers (one in the kitchen, the other front of house), with an attractive dining room designed by the owners’ father, the restaurant serves top-quality ingredients (especially fish and seafood) in dishes which include modern influences (the mango cheesecake is delicious) and a pleasing classic appeal (raw fish dishes).

Name: Il Tartufo
Description: Housed in a small villa in the residential area of the village, this intimate and secluded restaurant serves delicious cuisine with distinctly regional roots. In season, locally sourced truffles take centre stage, while fish and seafood dominate the menu at other times of year.

Name: Il Teatro²
Description: Founded in 1984, this family-run establishment located close to the Staatstheater (hence the name) is now run by the second generation, with Daniele di Sario taking the helm several years ago. He delivers classic Italian and French-style cuisine that is in keeping with the zeitgeist: The spaghetti carbonara, turbot with Champagne sauce or lemon dessert ("Kreation von der Zitrone") are shining examples. In keeping with the name of the restaurant, the menu is divided into different sections: Act 1, Intermezzo, Act 2 and Epilogue. Veteran chef Giovanni likes to get in on the action front of house, joining forces with the enthusiastic and attentive service team. In summer, the terrace seating out on the wide pavement is especially appealing.

Name: Il Trillo
Description: On the hills overlooking the town, an ancient residence transformed into a refined hospitality venue – and today home also to the estate’s own winery – receives its guests in surroundings of considerable elegance. A charm that reaches its apogee in the warmer months, when dinner is served in the evocative limonaia: a romantic panoramic terrace bathed in soft light and surrounded by lemon, orange, bergamot and mandarin trees. The kitchen engages in a dialogue with the territory, weaving together ingredients from sea and land along classical lines enriched by touches of imagination and careful presentation. Among the dishes that drew particular appreciation from our Inspector, the tortellini filled with pear and pecorino in a saffron and pistachio sauce, and the duck breast with mandarin accompanied by a celeriac tartlet.

Name: Il Trionfo
Description: Il Trionfo is both an elegant restaurant and a family story. The father and daughter-in-law preside front-of-house, and their enthusiasm is infectious. He also has some fantastic wine recommendations up his sleeve. Upon entering the restaurant, you will catch a glimpse of the mother and son at work in the kitchen. You can opt for the more creative set menu or order à la carte from a selection of traditional robust Mediterranean classics like vitello tonnato and spaghetti vongole. Don't miss the osso buco – the meat is unbelievably tender, and that typically rich tomato sauce is simply divine. The quintessence of Italian generosity!

Name: Il Tufo Allegro
Description: In the heart of one of Tuscany’s most spectacular villages, steps from the Synagogue, sits a small restaurant carved into the tufa stone, with intimate dining rooms and a truly well‑stocked wine cellar. The cuisine is authentically Tuscan: tradition and quality meet in every dish, thanks to local ingredients such as extra‑virgin olive oil, meats, cured meats, and cheeses carefully selected from the surrounding area. An experience to savor, with genuine flavors and a timeless atmosphere.

Name: Il Vecchio
Address: 332-12 World Cup buk-ro, Mapo-gu, Seoul, 03930, South Korea
Description: Il Vecchio is a down-to-earth, homey ristorante run by the chef couple Min-kyun Kim and Bin-na Kim. The eatery's signature dishes, made with fresh local produce and seafood, perfectly capture the tastes of the season. The chef duo's meticulous cooking brings out nuanced flavours, aromas, and textures in every ingredient, with semi‑dried fresh pasta exemplifying their precision. Continuous innovation is the standard at Il Vecchio, with the goal of providing diners with varied yet reliable dining experiences.

Name: Il Verso del Ghiottone
Description: This restaurant housed in an 18C building has a warm, rustic feel with terracotta, stone and brick decor and black tables with American-style place mats, resulting in a vibrant yet elegant atmosphere where the service is informal and yet also highly professional. The cuisine is inspired by regional recipes which are reinterpreted and given a lighter flavour. There’s no shortage of interesting fish dishes, including the exquisite red shrimp, which is half-cooked, half-raw and served with passion-fruit caramel.

Name: Il Vicolo Rosso
Description: This small Italian wine bar and osteria is run by a chef from Rimini and his French wife, who curates the broad selection of wines from small producers and renowned estates – which you can drink on site or take away.
