Once inside the exclusive-feeling dining room, sit back and watch the changing projections on the wall and let yourself be immersed as each creative, complex dish arrives. The chef’s travels are a heavy influence on the dishes, as are his experiences working at the likes of Ynyshir and The Fat Duck. Plenty of punchy flavours and relaxed, well-versed service ensure the experience is an enjoyable one from start to finish.

Name: JUE
Description: Resembling the Chinese pronunciation of a word which refers to a title of nobility, Jue is a restaurant that specializes in Cantonese cuisine. The set menu is also named after the different noble titles in China. One of Jue's signature dishes is its barbecued pork which, after being marinated, is roasted in a high-temperature oven to ensure a supremely crispy skin and juicy, flavorful meat. Of the 13 different varieties of dim sum on offer, the cheung fan (rice noodle roll), shumai topped with abalone, and the spring rolls are not to be missed.

Name: JULIA
Description: The wife is the chef, the husband the sommelier in this couple-run restaurant. The omakase set menu consists of pairings only. An evangelist to the world for Japan as a terroire, JULIA specialises in Japanese foodstuffs and Japanese wines. Most ingredients come from Ibaraki Prefecture, where the husband was born and the restaurant originated. Uniquely, the couple favours pairings of vegetables and fish with fruit. Self-taught and freewheeling, the cuisine is colourful and light.

Name: JUNTO
Address: 2F, The Blue by Just Inn, 22 Guanqian Road, Zhongzheng District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: Walnut wood furniture sits nicely against the blue-grey upholstery and subway tiles in this space with bustling street views. The Hong Kong chef's set menus, with optional add-ons, comprise dishes rooted in Cantonese traditions but updated with creative twists and condiments from across the globe. His signature char siu uses tenderised local pork belly marinated in barbecue sauce with Malaysian dark soy, balanced by the acidity of pink grapefruit.

Name: JUWEL
Description: The fine dining restaurant at BEI SCHUMANN resort is aptly named (juwel means "gem"), starting with the plush interior featuring elegant touches and upscale details such as amethysts and Swarovski crystals. The wrap-around picture windows are also lovely, flooding the semi-circular room with light. Then there is Robert Hauptvogel's classically French-inspired cuisine, which is served as a four- to seven-course set menu. In keeping with the sophisticated setting, attentive, professional service is provided by a friendly and experienced team, who also share expert wine recommendations.

Name: Jaan Joor
Address: 78/1 Chang Phueak, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
Description: Easy to spot with its white façade and striking blue doors, this restaurant near Lanna Golf has a welcoming decor of wood, exposed brick and inviting lighting. The kitchen delivers well-executed Thai dishes – tom som kung ma now, Jaan Joor stir-fried beef, and the standout stir-fried prawns with roasted chilli paste and prawn oil. Expect generous portions made for sharing; it's excellent value, given the quality. Ample parking makes it a convenient option.

Name: Jabalina
Address: C. Padre Mier 859, Barrio Antiguo, Centro, Monterrey, 64000, Mexico
Description: They've opened elsewhere, but this location in Barrio Antiguo is the original. Sit indoors in the dining room with tall ceilings and raised beds with plants, or outside on the patio with a nice view of their parrilla and bar. Come hungry or with a group, as the plates are large and you'll want to enjoy a leisurely al fresco meal with a cocktail in hand. While there's plenty to choose from, don't miss the arrachera tacos, with three large flour tortillas with a cheese crust and topped with chopped arrachera and guacamole. Chicharrón mixto served with guacamole and quesadillas is another hit. Carrot cake with salted caramel sauce and a scoop of toasted coconut ice cream and cashews is an enticing dessert.

Name: Jaco
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted,Valet parking
Description: Jaco blends the well-heeled ambiance of Fort Jaco with a vintage interior dripping in contemporary elegance. A stylish beige colour scheme and an almost sensual charm set the scene for the chefs to craft sun-drenched Italian fare from Puglia, rich in light, refreshing flavours and bold originality. An example: juicy tartare of mackerel with fennel, courgettes and fresh bergamot, or fillet of seabass in a crunchy pistachio and focaccia case paired with a cream of squash, sweet chestnuts and dried fruit. We recommend coming early and sipping a cocktail at the bar as you plan a raid on the next-door delicatessens. Jaco is a culinary universe in a class of its own!

Name: Jacobs & Co. Steakhouse
Address: 81 Bay St., 4th Floor, Toronto, M5J 0E7, Canada
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Jacobs & Co., now located in CIBC Square, is a smart, sleek and airy space with a contemporary design, a place where bookmatched veneer-paneled walls blend with banquette seating and a marble-topped cocktail bar grooves to the tunes of a live pianist. Special touches abound; aged white cheddar popovers with roasted garlic and oregano butter arrive shortly after arrival, and they'll send you home with coffee cake muffins. With a range of fish and seafood from the raw bar and an unrivaled selection of steaks, there's plenty to like here. Don't know what to order? Opt for the chefs tasting with a range of striploins from Canada, Australia and Japan. The wine list is an oenophile's dream with strong selections from Burgundy and Italy.

Name: Jacobs Restaurant
Description: Accommodated in Hotel Louis C. Jacob, which boasts a prime location, this restaurant serves modern cuisine with classic touches in an elegant setting. Diners can order à la carte or opt for one of the six-course set menus – conventional or vegetarian. Recommended dishes include hand-cut beef tartare or "Jacob's bouillabaisse". The food is accompanied by a thoughtfully curated wine list and pleasant, attentive service. The seating out on Lindenterrasse is undoubtedly the highlight in summer – the view of the River Elbe is simply stunning! Large, floor-to-ceiling windows mean you can also enjoy the view from indoors.

Name: Jacqueline
Description: This former butchery is named after the grandmother of Evelien Swiers, who is in charge of the kitchen you can see behind the original counter. Good humoured Raf supervises the dining room, which sports a gentrified workshop vibe. Evelien’s delicious, no-frills cuisine revolves around a menu of four or five dishes. Guinea fowl from Maison Garat is cooked in a frying pan and underscored by a knockout jus enriched in miso, while chicory adds a fresh note with a mandarin sabayon. At Jacqueline, the food is rustic, gutsy and wholesome.

Name: Jacques Restaurant
Address: Rue de la Barre 5, Lausanne, 1005, Switzerland
Description: Now located in the historic city, chef Jacques Allisson's establishment sports elegant rooms spread over two floors and a spacious alfresco area. The modern Gallic score is precise and expressive and flanked by seamless, spot-on service. Three 3- to 5-course menus and an à la carte lineup means that there is something for everyone, from wild mullet, leeks and beurre blanc, followed by venison, beetroot and spatzli, to an iced parfait and a crispy praliné to finish. Splendid wine cellar of French and Swiss vintages. Pleasure and technique go hand in hand in this renowned culinary landmark of Lausanne.

Name: Jade Palace
Address: Forum The Shopping Mall, #B1-13, 583 Orchard Road, 238884, Singapore
Description: Both the décor and the menu show strong Hong Kong influences, all the more so as super-fresh seafood and veggies are shipped from the city twice a week. The must-tries (sautéed white eel with chives in black bean sauce and braised lobster with ginger and scallion in a claypot) boast exceptional wok hei and craftsmanship. You can also specify how you want your live seafood cooked – ask the friendly front-of-house staff for advice.

Name: Jade on 36
Address: 36F, Grand Tower, Pudong Shangri-La Hotel, 33 Fucheng Road, Pudong, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Even when this longstanding restaurant gets a makeover, nothing is really able to compete with the stunning views of Huangpu and the river. With an experienced French chef at the helm, the menu ushers in some sophisticated creations; they may be deeply rooted in traditions, but they are also jazzed up by modern touches and subtle Mediterranean influences. Blue lobster can be ordered in three servings and the lunch menu offers good value.

Name: Jadjan
Address: 4/27 Sakdidet Road, Talat Nuea, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: Chef Suthee, a former 5-star hotel chef, uses expertise to produce simple southern Thai fare that’s packed with flavour. The crab meat curry with betel leaves and southern Thai sour curry with fresh local fish and pineapple get our nod of approval.

Name: Jae Nueang
Address: 40 Phalochai Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, Ubon Ratchathani, 34000, Thailand
Description: This enduring local eatery is popular for its generous portions of satisfying Vietnamese noodle soup. Thick rice noodles in a peppery broth with pork ribs and sausage are elevated by adding a soft-boiled egg and fried dough. It's open for breakfast and lunch – aim to arrive early.

Name: Jagawirt zu Aumbach
Description: The climb up to around 600m above sea level is definitely worth it! A modern take on Bavarian tavern cuisine is the name of the game here. This encompasses delicious, beautifully prepared dishes that reflect the region's heritage while also showcasing international influences – for instance, "saddle of venison we hunted ourselves, with juniper jus" or "tonkotsu paitan ramen, seared pork belly, pickled egg, sweetcorn and edamame". Tip: the reasonably priced set menu ("Alpenmenü"), served Thu-Sat, featuring three or four courses including a starter, petit four, water and espresso. The well-stocked German and international wine list encompasses a fine selection, including half-bottles. Service is provided by a dedicated, cordial and attentive team. And you can soak up the wonderful, cosy "tavern" atmosphere and rustic charm in this meticulously renovated farmhouse with an abundance of wood, a charming historical decor and countless hunting trophies on the walls. The outdoor dining area planted with trees is also delightful. It's best to book in advance – Jagawirt is popular!

Name: Jagdhaus Waldfrieden
Description: Choose whether to enjoy your meal in the cosy dining room with its open fireplace, in the airy conservatory or on the lovely terrace shaded by trees… This restaurant is a charming location in which to sample good regional food: the menu includes dishes such as Glückstädter Matjes (PDO preserved herring) or fillet of wild boar, cooked rare in a juniper berry jus. Tip: The lunch set menu is an excellent deal. Should you wish to stay overnight, the pretty guestrooms are very inviting and all individually decorated.

Name: Jagstmühle
Description: With its cosy yet elegant interior and charming terrace, the restaurant blends seamlessly into the romantic setting of this estate on the banks of the Jagst. Light wood panelling, a tiled stove and pretty fabrics all create an inviting sense of warmth and comfort. Cordial and attentive service also contributes to the lovely atmosphere. The cooking follows the seasons and incorporates international influences. Diners can choose from an appealing à la carte menu. Good to know: The restaurant also opens for lunch at weekends. Tip: Before or after your meal, take a stroll through the beautiful grounds. Cosy guestrooms are available for overnight stays.

Name: Jaidee Shrimp
Address: 222/388 Ruam Mit Phatthana Road, Tha Raeng, Bang Khen, Bangkok, 10220, Thailand
Description: This casual eatery, which opened nearly two decades ago, is all about its signature shrimp dishes. Shrimp paired with bold Thai flavours and Southern influences delight fans of the crustacean. Diners can savour classics such as pad thai, alongside rich curries and flavourful soups. The shrimp comes from Jaidee Shrimp’s own farm in Surat Thani province, ensuring exceptional freshness and quality. With no red meat on the menu, the restaurant offers a wide array of fresh seafood, including squid, mantis shrimp and fish.

Name: Jaizkibel
Description: In this restaurant located in a residential district of the city, the undisputed stars of the show are the ingredients (such as bonito tuna to which a special section of the menu is devoted in season) and flavour. The extensive à la carte of traditional Basque cooking, including an array of rice and cod dishes and stews, is complemented by a tasting menu. One standout dish that we particularly enjoyed was the “cogote de merluza” – simply cooked and delicious neck of hake drizzled with garlic and parsley oil.

Name: Jaleo
Description: Chef José Andrés has opened locations of this tapas hangout from Las Vegas to Chicago to Dubai, but it all started here inside the Beltway. Unafraid of color and pattern, the expansive interior is a riot of glass, tile, hardwood and art, and the vibe is never dull or low energy.Sangria, vermouth and sherry make for wise starts before digging in to three tasting menus of Spanish favorites including the classics, Jaleo's Experience or José’s Way. Start with marinated olives and aged Manchego cheese and work your way toward their fresh seafood, like their calamares and su tinta, or squid with rice and a squid ink sauce. Chicken fritters are noteworthy, as are bigger plates like paella Valenciana with rabbit; gazpacho with goat cheese; and grilled pork sausage with white beans.

Name: Jaloux
Description: The concrete building hidden by lush greenery is easy to miss, but Chef Hong’s first-class slow food and artisan hand-made pasta are worth the hunt. Pappardelle with oxtail ragu boasts al dente noodles, balanced between richness and acidity, and generous dollops of fork-tender, melty oxtail ragu. The service can be slow, so just sit back and enjoy the music and wine between your orders. It doesn’t take reservations, so come early to beat the crowd.

Name: Jamantè
Address: Via San Vito 97, Polignano a Mare, 70044, Italy
Description: Located not far from the historic centre and the picturesque Lama Monachile beach, Jamantè is an elegant restaurant with well-spaced-out tables perfect for a stylish night out. As is traditional in Puglia, there’s a wide selection of raw options to start, followed by dishes with a focus on fish and seafood. Elaborate and creative cuisine is to the fore here.

Name: James Farmhouse
Description: Fresh and tasty cuisine is served here, and the menu is strongly influenced by the restaurant's own farm. For example, they raise their own Husum red pied pigs, chickens and German Angus cattle – exceptionally tender rump steaks guaranteed. The decor is a blend of industrial chic and charming retro style. Very friendly service. There is a smaller menu at lunchtime. Alongside the restaurants Das Grace and Minato, this is another dining option at the Hotel Das James, which enjoys a charming location on the harbour.

Name: James St
Address: 19-21 James Street South, Belfast, BT2 7GA, United Kingdom
Description: A cheery team help add to the vibrant buzz at this long-standing modern bistro. It’s a simple place, with exposed brick walls, a high ceiling and warehouse-style windows – and the classic brasserie menus suit it perfectly. The cooking is unfussy and generous, with the grill dishes always a hit; the succulent steaks are cooked on the Josper, served on boards and come with a choice of sauces – go for the tomahawk or Chateaubriand if you fancy sharing. Keep an eye out for their great value set menu.

Name: Jamn
Address: 8 Soi Chan 43 Yaek 41, Bang Khlo, Bang Kho Laem, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: Jamn offers a private dining experience in a family home. The menu is customised to your preferences or features typical Thai dishes. Their family set menu includes an appetiser, dessert, and a main course presented in the Thai samrap style with five dishes for sharing. We recommend starting with the crispy shrimp paste rice with sweet tiny shrimp and sour mango. A minimum charge per table is required.

Name: Jampa
Address: The Community House, Tri Vananda, 46/6 Mu 3, Thep Krasatti, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: Jampa continues its dialogue with nature through ingredients grown and gathered close to home. À la carte is available throughout the day, but the exquisitely prepared Jampa Experience at lunchtime is highly recommended, featuring complex natural flavours that evolve with the seasons. For a unique lakeside experience on Saturdays, Hideaway’s four-course lunch, cooked over a wood fire, both tantalises the taste buds and educates diners on mindful practices. A plant-forward menu is also offered as a thoughtful vegetarian option.

Name: Jan Diekjobst Restaurant
Description: Dating from the 16C, Detmolder Hof not only offers comfortable classical accommodation, but it is also home to Jan Diekjobst's restaurant, which is worth seeking out in its own right. After stints at Victor's FINE DINING by Christian Bau in Perl-Nennig and The Table Kevin Fehling in Hamburg (and others), here the chef cooks up a modern take on classic cuisine. The dishes, prepared with carefully selected ingredients, are available as a three-, five-, or seven-course set menu; the vegetarian version has three or five courses. À la carte dining is also possible. From Thu to Sat, there is also a "Gourmet Lunch". Service is very friendly and attentive. The interior is done out in a tasteful brasserie style, with high ceilings, a striking chandelier and handsome hardwood floors, as well as an open kitchen. In summer, the terrace in front of the building beckons.

Name: JanZen
Description: Housed in a lovely, meticulously refurbished Art Deco building surrounded by polders, JanZen is a place where you can unwind and dine in good company. Hostess Natasja provides attentive service; chef Jeroen's dishes are beautifully presented and packed with exciting flavours. Order à la carte, or opt for the surprise menu to explore his intricate creations. Think sea bass remoulade with vibrant cucumber and radish garnishes, as well as a clear tomato broth – a true delight for both the eye and the palate.

Name: Januarius
Description: Dedicated to San Gennaro, whose relics are kept in the nearby Duomo, this address pays homage not only to the city’s patron saint but also to the most authentic traditions of Campanian gastronomy. The table presents a procession of the specialities that have shaped the culinary history of Naples: from polpo alla Luciana to broken ziti with traditional ragù, through to the classic baccalà accompanied by Neapolitan-style escarole. Alongside these icons sit more contemporary offerings, described as ‘non-traditional special dishes’, born of the house’s own creative spirit. Guests are welcomed at the entrance by a well-stocked shop of excellent produce – salumi and cheeses above all – while to either side open two characterful dining rooms, authentic and full of personality.

Name: January
Address: Southall Farm & Inn, 2200 Osage Loop, Franklin, TN, 37064, USA
Description: The refined rustic style of Southall Farm & Inn, set on a sprawling estate a few miles outside of Franklin, is the perfect setting for this ambitious restaurant. Dramatic vaulted, beamed ceilings, herringbone wood floors and wood furnishings epitomize a modern take on farmhouse chic at January. Andrew Klamar and Nate Leonard spearhead this "seed-to-fork" concept where ingredients, some of which are grown on the property or sourced from nearby farms, are treated with the ultimate respect. At first glance, the menu reads like elevated comfort food but there's so much more going on in plates like a hominy soufflé layered with steamed Gulf shrimp and roasted beech mushrooms or Bear Creek Farm pork coppa steak wood-fire grilled with a sweet black garlic and sorghum glaze.

Name: Jao Nai Fish Ball (Bang Khae Road)
Address: 103/14 Bang Khae Road, Bang Khae, Bangkok, 10160, Thailand
Description: Nestled in a vintage townhouse, this popular street food joint serves up savory fish ball noodle soup. Expect fresh, made-to-order meals that might require a wait due to the frequent bustle. However, the wait pays off with homemade seafood like fish balls, fish dumplings, and fish cakes, all enhancing the soup's umami taste.

Name: Japans restaurant Shiro
Description: Shiro has been famed for serving traditional Japanese cuisine since 1989. In this intimate restaurant you will discover all the delights of kaiseki-ryori cuisine – a traditional interplay of intense flavours and subtle textures. Sushi made with the finest rice and ultra-fresh fish (it's best to order sushi when you make your reservation), beautifully crispy shrimp tempura, a deeply aromatic teriyaki sauce... Accompanied by exciting sake recommendations courtesy of your hostess.

Name: Jaras
Address: InterContinental Phuket Resort, 333, 333/3 Mu 3, Kamala Beach, Kamala, Kathu, Phuket, 83150, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Despite the luxury setting, Jaras retains honest roots. The intimate design draws influence from the Li Thai, Sukhothai era. The restaurant is named after the owner's grandma whose cooking inspired some of the recipes. Today’s chef embraces sustainability, serving a modern showcase of Thai flavours sourced locally, including microgreens grown on-site. For the full experience, request the Taste of Jaras tasting menu with wine pairing. Book at least 24 hours in advance.

Name: Jardin Secret
Description: Back from the rock of Monaco, Benoît Witz has hung his hat in a pretty estate in Provence. In the shade of olive groves and released from gastronomic codes, he crafts 100% authentic dishes in a style that he himself joyfully describes as “grandma’s country cooking”! Garden-fresh beefsteak tomatoes, fish of the day with summer veggies, melt-in-the-mouth chocolate cake. Scrumptious and generous – yummy!

Name: Jardin Tropezina
Address: 325 allée de la Mer, Ramatuelle, 83350, France
Description: Idyllically set on the legendary Pampelonne beach, this Mediterranean garden-terrace, dominated by wood and plants, lives up to its promise. An exquisite setting overlooking the sea, a luxury interior with silverware and Vallauris tableware, a large number of attentive staff, valet parking on arrival and even DJ nights. Devised by Jean-François Piège, the menu focuses on summer and Provençal dishes, as well as Italian specialities: local tromboncino with a tonnato and parmesan sauce; barbecued fish fillet with tangy sabayon; garden verbena ice cream.

Name: Jardin de Jade (Wan Chai)
Address: G3-4, GF, Sun Hung Kai Centre, 30 Harbour Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: The first Hong Kong venture of the renowned Shanghai restaurant group is certainly not lacking in grandeur, with its double-height ceiling and striking chandelier. Shanghainese classics and dim sum are made the traditional way but with updated presentation. The xiao long bao with beautifully pleated paper-thin skin, soupy filling and spot-on seasoning is the jewel in the crown. The seasonal menu covers regional specialities from beyond Shanghai.

Name: Jauregibarria
Description: Located in a 200-year-old farmhouse, restored with great success, where each of its corners enhances the experience and exalts the beautiful natural environment, this spot is an ideal place to go just for the mundane pleasure of taking a walk there, even if you’re not hungry.It has a cosy area for enjoying a snack at the entrance, a tavern-like area that invites you inside without involving a steadfast commitment, then a bistro (here they offer a set lunch menu and one they call Erro) and, finally, the well-kept gastronomic dining room, where you can order à la carte or taste the Ehiza and Beñat Ormaetxea menus (named after the owner-chef, who signs off on his most innovative proposal personally). With a traditional foundation but with very contemporary elaborations and a special devotion to hunting recipes, the cuisine surprises with dishes as delicious as the foie gras terrine, with a hint of pacharán and crunchy almonds, or the wild boar cheek stewed in Rioja Alavesa red wine.

Name: Javier Martín
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: Located in the modern Nuevo Cáceres neighbourhood, this restaurant impressively run by Javier and Esther is defined by them as their “life project”, where you can choose between contemporary-style cooking on an extensive à la carte and several tasting menus (Del Chef, Esencia, Origen and Experiencia Javier Martín) on which seasonal and locally sourced ingredients play a prominent role. Interesting dishes include the carpaccio of Iberian ham, foie gras and “tierra de Ibores”, red partridge stuffed with Pedro Ximénez, truffles and foie gras, and grilled wild red mullet, with salted flakes and olive caviar.

Name: Javier Montero
Description: Located on the outskirts of the town in a contemporary house that also serves as a hotel (with only four cosy rooms). The business is run by an attentive yet professional couple, with Tita taking care of everything in the dining room while Javier tends to the kitchen. You'll find a menu of traditional cuisine, with modern touches, as well as two set menus by reservation, a short one for weekday lunches (except summer) and a tasting menu called As Catedrais (a tribute to the famous natural beach, just over 6 miles away).

Name: Jawi House
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Nestled in a neighbourhood rich in cultural heritage, Jawi House blends in seamlessly. The retro room sets the backdrop for the chef to experiment with recipes that combine Malay, Indian and Middle Eastern influences. On the menu, a good selection of biriyani with different ingredients are found alongside jawi laksa lemak (rice noodles with flaked tuna and mackerel in coconut milk broth) and papadum. Fish curry is always good; ask servers about the catch of the day.

Name: Jay Jew Talew Bin
Address: 117/17 Mu 2, Soi Bangsai 6, Bang Sai, Mueang Chonburi, Chon Buri, 20000, Thailand
Description: This local favourite offers the freshest seafood with bold Thai flavours, cooked home-style. The restaurant is simple, without air conditioning. The menu primarily focuses on seafood options, and the chef excels at deep-fried and stir-fried dishes. The rice dishes and daily catch are listed on the blackboard at the front of the shop. Bookings are only taken for groups of 10 or more. Expect to wait for a table on weekends.

Name: Jay Jia Yentafo
Address: 564 Rama 4 Road, Maha Phruettharam, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: For 30+ years, office workers have been making a beeline to Jay Jia Yentafo for their eponymous pink-noodle soup and legendary homemade shrimp balls. The soup packs a knockout combination of shrimp, fish, fish sticks and fried wontons and explodes in sour and spicy notes.

Name: Jay Ngor Beef Noodle
Address: 679 Nakhon Chaisi Road, Thanon Nakhon Chai Si, Dusit, Bangkok, 10300, Thailand
Description: This 70-year-old eatery in a vintage low-rise block is near the historic sights of Dusit district. Now run by the family's fourth generation, it specialises in braised beef, tongue beef and hotpot – served with or without soup and a selection of noodles. The light brown broth is smooth, aromatic and packed with carefully braised meat. Order the mixed braised beef with offal and no noodles for the full effect. Arrive early for lunch as it gets busy.

Name: Jay Noi Kratoke
Address: 115 Mu 7, Pibool La-lad Road, Nong Phai Lom, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
Description: This three-storey house with simple décor is family run and in its second generation. Jay Noi's house special of hao-dong is a popular local treat using sliced pork and spicy Isan sauce, chilli and roasted rice. The four pad mee Korat is also recommended. Its sticky rice noodles are fresh and go really well with the sweet and sour sauce, fresh bean sprouts and chives. You can order the homemade curry puff for take away, with a variety of optional sides.

Name: Jaylu
Description: A family-run restaurant located midway between Los Remedios and Triana that has made a name for itself thanks to three key criteria: namely, quality, tradition and full respect for the ingredients they use. The elegant, classically styled interior provides the backdrop for an à la carte specialising in fish and seafood of the day, cooked simply without detracting from the quality of the ingredients used (many caught using traditional fishing methods). As a starter, don’t miss the delicate salmorejo with shrimp.

Name: Jayu
Description: Slip away from the hubbub of Rue de Flandre and venture into the almost theatrical venue of Jayu. This snug eatery, reminiscent of a speakeasy bar, features 12 stools around a counter (and one table). Three bells ring as the curtain rises at the start of a performance in twelve acts that lasts two hours. Sang Hoon Degeimbre and his skilled team favour a natural culinary style steeped in nods to Korea with an accent on fruit and veg, spices, umami and fermented flavours. For example, glazed langoustines are dusted in smoked paprika and flanked by a succulent dip of doenjang laced in briny seaweed. Don’t be misled by the understated setting, you are in for a mind-blowing dining experience. Consider us smitten!

Name: Jaz by Ana Roš
Description: In the heart of Ljubljana, within the delightful AS Boutique Hotel, this establishment bearing the name of celebrated multi-starred chef Ana Roš presents itself as a contemporary, young and lively bistrot with a dynamic cuisine full of personality. The dishes move between Mediterranean suggestions and Italian echoes, as in the Adriatic white fish ceviche with fermented cabbage, pomegranate, sweet potato and puffed buckwheat, or the indulgent focacce filled with oyster mayonnaise, sardines, tomato salad and basil. All of this is accompanied by a sound wine selection, also available by the glass, and well-crafted cocktails. Given the limited capacity and the great success of the establishment, booking well in advance is recommended.

Name: Jean Georges
Address: 4F, Bund 3, 3 Zhongshan Dong Yi Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, 200002, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Those who are familiar with Jean-Georges Vongerichten’s New York flagship will recognise some of the menu items here at his Shanghai outpost, such as toasted egg yolk with caviar, and tuna tartare with avocado. The cooking is light and fragrant, with plenty of choice on offer. The comfortable room comes with views and an open kitchen; it’s warmly lit and run by a well-organised and professional team.

Name: Jean des Sables
Address: 121 boulevard de la Dune, Hossegor, 40150, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This beachfront restaurant has a minimalist interior, combining polished concrete, a muted colour scheme, a live lobster tank and breathtaking ocean views. With a focus on seafood, the modern cuisine is presented in a concise, nicely curated menu; there is also a special lobster menu. Exceptionally attentive welcome and service.

Name: Jean-Georges at The Leinster
Address: 7 Mount Street Lower, Dublin City, D02 WK33, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: The famed French chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten, who owns restaurants all over the world, expanded his empire to the Emerald Isle with this top-floor restaurant inside The Leinster hotel. It’s a chic place, with two terrace bars that are ideal for a pre-dinner drink and surveying the Dublin skyline. The extensive menu (slightly reduced at lunchtime) includes Jean-Georges signatures like egg toast with caviar, alongside a range of international influences from paccheri with meatballs to crab spring rolls. High-quality Irish produce is the underlying theme binding it all together.

Name: Jean-Michel Couron
Description: Over more than 30 years, this chef has built up a loyal clientele of happy diners courtesy of his contemporary cuisine featuring nods to the Mediterranean, in dishes such as bouillabaisse jus and carpaccio of large wild prawns. The yakitori sauce on the duck fillet is one of his more exotic marriages. You can choose to dine in either the contemporary space or the former 14C cloister.

Name: Jean-Philippe
Description: Jean-Philippe and Sara-Sofia have crafted a cosy cocoon in this townhouse. Artwork by Isidoor Goddeeris underscores the restaurant’s classy interior and reflects the chef’s love of seafood. The couple’s experience shines through in every detail. Sara-Sofia seamlessly manages the front of house, while presenting her latest cocktails. Jean-Philippe draws on his flawless technical background as he works with outstanding ingredients. Examples include wild seabass, grilled to keep the skin crispy and flanked by different textures of fennel, a baby artichoke and characterful crab bisque. This consummate chef, a master of delicacy, has a way with flavour and gutsy sauces that is second to none.

Name: Jean-Pierre
Address: 9 Bridges Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: A meal at this bistro transports you back to Paris in the Belle Époque. Art Nouveau motifs, scarlet velvet upholstery and flickering candle flame embody the joie de vivre of the last century. The menu is equally classic: expect the likes of beef tartare, duck confit and onion soup gratinée, served in silver platters and country-style bone china. In "Poulet de Simone", local three-yellow chicken is stuffed with button mushrooms and roasted until golden.

Name: Jee
Address: 2F, 8 Lyndhurst Terrace, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: A veteran Cantonese chef has paired up with a local chef well-versed in Western cuisine to reimagine local flavours using modern techniques. Their 8- or 10-course menu embodies a creative take on Cantonese classics that is pleasantly surprising at every turn. Crispy Silkie chicken in Moutai liquor sauce is loaded with deep aromas; soft-shell turtle aspic highlights the meat’s umami and rich collagen. Ask the sommelier about Chinese alcohol pairing.

Name: Jeffrey's
Address: 1204 W. Lynn St., Austin, TX, 78703, USA
Description: Ensconced in the quiet historical Clarksville neighborhood, this smartly appointed space offers a genteel retreat from worldly troubles. Your table might be shy on elbow room, but posh furnishings and gracious service are sure to put you at ease. The menu features skillfully composed plates of contemporary fare boasting enticing seasonal flavors, as in an appetizer of English pea tortellini with morels and sweetbreads, or a crisp-skinned Pekin duck breast "au poivre." Alternatively, you can choose from array of elevated steakhouse offerings paired with deliciously updated sides like a creamed spinach gratin with Fresno chili and parmesan, or steak fries with horseradish aïoli.

Name: Jek Tod
Address: 3597/49 Chalaem Nimit Road, Bang Khlo, Bang Kho Laem, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: Since opening in 2024, Jek Tod has swiftly garnered attention for its generous portions and bold flavours. It serves an array of pork-based noodle dishes, crafted with fresh, carefully prepared ingredients and savoury broths. A standout is the "Signature Bowl", which is generously packed with pork condiments and offal. Customers can choose between a tom yam or clear broth. Adding an onsen egg lends extra richness and brings balance.

Name: Jennerwein
Address: Münchner Straße 127, Gmund am Tegernsee, 83703, Germany
Description: A truly delightful establishment with a charmingly rustic inn atmosphere – it's genuinely cosy here. The menu includes freshly prepared seasonal Bavarian cuisine such as braised shoulder of lamb with root vegetables, or beef tenderloin on a bed of fried mushrooms and potatoes, as well as parmesan risotto with king prawns. More limited options at lunchtime.

Name: Jeny
Description: Situated at 250 meters above sea level in the old part of Tučepi, the Jeny restaurant boasts breathtaking views of the Hvar Channel and the islands of central Dalmatia. The first thing that strikes upon arrival is precisely this spectacular panorama: Jeny overlooks the picturesque coastal village from above, offering unforgettable glimpses of the sea. Active since 1986 and run with passion by the same family, Jeny embodies authentic hospitality and contemporary cuisine. The dishes unite technique and creativity, always maintaining a harmonious balance between flavor and presentation. The culinary offering comprises three tasting paths: a seven-course menu, a five-course menu, and, only in high season (July through mid-August), a three-course menu. During warmer months, a terrace table is a true privilege, ideal for experiencing gastronomy immersed in the beauty of the landscape.

Name: Jeong
Address: 1460 W. Chicago Ave., Chicago, IL, 60647, USA
Description: This sleek operation arrives courtesy of two passionate young chefs, Dave Park and wife Jen Tran. In this kitchen, they aim to impart complex and authentic Korean flavors to a myriad of sophisticated diners. All this transpires in an elegant, intimate and ultra-modern setting—and the result is foodie date-night perfection. Chef Dave Park spins gorgeous, high-quality ingredients into incredibly inventive dishes, combining excellent products with a deft hand. A delicate disk of salmon tartare, for example, is topped with doenjang yuzu gastrique, miniature quenelles of crème fraiche, and crunchy rice crackers that are full of nutty flavor; while a sweet and sour peach sauce is the ideal base for a bowl of kimchi and braised and fried octopus.

Name: Jeong Yuk Jeom
Address: 621 S. Western Ave., Ste. 100, Los Angeles, CA, 90005, USA
Description: There are many Korean barbecue options in this section of town, so what sets this one apart, you might ask? It could be anything from the ample banchan and exceptional meats to the and attentive service. Courtesy of brothers Andrew and Jaeyong Son, this cavernous spot is perennially popular, thanks in part to the comfortable setting and sleek design.With a name that translates to "butcher shop," it's no surprise they proffer only the most premium beef. While the tomahawk steak costs a pretty penny, it will feed an army with leftovers aplenty. Other items—like top quality prime dry-aged prime rib or buttery marinated boneless short rib—arrive on a tray to be grilled tableside. Minimal embellishments, like soy and salt, ensure maximum enjoyment.

Name: Jericho
Address: 45 Barkstone Lane, Plungar, NG13 0JA, United Kingdom
Description: This rustic and rural restaurant in the Vale of Belvoir is located on the farmstead where Chef-Owner Richard grew up, divided across two buildings constructed using reclaimed materials from the farm. The menu takes a surprise tasting format, with an extended series of generous, heartily flavoured courses that often involve cooking over wood. Richard’s cuisine is informed by his surroundings, with game and kitchen-garden vegetables playing a particularly big role. The wine list has a similar ethos, with natural, organic and bio-dynamic options.

Name: Jerome
Description: With its black and white chequered floor tiles and bench seats lining the walls, Jerome is reminiscent of a snug Parisian bistro. Alexe, your hostess, supervises the front of house with seamless, classy elegance. Meticulous attention to detail prevails throughout the establishment, including in chef Van der Stappen’s authentic yet subtle Franco-Belgian repertory. The chef is particularly attentive to the plating. A standout: veal blanquette simmered in a creamy succulent sauce with meatballs, slightly tangy button mushrooms, flat-leaf parsley and house-made potato fritters. Gutsy, wholesome flavours – the epitome of indulgent!

Name: Jervois Steak House
Address: Sofitel Complex, 8 Duke Street, Queenstown, 9300, New Zealand
Description: There are times when only a steakhouse will do, especially a classic one complete with an open fireplace. A favourite since opening its doors in 2006, Jervois Steak House is found within the Sofitel Complex and occupies two floors, with a bar below the warmly lit main dining room. Along with grass- or grain-fed Angus beef from New Zealand, you’ll also find Wagyu cuts from Australia and Japan, all expertly cooked over charcoal and served with a wide selection of sauces and butters. Equal care has gone into the wine list, which offers over 40 wines by the glass.

Name: Jervois Steak House
Address: 70 Jervois Road, Ponsonby, Auckland, 1011, New Zealand
Description: Brick walls, brown leather chairs and chandeliers make for a classic steakhouse vibe. The room spans two floors; the terrace is great for al fresco dining on balmy days. On the menu, premium New Zealand Wagyu and Angus beef take centre stage, alongside a few options from Japan. Complement your favourite cut with the sauce of your choice – the truffle horseradish chipotle Béarnaise works especially well. Service is friendly and professional.

Name: Ješka Fine Bistro
Address: Trg fra Andrije Kačića Miošića 5, Makarska, 21300, Croatia
Description: This small and welcoming tavern, rustic in character yet modern in spirit, is run by the couple Ela Ožić and Ljudevit Blažević. Their cooking is founded on seasonal ingredients and carefully selected produce of notable freshness and quality. Dalmatian tradition is fused with interesting Italian influences, giving rise to dishes of considerable character, prepared to order and always thoughtfully presented. At lunch the menu is more concise, focused on generous portions and satisfying flavours, while in the evening the offering expands to include more refined creations.

Name: Jfree
Description: French cuisine with a healthy dollop of Japanese influence, by a chef well versed in Japanese cuisine. Soup of locally raised chicken uses chicken dashi stock with char-grilled chicken thigh meat, prepared with Japanese techniques and scented with vermouth for a French sensibility. ‘Jfree’ means ‘free’ as in ‘free expression’. Prix fixe offerings centre on the bounty of Miyazaki Prefecture, dovetailing the chef’s love of good ingredients with his love of his homeland.

Name: Jhol
Address: 7/2 Soi Sukhumvit 18, Sukhumvit Road, Khlong Toei, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: The menu maps out India's southern coastline, leaning into its bold, layered flavours. The à la carte and tasting menus eschew the usual butter chicken and naan – instead, you'll find dishes such as ghee-roast crab, coastal-style curries and playful reinterpretations of street food; vegetarian options are available upon request. Vintage refinement meets contemporary elegance in the space, and the Indian and Thai-influenced cocktails are equally inspired.

Name: Ji Chuan
Address: 1F, Atour Hotel, 2A West Dawang Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
Description: The chef champions a novel Sichuan cuisine based heavily on Chongqing cooking. Expect an intense tingly numbness in the mouth from signatures such as mapo tofu with marbled beef or the appetiser of pickled chillies with peach kernels. To quench the burn, round off the meal with bingfen – an iced dessert made with shoofly seed jelly, seasonal fruits, distillers' grains and red beans. The array of alcoholic drinks will also put out the flames.

Name: Ji Zai Ten
Address: 8 Lane 194, Xinhe Street, South District, Taichung, Taiwan
Description: Ji Zai Ten is Taichung’s first vegan ramen restaurant. Its house-made noodles are prepared without eggs yet remain satisfyingly chewy, paired with rich broths and well-developed sauces. The chef transforms seasonal fruits and vegetables into refined, flavour-driven dishes that blend Japanese inspiration with a subtle Taiwanese influence. Go for the set menu featuring vegan patties over rice alongside ramen for a more complete experience.

Name: Ji-Cube
Description: The restaurant reinvents its offerings every month, with dinner courses featuring Japanese ingredients in odd-numbered months and dim sum-focused lunch courses in even-numbered months. The omakase dinner is an elaborate affair, showcasing the chef’s deep experience and refined sensibilities. As dishes are rarely repeated, many regulars return in eager anticipation of what comes next. His extensive knowledge is the result of a steady, dedicated journey, one that guests can savour with every bite.

Name: Jia (Chaoyang)
Address: 1F, Nuo Hotel, 2A Jiangtai Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
Description: Chandeliers add visual appeal to the high-ceilinged room with ink murals and carved wood windows. The menu is predominantly Cantonese, borrowing occasionally from other provinces. The Cantonese kitchen team delivers authentic flavours in signatures such as sautéed grouper fillet with green chilli and wild rice stems. The slow-boiled soup menu on daily rotation is also worth checking out. At lunchtime, try the tofu skin roll with shrimp filling.

Name: Jia Xiang
Description: For over 50 years, the owner has been following her mother’s recipes to craft local favourites. Her mee siam is a definite standout – bee hoon in a spicy, sweet and tangy gravy topped with hard-boiled egg, pork crackling and more.

Name: Jia Yuan Xiao Guan
Address: 63 Sanbao Street, Zhonglou, Changzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: This eatery in a converted historic villa by a canal features a simple retro interior that complements the lush greenery in the courtyard. The menu revolves around no-frills Huaiyang classics, with an emphasis on technique and tradition – chrysanthemum tofu soup with matsutake mushroom embodies finesse and remarkable knife skills. Painstaking recipes such as sweet and sour yellow croaker or deboned and stuffed "calabash" duck are also well executed.

Name: Jian Bo Shui Kueh
Address: Tiong Bahru Market, #02-05, 30 Seng Poh Road, 168898, Singapore
Description: Shui kueh is quintessential local street food: white rice cake with salted diced radish and a secret tung tsai sauce, packed with oomph. The house-made sambal, oozing in dried shrimp flavour, is perfect with the rice cake.

Name: Jiang Nan Yu Ge
Address: 49-53 Shiwukui Alley, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: Tucked away in a historical back street, this place teleports diners to a bygone era. The rustic-style interior is quirky, with bottles of yellow wine, including its own brand, placed on the floor. The kitchen team tailors menus to diners' budgets and the fish-heavy Ningbo fare is rife with bold flavours and umami. Try the steamed crab on pork ribs with distillers grains. With only two tables for two in the main room, it makes sense to book a private room.

Name: Jiang-Nan Chun
Address: Four Seasons Hotel, Level 2, 190 Orchard Boulevard, 248646, Singapore
Description: This exquisite space, reached via a marble staircase, is warm and welcoming, with heavy leather chairs that are especially comfortable. The kitchen team excels in barbecue meats, double-boiled soups and seafood dishes that use the freshest ingredients of the best quality. Try clay pot braised soon hock fillet, which showcases a rich, meaty flavour and natural freshness,all enhanced by a delicious savoury sauce. Set menus are a great way to sample the popular hits all at once.

Name: Jiangnan Wok
Address: 1F, Shangri-La, 329 Zhongyang Road, Gulou, Nanjing, Chinese Mainland
Description: Jiangnan Wok opened its doors in 2014, with chef Hou, an iconic Huaiyang master, helming the kitchen. His home-style dishes cleverly incorporate influences from other regional cuisines – try his version of Buddha jumps over the wall, which melds braised fish head in Huaiyang tradition, and the abalone and sea cucumber cooked with scallion the Shandong way. With deep umami and oily flesh, the sautéed deboned rice paddy eel is another speciality.

Name: Jianna
Address: 600 S. Main St., Greenville, SC, 29601, USA
Description: Chef Michael Kramer's restaurant in downtown Greenville is a popular place and while reservations are always recommended, their full-service bar accommodates walk-ins. From the starters and pastas to the proteins and the wine list, it's Italian through and through. Enjoy items such as skillfully shaped agnolotti with a creamy spinach and ricotta filling or pan-seared red snapper, topped with sauteed cherry tomatoes, onions and garlic in a rich and flavorful tomato sauce. To finish, nothing beats a slice of olive oil cake with strawberry coulis sided by a scoop of creamy coconut sorbet and pine nut shortbread crumble.

Name: Jiao Cai Seafood
Address: Yishun Park Hawker Centre, #01-39, 51 Yishun Avenue 11, 768867, Singapore
Description: Cooked-to-order seafood dishes. Signature sambal stingray is spicy and delicious.

Name: Jie
Address: 73-M, Jalan Setiabakti, Bukit Damansara, Kuala Lumpur, 50490, Malaysia
Description: This local chef of Chaozhou descent, whose career boasts stints in upmarket kitchens, strives to break culinary boundaries at Jie. Her two 10-course tasting menus feature creative Chinese fare that often involves Western techniques and painstaking preparation. Free-range chicken soup with almond milk is slow-cooked for hours to build up layers of flavours; serrano ham adds extra depth. Book at least two days ahead.

Name: Jija
Address: 15F, Kimpton Hotel, 11 Middle Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: ‘Jija’ is the Cantonese equivalent of a gabfest, where people connect and have fun. Chef Vicky Lau has appointed this sea-view room in dark wood, chrome trims and soft lighting. The menu rolls out authentic Guizhou and Yunnan fare, pepped up with modern, creative touches. House-made pickles, cured meats and cheese rub shoulders with fresh produce from both provinces to showcase intense flavours and nuanced textures. Check out their selection of Yunnanese teas.

Name: Jikasei B
Address: 3/4 Soi Sukhumvit 43, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Helmed by a Portuguese chef who injects Japanese cuisine with his unique flair, this restaurant follows an Edomae-style meal progression. Seasonal catch flown from Tokyo and Kanazawa is paired with sushi rice seasoned with three vinegars for perfect balance. Highlights include luscious ankimo tucked into crispy rice-flour wafers. The modest room with an eight-seat counter feels intimate, and the English-speaking chef's engaging service adds to the experience.

Name: Jiki Miyazawa
Description: The original establishment of the Miyazawa chain of kappo restaurants. Jiki Miyazawa is best known for its famous baked sesame tofu, accompanied by rice served at its freshest, right after cooking. Other menu items are conceived by the chef, drawing on his experience at the ambassador’s residence in Poland. Each dish is layered with numerous ingredients, brightened by the freshness of citrus and tartness of other fruits. In true gourmet fashion, soba dishes are crafted using seasonal ingredients.

Name: Jikon Hiratate
Description: ‘Jikon’ in the restaurant’s name means ‘live with all your heart in this moment’. Dutifully listing the carefully selected ingredients in the menu, the house focuses with single-minded devotion on preparation. The proprietor starts by presenting a selection of seasonal recommendations. After sampling the flavours of the season, guests order items they fancy. The restaurant’s style is to stay grounded in the basics while demonstrating creativity through combinations of ingredients, as exampled by fruits dressed with white sesame seeds, tofu and miso. The menu forms a bond between chef and guest.

Name: Jimbocho Gokita
Description: This chef is breathing fresh life into the yakitori scene. His originality lies in adapting the poultry dishes he specialised in during his apprenticeship into yakitori. In place of traditional dipping sauces, he pairs his chicken dishes with French sauces, with red wine, Madeira or Américaine sauces chosen to suit each type of skewer. Familiar yakitori, reimagined with a modern, innovative touch.

Name: Jin
Description: This restaurant that has been around for 20 years is certainly an institution. The many regulars appreciate the upscale minimalist-style interior inspired by the Far East, and the flavoursome pan-Asian cuisine, in which a distinct Chinese edge, as well as Japanese and European influences, can be detected. Diners can choose between the "Jins Degustation" set menu and an appealing à la carte selection. We particularly recommend the spring rolls, the bluefin tuna tartare and the handmade dim sum. The wine list is also excellent – connoisseurs will find something to their liking here.

Name: Jin Cai Xuan
Address: 4F, Sanxing Tower, 31 Jinghui Street, Chaoyang, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
Description: The modern room sports muted neutral tones and wood with occasional splashes of red and motifs depicting the Great Wall of China. There are also private rooms for parties of varying sizes. The menu errs towards Cantonese with occasional Jiangzhe accents. Cantonese barbecue and slow-boiled soups are permanent, ever popular dishes. The sautéed abalone slices with aged, dried radish unveil interesting textures, smoky wok hei and briny umami.

Name: Jin Dweji Gomtang
Address: 2F, 4 Gwanganhaebyeon-ro 284 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48283, South Korea
Description: Since opening in 2024, this spot has quickly become a favourite among Busan’s younger crowd. Its charming space centres on a U-shaped counter, creating an atmosphere that feels both lively and intimate. The signature dweji gomtang is made with Berkshire K black pork from the Jirisan region, prized for producing a clean, delicate broth. Another highlight is the suyuk nengchae, featuring precisely sliced pork belly with tender lean meat and fat that melts in the mouth, leaving a satisfying finish.

Name: Jin Hua
Address: 51 Old Airport Road Food Centre, #01-120, 51 Old Airport Road, 390051, Singapore
Description: Come here for flavourful made-to-order grouper broth with milk added for extra creaminess. Try the soup on its own or with bee hoon, sliced fish, fried fish meat and fried fish head. The spicy bean sauce and deep-fried shallot work magic with the broth.

Name: Jin Jing Ge
Address: 1F, Four Seasons Hotel, 88 Siji Road, Suzhou Industrial Park, Suzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The elegant room has an airy feel thanks to picture windows that overlook a water feature. The veteran Shanghainese chef, who boasts a stint in an iconic Hangzhou restaurant, imbues Jiangsu classics with novel twists to keep the menu fresh and exciting. Inspired by the Qing Dynasty gastronomic bible, Recipes from the Garden of Contentment, he reinterprets heritage dishes in line with the seasons. The handcrafted dim sum lunch is another highlight.

Name: Jin Ting Wan
Address: Marina Bay Sands Hotel, Tower 1, Level 55, 10 Bayfront Avenue, 018956, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Perched atop the iconic Marina Bay Sands Hotel, the room affords gorgeous city and harbour views. Gold trim nicely contrasts with the muted dark blue walls in the Song Dynasty-inspired interior. Chef Albert Li is famous for his refined Cantonese fare, such as roasted pipa duck with aged tangerine peel – the bird is deboned, minced and stuffed back into its own skin before being roasted to perfection. The predominantly Chinese wine list includes some rare gems.

Name: Jinmi Pyeongyang Naengmyeon
Description: According to owner and chef Yim Se-kwon, long time experience in the kitchens of one of the most iconic Pyeongyang cold buckwheat noodle restaurants is the secret to the success of this place. The menu here is what you would expect to see in a typical cold buckwheat noodle restaurant. Other than the noodles, it offers staples such as boiled pork and beef slices, bulgogi, dumplings and Pyeongyang-style beef hot pot.

Name: Jinmi Sikdang
Description: This humble yet busy restaurant has been serving raw soy-marinated crabs and nothing else for the past decade. Only the freshest local blue swimmer crabs, sourced from the west coast, are prepared daily with the kitchen’s special recipe soy sauce marinade. Keep in mind that just enough crab for consumption is prepared each day, so if you drop by at a late hour, they may be completely sold out. A prior reservation is highly recommended.

Name: Jiribilla
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Here, next to the Sant Antoni market, they say that the “Jiribilla”, a Pacific wind that is common in Mexico, is blowing strongly in Barcelona! After almost two decades in Mexico, Catalan chef Gerard Bellver has returned to his native region to showcase his cooking, which shows evident Mexican influences but with a nod to the cooking of his homeland. His various highly seasoned mole sauces, corn tortitas, and aguachiles, among other dishes, are often accompanied by a Mezcal-based cocktail. Dishes that stood out for us included the red prawn aguachile, with a chilli and jalapeño sauce, and the intensely flavoured crab “tetela”.

Name: Jit Seng Hong Kong Roasted Duck Rice
Description: The chef-owner started his own business after years as a chef in a larger restaurant. Open for three hours a day, the shop is famous for his roasted duck with deep-red skin and juicy meat, for which customers are prepared to queue. The roasted pork belly and char siew are tasty extras.

Name: Jium
Description: Behind a rather nondescript façade lies an authentic Korean canteen which boasts a lovely vintage vibe and is popular with a clientele from the land of the Morning Calm. It is the brainchild of photographer and guesthouse owner, Kim Hong-Seung, and his wife Sun-Hee, a former fashion designer. As well as bibimbap classics, the menu is packed with authentic delicacies (soft shell crabs, oyster fritters) and unusual recipes (seafood pancakes, kimchi stew, pork shoulder and tofu, etc). You can season these culinary delights with homemade soy sauce (or not) before finishing with a dessert, also homemade, illustrated by vanilla-flavoured rice pudding with red beans and caramelised pecan nuts.

Name: Jiva
Address: Jiva Hill Resort, route d'Harée, Crozet, 01170, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In Sanskrit, jiva means life, giving the visitor a foretaste of what to expect in this luxurious, understated resort. The restaurant specialises in exquisitely balanced French cuisine, using the best, fresh seasonal produce. Diners will enjoy a breathtaking view over Mont Blanc, whenever the weather permits, from the panoramic terrace.

Name: Jiyakiunagi Todoroki Hirasawa
Description: Located right by the Todoroki Station level crossing, diners can savour exquisite unagi in a Meiji-era house. Unagi is prepared in the jiyaki style. This un-steamed, direct-grilling method is favoured in western Japan to showcase the aroma of the charcoal fire. The unaju selections are named for Fukurokuju, one of the Seven Lucky Gods. The ‘Kotobuki’ selection (representing the “ju” in Fukurokuju and symbolising health and longevity) features a half-and-half pairing of unseasoned shirayaki and richly glazed kabayaki, side by side like a married couple. The ‘Fuku’ and ‘Roku’ options are equally auspicious.

Name: JoJo
Address: 160 E. 64th St., New York, NY, 10065, USA
Description: Chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten runs a restaurant empire today that spans the globe, but his journey started here back in 1991. A few years ago, the space underwent a refresh, and now this cozy, two-story townhouse is a contemporary respite for the area’s moneyed residents. The menu isn’t particularly groundbreaking—think roast chicken, seared salmon, and Maine lobster—but you’ll certainly find seasonality, quality product, and astute cooking in good supply. Recent highlights include warm asparagus with vegetable vinaigrette as well as rack of lamb with braised artichokes and peas. For dessert, try something new like the sour cherry pie or indulge in a bit of nostalgia with the likes of molten chocolate cake with vanilla ice cream.

Name: Joan Marc
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: In this bright restaurant, with its natural and contemporary design in which wood plays a central role, discover seasonal cuisine that always showcases the island’s flavours. It offers a huge array of tapas (vegetarian, classic, meat, fish and seafood, free-range eggs, tapas for dipping etc), along with dishes with a traditional Mallorcan influence and two tasting menus.

Name: Joca
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Wheelchair access
Description: A contemporary, on-trend atmosphere in one of the liveliest pedestrian areas, just steps from the elegant Riviera di Chiaia. Here, chef Gianluca D’Agostino, with solid experience both in the city and beyond, presents gourmet cuisine that plays on creativity and Campanian influences. Alongside the main menu, a dedicated tapas section: not Spanish-inspired, but rather reinterpretations of Italian and local classics in a smaller format. Among the most compelling offerings on the gastronomic journey are the sweetbreads with puntarelle, lupin bean mayonnaise, and mullet bottarga, while the main courses alternate between refined meat and fish preparations. The wine list is in the capable hands of Alfredo, who offers thoughtful recommendations and also curates the soundtrack, making for a complete and harmonious experience.

Name: Joe Beef
Address: 2491 rue Notre-Dame Ouest, Montréal, H3J 1N6, Canada
Description: Even just walking past this place you get a taste of the cheerful atmosphere and bonhomie that reign inside. Steaks and seafood, as well as incontrovertible French bistro classics (such as rabbit à la royale and calf sweetbreads) take pole position here. And be sure to add that extra portion of fries on the side. This indulgent cuisine is best enjoyed with your sleeves rolled up—little wonder they provide you with a napkin the size of a sheet. Proceedings are orchestrated with discreet efficiency, warmth, and good humor.

Name: Joe's Bakery & Coffee Shop
Description: This East Austin standby, run by the Avila family since 1962, is no frills but all heart. Slide into one of their built-in booths to enjoy Tex-Mex offerings available by the plate or platter. Not an early riser? Breakfast is offered all day here, and their twice-fried bacon is legendary for its crisp texture, so a bacon and egg taco is always a good idea. Another morning standout is the Migas tacos. Served on their house-made flour tortilla and filled with scrambled eggs mixed with crispy corn tortillas, peppers, and cheese, it's a delicious treat. Craving something sweet? The bakery case is brimming with conchas and other delights, but if you're not in a breakfast mood, the barbacoa is spot on. Add a tortilla and some pico and you're all set.

Name: Joe's Stone Crab
Address: 11 Washington Ave., Miami Beach, FL, 33139, USA
Description: When Joe Weiss opened his lunch counter in 1913, Miami Beach didn’t even have paved roads, and customers had to take the ferry to cross over. One century later, as high-rises and shopping districts blossom all around, this restaurant has endured as one of the city’s prime attractions. Celebrities, politicians and locals alike make a beeline to this crustacean hot spot, now open year-round. And if the dedicated parking lot across the street is any clue, waits for a table here can get lengthy. Boiled, chilled and served with a signature mustard sauce, stone crab claws are the signature dish (they're also sustainable, as crabs can regenerate their claws in around two years). End the meal with a refreshing, slightly creamy, slice of key lime pie.

Name: Joels
Description: It is impossible not to succumb to the magic of Joels. From the warm welcome to the little thank‑you card handed to you as you leave, every detail has clearly been endlessly puzzled and pondered over. This well‑oiled machine nonetheless overflows with genuine Campine hospitality. Choose from the pretty garden terrace or the bright interior adorned with lovely artwork. Johan Ariën’s polished repertory is rooted in heartwarming Franco‑Belgian traditions and further enhanced by deftly crafted, intense sauces. He elevates crispy spiced tender chicken breast with homemade fritters, asparagus and a knockout sauce of poultry stock, vin jaune and wafer-thin morels. Get ready for a delicious adventure.

Name: Johann Grill
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Overlooking Berchtesgaden, surrounded by stunning natural beauty and with a magnificent mountain backdrop, the location is to die for! At the restaurant of the luxurious Kempinski Hotel Berchtesgaden, you can enjoy delicious seasonal cuisine made with fresh, local ingredients. For dessert, we highly recommend the Eckerbichl-Haustorte. The sleek, modern interior design is a draw in itself. Incidentally, the restaurant is named after the first person to climb the east face of the Watzmann and Germany's first official mountain guide. Weather permitting, be sure to make the most of the spacious terrace. Tip: A short path around the hotel affords panoramic views of the mountains – especially magical at sunset.

Name: Johanniter-Kreuz
Description: This former farmhouse, which is over 350 years old, has been turned into the lovely Johanniter-Kreuz Romantik Hotel, complete with a tasteful, rustic-style restaurant in what was once the stable. Old beams and a central fireplace lend the space a cosy atmosphere. The food is rooted in classical culinary tradition, with regional influences and close ties to the seasons. Vegetarians are also catered for, and there is a decent wine selection.

Name: Johanns Living
Address: Hugo von Montfortgasse 2, Bruck an der Mur, 8600, Austria
Description: This restaurant is housed in a bijou boutique hotel of the same name. With only two guestrooms, the establishment is tucked away in a quiet side street in the city centre, creating an intriguing architectural juxtaposition with the adjacent district court. The compact restaurant with just four tables has a tastefully modern decor and a cosy atmosphere. In the adjoining open kitchen, Mike Johann prepares seasonal dishes. Diners can create a personalised tasting menu of three to six courses from a concise à la carte selection that changes daily. Things begin with "Johanns Abendmahl" ("Johanns Supper"), an assortment of small bites. Both the chef-patron and his wife provide friendly service with a pleasing personal touch – the former also presents his dishes himself and recommends wine pairings from a list of more than 900 labels.

Name: John Restaurant
Address: Via Santa Maria la Nova 35, Afragola, 80021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Follow the signs to Casamadre (the specialist food shop next door) to get to this gourmet restaurant, where the chef surprises guests with modern cuisine that is full of character. The dishes served here are inspired by classic recipes which are reinterpreted with creativity and a respect for local traditions, resulting in highly distinctive flavours. Each course reflects the region’s history, with a common thread running through the menu to create an authentic culinary experience. To accompany your meal, the wines are presented on a practical tablet which makes it easy to explore the different labels available. Among the different options, the excellent Costa D'Amalfi “Selva delle Monache” 2022 is particularly striking thanks to its fresh, earthy aromas.

Name: John's Food and Wine
Address: 2114 N. Halsted St., Chicago, IL, 60614, USA
Description: Meet your new neighborhood hangout. With exposed white brick, a comfy banquette stretching the length of the room, and a friendly bar with an engaging wine program, this restaurant isn’t going to struggle to make friends. One caveat: There are no servers so diners have to order at the counter before being escorted to a table. It’s not a tall ask because everything offered tends to be a hit, and you quickly get the sense that they just want to cook good food. Think country ham with fried sunchokes, lobster salad with leek aioli, and dry-aged steaks with potato pave. An order of beef fat fries for the table? Absolutely – this essential starter (or side dish) is impressive enough to trigger a return visit. Another glass of wine? Sure, why not?

Name: Johnson
Description: A few steps from one of the most beautiful beaches in the area, Johnson interprets a classic seafood cuisine founded on simplicity and the excellence of its raw materials. The undisputed protagonist is the catch of the day, sourced above all from the fishermen of Mošćenička Draga, which inspires an offering described exclusively verbally, respecting freshness and daily availability. The very best of local seafood is thus enhanced: the celebrated Kvarner langoustines – delicious both raw and grilled – molluscs and the freshest fish, often accompanied by vegetables grown by the chef himself. The preparations remain faithful to tradition, with simple, precise and delicate cooking techniques conceived to bring out the natural flavour of the ingredients. In the summertime, the panoramic, bright and relaxing terrace is not to be missed. For over thirty years, a true benchmark.

Name: Jok's Kitchen
Address: 23 Soi Charoen Krung 21, Phlapphla Chai Road, Pom Prap, Pom Prap Sattru Phai, Bangkok, 10100, Thailand
Description: This humble shop may get warm without air conditioning, but that doesn't stop locals from flocking here for the exceptional shrimp dumplings and soup. Add a touch of indulgence to your meal with tender crab meat and plump abalone. The shrimp wonton, deep-fried snow fish with soy sauce, and stir-fried kale with salted halibut are also recommended. For access to the complete set menu, booking is essential. A local favourite, where flavour trumps frills.

Name: Joki
Description: In the heart of historic Bordeaux, this cosy, casual eatery dishes up deftly crafted bistronomic cuisine that stars hand-picked produce: poached oysters, mousse of ham and samphire pickles; pigeon marinated in oriental spices and a combo of turnips and harissa jus. Don’t miss the house signature: food-cocktail pairings concocted by Jodie.

Name: Jolene
Address: 21 Newington Green, Islington, London, N16 9PU, United Kingdom
Description: Jolene is the sort of place that we'd all love to have at the end of our street. It's a bakery first and foremost, selling wonderful pastries, biscuits and cakes – as well as delicious bread from flour they mill themselves. There's also a daily written blackboard menu of confidently executed sharing plates, with their house-made pasta being something of a feature. The vibe is relaxed and the friendly service team will ensure you're well looked after. Consider a glass from the concise wine list too, which emphasises small producers and natural options.

Name: Jolie
Address: 620 N. Person St., Raleigh, NC, 27604, USA
Description: Sitting right next door to one of his other restaurants, Crawford and Son, Chef Scott Crawford has created his version of a classic French bistro in Historic Oakwood at Jolie. Inspired by family trips to Paris and named after his daughter, the menu blends French classics with more modern interpretations, marrying punchy flavors with clear respect for traditional techniques. Steak tartare and French onion soup are two signatures not to be skipped, as is the delicious rum-soaked baba. The wine list is strictly French; stop by and get a glass of bubbles from their champagne window out front or sip a glass on the semi-covered, first-floor roof terrace.

Name: Jondal
Description: Located in the cove of the same name and popular with a “VIP” clientele, Jondal occupies a bucolic Ibiza-style building where Rafa Zafra, a chef with a passion for the sea, is at the helm. Outstanding fish and seafood are, understandably, the stars of the show here, including an impressive selection of dishes built around caviar and created using a variety of different techniques (grilled, raw, fried, cured, salted etc). Many customers come here for the views, so we recommend booking as far in advance as possible – in summer it is not easy securing a table here.

Name: Jongjit Kitchen
Address: 9/1 Mu 4, Wichit Songkhram Road, Kathu, Phuket, 83120, Thailand
Description: Southern recipes, affordable prices and down-to-earth hospitality – this is why locals pack out this family-run business at lunch and dinner. Their family recipes pack great intensity. The Phuketian stir-fried pork rump with salt is lovely, with tender meat and lip-smacking pork skin.

Name: Joo052
Description: Joo052 is a portmanteau of 'Joo' (alcohol) and '052', the area code of the region the chefs live in. It is a Korean gastropub brimming with culinary ideas as playful as the restaurant’s name. Employing diverse fermented pastes and fermentation techniques, the basis of Korean cuisine, the chef duo offers unique dishes prepared with exceptional care and attention to detail to bring out unforgettable flavours. Additionally, the varied menu selections tend to go well together, making it easy to enjoy multiple items at once. These charms make Joo052 a perfect place to experience the exquisite harmony between Korean food and Korean alcohol.

Name: Josef Stube
Address: Località Certosa 29, Madonna di Senales, 39020, Italy
Description: Run with passion by the two owners who continue the long family tradition in this hotel-restaurant is one of the most picturesque sights in the Val Senales. Its beautifully kept dining room is romantic and typical of the region, providing a backdrop for just a few dishes which are prepared by the chef with a focus on local ingredients. A hint of Mediterranean influence adds to the appeal.

Name: Joseph Naus Stub'n
Description: This restaurant, named after the first climber to reach the summit of the Zugspitze, is not just an attractive place where service comes courtesy of very friendly staff; the food here is also delicious. At lunchtime, there is a reasonably priced two-course set menu and a small à la carte menu. In the evening, peruse the large menu, from which you can order either à la carte or a set menu. Hotel Zugspitze also has well-kept guestrooms, should you wish to stay overnight.

Name: Josephine's
Description: It's located in Houston's Midtown, but this restaurant run by Chef Lucas is all about the Gulf Coast. Booths and tables welcome everyone from families and couples on dates to solo diners at this laidback spot. The menu leans into Southern comfort with a seafood-forward approach—think raw oysters, po’boys, shrimp and grits, plus some fun nods like fried chicken on a stick and a Mississippi hot catfish sandwich. Biscuits served with seasonal jam and whipped butter are a must. Daily catch rotates but a recent redfish served over a bed of creamy corn hit the spot, as does the blue crab rice bowl with Carolina Gold rice and crab fat aioli.

Name: Josette
Description: It’s glamour galore at this grand French restaurant; come with friends for dinner to really experience it at its best, with its live music and DJ – and there’s even a button on each table to summon the champagne. No expense has been spared in the decoration and the menu is an appealing roll-call of classic French dishes, with everything from escargots to tournedos Rossini.

Name: Josto
Description: One of Cagliari’s most interesting restaurants, Josta boasts two small dining rooms with an original decor that combines modern design with a few traditional features – the room by the entrance has the open-view kitchen to the rear. The menu focuses on Sardinian specialities reinterpreted with a contemporary twist, such as the delicious ham (from a typical Sardinian breed of pig), fregula pasta, mullet, and traditional Saba dessert.

Name: Josè - Tenuta Villa Guerra
Address: Via Nazionale 414, Torre del Greco, 80059, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: 2025 has seen a change at the helm in the kitchen at this restaurant, in line with the new approach introduced by its enthusiastic owners. The full focus now is on the flavours of Campania, served in lighter versions and reinterpretations of traditional recipes. This is the case with the legendary Santa Rosa dessert, which has been transformed into a millefeuille made with the same ingredients as the original dish, namely crispy puff pastry, custard and sour cherries in syrup. Situated in one of the extraordinary villas on Herculaneum’s “Golden Mile”, the restaurant boasts an elegant dining room within this 18C building, as well as a room overlooking the villa gardens where pizzas are served from mid spring to late summer. Wine-enthusiasts will be pleased to hear that the wine cellar continues to offer an extensive selection of superb labels.

Name: José
Address: 104 Bermondsey Street, Southwark, London, SE1 3UB, United Kingdom
Description: Coming with all the rustic, no-frills charm you'd expect of a tapas bar, José was the original London operation from eponymous chef José Pizarro, who has since spread his brand of classic Spanish cooking all over London. His flagship spot features counter seating at the open kitchen alongside high-topped tables, all of which come with a bustling atmosphere thanks to the fact the place is perennially busy. The menu features plenty of Spanish favourites; the Acorn-fed Jamón Ibérico is a must, as is the chocolate pot for dessert. No bookings are taken, so get here early.

Name: José El Carnicero
Description: If you're looking for a steakhouse in the Palermo area, just a few steps from the Carlos Thays Botanical Garden, this is a great option.
