The restaurant, which catches the eye thanks to its display window featuring cuts of meat being slow roasted in front of your eyes, features a long bar with stools facing the coals (fueled by firewood, to add a subtle smoky flavour) and a dining area that seats about 30 guests. Between these two areas is a dry-ageing room, where you can see large cuts of beef being dry-aged. The à la carte, though not very extensive, features interesting appetisers, such as beef tongue with vinaigrette or the delicious chicken pâté with pickled turnips and a Port wine reduction, as well as some incredibly flavourful grilled main courses (900 g bone-in ribeye, 900 g Milanese cutlet, grilled ribs, etc.), prepared in the traditional rural style but with an innovative twist. For dessert, don't miss the flan—it's incredibly creamy!

Name: José María
Description: The sense of space and attractive Castilian-style decor in this “asador”-style restaurant come as a pleasant surprise in what is one of the city’s classic dining institutions. Without a shadow of a doubt, the signature dish here is the traditionally cooked roast suckling pig reared on the family farm (Agrocorte Gourmet). The extensive, traditionally inspired à la carte, is also enhanced by seasonal dishes (pumpkin, leeks, and game such as wild boar and venison) and complemented by the Nuestra Cocina Segoviana tasting menu, with the icing on the cake provided by the superbly innovative Pago de Carraovejas wines from the Ribera del Duero region.

Name: José by Pizarro
Address: Conrad Etihad Towers Hotel, West Corniche, Corniche Road, Abu Dhabi
Description: A small space on the ground floor of the Conrad Etihad Towers Hotel is the chosen venue for José Pizarro's first venture outside London but, instead of adopting a similarly rustic look for his tapas bar, the designers have used plenty of marble to create a more elegant environment. The small sharing plates include great anchovies, satisfying meatballs in a spicy tomato sauce and the unmissable chocolate pot.

Name: Joy Vegetarian Restaurant
Address: 117 Huqian Street, Xizhi District, New Taipei, 221022, Taiwan
Description: Perched on the shore of Jinlong Lake, the room is furnished in a modern Chinese style with round perforated windows and dark wood furniture. The chef, whose career spans over 20 years, excels in vegetarian dishes that cross geographical boundaries, showing Chinese, Japanese, Southeast Asian, Indian and Western influences. Try sweet potato leaves dressed in a silky, nutty sesame peanut sauce and soothing Longan floral tea.

Name: Joyce
Address: V Spaa Hotell, Riia 2, Tartu, 51004, Estonia
Description: A shopping centre might not be the first spot that comes to mind for a night out, but Joyce – part of the V Spa hotel that adjoins the Kvartal complex – is certainly worth a visit. A large, split-level brasserie with bold modern décor, it comes with a buzzy vibe that grows throughout the day and peaks late at night. Start with a drink in the cocktail bar, then move on to an appealing selection of creative local and Baltic dishes that are not only pleasing to the eye, but pack a punch with their flavours too. The name doesn't refer to a person but to the fact that there’s ‘Joy’ and ‘Choice’ to be found here.

Name: Jozy
Description: Behind a discreet green frontage, this restaurant bears the signature of a couple with international experience: Noé Viviès, from Brittany, in the kitchen; Lucy Rosedale, an English wine specialist, front of house. The short menu, updated weekly, takes a straightforward approach: flavour, jus and seasoning take precedence over fancy plating. Ideas picked up during their travels make their presence subtly felt: scallop tartare with XO sauce and watercress cream; barbecued duck with smoked potato purée and reduced jus; or a cardamom cream puff topped with hot chocolate – formidable in its effectiveness. Booking is strongly recommended.

Name: Juan Carlos Ferrando
Address: María Teresa Gil de Gárate 7, Logrono, 26002, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: A contemporary, family-run restaurant offering what they define here as “contemporary Rioja cooking”. The cuisine is showcased on an impressive à la carte and two set menus (Mercado and Cruce de Caminos) based around traditional recipes from the region which have given a modern twist and an added international touch, and make the most of the very best local products. We particularly enjoyed the cod cheeks with a pilpil sauce, a dish that they also make with hake.

Name: Judith
Address: 36 Ball Park Rd., Sewanee, TN, 37375, USA
Description: It's a woman's world at Chef/owner Julia Sullivan's Judith, named for the first woman to matriculate at Sewanee: The University of the South. It's just off the main road that runs through this sleepy college town and is set in a large, bright warehouse that was once the Steam Laundry for the university. Inside, find a stylish blend with contemporary furniture and touches adding warmth to the industrial space. Chef Sullivan's cooking is talented, but the menu doesn't take itself too seriously, delivering crowd-pleasing dishes like chicken Milanese that isn't a strict interpretation but is just as delicious. A piping hot bowl of strawberry and rhubarb cobbler with a crust that's a cross between a cake and a biscuit is exactly how you'll want to end your meal.

Name: Jui Cuisine
Address: 117 Sinle Street, Yancheng District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
Description: Tucked behind a sake shop, this tiny gem is clad in wood and softly lit. Having honed his skills in Western restaurants, the chef crafts novel cuisine that defies easy categorisation. From Taiwanese home-style favourites to exotic delights from every corner of the world, his food pairings never fail to surprise. The single tasting menu may include creamy tofu clam soup with pickled chilli purée and miso, which imparts smoky, spicy accents.

Name: Juju
Description: Juju is from the same folks behind Susuru, and it shares the same quirky dining room with an izakaya menu, but here they take it to another level with a six-seat kappo bar that features something similar to kaiseki yet original. Seasonality reigns and diners choose from a wide menu of snacks and soup before selecting from the fried, grilled and dry-aged sashimi courses. Slices could include Japanese rock fish with citrus zest and skin-on goldeneye snapper, both aged a few days. Two-week-aged king salmon and four-week-aged otoro finished with Kaluga caviar are loaded with depth and prove that this spot is putting a different spin on sashimi. Steamed chawanmushi made with spiny lobster and mushroom is hit with a supremely creative lobster head dashi that packs on the flavor.

Name: Julia
Description: When we see a restaurant with a long waitlist, there’s a good reason for it! This modern, bistro-style eatery run by Julio Martín Baez, a chef who hails from the town of Chacabuco on the outskirts of Buenos Aires, and ably supported by chef Sol Peretti, describes his cuisine at his restaurant in the district of Villa Crespo as “indie” to give himself completely free rein to expand the concept of “less is more”. He has been highly successful in this, building a culinary model with lots of personality and one which is reliant on a team effort. Although the à la carte is not extensive, it is well supported by a tasting menu, featuring dishes such as mussels in a saffron escabeche; cordyceps ramen, aubergine broth and onigiri; milk ice-cream with a chocolate cream etc. The end result is one that is fresh and contemporary, toying with strong flavours and incorporating acidic and spicy nuances, while at the same time elegantly showcasing micro-seasonality. Vegetables are ever present here, as the chef loves to use herbs, seeds and tender shoots in his cooking.

Name: Julia Fish & Oysterbar
Description: A fishmonger (Mare Nostrum) at the head of a fish bistro, complete with a maritime interior, right down to the fish scales? It sounds so authentic that it just has to be true… Fish and oysters from the “sea to the fork” and the best shrimp fritters of the Belgian coast into the bargain. Julia’s simple, generous cooking is heaven for foodies.

Name: Julie's
Address: 135 Portland Road, Holland Park, London, W11 4LW, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Judging by the amount of diners flooding through its doors, the residents of Notting Hill are glad to have this bright bistro de-luxe among their roster of neighbourhood haunts. Inside, it’s an eye-catching place with rich, warming colours and booths that are perfect for date night. The menu offers an appealing range of dishes, from the light (chopped salad of the day) to the luxurious (lobster soufflé). The extensive wine list and cocktails from the trolley will ensure you’re well-refreshed, while the service team are friendly and engaging.

Name: Julien by Daniel Boulud
Address: Ground Floor, Four Seasons Hotel Riyadh, Kingdom Centre, Olaya Street, Al Olaya, Riyadh, 11321, Saudi Arabia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,No alcohol served,Valet parking
Description: Hidden inside Café Boulud, set in the Four Seasons Hotel Riyadh within the landmark Kingdom Tower, is this 12-seater counter dining restaurant. Taking the name of both acclaimed chef Daniel Boulud’s son and father, this elegant space offers a 10-course tasting menu. Modern French dishes take inspiration from iconic plates blended with local influence, which are refined and prepared in front of you. Both flavour and texture are mastered in enjoyable combinations and paired with a selection of non-alcoholic wines and mocktails. The friendly team are also on hand to keep you entertained without intruding too much. It’s a three-hour experience, but time passes quickly.

Name: Julienne
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This upmarket establishment dripping in marble, which is bright and airy by day and cosy by night, extends a warm welcome typical of the Kempen region, before presenting an enticing menu and list of daily specials. Seasoned chef, Tim Moeskops, knows his classics and skilfully turns out dishes ranging from crispy, generously filled shrimp fritters and fresh, juicy sole to flavoursome eel in sorrel or a Poire belle Hélène, straight from his own pear orchard. Julienne celebrates heroic classics and does so with flair and know-how.

Name: Juliet
Address: 49 London Road, Stroud, GL5 2AD, United Kingdom
Description: Imagine dropping a French bistro into the Cotswolds and you’ve got something a lot like Juliet. Combining a buzzy vibe with an enthusiastic and affable team, plus delightful dishes from beyond France’s borders, it’s easy to see why the place is so popular. The menu largely sticks to the classics, providing satisfying versions of time-honoured favourites; keep an eye on the dish of the day, for treats such as cavatelli with lamb ragù. If you’re celebrating, consider booking the private Piano Bar, where a live musician will soundtrack your evening.

Name: Juliet
Address: 8888 Washington Blvd., Culver City, CA, 90232, USA
Description: Chic and French go hand in hand, especially at Juliet in Culver City. This gorgeous space has a contemporary French aesthetic with as much seating outdoors on the posh patio as indoors. The open kitchen buzzes all day, but dinner is where this team shines. Oysters, tartare or tuna carpaccio could kick off the meal, but the mousse au foie de volaille, with its delicate tart filled with chicken liver mousse, toasted hazelnuts and an apple gelee, is an auspicious beginning. Sea bream with ratatouille and pistou is simple but well executed, and pairs well with one of their many wines available by the glass. Don't skip dessert—whether you choose the éclair or the crème fraiche cheesecake with passion fruit gelee, it's a perfect ending to a delightful meal.

Name: Juliette
Description: Are you looking for a slice of the French way of life in the middle of Potsdam? In the Holländisches Viertel (Dutch Quarter), you will find this beautifully designed restaurant, which is housed in a charming 17C half-timbered house. The dining space comprises three different levels, where you can enjoy ambitious classic cuisine accompanied by just the right wine, as a discreet soundtrack plays in the background. In addition to the menu, you can also choose a few dishes à la carte. If the weather is nice, would you like an aperitif at one of the small tables on the pavement before your meal?

Name: Juliette Plaza
Description: Adjacent to Montréal Plaza, Juliette Plaza is a small restaurant with some 20 seats and a unique interior featuring eye-catching wallpapered ceiling panels, a suspended boat, and Asterix comic strips framed on the walls. The chefs serve up flavourful modern cuisine, which, although simpler than the food served in the main restaurant, has bags of personality – a cone of delicious fish tartare or the tender slow-braised beef chuck. Table d'hôte menu served in the evening.

Name: Julijana
Description: Housed in the Grand Hotel Toplice which stands amid some of the most popular landscapes in Slovenia, this restaurant boasts truly breathtaking views of Lake Bled from its dining room and its outdoor terrace. Here, the chef offers tasting menus of various lengths featuring meat and fish specialities with the occasional international influence, as well as a 4-course option (the Gorenjska selection menu) with a stronger regional focus. On the latter, the array of local ingredients is showcased via a delicious hazelnut crème brûlée served with ice-cream made from cherries soaked in Terrano liqueur.

Name: Julius Ernst
Description: This is not your average, run-of-the-mill restaurant – the concept is relaxed and professional in equal measure. It is, in a sense, the younger sibling of ernst, Dylan Watson-Brawn and Spencer Christenson's restaurant. Its interior is minimalist and sleek, the atmosphere youthful and laid-back. Service, courtesy of an exceptionally friendly international team, runs like clockwork. The kitchen, which is visible behind the counter, sends out creations that blend French and Japanese influences: delicate, refined and intensely flavourful dishes such as "Rose shrimp, nori, yuzu" or "Grilled scallop and Tetsukabuto squash with kale". In addition to the à la carte selection, there is an omakase menu. Breakfast and a small lunch menu are also served at weekends, along with coffee, pastries and snacks throughout the day.

Name: July
Description: July is the longest-standing fine dining restaurant in Seorae Village offering the chef's modern interpretation of European dishes inspired by his travels. He uses Korean vegetables, fish, and other seasonal ingredients to create technically refined and complex contemporary cuisine. This artistry is evident in the sauces, which combine different flavors with classic sauce recipes to create a variety of different flavor profiles. The wood-toned interiors and soft lighting create a cozy dining space - well suited for both business and romantic dates.

Name: Jun
Address: 148, Section 1, Tiedao Road, East District, Hsinchu City, Taiwan
Description: The chef garnered 10+ years of experience in Japan and Taiwan before starting his own venture in his hometown. The menu is essentially Japanese, but jazzed up with creative twists. Grilled fish is seasoned by salt laced with dried salmon roe for extra umami. Champion rice from Taitung is cooked in spring water from Mt Fuji in a donabe. For a sweet finale, koya tofu mousse is drizzled with toffee sauce and sprinkled with strawberries and pistachios.

Name: Jun's
Address: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Boulevard, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef and restaurateur Kelvin Cheung’s larger-than-life personality has found the perfect outlet here in Downtown Dubai. His Chinese heritage, Canadian/American upbringing and international peregrinations all inform his cuisine. Rainbow heirloom carrots; scallops and corn; and char siu short ribs – these are just some of the dishes that are busting with flavour and will have you licking your lips for long after. It’s contagiously fun.

Name: June
Address: 700 E. Washington St., Orlando, FL, 32801, USA
Description: This Thornton Park newcomer could be equally at home in Mexico City with its contemporary styling and mix of chic, neutral tones. It's a charming spot, featuring both patio and interior seating options blending wood, fabric and pops of color. The kitchen turns out creative Mexican dishes with a focus on wood-fired cooking, and it's all about sharing here, where larger protein-heavy dishes or a series of small plates are just right for groups. Ones to consider include the rich, buttery crab tostadas and the pillowy tamale dumplings mixed with pan- seared rock shrimp, pasilla chili sauce and lime crema. Cocktails are a highlight, as are the refreshing agua frescas.

Name: Juniper
Address: GF, Shangri-La Plaza, Shaw Boulevard, Ortigas Centre, Mandaluyong - Metro Manila, The Philippines
Description: On the first floor of Shangri-La Plaza, Juniper combines soft grey hues and a sleek semi-open kitchen with a relaxed, modern feel. The menu blends global influences – charcuterie, pasta, roast chicken – and leans into Asian flavours at lunchtime. The UK-and Philippines-trained chef favours creativity over rigid styles. True to its name, Juniper has an impressive gin selection, with guests invited to choose their tonic for a refreshing start to the meal.

Name: Juniper & Ivy
Address: 2228 Kettner Blvd., San Diego, CA, 92101, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Set within a 1920s warehouse, redwood beams and tan leather furnishings lend this popular eatery a certain rustic charm. A sizable bar area with a long curved booth looks out across a sunken dining room and a bustling kitchen. The approachable menu offers a thoroughly contemporary take on SoCal cuisine, rooted in quality ingredients seasoned judiciously with Latin and Asian flavors. Think grilled swordfish skewers with peanut crunch, bluefin crudo with pickled jalapeños and hearty pastas featuring the likes of Santa Barbara uni or fire-roasted squash.

Name: Junoon
Address: 19 W. 24th St., New York, NY, 10010, USA
Description: Pendant lights strung with thick grass ropes, vintage mirrors, and a gleaming white marble bar set a sophisticated tone at this long-standing Indian restaurant. With an eye for presentation and a taste for new ideas, the menu offers a range of dishes. Tuna puchka brings three bite-sized semolina puffs tucked with finely diced raw tuna topped with a dollop of caviar. The tomato-based tile fish Assamese curry offers a delicious spice journey with gentle heat and notes of cilantro. Meanwhile, savory dal makhani calls for a house-spiced naan. To finish, a bright Madras curry-scented whipped cream infused with condensed milk makes for a proper send-off.

Name: Jupiter
Address: 20 W. 50th St., New York, NY, 10020, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: The team behind SoHo's beloved King has headed uptown to Rockefeller Center with Jupiter. The bright dining room boasts a bar counter and open kitchen, while green lacquered chairs, tiled columns and upholstered nooks set a sophisticated tone.The menu is clearly defined and concise. Starters include a wonderfully hearty mozzarella plate arranged with crushed chickpeas and roasted radicchio. The delightful pasta offerings include luscious strands of spaghetti alle vongole and paccheri verdi dressed with a light-bodied sugo of slow-roasted pork, sage and lemon zest. Desserts, like the creamy, quivering panna cotta with Amarena cherries; and cocktails, such as the negroni sbagliato bianco, round out the enticing experience here.

Name: Justa Pasta
Description: As you walk down the street you’ll see the chefs beavering away behind the windows of this shop conversion, crafting various types of pasta and gnocchi with 00 flour. Exposed brick walls lend the place a rustic air, yet the room is quite formally laid. Alongside the more familiar dishes such as meatballs or ravioli with a potato filling, you’ll find some different dishes such as a delicious tacchino tonnato; the coconut panna cotta is a great choice for dessert. You’ll get a proper taste of Italy without breaking the bank.

Name: Juumpo
Address: GF, Hotel Gahn Khao Lak, 1/96 Mu 5, Phet Kasem Road, Khuk Khak, Takua Pa, Phang-Nga, 82220, Thailand
Description: The cuisine of the local Baba (Chinese-Thai) people lives on here. Named in honour of the owner’s grandfather, a 'Juumpo' or chef on a Chinese boat more than 80 years ago and the source of many unique recipes, the open-air restaurant is fitted out with décor that reflects Chino-Portuguese design and culture. Baba-style coconut milk soup with shrimps and Thai herbs, chilli dip with shrimp, and fried fish with sweet and sour sauce are all recommended.

Name: Jwala
Address: E-02-01, Block E, The Five@KPD, 49 Jalan Dungun, Bukit Damansara, Kuala Lumpur, 50490, Malaysia
Description: Named after the Sanskrit word for fire, Jwala is famous for chargrilled dishes and artisanal bread from its custom-built tandoori oven. Try their tandoori tiger prawns, puff pastry naan and gluten-free roti. On the menu, familiar ingredients like chicken and lamb chops rub shoulders with less common items such as croissant, cottage cheese and hamachi collar. Vegetarian diners will also find a substantial veggie lineup.

Name: Jyu Dim
Address: 91 Dongsing Road, East District, Tainan, 701, Taiwan
Description: The owner from Hong Kong opened this dim sum restaurant in 2018. The room is simple and cosy; full-length windows let in natural light. Open only for breakfast and lunch, it prides itself on bite-sized gems crafted in-house from scratch. Seasoning is slightly tweaked for the local palate, but the owner strives to stay true to his childhood memories. Try the steamed tofu skin roll with chicken, fish maw and taro. Booking mandatory.

Name: Jäger & Lustig
Description: What a cosy and quaint-feeling place, serving what the owners term "Heimatküche": think hearty, fresh, flavoursome cuisine. Classic German dishes are the stars of the show – game and goose are specialities of the house. They are at pains to use regional ingredients and remain aligned with the seasons. Service courtesy of friendly and competent staff. Make the most of the beer garden in summer.

Name: Jägerstube & Walserstube
Description: In the small fine dining restaurant of Hotel Jagdhaus Monzabon, Michael Broger and his team deliver interesting modern cuisine that is big on flavour. Guests will also enjoy the charming service and expert wine recommendations that come courtesy of junior manager and sommelier Tobias Schneider, who also happens to be a certified sake sommelier – there is an extensive selection, and almost all are also served by the glass. The food, which delves into the region and uses many ingredients from local suppliers (the local game is excellent, for example), is also decidedly cosmopolitan. You can put together your own menu from an appealing selection of dishes. There is also a cosy bar for an aperitif. Tip: Make a reservation, as there are only a handful of tables.

Name: Jérôme Brochot
Description: Jérôme Brochot rustles up market-fresh cuisine in the guise of his "côté cuisine" set menu, which changes on a weekly basis. On weekends, the spotlight is on the fine dining surprise set menu. They offer a cookery class on Sunday mornings.

Name: K
Address: Level 37, Menara Ilham, 8 Jalan Binjai, Kuala Lumpur, 50450, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed
Description: The open kitchen clad in stone and wood exudes a luxurious vibe and boasts lovely city views through panoramic windows. On the food side, the Japanese head chef offers a single tasting menu of over 15 courses that showcase his creativity and solid skills with a nod to tradition. Ingredients are sourced locally whenever possible. Try his abalone with soba noodles made from scratch, delivering soft, but bouncy texture.

Name: K by Vicky Cheng
Address: 56F, The Empire, 1 South Sathon Road, Yan Nawa, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Vicky Cheng's first restaurant outside Hong Kong promises an upscale dining experience that sees Chinese culinary traditions with a contemporary twist. His use of Cantonese and Teochew flavours with seasonal ingredients shines in the mud crab with olive leaf and garlic, inviting hands-on dining. In this stylish, refined and inviting setting, choose between private sofas or seating with splendid views of Bangkok's skyline.

Name: KA-ORŪ SUSHIBAR & COCKTAIL
Description: A reinvented dining option that has taken on a new lease of life and name, the latter a combination of the Japanese words for family (kazoku) and olive tree (Orību). The cuisine here, which remains faithful to the traditions of Japanese cooking, is centred around two menus that need to be ordered in advance (Kazoku and Ka-Oru) and can either be enjoyed at the counter while watching the sushi chefs at work, or at one of the three tables. Options include top-notch nigiri, fresh wasabi, top-quality tuna etc. There’s also an interesting nod to local cuisine, such as the delicious Katsu Sando (a type of Japanese sandwich) filled with pork head.

Name: KABUFF
Description: The small restaurant is furnished in a minimalist, upscale, modern bistro style, with a small kitchenette at its centre. The focus is on the fine dining sharing menu, which is served to two or more people – but all dishes can also be ordered à la carte. Creative, technically sophisticated and pleasingly stripped back, combinations such as "tomato, elderberry, black garlic, sunflower seeds" or "onion & onion, whey, sage" are presented. The cuisine is vegetarian for the most part, with meat and fish available depending on availability. The excellent house-baked sourdough bread served at the start of your meal is also worth mentioning! Then there is the selection of organic and natural wines, as well as house-made alcohol-free drinks. Worth noting: on Sat and Sun, they are open for breakfast, coffee, cake and drinks in the morning.

Name: KAENKRUNG
Address: 521/11 Arunamarin Road, Bangkok Noi, Bangkok, 10700, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: With its soft lighting and Northeastern-inspired decor featuring woven lampshades and wall art, KaenKrung exudes a warm atmosphere. The chef-owners present contemporary Isan flavours from Khon Kaen in a menu of well-balanced Thai and Isan dishes. Made with local ingredients, the signature Hao Dong, comprising grilled pork tossed in a fragrant herb and spice mix, delivers bold, spicy, smoky notes with a refined finish. Perfect for those who love strong, punchy flavours.

Name: KAISEKI BY MANABU
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At the Hôtel Des Trois Couronnes, beautifully situated on the lakeside, chef Alastair Long offers authentic Japanese cuisine. Selected products (e.g. Hamachi, Kagashima Wagyu, scallops, etc.) are given pride of place. In the evening, three menus are available: ‘Signature’, ‘Connaisseur’ and ‘Kaiseki’, while at lunchtime a more affordable lunch menu is available. Service takes place in an elegant atmosphere, under high ceilings decorated with stucco. In summer, the terrace is a veritable dream, offering magnificent views of the lake and mountains.

Name: KAKAN
Description: The restaurant showcases the appeal of Japan through domestic ingredients. Its name derives from the word ‘kakan’, meaning ‘bold and fearless’, and the team takes on challenges boldly and without fear of failure. The dishes draw on experience in Italian cuisine while remaining unconstrained by genre. A Basque-style cheesecake made with onion is one of the restaurant’s standout creations. To finish, guests may be served dishes such as ramen made with house-made pasta or grilled onigiri, reflecting the kitchen’s playful creativity.

Name: KAMINOZA
Description: Love of cooking, attentiveness to guests: the spirit of gratitude is etched in the restaurant’s name, which means ‘gathering of the gods’. The chef recreates traditional Japanese dishes and serves them on vessels by modern ceramic artists, expressing the Japan of today. His process for drawing dashi for soup resembles that of a coffee drip; to preserve the natural flavour, the only seasoning is salt. Meticulous food preparation and attentive service say ‘thank you’ better than any words.

Name: KAN10
Description: “Original”, “captivating”, “adventurous” and “regional” sum up the ethos of this cosy urban eatery. As a result, you can expect to sample a mind-blowing range of flavours and savours. Asian flair depicts the semi-cooked salmon, underscored by excellent homemade sambal and flanked by a traditional beurre noisette… A culinary banquet! Ask the lady of the house to show you the popular menu of shared dishes and get ready to embark on an exciting voyage of international flavours in a casual vibe.

Name: KANTA
Description: Not wanting to be confined to a single concept, the chef honed his craft by studying Japanese, Western and Chinese cuisines. The menu, which champions a playfully hearty approach, avoids classification by genre. Dishes range from original creations pairing dried mullet roe and rice vermicelli to familiar favourites such as pasta and mapo tofu. Preparing kombu dashi and blending spices, he follows his own inspirations in pursuit of flavour. Generous portions leave a lasting impression.

Name: KAO SOY PRIN
Address: 5F, Dusit Central Park, Rama 4 Road, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: On the fifth floor of Dusit Central Park, this small shop delivers quality Northern Thai noodle soups. Chef-owner Prin Polsuk's Lampang roots shine through in dishes layered with spice and aroma. Standouts include khao soi with coconut-rich curry and a rarer clear-broth option.

Name: KCC by Mauro Colagreco
Description: KCC stands for Kulm Country Club. The handsome L-shaped building is located right next to the ice rink and has a garden for summer days. Local produce takes centre stage in the dishes, which often draw on Mediterranean influences. As well as an appealing selection of starters and pasta dishes, the menu includes dishes for two, such as beef cutlets and lamb shoulder. Much of the food is flame-grilled or roasted over embers. The atmosphere is relaxed and the decor tasteful – the vintage sledges adorning the ceiling are bound to draw the eye! There is also a fabulous terrace. Live music and vinyl sessions provide the acoustic backdrop.

Name: KEI Collection PARIS
Address: 49F, Toranomon Hills Station Tower, 2-6-2 Toranomon, Minato-ku, Tokyo, 105-5549, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: A project by Kei Kobayashi – the chef who charmed the Paris culinary community. Billing his restaurant as a ‘grill with gastronomy’, he sends out his new wave in cuisine from the top of a skyscraper. In a first for him, KEI Collection PARIS focuses on à la carte items. Appetisers boast a spirit of playful creativity. Wagyu beef is grilled with grass over a traditional charcoal stove. The stylish interior and lights glittering like jewels create a real sense of being in the heart of the big city.

Name: KELINA Fine Dine
Address: Strada Lech de Boà s.n., Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: From Corvara, take the ultra-modern Boè cable-car to this restaurant (accessible also on skis or by foot) which is one of the dining options at the Piz Boè Alpine Lounge (for access, turn right as you exit the cable-car). Open at lunchtime only, KELINA serves unexpectedly gourmet cuisine in a minimalist-style dining room which allows the stunning views of Sassongher, Santa Croce and La Varella to take centre stage through the restaurant’s large floor-to-ceiling windows. The dishes are always modern and creative, combining Alpine ingredients with fresh fish – the red prawns with scampi mayonnaise and sea asparagus sorbet is a good example.

Name: KHAO BIRD
Address: 24 Brewer Street, Soho, London, W1F 0SN, United Kingdom
Description: Having developed a following with a residency near Borough Market, the team found a permanent home for this restaurant amidst the bright lights of Soho. A typically energetic spot that feels right on-trend with the times, the cooking here is focused largely on Northern Thai barbecue – although dishes from the country’s other regions do feature. Expect to find measured yet vibrantly flavoured creations such as the moreish ‘Prawns KJ’ and the ‘Khao Soi’ with barbecued chicken thighs. Leaving without being hit too hard in the wallet adds to the appeal.

Name: KI'IS
Address: The Riviera Maya EDITION at Kanai, Paseo Kanai 14, Solidaridad, Playa del Carmen, 77730, Mexico
Description: Located inside the stylish and meticulously groomed The Riviera Maya EDITION at Kanai, this breezy oasis features verdant views as well as pools of water that flow gently alongside the restaurant and all through the property. Sourcing ingredients from across Mexico, the kitchen delivers familiar dishes with unexpected inspiration. Tlayudas arrive smeared in artichoke puree and topped with tuna and Serrano peppers. Lamb is charred to the hilt and paired with guacamole garnished with pistachios and cocoa nibs. A dark chocolate tamale sings with passion fruit sorbet and crispy hoja Santa. Friendly, attentive servers dressed in crisp whites keep close watch over the spacious dining room fit with a cocktail bar in the center.

Name: KIAS Restaurant
Description: Bringing a slice of Brazil to Vienna's bustling 6th district, this restaurant is a hit both with locals and tourists on account of its exotic cuisine. In an inviting, laid-back urban setting, traditional Brazilian fare is presented with modern twists that add a fresh lift to the flavours. Diners can opt for a seven-course set menu or select from it individual dishes à la carte. Exceptionally friendly service completes the experience.

Name: KIKU Restaurant by Jan Fribus
Description: Kiku means "chrysanthemum" – the Japanese national flower – and, indeed, the cuisine here is strongly marked by Japanese elements, along with seasonal influences and the odd subtle classic French touch. Comprising eight courses, the set menu features dishes such as dim sum with prawns and bisque, and hibachi venison with pumpkin and hoisin. The restaurant is located in a tastefully restored historical building in a small street lined with half-timbered façades, not far from the city centre. Inside, the atmosphere is laid back and elegant, and there is a secluded terrace in the courtyard. The service is friendly and informal – the charming chefs also come to your table to talk you through their dishes. A short yet carefully curated wine list complements the food perfectly, and most wines are available by the glass. Tip: Just upstairs from the restaurant, Anno 1560 offers cosy and stylish apartments.

Name: KLE
Description: Housed in Huber's Boutiquehotel, this restaurant has a pleasingly laid-back feel. The set menu can be customised – select three to seven courses – and features highly appealing dishes packed with flavour. For the most part, they are made with a penchant for regional produce, but a lobster soup is also listed. Friendly and adept service. Oenophiles should peruse the glass-paned wine cabinet at the entrance.

Name: KOHYAMA
Description: The friendly welcome by the Koyamas will make you feel at home at this restaurant with no sign outside. The wife is the chef and her husband is the sommelier. Wine and sake are paired with the set menus. The dishes are based on dashi from kombu and katsuo, and Western elements are incorporated for a touch of creativity. Not only is there synergy between the dish and the sake, but the husband-and-wife team makes for a sense of easy-going togetherness.

Name: KOI
Description: Fans of modern Japanese cuisine should head here for the extensive range of sushi, as well as meat, fish and vegetable dishes and snacks. Some items are cooked on the Robata charcoal grill. Tempting options include "beef fillet teriyaki, Jerusalem artichoke chips, wafu" or "grilled miso aubergine, daikon salsa". With its dark wood, warm lighting and stylish details, the interior has an elegant, urban atmosphere; meanwhile, the bar on the upper floor exudes a loungey vibe. On fine summer days, the terrace is highly prized.

Name: KOICHIRO
Address: 5F, 301 Lequn 3rd Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: From appetisers and hot dishes to nigiri and desserts, the thoughtfully curated menu embodies kaiseki artistry, together with a host of surprising intricate details. Nigiri sushi are elegantly delivered to the table in a bespoke wooden box instead of on a plate or platter. Equally noteworthy is the chef and his wife’s warm, personalised hospitality as they graciously unveil each course.

Name: KOKYU
Description: A genre-defying cuisine paired with tea-based cocktails. While rooted in French techniques, the chef seamlessly weaves in elements of Chinese and Japanese cuisine. The duck dish, for instance, is prepared by ladling hot oil over the skin, much like Peking duck. The tradition of serving tea and sweets after a meal, known as ochauke, reflects Japanese hospitality. Chef and mixologist work in harmony, refining the distinctive world of ‘wither and decay’ or ‘kokyu’.

Name: KOLLÁZS Brasserie & Bar
Address: Four Seasons Hotel Gresham Palace, Széchenyi István tér 5, Budapest, 1051, Hungary
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: The Four Seasons Gresham Palace hotel is a beautiful art nouveau building which was constructed in 1906 for the Gresham Life Assurance Company. Set in the heart of Budapest, directly opposite the Széchenyi Chain Bridge, its restaurant makes the perfect place to dine when visiting the city. The relaxed, cosy atmosphere is matched perfectly by a menu of familiar French brasserie classics, with a few Hungarian dishes thrown in. The steak tartare is made at the table, the roast chicken for two is carved in front of you and the rum baba is a hit.

Name: KOMFORTA
Description: ‘Komforta’ is Esperanto for ‘comfortable’ or ‘cosy’. An apt description of this restaurant, which is reminiscent of a mountain hut and on a hill, as its wood accents create a warm and inviting space. The cuisine bursts with creativity, crafted by a chef who gives his imagination free rein. Nara ingredients reflect the tempo of the seasons. Born of the land, its people and environment, each dish is thoughtfully conceived with Nara at its core.

Name: KOSTBAR
Description: Following Marco Akuzun's departure, Daniele di Fabio is the new head chef. As well as a good à la carte selection, a five-course set menu is served in the evening (vegetarian version available on request) and there is an attractive "business lunch" formula comprising two or three courses. The mouthwatering options include ricotta gnocchi with summer truffle and Parmesan, or guinea fowl saltimbocca with olive marinara sauce and basil purée. Furthermore, a creative tasting menu can be ordered in the evening. The upscale interior is both stylish and cosy, featuring warm wood and a minimalist design that creates a welcoming atmosphere. Lovely covered terrace with a working water wheel as the standout feature!

Name: KOTARO Hasegawa DOWNTOWN CUISINE
Description: DOWNTOWN CUISINE is located in the chef’s local Satake Shopping Street. The chef arrays each table with Japanese vessels that recall memories of the working-class neighbourhood. The inspiration for the restaurant came from a world cooking contest, in which the chef competed with a concept designed to showcase the culture of Japan. Each plate is imbued with the passion to aim ever higher and the desire to thank and give back to the chef’s hometown.

Name: KR Prime Steak
Address: 52 Shizheng North 2nd Road, Xitun District, Taichung, 407, Taiwan
Description: This restaurant set amid luxurious apartment towers is famous for its precisely cooked wet-aged US steaks, especially the Certified Angus Beef USDA prime rib eye cap, prized for its tenderness, flavour and succulence. Consider ordering the set menu that includes an appetiser, side and sweet; opt for the umami-laden bottarga sauce to go with your steak. The house-made desserts – such as silky crème brûlée with fresh berries – are also a must.

Name: KRU
Description: Husband-and-wife Chefs Ohm Suansilphong and Kiki Supap are behind KRU, which is Thai for "guru." Indeed, you will get a lesson in traditional Thai dishes albeit ones that have been spruced up in a decidedly contemporary way. Sleek and airy, the interior is equally of-the-moment with exposed brick walls and ductwork along with cement tiled floors. First up? Braised beef shank and tripe in a rich, flavorful broth with pork cracklings, bean sprouts, and Chinese broccoli with a nice balance of sour and spicy. Then, red curry-rubbed branzino over steamed egg and Napa cabbage is served on a banana leaf with white rice.

Name: KUMA
Description: A restaurant with a refined decor in which you can enjoy a culinary dining experience to the full thanks to chef Daniel Lomana’s frequent visits to Japan to train and to develop his technique further, skills that can you enjoy at close quarters by taking a seat at the bar or at one of its adjoining tables. His focus is on Japanese fusion cuisine that includes interesting à la carte dishes (hamachi sashimi, amberjack with KUMA ceviche, sea bass nigiri, fried aubergines with a white sesame vinaigrette etc), plus a recommended tasting menu. Don’t leave without trying their deconstructed cheesecake!

Name: KUR
Address: 6, Lane 109, Section 1, Anhe Road, Da'an District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: The discreet entrance has an elegant feel; the wood-rich interior with 16 counter seats makes for a relaxed, intimate vibe. In his tasting menu, the young Japanese chef applies French techniques to contemporary washoku to deliver bold but balanced flavours. In his surf clam with wakame and rose tosa vinegar, fruity, floral depth complements the bouncy, umami-laden clam. The well curated alcohol-free drinks pairings are also a delight.

Name: KUTSCH
Description: Located close to the Kutschkermarkt, which is open on Saturdays, this welcoming restaurant's theme "cook the market" could hardly be more apt. The cuisine is regional and seasonally inspired. Simple, satisfying dishes are presented in a modern and ambitious style, including pig's tail with Semmelknödel (bread dumplings) and cabbage salad, or bouillabaisse made with local fish, accompanied by Comté bread, potato and sauce rouille. Lunch is à la carte only, and in the evening, there is an additional set menu comprising three or four courses. In the cheerful and relaxed bistro setting, service is pleasingly informal yet adept. Tip: At weekends, you can also come for breakfast or brunch.

Name: Kaagman & Kortekaas
Description: Giel Kaagman and Bram Kortekaas have given their restaurant a stylish makeover without dimming its lively spirit. An open kitchen now forms the heart of the space, with charming counter seats and tables clustered around it. The chef draws inspiration from nature, giving pride of place to vegetables, game and fish in bold dishes that pulse with energy and fearlessly explore contrasting flavour profiles. Pike-perch from the IJsselmeer, for example, is seared a la plancha and accompanied by beluga lentils, a crab salad and a punchy bordelaise sauce. You can count on the ever-evolving set menu and wine list to keep the surprises coming.

Name: Kabawa
Address: 8 Extra Pl., New York, NY, 10003, USA
Description: Chef Paul Carmichael pens a deeply personal love letter to the Caribbean with Kabawa. From its elegant dark green dining room with subtle regional references to its sophisticated three-course tasting menu, expect an elevated take on the tropics. Meals begin with bread service comprised of roti served with curry chickpeas and eggplant, as well as butter. Then, fried sweet plantain is topped with crispy salt cod and sided by soft scrambled eggs with caviar for a memorable first course. Main dishes like seared black bass with yellow curry are served with sides like pineapple-glazed sweet potato and stewed pink beans before sweet send-offs like a coconut turnover. The cocktail list is packed with enticing selections.

Name: Kabia
Description: In this centrally located family-run property, which has close ties with the soil and has been in business for over 25 years, the focus is on traditional cuisine with a contemporary twist, an honest approach and locally sourced seasonal ingredients. The cuisine is centred on two menus, one daily version, the second a tasting option – on the latter guests can choose a main dish from a list of different options. We can highly recommend the braised veal cheek with port wine.

Name: Kabooki Sushi
Address: 3122 E. Colonial Dr., Orlando, FL, 32803, USA
Description: This freshly minted space wears all the contemporary touches that pepper our Instagram feeds. There are hexagonal tiles and a green "living" accent wall donning a neon sign that reads "Good Vibes Only." The marble bar hums with activity, not unlike the booths situated along the center.It may be billed as updated Japanese fare fused with inventive Pan-Asian elements, but make no mistake—this is not an average strip mall spot. This cooking is unbound by tradition. Sushi is de rigueur, but splurge on the omakase for a worthy venture with the likes of torched salmon with truffle pâté, smoked trout roe and aji amarillo. Other oceanic delights include a bluefin sashimi flight, hamachi nigiri with truffled caviar and uni rice with seared lobster.

Name: Kabuki Madrid
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The Kabuki Group’s latest culinary venture, in the heart of the city’s Salamanca district, remains faithful to its roots, inviting guests to explore dishes with their essence in Japanese cuisine but with an Iberian touch – a tried and tested concept which has transported diners to Japan for many years. In this spacious setting, with its restrained lighting and meticulous decor, there is the option of ordering à la carte, a short set menu for weekday lunches and an interesting tasting menu (with an extended option). There is also a wide range of cocktails available!

Name: Kabukizaura Masashi
Description: Diners are greeted by the open owner-chef and the graceful proprietress. The playful riot of colours on the wall is a tableau on the theme of people’s relationship with food. In this vision stretching from the past to the future, faces are drawn in kumadori, the shaded kabuki makeup fitting for a restaurant ‘behind the kabuki theatre’ (kabukiza-ura). The omakase set meal abounds in changes in inflection: two pieces of nigiri and two types of fried items (tempura and deep-fried) highlight contrasting textures. The chef’s experience with Chinese cooking bursts from his baked gyoza. For the best drink pairings, let the proprietress choose.

Name: Kadena
Description: Among the city's most elegant restaurants, this venue boasts a magnificent panoramic location by the sea: the terrace, overlooking from above, provides a truly enchanting view. The interiors are tastefully furnished with fine materials, providing a comfortable environment with attention to detail. The friendly and attentive service contributes to an even more enjoyable experience. The kitchen is dominated by fresh fish, displayed in iceboxes and starring in many menu items, alongside good meat options and a selection of sushi. Also of note are the excellent dishes designed for two people, perfect for sharing. The wine list is well structured, with an interesting choice of Croatian and international labels, including sparkling wines and champagnes; a surprising selection of high-end cognacs, whiskies and gins rounds out the offerings.

Name: Kaen
Address: 140/64, Mu 14, Soi Adunyaram 7, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Chefs Paisarn and Kanyarat present a refined take on Isan cuisine, blending traditional flavours with modern presentation in a casual fine dining menu. Rare ingredients – many are sourced from local small-scale farmers and aren't available at the market – are prepared using inventive techniques. Try the earthy, comforting and robust kaeng ploe: an Isan minestrone with free-range chicken and 20 kinds of hand-cut vegetables in a bowl of fresh yanang broth.

Name: Kagurazaka Marutomi
Description: Wagyu beef is the tie that binds the family of Kenichi Onodera. He named his restaurant ‘Marutomi’ after his grandfather’s cattle farm, and his parents ran a butcher’s shop in Ichinoseki. For that reason, he focuses on wagyu from Iwate Prefecture. Char-grilled and fried items are on the menu, as is sukiyaki with edible wild plants and matsutake mushrooms. The menu changes twice monthly, so a wide range of ingredients are sourced. The combination of traditional multi-course meals with beef dishes is pure Onodera.

Name: Kai
Address: 65 South Audley Street, Mayfair, London, W1K 2QU, United Kingdom
Description: With its glitzy interior and tropical fish tank, this certainly isn’t your average Chinese restaurant. The whole country is represented on the wide-ranging menus, with an emphasis on the southern Nanyang region. Around 20% of the dishes are classics, such as the 18-hour slow-cooked pork belly; the other 80% are more elaborate, adventurous constructions like spring chicken and Szechuan spicy crumble. Afternoon tea is also a feature, offering fine infusions, bao buns and sweet treats. The wine list includes some interesting Chinese options.

Name: Kai Asian Street Fare
Address: 1555 State Rd. 436, Ste. 1171, Orlando, FL, 32792, USA
Description: Opened in 2018, this restaurant is the brainchild of Thai-born Isra Sunhachawi and his Vietnamese brother-in-law, Quan Van. Found in a Winter Park shopping center, the space is tiny and simple, offering seating for a handful at a dark granite counter as well as at a few tables. Everything is freshly prepared, and the room quickly fills with the sounds and scents of the crew at work.The concise menu never loses focus, and regulars are well aware that it's all about stir-fried noodles and spicy Korean-style chicken wings. Ramen is also a treat, like the tonkotsu shio, featuring a richly flavored, slow-simmered pork bone broth, stocked with toothsome, thin and wavy noodles, slices of tender, lean pork belly, a shoyu egg and a host of other tasty additions.

Name: Kai Kai BBQ & Dumplings
Address: 1110 E. Colonial Dr., Orlando, FL, 32803, USA
Description: They're no strangers to these parts, having run a popular food truck before, but this food stall inside Mills Market is proof that they're here to stay. Kai Kai shines a spotlight on Cantonese cooking. Not sure where to begin? Take one look at that case of barbecue and roasted meat tempting from just behind the counter and it becomes clear. Sold by the pound or as a meal with steamed rice and two or three selections (crispy pork, soy sauce chicken, and char siu are go-to choices), the menu also includes noodle and rice dishes, as well as an entire section devoted to dim sum. Roast duck bao is a surprising delight, as is the fried mochi pork dumpling with just a hint of sweetness that delivers an impactful bite.

Name: Kai Restaurant
Address: 22 Sea Road, Galway, H91 DX47, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: This long-standing, rustically charming restaurant is really two places in one. At lunch, they take walk-ins only and serve one course followed by homemade cakes and pastries (they also have their own bakery). Things ramp up a gear at dinner, with a three-course à la carte heavily guided by the seasons and the local area. Dishes are often understated in appearance, with just a handful of ingredients needed for plentiful flavour. The concise wine list pushes lesser-known producers to the fore and features on-trend natural and orange wines.

Name: Kai Yang Sueb Siri
Address: 49 Sueb Siri Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
Description: Having clocked up over 50 years, this enduring favourite remains a top spot for flavour-packed Isan fare in Korat. The tender grilled chicken – crisp-skinned and marinated to perfection – is a must, pairing well with the fiery som tum made with their own fermented fish sauce. The menu also features korat noodles, tom sap and well-charred meats. Suitable for friendly gatherings or even just a quick stop, there's plenty of seating both indoors and out.

Name: Kai Yang Wanna
Address: 271 Mu 11, Mittraphap Road, Kham Muang, Khao Suan Kwang, Khon Kaen, 40280, Thailand
Description: Since 1973 this down-to-earth restaurant with a family-style vibe has been a favourite among locals for its grilled chicken. The birds are butterflied and lovingly tended over charcoal every day, emerging with crispy skin, a smoky aroma and succulent, well-seasoned meat. Other Isan favourites, such as som tam, lap and nam tok, are made with that same home-cooked pride. Seating is available inside with air-condition or outside on the veranda.

Name: Kaia Kaipe
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: A classic address (the Arregi family opened the restaurant’s doors in 1962) that stands out for its superb views of the port of Getaria (hence its name – “Kaia” translates as “port” in Basque while “Kaipe” means “below the port”) and distinct maritime feel. It features a pleasant terrace, attractive dining rooms, its own live fish and seafood tanks, a superb wine cellar, plus an open grill (the star of the show) out on the street. Make sure you try the prawns (either grilled or fried in batter) and the superb grilled turbot (for two). The impressive wine cellar is home to around 1 500 labels and over 40 000 bottles!

Name: Kaigi
Address: Rua De Eugénio De Castro 226, Porto, 4100-225, Portugal
Description: Following something of the philosophy of traditional Japanese izakayas, this restaurant, located on the ground floor of a residential building on the outskirts of the historic centre, revolves entirely around a large, U-shaped sushi counter that can seat 16 diners. What is found here? An intriguing Japanese-Portuguese fusion cuisine, offered in an exclusive nine-course tasting menu based on the best ingredients of the day. The atmosphere is welcoming and the flavours are surprising!

Name: Kaiseki
Description: If you find yourself on one of the Mediterranean’s most beautiful islands and craving Mediterranean–Asian fusion cuisine, head to Noel Azzopardi’s Kaiseki. This basement restaurant sports a cosy, welcoming vibe, and the chef-owner, working alongside youthful Mark Zammit, crafts intriguing dishes such as cauliflower and goat’s cheese risotto with crunchy sunflower kernels, Iberico pork with glazed, tender meat, Japanese fried rice with char-siu and fried egg, and excellent desserts like an exotic mille-feuille with yuzu and white chocolate. Last, but not least, the informal, relaxed vibe adds a final flourish to this enjoyable experience.

Name: Kaisers Eck
Description: Right next to Ahlbeck's main church, this cosy restaurant has a charming and down-to-earth atmosphere. The proprietress manages the service with warmth, ease and expertise, while her husband takes care of the cooking. The cuisine is predominantly regional. Both of the three- to five-course menus (one of them vegetarian) and the à la carte options are popular – the decision won't be easy. If you wish to stay on, two holiday apartments are available.

Name: Kaito
Address: Four Seasons Resort Megève, 373 chemin des Follières, Megève, 74120, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: At the Four Seasons Hotel, flawlessly fresh sashimi, tataki and sushi rub shoulders with delicately crafted alpine specialties. Fusion cuisine to be enjoyed on the terrace commanding a splendid view of the slopes or in the softly lit interior.

Name: Kaiyuan Road No Name Milkfish
Address: 313 Kaiyuan Road, North District, Tainan, Taiwan
Description: A firm favourite among locals, this shop doesn’t have a name, but regulars call it ‘the milkfish shop next to the big tree under a balcony’. Unsurprisingly, one can expect to find various cuts of milkfish on the menu: the fatty belly, skin, intestines and fish balls. Fish skin soup is especially popular; the skin is stuffed with fish paste, giving it a unique texture unlike others. Note that intestines tend to run out early in the morning.

Name: Kai’s Songbird
Address: Porto Arabia, The Pearl, Corinthia Yacht Club, Doha, Qatar
Description: Kai London and their songbird have flown east – with no expense spared – to this spot at the Yacht Club. The glamorous interior is certainly something to behold, but there is much to be said for a table on their air-conditioned terrace. The menu fuses original and modern Chinese Nanyang cuisine, so expect plenty of seafood like their standout soft shell crab or wok-hei prawns; there are other London classics too such as their legendary aromatic crispy duck.

Name: Kajiken
Address: 112 S. B St., San Mateo, CA, 94401, USA
Description: Originally from Nagoya, Japan, Kajiken has landed on the West Coast with the promise of shaking up your noodle routine with abura soba. This noodle dish is similar to ramen but eschews the broth, instead punching up the flavor courtesy of a special blend of oils and sauces. The springy noodles are made in house (score a seat facing the windowed noodle-making area) and are satisfying enough to eat plain, but with nine varieties, why? Toppings range from ajitama and chives to kimchi, ume or spicy mentaiko. Tables are topped with a well-chosen selection of vinegar, hot sauces and powdered nori for adjusting to your liking. The menu is rounded out with a small selection of karaage, takoyaki, edamame, gyoza and sides.

Name: Kajo
Description: If you’re looking to take a train trip outside the city, then this inconspicuous little restaurant opposite Tampere Central Station makes the perfect stop off. Regional and international ingredients come together in recipes that favour Asian techniques – like chawanmushi with peas and crayfish or sea buckthorn with lime leaf and Arctic cloudberry – and the superb stocks and sauces really show the depth of the kitchen’s skills. The chef is a very affable character, delivering his dishes and explaining their composition, while the young service team present some interesting wine pairings.

Name: Kakehashi
Description: This place is a mecca for good, authentic Japanese food. Top-notch fresh ingredients go into the set menus – a two-course sushi and sashimi set, six-course "Mini Omakase" and seven-course "Koichi's Special". Subtle Franconian elements also make occasional appearances. These dishes are accompanied by Japanese Kirin Ichiban beer on tap or sake from an enticing selection. The upscale interior has clean-lined Far Eastern aesthetics – the five tables at the counter with a view of the open kitchen are particularly prized. It is from this vantage point that diners can best observe the craftsmanship of chef Koichiro Yoshida. The extremely pleasant, almost family-like atmosphere is due in no small part to the truly cordial service, which ensures that you immediately feel at home.

Name: Kakinuma
Description: This small restaurant in the lively Eaux-Vives district is definitely worthy of its current success. The couple that run it create fresh and elegant dishes that include the most exquisitely sliced fish, tempuras that are as light as a feather, and silky chawanmushi (an egg flan). A feast for the senses!

Name: Kalank
Description: Kalank channels the spirit of Marseille on Boulevard de Charonne – quite a feat! The space has the easy charm of a stylish beach hut, with straw lampshades, bamboo chairs and seagrass flooring. At lunchtime, linger over sun-drenched Mediterranean cuisine on the sunny terrace – the value for money is unbeatable. In the evening: a more refined ambience, with à la carte options or a single set menu. The chef conjures up appealingly fragrant dishes: panisses with aïoli, veggie petits farcis, barigoule-style baby artichokes, and Iberian pork belly with sage-infused green and yellow courgettes.

Name: Kalaya
Address: 4 W. Palmer St., Philadelphia, PA, 19125, USA
Description: First established in South Philly and now blossoming in Fishtown, Kalaya is the creation of Chutatip "Nok" Suntaranon. Named after her mother, the restaurant is a celebration of Southern Thai cuisine and of her formative years spent in the coastal province of Trang. You can expect authentic levels of heat, homemade pastes and quality ingredients, in dishes whose flavors are deep and satisfying. Start with Gui chai – a crispy rice cake with sweet soy sauce that shows the Chinese influence in the south. Turmeric features in dishes like pla tod kamin (wok-fried barramundi), while prawns and pork are two other specialties of Trang and feature here in a number of dishes; caramelized pork belly with tamarind is a favorite of many. The large, bright room comes complete with palm trees and modern art and is a great spot for meeting up with friends.

Name: Kaldera
Address: 18 rue de la Bergerie, Biarritz, 64200, France
Description: You can't miss the red façade with large white letters spelling Kaldera, "cauldron" in Basque. This is the new hotspot drawing in foodies in the Saint-Charles neighbourhood. Inside, ochre walls, soft lighting, red velvet banquettes and light wood flooring make for an inviting atmosphere. Partners Guillaume Goyeneche, a local, and Camille Hausseguy provide attentive service. The chef's dishes are simple but creative, for example prawns with parsley fritters, puffed tapioca, spring onions and prawn hollandaise. Classic desserts – Grand Marnier soufflé, raspberry and hay tartlet – are put together with great precision.

Name: Kaldero
Address: Unit 4B, Stephen’s Green Shopping Centre, King Street South, Dublin 2, Dublin City, D02 HD30, Ireland
Description: Keep your eye out for this Filipino restaurant’s discrete entrance as you walk down King St South, because to miss its warm atmosphere and flavour-packed cooking would be a crying shame. Situated in a welcoming basement, its best seats are near the open kitchen, where you can feel the infectious buzz of the chefs. The menu is designed for sharing, so bring a few friends and try as many of the Filipino-Irish chef’s dishes as possible; look out for big, punchy flavours in the likes of ‘Dynamite Lumpia’ – chillis stuffed with pork mince.

Name: Kale & de Bril
Description: Be careful not to walk right past this unassuming building – you'd be missing out. Chef-patron duo Marc ("the bald one" or "Kale" in Dutch!) and Niek ("the one with glasses" – "de Bril" in Dutch) immediately set a relaxed, welcoming tone. Zeeland produce (also from the lobster tank) and vegetables prepared in a multitude of ways are showcased in creative dishes. For example, scallops are combined with various salsify and pear creations, as well as a lobster salpicon and a vanilla-infused broth. In both the set menu and the lobster menu, the seasons and the Zeeland terroir are the stars of the show.

Name: Kallos Cafe & Wine Bar
Address: Cortland at Colliers Yard, 5 Bankside Boulevard, Salford, M3 7HD, United Kingdom
Description: With its all-day dining, caring service and sumptuous flavours of the Mediterranean, this is the kind of neighbourhood operation you could quickly find yourself visiting week after week. Part of the city’s Greengate development, its offering starts with brunch, before morphing from a café vibe into a wine bar and restaurant. The evening meze menu is a treat for all fans of Greek cuisine, with the likes of topped flatbreads (the lamb shoulder option is terrific), a supremely comforting chickpea stew and a selection of high-end tinned fish.

Name: Kalteis
Address: Melker Straße 10, Kirchberg an der Pielach, 3204, Austria
Description: This family-run inn in Pielach Valley (Dirndltal) serves flavoursome, highly seasonal cuisine that remains rooted in local tradition. Highlights include game offal ragout with Topfenknödel (curd dumplings), dried venison with cornelian cherry and sheep's yoghurt. Beyond the appealing à la carte selection, there is a more contemporary set menu, which changes frequently. Food is served in cosy, rustic dining rooms or out on the inviting terrace in summer. Comfortable accommodation is also available.

Name: Kaltwassers Wohnzimmer
Description: It is little wonder this restaurant remains so popular. The cosy setting has a "living room" feel, enhanced by charming nostalgic touches that lend the space character. The service is attentive and friendly. The cuisine is modern and ingredient-led… Diners are presented with a "market basket" of the day's featured produce, which forms the basis of a surprise set menu available in three to six courses. For those who prefer to dine al fresco, the Atrium in the inner courtyard is an appealing option with its views into the glass-fronted kitchen.

Name: Kamado
Description: A wood fire blazes in a kamado, or traditional wood-fired stove. Echoing the shop’s name, the meal begins with a bowl of freshly cooked rice straight from the kamado. The style is fusion of Italian and Japanese cuisine, with wood-fired cooking the unifying concept. The hearth is a primaeval scene of meat roasting over glowing embers, yet the flavours are distinctly contemporary. A dish of pasta wraps up the evening. Continuing the theme, the pottery on which the fare is displayed was also fired in a wood-fuelled kiln.

Name: Kamakura
Address: E.C. Building, Greenhills Road, Casuntingan, Mandaue, Cebu, The Philippines
Description: With just nine seats, this intimate soba bar is run by a Japanese chef who has called Cebu home for over 30 years. Named after his hometown, Kamakura promises a convivial counter experience. The thin, fragrant noodles are made to order using Japanese buckwheat flour. Appetisers include tofu, marinated tuna and the speciality of grilled eel bowl. The chef's devotion to tradition shines through in both technique and flavour.

Name: Kamanza Nagashima
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Shoes must be removed
Description: A kappo run by a kind-hearted couple, who pour their hearts into making diners feel welcome — which is why they only cater to one party per evening. The meal begins with congee, or steamed mochi rice topped with seasonal items and then continues to a cup of sake accompanied by an assortment of snacks. In true Kyoto style, the wanmono is a white-miso soup. To close the meal, white rice cooked in clay pots is served — a dish the chef believes best reflects cooking skills; enjoy it with pickled vegetables hand-made by the proprietress.

Name: Kamayan ATL
Address: 5150 Buford Hwy. NE, Doraville, GA, 30340, USA
Description: You'll see the sign, but the crowd out front will signal that you've arrived at Kamayan ATL. Once a pop-up, this place from owners Mia Orino and Carlo Gan has a serious fan base, so reservations are a must. The tables are tight but it's homey, and the busy cadence, coupled with the tropical island decor, adds to the vibe. Tagalog for "by hand," kamayan is the traditional Filipino form of dining. Choose from a menu of family-style dishes, with a good dose of classics mixed with regional items. Lumpia are always a hit, while the sinigang, with tender pork ribs bobbing in a tamarind-based broth, is spot on. Sided by rice, it's a feast unto itself. Halo halo is on offer, but most of the items are packaged from local Filipino bakery, Hapag.

Name: Kamekichi
Description: The restaurant takes its name from the chef's nickname which it why it sounds so friendly. A counter set up at the open kitchen brings the chef closer to his guests. Billing itself as an everyday bistro, it offers a wide range of traditional dishes. Jellied pork, roast lamb and duck confit are also familiar menu items. Lunch offers a choice of prix fixe menus. À la carte items at dinner are best shared.

Name: Kamino
Description: The Zumkeller family have transformed what was once Chämi-Hüsli into this cosy restaurant and tapas bar – the striking fireplace with extended flue after which Kamino is named presides in the middle of the dining area, which has a high ceiling and a round floor plan. The classic and Mediterranean cuisine always has a modern touch and a certain pizazz. Dishes such as roasted sea bass fillet with home-made tagliarini and lobster cream give the tasty tapas a run for their money. The icing on the cake is the charming service provided by owner Stefanie Zumkeller and her team. For an overnight stay, there are three pretty and cosy guestrooms.

Name: Kaminstube
Description: The stylish and elegant dining area boasts the fireplace after which this restaurant is named. Classic and traditional cuisine with international influences is served – small portions are also possible. The terrace with a view of the Ellbachtal is popular in summer.

Name: Kamkinsuk
Address: 2469/7 New Phetchaburi Road, Bang Kapi, Huai Khwang, Bangkok, 10310, Thailand
Description: This restaurant hidden among buildings on New Phetchaburi Road has a calm interior done out with timber, white walls and floaty curtains – it feels like a friend's home. Mildly spiced recipes from the owner's family in Phrae Province are well balanced, kid friendly and include vegetarian options. Go for the rice noodles in clear soup with pungent fingerroot and spices, pork broth and a crunchy and spicy herb dip. Good for solo diners or a quick meal.

Name: Kampun Kai Yang
Address: 94/7 Mu 6, Rochana Road, Phai Ling, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: Opened in 2017, this restaurant serves authentic Isan food in a commercial building on Rochana Road. Air-conditioned and spread across two floors, the casual dining room is decorated with wood panelling and other touches that suggest traditional Thai houses. The skilled chef cooks halal-friendly food following recipes from his grandmother, who is from Nakhon Phanom. The signature dish is Kampun grilled chicken, but their grilled beef is also interesting and worth trying.

Name: Kamín
Description: This contemporary restaurant, whose name is a nod to the chef's mother (Camino), has become a great spot in the Barrio Húmedo. He surprises us by placing the kitchen in the centre of the restaurant, completely open and with a bar around it where we can also eat while watching the chef, Mario Gómez, hard at work. It also features several tables, each with a system of white sheer curtains running from the ceiling to the floor, allowing guests to create spaces with a degree of privacy.Here you will find a modern, daring, international proposal not exempt from powerful flavours (they like pickled foods and fermentations), which sees the light through two tasting menus, one called Origen and another, more complete, called Kamín, both with market and seasonal products. We were especially surprised by the trout, herbs, fennel and lemon. Be sure to visit La Postrería Kamín, the store dedicated to the world of sweet treats in Calle Ancha!

Name: Kan
Description: This single-character surname, Kan, meaning ‘interval’, refers to the chef as intermediary between cuisine and guest. The menu begins with a fruit salad with mashed tofu dressing, to whet the appetite with the tartness of the fruit. Wagyu red meat is served chargrilled or as deep-fried crumbed fillet; potato salad is dressed with fried fat and called ‘Kanfu’ (‘Kan-style’). Technique and playfulness are on full display here.

Name: Kan Coffee Fujifuji
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed
Description: The couple behind the restaurant share a love of ‘kanzake’, warm sake. The proprietress was once a coffee barista, and as both surnames contain the character ‘fuji’ (wisteria), the restaurant was named ‘Kan Coffee Fujifuji’. The nostalgically styled interior evokes the charm of a small neighbourhood restaurant. The owner devotes himself to the cooking, while the proprietress oversees the warming of sake. It occupies a space somewhere between an izakaya and a kappo. The menu is extensive, with inventive touches throughout. The meal concludes with sweets and, true to the house’s name, coffee.

Name: Kan Kiin
Address: 201 Southgate Ave., Daly City, CA, 94015, USA
Description: An unremarkable Daly City strip mall might not be the most obvious spot to find well-crafted Thai cuisine, but putting appearances aside, this cheery little spot delivers on flavor. During the daytime, you’ll find an assortment of fusion brunch items (for example, a take on chicken and waffles that features hat yai, fragrant Southern Thai-style fried chicken) alongside a variety of more typical Thai restaurant fare. The menu includes the usual suspects of stir-fried noodles and curries, as well as less ubiquitous items like spicy clay pot catfish, and across the board special care and bold seasoning sets the cooking apart. For a case in point, try the hand-made curry puffs, which boast an impeccably delicate, flaky crust.

Name: Kandanishikicho Sushi Takaharu
Description: Novel ideas meet time-honoured craftsmanship. The signature snack is cream croquette of tiger prawn, dressed in a reduction of shrimp miso. Deep-fried items are also offered, bringing a satisfaction rarely found at sushi shops. For its part, the sushi is prepared traditionally: brined, marinated or simmered. In part because of his language skills, the chef was tapped to cater a dinner meeting between the Japanese and American leaders.

Name: Kandoo Nippon Restaurant
Description: Contemporary spaces spread across two floors, plus a veranda terrace, make this solid restaurant a great choice for lovers of Japanese specialties – both cooked and raw preparations of meat and fish – executed with a light touch and clean, distinct flavors. At lunch (weekdays only), the kitchen also offers rice bowls and noodle dishes accompanied by various sides. Wine enthusiasts will appreciate the dedicated Champagne section on the wine list.

Name: Kang
Address: Jing Jai Market, 46 Atsadathon Road, Pa Tan, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Opened in 2023, Kang is a fresh addition to Jing Jai Market. It offers a cosy retreat with a laid-back approach to dining, plus a menu that's ideal for sharing the highlights of Indonesian, Malaysian and Thai cuisine with friends. We suggest opting for their signature Nasi Lemak, or one of the bold, aromatic curries. All dishes are made to order, so diners may need to have a little patience while waiting for their delicious meals.

Name: Kang Le Fishball Noodles
Address: Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre, #01-29, Blk 505, Jurong West Street 52, 640505, Singapore
Description: Although the menu also offers laksa, pork balls and fish dumpling soup, the bouncy, flavoursome fishballs with noodles remain its speciality. Choose between wheat or rice noodles, served in a clear broth or tossed in sauces.

Name: Kang's Wanton Noodle
Address: Zion Riverside Food Centre, #06, 70 Zion Road, 247792, Singapore
Description: Alongside wanton or dumpling noodle soup, this stall serves deep-fried wanton and char siew. The springy noodles are best enjoyed with a dollop of chilli sauce, while the wantons encase a tasty filling in their paper-thin skin.

Name: Kanishka
Address: 17-19 Maddox Street, Mayfair, London, W1S 2QH, United Kingdom
Description: Owner Atul Kochhar’s signature style is writ large across the choice of menus at this smart Mayfair restaurant. The Anglo-infused Indian dishes – epitomised by the signature chicken tikka pie – provide plenty of interesting options, alongside a wide selection of traditional recipes from across the Indian regions. There’s a feeling of glamour to the surroundings that would suit a special occasion, with the ground floor the most fun place to sit. The fixed-price menu at lunch and early evening offers the best value for money.

Name: Kanoyama
Address: 175 Second Ave., New York, NY, 10003, USA
Description: Occupying a prized corner location in the heart of East Village since 2010, Chef Nobuyuki Shikanai’s restaurant is a verified veteran of the city’s sushi scene. There are two dining rooms: One is bright with ample table seating where guests order the likes of tempura, sushi rolls and nigiri à la carte, while the other is an intimate counter for a serious, pricey omakase offered on select days of the week. Sake aficionados will be impressed by the list, and diners are even invited to select their own cup from an assortment of options.

Name: Kanpai Classic (Huangpu)
Address: 5F, Bund 5, 20 Guangdong Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: If anything demonstrates how international a restaurant is, it’s this: a Shanghai restaurant from a Taiwanese group, specialising in Australian Wagyu beef that also serves Japanese dishes. Premium Wagyu cuts, along with other meats and seafood, are grilled on charcoal stoves at each table. Caramelised and juicy, the thick-sliced skirt steak strikes a balance between toothsome texture and meaty flavour, with yuzu kosho to cut through the richness.

Name: Kanshin
Description: The name ‘Kanshin’ draws on words that express relaxation and a generous spirit — and the house lives up to its name. With guests always the priority, the space offers calm comfort, warmly attended by bright, welcoming smiles. The meal begins with a selection of smaller dishes, after which guests select what they like from the menu. The chef is a Kyoto man born and bred, so Kyoto vegetables and tofu skins are served and wanmono are light and wholesome. Enjoy ryotei preparations in a way that feels right for you.

Name: Kantine.WTF
Description: This place showcases a winning fresh concept that combines a relaxed, casual vibe with ambitious food. The modern cuisine is based on carefully selected ingredients. One shining example is the "'Dönninghaus & k.wtf calf sweetbread bratwurst' x morels x Aztec Gold potato purée" – the sausage comes from the very same butcher's associated with the song Currywurst by Herbert Grönemeyer.
