Grilled celery with vinegar and miso dressing, bite-sized beef cutlets and crab cream croquettes are popular year-round. Like an Osaka kappo, the chef is happy to adjust salt and portion size to suit customer tastes; like a ryotei, items are beautifully plated on attractive serving-ware.

Name: Kitashinchi Kushikatsu Bon
Description: Kitashinchi Kushikatsu Bon serves skewers of unstinting luxury, including chateaubriand and foie gras. Creative combinations of delicacies, such as ‘pregnant kombu’ (kombu kelp with Pacific herring roe attached) with sea urchin and caviar or name-brand pork with truffles, are especially fun. To ensure a light palate, items are coated in powder-fine breadcrumbs and deep-fried in cottonseed oil. Osaka soul food, enriched with uniquely conceived ingredients.

Name: Kitashinchi Okurano
Description: The menu, incorporating seasonal ingredients when available, changes each month. The head chef, whose passion is cuisine that sparks conversation, respects tradition while sneaking a little playfulness into his menus. Even familiar items are presented with ingenuity: the crab croquettes, for example, are suffused with the aroma of toasted crab shells to add the flavour of baked crab to the creamy fillings. The counter features sleek, modern design and five private rooms are available. Guests are graciously attended by kimono-clad staff.

Name: Kitashinchi Shien
Description: Only prix fixe menus using chicken from Kyushu, prized for its quality, richness and texture, are available. Appetisers and stews, served first, are meticulously prepared, worthy of a much more formal restaurant. Zucchini smothered in Italian cheese suggests snow-clad landscapes of purest white. Chicken wings are lightly scored to make them easier to eat. A serving of white rice brings the meal to a close.

Name: Kitashinchi Yumiba Shinnosuke
Description: The owner-chef prizes nothing more than the temperature and aroma of his cooking. All dishes are prepared and served fresh, so counter seating is arranged around the preparation surface. In a twist, the sashimi is served with unconventional dressings such as nori seaweed soy sauce and monkfish liver with ponzu. Char-grilled beef and, in winter, shabu-shabu of bear and boar are prepared in front of customers. To finish, a selection of takikomi-gohan, rice seasoned with various ingredients, allows diners to enjoy comparing flavours.

Name: Kitchen Library
Description: A great team of two, Daniela and Udo Knörlein run this place together - she looks after the guests cordially, while he cooks up the international "Kleine Dinger" set menu. Available with either four or five courses, an eight-course version for sharing is also possible. The characterful decor is reminiscent of a library: rustic-style charm and over 600 collector's items related to cookery.

Name: Kitchen Ter(re)
Description: In his third establishment devoted to pasta, William Ledeuil crafts a kaleidoscope of pared-back tastes and flavours, starring high-flying creations from spelt, durum wheat, einkorn or tender Roussillon wheat by artisan Roland Feuillas. Chef Julien Jéquier (with stints at Le V and L’Écrin) orchestrates a balanced score in which Asian notes and fresh herbs play major supporting roles. From the exquisitely laid tables to the plating, balance is the key word, as is illustrated by his dish of coquillettes (small pasta shells) made out of fresh milled khorasan wheat flour with chicken wings, Taggiasche olives, spinach and Thai broth! Vibrant, lively and the epitome of charming!

Name: Kiti Panit
Address: 19 Tha Phae Road, Chang Khlan, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50100, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Turning their great-great-grandparents’ 1880s mansion into a restaurant, Kiti Panit’s owners decided to create an updated take on traditional Lanna cuisine. The results include intense and complex hang le, or northern Thai curry, and savoury grilled chicken salad with coriander. The stir-fried beef with prickly ash is spicy, aromatic and wonderfully tender, while the hang le mu is rich, full of flavour and perfect with rice.

Name: Kitten Deli
Description: The atmosphere here is friendly and vibrant, both on the terrace, with tables laid out on the street in front of the restaurant, and inside, where diners are seated at small tables (no tablecloths here), and old floorboards, panelled walls and a counter make for a traditional tavern-like atmosphere. The restaurant serves vegetarian Levante cuisine, including dishes that are perfect for sharing, such as hummus with roasted cauliflower or shakshuka. The delicious pita (flatbread) and the aromatic challah (yeast-leavened bread) come fresh from the oven – both can also be purchased to take home.

Name: Kiyamachi Ran
Description: This sushi kappo is run by the third-generation owner-chef, who previously worked at Kitcho, and his mother. From below the ledge, water flows to rinse the fingers, stirring fond memories of Showa-era times. Orders are placed old-style too: patrons choose as they converse with the chef. Among the snacks, a favourite is sashimi of the fatty cut of tuna near the collarbone. Grated daikon is wrapped in fatty tuna to create a clean finish. Pickled nigiri oozes the culture of Kyoto.

Name: Kiyomi
Description: An elegant entrance with reception and an open kitchen welcome guests to this vibrant Asian restaurant. Drawing on experience gained in Japan and China, talented chef Vid Nikolić offers a rich and dynamic cuisine, spanning dim sum and robata grill, tempura, sashimi, gunkan, temari, and hand rolls, all prepared with authentic techniques and in full respect of Asian tradition. The modern, pleasantly fashionable dining room invites lingering at the bar, ideal for enjoying one of the many cocktails or a wine selection from the extensive list.

Name: Kiyosumi Takahara
Description: Kyoto cuisine has left its mark on chef Shimon Takahara. Like his father before him, he apprenticed as a chef in Kyoto, devoting himself to his gastronomical studies. Guided by the teachings of his mentor, Takahara dedicates his heart and soul to creating dishes that offer a sense of the seasons and reverberate in the senses. Each day’s appetiser, prepared from what is most seasonal, shows this devotion. In spring, expect dishes laden with the colours and aromas of daily variations such as bamboo shoots and asparagus.

Name: Kiyosuminosato AWA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Shoes must be removed
Description: Seasonal crops are lined up on the zataku. Yamato vegetables and vegetables from various countries spruce up the plates. The Miuras visit farms and grow the seeds they collect. The harvested vegetables are used in local dishes they learned how to prepare in each area. You’ll enjoy items grilled on a ceramic plate in spring and summer and soy milk nabe in autumn and winter together with colourful takiawase. The menu makes you feel like you’re strolling around a market garden.

Name: Kjun
Address: 334 Lexington Ave., New York, NY, 10016, USA
Description: Chef Jae Jung’s Kjun brings together Korean and Cajun cooking through a perspective shaped by her Korean heritage and her experience working under the legendary Leah Chase at Dooky Chase in New Orleans. What began as a small neighborhood operation has grown into a larger Murray Hill restaurant centered on a thoughtful and approachable take on the intersection of these two culinary traditions. The menu combines Southern comfort and Korean flavors through dishes that reinterpret familiar ingredients and preparations without losing sight of either influence. Rice dishes, fried specialties, banchan and Louisiana-inspired classics sit comfortably alongside one another, creating a meal that feels distinctive without being forced.

Name: Klai Lib
Address: 126 Bangsaenlang Road, Saen Suk, Mueang Chon Buri, Chon Buri, 20130, Thailand
Description: Attracting younger diners, this eatery has a reputation for fresh, affordable Thai seafood of uncompromising quality. The generous portions with sweet seasonings are good for sharing; the deep-fried mackerel with fish sauce is a must for its crispy skin and tender meat.

Name: Klang Na Pla Khao
Address: 5 Mu 9, Nong Tamlueng, Phan Thong, Chon Buri, 20160, Thailand
Description: This country-style restaurant serves up a splendid array of Isan dishes and Eastern Thai specialties from land and sea. The highlight is a spicy stir-fry with an original curry paste recipe from Chanthaburi province, capturing the authentic essence of Thai cuisine. There's no compromise on bold, genuine Thai flavours. The tranquil outdoor setting affords views of lush green rice fields, and the relaxed atmosphere makes it perfect for friend and family gatherings.

Name: Klaver
Description: Klaver is proof that high-flying cuisine need not be incompatible with a friendly vibe. In this vein and in keeping with the establishment’s playful character, chef Korneel Verhulst often kicks off your meal with piping hot French fries and a spicy caper-spiked mayonnaise. The youthful chef shines the spotlight on first-class produce, with the odd Japanese lilt and a clear fondness for textbook Gallic classics. An example: a rich, creamy foyot sauce adds depth and peps to juicy guinea fowl, while your coffee may well be flanked by a small pancake, in tribute to the region. Klaver adds a brand-new lively dimension to fine dining, embodied by Grace, your charming hostess.

Name: Klebers
Description: Whether you are seated in the pleasantly bright interior or on the delightful terrace in summer, you can look forward to friendly and charming service as well as international and regional cuisine made from excellent produce. There are various set menus (including a vegetarian one) to choose from, plus a selection of dishes à la carte. The restaurant is housed in the tasteful Kleber Post hotel.

Name: Klei
Description: Inconspicuously located on the historic Grand Place, this cosy restaurant has a somewhat mysterious feel to it. At the helm, an experienced duo showcase their talents. Sommelier Carl Couvreur bowls diners over with his astute recommendations, while chef Jonathan Devogel delivers haute cuisine in which intricate sauces and influences from around the globe bring the flavours to life. Though his creations can be elaborate, they are ultimately defined by their boldness. Think marinated weever as the main ingredient in an aromatic dish with fig and celery in various guises. The short menu never fails to intrigue!

Name: Kleine Flamme
Description: In his small open-view kitchen situated in the centre of this restaurant, chef Bacher Burkhard develops his vision of fusion cuisine with energy and precision, combining flavours from Italy and the Alto Adige with Asian spices and techniques to create delicious and imaginative dishes. His tuna tataki is superb, seasoned with salty lemon oil and accompanied by intriguing bitter herbs that (as Professor Montanari has noted in a recent book) are particularly popular with Italians. The chef’s wife Annelies works front of house, where she looks after guests in a friendly and professional manner.

Name: Klinker
Description: It's no surprise that this spot in central Harvestehude draws such a crowd, with its trendy urban design, lively atmosphere and floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the street's activities – plus terrace tables available in summer. The food is predominantly vegetarian. The establishment's commitment to ecology is reflected in the exclusive use of regional ingredients, primarily sourced from Demeter farms. Fermenting and preserving are also part of their practice – with about 3 000 jars of preserves in stock, their dedication speaks for itself! Some jars are also used as decoration in the restaurant. Tip: The sharing option allows you to sample various dishes. Highlights include ‘Aubergine, tomato, miso, nectarines & parsley’ or ‘Potato, lovage, kombu, cucumber & mustard seeds’.

Name: Klostergasthaus Löwen - Gaststube
Description: This is Pascal Schwarz's second restaurant on the estate of the former 12th century monastery. In addition to the gourmet restaurant, he also has his ‘Gaststube’ in the historic monastery inn in the St. Urban district - also on the first floor. Modern interiors have been attractively integrated into the traditional setting - on the terrace behind the house you can enjoy the good cuisine of Pascal and his team as well as the view of the imposing monastery church, which is well worth a visit. The cuisine is regional, seasonal and international. In the evening, there is a nice selection of dishes ranging from ‘pastrami burgers’ to ‘pink roast duck breast from France’ and ‘vegetarian carbonara-style mushroom risotto’.

Name: Klostergasthaus Löwen - Negral
Description: With the ‘Negral’ and the ‘Gaststube’, there are two concepts under one roof here, in the ‘Klostergasthaus Löwen’ dating from 1870 on the grounds of the imposing former Cistercian monastery dating from 1194 in the St. Urban district. On the first floor, Pascal Schwarz and his team offer modern, classically based cuisine in the form of a surprise menu, including vegetarian options, in the chic little gourmet parlour ‘Negral’. The six, eight or ten courses are prepared using excellent seasonal, regional and international produce. The terrace offers a beautiful view of the monastery church. Tip: In good weather, enjoy your aperitif outside in the lounge or round off the evening in the cigar lounge in the vaulted cellar.

Name: Klub Književnika by Branko Kisic
Description: The youthful chef of this culinary and cultural landmark, popular with the locals and tourists alike, has been at the helm since 2019. Diners can choose to eat in a winter garden or in the dining room, often accompanied by live music during the colder months. The menu showcases a patriotic Serbian lineup, including the Krempita dessert that has been served here since the restaurant opened in 1946, and other Serbian specialties (there’s a 25-minute wait for the savoury Gibanica dish), with the occasional interesting, personalised touch and a focus on plating. Since it opened at the end of the Second World War, the ‘Writers’ Club’ has been a magnet for authors, journalists and politicians and it continues to host cultural events, including exhibitions and concerts. Sustainability issues, such as reducing food waste, are at the core of the ethos of this quintessentially traditional establishment.

Name: Kluth
Description: In the heart of the Ehrenfeld district, Hannes Radeck and Kevin Rademacker (formerly of Cologne's Ox & Klee) have struck out on their own. The ambitions of this chef-owner pair are evident in delicately composed, creative modern dishes, such as "Potato brioche, Comté, celery, grapes" or "Bresse chicken, hazelnut, leek". As an alternative to the à la carte selection, there is a six-course surprise menu dubbed "Et kütt wie et kütt" ("It is what it is"), available in a meat/fish or vegetarian version. Seasonality and organic produce are central to the concept, with many fermented and pickled ingredients being put to use – preserving jars serve as decorative touches throughout the trendy, Nordic-minimalist dining area. Seating options include standard tables, high tables, and spots at the service counter. The pleasingly relaxed, attentive and assured service also contributes to the appealing atmosphere. Don't forget to book.

Name: Knausbira Stüble
Description: This family-run business in the Hedelfingen district has been renowned for its fine cuisine for many years and is popular with older and younger diners alike. It all began in 1985 with Susanne and Hendrik Schallmeir, and now their son Gabriel and his wife Lia – the second generation – have joined the team. In the small open kitchen, father and son work like a well-oiled machine, upholding Swabian culinary traditions while embracing inspiration from modern international cuisine. Their menu ranges from classics such as Zwiebelrostbraten (braised beef with onions and gravy) and Kässpätzle, to Kalbsleber Berliner Art (veal liver with onions and apple), or skrei with fregola sarda, Mediterranean vegetables and cavolo nero. Tip: Purchase house-made Maultaschen (Swabian pockets) to enjoy at home. In keeping with the traditional roots of the cuisine, this place oozes rustic charm and has a really cosy atmosphere. The leafy terrace is lovely in summer.

Name: Knepp Wilding Kitchen
Address: Knepp Estate, Worthing Road, Dial Post, Horsham, RH13 8NQ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The Knepp Estate is such a special place; from a dog walk around the gorgeous natural grounds to browsing produce in the farm shop, you could easily spend most of your day here. At the heart of it all is an ethos of rewilding, something which drives the menus at its restaurant housed inside an 18th-century barn. Here, the cooking is overtly seasonal and often uses ingredients from the Estate; try to kick off your meal with one of the fine flatbreads and punchy wild garlic butter. They are mostly open just for lunch, with some BBQ evenings in the summer.

Name: Knife & Spoon
Address: The Ritz-Carlton Orlando, Grande Lakes, 4012 Central Florida Pkwy., Orlando, FL, 32837, USA
Description: Located within the Ritz-Carlton, Grande Lakes, this restaurant from Chef John Tesar cuts an impressive figure. It is a vast, modern space sporting beachy hues, weathered wood, and a well-stocked bar. The dimly lit dining room is front and center, while an open kitchen resides in the back. In-house, dry-aged steaks from 44 Farms, inventive pastas like cacio e pepe made with ube noodles, and top-shelf seafood give diners plenty to choose from. The kitchen is quick to highlight local farmers who supply a range of produce, though no matter where you look, decadence and indulgence are on full display. An adventurous cocktail list and an attentive service team round out the experience.

Name: Knife Pleat
Address: 3333 S. Bristol St., Ste. 3001, Costa Mesa, CA, 92626, USA
Description: This elegant little operation, set on the third floor of South Coast Plaza amidst fashionable stores, has plenty of charm. With a gleaming open kitchen edged by a chef’s counter, plus a secluded patio, this is a spot to dine in style. Chef Tony Esnault offers his personal take on classic French cuisine, tinged with international influences, offered at both lunch and dinner as prix fixe menus of varying length. Open with small bites, before proceeding to more substantial courses like steelhead trout with fennel and rainbow chard, or barley risotto with chestnut, parmesan and brassicas, before ending on a sweet note with composed desserts like a meringue shell decked out with roasted pineapple, lime and toasted coconut cream.

Name: Knox Bistro
Description: There’s an experienced team of French émigrés behind this bright and breezy bistro and it shows in all departments. This may be a French bistro—and one that’s a perfect fit for sophisticated Knox Street—but it doesn’t overdo the Gallic decoration. Instead, it concentrates on offering authentic and satisfying classics that’ll have you dreaming of weekends in Montmartre in no time. Lunch sees a simpler menu but one that includes a fine rillettes de poisson and a selection of oysters. At dinner all the French bistro favorites appear, like lapin à la moutarde or canard à l'orange; and for dessert, the kitchen really shows its skills with a textbook Paris-Brest that you won’t want to share with anyone.

Name: Ko Chia Pen Se
Address: 28 Puxin Street, Beipu District, Hsinchu County, Taiwan
Description: Since 1999, diners have been coming to this no-frills joint for black pepper duck, a revamped traditional banquet classic. The owner seals in the juices with complicated steaming steps and imbues the bird with rich peppery aromas using a secret marinade. Other home-style Hakkanese dishes may look unassuming, but are all meticulously prepared. Come with a posse as the potion sizes are generous. Reservations recommended on weekends.

Name: Ko Kia
Address: 602 Mu 10, Khok Kruat, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30280, Thailand
Description: For over 20 years, Ko Kia has been drawing the lunchtime crowds for its boat noodles. The bold, aromatic pork and beef broths are enriched with a touch of blood for depth, but the beef stands out. The clear soup is lighter, but full of flavour and the natural sweetness of daikon.

Name: Ko Seng
Address: 226/9 Mu 1, Soi Mae Nam 5, Mae Nam, Ko Samui, 84330, Thailand
Description: Prioritising flavour over fuss, this modest spot has championed Thai and Southern Thai seafood for over 50 years. Fresh local catch is cooked to order, delivering bold, soothing tastes in highlights such as black pepper crab, stir-fried prawns and traditional steamed fish. Fairly priced, generous portions thrive in a simple, air-conditioned, no-frills interior, with the Southern yellow curry of giant sea catfish roes and taro stems proving truly irresistible.

Name: Ko-sometsuke 2K
Address: 156 boulevard de la Plage, Arcachon, 33120, France
Description: Originally from Cambodia, the Khong family settled in Arcachon, and now they are the ones inviting diners on a journey: from China and Japan to Southeast Asia, using regional ingredients. Don't miss the dim sum, the real stars of the show, wrapped in a remarkably fine dough.

Name: Kobe Bistro
Address: 23C Ton Duc Thang Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 710000, Vietnam
Description: Owner-chef David Thai spent time in France, together with stints in Dubai, Spain and various Asian countries. Formerly a Japanese produce trader and culinary consultant, he makes the most of his connections and expertise in this bistro. On top of French classics such as bouillabaisse and duck leg confit, the menu also features a line-up of marbled Kobe Wagyu steaks, including Bushu Oguma A4 and Satsuma A5+, served with a range of sauces.

Name: Kockeriet
Description: In a characterful 17C former grain warehouse, owned by Malmö-born TV chef Tareq Taylor, a young and talented team prepare well-balanced contemporary dishes with great precision. Scandinavian produce is at its heart, with some coming from the kitchen garden. The timbered dining room is relaxed and inviting, the service friendly, and the drinks pairings well-conceived.

Name: Kodawari (Salcedo)
Address: 121 L.P. Leviste Street, Adamson Centre, Salcedo Village, Makati - Metro Manila, The Philippines
Description: This snug eatery with a vibrant atmosphere has won over a youthful crowd with its take on Japanese home cooking. Their gyudon is the ultimate comfort food: a rice bowl with juicy marbled beef, a silky soft-boiled egg and crisp local greens, which come together with a sweet-salty sauce and fragrant rice. The bright space is welcoming, whether for solo dining or a meal with friends. Pair each bowl with a refreshing drink. It is well worth the short wait!

Name: Kogel Mogel
Description: There’s a chic, retro quality to this lively brasserie in Kraków’s Old Town, which sports several dining rooms – including one with a vaulted brick ceiling – plus an enclosed garden terrace. It's a smart place, with the menu bringing modern updates to classic Krakovian dishes, as well as those from wider Poland. This is simple, satisfying cooking with a generous touch that no doubt pleases their regulars. For dessert, the hot apple pie made with Polish Szara Reneta apples is not to be missed.

Name: Kogo
Description: Set slightly apart from the centre but easily reached by car, Kogo – “cook” in the Istrian dialect – welcomes guests in a modern and carefully finished setting: to the right of the entrance lies the elegant wine shop, to the left the restaurant, with its contemporary lines and design accents. The cuisine, firmly anchored in tradition, is presented with a current approach: alongside a generous selection of local and non-local charcuterie and cheeses, meat dishes predominate, with occasional forays into seafood. A sound wine list, available on tablet, completes the offering.

Name: Koh Lipe Thai Kitchen
Description: Koh Lipe stands out among its Chinatown neighbors for its lively atmosphere and its authentic southern Thai cooking. Set over two floors and boasting a popular terrace, this place just feels fun, a mood buoyed by the friendly young staff.The kitchen dishes out regional specialties that deliver heat and flavor in spades. Coconut green curry beef with plantain and stink bean is a classic bowl of piping hot, delicious comfort. The chef's specials are always a sure bet, but for those diners who may be less familiar with Thai food, the noodle dishes are a perfect introduction. Don’t worry if there is a line—they turn around tables swiftly, so you won’t be waiting long to bite into those meaty prawn tails served with a kicky lime-chili dip.

Name: Koh Thai Kitchen
Address: Four Seasons Resort Koh Samui, 219 Mu 5, Ang Thong, Ko Samui, 84140, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Koh Thai Kitchen is located on a hilltop within the Four Seasons Hotel. The restaurant's alfresco dining areas sport a rustic style. Diners can enjoy southern and central Thai dishes made with premium ingredients such as local seafood, Australian lamb and Wagyu beef. All of which while breathing in the fresh air as you admire the drop-dead vista of sprawling jungle and blue sea dotted with nearby islands, as you snap the dramatic Instagram-perfect sunsets.

Name: Kohaku
Description: On a street running parallel to the celebrated Via Vittorio Veneto, Kohaku brings the elegance of Japanese kaiseki cuisine – the country’s haute gastronomy – to the capital. The menu offers a broad range of classic and traditional dishes, with quality at its heart: impeccable ingredients, precise knife work and carefully composed presentations. The freshness of the fish is evident in the many raw dishes, among which – according to the Inspector – the scallop and amberjack tartare stands out, mixed with cubes of avocado and dressed with a delicious ponzu sauce and sesame oil. The meats, too, are of notable quality. Depending on personal taste, guests may choose the celebrated gyoza dumplings, tempura, noodles or the many charcoal-grilled preparations, to name only part of the offering. For those seeking total immersion, the “Kohaku kaiseki” tasting menu is also available at dinner: an eight-course itinerary dedicated to lovers of great Japanese cuisine.

Name: Kohout NA VÍNĚ
Address: Dům umění města Brna, Malinovského nám. 652/2, Brno, 60200, Czechia
Description: This charming modern restaurant on the premises of the House of Arts is a cosy setting. The names of artists who, through donations, have contributed to the upkeep of the establishment are displayed on the ceiling. Wine plays an important role here, as the eye-catching floor-to-ceiling wine store suggests. As well as two tasting menus and a vegetarian set menu, there is an à la carte selection. The terrific wine list focuses on the Czech Republic, Slovenia and Hungary. They also use the Coravin wine system. Tip: Be sure to reserve, especially on weekends – they get fully booked quickly.

Name: Koi Japanese Cuisine
Address: 600 Pacific Coast Hwy., Unit 100, Seal Beach, CA, 90740, USA
Description: Helmed by chefs have a century of experience under their collective belts, Koi Japanese Cuisine may have a familiar name, but this spot stands firmly on its own. It's not hip or trendy, but it is beloved by regulars who are known by their first names and have a clear rapport with the chefs. Though it has history and heart, these regulars are here for more than just a warm welcome. From orange clam and kampachi to Kumamoto and Kusshi oysters, the sashimi lineup is impressive. A tempura of zucchini flowers stuffed with scallops serves as a culinary intermission between the sashimi and nigiri, which presents eight selections with a variety of flourishes ranging from seabass with a dab of yuzu kosho to scallop topped with uni.

Name: Koinè
Description: Whether you dine in the modern dining room at this centrally located palazzo or in the small courtyard in fine weather, Alberto Buratti offers a choice of tasting menus (including the vegetarian “1MQ d’orto”), alongside a concise à la carte. His cuisine includes a combination of local dishes (from classic risottos to breaded veal) and more creative fare.

Name: Koiné
Description: Koiné’s name refers to a variant of the Greek language once used in Ancient Greece. Here, the cuisine has returned to the origins and roots of Mediterranean cooking, working in tandem with the culinary traditions of Andalucia and with a style that has adapted to contemporary tastes. Chef Juanlu Parra has previously worked in the R&D department of the Dani García Group – a detail that is obvious on the menu. If you’re looking for a standout dish, try their award-winning aged picaña steak tartare, with creamy smoked eel on marrow and warm croissant.

Name: Koizen
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the Gothenburg Natural History Museum and Slottsskogen park, is this 22-seater Japanese restaurant comprising a counter and two high-level tables. It’s owned and run by John and Teresa Chu, who offer an omakase experience encompassing appetisers, sashimi, nigiri, aburi nigiri, soup and dessert – as well as monthly special events featuring the likes of bluefin tuna or Wagyu beef. John carefully crafts the dishes in front of you, presenting them along with an explanation of their make-up, while Alven recommends Japanese drinks, sakes by the glass and even sake pairings.

Name: Kojacha
Description: Kojacha—named to reflect the convergence of Japanese cuisine crafted by a Korean chef (KO), Japanese technique (JA), and Chinese influences (CHA)—offers a dining experience that deliberately defies convention. The courses alternate seamlessly between Japanese and Chinese dishes, from abalone salad presented in an imperial-era soap dish to Osaka-style hassun. Chefs personally present each course at the table, adding narrative and theatrical flair, while the restaurant’s all–private-room layout ensures an intimate and immersive experience throughout.

Name: Koji
Description: Japanese teppanyaki cooking is nothing short of theatrical with its spectacular flames, so be sure to bag a front-row seat at the counter. Before your eyes, chef Koji Hashimoto carefully prepares premium ingredients. His elegant brand of craftsmanship, honed by years of experience in prestigious kitchens, never overwhelms the produce with culinary gimmicks. Both fish and meat (a Normandy beef fillet, for example) are cooked just right, and enhanced by impeccable sauces (eg white miso and sherry vinegar sauce on an assortment of grilled fish). Traditional Japanese decor dominated by wood.

Name: Koji
Address: 12 Majoribanks Street, Mount Victoria, Wellington, 6011, New Zealand
Description: After honing his skills in Australia, the chef opened Koji in an emerging foodie neighbourhood, espousing a unique Asian cuisine that fuses Chinese, Japanese and Thai traditions. His creative dishes strike a balance between sweet, sour, salty and spicy elements. His flavoursome yellow curry beef doughnut is accompanied by curry mayo and pickled daikon that cut through the richness. The nine-course "Just feed me" menu offers the ultimate overview.

Name: Kojin 2.0
Address: 804 Ponce de Leon, Coral Gables, FL, 33134, USA
Description: Chefs Pedro and Katherine Mederos are back with Kojin 2.0 and it's not just the Coral Gables location that's new. This iteration's contemporary menu has clear Japanese influences and whether you swing for the tasting menus or order a la carte, expect bold cooking that takes risks while delivering approachable dishes. Foie toast—rye bread topped with a round of goose liver ganache and a dot of strawberry preserves—captures the culinary spirit of this place, where you may encounter equally creative dishes like bone marrow panna cotta finished with a stunning house-made coffee shoyu; a savory-sweet goat cheese cavatelli in a thick butternut squash sauce; or a creamsicle ice cream sandwich.

Name: Kokkari Estiatorio
Address: 200 Jackson St., San Francisco, CA, 94111, USA
Description: Zeus himself would be satisfied after a soul-warming meal at this Greek favorite, which serves up San Francisco chic with a side of old-world taverna hospitality. Once you’re seated at the bar or settled near one of its toasty fireplaces, the thoughtful staff will cater to your every whim.The intoxicating scent of caramelizing meats and lemon will certainly whet your appetite for what's to come. Kokkari's menu leans heavily on the wood grill and rotisserie, which turns out such simple delights as bizelosalata — spring peas topped with olive oil, feta and scallions — followed by the eternally classic chicken souvlaki. For dessert, stay traditional and order the walnut and honey baklava with vanilla-praline ice cream.

Name: Koko
Address: 24 N. Orlando Ave., Cocoa Beach, FL, 32931, USA
Description: Concrete floors and a black ceiling lend a contemporary-cool vibe to this small space located a few blocks from the ocean in the center of Cocoa Beach, while Chef Daniel Joseph Penovich's kitchen is a quirky mashup of Japanese styles that doesn't take itself too seriously. The omakase is a splurge (available by reservation) but bento boxes at lunch are a great value. Some of the strongest dishes include gambas al Japón, featuring tail-on binchotan-grilled Canaveral white shrimp with crispy garlic, as well as the Everything (Everywhere, All At Once) roll with its riot of ingredients and distinctive flavor. Vegan Japanese curry and French onion soup-inspired ramen are among the hearty entrees, and the sake selection is worth perusing.

Name: Kokovin
Description: Warm and stylish, Kokovin boasts a superb garden patio, but above all, it is the scene of a successful family adventure. The cheerful lady of the house, Peggy, greets guests warmly, plying them with insightful wine tips along the way, while her hubbie, Dominique, and son, Francis, conjure up recipes that range from modern to classical. In addition to textbook prepared sole, you may sample generous shrimp fritters that melt in the mouth and duckling served with piping hot fries, together with a host of more unusual textures. Consider us smitten!

Name: Kol
Address: 23 Ponsonby Road, Grey Lynn, Auckland, 1011, New Zealand
Description: This cosy, peach-pink corner house is hard to miss. The menu revolves around the traditional Indian wood-fire stove, or chulha, which lends breads, vegetables and meat subtle smokiness and handsome char marks. In addition to Indian classics, there are plenty of creative recipes with eclectic influences. Try the BBQ broccoli in char siu glaze, or lamb seekh taco – a juicy ground lamb skewer slathered in pickled chilli mayo and wrapped in flatbread.

Name: Kolm
Description: Here in the natural surroundings of the Waldviertel region, you can enjoy not only the beautiful view of the surrounding area but also the ambitious cuisine of Michael Kolm and his team. The dishes are rooted in the region but with a cosmopolitan edge, as demonstrated by creations such as veal fillet, ravioli, wild broccoli, and hamachi, rutabaga, avocado. You can choose between the set menus – "Bärentrail Menu" and vegetarian "Animal-Friendly Menu" – and à la carte options. The service team is pleasant, cordial and competent – the first appetisers are plated in the restaurant itself. The bright, friendly ambience is aptly described as "casual". In winter, the fireplace is lit for a cosy feel. Interesting fact: The Bärenwald bear sanctuary run by the Four Paws association is right next door. Considering staying overnight? There are five lodges a little way down, set in the greenery.

Name: Kolm Sõsarat
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park
Description: Three Sisters run this small, remotely set restaurant and each has their role to play: Kerti does the cooking, Triin looks after the service and Kadri tends to the kitchen garden. The playful set menu is a showcase of the area, featuring top quality produce from their garden and farm – such as in the country-style mushroom, potato and sauerkraut – while superb honey from their father’s long-established hives is celebrated in desserts such as honey, apple and milk with sea buckthorn. This is a truly special place where the passion of the team is palpable, as they go above and beyond to care for every guest.

Name: Kolonialen Bislett
Description: Close to the stadium you’ll find this popular neighbourhood bistro, which was previously a grocer’s shop for nearly 80 years. The concise, keenly priced menu includes oysters, cured meats and wholesome Norwegian classics that have been brought up-to-date. There’s a diverse selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Koma
Address: Paseo de los Rosales 48, Collado Mediano, 28450, Spain
Description: Part of the La Torre Box Art hotel, Koma occupies a glass-fronted pavilion with access via the garden. It is skilfully run by chef Álex Marugán, a particularly talented cook (he also holds a Bib Gourmand in Madrid, at Tres por Cuatro). Here the cuisine strives to be more essential, direct and conscious, giving greater prominence to the grill without closing the door on some good stews and stocks. The idea is that, with honesty at the core, fire becomes the language spoken here, with a contemporary stamp and the possibility of crossing borders to encounter far-away flavours.

Name: Komatsu Cucina Italiana
Description: Shinji Ishida refurbished a restaurant formerly run by his grandmother, whose family name lives on in the shop’s name. The chef feels affection for his roots and home region. Vital to each prix fixe meal is the ambience of the season. He creates dishes that remind us we’re in Kyoto through combinations of fresh seasonal ingredients. The course features two pasta dishes—one using dry noodles and the other, handmade. Dishes are cooked and seasoned just right to express the flavours of ingredients directly and honestly.

Name: Komboi
Address: 28, Lane 270, Section 1, Dunhua South Road, Da’an District, Taipei, 10685, Taiwan
Description: Komboi is the homophone of the Taiwanese phrase for ‘empty plates’, as the chef hopes his guests enjoy their meals down to the last bite. Modern dishes embody his novel ideas, finessed by techniques acquired when travelling in France. While a shorter set menu is offered at lunch, we recommend the unabridged ‘experience’ menu to best appreciate his vision. The minimalist room boasts warm hues, dark wood furniture and ribbed glass pendant lamps.

Name: Kommod
Description: This popular restaurant serves a set menu – you can decide to have five or six courses and whether or not you want fish and meat. Salzburg caviar, cheese from the trolley and wine pairings are available upon request. The kitchen places great emphasis on carefully selected, high-quality ingredients, with vegetables grown locally. The chef personally presents and explains each dish to diners. Temporary art exhibitions make for an extra point of interest.

Name: Konijnenvoer
Description: (Konijnenvoer moved to Kerkstraat 19 in Arnhem) Plant-based dishes were long thought of as rabbit food (konijnenvoer in Dutch). Thanks to places like this, those days are over. Demian Parasmo and his team bring together local ingredients and creative ideas, often infused with influences from the Mediterranean and further afield. Fermented flavours and playful textures bring each plate to life. Oyster mushrooms from Arnhem, for example, are fermented in shio koji and barbecued, yielding a rich umami taste. These are served with a yeast crumble, a hazelnut cream and wild onion tops braised in Tomasu soy sauce. As for the setting, old world-charm is artfully fused with contemporary design. For a more low-key alternative, head to the antipasti bar at the front. A treat for food lovers!

Name: Konno
Description: Smitten with the cuisine of Kyoto, the proprietor broadened his gastronomic repertoire with stints at a ryotei and kappo. He makes the extra effort to bring his guests the aroma and flavour of fresh-from-the-kitchen goodness. The preparation area is adjacent to the fry stations, minimising the distance food has to travel. ‘Takiawase’, a delicately simmered assortment of vegetables, brings out the native flavours of each ingredient, attesting to the proprietor’s experience. The friendly proprietress engages with guests, supporting her husband as he focuses on his cuisine.

Name: Konnubio
Address: Via dei Conti 8 r, Florence, 50123, Italy
Description: An informal yet polished setting where the kitchen draws on Italian flavors, reinterpreting them through a modern lens. Beyond the à la carte offerings, tasting menus dedicated to land, sea, or garden guide guests through dishes crafted with technique and contemporary sensitivity. Among the highlights: cuttlefish tagliatelle with its own ragù, mussels, and potato cream; braised pork saddle with squash millefeuille, green peppercorn sauce, and peanut cream; and the “moretta” from Fano served with coffee and rum gelato, indulgent and impeccable. Alongside a well-calibrated wine selection, the cocktails stand out, prepared with notable care. Be sure to book well in advance for the romantic table on the staircase, one of the most coveted seats in the house.

Name: Konoba Boba
Description: A gastronomic landmark on the island of Murter, gateway to the Incoronate archipelago and connected to the mainland by a small bridge. A konoba (tavern) in name but elegant in execution, with an intimate dining room complemented by outdoor seating in warmer months. Mediterranean cuisine in which every detail receives careful attention: the fish is impeccably fresh, the cooking classical, yet the overall effect is modern and convincing. Standout dishes include traditional fare such as maništrun of chickpeas served in the typical terracotta pot, an authentic homage to home cooking. The pastry program merits special mention, with tempting desserts beautifully presented: don’t miss the Coffee and Chocolate, truly outstanding. The wine list, while not extensive, is well-structured, interesting, and approachable, perfectly aligned with the restaurant’s spirit.

Name: Konoba Buščina
Description: Set among the countryside at the edge of Umag, in the village of Bušćina just a short distance from the Slovenian border, this rustic and charming trattoria can boast over thirty years of history. The cooking is curated and genuine, celebrating local ingredients from both land and sea – from langoustines to Boškarin beef, from Istrian prosciutto to truffle. The atmosphere is warm and familiar, with attentive and professional service. The dishes are accompanied by excellent wines and selected oils.

Name: Konoba Campanelo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: It’s not easy to find Konoba Campanelo: from the center of Šibenik, it takes about thirty minutes of winding roads, straightaways, and a brief path leading to a quiet village nestled in nature. But the journey is rewarded by young, straightforward cooking founded on quality ingredients, technique, and a modern yet tradition-respecting approach. Be sure to reserve in advance for a dish prepared in the peka, the ancient Croatian technique of slow-cooking meat, fish, or vegetables under a terracotta or cast-iron dome covered with hot embers: an authentic taste of times past.

Name: Konoba Fetivi
Description: A very popular restaurant in the city, which is well worth a visit for its traditional cuisine served in a simple yet beautifully kept dining room. The menu features unpretentious Mediterranean fish dishes and traditional meat specialities, with ingredients purchased fresh from the local market every day. Among the desserts, don’t miss the delicious dried fig and walnut cake. The friendly welcome from all the staff is an added attraction!

Name: Konoba Griblja
Description: The restaurant is located in a picturesque town near Zadar, a short walk from the seafront. The cuisine is inspired by Dalmatian tradition with a modern twist, paying special attention to the seasonality and freshness of ingredients, and the offerings range from typical regional specialities to classic grilled dishes, through fish dishes and more refined preparations. Try the smoked swordfish carpaccio served with barley, cranberries, and timut pepper or the tagliatelle with shrimp, sun-dried tomatoes, and pistachio powder. The wine list favours selected labels of the best Croatian production. The setting is warm and quaint, with stone walls decorated with pieces of local crafts, but in summer opt for the pleasant terrace.

Name: Konoba Kala
Description: A small gastronomic treasure, elegant and refined, hidden among the picturesque alleys of the largest town on the island of Brač. Here, chef-patron Dino Šeparović offers two tasting menus of 4 or 6 courses, centered on island traditions and built around seasonal ingredients, from fresh Adriatic fish to tasty local lamb. Some dishes are cooked over a wood fire, imparting a sophisticated smoky touch. The highlight of the restaurant is the desserts, true must-haves that elegantly complete the dining experience.

Name: Konoba TRS
Description: In a small alley in the cosy and bustling old town, Konoba TRS welcomes guests in an elegant setting with exposed stone walls and a beautiful outdoor area. The cuisine is Mediterranean, traditional but with some modern touches, offered mainly in a small menu or in three interesting menus of three courses each. Excellent cod fillet with mashed potatoes and beetroot powder. Particularly pleasant is the secluded and shady terrace, ideal for a quiet dinner.

Name: Konoba Tri Piruna
Description: A historic address of the local area, with over 50 years of business, this rustic, welcoming restaurant offers an authentic, traditional atmosphere, with furnishings made of wood and local stone. The cuisine celebrates regional and Mediterranean flavors, with dishes prepared exclusively using ingredients sourced from local producers. During the warmer months, it's worth securing a table in the cool and shaded outdoor seating area, ideal for a relaxed lunch or dinner al fresco.

Name: Konoba Zijavica
Description: In a charming fishing village, this cosy restaurant brings the sea right to your plate... and just steps away from your table! The real gem is the veranda overlooking the water: once seated, you are lulled by the sound of the waves and enchanted by a picture-postcard view. The patron, Stiven Vunić, devotes himself with great skill to seafood cuisine in which the very fresh and fragrant product is the real star. The recipes are simple but refined: sometimes a modern twist appears, but more often the focus is on the reassuring comfort of well-executed tradition. Raw dishes, pastas, catch of the day, shellfish and crustaceans served by weight make up an offering that faithfully follows the season and local market availability, so don't be surprised if some dishes are not available. The small, curated and interesting wine list will especially appeal to lovers of natural wines.

Name: Konrad's
Address: Platz der Vereinten Nationen 4, Bonn, 53113, Germany
Description: This restaurant on the 17th floor of the Marriott Hotel has the "wow" factor of a great view over Bonn through its floor-to-ceiling windows. In the open kitchens they cook up modern dishes with Mediterranean influences. Pre- or after-dinner drinks are served in the bar right next door. Parking is available in the underground garage, and the lift leads directly to the restaurant.

Name: Koo Madame
Address: 1st Floor, Rosewood Hotel, Marina District, Building 11, Street 309, Zone 69, Lusail, Doha, Qatar
Description: The Rosewood Hotel is home to this 1920’s-inspired Chinese restaurant. Dark and moody, the space has an open kitchen, an enclosed wine cellar and a smartly dressed team that are ready to serve. The menu is a roll call of some familiar and enjoyable dishes. They serve dim sum, wonderfully fresh-pulled noodles – the Fried Flying Dagger is the one to choose – and of course, the signature Beijing Duck is beautifully lacquered, flavoursome and carved at the table – don't worry, the kitchen will do a half if you can’t manage a whole. Their tea selection is also worth exploring.

Name: Kook Atelier op Oost
Description: Nature takes centre stage at this tastefully converted 18C farmhouse, which also includes a boutique hotel. The restaurant's Nordic-inspired design and large windows that make you feel connected to the outdoors reflect the house's commitment to sustainability. The menu is centred on ingredients from the Wadden Sea and Texel, which they have either grown themselves or sourced from trusted local purveyors. Chef Joram structures his menu around the elements of earth, air, fire and water. For example, cured hamachi from Zeeland, brushed with a fruity glaze and served with pickled vegetables and a cucumber jus. Fermentation and other artisanal methods lend the dishes extra character. This exploration of Texel's ecosystems is truly captivating.

Name: Kopitiam by Chandy's
Address: Al Falah Street, Old Passport Rd, Zone 1, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,No alcohol served,Pets not allowed
Description: Owner Chandy and his team runs this sweet little Malaysian restaurant with passion, politeness and professionalism - and clearly want everyone to enjoy themselves. That proves easy, thanks to the inexpensive, fresh and flavoursome dishes on the short menu that’s supplemented with a blackboard of specials; roti jala is always well worth ordering. The place is immaculately kept, with views into the equally spotless kitchen.

Name: Kor Lhai Toh
Address: 285 Sappasit Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, Ubon Ratchathani, 34000, Thailand
Description: This lively local restaurant specialises in fish, with daily catches such as grouper or sea bass prepared in a variety of traditional Thai styles. They can be served whole for sharing or in individual portions. The confident cooking delivers authentic Thai flavours, while meat dishes are equally rewarding: the stir-fried beef is fragrant with young galangal and Thai herbs. Finish with the toddy palm jelly in fresh coconut milk, a speciality of the province.

Name: Korill180
Description: Fun, friendly and full of atmosphere, this is Wrocław’s go-to destination for Korean barbecue. Inside the on-trend, industrial-chic dining room, each table is topped with its own gas grill – over which you can cook a range of high-quality meat and seafood exactly to your liking. Non-grill dishes are available too, like bibimbap and bulgogi, while the starters take influences from Japan with tempura and gyozas. Come with friends, order away and you’ll have a brilliant time.

Name: Korus
Description: In this bubbly bistro near Bastille, you will sample a single set menu that shines the spotlight on the best of France, courtesy of top-notch produce and succulent recipes. Cheerful service and a lively, welcoming vibe.

Name: Koryori Takaya
Description: The charm of Koryori Takaya is that it’s a kappo, but with the comfortable familiarity of a neighbourhood eatery. Freshly cooked dishes and smiling conversation put diners in a good mood. For lunch, set meals with a variety of small side dishes are served; in the evening, the chef displays his talent with omakase, concluding with rice in earthenware pots and accompaniments. A choice of pickled tuna, grilled fish or sukiyaki makes the end of the evening fun.

Name: Koryu Keishin
Description: ‘Naniwa’ is an old name for Osaka; ‘kappo’ derives from the words meaning to chop and cook ingredients. And to convey the character of Osaka people and the foods they love, the ‘Naniwa kappo’ was born. That spirit living on through the extensive menu reflects Osaka’s culinary ethos of preserving the native flavours of ingredients while pursuing the preferences of guests. Being spoilt for choice, unable to decide which of many tempting choices to order, is all part of the fun.

Name: Koshita
Description: The counter of ancient buried cedar is an heirloom from the chef’s honoured mentor. On a foundation of technique cultivated in his apprenticeship, he builds unique combinations of foodstuffs and techniques to place his own stamp on his craft. For wanmono, broth is drawn from two types of makombu seaweed, multiplying the flavours. Flame-broiled items are paired with pureed vegetable soup. Ingredients unfamiliar to Japanese cuisine are enthusiastically added to the repertoire. Expressing freedom of spirit, the chef is resplendent in black shirt and bowtie.

Name: Kosmo Taste the Mountain
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the centre and also accessible from the ski slopes in winter, this contemporary, Alpine-style restaurant boasts a spacious dining room and large picture windows. The cuisine reflects the traditions of the Valtellina mountains, with a dedicated space for the charcoal grill and an excellent selection of cheeses. The extensive wine list pays particular attention to mountain wines produced by wineries with a sustainable focus.

Name: Kosushi
Description: The name of the restaurant has a direct link with Japanese philosophy as the word “ko” (which translates as “turtle”) is associated with long life and the symbolism of the number 1. Opened in 1988 by chef George Yuji Koshoji, it is now located at a different address (in the Itaim Bibi district), where it has become a popular meeting place for locals. It boasts a welcoming, contemporary ambience, soft lighting and a decor of bright colours, plus an impressive large balcony from where guests can watch their dishes being prepared. The extensive menu offers a variety of options such as gyosas, tartares, ussuzukuri, uramaki, sushi and sashimi, as well as hot dishes that include yakisoba, octopus yaki and Wagyu medallions. It also features a superb selection of sakis and innovative cocktails.

Name: Kota
Address: Celtic House, The Shipyard, Porthleven, TR13 9JY, United Kingdom
Description: Located in a prime spot on the harbourside, Kota operates as a separate restaurant from within its sister operation, Kota Kai. The tasting menu, with a choice of fish or meat at each course, draws on influences from cuisines around the world, including some subtle nods to Chef Jude Kereama’s Maori, Chinese and Malaysian heritage. The restaurant’s name means ‘shellfish’ in Maori, so look out for Cornish seafood on the menu. Linger a little longer in the area by staying overnight in one of the bedrooms, one of which overlooks the harbour.

Name: Kota Dine & Coffee (Fort Cornwallis)
Address: Fort Cornwallis, Jalan Tun Syed Sheh Barakbah, George Town, 10200, Malaysia
Description: It feels relaxing to sit in the glass-clad room drenched in natural light and furnished in faux-industrial style. In terms of food, they serve a neo-Nyonya menu with a strong East-meets-West concept. On top of Peranakan classics like otak-otak, Western influences are manifested in more adventurous creations such as laksa capellini. Even the desserts take a surprise twist, as in teh-ramisu that uses tea instead of coffee.

Name: Kou Gyu Rou
Address: 6 Minle Street, Datong District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: The Japanese chef once owned a ramen shop. He open this joint to promote the beauty of Taiwanese beef noodles. His kombu beef bone broth is seasoned with sea salt and soy, not the herbs and aromatics that dominate the typical taste profile of the Taiwanese speciality. The beef cured in kombu and soy is tender and juicy; the springy noodles pick up the broth well. It tends to sell out, so come early.

Name: Kous Kous
Address: Carr. Tecate Ensenada, Km 73.30, Valle de Guadalupe, 22750, Mexico
Description: This stunning restaurant with dramatic views may seem like other outdoor spots in the area but keep down the path and a lively space draped with curtains and Moroccan lamps soon appears, revealing the singular experience. Come for an unexpected yet memorable meal spotlighting Moroccan cuisine. There is plenty of heart and loads of flavor in this family-style selection where guests take their pick of protein for the tagine. Kick the meal off with flatbread, made in-house, along with a refreshing cucumber salad. From the chicken with olives to the honey lamb, the tagine offerings are exceptional, but their namesake couscous, with caramelized onions, garbanzo beans and golden raisins, almost steals the show.

Name: Koy Hermitage
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: If you’re keen to try some authentic yet innovative Japanese cuisine, this restaurant bearing the signature of famous culinary maestro Hideki Matsuhisa, who has already tasted major success at Koy Shunka in Barcelona, is definitely this place. The Japanese-Mediterranean philosophy here is one that is not based on a fusion approach; instead, it is more of a reproduction of Japanese techniques but with the use of essentially Mediterranean ingredients, with addition of others from Galicia and Huelva. At the comfortable, U-shaped bar counter, with the kitchen in the middle of proceedings so that guests can watch the full preparation process, the culinary focus is always on seasonality on a concise à la carte that gives pride of place to classic dishes, plus two splendid tasting menus, Koy and Hermitage. A standout dish that we particularly enjoyed was the intensely flavoured Ebro Delta eel nigiri with an eel salsa.

Name: Koyal
Address: 59-63 Brighton Road, Surbiton, London, KT6 5LR, United Kingdom
Description: Keep your eyes peeled for the tall clock and bell tower which marks out this Indian restaurant just off Surbiton High Street, then feel yourself drawn in by its bright and colourful interior. Kick off with a street food snack, such as koliwada fish with fiery green chutney, then choose from a pan-Indian menu that ranges from the tandoori dishes of the north to the more subtle spicing of the south. The muntjac dum biryani and the coastal lamb curry are two signatures, while bright, distinct flavours and well-balanced spicing run throughout.

Name: Koyo
Address: The Burman Hotel, Dunkri 8, Tallinn, 10123, Estonia
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Notable sake list
Description: Chef Kazuto Hokari relocated from Japan to open this restaurant and share his love of his native cuisine. 11 bright-red upholstered seats skirt an L-shaped counter in the stylish dining room, where Kazuto serves his omakase menu to two sittings of guests each evening. Sushi is the main event, with the eel and akami tuna particular highlights and also a favourite of the chef himself. He fully guides guests through the menu in an informative and personable way, and service is professional and engaging all-round. A concise but carefully selected range of wines, champagnes and sakes complete the picture.

Name: Kraft Bistro
Description: Tucked away down a cul-de-sac filled with several other eateries, this understandably popular brasserie is underpinned by the flame-centric cooking of the Josper grill. Top-quality produce from jumbo prawns to beef tenderloin are grilled with skill and served with simple, complementary garnishes. Enjoy the cooking on the terrace, in the conservatory or in the main dining room near the buzzing open kitchen. The efficient team run the busy space with skill.

Name: Kraftwerk
Description: This restaurant housed in a converted power station is more than a stylish location – it also serves extremely good food. The cuisine combines classic, Mediterranean and Austrian influences, including appetising dishes such as lobster with truffle sauce, beef fillet Rossini; the "Austrian classics" section on the menu features the likes of "Bertl's Kalbsfleischpflanzerl mit Kartoffel-Rahmgurkensalat" (veal patties with potato salad in a creamy cucumber sauce). In addition to à la carte dishes, there are two set menus: "Kraftwerk Classics" and "Kraftwerk Finest". The international wine list is comprehensive. In summer, tables are set up on the terrace. Friendly, attentive and professional service.

Name: Kreuz
Description: Take a seat in one of the gorgeous dining spaces, or on the lovely, pleasantly peaceful garden terrace, to enjoy traditional and regional fare. The menu features, for instance, local lake fish; European perch from the Lötschberg mountains is also popular. The good food is complemented by a really friendly family atmosphere, which comes courtesy of the attentive service team. In the simpler Gaststube, you can order the dish of the day.

Name: Krevette
Description: Chef Florent Ladeyn (Auberge du Vert Mont) has opened this restaurant serving dishes that are full of zesty nods to the treasures of the sea! Devilled eggs with lovage and trout roe; yakitori-style pollock fillet, barbecued aubergine and cream-enriched fish fumet; acacia flower fritters dusted with blackcurrant leaves. These tasty seafood creations using local, seasonal produce reflect the chef's commitment to local sourcing. Bon appétit!

Name: Krietsch
Description: This centuries-old establishment has a rich and eventful past, having functioned at various times as an arms factory, an orphanage, a prison and finally the restaurant Fuggerei. Today, as Krietsch, it serves seasonal, regional cuisine, but it also draws on international influences. As well as flavoursome dishes à la carte, such as Black Angus Sauerbraten (marinated pot roast) with bread dumplings and Brussels sprouts with bacon, a six-course set menu is available on Thu-Sat evenings (with 48hr notice). At lunchtime, a daily set menu is served. The interior boasts a soaring period vaulted ceiling, and there is a gorgeous terrace outside. Tip: Take the opportunity to visit the minster right behind the restaurant.

Name: Kristoforas
Description: A great example of classical architecture in Lithuania, Vilnius Town Hall is a special place and, hidden within it, is this comfortable and well-run restaurant. Its blue frescoed ceiling is certainly eye-catching and adds to the elegance of the room. The cooking keeps things fairly classical too, with its mix of French and Italian dishes; you can expect assured flavours, but the kitchen also displays a delicate touch when needed. Do start with the baby squid and octopus with white beans; then head for venison in the fashion of a Rossini tournedos.

Name: Kro
Address: Via Tollarini 70/c, località Pontagna di Temù, Ponte di Legno, 25050, Italy
Description: Old stables have been converted into this restaurant, which boasts a stylish decor of wood and stone and the sort of romantic atmosphere that you would expect from the mountains. Although a few fish options are included on the menu, the cuisine focuses mainly on Alpine cuisine, featuring ingredients such as mushrooms, meat and game.

Name: Krogs Fiskerestaurant
Description: This handsome 18th-century red-brick building stands on the site of Copenhagen’s old fish market and has operated as a seafood restaurant since 1910. Its latest owners keep up the tradition, from the sea-themed wallpaper – hung with portraits of the King and his father, who was a regular customer – to the lobster tank and seafood-centric menu. You’ll find everything from bouillabaisse to turbot on the bone to share, accompanied by a fine wine list that’s strong on champagne and burgundies. Solo diners will feel comfortable here too, thanks to the granite bar counter opposite the glassed-in kitchen.

Name: Krokodilos
Address: Lancer Square, 28A Kensington Church Street, Kensington, London, W8 4EP, United Kingdom
Description: From its linen canopy to its wooden shelves filled with Greek wines, there’s an inviting rustic-chic vibe to this large Greek restaurant – enhanced by the presence of a homely fireplace. The team know how to put their guests at ease and are happy to tell you the story behind each authentic dish. If you want a taste of proper taramasalata without leaving London, this is one of the best places to be – and the ‘Greek Olive Oil Experience’ is a brilliant way to start. Ensure you save room for the 'karidopita' chocolate and walnut cake with ‘kaimaki’ ice cream.

Name: Krone
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: This restaurant in the hotel of the same name stands within a medieval castle complex on top of the mountain – the view couldn't be more beautiful! The stylish decor is a winning combination of modern design and historical charm. Drawing on classic influences, the cuisine takes its cue from the changing seasons and is made with fresh produce sourced from Switzerland and the region – be sure to try the porcini in season or their novel pasta dishes such as "tagliolini, white truffle, pecorino foam". Choose à la carte Tue-Thu; on Fri and Sat, there is a fine dining menu. The service is friendly and professional. N.B. Due to the location in a reduced-traffic zone, you will need to park a few minutes' walk away – the hotel also provides a shuttle service, to be booked in advance.

Name: Krone
Description: Nestled in the heart of Steinenbronn, this family-run establishment has been welcoming diners for many years. Here, modernity meets tradition in both the decor and the cuisine. The menu features timeless classics such as pork fillet in a creamy sauce, alongside more ambitious dishes, some made with game that they hunt themselves. For a pleasant, laid-back alternative, head to Krönle – the options written up on the board are very reasonably priced. Some house-made food items such as greaves lard spread, tripe, spaetzle, sauces and maultaschen can be purchased to take home. Decent guestrooms.

Name: Krone
Description: Krone has been properly invested in: from the façade to the hotel rooms, everything is chic and high quality, the restaurant is modern and sleek. The food is very good, with select produce turned into aromatic dishes with plenty of flavour. At lunchtime, a smaller range of interesting options. If you are staying longer, Basel and Alsace are very close by.

Name: Krone
Description: You will feel at home here for a number of reasons. Not only can you enjoy the modern, classic and seasonal cuisine showcasing local produce, but there is also the friendly, attentive service that comes courtesy of the owner and her team, who also know their way around the wine list. The elegantly pared-down interior is equally inviting, not to mention the beautiful garden with shaded seating that draws diners in summer. Well-kept guestrooms are available should you wish to stay the night.

Name: Krone
Description: This long-standing family business is run with real dedication. No compromises are made when it comes to the quality of the produce, and the dishes taste great! No wonder the restaurant is widely known and popular – this also means it is better to make a reservation. Tip: the very reasonably priced lunch menu.

Name: Krone Schlier
Description: In a charming location between Lake Constance and the Allgäu, just a few kilometres from Ravensburg, this lovely restaurant serving excellent cuisine is run by the Geßler family. Chef-patron Benedikt Geßler comes from a family of restaurateurs and has worked in several renowned kitchens. Here, he cooks modern, seasonal dishes, placing great importance on organic and Demeter produce. Choose one of two set menus ("Chef Menu" and "Végétal Menu"), from which, alternatively, you can order à la carte. The setting is extremely inviting, too, with friendly, professional staff serving you in a cosy interior with stylish details such as old oak floors, smart cherry-wood panelling and chic, comfortable seats. There is also a pretty terrace.

Name: Krone am See
Description: Right by the lake, complete with a small harbour, this modern, low-rise building stands next to the traditional Krone restaurant after which it is named. Inside, an upscale contemporary decor with clean lines welcomes diners; outside, the terrace beckons. As for the food, the good à la carte selection of Mediterranean, French and regional dishes has a pronounced emphasis on local, seasonal ingredients, such as Thurgau rainbow trout and salmon from Lostallo. In addition, there are two three- or five-course set menus, one of which is vegan. The extensive wine list features over 160 labels. For a more casual approach, the separate "Krone Easy" self-service and takeaway concept operates throughout the milder seasons.

Name: Kronenhalle
Description: This Zurich institution located on Bellevueplatz has housed a restaurant since 1924. Be sure to look around – the walls are adorned with original art by Joan Miró, Marc Chagall, Pierre Bonnard! You can choose to dine in the lively atmosphere of the Brasserie or the more intimate ambience of the Chagall Room. There is also the Swiss Gallery on the first floor. In this beautiful, stylish setting, diners tuck into classic, traditional cuisine at its most heartfelt and satisfying! Much of the food is presented to diners tableside. A signature dish is their Kronenhalle sliced fillet of veal with rösti.

Name: Kronenschlösschen
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The setting is lovely, whether under the elegantly painted period ceiling or out on the pretty terrace with its adjoining garden. The cooking is a modern take on classically based cuisine, enhanced with international influences. At the helm is Marcus Langer, most recently head chef at the Atelier Sanssouci in Radebeul. His set menu (with meat/fish or vegetarian choices) can be ordered in a five- to seven-course format – with the option to extend it to 10. Tempting dishes include cauliflower and "Périgord truffle délice with hazelnut vinaigrette and tarragon" or king crab tartlet with wild garlic and morels. The wine list ranks among the best in Germany. The bistro on site is an alternative to the fine dining restaurant. There are cosy, well-appointed guestrooms in the hotel of the same name.

Name: Kronenschlösschen - Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Dating back to 1894, the Kronenschösschen hotel is a classic establishment of the Rheingau. Its bistro offers a pleasant alternative to the fine dining restaurant. A cosy interior with bags of traditional charm is the backdrop for seasonal cuisine based on carefully selected ingredients – think sautéed leg of lamb with wild garlic spaetzle and mushrooms. Diners can choose from the à la carte selection or opt for the four- or five-course surprise menu. Also highly recommended: classics such as "Salmon trout from the Wispertal" or "Whole lobster served in two courses" (for two people). The experience is rounded off by a well-curated wine list and attentive service. In fine weather, head for the exceptionally pretty terrace set in a beautiful garden planted with mature trees. Comfortable guestrooms and stylish suites make this an appealing option for an overnight stay.

Name: Kronenstübli
Description: Premium materials, tasteful fabrics and attractive Swiss stone pine panelling make for a cosy yet elegant atmosphere – just the right backdrop for the sophisticated cuisine served here, which combines classic French culinary tradition with Italian influences. Opt for one of two set menus: the "Degustations Menu" or the "Geniesser Menu". Alternatively, dishes are also served à la carte. Tip: Try the canard à la presse – pressed duck – (prepared for two or more diners, served in two courses). Wednesday special: Chateaubriand for two or more diners. The restaurant is housed in the long-established and stylishly luxurious Grand Hotel Kronenhof.

Name: Kropka.
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: A cool and casual spot, there's a welcoming vibe to this neighbourhood operation that’s very much in the bistro mould. If you like a ringside seat for watching the chefs, ask for a spot at the kitchen counter. The cooking mixes a Polish base with influences from over the world, while the generous portions are indicative of the restaurant’s spirit. The interesting and ever-evolving wine list spotlights natural options, with plenty of orange and skin-contact varieties.

Name: Krua Jay Miad
Address: 104/3, Map Phai, Ban Bueng, Chon Buri, 20170, Thailand
Description: Diners come to this simple, rustic place for its range of less common proteins, including venison and wild boar, as well as frog, eel, snakehead fish and fresh blue crab. Ingredients are fresh, and staff are happy to guide you through the daily specials. Flavours land bold and intense, with clear character. Don't miss the garlic-fried frog with fried green pepper and chilli, or the jungle curry with snakehead fish or eel, depending on the day's consignment.

Name: Krua Nai Baan
Address: 124/5 Mu 6, Soi Naklua 13/9, Pattaya, Na Kluea, Bang Lamung, Chon Buri, 20150, Thailand
Description: Thanks to direct links with fishers, this local favourite in a small alley uses the day's catch in a changing menu revolving around seafood, with squid, shrimp and whole fish cooked in a straightforward Thai style. The bold, confident seasoning is aimed at local palates, rather than toned down for visitors. Sharp, fragrant and comforting, the sour soup with snakehead fish and bilimbi is not to be missed. Weekends can be busy, so booking ahead makes sense.

Name: Krua Phech Doi Ngam
Address: 267/1 Mu 2, Mahidol Road, Pa Daet, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50100, Thailand
Description: This popular open-air eatery serves well-sized northern Thai favourites at fair prices. Kang Liang, the peppery curry paste in spicy mixed vegetables goes well with the prawns’ natural sweetness; while the local fish marinated in herbs and spices is grilled in a bamboo tube until soft, with a smoky aroma. Do check the blackboard for specials of the day, which often focus on seasonal dishes.

Name: Krua Pla Tu Tid Oun
Address: 8/1 Nadedee Road Soi 5, Saen Suk, Mueang Chon Buri, Chon Buri, 20130, Thailand
Description: This place near Bang Saen beach has been popular with tourists for decades. The signature is, of course, pla tu (Thai mackerel), but the menu extends from seafood options such as sillago, sea bass and local scallops – all cooked in classic Thai style – to crispy deep-fried mackerel cheek with a chilli-garlic aroma that's addictive. If you prefer a milder taste, the staff are happy to adjust the spice level to suit your palate.

Name: Krua Sa Ros Jad
Address: 112/1 Soi Vibhavadi 44, Vibhavadi Rangsit Road, Lat Yao, Chatuchak, Bangkok, 10900, Thailand
Description: "Krua Sa Ros Jad" combines the owner's mother's name and a Thai phrase meaning "intense flavour" – an apt description of the boldly seasoned food made with fresh ingredients. Try the deep-fried fish in Choo Chee sauce, the robust, well-spiced flavour of which pairs well with the hot Tom Yum chicken soup with young tamarind leaves. The restaurant boasts a unique collection of Buddha statues and antique European ceramics, as the owner is an avid collector.

Name: Krua Samchai
Address: 282/1 Phalochai Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, Ubon Ratchathani, 34000, Thailand
Description: Two roosters stand guard at the entrance. Krua Samchai is famous for serving iconic Isan food befitting of the region. Fresh fish from the Mekong and Mun rivers is cooked using the chef's secret mix of herbs and spices that produces a powerful aroma. The grilled chicken has a crispy golden skin from the charcoal flame but retains its juicy meat. The Isan-style spicy fish maw and bamboo shoot soup uses tiliacora juice to perfection.

Name: Krua Supanniga by Khunyai Somsie
Address: Supanniga Home, 130/9 Phothisan Road, Phra Lap, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: Named after the Supanniga flower, this cute shop offers delightful dishes blending flavours from the eastern seaboard and Isan cuisine. Grandma's recipes inspire the food here. Don't miss the must-order chamuang pork—a juicy stewed pork infused with Chamuang leaf's slightly sour flavour. The restaurant provides indoor and outdoor seating, including shaded tables in the tree house.

Name: Krua Taan
Address: 65/16 Mu 7, Soi Mu Ban Chang, Pai Ling, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: This rustic, open-air restaurant brings the charm of a family kitchen to life, serving Thai classics with a local twist. Freshwater fish and herbs shine across the menu, but the standout is the spicy stir-fried minced pork ribs with soft bone – fiery, fragrant and balanced by sweet, house-pickled garlic. Each dish is unfussy yet thoughtful, ideal for sharing. Featuring wooden décor, the laid-back setting makes it perfect for relaxed meals with family or friends.

Name: Krua Yai Pleng
Address: 8 Soi Borommaratchachonnani 101, Sala Thammasop, Thawi Watthana, Bangkok, 10170, Thailand
Description: On a serene canal bank outside the city centre, this restaurant leans into intense, authentic Thai cuisine, even dabbling in exotic ingredients, such as frog, wild boar and river fish when these are available. The flavoursome wild boar in spicy soup is a top pick, packed with fresh herbs for pungent aromas and succulent meat – the spiciness can be adjusted to your preference. Arrive early or phone in advance to check the availability of specific dishes.

Name: Kruiden & Jasmijn
Description: Located just inside the historical city walls, this is an elegantly appointed restaurant featuring modern art and imposing chandeliers. The terrace exudes tranquillity, and the attentive service creates a warm and welcoming atmosphere. A passionate advocate for local produce, chef Patrick de Rade especially loves Eastern Scheldt lobster when it is in season. He also regularly harvests fruit and vegetables from his garden. Sourced from a friendly local farmer, red cabbage adds a touch of sweetness to his venison fillet, perfectly complementing the sweet-and-sour pickled red beets. His rich sauces are testament to his culinary expertise and generosity.

Name: Kruvit Raft (Ban Laem Hin)
Address: 98/7 Ko Maphrao, Mu 6, Ko Kaeo, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: To reach this floating restaurant near Ko Maphrao, take a 5-min boat ride across sparkling waters reflecting the sunshine. Onboard, panoramic views, a gentle breeze and uber-fresh seafood await. The distance from sea to plate couldn’t be shorter. Start with a freshly picked coconut before tucking into delicious southern and central Thai seafood. The grouper soup with Chinese soybean paste and stir-fried black tiger prawns with salt and chilli are highlights.

Name: Kräutergarten
Description: Since as far back as 1983, the friendly and dedicated owners have been running this restaurant with its pleasant and elegant interior. It is easy to see why they have so many loyal regulars. The cooking, rooted in the classical tradition and using excellent fresh ingredients, is shaped by the seasons and Mediterranean touches. Diners can order à la carte or compose their own three-course menu from the same selection. The service comes courtesy of an attentive team. You'll certainly want to come back again!

Name: Krüs Kitchen
