The kitchen tells tales of both land and sea: earthy, satisfying dishes such as the juicy young heifer entrecôte wrapped in golden potatoes with mustard dressing, and tempting seafood offerings such as the fragrant, comforting linguine with scampi alla busara. Quality ingredients take center stage! At lunch, the menu streamlines and service quickens, with lighter prices to match; come evening, the carte expands and the experience becomes complete and gratifying.

Name: La Citadelle
Address: 9 place de la Motte, Châteaubriant, 44110, France
Description: The restaurant occupies a prime position in the heart of this medieval town, strewn with old stone buildings and half-timbered houses. Maxime Leloup, a local lad, and his wife Patricia, who hails from Lima, graciously welcome diners into their updated eatery. The food in the zeitgeist is depicted by meticulous plating and down-to-earth, voluntarily indulgent flavours. For example: pressé of beef with foie gras or caramelised millefeuille with ganache pralinée, hazelnuts and vanilla-laced caramel. The odd Latin American occasionally finds its way onto the menu.

Name: La Closerie des Roses
Address: 455 rue de la Haute-Meilleraie, Varades, 44370, France
Description: Surrounded by rose bushes, this restaurant, which has stood on the banks of the Loire since 1938, affords a stunning view of the river and the abbey church of St-Florent-le-Vieil. In a tasteful contemporary interior, the chef crafts a traditional lineup drawing on regional fare (hake, pollock, farm-reared lamb, calf sweetbreads) flanked by classic sauces (beurre blanc, shellfish jus, wine sauce).

Name: La Coccinella
Description: This warm and welcoming establishment evokes the reassuring atmosphere of a country house. The menu, a single offering, presents a well-judged balance between meat and fish dishes, complemented by the daily specials presented verbally at the table, a detail that underlines a direct and convivial rapport with the guest. The wine list is well-constructed, with a predominantly local selection enriched by some interesting forays into older vintages, and prices marked by a most pleasing honesty.

Name: La Cocina de Colacho
Description: This unique restaurant with an open-view kitchen and numerous designer details is run by a friendly couple. Chef Nicolás Machín, who is known to everyone as Colacho, creates an up-to-date take on traditional cooking that is always built around ingredients from the island (the restaurant also has its own vegetable garden) and is showcased on a single tasting menu. Dishes that you’ll find on the menu that we particularly enjoyed for their flavour included the loin of cherne fish with vegetable pisto and creamy potatoes with thyme.

Name: La Cocina de Cristine
Description: Located in the captivating boutique hotel Cristine Bedfor, with a MICHELIN Key, this restaurant reflects the same character or aesthetic ambiance, with carpets, mirrors and vintage furniture not lacking in charm. The young chef at the head, Menorcan Pau Sintes, offers a Mediterranean market cuisine rooted in the island's own products (sourdough bread with Menorcan seasonings, red prawns, sobrasada de payés, Sa Llotja's catch of the day...), which reaches the diner through the à la carte menu and a tasting menu.

Name: La Cocina del Principal
Address: Fernando El Católico 13, Sos del Rey Católico, 50680, Spain
Description: Situated in the centre of the historic quarter, this restaurant occupies a charming building which provides the backdrop for a traditionally inspired à la carte featuring numerous grilled dishes. The terrace with beautiful views is an added bonus.

Name: La Collina dei Ciliegi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated within the La Collina dei Ciliegi wine estate amid the verdant Valpantena hills, this first-floor restaurant (lift available) is home to two chefs – he is from Calabria, while she is from Puglia. Together they create exciting, modern Mediterranean cuisine using ingredients from their native regions, including their signature dish – homemade spaghetti served with a delicious, well-balanced 'nduja, smoked ricotta and tomato ristretto sauce. Top-quality local ingredients take pride of place, as demonstrated by the Brogna mutton, which is raised on site, barbecued and served with an exquisite caper sauce and seasonal mushroom pie. The concise wine list features labels from the Veneto alongside a few French options.

Name: La Colline du Colombier
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Deep in the countryside, overlooking the Loire, this restored farmhouse boasts a chic and pared-back rustic style – a natural and stylish setting in which to enjoy Léo Troisgros's contemporary and poetically named dishes (eg "rose marine" or "in the shade of the fig tree"). Should you wish to extend your stay, there are various types of accommodation, including the famous "cadoles" – lodges on stilts!

Name: La Colombe
Description: Sesame salmon tataki with a crunchy vegetable salad; turbot fillet, pan-fried chanterelles and a black garlic jus. With their generous, seriously Provençal cuisine, Pascal and Nadège Bonamy have elevated their restaurant at the foot of the Maurettes mountains to one of the best in the region.

Name: La Colombe
Description: At the foot of Mont Ventoux surrounded by vineyards, this gourmet dove coos a delicious tune. Chef Christophe Schuffenecker serves modern, spot-on, legible dishes, founded on local produce, such as Sarrians pigeon with geranium-perfumed mashed carrots. When the weather is fine, make a beeline for the terrace shaded by awnings overlooking the vineyards. The traditional interior sports bare beams and a large Provençal fireplace.

Name: La Conchiglia
Description: This small restaurant with a vaulted ceiling provides the setting for dishes that have by now become classics thanks to their focus on top-quality ingredients. The cuisine is light and simple rather than bold and elaborate, with a focus on bringing out the full flavour of the fish (a few meat dishes are also available). If you’re keen to learn more about Ligurian gastronomic specialities, take time between courses to chat with the friendly owner, who has an impressive knowledge of the region.

Name: La Conchiglia d'Oro
Address: Via Nazionale Adriatica nord, Pineto, 64025, Italy
Description: The rather anonymous location does not in any way detract from the quality of this historic restaurant, which is renowned for its excellent fish and seafood. The menu showcases fish from the Adriatic cooked using classical techniques with the occasional modern twist, such as in the tuna tartare seasoned with caramelised onions and citrus powder-flavoured mayonnaise. Considering the quality of the fish here, the prices are very reasonable. The beautifully presented desserts are an added bonus.

Name: La Condesa
Description: Blending industrial design accents with soft lighting, this spot has a chic, modern ambience that's just right for bringing people together. La Condesa honors and celebrates the cuisine of Mexico with a particular focus on Mexico City. Seafood enthusiasts can expect a menu featuring the freshest ceviche or tiradito alongside an eye-catching grilled whole fish. Savor the tangy, delicious flavor of silky raw tuna atop a super crisp tortilla with aji amarillo. Sided by creamy cubes of avocado and salsa macha, it's a refreshing way to begin a meal here. Huarache de huitlacoche is a well-known dish prepared with care, and nothing completes the meal quite like cinnamon-dusted churros.

Name: La Condesa
Description: Designed by Camille Flammarion, this pint-sized, sleek restaurant stands on a street corner in the 9th district of Paris. On entering, you will admire the kitchen where the chef, who learned the ropes in nine countries, enjoys explaining his philosophy. He rolls out a 3-, 5- or 7-course surprise menu – the latter of which provides the best insight into a globetrotting tasting journey that spans numerous world cuisines. The delightful on-the-ball staff is always close at hand and there is a half glass food-wine pairing option.

Name: La Coopérative - Domaine Riberach
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This converted wine storehouse with its authentic metal frame is spacious, comfortable and oozing in charm! The cuisine is aligned with the seasons and relies on small-scale local producers. Delicate, colourful dishes can be paired with wines from the estate, which are produced without additives, using agroecological methods. Pleasant guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: La Coquerie
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Close to the famous naval cemetery, this chic, contemporary little place boasts the Mediterranean as its backdrop and a panoramic terrace for fine weather. The restaurant serves exceedingly fresh cuisine focused on market produce and local producers, served in the form of a single set menu. The dishes concocted by chef Guilhem Blanc-Brude range between Mediterranean-inspired creations and more inventive fare, such as herb-roasted saddle of lamb with apricot caponata. Natural wine list.

Name: La Corniola
Address: Via dei Mastri Lombardi 24, Pescocostanzo, 67033, Italy
Description: Known throughout Italy for its pillow lace, the small town of Pescocostanzo in the Parco della Maiella is one of the most beautiful in Italy. It is also home to the Relais Ducale hotel and its La Corniola restaurant, which is renowned for its excellent modern Abruzzo cuisine, including delicious, seasonal dishes made from different vegetables, potatoes and onions grown in the hotel’s own kitchen gardens. Simple yet elegant dining room.

Name: La Corte
Description: Situated in the luxurious Villa Abbazia hotel, this splendid restaurant boasts a fireplace, frescoes and period decor, as well as an elegant outdoor space for summer dining. Both provide the perfect backdrop for the cuisine prepared by Giuseppe Francica, a young chef who practically grew up in the kitchen here. Served on vegetarian and tasting menus from which dishes can also be chosen individually à la carte style, this chef’s fresh and colourful dishes are made using herbs and vegetables from the property’s own kitchen garden, plus ingredients sourced from trusted local producers. The excellent wine list is particularly strong on Riesling labels. A perfect all-round evening dining experience, with the option of a bistro for more informal meals at lunchtime.

Name: La Corte
Address: Via San Pancrazio 41, Palazzolo sull'Oglio, 25036, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in a tranquil street that leads to the centre of Palazzolo sull’Oglio, this stylish restaurant in a 16C palazzo boasts classic elegance and authentic cuisine which is delicious and full of flavour. Here, Aldo and his wife offer guests a warm and informal welcome, always with a smile on their lips.

Name: La Corte degli Dei
Description: Relax amid the greenery on the patio terrace at this restaurant, which is housed in an old palazzo full of timeless charm and history. The interior is as charming as the exterior, boasting delightful dining rooms teeming with character. The cuisine skilfully encompasses traditional classic favourites alongside more innovative dishes, offering guests a culinary journey that combines past and present with elegance and flavour.

Name: La Costanera
Address: Oceano Hotel, 260 Capistrano Rd., Half Moon Bay, CA, 94019, USA
Description: Where else can you stroll in after a day at the beach and get a delicious Peruvian meal? La Costanera, nestled within the darling coastal town of Half Moon Bay, of course! Traditional and modern art abound, but it's the boldly flavored plates from Chef Carlos Altamirano and his team that garner attention. Palta rellena, which fills half an avocado with roasted chicken chicharrones and lime-infused mayonnaise, is a fun and light-hearted interpretation of the dish. Cebice pescado marinated in aji rocoto leche de tigre is both tangy and kicky, while lomo saltado is savory and hearty. Be sure to sample the creative cocktails. Alternatively, try a delicious and refreshing chicha morada.

Name: La Cotriade
Address: 18 quai Emmanuel-Garnier, Les Sables d’Olonne, 85100, France
Description: At this family-run restaurant on the quayside opposite the fishing port, the seafood counter piled high with fish and shellfish sets the tone. The seafaring theme continues inside, where the chef busies himself in the open kitchen. The menu features seafood platters and specialities such as the famous cotriade (hence the name) – Brittany's answer to bouillabaisse. Then there is the selection of fresh fish chalked up on the daily specials board, and a few meat dishes.

Name: La Coupole
Description: La Coupole in the centre of De Panne has been a blue-chip value since 1989. Christine, in charge of the front of house and chef Jean-Paul bend over backwards to pamper their guests. The menu showcases timeless seafood classics: mussels in white wine, fresh North Sea shrimp and lobster straight from the fish tank. The menu shines the spotlight on produce like crab that is presented to diners before it is served with a spicy mayonnaise and fresh green salad, or translucent gleaming white cod, flanked by a rich, creamy Dugléré (tomatoes, shallots, white wine and butter) sauce. Heaven for foodies!

Name: La Coupole - Matsuhisa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: "Irasshaimase" – this is the exclamation with which diners are greeted here. Housed in the building that was once home to Europe's first indoor tennis courts, Nobuyuki Matsuhisa's restaurant buzzes with infectious vibrancy. The wide-ranging menu features a fusion of Japanese and Peruvian cuisines – everything is prepared in the open kitchen (there is also a sushi bar). The black cod miso is definitely worth trying.

Name: La Cour des Sens
Description: In a village house, the dinky dining room blends parquet floors with bare stone. Chef Benjamin Royer creates dishes that showcase a soft spot for premium produce and undeniable savoir-faire: langoustines flambéed on a stone and paired with Mirabelle plums or confit of Polmard lamb. Attentive front-of-house team.

Name: La Couronne
Address: 285 rue Charlet-Straton, à Argentière, Chamonix Mont-Blanc, 74400, France
Description: Built in the 1860s, this imposing building near the Swiss border has accommodated a hotel for over 160 years. It has since been nicely refurbished, while retaining its name. A young local chef cooks up appetising dishes that pay homage to the terroir: courgette tartare, soft-boiled egg, faisselle mousse; pork, polenta, Alpine harissa. At lunchtime, there is a simpler set menu. The pleasant terrace affords a view of the mountains.

Name: La Couronne
Description: This restaurant is run by a pair from Alsace who are passionate about what they do: Benoît Ligabue is a self-taught chef and Thiébaut Flory provides attentive service and spot-on wine recommendations. At this refined restaurant with a focus on the terroir, there is a bistronomy formule (except Fri and Sat evenings and Sun) and a fine dining menu featuring premium ingredients such as white truffles and Muscovy duck. The cooking is precise, the sauces flavoursome, and the presentation meticulous. Their take on bouillabaisse with scallops, monkfish and lobster is a favourite with regulars. They also have a delicatessen, and guestrooms in nearby Wittersdorf.

Name: La Coursive des Alpes
Description: Welcome to the ski resort’s former cinema, with a lounge bar on the ground-floor for snacks and a drink, and the restaurant proper laid out around a mezzanine of galleries. Chef Laurent Hillairet cooks noon and evening, 7/7, rolling out a modern, tasty, deftly crafted score. Sweetbread is the house signature, but their vitello tonnato paired with harissa seasoning, carrots and parmesan or the almost ethereal raclette of soft brioche bread and the ‘7 hour’ confit of beef à la royale are definitely recommended. The rice pudding with confit pears, grilled almonds and vanilla ice cream is just too wickedly tempting…

Name: La Courtille
Description: Trained by Raquel Carena at her Parisian institution, Le Baratin, Natalia Crozon serves deliciously down-to-earth regional cuisine in this restaurant accommodated in a converted silkworm farm built of white stone. Poached calf brains with lemon butter; pan-fried bluefin tuna steak with tomato ragout; apricot cake... plenty to whet the appetite. Take your pick from the appealing wine list that focuses on natural wines and local Tavel and Lirac labels. In summer, tables are laid out on the pretty terrace sheltered by an ancient cedar tree.

Name: La Courtille de Solutré
Address: 296 route de la Roche, Solutré-Pouilly, 71960, France
Description: A pretty country house, its charming terrace in the shade of an old chestnut tree... and a dynamic Basque chef, who puts passion and good - quality ingredients into his cooking, nicely accompanied by a fine selection of Pouilly - Fuissé wines! There is a handful of guestrooms.

Name: La Cravache
Description: The culinary classics have no secrets for Koen Devos, whose team can be relied on to add the odd contemporary touch to pedigree dishes. You can expect a repertory of premium produce such as lobster and partridge and recipes that show a reverence for authentic flavours, albeit with modern side dishes. Chef Devos is a horse lover, as you will quickly discover when you admire the elegant interior of this lavish villa. The B&B offers a view of the horses grazing from the windows.

Name: La Cristallerie
Description: La Cristallerie is the picture of lavish elegance. Located in the heart of Luxembourg and in the boutique hotel, Le Place d’Armes, the restaurant, which is fully the equal of its host, sports a glitzy interior dripping in gold leaf fixtures and Art nouveau stained glass. In the kitchen, chef Milan Brée draws upon his experience honed in top international establishments. His score calls upon Gallic traditions and exceptional premium produce, reworked with sophisticated contemporary techniques. The calf’s sweetbread is crispy on top and velvety inside, with a succulent intense gravy spiked with a hint of rum and a medley of Jerusalem artichoke textures. An outstanding front-of-house team adds flair to this quest for excellence and quality.

Name: La Croix Blanche
Description: Hard at work in the kitchens, the chef makes it a point of honour to use great seasonal ingredients. The dishes are a taste sensation, for example, the chicken supreme with mixed vegetables. Definitely a place you will want to tick off.

Name: La Croix d'Or
Address: 6 rue de la Herse, Le Pin-la-Garenne, 61400, France
Description: This welcoming hostelry, which belonged to the chef’s great grandparents, boasts an authentic family atmosphere. After learning the ropes in prestigious restaurants, the chef has returned to his roots in the company of his wife, who hails from the southwest as you might be able to guess from her accent. A quintessential French country inn, particularly when lunching on the small patio in fine weather.

Name: La Croix d'Ouchy
Description: A culinary landmark of Lausanne for over 30 years, this establishment can be relied upon to deliver a fresh, seasonal, pedigree score, founded on top-drawer, sometimes regional produce. The “suggestion menu” (lunch and evening) shines the spotlight on the chef’s talent and knack for sauces. The best tables are near the window or in the quieter room to the rear. Some dishes are available to take home. The Royal Savoy public carpark is conveniently located opposite. Bookings advised.

Name: La Croustade
Description: Lovingly tended flowerbeds, a delightful cottage garden and goldfish in the pond - dining on the terrace of this exquisite country house is heavenly in fine weather. Every month, chef Thierry composes a new menu that demonstrates his classical training and know-how. He freely delves into the cottage garden to enhance dishes such as mint-crusted rack of lamb and pan-fried foie gras.

Name: La Cucina
Address: Andaz Pattaya Jomtien Beach 345 Mu 3, Na Chom Thian, Sattahip, Chon Buri, 20250, Thailand
Description: Off the beaten tourist path, La Cucina offers an escape to a lush, tropical garden setting, where blue and white tiled floors, French windows and bossa nova tunes foster a relaxed atmosphere. This restaurant helmed by local chefs and an affable service team has an enticing Italian menu. Handmade pizzas are the stand-out.

Name: La Cucina Italiana
Description: In this cosy, romantic restaurant comprising just eight tables, chef Allesio Fioriniello continues his father’s legacy by cooking up authentic Italian dishes with southern overtones (the family hails from Naples). He is helped along in his mission by childhood friend, Enzo, who takes charge in the restaurant. Carefully prepared, seasonal dishes are a model of their kind and could include the likes of a rich, beautifully textured parmigiana di melanzane or Rossini venison with seared milk bread and panzerotti.

Name: La Cucina de' Mibabbo
Description: Exposed brickwork and lots of wood create a rustic, refined and welcoming atmosphere. Tuscan cuisine takes centre stage here, from the excellent charcuterie selection to the famous Florentine T-bone steak. When the weather warms up, a small covered terrace on the pavement offers the pleasure of al fresco dining.

Name: La Cucina dei Frigoriferi Milanesi
Description: An interesting location in the artistic-cultural setting of the Frigoriferi Milanesi industrial complex for this restaurant with a modern feel both in its decor and its market cuisine.

Name: La Cucina di Donna Carmela
Address: Contrada Grotte 7, località Carruba di Riposto, Riposto, 95018, Italy
Description: Generous Sicilian specialities reinterpreted with imagination and prepared using top-quality produce from the hotel’s orchards and vegetable garden, all beautifully presented in contemporary style, take centre stage here. There’s an extensive choice of meat and fish dishes showcased on tasting menus and an à la carte, which can be enjoyed either in the elegant dining room or on the attractive outdoor terrace shaded by palm trees. Courteous and professional service completes the picture.

Name: La Cuina de Can Simón
Description: Tossa de Mar, the “blue paradise” that so enchanted Marc Chagall, is a medieval town full of opportunities for visitors, who can enjoy a stroll through its alleyways or a swim in its coves. If this appeals, make it the perfect day by heading to this gastronomic restaurant. Here, at the foot of the town’s walls, siblings Lores, Josep María and Xavier conjure up contemporary dishes that pay homage to their grandparents: in their own words, “our family is one of artists and fishermen, and it is from this heritage that our cooking developed, using natural, artisanal and locally sourced ingredients”. In keeping with the traditions of Mediterranean cuisine and the local fishing industry, fish and seafood are understandably their strong suit, sourced daily from the fish auction (as an example, we loved the simple flavours of the stew with red mullet). However, they also offer dishes featuring rice and select cuts of meats that are more synonymous with the mountainous landscapes of inland Costa Brava.

Name: La Cuisine
Description: In the town centre, “la cuisine” is well and truly the star of this excellent eatery. Chef Johann Dubernet and his cheerful partner, Isabelle, in the dining room, sign colourful, fragrant and beautifully plated dishes whose influences are manifold: tartare of Basque trout, goat’s cheese naan, beetroot, lamb’s lettuce and Romeiko vinegar; iberico pluma pork, bulgogi, lemongrass-spiked garlic puree, pak choi cabbage, mashed sweet potato. The summum of gourmet indulgence!

Name: La Cuisine Mario Kalweit
Description: A nicely restored building from the late 19th century houses this stylish, modern, elegant restaurant serving creative cuisine. Pleasant terrace.

Name: La Cuisine d'Amélie
Address: Domaine de Fontenille, route de Roquefraiche, Lauris, 84360, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The restaurant of the Domaine de Fontenille, which sprawls over 70 acres of vineyards and grounds, serves aromatic Mediterranean cuisine with a distinct weakness for produce from the property’s own kitchen garden. The menu changes with the seasons and, in the evening, stars a splendid cast of noble produce (calf’s sweetbread, morels, turbot). As you sit on the superb terrace overlooking the grounds, be sure to try the estate's organic wines.

Name: La Cuisine d'un Gourmand
Description: Ambitious John Maes is a genuine good food lover. His mission in life is to source the best regional ingredients, to unfetter his creativity and to please or surprise his patrons with subtle fare. Outstanding quality at affordable prices. The tasteful, modern interior commands a fine view of the river Meuse.

Name: La Cuisine de Bertrand
Address: 22 quai Ernest-de-Franqueville, Les Sables d’Olonne, 85100, France
Description: Opposite the fishing harbour, it is well worth keeping an eye open for this low-profile restaurant. The chef unashamedly crafts textbook French recipes with the objective of showcasing first-rate ingredients in dishes that hit the spot every time. Diligent service.

Name: La Cuisine du Cloître
Description: At the foot of the cathedral, this former 17C cloister has plenty of character, courtesy of its old stones blended with more contemporary decor and furnishings. The chef's market-fresh cuisine varies with his mood (multi-course surprise menus in the evening) and the season. His consummate technique and the quality of the ingredients make for a pleasant experience, with a simpler, shorter menu at lunchtime. From the shaded terrace, you can even catch a glimpse of the chef at work in the kitchen.

Name: La Cuisine du Côté Vert
Description: The restaurant of Le Côté Vert Hotel unsurprisingly bears the hallmark of nature. Natural materials adorn the interior, whose floor to ceiling windows command a splendid view of the garden. Vegetables are the stars of the show in the chefs’ updated recipes, without forgetting meat and fish. The focus is on allowing each natural ingredient to shout its name.

Name: La Cábala
Description: A rustic-cum-contemporary restaurant somewhat tucked away in a narrow street with plenty of character just a few metres from the cathedral. The former taberna here has been completely transformed to make the most of the interior space, which is dominated by a white colour scheme and open brickwork. The contemporary-inspired à la carte, featuring a few dishes for sharing and what the restaurant calls “small individual bites” (don’t miss the Iberian ham croquettes with torrezno-style popcorn or the addictive spider crab ravioli with a saffron cream), is complemented by two set menus: Tradición (lunchtime, midweek only) and Gastronómico.

Name: La Cène
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Established in the historic town, the smart, understated interior decked in works of art is always a treat for the eye. The enthusiastic kitchen team rolls out a seasonal, creative score crafted from fresh produce. The menus change monthly: the lunchtime lineup is entitled ‘Inspiration’ and ‘Eclosion des sens’ in the evening. The culinary slant is purebred classical, served by an on-the-ball front-of-house team, all of which to the delight of a discerning business clientele. Splendid wine list, food-wine pairing evenings and a lounge with a cigar cellar are some of this establishment’s other distinctions.

Name: La Côte Bleue
Description: The Étang de Thau, a major shellfish farming site and lake in Languedoc, famous for its mussels and the legendary oysters of Bouzigues, is also well-known for its biodiversity on land, in the sea and in the airs. So, taking a seat on the terrace overlooking the lagoon is an opportunity not to be missed. Expect to tuck into delicious, ultra-fresh seafood, including oysters, mini squid in garlic and parsley or mussels broiled in garlic butter.

Name: La Côte des Monts Damnés
Address: 12 place de l'Orme, à Chavignol, Sancerre, 18300, France
Description: Always in synergy with the wines from the Bourgeois family winegrowing estate, the bistronomy menu particularly showcases the local terroir: green lentils from Berry and smoked bacon, roast quail in chestnut leaves and a reduction of the estate's grape juice; Sancerre croquettes with a cloud of vanilla and raspberry sorbet – pure indulgence. They also have comfortable guestrooms.

Name: La Cúpula
Description: Located on the top floor of the Jardines de Nivaria hotel, this restaurant has panoramic views and surprises for its colourful dome, which brings to mind the explosion of a supernova! The à la carte, featuring international and Canary Island cuisine that is brought to life in quite modern dishes (lime stuffed with foie gras and Oloroso sherry, fish from the island with potato foam, umami and spinach, and many more), is supported by two tasting menus: La Cúpula and Gastronómico.

Name: La Dariole
Description: In the heart of the old town and not far from the cathedral, this 15C half-timbered house showcases an easy alliance of old stonework and cosy touches. The chef, who even trained here when he was learning his trade, hits the mark with delicious cuisine that is in tune with the times. The seasonal menu changes regularly and features appealingly tasty dishes such as pork chop with potatoes and a caper jus.

Name: La Despensa del Etxanobe
Description: Situated next to the Etxanobe Atelier, with which it shares its kitchen facilities, this restaurant is much more informal in style, with exposed brick walls and an original iron structure that helps to distribute light. The cuisine here is traditional with a modern touch and is showcased on an à la carte plus three tasting menus: Bilbao, Gastronómico, and Arraigo País Vasco (the latter can be enhanced by choosing the Maridaje Plus wine-pairing option). We recommend asking for one of the dishes off the menu – if it’s available, don’t miss the delicious cod cheeks in a traditional Basque fish stew.

Name: La Deuvalière
Address: 18 rue de la Monnaie, Tours, 37000, France
Description: Julien and Alexandra have poured every ounce of their enthusiasm into successfully wooing local and visiting gourmets. Their seasonal cuisine is a treasure trove of culinary gems. The charm of their old country house, appointed with bare beams, terracotta tiled floors and a fireplace, together with the odd contemporary detail, further adds to the experience!

Name: La Devozione: The Oval
Address: 428 W. 16th St., New York, NY, 10011, USA
Description: This international outpost from Italy's 110-year-old, family-run Pastificio Di Martino, is a multi-concept space nestled within the Chelsea Market. The restaurant houses a pasta shop along with two dining spaces, including The Oval. It is aptly named, as the 30-seat counter awaits diners who will twirl their forks through a pasta tasting menu. It's all shapes, styles, and sizes, and it's far from dainty, with plate after plate of pasta. The manicotti is filled with sole and served with a bracing butter and caper sauce. Enjoy the penne served with rabbit confit and artichokes, and finish with a refreshing Mojito-inspired dessert with granita and grapefruit foam.

Name: La Diligence
Address: 13 rue du Bourg, La Ferté-Saint-Cyr, 41220, France
Description: This nicely restored former coaching inn offers tasty dishes showcasing produce of the local terroir; it also has comfortable guestrooms and a popular summer swimming pool. The welcome is particularly charming. A restaurant that is as friendly as it is stylish.

Name: La Dispensa
Description: Let yourself be courted by culinary creations in which the Mediterranean meets elegant Gallic cuisine. The house signature, Bottoni Carbonara, delicious raviolis with a melt-in-the-mouth centre, are flanked by a fragrant Parmesan mousse and crispy slivers of pork crackling. The tender veal fillet, enhanced by a velvety sauce, is truly worth writing home about. Make yourself comfortable in the glamorous, clean-edged interior, or on the terrace in summertime. A carefully chosen selection of wines by the glass completes this gourmet interlude. An address to discover forthwith!

Name: La Docena
Description: La Docena has been making a name for itself since 2012. Known throughout Mexico for their upscale but far from fussy style, this Guadalajara restaurant has a rustic charm thanks to brick walls and tile floors set with wood tables and chairs. Seafood is the focus here, though there are plenty of other options, and many dishes are kissed by the flames from their live-fire grill. The kitchen shows careful restraint, letting the quality ingredients stand on their own. Start with a plate of oysters, served raw or cooked over the grill, before moving on to tacos like the taco de jaiba with softshell crab over a split yellow and blue corn tortilla. Entrees, including their grilled young octopus with sweet potato chips and an herb mayonnaise, never disappoint.

Name: La Dotta
Address: 10/15 Convent Road, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: Relocated to the Si Lom area, the same team continues to operate under Chef Francesco Deiana. Vibrant blue and white tones greet you, and the atmosphere inside remains welcoming. Enjoy dishes from Italy's regions and watch fresh pasta being shaped by hand at the counter. Finished with pungent Pecorino Romano, the saffron gnocchetti with baby lamb ragù are gently aromatic, the pasta shells perfectly chewy. Weekend cookery classes reveal the secrets behind his recipes.

Name: La Ereta
Address: Parque de la Ereta, Alacant, 03001, Spain
Description: A striking modern property on the ascent up to the Castillo de Santa Bárbara, hence its superb views of the city. Here, Alicante-born chef Dani Frías offers two Mediterranean-based, contemporary menus (Ereta and Degus) that focus on seafood. This is demonstrated by one dish we particularly enjoyed: his delicious version of red shrimp stew (“caldereta de gamba roja”).

Name: La Fabrique
Address: 1 bis rue du Coq-Gaulois, Brie-Comte-Robert, 77170, France
Description: This industrial - style loft is well hidden at the end of a small alley. Guests enjoy the warm, convivial atmosphere at this contemporary restaurant, which offers delicious, bistro - style gourmet cuisine.

Name: La Femme du Boucher
Description: Established in a former butcher’s, energetic Laëtitia Visse, who trained at the Paris Ferrandi School before stints in star restaurants and renowned bistros (Guy Savoy, Alain Dutournier, Cyril Lignac, Olivier Nasti at Kaysersberg) has, unsurprisingly given the name, decided to focus on meat: homemade pâté, fried black pudding, sausages, pig’s trotters, etc… Equally in tune with the zeitgeist, her wine list is strongly focused towards natural and biodynamic wines. Casual service and vibe. In the finest traditions of a Gallic bistro!

Name: La Fermata
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the countryside around Alessandria, this 18C farmhouse has a modern, minimalist decor which serves as a backdrop for traditional Piedmontese cuisine with a clever modern twist. The chef offers just the right amount of creativity, with a focus on meat dishes and satisfying, memorable flavours that appeal to the emotions as well as the palate. Adding to the appeal, the elegant and exclusive ambience is the result of careful refurbishment, which has transformed the dining room into a triumph of art and design.

Name: La Ferme Ilharregui Baita
Description: This old 17C farmstead has been tastefully renovated both inside and out and is now the HQ of a modern Basque inn boasting an airy contemporary dining room. One tasting menu and three set theme menus shine the spotlight on the Basque terroir: the first revolves around pulses, the second is based on seafood and the third showcases local ingredients. The colourful dishes taste as good as they look, a case in point being the lamb with Tarbais beans and smoked aubergine caviar.

Name: La Ferme aux Grives
Description: This village inn retains all its old-world charm – exposed beams, terracotta floor tiles and a kitchen garden make an ideal setting in which to savour generous, nostalgic regional cuisine. Abounding in rich sauces and buttery, flaky pastry, this is traditional, hearty cooking at its most indulgent – think cuts of meat and poultry roasted in the open fireplace. In fine weather, guests can make the most of the lovely terrace laid out in the garden. Finally, those looking to prolong the experience can get a peaceful night's sleep at La Maison Rose.

Name: La Ferme de Cupelin
Description: In the upper reaches of the resort, this former 19C farmstead and haven of tranquillity is the lair of Florian and Lauriane Langellier, a youthful couple with an enviable CV (Four Seasons and Flocons de Sel (Megève), L'Armancette and finally Père Bise with Jean Sulpice where he worked as a pastry chef and she was in the front-of-house). The set menu showcases local produce from the lakes (arctic char), rivers (crayfish) and forests (game in season), without forgetting forays to Italy (Piedmont hazelnut gnocchi and Colonnata bacon). A fine dining experience starring tasty modern cuisine with a knockout view of Mont Blanc to boot - what’s not to like?

Name: La Ferme de Voisins
Description: You reach this lovely 19C farmhouse via a flower-decked courtyard, which serves as a patio in summertime. The relatively concise menu shines the spotlight on the house classics, which are prawns on sticks, the ‘irreplaceable’ calf’s head and signature desserts such as the rum and orange punch baba, together with a range of tasty and creative dishes. A fine establishment to try out post-haste!

Name: La Ferme du Chozal
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The restaurant may sport a characteristic rustic Alpine vibe, but the appetising cuisine is no less modern, made with fine local ingredients. And let's not forget the remarkable list of Alpine wines.

Name: La Ferme du Pré
Address: Route de Suresnes - Bois de Boulogne, Paris, 75016, France
Description: In a characteristic Normandy-style outbuilding, just opposite his restaurant Le Pré Catelan, chef and Meilleur Ouvrier de France Frédéric Anton fetes bistro classics, with simple, generous dishes such as boudin noir, chou farci, skate wing with beurre blanc, and profiteroles. The long narrow dining area with exposed ceiling beams exudes rustic charm with its vintage decor and old-fashioned crockery. A delightful terrace shaded by the trees of the Bois de Boulogne.

Name: La Ferrata
Description: The walls tell stories through photographs of locomotives and the warm glow of copper pots and lids at this century-old osteria. Rustic charm and conviviality define this welcoming venue, nestled in the picturesque historic center of Pordenone. Generous portions steeped in tradition emerge from the kitchen: cured meats, hearty cuts, and local cheeses share the stage with simple, authentic dishes such as beef cheek braised in Refosco wine, served alongside creamy polenta, a rustic, flavor-rich experience.

Name: La Fiaschetteria
Description: Enjoy excellent reinterpretations of Emilian classics in this large 18C farmhouse. It is lit with modern designer - style chandeliers and warmed by a large fireplace. The three splendid guestrooms combine elegance with typical regional decor.

Name: La Filanda
Description: Situated in the heart of the historic centre, this restaurant occupies an old spinning mill ("filanda") that has been completely restored without losing any of its original charm. Here, self-taught chef Barbara serves traditional dishes reinterpreted with real flair, such as the involtino di ciaffagnone filled with Maremma beef on a bed of melted pecorino cheese and crispy leek. The chef’s husband oversees the wine list, which includes a selection of Tuscan labels.

Name: La Filanda
Description: Housed on the first floor of an old silkworm factory, with a contemporary-style dining room that opens out on to a beautiful terrace in fine weather, this restaurant is one of the few in the province to serve top-quality fish and seafood, including a good selection of raw options. The cooked dishes on offer demonstrate a light modern touch and are prepared whenever possible using vegetables from the restaurant’s own garden.

Name: La Fine Bouche
Description: The chef's interest in regional traditions and his creative spirit are reflected in his use of the capuchin, an ancient utensil with a cast iron cone attached to a long rod, in which pieces of bacon are melted and used to flambée his scallops, lending them a slight grilled and smoked taste. With its hardwood floors, mouldings and exposed stonework, the tastefully refurbished dining room makes for an intimate dinner setting.

Name: La Fine Fourchette
Address: 2500 avenue du Bugey, à Virignin, Belley, 01300, France
Description: A jaw-dropping view over the Canal du Rhône and an elegant interior set the scene in this renowned regional temple of good food. Generous portions of Ain produce take the limelight in the chef’s well-crafted score, depicted by fascinating flavour combinations and impeccable plating. Special mention for the strawberry-themed dessert that will knock the tastebuds off fans of fine French fare!

Name: La Finestra in Cucina
Description: Set in Prague's Old Town, this is a great establishment for top-notch Italian food. Made with select ingredients and clear craftsmanship, dishes such as calamari fritti, brasato al Barolo or spaghetti alla carbonara are sure to impress. Also of note is the fine selection of aged meats cooked on the grill. The tasteful decor teamed with red-brick vaulted ceilings is also inviting – and you can see into the kitchen through a window.

Name: La Flamiche
Description: A classical interior lies behind the large windows of La Flamiche. Here, cuisine with robust traditional foundations is enhanced by a touch of modernity: one example would be the duck foie gras and smoked trout in a Granny Smith jelly, cucumber pickles and apple chutney – a beautifully crafted starter. Then there are the medallions of monkfish with lime, carrot and rocket, perfectly cooked in butter, the good old-fashioned way.

Name: La Fleur de Sel
Description: This spruce family-run business en route to the ski resorts is eminently welcoming. The several-course menu respects the seasons and showcases the cornucopia of excellent Savoyard produce. Cosy and fashionable, the interior also sports a warm rustic edge courtesy of a fireplace insert in the centre of the room. A lovely alfresco terrace adds to the establishment’s appeal.

Name: La Fleur de Thym
Description: David and Olivia embark you on an Ardennes adventure that is both familiar and polished in their welcoming house appointed in a modern vein. The chef’s deft, modern score is an ode to first-class ingredients which are allowed to shout their name. He may underscore scallops marinated in sake with a mirin dressing and textures of yellow beetroot, while Anjou pigeon acquires a worldly dimension in two dishes flanked by autumn veggies, fried panisse (chickpeas) and a knockout port wine sauce. Recognisable, contemporary fare with a respectful light touch that takes regional cuisine to new heights.

Name: La Flèche d'Argent
Address: Hôtel Princesse Flore, 5 place Allard, Royat, 63130, France
Description: La Flèche d'Argent – the name is a nod to the incredible "Silver Arrows" Mercedes-Benz Formula 1 cars of the 1930s – references the nearby Circuit de Charade racetrack. In a plush decor, chef Clément Lorente serves up his contemporary cuisine in a multi-course set menu format. His dishes display excellent technique and incorporate creative touches. The ingredients are of the highest quality: foie gras from the Plaine de Limagne, artichokes from Roussillon, saffron from Mazayes, bluefin tuna from the Mediterranean. For dessert, a tribute to the chef's grandmother's Agen prune flan is a real hit, flambéed tableside. Market-based set menu at lunchtime; brunch on Sundays.

Name: La Font
Address: Rafael Masó 1-3, Canet de Mar, 08360, Spain
Description: This bright restaurant with a strong family feel is run by several siblings. Everything here revolves around the counter in the centre of the dining space, with an unusual curved glass partition that enables guests to watch the live action in the kitchen. The traditionally inspired à la carte, which is well complemented by a daily menu, has a strong focus on the sea, although it also includes several top-quality meat dishes.

Name: La Fontaine
Address: 2F, Trade Center, River Garden, 170 Nguyen Van Huong Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 70000, Vietnam
Description: This bistro with a vintage Parisian vibe is a spin-off of La Villa, operated by the same French owner-chef. Open for breakfast, lunch and dinner, it serves classic, no-frills Gallic fare ranging from pastries and baguette sandwiches to pork terrine and pâté en croûte. Inspired by the chef’s childhood souvenirs, the rustic Provence-style lamb ragout is unbelievably rich and flavoursome. Also check out the wine list leaning towards French labels.

Name: La Fontaine - L’Artiste et le Cuisinier
Description: Set in a charming village, tucked away in a narrow street, this trendy bistro is accommodated in an attractive old house adopted by a well-travelled couple… They – she is the "artiste" and he the "cuisinier" (or cook) – invite us to sample their contemporary bistronomy cuisine in a friendly, pleasant setting. Following the seasons, their menu draws its bold flavours from the produce of local suppliers. On the restaurant floor, the service is efficient and the wine list is well explained. The bill is absolutely fair, and the cheerful terrace is a real bonus!

Name: La Fontana Restaurant & Bar
Address: Via ai Monti della Trinità 44, Locarno, 6600, Switzerland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Splendidly located inside the Hotel Belvedere, at an altitude of approximately 240m, this elegant south-facing restaurant boasts a splendid terrace and a lounge space. Depending on where you sit, watch the chef at work in the kitchen or enjoy the impressive views through La Fontana’s ground floor picture windows overlooking its verdant surroundings. The culinary focus here is on modern and seasonal Mediterranean cuisine without neglecting the region’s gastronomic roots. In addition to the classic menu, you can also choose the 4- or 5-course tasting option as well as the restaurant’s signature dishes such as the La Fontana tartare, the Chateaubriand, and the Raviolini del Plin. The extensive glass-fronted wine cabinets at the entrance provide an impressive backdrop.

Name: La Fontanella
Description: The family-run La Fontanella, which opened back in 1977, is today in the hands of the second generation. The visitor is immediately struck by the elegant warmth of the premises, depicted by artwork, soft lighting and bouquets of fresh flowers. The entire team is cheerful and good-natured, particularly when they liberally scatter shavings of white alba truffle on your taglioni alla parmigiana. In addition to reverently crafting a purebred Italian lineup (the house specialty is osso bucco), the chef enjoys adding contemporary twists, together with nods to Belgian cuisine, like pheasant à la brabançonne in autumn. Highly popular so bookings are advised.

Name: La Foresteria
Address: Contrada Passo di Gurra SP 79 km 91, Menfi, 92013, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Planeta’s elegance is reflected in this property nestled among Sicilian vineyards. The rooms bear the signature of the celebrated winery, while the restaurant offers modern Sicilian cuisine, with an à la carte menu and two tasting journeys. Don’t miss “Casa Planeta”: five iconic courses inspired by the monsù, the chefs of ancient noble residences.

Name: La Forge
Address: 1 rue de la Brosse, Le Subdray, 18570, France
Description: This restaurant run by a sincere and welcoming couple in an old farmhouse about 15km from Bourges is definitely one to recommend. Everything is house-made, most of the vegetables come from the family's own garden, and freshness is the order of the day in each dish. Multi-course set menus – more elaborate in the evening and at weekends – to be enjoyed on the shaded terrace bordered by the garden.

Name: La Forge
Description: Fontaine-Daniel is the epitome of an old French country village and the birthplace of the famous Toiles de Mayenne fabrics. Overlooking a pond and the forest, this venue is housed in a former outbuilding of a Cistercian abbey, which became the hub of this textile manufacturing enterprise in the 19C. Chef William Blondel cooks primarily with local produce that he doesn’t hesitate to enhance with modern and creative twists gleaned from his own globetrotting travels.

Name: La Forquilla
Description: La Forquilla is definitely a restaurant with a difference given that owner-chef Vidal Gravalosa takes care of everything, including a huge amount of preparation before every sitting, impressive work in the kitchen, as well as service at the handful of tables. His cooking is centred around a tasting menu plus a creatively inspired à la carte featuring an array of seasonal recipes. Standout dishes include the Maresme peas with baby squid and Iberian pork jowl, and the crispy Segovian suckling pig served with its own sauce, parsnip purée and baby gem lettuce.

Name: La Fortaleza
Description: An elegant, unique and very special restaurant that is a must on the island. It offers two creative menus that showcase the best of Mallorcan cuisine accompanied by superb views from the rooftop terrace in summer.

Name: La Fortuna
Address: Via Ponte Rino 6, Campagnola Cremasca, 26010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated less than five minutes’ drive from the centre of Crema, this delightful contemporary-style trattoria boasts a modern dining room with a minimalist decor brightened by splashes of colour. The equally attractive cuisine is inspired mainly by Italian traditions, especially at lunchtime during the week (when the prices are very competitive), while in the evenings (at the weekend) dishes are enhanced by additional contemporary touches. The wine list is divided between Italian and French labels, including an excellent selection of champagnes.

Name: La Fossa del Grano
Description: A must for anyone looking for traditional home cooking and authentic cuisine from Puglia. Make sure you try the antipasti, and then move on to a first or main course.

Name: La Foucaudière
Address: 2 place de la Foucaudière, Senillé-Saint-Sauveur, 86100, France
Description: This quiet restaurant on the outskirts of Châtellerault features a minimalist decor in a palette of sandy hues. In the kitchen, Richard Robe demonstrates his experience – his perfectly balanced dishes reveal strong technical skills: crispy tempura frogs' legs, home-made ketchup and herb pesto; free-range chicken grilled flat on the yakitori barbecue, served with sauce diable; vanilla and buckwheat caramel millefeuille. Generous food that exudes sincerity.

Name: La Fourchette
Description: In the historic city centre, this warm and lively bistro wins diners over with its smiling welcome and convivial atmosphere – and is frequently full. The traditional cuisine, rooted in the South of France, focuses on well-executed, comforting dishes: white pudding, breaded pig's trotters with mustard, veal onglet with mustard sauce and pommes dauphine, Avignon-style beef daube… and a praline meringue glacée, a special suggested that day by the waitstaff. An unpretentious and indulgent family-run restaurant.

Name: La Fugascina Ristorante
Description: Situated on a small square with an attractive outdoor space, this restaurant offers a menu which features fish from the lake and other seasonal produce prepared with both modern and traditional techniques, but always with a contemporary flair. The focus is on locally sourced (zero-mile, wherever possible) produce.

Name: La Fábrica
Description: Chef Ricardo Temiño’s restaurant, located next to the San Juan civic centre, boasts an elegantly minimalist interior which provides the backdrop for high-quality contemporary cuisine teeming with flavour and inspired by traditional and international recipes. The à la carte includes an option to order small plates and dishes for sharing, enabling guests to discover many different dishes. This is complemented by a constantly changing menu called Temporada (Season), which is only available for lunch from Tuesday to Friday. An adjoining dining space (Ricardo Temiño), but with the same entrance, offers more personal, sophisticated and gastronomic cuisine.

Name: La Gaetana
Address: 352 Phuket Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: It may be tiny, with 6 tables, but La Gaetana, decorated like an Italian house in warm colours, provides a warm welcome and is big on charm. They import most ingredients from Italy and make the sourdough, pasta, gelato and limoncello in-house. Chef Gianni cooks the fettucine with tomato sauce and crab meat using his family recipe from Campania. The menu is largely influenced by such southern classics. As Gianni takes a summer holiday each year, call ahead first.

Name: La Gaffe
Description: Chef Yann Le Scavarec, who hails from Morbihan, is at the helm of this restaurant, which boasts an ideal location on the Saint-Florent harbour front. His well-crafted contemporary cooking showcases local produce, eg lamb and veal from Oletta, fish sourced directly from a local fisherman, barbecued crayfish. Try the bluefin tuna, puffed rice crust, served as a tartare with nori, miso-cooked aubergine and a sesame and lime condiment. The elegant modern interior reflects the philosophy behind the food.

Name: La Gallina
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Villa Sparina is an elegant rural resort named after its winery. The Orangerie hosts guests, whereas fine dining unfolds at La Gallina restaurant: amid rustic and elegant settings, contemporary cuisine is presented, drawing ample inspiration from Piedmont, as well as nearby Liguria (the dessert "Good Morning Genoa" playfully mimics breakfast with cappuccino and focaccia), though Campania references, the chef's homeland, never falter. Personalised wine selection: exclusively Champagne, abundant Piedmont choices, with particular emphasis on Barbaresco and Barolo.

Name: La Galupe
Description: Moored on the banks of the Adour, this former bargemen's inn is said to be over three centuries old. It still proudly boasts its spruce white façade with the characteristic red shutters of the Basque Country and an interior with its cachet intact – stone flooring, exposed beams and an open fireplace. Even the original fish counter and the hooks for drying the fish are still present and correct. This restaurant, which for 30 years was run by famous Basque chef Christian Parra, now has Stéphane Besse at the helm. Very local ingredients are the foundation of his fresh, colourful cuisine; the fishermen, duck and lamb farmers, the baker, the ceramist (who designed the plates) are all from the village.

Name: La Gare
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A very contemporary local institution (since 1874)! It has a perfect combination of elegance, vitality and conviviality, offering a brasserie for those in a hurry or carefully-prepared modern cuisine in a conservatory setting... all accompanied by one of the finest wine lists in the country.

Name: La Garenne
Address: Le Dracy, 4 rue du Pressoir, Dracy-le-Fort, 71640, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An appealing place where you can enjoy, for example, a venison and foie gras pâté en croute with pickled vegetables and gherkin condiment, or a lobster-stuffed veal tournedos, with conchiglie and mushrooms. The contemporary-style dining room, with glass-fronted wine cellar, overlooks the terrace and grounds. The hotel, meanwhile, boasts pleasant guestrooms, a swimming pool and a spa.

Name: La Gloire
Description: A venerable Montargis institution, located alongside the N7. For several generations, culinary tradition has been revisited with flair and generosity; do not miss out on the rather imposing dessert trolley.

Name: La Gloriette
Description: Overflowing in charm, this townhouse appointed in a contemporary vein sports an idyllic terrace overlooking the kitchen garden of chef Olivier Bauche. The chef works with sincere affection and a warm heart and doesn’t hesitate to try out new ideas, sometimes surprising us with amusing combinations of sweet and sour flavours or, for example, with a spicy lovage ice cream that he serves with a saddle of medium rare lamb. In season, he frequently has game from Ardennes on the menu. Dive into the wine list safe in the knowledge that La Gloriette Hotel, just opposite, can put you up for the night in style...

Name: La Golmotte
Description: Not far from Le Mont-Dore, authenticity is guaranteed in this inn, where the dining area was originally a cowshed! Fresh ingredients and copious portions of tasty traditional cuisine, such as tender pork cheeks, home-made potato purÉe and Saint-PourÇain white wine sauce… even if the chef allows himself a few incursions into more contemporary territory, with dishes such as salmon gravlax.

Name: La Gordita
Address: 6 Montague Street, Dublin City, D02 XE65, Ireland
Description: There’s a simple, cosy quality to La Gordita thanks to its narrow dining room with a wooden floor, brown leather upholstery and soft lighting. It’s got a lively atmosphere too, a great accompaniment to the authentic Spanish sharing plates, such as the 'arroz negro a la llauna' – fragrant, umami-packed squid ink rice with octopus and squid – whose extra cooking time is well worth the wait. Friendly service enhances the experience, and the extensive menu will have you rounding up friends so you can sample as much as possible.

Name: La Gouesnière - Domaine du Limonay
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: This hostelry founded in 1936 is a fine dining establishment whose delicate, creative recipes celebrate Brittany’s splendid produce: seafood from Saint Malo Bay, lamb from the salt marshes, buckwheat… A gourmet experience in every sense of the word, further enhanced by the chef’s inimitable flair for jus and sauces.

Name: La Gourmandière
Description: A longstanding Ardennes institution, this plush 1890 property is enjoying a new lease of life courtesy of two young brothers-cum-partners. The deftly plated dishes slalom between tradition and modernity: pressed foie gras laced in old rum, veal sweetbread, Rossini tournedos steak, turbot and risotto of fregola sarda… Gloriously peaceful patio to the rear.

Name: La Grande Brasserie BIB
Description: In the heart of Avignon, in a fine historical building – once a cloister – Mathieu Desmarest (Pollen) has swapped bistronomy for this brasserie, which is open seven days a week. The focus is on traditional French cuisine: devilled eggs, pâté en croûte, Burgundy snails or andouillette with mustard sauce, plus a weekly special (eg confit duck parmentier with aioli). Three concepts under one roof: brasserie, cocktail and tapas bar, and cheese bar. For fine weather, the leafy terrace in the courtyard is one of the city's loveliest spots.

Name: La Grande Georgette
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The name is a nod to an amusing tradition whereby a fire engine’s ladder was named after the captain's wife. In the former Chanzy fire station (1926), chef Julien Raphanel crafts a high-flying score: lightly seared langoustine with a briny seaweed sabayon; pan-fried Racan pigeon, caramelised apples and buckwheat espuma… The terrace commands a jaw-dropping view of Reims cathedral. Next-door, Little Georgette rolls out a bistronomic lineup of French family favourites at reasonable prices.

Name: La Grande Salle
Address: Hôtel de France, place de la Libération, Auch, 32000, France
Description: Revamped from top to toe, this city-centre institution is still going strong under the aegis of a family team, namely three brothers – one in the dining room (an MOF), one in the kitchen and one is a pastry chef! The culinary lineup aims to highlight the gastronomic heritage of the Gers region: raw and cooked scallops; Bigorre black pork and leeks; duck and foie gras pie, sliced at the table; baked Alaska, flambéed in front of you! Foodies with an appetite will be delighted to learn that the sauce boats are left on the table – irresistible with the house made bread! Simpler fare at Le 9ème brasserie.

Name: La Grange
Description: This former barn is now an inviting country chic restaurant appointed in an alpine vein. The menu stars tasty well-crafted food, made with premium regional ingredients such as marinated salmon trout from Lake Oô; confit of egg, shredded confit of duck and creamy sweetcorn… What’s not to like?

Name: La Grange
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A wood-rich interior and a striking feeding trough set the scene in this isolated old farmstead that is clearly proud of its rural origins. A few modern details do however contrast with the initial portrait, starting with stylised photos and a glazed wine cellar. In the same vein, the chef orchestrates a modern score founded on tradition. The menu is concise and enticing: beef tartare, 30-day aged on the bone rib of beef, sole meunière, wild seabass...

Name: La Grange
Description: On the banks of the Nive beneath the arcades, this inviting eatery savvily mixes old stones and beams with a contemporary edge. The traditional score, updated with Basque overtones, stars wholesome indulgent flavours: bourguignon-style braised chuck beef and cheeks with a pastry stuffed with fresh herbs and winter veg or the granny-approved house dessert, cocolait. Very popular with the locals, La Grange is just the place to get a glimpse of the real Bayonne.

Name: La Grange des Agapes
Description: Like every true enthusiast, Thierry Barot is a master of multi - tasking. Not content to offer tasty and appetising theme - based menus (vegetables, Provence, asparagus, truffles etc), he regularly runs cookery classes and is the author of a book of chocolate recipes. What a feast!

Name: La Grangée
Description: Chef Jean-Baptiste Girard, an enthusiastic champion of his region, and his Japanese-born wife, Maiko, have turned this village inn around. Local produce (Charolais beef, organic vegetables, saffron…) and what the chef forages take centre stage on the menu - the wild garlic brioche is simply delicious ! Attentive service and tableware crafted by a local artisan make for a delightful experience.

Name: La Grappe d'Or
Description: A restaurant where superb flavours and a friendly atmosphere go hand in hand. Chef Theotim Bioret is strongly inspired by northern Italy, from Venice to Ventimiglia: Piedmont-style agnolotti del plin, sage and a parmesan jus; calf's liver saltimbocca, spinach and polenta. In addition to the à la carte menu, the chef serves a more affordable weekly dish. Meticulous plating, precise cooking and delicious sauces combine to create a faultless dining experience.

Name: La Grappe d'Or
Description: This flower - decked house built in 1554 could not be more inviting and the characteristic regional interior has lost none of its yesteryear appeal. Classic regional delicacies on the menu: choucroute, baeckeofe, knuckle of ham, stuffed trout, etc.

Name: La Grillade Gourmande
Description: The restaurant specialises in cooking top-drawer produce over a wood fire: whole sea bass with fennel, rib of beef, pluma de pata negra, venison with a peppery sauce poivrade – all dishes are the handiwork of a cheerful chef of Lyon origins. The atmosphere is friendly and buzzy and, come summertime, the garden is bliss.

Name: La Gritta
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Two of your senses will experience powerful marine sensations in this place. Your sight will be delighted with the enchanting view, especially from the terrace, and your taste will be tantalised by the imaginative, top - quality cuisine.

Name: La Guisandera de Piñera
Description: A restaurant that offers traditional Asturian cuisine, including delicious stews and other famous dishes from this region of Northern Spain such as “arroz con pitu de caleya” (a type of chicken paella), La Guisandera’s signature fabada stew, and arroz con leche.

Name: La Hermosa de Alba
Description: A restaurant with a fun, modern feel that is enjoying considerable success in the city. The menu here is contemporary in style with elements of fusion cooking and dishes designed for sharing.

Name: La Huertona
Description: If you enjoy dining with a view, La Huertona could be the place. Located a stone’s throw from the mouth of the Sella river, this delightful restaurant with a rustic ambience features dining rooms with superb vistas of green meadows and cows grazing from its idyllic setting. Options here include a concise à la carte of market-inspired options on which grilled dishes take centre stage, with a strong focus on fish and seafood sourced from local auctions, and an extensive tasting menu that needs to be pre-booked. We loved the freshly prepared “salpicón” of Ribadesella lobster and the locally caught fish cooked on the holm oak grill. Seasonal eel dishes are also a must here.

Name: La Ideal Mar
Description: Located on the ground floor of a modern building close to the bullring, La Ideal Mar’s main focus is on the sea, as you’ll deduce from its name. Chef Andrés Conde has returned home after a long stint working in kitchens around the world (France, USA, Peru, South Africa, Dubai, etc) to offer locals his relaxed, traditional style of cuisine with the occasional contemporary touch. On the menu you’ll find oysters, oven-baked fish sourced directly from the market, a superb seafood stew, an extensive array of rice dishes (for two people), plus a couple of meat options. The glass-fronted kitchen overlooks the dining room where the colourful live lobster tank is a key feature.

Name: La Jovita per L'Esteve GV
Address: Carretera de la Bisbal D'Empordà 46, Calonge, 17251, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: This historic establishment has taken a new direction under the leadership of chef Esteve Garcia and his partner, Celine Wu, who decided to pack their bags and leave their respective jobs in Singapore to embark on a more personal project, where Catalan cuisine is the epicentre of everything. They offer traditional-regional cuisine with modern touches, which takes shape under the umbrella of a comprehensive menu that includes daily specials, options for sharing, fish from the Palamós fish market... as well as delicious rice dishes and fideuás (minimum two diners). Their speciality? Without a doubt, their lobster au gratin with hollandaise sauce and mushroom duxelle (must be ordered one day in advance).

Name: La Kanro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Presentation sparkles with colour here as the chef skilfully weaves in flowers and herbs and decorates his plates with sauces of vegetable and spices. Combo platters of appetisers, garnished with flowers, beguile the senses. Trying out a departure from normal French practice, meat dishes are stripped of garnishes. Prix fixe menus change monthly and the chef repeatedly updates his menus.

Name: La Kuccagna
Address: Via Milano 14, località Barbuzzera, Dovera, 26010, Italy
Description: La Kuccagna's fresh, quality offerings are bolstered by management that is always full of energy; menus range between land (tripe with legumes, squash and mushrooms) and sea (amberjack with coconut sauce, sea urchin and herbs), while the grill is always ready to accommodate the most suitable cuts of meat. A fine selection of wines starting with labels from beyond the Alps. The location is exquisitely bucolic, while the interior is modern and comfortable.

Name: La Kucina
Address: via Giulio De Petra 67, Foggia, 71121, Italy
Description: Welcoming and a short distance from the centre, the restaurant distinguishes itself through an architectural character of clear contemporary orientation and an equally modern gastronomic offering. The cooking ranges with balance between fish and meat dishes, interpreted through modern recipes and contemporary cooking techniques, among which the use of the Josper oven stands out, reserved in particular for selected meats left to mature in the dedicated dry-ageing unit. Among these, prized Iberian cuts feature prominently on the evening menu. At lunch, the offering broadens to include more immediate and accessible proposals, conceived to meet different tastes and budgets without any compromise on quality.

Name: La Laiterie
Address: 138 avenue de l'Hippodrome, à Lambersart, Lille, 59130, France
Description: Once a dairy, this farmhouse steeped in history lies next to the Parc de la Citadelle and close to the banks of the Deûle Canal. Elegant contemporary rooms inside and a large garden with a terrace are the perfect foil for the chef's creative cuisine, which delves freely into produce from Northern France, with a fondness for surf and turf recipes.

Name: La Lanterne
Address: 17 place de la Chambre, Metz, 57000, France
Description: La Lanterne is inspired by "La Lanterne du Bon Dieu", the nickname given to Metz Cathedral, which looms over the restaurant. It is run by a young couple who really give it their all: chef Célia Bertrand, originally from Metz, and Romain Bouchesèche, from the Jura, who takes care of matters in the dining room and in the wine cellar. They propose modern cuisine (pollack, morels, vin jaune) that draws inspiration from the Jura, where they met.

Name: La Leggenda dei Frati
Description: After an uphill approach if you’re arriving here on foot, you come into the Villa Bardini museum complex and from there into this elegant and welcoming restaurant which provides the setting for delicious, creative and modern cuisine. Here, chef Filippo Saporito, never one to rest on his laurels, continues to experiment and perfect his cuisine, which focuses mainly on Italian culinary traditions and a scrupulous selection of top-quality ingredients, preferably from sustainable supply chains (various types of meat, bread and pasta), all showcased on different menus, including a vegetarian option. In summer, enjoy your meal on the romantic terrace surrounded by greenery and the scents of herbs, with a glimpse of Santa Croce church as a backdrop. Although the centre of Florence is not far away, it seems as though you’re already in the Tuscan hills, even with the occasional sound of cicadas in the background.

Name: La Ligne Rouge
Description: This stylish contemporary eatery depicted by crisp clean lines is the epitome of tranquil. On the edge of Soignes Forest, get ready to be pampered by a friendly waiting team. Guillaume Desart himself describes his style as “nouvelle classical cuisine”. Indeed, his passion for top-drawer ingredients and his flair for sauces are indicative of a desire to uphold tradition, albeit scattered with playful notes, such as crispy calf sweetbread flanked by a velvety béarnaise with nasturtium-flavoured vinegar.

Name: La Limonaia
Description: Away from the centre, nestled within a residential neighbourhood of quiet apartment buildings, this address surprises from the very first glance: the interior calls to mind a large veranda, furnished with an original and harmonious mix of objects and decorative pieces chosen with great taste – among them a piano that catches the eye – and looking out onto an intimate yet splendid terrace where, in the warmer months, dinner is taken in the shade of lemon trees. The cooking favours fire and the grill, from which generous, personal and intriguing dishes emerge, not always bound to tradition, but built around the finest the market has to offer. Worthy of particular note, for instance, is the ‘grilled fish collar finished all’acquapazza’, based on grouper, sampled during our most recent visit. The service, entrusted to a courteous and attentive all-female team, moves with natural ease, while the excellent background music contributes to an atmosphere of pleasingly elegant relaxation.

Name: La Llorería
Description: A restaurant that exudes a sense of freedom, excitement and youthful exuberance in equal measure – qualities which combine perfectly with consistency, technique and a passion for hard work. The setting, which takes on the appearance of a bar with just a few tables and has a counter set up for dining, is relatively simple, but this is compensated in spades by contemporary cuisine featuring flavours and textures that are always interesting. Choose between an à la carte particularly designed for sharing, with the option of “raciones” and half plates.

Name: La Llotja
Address: Sant Roc 23, L'Ametlla de Mar, 43860, Spain
Description: At La Llotja, chef Marc Miró pulls out all the stops to ensure that ingredients and flavour are very much the stars of the show here, as showcased in recipes based around fresh and seasonal market cuisine and a strong maritime feel. The à la carte is well supported by excellent daily suggestions and, if you’re looking for a more extensive dining experience, a tasting menu option. The rice dishes never fail to impress here, while the tuna loin tartare is always of excellent quality.

Name: La Locanda dei Beccaria
Description: Housed in the village’s historic wine cellar, this well - kept, rustic - style restaurant with typical wooden ceilings serves traditional, regional cuisine.

Name: La Locanda del Cardinale
Description: Situated right in the centre of Assisi, La Locanda del Cardinale occupies an old palazzo that is home to the perfectly preserved remains of a Roman villa dating back to 70 BC in a fascinating setting full of history. The menu features simple recipes such as crispy organic egg with asparagus and marjoram, as well as more elaborate, modern dishes including quail and Danubio brioche with barbecued artichoke. It’s not surprising that this delightful restaurant also boasts a superb wine cellar with an array of carefully chosen labels that will delight wine-enthusiasts.

Name: La Locanda di Fabio e Vale
Description: Young, informal and friendly owners Fabio and Vale welcome guests to their restaurant in Offanengo, just a few kilometres from Crema. A good choice for anyone looking for a change from traditional cuisine, the restaurant serves moderately creative dishes including a good selection of fish options (the Mazara del Vallo red prawns served with green gazpacho, caviar and lemon are particularly delicious).

Name: La Locanda di Piero
Address: Via Roma 34, strada per Dueville, Montecchio Precalcino, 36030, Italy
Description: Housed in a small country villa with the ambience of a private residence, this restaurant boasts a dining room with a welcoming fireplace in winter and a veranda full of natural light, giving it a classic feel that makes it perfect for an elegant and romantic dinner. The cuisine is distinctive and full of substance, featuring a selection of meat and fish dishes that includes classic and creative options alike.

Name: La Locanda di Pietracupa
Address: Via Madonna di Pietracupa 31, San Donato in Poggio, 50028, Italy
Description: The gastronomic dream of every traveler in Tuscany takes shape at this restaurant, housed in a quintessential Chianti farmhouse with a shaded terrace dedicated to summer service. The menu presents a notable procession of regional flavors guided by the seasons: pici with salt cod, three peppers, and pistachio pesto; squab with truffle vinaigrette; ricotta and citrus cake with ginger sauce… culminating in the unmissable Fiorentina, the territory’s timeless icon.

Name: La Locandiera
Description: At the bottom of a steep valley, a rustic restaurant that offers fine cuisine, much appreciated in the area, with a great preference for local products. Old traditional recipes are revisited with a personal touch.

Name: La Loggia Bistrò
Description: Tucked into a slightly secluded courtyard yet still in the heart of the city, this venue offers alfresco service of discreet charm during the summer months. The interiors surprise with dramatic hot-air balloons descending from the ceiling, design details that help create a distinctive and welcoming atmosphere. The culinary offering moves between dishes rooted in local tradition and more creative forays, including some appealing fish options.

Name: La Lozerette
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: In the heart of the Cévennes, this charming inn is the domain of a chef who specialises in cleverly crafted dishes using regionally sourced produce. On the wine side, Pierrette, a talented sommelier, will help you choose from the 300 references available… Let’s not forget the splendid cheeseboard!

Name: La Lucciola
Description: A small light shines from a back alley. The restaurant’s name means ‘firefly’, and the chef’s sunny smile lights up the spirits of his guests. The fare is Italian, yet Japanese sensibility lives within it. Counter seating is kappo-influenced, while the charcoal grill reflects use of longstanding Japanese methods. Japanese and Western serving-ware are used to suit each dish; the chef personally repairing pottery with kintsugi gold and lacquer comes from the Japanese spirit. Many customers frequent La Lucciola to enjoy the presence of the good-humoured chef.

Name: La Luce
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Set in a panoramic location, slightly set back from the town centre, La Luce is the gourmet restaurant of a hotel with classic charm and an intimate atmosphere. In the warmer months, guests are enchanted by the veranda, which offers truly stunning views, whilst in winter the elegant dining rooms provide an intimate and refined welcome.
