The cuisine is built on a solid foundation of traditional techniques, showcasing local produce with subtle Mediterranean influences and a careful respect for seasonality: meat and fish are presented on an equal footing. The wine list is well-curated, extensive and diverse, featuring interesting labels and a few rare vintages for connoisseurs. The setting further enhances the experience: far from the hustle and bustle of the city, with views opening out onto the lake and mountains.

Name: La Luce
Description: Tucked away down a cobbled street in the heart of the city, this well-run restaurant is easily spotted thanks to the Italian flag hanging outside. The kitchen delivers on that promise, with a menu firmly rooted in the Italian classics. Homemade pastas are at the heart of the appeal, including the likes of orecchiette with truffle and egg yolk. The genial service team are keen to please and the room has a rustic feel courtesy of its exposed brickwork.

Name: La Luge
Address: Perreres, loc. Varvoyes, Breuil Cervinia, 11021, Italy
Description: Situated in a tranquil, panoramic location on the road to Breuil-Cervinia (less than 4km away), this old farm has been transformed over the past decade into an intimate little hotel with a good restaurant decorated in attractive mountain style and enhanced by a fireplace that is always lit in winter. Here, you can enjoy simple, authentic cuisine prepared from top-quality ingredients with careful attention paid to seasonality. The owner himself oversees the well-stocked wine cellar.

Name: La Lumira
Description: In a town synonymous with tortellini, Lumira offers an authentically regional experience with a touch of modernity; contemporary interiors and warm service ensure a memorable visit. The menu draws on the generosity of Emilian and Romagnolo cuisines, a natural expression of the chef-owner, born right here. The house-made fresh pastas are essential: from tortellini in capon broth to pumpkin tortelli dressed with garlic, olive oil, chili, and broccoli. Special praise goes to the bollito misto, served with excellently crafted sauces.

Name: La Lune
Description: Japanese elements are woven into French cuisine to evoke a sense of Japan. Amuse-bouches focus on seafood, a tribute to the abundance of the sea. Service on wooden trays with chopsticks adds a distinct Japanese touch. The shifting seasons are expressed through vegetables and fruit — pulses in spring, watermelon in summer, chestnuts in autumn, and Shogoin daikon in winter. Foie gras poêlé is a house staple, expressing the chef’s respect for tradition.

Name: La Lune
Address: L628, 6F, The Mixc, 701 Fuchun Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: The high-ceilinged room is lavishly furnished with elegant chandeliers, ceiling fans and elaborate trims. The kitchen team excels in fusion Chinese cooking that creatively mixes and matches influences and techniques from various regional cuisines. Thinly sliced air-dried mackerel steeped in a special briny-sweet sauce is loaded with umami. The slow-cooked veal in a truffle sauce literally melts in your mouth. The curated tea list is intriguing!

Name: La Maadeleine by Benoît Neusy
Address: rue de la Halle 42, Mons, 7000, Belgium
Description: The crisp minimalist lines and natural dune coloured palette of La MAAdeleine bear the distinctive hallmark of MAArchitects. Seasoned chef Benoît Neusy unveils the full gamut of his delicate score, as he shines the spotlight on fish and seafood, as well as surf ‘n turf dishes. He may enhance textbook vol-au-vent (crisp melt-in-the-mouth puff pastry and a velvety sauce to die for) by adding crispy calf’s sweetbread and prawns to the traditional chicken filling. The chef often adds playful touches to full-bodied, familiar flavours, illustrated by cod prepared in a crust of mimolette cheese. Neusy has managed to progress and evolve, whilst remaining true to the heart-warming culinary signature that has earned him so many faithful and enthusiastic followers.

Name: La Machine à Coudes
Description: Welcoming and bubbly owner Marlène has a knack for always surrounding herself with a motivated team. They are happy to work with the seasonal produce – scallops and squash – that goes into creating a single set menu at lunchtime, and a more creative and ambitious dinner menu. Good food and wine pairings. An enjoyable moment of bistronomy.

Name: La Maddalena
Description: Situated in a prime spot on the banks of the River Oder, there are few restaurants with a more enticing terrace than this. Ask for a seat here and, on a warm summer’s night, watch as darkness falls and the streetlights gleam on the river’s surface. The setting is matched by cooking that puts an emphasis on top-quality local meats – for dessert, look out for the chocolate fondant with a fruity punch. Let the knowledgeable staff guide you in picking complementary wines.

Name: La Madia
Description: This authentic rural trattoria overlooking the valley and Franciacorta specialises in regional produce and typical Italian cuisine. Each dish on the menu lists the origin of the ingredients used, plus the name and address of the producer. Specialities include tagliolini pasta sautéed in a walnut sauce with tuna. Top quality cuisine offering excellent value for money.

Name: La Maison
Description: In a pedestrian street of downtown Orthez, this vast bistro is housed in what was once a fishing tackle shop. The interior sports a patchwork of mismatched objects. The single set lunch menu changes weekly and at weekends and in the evenings, you will find a concise à la carte lineup with starters to share and upmarket ingredients in a bistro vein.

Name: La Maison
Description: You are made to feel right at home here at La Maison, once a winegrowers' home, with a magnificent stone interior. Creative cuisine is served in the form of dishes in which a number of different elements are juxtaposed. Ludovic Davouze always makes sure to showcase local producers, and enjoys adding an element of surprise, with original combinations of flavours such as just-seared little tuna marinated with chives, with smoked aubergine and miso sauce. The patio is a joy in fine weather.

Name: La Maison Alyette - Domaine de Locguénolé
Address: Route de Port-Louis, Le Hingair, Kervignac, 56700, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A bistro on the Domaine de Locguénolé, La Maison Alyette pays tribute to the château's former owner. Devised by chef Yann Maget (a Meilleur Ouvrier de France), the menu revolves around traditional cuisine made with quality local ingredients. The portions are generous – a case in point being the pork belly and its creamy fregola sarda risotto; the flavours are winning – take the whiting quenelles and their flavoursome bisque; the dishes are moreish – for instance the religieuse with caramel mousse and ice cream. Attractive lunch set menu. View of the gardens, and a lovely terrace.

Name: La Maison Confortable
Description: Yosuke Akasaka studied for years under Pierre Gagnaire. From this legend of the French culinary world, Akasaka inherited the avant-garde sensibility that inspires his creativity. Combining seafood with meat and vegetables with fruit, Akasaka teases out unexpected qualities of the ingredients with which he works. While Gagnaire chose a table for his logo, Akasaka favours a house for his motif. The subtext is the same: a space that evokes the feelings of home, comfort and belonging; hence the name of the restaurant.

Name: La Maison Delfino
Address: Via Lagrange 4, borgo Mercato, Moncalieri, 10024, Italy
Description: This small, elegant restaurant outside the centre is enthusiastically run by two brothers: round tables and well - kept dining room for savoring seafood specialities.

Name: La Maison Eric
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Terrace
Description: This absolute gem of an old half-timbered house is tucked away in a side street. The interior is tastefully decorated and replete with charming details; outside, a gorgeous terrace gives onto the wonderful garden. Classic French cuisine is served as a four-course lunch menu. Fresh, top-quality ingredients go into dishes such as sea bass fillet with fennel risotto or Barbary duck breast with root vegetable purée. Attentive, courteous and committed to the well-being of his guests, owner Eric Grandgirard is always on hand and glad to recommend wine pairings from a list dominated by local and French labels.

Name: La Maison Forte
Address: Place de la Maison-Forte, Farnay, 42320, France
Description: This stately stone manor is aptly named. Inside, a certain Scandinavian simplicity reigns – with exposed stone walls, light oak tables and grey upholstered chairs. This is the first venture of a young couple of professionals who honed their skills in starred establishments: Mickaël Marcoux in the kitchen and Marie-Jeanne Rault in the front of house. Playing on the full spectrum of textures, the dishes showcase savvy combinations (green asparagus, buckwheat, smoked pike roe and wild garlic sabayon) and punchy flavours (stuffed morels, fregola risotto, vin jaune emulsion). Slick, polished service.

Name: La Maison Rouge
Description: Chef Jean Kuentz (dubbed Petit Jean), who learned the ropes in top Parisian establishments, runs this iconic establishment in Colmar's historic centre, a stone's throw from the Petite Venise quarter. In an 11C edifice, he crafts gourmet fare, navigating between regional and more modern dishes, accompanied by well-chosen wines.

Name: La Maison Tourangelle
Description: Rustic meets modern in this 18C Touraine building. It boasts a delightful terrace on the Cher and fine cuisine using quality ingredients.

Name: La Maison d'Avignon
Description: Once the sommelier at Petit Amour on Spritzenplatz, Mathias Mercier has now realised his dream and opened his own restaurant just a short distance away. In a relaxed setting, diners are offered a small à la carte selection; if they wish, they can create a small set menu comprising three to six courses from the individual dishes. Alternatively, they can opt for the nine-course tasting menu – the value for money is excellent. The cuisine clearly draws on the chef-patron's southern French roots, featuring delicacies such as fougasse with a superb anchoïade (anchovy sauce) and pralines infused with lavender or pastis. A standout dish is the sea bass with peach, verbena and navy beans. The wine list includes some rare gems at reasonable prices. Friendly and attentive service.

Name: La Maison d'Estournel
Address: Lieu-dit Leyssac, route de Poumeys, Saint-Estèphe, 33180, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Formerly Château Pomys, Maison d’Estournel oozes understated glamour with its well-heeled interior and fine terrace overlooking the grounds and vineyards. Consultant chef, Jérôme Banctel (Le Gabriel) is behind the new take on classical recipes and seeks to celebrate the gardens and producers of Médoc: green asparagus, smoked Aquitaine sturgeon and Baerii Sturia caviar; roast poultry, morels and supreme sauce. Seasonal and indulgent depicts this restaurant in the heart of wine-growing France.

Name: La Maison d'Œuvres
Description: Having earned his stripes in renowned kitchens (Christophe Dufossé, Patrick Henriroux), chef Kévin Dos Santos has set up shop in an old building a stone's throw from the 1 000-year-old church, Église St Pancrace. The decor is understated, with tables upstairs and out on the small courtyard terrace. This 30-something chef crafts his menu to the rhythm of the seasons and the zeitgeist: creamy cauliflower, blood orange and sunflower seed praline; truffle-infused scallop quenelle, celeriac millefeuille, hazelnuts and a reduced jus. The evening menu is updated regularly and calls on more premium ingredients. On weekday lunchtimes, the menu is simpler. The fine wine cellar caters to a wide range of budgets.

Name: La Maison de Filip
Description: Situated at the entrance to the pedestrian section of the beautiful city of Trento, this intimate restaurant has a modern, minimalist and vaguely Nordic style, with just a few solid wood tables and stools of different sizes. The menu features a concise selection of carefully thought-out dishes, with starters, first and main courses (meat, fish or vegetarian) that are elegant, well prepared and contemporary in style. Beautiful presentation completes the picture.

Name: La Maison de Petit Pierre
Description: Enthusiastic chef Pierre Augé is at the helm of this restaurant with a personalised decor that is located close to the bullring. He greets each and every customer with an infectious smile because he is there to spread joy with his tasty creative cuisine based on local ingredients! Rather than bask in the media hype, he is clearly driven by a desire to continuously explore new culinary avenues. It's a joy to behold – and tuck into – dishes such as his whisky-marinated pavé de bœuf steak and cauliflower mousseline with vanilla; hake with piperade and green jus; or stracciatella with asparagus and bacon tuile. A buzzy, friendly vibe, enhanced by the personality of the chef, and the warm, cheerful service of his wife, adds the final flourish: recommended!

Name: La Maison des Blés - Le Bouche à Oreille
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A contemporary setting, a modern interior and a choice of two venues to treat yourself to a slap-up meal: Brasserie Louis and its traditional lineup or its gourmet sibling, Le Bouche à Oreille. Slick, professional service and food that showcases top-notch ingredients (including lobster, scallops and foie gras) with a creative twist. Modern, comfortable guestrooms.

Name: La Maison des Bois
Description: Beneath a thatched roof and smothered in Virginia creeper, this spruce, hundred-year-old inn has been welcoming travellers since 1926. Three generations have preserved its authentic character, whilst breathing a new lease of life thanks to a tasteful restoration. The same spirit prevails on the menu, with traditional fare and market-fresh dishes made with premium produce. The house signature is lobster stew in season. Terrace in the shade of old plane trees. The epitome of a French country inn!

Name: La Maison des Toqués
Address: 26 rue de la Prée-aux-Ducs, Noirmoutier-en-l'Île, 85330, France
Description: Aurore and Sébastien Duchenne share the same passion for top-quality regional produce, often organic, which they transform into delicious recipes that capture the zeitgeist and are inspired by market availability. As you enter, you are greeted by a colourful, modern interior whose blue and white walls are adorned with artwork, providing the perfect foil to elegantly plated ingredients such as lobster, local oysters, John Dory or royal Charmilles pigeon. Booking highly advisable.

Name: La Maison du Village
Address: Rue de la Fontanette 41, Sauges, 2024, Switzerland
Description: With its resolutely relaxed ambience, this auberge is far from the traditional image of a high temple of gastronomy. Here, Marc Strebel, a young chef from the Valais, conjures up dishes very much inspired by a return to nature. Superb view of the lake from the terrace.

Name: La Mangeoire
Description: Near Lake Madine, this beautifully restored farmstead sports a chic rustic vibe, depicted by the straw-filled manger (its namesake) that continues to line one wall. It is the HQ of Quentin Pierre, a nature lover who spares no effort in bringing local producers into the mix thanks to ingredients such as trout from Saint-Mihiel, pork from Vilotte-sur-Aire, organic veg from Belleray. His cuisine is seasonal, fresh and simple. The tasting menu incorporates more premium ingredients (foie gras, arctic char sweetbreads). The wine list shines the spotlight on local Côtes de Meuse vintages.

Name: La Mangeoire
Address: 2 rue du Castrum (Le Bourg), Floirac, 46600, France
Description: In this picturesque Lot village, the traveller cannot fail but notice the handsome limestone edifice with a slate roof, flanked by a terrace and Belle Époque conservatory. The globe-trotting chef demonstrates a weakness for exotic combinations: velvety, humus-like aubergines, burnt rye bread, fried Camus artichoke and pork fillet dried in the hearthplace; lightly seared secreto pata negro pork with peanuts and ginger, roast fennel and whole wheat noodles. Bistronomic in style, internationally sourced and strewn with tributes to Asia and North African spices.

Name: La Mar Madrid by Gastón Acurio
Address: Avenida del General Perón 36, Madrid, 28020, Spain
Description: This casual restaurant with a festive atmosphere (it even has Latin music playing) is located just a short hop from the Santiago Bernabéu stadium and marks the arrival in Madrid and Europe of the Gastón Acurio group, which has other similar establishments under the same La Mar concept in Santiago de Chile, Bogotá, Miami, San Francisco, and Dubai. You will find a bar area with high tables, designed for snacking and cocktail tasting, as well as another bar for cold dishes and a comfortable dining room with the kitchen at the back. What's on offer? A fairly comprehensive Peruvian-based menu, with starters and snacks, tiraditos, ceviches, grilled and wok-cooked dishes that reflect Creole, Chifa and Nikkei cuisine. Don't miss the delicious Nikkei ceviche, with bluefin tuna, cucumber, sesame oil and Nikkei leche de tigre!

Name: La Mar by Gastón Acurio
Address: Atlantis The Royal, Crescent Road, The Palm Jumeriah, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Enthusiastic staff are here to greet you at this first-floor restaurant at the Atlantis The Royal hotel – the views are impressive and the DJ ensures the atmosphere never lets up. The large fish counter is busting with prime seafood and the menu is full of classic Peruvian dishes, from ceviche and tiraditos to anticuchos. A pisco sour will help you make your choices.

Name: La Mar by Gastón Acurio
Address: InterContinental Doha Beach & Spa, Street 900, Bldg.25, Zone 61, Al DafnaWest Bay, Doha, 6822, Qatar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Come for the beachfront location, stay for the vibrant Peruvian dishes at this light and airy restaurant within the grounds of the InterContinental Hotel. Gastón Acurio is a fine ambassador for Peruvian food and all bases are covered here, from ceviches to anticuchos. The colourful, rustic dishes deliver plenty of punchy flavours and are perfect for sharing. As you sit and soak up the lively atmosphere, you’ll be struck by what a fun night out it all is. And the wallet-friendly prices make it even more appealing.

Name: La Marcha
Address: 2026 San Pablo Ave., Berkeley, CA, 94702, USA
Description: This Spanish delight is a coveted spot for both tapas and paella, offered in varieties from the traditional mixta (prawns, chicken, chorizo, garlic, peppers) to the inventive “tres cerditos” (three little pigs) featuring pork chorizo, shoulder and belly. The classic tapas are also out in full force — from grilled head-on garlic shrimp and salt cod croquettes with nutty romesco, to tortilla Española. Located on busy San Pablo Avenue, the lively space offers enticements for groups of all sizes: foursomes can make the most of the sizable paellas, while a duo of happy hours offer discounts on wine at the L-shaped bar and a selection of free tapas, perfect for solo diners or couples.

Name: La Marianna
Description: A historic seafood trattoria of Rimini near the Tiberius Bridge, various managements have succeeded one another since 1908, yet the current proprietor remains true to the spirit of the place: almost exclusively seafood dishes, prepared simply and straightforwardly to showcase the freshness of the ingredients, served in modest yet atmospheric dining rooms with a convivial and informal ambiance.

Name: La Marmite du Pêcheur
Address: Boulevard des Tilleuls, Les Mées, 04190, France
Description: This restaurant, a former mill, stands at the foot of the village’s iconic jagged cliffs, Les Pénitents. It serves fish and seafood specialities (bouillabaisse to order), together with succulent meats, including lamb from Sisteron. The interior sports a modern vibe, offset by an old mill wheel that endows the interior with a characterful dimension.

Name: La Martinatica
Description: Housed in an old mill, this restaurant boasts a warm and welcoming dining room crowned by wood beams and elegant furnishings. The menu offers a selection of meat and fish dishes, although the latter are the main speciality of the owner-chef, who can usually be seen taking orders in the dining room. The raw seafood option demonstrates the skill and imagination of the chef, with its array of small bites which are both creative and delicious. The attractive outdoor space is perfect for summer dining.

Name: La Maruca - Castellana
Address: Paseo de la Castellana 212, Madrid, 28001, Spain
Description: A restaurant with the same name as its older sibling in Calle Velázquez, although this one is located along an elegant section of the Castellana avenue! This spacious eatery is decorated in pleasant white tones and boasts two terraces (a smaller one by the entrance, and a second, much larger internal one designed in the style of a garden). The essence of the cooking here is rooted in tradition with a nod to Santander, the culinary DNA of the Cantabria region and, in particular, a desire to bring the authentic flavours of the sea to the Spanish capital. We highly recommend the fish soup, served two ways and teeming with flavour.

Name: La Maruca - López de Hoyos
Description: In keeping with the focus in its sister restaurants along the city’s Castellana and Velázquez streets, the region of Cantabria takes complete centre-stage here. The standout features in this spacious, contemporary eatery with its large windows looking out onto the street are the welcoming terrace to the rear and an unwavering focus on time-honoured Cantabrian cooking. The latter is based around quality ingredients and simply prepared dishes that retain a strong emphasis on detail. Specialities include anchovies, Santander-style fried squid, brandade fritters, stews (mountain stew and Lebaniego stew from the town of Liébana), and Cachopo, a typical dish combining steak, ham and cheese.

Name: La Maruca - Velázquez
Description: A restaurant that exudes a fresh, optimistic approach through two iconic themes, namely Santander and Cantabria. This lively and informal setting features a multi-purpose bar and contemporary dining spaces embellished with the occasional designer detail. Its à la carte reflects cuisine that is 100% traditional, with a predominance of Cantabrian dishes (Cantabrian anchovies, fried squid from Santander, hake direct from the fish auction etc) with an equal focus on preparation and high-quality ingredients. Make sure you try the famous Cañadío cheesecake, the recipe for which has remained unchanged since 1981.

Name: La Maréa
Description: Opposite the sea and the ochre-coloured rocks of the Estérel mountains and looking down on the beach and port of La Figueirette, this restaurant was founded in the 1950s by a local fisherman. It has passed into the capable hands of Jérôme Cervera, a former fishmonger. The chef whips up a menu featuring ultra-fresh seafood and carefully crafted dishes, such as lightly seared red mullet served with fruity olive oil and seasonal vegetables. The attentive and bright service adds to your enjoyment of the meal. At lunch and dinner, an appealing set menu reprises dishes from the à la carte menu – tuck in on the terrace or in the pretty dining area with a sea view.

Name: La Masseria
Address: Via Chiesa 61, località Marzaglia, Modena, 41123, Italy
Description: A corner of Puglia at Modena’s doorstep: not a masseria, but an old mill that welcomes with the aromas and flavors of the heel of Italy. Vegetables reign supreme – stuffed peppers, eggplant parmigiana, fava purée with chicory – while, despite being in egg-pasta territory, fresh Mediterranean interpretations shine. Among the entrées, ample space is given to meats cooked over live embers, the authentic heart of Puglian tradition. To close, desserts arrive in a large basket: small delights, often featuring dried fruit and chocolate, celebrating a simple and genuine indulgence.

Name: La Masía de Chencho
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This restaurant delights guests thanks to its setting in an attractive farmhouse with a rustic yet elegant ambience and plenty of space for private events. Good traditional cuisine with a focus on high-quality ingredients, including an appetising choice of rice dishes. The impressive and extensive wine cellar is an added bonus.

Name: La Matelote
Description: A family-run business that pays tribute to women must be a good sign! A “matelote” is the fisherman’s wife, whose talent cannot be equalled when it comes to preparing fish, just like that of this establishment devoted body and soul to seafood (but not to the exclusion of other ingredients). Fish and shellfish are crafted in keeping with culinary tradition and with the firm intention of encouraging sustainable fishing. Save room for the patriotic line-up of Gallic desserts, such as soufflé, the house signature dish.

Name: La Mer
Description: Having earned his spurs at some award-winning restaurants, most recently at Seesteg, owner and head chef Hilko Uphoffis, together with his partner Giulia Casto, is at the helm of this smart restaurant located right next to the Michels Thalasso Hotel Nordseehaus, on the edge of the pedestrian/shopping zone. His classically French cuisine also demonstrates the odd modern flourish, as in the North Sea ling, cooked in nut butter, with lobster ravioli. The restaurant itself is also inviting, with its beautifully bright, pared-down and modern interior, as well as its appealing terrace laid out in front of the large window façade.

Name: La Mercerie
Address: 53 Howard St., New York, NY, 10013, USA
Description: This hot spot is surely an essential SOHO experience, set in an opulent emporium by noted interior design firm Roman and Williams. Especially at lunch, the room basks in its own beauty and in the beauty of the well-heeled patrons who huddle around tiny tables adorned with delicate blooms. The open kitchen, too, is a sight unto itself with sage-green tiles and gleaming cookware. It all feels very chic and very French, accented by a menu that delivers in careful indulgence. Chicken consommé with foie gras is a delicious study in contrasts, while cod steamed in a donabe with grain mustard, leeks, and potatoes offers both sophistication and richness. A wealth of classic desserts like profiteroles, tarte tatin, and crème brûlée taste of sweet nostalgia.

Name: La Mercerie
Description: Just a hop from Marseille’s historic Canebière, this bolthole is one of the stars of the city’s fine dining scene. At the helm is English-born chef, Harry Cummins, assisted by Quebec-born sommelière, Laura Vidal. A sensibly priced menu sets the lunchtime scene, while a more creative five-course cast takes front stage in the evening. A feelgood bistronomic score and seasonal produce: finely diced veggies, a barbecue edge and savvy seasonings. A cosmopolitan team and a funky R&B soundtrack depict this eatery that is almost always fully booked, although you will have more chance of finding a seat at non-peak times, at the counter facing the kitchen or, from April to October, on the terrace on Cours Saint Louis.

Name: La Meridiana
Description: In business for over 50 years, this long-established, centrally located restaurant has changed its look over the years and is now a modern bistro with an attractive outdoor summer space overlooking the magical town centre. Here, the owner-chef serves fish prepared in two different ways, either in typical Italian tradition or in a style inspired by his native Spain – his paella is definitely worth sampling! The front of house is overseen by the owner’s friendly wife, who is also at hand to help with your wine choices.

Name: La Mesa de Conus
Description: Attractive, modern and different, and designed for just 12 people to dine at the bar, hence our strong recommendation to book ahead. Chef Víctor Conus conjures up contemporary cooking with a focus on quality ingredients, the seasons and his own personal experiences. This is showcased on a single surprise tasting menu built around the best Galician ingredients available daily albeit with a nod to his Andalucian roots. Produce sourced from his kitchen garden in Nigrán are always present (including delicious Loba beans) as are pork-based products (charcuterie, as well as cuts such as “abanico”, “pluma” and “secreto”), given that his family runs the Jamones Doña Lola company in the town of Bollullos Par del Condado, in Huelva province). They always start with a plate of Paleta Ibérica Edición Especial “La Consentida” ham and the famous “de la Yaya” croquettes”!

Name: La Milla Marbella
Address: Urbanización de los Verdiales, Marbella, 29604, Spain
Description: Located on the sand at the heart of the Playa de los Nagüeles, this former “chiringuito” (beach bar) has been successfully brought up to date to add a stylish decor to its unbeatable setting. Here, you can enjoy traditional Mediterranean cuisine that flies the flag for fish and seafood of the highest quality and which is enhanced by modern touches yet without losing its Andalucian flavour. Although the dining room boasts stunning views, La Milla also features two pleasant terraces. The menu includes a selection of charcoal-grilled dishes, as well as appetising options such as the Andalusian ceviche and red prawns, or their dry rice with clams and green sauce.

Name: La Mira de Gredos
Address: Carretera de El Barco, Hoyos del Espino, 05634, Spain
Description: Found on the first floor of the hotel La Mira de Gredos, this restaurant is furnished with a large windowed room, to marvel at the Sierra de Gredos as you eat. Out of the kitchen comes an updated traditional cuisine, with a choice of à la carte service and one tasting menu. Dishes not to be missed? Try the popular Patatas revolconas, with paprika from La Vera and pork crackling, or the very tasty white bean stew from El Barco with its traditional sacramentos (cured meats and sausages).

Name: La Miranda Gourmet Stübli
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: At the wonderfully elegant yet cosy fine dining restaurant of Chasa Montana hotel, chef Bernd Fabian and his team conjure up a surprise menu comprising three to five courses. Each dish celebrates an extraordinary diversity of exceptional and predominantly regional produce, showcasing them in modern and precise dishes. With a limited number of tables, the restaurant ensures friendly service – the chefs serve and explain the dishes personally, and even the head chef and his sous-chef are on hand to engage with diners. The fantastic wine list boasts an impressive range of renowned labels. Host and sommelier Daniel Eisner embodies a passion for wine shared by the whole team.

Name: La Mirande
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Set within the historical walls of La Mirande, the mansion right next to the Palais des Papes, this fine dining restaurant is beautifully decorated. At your table in the superb 18C interior or in the gorgeous garden, tuck into delicious cuisine that exudes the flavours of the South of France.

Name: La Morena
Address: Paseo de la Castellana 210, Madrid, 28046, Spain
Description: A contemporary yet informal bistro that aims to bring the unique maritime world of the waters off the coast of Tarifa to the Spanish capital, both in terms of its aesthetics and gastronomy. The cooking, featuring an array of light yet extremely delicious dishes, is a fusion of Cádiz, Japanese and Latin American cuisine, and is especially designed for sharing (Dogfish saam in citrus dress with pork airbag and crunchy onion, Red tuna tataki with roasted chili sauce and tomato chutney, Katsu-Sando with cheek meat in tonkatsu sauce and cabbage salad...).

Name: La Morera de Pablo & Ester
Description: With a convenient location near the Plaça de la Pau, away from the tourist crowds, this restaurant boasts a completely glass-fronted dining room complemented by an attractive outdoor terrace in the shade of a large mulberry tree. The modern, fun and traditionally based menu includes short explanations and sketches of the dishes, which are always meticulously presented. A tasting menu is also available.

Name: La Mulata
Description: One of the classic addresses in the Puertochico district of the city, La Mulata owes its name to a species of black crab that lives in the rocks dotted around its docks and jetties. It features a maritime-inspired minimalist interior which includes a bar that is always very busy thanks to its array of tapas and “raciones”, a striking fish and seafood display (close to it there’s also a live lobster tank), plus a pleasant dining room. The à la carte menu also offers a few meat dishes plus an interesting selection of savoury rice options with a focus on the sea. Make sure you try the superb pan-cooked clams and also enquire about the fresh fish of the day.

Name: La Musardière
Description: Located in the heart of the village, close to Claude Monet's house and the Musée des Impressionnismes Giverny, La Musardière serves a bistronomy lunch menu at Le M and more ambitious dining options in the evening at Révélations. The convivial, contemporary bistro setting is complemented by a pleasant terrace that receives plenty of sun in summer. A number of guestrooms are available, should you wish to extend your stay.

Name: La Muña
Description: In this elegant, contemporary-style setting, friendly waitstaff serve up food that is an interesting fusion of Peruvian and Asian cuisine. The four- or six-course omakase menu is highly recommended. Alternatively, there is a good range of à la carte dishes listed under four headings: "Crudo", "Gyoza & Crujiente", "Caliente" and "Guarnición". Housed in Schweizerhof hotel, this restaurant is only open on winter evenings, presenting an authentic culinary experience using top-quality ingredients. Incidentally, la muña is a medicinal plant in the Andes that is said to help against altitude sickness.

Name: La Muña
Description: This restaurant on the sixth floor of hotel La Réserve Eden au Lac, on the shores of Lake Zurich, serves Peruvian-Japanese cuisine in the form of interesting and unfussy dishes made from top-notch ingredients. Up here you can dine in a cosy atmosphere beneath the exposed roof beams or out on the fantastic rooftop terrace – the view over the lake and the Old Town is magnificent! Service is attentive and professional. Exceptional wine list.

Name: La Mère Anne
Description: La Mère Anne is a huge business encompassing a range of activities. You can hire the venue for parties, spend the night in modern guestrooms, but above all, enjoy good food! The chef favours regional produce, which he showcases in contemporary dishes. These steer clear of frills, focusing instead on straightforward, delicious flavours.

Name: La Mère Germaine
Description: Jean Cocteau used to eat at this local institution, which has been serving fresh fish and seafood since 1938. It is lovely just to sit on the terrace and gaze out over the harbour!

Name: La Mère Germaine
Description: En route to the French Riviera, Paris's upper crust, including movie stars from Mistinguett to Jean Gabin and Fernandel, used to stop off in this village so beloved of wine buffs. The restaurant, still named after its 1922 founder, Germaine Vion, features huge murals evoking Belle Époque Paris, in the style of Toulouse-Lautrec, and a delightful terrace commanding a panoramic view. The Mediterranean-inspired cuisine elevates the ingredients and vegetables of Provence. The splendid wine list includes a good selection of Châteauneuf-du-Pape labels.

Name: La Mère Hamard
Description: This stone-built inn, which opened in 1903, is a genuine institution. The delightful dining room is flanked by a welcoming terrace shaded by wisteria, ideal to sample delicate, generous dishes, tinged with the occasional exotic influence. Attentive welcome and a few guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: La Méditerranée
Description: This elegantly understated establishment opposite the Odéon Theatre pays tribute to the sea and the flavour of authentic produce. In a bright space decorated with Mediterranean frescoes, guests tuck into egg mayonnaise with king crab and lime, fragrant bouillabaisse or delicately golden sole meunière. Attentive hospitality and highly professional service are the icing on the cake.

Name: La Môme
Address: No. 02, 7F, West, JLC, 29 Wangfu Street, Qinhuai, Nanjing, Chinese Mainland
Description: The view of the rooftop garden from the glazed interior sets the lush green vibe. The chef adds a creative spin to French cuisine with chargrilled dishes like local turbot that is semi-dried in the ichiya-boshi tradition and then grilled and served with bearnaise laced with shrimp oil and pork crackling for extra richness. Foie gras terrine is sandwiched between wafer-thin, duck-shaped cookies and plated over caramelised apple.

Name: La Nicchia
Description: This tastefully decorated restaurant is housed in a late - 18C building, which is marked on an old map from the Napoleonic era. Here the best local ingredients are selected to create regional dishes with the occasional contemporary twist.

Name: La Nigra
Description: Located in the old port, it is a restaurant with tasteful and very pleasant interiors, where chef-patron Gaetano, together with his wife Sonia, welcomes guests first thing in the morning for breakfast and a wide selection of homemade pastries. The kitchen offers a wide selection of traditional island and Sicilian dishes, prepared with the day's catch, such as the delicious “Paccheri alla carbonara di mare”, made with swordfish, raw prawns, amberjack roe and mullet bottarga. It is, of course, essential to save room for their delicious desserts, including a signature deconstructed cannolo.

Name: La Notizia 53
Description: Although situated away from the tourist centre, Enzo Coccia’s pizzeria continues to be considered one of the best places for pizza in Campania. Featuring classic Neapolitan pizzas with soft, stringy dough, the menu offers traditional and creative toppings alike. The “'mpustarella”, a five-grain and wholemeal flour roll with different fillings, more than compensates for the lack of “fritti” on the menu. The first historic restaurant at number 53 has now been joined by a second address at number 94/a nearby.

Name: La Nunziadêina
Description: A landmark occasion: in 2026, the fourth generation celebrated one hundred years of history of this establishment, also with its inclusion in the Guide. The venture was first set in motion by Annunciata in Cittanova, before closing in 2002 and reopening four years later at its present address, directly opposite the magnificent Abbey of Nonantola, taking on the name that had long served as its founder’s nickname: Nunziadêina. Since then, the common thread has remained the same: the delicacies and indulgent treats of Emilia-Romagna.The dining rooms are homely, yet attentive to detail; fresh flowers on every table lend a pleasing touch, while a fire crackling at the back of the room offers a foretaste of one of the house’s specialities, charcoal grilled meat. Alongside this, there is always fresh pasta, outstanding charcuterie and a wealth of traditional recipes, all rounded off by the customary irresistible dessert trolley. An impressive wine list completes the offering. A truly deserving venue!

Name: La Oficina
Description: Carito Lourenço and Germán Carrizo's more casual proposal, a short hop from Fierro, their award-winning restaurant, has found its space in an old bar in the Ruzafa neighbourhood. Conceptually, we find a modern bistro with a wide and varied menu, even featuring a cocktail section. A maturation chamber with various fish (brimming with sea bream or sea bass, which usually mature for seven days) is a surprising sight, and appetizing pieces of both picaña and Galician blonde cutlet (requiring about 50 days of maturation). The menu, which allows the grill to take the limelight, includes small bites and tasty market dishes, such as its Tart, onions, endive. Prefer to be guided? Order one of their tasting menus: Grilled Matured Fish, Grilled Vegetarian, Grilled Meat or, if you want to treat yourself, the one called Te damos de comer.

Name: La Padrona
Description: This glamorous, two-story looker is the place to be. Located within Raffles Boston, this playful Italian restaurant starts with an easygoing ground floor bar and lounge. Up the grand staircase, find a high-energy dining room, while a large, U-shaped bar anchors this gorgeous space fit with big windows, globe lights and gold accents. Thankfully, these stylish environs also come with substantial cooking. Start with cheese and fennel breadsticks before digging into beautifully seared scallops finished in saffron butter. The pastas are all made in-house and many of the entrees are portioned to share. An extensive wine selection, an astute cocktail program and a sharp service team complete this proper night out.

Name: La Palomba
Description: Boasting the attractive ambience of a typical Italian trattoria, La Palomba has been run by the Cinti family since 1965 and is now in the hands of the third generation. The menu features Umbrian specialities including delicious home-made umbrichelli pasta served with various sauces.

Name: La Palombe
Address: 267 Kensington High Street, Kensington, London, W8 6NA, United Kingdom
Description: Ideally located on Kensington High Street, this inviting bistro beckons you in with its friendly team and enticing menus. The soft pastel décor is studded with references to the colourful owner’s love of shooting, including framed lithographs of wild birds and deer antlers hanging on the ceiling – so it’s no surprise to find plenty of seasonal game on offer. Despite a few hints of tempered creativity, the cooking is classical French at its heart, with the likes of confit duck leg and Paris-Brest among the boldly flavoured dishes.

Name: La Pap Restaurant
Description: The Papin couple have set up their contemporary restaurant in a tastefully renovated old building marrying rustic and chic elements. An open kitchen, exposed beams and raw materials make for an inviting space, in which the chef, a farmer's son and tireless traveller, showcases modern cuisine inspired by his experiences in London, Montreal and Tokyo. Local produce, seafood influences and creative touches are perfectly expressed in refined dishes, such as tempura oysters or delicious pork secreto with clams and artichokes.

Name: La Part des Anges
Description: Tucked away in a pedestrian street behind the marina, this bistro was opened by two friends who are familiar faces around the Gulf of Saint Tropez and connoisseurs of its top restaurants. The chef honed his skills at Fréchon, after a stint in Grimaud; front of house, cordial and meticulous service comes courtesy of a pro from the local scene. The capacity of the cosy little space has been significantly increased by the addition of a terrace; music from the 1970s-90s, especially chanson française, makes up the soundtrack. Expect generous and discerning bistronomy cuisine. The dishes change with the seasons, and, with vegetarian and gluten-free options, there is something for everyone.

Name: La Part des Anges
Description: The market-fresh menu demonstrates deep respect for the seasons and a desire to highlight the work of local producers. Healthy appetites are encouraged and appreciated and the front-of-house team is pleasantly attentive. Its enduring popularity with the locals says it all!

Name: La Passerelle
Description: The chef now at the helm of this maritime-inspired restaurant, where she once trained with her father, is giving us her own modern take on family tradition. She likes to add good concentrated jus to her dishes (octopus with pork jus) as well as sweet-and-sour flavours (langoustine, turnip, almonds). She is also a sommelier, and puts her heart and soul into coming up with optimal food and wine pairings.

Name: La Passerelle
Description: At La Passerelle, on the banks of the Seine, chef Mickaël Meziane invites you into a bright dining space with a large counter, a green wall and a pleasant terrace overlooking the river. Celery royale, rockfish soup and pavlova with exotic fruits are part of a spot-on skilful culinary offering that is served with care by an attentive team. Ingredient quality and technical precision take precedence at this place run with sincerity.

Name: La Passion
Address: Via San Nicolò 5/b, Vandoies di Sopra, Vintl, 39030, Italy
Description: A small, cosy, completely wood - panelled stube has been set up in this residential building. The menus are traditional but inventive.

Name: La Paulée Marie-Pierre
Description: This friendly establishment is named after an ancient Burgundy wine festival, which is far from a coincidence. It is even possible to buy a bottle to take home from the sensibly priced wine bin. The culinary score errs towards the traditional, albeit with a more contemporary lineup of suggestions. Examples include tender juicy veal garnished with a poultry sauce enriched in Comté cheese and a gratin of sliced potatoes and onions. The lunchtime menu embodies the big-hearted mindset of this culinary landmark of Tournai.

Name: La Perla
Description: Housed in a historic palazzo on the charming Piazza della Motta in the town centre, this restaurant is one you will immediately want to share with family and friends thanks to its delicious cuisine. The menu focuses mainly on fish and seafood (including impressive raw fish dishes) although a few meat options are also available. Good choice of wines and spirits.

Name: La Perla de Jávea
Address: Avenida de la Llibertat 21, Xàbia, 03730, Spain
Description: Located directly on the seafront promenade, hence its perfect sunset setting. In this bright, contemporary restaurant boasting superb views, the full bounty of the sea is honoured through traditional cooking that is always based around the freshest ingredients (in fact, their motto is ‘we cook the Mediterranean’). Choose between an array of rice (for a minimum of two people) and fideuá dishes, as well as a good choice of meat, plus a selection of superb fish from the auction in Xàbia. The turbot with pilpil is worthy of special mention, thanks to its mouthwatering grilled aromas.

Name: La Petite Grocery
Address: 4238 Magazine St., New Orleans, LA, 70115, USA
Description: Tucked into a historic corner building on Magazine Street, La Petite Grocery captures the easy elegance that defines the best of New Orleans dining. Beneath yellow walls and crisp white tablecloths, Chef Justin Devillier’s kitchen delivers Louisiana flavors with a light touch and a strong sense of place. Signature blue crab beignets remain a must-order, arriving hot, airy and surprisingly delicate. Elsewhere, feather-light ricotta dumplings with wild mushrooms and beautifully fried paneed rabbit showcase the kitchen’s knack for balancing comfort and refinement. Finish with the warm gâteau Basque, a fitting finale to one of Uptown’s most enduring neighborhood favorites.

Name: La Petite Maison
Description: You come to this lovely restaurant ensconced in a terracotta-coloured "little house" on the outskirts of Cogolin. It is run by Damien Levivien, a trained pastry chef who learned the ropes under Jean Sulpice and Yannick Alléno. He and his wife serve precise and elegant market cuisine that won't break the bank. House-made pâté en croûte, ravioli crafted on site, meticulous dishes and classic desserts are all skilfully made. In this intimate setting, the terrace shaded by wisteria and mulberry trees adds to the charm, offering a peaceful stopover on the outskirts of Saint-Tropez.

Name: La Petite Maison (LPM)
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: A popular and bright French brasserie with high ceilings, an open kitchen and a buzzing atmosphere. The menu offers tried-and-tested French classics with some Mediterranean influences and dishes are fresh, well-crafted and very tasty. End on a sweet note with desserts mostly complemented by homemade ice cream. The friendly service team put their guests at the centre of the dining experience. Be sure to book in advance to secure your spot in this busy restaurant.

Name: La Petite Maison (LPM)
Address: L1, The Galleria, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The history of La Petite Maison (LPM) began in London in 2007, with further outposts opening around the world in the years since. Here in The Galleria, customers can judge it for themselves, with cuisine prepared with French-Mediterranean touches and served by a well-trained team in elegant surroundings. Dishes like thinly sliced octopus or salt-baked sea bass will put you in a sunny mood; and be sure to leave room for desserts.

Name: La Petite Maison (LPM)
Address: Al Maha Island, Lusail, Doha, Qatar
Description: Up in Lusail on Al Maha Island, this outpost of La Petite Maison has a prime location on the waterfront; the sunsets are always impressive. It’s very chic and elegant – and that’s just the service. The open kitchen offers bright, flavour-packed Niçoise and Mediterranean cooking – try the crevettes, confit de canard and finish with the tarte aux fraises. Add in an appealing cocktail, mocktail and wine list and you have all the ingredients for a fun night out, although it’s also worth coming during the day for their business lunch, which is a steal.

Name: La Petite Plage
Description: In this restaurant in the village port, Eric Frechon devises the menu, and the sea does the rest. Enjoy a new take on flavoursome Mediterranean cuisine, as you bury your feet in the sand overlooking the yachts, ever a subject of conversation. On summer evenings, a DJ provides the soundtrack, as is the norm in Saint-Tropez! Attentive service despite the bustle.

Name: La Petite Table
Address: 7 quai de la Pêcherie, Capbreton, 40130, France
Description: Whether seated on the terrace or inside, you are promised an enticing culinary interlude at this really inviting compact restaurant on Capbreton harbour. Generous and colourful dishes enhanced by citrus fruit and spices get to the heart of the matter, showcasing the local catch, lamb from the Pyrenees and vegetables from a market gardener in nearby Tosse. Don't miss the chocolate tart – a proper showstopper!

Name: La Petite École
Description: This restaurant moved into the premises of the former village school a few years ago. The delicate, flavoursome cuisine is definitely worth an A. Ten out of ten, too, for the chef, a lover of fine produce, who concocts precise, succulent recipes. Even better, it is excellent value for money - if only our school canteen had been like this!

Name: La Piazzetta Lake Como
Description: Tucked among the picturesque streets of Cernobbio, this modern, inviting bistro blends retro charm with contemporary furnishings and personalized touches. At the entrance, a cozy lounge with a bar counter beckons guests to linger over aperitifs and signature cocktails, while in summer the outdoor terrace offers moments of pleasure amid the lake breeze. In the kitchen, a young, dynamic team reinterprets Mediterranean flavors through contemporary recipes that are both authentic and aromatic. Not to be missed: “Pappa e Gambero,” crusted shrimp atop tomato and basil pappa, and “Tagliolino ai tre pomodori,” a tribute to refined simplicity.

Name: La Pie qui Couette
Description: Bang in the heart of Nîmes’ bustling food market, this eatery, run by a seasoned chef, will knock the socks off your tastebuds. Market fare crafted with fresher than fresh produce from the neighbouring market stalls. House specialties include matured meat, cod brandade, chopped beef tartare and île flottante (vanilla custard and meringue). Hearty helpings, an intelligent wine list, tightly packed tables and a good-natured, jovial vibe. No bookings possible, open from 11.30am to 3pm and always packed (try and come off peak at the weekend).

Name: La Piemontese
Address: Via San Martino 48, Mariano Comense, 22066, Italy
Description: The focus at La Piemontese, a simple yet modern restaurant with a convenient car park, is mainly on meat dishes, although game and fresh truffles also feature in season, plus there’s a generous business menu at lunchtime. An enjoyable dining experience that offers good value for money.

Name: La Pierrevue
Address: 2 place de la Mairie, Saint-Rogatien, 17220, France
Description: "There are six seasons in the year": with this saying in mind, chef Cécile Richard adapts her recipes to the times, with a drive for creativity that can be sensed in her fresh and precise cuisine. Locally caught fish, fruit and vegetables from organic market gardeners, aromatic herbs and flowers from the garden can be enjoyed in this farmhouse, converted in a pleasant rustic style. Attractive glass-paned wine cellar. New menu every two months.

Name: La Pineta
Address: Via Gualco 82, località Struppa, Genoa, 16165, Italy
Description: Now a gastronomic institution in the city, in a secluded setting immersed in nature, La Pineta occupies the ground floor of a nondescript building in which the simple, “dated” yet comfortable decor provides the backdrop. Although there is a menu (but no wine list), the dishes are usually announced in person at your table by the owners. Simple, traditional and abundant cuisine which is mainly cooked on the open grill in the centre of the room, including meat (its signature speciality) and fish.

Name: La Pinède
Address: Chemin du Langoustier, Ile de Porquerolles, 83400, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Patrons of this out-of-the-way hotel are collected from the village in a shuttle bus; the laidback restaurant of Le Mas du Langoustier is only open at lunchtime. The menu showcases the Mediterranean and Provençal dishes: pistou soup, "panier du pêcheur façon bourride", grilled fish and crayfish etc – to savour against a backdrop of Mediterranean plants and the sea: simply sit back, tuck in and enjoy the moment.

Name: La Pinède
Address: Strada di Cala Rossa, Lecci, 20137, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Whether for a relaxed lunch by the beach or dinner beneath the arbour, the intimate and romantic setting is utterly magnificent. The simple and delicious Mediterranean cuisine is a celebration of local ingredients. Herbs and vegetables from the 3 000m2 organic kitchen garden are often incorporated. And let's not forget the maturing cellar for cheeses and the enticing wine list.

Name: La Pira
Description: In historic Valletta, among the major tourist attractions, La Pira rolls out authentic Maltese cuisine, packed in flavour and served in a simple and informal setting. Among the standout dishes are pulled rabbit rigatoni, house-made stuffed pasta, Maltese stuffed marrows, pan-fried octopus and aljotta, the island’s iconic fish soup.

Name: La Pista
Address: Centro Commerciale Lingotto - via Nizza 262, Turin, 10126, Italy
Description: The top floor of the Lingotto shopping center – a quintessential Turin landmark, once a Fiat factory whose rooftop test track has been transformed into a visitable botanical garden – is the site of an easily reached restaurant thanks to clear signage at the entrance. Once seated, guests may choose from four tasting menus (all available à la carte): the Piedmontese tradition of Radici, the contemporary restraint of Gli Essenziali, the vegetarian Botanic World and the creative Zero/100 km/h, as well as Trust, a ‘blind’ journey guided by the kitchen’s sensitivity. Whichever the choice, the experience turns out to be convincing: solid, harmonious dishes with clear, perfectly-calibrated flavors.

Name: La Place
Description: Cristina and Vincenzo De Rosa run this restaurant with passion and enthusiasm. Throughout the year they delight guests with their modern and colourful cuisine, with dishes such as lobster ravioli in a Thai red curry sauce featuring on the menu.

Name: La Place de Mougins
Description: This delightful eatery, bang on the village square as the name suggests, is depicted by a chic yet cosy vibe and a bubbly culinary score courtesy of a creative and enthusiastic chef. Every month, he showcases a seasonal ingredient from truffles to asparagus, etc. We recommend asking for a seat in the conservatory.

Name: La Plage
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: This beachfront restaurant has looked out onto the ebbing and flowing tides since 1924. An idyllic setting in which to enjoy dishes that showcase fine ingredients, in particular fish and seafood, such as line-caught pollock, shallots, potatoes, mushrooms in a seafood emulsion…

Name: La Plage Casadelmar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: On the Benedettu peninsula, tucked away in the vegetation by the beach, this contemporary haven is the younger sibling of Casadelmar – its "casual" beachfront version. Everything happens on the terrace looking out to the Gulf of Porto Vecchio from beneath driftwood pergolas that blend into the landscape. In this divine setting, select your dishes from a menu of refined brasserie cuisine with Italian influences: vitello tonnato, tuna crudo, fritto misto, grilled lobster, appetising pasta dishes and fresh salads. The classic desserts absolutely do the job: profiteroles, tiramisu, lemon meringue pie. The freshness and quality of the ingredients inspire confidence.

Name: La Plancha
Description: The polished culinary score of this modest establishment makes it well worth hunting out. The stripped-back, competent and a tad creative dishes are packed in striking flavours: e.g. flame-licked slices of monkfish with a wasabi foam or roast pollock with green peas, verbena and apricot. The textbook perfect profiteroles are wickedly addictive.

Name: La Planque
Description: In the buzzing neighborhood of Limoilou, La Planque is hidden away among the bohemian shops and cafés. The short menu evolves regularly and features comforting bistro dishes alongside the chef's inventive creations. The eclectic wine list is cleverly put together (minor appellations at various price points, ciders, and craft beers). An enthusiastic young team provides the service—all in all, an ideal place for a relaxed evening with friends.

Name: La Pointe du Cap Coz
Address: 153 avenue de la Pointe, au Cap Coz, Fouesnant, 29170, France
Description: This white cottage seems to sit right on the ocean. The chef has chosen this isolated location to craft delicious cuisine in line with his commitment to local surf and turf produce. The result is beautifully presented dishes, such as slow-cooked pork cheeks in cider vinegar served with cabbage and apples baked in salted butter.

Name: La Ponche
Description: This iconic Saint-Tropez establishment stands looking out to sea in the neighbourhood of La Ponche. The Mediterranean cuisine showcases the catch of the day and locally sourced vegetables, as well as high-quality meats. While the lunchtime menu keeps things simple, in the evening guests can indulge in dishes such as fresh prawn ravioli with spicy Calabrian sausage, prawn head bisque with almonds, or the day's catch grilled and served with sorrel cream and sauce provençale. An extensive cocktail list rounds off the experience perfectly.

Name: La Popote
Address: Church Farm, Manchester Road, Marton, SK11 9HF, United Kingdom
Description: Tucked away in the Cheshire countryside, La Popote is one of several businesses occupying a centuries-old former farm, and the red-brick converted barn in which it's situated has retained a warm, rustic touch thanks to its brick floors and exposed beams. The owners spent several years working in Paris and this is evident with one scan of the menu, where you'll spot the likes of coq au vin, cassoulet and clafoutis. Classical techniques underpin the cooking, while there's a subtle modernity in the presentation. Service is friendly and assured.

Name: La Porta Antica
Address: Via Quarto dei Mille 16, Brescia, 25128, Italy
Description: Contemporary interiors and a prime location in a quiet residential neighborhood provide the backdrop for a seafood-focused kitchen that balances measured creativity with precise flavors. The shellfish selection excels: from prized Sicilian red prawns to steamed jumbo shrimp, refined and elevated by a soft bean purée with crispy guanciale.

Name: La Porta Restaurant
Address: Piazza Vieira de Mello 4, Bologna, 40128, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: "Housed in a futuristic building which extends like a bridge across Via Stalingrado, La Porta Restaurant is a highly versatile establishment. Set within a futuristic building that spans Via Stalingrado like a bridge, La Porta Restaurant is a versatile venue: the garage provides access to the café’s delicacies and, at lunchtime, the bistro opens with simple dishes, while gourmet diners can enjoy the evening menu in the restaurant with its elegant wooden decor. The menu features an array of fish, meat and vegetable options, while service comes courtesy of a mainly female team, all of whom are extremely friendly and welcoming. With some references to the culinary traditions of Emilia, the kitchen serves dishes featuring ingredients (both meat and fish) and recipes from various regions, complemented by the chef's creative touch. "

Name: La Portada de Mediodía
Address: San Nicolás de Bari 31, Torrecaballeros, 40160, Spain
Description: Located next to the San Nicolás de Bari church in the impressive setting of a restored 16C posthouse. In its delightful dining rooms with a welcoming rustic ambience, enjoy hearty Castilian cuisine featuring top-quality grilled and roasted meats – the latter ever-present on the menu. The Segovia suckling pig is without doubt the star dish here, although you can also pre-order delicious lamb and goat. Full-day food events dedicated to offal are also organised from time to time.

Name: La Porte Arrière
Description: Behind a glass façade, this restaurant with a long, narrow dining space has a trendy decor. The open kitchen with a counter provides a few diners with a front-row seat to watch the chefs at work. As concise as a haiku, the tempting menu (including a standout specialty of veal sweetbreads, mushroom, and shallot) gives pride of place to local produce. This modern, seamlessly executed cuisine combines spontaneity, creativity, and precision in a festive atmosphere.

Name: La Posada de Águeda
Description: This attractive restaurant occupying a chalet-style property by the main road is one of the best dining options in the Utiel-Requena area in Valencia province. Here, the family in charge, with Julio manning the stoves and partner Águeda and their daughter at the helm in the dining room, focuses on traditional cooking based around quality ingredients and simple yet impressively prepared dishes, with an emphasis on Spanish and local recipes. Standout options include hearty dishes such as the rice-based “arroz al senyoret” and lobster paella, but it’s also possible to order smaller plates such as artichokes, oxtail cannelloni, cod fritters etc.

Name: La Poste et Hôtel La Reconce
Description: The Restaurant de la Poste is run by a chef who hails from the village, ably assisted by his wife. His ambition is clear: to regale diners with modern dishes that celebrate good local produce – braised Charolais beef shank wrapped in celeriac, with pot-au-feu bouillon and wasabi, is a good example. Well-kept rooms, should you wish to stay over.

Name: La Potinière
Address: Main Street, Gullane, EH31 2AA, United Kingdom
Description: An icon in the Scottish hospitality industry, this sweet little restaurant is run in a very personal way by owners Mary and Keith, who share the cooking and have showed great professionalism and dedication over the years. They offer a choice of two dishes per course, each prepared with care and pride. The cooking is traditional at heart with the odd ambitious edge, but with technique this accurate and ingredients this delicious, there's really no need for unnecessary frippery.

Name: La Poule au Pot
Description: The great classics of the French culinary repertoire are given an overhaul here by Jean-François Piège. Service on a silver tray, old-fashioned bistro decor, zinc counter: it has all the trappings. It's Audiard's Paris down to a T... right down to the food: onion gratinée, quenelle of arctic char, beef chuck hash, Colbert fried whiting with tartar sauce.

Name: La Poya
Description: In a mountain-inspired decor, the chef serves up good-quality traditional cuisine that often takes meat as its starting point… but does not exclude the odd Asian note (eg gravelax salmon tataki marinated in beetroot, served with mustard sorbet). The dishes are beautifully presented and service comes with a smile. A good place to recharge your batteries after hitting the slopes on your skis!

Name: La Presqu'île
Address: Parking de la Presqu'ïle - esplanade Port-Miou, Cassis, 13260, France
Description: At the tip of the calanque of Port-Miou, this drop-dead seaside property commands a breathtaking vista over Cap Canaille from the conservatory dining room and the terrace. The chef rolls out polished, modern Mediterranean fare, crafted mainly from regional goodies (red mullet, mackerel, squid from the Mediterranean, veg and local goat’s cheese), but also from further afar (like pluma iberico).

Name: La Péniche
Address: Via Lungo Brugiano 3, Marina di Massa, 54100, Italy
Description: A corner of France along the Brugiano Canal. We eat in a stilt house with original and romantic settings that marry colonial style and Parisian model with a very warm and romantic result. Vast à la carte choices, there is something for everyone, from a list devoted entirely to oysters to some of Spain's most famous products, such as pata negra and anchovies from the Cantabrian Sea, as well as, of course, many more elaborate meat and fish dishes. In summer, tables on the raft are coveted, recalling the péniches on the Seine even more. Best to make reservations well in advance.

Name: La Quartina
Description: Outdoor service in the summer on the terrace with an exceptional view of the lake. Original furnishings and extremely well kept rooms. Menu including lake specialities. The rooms are simple, comfortable and always neat and tidy.

Name: La Quincaillerie
Description: Set in a former hardware store, the first-floor dining room, reached by an imposing wooden staircase, sports a retro feel. The ground floor is home to the open kitchen and a wine boutique. The score errs towards traditional French (from pâté en croûte to loin of veal with truffles, without forgetting an île flottante dessert), dotted with a handful of international accents. The seasons are reverently respected in dishes that are packed in flavour.

Name: La Quintessence
Description: Housed in a converted 16C Jesuit refectory, this restaurant in the Presqu'île district has plenty of character, with its stone walls, columns and arches, its vaulted ceiling, hardwood floors and tall windows. Chef Anthony Baud cooks up balanced modern cuisine that emphasises the freshness and quality of the ingredients, in dishes such as Arctic char with pak choi, or a delicious persimmon dessert incorporating ginger and pumpkin seed praline. The set menus are changed up on a regular basis to showcase the ingredients of the season.

Name: La R'mize
Address: 160 rue du Vieux-Village, Les Gets, 74260, France
Description: In the village, near the church, this family-run restaurant serves tasty traditional cuisine. An experienced chef delights with well-crafted recipes: creamy burrata, tomatoes, peaches, peas and crunchy almonds; Arborio risotto with Abondance cheese, scallop carpaccio and shellfish jus. The menu also includes classic Savoyard specialities, like an indulgent gratin or Savoyard fondue with champagne!

Name: La Racine et la Moelle
Description: In a lane of the historic town, this neo-bistro is depicted by a bubbly vibe and spot-on cooking in the zeitgeist. Chef Julie changes the menu constantly, rolling out modern indulgent recipes like grilled squid, melt-in-the-mouth Aubrac hanger steak and a small red fruit almond financier cake to finish. By her side, Michael’s carefully curated cellar unveils a natural wine focus. This bouncy, vibrant venue has captured the hearts of Figeac.

Name: La Rameaudière
Address: 10 rue de la Gare, Ellange, 5690, Luxembourg
Description: Daniel Rameau is a connoisseur of luxury produce, among which foie gras, lobster and pigeon, which he prepares refreshingly simply in dishes that blend generosity and tradition. The equally enticing wine list features a savvy selection of Luxemburg vintages. This former village train station and its flower-decked terrace are steeped in vintage charm.

Name: La Rascasse
Address: Le Provençal, 113 place Saint-Pierre, Giens, 83400, France
Description: At the tip of the Giens peninsula, this hotel-restaurant, which sports a colourful, restored façade commands a knockout view of the sea and the Îles d’Or. In a warm, timeless setting, Sébastien Graize signs spot-on Mediterranean fare that pays tribute to local market gardeners from Vars and fishermen from Niel. The house signature is bouillabaisse, packed in flavour and aromas. The fashionably refurbished guestrooms are blissful, as is the saltwater pool carved out of the rock down by the shore.

Name: La Rebotica
Description: Well located in the town’s historic quarter, La Rebotica occupies the interior of an old house that has managed to bring itself up to date while maintaining its welcoming rusticity. Its updated take on traditional cuisine, with a focus on Retinto beef as well as cod dishes, is well supported by a good selection of Ribera del Guadiana wines. Don’t miss the delicious “trilogy of Iberian meat (“presa”, sirloin and “secreto”)!

Name: La Refezione
Description: An imaginative cuisine for the elegant "club - house" located inside a sports centre; managed by two great enthusiasts of the culinary art. You will receive a hearty welcome.

Name: La RiMa
Description: This restaurant in the heart of the town serves excellent contemporary cuisine (meat and fish, plus a few vegetarian options). The menu features dishes such as fregola sarda (a type of couscous) with tomato, buffalo mozzarella, friggitelli peppers and fried capers, with a personalised twist added by talented owner-chef Matteo Ridoni.

Name: La Rigue
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The stunning La Réserve hotel boasts a brasserie that is fully the equal to its classy host. The Zegemeer landscape, visible from the handsome terrace, provides the perfect foil to this urbane restaurant. Local foodies swarm here, like bees to a hive, for its lineup of patriotic and Gallic favourites, jazzed up with a delicate new spin. For example, a subtle carpaccio of scallops is paired with tart green apples, avocado and salmon roe, while a bouillabaisse of North Sea fish, langoustine and lobster explodes with big-boned gutsiness… Finish your meal with a flamboyant flambéed crêpe suzette. A tailored culinary experience overflowing in generosity and a capacity of some 120 diners. Be it for a snack or a special occasion, La Rigue ticks all the boxes.

Name: La Ripadoro
Description: Tucked away in the small medieval village of Rivalto, with stunning views of the surrounding Tuscan hills, the Ripadoro agriturismo is home to this rustic yet elegant farm-restaurant serving traditional Tuscan dishes made from produce grown on the property. There’s an authentic charcoal grill which is used to cook classic ribeye steak, as well as the superb “girarrosto” – boned pigeon and quail served with potato rosti, yellow carrots with ginger and Jerusalem artichokes in foil. Make sure you save space for one of the delicious desserts! In summer, it’s well worth booking one of the outdoor tables under the shade of large lime trees.

Name: La Risacca Blu
Address: Viale Tunisia, angolo via Tadino, Milan, 20124, Italy
Description: The first thing you see when you enter this restaurant near the central railway station is its large display of fresh fish, all delivered daily. The menu features a selection of classic and authentic fish and seafood options, with pride of place given to its raw fish dishes.

Name: La Rissole
Description: The name of this bistro pays tribute to a great chef of the last century and celebrates the joys of cooking. The concise menu highlights the changing seasons and regional produce (asparagus, snails, freshwater fish). A flair for seasoning makes for simple and tasty food, such as white asparagus mimosa, broccoli and vadouvan. There are only a few tables, so be sure to book!

Name: La Ristobottega
Address: Via Vittorio Veneto 46A, Reggio Calabria, 89121, Italy
Description: As the name suggests, this restaurant is divided into two sections: a shop on one side, which sells local products such as tempting salumi and cheeses (they also serve informal lunches at midday); and on the other, in the evening, an attractive bistro with wooden tables and soft lighting, where you can enjoy delicious cuisine. Among the fish dishes (aged on site), we particularly recommend the grouper fillet with vegetable caponatina and raw scampi on a bed of mashed potato, while the meat options include top-quality cuts such as Wagyu beef. A small outdoor space on the pavement completes the picture.

Name: La Roba
Address: Building 7, Zaojun West Lane, Zaojunmiao Road, Haidian, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
Description: The owner has paid tribute to his ethnic roots by naming his restaurant, La Roba, after a subgroup of the Nuosu tribe in Yunnan. The exotic ethnic flair is manifest on every level from the decor and artwork to the waiters’ outfits and background music. The menu features all Yunnan’s classic dishes, such as the deliciously chewy millefeuille pea flour pancake. The Dali-style fish braised in pickled papaya is tart, fruity and appetising. Expect to queue at peak periods.

Name: La Roca
Address: Avenida de Europa 25, Pozuelo de Alarcón, 28223, Spain
Description: La Roca’s simple contemporary decor provides the backdrop for cuisine that showcases quality ingredients. This comes as no surprise given that is overseen by chef Alberto Molinero from the award-winning Erre de Roca restaurant in Miranda de Ebro. Despite its global influences, the cuisine has a clear Spanish DNA, highlighted in signature recipes such as the oxtail ravioli, an array of hot and cold options, plus a good selection of more substantial dishes.

Name: La Roche Le Roy
Description: This pretty little manor house on the outskirts of town has recently been refurbished and modernised, all the way from the decoration to the kitchens, the domain of chef Maximilien Bridier. Taking an enthusiastic approach to high-quality ingredients, he presents elegant, precise dishes with no frills. Without fail, the menu features a vegetarian option. There is a fine selection of wines by the glass, and the service is attentive. Sit out on the terrace on warm days.

Name: La Rosa dei Venti
Address: Via Piero della Francesca 34, Milan, 20154, Italy
Description: Simple, authentic seafood cuisine anchored in tradition: the roasted turbot is emblematic, served in season with porcini mushrooms and potatoes, a testament to a philosophy built entirely on freshness and clean flavors. The recipes draw on Sardinia and, more broadly, Italian cuisine, free of pretense or unnecessary flourishes. The recommendation is to trust the owner and be guided through the day’s off-menu offerings, often tied to what has just arrived from the market and perfectly capturing the soul of the place.

Name: La Rosina
Description: With over 100 years of history behind it, La Rosina is still looking good, thanks to renovation work carried out a few years ago which has given the restaurant a new look. Situated in an attractive location in the hills around Marostica, this excellent restaurant is a sound choice for good food in the province of Vicenza, serving modern regional and Italian dishes which are full of flavour. Enjoy beautiful views of the surrounding hills from the guestrooms.

Name: La Rotonde
Address: Hôtel du Palais, 1 avenue de l'Impératrice, Biarritz, 64200, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: One of the most prestigious establishments on the Atlantic coast, the Hôtel du Palais needs no introduction. In this swanky setting overlooking the ocean, the great traditions and classics of French cuisine take centre stage. The chic brasserie menu offers diners a lunchtime treat (al fresco in fine weather) and a more refined and ambitious lineup in the evening, when premium ingredients (caviar, lobster, foie gras), as well as Basque regional specialities (Banka trout, free-range poultry, Ossau-Iraty cheese) are showcased. It would be a crime to skip dessert – crêpe Suzy in tribute to Raymond Oliver.

Name: La Rotonde
Address: Le Negresco, 37 promenade des Anglais, Nice, 06000, France
Description: The rotunda-shaped brasserie of the legendary luxury hotel has resolutely entered the modern world. In this light-filled space (with a terrace), you choose from a menu (designed by Michelin-starred chef Virginie Basselot) that celebrates a flavoursome and colourful cuisine full of Mediterranean flair, with nods to Nice's traditions.

Name: La Route d'Argent
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: On the ground floor of the hotel, this restaurant, which sports a bright, modern interior, is enthusiastically helmed by Loïc and Océane Gay. Regional produce (Aubrac beef and trout) takes front stage in soul-warming, indulgent dishes: persillade of lamb sweetbreads or squab breast. Traditional aligot (mashed potatoes and cheese) is served with the main course.

Name: La Récréation
Address: 70 rue de la Vialotte, Le Bourg, Les Arques, 46250, France
Description: School’s out! In its place, this gently nostalgic establishment has a classroom - style dining room, courtyard terrace and kitchen garden in the old playground. Contemporary cuisine.

Name: La Récréation Gourmande
