The same high standards apply here as at La Galinette in Perpignan: vegetables, herbs, oil and honey come from the restaurant's own gardens; organic and natural wines. Fantastic!

Name: La Terrasse des Cigales
Description: Between the Durance River and the Sud Luberon, this modern restaurant lives up to its name with a lovely shaded terrasse enveloped by the sound of the cicadas (cigales)… plus, you get attentive, smiling service! Mathieu and Sébastien serve an appetising traditional Provence-inspired menu, as well as a daily special that is great value for money. The delicious dishes are carefully crafted with no messing around. The aim is to keep things simple, flavoursome and generous, while using selected regional ingredients: vegetables and olive oil from the village, lamb from the Alpilles, fish from the Bay of Cannes, beef from the Alpes-de-Haute-Provence. In winter, wood-fire cooking. A pleasant restaurant.

Name: La Terrasse du Fesch
Address: Hôtel Fesch, 7 rue du Cardinal-Fesch, Ajaccio, 20000, France
Description: Perched on the rooftop of a hotel, this place delivers a stunning view of Ajaccio, the bay and the surrounding mountains. Thanks to modular wall sections, panels can be opened and closed at will, depending on the weather. In the open kitchen, chef Franck Radiu can be seen working hard to a soundtrack of electronic music. A local man, and a pastry chef by training, he serves up a well-paced meal that makes the most of the riches of Corsica's terroir. On this occasion: a spider crab cannelloni, with a twist in the form of grapefruit supremes; sea bream on potato patties topped with a delicious bouillabaisse jus, and a trompe-l'œil lemon in a delicate white chocolate shell – a light, citrus dessert.

Name: La Terraza de Alba
Description: This restaurant, which has undergone a major evolution and whose owner (Óscar Fernández) is always on hand to oversee everything, favours the flavours of traditional cuisine with a modern twist. The menu, which offers half portions for many dishes, has a special section for rice dishes (minimum 2 people) and another very tempting section dedicated to bluefin tuna. Standout dishes? There are two that are prepared right before your eyes: the salt-crusted beef tenderloin with fine herbs and, among the desserts, the almond mortar, cream cheese and passion fruit ice cream. They have a adjoining multipurpose room with its own entrance, which is particularly useful for businesses or presentations (available on request only).

Name: La Terrazza
Description: Overlooking the Torbole lakefront, just steps from the center, this small restaurant with a panoramic veranda is a tribute to the flavors of the lake. The cuisine is meticulous in its details, with dishes that tell the story of the territory through refined presentations. The tasting menu celebrates lake products, while the à la carte selection strikes a balance between lake, land, and garden. Don’t miss the “Del Leone” spaghetti: freshwater prawns, ginger, and lime in a fresh and spicy embrace.

Name: La Terrazza
Description: A salon en plein air overlooking Asolo’s historical center, this charming spot offers attentive service and Italian cuisine presented with a modern touch. The menu spans land and sea, with vegetarian options as well. A classic and welcoming atmosphere makes it an ideal setting for a romantic dinner.

Name: La Toq'
Description: In the historic town near Saint Epvre Basilica lies an inviting eatery whose plush, stylish décor blends contemporary notes with century-old stone arches. The chef crafts a flavoursome score by way of several menus that keep pace with the seasons: Arctic char, mousseline of asparagus, chervil-flavoured veggie ravioles; a crunchy vanilla mille-feuille drizzled with caramel – to die for! Fine wine list.

Name: La Torre
Description: Situated on the ground floor of Spilimbergo’s beautiful medieval castle, this restaurant has equally beautiful interiors which welcome guests into a romantic atmosphere, steeped in history but accompanied by every contemporary comfort. For a really special dinner for two, we highly recommend booking the intimate alcove table. The cuisine is modern and beautifully presented with a special focus on meat, although the fish dishes are every bit as delicious.

Name: La Torre
Description: Overlooked by a medieval tower in the main town square, this restaurant is perfect for anyone keen on classic, traditional cuisine. House specialities include dishes cooked over the barbecue grill.

Name: La Torre
Address: Grabenstraße 39, Sankt Veit an der Glan, 9300, Austria
Location: Sankt Veit an der Glan, Austria
Description: The keep of the medieval St Veit fortress is a truly remarkable setting. Nestled within the historic walls and surrounded by greenery, the small terrace is a particular highlight. This restaurant is run by husband-and-wife team Rosemarie and Ammar Trabelsi, who create a welcoming atmosphere with a personal touch. The Sicilian presides front-of-house and has charm in his blood. His dapper, old-school style is anything but stuffy. She is in charge of the kitchen and cooks up ambitious Italian and Mediterranean cuisine using select ingredients. Her dishes are pared down to just a few components, allowing their natural flavours to shine through. Turbot with samphire and datterini tomatoes or house-made paccheri with wild prawns, tomatoes and rocket are prime examples. Fish and seafood take centre stage and vary depending on what the market has to offer. The tasting menu is definitely worthwhile, but you can also order à la carte. Italian wine list.

Name: La Tour
Description: Nestling at the foot of a 14C tower in the heart of the famous wine-growing village, this traditional townhouse boasts an elegant, contemporary dining room offset by a scattering of period details (beams, ceiling and mouldings). Simplicity, authenticity and bags of character are the hallmarks of the food characterised by premium ingredients that keep pace with the seasons presented in an enticing lunchtime menu (that is also a steal!) and a surprise menu available in different versions in the evening. There is also an entirely vegetarian menu.

Name: La Tour
Address: 7 ter route du Fraisse, Dunières, 43220, France
Description: Local ingredients (Puy green lentils, Grazac snails, free - range guinea fowl etc) are transformed into appetising meals by the chef. The food is good and hearty, as well as carefully prepared. The cheese trolley, which includes lots of cheeses from Auvergne, is an added bonus. It is all very appealing, not least the very well - appointed rooms.

Name: La Tour des Sens
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: On the upper reaches of Tencin, this Tower is a treat for the five senses! Run by the same chef since 2016 (2017 Top Chef winner), his creative, natural menus aim to stimulate the taste buds of diners and thus call upon their emotions. When the weather’s fine, why not enjoy the fabulous view of the Chartreuse range from the terrace?

Name: La Tradizione - Cucina Casalinga
Description: A corner of traditional Apulia to be experienced in a trattoria in the centre, in a typical and pleasantly homely atmosphere. The dishes are listed verbatim, not to be missed are the series of starters, but also the characteristic fresh pastas.

Name: La Traverse
Description: La Traverse is the quintessence of a contemporary brasserie, sporting a warm, welcoming interior and a menu that mingles Flemish classics with more up-to-date dishes, of which shrimp fritters and braised pork cheeks or dimsum and cauliflower steak are just a few examples. We recommend the matured beef, cooked to perfection in a Josper oven. On Saturday evenings, La Traverse offers a menu of varied dishes to share and a platter of cured meats to nibble on.

Name: La Trinité
Description: The stylish and laid-back La Trinité is housed in a former bank building in a gorgeous waterfront location. François de Potter is a seasoned chef who effortlessly unites the generous spirit of French cuisine with the versatility of the Asian culinary world. Whether expertly roasting Anjou pigeon on the bone or making pork belly gyoza with an edamame vinaigrette, he brings East and West together with a sure touch. This restaurant is a sure bet, boasting an excellent wine selection and warm hospitality courtesy of hostess Evelyne.

Name: La Tronera
Description: It's perfect for a getaway, since it's in the same building as the little country hotel of the same name! At this family-run restaurant, where the children are fully integrated in the business, with their son in the dining room as sommelier alongside his mother, while their daughter helps her father in the kitchen, you’ll find à la carte service and the option of a tasting menu. They present a modern take on traditional cuisine, always bringing local products to the fore with a Bercian flair. They really make you feel at home here!

Name: La Truffe Noire
Address: boulevard de la Cambre 12, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
Description: As soon as you cross the threshold of this elegant eatery, you will be enthralled by the truffle aromas. Since 1988, La Truffe Noire has been a model of fine dining, as traditional dishes are enhanced by luxurious hints of truffle and Mediterranean flamboyance. Taglioni with langoustine and seasonal vegetables or seabass with aromatic black truffle are some of the dishes that are as legible and familiar as they are mouthwatering and polished. The house signature remains the iconic beef carpaccio prepared by your table. In addition to an enticing array of set menus, the sensibly priced lunchtime lineup makes this culinary experience accessible to a wider public.

Name: La Tulipe Noire
Description: In a tastefully converted wine barn, the chef and his wife are in tune with the seasons, in particular thanks to their cottage garden that supplies the majority of veggies here. Do not be misled by the apparently simple names of the dishes, each one is a compendium of consummate technique and happily reinterprets the classics (onion soup, tarte tatin).

Name: La Tupina
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: A genuine institution, this country inn champions dishes of yesteryear... Sanguette (blood pudding), macaronade (pasta with beef and tomato sauce), chips fried in duck fat: local produce is promoted with conviction in hearty dishes from South-West France, but also seasonal vegetables and meat roasted in the hearth. The fine produce on the counter certainly whets the appetite.

Name: La Turlutte
Description: This modern, cheerfully down-to-earth micro-bistro a stone's throw from the lighthouse promises a treat for your taste buds. At the helm: a local (front of house) and a chef who used to come to the area on holiday. Indeed, this place radiates a free-spirited, playful energy, with a menu of small plates for sharing, eg cockles with chorizo, satay coconut milk broth; fried chicken, chilli butter and Fourme d'Ambert cheese – fresh produce, impeccable fish, full-flavoured dishes. The small dining room centres on a large counter; the tables and chairs have an artfully weathered look, a wall of azulejos with marine motifs. Vintage plates, and knife handles made from traditional jigs for luring cephalopods – turluttes.

Name: La Tête au Loup
Address: Lieu-dit la Tête-au-Loup, Le Pin-au-Haras, 61310, France
Description: (Temporarily closed) Stéphane and Agnès Mabille greet guests warmly in their spruce, traditional inn, appointed in a rustic vein. The seasoned chef concocts homemade terrines and assorted Normandy delicacies. In fine weather, make a beeline for the garden and terrace, which overlook the horses grazing in the next-door world-famous Haras du Pin stud farm. Unstarched, friendly vibe.

Name: La Tête de l'Art
Address: 11 rue de la Porte-Calon, Guérande, 44350, France
Description: A meal at this restaurant housed in the outbuildings of a 13C manor on the outskirts of Guérande is a must. Quality ingredients that are meticulously sourced from the region go into modern cuisine with bold flavours. This lunchtime, the starter of asparagus and octopus, enhanced by pronounced herbaceous flavours, was well made; the cod precisely cooked in hazelnut butter was accompanied by tasty ravioli. The pear dessert plays on sweet and sour with great success.

Name: La Tête d’Or
Address: 318 Park Ave. S., New York, NY, 10010, USA
Description: Glamorous and grand, this Flatiron looker is a reminder of what steakhouses can be in their most satisfying and beautiful form. Thank Chef Daniel Boulud, who brings his signature French flair to this classic genre. Start in the bar, a striking stage with leather-paneled walls and smart cocktails, before heading to the table. The setting is expansive with soaring ceilings, walnut floors, and servers positioned like turrets, ready to swoop in at any moment. Indeed, this is a room where deals get done. Caesar salads made tableside and prime rib sliced on roving trolleys up the charm on a menu that covers all the bases with dry-aged steaks, prime seafood, and ice cream sundaes. Expense accounts will take to the top-shelf Bordeaux and private dining rooms.

Name: La Vallée
Description: While the interior, with its picture windows, is very pleasant, it is outdone by the knockout south-facing terrace just above the picturesque Bec de la Vallée slipway. It is the perfect place to sample fine seafood, as well as classics from Brittany's terroir, e.g. local country bacon or far Breton (traditional flan-style dessert).

Name: La Vallée - Das Bistro im Casino
Description: In the casino building in the centre of Riezlern, a seasoned duo bring dedication to the table. Charming and competent restaurant manager Lillian Roth looks after diners; meanwhile chef-patron Sascha Kemmerer (known from Kilian Stuba in A-ROSA Ifen Hotel Kleinwalsertal in Hirschegg) is in charge of the kitchen. His dishes draw on French classics and impress with their craftsmanship, flavour and the quality of the ingredients underpinning them. The atmosphere is inviting and friendly: modern bistro style, Alpine details from bygone days, such as tiled stoves and wood-panelled ceilings, and "Culinary Timepieces" – limited edition prints by Annette Sandner – form a beautiful impression. There is also a bar and terrace. Tip: Why not visit the casino before or after your meal?

Name: La Vaquería Mediterránea
Description: A brasserie-restaurant with a friendly, informal feel and pleasant terrace. Here, the house speciality, gently influenced by Basque cuisine, are the grilled meats and T-bone steak, although plenty of other options are available, including tapas, flatbreads, seasonal vegetables and excellent fish dishes (make sure you ask about the fresh fish of the day). The à la carte is complemented by a tasting menu for a minimum of two people sharing.

Name: La Vara
Description: Chef Alex Raij knows her tapas, helping to kickstart the craze in Manhattan. More than a decade ago, she jumped boroughs to Brooklyn and opened La Vara, which she co-owns with husband, Eder Montero. Billing itself as “cocina casera” or “home cooking,” this kitchen elevates humble cuisine to impressive levels. Product quality is excellent, and the playful spirit behind these dishes is the definition of creative cooking. Menu highlights include huevos rellenos, judías a la plancha, or grilled romano beans and butter beans in a bright Romesco sauce, and cochinillo, or a slow-roasted suckling pig leg with chimichurri.

Name: La Veranda
Description: Situated a few metres from the lake in the centre of the village, this welcoming and long-established family restaurant boasts a dining room that transforms into a veranda with outdoor dining in summer. The cuisine here is traditional, with generous portions of fish from the lake and sea.

Name: La Veranda
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: In summer, the terrace by the lake offers a splendid view and is the perfect setting for dishes that highlight Italian tradition but also satisfy the most cosmopolitan palates. The foie gras escalope served with parsnips, apple compote and pink grapefruit, for example, is excellent. If the weather's not so great, you'll be just as comfortable in the elegant indoor dining room overlooking the lake (the most popular) or the garden. The evening dress code is elegant (we are, after all, inside the luxurious Villa d'Este hotel).

Name: La Veranda
Description: In this restaurant with the flair of an Italian country house and decorative shelves full of cookbooks, small tables make for a friendly, elegant ambience. The modern european cuisine is served à la carte or as a set menu. The front-of-house team provides attentive, competent service, and there is a good selection of wines to choose from.

Name: La Veranda del Color
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This aptly named restaurant in the Color Hotel just a short distance from Lake Garda boasts a modern, colourful decor and cuisine worthy of its name. Dishes are inspired by Mediterranean traditions and are showcased on a number of different tasting menus.

Name: La Verdoyante
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Standing among the vines, this former rustic farmhouse enjoys a fine panoramic view... But La Verdoyante would be nothing without the enthusiasm of the couple who hold the reins. In the stylish interior or on the charming terrace, diners savour delicious Provençal cuisine that smacks of the garigue.

Name: La Vid - Bodega Norton
Description: We’re not understating anything when we say that Luján de Cuyo, at the foot of the Andes mountains, is always worth visiting. And once you’re here, the century-old Norton wine estate is a splendid option. The reason? Its wines, obviously, but also the delightful gardens designed by landscape gardener Carlos Thays, an array of interesting wine-focused excursions (tours, tastings, bike trips, etc.), South America’s largest underground cellar, plus this restaurant, which showcases Mendoza’s local recipes and native ingredients and products (cured trout, marinated pork, river crab, goat’s cheese, and more). The chef at the helm, Facundo Di Fabrizio, has revived the full flavours of the local region on several tasting menus, all based around an updated take on traditional cuisine and accompanied by highly interesting wine pairings (3-course Argentine-style set menu, 4-course menu with options, and 6-course tasting menu). We recommend that you enhance your experience with a visit to the wine cellar.

Name: La Vie
Address: Le Dream Boutique Hotel, 139 Jalan Pintal Tali, George Town, 10100, Malaysia
Description: This casual neighbourhood dining spot started out as a steakhouse, but switched to serving European cuisine with Asian influences. Their signature kataifi prawn is tiger prawn wrapped in crispy noodles, fried and served in a prawn bisque sauce. Meat lovers should check out the Australian Wagyu ribeye which is cooked to perfection on a charcoal grill. It comes with a range of condiments but the wasabi works best. Wine is available by the bottle only.

Name: La Vieille Auberge
Description: Splendid high vaulted timber ceilings and huge floor-to-ceiling windows reminiscent of a conservatory overlooking the garden: the scene is set in this well-known culinary landmark. Matthijs Bartman rolls out modern, enticing dishes illustrated by pastrami of bazadais beef, smoked beetroot and blueberries or a more classical choux pastry stuffed with tonka bean diplomat crème, yuzu caramel and mango sorbet… A traditional lineup with a modern twist, presented in two eater-friendly priced menus. Enthusiastic and delightful front of house team.

Name: La Vieille Enseigne
Description: Despite the name, this is a brand new winstub! The magnificent traditional wainscoting is the work of a cabinetmaker, lithographs by Tomi Ungerer adorn the walls, while copious helpings, local ingredients and traditional regional recipes (presskopf, choucroute, game) depict the gourmet tribute to Alsace, down to the splendid selection of mainly organic wines.

Name: La Vieille Fontaine
Address: Hôtel d'Europe, 12 place Crillon, Avignon, 84000, France
Description: Wood panelling, mouldings and a fireplace set the elegant Provençal scene of this venerable establishment. Pascal Auger is in his element, crafting Mediterranean fare steeped in the aromas and flavours of the south. On sunny days (you’re in Avignon!) you can enjoy these delicacies beneath the ancient plane tree on the terrace facing a fountain.

Name: La Vieille Tour
Description: We could not but fall in love with this authentic inn, run by a couple of professionals. Their generous restaurant, close to the “Petite France”, nurtures traditional flavours (breast of chicken with jus, cod fillet with vegetables and mushrooms, game in season) depending on market availability. The simple décor is embellished with humorous posters on Alsace by the renowned Tomi Ungerer.

Name: La Vieja Bodega
Address: Avenida de La Rioja 17, Casalarreina, 26230, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: A restaurant with a touch of charm? This one has it in spades; in fact... it has restored a beautiful 17th century wine cellar! Here they see gastronomy as a pleasure to be shared and that is their priority, always highlighting the goodness of Rioja cuisine. In their well-kept dining rooms, all with a rustic feel, they offer a traditional menu, with modern touches and interesting suggestions of the day. We particularly liked the slow-cooked egg and their deliciously tender oxtail, stewed and shredded!

Name: La Vieja by Jonay Hernández
Description: A restaurant with a distinct urban feel which is striking for its genuine graffiti (note the huge octopus!) and the influence of the Canary Islands (chef Jonay Hernández’s homeland) in its cuisine. The cooking here is described here as ‘new Canarian cuisine’, based on local ingredients and with a wealth of history behind every dish. A great option for those who enjoy fish and seafood.

Name: La Villa
Address: Seven Villas, 1 Bapanling Road, Xihu, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking
Description: In a resort, this monastery-turned restaurant imparts a serene vibe. The all-wood architecture is elegantly enhanced by floral arrangements, white table linen and leather chairs. Only open to the public for dinner, it serves a seasonal-centric menu, finessed with European techniques and artistic plating. Some dishes pay tribute to the chef’s mother’s cooking. Bookings advisable due to limited seating. Ask about wine or tea pairings.

Name: La Villa
Address: 14 Ngo Quang Huy Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: The distinctly Gallic menu whisks diners from Ho Chi Minh City to Paris in an instant, with foie gras, meat-filled puff pastry pies, American lobster with champagne and Grand Marnier crème brûlée among the highlights. Decorated with artwork, velvet curtains and a stunning chandelier, La Villa also offers al fresco dining in the garden. Attentive, suitably formal service, a fine wine list and cheese selection. The starched classical vibe of this restaurant will appeal to those who appreciate vintage charm and nostalgia.

Name: La Villa - Bistrô Francês
Address: Rua Alvaro Ramos 408, Rio de Janeiro, 22280-110, Brazil
Description: This French brasserie occupies a unique property in Botafogo dating back to 1775 and has established itself as a trusted option for those who enjoy authentic Gallic cuisine. Under the management of French owner Gregoire Fortat, La Villa features a simple decor, high ceilings, outdoor tables and a pleasant and hospitable ambience. The menu here is centred around traditional French bistro fare with an added Brazilian touch. The experience begins with a delicious pâté de champagne served with bread baked on the premises, followed by the classic onion soup, and an authentic duck cassoulet. On Sundays, there’s also a French-Brazilian barbecue including an impressive array of fish and seafood.

Name: La Villa Agua Amarga
Address: Carretera de Carboneras 18, Agua Amarga, 04149, Spain
Description: Located next to the Mikasa Hotel and exuding its own charm, this spot is housed in a villa with several Mediterranean-style dining rooms and a quiet terrace, where the tables are arranged around a small pool. The à la carte, with its contemporary flair and meticulously presented dishes, features a good selection of seasonal offerings and places a particular emphasis on grilled dishes. We especially liked their grilled turbot with Grenoble-style sauce, capers, and grapes.

Name: La Villa Lorraine
Address: Avenue du Vivier d'Oie 75, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking
Description: The iconic Villa Lorraine has been treated to a makeover in the shape of a cosmopolitan interior steeped in stylish modern luxury and urban effervescence and enhanced by soft, intimate lighting. The spot-on front-of-house team is at hand to cater to your every need. Chef Ruben Christiaens slaloms between brasserie classics, like sole meuniere and Black Angus steak with fries, and more creative recipes strewn with subtle Asian notes. He may pair juicy fillets of pigeon with a big-boned gravy and finely diced red beetroot in a puree of fermented raspberries. The enticing à la carte and set menus amply demonstrate that this emblematic institution has lost nothing of its former splendour.

Name: La Villa Tartary
Description: Dressed stone vaulting and designer furniture set the stage in this converted water mill. The chef rolls out a seven-course set menu dotted with classical nods and globetrotting inspirations: Thai carrot soup, shrimp and buckwheat; escalopes of pork with mashed potatoes; confit apple and chocolate mousse.

Name: La Volta
Address: GF, 9 Lan Fong Road, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: With soft lighting and exposed brick walls, this pasta bar helmed by chef Roland Schuller exudes rustic charm. The rotating menu features both fresh and dried pasta alongside seasonal produce. One standout is the handmade pappardelle alla genovese – the meat ragù clings to each ribbon of pasta beautifully and imparts deep, layered flavours. Save room for the signature poached Williams pear tart with a flaky puff pastry crust and house-made gelato.

Name: La Yerbita
Description: A restaurant with no little charm located close to the Parque de la Naturaleza de Cabárceno. Here, simplicity is lauded as a true gift, hence the focus on simple traditional cuisine but with careful attention paid to preparation and presentation. The dishes here are copious; almost all, however, are available as small plates.

Name: La Yole de Chris
Address: Plage de la Concurrence, La Rochelle, 17000, France
Description: This dazzling place by Christopher Coutanceau offers two incomparable pleasures: for the eyes and for the taste buds. A long counter in the shape of a skiff (light, long and narrow boat), houses the open kitchen, where the cooks can be seen in action. Seafood (oysters and shellfish) and fish of the day enjoy pride of place on the menu here... to be enjoyed on the terrace that overlooks the sea, in fine weather. Booking recommended.

Name: La façon Koga
Description: Sauces are the soul of French cooking and the passion behind this fare. Bouillon base is drawn with meticulous care to capture every drop of umami. Ingredients are prepared to best effect, while sauces multiply the flavour. Occasional addition of yuzu or salted koji lends a dash of originality. Heir to the spirit of his mentor, the chef pours his accumulated knowledge into a style distinctly his own—hence the restaurant’s name, meaning ‘Koga style’.

Name: La fleur de Sel
Description: The initiative by this pair, chef Willy Lardry and maître d' Edwin Smietanski, to open their restaurant here is most welcome. Both hail from Le Creusot but met while working for Yohann Chapuis in Tournus. The interior is inspired in part by nature (with, in particular, wallpaper depicting a forest in the mist). The chef, working alone in the kitchen, shows undeniable maturity. Delicacy and finesse are the order of the day, for example, the lovely courgette flower with cod stuffing and the olive oil sabayon accompanying the cod tournedos, or the mackerel and its marinated cucumber ravioli.

Name: La nouvelle Auberge
Description: This intimate restaurant could easily be called an inn 2.0. Be sure to ask for a table in the chic conservatory to fully enjoy the green surroundings. Fans of rich dishes will be right at home here. The chef works with local delicacies, cooks according to French tradition and pays attention to global influences. He charms with a saignant piece of beef with a powerful gravy and surprises with a dessert featuring red cabbage, ruby ice cream, pear, vanilla and red wine vinegar. The young team brings it all to the table with flair and creates a fresh dynamic.

Name: La table du Royal Snail
Address: avenue de la Plante 23, Namur, 5000, Belgium
Description: This laid-back restaurant is appointed in the same trendy, glamorous vein as the Royal Snail Hotel in which it is housed. The welcoming, casual vibe provides the perfect foil to sample Carl Gillain’s bistronomic vision. The slate menu features a pageant of unconventional bistro dishes and sensibly priced wines. He might add depth to ravioli of turnip with a stock of roast onion and veal, imparting subtle umami, but then again, he may simply pair a juicy entrecote with a fresh, wonderfully light, silky bearnaise sauce. Most of the dishes are designed to be shared, although you may not always wish to do so…

Name: La'Shukran
Address: 417 Morse St. NE, Washington, DC, 20002, USA
Description: La' Shukran feels like a discovery, as you'll need to walk down an alley, look for a green door and climb the stairs to arrive at this cool spot with a funky, retro vibe. It's definitely a hot spot for drinks, but the Levantine cuisine designed for sharing is far from second place.From escargot and sweetbreads to labneh with Maryland crab, summer peppers and corn in green harissa, some dishes lean less traditional, while others, like haswei, or fried rice with seven-spice lamb, seem simple but are spot on. Every table needs an order of their soujek dumplings. Filled with beef and lamb shoulder and resting in a vibrant smoked corn and tomato brodo with urfa chili crunch and toum, it's easy to see why reservations are snapped up so quickly here.

Name: Laab Ton Yang (San Phi Suea)
Address: 199/330 Mu 9, San Phi Suea, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
Description: A solid choice for no-fuss Northern Thai food, this laid-back restaurant serves rustic, traditional dishes in small sharing portions. Highlights include the well-balanced kaeng om and boldly flavoured lap nuea, available with pork, beef or fish – raw or cooked – all prepared in classic Northern style. In an open-air setting with a relaxed local vibe, the place fills up with Thai diners at peak times. Service is friendly, with staff often speaking Northern Thai.

Name: Lab Mu Worachai
Address: 26/3 Posri Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
Description: Pork reigns supreme at this traditional Isan eatery, which may be renowned for its namesake Lab Mu – minced pork, skin and liver – but the flavourful Somtum Lao is another standout. Lunchtime can get hectic, but service is swift. The sharing sets of four to six dishes are perfect for groups.

Name: Labri
Address: 2F, 113 Bui Thi Xuan Street, Hai Ba Trung Ward, Hanoi, 112306, Vietnam
Description: A neon sign in the upstairs window is the clue to finding this modern-day bistro, tucked away on the 2nd floor of a nondescript building. Abri is French for shelter and the restaurant imbues a sense of cosy luxury. The open kitchen takes centre stage and four huge crystal chandeliers hang from the ceiling. The chef delivers virtuoso cuisine using French techniques and Vietnamese ingredients. For the full experience, opt for the 7-course menu.

Name: Lacertus
Address: 4 boulevard Franklin-Roosevelt, Les Sables d’Olonne, 85100, France
Description: Good-humoured staff, friendly service, a convivial atmosphere, modern cuisine with a touch of inventiveness (eg fish sausage or a seaweed/mustard sorbet as part of the mackerel starter; a lime/pea sorbet alongside a chocolate dessert), quality local produce and a few ingredients gathered wild (mustard seeds): this is the winning formula behind this small restaurant a stone's throw from Le Remblai promenade. In case you were wondering, the name Lacertus means "mackerel" in Latin.

Name: Lackner
Description: The splendid location of this restaurant with a wonderful terrace overlooking Mondsee is as much of a draw as the cuisine of chef-patron Martin Lackner. His dishes have classical leanings and take their cue from the seasons. The quality of the ingredients – many from the region – is exceptional. Order the set menu or à la carte, taking your pick from appetising dishes such as "Hausruck beef tartare, ciabatta-parmesan ice cream, oven-baked tomato". The in-house wine shop is also worth a look. For overnight guests, Seehotel Lackner offers tasteful guestrooms, a beautiful spa and sauna area, plus direct access to the lake.

Name: Ladinia
Address: Strada Pedercorvara 10, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: Both the Berghotel Ladinia and its restaurant of the same name boast a warm, vintage Alpine-style ambience, with wood decor that tells the story of this business which opened as a simple inn back in 1930. Little has changed since then and guests return here time after time thanks to the warm welcome and attention to detail offered by the Costa family. The traditional cuisine has the occasional modern twist, while the few Ladin-style guestrooms are decorated with a profusion of wood.

Name: Lado
Description: This restaurant is a bit of a surprise, being hidden inside a historic building in a tiny village that has been lovingly restored to offer a quiet and honest experience. The proposal, in the charge of young chefs Elia Pereira and Borja Piñeiro, takes Galicia as a great dynamising axis to talk about shared memory, the characteristics of the territory, the best local products, always from a contemporary and rather creative standpoint. Everything revolves around a fixed-price à la carte menu, and two additional tasting menus: Brétema (8 course) and Lado (14 courses).

Name: Lafarques
Description: This historic country manor house, gleaming with classy elegance and set amidst unspoiled rolling countryside, will take your breath away. Now add exquisitely tasteful guestrooms and you have yourself an idyllic country retreat! The seasoned virtuoso chef allows the (preferably local) ingredients to shout their name, whilst seeking to generously and delicately enhance their traditional flavours. He may pair locally reared chicken with a sublime Albufeira sauce, a subtle duxelles of mushrooms, chunks of foie gras and shavings of truffle. Crispy skin and poached curly kale add a playful dimension to the sides. The set menus, particularly game in season, tick all the boxes – what’s not to like?

Name: Lafayette
Description: Abutting his first restaurant, chef Xavier Pincemin has opened this trendy bistro that sports a series of adjoining Art deco rooms. He is enjoying himself and, in the process, delights us with a menu of varied influences (tacos, ceviche, tiger beef) and a selection of outstanding matured beef displayed in an ageing cabinet, such as the knockout black Baltic rib steak. Casual vibe.

Name: Lagrange
Description: Picture the scene: You are in the lovely town of Buren, and step into an elegantly converted barn in anticipation of an intimate dinner. You are served dishes that embody a refined modern take on French cuisine. This chef brings a clear culinary vision and deep, expressive flavours, uniting local and international influences. A particular standout: pan-seared cod with asparagus and set egg yolk, crispy pommes dauphine and a rich hollandaise espuma. The appealing à la carte selection and set menu are well worth exploring.

Name: Lahnyai
Address: 31 Soi Suan Phlu 2, Thung Maha Mek, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: Initially conceived as a tribute to the owner's grandmother, Lahnyai showcases modern interpretations of royal Thai cuisine. Guests are given the royal history behind each dish, which is thoughtfully explained during the meal. The refined dining room delivers an intimate ambiance with velvet walls and Jacquard-covered furniture. Infusing a contemporary twist into historical recipes, dishes satisfy with tried-and-tested flavours. If you’re lucky, you might find saeng wa pu on the menu – an aromatic, herbal dish, rich in flavour.

Name: Laia Erretegia
Description: Located on the outskirts of Hondarribia, surrounded by verdant meadows, Laia Erretegia boasts plenty of originality in its setting occupying what were once the stables of an old country house. Its cuisine is centred around the grill alongside some excellent market-inspired suggestions, and always includes two fish options (cod and monkfish, respectively). Its selection of meats is outstanding and includes its Premium rib of beef (aged for a minimum of 30 days) and its dry-aged rib of beef (aged for a minimum of 60 days). The wine cellar here is particularly striking and attractive.

Name: Laila
Description: On the ground floor of a small rural hotel near Santander! Here, in a setting of simple contemporary elegance, you'll find a full menu of updated traditional cuisine, with modern details, and the option of a tasting menu, although the latter requires a reservation at least 24 hours in advance. The terrace is a delight on sunny days!

Name: Lakasa
Address: Plaza del Descubridor Diego de Ordás 1, Madrid, 28003, Spain
Description: A restaurant that is on the tip of everyone’s tongue and as such is full almost every day. Its updated take on traditional market-based cuisine is constantly being updated and includes the option of half-portions. Don’t miss the signature Idiazabal cheese fritters!

Name: Lakeview Palace
Address: GF, West Esplanade, Wynn Palace, Avenida da Nave Desportiva, Cotai, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The emerald green and gold room sports panoramic windows so guests can admire the musical fountain while dining. The chef, who worked in Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Shanghai for years, melds the rounded flavours of Jiangnan fare with Sichuanese mala seasoning and Cantonese subtlety and freshness. His eight-treasure roast duck is a hybrid between the Huaiyang and Cantonese varieties – sticky rice is wrapped in crispy duck skin and topped with caviar.

Name: Lakruwana
Address: 668 Bay St., Staten Island, NY, 10304, USA
Description: Prepare for a sensory overload the moment you set foot into Lakruwana—the Sri Lankan hot spot is covered from floor-to-ceiling in murals, sculptures, flags, and more. The kaleidoscope of textures and colors is a welcome sight, as is the energetic owner who drifts from table to table.Street food takes center stage here, where you a variety of traditional dishes hit the mark. Don't miss the kottu roti, a stir-fried dish with godamba roti, chicken, vegetables and chicken curry or the traditional hoppers, with its bowl-shaped crepe served with a yellow fish curry. The oversized platter is ideal for sharing.

Name: Lalibera
Description: In the heart of Alba, just a stone's throw from the cathedral, this refined and elegant restaurant offers guests a warm and simple welcome. The aromas of Langhe cuisine combine with the chefs' creativity to deliver dishes that reflect the region's flavours with taste and harmony. The wine list, lovingly curated by Flavia, offers a wide variety of labels, with Piedmontese wines taking centre stage.

Name: Lalou
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted
Description: Mario Ridder has chosen a historical building brimming with character in the heart of Delft in which to celebrate wine and French cuisine. Divided into a bar, wine bar and brasserie, Lalou is the epitome of nostalgic charm – think leather ceiling, Renaissance paintings and chandeliers. The exclusive wine list exceeds 700 labels, reflecting the chef's passion for the grape. The appealing menu includes many dishes that can be ordered as half portions. An indulgent salad niçoise, lobster ravioli with a frothy bisque, delicately sweet crêpe suzette: expect no unnecessary embellishments, just fantastic ingredients and generous brasserie flavours.

Name: Lam Phu 2
Address: 23/1 Mu 3, Pak Nam Road, Bang Kung, Mueang Surat Thani, Surat Thani, 84000, Thailand
Description: Watch the fishing boats on Tapi River while enjoying a bright and airy setting and local seafood cooked southern style. The oyster omelette is gorgeous with a crispy egg base, spot-on seasoning and fresh local oysters; it goes well with steamed rice. The tender stir-fried squid with salted eggs is packed with flavour and flanked by an impressively creamy sauce. With over 100 seats, there is ample room for large groups to enjoy the scenic view.

Name: Lamaccotte
Description: Generosity, flavour and good ingredients are the elements underpinning Maxime Fillaut's cuisine, which reaps the rewards of his time at La Mare aux Oiseaux and Le Clarence in Paris. The restaurant occupies a modern, light and airy ground-floor space in a stone building in the historical city centre. The menu changes daily, reflecting the produce available at the market, and the dishes are beautifully presented. This is simple and delicious food: fondant home-made gnocchi, vegetable tops and roasted almond pistou; vegetable carbonara, parmesan emulsion, paprika-glazed celery and helianthis; meadowsweet parfait glacé, blossom honey and lemon marmalade, buckwheat sablé and caramelised dried fruit. Fast, well-paced service.

Name: Lamai Garden
Address: 36B De Quai Street, Tay Ho Ward, Hanoi, 11208, Vietnam
Description: Reimagined by chef-owner Hieu Trung Tran in 2022, Lamai Garden serves a seasonal tasting menu and vegetarian menu in line with a contemporary Vietnamese farm-to-table concept. Diners pass through a garden to the dining area with counter seating by the open kitchen. They use ingredients from their Phú Thọ farm – garden herbs, ducks and black pigs. The squid "noodle", inspired by phở chua, highlights the chef's creativity. Only open for dinner; reservations are a must.

Name: Lamark - Stube
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Located right next to the cable car station, Hotel Lamark is run by Alexander Fankhauser. The restaurant boasts a number of cosy, tastefully designed dining areas with classic Alpine-style decor. The varied menu features both traditional regional fare and more ambitious creations to be ordered à la carte or as part of a set menu. Options include veal lights in a Riesling sauce, Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) with all the trimmings and confit char fillet with pointed cabbage, greaves dumplings and a mustard sauce. There is also a fine selection of wines. Affording panoramic views, the terrace is a delightful spot all year round.

Name: Lamelas
Address: Rua Cândido da Silva 55 A, Porto Covo, 7520-437, Portugal
Description: The name of this restaurant is a reference to chef Ana Moura’s grandfather, who was from Porto Covo, a small coastal village south of Lisbon where she spent her summers as a child. Having worked in renowned restaurants such as Eleven and Arzak, she made the decision to return to her family roots. In this informal restaurant, she showcases the “Flavour of the Alentejo”, combining contemporary ingredients with impressive technique and traditional flavours. We particularly recommend the “migas de chouriço” with spare ribs; the forkbeard fish with clams in green sauce; and the cheesecake with caramel and pistachio. The superb views from the tables on the terrace are an added bonus!

Name: Lamm
Description: For a start, the impeccable façade is inviting, and inside the decor is charming, the service extremely cordial and the food an absolute treat! Choose between the "Bodenständig", "Classic" and "Vegetarian" set menus, in either a three- or four-course format, or order individual courses à la carte – everything is prepared using selected seasonal ingredients. In summer, the delightful garden terrace is a real draw.

Name: Lamm
Description: A tasteful, modern interior incorporating a sleek design, premium materials and warm tones goes hand in hand with the hospitality of a traditional inn. The menu whets the appetite with an interesting array of regional and international dishes, such as roast Angus beef served with two kinds of onions, warm potato salad and maultaschen>/i> (Swabian dumplings) sautéed in butter or Barbary duck breast accompanied by stir-fried Asian vegetables and Himalayan basmati rice. The five different set menus, which include a vegan one, are also excellent. A very popular establishment – book early if you are looking to come at the weekend!

Name: Lammekeshoeve
Description: The epitome of a swish, luxurious brasserie, Lammekeshoeve also boasts an exquisite garden patio for fine weather alfresco dining and a conservatory packed in summer vibes for the rest of the year. The chef has no qualms about forging his own path, whilst delving into a repertory of Franco-Belgian classics. Generosity is his overriding goal from the crunchy shrimp fritters and vol-au-vent stuffed with juicy Malines chicken in a creamy sauce to the decadent dame blanche (vanilla ice cream and hot chocolate sauce) dessert. A firm favourite with a business clientele, it has also found favour with families, courtesy of a play area in the garden. The establishment’s obsession with quality also extends to the expertly curated wine list.

Name: Lan y Môr
Address: Coppet Hall Beach, Saundersfoot, SA66 9AJ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Meaning ‘seashore’ in Welsh, Lan y Môr is an apt name for this stunningly located beachside restaurant; grab a table on the enclosed terrace to make the most of the view. The menu offers something for everyone, whether you’re after ‘Sea’, ‘Pasture’ or ‘Land’, but in this location your eye is sure to be drawn to the oysters, ‘frockles’ (fried cockles) and fish of the day. Ensure you save some room for pudding, especially if the terrific chocolate and cherry cake is on the menu.

Name: LanZhou Ramen
Address: 5231 Buford Hwy. NE, Doraville, GA, 30340, USA
Description: Located on Buford Highway in a busy shopping center, LanZhou is both the name of a Chinese city and a type of hand-pulled noodle that just so happens to be this spot's main attraction. Those delicious noodles are available in hearty soups with a variety of proteins, and also come broth-less. From there, broad Sichuan-leaning dishes tempt diners. Fried pot stickers sport a beautiful crispy, lacy base and delight with a savory goodness. Roast duck hand-pulled noodle soup is pure, unadulterated satisfaction, slurp by glorious slurp. Served in a massive bowl bobbing with bouncy noodles, baby bok choy, roast bone-in duck and scallions, it's loaded with flavor and will certainly cure whatever ails you.

Name: Lana
Description: An Argentinian restaurant that continues to gain in popularity, where the open grill is the focal point for everything that happens here. In this pleasant eatery run by two brothers, savour traditional dishes, gaucho specialities and different cuts of meat from a variety of breeds (Aberdeen Angus, Wagyu, Hereford, Vaca Gallega, etc.), all explained in detail and on display for diners to see in the display case at the entrance. The unusual collection of artisanal knives and the extensive list of Argentinian wines add to its appeal.

Name: Land
Address: 30 Great Western Arcade, Colmore Row, Birmingham, B2 5HU, United Kingdom
Description: The Great Western Arcade in the heart of the city is home to this intimate restaurant, where the chefs harness the power of plants for their creative vegetarian dishes. There's an original streak running through the seasonally evolving set menu – which is largely vegan – alongside a scattering of pan-Asian influences ranging from carrot char sui to sake lees, all executed with care and skill by the chefs. Wine flights are available to enhance the experience and the friendly service team will see to your every need.

Name: Landerik
Description: A modern and minimalist atmosphere characterises this small restaurant overlooking one of Ljubljana’s most characterful streets; in fine weather, booking an outdoor table to enjoy the position at the heart of the city is strongly advised. The kitchen brings contemporary sensitivity to produce from the territory, selected from small local suppliers and transformed with respect and creativity. Beyond the à la carte, the tasting menus, which tell the story of the Slovenian landscape through the chef’s dishes, are well worth exploring. Among the desserts, a light and indulgent revisitation of the Kaiserschmarrn stands out, available in versions with apple or hazelnut mousse.

Name: Landersdorfer & Innerhofer
Description: With their delicious, classic-based cuisine, served in a pleasingly down-to-earth space, friends Johann Landersdorfer and Robert Innerhofer draw throngs of diners to their restaurant in Munich's city centre. Chef-patron Johann Landersdorfer ensures that dishes such as "guinea fowl and duck liver terrine with cranberries" or "cod medallions and patties, chive sauce and potato salad" are meticulously prepared using top-notch ingredients. In the evening, the four-course menu can be extended with add-ons. At lunchtime, choose between a two-course set lunch or eating à la carte. In addition, the experienced, ever-present front-of-house team provides pleasingly relaxed yet attentive service, as well as wine recommendations that pair harmoniously with the food. The wine list is terrific and includes a handful of rarities alongside an array of top-notch wines.

Name: Landgasthaus Essl
Description: A pleasant atmosphere awaits you in this lovely inn in the middle of the village. The comfortable interior dotted with modern decorative touches feels friendly, and service is attentive. In summer, the pretty garden terrace is delightful. The delicious food is regional and seasonal, with options ranging from classics such as cordon bleu or Backhendl (Viennese breaded fried chicken) to the "Essenz:Menu", a four- to six-course set menu, from which you can also choose à la carte.

Name: Landgasthaus Schiller
Description: Steeped in tradition and family-run since 1908, this country inn sees chef-patron Gerhard Schiller serving up ambitious seasonal regional cuisine with modern influences. You can choose to have four, six or eight courses of the tasting menu or simply order the dishes à la carte. Tempting examples include Attersee tench with yellow carrot, coriander and mustard seed, or Leithaberg venison saddle with potato roulade, green beans and loquat. Classics such as Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) or chanterelle goulash are also available. The thoughtfully curated wine list homes in on Austria and the local region but also features international labels. Dine in the cosy, rustic-style interior or out on the terrace in the garden to the rear of the building.

Name: Landgasthaus Schuster
Description: The Schuster family's country inn is thoroughly charming! This is primarily down to the warm hospitality extended by the lady of the house, and the tasteful interior design. And then there are the chef-patron's seasonally influenced classic dishes such as pike-perch sausage accompanied by creamed sauerkraut with dates, or venison with nuts, black walnut sauce, cranberries and Savoy cabbage. Individual courses from each of the two set menus ("Tradition" and "Genusswerk") can be ordered à la carte. Decent wine selection with good options available by the glass.

Name: Landgasthaus Zum Kreuz
Description: The appealing alliance of regional and modern influences is omnipresent at the Neumaier family's establishment – whether in the cosy restaurant, the food or the lovely comfortable guestrooms in the Speicher guesthouse next door. Chef-owner Peter Neumaier's sons Lars and Tim are now also involved in the kitchen. The menu features classic and seasonal dishes – be sure to check out the "mini Versucherle" (mini appetisers). You can eat à la carte or choose a set menu – vegetarian options are also available. Owner Michaela Neumaier heads up the team providing friendly service. In summer, the wonderful terrace is the best place to soak up the gorgeous rural location!

Name: Landgasthof Adler
Description: This centuries-old inn has long been known in the region for serving good food. Since February 2022, chef Michael Vogel has been perpetuating this tradition as the chef-patron with great dedication – he had already worked here years earlier and took over the reins after a stint under top chef Andreas Caminada. The restaurant serves seasonally inspired dishes, available as a surprise menu or à la carte. The inviting decor seamlessly blends tradition and modern design. Tip: The charming guestrooms complement the restaurant perfectly and reflect the establishment's distinctive character.

Name: Landgasthof Backers
Description: The Backers family business has a long tradition to its name, stretching back to 1843. Today, the sixth and seventh generations are running the show with great dedication. The fresh and flavoursome food draws on the region and the seasons, and ingredients are sourced locally wherever possible, including the venison and Diepholz geese. The restaurant is a long-standing member of the Slow Food community. There are also a few comfortable guestrooms. Try the "Backers zum Kennenlernen" deal: four-course regional set menu with drinks, plus overnight accommodation.

Name: Landgasthof Bären
Description: The exterior of this 17C half-timbered house exudes historical charm; the interior is traditional and lovingly decorated with upscale furnishings. It is the garden terrace, though, that is the real highlight! In the evening, there is an ambitious set menu, its appealing vegetarian alternative, or regional classics and modern dishes à la carte. More limited options at lunchtime. There is also a good wine list, and service is cordial and competent. Contemporary guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Landgasthof Hirschen
Description: The dedication of chef Verena Martin and her team is palpable. In a charming setting diners enjoy cordial service and good food that is made primarily with produce from the region and draws inspiration from the seasons. The kitchen staff put their heart and soul into their work – the motto here is ä weng eppis Feins, or "a little something fine" in the local dialect. Tip: "Unser badisches Menü" or "Unser großes Menü" (for two or more people).

Name: Landgasthof Löwen
Address: Kirchdorfer Straße 8, Kirchdorf an der Iller, 88457, Germany
Description: Alexander Ruhland represents the fourth generation of his family to run this traditional country inn, and his kitchen turns out top-notch dishes. Two set menus are proposed: a seasonal one comprising three courses and a more ambitious four-course fine dining menu. There is also an à la carte selection featuring classics such as Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) with Allgäu beef loin, as well as international dishes and vegetarian options.

Name: Landgasthof Rössli
Description: Since 1995, Susy and Markus Sager-Meyerhans have been the friendly faces behind this long-established restaurant with its roots in the 18C, when it was a tavern. In addition to cordial service, you can expect a hybrid of traditional and modern-meets-classic cuisine; at lunchtime there is a somewhat reduced menu. Outside you will find the Rosenterrasse and Rössligarten. Charming guestrooms are also available.

Name: Landgasthof Wartegg
Description: Run by the Frei family since 1982, this long-standing restaurant with its well-maintained shingle façade serves fresh, flavoursome seasonal fare rooted in classic cuisine and crafted from excellent ingredients. The set lunch is very popular. Tip: There is an especially fine selection of Swiss wines. Diners can choose between rustic cosiness and refined elegance in the various indoor spaces or head for the lovely tree-shaded terrace. Cosy guestrooms are available for overnight stays.

Name: Landgoed de Wilmersberg
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At Landgoed de Wilmersberg nature takes centre stage, beginning with a wonderful view of the landscape of Twente, both on the terrace and in the charming dining room. The chef makes vegetables the focus in his modern dishes. He is bold enough to present the occasional challenging combination, always applying the correct techniques.

Name: Landhaus
Description: This 16C farmhouse has been turned into a really charming restaurant boasting a splendid view of Lake Constance. Featuring warm wood finishings and sleek design, the decor embodies a winning combination of the old and the new. Hostess Ariane Cresta provides cordial service in the cosy dining area, while chef-patron Lino Cresta cooks up his modern take on classic cuisine with a regional touch. On the menu, you will find veal cordon bleu, as well as beef tenderloin and brasato with potato, cauliflower, parsnip and XO, or even porcini tortelloni. In the evening, the à la carte selection is complemented by an ambitious three- to five-course set menu (vegetarian version available) and at lunchtime, by daily specials and a "Business Lunch" deal. In summer, head for the gorgeous terrace. There is a hall for events in the modern converted barn.

Name: Landhaus Drei Raben
Description: The Koep family has been synonymous with excellent cuisine since 1995… and you can expect just that when you come to eat here on this property on the 18C Landgut Jaquetrois. This former agricultural estate is planted with beautiful old trees. The restaurant has a cosy dining area (warming fireplace in winter) and a fabulous terrace with views over the Mahnensee – especially charming at sunset! The food is international, regional and seasonal. Tip: Coffee and cake are served on Sundays.

Name: Landhaus Gräfenthal
Description: Steeped in tradition, this establishment has a solid reputation in the area. Peter Lauterbach represents the fourth generation to run this family restaurant in an idyllic location. The food is a contemporary take on regional, seasonal cuisine and influenced by Mediterranean culinary tradition. Inside, pale wood, a tiled stove and pleasing decorative touches make for an inviting setting; outside there is a beautiful garden terrace. With warm and attentive service, this place has everything it takes to ensure a comfortable dining experience.

Name: Landhaus Hadrys
Address: An der Halberstädter Chaussee 1, Magdeburg, 39116, Germany
Description: The name Sebastian Hadrys has been synonymous with quality cuisine since 2003. His seasonal dishes have a Mediterranean edge. In addition to an enticing à la carte selection, there is a sophisticated set menu comprising four to nine courses, as well as a special set menu to kick off the weekend on Friday evenings. The wine list is also very good. The pleasingly bright, modern space has a casual feel, plus a large terrace. Experienced staff provide friendly service. Tip: Cookery courses are also organised here.

Name: Landhaus Halferschenke
Description: In this beautiful quarry-stone building dating from 1832, the Schmah family serve ambitious cuisine that revolves around top-notch ingredients and the seasons – from sole and Aubrac beef to oysters and turbot from Brittany. You can opt to dine à la carte or go for a set menu. In addition to the food, diners can look forward to attentive service in a tasteful setting with a country-house feel. In summer, the gorgeous terrace beckons. In addition, MA PETITE CHAMBRE is a small gourmet haven serving a set menu. They have four well-kept guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Landhaus Hohenlohe
Description: This long-standing family business, now with Matthias Mack at the helm, is run according to a winning formula. In a very pleasant informal atmosphere, extremely friendly and experienced waitstaff are always on hand. The delicious food is freshly prepared and feautures regional and international influences. You can compose a three- or four-course set menu from the appealing list of options (also vegetarian) or order à la carte. Appetising dishes include porcini ravioli, baby spinach, Brettenfeld Jerusalem artichokes, truffle fonduta. The restaurant also has its own herb and vegetable garden. Overnight accommodation is available in this well-kept country house nestled in a residential area.

Name: Landhaus Mönchenwerth
Description: This inviting establishment has its fair share of regulars, and deservedly so. One of the main attractions is its location right by the Rhine – tables with a view of the river, as well as those on the gorgeous terrace, are in high demand. No less captivating are the creations of chef-patron Guy de Vries, whose French heritage shines through in work. Drawing from the bounty of each season, he concocts mouthwatering plates with a Mediterranean twist. The well-curated wine list includes an impressive selection of Champagnes. Friendly and adept service.

Name: Landhaus Rössle
Description: Expect ambitious cuisine is in a classic/French vein with regional and seasonal influences – dishes include the likes of seared scallops on orange fennel, and the classic Zwiebelrostbraten (beef and onions in gravy). You can dine à la carte or opt for the set menu – available in an omnivore or vegetarian version. Attentive and charming service is the forte of the lady of the house. The interior is modern and elegant, and in winter tables by the fireplace are very much in demand. In summer, the garden terrace is a boon. There are attractive rooms for overnight guests.

Name: Landhaus am See
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The lakeside setting, nestled in lush greenery, is altogether exceptional – particularly if you dine on the terrace with views across the magnificent garden to the water. Inside, the decor is equally lovely, featuring tasteful and welcoming country-house-style decor. The kitchen emphasises seasonal and regional sourcing, with dishes that are meticulously prepared and full of flavour. Choose from the enticing à la carte selection or compose your own set menu. For overnight stays, there are charming, individually appointed guestrooms.

Name: Landhotel Donner
Description: At the idyllically located Landhotel Donner, diners sit in snug dining rooms where warm wood and pretty fabrics create a charming, traditional setting. The cuisine is classic and regional with seasonal influences; tempting choices include house-made jellied knuckle of pork with remoulade sauce and fried potatoes, or braised leg of wild boar in a liquorice jus with parsley root purée. Order à la carte or opt for the four-course surprise menu. Service is friendly and attentive. In the summer, the terrace to the rear of the building is a lovely spot. Now run by the third generation, the Donner family's hotel offers well-appointed, comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Landhotel Krone
Description: Here, tradition rubs shoulders with current trends in cosy little spaces that feature an attractive blend of old brickwork, wood, steel and glass. The regional and seasonal cuisine is scattered with international influences. Medieval vaulted cellar for events. This family-run business also offers attractive, individually designed guestrooms and wellness facilities.

Name: Landline
Address: Park Hotel, Shelbourne Street, Kenmare, V93 X3XY, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated within the grand Park Hotel Kenmare and overlooking Kenmare Bay, this elegant dining room comes with the added bonus of being decorated with original paintings by Irish artist Sean Scully – the restaurant is even named after one of his works. The kitchen showcases a bounty of prime Irish produce, from scallops and sole to venison and Irish farmhouse cheese – all embellished with precise, well-judged accompaniments. Oenophiles will appreciate the strong choice of classic vintages.

Name: Landua
Description: Occupying an old stone house in the heart of the countryside and equipped with its own greenhouse-vegetable garden, Landua is run with great enthusiasm by a young couple. In the beautiful dining room, which has been converted from what was once the stable, you will be offered a unique surprise menu with simple yet well-balanced and elegant dishes. Although they use ingredients from the nearby coast and meadows, the vegetables take centre stage. The access road is very attractive, as it partly runs alongside the Santa Uxia reservoir!

Name: Lang is her
Description: "Lang is her" is the appetising culinary concept brought to Hotel an der Wasserburg by a dedicated team led by the Rohde family (the owners). The modern, international cuisine with seasonal influences is served as a three- to seven-course set menu or à la carte. Both in the chic interior, which has a friendly vibe, and, in summer, out on the lovely terrace with its walnut tree, staff provide attentive service and will be happy to recommend the perfect accompaniment from the well-stocked German/international wine list. Wasserburg Bistro & Bar, also part of the property, has a separate menu. Tip: The medieval castle, Burg Neuhaus, is within walking distance.

Name: Langan's
Address: Stratton Street, London, W1J 8LB, United Kingdom
Description: Few London restaurants can boast quite as colourful a history as this Mayfair institution, which was a veritable trailblazer when it opened back in the 1970s. Now refreshed and relaunched, it beckons you in from the street with its glowing neon sign, and inside it retains much of what made it so popular in its heyday. The art-filled dining room has an eye-catching elegance, the service is friendly yet formal and the menu is filled with all the brasserie classics, from Caesar salad and fish pie to beef Wellington for two and 'mousse au chocolat'.

Name: Langdon Hall Country House & Spa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Located a mere hour away from Toronto, this historic 19th-century Cambridge estate has long been something of a special retreat in Ontario. The mansion sits on 75 acres with a spa, walking trails, culinary gardens and, of course, its signature restaurant. A stately interior with white tablecloths and a well-heeled staff fit the aesthetic. Chef Jason Bangerter has led this kitchen since 2013 and cooks with a kind of familiar French classicism. Think lobster with buttermilk and passion fruit or an indulgent foie gras parfait paired with a superb slice of warm, buttery brioche. To drink, the wine list is an impressive collection of top producers, older vintages and Canadian bottles.

Name: Langosteria
Description: This is a place to see and be seen on the ski slopes overlooking St Moritz. The terrace affords magnificent views, making it a delightful spot in which to savour freshly prepared Italian cuisine. Langoustine, lobster and fish, truffle pizza and pasta are the specialities of this restaurant, which also has locations in Milan, Paris and Paraggi. If you're not skiing, the best way to get here is by taxi.

Name: Langosteria
Description: This is an establishment of soft lighting and music, a highly fashionable address and among the best known in the city. The elegant atmosphere provides the setting for a culinary offering entirely dedicated to seafood, interpreted through classic preparations that are never banal, enriched by indulgent, personal touches. The selection of raw fish is extensive and carefully curated, closely tied to the daily market arrivals. Also of note is the wine list, comprehensive and well constructed, featuring important and prestigious labels.

Name: Langosteria
Address: Cheval Blanc Paris, 8 quai du Louvre, Paris, 75001, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: On the 7th floor of La Samaritaine, in the heart of the swanky Cheval Blanc Hotel, this smart brasserie, part of the Langosteria group, marries Italian cucina with a chic urbane vibe. Its spacious elegant dining room welcomes hotel residents and a well-heeled clientele who come to sample its seafaring menu. Examples include refined crudos (tartare of yellowtail, gambero rosso) and pasta to die for: spaghetti with Galician sea urchins, paccheri with line-caught seabass, capers, olives and Amalfi lemons. Among the decadent desserts, the orange, grapefruit and limoncello meringue soufflée is a highlight. Swish service and a knockout wine list: a place to eat and be seen!

Name: Langosteria Paraggi
Address: Via Paraggi a Mare 1, Paraggi, 16038, Italy
Description: The elegant Milanese style of the famous Langosteria restaurant has been given a maritime and holiday feel in its seasonal sibling which is housed within the Bagni Fiore overlooking the small yet stunning Paraggi bay. Langosteria Paraggi boasts a vintage decor which is at the same time glamorous and up-to-date, views of the beach and the sea, and a menu focusing on delicious fresh fish and seafood such as oysters and shellfish.

Name: Langwies Wirtshaus
Description: A self-proclaimed "lodge hotel for gourmets", Langwies Wirtshaus combines several facilities under one roof: a restaurant, a spa hotel, a conference centre and long-stay apartments. The menu features a contemporary selection of regional classics, steaks and seasonal dishes, as well as vegan and vegetarian options. There are several attractive dining spaces – for example, you can book a table in the cosy, spruce-panelled bay room.

Name: Lantaw (Compostela)
Address: Guiwanon before Shell, Compostela, Cebu, The Philippines
Description: For a seaside dining experience, Lantaw ranks high, with open-air and outdoor seating areas offering sweeping sea views. The atmosphere is relaxed yet vibrant, especially at peak hours. A must-try is the chicken bacolod – tender, smoky and full of char-grilled flavour, it pairs perfectly with the fragrant rice. Whether or not you come for a celebration, the cheerful staff, music and birthday dance performances add a festive, memorable experience.

Name: Lanzani Bottega & Bistrot
Address: Via Albertano da Brescia 41, Brescia, 25127, Italy
Description: This modern restaurant (open from 7am to 11pm), once the family butcher’s, is also a delicatessen and wine boutique. It serves top-quality produce such as Pata Negra and other hams, anchovies from the Cantabrian sea, an excellent selection of cheeses and more elaborate dishes. At mealtimes, the venue transforms into a proper restaurant, with a smaller menu available at lunchtime.

Name: Lao Chen Chia
Address: Shop 92 & 97, Zhong Yang Market, 2 Lane 2, Ximen Street, North District, Hsinchu City, Taiwan
Description: For over 70 years, this stall in a wet market has been a hit with the locals who can’t get enough of their dumplings, wontons, pork meatballs and pork ribs served in milky, flavourful pork bone broth. Their signature sticky rice dumplings are shaped like oval tangyuan and generously filled with pork leg meat. If you would like to try their hand-torn pork ribs, make sure you arrive by 9am; the ribs aren’t ready before and tend to run out soon after.

Name: Lao Dian Ginger Chicken (North)
Address: 51, Shaonian Street, North District, Hsinchu City, Taiwan
Description: This simple shop specialises in health tonic hotpots. As its name suggests, ginger chicken is the must-try, especially in winter. The broth is made fresh daily with loads of ginger and 10-plus Chinese herbs sautéed in sesame oil for two hours to mellow out the flavours, while freshly slaughtered free-range Silkie chicken boosts vital energy. Also try their yan wan dumplings – pork leg meat wrapped in silky wonton skin made with starch and pounded pork.

Name: Lao Hsu
Address: 9, Baodao Lane, Section 3, Xinwu Road, Xindian District, New Taipei, Taiwan
Description: Lao Hsu has been in business for over 30 years and at the current address since 2015. The owners, a couple from Jiangxi, enjoy making Taiwanese and Jiangzhe dishes with uniquely local produce such as river shrimps and wild greens. Dozens of ingredients go into their sticky rice dumplings, which are based on a Cantonese recipe and take three days to make. Be sure to try the tiger-skin pork trotter, too – it is slow cooked for 6 hours for a soft texture.

Name: Lao Jie Fang
Address: Mei Ling Market & Food Centre, #02-15, 159 Mei Chin Road, 140159, Singapore
Description: Cantonese-style noodles topped with beef brisket, pork ribs, pork knuckles or beef tendon are the name of the game here. The noodles are springy, and the pork knuckles are braised until gelatinous in a secret soy sauce.

Name: Lao Tou Pai
Address: 46-1, Neighborhood 4, Dalin Village, Beipu Township, Hsinchu County, Taiwan
Description: The owner’s family used to run a tea leaf factory and some 30 years ago, he remodelled the factory building into a Hakkanese restaurant. Red bricks, wooden beams and wood-fired ceramics impart a rustic edge. Traditional Hakkanese fare defines the menu, starring unique ingredients like red shiso. Slow-cooked succulent braised pork belly with homemade preserved mustard greens allows the flavours to meld and intensify.

Name: Lao Xing Xian (Huangpu)
Address: 5F, Parkson, 918 Middle Huaihai Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: Xian, or umami, is the fifth core flavour of food; it also means “fresh” in Chinese. At Lao Xing Xian, the owner aims to serve the freshest seafood, caught by his own fleet in the East China Sea that is deftly crafted with a knockout umami kick. The fish is neatly displayed for diners to choose – beltfish and yellow croaker taste best when steamed plain. Braised wild rice paddy eel is lightly seasoned to accentuate its natural flavour.

Name: Lapprodo
Address: Via Roma 22, Vibo Valentia Marina, 89900, Italy
Description: This restaurant close to the port of Vino Marina is a long-established favourite in the area and is renowned for its seafood cuisine which showcases traditional recipes made using the best-quality fish. In summer, make the most of the dining space on the delightful outdoor veranda.

Name: Larb Duang Dee Mee Sook
Address: 74 Soi Ban Huai Sai, Mu 4, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
Description: With its simple, rustic look, this quaint eatery specialises in northern lap dishes, paired with a local chaeo dipping sauce with the aroma of toasted sticky rice. The spicy, sour and fragrant beef soup is a must.

Name: Larb Thai-Isan
Address: 6234 N. Federal Hwy., Fort Lauderdale, FL, 33308, USA
Description: This restaurant brings plenty of color, character, and Thai flair (note the tuk tuk in the back) to a space nestled within a busy shopping center in Fort Lauderdale. It's always busy and there are no reservations, but it's worth the wait. Their large menu is far from standard, including everything from curries, noodle dishes, and salads to signature dishes from the Isan region. Like spicy? They'll ask for your preference and won't hold back if you indicate you're a heat seeker. Dishes to order include Yum Naem Khao Tod, a classic crispy rice salad studded with fermented sausage and mixed with peanuts, ginger, and fresh herbs. Fried banana is a must-order, as is a classic mango sticky rice.

Name: Larder Brasserie and Grill
Address: 17 Bore Street, Lichfield, WS13 6LZ, United Kingdom
Description: ‘All flavour, no pomp’ is the tagline at this relaxed, warmly run restaurant – and that’s exactly what you’ll get. Sit in the boldly decorated first floor restaurant or book a seat at the chefs table to be close to the action. Attractively presented modern dishes are sure to satisfy.

Name: Lark
Address: 6A Angel Hill, Bury St Edmunds, IP33 1UZ, United Kingdom
Description: This small, sweet building overlooks an abbey and a cathedral in the centre of this historic market town. Over the years, it has been a police station, a bus shelter and a florist; now it’s a pared-back restaurant with modern art adorning the whitewashed walls. Choose from a great range of modern small plates that deliver satisfying, carefully judged flavours with a definite Mediterranean influence. Dishes could include cod cheek tempura or sopressini cacio e pepe – if you can’t make your mind up, go for the ‘Kitchen Selection’.

Name: Las Lías Bilbao
Description: Tucked away in the lively and bustling city of Bilbao, this gastro-bar is the perfect setting in which to enjoy the true culinary flavour of the Basque Country. Take your pick between an extensive array of tapas and “raciones” and a small menu, but whatever you choose, make sure you try the flavoursome crab-filled scallops, and the entrecôte of aged Frisona Gallega beef. There’s an extensive choice of local wines that the friendly staff will be happy to serve by the glass.

Name: Las Redes
Address: Avenida de los Soportales 24, San Vicente de la Barquera, 39540, Spain
Location: San Vicente de la Barquera, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: A family-run restaurant well situated along the main street running through this small town, where the focus is on sourcing the freshest possible ingredients from the local auction. Traditional à la carte featuring fish, seafood and a few savoury rice dishes. Pleasant terrace.

Name: Las Torres
Description: A classic-cum-contemporary restaurant with a profusion of wood that has been in business for over 30 years, and which takes its name from the area in which it is situated, known affectionately as “the three towers”. Its à la carte of traditional cuisine with a contemporary touch always features top-quality ingredients and is complemented by a tasting menu.

Name: Lasai
Description: Lasai takes its name from the Basque word for “calm” or “tranquillity”. This discreet restaurant in a narrow street in the centre of the city, just a few metres from the river, invites guests to discover its modern take on traditional cuisine via a simple daily set menu entitled 'Hiria' (lunchtime only, Monday through Friday, excluding holidays) and two more extensive tasting menus ('Lasai' and 'Crystal') that showcase dishes with their roots in the region as well as time-honoured flavours.
