Whilst he does offer a seasonal and good value à la carte menu of handsome-looking dishes like gurnard with courgettes, or Ebony Black Angus beef with asparagus, your best bet is to go for the full experience and enjoy the five- or eight-course tasting menu of dishes chosen by him. The room has a cool, contemporary feel. If it’s date night, ask for one of the intimate booths.

Name: Lillotatini
Description: Situated in the heart of a small medieval castle-hamlet, this traditional-style restaurant with an attractive terrace on the historic square provides the setting for local specialities such as freshwater fish and truffles in season. There’s also a wine boutique on the same piazza (reached as soon as you come into the historic centre), which sells typical local produce and a good selection of wine. The latter also features on the restaurant’s wine list, with the family on hand to offer recommendations.

Name: Lilou
Description: This restaurant set in a row of townhouses in the centre of Goes evokes the spirit of Paris. Round marble-topped tables, high ceilings, tiled floors, French chansons – this bistro has it all. Both the tempting menu and the wines also draw on French tradition. Well-seasoned hand-cut steak tartare; pan-fried sea bream accompanied by a rich beurre blanc with fresh, zesty notes; a shellfish platter, or profiteroles with vanilla ice cream and chocolate sauce: diners are spoilt for choice! If in need of recommendations, ask the amiable hostess, who will be happy to help.

Name: Lily's
Address: Avenue Emile de Mot 1, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
Description: Lily’s, which recreates the vibe of a Saint Tropez or Los Angeles club in Brussels with elegant, premium materials, a pretty green pergola in summer and dancing at the weekends, has become a hotspot of the Belgian capital. Indulge in a glass of wine or a signature cocktail as you cast your eye over the awesome menu. Familiar Belgian favourites, such as immaculately cooked veal chop with fresh béarnaise sauce, are prepared with the same flair and talent as a ceviche of seabass or truffle taglioni. Attracts A-listers like bees to honey for an unforgettable evening!

Name: Lima
Address: 31 Rathbone Place, Fitzrovia, London, W1T 1JH, United Kingdom
Description: From Lima to London, this fun and informal restaurant brings a bright burst of Peruvian flavour to the British capital. Start with a cocktail – a pisco sour if you want to get in the South American spirit – before choosing from a selection of dishes featuring some fantastically vivid colours. The menu veers between authentic classics, such as stone bass ceviche with "tiger's milk" sauce or beef fillet anticucho, and influences from further afield. Make sure you save room for dessert, as the chocolate mousse with almond crumble and candied sesame is a real winner.

Name: Liman İstanbul
Address: Kılıçali Paşa Mahallesi, Meclis-i Mebusan Sokak O2 Blok No:8 D:102 Galataport, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34433, Türkiye
Description: Start with a cocktail in the bar on the ground floor before moving up to the first floor, where Liman is ensconced in a laid-back yet stylish setting boasting a stunning terrace overlooking the Bosphorus. Time-honoured recipes are given a refined modern twist with meticulous attention to detail. Examples include crispy lahmacun bursting with the rich flavors of lamb and beef, finished with fresh herbs and lemon, or sourdough pide with house-made pickles. Then for dessert: katmer with pistachio and Maraş ice cream. These chefs masterfully balance a reverence for tradition with cutting-edge technique – therein lies their genius.

Name: Limapulo
Address: 50 Jalan Doraisamy, Chow Kit, Kuala Lumpur, 50300, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: The restaurant has a rustic edge with vintage canteen-style furniture that evokes waves of nostalgia across a dimly lit venue. Limapulo (which means fifty in Malay), is managed by a team of Malaysian chefs. It’s best to choose plates for sharing and be sure to order the popular Nyonya laksa – a standout dish indeed. The signature sate has a special sauce homemade from star fruits and pineapple. Some menu items are only available on certain days.

Name: Limbourg
Description: A wonderful addition to the Belgian Quarter's fine dining scene. The atmosphere is pleasingly laid-back and the vibe tasteful, whether you dine in the ground-floor space or at BelEtage. Chef-patron Alen Radic showcases his cosmopolitan cuisine, which draws on French influences and is made with fresh, good-quality ingredients – served as a five- or nine-course set menu of which there are two versions: "classique" and "veggie". During the week, there is also a five-course lunch, which includes dishes from the evening menu. The sheltered courtyard terrace is particularly inviting in summer.

Name: Lime
Description: The open kitchen immediately catches the eye at the contemporary Lime, which also has a charming veranda. A table by the kitchen is a must if you want to see accomplished chef Ysbrandt Wermenbol at work. He gives traditional dishes a carefully considered personal twist, often taking inspiration from Mediterranean and Asian cuisine. His surprising ideas dare to be complex, while retaining a sense of generosity and balance.

Name: Limosneros
Description: Taking its name from the "limosneros walls" built in ancient times, this centrally located spot is perfectly poised for downtown dwellers and visitors. From the remnants of an old fountain in the entrance hall to the walls hung with mirrors from Tlayacapan, Puebla talavera, and Huichol embroidery, this place is loaded with charm. This kitchen has a clear respect for tradition, even reviving old recipes, but it's all done with an infusion of contemporary flair. Opt for the tasting menu and you'll be rewarded with a tour of their flavorful, well-prepared cuisine, or choose the unusual-but-intriguing taco tasting, which also includes a sweet offering.

Name: Limpide
Address: 170 avenue de l'Hippodrome, à Lambersart, Lille, 59130, France
Description: Previously home to Empreinte, Limpide has retained its predecessor's pared-back aesthetic. The small dining area is bathed in light thanks to large windows with antique stained glass depicting the art of brewing. At the helm, young chef Karl Widmer (who trained in the kitchens of Le Val d'Auge, Yannick Alléno and Damien Laforce) cooks up personal cuisine with principles, as evidenced by a wealth of details on the plate. But this chef also likes to keep things simple, as illustrated by his monkfish in barigoule, delicate white butter sauce and tender little pieces of artichoke heart in parsley.

Name: Lin
Address: 6, Alley 25, Lane 300, Section 4, Ren’ai Road, Da’an District, Taipei, 106, Taiwan
Description: Chef Lin, who has years of fine dining experience under his belt, chose to open his venture in a quiet alley to offer diners an intimate experience. His set menu delivers refined Gallic fare made with Taiwanese ingredients, informed by his extensive travels. The island in the open kitchen is the stage where spectacular performances unfold. Consider ordering add-ons, such as crêpes suzette prepared tableside.

Name: Lin Family of One - The Bund
Address: 4F, The Central, 123 East Nanjing Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: This upmarket dining concept nests in a shopping mall where century-old buildings are connected by a glass dome. The owner Mr Lin, a Taizhou native, has been cooking since the age of 19 and he ensures dishes are as authentic as they can be. Homestyle braised pomfret boasts a velvety texture and deep flavours, served with hand-made glutinous rice cake. Marinated tofu, and sweet potato noodles with sea anemone are also worth trying.

Name: Lin Ji Lao Chu
Address: 299 Wensan West Road, Xihu, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: The unadorned two-storey house with grey brick walls may not look exciting, but diners have been flocking here for over 20 years for its Tonglu farm-style cooking – it's simple, rustic and delicious. Photos and the names of dishes are shown on a wall of lightboxes on the ground floor, where servers take your order. Try the organic fish from Qiandao Lake two ways: the fish head soup is milky and rich; and the braised fish fillet is silky and mildly spicy.

Name: Lin Jia Tai Cai (Henghu North Road)
Address: 96 Henghu North Road, Wenling, Taizhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: The brand was founded in 2003 in a small coastal town facing the East China Sea. This branch near the scenic Lake Jiulong stays true to the brand’s ethos, focusing on Taizhou recipes with uniquely Wenling accents. As in other seafood restaurants, expect to make your pick from the live fish tanks. Red-braised spicy whelks are plump, bouncy and sweet. Sea anemone on rice cake stands out with intense briny umami.

Name: Lin Jiang Yan
Address: 216 Fucheng Road, Pudong, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: Remodelled from a heritage building (c 1902), this restaurant is perfect for banquets and entertainment. The main area and private rooms all share the same river views. The young head chef, who used to work for a hotel in Shanghai, updates traditional Jiangzhe cooking with creative twists. Pre-order his Fukubukuro Yanduxian – tofu skin pouches stuffed with ground pork and shepherd's purse in a rich broth of cured and fresh pork with bamboo shoots.

Name: Lin Ju
Address: 100 Dunhua North Road, Shongshan District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: This restaurant at Illume Taipei exudes understated elegance. It serves fittingly refined Cantonese food that showcases premium ingredients and the chef's well-honed skills. The veteran Hong Kong chef, in his 70s, specialises in season-driven dishes and dried seafood. The baked crab shell is stuffed with crabmeat, roe and cheese, and boasts deep umami. There are two customisable menus. Book at least three days ahead.

Name: Lin's Vegetable Lamb Hotpot
Address: 327 Jilin Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, 104, Taiwan
Description: Lamb hotpot here differs from others thanks to its special soup base which is fragrant and nourishing – it’s made with shellfish, lamb bones, goji berries and ginger, plus mustard cabbage stems in winter or white radish in summer. Order an extra portion of sliced lamb belly or loin to be blanched in the soup. Lamb trotters braised in spiced marinade are also worth trying. Choose between the wood-clad dining room and al fresco seating.

Name: Lina
Description: If you are looking for gastronomic personality, this restaurant deserves your attention, because Mediterranean cuisine with Argentinean and Caribbean touches are hard to find! With Patricio Massimino behind the stove and his brother Diego in charge of hospitality, this restaurant presents itself as a coquettish bistro named in honour of their grandmother, who instilled in them the love for this mixed cuisine and the values every good host needs. The menu, with dishes that combine perfectly and are as striking as the Mahi Mahi (a tropical fish accompanied with a Thai pesto), is complemented by a set lunch menu (only offered on weekdays).

Name: Lina
Address: Av. Yucatán 147, Roma Norte, Cuauhtémoc, 06700, Mexico
Description: With a welcoming vibe and an open kitchen, this quaint spot in Roma bursts with contemporary charm. The service is all heart here, where Chef Mariana Villegas Martínez draws on her experiences and travels to inspire her contemporary Mexican cooking. From the seasonal products highlighted to the harmony of flavors, this is cooking that shows great care and thoughtfulness. Far from flashy, it's straightforward but skillful, perhaps best seen in a plate of beautifully charred squash sided by a smoky pine nut sauce. Chicken with crispy skin is set with roasted peaches and a mushroom medley, but it's the rich mole coloradito that makes the dish especially memorable. Close out with a fruit-layered tres leches for a real treat.

Name: Lindenhof
Description: Like their hotel with its cosy individually designed guestrooms, the Hankhs' restaurant is also very popular. This is down to the excellent seasonal cuisine, which has regional and Mediterranean influences. A great deal of dedication and care is invested in preparing the often complex dishes. You can order à la carte or opt for a set menu (vegetarian version available). Friendly and competent waitstaff. The small terraces in front of and to the rear of the building are delightful.

Name: Lindenhof 1887
Description: This North German family-run establishment is pretty as a picture! After being welcomed into the attractive inn built in 1887 with a lively local greeting ("moin"), you can expect good, attentive service in a modern and thoroughly chic ambience. Chef Tjark-Peter Maaß cooks tasty dishes of a regional bent. For example, the fried North Sea plaice, fried potatoes, cucumber salad, Tönning shrimps is a tasty and fresh option – one of the classics. There are also some appealing and cosy guestrooms for an overnight stay.

Name: Lindenhofkeller
Description: This establishment bills its cuisine as a sophisticated version of home cooking. But soul food is also a very apt description of what is served in this gorgeous traditional restaurant in a desirable Old Town location. Sebastian Rösch delivers genuinely feel-good fare through a symbiosis of his Franconian heritage and Swiss influences. Shining examples include sausage salad with Gruyère and slices of radish, or a classic braised beef roulade served with parsley root, spiced gingerbread and bone marrow jus. The chef strikes a balance between tradition and modernity, always showcasing high-quality ingredients. Diners can go à la carte or opt for the "Schmankerl Menü" (available with or without meat); the "Brotzeit" platter makes for an appealing starter. The modern decor and relaxed ambience are reminiscent of a chic, trendy gastropub; the courtyard terrace is also pretty. Extremely friendly waitstaff. Real passion has gone into curating the wine list – a fine selection of well-established names but also lesser-known or smaller winegrowers. They are also open for lunch on Wed (shorter menu). Tip for motorists: Parkhaus Urania is just a short (if steep) walk away.

Name: Lineadombra
Address: Ponte dell'Umiltà, sestiere Dorsoduro 19, Venice, 30123, Italy
Description: Boasting a splendid location with an outdoor dining space on a kind of raft-cum-platform, this restaurant boasts one of the most delightful views in Venice, with the Giudecca on the opposite side of the canal. Contemporary cuisine with a focus on fish and the occasional creative twist.

Name: Ling Kitchen
Description: Chef Ling Qi Wu is known in Austin for several restaurants, but Ling Kitchen offers something considerably more personal. Hosted inside the commissary kitchen that supports her restaurant group, this intimate communal dining experience invites guests directly into the heart of the operation for a tasting menu that blends Chinese culinary traditions with playful presentations and luxury ingredients. Dishes like the Water Lilies Goldfish Soup, featuring delicate seafood dumplings served in a clear broth, show both technical precision and a sense of whimsy, while crisp pork belly with fermented red tofu sauce demonstrates a more restrained approach. Throughout the meal, familiar flavors are reimagined through elaborate presentations.

Name: Ling Long
Address: L2-04, Block E, The Five@KPD, 49 Jalan Dungun, Bukit Damansara, Kuala Lumpur, 50490, Malaysia
Description: Born into a Chinese family of chefs and formally trained in Gallic cuisine, the head chef strives to add a French spin to Chinese gourmet classics. The tasting menu embodies his culinary vision – crispy duck is aged for seven days making it juicy and tender; the must-try botan ebi dressed in fermented Chinese tofu sauce is marvellously ingenious. The chef occasionally pops out of the kitchen to serve the food himself and chat with diners.

Name: Ling's Ravioleria Migrante
Description: A young couple (she was born in China; he’s half-French, half-Italian) have settled in this quiet residential district where they now run a tiny yet successful restaurant with around 20 seats in the dining room and a few small tables outdoors in summer – booking is essential! The menu includes various types of Chinese ravioli as well as dishes described by the couple as “migrant”, in other words “which draw inspiration from different cuisines from around the world, not only Asia but also the Mediterranean, France and Italy, with Emilia Romagna at its heart”. Examples include Peking-styleMora Romagnola coppa ham and pink Adriatic prawns marinated in mirin and soy sauce. The menu changes daily in line with market availability and the inspiration of the chef. Drinks include tea, beer and a small selection of wine.

Name: Lingo
Description: Lingo, which means "apple" in Japanese, is an homage to American and European comfort food with elegantly blended Japanese influences. Here, chawanmushi is dressed up with rock shrimp, scallop tartare, bisque foam, and sea grapes for a delightful cultural collision. Roasted bone marrow steak tartare is unctuous and savory with creamy, nutty tones from black sesame but perhaps the best example of Lingo's unique style is their beef pie. Made with Hokkaido-style braised beef curry, this oval pie with a golden pastry crust is a beautiful riff on the classic.

Name: Linny's
Description: Linny's is the latest addition to David Schwartz's growing collection of popular spots (which also includes Sunnys Chinese and Mimi Chinese). Named after his mom, Linda, and designed with Jack Lipson, this restaurant blends old-school steakhouse energy with subtle deli touches. Prices skew high but the atmosphere is perfect for special occasions.The menu is a hit list of comfort classics with a twist like the challah service sided by bowls of pickles, house-made sauerkraut and whipped cheese with berry jam or a Caesar salad that substitutes crispy chicken skin for the typical crouton. Steaks, fish and other proteins like roast chicken and lamb neck are solid, while caramelized apple cake with a tableside pour of chantilly cream is the perfect send-off.

Name: Lino Bistrot
Description: In the heart of Pavia’s old pedestrian centre, precisely in the piazza where linen was once traded, this new restaurant shares its entrance with its more distinguished “elder brother”, the fine dining restaurant Lino. In fact, although now the younger sibling, it was the first step of the project, which subsequently evolved into the fine dining establishment. The spaces, which once housed a bank and later a bookshop, have been transformed into a welcoming venue where honest and immediate cuisine is proposed, carefully presented and faithful to pleasing simplicity. The menu features dishes of clear flavour and sound construction, such as house-made gnocchi with Nerano sauce and shavings of Provolone del Monaco, cod with creamed rapini and Taggiasca olives, or an indulgent tiramisù with cream, salted cocoa crumble, coffee-soaked savoiardi and chocolate sauce.

Name: Linou Soumpasis & Co.
Description: A casual and contemporary “new-age taverna” in the central Psiri district of the city where it occupies a former candle shop (whose products are still sold here to this day). Greek cooking is based around unpretentious yet delicious dishes that always showcase the restaurant’s commitment to organic ingredients.

Name: Linéa
Description: Frederic Scavone made a name for himself at Le Pontecino in Liège, before setting up shop in this impressive edifice, flanked by a modern wing. His contemporary spin on Italian cooking does feature the occasional Gallic twang, but Mediterranean exuberance is probably its overriding characteristic. Rigatoni alla norma, homemade ravioli with fresh sausages and a personal interpretation of tiramisu… Flavour is the watchword of Linéa. Book a room and treat yourself to a truly relaxing weekend in style.

Name: Lin’eau
Description: This former flax factory (1907) is steeped in history, as is illustrated by the bare stone walls, authentic details and old photos. This industrial legacy has been cleverly updated with a wealth of trendy details and personalised works of art, creating a happy mix of old and new. The young couple at the helm shines the spotlight on a modern, deftly-crafted, international score, while lavishing great care on the fascinating sauces and textures. Kick off with subtle dogfish, enhanced by a dried lime dressing and oil of linden leaf, before moving on to sample red gurnard marinated in a tangy dressing and flanked by a gutsy lemon-spiked mayonnaise. The chef is a member of the NorthSeaChef movement, which aims to raise the demand for lesser-known fish and bycatch seafood.

Name: Lio Pellegrini
Description: Refined interiors, attentive to the smallest detail and enriched by a generous selection of quality objects – also available through a dedicated catalogue – define the style of this venue in the heart of the city, just steps from the Accademia Carrara. Completing the experience is an elegant outdoor terrace, a genuine oasis of calm, ideal for dining al fresco. The cuisine moves between Mediterranean suggestions of land and sea, striking a balance between tradition and contemporary touches: on one side more classic dishes, on the other offerings enriched with creative flourishes. A gastronomic journey that looks to the local area without forgoing occasional forays into Tuscan culture, the owner’s homeland. A spacious and elegant room, designed for boutique hospitality, completes the offering.

Name: Liquide
Description: The quirky decor is delightfully amusing: a horn chandelier and mismatched armchairs, chairs or sofas, plus a 12m-long marble table d'hôte by Philippe Starck. Trendy, but friendly and ideal for hanging out with the mates, sharing dishes, sampling cocktails and a fine bottle (or two). The brainchild of Matthias Marc, variety and creativity set the culinary scene at Liquide.

Name: Lisa Marie
Description: A delightfully unpretentious restaurant run by a pleasant team in Coburg's old town. The modern interior is lovely, and the service is friendly, attentive and professional. Seasonal dishes with international influences are rustled up in the partially visible kitchen. The lunch menu is somewhat more limited. Tip: Visit the palace, Schloss Ehrenburg, opposite. For motorists: There are two underground car parks (Albertplatz and Mauer) underground car park just a four-minute walk from the restaurant.

Name: Lisander
Description: A Sicilian chef proposes a cuisine that straddles tradition and modernity, with a broad and generous offering of several tasting menus and an à la carte selection encompassing both land and sea, sweet and savoury, with occasional gastronomic echoes of his native region. All this is served in the elegant dining room carved from the common spaces of the Hotel Promessi Sposi, overlooking the lakefront.

Name: Little Bear
Address: 36 Nguyen Ba Huan Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 70000, Vietnam
Description: This newcomer to HCMC’s bistro scene greets diners with a cosy dining room that offers both counter and table seating. The theatrical open kitchen is where the alchemy takes place. The menu consists of modern dishes inspired by the chef’s childhood memories and Vietnamese food culture, including cheese and noodles made from scratch in-house. The wine list features a wide range of wines by the glass, covering organic, biodynamic and natural tipples.

Name: Little Bull
Address: 810 N. Mangum St., Durham, NC, 27701, USA
Description: Blending his experience cooking across America with his Mexican heritage, Chef Oscar Diaz has created his own style of cooking. His time on the West Coast is evident and best seen in the vibrant and fresh small and larger plates designed for sharing. Judicious spicing and an array of textures add to the allure of these dishes, and house recommendations include the al pastor skewer and the tom kha ceviche. Really hungry? Tuck into the half chicken with pita for a satisfying meal. It's all better paired with one of their very cold beers or a house cocktail.

Name: Little Capo
Address: 18 Howe Street, Edinburgh, EH3 6TG, United Kingdom
Description: With its bold salmon-pink exterior, it’s hard to miss this endearing Italian restaurant and bar on a prime New Town corner site. Inside, there’s a relaxed, on-trend feel with a supreme sense of style to both the décor and your fellow diners – who help to create such a good buzz. The handwritten menu comprises small plates and larger dishes to share, along with homemade pastas; everything is fresh and flavoursome, from the mackerel crostini to the caponata. The polite and caring service team have a charming confidence and will happily chat away if you sit up at the counter.

Name: Little Dragon
Description: Behind the typical bamboo plants in the window of this always-busy restaurant just a few metres from the Plaza de España, you’ll find a contemporary interior that still manages to retain an Oriental feel thanks to the decor of dragons’ heads, red Chinese lanterns and even cuddly panda bears. The cuisine offers a strong insight into the cooking of Shanghai through different types of dumplings (xiaolongbao, shenjiangbao, wonton, etc), and homemade Chinese noodles (lamian). The young, informal ambience adds further appeal.

Name: Little Em’s Oyster Bar
Address: 1024 S. Alamo St., San Antonio, TX, 78210, USA
Description: Cute as a button, this breezy seafood hangout is dressed head to toe in cupcake-pink and white frosting. A spacious patio deck doubles the size of the dining room and is shaded by surrounding trees. The menu matches the décor, starting with a revolving selection of oysters and moving into light and bright preparations of seafood and salads. It is hard to imagine stopping by and not ordering fish tacos or, even better, a lobster roll served with herbed fries. A glass of rosé completes this summery daydream.

Name: Little Fish Market
Address: 10 Upper Market Street, Brighton and Hove, BN3 1AS, United Kingdom
Description: As the name implies, fish is the focus at this unassuming restaurant, which is fittingly located in a converted fishmonger’s opposite the old Victorian fish market. For many years, passionate chef-owner Duncan Ray has been quietly cooking, refining and pushing his restaurant forward – and he is ever-present in the dining room, ensuring his guests are having a good time. The 6 course set menu is packed with skilful seafood cookery which demonstrates great balance and understanding of the ingredients.

Name: Little Jarana
Description: Chef Abraham Artigas' small bistro, which has carved out a niche for itself within the city's culinary scene, presents a fairly informal and fun menu, based on Mediterranean cuisine but incorporating some international touches. Among its offerings, with many dishes designed for sharing, we were particularly impressed by its Scarlet shrimp, ham and lime, as well as the Gnocchi, cockles and bottarga (the latter, a huge hit, has never been taken off the menu). They don't serve soft drinks, beer or coffee, just wine (mainly from small producers), some vermouth and water!

Name: Little London
Description: This lively steakhouse not far from the Isartor is fronted by a classic bar of impressive dimensions – there are over 320 types of gin to choose from here! The attractive interior design successfully brings together a certain rusticity and a touch of English elegance. Meat eaters can look forward to high-quality cuts cooked on the Montague grill – tantalising examples include US Black Angus Prime Beef and Wagyu Kagoshima A5. There are over 250 wines on the wine list. Tip: Why not sign up for one of their beef-tasting sessions? With its various lounges, the restaurant also caters to private parties.

Name: Little Mama's
Description: Don't have an Italian grandmother? Then head to Little Mama's, where you can sit at the counter, slide into a booth or find a seat in the main room and watch as they make their own mozzarella. This is a kitchen that takes a few prime ingredients and turns them into something special, with homemade pasta and pizza, as well as entrees. Begin the meal with some of their house-made mozzarella or stracciatella and add a few of the suggested accompaniments to fill your own crostini before twirling your fork into a pasta or tucking into meat or fish. Brunch is also available on the weekend, and a second location in Rea Farms was opened in 2024.

Name: Little Miss India
Address: Fairmont The Palm, Palm Jumeirah, Dubai
Description: Dine in the brightly decorated bar, in the sumptuous dining room or out on the glorious terrace with its views over the water; the setting is romantic and the cheerful staff go out of their way to please. Carefully executed Indian cooking exhibits bold yet balanced spicing; the homemade chutneys are delicious.

Name: Little Mountain
Address: 516 San Ysidro Rd., Montecito, CA, 93108, USA
Description: Chilean-born Chef Diego Moya cut his teeth working in kitchens around the globe before opening Little Mountain in Montecito. The rustic yet elegant dining room draws inspiration from the region's Spanish Colonial history, with tall, white walls, brick floors and wood beams. The intimate ambience makes it a natural fit for date night; be sure to make reservations (though the bar accepts walk-ins). Meanwhile, the menu uses local ingredients to tell a globally inspired story. To begin, a tile fish ceviche with yuzu kosho and sweet peppers is a perfect choice. It's hard to go wrong with any of their main dishes, but their Mt. Lassen trout with wild mushrooms and beurre blanc is a strong choice. Cherimoya panna cotta is the perfect conclusion.

Name: Little Seeds
Address: 16-18 Radford Street, Stone, ST15 8DA, United Kingdom
Description: Little Seeds has a bright, fresh, natural look with green walls, foliage and rustic, upcycled furniture. A smattering of cookery books adds to the homely feel – and there’s a walled garden and drinks terrace out the back too. Great quality regional ingredients are used to create eye-catching British dishes with the occasional playful touch. The popular Sunday lunch menu features roast Staffordshire beef.

Name: Little Sparrow
Address: 1198 Howell Mill Rd., Atlanta, GA, 30318, USA
Description: We'll forgive you if you're looking through rose-colored glasses after a meal here. After all, Little Sparrow was singer Édith Piaf's nickname, and this très French bistro hits all the right notes from its design to its dishes. The menu, though compact, features all the favorites. Meals begin with a warm baguette and delicious butter before moving on to a fragrant and hearty onion soup and beef tartare. Entrées run the gamut from pork belly to chicken schnitzel with a mound of seasonal greens. Of course, there must be fries, and these house-made delights are thick cut and triple fried, accompanied by aïoli, Bearnaise sauce, or Raclette cheese service. End with a traditional chocolate soufflé or opt for a unique soft serve sundae.

Name: Little Water
Description: This airy, seafood-inspired restaurant from husband-and-wife team Chef Randy and Amanda Rucker immediately charms with its pressed tin ceiling, globe lights and well-worn wood flooring. The menu is tight, starting with a raw bar of oysters, shrimp cocktail and scallops. Seafood gumbo arrives with lobster, crab and Carolina gold rice, and Caesar salads are showered in nori and toasted benne. Heartier fare like fried oyster BLTs and applewood-smoked steelhead trout show care, quality and sophistication. A seat at the raw bar in the back offers an up-close view of chefs in action.

Name: Livello 1
Address: Via Duccio di Buoninsegna 25, Rome, 00142, Italy
Description: Situated in the suburbs off the main tourist trail, this fish restaurant also has a fishmonger’s next door. The fish and seafood cuisine served here is highly interesting, featuring modern recipes made from top-quality ingredients. There’s also a small lounge in which to enjoy a cocktail, plus a selection of good wines. The open-view kitchen allows guests to observe the skilful chef at work.

Name: Liz
Address: Rua de Mota Pinto 170, Porto, 4100-354, Portugal
Description: In this cosy bistro-style restaurant, away from the bustle of the city centre, chef Daniel Carvalheira pays homage to his daughter and presents a highly gastronomic proposal, demonstrating a high level of technical mastery. In an intimate space lit by candlelight, the chef offers a tasting menu that blends his Mozambican and Portuguese roots with French cuisine, revealing flavourful dishes and refined presentations. Through a proposal based on seasonal products, delicacies arise such as pink coastal prawns with curry, adorned with crunchy cubes of guanciale and roasted‑lemon paste, monkfish served over a dashi beurre blanc with a creamy broccoli purée and, at the end, a little journey to the Azores archipelago, with pineapple and São Jorge cheese—an elegant, gentle finale!

Name: Liza
Address: 14 rue de la Banque, Paris, 75002, France
Description: Originally from Beirut, Liza Asseily gives pride of place to the food of her homeland. In a bright interior strewn with Middle Eastern touches, you can expect mezze to share, grilled meats or fattet batinjan (aubergine, minced lamb and yoghurt). Numerous vegetarian dishes and a fine selection of Lebanese wines.

Name: Lizanna
Description: Their respective grandmothers, Liza and Anna, bequeathed a love of cooking to chef Levy and your hostess, Stéphanie. The couple shares this passion with guests in their elegant restaurant flanked by a lovely terrace. The chef rolls out his consummate know-how in a classical register. He might pair pheasant roasted whole with crispy, fluffy dauphine potato puffs, a creamy fricassée of thighs, cèpes and an exquisite cognac-laced sauce. The pinnacle of French fine dining with a personal twist.

Name: Llama Inn
Address: 1 Willow Street, Shoreditch, London, EC2A 4BH, United Kingdom
Description: Look for the bright yellow door, then take the lift to the seventh floor and you’ll find this colourful Peruvian restaurant, sister to the Manhattan original. The long, narrow room is bright and sunny, with an open kitchen and bar counter running along its length; there’s also a great terrace. A pisco sour, with some cheese yucas, will let your taste buds know that fresh, perky flavours are coming their way. If you’re new to Peruvian cuisine, then there’s a glossary on the back of the menu and the service team can offer helpful advice.

Name: Llama Inn - Madrid
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: A restaurant with a relaxed, informal feel which sees itself as a clone of the original Llama Inn in Brooklyn (New York), the name of which pays homage to this typical Andean animal and to this traditional type of hostelry that always extends a warm welcome to guests. The aim of the cuisine here is to bring Peruvian flavours to the Spanish capital in dishes that are mainly designed for sharing (scallop ceviche, yakimeshi of king prawns, yellow pepper curry and vegetable crudités, etc), alongside others they describe as the “fiesta final” (sautéed beef and duck jerky with rice). A tasting menu, entitled “Trust The Chef” and served to the whole table, is also available.

Name: Llantén
Description: If you’re celebrating a special occasion and are on the lookout for a restaurant with plenty of charm, look no further than this eatery located in the “Pinar de Antequera”, a residential development on the outskirts of Valladolid, which continues to surprise thanks to its landscaped surroundings and feel of a Menorcan farmhouse – the latter enhanced by the welcoming open fireplaces that provide the perfect ambience for a romantic candlelit supper. Here, the honest, traditional cuisine has been given an impressive modern makeover, including highly memorable dishes such as goat with alioli, beef tripe, 70-day-aged Sanabresa T-bone, as well as Albufera rice dishes that never fail to hit the mark.

Name: Llewelyn's
Address: 293-295 Railton Road, Herne Hill, London, SE24 0JP, United Kingdom
Description: Sitting just outside Herne Hill station, with its large windows letting diners look out and passers-by to look in, Llewellyn’s feels like a proper neighbourhood restaurant at the heart of the local community. The menu offers an appealing mix of dishes with a Mediterranean accent which focus on the freshness of the ingredients, and service is young and endearing.

Name: Llisa Negra
Description: A popular restaurant with an open-view kitchen and the hallmark of chef Quique Dacosta. The focus here is on high-quality produce with no artificial flavourings, top-quality cured ingredients, and superb rice cooked on orange wood and vine shoots. We can definitely recommend the creamy rice with smoked eel and free-range chicken, and delicious stews, with special mention to dishes cooked on the open grill. The à la carte is complemented by the Temporada (Season) tasting menu. The finishing touches to some dishes are added at your table.

Name: Lo Scalco Grasso
Description: A small, intimate restaurant with a welcoming ambience and simple yet lively feel, where the owner-chef at the helm in the kitchen also makes an appearance front of house. Mantuan traditions are evident in the generous portion sizes as well as in dishes such as the legendary pumpkin tortelli (served with butter or a tomato and sausage sauce), while other options are more creative in style – the Emilian lamb tartare delicately flavoured with its own cooking juices, and served with sautéed chard, savoury sbrisolona cake and black truffles from the lower Mantova region in season is particularly delicious.

Name: Lo Scopiccio
Description: Run by the owner-chef and her husband, Locanda Lo Scopiccio is a charming restaurant where careful attention is paid to every detail so that guests feel totally pampered. The cuisine is regional with the occasional hint of creativity, with a choice of two surprise menus or à la carte dining. There’s also a winter garden with a bright yet romantic feel.

Name: Lo Scudiero
Description: Young, enthusiastic chef Daniele Patti is at the helm at this restaurant housed in the delightful stables of a restored 16C palazzo. Here, he serves a selection of creative dishes, including two tasting menus – the intriguing Vieni in Sicilia con me (inspired by his native Sicily) and the Adriatico - and an à la carte which focuses on the local region’s abundance of fine ingredients. Wine-enthusiasts can ask to visit the impressive cellar, which also offers a good choice of wines by the glass.

Name: Lo Squalo
Description: With a long history, this restaurant has a contemporary vibe, where expert management offers exclusively seafood dishes, with well executed classic preparations, elevated by careful plating and lively pairings, often featuring fresh vegetables. Both the menu and the wine list are still handwritten, but the overall quality is thoroughly modern.

Name: Lo Stornello
Description: Offering quality and professionalism in a tourist setting, this small restaurant is popular with locals as well as visitors. The menu focuses on imaginatively presented Mediterranean cuisine.

Name: Loba Bang Niao
Address: 18/61 Mae Luan Road, Talat Nuea, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: This shop serving loba, a traditional snack of pork offal fritters, is testament to Hokkien influence on Phuket's cuisine. The menu also includes non-greasy bites such as bean sprout pancakes, fried spring rolls, fried tofu cubes and pork satay. Or try the comforting herbal pork rib soup.

Name: Loca
Description: This is the kind of cosy neighbourhood restaurant where locals gather to indulge in appealing tapas-style creations that showcase regional ingredients. Chef and owner Rob takes a straightforward approach when it comes to bringing bold flavours to your plate. The crispy brioche toast topped with smoked eel, sour cream and green apple is a wonderful starter. Or you might try the crispy veal sweetbreads served with a veal jus seasoned with cumin. Conviviality is the name of the game, and the menu of shareable dishes certainly reinforces that. Dinner at Loca is the perfect excuse to venture out of the city centre and explore Klarendal.

Name: Loca Café
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: In Granville, Stéphane Haissant cooks up unpretentious cuisine rooted in the maritime terroir. Quality ingredients are prepared with a true understanding of their flavours: flaked pollock lifted by fruity green peppercorns, leek coulis brightened with curry oil, buckwheat seeds for a crunchy touch; roasted line-caught whiting with toasted hazelnuts, polenta with Parmesan, scallop cream flavoured with pink ginger and tender endives. In the dining room with its "modern beach hut" vibe, you feel like you are on a seaside holiday.

Name: Loca Niru
Address: House of Tan Yeok Nee, #02-01, 101 Penang Road, 238466, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list
Description: In this restaurant in a restored heritage building, original vintage architectural features meet subtle wabi-sabi touches to great effect. The single tasting menu, which reflects the chef's Japanese background, demonstrates precision and meticulous layering of flavours. His balanced abalone chawanmushi is testament to a deft control of heat. Served tableside, the pan-fried isaki fish in Nyonya beurre blanc is prepared with aplomb.

Name: Local de Ensayo
Description: Located just a few steps from the cathedral, with a completely revamped concept that comes as a pleasant surprise in a setting occupying the former home of the equally successful Ajo y Agua restaurant. The contemporary and elegant interior features an initial dining room with a large table for groups, and then a second dining space from where the kitchen is partially visible to guests. Here, chef David López conjures up cuisine that is high on presentation and showcases a strong creative flair that he describes as “experimentation", with an extensive à la carte and no fewer than three tasting menus (Tradición, Endocardio and Desfibrilador).

Name: Locale Firenze
Description: Within a palazzo steeped in history, spanning from its medieval underground cellars to the Renaissance piano nobile housing the restaurant, guests enter through the ancient courtyard, now a refined lounge bar with a large counter dedicated to mixology and small tapas-style bites. From here you reach the splendid interior dining rooms, the ideal backdrop for an avowedly creative cuisine shaped by the chef’s international experiences across Australia, Japan, and France. The evocative medieval cellars also house “Labo-ttega,” an exclusive experience combining avant-garde cuisine and mixology, available by reservation for up to four guests. A vibrant destination brimming with energy and quality, interpreting contemporary gastronomy with distinct personality.

Name: Locals
Description: Housed in the same building as Hotel Haarhuis, just across from Arnhem Central train station, Locals boasts a cosmopolitan atmosphere. Ingredients are sourced as locally as possible, according to the principles of Dutch Cuisine. The abundance of plants and warm colours reflects that philosophy. Upstairs, there is even a vertical farm. The chef delights in working with vegetables, eg incorporating lentils from the Netherlands into a curry with herbs from the farm, seasonal vegetables and briny seaweed, and most of the fish and meat are locally sourced. . This place really lives up to its name!

Name: Locanda '800
Description: Whether you dine indoors, on the bright veranda or in the wine cellar with its barrels and wines produced by the estate, you’ll enjoy cuisine at this family-run restaurant which has gained a reputation in the region for its balance of meat and fish dishes. Excellent service and a pleasant setting in a rustic building surrounded by greenery.

Name: Locanda 4 Cuochi
Description: A simple, albeit pleasant and lively, restaurant just behind the famous Arena, well run by two good students of chef Perbellini. You can sit at classic tables or sit on stools at the small counter facing the kitchen. In any case, full speed ahead with a contemporary Italian line, with dishes such as "Mozzarella & Carrozza," spaghetti aglio olio peperoncino and raperonzoli with shrimp and lime... to finish – perhaps – with a good tiramisù.

Name: Locanda 53 Supper Club
Description: Situated on the second floor of a building in the historic centre of Arco, this restaurant is an intimate and romantic inn with the feel of a private home. Here, Evelyn and Carl have poured all their love for travel into the decor and the cuisine, the latter on two tasting menus (one focusing on meat, the other on fish) which are served to the few fortunate guests at the restaurant’s three tables. The creative recipes are influenced by the Trento region, as well as elsewhere in Italy and across the globe in dishes that awaken guests’ curiosity and delight their palate. The amusingly “Nigiri in crisi di identità” (Nigiri in an identity crisis) features a deconstructed version of this classic Japanese dish.

Name: Locanda Alpina
Description: Along the enchanting Val di Non, amid rows of apple orchards and the silhouettes of ancient castles, this building of nineteenth-century origin is home to a dependable family-run establishment, in operation for nearly a century, since 1933 to be precise. The cooking interprets the flavours of the territory with quiet competence, drawing out its seasonal excellences – such as white asparagus and venison preparations – while not shying away from occasional forays into broader national influences. Emblematic in this regard is the excellent pistachio ice cream, singled out by our Inspectors as not to be missed.

Name: Locanda Altobelli
Description: A pleasant little restaurant that differs from the many fish options in town with its traditional regional meat-based cuisine. There’s a real alchemy here between the young owner who is passionate about wine and the talented chef who boasts an impressive CV. Carefully chosen ingredients sourced directly from small local producers are the basis for its exciting, delicious dishes, while the wine list features some interesting organic wines. Small outdoor space for alfresco dining.

Name: Locanda Baggio
Address: Via Bassane 1, località Casonetto, Asolo, 31011, Italy
Description: A warm and welcoming dining room, together with professional yet pleasantly friendly and informal service, provide the perfect complement to the extraordinary cuisine: hearty, full of flavour, unsullied by unnecessary artifice. The pasta tubes with a rich sauce of baby cuttlefish, dried seaweed and sea urchins are unforgettable, as is the grilled fish with a sauce made from clams, leeks and seaweed oil.

Name: Locanda Belvedere
Address: Via San Giuseppe 736, frazione San Rocco, Saludecio, 47835, Italy
Description: Reached by climbing panoramic hill roads, one eventually finds the restaurant that is an excellent example of the quest for and celebration of local produce, beginning with their outstanding olive oil. One may choose between two tasting menus, the longer of which expands upon the shorter one with the addition of other dishes, dining in the tranquillity of a terrace that in summer opens on one side onto the greenery surrounding the restaurant.

Name: Locanda Grappolo d'Oro
Description: It really is a joy to dine at this restaurant, which has been run by the same family with great dedication for years. The decor is bright and cheerful, and warm hospitality and service come courtesy of the lady of the house. The Mediterranean-inspired cuisine is fresh and delicious. The pasta, the gnocchi, the bread… It's all house-made. No wonder this place draws so many regulars from the region.

Name: Locanda Gulfi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: In an isolated but well‑marked location that doesn’t escape the notice of oil and wine enthusiasts, Locanda Gulfi produces both, as you can tell from the view of the wine cellar visible from the dining room. The cuisine offers revisited Sicilian dishes, with the possibility of overnight accommodation and, naturally, tastings of the estate’s products, accompanied by dedicated menus or simple snacks specially designed for the occasion.

Name: Locanda La Posta
Description: A traditional setting reflecting the style of the early 20th century, with photos and documents telling the restaurant’s story, and numerous small dining rooms characterised by wooden ceilings. The restaurant’s traditional-style cuisine features excellent home-made pastas and a typical boiled meat trolley (“carrello dei bolliti”). One of the signature dishes here is rabbit stew served with a generous portion of Carmagnola peppers. In the summer, guests can sit in a welcoming outdoor area adorned with green plants and flowers.

Name: Locanda La Raia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The magnificent biodynamic La Raia farm, an enchanting 180-hectare oasis between Novi Ligure and Gavi, is home to a contemporary art foundation, the Rossi Cairo family winery, a Steiner school for employees’ children, guest accommodation, and this restaurant which benefits from a fertile ecosystem that provides much of its zero-mile produce. The cuisine is rooted in local traditions which have been reinterpreted in contemporary style. In the evening (and at lunchtime at weekends), choose between an à la carte, a tasting menu inspired by wines from the property’s estates between Gavi and Langhe, and a delicious “Sei mezze” menu featuring small samples of the restaurant’s most iconic dishes.

Name: Locanda Le Logge
Description: Occupying a period building in the heart of this beautiful village, with an outdoor dining space laid out under the portico in summer, this restaurant serves typical cuisine from the Marche on its various tasting menus and à la carte supplemented by daily specials. Boasting a rustic and pleasantly informal atmosphere, the restaurant also offers six romantic guestrooms with wrought-iron beds, including a four-poster bed in the Sogno room.

Name: Locanda Locarnese
Description: Hidden away in a little alley, this pleasant, modern-style restaurant offers Mediterranean and traditional cuisine made with excellent ingredients. Among its unmissable dishes are the honey and mustard pork belly, thyme-roasted eggplant with cherry tomato cream, and the chocolate fondant with passion fruit sauce. The large fireplace gives character to the setting, while the warm and friendly service makes guests feel as if they are visiting a private home.

Name: Locanda Marchesani
Description: In addition to specialities such as oysters and caviar, this restaurant serves sophisticated classic, traditional cuisine reinterpreted with a modern twist. Choose between à la carte options or tasting menus prepared with refined ingredients of the highest quality.

Name: Locanda Martinelli
Description: It’s well worth leaving the coast and climbing into the foothills to get to this small restaurant serving excellent cuisine. Housed in a rustic-style house with individual furnishings, in what could be the sitting room of a private house, the restaurant serves meat and fish specialities prepared with imagination from local produce and ingredients from further afield. As well as being a wine expert, the female owner gathers herbs, flowers and berries to flavour her recipes.

Name: Locanda Nelli
Address: Via Vittorio Veneto 15, Pietra Ligure, 17027, Italy
Description: A friendly and welcoming little restaurant in the heart of the town’s historic centre. It’s no surprise that the specialities here focus mainly on fish and seafood, with an emphasis on Mediterranean cuisine, homemade pasta and the use of extremely fresh ingredients – the menu changes daily depending on market availability. The charming outdoor space boasts tables set out along the small pedestrianised street.

Name: Locanda Perbellini
Description: Highly renowned in his native Verona, Michelin - starred chef Giancarlo Perbellini has now opened a restaurant in Milan, where he continues to offer traditional Italian cuisine from the north and south of the country, with a nod to new techniques and contemporary trends. Situated in the central Brera district, his warm and welcoming restaurant is small, discreet and, of course, highly elegant.

Name: Locanda Perbellini - Ai Beati
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: On the first hills behind Garda, the view from the terrace surrounded by greenery is an enchantment, embracing the southern part of the lake, while the interior rooms have been carved out of an old mill with stone walls, now comfortable, "light" and cosy spaces. Here chef Perbellini has set up a cuisine that starting from the territory, from freshwater fish in particular, opens up to proposals of sea and land with Mediterranean and contemporary taste, the steamed seafood salad topped with a wasabi mayonnaise is really delicate and fragrant. Do not miss one of the signature dishes of the famous chef, his legendary mille-feuille.

Name: Locanda Perbellini al Mare
Description: The flavors of Sicily – and not just seafood – are reimagined in a modern way, with personal touches (such as the tuna cutlet cooked and raw with soy mayonnaise and mashed potatoes), as well as vegetarian recipes inspired by the multi-starred chef Perbellini, executed with good technique and a dedication to taste. This all takes place in a modern beach establishment, complete with loungers and umbrellas. In the summertime, the windows open, and you practically all dine on the terrace, surrounded by the scent of the sea.

Name: Locanda Radici
Address: SP 21, contrada San Vincenzo, Melizzano, 82030, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: A rustic restaurant with contemporary Mediterranean-style decor surrounded by the greenery of the Sannio region, which can be admired through the large windows. Modern cuisine made from locally sourced ingredients by the owner-chef, who has vast experience working in top restaurants, both in Italy and abroad.

Name: Locanda San Martino
Address: Via Don Ermolao Barattin 23, Chies d'Alpago, 32010, Italy
Description: Founded in 1952, this inn has been run by the same family – and especially its female members – ever since. It now boasts the presence of a chef whose many years of experience are evident in his dishes. Much of the meat (especially lamb) is raised in the restaurant’s own farm nearby, while the dishes on the menu are seasonal and classic in style yet with a hint of modern flavour. When the weather allows, make the most of the large terrace boasting fine views of the sunset over the surrounding Alpago region.

Name: Locanda San Michele
Address: SS 491 3, Contrada Camerale di Tossiccia, Montorio al Vomano, 64046, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Practically on the slopes of Gran Sasso with views of the verdant landscapes of the Abruzzo, this restaurant is home to a local chef who has returned to his roots having spent time away gaining experience in Michelin-starred restaurants. Here, he serves regional cuisine with a modern, contemporary twist and a focus on meat and fish alike (examples include tuna tartare with strawberries finished in the dining room with lemon “snow”) in generous portions that are typical of the Abruzzo.

Name: Locanda Sant'Agata
Address: Via del Brennero, SS 12 km 5,812, San Giuliano Terme, 55016, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Not far from the village, this pleasant boutique hotel is home to a friendly, well-kept restaurant surrounded by a relaxing garden where guests can enjoy alfresco dining in summer. The menu features traditional meat and fish dishes with the occasional modern, personalised twist, such as “calamarotto” – squid (calamaro) stuffed with seafood pancotto, vegetables in dry vermouth and confit plum tomatoes.

Name: Locanda Sensi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A country retreat that captivates with simplicity and passion: modern, comfortable rooms open onto a landscape that embraces the hills of Piacenza, while outdoor dining offers glimpses of light and nature. The menu invites guests to enjoy a tasting menu in which the grill releases intense aromas, or à la carte dishes that range from land to sea to garden, in a balance of scents and colours. Two cosy suites, a holistic wellness centre scented with natural essences and, in fine weather, a Zen garden that invites you to relax, complete the experience.

Name: Locanda Solagna
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Although this restaurant has been in business since the 1950s, it feels much more modern thanks to its updated appearance. Renowned for its excellent regional cuisine served in the evening, the restaurant pays careful attention to seasonal ingredients. At lunchtime, the ”osteria”-style menu is much simpler. Excellent wine selection.

Name: Locanda Stella d'Oro
Description: The original flavour and magic of a trattoria can still be found in this establishment. The cuisine is traditional with a personal touch.

Name: Locanda Toscano
Description: The central location, overlooking the rocky shore just steps away, makes this venue an ideal stop for those seeking straightforward, no-frills Mediterranean cuisine. The menu favors the sea, with an excellent raw trio and a series of well-executed pastas, among which the ricotta and red prawn tortello stands out, elevated by a touch of black garlic. The welcome is warm and attention to guests evident in every detail. In short, an excellent gourmet stop.

Name: Locanda Viola
Description: A refined restaurant where the design plays with tables and seating of varied, original craftsmanship, yet it is the cuisine that captures attention, thanks to the talent of Filippo Moriggi. The starters are the calling card: an exotic-tinged journey that surprises with the fish bao, a soft steamed bun also available with BBQ sauce, or with the empanadas chilena, filled with white Sorrento scamorza, shrimp, and coriander-cumin mayonnaise. The journey continues toward more familiar flavors: well-executed pastas and risottos, fish dishes, and Bergamo lamb, leading to desserts that play on the freshness of gelato, served simply or affogato-style, for a light, flavorful finish.

Name: Locanda dei Salinari
Description: In the old village of Salinari, a young enterprising chef runs this simple restaurant. His creative cuisine is prepared with the best regional produce of Romagna.

Name: Locanda del Falco
Address: Castello di Rivalta 4, Rivalta Trebbia, 29010, Italy
Description: In the heart of a medieval village, an inn of authentic charm welcomes guests with the captivating aromas of Piacenza cuisine and imaginative creations that surprise the palate, accompanied by local wines and distinguished labels from beyond the region. Heritage dishes speak of time-honored flavors, revisited with modern touches, while the inspector’s favorite remains the grilled cardoncelli mushrooms: intense aroma and pure taste. In the dining room, Sabrina radiates energy and smiles, presenting each dish with infectious passion. On winter evenings, crackling fireplaces warm the atmosphere; in summer, a centuries-old wisteria drapes the courtyard tables in fragrant, romantic shade.

Name: Locanda del Feudo
Address: Via Trasversale 2, Castelvetro di Modena, 41014, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In the upper and most ancient part of the picturesque village, this romantic retreat – which also offers six elegant suites – offers genuine and deeply satisfying cooking. The menu is split between dishes from the land, with numerous recipes that evoke the Emilian tradition, such as hand-rolled tagliatelle with ragù, tortelli in capon broth, or a selection of the finest local cured meats, and seafood offerings distinguished by a modern and lighter touch. In the warmer months, guests may take their place on the small and charming terrace overlooking the main street, ideally suited to savouring the village in its most relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Locanda del Marinaio
Description: Delicious cuisine full of the flavours of the Mediterranean (prepared by the German owner - chef! ) in a delightful little restaurant in the bustling centre of Cefalù. Simple surroundings but excellent food!

Name: Locanda del Molino
Description: This rustic yet charming restaurant occupies an old family mill. It has attractive guestrooms that reflect the elegant simplicity of the Tuscan countryside. In the kitchen, the female chef creates traditional specialities such as fried rabbit and nettle with ricotta cheese gnudi (ravioli filling without the pasta) in a fresh tomato sauce.

Name: Locanda del Villoresi
Description: What was once a post station is now a renowned restaurant overlooking the Villoresi canal. Although the attractive dining room has retained some of its historical features, the decor here is more contemporary in feel. The Mediterranean-style cuisine focuses mainly on fish and is beautifully presented, with dishes such as fried artichokes with red prawns and bottarga on the menu in season. Raw fish dishes are also occasionally available.

Name: Locanda dell'Angelo
Description: This stylish, elegant restaurant occupying a historic 17C building in an attractive medieval village serves contemporary cuisine which is influenced by recipes and ingredients from Liguria and Piedmont alike. Dishes include Ligurian-style rabbit terrine with a pine nut and gravy sauce, and Piedmontese white suckling pig tomahawk on sauerkraut with a spicy, sour apple sauce.

Name: Locanda dell'Arcimboldo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At the town gates, a friendly inn with a family atmosphere in a fine building, with a pleasant veranda. Fish dishes prevail on the menu, featuring an interesting selection of oysters. At midday there is also an easier set menu.

Name: Locanda della Luna
Address: Via delle Oche 7, San Giorgio del Sannio, 82018, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: In a remote location in the Sannio, this authentic inn offers fine views from its well-kept dining room-cum-veranda and outdoor terrace. The owner-chef creates dishes with a regional flavour using produce from his own garden, without straying too far from local traditions.

Name: Locanda delle Tre Chiavi
Description: This restaurant housed in an 18C building is run by its talented and enthusiastic owners Sergio (front of house) and Annarita (in the kitchen), who do their utmost to provide guests with the best seasonal, regional ingredients prepared in classic dishes full of flavour. The wine list focuses on good-quality labels from the region.

Name: Locanda di Nonna Ida
Address: Località Pontarola 12, Marano di Valpolicella, 37020, Italy
Description: A welcoming inn nestled amid the last vineyards of Valpolicella and the first pasturelands of the lower Lessinia region, where a young chef serves cuisine with a focus on local ingredients and classic Italian recipes with a modern twist. In summer, the terrace offers a fresh, cool setting with extensive views. The barbecued meat is superb.

Name: Locavore (Taguig)
Address: Forbes Town Center, Burgos Circle, Bonifacio Global City, Taguig - Metro Manila, 1634, The Philippines
Description: At this bustling spot, local flavours meet French techniques, as Filipino home-style cooking and street food are given a modern twist by Paris-trained chefs. Long-time favourites include sizzling sinigang and oyster sisig, and desserts such as pandesal pudding and refined banana turon. With a DJ booth and upbeat atmosphere, this casual restaurant divided into several areas blends Manila energy with culinary creativity rooted in proudly local traditions.

Name: Lockstein 1
Description: This really is a special place: you enter the charming kitchen through the 500-year-old farmhouse, which is run by an established mother-and-daughter team. They inject love and skill into their cooking, which takes the form of a vegetarian set menu comprising fresh dishes made using regional produce. The two pretty holiday flats are also popular.

Name: Loco by Jem's
Description: A hit with the locals, this buzzy, youthful bolthole is home to Jérémy, nicknamed Jem’s by his mates who think he’s a bit wacky (loco in Spanish). Jem finds inspiration in local ingredients which he crafts into dishes rich in crisp, contrasting flavours. The counter commands a fascinating view of the kitchen team at work. Bargain-priced lunchtime menu and tasting menu in the evening with wine-food pairings; vegetarian menu on request.

Name: Locàle by Kok au Vin
Description: Locally sourced ingredients and a deep respect for nature and the seasons are the cornerstones of this cosy establishment. Influences from around the globe and the occasional use of a Mibrasa charcoal oven take things up a notch. Examples include a salad of endives, apples and walnuts, enhanced with Damse Mokke cheese and a subtle dressing, or ibex, cooked to order, flanked by a beurre blanc, fermented carrots, tarragon sauce and potato straws… Nothing overly fussy, just playful, succulent fare in the zeitgeist. The set menus are designed to be shared, but if that isn’t your cup of tea, choose something from the à la carte lineup.

Name: Loewengrube
Description: This building has been home to a restaurant since the 16C, making it one of the oldest in Bolzano. Today, it houses an elegant restaurant that serves a combination of traditional Alpine cuisine and classic Italian dishes with a contemporary twist, such as carbonara tortelloni filled with parmesan cream and crispy bacon. The attractive wine cellar boasts a selection of approximately 1 000 wines from the region and elsewhere in Italy, as well as a choice of labels from further afield.

Name: Lofficina
Description: This building with a minimalist, contemporary design is situated on the edge of the historic centre at the Sant'Erasmo belvedere, from where, in summer, panoramic views extend over Monte Conero and the sea (booking ahead is recommended). In the kitchen, owner-chef Davide Breccia conjures up creative dishes featuring original combinations and mainly inspired by the sea. There are two tasting menus, Iconico and Idee, for guests who like to be guided, plus an à la carte for those who prefer to choose their own courses.

Name: Loft Elia
Address: Gölköy Mahallesi, 325. Sokak No:7, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The olive trees around you and the views over the bay accentuate Loft Elia's Zen feel. Although this lounge-style restaurant is fully open to the elements, it nonetheless has an intimate atmosphere. The natural vibe suits the menu down to the ground. A commitment to local produce and sustainable practices are part of their ethos underpinned by respect for the planet. The kitchen team's inspired, fine dining-quality dishes are deliciously spicy. For example, their airy feta sponge cake is freeze-dried with three varieties of tomato to give it delicate sweetness and tang. This cuisine is truly inspiring!

Name: Loibnerhof
Description: This beautiful inn in a 400-year-old wine-growing estate has been run by the Knoll family for over a century. Sepp and Josef – father and son – serve classic Austrian cuisine here, including dishes such as foam soup made with crayfish from the Danube or excellent veal and beef from the region – the creamy veal goulash and Tafelspitz (beef boiled in broth) are a must. And leave some room for the delicious apricot Buchteln (sweet yeast buns) or Topfenknödel (quark dumplings)! To wash it all down, there are wines from Weingut Emmerich Knoll, which is just a stone's throw away. The restaurant interior is done out in a charming country style and, in summer, tables in the outdoor dining area across the street are highly prized – the setting beneath the boughs of the apple trees is lovely.

Name: Lois Stern
Description: Maria and Lois Stern have been welcoming diners to their restaurant in a traffic-reduced zone in the centre of Kitzbühel since 1994 and have built up a loyal following. An inviting atmosphere reigns in the modern interior. The focal point is the open kitchen, where the chef-patron cooks up Asian-European fusion dishes. The quality of the ingredients is excellent. In addition to the regular menu, there are daily specials. The friendly proprietress and her well-trained team provide attentive service.

Name: Loiseau d'à Côté
Description: Opposite Saint-Sauveur Church, this unusual-looking building resembling a small castle houses the restaurant of chef Alexandre Loiseau and Sandra Côté. The traditional cuisine served here is made using impeccable local produce: knuckle of suckling pig from the Gaspor family farm, boudin noir and maple-glazed sweetbreads, or flat iron steak cooked with mushrooms and red wine. Lunchtime revolves around a set menu formule (with optional extras); the evening à la carte menu offers more choice. Delicious desserts and a warm welcome seal the deal – a lovely place.

Name: Loiseau des Vignes
Description: A Bernard Loiseau stamped score and a chic bistro vibe (stone, wood and velvet-upholstered banquettes) paint this culinary portrait. The menu includes classics such as eggs in a red wine sauce, pâté en croûte, Charolais ox cheek and Saône catfish, without forgetting beautifully fresh Burgundy veal tartare with smoked eel. The wine list also unveils a wide range by the glass.

Name: Loiseau du Temps
Description: In a former 18C grain store, this imposing vaulted dining room, dotted in contemporary details, is the Besançon HQ of the Bernard Loiseau Group. The menu highlights produce and recipes from Bourgogne-Franche-Comté: mushroom pie, blanquette-style chicken in vin jaune, cabbage stuffed in Morteau sausage… Each dish is painstakingly plated and packed in flavour. A wickedly irresistible dessert trolley winds up this gourmet feast.

Name: Lok-Un
Address: 85 Si Mueang Road, Takua Pa, Phang-Nga, 82110, Thailand
Description: The signature pork leg, which is stewed for 6 hours, has a spicy, charcoal flavour – the tasty recipe comes from the chef-owner’s Chinese great grandfather. Photos of visiting royals confirm its prestige; one of the most popular places among the Sino-Portuguese buildings of the old town.

Name: Lokaal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Nowadays, Villa Ruimzicht is both a hotel and home to this elegant, chic yet warm and welcoming restaurant. The name Lokaal can be translated as "classroom" and is a nod to the building's past as a school. But it is also much more than that: it reflects Bjorn Massop and his team's commitment to sustainability. They source everything from vegetables to meat and fish from local small-scale suppliers who share their values. This dining experience is a real education – you will learn that coffee grounds are used to lend earthy notes to a medlar and sherry dessert. Embracing a zero-waste philosophy fuels the chef's innovation. For example, by fermenting spruce in a vegetable broth, he creates a harmonious accompaniment to trout from De Smallert fish farm. The set menu is a celebration of the riches of the Achterhoek terroir.

Name: Lokal at the Lake
Description: It’s all in the name. Set in a small village on the southern banks of Lake Balaton, just a stone’s throw from the water, this intimate bistro follows a purely local ethos. From the fixtures and fittings to the furnishings and the food, everything you see has been produced in the region. The rustic small plates have a fittingly traditional Hungarian heart and come with bold flavours – you might find green pea soup with goat’s cheese and mint, followed by rabbit with vegetable sauce and bread pudding. Choose four per person or opt for the excellent value Chef’s Menu of current kitchen favourites.

Name: Lokanta 1741
Address: Alemdar Mahallesi, Profesör Kazım İsmail Gürkan Caddesi No:34, Cağaloğlu Hamamı, Fatih, Istanbul, 34110, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: This beautiful contemporary restaurant with a romantic roof terrace is right next to Cağaloğlu Hamam. It serves Turkish culinary classics, some dating back to 1741, with a modern twist. The chef sometimes introduces surprising textures and flavours but never loses sight of tradition. In the evening, they serve only a more sophisticated fine dining menu. Here, you can savour a zesty sea bass ceviche, as well as lamb brochettes with distinct barbecue notes and a punchy aubergine caviar. Oenophiles should definitely take the opportunity to explore the wine cellar.

Name: Lokanta Feriye
Address: Yıldız Mahallesi Çırağan Caddesi No:44, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34347, Türkiye
Description: Dining in the gardens of the fully refurbished Feriye Palace is a new experience each time. Here on the edge of the Bosphorus – some diners even arrive by boat – you have the ever-evolving backdrop of the constant coming and going of the ships. And there is something magical about the view of the illuminated Ortaköy Mosque and Bosphorus Bridge, especially when you have a delicious cocktail in hand. This restaurant strikes a fine balance between chic and relaxed, and the service is attentive. The chefs, who can be seen at work in the open kitchen, let the ingredients speak for themselves. Their dishes are not overly elaborate, but rather classic fare with subtle zesty and spicy nuances. They give aubergine purée a delightful tang by mixing in yoghurt, making it an excellent accompaniment to barbecued lamb.

Name: Lokanta Limu
Address: Yeniköy, Köybaşı Caddesi No:158 D:B, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34464, Türkiye
Description: With its bright interior and appealing artworks, Lokanta Limu stands out even in this bustling neighbourhood. The decor radiates a sense of serenity, and the closely spaced tables create a convivial atmosphere. Sara Tabrizi and her team of chefs delight in creating generous mezze spreads that bring a fresh perspective to authentic Turkish flavours. Think tuna marinated in raki and served with parsley, apple and red onion, or briefly seared lamb's liver with fried potatoes and onion. The extensive menu features plenty of enticing options that lend themselves well to sharing. To explore a wide range of dishes without breaking the bank, choose the Çilingir Sofrası set menu.

Name: Lokanta by Divan
Address: Asker Ocağı Caddesi No:1, Şişli, Istanbul, 34367, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Valet parking
Description: Since opening in 1956, the luxurious Divan Hotel near Taksim Square has established itself as a cherished institution, and Lokanta embodies the same timeless elegance and grandeur. The first room is dominated by a piano, which is regularly used for performances. The cocktail bar is the focal point of the second room, and the last room is ideal for family gatherings. Against this magnificent backdrop, the entirely à la carte menu presents contemporary interpretations of Turkish cuisine that celebrate regional ingredients. Manyas, for example, is a traditional cheese from Balıkesir that lends a gentle note to grilled prawn, red wine "caviar" and a delicate vegetable sauce enriched with butter and saffron. Lokanta offers a fine dining experience featuring bold, no-nonsense flavours.

Name: Lola
Address: place du Grand Sablon 33, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
Description: Lola has been a firm fixture of the well-heeled Sablon district since 1994. A neutral colour scheme adorns the modern interior, while the terrace, decked in vibrant reds, awaits you in fine weather. The extensive à la carte menu stars a cast of pedigree classics: beef carpaccio à la Harry’s Bar, fork-tender calf’s sweetbread vol-au-vent, linguine in salted butter or a subtle creation of scallops and caramelized endive with a Riesling-flavoured fluffy mousseline. Something of a darling with the foodies of Brussels – and rightly so!

Name: Lola Helen
Address: 425 J. P. Rizal Street, Marikina - Metro Manila, The Philippines
Description: Noodle lovers! Don't miss this humble spot opened 20 years ago and known for Filipino-Chinese stir-fried noodles. Diners can choose from rice vermicelli, egg noodles, or a mix of both. With its moist, springy noodles and crispy pork, the aromatic bihon canton con litson deeply satisfies. Generous portions, fair prices, and a well-ventilated upstairs area – make it a constant favourite among locals.

Name: Long Chim
Address: Al Bujairi Terrace, Diriyah, Riyadh, 13711, Saudi Arabia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,No alcohol served,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: If you’re walking in the bustling Bujairi Terrace and fancy a trip to Thailand, you should head to this spot that literally means “come and try.” Take a seat on the terrace, or if it’s open, the upstairs area to enjoy a selection of famed David Thompson recipes that may include chicken satay leu, green papaya salad, khao soi Chiang Mai and homemade ice creams. Their set Maa Long Chim menu is vibrant and authentic – and well worth a try. The service is also a plus, thanks to the endearingly friendly team.

Name: Long Dtai
Address: Cape Fahn Hotel, 24/269 Mu 5, Bo Phut, Ko Samui, 84320, Thailand
Description: After crossing shallow waters, you reach this private island resort off Samui’s east coast. From the restaurant’s terrace, diners enjoy panoramic views of the bay as they sample chef David Thompson’s fab creations. His Southern Thai menu is deceptively simple and his consummate culinary talent is revealed in the details. Start with grilled squid, marinated in turmeric and coconut milk to accentuate its freshness. Marine sustainability is the name of the game here.

Name: Long Kee Wanton Noodle
Address: Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre, #01-185, Blk 505, Jurong West Street 52, 640505, Singapore
Description: The signature wonton noodles feature flavoursome bite-size dumplings, served either in soup or tossed in sauces. The noodles are cooked to perfect consistency with a lovely chew. Sliced char siew adds depth.

Name: Long March Canteen
Description: A cool spot with a buzzy atmosphere, where diners can choose to sit at small tables or at long tables for a convivial group experience. The open kitchen sends out Cantonese dishes such as various dim sum and dumplings. N.B. When they say it's "spicy" here, they mean it!
