You can dine à la carte or choose from several set menus designed for sharing. The food is accompanied by an extensive selection of wines, spirits, cocktails and long drinks.

Name: Long Yan (Jiaojiang)
Address: 2-3F, 226 Jingzhong Road, Jiaojiang, Taizhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Foreign credit cards not accepted,Valet parking
Description: This upscale restaurant has been serving the freshest local seafood since 2004. As in other similar establishments, the norm is to take your pick from the live fish tanks, or the display cases for cold appetisers and dim sum. In the signature dish, the razor clams' natural sweetness and bouncy texture is highlighted by scallion oil. The sizzling claypot rice with chives and marine spoon worm is another must-try. Reservation recommended.

Name: Longueville Manor
Address: Longueville Road, Saint Saviour, JE2 7WF, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Situated within the grand hotel of the same name – whose acres of grounds include tennis courts and a swimming pool – this characterful 15th-century restaurant is a fitting match for its surroundings. Sit in either the oak-panelled dining room, the brighter Garden Room or on the terrace in summer, and make sure you ask to see the impressive wine cellar too. Look out for the 'Market Menu' which offers great value for money and champions island produce, including local seafood and vegetables from the kitchen garden. Ensure you save room for something from the cheese trolley.

Name: Longyin Shanfang (Jiangning)
Address: Villa No. 9, Qinglong Mountain Villa, 888 Shenfeng Road, Jiangning, Nanjing, Chinese Mainland
Description: This nature-inspired restaurant in an idyllic setting truly blurs the boundary between nature and culture. Jaw-dropping views can be enjoyed from the main room as well as all private rooms. Depending on the season, there are several set menus, which may include specialities such as peony-shaped tofu in consommé that highlights the ingredients' natural flavours. Cultural elements from tea-making to incense rituals make for a fun-filled experience.

Name: Lonxa d´Alvaro
Description: A family-run restaurant with a contemporary feel and independent extractor fans on each table, located a stone’s throw from the boats anchored in the harbor. What's on offer? Magnificent fish and seafood (usually large pieces), tasty grilled meats (Galician and Wagyu), as well as delicious seafood rice dishes. Everything is local and aligned with a traditional cuisine that always makes room for contemporary details. Don't miss the octopus with sea urchin cream and potatoes!

Name: Loong Kee Yong Tau Fu
Address: Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre, #01-31, Blk 505, Jurong West Street 52, 640505, Singapore
Description: Serve yourself with the stuffed tofu or vegetables. You may also add soup, chee cheong fun, laksa, mee or rice.

Name: Loong Loy Pa Lan
Address: 1010 Phet Kasem Road, Huai Chorakhe, Mueang Nakhon Pathom, Nakhon Pathom, 73000, Thailand
Description: A passion for wild ingredients like wild boar, frogs, seafood, and even greens, along with a zeal for local flavours—intense, tangy, and spicy—shapes everything on the menu here. The stir-fried wild boar with chilies and the tom yam soup with snakehead fish are both recommended, as is the seafood cooked according to local recipes. The atmosphere is relaxed and homely, with air-conditioned dining rooms and outdoor seating available.

Name: Lor 9 Beef Kway Teow
Description: Cantonese and Fujian dishes prepared with local ingredients are tweaked to cater to local tastes. The beef kway teow is the main event. Comfort-food classics such as coffee pork ribs and sambal sweet potato leaves are also excellent.

Name: Lor Mee 178
Address: Tiong Bahru Market, #02-23, 30 Seng Poh Road, 168898, Singapore
Description: The rich, robust stock that clings to the egg noodles is the secret behind their tasty lor mee. Deep-fried fish nuggets, pork, and bean sprouts also make every bite satisfying. Grated garlic and cilantro add a zesty boost.

Name: Lord Nelson
Description: Set right on the seafront, with a delightful outdoor seating area, this historic restaurant – opened in 1969 and dedicated to the famous English admiral – boasts classic elegance with mahogany furnishings and light-coloured curtains reminiscent of unfurled sails. Mediterranean-inspired cuisine plays with modern and creative touches, such as slow-cooked amberjack served with baby spinach, pine nuts, marjoram and date tomato sauce.

Name: Lord Stow's Bakery (Rua do Tassara)
Address: 1 Rua do Tassara, Coloane Town Square, Coloane, Macau
Description: For over 30 years, the store has prided itself on its Portuguese egg tarts that have a crisp shell and silky, smooth filling. Tarts are made from scratch, baked throughout the day and sold fresh from the oven. Takeout only.

Name: Lord's
Address: 506 LaGuardia Pl., New York, NY, 10012, USA
Description: It feels straight out of London at this meat-centric restaurant with a nose to tail ethos from Chef Ed Szymanski and Patricia Howard, the partners behind smash hit, Dame. It's ever so charming, with cozy nooks and banquettes, and even when it's packed, the bar maintains space for walk-ins. Come on a cold day for hearty English classics with a touch of creativity (think curried lamb scotch egg). Like most of the dishes, duck-stuffed cabbage with mashed potatoes could feed an army, so order shared plates-style to sample without becoming stuffed. The apple and calvados trifle closes things out with just the right note of sweetness.

Name: Lore
Address: 3F, West Super Block Retail, One Bonifacio High Street Mall, 3rd Avenue, Bonifacio Global City, Taguig - Metro Manila, 1214, The Philippines
Description: On the third floor of One Bonifacio High Street Mall, this is chef Myke "Tatung" Sarthou's homage to Filipino cuisine – traditional, yet thoughtfully reimagined. Known for his Simpol channel and cookbooks, Tatung blends heritage and creativity in dishes that tell a story, highlighting the depth and diversity of the country's food culture. His journey is echoed in each plate and his work continues to shape the way Filipinos enjoy their culinary traditions.

Name: Lorea
Description: Named after the Basque word for flower, this Roma Norte restaurant is Chef Oswaldo Oliva’s way of evoking memories of his life back in Spain. The multilevel space has handsome wood tables and smooth finishes all over, but perhaps the best seat in the house is right at the chef’s counter, where guests can watch all of the action. This quiet, perpetually clean kitchen prepares only a single, seasonal tasting menu that is loosely based on Mexican cooking but more widely takes culinary inspiration from all over (take the fried chili filled with an eggplant and blue cheese puree or the chinchayote with smoked stingray dressing and ikura). Main dishes range from a huitlacoche taco with requeson, lardo, and an aromatic pipicha oil to their baby corn in a creamy sauce with romeritos and caviar.

Name: Lorenz in der alten Mühle
Description: This modern restaurant stands on the foundations of a mill that were laid in 1569 – the preserved millstone can be admired at the entrance. Wood finishes, clean lines and an open kitchen are prominent features of the interior, which has a pleasant, vibrant atmosphere. In the evening, there is a regional à la carte selection as well as a set menu with dishes cooked over hot charcoal on the robatayaki. There is also a Japanese omakase menu comprising three to six courses. The lunchtime offering revolves around the "beer garden menu", which also includes some of the evening dishes. They also have a lovely terrace.

Name: Lorenzo Ruta
Address: C.da Zimmardo SP45 km5, RG, Modica, 97015, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Situated in a new, low-rise resort in a secluded location, this attractive, contemporary-style restaurant is run by a local chef with plenty of experience behind him, together with the women of his family, namely his wife and sommelier sister-in-law. The extensive selection here includes various tasting menus plus an à la carte, all of which showcase meat and fish dishes featuring imaginative combinations. The impressive wine list includes labels from outside Sicily and Italy, with a strong focus on French wines and champagnes in particular.

Name: Loris
Address: 125 Porto Arabia Drive, The Pearl, Doha, Qatar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,No alcohol served,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: It’s a pure Lebanese experience at this eatery located on The Pearl. Everything from the plush décor to the food alludes to the country located to the east of the Mediterranean. The flavours are all authentic, almost as if grandma was cooking up the dish. Of course, the dishes are made for sharing, with silky hummus and tasty kebab with cherry being the most popular choices. Aish el Saraya is a notable dessert that you mustn’t skip. After dinner, take a stroll on the walkway nearby to take in the city vistas.

Name: Lorne
Address: 76 Wilton Road, Victoria, London, SW1V 1DE, United Kingdom
Description: They keep things honest at this narrow little restaurant and you can see the pay-off: a dining room full of happy customers, who are a mix of locals, tourists and business types. Staff are on the ball and well-versed on the menu, while the classically trained kitchen sends forth reliable and consistently good dishes, like Cornish cod with smoked eel, and chocolate delice with cookie crumble. The lunch and early evening menus are very good value.

Name: Los 33
Address: Plaza de las Salesas 9, Madrid, 28004, Spain
Description: Trends come and go and as such there are some restaurants, such as this one in the Salesas district of the city, that everyone is talking about and where you’ll find it difficult to book a table. The couple in charge, Nacho and Sara, have created a space that is particularly welcoming, with two highly distinct sections: a bar with tables for tapas, or enjoying a glass of wine or cocktail (no bookings are taken for these); and the dining room itself (you’ll need to book online) with its sturdy oak pillars, and an open grill visible behind the long bar counter. The enticing à la carte features contemporary dishes alongside more traditional recipes from Uruguay, all of which are prepared with top-quality meats. Make sure you try the bikini sandwich of grilled prosciutto.

Name: Los Agaves
Address: 600 N. Milpas St., Santa Barbara, CA, 93101, USA
Description: Note: Temporarily closedServing generous portions of hearty south-of-the-border favorites by way of California, along with a relaxed, family-friendly vibe, this place deserves every bit of praise lavished upon it. The staff may bring chips immediately to your table, but salsa and drinks are both self-service. Remember to order at the counter and collect a number before taking a seat. Start with the likes of lime-marinated halibut ceviche tostada with cilantro and avocado. Then pick from a variety of sizeable burritos or go for the satisfyingly cheesy and crispy costra taco al pastor, with pineapple, marinated pork, and chipotle—enlivened with pickled onions.There may be four locations, but this one is the original. The room can get crowded, so takeaway is a popular option.

Name: Los Bocheros
Address: Roque Sáenz Peña 8450, Mendoza, M5549, Argentina
Description: Part of the Lamadrid Estate Wines bodega, in the district of Las Compuertas, this restaurant is known for its honest and generous cuisine, and a continual desire to revive the culinary traditions of Mendoza, hence its name, which refers to players of the game “bocce”. The delightful surroundings here take centre stage with picture windows looking out on to the covered terrace and meticulous landscaped garden. On the menu you’ll find charcoal-grilled dishes, select cuts of meat, typical specialities such as the signature Empanada Los Bocheros filled with meat and a mix of fresh herbs, and delicious ribs that that are cooked at low temperature. Combining his work here with other culinary projects elsewhere, renowned chef Lucas Olcese also showcases his cooking on a single 4- or 7-course tasting menu, with a wine pairing option included that only features wines from the estate.

Name: Los Burritos Juárez
FacilitiesAndServices: Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Los Burritos Juarez is a compact Fort Greene shop serving burritos in the border style of El Paso and Ciudad Juárez. The foundation is its house-made flour tortillas, cooked to order with lard, yielding wraps that are soft, warm and pleasantly chewy. They encase generous guisados, or slow-cooked stews, such as pork simmered in red chiles or brisket braised in a mellow salsa verde, finished with a swipe of pinto beans that brings the components together. The menu is concise and the flavors are deeply comforting, offering a regional burrito tradition rarely found in New York. Breakfast burritos are available from opening until they sell out.

Name: Los Caños
Address: Plaza de San Martín 5, Haro, 26200, Spain
Description: If you find yourself on a tapas and ‘pinchos’ crawl in the La Herradura section of historic Haro, we can highly recommend a refuelling stop at Los Caños, occupying a delightful 16th-century palatial-style property. In this attractive restaurant, which has tastefully combined historic details with a more contemporary aesthetic, the emphasis is on deep-rooted traditional cuisine that has been able to take classic tapas to a higher gastronomic level, as showcased in options such as Rioja-style cod and, off the menu, interesting proposals such as grilled artichokes or peas in omelette. They have a small plot of land where they grow some of their products!

Name: Los Danzantes Mexico City
Address: Parque Centenario 12, Jardín Centenario, Coyoacán, 04000, Mexico
Description: Located in downtown Coyoacan, Los Danzantes is often busy with a mix of locals and foreigners. Set in a historic building, this restaurant shines a spotlight on contemporary Mexican cuisine, and the menu is packed with a wide variety of dishes. Chef Alejandro Piñom knows what works--the hoja santa with a base of goat cheese and a miltomate sauce with chile, has been on the menu for more than two decades. Filete de res en chichilo has a hint of smoke from the grill but it's the mole that stands out. Empanada de membrillo pairs quince and cheese for a pleasant taste. Their sister spot in Oaxaca shares the same name but offers a different style and menu.

Name: Los Fuegos by Francis Mallmann
Address: Faena Hotel Miami Beach, 3201 Collins Ave., Miami Beach, FL, 33140, USA
Description: “Theatrical” barely begins to describe the scale and style of Francis Mallman’s restaurant set inside the FAENA Hotel. Much like the hotel itself, the director of Moulin Rouge is responsible for such décor elements as leopard-print booths, striking red-cushioned seats and flashes of gold that appear on everything from the bar to the carpet.Known for open-fire cooking, Chef Mallman is not outmatched by the room’s design, delivering an asado experience that rivals the city’s best steakhouses. Beets buried under coals for eight hours and festooned with pistachio yogurt and garlic chips are a must, followed by big proteins like Australian filet that's grilled, coated in breadcrumbs and fried.The bustling bar at the end of the room draws a stylish crowd.

Name: Los Marinos José
Address: Paseo Marítimo Rey de España 161, Fuengirola, 29640, Spain
Description: Everyone is familiar with or has heard of Los Marinos José, an icon of maritime-inspired dining along the Playa de Carvajal on the Costa del Sol. The restaurant, which is modern and elegant, features a kitchen open to the dining room, its always incredible display cabinets (its fish and seafood are striking for their exquisite quality) and a semi-glass-enclosed terrace. Everything is delicious here, but if we had to make a recommendation we would suggest the shrimp from Fuengirola, the langoustine from Huelva, and the famous red prawns. Much of the catch is from the restaurant’s own boats!

Name: Los Naranjos
Description: If you are looking for the best rice dishes in Segovia, in Torrecaballeros, about 10 km (6 miles) northeast of the city of Segovia, you will find some that dazzle the palate. And no wonder, the couple at the helm (Antonio Sinsaez behind the stove and Begoña Danvila patrolling the dining areas) are originally from the city of Turia and he, specifically, finished in the top five in the world in the Concurs Internacional de Paella Valencia de Sueca (2023 edition). Paella and rice dishes (Barbate bluefin tuna with scallops; partridge with tender garlic shoots and truffle; scarlet prawns with foie gras; a banda with all i oli, etc.) are the specialty, of course, but they also offer excellent starters (mainly crustaceans or molluscs) and grilled fish.

Name: Los Tres Gallos
Address: Leona Vicaria Esquina 20 de Noviembre, Col. Centro, Cabo San Lucas, 23469, Mexico
Description: This popular operation commands a corner of downtown Cabo San Lucas. The sprawling space is centered around a grand courtyard, and the setting, with its brick structure, paver stone patio, and wood furnishings, is brightened by pink and red painted stucco. A roof terrace is open during the evening.Los Tres Gallos serves a crowd-pleasing menu of generously portioned traditional Mexican cuisine like chile rellenos, enchiladas, and mole con pollo. The pozole is a vivid broth enriched with roasted chiles and tomatoes. Stocked with plump kernels of toothsome hominy alongside chunks of braised pork, it is served with a host of embellishments. The flan de casa is as big as a house, so plan on sharing dessert.

Name: Los Trujis
Address: Avenida de la Constitución 7, Talavera de la Reina, 45600, Spain
Description: Located in a central residential area, this family-run restaurant will pleasantly surprise guests thanks to the efforts of the Trujillo brothers (with David in charge of front of house, and Pedro in the kitchen) who showcase their creativity through dishes teeming with local flavour and tradition. The menu, which includes several dishes inspired by the world of hunting, begins with a selection of small bites and several dishes designed for sharing. Don't miss their creamy, award-winning Manchego cheesecake!

Name: Lotti
Description: This chic cafe in the city's La Roma neighborhood is tucked within a former residence dating to the early 1900s. It's set on a corner with sidewalk tables for al fresco dining, while the interior's creamy hues and linen-draped tables display a touch of elegance. Swiss-born chef Luc Liebster's menu presents an intriguing offering of European cuisine with a Mexican accent. Expect dishes such as scallop crudo set over white bean puree and dressed with a tomatillo broth or hearty capuns, or Swiss dumplings, wrapped in chard and served with a creamy onion sauce and shaved black truffle. To end the meal, one could go with something sweet, or with a selection of cheeses from Querétaro accompanied by Alpine bread.

Name: Lotus Noodle Bar
Address: 56 Grove Ave., St. Augustine, FL, 32084, USA
Description: Lotus Noodle Bar began as a series of pop-ups from chef/owner Barry Honan and finally landed its brick-and-mortar spot in St. Augustine in 2023. It's a welcoming space with several different seating options, including a noodle bar. As expected, noodles are indeed the main event but kick off the meal with the sweet and spicy sunomono, made with cucumber and miso cashews, before slurping those namesake noodles. One worthy of consideration is the spicy Maple Leaf Farms duck tan tan ramen, with sesame Sichuan coconut broth made with three-month Kyoto white miso. To finish, try the NYC Dreams, with white chocolate mousse with a red rice aged sake and cherry reduction sauce sprinkled with brown butter sable crumble and a quenelle of caviar.

Name: Lou Mitchell's
Address: 565 W. Jackson Blvd., Chicago, IL, 60661, USA
Description: Strategically set near Union Station, this beloved diner has stood the test of time. Open since 1923, locals and visitors alike have scooched into booths and sat at the bar for homey comfort food that never promises to be more than what it is. Eggs, waffles, and pancakes come prepared in a dizzying number of ways. There are all sorts of salads and sandwiches; try the La Conga Delight (cheese, bacon, tomato) or the hearty open-faced Reuben on homemade rye and served with a hot stack of thick-cut steak fries. Servers roam the floor with hot coffee and complimentary donut holes. Especially after a long night, such simple pleasures go a long way.

Name: Lou Pinatou
Address: 242 rue de la mairie, Solignac-sous-Roche, 43130, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The windows of the dining room of this inn tucked away between Saint Etienne and Le Puy en Velay overlook a magnificent landscape of valleys, as you wonder where the family’s immense 5000m² kitchen garden, orchards and hives that supply most of the kitchen produce are located... The chef, who is from the hills of Le Puy and a fan of bold, crisp flavours and premium produce, works with his pastry buff wife, who hails from Marseille. Their gourmet repertory is two-fold: tomato, courgette and mousseline of smoked sardines; duck, cabbage stuffed with walnuts and honey roasted squash; rice cracker, peanut gateau and crème. Splendid wine cellar with a distinct fondness for local “Volcanic Loire and Ardèche” wines.

Name: Lou Ressignon
Description: Founded in 1966 and now run by the fifth generation, the Lou Ressignon family trattoria (in local dialect the name translates as “the night snack”) serves authentic cuisine full of character which showcases the produce and traditions of the Aosta Valley. The dishes include a delicious Valpellinese soup and excellent tripe with borlotti beans and polentina. In addition to the first-floor dining room, there’s also a historic taverna, while four welcoming guestrooms are available for anyone wishing to extend their stay.

Name: Lou im Cavalierhaus
Description: The estate is worth a visit in its own right. The palace and 620ha Branitz Park landscaped by Prince Hermann von Pückler in the 19C are conducive to a stroll. Lou (a nickname given to Prince Pückler) is an elegant restaurant housed in the smart Kavaliersbau (squire's lodge). Here, chef-patron Tim Sillack serves up modern seasonal cuisine with an artful juxtaposition of regional and international influences. The individual courses of the menu can also be ordered à la carte. "Pückler Eis" (Neapolitan ice cream) has a permanent place on the menu and is something of a signature dessert. There are also three tastefully furnished guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Louison
Address: Villa La Coste, 2750 route de la Cride, Le Puy-Sainte-Réparade, 13610, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: In the heart of the Chateau La Coste estate, Louison embodies a rare combination of wine, architecture and contemporary art. In a clean-cut, glazed extension of Villa La Coste, the restaurant helmed by chef Florent Pietravalle unveils a lineup that is emblematic of his Mediterranean roots: expressive recipes depicted by surf-turf combinations and a distinct weakness for bitter notes. The chef’s distinctive signature can be tasted in each dish, which is a masterpiece of meticulous handiwork. Local produce, the harvest from the kitchen garden and olive oil from the estate take pride of place on the menu. The slick, flawless service is quite the equal of the decadent setting.

Name: Loulou
Description: The Arts Décoratifs Museum promises an enchanted interlude opposite the Louvre gardens. In the kitchen, Benoît Dargère reinvents Mediterranean classics by means of meticulously selected produce. On the terrace or in the elegant dining room, the service is as exquisite as the food (risotto of the day; piccata of milk-fed veal al limone and sage; grilled octopus and aioli). Cosy, refined and delicious.

Name: Loup
Address: Dr. Mário Ferraz 528, São Paulo, 01453-011, Brazil
Description: Loup’s unique decor and atmosphere, featuring several dining spaces, designer details, lofty glass ceilings and an impressive vertical garden, have been very carefully curated, and provide the backdrop for an enticing fusion of cuisine from different parts of the world, prepared with top-quality ingredients. The menu includes delicious mini palm heart pastries with prawns, appetising dishes such as arroz de pato (rice with duck) that take you back to Portugal, and for dessert, the irresistible cannoli with a light yet crunchy dulce de leche and red berries, which transports you to the shores of Italy. It’s also worth taking time out to enjoy a cocktail in the lounge.

Name: Lovage
Address: 115 St George's Terrace, Jesmond, Newcastle Upon Tyne, NE2 2DN, United Kingdom
Description: Chef Kleo Tabaku is Albanian by birth and spent time in Italy before making the UK his home, so it’s no surprise to see the flavours and colours of the Mediterranean feature at this charming neighbourhood brasserie. There is a welcome lack of fussiness to the cooking, as each dish bursts with flavour. Go for the à la carte for the most choice, the fixed-price menu for the best value or the tasting menu for the full experience; sensibly priced wines from across Europe are an added bonus whatever you choose. Lisa Hide, Tabaku's partner, looks after the service and is a natural host.

Name: Lovage
Address: Bath Street, Bakewell, DE45 1DS, United Kingdom
Description: In the heart of a historic market town, famed for its puddings and tarts, you'll find this cosy restaurant located inside a former stable block. That past occupation makes itself known in the wonderfully rustic décor with wood-panelled walls, exposed brickwork and beamed ceilings. The chatty, informative team are sure to put a smile on your face as they enthusiastically explain the modern dishes made up of quality local ingredients and featuring classic combinations like roasted beetroot with goat's cheese. The team also run a more casual coffee shop next door.

Name: Lovis
Description: An impressive architectural feat – a former prison has been transformed into an attractive restaurant. High ceilings and exposed brick walls, sleek interior design and a great lighting concept make for a special atmosphere. Diners take their seats in the former lock yard, now covered and fitted with large windows – the "Aquarium" room is truly original. The modern vegetable-oriented cuisine is available as a set menu or à la carte – regular, vegetarian or also vegan upon request. A selection of wines from around the globe. Tip: Enjoy an aperitif in the lovely bar, which also boasts a terrace. You can enjoy a night in Wilmina, the adjacent hotel.

Name: Lowland
Address: The Pinch Hotel, 36 George St., Charleston, SC, 29401, USA
Description: Find Lowland just off busy King Street in a two-story brick former residence across from the boutique Pinch hotel. The first floor is home to a buzzy bar room and casual dining space, while upstairs is a bit more formal. Come for comfort food like the tavern burger with fries and a cognac sauce. The range of entrees feature grilled local fish and squid-ink tinted pasta shells neatly tossed with a luscious rouille-inspired sauce stocked with rock shrimp and little neck clams. Elevated comfort continues through dessert with house-made hand pies with a seasonal fruit filling and vanilla-infused whipped cream.---

Name: Loxalis
Address: 150 Rue de la Libération, Dudelange, 3511, Luxembourg
Description: Immense floor-to-ceiling windows command a splendid view of the surrounding countryside, with the bonus of a peaceful terrace (weather permitting): the scene of Loxalis is set. Diners are greeted by a genuine maitre d’, who carefully takes the time to explain the appetising menu. The chef subtly adds a modern spin to characteristic Mediterranean recipes, such as his new take on vitello tonnato flanked by a characterful sauce. Familiar flavours abound but with intriguing new dimensions. The lunchtime menu is a best-seller!

Name: Loy Fah
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: This chic restaurant on the fourth floor of the tasteful Panorama Resort & Spa boasts a stunning panoramic view over Lake Zurich. Inside, you are served by an extremely friendly and attentive team. The food is a modern take on authentic Thai cuisine, which is also adapted to European palates in terms of spiciness. You can put together your own menu.

Name: Lu Pisantinu
Address: Viale Giovanni Maria Orecchioni snc, loc. Liscia di Vacca, Porto Cervo, 07021, Italy
Description: A terrace framed by granite columns overlooks the coast, the sea, and Porto Cervo (about 2 km away): both the culinary style and the overall décor of the welcoming spaces are classic. The menu features primarily seafood, though there are also dishes and flavors from the inland area, with nods to Gallura traditions, such as the strictly handmade chijusoni gnocchetti. Welcoming you is a local family that has been operating here for over 40 years.

Name: Luca
Description: The restaurant name comes from Lucas, ‘bringer of light’ in Latin, out of the chef’s desire to make it a place of bright smiles. He delights in creating beautiful arrangements where every plate is a medley of elements. Aromas, textures, tastes modulate gracefully as the meal progresses. Amuse-bouche arranged like the sun seem to give physical form to light, presenting a rich variety of expressions.

Name: Lucale
Address: Shop 5-8, GF, Hang Fai Building, 28-32 Pok Fu Lam Road, Sai Ying Pun, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Named after a portmanteau of the two chefs’ first names, this neighbourhood joint uses fine artisanal ingredients from Italy to craft Italian favourites, ranging from homemade pasta to seafood and meat dishes, best enjoyed with their selection of Italian wines. Black truffle chitarrino with Pienza pecorino is guaranteed to melt your heart with its al dente texture and tantalising aroma. The eater-friendly prices also explain its popularity despite its hidden location down an alley.

Name: Lucente
Description: If you are hungry for good Italian-Mediterranean cuisine in Rüttenscheid, then this ristorante is the place for you. On the menu, dishes such as "venison tonnato" or monkfish saltimbocca with ratatouille whet the appetite; in addition, daily specials are announced by waitstaff. The atmosphere is young, fresh, friendly – a sense of Italian joie de vivre is in the air here!

Name: Lucenti
Description: This small, family - run restaurant furnished in warm, pastel shades offers a traditional setting in which to enjoy local cuisine. The dishes served in the younger, more informal Enoteca are even simpler and more traditional in style.

Name: Lucheng
Address: 39F, Conrad Hotel, 186 Yanwu West Road, Siming, Xiamen, Chinese Mainland
Description: Perched atop the city’s sail-shaped landmark, Lucheng commands fantastic views. Traditional Chinese motifs are stylised and melded with elegant fixtures and fittings for comfort. The kitchen team of Fujian natives managed by a young Minnan chef excels in Fujian classics with creative twists, showcasing the province’s wide range of produce. Try deep-fried starchy taro in aged vinegar reduction, and braised river eel with fish maw and pickled cabbage.

Name: Lucia
Description: Having just celebrated their 50th anniversary (they opened in 1971), this restaurant and hotel of the same name remain a solid culinary reference on the Abruzzi coast. The menu here is dedicated solely to fish and, as a result and is often the case, the wine list focuses almost exclusively on white wines. The fish (almost all of which comes from the Adriatic) is carefully sourced, while in the kitchen the chefs prepare classic dishes (such as enormous local langoustines cooked – and served – in a pan with oil, wine, garlic and rosemary) and a few more modern recipes (crispy mullet served with the award-winning spicy Ventricina salami).

Name: Lucia Restaurant & Bar
Address: Bernardus Lodge & Spa, 415 W. Carmel Valley Rd., Carmel Valley, CA, 93924, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This dining room in the luxe Bernardus Lodge & Spa boasts its own garden, which provides many of the superb ingredients, and is proof of the kitchen’s dedication to local and seasonal food. It might show a talent and focus on vegetables, but highlights from the nightly menu as well as à la carte may include brilliantly tender lamb, served as medallions of deboned ribeye with rosemary jus on a bed of sautéed greens.There is a casual feel to the upscale lodge-like interior, with its large fireplace and muted colors. It's located just off the lobby but draws diners from well beyond mere hotel guests. The view alone, overlooking the Carmel Valley and Bernardus vineyards, may be worth a visit. Better yet, come on a sunny day and dine alfresco on the patio.

Name: Luciano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Surrounded by the nature that envelops the characterful medieval hilltop town of Buje, this elegant resort embodies the authentic and restful charm of Istrian architecture. Luciano is its principal restaurant: the interior dining room is refined and contemporary in style, while on the terrace, simpler in its setting, it is the view over the generous surrounding countryside that captures the eye. The cuisine is well structured and capable of satisfying varied tastes, moving with ease between meat and seafood and celebrating above all the ingredients of the territory. At lunch the offering becomes simpler and more classically oriented. The wine list is broad and well constructed, enabling well-considered pairings; enthusiasts will be particularly pleased by the dedicated selection of vintage Champagnes.

Name: Luciano Cucina Italiana
Address: Piazza del Teatro di Pompeo 18, Rome, 00186, Italy
Description: It is said that one of the capital’s finest carbonaras is served here, and we can only agree: no small feat, given the dish’s sacred status in Rome. But the experience at Luciano Monosilio extends far beyond his famous signature; the menu offers other equally compelling preparations that strike a balance between deep Lazio roots and flashes of measured creativity, always delivering intense, well-defined flavors. In the basement, adjacent to the pasta laboratory, Veleno provides the ideal setting for an aperitivo or intriguing cocktail pairings. A new lounge area now also welcomes guests on the upper floor, rounding out a dining and mixology program designed for a fully immersive experience.

Name: Lucie
Description: Owner Yannick Bigourdan named his French restaurant after his grandmother who clearly inspired his journey into the world of hospitality. No doubt she would approve of the warm, inclusive atmosphere and the attentive service. It’s a sizeable space, whose quasi-industrial looks are tempered with an abundance of hanging pendant lights, while shaded glass in front of the kitchen allows hints of the activity within. While the food is recognizably Gallic, there’s a discernible contemporary edge to the dishes. Even the cocktails have something of a French accent.

Name: Luciole Restaurant
Description: Luciole is the quintessence of seasonal, spot-on cooking. The exclusively vegetable lineup of this dinky establishment in La Chaux-de-Fonds celebrates produce from the garden and nearby. Entirely ruled by the seasons, they deploy ancestral and modern techniques: fermentation, cryoconcentration, wild herbs and flowers. The menu may skip from tomatoes, rhubarb, peach and basil to absinth-laced grilled green peas or violet-perfumed sweet titbits to finish. An open kitchen, lovely tableware and delightful service set the scene in this eatery run by a nature-loving couple whose commitment to excellence is second to none. Note: maximum of eight guests per service.

Name: Lucky Cat Mayfair by Gordon Ramsay
Address: London Marriott Hotel Grosvenor Square, 10 Grosvenor Square, Mayfair, London, W1K 6JP, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Wheelchair access
Description: A welcome buzz fills the air at this dark, moodily decorated restaurant from the Gordon Ramsay stable. It represents the chef's foray into East Asian cooking, bringing together diverse flavours from a number of cuisines on one mightily appealing menu. Start in Japan with mushroom tempura, then hop over to China for a bonito fried duck leg bao bun, via the 'GFC' (Gordon's Fried Chicken) with hot Korean miso. Or if sushi is more your bag, take a seat at the raw bar and feast on the sashimi, nigiri and maki. The express lunch menu offers the best value for money.

Name: Lucky Hole
Description: Once a factory, this space furnished in retro industrial style fizzes with energy – not only because of the sizzling charcoal grill in the open kitchen, but also the fun, passionate service team. Chargrilled meats, seafood, and vegetables are the main event; the wild-caught giant shrimps with crispy garlic crumbles and chilli oil are a very popular choice. The warm banana cake with Baileys ice cream presents interesting contrasts in temperature.

Name: Lucky Star
Address: 1050 Howell Mill Rd., Ste. 110, Atlanta, GA, 30318, USA
Description: Lucky Star, located inside the lobby of Atlanta’s Star Metals office complex, is a two-in-one concept kitted out with green velvet couches and a stylish appeal. By day, it's a café pouring coffee and serving pastries and Taiwanese fare. Then, when the sun goes down, it flips into a cocktail bar with a focused à la carte menu. Breakfast sandwiches, noodles, French toast and house-made pastries make appearances on the brunch menu, while oyster omelets and rice bowls, along with a small but fun dessert section that includes mochi “dumplings” and a strawberry cheesecake cookie, show up throughout the day. A house-made scallion pancake stuffed with braised beef shank is a tasty treat any time of day.

Name: Luckys Restaurant Haus am Hang
Description: The "place to be" is a pretty apt way to describe this restaurant from which you can take in a wonderful view of the lake (Wolfgang See), Sankt Gilgen and the surrounding mountains. As you can imagine, the sophisticated terrace is coveted in summer… and then there is the good food added into the mix. Susanne and Lucas Bocsa have been putting their heart and soul into their role as hosts for many years and, over time, have established a chic restaurant where Lucas Bocsa cooks up flavoursome dishes, both classic and international. With the two set menus, "Luckys" and "Luckys All Around the World", you can also dip in and go à la carte. The glass wine cabinet in the entrance area whets your appetite for a good glass of wine off the bat. The friendly and professional service team is headed up by the likeable Susanne.

Name: Luigi Pomata
Description: This famous classic restaurant in Cagliari serves top-quality cuisine in its modern dining rooms and on an outdoor terrace. The menu features interesting reinterpretations of Sardinian dishes among other options, including their own tuna (the house speciality), which is also available in tins to take away.

Name: Luk Lak
Address: 28 Bach Dang Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: Perched on the banks of the Han River, this outpost of its Hanoian namesake boasts a dining room dripping in lush greenery. This branch shares the same culinary ethos as its flagship – creative Vietnamese fare packed with bold flavours. Grilled ground beef skewer with herbs and lemongrass seduces with aromas. Wrap in rice paper with veg and fruit for a hunger-quenching kick or pair with sticky rice and cassava root in a claypot.

Name: Luk Yu Tea House
Address: 24-26 Stanley Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Large numbers of both regulars and tourists come to Luk Yu Tea House for the traditionally prepared and flavoursome dim sum, and its three floors fill up quickly. The animated atmosphere and subtle colonial decoration are appealing but no one really stays too long; the serving team in white jackets have seen it all before and go about their work with alacrity. Popular dishes are crispy deep fried chicken and fried noodles with sliced beef.

Name: Lukas Izakaya
Description: The clue is in the name: this restaurant is dedicated to Japanese food. The menu features not only sushi and sashimi, but also tempting dishes to share and items from the Konro grill; there is also an izakaya set menu. The taste and quality of the ingredients live up to expectations. The magnificent vaulted ceiling makes for a unique setting – with a chic and urban design and cosy atmosphere. You can steal glimpses of the chefs at work in the open kitchen at the entrance. The service is friendly and professional, and the chef is also present on the restaurant floor. A popular place that has many regulars. Chef Lukas Kienbauer has his fine dining restaurant right next door.

Name: Luke's
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: A favourite with local office workers, this steakhouse and oyster bar, run by a U.S. national, bustles with patrons all day long and is ideal for power lunches or after-work cocktails. It has acquired a faithful crowd of regulars thanks to high-quality food and friendly, slick service. Expect to see U.S. classics on the menu, such as New England clam chowder and Maryland crab cake. The generous portions make it a great venue for get-togethers.

Name: Lulu
Address: 10899 Wilshire Blvd., Los Angeles, CA, 90024, USA
Description: Think dining at a museum requires toting a silver tray? Meet Lulu. This charming restaurant may be nestled within a courtyard at the Hammer Museum, but there's nothing ho-hum about it. Helmed by David Tanis with a little help from none other than Alice Waters, Lulu rewards guests who take a midday break from grokking the art. Fresh produce on display is more than just a design element; it's a hint at the philosophy of this spot, where the three-course and à la carte menus shift daily.Solid cooking leans heavily into the seasons while letting the ingredients shine. Dishes are a moving target, but a recent meal of blood orange citrus salad, chicken saltimbocca and Meyer lemon gelato proves that hyper-seasonal and local always steal the show.

Name: Lulu le Bistrot
Description: The building is modern, but inside the establishment the decor leans into an old-fashioned bistro theme, which is also evident in the dishes: eggs mayonnaise, terrine de campagne, steak with peppercorns, chocolate mousse or île flottante. At the helm, chef Ludovic Pouzelgues (Lulu Rouget) spoils diners at this relaxed restaurant in the Création neighbourhood, a stone's throw from the Les Machines de l'Île attraction. At lunchtime, good traditional home cooking is served at wallet-friendly prices, perfect for a meal between visits.

Name: Luma
Address: 113/9-10 Soi Sukhumvit 55, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: Keen amateur cooks should ask for a seat at the L-shaped counter if they want a full view of a busy kitchen in action; if you’re coming in a larger group then request a table on the mezzanine floor. Spanish food in all its colour and vitality is celebrated here, from assorted tapas to classics like paella and suckling pig. All the dishes are generously sized and most are for sharing, so tend towards under-ordering unless you want plenty to take home with you. Start with Gilda, the classic Basque pintxo, and some jamón ibérico while you browse the menu.

Name: Lumbre
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Lumbre boasts an impressive setting in a delightful 17C bodega with pleasant dining rooms suitable for individual guests and groups, an attractive underground cellar, an attic-style lounge for post-dinner drinks, plus dining options that are exclusively centred around three meticulously crafted menus: Origen (midweek only), Fuego, and Lumbre. The experience here usually starts off with a selection of appetisers (called La Huerta) in its stunning “calados” (underground tunnels in which wines were laid to down to age in days gone by).

Name: Lumbre
Address: Jose Maria Morelos 162, San José del Cabo, 23400, Mexico
Description: Located just off the art walk in San Jose del Cabo, Lumbre is a contemporary, stylish space from César Pita. It's a Mexican and live fire concept with global influences where creativity and originality reign supreme. Case in point? The grilled bread that kicks off the meal that's served with a bone marrow butter, served in the bone with hibiscus salt. And that's just the beginning. Compressed watermelon is a riot of colors and flavor, then a classic chile relleno is revamped with a Pasilla chile, stuffed with a "scallop chorizo" with gooey cheese, and fried until crispy. Pork belly in a Recaudo Negro sauce sided by carrot puree and a croquette of plantain puree is highly original. The friendly, welcoming staff caps off the experience.

Name: Lumdee Te Khuadang
Address: V Community, 345/9 Mu 3, Wongwaen Rop 2 Road, San Phra Net, San Sai, Chiang Mai, 50210, Thailand
Description: This spacious restaurant balances scale with efficiency, accommodating 200 diners in the air-conditioned room, VIP room and out on the terrace. Locals and visitors flock here for home-style Northern Thai food, cooked to order and piping hot. Highlights include stir-fried termite mushrooms with aromatic herbs, and the fresh and flavoursome saep pork rib. The wooden Lanna-inspired structure has character, making this a welcoming spot for families and groups.

Name: Lume
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: In a cobbled street in Bordeaux's old town, Lume enchants with its intimate atmosphere and Italian cuisine. Venetian chef Riccardo Suppa showcases seafood and organic vegetables in elegant dishes served on crockery handcrafted by a local ceramist. The creations on the single set menu include a flavoursome reinterpretation of pasta e fasioi made with Zolfino beans, pasta mista and scallop crudo; or for dessert: pear, Barena honey and a touch of umeboshi. Authentic food to be savoured in a cosy and inviting setting.

Name: Luminist Cafè Bistrot
Description: Situated on the ground floor of the splendid Banco di Napoli building that is also home to the Gallerie d'Italia museum, this restaurant also includes a bar and pasticceria. The varied restaurant menu features international dishes (for a quicker meal), fish based around recipes from around the world, alongside more creative dishes and regional specialities from Campania. The latter, from the aubergine parmigiana to the candele pasta served with a Neapolitan ragu, and the popular babà, are truly delicious and showcase all the colours and flavours of Neapolitan cuisine.

Name: Lumière
Address: 40 Houbi Village, Houbi District, Tainan, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: In stark contrast to the century-old façade, the interior juxtaposes local serpentine stone and cypress wood for a sleek, Nordic vibe. The owner remodelled the family manor she inherited and manages the business; her partner, who received formal training in France, helms the kitchen. The menu showcases local ingredients such as Muscovy duck or glue berries into culinary gems using European techniques. To honour the family's roots in poultry farming, the menu includes a signature egg dish that celebrates their history.

Name: Lumière
Address: Hotel Edison, ul. Wypoczynkowa 60, Baranowo,, Przeźmierowo, 62-081, Poland
Description: Sitting a stone’s throw from Lake Kierski and not far from Poznań airport, this restaurant within the Hotel Edison is something of a hidden gem. The cooking comes with a Polish heart and centres around colourful, imaginative dishes that fuse quality produce with a creative streak – such as cured trout from Zielenica with fennel, quail’s egg, buttermilk and dill. The hotel is surrounded by vines, meaning the wine list includes some none-more-local options.

Name: Lumière
Address: Fairmont Century Plaza Los Angeles at Beverly Hills, 2025 Avenue Of The Stars, Los Angeles, CA, 90067, USA
Description: Nestled inside the Fairmont Century Plaza, Lumière is a relaxed brasserie-styled spot for French-inspired cooking. Friendly staff are on hand to offer guidance and share their favorite selections, but you'll certainly want to indulge in a variety of classics like fruits de mer and steak frites, if only for the delicious fries. Start things off right by ordering the velvety chicken liver mousse served with an olive jam, or sample the Bayonne, Fermin Iberico or five year-aged Iberico hams from the charcuterie menu. Seared sea bass is plated with a delicious onion soubise for a pleasing main dish. Then for dessert, you'll never go wrong with crème brûlée with its pure vanilla flavor and nutty caramelized crust.

Name: Lumperhof
Description: This family-run inn is a lovely spot in the countryside and has a charming terrace shaded by a majestic old lime tree. The menu is varied and full of delicious options. Made with regional and seasonal produce, the dishes draw on Mediterranean, Middle Eastern and Asian influences. Options such as the cream of sweetcorn soup with deep-fried mussels and purple curry, or the Allgäu cheese spaetzle with melted onions and a green salad are sure to whet the appetite. In the evening, you can dine à la carte or opt for a set menu comprising three or five courses. Cash payments only.

Name: Lumé
Address: Oude Zeeweg 74, Noordwijk aan Zee, 2202 CE, Netherlands
Description: Arriving at this Anglo-Norman-style villa (1902) feels like coming home. The cosy interior, reminiscent of a cottage, and the endearing personality of the hostess are irresistible. The youthful kitchen team favours a resolutely modern approach to cooking. They play with textures, allow the main ingredient to shine and sometimes come up with surprisingly imaginative ideas. Hand them a butternut squash, and they will turn it into something amazing, with great technical skill and subtle influences from around the globe.

Name: Lun Kee Rice Roll
Description: Since 2011, this simple shop has been serving rice rolls made and steamed to order. His spring onion and whisked egg rice roll is simple but delicious, boasting bouncy texture.

Name: Luna
Description: Luna may have retained its name and decor, but it's all change in the kitchen. Chefs Olivier Peyronnet and Kim Buyse, an experienced duo who honed their skills in Luxembourg and some top Parisian establishments, adhere to a stripped-down, modern approach. The tranquil dining space done out in a palette of linen, pale wood and almond green tones sets the stage for contemporary bistro cuisine that hits the mark. Japanese accents subtly offset tradition in precise, understated dishes – think market-fresh fish sweetened by a mirin beurre blanc and served with parsnip and salsify.

Name: Lunar
Address: World of Wedgwood, Barlaston, Stoke-on-Trent, ST12 9ER, United Kingdom
Description: Housed in the former staff canteen of the ‘World of Wedgwood’, this vast restaurant is named after The Lunar Society of which Josiah Wedgwood himself was a founding member. Naturally, fine Wedgwood china and tableware is a feature – as are prime British ingredients. The hidden bar is a great place for a drink and the chef’s table looks through a large window into the kitchen so you can get a good view of the team in action. Do take the time to immerse yourself in the amazing visitor experience as a whole.

Name: Lunch
Description: Lunch is an inviting operation run by Chef Mallory Tubbs and boasts a country store charm that's thoroughly authentic. The structure dates back to the 1930s, and features cream walls and wainscotting, a variety of wood tables, and displays of local vegetables, jams and honey, and dry goods. This Sewanee operation lives up to its name, open from morning to afternoon and serving a concise menu featuring products from local farms that may offer up the likes of seasonal salads, huevos rancheros or a steak sandwich on house-made baguette with Gruyère, tender peppers and onions, and chimichurri sauce. Be sure to save room for one (or more) of the freshly baked pastries, say a wedge of zucchini cake with buttermilk glaze.

Name: Luneta & Lorneta Bistro Club
Description: The Pałac Ciekocinko Hotel, a large house dating back to the 1920s, is home to this smart Belle Époque-style restaurant with a few plush details in its décor. Situated in the basement, there’s a pleasantly cosy feel to the dining room, which is accentuated by the cheery, welcoming service; a garden terrace is used to fine effect in the summer. The full-flavoured cooking incorporates French bistro and Italian influences such as confit duck leg and tarte Tatin.

Name: Lung Yai Thai Tapas
Description: You could drive down the street a dozen times and still overlook this intimate little nook that hides in plain sight. Little Havana is certainly an unexpected place to find one of the city’s hottest Thai kitchens, but the long waits are an indication (no reservations) that Chef/owner Veenuthri Trisransri knows what he’s doing. On a menu that mixes typical standbys with Northern specialties, begin with an order of homemade dumplings with a pork or shrimp filling, served steamed or fried. Khao Soi, a coconut-based curry with your choice of protein, bobs with egg noodles and has a rich, creamy profile without too much heat. Tables, plates and even the place itself is small, so order ambitiously and be prepared for a kitchen that sends out dishes faster than you can finish them.

Name: Lupa
Address: 73 Highbury Park, Islington, London, N5 1UA, United Kingdom
Description: From carbonara to cacio e pepe, this neighbourhood bistro aims to bring a taste of Rome to Highbury Village. Mirroring the rustic eateries of the Italian capital, the dining room is simply decorated but filled with atmosphere, while the cooking is rich and comforting. With the menu designed for sharing, you have the chance to try a good range of dishes, one of which must be a pasta, and there’s always a daily fish special too – to finish, you can’t ignore their particularly good tiramisu. Negronis to start and an Italian wine list complete a very Mediterranean picture.

Name: Lupaia
Address: Località Lupaia 74, Torrita di Siena, 53049, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: An enchanting setting, a Tuscan hamlet nestled among the hills between Montepulciano and Montefollonico, from which breathtaking sunsets may be enjoyed; tables in the open air during the warmer months, while in the cooler season the dining room looks out onto a splendid open kitchen. The gastronomic offering is determined daily by the chef, whose tasting menu draws above all upon the produce of the estate. Booking is essential for those not staying in the hamlet, and the journey to reach it is thoroughly bucolic.

Name: Lurgbauer
FacilitiesAndServices: Brunch,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Nestled amid forests and meadows at an elevation of approximately 900m, this farmhouse is accessible via a gravel road. Its origins can be traced back to 1390. With bare wooden tables, floorboards and cowhides as decoration, the small restaurant has a clean and modern yet rustic look. Floor-to-ceiling windows afford views of the idyllic countryside, including their own Black Angus cattle grazing in the pasture – they are a focal point of the cuisine. At lunchtime, classic dishes are served à la carte or as a set menu. In the evening, you have the choice between two set menus: the seasonal and creative "Lurg-Menü" and the "Klassiker-Menü". The beef soup or boiled beef alone are worth the trip!

Name: Lurrak
Description: On the Basque pelota court, there is more to this pretty, traditional Basque building, dating back to the 1900s, than meets the eye, as it now sports a distinctly Scandinavian vibe. Notably passed by David Toutain's restaurant, chef Romain Goyeneche's fresh cuisine errs towards sophisticated, with an emphasis on plants and regional produce: green peas and broad beans, rhubarb and trout roe; strawberry, rose honey, fermented milk and fennel. Having spent time in Copenhagen, the chef employs various Scandinavian preservation methods.

Name: Lury
Address: 8 Cambridge Road, Hastings, TN34 1DJ, United Kingdom
Description: Chef Jack Lury skilfully blends his British, European and Sri Lankan heritage at this personal little restaurant in the town centre. Look out for the discreet entrance, then head down to the relaxed dining room where Lury cooks alone for just 10 diners. His original tasting menu is filled with enticing, interesting dishes that enhance British ingredients with deft spicing. Stand-out dishes include the likes of puréed aubergine with mustard seeds, crunchy turnip and Brussels sprouts, or tender venison with a spiced garlic sauce.

Name: Lusi Brasserie
Description: A tip before we get started: In fine weather, be sure to nab a table on the terrace in front of the building, from which you can take in stunning views of the Matterhorn! But the brasserie of the long-established Grand Hotel Zermatterhof also provides a delightful, classically elegant setting with its lovely walnut panelling and partially glass-paned vaulted ceiling. The cuisine is French and draws on international influences. The menu includes "Lusi Classics" such as calf's head, and traditional dishes such as Wiener schnitzel, steak tartare, burgers and flammkuchen – and there is always an evening special.

Name: Lusin
Address: Centria Mall, 210 Olaya Street, Al Olaya, Riyadh, 11672, Saudi Arabia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,No alcohol served,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Set on the third floor of Centria Mall in the heart of the Olaya district, this Armenian restaurant has a rustic style with a warm, authentic feel. Its two rooms have a stone-faced décor, wood flooring and a central kitchen partially on view between the two areas, while a small terrace offers a street vista. The menu is extensive, offering appealing, authentic Armenian dishes. Take your pick from fresh salads, appetisers such as delicious cheese borak and some great Middle Eastern dips – but certainly don’t miss their classic kebabs and signature honey cake.

Name: Lusso (Legazpi)
Address: Greenbelt 5, Legazpi Street, Makati - Metro Manila, 1228, The Philippines
Description: Founded by the late chef Margarita Forés, who trained in Italy and France, Lusso brings classic European elegance to Greenbelt 5. Dishes such as foie gras brûlée and spinach tagliolini reflect her roots; Lusso tiramisu croccante is a playful twist on the classic dessert. A chandelier casts a soft glow over the compact space, where staff in black and white add polish and nostalgia. Dine on the terrace for a breezy escape with a view of the verdant garden.

Name: Lustre
Description: The guiding theme here is ‘Umami French’. Drawing on the five flavours of Japanese cuisine, French cooking is fused with the umami of Japanese ingredients. The foundations remain firmly classical, from technique to sauces. Kombu stock and fish sauce are added to the essences of vegetables, seafood and meat to draw out a powerful umami synergy. Named after the French word for chandelier, the restaurant shines a light on French cuisine shaped by Japanese sensibility.

Name: Lutie's
Address: Commodore Perry Estate, Auberge Collection, 4100 Red River St., Austin, TX, 78751, USA
Description: Located within the landmark Commodore Perry Estate, Lutie's is a grand space done in a green and gold palette with windows overlooking a stunning patio with gardens and a fountain. Run by the husband-and-wife team of Chef Bradley Nicholson and pastry chef Susana Querejazu, Lutie's offers a seasonally inspired, refined approach to Texas heritage cooking, available à la carte and as a tasting menu. Their estate bread, made with a decades-old starter and fermented corn grits and given a good sear, is even better with their exquisite cultured butter with layers of brown butter. House-smoked trout roe adds a pop of flavor to the Mt. Lassen trout with crispy skin. Finally, a scoop of Kouign-amann ice cream with a mini Kouign-amann topped with warm caramel sauce is a perfect classic.

Name: Lutèce
Address: 1522 Wisconsin Ave. NW, Washington, DC, 20007, USA
Description: With bottles of wine lining the shelves above, the dining room at this delightful Georgetown bistro s a charming, date-night oasis, thanks to exposed brick, hardwood floors and a pressed-tin ceiling. Not far behind the décor, the seasonal menu is tight knit, offering only a handful of appetizers and mains that could change on a moment’s notice. The kitchen team turns out an impressive array of cleverly rendered hits, like hand-cut fluke tartare of with green strawberry, granny smith apple and marigold, or duck breast with duck sausage, cherries and bigarade. For dessert, consider the honey semifreddo with honeycomb and 18-month-aged Comté cheese. Organic and biodynamic wines comprise the list, and thoughtfully crafted cocktails are equally tempting.

Name: Lux Dag för Dag
Description: A stylish, red-brick former factory dating back to 1916, set beside the water, is home to this brasserie-style restaurant that has a welcome brightness to both its décor and its atmosphere. Local produce is key to their ethos, including the likes of Östergötland lamb and Ängsö pike-perch, along with plenty of seasonal ingredients such as asparagus and rhubarb. Unfussy, classically based dishes allow this fresh produce to shine, with the flexible courses ranging in size from 'mini' to 'large'. There's also a set Kitchen Menu available for those that can't quite decide.

Name: Luyu Dumplings
Address: 17980 Castleton St., City of Industry, CA, 91748, USA
Description: This bare-bones operation hides in the back of a shopping center in City of Industry. The space is Spartan and deadly quiet, except for the sound of the refrigerators that hum constantly and the steady chop-chop of a chef’s knife in the nearby kitchen. If you want anything to drink, including water, you have to ask, and if you have questions about the menu, you’re better off looking at the poster of dishes on the wall. All to say, this humble restaurant is short on creature comforts but delivers admirably in the realm of excellent, handmade dumplings and bowls of chewy noodles glossed in scallion oil. From lamb with fennel to chicken with celery, dumplings come with a multitude of fillings, but the tender ground pork with lotus root win.

Name: Lvdao Seafood
Address: 447-451 Jiu'er Road, Shishi, Quanzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: In 1989, Lvdao opened its doors with only six tables. Nowadays, it has turned into a leading F&B chain in Shishi and this flagship establishment now spans two floors. Though it specialises in Fujian fare, especially seafood, there are some Cantonese options on the menu. Try the umami-laden swimmer crab – the locals prefer it steamed with black sticky rice or taro balls. Round off with custard-filled buns, best enjoyed with sweet peanut soup.

Name: Lwia Brama²
Description: There is so much beauty to admire when you visit this restaurant in Ostrów Tumski, Wrocław’s oldest district and without doubt one of its most attractive. If you dine inside, marvel at the red-brick vaulted ceiling of the atmospheric medieval mansion; alternatively, sit on the pavement terrace in the shadow of the stunning St. John the Baptist Archcathedral. The kitchen does a good job of living up to the setting, with dishes such as precisely made venison pierogi.

Name: Ly Ly Vietnam Cookhouse
Address: 306 E. 81st St., New York, NY, 10028, USA
Description: Orange-and-white checkered floors, mustard-colored booths, and paper mâché flowers suspended from the ceiling—this Upper East Side spot is just plain charming. It's the kind of place you want to drop in on a cold winter's night to boost your mood but don't let the whimsical vibe fool you, as the Vietnamese dishes are seriously good. The concise offerings range from rolls and appetizers to larger plates like shaking beef. Kick off a meal with a plate of crispy spring rolls filled with pork, mushrooms, and glass noodles before moving on to a Vietnamese crepe with pork belly and nuoc mam sauce. Of course, pho is a must and the "UES" bowl doesn't disappoint with its complex 20-hour broth and meltingly tender five-spice smoked short rib.

Name: Lyf's
Description: One of this neighbourhood restaurant's main assets is its convivial atmosphere. The commitment to quality is palpable on every plate that is brought to your table. Martijn Stroosma serves up beautifully presented dishes that showcase his creativity. This astute chef never goes over the top. For instance, he will mellow the combination of langoustine tail tempura and confit bacon with touches of mango and celeriac. He always strikes the right balance, including in the mouth-watering à la carte and lunch options.

Name: Lyla
Description: The name is an amalgam of the French words ‘lyrique’ and ‘laboratoire’. Leveraging his poetic creativity, the chef showcases the fruits of his research in his prix fixe offerings. The first half of the proceedings is steeped in playfulness, beginning with a balloon-shaped cocktail. In the second half, we get back to essentials, with fish and meat dishes dressed in sauces. Foodstuffs from Kyushu reflect the chef’s roots in Oita Prefecture. Be sure to try Oita’s famed kabosu citrus and its wines.

Name: Lyla Lila
Address: 693 Peachtree St. NE, Ste. 118, Atlanta, GA, 30308, USA
Description: It bears repeating that Chef/owner Craig Richards' Lyla Lila is a good find in the heart of midtown. Sharing a contemporary design with a darker, moody color palette, the restaurant is divided into several rooms, starting with a handsome curved bar up front and a sunlit dining room further in. The kitchen follows the seasons and puts pasta as a key focal point. House staples include crispy duck lasagna with a cocoa béchamel, as well as roast chicken or snapper with pistachio pesto. Everything is scaled for sharing, down to dessert. Rotating flavors of gelato and sorbet or perhaps a wedge of tiramisu will close out the meal nicely.

Name: Lyran Matbar
Description: There’s a pleasingly relaxed air at this small, simply styled restaurant, where the experienced team lead the service with a friendly smile. Upstairs it’s more about drinks, so if you’re here to dine then head down the spiral staircase to the rustic cellar. The well-balanced tasting menus come in Mixed, Pescetarian and Vegetarian versions and are created daily from the best local produce available. All you are presented with is a list of ingredients, which are then turned into modern Swedish creations such as ‘yellow beet, skyr, pistachio, cedrat, fennel pollen, burned butter and sherry’.

Name: Lys d'Or
Description: Black marble, gilding and a grand piano set the scene in this swanky yet supremely tasteful Gent townhouse. The epitome of classy luxury, it provides the perfect foil to the high-flying, pedigree score signed by chef Wattenberge. Wagyu and North Sea crab, jazzed up with a tangy guacamole and radish cannelloni with furikake-laced sushi rice are emblematic of the talent and creativity of this virtuoso chef. Make sure you peruse the impressive wine list that stars a remarkable collection of Chateau Pétrus vintages (from 2000 on).

Name: LÍMO Heritage Kitchen at Suelo Sur
Address: Lote 320, Centro, San José del Cabo, 23400, Mexico
Description: Just outside of San José del Cabo, this farm to table, open-air restaurant is the showpiece of Chef Guillermo J. Gómez, who displays his affection for local ingredients on a menu divided by garden, sea, roots, and live fire. Begin with bread crafted from blue corn and organic whole wheat then grilled over a live fire and set with a puree of seasonal vegetables. Appetizers are equally enticing, as in the yellowtail jack that's gently grilled, then sliced sashimi-style and served with a coconut aguachile and plantain puree. Berkshire pig "Matamabre" with toasted sweet corn and poblano chili stew is just one of the alluring main dishes at this garden oasis where a laidback ambience adds to the experience.

Name: Là DN
Description: Open only on weekday lunchtimes, this small restaurant with an experienced chef at the helm serves an indulgent but wallet-friendly menu-carte. His pleasant bistronomy cooking is inspired by the market, and includes dishes such as gurnard with Jerusalem artichokes and vegetable colombo, or caramelised veal breast, crispy polenta and parsley mushrooms.

Name: Là-bas
Description: Just a stone's throw from Croix de Chavaux metro station, this new kid on the block catches the eye. The large dining space has a fireplace, original wooden floorboards, a sofa, mismatched upcycled furniture, vintage knick-knacks; there is an old piano in the next room, and the kitchen is located at the entrance. On sunny days, the terrace on the patio is a treat. Founded by three partners, the same as at the Des Terres restaurant in Paris, this establishment prides itself on its modern, convivial cuisine, with dishes to share and a five-course set menu in the evening. The cellar is quite something, with over 1 300 wines, some produced by young French vintners, others abroad; expert recommendations from the sommelier.

Name: Léonor
Address: 11 rue de la Nuée-Bleue, Strasbourg, 67000, France
Description: Behind a 19C façade and within 18C walls, this contemporary hotel designed by Jean-Philippe Nuel has its own lounge-style restaurant adjoining the bar. The menu is in keeping with the culinary zeitgeist: for example, tuna sashimi, mango, avocado, with soy and sesame sauce, or sautéed calf’s sweetbreads, celery and lovage. For tables of friends, there are large dishes designed to share (whole seabass, rib steak etc). For those with a sweet tooth, there’s a choice of plated desserts or pretty pastries laid out in the display cabinet.

Name: Léontine
Description: An authentic little corner of France, tucked away in a quiet yet central location near the Stadtpark. The bistro atmosphere is charming, the service provided by the owner is cordial and professional, and the modern French cuisine is delicious. The dishes revolve around the seasons and are made with select ingredients. The pair serve a five-course tasting menu and an à la carte selection; at lunchtime there is the more affordable "Menu du Midi" – a three-course set menu. The wine list takes you through the regions of France.

Name: Lóla
Description: A stylish room, a welcoming service team, chefs on show in the open kitchen and an appealing Italian menu, all make this spot near the harbour an understandably popular destination, whatever the occasion. You can put yourself in the kitchen’s hands and go for the set five-course menu for the table or order your own dishes from the à la carte. Start with the focaccia and delicious whipped ricotta, then move on to an in-house pasta such as the Black Angus short rib tagliatelle, while for dessert, it has to be the tiramisu, which is spooned out at the table ‘Italian style’. They have a terrific little cinema next door too.

Name: Löffelspitze
Description: Hotel Alpenstern boasts an enviable location above the village, perched at an altitude of 1 580m. In addition to cosy guestrooms and panoramic apartments, the hotel has an interesting gastronomic identity. The restaurant, named after the 1 962m-high Löffelspitze mountain, serves dishes with seasonal and Alpine influences, in the form of an eight-course set menu. To accompany your food, you have a choice of wine (peruse the well-curated wine list of over 2 000 labels) or cocktails, including alcohol-free options. The attentive service is very pleasant. Amuse-bouches are served in the bar area before you are shown to your table in the elegant space. The aesthetic is modern, chic and appealingly casual – there are only a handful of tables, which creates a certain intimacy. Alternatively, you could head to Panoramarestaurant.

Name: Löwen
Description: In this cosy little restaurant in the vaulted cellar, you can look forward to the "Gourmet Menu", which is served at lunch and dinner, with the option of up to seven courses. At lunchtime, Beiz serves a set menu, as well as a choice of à la carte dishes. There is also a decent wine selection, and the front-of-house team is friendly and competent.

Name: Löwen
Description: In Söflingen, a district of Ulm, the historic courtyard of a former Clarissan convent dating from 1258 is home to an attractive hotel with individually designed rooms and a lovely restaurant. In the modern setting that has been created within the old walls, a friendly, attentive team serves delicious dishes made with carefully sourced ingredients. The accomplished chef presents a focused à la carte selection of classics, including cheese spaetzle tartufo, roast beef, and caviar specialities. On Tue there is an additional three-course schnitzel menu; Wed-Sat, a fine dining set menu of four, six or seven courses – think "scallop, onion, hazelnut" or "veal neck, mushroom, cabbage, truffle". A vegetarian version is also available. Well-chosen wine list.

Name: Löwen - Gaststube
Description: Run by Rita and Domenico Miggiano-Köferli, Gasthof Löwen's second eatery is a delightful and more down-to-earth alternative to the fine dining restaurant. The atmosphere is inviting, not least because of the warm hospitality provided by the waitstaff. The freshly prepared, flavoursome dishes include pan-fried Lötschberg perch fillet with lemon thyme and almond butter, and Zurich veal ragout with glazed vegetables and butter rösti. Vegetarian options available. Popular lunch deal.

Name: Löwen Gourmet
Description: Steeped in tradition, this inn housed in a handsome building from 1822 presents an appealing two-in-one concept: Die Land Brasserie and Löwen Gourmet. Under the direction of Jonas Ingold, the latter serves an eight-course set menu for a maximum of 10 diners in the evening. A vegetarian version is also available. Great emphasis is placed on seasonality, with many ingredients sourced from the local region. Service is very friendly and adept. In summer, tables on the tranquil terrace to the rear of the building, which overlooks the old village church, are coveted. For a pleasingly down-to-earth alternative, head to the Brasserie, which specialises in regional fare.

Name: Löwen Messen - Die Land Brasserie
Description: Set in a charming historic half-timbered house in the heart of Messen, Löwen has much to offer on the culinary front. The regionally and seasonally oriented Brasserie serves as an excellent alternative to Löwen Gourmet. The attractively presented dishes boast bold flavours – think "steak au poivre": beef fillet, creamy peppercorn sauce, a vegetable medley, sautéed potatoes and spring onions, or braised veal cheeks with petits pois à la française. These can be ordered à la carte, or as part of a four- or five-course set menu that showcases the kitchen's ambition. At lunchtime, there is also a good-value selection of daily specials. The wine list features around 300 labels, including some notable rarities. Add to this friendly, attentive service and charming rustic yet refined interior design. Passing the modern open kitchen on your way into the restaurant only heightens the anticipation.

Name: Löwengrube
Description: Since chef-patron Amadeus Kura took over, this former wine tavern has had a makeover – with fantastic results. The traditional character of the historical building has been intentionally preserved, and combined with sleek, modern elements. The chef's culinary vision is just as contemporary: he primarily uses regional ingredients but also draws on international influences. Delicious dishes such as northern Black Forest salmon trout with peach, pepper and cashews, or veal loin with aubergine and polenta are available in the evening either à la carte or as part of a five-course set menu. A similar selection is often served à la carte for lunch. The well-curated wine list includes a good selection of Baden labels. The sheltered terrace is a lovely spot in which to soak up the Old Town atmosphere. Parking tip: The restaurant is a stone's throw from Schlossberggarage.

Name: Lüne
Address: 17/14 Le Thanh Ton Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 71006, Vietnam
Description: The restaurant offers an elegant and welcoming setting, with several private dining rooms well suited to special celebrations. French chef Adrien Guenzi, originally from Lyon, reinterprets classic dishes through a modern lens, with a strong focus on form and aesthetics. The Canadian lobster raviolo is a standout: a single, generously filled parcel is paired with a lobster cream that delivers depth and clarity of flavour. Subtle herbal notes bring freshness, while smoked ikura adds an extra layer of complexity.

Name: Lửa
Address: 2 Street No. 11, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 7000000, Vietnam
Description: The al fresco wine bar, whose tables are set in a courtyard surrounded by lush greenery, is perfect for a drink and nibbles. There are about 100 wine references to choose from with a substantial by-the-glass selection. The wine list changes every month, but the home-brewed sake, a firm fixture, is worth trying. The menu, which features only organic produce from small local farms, combines European dishes with a twist of Japanese elements as both the manager and head chef hail from Japan.

Name: L’Alchimia
Description: The parquet floor, wood-beamed ceiling and exposed brickwork lend a warm ambience to this restaurant, which is bright and airy during the day and romantic in the evening thanks to its soft lighting. With Giuseppe Postorino at the helm, the cuisine here includes classic recipes alongside more personalised dishes all prepared using top-quality ingredients that are typical of Italian cuisine. Additional features include a small, beautiful brick-vaulted wine cellar (open to visitors), plus an adjacent bar-bistro which serves quick lunches and excellent aperitifs.

Name: L’Antica Pizzeria da Michele
Address: Mercure ICON Hotel, #01-08, 8 Club Street, 069472, Singapore
Description: This 150-year-old Neapolitan pizza chain opened their first Asian outpost in 2024 and offers 18 different toppings.
