The wine list comprises a constantly evolving selection of well-priced bottles (mostly biodynamic or natural) from small producers, and the enthusiastic front-of-house team is on hand to recommend just the right tipple.

Name: Maison Kieny
Description: This inviting coaching inn (from 1850) not far from Mulhouse occupies an imposing traditional Alsace building in the centre of the village. In a pretty dining room with a new decor, the food now leans more towards bistronomy but is still built around seasonal ingredients: spiced sauerkraut fritter, pulled wild boar and radish pickles; venison bourguignon, sweet potato purée; apple and buckwheat dessert.

Name: Maison L'Essentiel
Description: After 10 years at L'Essentiel, Richard and Fanny Bernigaud are writing a new chapter in this 1930s house, with tables laid out over two floors. The chef trained in some top kitchens – Lameloise, Guy Savoy, Joël Robuchon and Stéphane Derbord – and crafts a delightful seasonal menu: Aube trout with a pearlescent finish served with cauliflower and grapefruit, pan-seared beef with a creamy parsnip and green apple purée, and a cardamom jus. For a look behind the scenes, book the eight-place table d'hôte, which is right next to the kitchen.

Name: Maison Lagure
Address: 78 boulevard de la République, La Garenne-Colombes, 92250, France
Description: In this bistro, named after a coastal dune plant, chef Julien Dumas (Bellefeuille, Lucas Carton) works hand in hand with his talented associate Lucas Boisseau to cook up tempting bistronomy cuisine. The focus is on the essentials, with a few creative flourishes: fillet of pollack, grilled wild asparagus with a little bite, cockles and onions served in their jus; to finish, a fresh and vibrant fennel and grapefruit dessert rife with contrasting flavours. The concise menu is always evolving, with a good-value set menu at lunchtime and tasting menus in the evening. The sleek and elegant interior features a large mottled mirror, suspended lighting, faux concrete walls, hardwood floors, a glass-fronted wine cellar and eclectic decorative touches.

Name: Maison Léa
Description: This culinary landmark on the Saône embankment enjoys a fine view of the Fourvière and St-Jean districts. Hearty Lyon specialities still feature prominently in two good value-for-money set menus and a well-crafted à la carte menu. Simpler fare at the next-door Bouchon Léa, the historic cradle of Mère Léa.

Name: Maison Minori
Description: In a wine-growing village on the Côte Chalonnaise, this pretty building with a yellow façade houses a spacious restaurant featuring exposed stonework and beams, a red hollow-brick ceiling, a monumental fireplace, polished concrete, Corten steel and designer lighting. The chef-owner, a Jura native with seven years of experience in Japan (Tokyo, Kyoto), treats diners to a set menu inspired by the local markets: slow-cooked egg, Morteau sausage, chestnuts in veal jus and potato "broth"; deconstructed lemon tart with shiso ice cream. Minori, meaning "harvest" or "ripening", is a fitting name for a restaurant born of a wealth of culinary experience.

Name: Maison Nipa
Description: This restaurant, opened by an experienced Franco-Philippine couple (Jason is in charge of savoury dishes, while Sharon rustles up desserts), specialises in Gallic cuisine influenced by the flavours and aromas of the Philippine archipelago. The food takes you on a culinary tour from Sarthe to the Philippines, depicted by Croisic squid à la “Adobong Pusit”, stuffed with a sisig of bellota chorizo and coated in a subtle cuttlefish ink sauce or wild duck with coffee-flavoured ceps and an “Adobo” sauce, together with other delicately perfumed dishes that might feature sweet-savoury or surf-turf notes. The roof may not be covered in palm leaves (meaning of nipa), but the modern dining room which cleverly mixes materials, is delightful, as is the seamless service.

Name: Maison Passerelle
Address: 1 Wall St., New York, NY, 10005, USA
Description: Nestled within the luxe and glamour of Printemps is this stylish restaurant by Chef Gregory Gourdet, who pulls French, African and Asian influences into a tight menu teeming with personality. Striking tilework, an open kitchen and a green, patterned booth make for a distinct, photo-ready setting. Mature and composed, dishes like smoked beets with nuoc cham and pickled strawberries or asparagus soup with crab and grilled cucumber deliver flavor and finesse in spades. Duck glazed in cane syrup and finished with a tamarind jus is pure fireworks, while jasmine rice with red kidney beans is at once subtle, confident and deeply satisfying. Beautiful cocktails round out the experience.

Name: Maison Pavlov
Address: 199 avenue de la Libération-Charles-de-Gaulle, Le Bouscat, 33110, France
Description: Nowadays, this 17C Carthusian monastery is home to a small boutique hotel and its restaurant. Opt for a table out on the terrace, which overlooks the swimming pool, or in an atmosphere reminiscent of an elegant boudoir (velvet banquettes, cane chairs and upcycled objects). In keeping with this setting, the cuisine is meticulous and comforting; it draws on the house's permaculture vegetable garden for some of its ingredients, and promotes subtle, delicate flavours. Tempting bistro set menu at lunchtime, distinctly fine dining menu in the evening.

Name: Maison Renard
Address: 15 place de la République, Béthune, 62400, France
Description: Chef Sébastien Renard (who appeared as a contestant on Top Chef) has taken over the sumptuous premises of his mentor, the great chef Marc Meurin. This red-brick mansion is truly magnificent, and its bar and elegant glass roof lend it undeniable flair. The young chef, who hails from the region, shows his firm commitment to local produce by showcasing local ingredients and championing their suppliers. He serves up a carte blanche-style set menu that leaves no doubt as to his technical expertise: squid tagliatelle with apple, celery and ginger; monkfish tail with a medley of white asparagus and hay sabayon. Five comfortable guestrooms are available for those wishing to stay on.

Name: Maison Seed
Description: In a narrow pedestrian street of Millau, near the Fontaine du Mandarins, the dinky Maison Seed is the lair of a globe-trotting couple. A vaulted dining room provides the backdrop to indulgent, fusion-style dishes that incorporate oils, vinegars, sourdough bread, etc, all made in-house, and available to take home. An intimate, eco-conscious restaurant that combines flavours from near and far.

Name: Maison Soubeiran
Description: This endearing family-run eatery is the lair of a chef who crafts healthy, intuitive, regional cuisine using fresh, seasonal ingredients from local organic market gardeners. Scents from the garrigue, Camargue and Mediterranean, flanked by homemade sourdough bread made with heritage wheat. Warm welcome and an exquisite shady patio.

Name: Maison Vanobel
Description: In this peaceful village on the Gulf of Morbihan, this old crêperie has been given a new vocation by Sophie Coulombel and Rémi Vanoverschelde, both of whom honed their skills in some top-tier establishments. The first dining area looks onto the open kitchen; the second is laid out in a light-filled extension – the contemporary decor is inviting, as is the overall ambience. In the kitchen, Rémi makes full use of the large period fireplace for his wood-fired cooking, including barbacoa tacos, langoustine and confit pork ssam and sheep's cheese bao – all made with meticulously sourced ingredients. The restaurant also doubles as a tea room.

Name: Maison Vermer
Description: In a spruce house a stone’s throw from Rochebonne beach, rather than a Dutch painter, you will find a chef whose culinary ambition is to unite land and sea (hence the pun: “ver(t)”/green for the land and “mer”/sea for the… sea!). In his open-plan kitchen, he works with locally sourced produce, delivering well-balanced dishes. Market-fresh fare, sensibly priced lunchtime menu, more ambitious in the evenings.

Name: Maison Vidal - La Table gastronomique
Description: In an elegant and modern setting, Aurélien Vidal delivers ambitious cuisine that showcases both the terroir and premium ingredients, eg langoustines from the Brittany coast, line-caught meagre, veal "des Monts du Velay". There is also a fine selection of local cheeses. Aurélie, who is also in charge of desserts, is a pleasant and attentive hostess.

Name: Maison de Bacon
Description: Le Bâcon, an Antibes institution since 1948, has been transformed into the Maison de Bâcon. In the kitchens, Nicolas Davouze, formerly of Bocuse and Le Bristol, celebrates the house's signature dishes (such as rockfish soup, bouillabaisse, millefeuille), alongside a fine selection of fish grilled over a wood fire. Splendid view of the sea.

Name: Maison du Luxembourg
Description: Just a short stroll from the European institutions, this contemporary establishment champions the bounty of Luxembourg's terroir. It has become something of a local culinary beacon, as the large numbers of regulars bear witness. An international crowd flocks here to sample a banquet of culinary treats, frequently sourced from the province of Wallonia, among which seasonal specialties like asparagus and wild game. Slick seamless table service and the insightful tips of sommelier Vincent. The traditional score is adapted to the urban palates of the capital’s diners with a light touch and a dusting of exoticism, without sacrificing the core flavour. The chef may warm us up in winter with quickly seared scallops served on a bed of finely diced Jerusalem artichoke and celeriac, flanked by a subtly spicy celery cream and a squash cream.

Name: Maiz
Address: Al Bujairi Terrace, Diriyah, Riyadh, 13711, Saudi Arabia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,No alcohol served,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Nestled in historic Diriyah, known as the birthplace of Saudi Arabia, this Saudi restaurant boasts specialities originating from the country’s 13 provinces. Dishes like the lamb mantu (steamed dumplings), mandi lamb shoulder and freshly baked breads served with dips and local honey are delivered with obvious pride. To get the full experience, opt for one of their tasting menus known as the Maiz Experience – one offers six courses, another has eight and the last has 12.

Name: Maizajo
Address: Fernando Montes De Oca 113, Condesa, Cuauhtémoc, 06140, Mexico
Description: While their downstairs taqueria is standing room only, upstairs at Maizajo, diners are encouraged to pull up a chair. There is a clear industrial chic aesthetic to this dining room, where I-beams stand in for legs at metal tables and chairs are made from heavy rebar.You'll be greeted with some tostadas and a spicy habanero and pepita salsa at your table as you peruse Chef Santiago Muñoz Moctezuma's menu. Top picks include an oven-roasted blue corn tostada topped with avocado puree and sliced raw yellowfin tuna in a black sesame oil and soy dressing, as well as the tamal de boda. This vegetarian corn tamal filled with stewed poblano chile, leeks, and chard in an achiote, tomato and habanero salsa is topped with thinly sliced tubers for a dish that is equal parts sweet and earthy.

Name: Majestic
Address: Marina One, The Heart (East Tower) #04-01, 5 Straits View, 018935, Singapore
Description: Laid out beneath a glass roof, the airy dining area overlooks a garden. The food, which draws on modern techniques and time-honoured traditions, is exquisite in both taste and appearance. The claypot chicken with glutinous rice wine, ginger and wood ear fungus boasts silky, free-range meat and spellbinding aromas. The business clientele can opt for items in individual servings. Booking a week ahead recommended.

Name: Majka
Description: Husband-and-wife team Alex Sherry and Chutharat Sae Tong are the driving force behind this charming neighborhood spot, which has risen to the forefront of the Sacramento pizza scene thanks to excellent ingredient-driven pies with naturally leavened crusts. The standout offering is an ever-changing daily creation highlighting seasonal toppings—as in the inspired combination of white asparagus, English peas, and ramps with peppery pecorino Calcagno. Better yet, Friday and Saturday evenings come with specials like lemony Ora king salmon crudo, crisp-skinned roast chicken, and skillfully made agnolotti with a silky filling of fava beans and mint. An exceptional assortment of natural wines (notably, grower Champagnes) further gilds the lily.

Name: Majorelle
Description: Named after the vibrant botanical garden in Marrakesh, this Moroccan restaurant, set in an impressive five-storey building boasting a balconied frontage, certainly won’t disappoint. All the Moroccan greats are here, from pastilla and briouats to zaalouk and tajines, and Chef Saad imports his spices directly, so his dishes burst with authentic combinations of spicy and sweet. Sharing is a given, but maybe not when it comes to the delicious jawhara (crisp layered pastry filled with orange blossom cream). The fresh mint tea is a must-try, delivered by a warm, friendly team.

Name: Mak Kee (May Ka Mansion)
Address: Shop 1, May Ka Mansion, 21 Fort Street, North Point, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: This shop serves Shanghainese delicacies made fresh daily, such as pot-stickers, pan-fried pork buns and sour and hot noodle soup. Scallion pancakes are available from 3pm until they run out.

Name: Makorè
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Makorè today tells the story of over a decade of evolution, a journey born in close partnership with the neighbouring fishmonger’s and always deeply connected to the sea. Over time, the experience has been refined with consistency, supported by a thoughtful kitchen and an ongoing exploration of seafood as its central ingredient. In the elegant dining room, with views onto the brigade at work, the experience is divided between an à la carte offering – devoted entirely to fish, shellfish and vegetables – and a six-course tasting menu, the current synthesis of the restaurant’s philosophy. The cuisine speaks a contemporary language of balance and restraint, with light, well-judged forays towards the East: from the sashimi and marinated fish platters to fresh pasta buttons with katsuobushi, through to marinated sturgeon with an Asian-style sauce and black sesame mayonnaise. The pairings are devised with rigour, always in service of the essential purity of flavour. Before the sweet finale, room is made for a selection of Italian and international cheeses, both fresh and aged, adding a further gourmet note to the journey. The service stands out for its precision and attentiveness, with a special mention for sommelier Isacco Giuliani.

Name: Makoto San
Address: Rua Leandro Dupré 108, São Paulo, 04025-010, Brazil
Description: Fancy a little trip to Japan? Ring the doorbell at the entrance of this spot, and you can make that dream come true — no jet lag required. The moment you step into this extremely simple, rustic-minimalist, and unpretentious space, you are in the hands of chef Helio Makoto Yamashita, a sushi master who has refined his omakase menu over the years, drawing on outstanding technique and the exceptional quality of the fish he works with. There are a handful of tables, generally small, but the best seat in the house is at the counter, where you can watch up close the preparation of both the sushi and the sashimi. Details that make all the difference? As you enjoy your meal, the chef celebrates the singular culture of Meibutsu Ryouri — the love and respect for Japan's regional specialities — enthusiastically sharing fascinating stories about the ingredients he uses and anecdotes from his nearly 10 years living in Japan... Live the experience!

Name: Mala Hierba
Description: If you like grilled dishes and feel like experiencing a new way to enjoy them, we recommend you to go to Mala Hierba, a bistro where sincerity is the order of the day and they make you feel at home. Chef Lester López, originally from Guatemala but professionally trained in both the Canary Islands and the Basque Country, has created a suggestive and quite varied menu, with good options for quick bites, dishes from the Mediterranean pantry (his Vega Baja artichokes with truffled potato parmentier are wonderful), homemade cocas baked on the spot... and a special section dedicated to grilled meats and fish, with the curious detail that here they work with a Japanese kamado.

Name: Mala Hiza
Description: Mala Hiža – literally the “Little House” – has a fascinating story: the oak building dating from 1887, originally situated near Zagreb, was carefully dismantled and painstakingly rebuilt in 1997 within an old abandoned orchard. Today it is a warm and romantic family-run restaurant, where the chef-patron celebrates the cuisine of the region through a seasonal approach and a sound selection of local wines. Among the dishes: filled pastas, meats such as beef and lamb, and, to conclude, gibanica, the traditional layered cake with cheese, eggs and pumpkin.

Name: Malai
Address: GF, Menara Ample West, 6 Jalan Puncak, Kuala Lumpur, 50250, Malaysia
Description: Every detail, from the imported tableware to the authentic Thai dining experience, has been pondered and puzzled over. Malai relocated to this venue at the end of 2022 to offer greater comfort and more spacious dining on two floors. It’s regularly packed with office workers, especially at lunchtime. The mostly Thai team of chefs conjures up a traditional Thai menu with modern twists. Don’t miss the tom yum soup or the gaeng keaw waan (green curry).

Name: Maleducat
Description: This restaurant, located just a few steps from the San Antoni market, has made a name for itself thanks its mix of cuisine from the sea and the mountains. Here, they like to say that they create food for “nonconformist gourmets”, for whom they have created varied cuisine with a modern touch and an impressive array of dishes and tapas, along with daily specials and main dishes made for sharing. We particularly enjoyed the rice dish with red Palamós shrimp tartare, shrimp head emulsion and pig’s trotter carpaccio, a dish that pays homage to the legendary Els Tinars restaurant in Llagostera. There’s also a menu entitled “At your service, chef!”

Name: Malenco
Address: Via Funivia 22, Chiesa in Valmalenco, 23023, Italy
Description: This typical family-run restaurant serves typical mountain cuisine, although a few fish dishes also feature on the menu. Highlights include game, cheese and the delicious homemade pizzoccheri pasta. Ask the young son for recommendations from the wine list, which includes labels from Valtellina.

Name: Malga Roncac
Description: In a former Alpine dairy on the slopes overlooking Moena, romance continues in the wood-clad dining room complete with fireplace, complemented by a small panoramic veranda. Yet the cuisine here is no mere afterthought: hearty, predominantly mountain fare, almost exclusively meat, is of excellent quality. With limited seating, reservations are recommended.

Name: Malhadinha Nova
Address: Herdade da Malhadinha Nova, Albernoa, 7800-601, Portugal
Description: Its location, far from all the city’s bustle, is extremely pleasant, and the calm becomes perceptible as you approach. The restaurant sits within Herdade da Malhadinha Nova, an agricultural estate surrounded by vineyards and nature and, at times… a Blue peafowl wandering the meadows. It is also a perfect refuge for wine lovers. The menu bears the signature of the German chef Joachim Koerper, who makes use of ingredients produced on the estate to present Alentejo cuisine allied to contemporary techniques. Our recommendation? Alentejo gazpacho prepared with a variety of garden tomatoes, fresh cheese and mint, PDO Alentejo beef from Malhadinha prepared in two stages and served with vegetables and a vinaigrette underscoring the region’s flavours and, for the grand finale, Mel da Herdade (estate honey), super delicate and with a surprising technical level!

Name: Malinowa
Address: Grand Hotel, ul. Piotrkowska 72, Łódź, 90-105, Poland
Description: The Grand Hotel has been hosting visitors to Łódź for over 130 years and its former ballroom is now home to this delightful restaurant. Fusing old-world charm with a striking contemporary interior, it has an elegant, restful vibe and is run with a smile by the welcoming team. The menu is full of bright, fresh and well-crafted dishes, such as the homemade linguine with a rich bisque and plenty of crab meat, and the classic rum baba with a well-judged punch.

Name: Malix
Address: Av. Isaac Newton 104, Polanco, Miguel Hildalgo, 11560, Mexico
Description: This Polanco spot offers sidewalk tables, a bar area with a U-shaped counter, and seating at tables in a rear dining room where the kitchen is on display. Throughout, the room boasts a creamy color palette with latte lacquered tables, beige leather banquettes, and light wood- accented concrete walls.Malix's free-roaming menu incorporates Mexican cuisine as well as global influences in items like pâté with madeleines and pickles; a selection of local cheeses; and house-made Lao-style sausage. There is a respect for sustainable gastronomy, as the menu highlights a long list of local producers. The grilled duck breast is a worthwhile recommendation, presented with crisped skin, wedges of figs and beets, plated with a house mole, and accompanied by a stack of excellent tortillas.

Name: Malverleys
Address: Sungrove Farm, East End, RG20 0AF, United Kingdom
Description: Tucked away in what is surely one of England’s prettiest hamlets, dining here is like stumbling upon a hidden slice of paradise. Surrounded by beautifully kept grounds but also their own farm, the restaurant sits inside a gorgeous farmhouse alongside a bakery and shop. Take your seat in the dining room in full view of the open kitchen and feast on the seasonal dishes that make great use of the wood-fired oven. Grilled spatchcock quail with cherries from the estate is a prime example, succulent and full of gamey flavour.

Name: Malá Dvorana
Description: In a side wing of the historical Grandhotel Pupp, this restaurant is accommodated in a magnificent hall. Elaborate mouldings on the ceiling and walls and an imposing crystal chandelier are a stylish throwback to bygone days; decorated with gold leaf, the modern glass bar in the middle of the room is also noteworthy. The contemporary dishes include pan-fried mackerel, sliced beetroot, leek mousse, honey, or chicken ballotine, Jerusalem artichoke, sautéed kale, chicken demi-glace.

Name: Mama Fatma
Description: On name alone, you can bet that nobody leaves this colorful restaurant hungry. Kebabs charred over glowing coals, meats spinning on a spit and fluffy, dome-like rounds of pita cooked in a wood-burning oven are served here in abundance. Such is the appeal of this local favorite that has fed families well for years. In fact, it’s not uncommon to see large groups huddled around a feast that covers every corner of the table. The menu is expansive but consider starting with a mixed platter of dips like baba ghanoush, pembe sultan and ezme. Tiny poached beef dumplings coated in a garlicky yogurt sauce (kayseri mantisi) could be a meal of their own. There’s rarely room for dessert, but there’s always a place for hot tea.

Name: Mama Konstantina
Description: Following on from Konstantin Filippou and O boufés, chef Konstantin Filippou has established another culinary hotspot in Vienna – this time in the city's 19th district. In a high-ceilinged space with a snazzy open kitchen, diners sit together at a large communal table in the thick of the action. At lunchtime (Mon-Fri), there is a short menu, also available to pick up and take away; in the evening a wonderful à la carte selection awaits you. First-class ingredients go into creating modern Greek fare, in a nod to the chef's roots. The congenial, charming service includes helpful wine recommendations. You may be interested to know that the owner named his restaurant after an olive farmer friend – and inspiration – of his, who hails from Kalamata.

Name: Mamacita
Address: Forbestown Road, Bonifacio Global City, Taguig - Metro Manila, The Philippines
Description: Mamacita brings the fiesta spirit to Forbes Town with its Día de Muertos decor, lively music and vibrant late-night energy. Kick things off downstairs with tequila at the bar. Upstairs, settle in for tacos, quesadillas and hearty dishes such as beef asado – perfect for sharing. Colourful calaveras and bold flavours set the tone, and guacamole, pico de gallo and chilli con carne round out a menu rooted in tradition. A slice of Mexico in the heart of Manila!

Name: Mamma - Les Roches Brunes
Description: Clinging to a rocky outcrop, Les Roches Brunes is a feast for the eye: the hotel overlooks the sea and offers a breathtaking view of the Château royal de Collioure opposite. In the bohemian-chic restaurant, the gourmet score celebrates local produce. You will taste creative, hearty Catalan recipes with a weakness for seafood: Palamos prawns, mushrooms and a coffee emulsion; arroz seco, baby squid and blue crab stock; fillet of dentex cooked on a plancha served with a seafood suquet (sort of Catalan fish stew).

Name: Mamma Orso
Description: Situated in the lively Nomentano quarter, to the north-east of the city and behind Piazza Bologna — not a tourist area, but rather one of Rome’s student districts — this youthful operation offers fragrant and unfussy Italian regional cookery, reinterpreted with evident passion. The recipes traverse the Italian peninsula from north to south, before being reinterpreted with a personal touch: the traditional Mantuan pumpkin tortello, for example, becomes a slice of roasted pumpkin with sour butter, curry sauce, licorice, and amaretti.While many dishes retain an almost home-cooked feel, there is no shortage of imagination: the barley crème caramel, served with crushed salted peanuts, is excellent. All of this unfolds within a single, intimate and welcoming dining room, possessed of a charming vintage spirit.

Name: Mamma Rosa
Address: Via XXIV Maggio 1, San Polo d'Enza, 42020, Italy
Description: On the outskirts of town in a verdant area near a sports center, with convenient parking, warm hospitality, and family management, this restaurant focuses all its efforts on delivering seafood cuisine based on excellent market selections. Dishes are often paired with vegetables, some grown in their own garden, following the most authentic Mediterranean style.

Name: Mammaròssa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At this restaurant, owner-chef Franco Franciosi focuses on the Abruzzo in dishes which are both traditional and modern. The cuisine showcases the best ingredients from the region, including home-grown vegetables from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden and excellent bread made with solina wheat (typical of the Apennines), amid a decor that focuses on sustainability. Daniela looks after guests front of house, offering recommendations from the short yet carefully chosen wine list.

Name: Mammà Isola di Capri
Description: Situated within the multi-functional Sondo building (also home to a museum, offices and exhibition spaces), this large restaurant decorated in contemporary, post-industrial style provides the backdrop for chef Raffaele Amitrano’s Mediterranean cuisine which is strongly influenced by the flavours of Campania. His plin pasta dish pays tribute to the region and is particularly interesting thanks to ingredients such as cacio cheese, pepper and raw prawns. Make sure you arrive early if you want to visit the building and maybe even take advantage of the large sharing table.

Name: Mamy Louise
Description: This elegant edifice, built out of wood, glass and steel, is home to a brasserie, a cocktail bar with a terrace, lounges and meeting rooms. The equally varied menu ranges from shrimp fritters and sole meunière to veal kidneys and ossobuco in a lineup of Franco-Belgian inspiration, dotted with a few Italian classics, all of which is underscored by a love of cooking and generous helpings. There is something for everyone at Mamy Louise.

Name: Maménakané
Description: On the other side of the River Têt, in a residential neighbourhood at a slight remove from the city centre, this restaurant puts its best foot forward with understated decor in a Japanese or Scandinavian style. Self-taught sommelier Kotaro Ike's discerning wine list has been curated to accompany the single multi-course set menu. Chef Maiko Ike (his wife), who trained in Kyoto before moving to L'Axel in Fontainebleau, crafts a clear and subtle menu: salt-marinated and flame-seared yellowtail, steamed sea bream with yuzu, and French toast with olive oil and citrus fruits. In this balanced cuisine, vegetables, seafood and seasoning come together in perfect harmony.

Name: Mamó
Address: Harbour House, Harbour Road, Howth, D13 E9H9, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An experienced couple run this friendly bistro located in a pleasant spot on Howth seafront; start with a drink in the ground-floor bar before heading up to the bistro-style dining room. Irish ingredients are the bedrock of the menu, including Boyne Valley cheeses, Winetavern Farm pork from Wicklow and plenty of seafood from the harbour just over the road. This produce is fashioned into fresh, flavoursome dishes that are carefully cooked and neatly presented. Stick around for dessert, as it’s likely to be a highlight.

Name: Man Ho
Address: GF, Marriott Hotel Manila, 2 Resort Drive, Newport World Resorts, Pasay - Metro Manila, The Philippines
Description: Man Ho delivers authentic Cantonese cuisine in a grand, modern setting. At the helm in the kitchen, the Hong Kong chef crafts dishes such as char siu, braised abalone, Hong Kong-style crispy chicken and a rich double-boiled soup. Dim sum at lunch is a highlight. He also concocts some appetising original dishes incorporating premium Western ingredients, from caviar to truffles. You can book one of five private rooms if you prefer a more discreet dining experience.

Name: Man Ho · Jing
Address: 27F, Marriott Nanjing South Hotel, 1519 Shuanglong Avenue, Jiangning, Nanjing, Chinese Mainland
Description: Perched atop a hotel tower, the restaurant commands 270° views of the city and the lake; the room is adorned with modern, stylised Chinese motifs. The menu showcases creative Huaiyang cooking with a unique touch – the classic braised pigeon stuffed with bird's nest is now doused in a black truffle sauce. Thanks to his extensive experience, the head chef's meticulous skills are indisputable. Call to ask about items that need to be pre-ordered.

Name: Man Kee Cart Noodles (Sham Shui Po)
Address: 121 Fuk Wing Street, Sham Shui Po, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: The number of topping choices can be overwhelming, but Chinese chive dumplings and Swiss chicken wings are especially good. Fancy a spicy kick? Try the house-made chilli sauce over your noodles.

Name: Man-u
Description: Man-u’s ingenious oden, which borrows from other Japanese cuisines, is a whirlwind of flavour changes. Items are selected from a large pot and paired with condiments and broth to bring different flavours to the fore. Beef sinew is cooked with green onions; octopus is paired with unripe pepper. Clams, wakame seaweed with bamboo shoots, and pike conger with matsutake mushrooms are served as soup dishes. Lettuce, tomato and figs dressed with starchy dashi soup stock sauce provide interesting alternatives. Painstaking preparation results in an oden with a unique finish.

Name: ManO2
Description: Just outside the historic center, this elegant restaurant welcomes guests in contemporary spaces with a pleasant outdoor terrace at the entrance. The cuisine, rooted in local tradition but interpreted with creativity and technique, offers seafood and land dishes, with premium cuts of meat prepared on the grill standing out. Two tasting menus of five and eight courses are available, along with an extensive, carefully curated à la carte. Be sure to try the flavorful venison fillet with black cabbage cream, blackcurrant sauce, and caramelized shallots.

Name: Mana
Address: 420 Mu 21, Sri Chan Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: After working for years at Thai-Chinese restaurants in Bangkok, chef-owner Mana returned home to open his own outlet. He’s now been serving flavoursome Thai-Chinese-style seafood dishes that are easy on the pocketbook for over a decade. Inside his restaurant’s one-storey white building are two dining areas, one with AC and another open-air one. The oyster omelette and crispy salad with fish maw, shrimp and cashews are recommended.

Name: Manao
Description: Enter Manao, and you will be greeted with exotic vibes bolstered by seek décor and an array of art objects brought directly from Thailand. Its prix-fixe menus consist of multiple dishes in small portions, allowing guests to enjoy a variety of plates in one meal. The kitchen does an excellent job of presenting authentic Thai cuisine with its characteristic spiciness. Another appeal of this spot is that the meat and seafood are grilled to order over charcoal. Manao means “lime” in Thai, and its fare is as refreshing as its name.

Name: Mandarin Grill + Bar
Address: 1F, Mandarin Oriental Hotel, 5 Connaught Road Central, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: (The restaurant is temporarily closed.) Perfect for power lunches and romantic dinner dates, this is the place for updated steakhouse classics. There is something for everyone on the menu. Raw oysters on the half shell from around the world start the meal on a decadent note, followed by quality meat from the U.S., New Zealand and Australia, chargrilled to perfection. The classic tasting menu experience also features French favourites like dover sole Véronique and tournedos Rossini.

Name: Mandu
Address: 453 K St. NW, Washington, DC, 20001, USA
Description: Credit to Chef Yesoon Lee and her son Danny for showing this city that Korean cuisine is more than just bibimbap and barbecue. You can trace their steps back to 2006 when they opened the original Mandu in Dupont Circle, now reborn as Anju after an unfortunate fire in 2017. Fans who miss the original can still find pointed, fiery stews and broths at this Mount Vernon location, which sports soaring ceilings and a long bar. From plump, steamed beef and pork mandu to vibrant banchan, this is homey cooking that warms the spirit. And regardless of the weather, no visit would be complete without gamjatang, a bubbling-hot soup featuring tender, bone-in pork ribs and potatoes swimming in a devilishly red broth fired up with gochugaru and perilla seeds.

Name: Manero
Description: A unique restaurant that has recreated the ambience of a traditional grocery store, where you can enjoy delicate tapas, Iberian hams, salted dishes, high-quality tinned products and even seafood, many of which are packaged ready to take away.

Name: MangasVerdes
Description: A somewhat atypical gastro-bar located closed to the city’s cathedral. The à la carte features a choice of contemporary and fusion dishes and is complemented by a tasting menu and an impressive choice of wines by the glass.

Name: Manger & Dormir sur la Plage
Description: This modern spacious seafront restaurant boasts a panoramic terrace, ideal for sunset snapshots, and indoors, a suspended fireplace for warmth during colder months. The cheerful, spot-on service team celebrates a seafood-centric menu sourced from local fish auctions and the emblematic oysters of the Gillardeau family, who owns the establishment, as well as a fine lineup of meat dishes. The chef adds an exotic touch courtesy of spicy seasonings and influences from further afield. Stay for longer in one of four suites which have a balcony or a terrace with a sea view.

Name: Mangiare Bere Uomo Donna
Description: She’s from Hong Kong, while he’s from Suzzara – together this couple run this welcoming restaurant where their international focus extends from the dishes which feature on the menu to the wine selection and the couple’s love for applied arts. Once seated, you can either choose traditional fare, including a few delicious fish dishes, or you can be tempted by the decidedly Asian options. Whatever you decide, one thing’s for sure – authenticity and seasonal, locally sourced ingredients are guaranteed.

Name: Mango Bay
Description: Tucked inside a Fort Greene brownstone, the look hints at the islands (hello, floral wallpaper) blended with city chic (leather booths and exposed brick walls). Casual and welcoming with a new take on Afro-Caribbean cuisine, it's the sort of place you want to go again and again with friends. Snack on starters like a char-grilled octopus tentacle with jerk gremolata over braised collards tossed with burrata, then move on to main dishes like braised oxtail with roasted rainbow carrots. Sides like spicy-sweet mango chow or tender, fried plantains round out the meal in the very best way.

Name: Manhatta
Address: 28 Liberty St., New York, NY, 10005, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Set in an iconic skyscraper in the heart of the Financial District, this stylish dining room possesses all the allure and magic of a penthouse. Indeed, some 60 floors up, a talented team bucks the trend with cooking that is as impressive as the views. Reflecting the bounty of the seasons, a flexible, contemporary tasting menu tempts with diverse choices each step of the way. Soigne in look and bold in taste, past highlights include Jonah crab with coins of asparagus, paper-thin slices of apple and sorrel as well as glazed Sweetbreads with parsnips. The beverage program is complete through and through with a deep wine list bursting with gems as well as a smart cocktail program that meets every need.

Name: Manhattan Beach Post
Address: 1142 Manhattan Ave., Manhattan Beach, CA, 90266, USA
Description: Just a stone's throw from Manhattan Beach Pier, this restaurant is big and buzzing. It's almost always packed, especially with plenty of young families, and they're all here for a taste of Chef/co-owner David LeFevre’s globally minded creations with a clear California point of view. Head-on Caledonian blue prawns ajillo atop diced potatoes with saffron mayonnaise. Beeler's Farm pork porterhouse is grilled and accompanied by Asian pear kimchi and a black mustard sauce. Everything revolves around gathering, conversing and sharing, and portions lean small, so plan your ordering as a group to explore a majority of the menu.

Name: Manifest
Address: 4a Watkinson Street, Liverpool, L1 0AG, United Kingdom
Description: In Liverpool's regenerated Baltic Triangle district, you'll find this restaurant situated on the ground floor of a converted former warehouse. An open-plan kitchen dominates the room and there are counter seats for those who wish to be close to the action. Carefully cooked, flavourful modern British dishes are available either as an à la carte or a seasonally influenced tasting menu. Whatever you choose, accompany it with some wine from the well-presented list, with each bottle available by the glass.

Name: Manjar dos Leitões
Address: Aldeamento Santana Rua 5, nº 51, Póvoa de Varzim, 4490-007, Portugal
Description: Who said you can’t enjoy a proper Bairrada-style suckling pig in Póvoa de Varzim, just like the ones served in central Portugal? At this establishment, right by National Road 13, you can enjoy the traditional leitão, here called Leitão assado a manjar, suckling pig roast, with crisp skin, wafer-thin chips, a generous salad and a flavoursome leitão sauce. And it would be impossible not to mention the other specialities that round out the menu, such as Bife de vazio à brasa, grilled bavette steak; the classic Bacalhau à lagareiro, salt cod with olive oil and garlic; Arroz de pato à antiga, old-style duck rice; or the robust Feijoada de Leitão, a hearty suckling-pig bean stew. The venue offers spacious, light-filled dining rooms with restrained décor and contemporary touches, plus a well-stocked wine cellar to accompany the treats. You can also order the suckling pig to take away!

Name: Manna
Description: Hidden away in a quiet district, this semi-pedestrianised area comes to life in the evening thanks to the restaurants nearby. The bar at Manna serves excellent cocktails, with a few tables outside on the street, while inside the new, elegant and minimalist-style dining room you’ll enjoy personalised cuisine that skilfully combines tradition and creativity. Perfect for a romantic dinner or a business lunch, with a faster menu available for the latter. Among the desserts, we highly recommend the delicious and not-to-be-missed Tarte Tatin.

Name: Mano
Description: A quiet street in a residential area, a contemporary bistro and a buzzy vibe paint the portrait of Maximilien Kuzniar’s fine dining haunt. Ceviche of seabass, mashed sweet potato and leche de tigre sauce; egg parfait, purée of carrots and ginger: a festival of forthright flavours crafted from wholesome seasonal ingredients. The lunch set menus are excellent value for money, while the evening dining options are more creative and ambitious.

Name: Mano Libera
Description: Located on a tree-lined, twinkly lit residential street with a neighborhood feel, this restaurant with strong Neapolitan roots offers an array of both modern and classical Italian dishes. Begin with a basket of their fresh breads, including rustic grissini and focaccia, served with creamy house-made ricotta. Move on to the gamberi and calamari fritti, properly enrobed in a double crispy batter, with a spritz of Amalfi lemon and a Dijon mustard dipping sauce. Pastas are the highlight here, particularly the Linguine alla Nerano — a fine base of Gragnano pasta, perfectly al dente, enveloped in light creamy sauce with a mix of fresh and dried zucchini and rounded out with Parmesan foam and plenty of freshly ground pepper. Don't ignore dessert, as their pistachio ice cream is truly special.

Name: Manohar’s Delhi Palace
Address: 581 Azusa Way, La Puente, CA, 91744, USA
Description: Manohar's Delhi Palace is a mainstay thanks to their delicious Punjabi cuisine, and there's a welcoming vibe about this place, where the waitstaff is especially friendly and attentive. Indicative of its north Indian focus, the food here leans on the milder side, so don't expect an onslaught of spices. Order à la carte or go all in on the tandoori dinner but be sure to get an order of the samosas, fried to a perfect crisp with that comforting filling of potatoes and peas. Chicken tikka masala features a generous amount of tender and juicy chicken that's skewered and seared before being added to the vibrant sauce. For dessert, the gulab jamun is a clear winner.

Name: Manoir de la Pommeraie
Address: 1770 route de Tinchebray, L'Auvère, Vire Normandie, 14500, France
Description: This 18C building, whose conservatory overlooks wooded grounds planted with hundred-year-old trees, is run by a Franco-Japanese couple who continues to knock the socks off our tastebuds. While Masako pours her talents into pastries, Julien finetunes his exquisite, flawlessly balanced culinary score: roast monkfish, girolles, mussels and hay or lightly seared tuna in spices, aubergine and cucumber. Regional ingredients invariably take the limelight (Normandy beef, Cahagnes poultry, cheese from local farms and locally grown veggies) and the chef often waxes lyrical about his suppliers when he pops into the dining room, as is his wont.

Name: Mansou'
Description: Opened in the 1980s by Fatéma Hal and taken over by her daughter in 2021, Mansouria has moved from its historic address to start a new chapter on Rue de Charonne as Mansou'. Featuring traditional Moroccan objects and contemporary details, the decor combines warmth and modernity. The menu remains faithful to its origins: couscous, tajines, Moroccan pastries and mint tea reign supreme. The pepper briwattes are perfectly crispy, and the chicken tajine with olives and candied lemon is expertly made. Taste the flavours of Morocco in all their generous simplicity at this sincere, unpretentious restaurant.

Name: Manta
Address: The Cape Hotel, Carr. Federal 1 Km. 5, Fracc. A, L-21, Cabo San Lucas, 23456, Mexico
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking
Description: Set within the Cape Hotel in a stunning space that frames picture-perfect views of Cabo's famed Lands End, this modern dining room under Enrique Olvera's umbrella isn't just impressing with its good looks. The contemporary Mexican cuisine is punctuated by clear Peruvian and Japanese influences. Offered as a tasting menu and à la carte, expect bold dishes from a kitchen that's unafraid of bringing the heat. Begin with sashimi or a Peruvian ceviche before savoring a refreshing melon salad with diced honeydew and cantaloupe in a leche de tigre fueled by yuzu. Next, a sweet potato with a tamarind and soy crust in an almond mole is at once simple and elegant. From Korean fried chicken and tempura fish tacos to cochinita served in bao buns, Asian accents run from beginning to end on the à la carte menu.

Name: Mantesino
Description: The Naples-born chef, who used to be an engineer, has enthusiastically donned an apron (mantesino in Italian) and opened this small bistro in a street near the Église Saint-Aubin. He gives pride of place to his roots by tapping into the culinary traditions of Southern Italy, from Campania to Puglia. A far cry from stereotypical Italian fare, his no-nonsense bistro cuisine wins diners over by drawing solely on flavoursome, meticulously selected ingredients: mortadella from Bologna, hazelnuts from Piedmont, Ibaïama pork, as well as meat from Aveyron and vegetables from local growers. Uplifting!

Name: Mantis
Description: Looking for a casual and minimalist atmosphere? In L'Antiga Esquerra de l'Eixample lies a restaurant with an industrial aesthetic and, beyond the tables, surprises with two oriental-inspired bars, one for cold dishes and the other for hot. The young chefs at the helm, Toni Solans and David Romero, offer an eclectic and international cuisine with heavy Asian and Catalan influences. The simple and concise menu is complemented by an economical Fórmula Mediodía (3 courses) and a good Tasting Menu (11 courses). A particular highlight? The skate was cooked to perfection and the accompanying béarnaise sauce, with a spicy touch from the peanuts, was tremendously unctuous.

Name: Mantra
Description: Behind the black glass façade on a street with a wealth of eateries, this intimate restaurant is presided over by chef Manogeran Shasitharan. He invites his guests on a culinary escapade in the form of a multi-course tasting menu combining French produce with spicy Malaysian touches – a nod to his heritage. Fragrant sea-fresh cuisine.

Name: Manuel Cozinha Portuguesa
Address: 90 Rua de Femão Mendes Pinto, Taipa, Macau
Description: After a spot of renovation for cosier feel, authenticity and hospitality remain the establishment’s hallmark. The friendly owner-chef has revamped the traditional Portuguese menu, now arranged by key ingredient. Using only top-notch seasonal produce, most dishes are barbecued traditionally. Grilled codfish and fried rice with squid ink are the must-tries. Check out the daily specials on the blackboard before ordering.

Name: Manuela
Address: 907 E. 3rd St., Los Angeles, CA, 90013, USA
Description: Tucked inside the multi-use Hauser & Wirth Arts Complex with an open-plan kitchen and conceptual art, Manuela has a creative, contemporary look and feel. The cooking is strong, with a Southern leaning, and features a menu with a heavy leaning toward local ingredients (including from their own garden). Choose a cocktail from their classic list, all elevated with house-made bitters and tonics. Warm, flaky biscuits with aged country ham and whipped butter are a must before a main course like their roasted duck breast with nicely rendered, crispy skin served over a bed of smoked soubise and paired with sliced yellow peaches. End the meal with one of their desserts, like their take on s'mores or their Harry's Berries and genmaicha shortbread ice cream.

Name: Manuelina
Description: Very few restaurants in Liguria can compete with the long gastronomic tradition of this restaurant, which was named after its original owner back in 1885! It was Manuelina herself who made the typical focaccia of Recco famous, offering it as a dish in her tavern. The fourth generation of the family now runs the business with the same passion and enthusiasm – part of the building houses the typical Focacceria, where family traditions are kept alive, while the other is home to the restaurant itself (even here the legendary and highly recommended focaccia is on the menu) with its round tables. The cuisine is traditional yet with modern touches and based on Ligurian ingredients with a focus on fish (although meat also features).

Name: Manzanilla
Address: Teniente Azueta 139 Recinto Portuario, Zona Centro, Ensenada, 22800, Mexico
Description: Manzanilla offers a truly worthwhile dining experience brought to you by chefs and partners Benito Molina and Solange Muris. A local favorite, the establishment feels like a world unto itself, located within a gated area and unwinding into a prettily arranged courtyard area and spaciously arranged dining rooms anchored by an ornate, carved wood bar. Speaking of drinks, an extensive selection of classic cocktails is on offer, as well as wines from the Valle de Guadalupe.The dishes lean simple but remain elevated and refined, showcasing a mastery of flavor and impeccable quality with dishes like their arroz de mar with guajillo chili and a myriad of seafood. The meal is not complete without their daily rotating crème brûlée, perhaps adorned with fig leaves from their garden.

Name: Mao Su
Address: 43 Fudong Street, East District, Tainan, Taiwan
Description: Light wood furnishings, arched windows and a crackle effect wall combine to create a relaxed, modern space. Run by a Tainanese catering group, this restaurant is aimed at omnivorous diners who wish to reduce their carbon footprint by forgoing meat once in a while. The lacto-ovo-vegetarian dishes are loaded with Asian spices and condiments, such as satay, Sichuan pepper and kimchi. Try the classic stir-fried king oyster mushroom with basil.

Name: Maple & Ash
Address: 8 W. Maple St., Chicago, IL, 60610, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Credit cards not accepted,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Did someone say scene? Oh darling, that’s half the fun at Chicago’s buzziest steakhouse, Maple & Ash. Deep-set leather couches, clubby music and even a photo booth lend the multilevel marvel an irresistible party vibe.This restaurant is set to the soft glow emanating from the semi-open kitchen, where a wood-fired hearth lights up dry-aged steakhouse classics, cut to generous proportions. Seafood lovers will find plenty to mull over too, like a tangle of octopus and squid, prepared in the wood-fueled oven and served with dill yogurt, arugula and roasted potatoes. Then, a fire-roasted seafood tower is brought tableside, featuring lobster tail, scallops, Manila clams and king crab, all bathed in garlic butter, chili oil and served with house-made pasta.

Name: Mar'sel
Address: Terranea Resort, 100 Terranea Way, Rancho Palos Verdes, CA, 90275, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: At the end of the Palos Verdes Peninsula, find a windy road that meanders through the plush grounds of the Terranea Resort. Beautiful herb gardens are planted along the sidewalk leading you to Mar’sel, a blend of the Spanish and French words for sea and salt. Inside, breathtaking ocean views and a roaring fireplace take the chill off the evening breeze. A sense of opulence pervades everything here, including the superb service. Meals commence with a warm homemade English muffin that may have its own cult following. Every dish looks beautiful and well made, especially those cubes of supremely tender wagyu beef short ribs, with celery prepared four different ways. For dessert, caramel pot de crème is the house specialty, with ganache, cocoa nibs and flecks of sea salt.

Name: Mara
Address: 11 O'Connell Street, Waterford, X91 F304, Ireland
Description: What was formerly known as The Old Couch Café has been reborn as Mara, retaining its predecessor's quirky vibe and bijou space. Chef-Owner Luis Martin has both passion and ambition in abundance, largely working alone in the kitchen and serving his dishes in the cosy, well-lit room to just six tables. His well-balanced cooking incorporates locally foraged produce alongside a few influences from his native Spain, such as ajo blanco or cod buñuelo; the cep tiramisu, meanwhile, has become something of a signature.

Name: Maragoncello
Address: Via San Giovanni 1, località Vighizzolo, Montichiari, 25018, Italy
Description: An elegant, modern restaurant where excellent cuisine is served, with a strong emphasis on seafood. In the dishes of the Neapolitan-born chef, the vibrant colors and flavors of his native culinary tradition sometimes make a welcome appearance, alongside a few offerings inspired by the north.

Name: Marble 8
Address: 56F, Menara 3 Petronas, Persiaran KLCC, Kuala Lumpur City Centre, Kuala Lumpur, 50088, Malaysia
Description: It takes a few lift rides to get to Marble 8, but as soon as you set foot in the dining room, you know it’s all worthwhile. The stunning skyline with the Twin Towers in the foreground is the perfect backdrop for a sumptuous meal featuring top-quality halal-certified Wagyu and Angus beef straight from Australia. Premium cuts are dry- or wet-aged for at least 21 days for deep flavours and tender texture, and then grilled to perfection.

Name: Marc Lanteri
Description: Situated right next to the Fratelli Massucco winery, with which it shares its comfortable outdoor spaces as well as stunning views of the surrounding hills and vineyards, this restaurant is run by Marc Lanteri and Amy Bellotti, partners in life and work, who have chosen this setting for their new Piedmontese adventure. Their cuisine is full of individual character, with three tasting menus (including a vegetarian option featuring produce grown in their own garden) and dishes also available à la carte style. Local ingredients and recipes naturally take centre stage, always enhanced by small touches of colour and imagination. The wine list showcases the property’s own wines, as well as offering a choice of labels from elsewhere in Italy and further afield.

Name: Marcano
Description: This restaurant just a few steps from the Retiro park reflects the culinary passion of chef David Marcano, who trained alongside the San Sebastián-born maestro Juan Mari Arzak. In this contemporary space, enjoy innovative and contemporary dishes showcasing Basque touches, an international influence, plus a continual quest for flavour. The à la carte, complemented by a special lunchtime menu, includes several dishes for sharing (we particularly liked the spicy tuna tartare Mexican taco) and the option of ordering many of the dishes as half-plates. The chef can often be seen in the dining room talking with guests to personally check that everything is to their liking!

Name: Marcel
Address: 1170 Howell Mill Rd., Atlanta, GA, 30318, USA
Description: Here on the west side of town, take a step back in time at this vintage steakhouse named for French boxer, Marcel Cerdan. From the low lighting to the red leather banquette, Ford Fry has created a speakeasy-style space that checks all the boxes. It comes with a high price tag, certainly, but who cares when you're having this much fun? The menu features a few French and European elements in addition to classic dishes. Start with a salad or go big with steak tartare with bone marrow and sourdough. The many steaks include a bone-in côte de boeuf or 60-day dry-aged ribeye. Don't skimp on the sides with French leanings, including pommes aligot and pommes Dauphinoise. Keep things decadent through dessert with a slice of rich chocolate cake.

Name: Marcel
Address: 945 Madison Ave., New York, NY, 10021, USA
Description: Set within the restored Marcel Breuer building that once housed the Whitney Museum, Marcel is the elegant Uptown counterpart to La Mercerie from Chef Marie-Aude Rose and the Roman and Williams team. Walnut paneling, candlelight and views onto a sculpture garden create a distinctly Upper East Side atmosphere, and the menu leans heavily into French café and brasserie classics. A roast beef tartine with cornichons and dressed greens channels the spirit of a Left Bank café, while omelets, steaks au poivre and escargots round out the offering. Desserts, including warm madeleines, shouldn't be skipped.

Name: Marcela
Address: Plaza de San Marcelo 9, Leon, 24003, Spain
Description: Marcela boasts an outstanding location just a few metres from the Museo Casa Botines Gaudí. It features two dining spaces: an informal tapas option on the ground floor and a more sophisticated dining room upstairs - between the two is a striking glass floor adorned with a water feature. The cuisine here is based around ingredients of the highest quality, with a market menu that includes some dishes made to order (such as seafood or their famous Sirloin Wellington). They collaborate with the Auditorio Ciudad de León, so on Fridays and Saturdays there are usually live concerts with artists from the auditorium!

Name: Marcelin
Address: Piazzetta della Vecchia Segheria 1, Montà, 12046, Italy
Description: The dishes on the menu are often creative but usually maintain a link with the local area, its products and its recipes, imaginatively reinterpreted by the chef.

Name: Marcelle - Domaine de Verchant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: On the way into the Domaine de Verchant, Marcelle occupies contemporary premises, depicted by a light airy dining room and a stepped terrace with sweeping views of the surrounding countryside. The menus are inspired by local, seasonal produce, in particular from the restaurant’s own cottage garden.

Name: Marchese
Description: Located in a still-central area of the city, this restaurant is not a new opening but has recently reinvented its identity by entrusting the kitchen to a Roman chef with a solid background. The culinary offering maintains a classic structure, with a choice between a “surprise” tasting menu and an extensive à la carte selection. In the kitchen, local and national traditions intertwine, enriched by an international touch that translates into visually striking, colorful creations that above all deliver on the palate. The dishes, both meat and fish, follow the seasonality of ingredients, with particular attention to vegetable pairings. Among the standout offerings: the pumpkin risotto with blue prawn, red berry umami, and Caesar salad crisp, a successful balance of technique, flavor, and creativity.

Name: Marché Moderne
Address: 7862 E. Pacific Coast Hwy., Newport Beach, CA, 92657, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Chefs/owners Florent and Amelia Marneau deliver modern dishes with hints of French classics. This is a stunning, elegant and sumptuous establishment that feels and tastes familiar yet original. The cooking follows suit from the glassed-in kitchen with soft globe lighting to the fire engine-red Berkel that's ready to slice their superb charcuterie. The classics, from coq au vin to the poached Maine lobster tail flambéed in Courvoisier and paired with a quenelle of scallop, are perfectly on point. End with a cheese plate or a traditional baba au rum. Handcrafted cocktails mirror the bounty of the seasons and may feature a host of aged spirits or enjoy the well-priced wine pairings.

Name: Marco Polo
Description: In the heart of Dubrovnik's historic center, this intimate, elegant restaurant offers a cuisine with strong Mediterranean and traditional characteristics. The à la carte menu features iconic dishes such as fuži istriani – homemade fresh pasta served with a creamy white sauce of shrimp and mixed mushrooms, enhanced by the aroma of Istrian black truffle. There is also plenty of focus on fish, with both classic and more creative recipes. The selection of Croatian wines is noteworthy.

Name: Marco's Coal-Fired
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Set in the shadow of Coors Field, Marco's takes pride in being the only spot in Colorado to be certified by the Associazione Verace Pizza Napoletana — a stamp of approval from the Italian birthplace of this beloved staple. The crust alone makes a strong case, made with flavorful, hand-stretched dough, expertly fired in a traditional oven, with beautifully blistered, flame-kissed edges, but the quality of the toppings impresses as well, from San Marzano tomatoes, to prosciutto di parma, to aged pecorino. Guests can build their own pizza by selecting from an assortment of toppings or opt for signature pies. Though the menu does have other offerings, as in salad and lasagna, pizza is rightfully the focus.

Name: Marconi
Description: In the heart of the picturesque town that serves as a gateway to Val Formazza stands a welcoming establishment where familial warmth blends with a touch of contemporaneity. In the kitchen Denis, joined in the dining room by his wife Sabrina, knows how to pamper guests with a series of dishes that evoke tradition while being reinterpreted with imagination and modern sensitivity. Not to be missed is their signature “Walser Beef Filet,” a true house specialty, though the “venison ossobuco with cream of potato and blueberry compote” also merits a taste.

Name: Marcus
Address: Four Seasons Hotel Montréal, 1440 rue de La Montagne, Montréal, H3G 1Z5, Canada
Description: Marcus Samuelsson, a chef with Ethiopian heritage, grew up in Sweden and has made his name in New York. He heads up this restaurant located on the third floor of the Four Seasons Hotel. With its large bay windows, the place is transformed into a terrace as soon as temperatures rise. The eclectic and modern menu is seafood-forward (lobster, crab, oysters, Dover sole, caviar); also contains lamb chops or Wagyu beef.

Name: Marea
Address: 240 Central Park South, New York, NY, 10019, USA
Description: Ritzy and elegant, Marea couldn’t ask for a better home than Central Park South. This airy dining room, dressed to the nines with Indonesian rosewood, is abuzz with power crowds. It's hard to beat this scene but the food is appealing in its own right. The focus of this Italian cuisine is seafood and offers an array of raw fish and crudo such as diced branzino that is presented with chopped pistachio and flecks of crispy garlic and shallot.Finely made pastas include casarecce with pieces of lump crab, uni puree, and tomato. Finish with a beautifully made dessert like the blueberry filled meringa with whipped white chocolate

Name: Marechiaro
Description: A refined and elegant atmosphere that takes on a decidedly romantic character in the evening: for over twenty years this has been the venue of choice in Bolzano for those wishing to enjoy fish prepared according to the most classic recipes of the Italian maritime tradition, founded upon the quality of the catch – sourced predominantly from the Mediterranean – and upon clean flavours. At the helm are two brothers of Neapolitan origin, a detail that accounts for certain Campanian echoes among the offerings and for the presence of pizza, available in the evening only and baked in a wood-fired oven. Not to be missed is the generous daily selection of raw fish, the true calling card of the house.

Name: Mareida
Address: 160 Great Portland Street, London, W1W 5QA, United Kingdom
Description: Adding to London’s status as a truly great city for international dining is this slickly decorated restaurant offering the flavours of Chile, where the rocks and marble decorating the sultry room all come from the country. The large open kitchen adds to the animation and dinner is when the place comes alive, although if you come at lunch you’ll benefit from a good value menu. Highlights could include the choice of empanadas to begin or the flan to finish; throughout your meal, accompany it with the exclusively Chilean wine list.

Name: Marelet
Description: The name of this restaurant discreetly hidden away in an alleyway on the edge of the town centre is a dialect word meaning “old bachelor”. Small tables set close together give the ambience of a French brasserie and provide the setting for modern, Mediterranean-inspired cuisine. There’s a simpler menu at lunchtime, including salads, tapas and sandwiches, while more choice is available in the evening. Lively atmosphere.

Name: Maremma
Description: Stepping into this smartly dressed restaurant is like being transported directly to Italy. The Polish owners also have a farm in Tuscany and their true understanding of Italian cuisine is clear to see across dishes that are simple, ingredient-led and bursting with flavour – be sure to try the homemade pasta. The premises also operate as a wine shop, so it’s no surprise that the list is impressive, and it’s accompanied by caring, knowledgeable service from the sommelier.

Name: Marena Cucina
Address: Rua Pais De Araújo 138, São Paulo, 04531-090, Brazil
Description: In the heart of Itaim Bibi, one of São Paulo's most sophisticated districts, you’ll come across this Italian restaurant that oozes personality, both in its warm Mediterranean-inspired decor combining exposed stone and wood, and its unique cuisine. Although it offers an array of pasta and specialities from across the country (Rome, Naples, Tuscany etc), the aim here is to also incorporate the specific flavours of the Puglia region in the “heel of the boot” in the deep south of the country. The cuisine is unpretentious yet delicious, and is showcased in dishes such as artisanally produced Ficchi & Aceto IGP burrata, grilled octopus, and Tagliolini Marena with fresh pasta, prawns, octopus, squid and pomodorini. The mouthwatering prosciuttos here are also a must.

Name: Margaret's
Address: 18 Chesterton Road, Cambridge, CB4 3AX, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: A labour of love from the owners behind Restaurant Twenty-Two – and located right next door – this soothing space comes with plenty of neutral tones, giving it a simple, relaxing elegance. The opening selection of breads, dips and nibbles is a brilliant way to start, featuring highlights such as a beautifully made focaccia and a creamy whipped butter bean dip. Across the menu, the vibrant cooking moves with the seasons and pushes delicious natural flavours to the fore. The wonderful service team are engaging and knowledgeable in equal measure.

Name: Margaux
Address: Kornmarkt 7, Limburg an der Lahn, 65549, Germany
Description: Behind the beautiful historical half-timbered façade of this listed 14C building in the heart of the Old Town, there lies a tasteful, modern interior. In this setting, Fabian Sollbach serves up a modern take on French cuisine, in which select ingredients take centre stage. The ambitious dishes include elegant fjord trout with Maine lobster and pearl barley. The attractively priced lunch menu is also very popular. There are a handful of places to be had on the small gallery level and, in summer, tables are set up on an inviting terrace on the Kornmarkt. Tip: The cathedral is just a stone's throw away – it is well worth having a stroll through the charming Old Town.

Name: Margo
Address: 303 Soi Naradhiwas Rajanagarindra 10 Lane 20, Thung Wat Don, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Warm wood, geometric patterns and an open kitchen set the tone for a modern bistro, and the buzzy dining room adds to the charm. Chef Wilfrid Hocquet brings polished French classics to this lively, design-forward space, which opened in July 2025. The compact menu follows the French seasons and includes house-made delights such as Kurobuta pork terrine, beef tomato farcie and Paris ham pithiviers. It's best to book ahead – Margo is already drawing crowds.

Name: Margot
Address: 163 Riddiford Street, Newtown, Wellington, 6021, New Zealand
Description: “Come as you are” it says, above the bright red door of this cute, intimate little spot in a Newtown side street. Run by a lovely couple who certainly know how to make diners feel welcome and relaxed. Their menu isn’t that big, but does change regularly, with dishes informed by what’s fresh and in season, and given little twists here and there inspired by their peregrinations. Start with one of their cocktails and finish off with the excellent chocolate ganache.

Name: Margotto e Baciare
Description: The restaurant’s name translates as ‘a whole kiss’. Truffles can be chosen not only whole, but also by the gram. The consommé, enjoyed in a large glass, offers the full, aromatic fragrance of truffles. The fried eggs on toast are accompanied by a rich truffle sauce. Both dishes showcase the synergy of fragrance and flavour created by truffles. Cuisine that proves that true value cannot be found in simply devouring truffles whole.

Name: Marguita
Description: This restaurant in the magnificent Grand Hotel Baur au Lac, which dates back to 1844, exudes all the glamour of the Riviera. In the hands of interior designer Martin Brudnizki, the airy, light-filled rotunda has been imbued with an extremely elegant, luxe ambience with eye-catching features such as a stylish Art Deco chandelier and wonderful mosaic floor – although the beautiful view of the garden or the Schanzengraben steals the show. The Mediterranean-inspired menu includes numerous French and Italian classics, many of which have been given a modern twist. Seafood lovers should definitely look out for the "Lobster Love" dishes. You can count on the dedicated front-of-house team for attentive and courteous service.

Name: Maria Isabel
Address: 500 Presidio Ave., San Francisco, CA, 94115, USA
Description: This fashionable hotspot is the latest coup for culinary power couple Laura and Sayat Ozyilmaz. Named after Chef Laura’s sister and mother, the cooking draws upon Californian ingredients and the flavors of Guerrero (a nod to her upbringing) laced through with heirloom corn from Oaxaca and other regional specialties. Take for instance the aguachile negro of Pacific yellowtail and Monterey Bay squid, paired with fried chicharrónes and shaved daikon in a tangy, savory sauce of charred chiles, or a crunchy masa buñuelo decked out with guacamole and Kaluga caviar pure indulgence. A singular beverage program encompasses vibrant cocktails made from regional spirits like pox and sotol, plus compelling chocolate drinks like tascalate, flavored with blue corn masa, chile and cinnamon.

Name: Maria Restaurant
Address: 11 Huguenot St., New Rochelle, NY, 10801, USA
Description: Boasting a rustic and sleek interior, midnight-blue leather banquettes, chandeliers, and exposed brick adorn the room; a long bar is populated by chatty locals and well-heeled visitors. While the kitchen sticks to beloved Italian classics, it also pivots seamlessly towards a more contemporary approach. This is food that soothes the soul, as in Mom's meatballs, smothered in marinara and grated cheese and sided by a scoop of ricotta and a grilled baguette. Of course, there's also the Italian sausage and chopped broccoli rabe sandwich with melted gouda and parmesan that satisfies the comfort food quotient, too.

Name: Marie Akaneya
Description: This is Paris's first sumibiyaki-style restaurant. Particularly popular in Kyoto, this cuisine is prepared with top-drawer ingredients, not least the Wagyu that is shipped here from Ito Ranch, a beef farm on the outskirts of the town of Matsusaka – and according to the Japanese themselves, this is the ultimate breed of Kobe beef. Everything is cooked over the famous binchotan charcoal, which is made mainly from Ubame oak wood – every table in the restaurant has its own barbecue taking pride of place. Some of the menus feature Fukuroi's renowned Crown Melon, which can sometimes fetch a price of several thousand euro.

Name: Marie B
Description: Set in a 14C townhouse, the restaurant is accessed through a covered courtyard entrance. Behind a somewhat shabby-looking front door covered in graffiti, a minimalist and trendy interior with an urban feel awaits. Beneath a rustic old vaulted ceiling, diners sit at a counter forming a U-shape around the open kitchen, they can watch the action up close. There are also two modern light installations by Berlin artist Anselm Reyle that draw your attention. Another interesting detail is the cookery book dating back to 1894, on display behind glass – it was written by chef Marie B Svobodová, after whom the restaurant is named. Comprising four courses, the carte blanche menu features creative modern dishes rooted in Czech culinary tradition. The nicely curated wine list places the emphasis on Moravian labels. The establishment also operates Vin de Marie wine bar in the same building.

Name: Mariette
Description: Dad and son-in-law in the kitchen, mum and daughter in the front of house: Mariette is the quintessence of a family-run establishment. Adorned in elegant details, it also boasts a lovely patio in the garden. A Franco-Belgian lineup with the occasional international twist sets the tone of the varied menu, many dishes of which are ideal for sharing. The quality of the ingredients, like the turbot and scallops, is superlative. The juicy pheasant is fork-tender and served with lightly caramelised endives, hand-rolled fritters and a cognac sauce. A warm authentic vibe and big-boned family favourites.

Name: Marile
Description: Housed in the lovely Hotel Berghof, this compact wood-panelled restaurant is rustic and cosy yet stylish. Tradition meets modern gastronomy in regional dishes with a contemporary twist – from fermented organic carrot and celery millefeuille with summer truffle to Vorarlberg Wagyu paired with porcini, and waffles with stewed sour cherries for dessert. There is also an impressive wine list dominated by Austrian labels but including options from elsewhere in the Old World and beyond. Attentive service is provided by a friendly and professional front-of-house team. Don't miss the opportunity to have a drink in the fantastic bar – this is where it all began in the 1950s. At lunchtime and in the afternoon, the hotel restaurant is open, with a small menu of daily specials and a trolley bearing pastries and other sweet treats.

Name: Marilor
Address: Nosalowy Park Hotel & Spa, Tadeusza Kościuszki 18, Zakopane, 34-500, Poland
Description: Forming part of the grand Nosalowy Park Hotel & Spa in this winter sports resort town, Marilor is a bright, stylishly designed restaurant that feels worlds away from the kind of wood-heavy Alpine chic often found in the area. Careful execution and quality ingredients guide the cooking, resulting in the likes of marinated trout tartare or rack of lamb with a rich demi-glace sauce, followed by a textbook tarte Tatin with sour cream ice cream for dessert.

Name: Marina
Description: Directly opposite the marina of the small tourist harbour, on the first floor of an unassuming building, lies this intimate and refined restaurant, a genuine surprise, elegantly furnished and graced by a small terrace with just two tables overlooking the sea and the boats – to be reserved well in advance. The talented chef-patron Marina Gaši interprets the finest local seafood with a modern and creative style, offering exclusively two tasting menus: a more concise four-course journey and a more expansive eight-course experience, with the dessert chosen at the table as the optional conclusion. Our Inspector was particularly struck by the raw prawn tartare, whose natural sweetness is brought out by an almond broth, almond crumble and mint-scented extra-virgin olive oil; equally accomplished was the tagliolino with spring onion, house-made colatura di alici and garlic breadcrumbs. In the dining room, Davor accompanies guests with professionalism and style, contributing greatly to the pleasure of the food experience.

Name: Marina Gaj
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In a prime spot alongside a marina near the edge of Lake Pątnowskie, this well-run restaurant has an understandably nautical theme, with its colourful interior including faux anchors hanging from the ceiling. The menu is an equal mix of meat and fish, but you may feel like ordering seafood when by the water – and the team certainly know how to cook it. The likes of baby squid with chilli, garlic and parsley hit the mark with their satisfying flavours.

Name: Marina Grande
Description: Situated directly on the beach, this pleasant restaurant with a contemporary decor boasts splendid sea views and a small private beach club. Although the setting obviously has a tourist feel, the traditional cuisine served here is full of flavour. We particularly recommend the “gamberi in carrozza” (shrimp) with fior di latte and a variation on puttanesca sauce.

Name: Marina del Nettuno
Address: Viale della Libertà-Batteria Masotto, Messina, 98121, Italy
Description: As its name suggests, this restaurant and lounge bar is situated right on the jetty of the Yachting Club Messina. Elegant and minimalist - style decor, as well as creative cuisine with a focus on fish dishes.

Name: Marine Restô
Address: Avenida Atlântica 4240, Rio de Janeiro, 22070-900, Brazil
Description: Enjoy one of the most breathtaking views of Copacabana beach at this restaurant on the sixth floor of the luxurious Fairmont Rio de Janeiro Copacabana hotel, where the panoramic terrace and swimming pool come as a highly scenic surprise! In addition to the picture-postcard views of the city, the restaurant boasts a large, contemporary space with an open-view kitchen, where the Brazilian cuisine combines ingredients and spices from different regions around the country, with a strong focus on the grill. As a result, some of the standout dishes on the menu are cooked on the Josper grill, such as the crunchy courgettes with a Serra da Canastra cheese sauce, the mouthwatering Angus skirt steak with a guaraná demi-glaze, and vegetarian options that include the heart of palm moqueca stew, served with manioc farofa with coconut.

Name: Marinheiro
Address: Rua Gomes de Amorim 1842, Póvoa de Varzim, 4490-091, Portugal
