Description: This architecture does not go unnoticed, given that the restaurant is housed in a boat-shaped building! Upon entering, you will see a display packed with fish and seafood well worth admiring. The spacious interior is divided into two floors and boasts décor inspired by the nautical world, with light, sophisticated colours predominant. As is expected from such an establishment, the menu includes dishes such as seafood açorda stew, various rice dishes, grilled fish and Bacalhau à Marinheiro. There are also excellent meat options, like a fine house-style kid goat or an irresistible picanha steak. The priority here is the quality and freshness of the ingredients, along with excellent service — which makes it well worth a visit!

Name: Marini's on 57
Address: 57F, Menara 3 Petronas, Persiaran KLCC, Kuala Lumpur City Centre, Kuala Lumpur, 50088, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed
Description: At this iconic rooftop venue, diners enjoy superb sunsets and panoramic cityscapes through floor to ceiling windows. Besides the à la carte menu, there are several tasting menus that offer a knockout selection of Italian dishes, featuring innovative elements, choice cuts of imported beef and artisan pasta. The intriguing tiramisu, which comes in a tin of caviar, is made with coffee caviar (rather than fish eggs!).

Name: Marino
Description: As you drive along the scenic road from Pesaro, the sunset appears to the west, emerging from the greenery, while to the east the sea appears and disappears, finally settling as the backdrop to the pleasant outdoor area of this restaurant. This is the creation of the chef-owner, who, after traveling the world and working in Michelin-starred kitchens, has returned "home." He incorporates everything he has learned into modern and sometimes creative recipes, occasionally adding a light fusion touch, such as using fruit in dishes such as spaghetti with mussels and sea urchins enhanced by two well-balanced textures of peach.

Name: Marino Bistrot
Description: Hidden away in a residential area, this basement restaurant sports rustic exposed brickwork and simple bistro furnishings. It’s named after Chef Livio Marino, who has a passion for authentic Italian dishes that manifests itself here in an extensive menu that includes a selection of homemade pastas. Look out for the pasta dishes and the likes of sea bream cooked over an open fire. For dessert, it’s very hard to resist tiramisu in a place like this.

Name: Marino e Silvana
Address: Via San Salvatore da Horta 7, Cagliari, 09124, Italy
Description: Situated on the edge of the pedestrianised area near the Bastione di Saint Remy, this restaurant is named after its charismatic owner Marino, who helps guests with their choice of menu and is happy to tell them all about the history of the restaurant (the street in front of the restaurant, for example, has not always been there). At the helm in the kitchen, his wife Silvana prepares Mediterranean dishes with a Sardinian flavour – the fish and seafood options are particularly delicious.

Name: Maritime
Address: Jeddah EDITION Hotel, 7044 Al Kurnaysh Br Road, Ash Shati, Jeddah, 23613, Saudi Arabia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,No alcohol served,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Located on the ground floor of design-forward and minimalist The Jeddah EDITION Hotel in a wonderful location on the edge of the famous Jeddah Yacht Club, this restaurant by Cédric Vongerichten, son of Jean-Georges, offers a menu mixing French and Asian dishes. Some favourites include crispy spring roll with pepper sauce and a local seabass with tomato. Take a seat on the terrace when weather permits and enjoy being pampered by the warm and caring team.

Name: Marius
Description: Chef Sébastien Sanjou from the Bigorre region (with stints at Michelin-starred Trente-Trois in Paris and Relais des Moines in Les Arcs) opened this restaurant – installed on the higher ground behind Biarritz, it is blessed with a large terrace overlooking La Rhune mountain. Conviviality and indulgence are the order of the day here! Executive chef Kévin Bigot (former colleague of chef Jean-Marie Gautier at the Hôtel du Palais restaurant) treats his guests to a generous helping of family-style cooking (sides are placed on the table). Everything is prepared with the finest local produce: pot-au-feu of fresh foie gras; quail "ortolan" wrapped in bacon; savarin with traditional Armagnac. In short, this is the ideal place to spend some quality time with family and friends.

Name: Marius
Description: Not far from the Parc des Princes, this chic restaurant with an understated contemporary decor serves delicious seafood dishes: fish soup with rouille, whiting Colbert and fabulous whole fish to share (dictated by the catch). Alternatives include a handful of meat dishes, such as the beef fillet with black pepper, crispy calf sweetbreads or even risotto Milanese.

Name: Marius et Janette
Description: This elegant yacht-style décor, replete with fishing rods, nets and copper portholes, caters to discerning food lovers. The chef highlights fish and seafood, with a menu that is renewed daily, according to the catch. Carpaccio of salmon and basil, grilled seabass to share or linguine with lobster (a house speciality): a festival of flavours!

Name: Marixx
Description: Located well away from the busy city centre and overlooking the luxury yachts and boats moored in the harbour, this restaurant opened in the summer of 2021, at the same time as the modern Cala del Forte marina in which it is situated (the name of the marina comes from the Forte dell'Annunziata, the ruins of which are visible from the side facing the sea). Fish and seafood take pride of place here (especially raw fish dishes), served with classic, seasonal accompaniments, as well as snacks, while an oyster bar is an added attraction. Although the best tables are in the glass-fronted veranda overlooking the pedestrian promenade, the contemporary-style dining room is also attractive. The owner-chef has plenty of experience behind him, especially working in the region.

Name: Mark
Description: The produce of the Danish countryside is the inspiration behind this stylish city centre bistro that also features some classical French methods in the kitchen. There is a wonderful feeling of spaciousness to the dining room, with its central counter, high ceilings and modern décor. Top quality Danish ingredients are seasoned and cooked with real skill, resulting in a roster of refined and well-balanced dishes.

Name: Mark Jordan at the Beach
Address: La Plage, La Route de la Haule, Beaumont, JE3 7YD, United Kingdom
Description: This modern brasserie on Jersey's south coast is split across several areas: there's a small lounge and bar; a paved terrace with bay views; and a dining room with heavy wood tables, modern seashore paintings and animal ornaments. Unsurprisingly, locally caught seafood is a feature of the menu – with produce like wing of Jersey skate on offer – but there are also hearty meat dishes to satisfy.

Name: Markette
Description: Right on 7th Avenue in Chelsea, walls of mirrors, modern lights and cozy banquettes make for a stylish stage where Chef India Doris crafts an impressive, nicely trimmed menu that pulls European and Caribbean influences. Carefully prepared and packed with flavor, the best dishes are the most personal: Salt cod fritters arrive with a fiery habanero aioli, and braised oxtail capped with cheddar polenta is a dreamy pie that would outclass its British pub relative. To finish, strawberry cheesecake prepared as a Swiss roll is a clever, beautiful effort. A gorgeous cocktail bar framed in recessed lighting shakes and stirs all night long.

Name: Markt XI
Description: Benny and Katrijn have no lack of ambition, which you will appreciate as soon as you step foot into their bright, downtown eatery. Your cheerful hostess greets and seats diners and remains close by to suggest food and wine pairings. The chef crafts modern cuisine, which can be described as fresh, subtle and artfully plated. Contemporary recipes underscored by classical foundations and a sprinkling of creative touches. Examples include Scandinavian langoustines, which are quickly grilled, before being jazzed up with a sprinkling of spices and a highly distinctive chimichurri sauce. Markt XI is truly a blue-ribbon establishment!

Name: Marktküche
Description: One tip at the outset: be sure to reserve in good time – this restaurant always gets booked up, so it's hard to secure a table! The clue is in the name: the cuisine takes its cue from what the market has to offer, dispensing with meat and fish. Diners can look forward to a 100% vegan surprise menu made up of four to eight courses, with optional wine or alcohol-free pairings available. A special lunch set menu is served on the penultimate Friday of every month. In summer, head for the pleasant pavement terrace.

Name: Marktwirtschaft Besigheim
Description: This charmingly laid-back restaurant serves dishes made with regional and seasonal ingredients, drawing on influences from the Mediterranean and beyond. The best way to experience the culinary artistry is through the six-course set menu. There is also a popular lunch deal that changes weekly. In the summer, the terrace on the charming little market square beckons, whether for a meal, a glass of wine or a coffee. The service is friendly and attentive. Across the street is the Marktkeller brasserie and wine bar. They also put on regular themed evenings. Tip: Take a stroll through the enchanting little half-timbered town!

Name: Marle
Address: Heckfield Place, Heckfield, RG27 0LD, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Within Heckfield Place – a Georgian country house hotel decorated with the owner’s extensive post-war British art collection – you’ll find this charming, orangery-style dining room looking out over a lake and parkland. Locality and seasonality drive everything they do here, with a great number of ingredients coming from the estate’s own farm; these are fashioned into light, clean dishes that rely on honest, natural flavours. Look out for anything based around the 'farm vegetables', which give you an opportunity to really taste the land.

Name: Marly Privé
Description: The restaurant previously known as "Marly" has moved and is now operating under the name of Marly Privé. In its smaller space, this eatery serves classic French cuisine made from top-notch ingredients – chef-owner Gregor Ruppenthal's love for France is on full display. Accessed via Le comptoir 17, a cosy back room accommodates up to 12 diners who sit down to a five- or seven-course tasting menu – a four- or five-course version is served on Fridays. Dishes have names such as "Our octopus salad depuis 1999" or "Line-caught sea bass from Quiberon, leek, nori, pink onions", and are accompanied by a well-curated wine list. The service is friendly and attentive. Tip: Don't forget to reserve your spot!

Name: Marmitón
Description: An intimate restaurant with a rustic feel, run with great skill by two chefs. Classically inspired cuisine with a contemporary touch and a focus on strong, defined flavours.

Name: Marmo
Description: Right on the ski slope, close to the gondola lift station, this mountain restaurant enjoys a prime location – and that, of course, means spectacular views of the peaks from the terrace. Inside, diners soak up the cosy Alpine atmosphere of the charming chalet-style decor. The establishment is run by brothers Alessandro and Sergio Grand, with the latter fulfilling chef duties, crafting modern Alpine cuisine from select ingredients. Highlights on the menu include marinated char with duck tartare, Horu cheese fondue and Luma Black Angus burger, as well as their own take on a classic apple strudel, dubbed "An Apple a Day". Excellent wine selection and friendly service. They open for lunch five days a week in summer and every day in winter. In addition, there are evening events in winter: "Cheesy Tuesday" and "Schnitzel Thursday". The restaurant is part of Chalet MARMO, should you wish to stay overnight.

Name: Marmurio do Río
Description: A unique restaurant occupying the stone house that was once home to the century-old Casa Fandiño restaurant. Today, the name, which translates as the “murmur of the river” in Galician, pays a discreet tribute to the poem Dark Shadow by the renowned Galician poet Rosalía de Castro.The first thing that strikes you here is the meticulous, rustic-contemporary interior decor, which is almost an extension of the charm found in the streets of Allariz. Madrid-born chef Luis Moreno created this project in the town where he always spent his summers. Dining options are based around two tasting menus: one short option entitled Río and a second longer one called Marmurio (both with pairing options). The chef works with small-scale producers from the locality and the Sierra de Madrid, and even uses lemons from his own lemon tree! Through his menus, he tries to draw comparisons with the tame and at times wilder characteristics of the local River Arnoia. The desserts, such as the Oreo trompe l'oeil, are astonishing!

Name: Marnage - Hôtel La Marine
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Boasting a panoramic view of the sea and the harbour, this local institution on the Cotentin peninsula faces the Channel Islands of Jersey and Guernsey. In a pleasant contemporary interior, you will sample modern, deftly crafted food that highlights Normandy’s produce, with a weakness for local seafood, illustrated by line-caught whiting, celery risotto and a wild garlic emulsion.

Name: Maromi İstanbul
Address: Asker Ocağı Caddesi No:1, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34367, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed
Description: In Maromi, the Divan hotel boasts an excellent sushi restaurant, where you can dine at a regular table or sit at the counter – we highly recommend the latter to watch the chef in action. See how he tucks tender octopus and pickled daikon into a cradle of warm rice, or how he rolls salmon, spring onion and a fiery chilli pepper sauce in a mantle of toasted sesame seeds. Choose your sushi à la carte, or opt for the omakase menu and let the chef decide. On Tuesdays there's even an all-you-can-eat option!

Name: Marquize
Description: After globetrotting around the world, Kelly and Pieter have finally returned home. They have taken over and refurbished a pretty villa, breathing new life into what was something of a local institution. A quick glance at the menu reveals the importance they give to delicacies from the North Sea and the polders in food that is both pared-back and spot on. An example of the chef’s talent for showcasing the main ingredient is illustrated by fantastically fresh North Sea crab paired with crunchy kohlrabi, soft, oven-fresh bread and a punchy tomato consommé. Marquize is once again in the limelight thanks to this enthusiastic duo.

Name: Marqués de Riscal
Description: Located within the eponymous hotel-winery (recognised as the best vineyard in Europe in 2021) designed by the famous architect Frank O. Gehry and overflowing with imagination and creativity. Beneath the spectacular curved roof of pink, gold and silver titanium that represent the red of the wine, the golden hue of the wire mesh decorating Marqués de Riscal’s bottles, and the gold colour of their capsules, discover innovative cuisine overseen by award-winning chef Francis Paniego, with a constant nod to tradition, memories and the superb seasonal ingredients of the Rioja and Álava provinces. Everything is centred around two tasting menus (Torrea and Chirel) with different numbers of courses, both of which share the same Basque-inspired appetisers and fried dishes (such as the famous croquettes, the recipe for which Francis acquired from his mother).

Name: Marquês de Marialva
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Its name pays homage to this Portuguese nobleman who played a decisive role in several battles during the Restoration War. This establishment enjoys a certain prestige and a fine location, occupying a restored old house on the town square. It offers three intimate rooms combining classic and rustic elements — one with a fireplace — and a large banqueting room on the upper floor. The menu of traditional character offers à la carte options and a tasting menu (for a minimum of 2 people), which ranges from the classic clams in garlic‑cilantro dressing to the traditional Bacalhau à Lagareiro (oven‑roasted salt‑cod) with smashed potatoes.

Name: Marso & Co
Description: Tomy Gousset (Tomy & Co, near Les Invalides) runs this restaurant that sets out to take diners on a culinary journey: the food tours the entire Mediterranean basin from Greece to Portugal via Italy and Lebanon (but also Latin America). Examples of the Colombian born chef’s handiwork include an aguachile of seabream and shrimp, pink grapefruit, cucumber and coriander. The octopus-themed artwork on the walls is by street artist Kraken. Soul-warming recipes, spot-on flavours, fantastically fresh ingredients – a felicitous feast awaits you!

Name: Marsupino 1901
Description: Once the village bakery and now a landmark for those in search of authentic cooking, the trattoria Marsupino 1901 tells a family story spanning four generations. Here, tradition remains the anchor: solid, reassuring and sincere cuisine, yet capable of revisiting familiar flavours with contemporary sensitivity and a measured hand. Emblematic of this approach is the hazelnut semifreddo with Marsala zabaglione cooked in a bain-marie, an indulgent, beautifully judged dessert that brings the meal to an elegant close. In the dining room, the welcome finds its ideal interpreter in Luca: professional, warm and animated by a genuine passion for wine, he accompanies guests with competence and ease. His carefully chosen selection of labels, and his ability to describe them with clarity and engagement, enrich the experience, transforming the gastronomic journey into a harmonious voyage through memory, territory and conviviality.

Name: Martabaan by Hemant Oberoi
Address: Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental Hotel, West Corniche Road, Al Ras Al Akhdar, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: In contrast to the huge Emirates Palace hotel in which its located, this Indian restaurant occupies a surprisingly small and intimate space. Its eponymous chef has considerable experience around the world and the menu encompasses all his favourite dishes. The tasting menu is the best form of discovery. The enthusiasm of the service team is thoroughly infectious, and their recommendations are always worth heeding.

Name: Martim
Description: Taking full advantage of its location on the banks of the River Oder, Martim’s terrace and floor-to-ceiling windows help make it a lovely setting in which to enjoy the kitchen’s Portuguese-inspired dishes. Seafood plays a big role on the menu, in dishes like the rich, rustic and punchily flavoured cataplana stew. The wine list is exclusively Portuguese, with some fine Vinho Verde and, of course, a selection of top-notch and well-priced ports.

Name: Martin Comptoir
Description: Not far from the market (ideal for fresh produce), local lad, chef Martin Dumas, has acquired a faithful crowd of regulars. His culinary score, tailored to today’s tastes, features a concise seasonal menu, generous hunks of meat to be shared and the house speciality, “thickly sliced calf’s liver”, which he learnt from Jean-Paul Arabian in Paris. Peaceful small terrace.

Name: Martinelli
Description: If you’re looking for Italian hospitality and the food that goes with it, Martinelli offers seasonal, modern cuisine including dishes such as pecorino ravioli with walnut and balsamic vinegar or saddle of venison with quince. And to whet your appetite, there’s always a plate of air-dried ham and some delicious bread.

Name: Martino Wines
Description: You may be in a winery, but what draws your attention here is the fact that you’re made to feel at home! This attractive restaurant, occupying a separate conservatory-style building with a terrace and overlooking the surrounding garden through large picture windows, is enthusiastically run by chef Javier Quinteros. What's on the menu? This ambitious cuisine draws inspiration from around the world (Italy, France, Japan) and offers extremely colourful seasonal dishes that aim to win diners over with their honesty. The menu, which demonstrates a special desire to balance flavours and seasonings, revolves around several different options that take us on a journey through its offerings, all accompanied by a wide selection of wines (including a good number of international labels). The restaurant also organises the occasional food-themed event.

Name: Martié
Address: Rosario 10, Jerez de la Frontera, 11402, Spain
Description: In the heart of Jerez, in a good location behind the Real Convento de Santo Domingo, this restaurant is an ode to work and patience, necessary to achieve your dreams. The dining room, accessed via a staircase and with original nods to the animated film ‘Up’, is presented with a small glassed-in wine cellar and a minimalist aesthetic dominated by black and gold tones. Chef Isidro López is committed to a gastronomic concept that revolves exclusively around a tasting menu (Año 0, Tarab), offering a contemporary, locally based cuisine with international touches. What caught our attention? The tribute to his baker (Paco Ruiz, from Horno Artesa) and the quality of the product, something that is especially noticeable in the hake and fried bread dish.

Name: Martínez
Description: Chef/owner Lucho Martinez was inspired to open this eponymous restaurant by his daughter, Emilia, who once shared that her favorite thing to do in Paris was eat in the bistros with him. It sparked an idea—why not recreate that feeling right here in Mexico City—and Martinez is just that: a small restaurant with good food and wine.The ambience is young and bustling. Order at the bar and you'll get a sneak peek into the kitchen. The concise menu features a list of tasty dishes with nods to Mexican, French and even Japanese cuisine. Pollo a la parrilla is a main course hit, while chocolate cake with vanilla ice cream is spot on.

Name: Maru
Address: 18 Shepherd Market, Mayfair, London, W1J 7QH, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed
Description: Discreetly tucked away in Shepherd Market, it's easy to miss the entrance to the earnestly run Maru. As with many a good sushi restaurant, the high quality of the produce helps provide plenty of flavour; the ingredients are largely British, including seafood from Cornish waters. The menu takes an omakase approach, made up of around 20 different servings, and the sake pairing makes for a good accompaniment. There are two sittings at dinner, so arrive on time; you pay when you book.

Name: Maru
Description: This urban Korean eatery on the doorstep of the Châtelain district never fails to deliver. The locals flock here at lunchtime to polish off a main course or take their time over a more leisurely meal with a glass of wine. Pajeon is one of its star dishes: a crisp pancake filled with meat or fish flanked by a sweet vinaigrette and a spicy chili sauce. This dish symbolises the delicate balance between sweet, sour and spicy notes achieved by the chef, further underscored by a playful melody of varied textures. The epitome of authentic Korean nosh!

Name: Marugame Monzo
Address: 329 E. 1st St., Los Angeles, CA, 90012, USA
Description: This LA spot is appropriately named, as Marugame is a Japanese town where udon is revered. Here, diners are even privy to these large discs of dough being rolled out, stretched, and cut into deliciously chewy strands. The space is simple, clean, and welcoming, as evident by the groups of friends and families with tots in tow. Come early to put your name down, especially on the weekends, because everyone is here to indulge in these savory and slurp-worthy bowls. One fine example is the mushroom udon infused with miso for an umami-rich base. Other items include the uni and miso "carbonara" and the crispy-and-creamy agedashi eggplant, along with hot and cold udon choices, bonus toppings, and cold Asahi on tap.

Name: Maràngels
Description: Located just outside Girona and nestled in a beautiful 17th-century farmhouse with landscaped surroundings, the neat rustic atmosphere of this restaurant’s rooms and corners offer a certain intimacy, with traditional cuisine brought up to date with appetising suggestions and several set menus (there are options for groups, one at midday during the week and a tasting menu called Vall del Llemena).

Name: Maré
Description: An unexpected gourmet restaurant in a typical private beach club on the Romagna coast, with a dining room that opens on to the beach with its long line of beach umbrellas. The dishes here are carefully prepared and occasionally creative, and all of good quality. We particularly recommend the monfettini (fresh egg pasta) mantecati with cuttlefish, clams, mantis shrimp and ink, which looks like a risotto and is absolutely delicious. The restaurant also boasts a good wine list with an excellent choice of champagnes.

Name: Maré - José Avillez
Address: Av. Nossa Senhora do Cabo, 9000, Cascais, 2750-374, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This is the most maritime offering from the famous chef José Avillez and it sits in a privileged location, between Guincho and Cascais. Conceived as a tribute to the chef’s homeland, this restaurant boasts unrivalled views and is an outright invitation to savour the best of the Portuguese coast, with ultra-fresh fish and seafood displayed in the window of the open kitchen. Avillez’s signature menu, executed daily by chef Filipe Pina, presents dishes such as the flavourful Escabeche de fígado de bacalhau (cod liver in a vinegar‑marinade style), the Lombo de Corvina (sea bass loin) with olive oil and lemon—which shines without needing any other ingredient—the Polvo ao alho (garlic octopus) grilled over embers… The space, divided into two rooms and complemented by a welcoming terrace for summer days, combines elegant décor with maritime elements, such as an artistic mural and an impressive wooden sculpture of a giant ray.

Name: Marée
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: The location high above Vaduz is exceptional, commanding sweeping views over the town and surrounding mountains. Park-Hotel Sonnenhof draws acclaim not only for its tasteful, classic-style guestrooms, but also for Hubertus Real's cooking. Attentive and adept waitstaff serve dishes made from select ingredients, including house classics such as "spicy beef tartare, French fries allumettes", "mini bouillabaisse – fish, shellfish, sauce rouille, croutons" or "slow-cooked ray wing, capers, brown garlic butter, mashed potatoes". The extensive wine list is presented on a tablet. Dine in the elegant interior or, in summer, out on the magnificent terrace with its vantage point – the "Adlernest" (eagle's nest) – from which you can take in the stunning view.

Name: María Dolores
Address: ATELIER Playa Mujeres, Condominio Playa Mujeres SM-3 M-1 L-13 RTH-4, Isla Mujeres, 77400, Mexico
Description: Expect to be pampered like royalty from the second you step into this luxurious enclave within the sprawling Atelier Playa Mujeres hotel. Apart from hyper-attentive hospitality (including top-notch beverage service), the grand space features a balcony from which diners are serenaded with live music. The menu of contemporary Mexican cuisine, curated by celebrated chef Edgar Nuñez, is similarly ornate, featuring a multitude of à la carte offerings and specials, in addition to a signature tasting menu. The flavorful, original cooking draws upon the breadth of Mexico’s culinary landscape, reimagining familiar regional dishes with a refined modern style, whether it’s a tempura-fried shrimp taco in honor of Sonora, or a complex Oaxacan mole coloradito paired with roasted quail.

Name: María de la O
Address: Carretera de la Sierra 13, Granada, 18008, Spain
Description: In this restaurant with a contemporary ambience and occupying an attractive 19th-century mansion, his modern cuisine that usually revolves around seasonal ingredients from the Granada region, with plenty of focus on presentation and contrasts, particularly his acidic touches that are showcased in sauces that highlight the past of this former vinegar-producing property (this is particularly true of his delicious escabeches). The proposal revolves exclusively around a comprehensive tasting menu which, if requested by the customer, can be reduced by two courses. Interesting dishes? We enjoyed the Motril shrimp marinated in orange escabeche and the Monkfish in Mozarabic sauce, made with orange, carrot and spices.

Name: Mas Albereda
Address: Avenida Sant Llorenç 68, Sant Julià de Vilatorta, 08504, Spain
Description: Located just six kilometres from the town of Vic, this restaurant occupies a farmhouse with a pleasantly rustic ambience plus an attractive glass-fronted terrace. The updated take on traditional cuisine on offer here bears the quality stamp of chef Nandu Jubany, and is showcased via a surprising array of daily dishes (both sweet and savoury) as well as a tasting menu. We can particularly recommend the duck breast glazed with a heather-infused honey, plus the rum baba, the finishing touches to which are added at your table.

Name: Mas de Dardagna
Address: 1 chemin de Dardagna, Rangueil, Toulouse, 31400, France
Description: Now, this is simple, well-made fare that does justice to its ingredients (the chef uses short supply chains as much as possible): guinea fowl and black Gascon pork charlotte, artichoke cream, full-bodied gravy and fresh mushrooms. No doubt about it, this typical Toulouse farmhouse is a haven for foodies! On sunny days, make the most of the terrace beneath the wisteria.

Name: Masa's Sushi
Description: Respected veteran Chef Takatoshi Toshi crafts hearty and affordable sushi for a local crowd. Don’t be surprised to see him behind the counter here, breaking down a whole salmon while making small talk with his neighbors. The space is simple, understated and quiet, which seems to match its quaint downtown location, set amid boutiques and restaurants. Lunch combinations are an excellent deal, offering chirashi bowls as well as sushi and nigiri with miso soup. Come dinner, the affordable omakase selection unveils nigiri, salmon and tuna tastings. Bigger platters might arrive as lovely amalgamations of avocado and albacore rolls alongside ebi, yellowtail and cherry wood-smoked goldeneye snapper (kinmedai). Finish with a scoop of black sesame ice cream.

Name: Masaikuta
Address: 26 bis rue de la Fontaine-au-Roi, Paris, 75011, France
Description: Trained in Japan before moving to France (where he worked with Stéphane Jégo, Bruno Verjus and Bertrand Grébaut), chef Masahide Ikuta works in an unpolished setting typical of the neighbourhood: scraped walls, waxed concrete and mottled mirrors. In his single blind menu that draws on premium ingredients, France meets Japan, eg Mont-Saint-Michel cockles, matured Simmental beef or Cantabrian anchovies. Clarity characterises his dishes with complex sauces – sashimi-style sea bream enhanced with leche de tigre, trout roe, mango, oxalis and sea fennel for a tangy, herbaceous touch. The wine cellar boasts almost 400 labels.

Name: Masaki
Description: The chef learned at a ryotei how to produce rich flavours by combining ingredients. Having been responsible for the simmered dishes and soups there, he pours his strength into wanmono. His search for ever greater depth of flavour led him to combine first-draught dashi with fish bone broth. The chef’s pride and joy is surinagashi, with a distinct sense of season. The power of dashi makes ingredients all the more impressive. As a counterpoint to the varied tone of the menu, the meal ends simply, with white rice and clear soup.

Name: Masama
Address: 5 place de la Bilange, Saumur, 49400, France
Description: Experience a slice of South America behind this resplendent pistachio-green shopfront in the heart of Saumur. Colombian chef Marlon Medina made headlines in the local press when he coached his country's team for the Bocuse d'Or cooking contest in 2023. His cuisine may be multicultural, but it nevertheless shows clear South American leanings, which are sometimes allied with local ingredients (such as asparagus or mushrooms). For dinner, by means of a short and to-the-point menu, the chef proposes indulgent dishes such as an excellent picanha accompanied by an impeccable chimichurri condiment. Another signature dish is the ceviche, made with fish from the market. At lunchtime, there's a more typically French single set menu without options.

Name: Mashino Ken
Description: The cuisine of Hong Kong touched off a journey of exploration into the depth and richness of Chinese cooking. The chef studied each region’s history and culture to plumb the origins of each. His passion shines as he explains the roots of each cuisine, referring to his own experiences and the menu in Cantonese. Peking duck as standard fare ensures he never forgets where he came from. Patient work making miso and rolling dough drive his zeal for constant improvement.

Name: Maso Burba
Address: Via Pietro Bernardelli 32, località Piano, Commezzadura, 38020, Italy
Description: Housed in a traditional maso of wood and stone, the quintessential mountain atmosphere continues inside through warm, timber-clad interiors and a classic ceramic stove that heats one of the first-floor dining rooms. The cuisine, with occasional seafood exceptions, fully embraces the Trentino terroir.

Name: Maso Runch-Hof
Description: Surrounded by woods, a trip to this restaurant housed in an 18C farmhouse is like taking a journey back in time. Take a seat in one of the wood-adorned Stube-style rooms and enjoy generous portions of delicious home-cooked Ladin specialities featured on a single tasting menu, including cajinci t’ega (spinach-filled ravioli), excellent pork ribs with polenta, and apple strudel. The small wine list has the same local focus, featuring labels from the Alto Adige region. A recent addition, the restaurant also now has a few spacious, welcoming chalets available for guests.

Name: Massara
Description: This Southern Italian restaurant in the Flatiron District is helmed by Chef Stefano Secchi of Rezdôra. Here, the menu focuses on the regional cuisine of Campania and is designed with a shared plates mindset. The cooking is strong and clever. Kick off the meal with grilled ciabatta or tender pulpo before settling on pasta, the star of the show. Most is made in-house and the dishes are sized for sharing, so order several to sample their handiwork. Standouts include the whimsically named "If pasta fredda was eaten in Amalfi," a thicker noodle served cold and coated in a puréed tomato-based sauce and topped with raw red shrimp and lobes of uni. Cheesemakers raviolini, with six ravioli filled with burrata imported from Campania, is proof positive of this team's skill for pasta.

Name: Masseria Moroseta
Description: Chef Giorgia Eugenia Goggi offers a unique and authentic gastronomic experience that focuses on fresh ingredients (mostly vegetables), many of which are sourced from small organic gardens. The 90€ menu celebrates Mediterranean cuisine to the full, with colourful dishes that are full of flavour and in which the freshness of the ingredients is allowed to shine through. The beautifully kept, rustic dining room provides an ideal setting for an unforgettable dinner, while the selection of natural Italian wines offers the perfect accompaniment to the chef’s dishes, further enhancing your dining experience. There are six comfortable guestrooms available should you wish to extend your stay and immerse yourself in these peaceful rural surroundings. Booking in advance is highly recommended given the restaurant’s popularity and unique appeal.

Name: Master of Mushroom (Xinshe)
Address: 287 Xiezhong Street, Xinshe District, Taichung, 426, Taiwan
Description: In 2006, a mushroom farmer opened this mushroom-themed restaurant in Xinshe, the mushroom capital of Taiwan. Free-range chicken soup with shiitake tastes rich and flavoursome, while dried day lily flowers and assorted mushrooms add to the complex taste profile. Try also three-cup monkey-head mushrooms, and mushroom minced pork rice. Adjacent to the Sea of Flowers and Dakeng, it makes a great stop to recharge your body after a day out.

Name: Masti
Address: The Dubai Edition Hotel, Floor 1, Downtown, Dubai
Description: In 2023 this colourful and creative restaurant moved to a new berth within The Dubai Edition hotel – and it’s a good fit. There’s more than a hint of whimsy to the vibrant decoration and equal amounts of imagination are shown in the menu. The kitchen isn’t afraid of incorporating global influences alongside the Indian flavours, which results in intriguing but always enjoyable dishes that are meant for sharing. Fun and mischievous indeed.

Name: Masumasu Masuda
Description: The name combines the owner’s surname, Masuda, with an expression meaning ‘more and more’, in prayer that, through the family’s mutual support, the restaurant will prosper. The menu skews strongly towards the foodstuffs of Tochigi Prefecture, where the chef was born and raised. It changes monthly, variously including vegetables in season, trout raised by a friend of the chef in Nikko and served as oshizushi, and Tochigi wagyu beef. Rice cooked on a hearth is sourced in Tochigi as well. You’ll come to love it ‘more and more’.

Name: Masztalerz
Address: Arche Zamek Janów Podlaski Hotel, ul. Zamkowa 1, Janów Podlaski, 21-505, Poland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: Located in the basement of the historic Zamek Janów Podlaski Hotel, which has its origins in the 15th century, there’s a suitably old-school, atmospheric feel to this vaulted, brick-lined restaurant. Choose dishes from across both the ‘Green’ (vegetarian and vegan) and ‘Red’ (meat and fish) menus which showcase the kitchen’s skill with classic techniques; Polish beef tenderloin comes with a rich demi-glace sauce, while the chocolate fondant for dessert is a classic version.

Name: MatCha
Description: Everything is fresh and made from scratch at this bistro born of the partnership of MAThieu and CHArlotte (who comes from the village). Channelling the zeitgeist, the pair serve modern French cuisine in the form of a simple, reasonably priced menu at lunchtime and more elaborate fare in the evening, always showcasing seasonal vegetables from small-scale local growers and free-range meats. A lovely dining experience, complete with smiling service.

Name: Mater
Description: Mater is a "retreat" where time seems to stand still and silence reigns supreme. The surrounding nature provides the perfect backdrop for a culinary offering that harmonizes beautifully with the environment. The dining room, welcoming and elegant, features an open kitchen on one side and large French doors on the other, flooding the space with natural light and offering a stunning view. The offerings range from the “Madre” menu to a lighter option called “In libertà”: 3 courses of your choice, plus 1 dessert (the same for the entire table). We recommend the sweetbreads, delicate and tender, flavored with an excellent Casentino gray pork jus. Alternatively, try the grilled guinea fowl among the mains for a dish with traditional tones and a bold flavor.

Name: Mater
Address: B1, 16 Eonju-ro 154-gil, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, 06021, South Korea
Description: Chef Young-bin Kim reinterprets Korean and Asian traditions alongside Western and Nordic influences, with fermentation at the core of his cooking. By transforming ingredients through fermentation and weaving them into his dishes, he explores their flavours in nuanced and varied ways. This approach reflects his aim to balance acidity and savoury umami. In Korea, where fermented foods are part of everyday life, Mater’s thoughtful exploration of fermentation and pursuit of flavour harmony feel both distinctive and intriguing.

Name: Mater Bistrot
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted
Description: A small bistro situated in a street just behind Piazza Cinque Giornate, with a few tables and small lights that give the setting a cosy feel. The dining room is minimalist in style, with just a few tables and a counter where you can sit and watch chef Alex (Alessandro) at work in the kitchen. Guests have the option of two tasting menus or a selection of smaller dishes to share. A choice of natural wines accompanies the chef’s imaginative dishes.

Name: Mater Terrae
Description: Situated on the top floor of the Raphaël hotel just behind Piazza Navona, this restaurant serves some of the best vegetarian cuisine in Rome. Each of the elaborate dishes boasts numerous ingredients and every single course is a delightful surprise. Equally stunning is the panoramic terrace overlooking the city’s rooftops, where meals are served in fine weather.

Name: Materia Prima
Address: Località Piana Santa Liberata, Castel di Sangro, 67031, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A pleasant and intimate terrace overlooks the shores of an artificial lake dedicated to sports activities. The glass windows provide the same view from the modern, sleek, and minimalist interior rooms, just like the dishes: creative, yet reminiscent of local cuisine, such as the simple but tasty Pallotta Cacio e Ova, offered among the welcome bites. There are also various daily specials according to the market. The service is friendly and attentive, with a young and motivated team overall.

Name: Materia | Spazio Cucina
Description: One has the impression of crossing the threshold of the chef’s own home, through a door of pleasantly domestic character; inside, a welcoming dining room opens up, with shared tables and a striking wall entirely lined with jars filled with nuts, pumpkin seeds, red lentils and other ingredients. The cuisine, classic in inspiration yet open to contemporary technique and the use of the grill, offers land and sea in a Sicilian key, with close attention to seasonality. Our Inspector recommends beginning with the convincing “piatti del contadino”, a vegetable selection in which the “Onion on the BBQ with dry-cured black olives, tuma persa cream and parsley oil” stands out, alongside the delicate “Salt Cod Salad”, cooked with oregano oil and served with a sauce of almonds, olives, capers and orange zest.

Name: Material
Address: Eduardo Vila Fano 3, Malpica de Bergantiños, 15113, Spain
Description: Right in the heart of town, just a short stroll from the port, there is a contemporary restaurant where everything revolves around the grill. Their menu, specialising in grilled dishes, attributes its success to the quality of its ingredients, which is why they offer large cuts of wild fish depending on market availability (perfect for sharing) and select cuts of beef (such as Rubia Gallega, Frisona or Holstein) that they age themselves.

Name: Mathieu Kergourlay - Château de Boisgelin
Description: Chef Mathieu Kergourlay welcomes diners to this 450-hectare property, the small castle of which has been tastefully restored and decorated by his companion. The full-bodied, generous and consummately crafted food is full of surprises, such as scallops and Morteau sausage in a brioche bread roll with spinach and a reduction of pork jus. All the menus and the à la carte lineup are gluten- and lactose-free.

Name: Matière
Description: This vibrant, authentic and generous eatery is tucked away in a side street. Vintage furniture, an open kitchen, a few alfresco tables on a patio and a funky soundtrack from another era set the scene. The spotlight is on tradition and regional fare: pickled pork pâté en croûte (pork pie) with a perfect balance between texture, port wine jelly and gutsy seasoning. Juicy, tender, impeccably grilled lamb is served on a bed of fried cabbage with an acidic herby cream. A subtly daring chocolate and mushroom tartlet adds the final flourish to your meal.

Name: Matka
Description: Polish chef Piotr Korzen hosts diners in this old building on a narrow historical street dating back to the 13C. The space is an ode to his origins, with exposed stonework and beams, red leather banquettes and, the icing on the cake, an earthenware stove typical of Eastern European. A tribute to his mother's cooking (matka is Polish for "mother"), the menu is a culinary journey, comprising neatly plated dishes that whet the appetite: a rustic sourdough soup, potatoes, shredded dried pork belly and slow-cooked egg, pierogi ruskie (potato and cheese dumplings), grilled onion and sour cream. To finish off, the szarlotka – apple and cinnamon cake with vanilla ice cream – is made according to a comforting family recipe.

Name: Matsu Izakaya
Description: This simple “izakaya” is run by two young partners from the Dominican Republic who have embarked upon their first solo venture following several years working in restaurants in Barcelona. Thankfully, it has had a positive impression on locals thanks to their friendly approach and the varied selection of Japanese-inspired cuisine on offer, featuring an array of modern touches and dishes teeming with flavour. Here, you’ll also find the usual nigiri and sashimi, but almost everyone veers towards the crispy shiso starter with burrata stracciatella, truffled honey and Iberian pork jowl, the varied choice of sushi rolls, and ending with a dish or two cooked on the robata grill, such as the superb Katshu Sando, a fusion between the popular smoked pork chops from the Dominican Republic and tonkatsu sauce from Japan.

Name: Matsuhisa Munich
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted
Description: In keeping with the high standards of the luxurious Mandarin Oriental, this elegant minimalist-style restaurant is run by Nobu Matsuhisa, a renowned restaurateur with a global presence. The menu features a fusion of Japanese and Peruvian cuisines. As well as sushi and sashimi, there are exciting options such as Peruvian rib eye anticucho (skewers) or the house classic, black cod. Dishes are intended for sharing, allowing you to discover a kaleidoscope of flavours. In summer, you can dine on the hotel's roof terrace and take in fantastic views over Munich.

Name: Matsukawa
Address: 8 Queen Street, Smithfield, Dublin City, DO7 Y683, Ireland
Description: With only eight seats around its counter, don’t be put off if you can’t secure a reservation at this sweetly run sushi restaurant at the first time of asking. The omakase menu is based around fine seafood produce, most of it Irish, with multiple servings of nigiri forming a large chunk of the experience – the hamachi and the salmon are particular highlights. The team are endearing and the service is not drawn-out, allowing you to enjoy a satisfying meal that doesn’t take all night. A good selection of sake and other Japanese spirits completes the offering.

Name: Matsunoki
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Wheelchair access
Description: At the Japanese restaurant of the luxurious Hotel Bellevue, guests can choose to sit on the panoramic terrace or indoors in an elegant dining room with refined design, featuring an open kitchen and sushi counter. The menu offers excellent sashimi, available in both classic and creative interpretations, alongside premium meat specialties such as Wagyu beef. The extensive wine list includes selections by the glass, complemented by a carefully curated choice of sake and Japanese whiskies, perfect for rounding out the dining experience.

Name: Matsuzaki
Description: This intimate restaurant offers authentic kaiseki omakase by the chef who trained at a renowned culinary institute. The petite yet cosy space is decorated with fine tableware and glassware, along with paintings by the chef’s mother. The meal opens with a flavourful soup, followed by a beautifully composed hassun of seasonal bites, and concludes with a nabemono of freshly cooked rice, vegetables, and fish—Japanese cuisine that remains faithful to its fundamentals.

Name: Matteo Ristorante
Description: In elegant and intimate spaces with soft, muted tones, guests enjoy the contemporary cuisine of Matteo Marra. Meat and fish feature equally on the menu, with a constant emphasis on meticulously crafted and spectacular presentations of dishes. A small outdoor area sits under a portico, with tables that must be reserved well in advance during the warmer months. Coffee and aperitif service is also available at the adjacent Laboratorio, at No. 10.

Name: Matur og Drykkur
Description: 2026 heralded a move to stylish new premises for this earnestly run and authentic restaurant, where the ersatz-industrial space is lightened with some whimsical flashes of art and glassware. The cookbook of the same name by influential food-writer Helga Sigurðardótti is the inspiration behind the culinary philosophy of updating traditional Icelandic recipes and celebrating local ingredients. The open kitchen calmly delivers a well-balanced set menu, which could include deliciously sweet scallops with crab and chervil or succulent lamb with buttermilk and crowberries.

Name: Maté
Address: Park Hyatt Abu Dhabi Hotel and Villas, Al Saadiyat Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park
Description: Descend the stairs to the sound of pumping music and you’ll find yourself transported to Buenos Aires at his atmospheric restaurant in the Park Hyatt Hotel. The centrepiece is the open kitchen and the flaming wood-fired grills here. The menu does have some Lebanese influence but it’s really all about Argentinian dishes with great charred flavours and top ingredients, be they prawns or beef. If you really want to feel part of the action, sit at the counter.

Name: Maurachbund
Description: This listed building lies in the heart of Bregenz, in a side street not far from the town hall. It has welcomed diners for over 160 years. Historical rustic-style elements such as old floorboards and wood-panelled ceilings and walls have been beautifully combined with modern interior design details. The dedicated pair running operations are Carla Booz and Manuel Willi – she provides cordial and attentive service front of house, while he oversees the kitchen, cooking up delicious food, including "filet 'Stroganoff' with porcini and spaetzli", or sea bass with a bean and tomato salad served lukewarm. Classics such as Wiener schnitzel and Tafelspitz are also present and correct!

Name: Maurice
Description: The friendly eatery of delightful Kaatje De Blick and chef Karl Ave is in fact named after their cat! They aim for a home-from-home vibe and welcome guests like old friends: “Maurice is like coming home” in their own words. The veteran chef masterfully deploys his classical training to craft knockout dishes and sauces, albeit with the occasional more modern twist. For example, he often slips in Asian notes, illustrated by a ballotine of langoustine underscored by a sublime yuzu and dashi sauce.

Name: Mawa's Kitchen
Address: 305 Aspen Airport Business Center, Ste. F, Aspen, CO, 81611, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Mawa's Kitchen may not be the easiest to find with its tucked-away entrance, but stay the course because it's worth visiting this welcoming spot. Light colors, tasteful artwork and bare tables set with wildflower-filled vases create a mood-boosting vibe inside, while the outdoor terrace is a breezy perch. The food is equally appealing (think new-world meets old-world). Owner Mawa McQueen, who hails from the Côte d’Ivoire, delivers extraordinary quality with everyday value, such as black-eyed pea hummus served with pickled, charred and smoked vegetables and bread. The African chicken and seafood gumbo is boldly spiced and finger-licking good, but don't fill up because you'll want dessert—especially a wedge of that dreamy cheesecake.

Name: Max & Moi
Address: Grand Place Baudouin Premier 4, Braine-l'Alleud, 1420, Belgium
Description: Max & Pina have set up shop on Place Baudouin 1er in a tastefully refurbished town house dripping in understated glamour and sporting a suitably tasteful colour scheme. The couple works with a talented youthful chef, Julien Hauspie, who prefers to work with local produce while rolling out his experience gleaned in worldclass establishments at home and abroad. The chef’s know-how can be tasted in the beurre blanc that flanks seabass or in his way with carrots, which he might pair with a béarnaise sauce and tarragon and lemon oil, also demonstrating his creative side and fun-loving personality. Vibrant, exciting cuisine that comes in a four- or five-course menu.

Name: Maxens
Address: chaussée du Roi Baudouin 117, Saint-Symphorien, 7030, Belgium
Description: Stéphane Grulois, a man of many talents, played a major part in designing the stylish, cosy interior of this arty restaurant. Stéphane is, however, first and foremost a gifted chef. His love of traditional French cuisine shines through in flawless craftsmanship and know-how. He might cook veal medium rare in a parsley and mustard crust, which is paired with a subtle, delicate gravy, fluffy dauphine potato puffs and celery purée. The chef enjoys serving the food himself. Excellent value for money at lunchtime. A multisensory experience awaits!

Name: Maxi
Address: Via Luigi Serio 8, SS 145 Sorrentina km 14,500, Vico Equense, 80069, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Boasting a splendid location overlooking the sea, this gourmet restaurant is part of the Capo La Gala hotel. Head down to the seafront from the hotel entrance (lift available) to the restaurant, where the romantic lapping of the waves and a spectacular view (especially at sunset) accompany your meal, along with impeccable service overseen by the skilful Giulia Tavolaro. Chef Emmanuel Scotti, from Ischia, serves various tasting menus of meat and fish, with the option of choosing courses à la carte style. His cuisine focuses on local recipes and ingredients, giving them a modern twist with the occasional international influence, as demonstrated by the raw marinated amberjack – a softer, Mediterranean version of ceviche. For simpler, more traditional cuisine, try La Taverna Nerea.

Name: Maxime Colin
Description: Maxime Colin’s artistically appointed romantic establishment was made for a date night (or lunch), while the patio, tucked away in the garden of Jourdain castle, drips with alfresco charm come summertime. The menu quickly reveals the chef’s passion for stellar ingredients and international influences. His modern culinary style features subtlety, spot-on craftsmanship and a constant quest for innovation. For example, he may coat scallops wrapped in a cabbage leaf in a house-made XO sauce and pair them with a salad of green peas jazzed up by a zest of refreshing lemon juice.

Name: Maxine's on Shine
Address: 337 N. Shine Ave., Orlando, FL, 32803, USA
Description: In operation for more than a decade, Maxine and Kirt Earhart's Colonialtown charmer is everyone's favorite neighborhood hangout. Crowds spill out in front during the weekend for brunch, thanks to a host of comforting dishes that soothe and satisfy. Think plates of fried green tomatoes, flaky crab cakes and of course, chicken and waffles. Dinner follows suit with such familiar yet flavorful dishes as a half-pound burger, or skillet lasagna, which is available with roasted vegetables instead of beef.There are good vibes all round. The décor is eclectic and bears a whimsical slant by way of bold colors, lots of artwork, a dark, sultry bar, as well as tightly packed tables. Interior accommodations are supplemented by ample outdoor seating.

Name: Maxwell Fuzhou Oyster Cake
Address: Maxwell Food Centre, #01-05, 1 Kadayanallur Street, 069184, Singapore
Description: The second-generation owner still fries oyster cakes à la minute as her mother did in the 1960s. They may be darker than usual, but the minced pork, oysters, prawns and coriander are still soft and juicy under the crispy crust.

Name: Maxwells Trading
Address: 1516 W. Carroll Ave., Chicago, IL, 60607, USA
Description: It can feel as if half the city is dining in this quiet pocket of West Loop. Conversation and laughter bounce off the hard warehouse floors and large, black-framed windows and travel along a bar that looks almost endless from the front door. The cooking behind all this commotion assuredly plays with Japanese, Chinese, and Thai elements. Think Japanese eggplant with scallion bread, sweet potatoes with Thai green curry, or soup dumpling tortellini with maitake mushroom. Turbot with Swiss chard and kombu beurre blanc was a recent standout. Servers are not fazed by the crowds, while bartenders shake and stir drinks that keep energy levels high. And in stark contrast to the industrial setting, a rooftop herb and vegetable garden helps stock the kitchen.

Name: May Snow Hakka Food
Address: 16, Lane 329, Section 1, Dunhua South Road, Da'an District, Taipei, 106, Taiwan
Description: For 10-plus years, this restaurant has been feeding health-conscious diners with novel Hakkanese dishes that are lower in salt and fat than normal. Formally trained in Hunan cuisine, the chef lavishes great care over the freshness of his ingredients. His menu is dominated by seafood, such as umami-laden deep-fried red yeast cuttlefish. Some painstaking recipes, like salt-baked free-range Tainan chicken, require pre-ordering.

Name: MayRee
Address: 58 E. 1st St., New York, NY, 10003, USA
Description: Chef/Owner Orawan Sawangphol tells us a story of southern Thai cooking at Mayree, named for a character from the Thai folktale, Twelve Sisters. The space is cozy and charming, as is the compact menu. Spice levels are far from timid, and all of the dishes, including Isan specialties, showcase great personality. Park mor plates rice crepe dumplings with a sweet chopped peanut filling topped with coconut milk and fried garlic. Kua kling is a dry, southern-style roasted curry made with ground pork that really brings the heat and displays incredible flavors. After a fiery meal, refresh your palate with coconut ice cream served in a coconut shell. Sek Saraboon runs the serious cocktail program, while all of the creative sips are named for Mayree's sisters.

Name: Maya
Address: Crossroads Mall, Banilad Road, Cebu, Cebu, 6000, The Philippines
Description: This two-storey restaurant at Crossroads Mall has a bold interior with painted skulls adorning the staircase, dramatic lighting, and vivid colors. Parquet floors and sturdy chairs make for a lively vibe. Expect vibrant Southern California-style Mexican fare – fajitas, burritos, tacos and the country's largest all-agave tequila bar upstairs. Ideal for groups, it's festive and fun, especially on salsa nights and when DJs play.

Name: MayaBay
Address: Jumeirah Al Naseem Hotel, 906 Jumeirah Street, Umm Suqeim 3, Dubai
Description: Glamorous sister to the original in Monte Carlo, this restaurant’s unmistakeable Asian vibe comes courtesy of wood panelling, carvings and a cool red palette, while a resident DJ keeps things jumping until the wee small hours. The menu covers Japan, Thailand and China, so you can start with sushi or dim sum and then head for their signature pad thai or something from the robata grill. Grab some mochi buns from the counter on the way home.

Name: Maydān
Address: 1346 Florida Ave. NW, Washington, DC, 20009, USA
Description: Many restaurants boast of inspired flavors and technique, but few flaunt such cooking prowess as Maydān—a veritable showstopper whose roaring hearth verges on wildfire. The precision required of the team may be consuming and cooking technique elemental, but the results are delicious bliss. À la carte is available, but the prix-fixe is a popular feast, with bread and spreads; veggies and meats; and a dessert to round it out. Flatbreads with muhamarra, hummus, and smoked mutabal is a meal unto itself; while tahini-coconut rice pudding with candied cardamom makes a compelling finish.Guests seated in this rustic space—with patterned wood and lofty ceilings—are made even more comfortable with an array of singular Middle Eastern-inspired sips and labels.

Name: Mayha
Address: 43 Chiltern Street, Marylebone, London, W1U 6LS, United Kingdom
Description: There’s a real sense of style to this small Japanese restaurant that relocated from Beirut to London. The chic interior is dominated by a curved wooden counter where the chefs take centre stage, the tree-inspired lights casting it in an intimate glow. The highly seasonal omakase menu – which is available in a shorter form on weekdays – comes with an enjoyable dose of theatre and pushes luxury ingredients to the fore, with the generous nigiri selection forming the core part of the menu.

Name: Maymanta
Address: Plaza de Pius XII 4, Barcelona, 08028, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: If you’re on the lookout for a restaurant with a view and you like the sound of an “exotic culinary experience”, Maymanta is a great option for you. Located on the 19th floor of the luxurious Grand Hyatt Barcelona hotel, with its panoramic rooftop terrace, enjoy authentic Peruvian cuisine prepared with Mediterranean ingredients. Chef Omar Malpartida likes to say that he combines “what's here and there” when it comes to cuisine that takes guests on a gastronomic journey to Peru’s coast, its mountains, and its jungle. On the menu you’ll find a wide array of ceviches –we particularly enjoyed the “carretillero” (a mix of seafood served with a spicy tiger's milk), grilled dishes, house specialities, plus good options for sharing. Maymanta’s design is inspired by that of a wood hut in the Peruvian jungle!

Name: Maynats
Description: In this pavilion with an octagonal conservatory and a casual vibe, the Maynats (meaning "lads" or "kids" in the Béarn dialect) continue to tick all the boxes with their instinctive, playful cuisine, embodied by particularly spot on surf and turf combinations and a stunning dessert. The blend of an ambitious score and a happy-go-lucky ambiance have earned it a place in the hearts of the locals. Surprise menu with several courses in the evening and a well-curated organic wine list. What’s not to like?

Name: Mayu Cocoon
Address: 6, Lane 206, Section 2, Fucian Road, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
Description: Tucked away in a quiet alley, this place has a compact, Japanese-inspired space fitted with counter seats and brass pendant lamps. At dinner, all guests are required to order an izakaya-style nine-tapas dinner set, perfect with alcoholic drinks. Exact items depend on availability on the day; if you crave more, see the blackboard for add-ons. The chef behind the counter is happy to interact with diners. Later at night, order à la carte instead.

Name: Maza
Description: At Maza, the food tells a tale of travel and love between Robin and Julien Burnier, a cosmopolitan couple with stints in Japan, America and France. Together they sign a vibrant, indulgent score that involves dishes to share of European, Asian and Oriental influences, like tartare of trout on polenta chips or ginger-laced tataki of rump steak. Meticulously sourced local produce, well curated wine cellar and a pleasant patio in a pedestrian neighbourhood – bookings essential.

Name: Maza
Address: Rua Manuel Guedes, 243, São Paulo, 04536-070, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Valet parking
Description: As well as a highly enjoyable dining experience, Maza boasts a relaxing and welcoming setting, where the combination of wood and soft tones is clearly evident as soon as you walk through the door – a decor embellished by the beautiful cherry tree. The cuisine here is based around classic Japanese fare with a modern and personalised touch, including some Korean dishes. The different types of menus on offer include a seven-course option called Shinrai (served exclusively at table), the Omakase (only available at the bar counter), an à la carte. Exquisite dishes include karasumi, ussuzukuri, Wagyu tataki, “shake butter”, as well as sushi, sashimi, temaki. An impressive choice of sakes and cocktails completes the picture.

Name: Mazarine
Address: 22 Hanover Square, Mayfair, London, W1S 1JA, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: On the corner of the leafy Hanover Square in London’s most upmarket neighbourhood, Mazarine comes with an appropriately formal feel to both its service and the linen-laid décor. The neutral tones of the dining room ensure the focus remains on the premium seafood that drives the menu, which is generally prepared with a classically French approach. The likes of grilled scallops with roasted hazelnuts look simple but harbour depth of flavour thanks to the superior quality of the ingredients. If you’re celebrating, the oysters, caviar and grilled langoustines are all hard to resist.

Name: Mazette !
Description: Mazette is on point! As Laura, the pastry chef, and Maximilien, the chef, get to work in their pleasant little traditional bistro, we take a table alongside the ever-faithful clientele of regulars. On the menu: French bistro classics (pâté croûte, tourte au Comté and truffle ham, grilled pork belly), nods to the proprietors' roots in Alsace (spaetzle, poultry vol-au-vent with morel mushrooms, apple tart, rhubarb compote) and, on the blackboard, a short list of dishes for sharing.

Name: Mazi
Address: 12-14 Hillgate Street, Kensington, London, W8 7SR, United Kingdom
Description: A real neighbourhood restaurant with a pure Greek heart, there is a wonderful buzz to the intimate Mazi. It’s one of those places where you can leave the decision making to the passionate, engaging team, who are ready to recommend their favourite Greek wines and dishes – such as the terrifically tender spiced lamb rump. The menu is designed for sharing so order a good range between you; for dessert however, it’s hard to look past the loukoumades. A small front terrace and larger rear one add to the appeal – if the weather’s good enough, you can pretend you’re in Athens.

Name: Mazi
Description: Close to the city’s famous cathedral, you’ll find this charming neighbourhood restaurant with a distinctly Mediterranean vibe. From the bright, airy décor to cooking that is fresh, pared-back and abundant in olive oil, the pleasant warmth of the Greek and Italian coasts will feel within touching distance. The well-priced sharing dishes range from delicious, just-baked pitta with salt and herbs to a generous helping of cannoli. Chatty, welcoming service adds to the cheery atmosphere.

Name: Ma•dé
Address: 22 Spring St., New York, NY, 10012, USA
Description: This comforting charmer honors the communal dining traditions of Indonesia’s West Sumatra. Thick, knotted ropes hang overhead in a narrow, intimate room fit with white brick and a tiled wall that nearly looks like white seashells. Chef Cedric Vongerichten delivers a verifiable feast served in little bowls and plates that fill every inch of space on the table. With the exception of your entrée, there are no choices to make for this easy prix fixe. The entirety of the meal lands all at once, allowing diners to bounce between fluke sashimi dressed in a light sambal hijau, crispy sweetbreads sitting in a gulai curry, and egg balado with Thai basil. Pickles, garlic rice and crisp tapioca crackers also dot the table.

Name: Mdl le Bistrot
Description: A few minutes from his MICHELIN-starred restaurant, Matthieu de Lauzun ("MDL") has given a new lease of life to this place, which used to be a private wine cellar. Within these thick stone walls, a laid-back clientele embraces the culinary experience in this buzzing atmosphere. The menu draws on the treasures of the Mediterranean terroir: stuffed tomatoes, Andalusian gazpacho and house-made pâté en croûte sit alongside sea bream tartare and beef cheek confit. With both modest labels and renowned names, the well-constructed wine list, shared with the MICHELIN-starred restaurant, has something for everyone.

Name: Meadowsweet
Description: Tucked next to the steely skeleton of the Williamsburg Bridge, Meadowsweet cuts a stylish industrial figure with its glass-fronted façade, whitewashed brick walls and original mosaic-tiled floors. Inside, the restaurant jumps with a steady stream of locals and regulars, all here for well-priced and well-executed food.The fuss is quite merited. Despite ample competition in this section of town, Owners Polo Dobkin and Stephanie Lempert elevate the kitchen’s dishes ranging from crispy baby artichokes with shaved parmesan and orechiette with blue crab tossed in a lemon beurre fondue to spiced duck breast with sweet corn polenta, grilled escarole and Mandarin orange. It's all done in a lovely, urbane setting with loads of charm and friendly service.

Name: Mearkas
Description: It is an 11-minute drive from the highway to Mearkas. The short journey through the stunning Frisian countryside serves as a prelude to the sense of tranquillity that awaits you in this glass-walled restaurant flooded with light. The surrounding vegetable gardens, fields, and glamping tents form the backdrop to this ode to Friesland. Chef Kees and gardener Christiaan have joined forces to showcase the finest local produce. Everything is either homegrown or sourced from nearby suppliers. In his set menu, the chef skillfully marries the hearty flavours of Friesland with a touch of sophistication, in dishes characterised by vitality and freshness. Think North Sea sole, delicately marinated in lemon, enhanced with local bacon and expressive garnishes of sour cream, fennel, lemon, puffed quinoa and paprika sorbet. A digestif by the campfire makes for the perfect ending to a uniquely serene experience.

Name: Medici
Address: Weißadlergasse 2, Frankfurt on the Main, 60311, Germany
Description: Two brothers are your hosts in this city centre restaurant. International dishes with a Mediterranean influence are served in a modern atmosphere.

Name: Mediterraneo Dine&Wine
Description: Just steps from the picturesque port, in the heart of Hvar’s old town, this family-run restaurant has been a cornerstone of local cuisine for over 70 years, with a menu focused primarily on fish but offering much more. Try, for example, the Premium Ribeye: 330 g of beef ribeye aged for 60 days, served with red wine sauce, sweet pepper and onion potato cream, broccoli, and mushrooms. The spacious terrace provides a relaxed atmosphere, while the interior stands out with walls adorned with floral arrangements. A small private room houses a selection of fine wines, many of which come from the island and other regions of Croatia. Booking is essential, especially during high season.

Name: Medlar
Address: 438 King's Road, Chelsea, London, SW10 0LJ, United Kingdom
Description: After more than a decade of service, this neighbourhood spot is becoming something of a Cheslea institution. The locals keep it well-patronised and it's easy to see why, thanks to the relaxed air and spring-like decoration with apple green banquettes and faux blossoming trees. The kitchen doesn't compromise on ingredient quality, with fine produce used in classic dishes like crab raviolo or roast quail with a textbook potato terrine. The wine list is knowledgably curated and pairings are suggested for every dish.

Name: Meerok Super
Description: Meerok Super is a small six-seat restaurant that serves outsize creativity. The vegetables grown in the on-site vegetable patch, aged fish and meat, and seasonal ingredients are transformed into the day’s tasting menu. The grilled meat course, cooked over charcoal for aroma, texture, and juiciness, and served with rice, creates a seamless transition from Western to Korean flavours. Expect to be delighted by unexpected yet harmonious flavour combinations that change daily.

Name: Meesapam Khun Yai Chian
Address: 56/8, 65/24 Mu 1, Thep Krasatti Road, Ko Kaeo, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Grandma Chian opened this Hokkien restaurant in 1952. Her great-great grandchildren have stayed loyal to her recipes and proudly exhibit her cooking utensils. Serving Phuket favourites, the Mee Sapam, stir-fried Hokkien noodles with seafood, is great. The stir-fried oysters with crispy egg roll are beautifully crafted with beansprouts, kale and a tasty chilli sauce.

Name: Meez
Address: Sultan Street, As Salamah, Jeddah, 23437, Saudi Arabia
Description: This all-day eatery specialises in carefully prepared Middle Eastern and Saudi plates. Inside, the restaurant is simple yet with a warm and homely feel. The dishes are unique and well-flavoured, with Saudi ingredients at the forefront. Their mezze platters are made to share when you’re in a large group, and some noteworthy dishes are the Laban Setto and the sticky date pudding – all fairly priced.

Name: Mei Liang Jia
Address: 168 Dalian Street, Sanmin District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
Description: This eatery in a simple white room with wooden furniture is much-loved by locals. The signature soup – made daily with freshly slaughtered local chicken – comes in over 10 flavours, including pickled fried chilli, Chinese Angelica root or golden cordyceps. The lean pork version with sesame oil is especially popular – the depth and nutty notes work wonders with the pork and cabbage. Try the noodles tossed in scallion oil and the various sides, too.

Name: Mei Wah
Description: Mei Wah has been a beacon of authentic Chinese cuisine since 1965. Unadulterated piquancy and finesse, unyielding to Western palates, and imbued with a touch of refinement by the chef, who represents the third generation at the helm. He makes just about everything in-house, from the spicy chicken broths to the fiery chilli oils, guaranteeing bold flavours. Whenever feasible, he procures ingredients from the vicinity. Immerse yourself in the culinary heritage of far-off lands – think steamed dim sum filled with prawn, ginger and that addictively delectable chilli oil, succulent spicy prawn in a typhoon shelter wok dish, the traditional Peking duck that the chef carves at your table. Wine or sake accompany your food.

Name: Mei's Cuisine
Address: 1-1 & 1-2 Jiazi Old Street, Jiazhong Road, Jiaojiang, Taizhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: This is the first Taizhou branch of the sister brand of Xu's Cuisine in Chengdu, and it showcases not only authentic Sichuan fare but also some Taizhou seafood dishes. The wok-fried pork belly in Sichuan spices has remarkable wok hei; the blackened chillies bring colour contrast and smoky flavour. Tangy chillies and radish pickled in-house lend nuanced, rounded heat to the sautéed bullfrog with chillies, angled loofah and young ginger.

Name: Meidz Seafood
Address: 473-2 Zhongshan Road, Shalu District, Taichung, 433, Taiwan
Description: Before opening this restaurant in 1989, the owners were fishers and fishmongers. Now a household name and managed by the couple's descendants, Meidz still prides itself on quality seafood, mostly from Penghu. The oyster vermicelli soup with sesame oil features handmade noodles from Taichung and plump baby oysters from Penghu. Check out the catch of the day, too. The chef can adjust portions to suit the size of your party.

Name: Meilenstein
Description: A listed building steeped in history is the attractive location that houses this chic restaurant with its bar and lovely terrace. Here, they propose a set menu that you can put together yourself and that draws on modern influences. The front-of-house team is friendly and accomplished. There is also an appealing selection of cocktails at this stylish venue with a variety of spaces you can hire for private events.

Name: Meissl & Schadn
Description: The schnitzel reigns supreme at this restaurant in the heart of the old town. Even from the outside you can peer into the open kitchen and see the house speciality, Wiener schnitzel, being prepared. The rest of the menu is worth perusing too, with other Austrian classics such as Tafelspitz, Esterházy lentils, or goose (when in season). And be sure to save room for dessert – traditional treats like Salzburger Nockerlor classic apple strudel are too good to miss! Highlights also include a nicely curated wine list and professional service that's both warm and attentive. The setting has its own appeal: inside, stylish details across two floors create a welcoming brasserie feel, and outside, the inviting terrace opens directly onto the iconic Getreidegasse. Tip: Leave your car in the multi-storey car park Altstadtgarage A.

Name: Meissl & Schadn
Description: Here, the Wiener schnitzel is the obvious choice – it's best to order it "mit allen Schikanen" (with all the trimmings)! At this attractive restaurant on the Ring that encircles Vienna's old town, good food is accompanied by classical music, Viennese service culture and an elegant yet pleasantly down-to-earth atmosphere. In the open kitchen (which is also visible from outside), you can see the schnitzels being pounded. Why not take part in the weekly schnitzel course. There is even a book for sale: The Wiener Schnitzel Love Book.

Name: Meister Lampe
Description: It's a real pleasure to eat here, and there's a good reason for that: chef-patron Daniel Stübler clearly puts his heart and soul into running his cosy little restaurant. He cooks up excellent regional and international dishes, and also does the serving himself – not only is he highly accomplished at what he does, he is also an extremely cordial host and single-handedly creates a fantastic atmosphere! The carefully curated wine list is also remarkable, featuring wines from Baden-Württemberg, Baden and the Palatinate only.

Name: Mekong
Description: In a shopping street in Chur's old town, this friendly restaurant on the first floor is expertly run by the enthusiastic Phommarath family. They serve authentic dishes from Southeast Asia, such as house-made wonton and spring rolls, as well as various curry and wok dishes.
