Description: The hum of contented diners, judicious lighting, a confident service team and a sophisticated feel to the room all reassure you the moment you enter that you’ve chosen the right spot, especially if it’s date night. Sharing is the key when it comes to the menu, where fish and shellfish are given center stage in an appealing collection of dishes, big and small. The seafood is responsibly sourced, and the flavors are global, whether that’s tamarind sauce with buttermilk-fried monkfish, or 'nduja with tuna. If you’re after some pasta, don’t look further than deliciously creamy spaghetti with Maine lobster.

Name: Mr & Mrs Bund
Address: 6F, Bund 18, 18 Zhongshan Dong Yi Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, 200002, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: On the city's dining scene for over 10 years, Chef Pairet's brasserie never ages. Lovely service, great music, a terrific wine list and bags of French joie de vivre make dining here a real experience. In the modern space – inside a former bank dating from 1922 – diners feast on chilled seafood platters, and charbroiled steaks and seafood. Original creations such as lemon & lemon tart with a sorbet-filled whole lemon also stand out.

Name: Mr & Mrs Hawker
Address: 3rd Floor, Andaz Doha Hotel, 23 Diplomatic Street, Zone 61, West Bay, Doha, Qatar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Whether you come here to rekindle your memories of Singapore or just to experience something a little different, this restaurant delivers on the famed Hawker street food. Wherever you sit in the spacious interior dotted with subtle Asian touches, the focus is firmly on the chefs at work in the lively open kitchen. The menu is headed up 'From the Garden City', 'From the Pot', 'From the Wok' and 'From the Hawker Street.’ Expect all the vibrant Singaporean classics, from chilli crab to mango sago pudding, all carefully prepared. Ensure you let them know your spice tolerance, as they don’t hold back.

Name: Mr Fox
Address: 38 Parnell Square West, Dublin City, DO1 X9TO, Ireland
Description: The basement of a red-brick Georgian townhouse plays host to this this welcoming restaurant, whose soft furnishings tie in with the colour scheme and the ornately patterned floor tiles. Cooking comes in the form of either an à la carte or a set chef's choice menu, with both of them containing fresh, flavoursome dishes. Prime Irish produce is a feature, such as Flaggy Shore oyster or Kilkeel crab, but so are global flavours and techniques in the likes of langoustine toast with yuzu kosho and bonito. Service comes from a charming team.

Name: Mr Guss
Description: Augustin Guibert, a.k.a. Guss, a chef with an impeccable track record, has gone solo in this contemporary eatery on the ground-floor of a handsome 19C stone building. This inventive cook impresses with his manifest technical skill, which allows him to play with flavours and textures, as is the case with a crunchy tartlet of velvety onions, carrots confit in their jus, calamansi gel, pesto ice cream and a cromesquis of feta and honey. Hats off to the loving care and attention lavished on the splendid local produce, particularly veggies. We warrant that each colourful dish will bring a smile to your lips.

Name: Mr Morris
Address: Britomart, Corner of Galway & Commerce Street, Auckland Central, Auckland, 1010, New Zealand
Description: Look out for Shane Cotton’s striking mural of pots outside the Britomart heritage trading building that houses this restaurant. Distressed walls, earthy tones and plenty of oak create a warm and effortlessly chic environment. The open kitchen forms the centrepiece of the room, from where dishes full of bold Pacific and New Zealand flavours are sent forth. The grill is used to great effect, in dishes like duck breast with pear and chestnuts, but the kitchen also shows its delicate hand via the silky squid with fried almonds.

Name: Mr. Ahn's Craft Makgeolli
Description: Mr. Ahn's Craft Makgeolli reimagines Korean banju culture through a contemporary lens, offering a wide selection of makgeolli paired with dishes designed to complement it. Signatures include house-made tofu served with saeujeot kimchi, pork belly, and pollock roe—a menu that highlights contrasting textures and layered flavours. Refined with modern technique, the menu features seasonal small plates and course options alongside a rotating selection of aged Korean liquors, making the venue suitable for both relaxed meals and convivial gatherings.

Name: Mr. Lam
Address: Rua Maria Angélica 21, Rio de Janeiro, 22470-201, Brazil
Description: Mr. Lam gained renowned for his culinary prowess in restaurants in New York and London, however he has run this modern, sophisticated eatery on the edge of the Rodrigo de Freitas lagoon for almost two decades. In contrast with other gastronomic restaurants these days, the majority of dishes on the menu have been mainstays since it first opened, in so doing keeping with the tradition of offering the best Chinese cuisine. Featuring a hint of cutting-edge innovation as well as a focus on top-quality ingredients, the menu boasts memorable dishes such as the lightly battered and crispy Senhor Batista prawns, with a delicious sweet and sour sauce. The restaurant is laid out on three floors, with an attractive dining room and welcoming bar on the top floor that includes picture windows and a glass roof that provide lots of natural light and stunning views.

Name: Mrs. Fong Chinese Desserts
Address: 198 Temple Street, Jordan, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: This busy family-run shop moved here in 2022. Over 10 Chinese sweets are made from scratch daily, such as red bean cake or put-chai cake. Black sesame roll is especially prized for its soft-springy texture and deep flavour.

Name: Ms.Maria & Mr.Singh
Address: 2F, 68 Soi Sukhumvit 31, Sukhumvit Road, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Inspired by a Mexican-Indian love story, two cultures combine in both gastronomy and design at this sensorily striking restaurant. Vibrant oranges and blues make for a colourful setting. The food also makes a statement, playing with spices and textures to twist conventional styles. The well-judged fusion cooking includes dishes like pork vindaloo tacos and papdi chaat served on a mini taco shell. The service team provide fabulous hospitality with their high energy and friendly manner.

Name: Mu Fan Bloom
Address: 52 Jianmei Road, East District, Hsinchu City, Taiwan
Description: This noodle shop with an inviting light-filled room is unusual in that it serves gluten-free noodles only, in broth or dressed in sauces. Choose from four sorts: tofu, konjac, corn and hand-torn rice noodles. The option with squid, fried egg, sliced pork, coriander and crispy seaweed with a squeeze of lemon stands out for its bright, zesty notes. The variety with rosemary chilli sauce with star anise, Sichuan pepper and olive oil is another smash hit.

Name: Mud Brick House
Address: 113 Changchun Street, Beipu Township, Hsinchu County, Taiwan
Description: Converted from a century-old courtyard residence, the room offers an insight into a bygone way of life. Since 1999, the owner-chef has been serving his grandma’s Hakkanese recipes. His signature poached free-range chicken boasts golden, bouncy skin and firm, juicy meat with a kumquat dip to cut through the richness. Golden sweet potato is added to local rice for fluffiness, fragrance and sweetness. Portion sizes can be tailored to your party size.

Name: Muggels by Gijs
Description: On the outskirts of Uden, this restaurant is accommodated in a quaint thatched-roof farmhouse. It features a snug interior with wooden ceiling beams and rustic-style decor, plus an outdoor terrace overlooking the surrounding fields. Having spent years honing his skills at De Lindehof in Nuenen, Gijs Hoevenaars has struck out on his own in this delightful setting. From classic tournedos Rossini to Mediterranean and Asian-inspired dishes, the chef displays proficiency across the board. Take, for example, his tuna sashimi, which he perks up with soy, citrus and pickled vegetables. The à la carte menu is pretty extensive, so deciding will not be easy.

Name: Mugunfa
Description: A modern floral sign serves as the restaurant's symbol as its name refers to the rose of Sharon, the national flower of South Korea. The chef vows to pay respect to his home country and contribute to the development of Korean cuisine. He relies on a palate nurtured by the flavours of his mother’s cooking. Unravelling the history of food culture, he utilises his experience in Western cuisine. Nori gimbap rolls are presented as rice crackers. Raw prawn ganjang saeu is served with a caviar and kiwifruit sauce. The chef presents new culinary expressions with a modern sensibility.

Name: Mugunghwa
Address: 38F, Lotte Hotel, 30 Eulji-ro, Jung-gu, Seoul, 04533, South Korea
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Notable sake list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Mugunghwa at Lotte Hotel offers a refined take on classic Korean cuisine, paired with sweeping city views from its top-floor location. Embracing the philosophy that 'food is medicine', the restaurant crafts dishes using seasonal ingredients to deliver flavours that are both comforting and complex. Highlights include burdock gangjeong with coastal hog fennel sauce, imjasutang in an autumn olive and sesame broth, and haesamjeung with sea cucumber and black garlic sauce. With a focus on traditional ingredients, natural seasonings, and fermented elements, Mugunghwa presents a distinctly Korean, health-conscious dining experience.

Name: Muji Beef Noodles
Address: 239 Wuxing Street, Xinyi District, Taipei, 110, Taiwan
Description: The three sisters who run the place are very specific about their cooking. The flavoursome broth is made with beef bones and meat, Chinese herbs, scallion, garlic and a secret fruit that lends a subtle sweetness. The signature beef noodle soup uses only local beef for its unrivalled meaty flavour. Equally addictive is their jinbing – a fluffy pancake made to order with beef or pork wrapped inside. Don’t miss their marinated food either.

Name: Mukjung
Description: Korean-American chef Austin Kang prepares his own fermented foods and jang in-house, guided by the Korean belief that food is medicine. Traditional Korean dishes are presented with contemporary flair, including a flourless pyogo mushroom and shrimp jeon with myeolchi-jeot aioli. The meltingly tender slow-cooked chicken is served with citrus- and herb-scented rice, pairing well with the banchan. Be sure to order the main dish a day in advance.

Name: Mulania Brasserie
Description: With its combination of sleek, contemporary style and rustic ceiling beams, this old Graubünden building provides an attractive setting. Host couple Yvonne Marx and Sascha Meyer have reimagined their place as a brasserie, serving tried-and-tested regional specialities such as capuns (chard rolls) or quark pizokels (buckwheat spaetzle), plus brasserie classics like moules frites or beef bourguignon. Last but not least, there are some delicious seafood options – the chef's first love. Delightful terrace. Open from 3pm.

Name: Mulcahys
Address: Main Street, Kenmare, V93 W35F, Ireland
Description: Having been a presence in Kenmare since 1995, this smart, warm restaurant has become a part of the town’s fabric, with plenty of the locals contributing to its lively atmosphere. Come for cocktails and snacks in the bar or settle in for the evening to enjoy a menu underpinned by local beef and seafood. The hearty dishes pack in plenty of flavour and are classic at heart, as evidenced by a terrific deconstructed version of a fish pie that shows off all the expected flavours via premium-quality seafood.

Name: Mum Foods Smokehouse & Delicatessen
Description: Geoffrey Ellis and Travis Crawford are the brains behind this popular spot in Mueller that is equal parts Texas barbecue and delicatessen. Located in a shared space, it's a classic no-fuss spot with concrete floors and booths made from wooden slats, but you're here for the food, most likely the house-made pastrami sandwich. Brined, then rubbed with black pepper and coriander before being smoked, they take their meat seriously. Piled high on house-made rye sourdough with mustard, it's their signature item for a good reason. Other sandwiches, meat by the pound, a variety of sides like collard greens, potato salad, and chips and pimento dip, plus classics like matzoh ball soup are all worth a try too.

Name: Munchi
Address: 37 Lane 52, Section 1, Meicun Road, West District, Taichung, Taiwan
Description: This casual neo-bistro reimagines familiar Asian flavours and aromas with contemporary flair. Helmed by a team of two chefs and one sommelier, it offers dishes best enjoyed with a carefully curated selection of natural wines and cocktails. Signature dishes such as black tiger shrimp and a Munchi-style Vietnamese pho go particularly well with the natural wines. The interior, reminiscent of a wine cellar, is sleek and modern, with a spacious open kitchen where counter seating adds some theatre to the meal.

Name: MundArt2015
Description: Nestled in a picturesque spot not far from Salzburg, the attractive Gut Edermann hotel awaits you with tastefully designed guestrooms and a 2 700m2 spa area, as well as appealing dining options. In a warm and welcoming setting, friendly waitstaff serve up flavoursome seasonal dishes such as veal topside terrine with wasabi, pumpkin and lemongrass, or young venison ragout with chestnut spaetzle and wild lingonberries. Alongside a set menu, there is also an appealing à la carte selection. Tip: Be sure to book in advance.

Name: Muraglia - Conchiglia d'Oro
Description: Here, choose between the simply furnished, bright dining room with a proudly vintage feel that dates back to its opening in the 1970s and a tiny yet attractive terrace with sea views (there are just a few tables, so it’s best to book in advance). Fish has always been – and still is – the house speciality, with fresh, top-quality dishes simply prepared according to classic methods such as the barbecue grill visible in the dining room. The fish is so fresh that the handwritten menu changes daily.

Name: Mural de los Poblanos
Address: C. 16 de Septiembre 506, Centro, Heróica Puebla de Zaragoza, 72000, Mexico
Description: In the shadow of the Catedral de Puebla, this famous address has history dating back to 1994. Located in a historic 17th-century building, the dining room is a sight unto itself with incredible murals, striking archways and bright orange walls. There is certainly a sense of occasion and ease here, and the setting is the ideal spot to enjoy a leisurely lunch in the fine care of a charming service team. The menu is expansive and covers all of Puebla’s most famous dishes, including chile en nogada and chalupas poblanas. Queso enchiladas with a trio of moles is an absolute must-order. A sharply dressed sommelier roams the floor, helping guests navigate the impressive wine list.

Name: Murena
Description: This modern sushi restaurant, decked out with yellow walls and dark furniture, occupies half of a larger space, with the other side being the colourful brunch and coffee spot, Seagull. The restaurant menu is all about spotlighting high-quality seafood, be that in the nigiri and sashimi with creative toppings and condiments, or the hot dishes that take on influences from around Asia, such as Korean-inspired aubergine with kimchi.

Name: Murmures
Description: In a lively pedestrian street near the opera house, this restaurant run by Noé Saillard proposes globally inspired cuisine. Drawing on his experience in fashionable Lyon eateries, international kitchens plus a stint in Lebanon, the chef combines personal Asian influences with technical skill in a single multi-course set menu. Precise cooking, perfect seasoning and creative pairings characterise dishes such as melt-in-the-mouth rutabaga with brown butter and katsuobushi cream. The relaxed ambience, carefully curated musical backdrop and small terrace make this a winning spot.

Name: Muro
Description: Situated on the beautiful main square in the historic city centre, keep an eye out for this restaurant’s discreet entrance, which hides behind it a series of interconnecting rooms bursting with the buzz of contented diners. The menu has a surf ’n’ turf approach and a strong Japanese influence, exemplified by the sushi selection and a choice of prime produce cooked on the robata grill. The aged steaks are a popular choice and understandably so.

Name: Muru
Description: You’d be hard pushed to find a restaurant with a greater focus on wine than Muru. This cosy little bistro is home to quirky touches such as a wine bottle chandelier, a bar made from old wine boxes and a raised ‘cellar’ – and that’s not to mention the nearby wine bar they run. Simple, tasty dishes are on-hand to accompany the excellent wine list, and the sommelier’s pairing suggestions are spot-on.

Name: Musa
Address: 14 You'ai Street, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
Description: The husband-and-wife team fell in love with Thai cuisine so much that they learned the art from the masters and opened this Thai restaurant with a warm-toned, rattan-filled room inspired by Southeast Asia. The menu covers Thai cooking from the north to the south, using spices imported from Thailand alongside local foods like salted eggs, pomelo and split mung beans. Try the stir-fried soft-shell crab yellow curry, or chicken sautéed with galangal.

Name: Musciora
Description: Run with passion by a close-knit family duo – father in the kitchen and son in the dining room, overseeing the cellar – this restaurant distinguishes itself through a total commitment that finds further expression in the new space recently created alongside the original one. Here, the open kitchen looks directly into the dining room, creating a continuous dialogue between the brigade and the guests. The gastronomic offering is structured across three tasting menus: one dedicated to the sea, one focused on the produce of the hinterland and meats, and a “Vera Esperienza Musciora”, a harmonious encapsulation of both souls. The dishes begin with island ingredients, celebrated through an essential approach and contemporary intuitions that bring out their authenticity and flavour. The wine list reflects the same attention to the local area, favouring Sardinian labels – often from small artisan producers – alongside a selection from beyond the region, oriented predominantly towards natural wines.

Name: Musoan
Description: This restaurant is named after the Rinzai Buddhist monk who founded the Muso School. Out of respect for ingredients, Musoan leans toward simple, honest preparations. Wanmono broth is pungent with the aroma of bonito, featuring a fish cake packed with seafood flavour. Beef, a perennial favourite, is grilled on a ceramic plate and served with rice cooked in clay pots. A mother-and-son team runs Musoan, with the son in command of the kitchen. Enjoy dinner while looking out on a garden tended by the gardener mother.

Name: Musoshin Ramen
Description: Hiding just off the main drag in Roncesvalles, this restaurant is not like other ramen-yas. For starters, none of them can bake like Chef Aoi Yoshida, who turns out trays of perfectly formed Japanese milk bread and other sweet treats. Her house-made noodles, bundled into every bowl, are also a cut above most. But perhaps the most fascinating part of this restaurant hides in the broths. Whereas a typical tonkotsu ramen favors heart-stopping, porky richness, the style here is a vegetable base that is both lighter and leaner and yet equally savory. In a testament to both her own talents and to modern technology, Yoshida learned both noodle and ramen craft by video chatting with an old friend who runs this restaurant’s original location in Kyoto.

Name: Mustard
Description: This halal restaurant specialising in Bengali and Punjabi cuisines is christened Mustard because the spice is used extensively in both cuisines. For instance, mustard oil is often used in place of coconut oil in Bengali cooking. Try their maacher cutlet – deep-fried fish croquettes served with a house-made fermented mustard sauce called Kashundi, which tastes strong and spicy. All food is made to order, but is so worth the wait.

Name: Mustard Seed
Description: This 22-seater has gone for tables rather than a counter to foster a cosy, sit-down ambience. Before you get to experience the head chef’s unique take on Singaporean-Japanese fusion cooking, you have to secure a table on its website on the first day of every month. The 8-course omakase-style menu changes every two months, reinventing national dishes like rojak and laksa with savvy Japanese twists and premium, globally-sourced produce.

Name: Mustards Grill
Address: 7399 St. Helena Hwy., Napa, CA, 94558, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At this iconic roadhouse, it’s a joy to eat your greens. Chef Cindy Pawlcyn is a wine country pioneer for incorporating onsite gardens that produce ingredients routinely seen on this seasonal menu. There’s something for everyone on this friendly menu: Vibrant salads, grilled fish and steaks, or even a smoked barbecue pork sandwich. A side of onion rings isn’t a bad idea either. The lemon-lime tart capped with brown sugar meringue fittingly described on the menu as “ridiculously tall” doesn’t disappoint. Not surprisingly, there’s often a wait during lunch. The wine list is worth an exploration as well.

Name: Muutto Anatolian Tapas Bar
Address: Kılıçali Paşa, Meclis-i Mebusan Caddesi No:8, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34433, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: To soak up Galataport's trendy atmosphere, a spot on the front terrace overlooking the passing boats is the place to be. But whether you sip your cocktail alfresco or inside the modern bistro, you're in for an exceptional evening. The restaurant specialises in Spanish tapas reimagined through a Turkish culinary lens. You might start with prawns accompanied by a spicy cherry cream, move on to a shared plate of patatas bravas and grilled squid, and choose a more traditional main dish such as a pide or baked sea bass. The chefs have a flair for reinvention and have curated an enticing menu. Eating at Muutto makes for a great night out!

Name: My Hanh Seafood
Address: 3-5 Vo Nguyen Giap Street, An Hai Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: The terrace with panoramic ocean views is one of the biggest draws of this beach-front restaurant. But the well-crafted seafood is more than equal to the setting. The live fish tank heralds a feast of fresh shellfish and fish, to be cooked in various ways. But the stellar attraction is definitely mantis shrimp, particularly in the typhoon-shelter style. The golden-fried garlic and crispy rice amplify the shrimp’s inherent sweetness, adding both aromatic depth and textural complexity. Mud crab from Hoi An is another exclusive speciality not found elsewhere in Da Nang.

Name: My Loup
Description: It is easy to fall for the charms and delights of this French bistro. The narrow space is dressed in well-worn wood, a lovely bar and bookshelves along the back walls. The bartenders are veterans, shaking and stirring with impressive speed. But what really makes this a frequent favorite is the food, which has all the joys and reflexes of a chef cooking in their own home. Smart, seasonal and astutely seasoned, the cooking eschews fuss and favors boldness. Ease into dinner with a round of oysters or a light bite of pickled shrimp with aioli, basil and saltines. After, a swirled, green garlic roll with escargot is a total powerhouse, while grilled quail with tzatziki feels like the best backyard barbecue. A slice of chocolate cake or another drink? Sure, why not?

Name: Myazū
Address: Al Basateen Mall. Prince Mohammed Bin Abdulaziz Road, Al Rawdah, Jeddah, 23431, Saudi Arabia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,No alcohol served,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Journey to Japan at this restaurant in the heart of Jeddah's city centre. The spacious eatery boasts a modern Japanese style with various seating options – sit at the counter to watch the sushi chefs in action or pick a table in the main hall or on the patio area. As for the menu, you can expect a wide selection of classics and modern interpretations – you’ll find popcorn shrimps from the tempura section, fine Wagyu kushi grilled skewers from the robata section and freshly prepared nigiri at the sushi section. Four dishes per person should suffice, with the chicken gyozas being a must-try!

Name: Myeongdong Kyoja
Description: Myeongdong Kyoja is a family-owned place in operation since 1966. The restaurant, which offers only four items on the menu, specializes in dumplings and noodle soup. An impressive number of patrons flock here daily, largely because all the dishes, including its signature garlic-laden kimchi, are made in-house. Simple décor and service come with hefty portions at affordable prices.

Name: Myojinshita Soba Oshin
Description: The shop is a stone’s throw from Kanda Myojin Shrine, a Shinto shrine dedicated to the protection of Edo, or current-day Tokyo. The menu ranges from an impressive variety of appetisers to creative soba dishes incorporating ingredients such as raw tofu skin and dried mullet roe. For cold soba, you can choose between Seiro and Inaka; both are cut into thin noodles that go down smoothly. Milling and kneading methods are adjusted to the buckwheat variety to convey their distinct personalities. In the evening, you can order just a single plate of soba, allowing you to spend your time as you please.

Name: Myranel
Address: 241 chemin du Roy, Deschambault, G0A 1S0, Canada
Description: In a charming village on the banks of the St. Lawrence, Myranel is surrounded by picturesque shops (antique dealers, bakery, and a renowned chocolate shop). This delightful late 19th-century house, complete with lovely original ceiling beams, is home to this Biosphere-certified restaurant run by a young couple. Chef Mathieu Janes, a strong believer in eating local, works exclusively with small-scale producers, sourcing the majority of his ingredients from Portneuf County (except coffee, some citrus fruits, and fish). The set menu, which changes every two months or so, comes in two versions; one is vegetarian. The chef likes to go off the beaten track, as with his aligot potatoes with a Quebecois twist, or to create surprises with daring sweet and sour combinations (duck, red cabbage, radicchio, and black currant). The authenticity of the setting and the sincere commitment to cooking local cuisine make this restaurant particularly appealing.

Name: Myrtos
Address: 260-262 Brompton Road, South Kensington, London, SW3 2AS, United Kingdom
Description: Next time the British weather is letting you down and you’re pining for the Mediterranean, head to Myrtos and you’ll be cheered up in no time. It’s an elegant spot with a bright, coastal feel, an eye-catching fresh fish counter and a menu packed with classic Greek dishes to share. Start with the super breads and a choice of dips (the tirokafteri is a winner) before sharing the likes of marinated sardines and lamb moussaka. It’s a great all-round experience, in part thanks to the smooth, attentive and knowledgeable service.

Name: Myungbodang
Description: Drawing from her experience at a top New York restaurant, Chef Hyeon-ju Lim develops a creative approach to Nu-American French cuisine. Known for her bold ingredient choices and keen sense of composition, Chef Lim delivers dishes that highlight the character of each element. The signature Truffle features a crisp shell filled with fermented mushroom and truffle cream—rich and refined. The meal concludes with a distinctive chocolate foam, offering a memorable finish.

Name: MÀU
Address: 5 Van Mieu Street, Quoc Tu Giam Ward, Hanoi, 10000, Vietnam
Description: The warm, sociable atmosphere is matched by the energy of the team. Counter seats facing the bar offer the most immersive experience, as the service unfolds, and sizzles emerge from the kitchen. You can choose between à la carte dishes and a chef's menu – either way, the food sees modern style balanced with Asian flavours, including subtle Vietnamese notes. Enthusiastic staff are happy to help you pick from the wine list. An enjoyably relaxed experience.

Name: MÁK by mizseijani
Description: Rustic charm abounds at this laid-back restaurant, from the décor to the vaulted brick ceiling. Seasonality is key here and Chef János takes time to visit his small, artisan suppliers personally. His travels inform the interesting set menu (go for the longer version), with vegetables treated as reverently as meat and fish, and curing, pickling and ageing all playing their part. Knowledgably prepared, consummately seasoned dishes have a delicate touch and could include grey catfish with buckwheat or duck with celery and pine. The unobtrusive, expertly paced service is spot-on too.

Name: Màloma
Address: Chemin des Deux Fermes 5, Rosières, 1331, Belgium
Description: Màloma is the culinary offshoot of Foster, an ethical and sustainable ecosystem of artisans, farmers and entrepreneurs, all of whom have the deepest respect for the environment. Georges Athanassopoulos’ bright, elegantly appointed restaurant shines the spotlight on the ingredient, primarily vegetables and fruit, with the odd piece of fish or meat from time to time. The ingredient is allowed to shout its name, courtesy of the chef’s craftsmanship, which can be complex but always aims to showcase the ingredient’s individual flavours. For example, he may stuff pumpkin flower with a subtle poultry filling, which is then fried in a crispy tempura batter, while grilled tomato adds refreshing intensity and creamy feta a final spicy note. A colourful, vibrant tribute to the seasons!

Name: Mâche
Description: Cuttlefish, broccoli, mint, pistachio; Tokyo turnip, ghormeh sabzi, black lemon, endive jus; duck, onion, turnip-and-pepper stuffing, blackberry, beetroot – this inventive cuisine is packed with striking colours and flavours that pack a punch (not least fermented or candied ingredients and condiments that add intensity to the dishes). As hinted at by the names of the menus "Sottsass" and "Memphis", which pay tribute to avant-garde Italian designer Ettore Sottsass, another passion is art. In the attractive interior, antique details meet contemporary geometric design, and service with a smile contributes to the friendly atmosphere.

Name: Mâm Amis
Address: Shop A & B, GF, Fu Fai Commercial Centre, 27 Hillier Street, Sheung Wan, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: The smart wood panelled front contrasts sharply with the distressed walls, vintage lamps and hanging greenery inside. Vietnamese chefs are keen on bringing authentic Vietnamese food to Hong Kong, with chargrilled items and phở among the highlights. Try the chargrilled river prawns that boast bouncy, briny-sweet flesh and exceptional smokiness. Phở comes in generous portions with a flavour-packed soup base.

Name: Mäska
Address: Rua Joana Angélica, 159, Rio de Janeiro, 22420-030, Brazil
Description: It's worth braving the frenetic traffic along Ipanema’s narrow streets to eat at this modern but relaxed restaurant with a contemporary bistro feel and a kitchen that opens onto the dining room to savour chef Danilo Parah’s innovative and contemporary cuisine. His recipes showcase ingredients of the very highest quality, including extremely fresh seafood, in dishes such as the unforgettable creamy rice with octopus, and the mouthwatering and perfectly cooked steak served with a truffled aligot mash. Not forgetting the masterfully prepared and delicate spaghetti with beurre blanc and braised prawns. The dining experience and atmosphere are enhanced by Mäska’s array of refreshing cocktails, which are an absolute must.

Name: Méditerranéo - Château Capitoul
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: In the Massif de la Clape, between Narbonne and the Mediterranean, vineyards and garrigue, this manor house sits pretty in a wine estate that has been run by the same family for seven generations. Chef Valère Diochet's cuisine is unabashedly Mediterranean. A host of aromatic plants – basil, purslane, lovage – enhance this aesthetic cuisine, which is refined, precise and light: marinated monkfish, courgette with lovage; red mullet cooked on one side. The restaurant's plush Art Deco interior overlooks the vineyards and the waters of the Étang de Bages. The wine list is informative, with wines from the estate, the La Clape appellation and other Languedoc wines.

Name: Mélange
Description: The small village of Saussignac (some 20km from Bergerac) is home to this charming stone building that is typical of the region and located right next to the château. Beyond the wooden terrace, the restaurant interior, which features exposed stone walls, hardwood floors and white-painted beams, is brought up to date by a handful of more contemporary decorative touches. In the kitchen, a blend of styles and influences goes into creating colourful, innovative dishes made with seasonal ingredients: confit turkey leg, mashed potatoes, mushrooms and a corn and bacon sauce.

Name: Mémo
Address: 644 rue Notre-Dame Ouest, Montréal, H3C 1J2, Canada
Description: Set against the backdrop of an industrial-style loft with exposed pipework, a central island houses a kitchen-counter. The eclectic and modern cuisine is enhanced by influences from around the globe and caters to all tastes. The dishes transport you to different corners of the world: ribs with gochujang sauce, hamachi crudo with ponzu, prawn ceviche, and mango and tomato aguachile…

Name: Mémoire
Address: 316 Lebuh Pantai, George Town, George Town, 10300, Malaysia
Description: This cosy restaurant is where Chef Fung experiments with his novel Asian fusion fare that melds local traditions and modern gastronomy. There is a theatrical element to his approach (think smoke, dry ice or sparklers), evoking a feeling both of déjà vu and jamais vu. His 6- to 10-course tasting menus may include playful interactive creations such as crispy flatbread on a mini easel, on which diners apply sauces in five colours with a brush.

Name: Ménade
Description: This establishment surprises both for its spaciousness and its quiet location, as it is situated within the Clubhouse of the Baviera Golf course. Behind this name, which refers to the beautiful mythological nymphs, followers of Dionysus, the Greek god of wine, we find the proposal of two chefs, the ‘Pablos’ (Pablo Vega and Pablo Domínguez), who complement each other perfectly to offer a current Mediterranean cuisine, with some international touches (especially French and Asian), in which there is no lack of creative nuances. The à la carte is supported by two tasting menus: Aristeo (three courses) and Minerva (eight courses, with the option of a wine pairing).

Name: Ménage
Description: Situated in the heart of the city near the Teatro Bellini and Piazza Università, this restaurant occupies an Art Nouveau-style building. Here, a trio of experienced young chefs from Catania have brought new life to the old “Da Turi Finocchiaro” restaurant, which has always been very popular with the city’s high society. Offering a small outdoor space near the entrance, the quiet, intimate dining room on the ground floor provides the backdrop for reinterpreted, contemporary Sicilian cuisine with an exclusive focus on meat (especially barbecued dishes which are the restaurant’s trademark), while the first floor is home to a cocktail bar run with passion by one of the partners. Two frescoes painted by Giuseppe Barone in 1930 add to the appeal.

Name: Méson Chalut
Address: 8 rue de la Corne-de-Cerf, Saint-Malo, 35400, France
Description: In his "méson" (which means "house" in Gallo, the language of Upper Brittany), the chef-owner goes all out Breton, showcasing seafood and other regional ingredients (buckwheat, lait ribot (Breton buttermilk), Coco de Paimpol beans, salted butter) that he sources locally. Freshness, flavour and a respect for nature.

Name: Métive
Description: After Baston in Bordeaux, chef Julien Borie and baker Pauline Celle have taken the same enticing concept of a restaurant-bakery, and rooted it even more in the terroir. The chef, who is from these parts, thus has an opportunity to work with local artisans and seafood. The result is confident and masterfully executed bistronomy cuisine, incorporating precisely prepared local produce – particularly the matured fish that can be seen in a display case in the dining area. The bakery turns out natural sourdough breads using organic flour and drawing on genuine artisanal expertise. The decor features stone walls, vintage posters and pale wood furniture; you pass through the bakery to get to the restaurant with a counter and open kitchen.

Name: Método
Description: In this modern restaurant, located along a pedestrian street in the centre of Teruel’s old quarter, you will find a modern proposal with some touches of fusion. The extensive à la carte, which basically revolves around two premium products, Balfegó tuna and Wagyu beef (the cattle are raised locally on the Mudéjar Wagyu farm), is supported by a tasting menu called Temático de Atún (through a variety of hot and cold dishes, you can discover the different types of cuts). Here they take great care in the staging!

Name: Mì Quảng 1A
Address: 1A Hai Phong Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: Mì quảng is a dish from Central Vietnam, popular throughout the country. So, unsurprisingly, this simple shop specialises in ribbon rice noodles in a yellow broth seasoned with fish sauce and turmeric and topped with peanuts and bean sprouts. There are two versions here, pork and shrimp or chicken, with or without hardboiled egg. Order the ‘special’ to try them all. Lettuce, cilantro, and banana flower on the side add aromas and a crispy texture.

Name: Mía Dining
Address: 12G2 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 710000, Vietnam
Description: The soft lighting, minimalist interior and romantic soundtrack make this venue the perfect spot for date nights. The most prized seats are at the counter offering intimate views of the kitchen. Three set menus star modern European recipes jazzed up by a scattering of local produce and seasonings. The must-try duck breast is velvety and juicy, clad in crackling skin as crisp as peanut brittle. Expect sound wine tips from the sommelier.

Name: Møntergade
Description: The charming team are a big part of the draw at this lively upmarket brasserie which offers generous, classically based dishes. While the chalkboard displays daily specials, there’s always a place for herring on the menu – with fried, pickled, marinated or even curried options. Their other dishes like Danish beef with black garlic cream and deep-fried goose fat potatoes or apples with white chocolate, lemon verbena and apple sorbet are equally appealing though. There’s a cosy vibe to the place and a small drinks counter where you can chat away with the waiters.

Name: Mühlenhof
Description: It is little wonder that Anette and Stefan Rottler's hotel is so popular: Their restaurant serves classic Baden dishes made with top-quality ingredients – from snail soup to pork fillet in cream of mushroom sauce to Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy). The smaller dishes and reasonably priced set menu of the day are also much in demand. The wine list is dedicated to local labels. Friendly and attentive service. Food is served in various dining rooms, some with a cosy, regional feel, others with a fresh and modern look. Delightful covered terrace.

Name: Müllers auf Norderney
Description: Affording unobstructed views of the sea, 1884's exclusive location alone is a major draw. The charming little boutique hotel is a spa-style building complex composed of Villa Mathilde and the adjoining Villa Olga. It is also home to a chic restaurant with modern and minimalist interior design and a fabulous terrace. In the kitchen, Nelson Müller's team prepares flavoursome and pleasingly uncomplicated dishes from fresh, good-quality ingredients. Soul food would be an apt label for this cuisine.

Name: Müllers auf der Rü
Description: Nelson Müller's fine dining restaurant, Schote, may have moved to Bergisch Gladbach, but this cherished Essen-based establishment at Rüttenscheider Stern U-Bahn station has stayed put. This is a market hall-style brasserie integrated into a shopping arcade. Sitting at high tables, diners tuck into delicious dishes ranging from currywurst to turbot, prepared in the centrally positioned open kitchen. Friendly service. Tip for motorists: public multi-storey car park around the corner.

Name: Müllers in der Mühle
Description: Nelson Müller's attractive modern brasserie is an inviting alternative to the fine dining restaurant Schote. Alongside Müller classics such as "Balik salmon Tsar Nikolaj with cucumber "noodles", potato pancakes & buttermilk broth", the top-notch steak cuts and the seasonal three- to five-course set menu are highly recommended. And for those who prefer something a bit more down-to-earth, you can't go wrong with the currywurst or Wiener schnitzel. In fine weather, the pleasant terrace beckons. Given the appealing location in a designated nature area, it's worth staying on at the wonderful boutique hotel Diepeschrather Mühle.

Name: Münsters
Description: This extremely popular place boasts fresh and flavoursome cuisine in the form of a short menu that changes with the seasons. Tables without tablecloths, wooden floorboards and partly exposed brick walls, as well as appealing wine-themed decorative details make for a cosy bistro feel with a rustic touch. The service is laid-back, friendly and attentive. The chef also gets in on the action front of house, providing charming service and excellent wine recommendations. There's also a great beer garden!

Name: Mürver
Address: Novotel İstanbul Bosphorus, Kemankeş Caddesi No:57-59, Karaköy/Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34425, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Take the lift to the top floor of the Novotel Istanbul Bosphorus and discover the world of Mürver. You can start with an aperitif in the hip cocktail bar, then soak up the romantic atmosphere of the restaurant. Finally, take in the breathtaking views of the metropolis from the fabulous terrace. An open fire is the centrepiece of the kitchen, where you can also see meat and fish drying. Smoky and barbecue notes form the basis of captivating creations featuring regional produce and original combinations. The dishes are spicy, bold and fiery. Think grilled squid rings with green beans and a subtly spicy muhammara sauce, or 28-day aged ribeye. This buzzing establishment is the place to be!

Name: Māsa
Description: The contemporary-looking ‘Sister’ sits at the heart of Riga’s Central District and is run by a friendly young team. Muted grey, beige and light wood tones provide a calming feel, yet at the same time the atmosphere is lively and animated. Start with a cocktail and some starters to share – maybe cold-smoked Baltic sprats with salted lemon, capers and wild garlic – before moving on to more substantial dishes like glazed chicken with spring carrot cream and grilled green onion. The fresh ingredients might originate from Latvia, but influences come from across the Mediterranean and occasionally Asia.

Name: Młoda Polska
Description: Celebrity chef Beata Śniechowska's restaurant has a full name that translates as ‘Young Polish Bistro & Piano’, which feels like a pretty apt description. It’s run by a young and enthusiastic team, there's an invigorating bistro buzz to the atmosphere and there is indeed background music from the house pianist. The cooking dispenses with fuss and instead focuses on the natural flavours of quality ingredients, such as pure-white cod. A large vodka selection will please connoisseurs.

Name: Młodnik
Description: A friendly welcome awaits at this family-run brasserie in the city suburbs. The interiors are decked out with modern furnishings and plenty of foliage, while a lovely paved terrace is the place to be when the sun is shining. The cooking offers clean, distinct flavours across dishes such as local herring with sour cream, apple and horseradish, as well as those with more of a Mediterranean influence. A strong version of the classic kogel mogel is a great way to finish.

Name: MŌDAN
Address: Unit 5, Level 1, Escalades East Tower, 20th Avenue, Cubao, Quezon - Metro Manila, 1109, The Philippines
Description: With just 14 seats, this minimalist, grey-toned counter restaurant provides an intimate yet vibrant dining experience. Guests perch on comfortable raised seats facing a sleek open kitchen – dishes are presented directly by the chefs. The cuisine leans Japanese with global accents, showcasing top-quality ingredients and elegant contrasts; think hotate with dill and ube, or Wagyu nabe with ikura. A concise list of wine and sake has the perfect accompaniment.

Name: MỘC Quán Seafood
Address: 26 To Hien Thanh, An Hai Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: Enjoy a rustic dining atmosphere that includes an outdoor seating area adorned with fairy lights in the trees. The array of fresh seafood in the large water tank can be served in a variety of Southeast-Asian styles. Gloved staff prepare your shellfish for easy consumption; the chef keeps the kitchen spick and span. The popular lobster is best savoured in garlic butter sauce for optimum flavour. Book in advance to skip the queue and indulge in top-quality seafood.

Name: Mỳ Quảng Cô Sáu
Address: 397 Tran Hung Dao Street, An Hai Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: Perched on the bank of Han River, the room with yellow walls and greenery feels relaxed and cheerful. The owner hails from Quảng Nam and naturally, he chose to sell mi quảng noodles, a speciality from his homeland. The intense broth is coloured yellow by turmeric and available toppings include chicken, fish and shrimp. Another must-try is thịt heo bánh tráng – thinly sliced pork belly rolled in rice paper with herbs and veggies.

Name: N'uovo Vino e Cucina
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Nestled in the refined Antico Borgo di Sutri resort, in the heart of the lush Tuscia Viterbese, this restaurant offers an intimate and modern atmosphere, characterised by soft lighting and large windows overlooking the surrounding greenery. The talented young chef Lezzerini offers cuisine inspired by the local area, revisiting traditional regional recipes with modern techniques and the finest local produce. Countless offerings have made a lasting impression, from the starter that echoes the restaurant’s name, N’uovo alla brace, to the quality of the fresh pasta and the meat main courses, such as the dry-aged wild boar served in the manner of roast beef.

Name: NANAHIRO
Description: The concept is ‘Japanese cuisine plus’. The menu reflects the chef’s background in both Japanese and Western cooking, blending traditions to create something uniquely his own. Only the ingredients are listed, heightening anticipation and offering an element of surprise when the dishes arrive. The progression moves from seasonal vegetables, seafood and meat to freshly steamed rice and a delicate sweet course. More than Japanese, yet not quite Western, this is a place to savour premium ingredients with a refined touch.

Name: NATURAL TEA MANOR
Address: 30, Lane 380, Xiding Road, Xizhi District, New Taipei, 221001, Taiwan
Description: Panoramic views of lush forest and a wood rich interior impart a sense of serenity. The century-old tea farm started practising organic cultivation about 30 years ago and opened a dining room serving creative tea-infused dishes. The husband is in charge of the kitchen while his wife runs the front-of-house. Their signature braised Dongpo pork belly with iron buddha tea delivers deep complex flavours; it is best enjoyed with steamed Pouchong tea buns.

Name: NAVAN NAVAN
Address: 55 Mu 7, San Pong, Mae Rim, Chiang Mai, 50180, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only,Counter dining,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Surrounded by rice fields, this stand-alone cement building affords a clear view of the open kitchen. The chef draws on various cuisines and uses a charcoal grill to cook local ingredients. His unpretentious style promotes healthy eating, and each dish highlights the natural flavours of the ingredients. Arrive before sunset to see the beautiful garden.

Name: NELU KORAIBASHI
Description: The red-brick Western-style building was constructed at the dawn of the 20th century. Restaurants opened one after the other in those days as the winds of modernisation blew through Japan. With its sparkling chandeliers, the dining room recalls the stately home of some European aristocrat. The prix fixe menu is crafted with abundant imagination, each dish telling a story. ‘Nelu’ derives from the Japanese word ‘neru’, meaning to knead or temper, and the first character in the word for ‘brickwork’. The chef mixes innovation with the traditions of French cuisine to create a modern culinary styling.

Name: NEMI
Address: C. Francisco I. Madero 565, Esterito, La Paz, 23020, Mexico
Description: Chef Alejandro Villagomez's extensive fine dining background both in Mexico and abroad converge at NEMI. The tasting menu highlights Baja California ingredients almost exclusively (though French truffle may make an appearance), and the Mexican wine pairing perfectly complements the experience. The meal begins with small bites such as green melon in an aguachile or watermelon infused with Mexican sake, while the chef's international influence is best seen in courses like butternut squash bisque with vanilla and apples. A hoja santa-wrapped tamal with salsa verde and huitlacoche, topped with a quesillo foam and truffle, may be next before entrees like totoaba served over mushrooms and a chileatole, or braised wagyu beef cheek with celery root puree and jus.

Name: NICE
Description: Housed in a newly built complex in the Werksviertel, a neighbourhood close to Munich's Ostbahnhof station, this restaurant presents a stylish, contemporary interior. Diners can sit at the counter overlooking the kitchen, at the bar, at high tables or in one of the booths. Floor-to-ceiling windows mean the space is flooded with natural light during the day. Dishes are freshly prepared with great care and technical skill. Mouthwatering examples include poulet noir with swede, cabbage and capers, or golden trout with borscht broth, sweet pepper, lángos and chervil. Lunch features a streamlined menu with daily specials; in the evening, there is a four-course set menu and an appealing à la carte selection. The wine list may be concise, but it is refined and well devised. Tip for motorists: PARK ONE underground parking facility. Thanks to the long opening hours (Mon-Fri 9am-midnight, Sat 6pm-midnight), a good option for weekday coffee and croissants or an after-work drink in the evening.

Name: NIJŪ
Address: 20 Berkeley Street, Mayfair, London, W1J 8EE, United Kingdom
Description: The Japanese concept of ‘katei ryōri’ – home-style family dining – is the driving force behind this slick Mayfair operation. Diners are split across two rooms, one more moody and clubby, the other brighter and featuring a small sushi counter. Endo Kazutoshi has designed the menus, which combine the katei ryōri sharing dishes with a sushi selection and Japanese beef cooked over charcoal. Unifying it all is an attention to prime produce, be it the wagyu, the hamachi for the sushi or roasted turbot with furikake and miso butter. Bookend your visit with a drink in the Nipperkin cocktail bar.

Name: NIKU RYOURI FUKU
Address: 145 Xiangshang North Road, West District, Taichung, Taiwan
Description: The owner of a Japanese barbecue restaurant opened this locale to serve creative small plates underpinned by European, Chinese and Japanese techniques. Marbled Wagyu beef is of course a highlight on the menu, but it's items such as grilled ox tongue in char siu glaze, and sugar-smoked pork offal that make the experience unique. If you do not fancy beef, local breeds of duck and chicken are also available. Order the day's special on the board.

Name: NIRI
Address: Building 9, Mamsha Al Saadiyat, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Notable sake list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Grab a seat at the counter of this contemporary Japanese restaurant to watch the chefs prepare your dishes over the robata grill. The ingredients are top-notch, and the kitchen is clearly motivated. The pared-back interior is very on-trend and comes complete with a sakura tree. People-watchers and anyone who enjoys a good sea view will prefer a seat on the terrace as this spot on Mamsha Al Saadiyat is hard to beat.

Name: NISCH
Description: This pleasantly relaxed little neighbourhood restaurant is sleekly and stylishly decorated with a monochrome colour scheme. For its part, the kitchen produces accomplished dishes and boasts some good eco-credentials. The modern, understated Nordic set menu is inspired by global flavours and changes every few weeks. The interesting wine list is mainly organic and biodynamic in nature.

Name: NISHIAZABU SHANGU
Description: The kitchen can be seen from the counter seating, making dining a theatrical experience. The chef commands his team while working his wok with consummate skill. Testifying that the appeal of Cantonese cuisine lies in seafood and dried items, the menu is laced with ingredients such as spiny lobster, abalone, dried scallop abductor and dried mushrooms. After dinner, guests can relocate to the lounge to bask in the afterglow of the performance. Desserts, a mix of Chinese and Western patisserie treats, close the evening.

Name: NOOKS
Description: There’s an appealing feel to this neighbourhood restaurant nestling in a corner basement; head straight for the hidden terrace to the rear when the sun is shining. Meats and seafood from the grill form the core of the menu, sometimes with global touches from togarashi to marinara sauce. Cooked in a semi-open kitchen, the dishes are hearty and packed with flavour. Friendly, enthusiastic service completes the picture.

Name: NOON
Address: Lua Resort, Anna Sétány 3, Balatonfüred, 8230, Hungary
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An exclusive lakeside resort plays host to this elegant restaurant (if you’re not staying the night, then pre-booking is essential in high season). Grab a cocktail in the stylish bar before enjoying a carefully curated selection of contemporary Hungarian dishes which fuse tradition with inventive modern touches. Local wines are a feature, and the smooth service shows the team’s knowledge and care. If the chocolate and cherry dessert is on the menu, be sure to choose it.

Name: NORA
Address: 7 West Lane, Canary Wharf, London, E22 3AA, United Kingdom
Description: Amidst the gleaming buildings of Canary Wharf, this Turkish restaurant aims to bring a taste of Istanbul to London. Sitting on the ground floor of a glass-fronted apartment block, it’s a strikingly attractive restaurant with moody lighting, tiled tables and a focal bar counter that makes a great place to sit if you’re in for a quick lunch; if you’re celebrating in a group, then the booths are perfect. Start by ordering the sesame caraway pide and one of the dips, and make sure you finish with the delightfully sweet, chewy baklava topped with pistachio.

Name: NORD
Address: 100 Old Hall Street, Liverpool, L3 9QJ, United Kingdom
Description: Located in the heart of the city, this spacious restaurant sports modern décor with an almost futuristic edge thanks to the pod-like booth seating. The menu offers plenty of variety, with a mix of international influences resulting in dishes ranging from tandoori beetroot to cod Kiev and asparagus tagliatelle to a traditional Sunday roast. It’s all carefully executed by the kitchen and doesn’t lack for flavour thanks to judicious seasoning. The cheery and chatty service team add to the appeal.

Name: NORRA by Le Nord
Description: Lieke Nicole-Creemers of restaurant Le Nord in Bilthoven has opened NORRA, a stylish and somewhat fashionable establishment. The atmosphere is relaxed, and she provides charming service. In the kitchen, a passionate chef serves guests both an appealing à la carte menu and a delightful set menu (including vegetarian options). French cuissons, well-considered exotic influences and playful textures add zest. For example, he uses black-legged chicken in a juicy ballotine, which is further flavoured with a cashew nut compote, a vinaigrette with balsamic vinegar, pommes fondantes and plum. Be sure to leave some room for the cheese trolley, because it is really worth it.

Name: NOVO New Dining
Address: Aan de Brikkenbouw 4F, Maastricht, 6211 XT, Netherlands
Description: Rodny Welters has created his own little world on the fifth floor of this factory building in Maastricht's Sphinxkwartier. Rugged surfaces meet stylish upholstery here in a tasteful symbiosis. All eyes are on the open kitchen, where chef Welters lets his cooking do the talking; his culinary creations draw inspiration from around the globe, underpinned by exquisite sauces. With dishes such as haddock à la meunière with a tandoori velouté or fried scampi with a red curry and coconut milk sauce, the "Experience" set menu certainly lives up to its name.

Name: NOÏS
Description: Laura is a warm and welcoming host, and she knows the outstanding wine list like the back of her hand. Her recommendations are absolutely spot on! If you like surprises, chef Vincent is your man. There's no written menu here; your options are presented verbally only, and your trust is rewarded with imaginative, plant-forward cuisine. Whether he's imbuing various textures of celeriac with zingy flavours, or putting pork belly centre stage in an Asian-inspired dish with a bay leaf cream sauce, his elaborate culinary creations are full of flair.

Name: NUH Osteria Contemporanea
Description: Situated in Tivoli’s historic centre, this restaurant has a young chef at the helm who skilfully pays tribute to the region’s gastronomic traditions. Although the menu also features a few fish dishes and the occasional ingredient from outside Lazio, it is the dishes made from local produce with their intense, delicious flavours that will linger long in the memory.

Name: NY Basement
Description: This atmospheric restaurant on the basement level of Hotel New York is reminiscent of a jazz club in the Big Apple of the 1920s and 1930s. The setting could not be any cooler! Kick things off with a cocktail at the 11m-long bar before getting stuck into the modern cuisine, which is right on trend and international. The chefs are as adept at handling yuzu and wasabi as they are at preparing a celeriac Wellington or elevating pan-seared sole with a full-bodied beurre blanc enriched with smoked eel. Fans of fresh oysters and shellfish will find the oyster bar simply irresistible!

Name: NYD - 48° Nord
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: On the road to Hohwald, deep in nature, this Scandinavian-inspired hotel-restaurant promotes simplicity and switching off. These values are reflected in the restaurant, which serves up generous cuisine made with 100% organic and local produce, prepared with simplicity by a mentee of chef Jérôme Jaegle (Alchémille in Kaysersberg), in an intimate rustic-style setting. There is a pleasant terrace with views of the untamed Alsace countryside and the Black Forest in the distance.

Name: Na Chae
Address: 35/1 Mu 3, Mitsamphan Soi 13 Yaek 3, Ban Puek, Mueng Chon Buri, Chon Buri, 20130, Thailand
Description: This local kitchen serves bold Thai flavours with fresh seafood and some wild meats in generous portions. The menu is based on the day's catch supplied by local fishers. Expect spicy, good-quality and honestly executed dishes, with curry pastes pounded by hand. They are renowned for their jungle curry soups: choose from a selection of wild meats and then sit back and embrace the intensity of the dark aromatic broth with ginger roots and Thai aubergines.

Name: Na Ka Seafood
Address: 11 Lane 394, Section 1, Wenhua 3rd Road, Linkou District, New Taipei, Taiwan
Description: The spacious, cheerful room is named after the Taiwanese transliteration of Linkou, where it is located. Seafood from the Penghu archipelago is the main event, alongside premium imported fish and crab. Make your pick from the live fish tank and ask the staff for the best ways to prepare them. Steamed garlic prawns on glass noodles stand out with bouncy meat and deep flavour. There are also set menus for parties ranging from 2 to 10 people.

Name: Na Oh
Address: Hyundai Motor Group Innovation Center Singapore, Level 3, 2 Bulim Link, 649674, Singapore
Description: The joint venture between a motor group and Korean-American chef Corey Lee advocates a ‘seed to table’ concept, whereby most of the veggies served are picked every morning from the ‘smart’ farm abutting the dining room. The combination of Korean culinary traditions and cutting-edge technology is quite inspiring. The kitchen of mostly Korean natives delivers a single seasonal tasting menu of refined Korean dishes.

Name: Na Spilce
Description: This restaurant stands on the premises of the Pilsner Urquell brewery. Diners are seated in a lofty vaulted cellar featuring a modern-meets-rustic decor and a striking service station in the middle of the space. Modern Czech cuisine and traditional hearty beer-hall dishes are all meticulously prepared and packed with flavour. The chefs put a premium on regional ingredients sourced from local suppliers. Of course, a good beer goes well with it. Tip: For special occasions, you can book the ‘Schalender’ in the brewery's lager cellars. Also interesting: brewery museum and shop.

Name: Na Ćošku
Description: Situated to the east of the city just outside the historic centre, a romantic tone sets the scene in this restaurant, which is something of a surprise when compared to its exterior. The dining room boasts all the trappings of a French bistro with small tables, background music (often French) and a few cubby-holes that are perfect for couples. Deeply rooted in Balkan traditions, the menu rolls out wholesome soups and stews, such as lamb in white wine served with mashed potatoes and seasonal vegetables, a lineup of fresh pasta dishes and vegetarian options like vegan curry with chickpeas, sweet potatoes and green beans.

Name: NaDo
Address: Callejón de la Estacada 9, A Coruña, 15001, Spain
Description: Located along a narrow street in the city’s old quarter, yet just a few steps from the boats moored at the Real Club Náutico de A Coruña, NaDo boasts a thoroughly modern look, with an open-view kitchen and just two long tables that can be adjusted according to the number of guests. Here, chef Iván Domínguez, who is constantly moving between the kitchen and the dining room, creates contemporary cuisine with its roots in Galicia and the Atlantic. This is showcased in particular on the Furancho surprise menu, on which the chefs themselves select the dishes to be served.

Name: NaNum
Description: As soon as you enter the restaurant, you can see into the open kitchen, where chef Jinok Kim puts a modern spin on the culinary traditions of her Korean homeland. Using regional ingredients, some from the restaurant's own garden in Brandenburg, she shows a particular interest in fermented foods. The ingredient-led dishes are beautifully precise. Natural wines accompany the five-course set menu (vegetarian or with meat) served on Wednesdays and Thursdays, and the seven-course set menu (vegetarian or with fish) available on Fridays and Saturdays. The space is pleasantly pared back and the service is very friendly. Jinok Kim is also a ceramicist and makes the crockery on which the dishes are served – the studio is also located in the building. The restaurant is located not far from Checkpoint Charlie, on a small square (with a lovely terrace) opposite the Jewish Museum.

Name: Nabi
Address: 201, Building No.1, WYSH, 168 Wuyi Road, Changning, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: Nabi is Korean for "butterfly", symbolising here the exciting metamorphosis of traditional Korean fare under the young chef-owner's stewardship. In the jet-coloured room, which is theatrically lit and dotted with butterfly motifs, the 17-seat counter encloses an open kitchen. Inventive techniques capture Korean flavours, in modern, meticulously plated dishes. There is just one menu and this changes from time to time.

Name: Nacha
Description: A neat bistro with an Argentine and Mediterranean soul, located opposite the versatile CondeDuque Contemporary Culture Centre (once a huge baroque-style barracks, built at the beginning of the 18th century). It has a unique character and is not devoid of personality, since it occupies what was an old café and maintains a certain retro or vintage air about it, with unpolished walls (they prefer to keep them chipped, so that they can tell us their story) and slender wrought iron columns. The food is designed for sharing, successfully fusing Spanish and Argentine flavours with some touches from other parts of the world. Its small menu includes grilled meats, of course, but it does not focus too heavily on them, instead offering other very interesting ‘little dishes’, such as the crispy empanada of knife-cut meat or the juicy cured trout, with a touch of spice.

Name: Nacl
Description: Nestled within the medieval ramparts of Vence, this small restaurant, whose name refers to salt (cast your mind back to chemistry lessons: NaCl is the chemical formula for sodium chloride), serves authentic seasonal cuisine that takes a no-nonsense approach. The menu changes depending on the food markets, and the lunch set menu is a great deal. Friendly service.

Name: Nadiu
Description: Under that name, which could be translated as ‘native’, we see how this restaurant fits, in one way or another, with the identity of the establishment. With its simple minimalist atmosphere, chef Marc Martorell tries to give all the prominence to his culinary roots, clearly tied to the Mediterranean culture (local ingredients, fish from the fish market, vegetables from the garden, meats from the interior of Castellón, etc.). His tasting menu reflects a constant dialogue between the sea and the mountains!

Name: Nadodi
Address: Level 7A, Four Seasons Hotel, 145 Jalan Ampang, Kuala Lumpur, 50450, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking
Description: Check out the spice table at the entrance for a preview of what's to come. Cosy and private, booth seats by the window command sweeping city views. Start with one of the magical concoctions mixed by the mixologists, followed by creative "nomadic" cuisine based on Southern Indian and Sri Lankan fare. The dinner set menu with 10-plus courses features different taste profiles and traditional snacks, best enjoyed with the alcoholic drink pairings.

Name: Nafta Neo Bistro
Description: Dining at this former coffin-making factory in an old industrial district feels like you’ve stumbled upon a secret little hideaway. The atmospheric bistro is spread across two rooms: the first has a red-brick, vintage feel with an open kitchen; the other is a winter garden room with a tree growing out of it and a bohemian atmosphere. In either, you’ll enjoy rustic, full-flavoured dishes with a hint of the Mediterranean. Friendly service helps maintain the relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Naga
Address: Rua Bandeira Paulista 385, São Paulo, 04532-011, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Valet parking
Description: A legendary Japanese restaurant in the city that has for a long time been a favourite address for aficionados of the country’s cuisine. It’s no surprise that the Nagayama group does not just have a single restaurant – in fact, in this area they own almost an entire block that includes the Bar do Naga, the Café do Naga etc. It is split between two floors, with access to the floor above via an attractive steep staircase. In the latter you’ll find two rooms: a waiting area with just a few tables, and a second more spacious room with a direct view of the pleasantly and subtly illuminated sushi bar. The extensive menu features a wide array of carpaccios, sushi, sashimi, uramaki, temaki, tartares and teppanyaki, and if there are several of you, you may want to try combination options such as the popular Naga Case 2 or the enticing Omakase-style tasting menu.

Name: Nage
Description: The character of this medieval mansion has been intelligently enhanced by the cosy, trendy revamp. Niki shares his know-how in terms of choice of excellent natural wines to pair with the modern French recipes crafted by Koen. The chef sprinkles his cooking with the occasional unexpected note in a bid to further highlight the ingredients’ authentic flavours. Examples include saddle of lamb cooked in butter with suave, flavoursome side dishes based on wild garlic. A word of warning: à la carte only at lunchtime and set menu only in the evening.

Name: Nagomi
Description: Two distinct restaurants in Les Pâquis district, run by a Japanese family: one dedicated to sushi, prepared by the father (who you can admire at work if you are seated at the counter); the other to tempura dishes cooked by the son. Both places have an authentic atmosphere, straightforward service, and top-notch ingredients: you're in for a simple treat.

Name: Nahita Cappadocia
Address: Tekelli Mahallesi, Kayabaş Sokak No:23, Uçhisar, Nevşehir, 50240, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Nahita immediately impresses with one of its finest assets: you enter via the magnificent terrace, which affords romantic views over the valley. Inside, the stone walls are adorned with elegant details. The kitchen team sources ingredients from within a 60km radius to ensure the utmost authenticity in their local cuisine. Think warm dolmas with rice infused with the aroma of the vine leaves and sweet-and-sour cherries, finished with a few cherries and dill – pure pleasure on a plate. The chefs pack bold flavours into every dish, such as the distinctive herbs accompanying pan-fried liver. Set within the Argos hotel complex, this is a dining experience not to be missed.

Name: Nai Ho Chicken Rice
Address: 88/14 Mu 4, Sisa Thong, Nakhon Chai Si, Nakhon Pathom, 73120, Thailand
Description: Nai Ho serves just one item: chicken rice with clear soup and a punchy dipping sauce. The fermented soy has been fine-tuned for extra depth, lifting the simple dish with bold flavour. Arrive early as they tend to sell out; the chicken liver, a prized extra, disappears even faster.

Name: Nai Khlong Boat Noodles
Address: 40 Soi Ayothaya 4/3, Phai Ling, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: This shop beside a canal exudes charm, with its simple wooden shelves and tables. Highlights include the boat noodles in a well-balanced broth and the richly flavoured dry beef soup with tender slices and slow-cooked meat, lifted by roasted peanut aroma.

Name: Nai Liak Beef Noodles
Address: 6/7 Pa Maphrao Road, Ho Rattanachai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: Mr. Liak, this eatery’s owner, started his business way back in 1961 – before moving to his current roadside location in 1977. He serves delicious beef noodle soup at wallet-friendly prices. Beef offal, braised beef, beef meatballs and stewed tendons are among the options available in the savoury broth – vermicelli, herbs and spices are also packed into this signature dish. Expect a wait during peak hours.

Name: Nairod
Description: Located in the heart of the city’s Eixample district, Nairod exudes personality everywhere you look, which doesn’t come as a surprise given that David Rustarazo (better known as Rusti) is at the helm – a self-made chef whose success is down to hard work and experience gained abroad. In this intimate, contemporary setting with a bistro vibe, you'll find market-fresh cuisine where flavour reigns supreme, with an increasing focus on fish and incredible game dishes in season (hare, venison, partridge and, in particular, pigeon). Fun fact: The name of the restaurant is an ode to the chef’s son, Dorian, but spelled backwards!

Name: Naissain
Address: 10 rue des Castaings, Le Teich, 33470, France
Description: “Naissain” means spat (or oyster larvae). This modern bistro was opened by Thomas Iglesias, a chef who has sailed the seven seas. He always has one dish devoted to this mollusc, which he sources from his brother's oyster farm in La Teste de Buch. As for the rest, this wayfaring chef admits to having a soft spot for vegetables, on which he lavishes his creative talent to tease out each flavour, in dishes such as a starter of mushrooms, miso, ham and Jerusalem artichoke. The concise menu is renewed monthly and the lunchtime menu offers excellent value for pleasure.

Name: Nakazen
Description: His grandfather was a caterer, his father a baker, so the path of the chef was a natural one for this owner-chef. Determined to be a culinary artist with roots in his community, the chef hung out his noren in a residential district. Seasonal menus weave in vegetables grown in his home region of Ohara. Fish come from Awaji, where the place he trained has ties. Items on the plate nestle together, evoking a sense of connections among people. Friendly service also puts the heart at ease.

Name: Nam Ngiao Yong
Address: Unit 19, Siri Wattana Market, 193 Chang Phueak Road, Chang Phueak, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
Description: This simple stall with limited seating draws crowds with its two flavoursome dishes. The khanom chin nam ngiao with tangy tomato broth and pork ribs, and khanom chin with red curry chicken with coconut milk and fish balls make it well worth coming to Siri Watthana Market.

Name: Nam Phuong
Address: 4051 Buford Hwy. NE, Atlanta, GA, 30345, USA
Description: Chef/owner Du Nguyen and co-owner Hoa Phan have created a welcoming spot at Nam Phuong, tucked inside a blue-roofed building on the side of Buford Highway, but comfortable booths aside, all eyes are on the large menu. Staples like vermicelli noodles and fried rice are on offer, and you'll never go wrong with a bowl of pho (try pho gâu, which bobs with tender brisket and bouncy noodles). However, it's the Vietnamese street food section that demands attention with treats like bôt chiên, pan-fried rice flour cubes with egg and a sweet soy dipping sauce. No matter your selection, the dishes are prepared with care. Come with a group, as family-style menus are designed for up to ten, sample a wide variety and offer great value.

Name: Namak
Address: Dusit Thani Hotel, Sultan Bin Zayed The First Street (Al Muroor Road), Abu Dhabi
Description: A culinary voyage around India drawing on myriad influences is the draw here at this colourful restaurant within the Dusit Thani hotel. The passion of the kitchen team really comes through in the carefully prepared dishes. The lamb specialities are particularly good, whether that’s Kashmiri Rogan Josh or Kakori Reshmi Seekh. There’s plenty for vegetarians too, including sharing platters.

Name: Namakzip
Address: #1068 A, W square, 145 Bunpo-ro, Nam-gu, Busan, 48515, South Korea
Description: Busan offers a wide variety of dwaeji-gukbap (pork and rice soup), befitting its position as the origin of this dish. Every restaurant adds its own twist to the soup’s broth while staying true to its authentic flavors. At Namakzip, the meat broth features a higher proportion of vegetable broth, so it tastes light and clean rather than heavy. In addition to this iconic soup, the menu includes kalguksu (hand-cut noodle soup) with meat; kalguksu with fresh noodles, both featuring meat broth from dwaeji-gukbap; boiled pork slices; and grilled pork belly. For those wishing to enjoy, amidst a modern dining space, a satisfying dwaeji-gukbap with a minimal aftertaste, Namakzip is the way to go.

Name: Nami
Address: Lake Nona Wave Hotel, 6004 Artist Ave., Orlando, FL, 32827, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Valet parking
Description: Set within the Lake Nona Wave Hotel, Nami makes a splash with its lofted ceilings and sexy vibe. There are two distinct dining experiences here: a dining room spotlighting contemporary Japanese cuisine (think skewers and maki) and a chef's counter tasting menu presenting a creative interpretation of Japanese cuisine. On the tasting, discover the likes of citrus-cured buri with yuzu-cured flying fish roe or a decadent riff on a corndog with caviar and triple cream Brie enhanced bechamel. Beef and broccoli, that Chinese-American staple, is given the luxe treatment with grilled wagyu and broccoli served four ways. À la carte standouts include barbecue unagi over rice and the Koshihikari rice pudding with berries and almonds.

Name: Nami Beef and Reef
Description: In an area of the city filled with restaurants, seek out this atmospheric spot where the menu reads like a ‘greatest hits’ of Japanese cuisine. Gyozas, nigiri, yakitori… all will be provided by the skilled kitchen team; and while the place lives up to its name with a wide sushi selection and multiple cuts of beef cooked on the robata grill, it’s worth diverting your attention to the terrific vegetable tempura. It’s all perfect for sharing, so bring some friends and sample as much as possible.

Name: Nammos Estiatorio
Description: Escape to Greece via Nammos Estiatorio, whose white-washed walls, bare wood tables and azure accents evoke a breezy, sunny feel. Vancouver has no shortage of Greek fare, but the cooking at this charming enclave sets itself apart thanks to a clear dedication to quality ingredients and careful preparation. Traditional dishes reign here, starting with spreads like tzatziki and taramosalata, to an excellent example of spanakopita, with ideally crispy phyllo pastry around a savory filling of spinach and feta. Seafood options are, unsurprisingly, a strength, from crispy fried kalamari to whole grilled sea bream with fennel salad. Sip on an assortment of Greek wines, and finish with loukoumades, classic fritters with walnuts and honey syrup.

Name: Nampo Myeonok
Description: Tucked away in a small alley among densely populated office buildings that sees a constant stream of foot traffic, the main building of this long-standing institution recently underwent a major facelift.
