A longtime favorite among patrons of all ages for its authentic Pyeongyang cold buckwheat noodles and beef hot pot, Nampo Myeonok continues to charm with its consistently good food and friendly service. Chair seating and floor seating are both available.

Name: Namu
Address: The Esplanade Mall, Prince Turki Bin Abdulaziz Alawwal Street, King Saud University, Riyadh, 12371, Saudi Arabia
Description: Korean barbeque meets a fun and elevated setting. It’s on you to cook up the meat as you like on a hot plate at the centre of the table. Get yourselves a couple of starters to share before choosing your preferred cut of beef. Expect a generously portioned selection of pickles and kimchi to complement your barbeque experience. If you’re still looking to prolong your evening, make your way to the nearby bowling alley and cinema for the ultimate fun night out.

Name: Namun
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: For fans of Thai food, this restaurant in the luxurious Grand Resort Bad Ragaz is the place to be! The focus is on Thai cuisine, but there are also Chinese dishes. Elegant and minimalist, the Far Eastern-style decor makes for the perfect setting. Tip: Ask about the Thai curry – even if it's not on the menu. In case you were wondering, the name Namun translates as "lukewarm water" and is a reference to the local thermal spring.

Name: Nan Bei
Address: 19F, Rosewood Hotel, 1041/38 Phloen Chit Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Car park,Cash only,Counter dining,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Nan Bei means ‘south’ and ‘north’ so it’s no surprise to discover that this restaurant specialises in China’s southern and northern regions, from where the recipes come and ingredients are flown in. It sits on the 19th floor of the Rosewood Hotel, offering fabulous views of Bangkok while you dine. Braised abalone and braised pork belly shouldn’t be missed, though the prized item is Peking duck. Sit at the counter to see the chefs at work or to watch the birds being roasted over lychee wood. Lunchtime dim sum is also worth exploring.

Name: Nan Qi Lou 1924
Address: 17 Daxi Street, Licheng, Quanzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Foreign credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: With dark wood finishes and painted tile flooring, Nan Qi Lou exudes a retro vibe in keeping with this century-old neighbourhood. Quanzhou has been home to the Chinese diaspora in Southeast Asia for centuries, hence the menu combining Minnan and Southeast Asian cuisines. The mildly spicy Quanzhou curry crab (without coconut milk) is infused with flavour by dried seafood. Their ginger braised squab leg is a variation on the classic ginger duck stew.

Name: Nan Tang (Tianshun Road)
Address: 2F, North Tower, Interaxx Plaza, 151 Tianshun Road, Wuhou, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
Description: This cultural dining concept spreads across several elegant rooms dotted with pierced carvings and calligraphy reliefs. The Chinese stacking food box motif symbolises culinary heritage. Various ingredients are prepared in traditional Sichuanese ways to great effect, examples being the crispy-skinned pigeon enhanced by Sichuan pepper, or the velvety fish tofu shaped like a crescent moon, with a veil of bamboo fungus and covered in a consommé.

Name: Nan Xing Yuan
Address: Building 12, 1728 Middle Huaihai Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: Helmed by a team of Sichuan chefs, this restaurant takes a deposit upon booking and serves only tailored menus, which diners pre-order. A typical menu builds a progression of flavours with classics such as napa cabbage in chicken consommé, and sautéed shredded pork with green chilli. Authentic dishes are meticulously prepared to showcase the 24 flavour profiles of Sichuanese cooking. Only private rooms are available, and reservations are a must.

Name: Nan's Gourmet
Address: No. 101, Block B, UPARK+, 666 Fuhua North Road, Wuhou, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
Description: In 2021, the Hongkong owner opened Nan’s Gourmet at this dining hub. In the F&B business for over 40 years, he convened a kitchen team of mostly Guangdong natives to capture the essence of Cantonese cooking. The menu features classics like dim sum, Cantonese barbecues, double-boiled soups and sizzling claypot dishes. Try the steamed pork patty with sweet dried cabbage – the springy half-fatty pork in a briny-sweet seasoning is simply addictive.

Name: Nananère
Description: A childhood treat – but better! Bang in the middle of town, this modern, stylish brasserie, decorated in a playful vein, is fronted by a lovely patio, decked out in olive green furnishings, overlooking a leafy, cobbled square. The culinary score stars local delicacies, like salade niçoise and pissaladière, that have been updated and reworked, many of which bear amusing names in keeping with the establishment’s theme. The free-range breast of poultry and risotto of spelt with morels and savory, which come straight from the family cottage garden in Vallauris, hits the spot every time, as does the delicious clafoutis of seasonal fruits. Professional, spot-on service. Now takes bookings.

Name: Nanas
Description: Nanas has been a fixture on the Durham dining scene since 1992, though new owners put their own stamp on it while respecting its history. Friendly and warm, the place has a smart retro look.This is the sort of place where there's something for everyone and you'll have a hard time deciding which dish to order. Italian and French classics with local products take center stage, while some old favorites like North Carolina shrimp remoulade remain as an homage to the original. Pasta dishes are especially popular, and some of the larger plates utilize the wood grill, but don't sleep on the dreamy chocolate soufflé.

Name: Nancy Bourguignon
Address: Lieu-dit de Bourgeac, 1 chemin de l'Ancienne-Voie-Ferrée, Paradou, 13520, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: What a pleasure it is to take a seat in this establishment where you are welcomed naturally and simply by a Burgundian family. In this charming restaurant, the chef concocts subtle and delicate dishes, sprinkled with Provençal innuendo. The patio, next to the swimming pool and surrounded by Mediterranean vegetation, invites you to slow down and take things easy. An oasis of peace and charm.

Name: Naniwakappo NOBORU
Description: ‘Flavour first’ is the watchword at this kappo-style restaurant, where food is prepared before your eyes. The chef also serves generous helpings of smiles and conversation. Orders are placed in kaiseki fashion but varied by the mood of the day and guest preference. ‘Shinjo o hakari, ninjo wo kurau’— words from the restaurant where the chef apprenticed, serves as an exhortation to be thankful for the good fortune of providing what the diner desires. The craftsman spirit of a Naniwa (Osaka) kappo is enshrined in the name.

Name: Naniwaryori Satou
Description: The chef honed his skills at a Naniwa (Osaka-style) kappo. The restaurant’s name, ‘Satou’, adds a kanji for the ‘u’ to his surname, Sato, in homage to the shop where he apprenticed. The long Japanese menu is written right-to-left, like a scroll. His speciality, passed down from his mentor along with his cherished serving bowls, is ‘Tenjin Kobai Mushi’, savoury egg custard prepared with dried-plum broth and finished with a delicate plum glaze. The chef prides himself on his quick thinking in picking up guests’ preferences. An heir to the spirit and skills of Osaka cuisine.

Name: Nannini
Description: This restaurant run by the young Nannini brothers (one front of house, the other in the kitchen) occupies one of Livorno’s most interesting buildings, situated in the district of Antignano with its period houses and typical atmosphere. The focus here is almost exclusively on fish, in dishes which are original yet at the same time respectful of their ingredients – matured fish is one of the specialities. A top-quality dining experience.

Name: Nanyang Blossom
Address: 12 Knightsbridge Green, Knightsbridge, London, SW1X 7QL, United Kingdom
Description: The Nanyang region encompasses parts of both China and Southeast Asia, so you can expect influences from a variety of countries at this understatedly chic restaurant hidden down a narrow passageway. The array of menus includes a tasting option, an extensive à la carte and set sharing options for more indecisive diners. The dishes show care, craft and vibrancy across the board – but it’s the signature Knightsbridge crispy beef ribs that steal the show. The endearing service adds to the appeal.

Name: Nao
Address: Miguel Hidalgo S/N, Centro, San José del Cabo, 23400, Mexico
Description: One look at Nao, with whitewashed brick and pops of blue, and you won't be surprised that it's Mediterranean-minded. What will come as a welcome surprise, however, is the high level of service and the exemplary dishes. Local chef Alex Branch has created a winning menu, and from the bread and pasta to the gelato, everything is made in house. Don't skip the starters, especially the roasted beets with pomegranate molasses. From there, tuck into house-made tortellini with flavors of cacio e pepe with shrimp, small tobiko, and pea tendrils. Main dishes, like lechón, are sized for sharing, which leaves plenty of room for yogurt gelato with crumbled baklava and macerated strawberries.

Name: Napoli
Address: 1 Courtenay Place, Te Aro, Wellington, 6011, New Zealand
Description: A stickler for tradition, the kitchen rolls out Neapolitan staples and pizzas that are simple but delicious. Their calamari fritti with lemon and aioli sauce is masterfully crafted, boasting soft, flavoursome squid and a delicate crunch. Their lineup of pizzas features top-notch ingredients, with classics like the margherita, pepperoni or funghi being the most popular. Consider ordering wine pairings or Italian cocktails to complement the food.

Name: Naramachi Sushi Hanako
Description: Latticework and white plaster walls exude a machiya feel. The ambience is charming at night, with light seeping in to add warmth to the stillness. This entire district, today known as Naramachi, was once the precinct of Gangoji Temple; the restaurant is on the former site of the main temple building. Two sisters run the eatery, the younger preparing sushi, and the elder handling service. Sharing an unspoken understanding, they move in quiet harmony, and diners naturally fall into the rhythm between them.

Name: Narbasu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: If you’re keen to find a place in which to “lose yourself” and relax in the purest sense of the word, you won’t find anywhere quite like the Palacio de Rubianes, an authentic 14C Asturian-style property surrounded by verdant meadows and with the impressive summits of the Picos de Europa as a backdrop. Facilities here include attractive guestrooms and impressive market-inspired cooking bearing the signature of Esther and Nacho Manzano. Their cuisine is showcased on an à la carte and on two menus (Tradicional and Narbasu), all of which reveal authentic local flavours and include classic dishes from Casa Marcial, albeit from a more local perspective. Added interest is provided by the restaurant’s own kitchen garden on an old golf course, and a restored old mill standing alongside a stream to produce their own cornflour, which they then use to make their superb “tortos” appetisers.

Name: Narda Comedor
Address: Mariscal Antonio José De Sucre 664, Buenos Aires, C1428DUB, Argentina
Description: The love that locals in Buenos Aires have for meat has been long documented, however Narda Lepes, a woman who is well known thanks to her cookery books and TV appearances, is slowly changing this attitude. She is a champion of healthy ingredients and a vegetarian diet, hence the predominance she gives to vegetables here. Her stuffed onion dish will satisfy even the most die-hard of carnivores, while her silky tofu is a culinary legacy that originates from her travels overseas. Although there’s a plethora of vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options, that doesn’t mean that her restaurant is fully vegetarian as evidenced by her ossobuco, a legendary dish in every respect. The bright and roomy white dining space gives the impression of being in a particularly elegant cafeteria, enhanced by the equally spacious open kitchen. Service here begins with breakfast, hence the different dining incarnations through the day, from morning coffee to lunchtime snacks and dinner with friends.

Name: Nare Sushi
Description: Situated in a small business park in a Poznań suburb, this well-run sushi spot is flooded with natural light and has a bright, contemporary Japanese look. The chef-owner shows great passion in her work and learnt her craft from respected sushi masters. Her menu mixes traditional nigiri, sashimi and maki with more creative and international touches. The hot dishes include a choice of ramen and the strong wine list features a sake selection too.

Name: Narla
Address: 19 Fore Street, Fowey, PL23 1AH, United Kingdom
Description: The picturesque harbour town of Fowey makes a great setting for this chic, clean-lined bistro enlivened by both the buzz of its happy diners and the energy emanating from the sleek open kitchen. Plenty of flavour is packed into each carefully presented dish, starting with snacks such as chicken wings and crispy cod bons bons, then continuing with the likes of roasted duck breast complemented by miso cauliflower and Cornish kea plum. The range of enticing menus includes vegan options, a good value lunch deal and even a Sunday roast.

Name: Narru
Address: San Martín 22, Donostia / San Sebastián, 20005, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: Located opposite the city’s Buen Pastor cathedral, Narru boasts a modern dining room in which the menu features traditional, market-inspired cuisine with an unequivocal focus on high-quality ingredients that tries to reflect its own character and provide an element of surprise. It features one informal space perfect for tapas and a second more elegant dining area with tables and tablecloths in which the à la carte (half portions are possible) is complemented by an impressive tasting menu. Do make sure you try some of their grilled dishes: red mullet, turbot, sole, lobster... The restaurant takes its name from the nickname of the chef’s great-grandfather, a former professional pelota player.

Name: Nasi Lemak Ayam Taliwang
Address: Yishun Park Hawker Centre, #01-33, 51 Yishun Avenue 11, 768867, Singapore
Description: Traditional coconut milk rice with Indonesian spicy chicken and sambal sauce.

Name: Nassau
Description: A centuries-old beamed ceiling, glossy parquet flooring, sleek furniture design and views of the beautiful Prinsentuin walled garden – you really dine in style at Groningen's Nassau. The chef knows the importance of an intense sauce and loves working with top-notch produce such as langoustine and Anjou pigeon, which he showcases in elaborate dishes. For instance, he elevates hamachi, along with a medley of vegetables and seasonings, with a Thai-style sauce made with miso, coconut and lemongrass. His plant-based creations are equally remarkable. A beautifully curated wine list featuring an interesting range of German wines has the perfect accompaniment in store. Sophistication is in Nassau's very DNA.

Name: Nast
Description: Dean Masschelein has added his inimitable stamp to a former chicory factory, retaining the original rough brick walls, but cleverly dotted with modern fixtures and fittings. The chef is a genuine West Flemish lad, as his exuberant personality and passion for regional produce quickly reveal. The food is succulent, straightforward and international and he might mix presa iberico with a sweet-sour baba ghanoush and Mediterranean fregola, all of which comes together thanks to an emulsion of bacon. Creative seasonal cooking, rendered even more flavoursome when paired with gueuze beers or organic wines.

Name: Nate's on Marsh
Address: 450 Marsh St., San Luis Obispo, CA, 93401, USA
Description: This affable spot is just outside of downtown San Luis Obispo. It's no surprise that Nate's on Marsh feels very welcoming—it's set within a converted residence. Inside is just as darling with palm-printed wallpaper and a Western/equestrian theme. Nate Long is the consummate host and the service is exceptionally warm, though it certainly doesn't hurt that the menu is loaded with classics and riffs on favorites that will have you coming back for more. Try the La Scala salad, a blend of shredded iceberg, salami, artichoke hearts, sun-dried tomatoes, and crispy chickpeas, all tossed in a red wine vinaigrette, before tucking into hearty mains. Hand-cut pappardelle with Tablas Creek lamb ragu and walnut gremolata isn't fussy but it's fantastic.

Name: Nathan Marshall Clarke House
Address: Clarke House, Farnham Road, Liss, GU33 6JQ, United Kingdom
Description: From the façade, you wouldn’t guess this was once a courthouse, but inside you’ll find a door leading to what was the judge’s bench. It’s a tiny place with exposed beams and a rustic style and is keenly run by a young couple. Cooking sees a little intricacy added to well-presented, country house style dishes.

Name: National Kitchen
Address: National Gallery Singapore, #02-01, (Coleman Street entrance), 1 St. Andrew's Road, 178957, Singapore
Description: Art and sculptures aren’t the only treasures found in the National Gallery – on the 2nd floor is this restaurant from Violet Oon, Singapore’s own national treasure and one of its greatest ambassadors. The handsome, panelled 1920s-style dining room is an ideal backdrop to the cooking which, through its spicing, contrasting textures and enticing aromas, showcases Singapore’s unique culinary heritage. This is a restaurant with genuine charm.

Name: National da Sergio
Description: Located in the Old Town, right on Klosterplatz, this invitingly down-to-earth restaurant serves classic Italian cuisine made from high-quality ingredients. The menu features pasta and a variety of traditional meat and fish dishes, with plenty of familiar favourites. Mouthwatering examples include "Piccata Milanese con Risotto ai Funghi Porcini" and "Fusilli 'Pasta di Gragnano' alla Scarpara". As you might expect, the wine list features Italian labels. Owner Sergio Salsi brings a personal touch – his charming, easy-going manner fills the restaurant with life and gives it real character.

Name: Natura
Description: Well-chosen seasonal Finnish ingredients are used to good effect at this intimate restaurant and techniques like fermenting, pickling, salting, chargrilling and smoking all play their part. Choose from a range of colourful modern small plates or opt for the 'All Out' menu – the full range of dishes in miniature!

Name: Natura Hill
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: It’s certainly worth the climb up the steep, narrow lane, as the two-hectare Natura Hill – comprising a restaurant, bedrooms, a small spa and an artisanal fruit and vegetable processing plant – boasts breathtaking Danube Bend views. Ingredients from their farm and the area underpin the cooking and the surprise menu evolves twice a day as new produce arrives; unfussy, vibrantly flavoured dishes could include duck with koji-dried porcini, plum compote and preserved onion foam. An overnight stay is a must, creating a holistic relaxation and wellness experience topped off with memorable sunset views.

Name: Nature's Own
Address: 1F, Meifan Plaza Proya, 588 Xixi Road, Xihu, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: An oasis amid the bustling city centre complete with a landscaped garden straight out of a Song Dynasty art book. The menu focuses on plant-based dishes of varying origins and styles. Cauliflower fungus tossed in lemongrass with Thai chilli and basil packs extra oomph; sizzling three-cup eggplant in a stone pot seduces with aromas and mild heat. Round off with sticky millet rice balls and a peanut filling. Check out the extensive tea menu.

Name: Nautika
Description: Among the most sought-after restaurants in the city – reservations are essential – Nautika offers a traditional, rich and well-executed cuisine, with no concessions to passing trends or exotic influences, in which Dalmatian recipes are elevated by solid French and Italian foundations. The service is impeccable, with a well-prepared team and a wine list of excellent calibre. Situated at the entrance to the old city, by the sea, its terraces afford a spectacular view of the Adriatic and the illuminated fortresses of Lovrijenac and Bokar: a venue with a decidedly romantic appeal.

Name: Nav
Description: One rings the doorbell and is welcomed into an intimate and convivial space: with just five tables and an open kitchen, the atmosphere deliberately recreates the impression of being a guest in the home of chef Tvrtko Šakota. The restaurant opens for dinner only and welcomes up to eight guests, for an intimate experience in which the chef cooks, serves and personally presents a twelve-course tasting menu. The seasons guide every decision, and the ingredients are sourced from Croatian organic and biodynamic farms, including the chef’s own property forty kilometres from the city: vegetables and fruit, wild-caught Adriatic fish, free-range meats, and game. The menu, with wine pairings from small Croatian producers, is a creative journey through the country’s regions. The bread and baked goods, including the traditional salenjaci, are remarkable. Reservation is compulsory, with payment in advance.

Name: Navio
Address: The Ritz-Carlton, Half Moon Bay, 1 Miramontes Point Rd., Half Moon Bay, CA, 94019, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Nestled inside the luxe Ritz-Carlton, Half Moon Bay, Navio enjoys one of Northern California’s most dramatic dining settings, with sweeping ocean views that make sunset particularly magical. The real draw, however, is Chef Francisco Simón’s polished, contemporary cuisine rooted in excellent ingredients and classical technique. Dishes strike an easygoing note of luxury, from pristine Dungeness crab with apple and sourdough to Liberty Farm duck paired with radicchio and pear. Desserts lean more playful, like a sculptural chocolate composition with pistachio, almond and hazelnut. Altogether, it’s refined coastal dining that feels both elegant and relaxed.

Name: Nazario Cano
Description: Located in a room by the entrance of the Ritual de Terra Moraira Resort & Spa hotel, the restaurant stands out as an exclusive area with independent access. In its cosy interior, dominated by earth tones and with a quaint ceiling decoration featuring circular figures hanging in different shapes, Chef Nazario Cano champions an extremely contemporary and personal cuisine with Mediterranean roots, with constant nods to local produce from the Marina Alta, respect for the natural cycles and traditional flavours, all through his tasting menus (Terra, Ritual and Nazario Cano). Standout dishes? We were particularly impressed by their eel dish, which featured several highly original touches, but above all the hare à la royale with daikon radish and a small cube of foie gras, as well as a hare loin fillet with an incredible texture, accompanied by a beetroot-infused milk jus and a thin layer of gelatin made from a reduction of the sauce itself.

Name: Nazka
Description: You might, for a moment, feel as if you have stumbled across a wine cellar, but you will soon see that this hip South American eatery is very much at home in this cosmopolitan city. Nazka unleashes a whirlwind of bold flavours on your palate, from pisco cocktails to ceviche and other Peruvian specialities. This is exhilarating cuisine featuring a captivating interplay of spicy and sweet chilli peppers, Asian umami and the zing of leche del tigre. The well-curated selection of wines from around the globe adds extra character to this unique dining experience.

Name: Naïfs
Address: 56 Goldsmith Road, Peckham, London, SE15 5TN, United Kingdom
Description: Plant-based Peckhamites must surely be in love with this friendly neighbourhood bistro serving solely vegan dishes. The restaurant is simply decorated and boasts an on-view kitchen, which produces hearty, original plates full of bold flavours. The set menu makes good use of what's in season, beginning with snacks and shared starters such as whipped tahini and fried aubergine with sourdough from the nearby TOAD bakery, while the main courses are served individually and dessert can be added on to complete the experience. For a more flexible option, go for the à la carte bar menu.

Name: Ne Quittez pas
Description: Toshio Tanabe was an Olympic gymnast candidate and a professional boxer before he became a chef, steering his ambitions for the wider world towards French cuisine. His billboard reads, ‘French cuisine with seasonal seafood and vegetables’. The secret stories behind the restaurant’s name, the fish soup and the grilled clams lay bare Tanabe’s mode of living. The ‘soil course’ and the watermelon prix fixe offerings are ideas from a unique imagination. Enjoy the flavours and share in the secrets.

Name: Nebuka
Description: Nebuka was opened by the proprietor of a wine bar. It is said that the best grapevines are those with the deepest roots (‘ne-buka’), and deep are the connections Nebuka cultivates with producers and in ingredients and cuisine. Omakase set menus focus on seasonal vegetables. Experienced in both French and Japanese cuisine, the chef applies expertise in both schools, and even creates pasta dishes. Each dish is arranged simply, placing the ingredients centre stage. A young team provides bright and pleasant service.

Name: Nectar
Address: Av. Andrés García Lavín 334, San Antonio Cucul, Plaza Jardin, Mérida, 97116, Mexico
Description: Located inside the attractive Plaza Jardin, with a stylish lofted interior and a spacious open kitchen, this striking restaurant was the proving ground that established Chef Roberto Solis’s status as one of the leading lights of modern Yucatecan gastronomy. The contemporary menu, offered either à la carte or as a 5- or 7-course tasting, encompasses traditional ingredients and flavors alongside global influences, as in crispy pork belly castacán with charred pineapple and xcatic chili, house-made rigatoni with lobster and foie gras, or an intriguing sweet finale of recado negro pavlova with caramelized figs and yogurt. Gracious, warmly attentive hospitality, combined with the approachable, satisfying cuisine, makes for an altogether enjoyable experience

Name: Nectari
Description: Chef Jordi Esteve dresses his signature cuisine with the enriching nuances provided by local raw ingredients, and it's no coincidence that he works very closely with small producers! The tasty offer of this centrally located restaurant, with a neighbourhood atmosphere, is based on seasonal products and, although it has an à la carte menu, it always shines especially in its tasting menu (which can be enriched with a wine pairing). You'll find interesting combinations, such as their foie gras and eel or the appetising topinambur cream with prawns and seasonal mushrooms.

Name: Neder
Description: At Neder, they are committed to working with local produce. From Eastern Scheldt salt and wild-harvested herbs to Veluwe red deer and Texel mustard seeds, everything, including the drinks, comes from within a 223km radius. What they don't grow themselves is sourced from responsible suppliers. This approach presents numerous challenges, but it also inspires chefs to be more creative. They bring each season to life with a new set menu, building on a foundation of ingredients preserved using a variety of methods. Marinated hogweed flowers and a chamomile beurre blanc lend the steamed pike-perch a fresh, floral lift. Summer venison is rubbed with wheat koji for that umami flavour – this is sophisticated, aromatic and innovative cuisine. The fact that Neder is an ambassador for the Dutch terroir is also expressed in the interior design, with its landscape paintings, visible fermentation room and a combination of rusticity and soothing natural materials.

Name: Neiburgs
Description: The crowds thin out as you wind your way down the cobbled streets of the Old Town and find yourself in this peaceful spot. Located on the ground floor of a boutique hotel, this restaurant is the place to dine if you’re looking for a smart environment but with a pleasingly unpretentious atmosphere; there’s also a lovely terrace for warmer days. The menus offer fresh, unfussy dishes with some Mediterranean influences, and the seafood options are particularly appealing. The crab and tiger prawn ravioli with bisque sauce is a real winner, while the herring dishes are always a popular choice.

Name: Neighbourhood
Address: 1 North Main Street, Naas, W91 RH96, Ireland
Description: What was once a pub on the town's main street is now this smart contemporary restaurant where the room quickly fills with the buzz of chatting diners. The appealing menu is the kind that gives you trouble choosing – even if you come for their Sunday roasts or dedicated Steak Nights – with high-quality ingredients shining through in the likes of grilled turbot with a full-flavoured shellfish sauce. If you're in a group, then look out for the larger cuts of beef designed for sharing, such as tomahawk, porterhouse and Chateaubriand.

Name: Neked Főztem
Description: This inviting roadside pub sits in an elevated spot and is fronted by a pleasant terrace. Inside it’s warm and welcoming with a rustic feel – thanks to a log burner crackling away on colder nights. Its name translates as ‘I cooked for you’. The concise menu lists all things Hungarian and the friendly team are happy to talk you through it and offer suggestions. The gutsy home-cooking has plenty of flavour and can be paired with a selection of local wines.

Name: Nelita
Address: Rua Ferreira De Araújo, 330, São Paulo, 05428-000, Brazil
Description: One of the standout restaurants in the Baixo Pinheiros area! This establishment, under the direction of chef Tássia Magalhães — who leads an all-female kitchen team — offers an enticing menu of Italian-influenced signature dishes. On the floor, the wine list is carefully curated by Danyel Steinle, who champions Brazilian labels without overlooking international references, ensuring pairings that are both precise and elegant. The experience is divided into three formats: the 11-course Experiência menu, served exclusively at the kitchen counter, a 6-course menu inspired by the delicacy and strength of female cooking, and an à la carte menu. In addition to the option of sitting at the chef's counter, the space — decorated in a modern style with a variety of distinct areas — offers tables throughout the dining room and a private room that can be reserved for groups.

Name: Nello
Address: Via IV Novembre 66, San Casciano in Val di Pesa, 50026, Italy
Location: San Casciano in Val di Pesa, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Federico at the stove and Chiara, pastry chef and the soul of the welcome, have brought new life to a long-established local restaurant, transforming it into a modern expression of Tuscan cooking. The menu, varied and stimulating, features dishes such as the raviolo filled with Parmigiano cream from Red Cows, served with chanterelles and onions – intense and technically accomplished – as well as their intriguing take on tiramisù, given an added dimension by a secret touch of tobacco. Over the years, the wine list has grown considerably, reflecting the deep passion of both proprietors; the bottles are kept in a captivating sixteenth-century space that is most certainly worth a look.

Name: Nemrod
Description: Tally-ho! At this restaurant dedicated to Nimrod, the biblical king and hunter, you can be sure of catching game in the sights of a chef who describes himself as a real hunter-gatherer-fisherman. After stints in some high-calibre establishments, chef Nicolas Gaulandeau has returned to roam his native land, crafting dishes from the finest vegetables and meats sourced from local market gardeners and producers. The result is sophisticated and tasty cuisine, as exemplified by line-caught meagre with herbs, fennel confit, hummus and black garlic hollandaise. Highly professional service and an attractive contemporary space.

Name: Neo
Description: Note: This restaurant is temporarily closedBorn out of the pandemic, this intimate sushi counter sports an unusual location inside of a couture clothing store in Montrose. The unlikely setting has only a precious few seats in the hands of friendly chefs who honor the traditions of Japanese omakase on their own terms. Focused and measured, they carefully prepare the sushi rice and meticulously slice fish at the start of the meal. Their style is not strictly traditional, and the tasting features a variety of fun flourishes. Think uni risotto or nigiri dabbed with black garlic or kumquats. The quality of seafood is noteworthy, with much of it flown in from Japan and dry-aged for weeks in fridges in the back. At this time, boozy beverages are limited.

Name: Neon Boat Noodles
Address: 395/7 Pattaya, Nong Prue, Bang Lamung, Chon Buri, 20150, Thailand
Description: Traditional boat noodles are served here with various toppings in a bold and savoury soup. We also recommend the spicy boiled pork and pork condiments, which have an intensely flavoured sauce and the aroma of fried garlic.

Name: Nephele
Address: 125/12 Nguyen Cuu Van Street, Gia Dinh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: Located in the alley of a newly renovated building steeped in history, this dinner-only restaurant serves a single tasting menu. The menu, made with ingredients that the chef selects from diverse regions, is perfectly paired with wine or non-alcoholic drinks. The experience begins on the ground floor, moves upstairs to the elegant main dining room, and ends back at the bar with mignardises served to the sound of vinyl records. Each course is distinguished by its sauce, with bold, original flavours that show a clear Vietnamese influence. A standout is the 36-hour fermented sourdough bread, charcoal-baked to a crisp finish and served with honeycomb, truffle butter and miso made from the bread.

Name: Neptune Oyster
Description: Located in the North End, Neptune Oyster features a dark blue facade with a large window revealing oysters displayed on a bed of crushed ice overseen by a blue aproned shucker in perpetual motion. The cozy setting is just short of boisterous, but it's charming. The narrow interior has mosaic tiled flooring, a slender white marble winding along the side of the room, and a red leather banquette on the opposite wall. The day's oysters are presented on a small card, and on the wood-framed, wall-mounted mirror.Keep it simple, as in some briny bivalves, a New England-style fritto misto sandwich on locally baked brioche and a nice bottle of wine picked from the thoughtfully curated list highlighting labels from European coastal regions.

Name: Neptune Palace Seafood Restaurant
Address: 470 S.W. Marine Dr., Vancouver, V5X 0C7, Canada
Description: Ensconced on the second floor of the Marine Gate shopping mall, this expansive banquet hall-cum-restaurant is no secret to locals in search of excellent dim sum and Cantonese specialties. The spacious room readily accommodates large groups, the better to sample a wide range of mouthwatering options—though at peak hours, you may face wait times. During the day, the menu offers the traditional array of carefully prepared dumplings, many featuring exceptionally plump, juicy shrimp, as well as warming bowls of congee. At dinner, expect a broader variety of seafood, including pricier delicacies like lobster, abalone and sea cucumber, as well as a wide selection of meaty options, from crisp-skinned roasted duck to sweet and sour pork with pineapple.

Name: Nern Khao View Talay
Address: 18/6 Mu 10, Soi Namtok Wat Khao, Khok Kloi, Takua Thung, Phang-Nga, 82140, Thailand
Description: Nern Khao View Talay offers stunning views of mountains and sea from up high on a hill. Serving Thai and southern cuisine, the stir-fried pork with shrimp paste is a highlight. The aromatic paste mixes nicely with herbal notes and deep-fried shallot, while the thick sour curry soup with shrimp has a deep orange colour, tasty acacia omelette and plump shrimps. What about tackling that steep slope? There’s a shuttle service from the car park at the foot of the hill.

Name: Nero Tondo
Description: While you can't count on enjoying the same dish on repeat visits to Nero Tondo, you can count on it being hyper-seasonal and Canadian to the core. Chefs/owners Devon Latté and Lucas Johnston have fashioned a farm-to-table spot where most of the ingredients hail from British Columbia, and the wine list is equally patriotic. These are ingredient-driven dishes, as in a bowl of kohlrabi mixed with caramelized honey and makrut lime nahm jim sauce, or albacore tuna served two ways for a simple but stunning plate. Dessert may include delightful offerings like a wildflower honey gelato or a Basque-inspired cheesecake. The space is small, a mix of counter seats and tables, so reservations are highly recommended.

Name: Nero&Oro
Address: Via del Parco Regina Margherita 45, Naples, 80121, Italy
Description: The dream of a young Neapolitan chef comes to life in an intimate, refined hideaway, tucked among the elegant streets connecting Vomero to the Chiaia waterfront. Here, dishes burst with vivid colors and Mediterranean aromas, accented by contemporary touches that reveal personality and culinary exploration. Two blind tasting menus invite discovery, or guests may opt for a well-balanced à la carte selection of land and sea, where each ingredient shines with clarity, lifted by subtle exotic nuances that awaken the senses. The wine cellar, dominated by Campanian labels, exudes tradition, yet upon request opens to selected wines by the glass, completing an experience that plays on harmony and curiosity.

Name: Ness
Description: In the quiet neighbourhood of Núñez, housed in an inconspicuous corner concrete building (there aren’t even have any signs), Ness presents itself as a rather unique restaurant, ideal for an informal experience and a good time. This original establishment occupies a huge industrial loft with a small bar area and then, behind a curtain, a large space that strives to break down the physical barriers between the kitchen and the dining room. Head chef Leo Lanussol is dedicated almost exclusively to the grill, although the kitchen is equipped with a grill, oven and griddle for a more immersive experience. This obsession with grilled cuisine is evident from the starters to the desserts, with dishes designed for sharing (portions are quite large) and the possibility of ordering half plates. They are very careful when it comes to the ingredients they use, which usually change with the seasons!

Name: Nest
Address: Kamana Lakehouse, 139 Fernhill Road, Fernhill, Queenstown, 9300, New Zealand
Description: The striking bar covered in brushed brass and the sculptural suspended fireplaces catch the eye, but the unobstructed views of the snow-capped mountains and Lake Wakatipu through the floor-to-ceiling windows are truly awe-inspiring. The two menus served at dinnertime showcase a creative take on New Zealand cuisine drawing on seasonal local ingredients. The gin & tonic menu featuring a range of New Zealand spirits is also worth delving into.

Name: Nesta
Description: As you enter the lifestyle boutique, you will notice the snug restaurant at the rear leading into a pretty garden, where, as you sit on the patio, you may even be forgiven for thinking you’re in Italy! Chef Kayes Ghourabi soaks his recipes in Italian sunshine as recognisable Mediterranean aromas and flavours unfold and captivate our tastebuds. Examples include a pedigree vitello tonnato or a breast of duck with a hazelnut crumble and a drizzling of subtle cooking juices. Bang on every time and always open to new twists.

Name: Netsu by Ross Shonhan
Address: Mandarin Oriental Jumeira Hotel, Jumeirah Beach Road, Jumeirah 1, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This Japanese steakhouse delivers a theatrical culinary experience thanks to the large open kitchen which takes centre stage. The cavernous room is light and airy, and menu highlights include dishes cooked over rice straw on the Warayaki grill. Start with the tuna tataki, followed by a Wagyu steak.

Name: Neuwirt
Description: There's something for everyone here! The varied menu features "Neuwirt Classics" such as beef roulade with mashed potatoes, alongside more international options like halibut with peas and grapefruit. Along with the good food, you can look forward to a pleasant setting combining modern and Alpine decoration. The terrace beneath the arcades in front of the building is also inviting. Skilful and charming service. The restaurant is located in the Schwarzer Adler hotel.

Name: Neva Cuisine
Description: The Neva is not only a river in Russia, but also the name of this restaurant, headed by Mexican chef Beatriz González, after stints in top establishments including Lucas Carton and La Grande Cascade. In a friendly, modern Parisian bistro setting, she conjures up modern, multi-facetted cuisine, illustrated by toasted brioche bread with king prawns, smoked avocado and citrus fruit-laced stock, or rack of pork with a parsley-apricot seasoning and a foamy Munster cheese sauce. Everything tastes of something!

Name: New Heights
Address: 2317 Calvert St. NW, Washington, DC, 20008, USA
Description: In contrast to many of the shiny new restaurants that open every year, this Woodley Park veteran under-promises and over-delivers in the best of ways. Coffee-colored carpet, a tame color scheme to match and a quiet crowd do not sound like the makings of a great dinner, but under new management, the restaurant cooks with delicious confidence. The menu covers a lot of ground but does so admirably. Broccolini with black garlic Caesar dressing, crispy fried oysters with pickled cauliflower, and tempura beach mushrooms dusted in a Moroccan spice blend are enough for a meal on their own. Rack of lamb with salsa verde or halibut with coconut broth strike familiar, satisfying chords. For dessert, the pistachio ricotta cake is a sweet finale.

Name: New Mandarin Seafood Restaurant
Description: This boisterous dining hall draws crowds for its highly enjoyable Cantonese fare, while dim sum rules the day and dinner service offers a wide range of specialties. The interior leans elegant with a curved wall of floor-to-ceiling windows, glittering crystal beaded chandeliers and a photo-realistic mural of cherry trees in blossom. However, families and groups looking for good eats and good times keep things grounded.Diners check off their dim sum choices from a printed menu bearing helpful photos for novices, and selections emerge from the kitchen freshly prepared and steaming hot. Some of the hits include black pepper pork biscuits; supple wasabi shrimp dumplings; and steamed hot/sour pork soup dumplings.

Name: New Peking Cuisine
Address: Shop 328-329, 3F, Yintai IN 99, 1199 North Section of Tianfu Avenue, Wuhou, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
Description: The brand is created by a kitchen team from Beijing aims to re-create royal recipes and street food with modern techniques. Some dishes are tweaked to cater to the Sichuanese palate. Try their low-fat Peking duck that is grilled twice to drain excessive fat, yet remarkably, the flesh remains juicy and tender. The Beijingese sugar fritter is fluffy and golden, and a surprising drizzle of balsamic vinegar cuts the richness.

Name: New World Mutton Soup
Address: Bedok Interchange Hawker Centre, #01-23, 208 New Upper Changi Road, 460208, Singapore
Description: The speciality here – mutton soup – is briny-sweet with plenty of umami, and finely shredded ginger to add zing. Other lamb specialities such as rib soup, kway teow, meatballs, lamb tendon and offal are also worth trying.

Name: New York Steakhouse
Address: 2F, JW Marriott Hotel Bangkok, 4 Soi Sukhumvit 2, Khlong Toei, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Located inside the JW Marriott Hotel, this restaurant really lives up to its name. Dark wood furniture, oversized leather chairs and monochrome photos of US cities evoke images of a classic Manhattan steakhouse. A selection of cuts are available – including those from the US, Australia and Japan – and the knowledgeable service team are on hand to help guide your decision. Start with the Caesar salad, tossed tableside with a dressing made from scratch, then finish with the creative and equally theatrical ‘Bomb Alaska’ dessert.

Name: Newport Seafood
Address: 518 W. Las Tunas Dr., San Gabriel, CA, 91776, USA
Description: Chinese, Thai, Cambodian and Vietnamese flavors and cooking styles come together at this seafood-focused San Gabriel Valley restaurant. The menu is comprehensive but don't be overwhelmed, as the helpful wait staff will guide you in the right direction. From seafood-studded chewy rice noodles to salt and pepper crab, seafood is certainly the highlight, but don't overlook other offerings like their deftly cooked beef loc lac. Newport Seafood's portions are generous, so bring a group to sample several dishes.

Name: Next Door
Address: 68 Main Street, Frodsham, WA6 7AU, United Kingdom
Description: A family business has been run on this 17th-century premises for three generations. For many years it was a butcher's shop, the current incarnation of which now sits two doors down, and today Sommelier Vicki has taken on the mantle to run it as this sweet restaurant with her husband Richard. His dishes are founded on excellent quality ingredients, from both specialist suppliers and their own butcher's – like supremely flavoursome Welsh Black beef. Low-ceilinged rooms and exposed beams add to the charm.

Name: Next Door by Imperial
Description: Located directly opposite its parent establishment, Café Imperial, this restaurant boasts an elegant blend of modern and classical aesthetics. In a stylish and invitingly vibrant setting, a highly competent and well-organised team provides attentive service. To the rear of the dining space you can see the chefs crafting classic dishes in the open kitchen: braised beef with a creamy sauce and bread dumplings, or sautéed rabbit kidneys with mustard sauce – the extensive menu has something to offer every palate! Breakfast is also available, and the restaurant remains open continuously throughout the day.

Name: Next2
Description: This restaurant is renowned for its excellent, modern and inviting cuisine. The menu showcases mostly regional ingredients (including meat) that are transformed into delicious recipes – the spinach ravioli with braised beef and blue bufala cheese, and the raw and cooked tuna with burrata, cherry tomatoes and basil are highly recommended. The impressive wine list and selection of cocktails can also be enjoyed as an aperitif or post-dinner drink at the wine bar.

Name: Ngao Kei Ka Lei Chon (1 Rua de Cinco de Outubro)
Address: GF, 1 Rua de Cinco de Outubro, Macau, Macau
Description: Don’t judge a book by its cover because the underwhelming signs outside reflect neither the quality of the food nor the service in this friendly, well-run noodle shop. The key draw is the swimmer crab congee – crabs are dressed on the spot and burst with seafood umami, while the creamy congee is rich in crab roe aromas. Curried beef brisket, noodles tossed in crab roe sauce and springy pan-fried cuttlefish patties are other standouts.

Name: Ngon Garden
Address: 70 Nguyen Du Street, Hai Ba Trung Ward, Hanoi, 112310, Vietnam
Description: On the banks of Thien Quang Lake, this restaurant, reminiscent of an Indochinese-style villa, boasts a patio surrounded by lush greenery. The menu features specialities from all over Vietnam, alongside Asian delicacies of Chinese and Thai origins. From the century-old Bat Dan phở recipe from Hanoi and bún bò huế grilled beef from Nha Trang to fresh veggies from Dalat and live seafood from all over the world, every dish is deftly crafted and delicately seasoned. A favourite in Hanoi, especially for its garden seating, the restaurant is very popular, so advance booking is highly recommended.

Name: Ni Hao
Description: This restaurant with an intimate Eastern feel introduces its guests to “chistro” dishes, a combination of bistro and Chinese cuisine. Chef Chen creates delicious contemporary dishes, which are made to share and which include specialities from Sichuan, Guangdong, Beijing and Wenzhou. An innovative approach to authentic Chinese cuisine.

Name: Nicholson Muir
Address: 480 E. Ocean Ave., Boynton Beach, FL, 33435, USA
Description: Its beachy cottage setting in Boynton Beach might not be the first thing you'd associate with a steakhouse-style menu, but Chef James Muir's gourmet butcher shop and restaurant is exactly that. The menu spans a variety of cuts and sides with salads and starters like wagyu nigiri and empanadas to carpaccio. Prefer to leave the decisions to the chef? Opt for the multicourse meat- forward omakase, or pick and choose from the menu which includes a 16-ounce ribeye given the crosshatch treatment on a woodfire grill. The flavor doesn't disappoint, though a blue cheese crust or one of the sauces adds a flourish. To finish, nothing beats three cookies straight out of the oven in all their gooey glory served alongside a chilled crème anglaise for dipping.

Name: Nico's Bar & Bistro
Description: A modern and dynamic establishment, divided between a cocktail bar area and a bistrot with contemporary, welcoming furnishings. The generous outdoor terrace is ideal for enjoying a pleasantly relaxed atmosphere. The kitchen offers dishes from Croatian and Mediterranean tradition, revisited with a creative and contemporary touch. Not to be missed are the “Štrukli vol. 2”, an original interpretation of a classic local speciality, as well as an inviting selection of desserts for the sweet-toothed.

Name: Nicolin
Address: Via Paisiello 4, località Maggianico, Lecco, 23900, Italy
Description: Restaurant-hotel not far from the centre, but in a quiet, residential area, this is where you can find some of the best cuisine in town. The cook revisits some national dishes in a personal way, with a few seafood offerings as well.

Name: Nicolo Polo
Description: On the waterfront of the Makarska Riviera, facing a charming small beach, you’ll find Marco Polo, a small, refined hotel hosting the Nicolo Polo restaurant. Whether you choose to dine in its cozy Dalmatian stone dining room or outside on the lovely terraces illuminated by moonlight and candles, the food will impress you with its sophistication and technical precision. The prawns are highly recommended, offered in a mix of traditional and more imaginative recipes.

Name: Nicos
Description: Nicos was once a humble stand selling sodas and snacks until one day a customer saw employees eating something delicious and the restaurant was born. The son of the founder now serves as chef, overseeing a tasting menu of classic Mexican cuisine features such standouts as taco de cecina crujiente on a corn tortilla that delivers characteristic intensity. and a flavor-packed, bright dish of camarones al tamarindo. An enchilada stuffed with tasado and beans and bathed in a pixtle sauce from Oaxaca is an aromatic, tasty crowd-pleasing dish, while the aguachile comes with a feisty kick thanks to fiery chili peppers.

Name: Nidaime Izumosoba Dandan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: Izumo soba is a local cuisine of Shimane. The family moved to this location from Shimane and opened this restaurant to introduce the taste of their hometown. Nana Nitta, who took over the restaurant from the father, mills the unpolished buckwheat. This is what gives Izumo soba its blackish colour. The thin juwari soba is served with broth poured over it. Another cultural tradition of Izumo is the three-tiered vermilion-lacquered serving dish called a ‘warigo’.

Name: Nido del Picchio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: This restaurant with a low-key, hushed atmosphere has the feel of a tastefully furnished private home, with an open fire to warm cold winter evenings while a cool, welcoming outdoor terrace becomes the ideal spot for al fresco dining in summer. The dining experience comprises four tasting menus and an extensive à la carte menu, offering a generous variety of dishes designed to delight every palate. The recipes range naturally between meat, fish and vegetarian options, offering a wide and well-balanced array of flavours. The desserts are all well worth trying and our favourites include Tribute to Gauguin, a tonka bean blancmange with passion fruit, mango, papaya and coconut ice cream for an exotic and refined finish. The chef’s wife, Lucy, manages the dining room service with the utmost courtesy and professionalism, contributing to a thoroughly enjoyable overall experience. The wine cellar is home to more than 700 of finest best Italian and international wines, with a curious and interesting emphasis on labels from cooler climes.

Name: Niesztuka
Description: There’s a mysterious, secretive feel to this restaurant tucked away inside a historic house, which sits surrounded by amber jewellers in the heart of the Old Town. Its ground floor has long high-topped tables that lend themselves to communal dining, while the first floor offers a bit more privacy. A concise menu uses excellent daily produce, with a distinct South American influence running through the dishes – from classic ceviche to delicious corn husk ice cream and meringue for dessert.

Name: Nightbird
Address: 330 Gough St., San Francisco, CA, 94102, USA
Description: Located just behind a beautiful wooden door with a carved owl and in a prime Hayes Valley location, Nightbird invites you into its nest with a small and sleek dining room. If you arrive early, don’t miss a delicious craft cocktail at their adjacent bar, Linden Room, as it’s the perfect lead-up to Chef/owner Kim Alter’s multicourse tasting menu. Though the menu changes often to follow the changing seasons, Alter’s presentations are consistently artful (consider the dry-aged squab with cabbage and mole). House-made breads like a crusty farro loaf or fluffy Parker House rolls arrive at separate points of the meal to gild the lily.

Name: Nightingale
Address: 1017 W. Hastings St., Vancouver, V6E 0C4, Canada
Description: A lofty, stylish room and downtown locale attract no shortage of business lunches, but this songbird is also a pitch-perfect fit for relaxed meals among friends. The name references a fable that gives us the proverb “a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush,” and an approachable menu of rustic fare aims to make the most of the season with a bounty of shareable plates. A wood-fired oven leaves its mark on beautifully blistered Neapolitan-style pizzas, while baked sweet potatoes reveal tender interiors with crispy, golden-brown skin and flavorful xo sauce. Desserts like peaches and cream cheesecake or sorbets and ice cream offered by the scoop end the meal on a sweet note.

Name: Nightingale Thai Cuisine & Bar
Description: Having spent years in the bustling metropolis of Bangkok, Dominik and May Carqueville are bringing a slice of the Far East to Dachau. Born and raised in Thailand, the chef has an innate talent for working with authentic Thai flavours. She skilfully incorporates contemporary influences and locally-sourced ingredients into the traditional cuisine of her homeland. Using only the freshest ingredients, she crafts dishes such as Ma Hor (caramelised minced pork with peanuts, pineapple, coriander and chilli) or pan-seared sea bass fillet in a choo chee curry sauce with kaffir lime leaves. Dishes can also be ordered to share. The trendy and chic setting is a combination of restaurant and bar – the latter serves cocktails, beer, wine and house-made soft drinks, as well as finger food. The name "Nightingale" is a nod to Bangkok's vibrant nightlife.

Name: Nightshade Noodle Bar
Description: North of Boston in Lynn, anything goes inside this black box of a restaurant. Risk takers and daredevils, the kitchen under Chef Rachel Miller favors a bold and borderless style that merges and mixes cuisines and seasons everything to the final degree. Where else will you find a custard of uni, brown butter and red curry hollandaise capped with torched cinnamon? Who else is making their own egg noodles and folding in caramelized garlic sauce, chili crisp, shredded beef and chopped peanuts? Whatever you choose, the experience will be anything but boring. A lively playlist and a friendly team further ensure a room in good spirits.

Name: Nigrum
Description: An impressive cross vault, elegant dark tones, designer elements, works of art – these former stables overlooking the city and a stone's throw from the New Castle have been stylishly converted. Drawing on modern influences, a three- to eight-course set menu is served – Beef tartare (classically prepared at the table) is available as an optional extra course. There is also a chic bar for an aperitif or digestif. Tip: You can reach the restaurant from the pedestrian area via the Burgstaffeln steps. There are several car parking spaces in front of the restaurant.

Name: Nihonbashi Kawaguchi
Description: The restaurant is run by a chef trained at Sukiyabashi Jiro and a proprietress from the UK. Keen to share Tokyo’s culinary history, the pair have delved into Edo cuisine to shape their selection of appetisers. True to the chef’s apprenticeship, the nigiri progresses from lighter, more delicate fish to those of greater depth and richness. Three pieces of tuna are followed by gizzard shad, its bright acidity providing a crisp finish. The rice, distinctly seasoned with rice vinegar, is another legacy of the chef’s mentor. Inspired by Nihonbashi, the cradle of Edo food culture, the shop embraces a romantic vision of sushi’s origins.

Name: Nijo Aritsune
Description: Billing itself as ‘a kappo for grown-ups’, Nijo Aritsune maintains a dignified tenor while offering a broad range of à la carte items. While elaborate dishes are the establishment’s forte, familiar friends such as chargrilled chicken meatballs and croquettes are on offer too. In a fresh take on rice topped with raw egg, only the whites of the eggs are whipped. ‘Aritsune’ means ‘changing so that things will not change’. An evolution of Japanese cuisine through a modern sensibility.

Name: Nika Club Omakase
Description: Located in the area known as Palermo Hollywood, on the first floor of a small building, you’ll need to ring the doorbell to gain access. Once upstairs, you'll find a large dining room, a sushi bar, and a second dining area, all featuring an abundance of light-coloured wood. What really sets this Japanese restaurant apart is its focus on healthy dining; it offers gluten-free dishes that are low in sodium, fat, and sugar, and even makes its own soy sauce, buckwheat noodles, and fermented products. Here you'll find classic Japanese dishes, as well as nigiri, sashimi, hand rolls, excellent gyoza, tiraditos, and ceviches, all made with fresh ingredients. They offer two omakase menus, one consisting entirely of items from the sushi bar and the other featuring several cooked dishes as well. We especially liked their delicious Gyu Ramen, with braised beef, homemade noodles, shiitake mushrooms, and ajitama egg, marinated in soy sauce.

Name: Nikaku
Address: GF, W Bangkok, 106 North Sathorn Road, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Valet parking
Description: This Japanese restaurant, originating from Kitakyushu, specialises in authentic Edo-mae sushi. Offering an omakase menu, it serves only 12 diners at a counter, showcasing the chef's skills. Ingredients are delivered every two days, mainly from Fukuoka, ensuring superb quality fish and shellfish, such as fresh uni from Hokkaido. The chef provides detailed seafood explanations, and diners can opt for special tea pairings.

Name: Nikos
Address: 905 W. Main St., Unit 21B, Durham, NC, 27701, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Nikos, named for the owner's father, is set within a restored red-brick tobacco storage warehouse dating to the early 1900s. The interior plays up that rustic industrial heritage and blends it with a simple sophistication, sharing a modern tavern appeal. As for the food, expect all of the Greek and Mediterranean classics, including spanakopita and octopus carpaccio to begin. Come with family or friends to tuck into the meze grand platter, add a glass of crisp Greek wine and you might just be convinced you're basking in the sun on a Greek island. Meanwhile, baklava and honey semolina cake round out the meal.

Name: Nikutoieba Matsuda
Description: The owner-chef, a butcher, prepares wagyu. The set menu meal begins with a bold, hearty meat dish. He uses mostly Yamato beef for his customers to get a feel for Nara ingredients. His creative touches include slicing it thin and pressing it between sheets of kombu and making minced meat into gyoza dumpling. Even the last dish features wagyu, and includes chopped beef and curry. Creative dishes and attractive presentations make this a popular spot.

Name: Nila
Description: Located in the heart of El Sauzal, next to the San Pedro Apóstol church, this pleasant family-run restaurant occupies a property where you’ll find a relaxed ambience, lots of personality and an interior that is striking for its vintage decor (wood, a female mannequin, rock and roll memorabilia, ceramic crockery made by the owners etc) and charming terrace. The à la carte, which usually changes every week, is highly varied and adapts to what is available in the market, so don’t be surprised to find dishes such as amberjack sashimi, sea bass ceviche, squid lasagne, Nilo’s truffled eggs etc on the menu... all designed with sharing in mind.

Name: Nils
Description: Nils is the epitome of a modern restaurant. Tasteful, low - key interior, delightful staff and a talented chef, whose cooking is both creative and refined. The interplay of textures highlights the subtle varying flavours. A night at Carnac Hotel will round off the experience perfectly.

Name: Nina's
Address: 59/1 Mu 6, Thanaratch Road, Nong Nam Daeng, Pak Chong, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30450, Thailand
Description: Nina’s homely restaurant, surrounded by greenery, has two dining areas. The inside is decorated with vintage furniture, chandeliers, standing lamps and a classic clock, while diners in the garden can enjoy nature’s shade. The dishes are well seasoned and many of the vegetables and herbs Nina's uses, such as betel leaves, coriander and basil, are grown on-site. The Thai dishes are tasty and well seasoned, with some uniquely created by the chef. One worth trying is long beans stir-fried with shrimp paste and shrimps.

Name: Nine-Ten
Address: Grande Colonial, 910 Prospect St., La Jolla, CA, 92037, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: There may be no better way to end a day of watching the seals and surf than savoring a plate of Jamaican jerk pork belly at Nine-Ten. Located in the century-old Grande Colonial Hotel, the dining room is more relaxed than grand, populated by beachy sorts who keep their shades on through dinner. During lunch, the menu offers casual fare like sandwiches and salads; the front sidewalk and back area overlooking the pool are excellent spots to tuck in. Those seeking the fullest experience at dinner may opt to put themselves at the “mercy of the chef,” their cheeky way of offering a tasting menu. The pastry program is a highlight, whether it’s freshly baked pastries at brunch or a “creamsicle” dessert with citrus cake, coconut ice cream and orange sherbet.

Name: Nineteen61
Address: 215 E. Main St., Lakeland, FL, 33801, USA
Description: It's fitting that this stylish, contemporary restaurant is located in the heart of Lakeland's downtown, as it's a hive of activity. Maybe it's the rooftop bar or maybe it's the Latin American-inspired menu, but Nineteen61 specializes in a good time. Kick things off on the roof before selecting from their large menu with plenty of Peruvian and Cuban influences. Expect dishes with plenty of spark, like house-made croquetas tucked with jamón serrano and Manchego cheese with guava sauce. Lechón asado served Cuban style offers a hearty portion of slow-roasted pulled pork with house-made mojo sauce with jasmine rice, black beans, yucca and crispy pork belly that is the very definition of comfort food.

Name: Ninive
Address: Emirates Towers Hotel, Sheikh Zayed Road, Dubai
Description: Set in a bustling area of the city, in the midst of grand towers, this charming restaurant exists in another world: a relaxing oasis, a step back in time. The design of this outdoor-only restaurant reflects a Bedouin tent, with rugs and lanterns, low tables and cosy sofas and lush greenery, representative of the ancient Mesopotamian city, Ninawa. Tasty and made-to-share dishes boast flavours from all over the Middle East and North Africa.

Name: Niomon MUI
Description: A counter kappo that is ready to serve whatever takes your fancy. The menu is crammed with the names of dishes and ingredients, and the chefs will adapt each dish to guests’ preferences. To begin, guests enjoy an assortment of appetisers as they select their meals. Ingredients change daily and are prepared simply, whether grilled, simmered or deep-fried. The meal wraps up with a variety of possibilities, including donburi, chazuke and somen noodles in soy-sauce broth. The flexibility of the chefs, who will even make you sushi if you want, is much appreciated.

Name: Nishiazabu Noguchi
Description: Honest Japanese cuisine, overlaid with inspirations from the chef. Keen to ensure everyone’s satisfaction, Nishiazabu Noguchi offers an extensive menu. The delicate broth in soup dishes gets its flavour from kombu. Tsukuri are dressed in salt water flavoured with sudachi to bring out the fragrance of the seafood. For the main event, white rice, takikomi-gohan (rice with a variety of ingredients) and unadon (rice topped with eel) are all served, enhancing satisfaction. Devotion to the spirit of service shines in the generous free rice refills.

Name: Nishiazabu Otake
Description: The chef practises ‘cuisine that lingers in the soul’ that he learned at a ryotei, or traditional high-end Japanese restaurant, in Gifu Prefecture. Croquettes, a perennial favourite, are as seasonal as they are whimsical, stuffed with hair crab in spring and porcini mushrooms in autumn. Char-grilled fare includes meat as well as fish, enhancing satisfaction. Uniquely, Nishiazabu Otake serves game such as winter duck and Asian black bear, sent by hunters in Gifu. Definitely Japanese cuisine, yet free of convention.

Name: Nishideria
Description: The style is ‘Naniwa Italian’, Italian cuisine that highlights the charms of Osaka. Interpreting Italian cooking techniques through Kansai ingredients creates a cuisine found only here. ‘Zeppole alla Osacano’ combines a Neapolitan pastry of deep-fried dough with an Osaka takoyaki. The restaurant works with farmers to grow the vegetables it uses, adopting a food producer’s point of view. For the chef, this attitude is a way of giving something back to the region that raised him.

Name: Nishijin Hashimoto
Description: A baseball fanatic since his youth, behind the counter the chef demonstrates the strength of will he developed on the baseball diamond. His favourite expression, then and now, is ikkyu nyukon: pour your heart and soul into every pitch. To broaden his menu, he prepares sushi and soba himself. The famous gomadofu is paired with pureed soup of vegetables in season. The proprietress’ handmade sweets make diners feel welcome and the couple’s genuine desire to make every customer happy is palpable.

Name: Nitan
Address: 177/38 Mu 6, Si Sunthon Road, Choeng Thale, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
Description: Nitan, or ’determination’ in Thai, may refer to the chef’s aim of creating a real gastronomic experience. This is most evident in the tasting menu and wine pairing, where quality seasonal and local ingredients inform the cooking. Contemporary techniques are used to prepare classic Southern Thai dishes, with well-balanced flavours and a dash of creativity. The restaurant has a warm vibe and is minimally decorated, with wooden furniture and a window into the kitchen.

Name: Nito
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: If you’re looking for a recommendation for a restaurant in which to enjoy excellent Galician fish and seafood, it’s well worth jotting down the name of this eatery inside the Hotel Ego, which has been in the hands of the same family since 1970. It takes its name from the owner, who continues to buy fish such as hake and tuna at the auctions in Celeiro and Burela. Standout out dishes here include “salpicón” of lobster, squid in its own ink, and the tuna roll in season. The modern and attractively laid-out terrace enjoys stunning views of the sea, beach and mountains.

Name: Niu Kitchen
Description: If anybody is going to blast Snoop Dogg over the speakers, it might as well be this restaurant in downtown Miami. With glossy concrete floors, a dark, dim interior and a handful of come-as-you-are servers, it's an effortlessly cool spot. The cooking speaks volumes, designed for groups and based around Spanish tapas. Follow the hype and start with the much-talked-about charbroiled oyster, branded tableside with a hot coal and paired with ponzu and rice vinegar-mayo. Branzino tartare with white garlic cold soup, hearty paellas and other seafood-forward dishes showcase big flavors and quality product enlivened with smart, creative flourishes.For a similar vibe, head next door where the team runs a bar and retail shop focused on natural wines.

Name: Nives
Address: Via Nives 4, Selva di Val Gardena, 39048, Italy
Description: Since December 2023, there has been a new chef at Nives who appeared on Masterchef and has left his work as a project manager to follow his passion for cooking. His cuisine is generous both in the choice of dishes offered (including a few fish options) and in portion sizes. The house specialities include convivial fondues (either Chinese style or made with local cheese) and premium local beef (Tomahawk, T-bone, ribeye, sliced etc). There’s also an interesting choice of wine by the glass.

Name: Niyyali
Address: Shangri-La Jeddah, Ash Shati, Corniche Road, Jeddah, 23611, Saudi Arabia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,No alcohol served,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Accessed via the main entrance of the shimmering Shangri-La Jeddah, with the fabulous terrace being the first thing that grabs your attention on arrival. The space is huge, with great views of the Red Sea. Inside, it’s all set around the central, traditionally styled domed oven, with a few private cabins also available. The menu is extensive, and offers an appealing mix of Lebanese dishes, some traditional, others with a modern makeover alongside numerous signature dishes. The flavours and textures are excellent, especially the kebabs. Bespoke mocktails add to the all-round experience.

Name: Niño Gordo
Description: The popularity of this Asian-style steakhouse, which was opened in 2017 by the owners of La Carnicería, demonstrates the perfect fit between this restaurant and the district of Palermo Soho. An ideal venue for a night out with friends, or a restorative weekend lunch, it is bold, lively and exuberantly decorated – the red hanging lanterns must have featured on thousands of Instagram accounts! It has the feel of traditional Japanese izakaya, especially if you sit at the bar directly in front of the chefs. The ingredients may be Argentinian, but the flavours and techniques are either Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese or Thai. If you were to choose a dish that sums up Niño Gordo it would be the ever-popular Katsusando, made with brioche-style bread instead of shokupan and with beef steak replacing the usual pork. Sweetbreads with miso and choclo (corn) are another original creation, while the spicy fried rice is both vibrant and highly satisfying.

Name: Njord
Description: Make a beeline for the top floor of the amazing ABC edifice and admire the jaw-dropping view over the port and marina below. Luxurious and trendy, the restaurant specialises in ultra-fresh delicacies straight from the local fish auction. Traditional, authentic flavours that respect the character and freshness of the ingredients. Slick service. The seafood platter is also available in individual portions.

Name: Nni Lausta
Address: Via Risorgimento 188, Santa Marina Salina, 98050, Italy
Description: Fish plays the starring role here, where the authentic traditional flavours and ingredients of Aeolian cuisine are skilfully interpreted with a touch of imaginative flair. If it’s not too hot to sit outside, ask for a table on the pleasant, shaded terrace on the first floor.

Name: No Code
Description: Not bound by existing frameworks, setting no limits, embracing a free style and rejecting categorisation: these are the ideas behind No Code. Guided by this philosophy, the cuisine draws on Mexican, French and Japanese influences. The omakase course combines ingredients, techniques and flavours from all three. Through food, established culinary codes are reimagined for today. Part of the pleasure lies in that freedom.

Name: No. Fifty Cheyne
Address: 50 Cheyne Walk, Chelsea, London, SW3 5LR, United Kingdom
Description: It's hard to miss this brightly painted, flower-festooned former pub that looks very much at home in its smart Chelsea location. The indulgent theme carries on inside, with the plush dining spaces set over two floors and featuring brown leather banquettes and yet more flowers. The menu offers hearty, modern British dishes, with fish and meats cooked over the grill a speciality. In true neighbourhood style, they also offer proper roast lunches at weekends, while a cocktail in the rich-hued Ruby Bar adds an extra touch of glamour.

Name: No.10 Nanmen
Address: 10 Nanmen Street, East District, Hsinchu City, Taiwan
Description: This tiny gem decorated with mosaic tiles and dark wood trimming specialises in handmade noodles and dumplings, alongside soy-marinated meats and other side dishes. Everything is fresh and made to order, including the signature wontons in red oil that boast chilli oil infused with five different spices for complex, rounded heat. The springy pork and shrimp filling goes down a treat with the silky wonton skin. It gets extremely busy at mealtimes, so come early.

Name: Noble Gastro House
Description: Noble Gastro House is both inviting and sleek, and a seat at the bar is perfect for watching the kitchen team up close. This is the kind of place where anything goes. Whether you're in the market for a quick bite or a multi-course dinner, you call the shots here! The set menu features a variety of interesting dishes, many of which can be ordered as either half or full portions. Monkfish fillet with an exquisite verjus beurre blanc, or al dente asparagus with morels that have been tossed in veal jus, accompanied by a buttery sauce with the subtle tartness of rhubarb: the familiar and the daring go hand in hand here. Drawing on a wealth of experience, the chefs delight in creating dishes with both high-end and everyday ingredients.

Name: Noble Rice
Address: 615 Channelside Dr., Ste. 112, Tampa, FL, 33602, USA
Description: Restaurants pack this area just off Channelside Drive, but Noble Rice deserves your attention, and not just because it's a sister spot to Koya. Unlike most minimalist Japanese restaurants, this place has a lively, modern vibe. There is an omakase on offer at a separate counter, but the real draw here is their à la carte sushi-focused menu with some izakaya and small plate options (think shrimp toast and karaage; skewers and ramen). Traditionalists should head for the king salmon nigiri sourced from New Zealand, while bold and creative flavor combinations are found in maki like the negi toro roll, with spicy fatty tuna, scallion, tobanjan kewpie in a black garlic soy sauce. Steer seasonal, as in the bright Dungeness crab salad.

Name: Noble Rot
Address: 51 Lamb’s Conduit Street, Bloomsbury, London, WC1N 3NB, United Kingdom
Description: With its dark, rough-lacquered wood and tiny candles, there is something pleasingly intimate about this wine bar and restaurant, where the walls are adorned with covers of the owners' Noble Rot magazine. This really is an oenophile's paradise, with the enthusiastic, clued-up team happy to suggest a smart, sometimes surprising, pairing to go with your meal. The cooking itself is decidedly classical, unfussy and more than a little French. The braised turbot with vin jaune sauce epitomises this spirit, which comes in tandem with gutsy, satisfying flavours.

Name: Nobu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The location is a huge draw at what is the largest branch of this globally recognised restaurant brand. Part of the Four Seasons Hotel, this Nobu sits in a stunning futuristic building surrounded by water, located at the end of a narrow peninsula, and offers impressive views of the Corniche promenade. Choose from a wide range of Japanese dishes, with South American influences adding a lovely twist. An open kitchen, stylish bar and cool music ensure a chic atmosphere accompanies the food.

Name: Nobu Budapest
Address: Kempinski Hotel Corvinus Budapest, Erzsébet tér 7-8, Budapest, 1051, Hungary
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Wheelchair access
Description: Wherever you hail from, there’s a high chance you’ll have heard of Nobu, as the group’s restaurants now span the globe. At the Budapest branch – which sits inside a chic hotel – you’ll find a stylish, minimalist aesthetic that takes in wooden tables, fretwork screens and Japanese lanterns. The extensive menu follows the usual Nobu format, with a wide range of sushi and both hot and cold Nobu classics (such as miso black cod or yellowtail tartare with caviar), and there’s also a section dedicated to Wagyu beef. Bento boxes are available at lunch and there’s an omakase on offer for the undecided.

Name: Nobu Dubai
