Description: Chef Gilles Joye and Heike, front of house, have converted the Marcus restaurant into a gastrobar: OYA. The interior has been treated to an exuberant makeover, without forgetting a lovely alfresco area. The varied à la carte and lunchtime menus unveil patriotic Belgian family favourites and Mediterranean-themed sides. A few examples: crushed carabineros prawns with grapefruit and crunchy croutons, hanger steak, cooked rare, with a shallot sauce and fresh mayonnaise, or a succulent pasta and seafood extravaganza. Chef Joye cherry-picks premium produce and makes ample use of a Mibrasa charcoal oven. A culinary patchwork packed in heroic flavours and subtle nuances.

Name: Oak
Address: 2 North Parade Passage, Bath, BA1 1NX, United Kingdom
Description: An eco-conscious ethos is the guiding light for this unpretentious bistro and its original vegetarian and vegan dishes. When dining in the front part of the restaurant, you'll find shelves adorned with ingredients from their allotment just outside the city – which provides around 40% of their produce. The well-priced small plates are designed for sharing, with the kitchen's knack for using complementary flavours and textures on show in the likes of Jerusalem artichoke with ajo blanco and apple & shallot vinaigrette. A five-course ‘feasting menu’ is available at dinner if you're feeling indecisive and/or hungry.

Name: Oak & Smoke
Address: GF, Pacquiao Mansion, 324 H.V. Dela Costa,, Makati - Metro Manila, 1227, The Philippines
Description: This inviting neighbourhood eatery centres on binchotan-grilled meats, with beef from Japan, Australia and the USA taking the lead. Vibrant skewers, prawn toast, croquettes and dumplings show global flair and Asian influences. There's generosity in both flavours and portions, but also flexibility. Drop by for cocktails and small plates or settle in for a full celebratory feast. The friendly team are happy to guide you through the menu.

Name: Oak Prime
Address: 4210 River Oaks Dr., Myrtle Beach, SC, 29579, USA
Description: You might come to Oak Prime for its full-service bar, its relaxed sophistication or even its friendly service, but the real reason to make a reservation here is their angus beef grilled with a Pittsburgh-style charred crust. Of course, other items delight too, including appetizers like sautéed wild mushroom bruschetta drizzled with ten-year-aged balsamic vinegar. High-quality steak, expertly seasoned and properly cooked, is naturally the highlight; an angus ribeye is even better with smoked tomato and Madeira butter. Dessert comes in the form of a baked-to-order blueberry bread pudding with lemon sauce and a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

Name: Oak Room
Address: The Abu Dhabi EDITION Hotel, Al Bateen Marina, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Dressed like a smart London club, all wood and leather – but with the music turned up loud – Oak Room is all about meat. Steaks, largely from Japan and Australia, come in various cuts and are accompanied by an impressive selection of sides; don’t miss the triple cooked chips. Sunday roasts are popular and there’s a wide variety of other dishes on offer too, from fish and chips to burgers.

Name: Oak at Fourteenth
Description: Smack dab in the heart of charming downtown Boulder, Oak at Fourteenth invites guests to settle in to a space where light wood floors, white walls and a minimalist design aesthetic set a modern tone. The kitchen echoes the contemporary mindset with a hearty menu focused on meat, but with equal care shown to vegetarian dishes. To begin, a vibrant disc of beet tartare is served with mustard ice cream and a beet-colored rice cracker for a dramatic start. Rotisserie chicken with a green apple and celery root slaw is a go-to, but save room for a slice of their peanut butter tart. With its thick cookie crust, thin layer of cherry gelee and a quenelle of celery sorbet balanced on chopped peanuts, it's a nod to that childhood classic: ants on a log.

Name: Oak-107
Description: Guided by the motto "Smoke. Grill. Fine Dine", this restaurant serves top-grade beef cuts from around the world, including Kobe beef and Miyazaki Wagyu from Japan – you decide on the sides, toppings and sauces to accompany your steak. They use a Dallas smoker at 107°C and oak wood – hence the name "oak-107". The menu also features house specialities such as sturgeon with miso beurre blanc or grilled courgette. Those who prefer a set menu can choose between the "Tasting Menu" and the "Steak Menu". The attractive interior has a modern, urban feel – you can even dine at the bar. In good weather, you can eat out on the terrace. Tip: easily accessible by car via Windmühlengasse multi-storey car park (exit Mariahilfer Straße, third floor).

Name: Oan Tafel
Description: Geert-Jan Vaartjes embraces the Dutch Cuisine philosophy by sourcing 80% of his ingredients from within the Netherlands. In this natural, somewhat rugged restaurant with its welcoming dining counter, the chef showcases local produce with subtle international accents and a penchant for zesty notes. The cauliflower transformed by an Asian-style marinade and a tangy sauerkraut beurre blanc is a highlight. The surprise menu lives up to its name every time. Consider extending your stay by booking one of the Oan Tafel Suites.

Name: Oar
Address: Toomullin, Roadford, Doolin, V95 KV02, Ireland
Description: In the rural heart of The Burren, with views out towards the Cliffs of Moher, you’ll find this well-frequented restaurant with a clean, modern interior. The menu offers an appealing choice of dishes crafted using top-notch produce, which is treated with care and skill by the kitchen team. A few ambitious, adventurous flavour combinations might appear too, like mango with salmon. The friendly service and simply furnished bedrooms complete a rather charming picture.

Name: Oarsman
Address: Bridge Street, Carrick-on-Shannon, N41 AK19, Ireland
Description: This traditional family-run pub sits close to the river and is filled with pottery, bygone artefacts, fishing tackle and, of course, plenty of locals. Service is chatty, there’s a lovely deli, and they even have a lager brewed specifically for them. Flavoursome cooking uses local produce, with the fish dishes being a sure-fire hit, and all of the bread is home baked. The upstairs restaurant opens later in the week.

Name: Oasi
Description: Over the years, the beach establishment has gradually developed: the beach and bar remain, but today's pride is the restaurant. The husband and wife divide their duties between the kitchen and dining area (including wine). They've built a good reputation thanks to classic seafood cuisine, highlighted by the chef's personal creative touches. A passionate and imaginative self-taught chef, his steamed oyster seasoned with lemon zest on tomato water is a particularly tasty shot that represents their style.

Name: Obelisk
Address: 2029 P St. NW, Washington, DC, 20036, USA
Description: Obelisk attracts a surprisingly young, casual crowd for a spot that has been serving a fixed five-course menu five nights a week since 1987. It's likely due to the restaurant’s warm, neighborhood feel. The light and seasonal Italian cooking begins with a bang, as an assortment of fantastic antipasti is quickly ushered to the table: perhaps creamy burrata imported from Lazio or a hot croquette filled with melting cheese. Dishes are never fussy and are presented simply, with honest flavors and purposeful ingredients. Entrées might include a dorade with a cracker-crisp sear, served with nutty romesco sauce and green chickpeas. All breads and desserts are made in-house. Don't expect to dash in; the full experience is worth the two to three hours.

Name: Obere Mühle
Description: From the outside, the carefully restored centuries-old farmhouse is really inviting; inside, wonderfully quaint rooms featuring rustic wood panelling ooze regional charm. The cuisine, too, is rooted in the Allgäu region, but with the occasional foray into the Mediterranean. The menu ranges from offal to various meats cooked on the charcoal grill, from locally farmed fresh fish to pasta and delicious desserts. Their commitment is plain to see, not least in the quality and provenance of the ingredients. In addition to the appealing à la carte selection, there is also a daily menu. The food is accompanied by good wines. Friendly, attentive service ensures a pleasant, family atmosphere. The restaurant also has its own organic cheese dairy. Tip: Bad Hindelang's local history museum is located here, too. Overnight guests staying in the holiday apartments enjoy access to the wellness area.

Name: Oberer Mönchhof
Description: The dining rooms in this lovely, centuries-old half-timbered building are tastefully and comfortably furnished. Outside a fabulous terrace is laid out under chestnut trees overlooking the lake. The cuisine is seasonal, traditional and international with an additional tasting menu on offer at lunchtime and in the evenings.

Name: Oberlechner
Description: From Merano you climb to an altitude of 1 000m to this restaurant, which boasts breathtaking views of the town and surrounding mountains. The menu here focuses mainly on local ingredients which are carefully prepared without too many creative twists, resulting in delicious and generous dishes such as braised beef with a Lagrein sauce (accompanied by rice and vegetables). All the attractive guestrooms have a balcony and the same stunning view.

Name: Oberländer Weinstube
Description: This townhouse, built in 1826, is full of charm: inside you sit in a cosy, traditional wood-panelled decor, while the charming courtyard beckons outside. And in addition they take really friendly care of you. The kitchen turns out dishes that are adapted to the seasons and really tasty. At lunchtime you choose from a smaller menu.

Name: Oberraindlhof
Description: The family that run this restaurant occupying an old farmhouse with origins dating back to the 16C has a relationship with the region that goes back decades. In later years, the farm became an inn and it has now been run by the same family for five generations, all motivated by a desire to introduce their guests to the best local recipes and ingredients. Dishes include excellent fresh ravioli stuffed with cheese produced in the nearby valley and served (in summer) with tomato and basil sauce. An excellent wine list and the hotel’s warm and friendly ambience add to the appeal.

Name: Oberwirt
Description: The various Stube-style dining rooms in the Oberwirt hotel restaurant have a typical Tyrolean ambience, while the cuisine is decidedly traditional with its focus on seasonal and regional ingredients, although a few fish options also always feature on the menu. Wine-enthusiasts will be delighted with the excellent wine selection.

Name: Oberża 86
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Tucked away amongst some more utilitarian buildings, sits this pretty red-brick cottage with a cobbled terrace out front. With a long history that includes stints as a shop, a shoemaker’s and a museum, it now feels like a perfect fit for this cosy, welcoming restaurant. Seasonal Polish produce is the bedrock of the cooking, which is allowed to shine with a lightness of touch and a French flourish, showcased in technically adept elements like a piquant butter sauce accompanying the sea trout.

Name: Obélix
Address: 700 N. Sedgwick St., Chicago, IL, 60654, USA
Description: French bistros are hardly known for restraint, but this River North arrival takes lavishness to another level entirely. On a quiet corner, duck and foie gras run up and down a menu that draws on hearty French classics spanning from pâté en croûte to steak frites to duck tourtière. Far from rote, everything is made in-house and executed with refreshing clarity. The boisterous, sun-soaked dining room is a sign of equally happy guests, all of whom happily rise to the occasion as escargot and bottles of wine grace tables with unusual regularity. If stopping by for brunch, do not expect light fare (beef Wellington, anyone?), while lunch offers a particularly good value. Do save room for dessert. House-made ice creams and excellent, warm pastries await at the finish line.

Name: Ocean
Address: Le Mont de la Pulente, La Pulente, JE3 8HE, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Ocean is a fitting name for this restaurant perched above St Ouen’s Bay. Its crisply laid, bright white dining room and shuttered windows certainly give it a nautical feel, backed up by stunning views across the grounds to the rolling waves. Island produce leads the way, with the likes of black butter, local fish and top-notch oysters featuring in dishes such as Jersey butter-roasted cod with sweetcorn and smoked eel. Desserts are a highlight and if the bavarois with strawberries is on the menu, be sure to choose it. Service is cheery and, as it's set within a hotel, luxuriously appointed bedrooms also await.

Name: Oceans
Address: 233 Park Ave. S., New York, NY, 10003, USA
Description: Park Avenue South may be brimming with restaurants—from expense account beauties to the massively trendy—but this dining room will stop you in your tracks. First with its looks (imagine an inviting bar that anchors the room up front, while the back is crowned by a raw bar and sushi counter); and then with its enticing cooking.If the glistening items on ice didn't give you the hint, seafood reigns, with local plus global sourcing and preparations ranging from ceviche and sushi to towering platters and delicious entrées. Toro tartare with caviar is a particular highlight, as is the East-meets-West Alaskan black cod with a sake glaze, braised bok choy, mushroom and yuzu dashi. Buttermilk panna cotta with cranberry mousse is a great way to wrap things up.

Name: Ochre
Address: The National Gallery, Trafalgar Square, St James’s, London, WC2N 5DN, United Kingdom
Description: Situated on the ground floor of The National Gallery's iconic William Wilkins building, this smart, comfortable bistro de-luxe is revolutionising museum dining. The all-day menus offer something for everyone, from a wallet-friendly 'prix fixe' to brunch and afternoon tea. The central dinner à la carte can be ordered in a standard three-course format, or as small and large plates to share. Running throughout are vivid flavours and international touches from schnitzel to korma. You'll get a lovely welcome from the team, who are serious about what they do and run their restaurant well.

Name: Ochsen
Description: Located just metres from the monastery, the venerable Ochsen dates back to 1596. In its current iteration with an avant-garde look, it is part of the three-building Hotel Caspar, which has stylishly designed guestrooms. In the open kitchen, regional ingredients go into modern and creative cooking – interesting cuisine that is "close to nature", with fire, aromatic woods, smoked and grilled dishes play a central role.

Name: Ocre
Address: Carrer de Can Ferrereta 12, Santanyí, 07650, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Inside the charming Hotel Can Ferrereta (awarded two MICHELIN Keys) sits Ocre, a restaurant which tastefully combines Mallorcan aesthetics with a contemporary rustic design. In summer, the experience moves to the Mallorcan patio, an ideal place to enjoy a romantic evening under the stars. The Mediterranean-inspired cuisine is based on honest cooking that respects the ingredients. The chefs at the helm, Àlvar Albaladejo and Tamara Lumbreras, strive to highlight the quality of the seasonal ingredients, meticulously selected from the best local suppliers, in each dish. Coinciding with the Santanyí weekly market, on Saturdays a special lunchtime menu (Menú de mercado) is dedicated to ingredients puchased there.

Name: Octavia
Address: 1701 Octavia St., San Francisco, CA, 94109, USA
Description: Tucked among the Victorians that line its picture-perfect street in Lower Pac Heights, locals count themselves lucky to claim this charming, elegant dame as their neighborhood spot—though they may still need to plan ahead to score a table.Chef/owner Melissa Perello's signature brand of simple-yet-elevated cooking shows creative touches while celebrating excellent local ingredients. A meal might progress from impeccably crispy fried artichokes to silky hand-made fettucine with morels, followed by juicy quail with grapefruit and spinach, each showcasing spectacular local products in their best light. Don’t skip the baked goods: house-made levain is excellent, as are seasonal desserts like a bay leaf panna cotta with rhubarb granita and tarragon crumble.

Name: Octo
Address: 1 E. 33rd St., New York, NY, 10016, USA
Description: They may be behind New York's oldest Korean barbecue restaurant, but Steve and Christina Jang aren't resting on any laurels. Chef Segeun Song leads the charge on the à la carte menu that channels a distinctive Korean-Chinese fusion cuisine. A tempting array of dishes includes noodles, rice, and lunch specials. Reserve ahead for their Peking black duck or tuck into signature dishes like beef tangsuyuk or cumin pork back ribs. Of course, one glance at the special dumpling workshop and it's clear they must be ordered. Pork and Thai chili soup dumplings with a dot of caviar are one way to go, but there's also the delicious spicy poached dumplings in a black vinegar sauce.

Name: Octo
Description: Start with crispy golden deep-fried fish fingers flanked by fresh tartare sauce or crunchy bone marrow, before continuing with a patriotic Belgian lineup of the likes of eels in sorrel or cod poached in butter and shrimps, to finish with an iconic dame blanche (ice cream and hot chocolate sauce). A relaxed, bouncy vibe sets the scene overlooking the pretty market square of Aalbeke. The youthful chef reveals an obsession with quality as he adds a novel twist to family favourites. The wine list, which is a treasure trove of sensibly priced gems, further adds to the establishment’s appeal.

Name: Octopus
Description: Claude and Sylvie bend over backwards to pamper guests in their seafood eatery near the seawall. Sylvie’s warm welcome and service are framed by distinctive artwork (of octopi), while Claude sensitively adds a new spin to a classical repertory, all of which in a playful vein. Grilled pork fritters, pedigree vol-au-vent, fish from the North Sea (his passion) or rice pudding with strawberries: it is always a pleasure to return to the Octopus.

Name: Octopus Garden
Description: Decades in, and Octopus Garden is still going strong. There is a reason why it's still difficult to score a reservation at this quirky charmer: quality fish at a very palatable price. The namesake cephalopod decorates every nook and cranny, but kitsch aside, it's a welcoming place that makes regulars out of first-timers. Guests feast well on supremely fresh fish, and specials, like jellyfish strips tossed in garlic ponzu and peanut tofu with brown sugar, are attention-worthy. Maki can stray from tradition, as in the lobster roll on vacation, a roll with tempura Canadian lobster and creamy avocado. Nigiri, whether it's moist saba or crunchy-delicious spot prawn, are ever-changing but always spot on. There is an impressive collection of premium spirits and sake to boot.

Name: Ode
Description: Get ready for an ode to Friesland rooted in Dutch Cuisine principles – typically 80% plant-based and 20% animal-based. A fully open kitchen with marble worktops forms the centrepiece of the elegant black-and-white interior. On this culinary stage, Liudger van der Meer and team give free rein to their creativity. A penchant for fermented flavours meets the odd international influence and meticulous preparation. An array of asparagus textures – including a vinaigrette made from the vegetable blended with pine nuts oil – pair beautifully with an eel fillet, an asparagus tube filled with a crayfish farce, saffron and marinated stem lettuce. This is a playful ode to the riches of the local terroir, presented in a compelling multi-course set menu. Take the opportunity to get to know this tranquil gem of a city better by booking one of the lovely guestrooms.

Name: Odette
Description: Two steps from Les Halles, in the luxurious Albar Hotel, the Rostang family demonstrates that they haven’t lost their touch in this urban inn. Odette regales us with succulent dishes to be shared: seabass in a pastry crust, one of the house signatures, veal cutlets, roast guinea fowl. Her score is spot on and dotted with fanciful notes, like veal belly paired with Gala apples or lightly seared scallops with parsnip and cashew nuts. The addictive desserts are to die for, illustrated by a hazelnut and pistachio millefeuille sprinkled with confit of orange zest.

Name: Odette en Ville
Description: Odette is a well-known eatery of the trendy Châtelain neighbourhood. The stylish 1920’s townhouse aims to combine British style, Parisian sensuality and New York glamour. The highly varied menu is equally fascinating: both classical and international, with an accent on the ingredient. Crunchy nems in a spicy sauce, al dente taglioni in lemon with pink shrimps, scallops and foie gras in a duck stock: a festival for fine food lovers. And why not treat yourself to one of the swish designer-inspired guestrooms to finish your evening in the lap of luxury?

Name: Odo East Village
Address: 536 E. 5th St., New York, NY, 10009, USA
Description: From the team behind Odo comes an izakaya that is casual in concept but serious in execution. A handful of bar seats overlook a minuscule kitchen that’s constantly in motion. The space is cozy, nothing more than a rustic wood counter and exposed red brick. The menu, meanwhile, offers an assortment of light starters and sashimi, grilled fish and wagyu, and other specialties that are fried, simmered or served over rice. This is food to be shared, and past highlights include charcoal-kissed mackerel with ponzu as well as dashi egg with rice, Hokkaido uni and seaweed. Best suited for couples, the experience is leisurely and intentional.

Name: Odoloste
Description: A restaurant located just a few steps from the Guggenheim Bilbao with a meticulous contemporary ambience and a menu where the pig takes centre stage – there’s even a fun image of a pig (with the name of the restaurant tattooed on it) drinking at a bar! The cooking here, an updated take on Galician cuisine, is fully focused around pork and pork-based dishes with two full-table tasting menus: Txerri (à la carte menu where the starters are proposed by txerri-txef, Igor Aguirre, while the main course and dessert are chosen by the diner) and Odoloste (more complete, with 11 courses).

Name: Oechsle
Description: Serving flavoursome dishes made from fresh, high-quality ingredients in a pleasant contemporary atmosphere, this restaurant on the corner is a real gem. Its short menu draws on both Mediterranean and classical influences. This place also doubles as a wine bar, so you can look forward to a well-curated wine list. Experienced and charming waitstaff provide great service with a personal touch. In summer, the tables out front, facing the street, are in high demand.

Name: Oegojip Seolleongtang
Description: Oegojip Seolleongtang, which means headstrong seollongtang in Korean, prides itself on the deep, full-bodied flavor. Made exclusively from 1++ grade hanwoo beef, the broth is rich yet clean, and the suyuk melts in your mouth. The dogani, is meticulously prepared for an exceptionally chewy texture and clean flavor, and the tender hanwoo suyuk topped with a mound of shredded green onion is a signature dish. The owner, who inherited his mother-in-law’s recipe and refined it with his own expertise.

Name: Oesterbeurs
Description: Lobster, oysters, sea lavender and mussels are just some of the Zeeland delicacies served in this restaurant which is decorated in warmly gilded tones. More than 80% of the dishes served here are fish based, with a richly flavoured classic bouillabaisse featuring on the menu alongside more creative fare. A true ode to Zeeland.

Name: Oesterput 14
Description: The oyster beds and the Eastern Scheldt are almost literally at your feet here. Inside this bright, modern restaurant, large windows afford wonderful views of the surrounding waters, setting the scene for a menu dedicated to the rich bounty of the North Sea and the Eastern Scheldt. The razor clams stewed in a fragrant green curry infused with lemongrass and ginger exemplify how international influences can add depth. The classic European lobster, cooked to order and accompanied by house-made mayonnaise and crispy fries, is equally impressive. A seafood platter is another tempting option. Zeeland's briny terroir speaks for itself here.

Name: Offbeat
Address: 2F, The Shops at Ayala Triangle Gardens, Makati Avenue, Makati - Metro Manila, 1224, The Philippines
Description: At Offbeat, nostalgia meets inventiveness in a vibrant space with red walls, blue accents and a lively open kitchen. Duo chefs rework traditional Filipino recipes with playful flair, resulting in an innovative spin on familiar favourites. Here, the monghe – deep-fried pork and cheese patties with banana ketchup – is a fresh and refined take on a dish with street food roots; the piaparan fish is inspired by Maranao cuisine.

Name: Ogata
Description: Ogata, a temple dedicated to Japanese art de vivre, is located in a private mansion in the Marais and masterminded by Shinichiro Ogata, world-famous designer and connoisseur. The (mainly) traditional Japanese food sports an omakase spirit, through a tasting menu comprised of immaculate seasonal produce (first-class sashimi). The best seats are at the counter. Pop into the shop or art gallery on your way out…

Name: Ogień i Sól
Description: Set in the striking regenerated Geyer Gardens district, this former factory has retained an on-trend industrial edge to its interiors, with the exposed red-brick walls and open kitchen catching the eye. Steaks are at the heart of the menu, cooked over charcoal either on or off the bone and served with a choice of sauces. The quality of the dry-aged meat provides plenty of flavour, with some wagyu options available if you’re looking to celebrate in style.

Name: Ogof
Address: 11 Kings Road, Pontcanna, Cardiff, CF11 9BZ, United Kingdom
Description: If you enjoy a natural wine or two and honest, no-fuss cooking, then this keenly run neighbourhood bistro is for you. Weekday lunches spotlight freshly made sandwiches, before things ramp up a gear in the evenings and on weekends, with a blackboard of enticing dishes built around high-quality vegetables. There’s a hearty, pared-back approach throughout, as with the Salt Marsh lamb accompanied by chard, nettles and a perfectly braised carrot. The wines on tap offers great value for money and the lesser-known choices are curated with great enthusiasm.

Name: OiO
Description: The pasta is prepared last minute, stuffed with a powerful ossobuco and then coated in a velvety parmesan and gremolata sauce. All the ingredients on the menu are as fresh as the homemade pasta. This fantastic Mediterranean osteria which boasts an exquisite riverside terrace on the banks of the Alzette, invites you to an Italian feast of great delicacy. Don’t miss the Negroni or the dessert trolley!

Name: Oii
Address: Al Qana Marina South, Al Maqta’ Street, Abu Dhabi
Description: Meaning ‘hi’ in Portuguese, Oii is located in Al Qana Marina, next to The National Aquarium. On the inside, this relaxed and casual spot is light and airy, thanks to its floor to ceiling windows, while the outside’s spacious, shaded terrace is ideal al fresco dining. Expect a wide-ranging breakfast menu, followed by a Mediterranean-inspired selection of smaller and larger colourful plates, snacks and salads. One way to start your meal is with a grilled octopus with vibrant mojo rojo, followed by the spiced peri peri baby chicken and finish with fruity passion fruit semi freddo.

Name: Oiseau - Oiseau
Description: Sven Chartier and his wife Marianne have built their new nest in this tiny Perche village, opposite a church several centuries old. Far from the madding crowd, the chef is flourishing in this country chic setting, pampering diners with wholesome fare that respects tradition: scallops, almond milk, cauliflower and citron; crispy chuck steak. Culinary precision meets comfort food…

Name: Ojo
Address: 76F, The Standard Bangkok Mahanakhon, 114 Narathiwas Road, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: Offering breathtaking views over the Bangkok cityscape, Ojo has the honour of being Thailand’s highest restaurant. Glamorous pink and gold décor adds to the appeal of a truly special location in which to dine, while the authentic Mexican cooking means this restaurant is far more than just its setting. The menu of attractive dishes includes tender cochinillo and a selection of raw seafood. Ask for a table by the window or on the terrace to make the most of the view.

Name: Okeya Kyujiro Montréal
Address: 1227 rue de la Montagne, Montréal, H3G 1Z2, Canada
Description: There is a distinct theatricality to this unique omakase experience, with a curtain lifting to the strains of dramatic music to reveal the kitchen! The seafood-centric menu features over 20 small dishes, including nigiri, tempura, and ramen, illustrating various Japanese techniques and ingredients. The creations and appetizers come thick and fast: the dishes progress from silky chawanmushi with delicately cooked trumpet fish, alternating with skillfully assembled nigiri, made with fish ranging from little-known usubahagi to premium classics such as otoro and uni from Hokkaido.

Name: Okeya Kyujiro Toronto
Description: Even for the most seasoned sushi aficionados, this counter offers a playful, high-energy experience that’s bound to surprise. With branches in Vancouver and Montreal, the restaurant delivers nigiri, tempura, and broths in rollercoaster fashion. Drums playing overhead raise the temperature of the room, just as chefs show off whole cuts of fish, some of which are broken down and sliced right at the counter for all to see. The room is a constant swirl of motion, everyone busy grilling, frying, and slicing, as courses arrive at a steady pace. Recent highlights include kelp-cured botan ebi with caviar, grilled unagi with sancho pepper, and a pressed roll of mackerel. Such theatrical cooking comes at a notable price tag, but the experience is one to remember.

Name: Okio
Description: Located just a few minutes from a number of the city’s main tourist attractions, this charming corner restaurant is perfect for a drink and a pleasant meal after a day's sightseeing. Here, chef Panagiotis Giakalis, ably supported by right-hand man George Tsolkas, creates contemporary Mediterranean cuisine with a strong hint of Asia, resulting in carefully balanced dishes and unexpected textures. Prepared using seasonal ingredients, dishes can be enjoyed via the à la carte and two tasting menus, and include perfectly prepared dishes such as bonito tuna with almonds, watercress, maple and sweet chilli sauce. In addition to the charming lounge space, you can also enjoy the relaxed atmosphere of a table on the terrace. The private space upstairs can also be booked for larger groups.

Name: Okovita
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Run by the same team as Naama in the city centre, this suburban spot has a stylishly modern feel, while its voile curtains dividing the tables add an intimate air. The house-made sourdough gets the meal off to a great start, before the carefully conceived and skilfully executed dishes such as butterflied trout with braised cabbage and tomatoes. Add in the warm, friendly service and you have all the ingredients of a perfect neighbourhood haunt.

Name: Okra FoodBar
Address: 2 Le Van Mien Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 71300, Vietnam
Description: In its new location and managed by a youthful, energetic team, Okra retains its cosy charm. The stylish bar facing an open kitchen is lined with counter seating for an immersive and relaxed dining experience. The chef crafts an unconventional menu from locally sourced ingredients, blending modern and traditional techniques inspired by chargrill and street food. Generous portions and a great selection of wines and cocktails make it a popular spot for relaxing.

Name: Okra İstanbul
Address: Osmanlı Sokak No:1/B, Taksim, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34433, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets not allowed,Valet parking
Description: Take the lift up to the 20th floor of The Marmara Taksim Hotel and absorb the scene for a moment. Okra's expansive windows afford breathtaking panoramic views of the Bosphorus and cityscape beyond. Treat yourself to a crisp cocktail and browse through the wine list, which features some outstanding Turkish labels. The chef delights his diners with exceptionally fresh fish from the local market, often cooking it over an open fire. His silky manti, for instance, are filled with succulent meat and served with a tomato and bell pepper sauce and yoghurt. And then there is the seafood platter, brimming with salty goodness… As you might have guessed, reservations are essential at this coveted destination.

Name: Oktobre
Description: In one of the most scholarly streets of the intellectual St André des Arts neighbourhood, Oktobre is warm and welcoming like an Indian summer. The chef's larder is stocked with premium, painstakingly sourced produce. His enthusiastic, creative approach to cooking involves varied spices and multiple Asian accents. Examples: linguine of cuttlefish, tomato and peanut pesto; line-fished pollock from St Gilles Croix de Vie, cranberry beans, miso-spiked beurre blanc and rhubarb; shoulder of pork, sweetcorn curry and fig seasoning; caramelised apple, almond praliné, herby cider sorbet and buckwheat. Buzzy, friendly vibe.

Name: Oktopussy
Description: At the restaurant of the New Wave hotel, the food is down-to-earth and delicious, and, while it revolves around the region, it also reveals international twists. On the à la carte menu, one dish that reflects the kitchen's characteristically harmonious flavour combinations is "octopus cooked sous-vide, aioli, olives, house-baked bread". There is also a selection specifically for children. The sleek, modern interior with a maritime feel, an open kitchen and a custom-built table for larger groups, is appealing. Service is cordial and laid-back. In summer, make a beeline for the secluded courtyard terrace. From May, the rooftop bar is open for delicious cocktails in a relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Oku
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only - lunch,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: The owner-chef opened a counter restaurant specialising in unagi after studying Japanese cuisine. The theme is ‘unagi and sake’, so the fare consists of the unagi set menu only. The menu uses fresh vegetables to impart seasonal moods. Ingredients are boiled, fried or straw-smoked for a unique sensibility. Unagi on rice brings the meal to a close, delighting the palate with rice freshly steamed in clay pots. The owner-chef’s experience also shines in the endless variety of vessels.

Name: Okuniya Mambei
Description: The chef opened Okuniya Mambei as the third-generation owner-chef of a river-fish restaurant in Nishiki Market. He realised his dream with the help of architects, calligraphers and potters. Décor of rustic simplicity, bold and vigorous calligraphy and tricolour earthenware pots exude a unique personality. The menu consists only of large kabayaki on rice. Eel is grilled with the fat intact and served with rice freshly cooked in an earthenware pot. In true Kyoto style, the leftover rice is topped with eel tsukudani (a preserve using sweetened soy sauce) and hojicha (roasted green tea) is poured over it.

Name: Old Boy
Description: Old Boy is the epitome of smoky, flame-licked Southeast Asian vibes, but with Belgian ingredients from local producers of the likes of Le Monde des Mille Couleurs and Dierendonck. The result is sparkling, lively fusion cuisine that spans Bangkok, Thailand and China, embodied by thrilling, fire-driven street food and carefully-calibrated spices. A grilled duck breast acquires a whole new dimension courtesy of green curry sauce, coconut milk, and Thai basil. The interior is cool, hip and packed with buzzy vibrancy. A refreshing trendy interior, a spot-on natural wine list and a mouth-watering menu. Book ahead for dinner — it is often packed to the seams.

Name: Old Cellar Bled
Description: Ideal for a summer lunch on the terrace, or inside during the evocative winter days when the lake, still and veiled in a light mist, creates an atmosphere of great enchantment. The welcoming interiors, distributed across several rooms, afford comfortable views of the lake’s beauty at every turn. The kitchen specialises above all in freshwater dishes, such as trout salad with potatoes or a flavourful fish soup. Among the main courses, the duck breast from the neighbouring valleys stands out, richly flavoured and served with pumpkin štruklji and an excellent red wine sauce.

Name: Old Manila
Address: GF, The Peninsula Manila, Corner of Ayala and Makati Avenues, Makati - Metro Manila, The Philippines
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Pass through the lobby of The Peninsula to enter an elegant Art Deco setting for a timeless fine dining experience. At Old Manila, French classics with bold touches meet aged steaks and refined seafood, all presented with care. The gracious hospitality and beautifully composed plates are in keeping with the restaurant's long-standing reputation, making this a fitting choice for special occasions and a showcase of Manila's enduring culinary class.

Name: Old New Taiwanese Cuisine (Jiuru 2nd Road)
Address: 227 Jiuru 2nd Road, Sanmin District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
Description: The kitchen team has remained the same since this household name opened in 2008. Three 8-course set menus feature traditional banquet dishes updated with delicacy and sophistication, that showcase the best seasonal produce. Guests can also pre-order their favourites. The signature taro and sago sweet soup is the perfect way to end a meal here – starchy taro from Jiasian is slow-cooked until creamy and melting.

Name: Old Vicarage
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: With a history dating back to 1846, this delightful stone-built former vicarage is situated in a semi-rural spot on the edge of the city. Two fixed-price menus – go for the 'Prestige' option if you want the full experience – offer ambitious, well-constructed dishes delivering assured flavours from high-quality ingredients. Roe deer from the Balmoral estate is a great example, providing a wonderful gamey flavour and cooked to a perfect tenderness. The grand-looking house is surrounded by mature grounds that are worth exploring.

Name: Olde Glen Bar
Description: This remote inn dates from the 1760s, and its somewhat modest façade gives little indication as to the charm and character that lies within. The bar is always filled with locals, and the large dining room plays host to a set menu which boasts plenty of fish and shellfish from nearby shores, including local oysters and house-smoked salmon; while the fermented potato bread gets things off to a great start. There are cosy bedrooms available too.

Name: Ole Liese
Description: Steeped in history, Gut Panker is a truly idyllic spot. The tranquil estate is the epitome of rural charm and is also known as a Trakehner stud farm – it forms the perfect backdrop for Hotel & Restaurant Ole Liese. The motto "Sunday cooking. Every day" underpins a menu of regional seasonal fare, which is served in the cosy, rustic interior, or out on the lovely terrace in summer. In addition, the estate's pretty café in the old night watchman's lodge serves coffee and cake from 2-5pm, and on Sundays, brunch is available by prior reservation. Overnight stays are possible in stylish, individually decorated guestrooms.

Name: Oleana
Description: The Eastern Mediterranean, the Middle East and in particular Turkey are celebrated at this longstanding and ever-popular Cambridge restaurant. The menu is divided into vegetables, fish and meat and it’s well worth exploring all sections when ordering a selection of the small plates. Highlights include wonderfully light ricotta and corn dumplings; meaty swordfish chraimeh with couscous; and intensely flavored quail kebab with pistachio. For a refreshing summer dessert look no further than the Turkish bici bici.The wood paneling creates the feel of a cozy chalet, while above it a row of boncuk – blue-glassed amulets – looks down protectively over the customers. The second, smaller room provides diners with enticing glimpses of the busy kitchen.

Name: Olhabidea
Description: In this 16C Basque farmhouse you can enjoy simple and unpretentious dishes prepared using ingredients fresh from the vegetable garden. Opt to eat in the hushed atmosphere of either the salon or the library. The guestrooms are overflowing with interesting objects and keepsakes. Outside, you can wander around 4ha of parkland planted with maples, conifers and camellias. Quite charming!

Name: Olio Fishbar
Address: Via Padre Luigi Monti 4, Saronno, 21047, Italy
Description: A modern bistro in the heart of Saronno, where guests leave their cars in nearby parking areas to settle into well-appointed tables (reservations recommended, even for lunch) and savor generous dishes, primarily seafood, though not exclusively. Fresh aromas, clean flavors, an abundance of raw preparations, and a few meat options, curiously without any pasta courses. We particularly enjoyed the “fish and chips” featuring coalfish, crispy and golden, and the Sicilian cannolo “our way,” indulgent and fragrant. The wine list is concise but thoughtfully curated, while both ownership and kitchen bear the signature of the Michelin-starred restaurant Olio in Origgio.

Name: Oliva
Description: An attractive, contemporary-style restaurant with an impressive setting on Plaza de España plus a delightful terrace. It is run by a charming couple (Carlos and Kim), with the former in the kitchen and the latter front of house. Choose between a Mediterranean-influenced à la carte that includes seasonal dishes, and an impressive tasting menu. We particularly enjoyed and can recommend one of its starters, the dish entitled Prawns / Kataifi / Foie Gras Sauce.

Name: Olive Branch & Beech House
Address: Main Street, Clipsham, LE15 7SH, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The Olive Branch is a picture-postcard village pub, with a fine stone exterior and rustic interior design that boasts the obligatory wooden beams and roaring fire which make country inns so inviting. Its cooking is comfortingly traditional in basis, with well-executed versions of confit duck leg, fish & chips and more hearty classics; local sourcing is key too, with suppliers proudly name-checked and vegetables coming from their garden. Over the road, you'll find Beech House, where guests can stay the night while exploring the surrounding countryside.

Name: Oliveiras
Description: The Oliveira family ensures a warm welcome in a harmonious, intentionally informal setting in which guests feel instantly at ease. Service is attentive, and the Mediterranean cuisine is based on top-quality ingredients, with fresh seafood a particular highlight. Be sure not to miss the zabaione with port wine and vanilla ice cream – available by pre-order only. Alongside an extensive à la carte menu, there is also a selection of daily specials and seasonal dishes. The food is complemented by an outstanding range of wines from the owner's Portuguese homeland, including fine ports, also available by the glass. A small boutique offers all kinds of delicacies to take home or give as gifts, such as wine, olives or fleur de sel from the Algarve. The annual summer party, featuring a selection of tapas, is especially popular.

Name: Oliver's
Address: 1639 S. Wabash Ave., Chicago, IL, 60616, USA
Description: There are just a few tables at the entrance looking out into the street, but don't be deceived, as a larger dining room awaits. The walls are hung with paintings and photographs, and cushioned chairs lend a 1930s Hollywood vibe to this stylish spot. Meanwhile, in the kitchen, it's all about seafood sporting global influences. Quality ingredients are allowed to shine without a lot of fuss. A single, grilled tiger prawn served over garam masala and kashmiri chili sauce is topped with cold pressed mustard seed oil for an appetizer that makes a big impression. Porcini mushroom risotto prepared with browned butter and topped with mimolette is another example of a winning dish. Don't skip dessert, especially the coconut key lime pie layered with pistachio praline.

Name: Oliver's Osteria
Address: 853 Laguna Canyon Rd., Laguna Beach, CA, 92651, USA
Description: Note: Temporarily closedSet just minutes from the Pacific Coast Highway near Laguna College of Art + Design, this Italian gem makes a delightful sight. Inside, the dining room oozes warmth, thanks to sleek banquettes, artwork-lined walls and an inviting bar—perfect for solo diners. It paints the very picture of Italian hospitality and that's even before you've had your first bite.Chef Erik De Marchi's menu has something for everyone. He takes a range of familiar dishes and enhances them with an authentic flair. Start with fiori di zucca, a zucchini blossom stuffed with ricotta cheese, anchovies and capers. Pasta is a natural choice, and while it's difficult to pick just one, tuck into a dreamy plate of bucatini all'amatriciana. Tempting desserts are all made in house.

Name: Olivia
Description: Come to this lively Catalan hotspot for tapas and small plates, which boast delicate handiwork, modern plating and lashings of flavour. Try the 'Segovia' style suckling Iberico pig or ‘A Feira’ octopus – pork belly and octopus in a silky potato foam with caramelised onion. Be sure to save room for their iconic creamy cheesecake. The chic interior by Barcelona-based designer Rosa-Violán embodies the Mediterranean soul, whisking diners instantly off to Spain.

Name: Olivia
Address: 3601 W. Swann Ave., Tampa, FL, 33609, USA
Description: Named after Chef/owner Chris Ponte's daughter, it's only appropriate that the cooking at this bustling, Italian-inspired venue should set itself apart thanks to extra care. That characteristic attention to detail includes efforts, like extruding all pastas in house before slowly drying them—but it’s the sort of work that pays off for diners.Although the cuisine draws heavily on classic flavors, don't expect by-the-books renditions—even the simplest dishes flaunt a bit of personality. Take, for example, mini rigatoni sauced with ragù Bolognese and a dollop of herbed ricotta; it's a departure from tradition that is unlikely to draw any objections. The pizza offerings are similarly appealing, like one with truffle honey, smoky speck and scallion.

Name: Olivia's Prime
Address: Lot G1-G4, GF, Indochina Mall, 74 Bach Dang Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: The family-owned restaurant is known for its quality food and service, as well as its friendly vibe. The menu focuses on beef steaks, including some top notch imported choices such as Japanese Hitachi A5 Wagyu, Aussie Sanchoku MB5 and Black Angus, and USDA Prime. Chargrilled to perfection and flawlessly seasoned, the steaks are tender, juicy and flavourful. Round off your meal with New York style cheesecake.

Name: Olivier Leflaive
Description: A plush house in the centre of the village, a glass-paned wine cellar, a bar with an Art Deco look, a chic and inviting dining room: welcome to Olivier Leflaive's place! The famous Côte de Beaune winegrower has created two eateries. Le Bistro d'Olivier offers a seasonal menu inspired by local produce, and the restaurant Klima has more fine dining ambitions. Great wine list, needless to say, thanks to the estate's 80 appellations.

Name: Olivomare
Address: 10 Lower Belgrave Street, Belgravia, London, SW1W 0LJ, United Kingdom
Description: Sardinian cuisine is the order of the day at this bright, well-run Belgravia restaurant. It’s been around for some time, which is a testament to the quality of the seafood-centric cooking. Whether it’s steamed mussels with garlic and parsley or monkfish with courgettes and lemon, the fruits of the sea are celebrated heartily – and the simplest dishes are often the best. Much of the high quality produce in the kitchen is also available to buy at their deli, Olivino, next door.

Name: Olivos Comida y Vinos
Description: This discreet and intimate restaurant close to Sants railway station is one of those that is easy to miss but continues to gain new admirers. Through its name, Argentinian-born chef Ezequiel Devoto pays a mini-homage to the country of his birth –Olivos is the district of Buenos Aires in which he grew up. His Mediterranean and globally inspired cuisine (a fusion of flavours from Argentina, Spain, Italy and elsewhere) is not short on creativity and is showcased on several tasting menus. Given its small size, Olivos only has a capacity for eight guests, so it advisable to book a table in advance.

Name: Olona - "Da Venanzio" dal 1922
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: A bastion of regional cuisine for over a century, this restaurant occupies an attractive group of buildings with a large outdoor summer area shaded by a pergola and a charming dining room with a retro feel. Traditional recipes with interesting and personalised twists take centre stage, including superb ravioli del plin with three roasts and a meat sauce – this is Lombardy, after all! Impressive wine list, including wines by the glass.

Name: Oltra
Description: Oltra refers to the village of Outer’s former Latin name. You will be greeted by the buzzy, casual ambience of a venue steeped in history, underscored by rustic ornamentation, like old stone tiles from a church and wrought-iron details. In the hands of a youthful team, Iwert seamlessly manages the front-of-house while plying diners with wine tips, while chef Jonathan rolls out creatively twisted Gallic fare. The chef frequently draws on ingredients like lemongrass and vinegar to enhance and complement his market-fresh score. For example, he may pair tomatoes and green olives with the umami of North Sea shrimp, adding horseradish ice cream for a spicy kick and a tomato and verbena-spiked water. Bang on confident and oozing in passion depict this temple to good food.

Name: Oltre.
Description: This restaurant in the lively Mercato delle Erbe district has an entrance adorned with hundreds of stickers, giving it the appearance of a record shop rather than a contemporary-style eatery with a bar counter and a highly original surfboard table near the entrance. The modern cuisine has its roots in the region yet also includes skilfully prepared dishes from around the world (we highly recommend the Bolognese ramen, which includes tagliolino in a mushroom broth, with parmesan, quail eggs marinated in balsamic vinegar, and spinach). There’s also a choice of cocktails to start or round off your meal. Booking is highly recommended.

Name: Oltremare
Description: Restaurant Oltremare was born of an ambitious project, conceived to give full expression to a coherent and contemporary gastronomic vision, capable of showcasing the talent of the chef and his brigade. Situated on the fifth floor of the Hotel Due Torri, the space has recently undergone a significant refurbishment that has heightened its elegance and atmosphere, making it more welcoming and visually striking than ever. Even in its name, Oltremare declares its identity: an authentic Mediterranean cuisine, expressed through seasonal, often farm-to-table, ingredients, and recipes rooted in local tradition. The result is a culinary journey capable of conveying the purity of flavour and the richness of aroma, always with an eye firmly on the contemporary. The offering is distinguished by a creative approach built on solid foundations, between nods to and reinterpretations of Campanian tradition, delivering balanced and recognisable dishes. Completing the experience, the extraordinary panoramic view over the Amalfi Coast: the broad windows frame glimpses of rare beauty, making every moment at the table all the more evocative and memorable.

Name: Oma San Francisco Station
Address: 1737 Post St., #337, San Francisco, CA, 94115, USA
Description: This simple wood counter serves some of the area’s better nigiri, right from the corner of a mall in Japantown. Blink and you’ll miss it—Oma is about the size of a kiosk near the Webster Street exit. Choose from the Mizuho, Sakura and Tsubame prix-fixe menus to match your appetite and budget, though prices are reasonable for such quality. Clean flavors and rich, silky fish are the hallmarks of dining here. Highlights include a lightly torched wild star butterfish that melts in the mouth, and a delicious handroll combining chopped bluefin tuna balanced with pickled yellow daikon wrapped in crisp nori.

Name: Oma Wilma Heimatküche
Description: This historical thatched-roof house in the heart of Keitum has bags of charm. Inside, diners enjoy an appealing modern take on Frisian decor; outside the gorgeous garden terrace beckons. The friendly front-of-house team provides pleasingly informal but professional service. The concept is dubbed "Heimatküche" – an ambitious blend of traditional and modern styles. A crowd favourite is the madras currywurst. Shorter menu at lunchtime followed by tempting coffee and cake options until 5pm. Tip: Be sure to book (only possible for the evening). The restaurant’s name pays tribute to the chef's grandmother.

Name: Omakai
Address: Ignacio Zaragoza 1311, San José del Cabo, 23400, Mexico
Description: Located near the heart of San Jose del Cabo, Omakai sports a serene Mexican minimalist design while putting Japanese cuisine front and center. There are three menus to choose from, but whether you choose the teppanyaki tasting menu, the omakase, or select from the a la carte offerings, you can't go wrong. Those who opt for the omakase will find good quality, with many of the fish sourced from the local waters of La Paz and Ensenada. House-made pork belly gyoza are executed flawlessly, while the nigiri leans traditional at first, becoming more complex as the meal progresses. Seared salmon topped with a truffle sauce is decadently delicious. The meal concludes with a charming vanilla ice cream on squares of coffee jelly.

Name: Omakase
Address: Plaza de María Pita 3, A Coruña, 15001, Spain
Description: A restaurant with a restrained decor and a philosophy based on Omakase-style dining (hence the name) in the emblematic Plaza de María Pita of the city, where you’ll find nothing more than a sushi bar and a fish-aging cabinet. Here, Vigo-born chef Adrián Figueroa, a true expert when it comes to slicing techniques and the preparation of tuna, showcases his skills on a single tasting menu (to which you can also add extras such as eel, crayfish etc) that changes according to availability at the daily auction. Bookings need to be made via the restaurant’s website.

Name: Omakase
Address: 665 Townsend St., San Francisco, CA, 94103, USA
Description: Edomae sushi is what makes Omakase a destination; reservations are required and punctuality is a must. The menu features hand-picked fish from Tokyo's Toyosu market, cured and aged using traditional techniques. A silky chawanmushi features snow crab, Hokkaido uni and house-brined ikura but the nigiri really shine, possibly showcasing kelp-cured sea bream, wonderfully sweet, buttery braised monkfish liver (which fully merits its moniker of “foie gras of the sea”), and Japanese mackerel balanced with a dot of punchy chive purée. Attention to detail is the hallmark of dining here, with customized portions of rice and wasabi adjustments suited for each guest’s palate.

Name: Omakase Experience by PrimeFish
Address: 2907 Providence Rd., Ste. 101, Charlotte, NC, 28211, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list
Description: Chef Robin Anthony is the driving force behind this ambitious six-seat counter, located just a hop away from its larger, more casual sibling. The price point is undeniably lofty, but a bevy of luxury ingredients—truffles, foie gras, imported fish from Toyosu market—provides ample justification as the offbeat omakase unfolds. This maximalist approach is demonstrated by an indulgent signature dish of toasted brioche topped with wagyu tartare, uni and truffle, and even a hand roll of grilled eel is enriched with a bit of foie gras. When it comes to the nigiri, however, a more understated edomae approach is deployed, allowing the impressive quality of the seafood and finely tuned rice to shine. Thoughtful sake and wine selections are an added bonus.

Name: Omakase RI
Address: Rua Garcia da Orta, 71c loja 1, Lisbon, 1200-678, Portugal
Description: Inspired by the “dive” bars of Tokyo, the ambience in this exclusive dining space for just 10 guests is relaxed and informal. Japanese-Brazilian chef William Vargas offers an Omakase menu, as part of which he presents and explains the names and origin of the fish he will be preparing. The experience consists of 15 courses, including delicacies such as “salongo”, served with its skin flambéed and a cold miso broth, and a delicate tuna dish served in nori seaweed which melts in the mouth. You’ll also love the excellent choice of saké on offer here.

Name: Omakase Wa
Description: Behind a small, discreet frontage, you’ll discover an authentic Japanese space. Here, chef Ashik Yonjan, supported by two sushi chefs, Danilo Moreira and Mateus de Jesus Martins, presents an omakase offering using Edomae techniques, through which he channels his passion and dedication into small bites full of flavour, skill and balance. With an offering that shifts constantly with seasonality and product quality, it’s also common to find fish brought in from Japan to complement the experience. The experience unfolds in a minimalist setting, entirely clad in wood, centred on a counter with a maximum capacity of 10 diners, served in two sittings, with everyone served together; for that reason, it’s essential to stick to your booked time. Did you know? The chef finds a new source of inspiration in every season, letting the freshness of the ingredients shape the course of each dining experience.

Name: Omakase Yume
Address: 651 W. Washington Blvd., Chicago, IL, 60661, USA
Description: Dinner here is an intimate, almost solemn, experience. In stark contrast to other sushi counters, Chef/owner Sangtae Park goes about doing things his own way on his corner of the West Loop. He rarely wields a knife on view, as fish are sliced before service; and he deploys non-traditional flourishes like kimchi puree and sesame oil to accentuate quality fish flown in mostly from Japan. The lightly seasoned rice can come off as rather tame, until he serves it in abundance with a grilled miso-marinated black cod. The entire progression is a largely speedy affair, with the chef staying laser-focused on the task at hand, ever diligent and deliberate, and rarely looking up to engage anyone else in the room.

Name: Omakase by Gino
Address: 304 N. Main St., Santa Ana, CA, 92701, USA
Description: Omakase by Gino is nestled amid a sleepy section of downtown Santa Ana but inside, this sushi den is firing on all cylinders. Distressed wood and exposed brick lend a tavern feel while decorative touches are decidedly Japanese. Chef Gino Choi brings palpable joy to this spot with his friendly but focused manner, and the food is just as smile-inducing. Imagine the likes of yuzu cream tucked with a ribbon of crisp Asian pear filled with house-cured ikura or a beautiful fillet of tuna sliced, hit with a flame and set atop an elegant swoosh of garlic and shishito pepper miso. Thick udon noodles are tucked with lobes of creamy uni and a thatch of Italian black summer truffles for a supremely enjoyable (woodsy) bite.

Name: Ombelle
Description: Ludivine La Rosa and Alexandre Frin run this restaurant in an attractive early-20C red-brick building near the sea, with picture windows with small panes and white frames. The chef composes a modern, open-minded and 100% seasonal menu that keeps things simple: just good ingredients (preferably with short supply chains) and aromatic herbs and flowers from the kitchen garden. Nearby PEP'S is the pair's second venture, which revolves around simpler cuisine and dishes for sharing.

Name: Ombra
Address: 199 Cuba Street, Te Aro, Wellington, 6011, New Zealand
Description: This place is inspired by the laid-back Venetian taverns or bàcari that serve small glasses of wine, known as ombra in Venetian slang. Pair your favourite drinks with bite-sized snacks such as baccalà mantecato: creamy salted cod paste on toasted bread. Ombra, however, isn't only a great spot for drinks and finger food, but also for a meal. The risotto, pasta, fish and meat dishes on the menu come in portions generous enough for sharing.

Name: Omemo
Address: 2F, VIBES OF NATURE 33/66, Mu 1, Muang Chao Fah Road, Kathu, Phuket, 83120, Thailand
Description: Set on the second floor of a modern building, this restaurant puts a delicious contemporary spin on classic Swiss cuisine. Expect balanced, well structured and cleanly presented Alpine dishes, such as house-made sausages, potato rösti and fondue-inspired specialities. Meat and cheese are central; the desserts, too, are carefully composed. To truly appreciate the narrative behind the cuisine, opt for the full experience menu.

Name: Omeraki
Description: This restaurant occupying a former workshop boasts a unique layout that includes access via a corridor lined by bookcases of cookery books, a bright and spacious dining room featuring a host of designer detail, and two kitchens (one a striking open kitchen in the centre of the room, and a second enclosed space that is still visible to diners). The cuisine here bears the strong hallmark of experienced celebrity chef Alberto Chicote, whose constantly evolving contemporary cuisine, showcased on three menus (Fiesta, Festival and Homenaje), is based around Spanish ingredients and fusion dishes with a Far Eastern touch. An interesting feature here is how all the team wear bracelets similar to the one worn by Chicote himself, which was given to him as a gift by a Masai tribe during a visit to Kenya and is a daily reminder to him of how we will never achieve our goals on our own.

Name: Omma
Address: 38 rue de la Poste, Roussillon, 84220, France
Description: Taking in the Luberon and the famous ochre cliffs of Roussillon, the view from this restaurant is nothing short of spectacular! As for the food, the short, seasonal menu proposes bistronomy-style dishes with Provençal influences: crispy aubergine, baba ganoush with coriander and fromage blanc with lime; grilled Ventoux pork, peppers stuffed with Coco de Paimpol beans, piperade and apricot condiment; Musquée de Provence pumpkin confit with vanilla, sponge cake with pistachios. A moment of culinary bliss far from the crowds of tourists.

Name: On Cru
Description: Housed in a listed building, this restaurant with its exposed brick walls is reminiscent of old England. Think Chesterfield chairs, a striking semi-circular counter and dimmed lighting. Kelvin de Pijper's classic market-fresh cuisine lets the ingredients take centre stage, for example, pairing freshly caught cod with a velvety creamed sauce made with fish fumet. Crispy sweetbreads are given a glossy finish with a veal reduction infused with cardamom, lovage and pink peppercorns. This chef honours the natural flavours of the produce while adding subtle, measured nuances. A real gem at the picturesque old port.

Name: Ona Cuina Oberta
Address: Duc Carles de Borja 28, Gandia, 46701, Spain
Description: The couple at the helm, with Paco Castelló at the wheel in the kitchen and Gabri Tarín in charge of the dining room, declare themselves to be 100% Mediterranean, so that gastronomic culture is evident in every dish. In this small restaurant, located in a pedestrianised street in the old town (the area known as La Ciudad Ducal), you will find a proposal that revolves exclusively around surprise menus (Ona and Ona Cuina Oberta) that change daily, depending on the market and always giving a great deal of prominence to fish and vegetables. We have loved their tiger nut ajoblanco with cherry granita, and the vegetable carbonara!

Name: Onakaya
Description: Post-renovation, Onaka is now Onakaya, in a nod to Japan's izakayas – casual dining spots where simple food is made to be shared. At this Nice establishment tucked away at the end of a cul-de-sac (accessed via rue de la Liberté), the serve vegetable tempura, salmon lightly seared with yuzu-miso, maki and sushi, as well as playful twists on local culinary tradition: prawn socca tacos and inventive takes on dragon rolls. Chic decor, an in-house cocktail bar and a fine sake selection. Upstairs, Onakasé offers an intimate dining experience with a 12-seat counter and a high-end tasting menu. Booking essential.

Name: Oncle Lee
Address: 222 avenue Laurier Ouest, Montréal, H2T 2N8, Canada
Description: This elegant and trendy little place is run by Chef Anderson Lee, who offers diners a window onto his well-honed take on contemporary Chinese cuisine, inflected with a typically Montreal touch. Great care goes into cooking staples such as sesame noodles and garlic fried rice; sweet and sour eggplant is finished with crunchy peanuts and bacon. Other creations show even more personality—think steamed oysters with fermented black bean sauce or beef tartare with doubanjiang. The quality of the ingredients is impeccable, and the flavors are always on point. The ingenious cocktails provide another outlet for the same creativity.

Name: Oncle Lee Kăo
Description: From the team behind Oncle Lee, this restaurant with subdued lighting from red lanterns focuses on grilled dishes (kăo is Mandarin for "grill"): lamb skewers with cumin and shishito peppers, spicy or grilled beef tataki, five-spice duck, sea bream with Sichuan sauce, octopus with lap cheong. Served with wok-fried vegetables and glazed with soy sauce and maple syrup, the grilled Cornish hen is a particular treat. Generous, fragrant cuisine perfect for sharing in this lively atmosphere.

Name: Onda Blu
Address: Via Orsa Minore 1, San Mauro a Mare, 47030, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Almost appearing to rise up directly out of the sand, this unexpectedly elegant restaurant is home to a simple yet stylish dining room with large windows overlooking the sea. Fresh fish of the highest quality takes pride of place on the menu, served in classic, traditional dishes from the Adriatic. Daily specials fresh from the market feature alongside the à la carte, such as the excellent porcini mushrooms we enjoyed on our last visit here, which were served with passatelli pasta, shrimp and scallops. Although individuals may change, an enthusiastic and professional approach is typical of the entire team here. The excellent wine list includes labels from outside Italy, with a particular focus on France.

Name: Ondersch Genusswirtschaft
Description: Going by the name "Ondersch" (a dialect word meaning different), this establishment located in the multipurpose "LOFT" building offers a street-food restaurant with a bar and the Genusswirtschaft gourmet restaurant. On the upper floor, a lively, urban atmosphere provides the setting for tasty modern cuisine made from seasonal and regional produce.

Name: Ondine
Address: Seaton House, 76 The Scores, St Andrews, KY16 9BB, United Kingdom
Description: A key feature of the Edinburgh dining scene for many years, Ondine has now made the move coastwards to the glorious St Andrews. Located inside the beautifully restored Seaton House hotel, its new location is befitting of the seafood-focused menu, with views over West Sands beach and close proximity to the East Neuk’s renowned fishing villages. Top produce from the area could include crab or lobster, with the dishes taking a classic approach to showing them off – look out for the likes of fish & shellfish soup and sole meunière.

Name: Ondine
Address: 10 petite rue des Dentelles, Strasbourg, 67000, France
Description: In the picturesque Petite France district, this dinky eatery attracts those looking for a lively and meaningful culinary experience. At the helm are Noémie D'Hooge, an art graduate turned chef, and her partner, Marin Rémy. Their delicate, modern, predominantly plant-based repertory stars cherry-picked, seasonal ingredients, sourced from small nearby producers. The culinary focus is clearly on nature, sustainable development and local biodiversity, albeit with a scattering of global influences. The pair works in full view of the diner in a pleasant, laid-back atmosphere. On the beverage side, you will find a weakness for natural wines, as well as home-made kombuchas and other non-alcoholic concoctions.

Name: One Club Row
Address: 1 Club Row, Shoreditch, London, E1 6JX, United Kingdom
Description: To get to this delightfully fun little bistro, arrive at the busy Knave of Clubs pub in Shoreditch, where the team will whisk you up to the first floor via a secret stairway. Here, you’ll find a bright, welcoming restaurant where the counter is one of the best seats in the house – in part thanks to the utterly charming team who look after you every step of the way. The menu is packed with appealing dishes, from the generously sized pork schnitzel with mustard sauce and gorgonzola, to the playful rice pudding crème brûlée to finish.

Name: One Degree North
Description: 'One Degree North refers to the latitude of Singapore. And true to its name, it serves popular Singaporean dishes and Asian style barbecue. The chef even imported the Apollo oven straight from Singapore to recreate the local flavors. The signature Cantonese style crispy roast pork, which strikes a perfect balance between the light and crispy skin and moist meat underneath, tastes authentically Singaporean. Another highlight is the incredibly popular and iconic Singaporean chicken rice.

Name: One Fish Street
Address: 17 Chandos Road, City of Bristol, BS6 6PG, United Kingdom
Description: Despite its name, this stripped-back seafood spot is actually located on Chandos Road, a mini food-loving hub in Bristol’s trendy Redland neighbourhood. Fish Street is in fact the restaurant’s previous address, before it relocated here from St Ives, and is a hint as to what to expect on the menu. A wide range of oysters is at its core, joined by other seafood plates such as red mullet with a piquant shellfish sauce. Look out for the selection of high-end tinned fish too. Sensible pricing and friendly service add to the appeal.

Name: One Harbour Road
Address: 7-8F, Grand Hyatt Hotel, 1 Harbour Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The high-ceilinged split-level room commands sweeping harbour views, and the sound of the fountain exudes serenity. Exquisite Cantonese cooking is the name of the game here: start with the appetisingly crispy deep-fried shiitake with an osmanthus honey glaze; for mains, opt for the spicy and tangy Wuxi-style Boston lobster. Some dishes are available in single serving sizes. Detailed and thoughtful service adds to the experience.

Name: One Pico
Address: 5-6 Molesworth Place, Dublin City, D02 YA32, Ireland
Description: Tucked away down a quiet city centre alley, this long-standing and much-respected restaurant has long enjoyed a loyal local following. The cooking modernises classically based dishes and the sauces are particularly impressive, adding depth and complexity to uplift the central ingredients; roast saddle of lamb with an expertly made provençal-style rabbit jus is a prime example. The extensive, lovingly curated wine list has options for a range of budgets and the sommelier's recommendations are well worth taking.

Name: One Tree Grill
Address: 9 Pah Road, Epsom, Auckland, 1023, New Zealand
Description: 2026 sees One Tree Grill celebrate 30 years as Epsom’s premier restaurant. It remains a great choice for those hoping to impress the in-laws or just wanting dinner at a more relaxed pace than many city eateries. There’s an appealing honesty to the place, with service that is earnestly attentive and always enthusiastic. The kitchen doesn’t try reinventing any wheels and just keeps the focus on the primary ingredients with European influences, alongside the occasional Asian note. Pair your dishes with something from the thoughtfully curated wine list.

Name: One White Street
Address: 1 White St., New York, NY, 10013, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This 19th-century townhouse, once the downtown hangout for John Lennon and Yoko Ono, is a charming and pleasing destination. Gorgeous marble, superb tile work and modern light fixtures decorate the intimate and attractive wood-clad space. The intimate setting offers both à la carte dining and a tasting menu, and the team operates a market next door as well. The menus throughout feature produce sourced from their upstate farm. Bold and clever flavors come easily to this kitchen team, as seen in grilled monkfish with a whey miso glaze over a lemon verbena butter sauce. A single scoop of husk cherry sorbet with an anise granita is a lovely ending.

Name: One80 St.Christopher Street
Address: 45A St. Christopher's Street, Valletta, VLT 1464, Malta
Description: In the heart of historic Valletta, a vibrant Mediterranean culinary experience unfolds within a low-key, bistro chic setting at One80 St. Christopher Street. Chef Vella draws on his international expertise to craft a punchy menu that showcases the breadth of Mediterranean cuisine. The range is very diverse and includes a thoughtful selection for vegetarians. Notable house specialties include the Chateaubriand for two, and for seafood lovers, a daily fresh catch that varies depending on availability. The well-curated cellar reveals an international selection with a weakness for prestigious Italian estates.

Name: Onglet
Description: At the front, Onglet is a butcher shop selling delicious meat products during the day; but in the evening, the cold store door opens, and diners are welcomed into a trendy restaurant with nostalgic decor reminiscent of a butchery of yesteryear. In the fully open kitchen, chef Alan and his team craft a tasting menu that marries familiar flavours with creative flair. Rare Holstein beef entrecôte with a velvety foie gras sauce, or tender chuck tataki accompanied by a chimichurri enriched with anchovies and green herbs as well as Kewpie mayonnaise – this cooking is precise and full of surprises. Perfect for sharing!

Name: Oniriq
Description: Located in the city centre, on the Old Town side of the Inn River, this is a compact restaurant with clean, modern decor. Working in an open kitchen, the chefs craft two distinct set menus – one vegetarian, the other with meat and/or fish. The cuisine is ambitious, rooted in classic culinary tradition yet refined with modern techniques. Select ingredients go into harmoniously flavoursome dishes such as "Alpine prawn, Swiss chard, peanut, plum" and "venison, porcini, spinach, berbere". Fine wine pairings and homemade non-alcoholic beverage pairings available. Attentive, professional service.

Name: Onslow
Address: 9 Princes Street, Auckland Central, Auckland, 1010, New Zealand
Description: Celebrity chef Josh Emett opened his restaurant in a spacious, lofty room that is fitted with banquettes and booth seating and leads onto a garden terrace. The menu features European-inspired cooking with Kiwi twists, and New Zealand ingredients enjoy pride of place. Start with Chatham Islands crayfish éclair, followed by Big Glory Bay salmon pastrami with savoury canelé served tableside in a salmon trolley for an engaging theatrical experience.

Name: Ontra
Description: This restaurant with a tastefully designed modern interior is located in TechSquare, the new centre for digitalisation south of the city centre. A friendly and professional team serves up seasonal cuisine that also includes vegetarian dishes. The shorter lunchtime menu proposes some cheaper options. The neighbouring Ontra's Gourmetstube serves a fixed set menu made up of seven courses in the evening.

Name: Onyva
Address: B1, 15 Dosan-daero 75-gil, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, 06015, South Korea
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Valet parking
Description: Tucked away in a quiet alley, Onyva embodies the chef’s vision of a relaxed, welcoming dining space. While rooted in French cuisine, the restaurant’s menu creatively incorporates Korean ingredients to present distinctive flavours. A standout is the buckwheat galette filled with grilled eel, crispy ginger, and caramelised onions for exceptional texture and depth. The six-course tasting menu is the standard offering, but à la carte options paired with wine are available at more accessible prices after 9 p.m.

Name: Onyx
Description: Pinpointing the Onyx experience can be a challenging task, as this is a place that undergoes constant evolution in the pursuit of self-improvement. What can be said, is that you will be part of a truly immersive experience, as you arrive at the same time as your fellow guests, ready to share a memorable evening together. The communal experience is a stimulating, sensory and provocative one, that uses a multi-course tasting menu to showcase the development of food in the past, present and future. Without giving too much away, your night here will include light, sound, capes and contemplation!

Name: Oogst
Description: With its warm and welcoming atmosphere, Oogst is right at home in the cosy Buurtschap Centrum 2005 neighbourhood. There is something of the lively Parisian bistro about this place, which makes it all the more enjoyable to dine here. The set menus are always determined by what the Laantje Voorham vegetable garden has to offer. The versatility of vegetables and herbs provides subtle nuances. By incorporating herbs into ice cream and broths, the chef gives dishes a new twist. His modern and always generous creations are fragrant with punchy flavours.

Name: Oostergoo
Description: Oostergoo is the ideal base from which to explore the picturesque village of Grou and, beyond that, the wider Friesland region. This long-established hotel and restaurant enjoys a magnificent waterfront setting, complete with its own private jetty and a terrace that overlooks the marina and is open throughout the day.
