Inside, a large bar, bistro chairs and a lively yet relaxed atmosphere create a wonderfully cosy, convivial feel. The menu lets the ingredients take centre stage through carefully crafted dishes that allow their natural character to shine. Take the smoked eel – a local speciality – soft and beautifully fatty, served with toasted brioche spread with dill mayonnaise, crisp apple and mostarda. If you opt for the steak tartare, it's prepared tableside in time-honoured fashion. The lunchtime menu is a little simpler, but the commitment to quality never wavers.

Name: Opal
Description: In quiet Chevy Chase, on the border of Bethesda, this buzzy restaurant is well on its way to becoming a neighborhood essential. Far from flashy, the team isn’t out to redefine a cuisine or break any culinary boundaries. Ricotta dumplings, beef tartare, a properly cooked filet of trout – these are familiar flavors handled in a confident manner. There is the occasional surprise, like the excellent lamb-stuffed pita. And for dessert, there is no escaping the tiramisu ice cream, a triumphant finale that nobody will want to share. A reasonably priced set menu appeals to those not in the mood to make any decisions. Either way, the homey space fills up fast, and even the bar can be packed out with guests perfectly content to eat while standing.

Name: Opaline
Description: In this modern, spruce little restaurant located next to the Comédie La Rochelle theatre, the cuisine is the handiwork of a motivated young couple who met at Alexandre Mazzia. The pair's trademark is creative, colourful cuisine, each dish coming with three satellite-style variations, such as hake with peas and cabbage, accompanied by lentils with a haddock emulsion and a seaweed blini with home-made taramasalata on the side. Bistronomy-style formule menu at lunchtime; for dinner, their fine dining tasting menus, which change every four months or so, comprise different numbers of "sequences".

Name: Open
Description: Open boasts an eclectic look in keeping with its name. This similar liberal philosophy is also evident in its open-view kitchen and on the à la carte, with the option of creating your own half portion-style menu. The chefs here explain and serve their own contemporary dishes centred around market-fresh ingredients. One speciality that is definitely worth ordering is the Gilda Open, one of the restaurant's great classics, or one of its new dishes, such as roasted peppers with a gorgonzola and gin sauce or the lobster salpicón with tomato broth.

Name: Opera
Address: Via Sant'Antonio da Padova 3, Turin, 10121, Italy
Description: The former nineteenth century refectory of the nearby church has become the laboratory of a chef who is as skillful as he is creative: wrapped in the warm atmosphere of the brickwork of the evocative dining room, all the dishes have fruit as a recurring ingredient, which adds a touch of acidity and flavor to dishes of creative cuisine, whether of meat or fish, further enhanced by the work of an excellent sommelier.

Name: Opera|02
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An oasis of taste to the east of Modena: here, the farm estate, also known for its production of balsamic vinegar, welcomes guests with rooms, a small spa and a restaurant immersed in the quiet of the countryside. The cooking tells the story of the Modenese territory through recipes that showcase local ingredients, alternating dishes faithful to tradition – such as tortelli in capon broth or the indulgent zuppa inglese – with others in which the chef allows himself greater creative freedom. The result is an honest yet carefully crafted offering, capable of uniting gastronomic memory with more personal interpretations, always in keeping with the seasons.

Name: Ophelia
Address: Carr. Tijuana-Ensenada 103, El Sauzal de Rodríguez, 22760, Mexico
Description: El Sauzal de Rodríguez's restaurants are typically laser-focused on seafood, but Ophelia offers something a little different. This spot with light walls, wood ceiling, and dark tiled floor, features a Mediterranean-themed menu with items ranging from salads, pastas, and pizza to entrees like roasted octopus, fish in mole, roasted quail, and lamb shank. Lasana de Susana, named for the chef's mother, is presented in a cast iron skillet. Its layers of fresh pasta are loaded with a coarsely ground meat ragu studded with diced mushrooms, and a rich cheese for a deliciously comforting dish that is accompanied by a refreshing green salad with sliced cucumber and cherry tomatoes in a creamy cilantro dressing.

Name: Ophelía
Description: Stunning murals, colorful carvings...Ophelía is quite literally a bright spot in Vancouver's Olympic Village. It's always packed, so make a reservation. Of course, if you didn't plan ahead, a bevy of special margaritas will help you pass the time. Chef/co-owner Francisco Higareda prepares traditional pan-regional Mexican fare just as his mother, Ophelia, did. Corn-crusted octopus sided by cilantro rice, braised kale and zucchini is bested with a Oaxacan mole blanco that's rich and creamy. A trio of tacos rewards diners with delectable ingredients piled high atop locally made tortillas. End things with that ultimate classic—tres leches cake.Weather permitting, the outdoor patio is the spot to while away the night.

Name: Opificio
Description: A modern restaurant in the province of Padova which, over the past ten years, has grown and evolved from a gastro pub to the top-quality eatery that it is today. The cuisine is fairly eclectic, featuring meat and fish dishes alike, with the option of a lighter menu at lunchtime. The best dishes are showcased on the à la carte and are often made using luxury ingredients such as foie gras, scampi and Wagyu beef. The impressive wine list demonstrates a passion for international sparkling wines, while the excellent selection of wines by the glass is further enhanced by a choice of cocktails (also available at midday).

Name: Opéra
Description: After stints in three-star restaurants in Italy and with the Bras family, at the Musée Soulages and at their flagship establishment in Laguiole, Italian chef Vasco Baldisserotto has gone solo in this smart restaurant outside the town centre. He signs a pedigree Gallic score, albeit tinged with Italian influences, particularly from his native Venetian region. Accustomed to top-drawer produce, he painstakingly sources and selects only the best local ingredients. The menus celebrate the seasons and his suppliers, on whom he frequently shines the spotlight. Examples include braised Aveyron beef shank in a carbonara sauce; raviolis stuffed with chocolate and hazelnuts and orange sorbet. If you now add the friendly welcome and seamless service, you will realise why everyone is singing the praises of this opera…

Name: Ora d'Aria
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Behind the Uffizi, a restaurant that stands out for its originality: not so much for its impressively large open kitchen as for its deliberate desire to encourage direct interaction between guests and the kitchen team. The restaurant’s name reflects its proximity to the historic Florentine prison of Le Murate and its intention to offer customers a moment of genuine relaxation.A small but charming dining room adorned with a ceiling frescoed with gold leaf, houses Marco Stabile’s delightful restaurant, where he serves creative cuisine that is equally accomplished in both meat and fish dishes, all based on top-quality ingredients.

Name: Orangerie De Pol
Description: Diners feel at one with the surrounding nature in this light-filled wood-framed orangery. In this unique setting, your charming hostess Marjolein and chef Mark express their love for Achterhoek. Outstanding locally sourced ingredients, fresh picks from their own kitchen garden and intense sauces are showcased in a surprise menu that is very much in step with the times. This regional bounty is enhanced by international nuances. A case in point is the kingfish, marinated in rhubarb broth, paired with a silken yuzu sorbet and an aromatic tomato and soy vinaigrette – a dish that speaks volumes about the chef's technical precision and feel for the seasons.

Name: Orangutan
Description: A Thai restaurant that showcases the cuisine of the ancient city of Chiang Mai and the Isaan region in northeastern Thailand. The menu includes a salad of pounded green papaya, fermented pork sausages, and a soup of stewed beef and herbs. The local style is to eat these with sticky rice steamed in a bamboo basket. The sour and spicy flavours of fermented seasonings, along with the aromas of citrus and fresh herbs, evoke a Thai dinner table.

Name: Orania.Berlin
Description: The restaurant belonging to the lovely hotel that shares its name has a stylish, warm and relaxed ambience. The lobby and bar (with its interesting cocktail menu) are directly adjacent. Modern, creative dishes are sent out of the large open kitchen that draws the eye. Attentive and accomplished service. Try the four-course "Xberg Duck" set menu (min. two people).

Name: Orbys
Description: Chef Adam Blondeau is a trained pastry chef originally from Châteauroux. After time abroad and having garnered valuable experience in some of the world's top kitchens, he is now back on home turf. He may be young, but he already has several strings to his bow: skilled at fermenting (eg pickles), using herbs grown in his own garden, and playfully referencing the terroir. He doesn't cut corners when it comes to the quality of the ingredients in his pared-down dishes, a case in point being his Chambord venison. His cooking is ingredient-led, right down to single-ingredient dishes.

Name: Orchestra
Description: Imola, the city in Italy’s Emilia-Romagna where the chef apprenticed, has a famous music academy. The restaurant’s name derives from the passion for classical music he learned from the students he befriended there. In Imola, the chef developed his belief that a restaurant resembles an orchestra, in that a wide range of players work in harmony to create a greater whole. Cuisine on plates decorated with musical instrument motifs and classical music piped into the dining room deliver a performance worthy of any conservatory.

Name: Ore
Description: Ore means "mouth" in Latin. A disarmingly simple name for this place that is quite simply exceptional – a 17C pavilion within the Palace of Versailles. Alain Ducasse is the Sun King of the premises, enforcing the culinary law for which he is known. That of naturality and a constantly renewed homage to fine ingredients.

Name: Orfoz
Address: Kumbahçe Mahallesi, Zeki Müren Caddesi No:13/1, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
Description: The beautiful bay this restaurant overlooks is the pride of the Bozçağa brothers – not only for the azure waters, but also the bountiful fish and seafood they have to offer. Their family-run restaurant specialises in seafood and plant-forward cuisine. A commitment to locally sourced ingredients and short supply chains ensures exceptional quality. The chefs' love for the sea is palpable in every dish, from sea snails cooked in a court bouillon and finished with a herb cream accented with a pronounced hint of garlic, to eel that is confit and lightly smoked, resulting in a buttery texture. It is worth perusing the wine list, as it is clearly a passion of the owners and even includes some of their own labels.

Name: Orient Dragon
Address: 271-1, Section 2, Gongyi Road, Nantun District, Taichung, 408, Taiwan
Description: This restaurant changed hands in 2022, but the festive interior with its red and black colour scheme stayed the same – as did the kitchen team. Rest assured that their signature Taiwanese home-style cooking, along with some novelty Sichuanese dishes, still taste as good as always. Popular choices include three-cup “springy” pork trotter, steamed fourfinger threadfin with pickled bamboo shoot, and sakura ebi fried rice.

Name: Origens
Description: Hidden in a narrow lane in Évora’s historic centre, this discreet bistro holds a compelling experience. It is a family‑run, welcoming space with an Alentejo soul, where the couple Gonçalo Queiroz (chef) and Eugénia Queiroz (front‑of‑house and sommelier) invite diners on a visit to the Origens do Alentejo (Origins of the Alentejo), offering traditional flavours through contemporary presentations and modern techniques. The menu, updated regularly according to the seasonality of regional products, offers à la carte options and two tasting menus (3 and 5 courses). A dish that enchanted us? The tender pork loin, slow‑cooked and lifted by a gentle touch of heat, served with sprouting greens, shallots and apricots. Pair it with a regional wine or let yourself be surprised by the mystery pairing proposed by the sommelier!

Name: Origin
Address: 83 Guanjing Road, Cangshan, Fuzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: Nestling at the foot of a hill, this historical mansion dates from the Ming Dynasty. The owner restored it in 2018, turning it into a restaurant-cum-gallery space. The chef imbues traditional Fujian recipes with a modern edge. Try his line-caught squid in Sichuan red oil – the squid is tender, but bouncy in texture, and loaded with umami. Private rooms only; book one and order a menu tailored to your budget and taste.

Name: Origine
Address: 1F, Brittany Hotel, 6 Mckinley Parkway, Bonifacio Global City, Taguig - Metro Manila, The Philippines
Description: Filipino-born Spanish chef Alexandra Cacho imbues her Spanish cuisine with heartfelt authenticity. Rather than localised adaptations, the menu reflects flavours from Spain's regions, for an overview of its culinary identity. In a long dining room bathed in natural light courtesy of panoramic windows, the mood shifts as the day wears on, setting the scene for memorable sunset dining, with warm service and honest food.

Name: Origine
Description: In this handsome, converted, red-brick farmhouse, Maëllie Poynard and Alexandre Laboureur champion local produce with heartwarming sincerity. Everything comes from small local producers from the seasonal veg to the meat. The chef has no qualms about expressing her creativity or trying out unexpected pairings: for example, caviar and chocolate in a match that turns out to be made in heaven. Spot-on technique, a contemporary interior and the relaxed, peaceful pace of a country village: Origine is very aptly named! Rooted, flavoursome food conjured up by an inventive, enthusiastic team.

Name: Origine
Description: Fantasy creatures and colourful plants, together with souvenirs sent by faithful regulars, set the scene in the whimsical interior chosen by Xavier Lizen for his urban neighbourhood eatery. The menu (vegetarian, meat or fish) changes monthly and illustrates the chef’s playful, unconventional approach. He may enhance a velvety risotto of celeriac with a stock of slightly fermented vegetables, to which he then adds big-boned truffle aromas. Unless you wouldn’t rather prefer a new take on vol-au-vent stuffed with delicate poultry, a creamy morel sauce and a foamy espuma of verjuice-laced potatoes? Origine is trendy, inventive and truly fascinating!

Name: Origine
Address: 2F, Commercial Bay, 7 Queen Street, Auckland Central, Auckland, 1010, New Zealand
Description: Origine benefits from its great spot overlooking Waitemata Harbour; you’ll even find a pair of sunnies on the window tables in the bright, open room. The appealing menu blends French flavours and techniques with local, seasonal produce and there’s a satisfying generosity to the cooking, both in size and in flavour. Gurnard comes with plump Mills Bay mussels; French onion soup is enhanced by an oxtail toastie; and the rich and velvety chocolate mousse is served tableside with a great selection of add-ons, from honeycomb to pistachios.

Name: Origines
Address: Rue de la Coupe 25, Mons, 7000, Belgium
Description: A narrow lane near the main square of Mons leads to the endearing restaurant of Céline, the charming and ever cheerful lady of the house. The sunny rear patio features an olive tree in its centre. Chef Watteyne crafts a menu dictated by market availability, the seasons and his innovative ideas. Examples include his personal take on vitello tonnato or a fascinating tomato-strawberry-burrata dessert. Bold, distinctive cuisine crafted by a chef who takes pride in ensuring that each flavour is spot on and punchy.

Name: Orizhon
Description: In their restaurant opposite the port of Audierne, this pair certainly broadens our culinary horizons. The chef is from Brazil and the floor manager hails from Finistère – the result is delicious, aromatic cuisine that will bring a smile to your lips. The chef naturally draws on the local pantry – most notably fish and seafood, to which she cleverly adds modern and exotic touches. The predominantly maritime score features a lineup illustrated by confit of seabass with grilled beetroot and a pomegranate dressing or seared scallops served with pearl barley, mango and a curry sauce. Pleasant colourful, contemporary interior and a terrace overlooking the port and marina.

Name: Orizon
Description: A pleasant establishment that holds the ingredients and artisans of the Côte d'Opale and Pas-de-Calais areas in high regard. Chef Emmanuel Pillot and Laura Gambart met at La Liégeoise in Wimereux, where he was sous-chef and she was front of house as cheffe de rang. The dishes leave you in no doubt that this seasoned chef knows his craft. The starter strikes a lovely balance of flavours with a slow-cooked egg, Wissant shiitake, parsley and buckwheat; the tender free-range chicken is accompanied by a medley of Ratte potatoes; and a delicious take on a classic riz au lait. Pure bliss!

Name: Orkide Balık
Address: Göltürkbükü Mahallesi, Sahil Sokak No:34, Bodrum, 48483, Türkiye
Description: At Orkide Balik, you can almost feel the sand between your toes as you enjoy your meal, and, on warm days, the terrace beneath the tall trees is especially inviting. The chef takes full advantage of the restaurant's seaside location to serve fish at its absolute freshest. But before you order your main course, be sure to sample starters such as "seacuterie" (seafood charcuterie) and stuffed mussels, and don't miss out on the mezze displayed in the refrigerated counter. The dishes are prepared without any fuss, and with that traditional sense of generosity. Think marinated squid or deep-fried sea bass with aubergine and a bechamel sauce seasoned with mustard. It is always a good idea to round off your meal with the exceptional soğuk baklava. Sometimes the best things in life are the simplest.

Name: Orma
Description: Behind this curious name, which we can interpret as a tribute to Alicante’s successful shoe industry (in fact, in the dining room you will see several old wooden lasts), lies a local, sober and modern style, which is only gaining in popularity. It is run by a young local chef with a lot of talent, Aaron Berenguer, and his proposal, confined within a set lunch menu (Mondays and Thursdays), another called 5 Sentidos and a more complete one called Experiencia, starts informally at the Mother Table, where the concept is explained and the first appetisers are served. Among the dishes served here, generally fresh and with nods to local produce (nougat, blanquet, red prawns, etc.), we were struck by what they call the Squid Trilogy (a good tartare, a false croissant with the body of the squid and a concentrated consommé of legs and offcuts).

Name: Ornellaia
Description: At this restaurant, dishes such as filetto Rossini, lobster carpaccio and house-made tagliatelle al ragù are cooked up in an open-view kitchen. This modern take on Italian cuisine is complemented by an appealing wine list that includes a selection from the famous Tuscan wine producer, Ornellaia. Front of house, host Antonio Bordone and team pull out all the stops. This gem of a restaurant is located in a beautifully refurbished building that was once a bank – the door even opens automatically. Sleek design meets decorative art and the historical charm of sandstone walls, lending the distinctive high-ceilinged space a modern and elegant Tuscan ambience. At lunchtime, there is a small selection of additional dishes.

Name: Ors
Description: The exquisitely crafted canapés set the tone right off the bat: ewe's-milk yoghurt with sudachi, beetroot with trout and kimchi, black garlic- blueberry-venison tartlet, and savory focaccia with chilli-infused ewe's-milk butter. Then comes a delicious surf 'n' turf dish of pan-fried foie gras with langoustines, citrus fruits, and fillet of local beef cooked extra rare and served with salsify, black trumpet mushrooms and a bone marrow jus – truly indulgent. Without a conventional background, local chef Stéphane Lapeyre creates cuisine that is astonishingly precise and remarkably good value. The renovated stone house in a village near Saint-Lary-Soulan features large bay windows and a timber terrace complete with mountain views.

Name: Orsay
Address: 1057 Lexington Ave., New York, NY, 10021, USA
Description: Its classic art nouveau styling makes this popular French brasserie de luxe infinitely more 7th arrondissement than Upper East Side. The efficient service is overseen by managers who gracefully tend to a sophisticated crowd. All the favorites are here, from chicken liver mousse and artichaut vinaigrette to profiteroles, and the kitchen prepares them with a healthy respect for tradition. There are also plenty of salads for those who’ve given up wondering how French women can eat this kind of food without ever going to the gym.

Name: Orso Grigio
Description: In the center of Cavalese, within the hotel of the same name, a young chef presents an intelligent and delicious reinterpretation of Trentino gastronomic traditions without distorting their identity. A stop not to be missed, complemented by a solid wine selection featuring several organic, biodynamic, and amphora-aged bottles. Essential is the Schüttelbrot gelato with black bilberry, wild spinach, and thyme.

Name: Orti Villadorata
Description: Part of the Country House Villadorata resort in the hills outside Noto, this restaurant boasts a delightful setting with the sea as a backdrop, surrounded by gardens which provide many of the vegetables used in the cuisine. Matteo Carnaghi is at the helm in the kitchen, with excellent results and a cuisine is firmly rooted in Sicilian ingredients, offered through two tasting menus of flexible length, with dishes also available à la carte.

Name: Ortica
Address: Via Giovanni Migone 4, Pieve Ligure, 16031, Italy
Description: You drive along 4.5km of winding, narrow (occasionally extremely narrow) roads to get to Ortica, the restaurant at the Tenuta Golfo Paradiso about 35min from Genoa. As is often the case, once at your destination the extensive views of the Tyrrhenian Sea from the restaurant more than compensate for the effort of getting here. Neither will you be disappointed by the cuisine, which is prepared using top-quality ingredients such as vegetables from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden, local fish and carefully selected meat. Dishes are fresh and modern, and occasionally cooked over the barbecue grill.

Name: Orto
Description: At Nina Trulli Resort, nestled in one of the most enchanting areas of the Puglian countryside, among dry stone walls and typical vegetation, you can reconnect with nature. Walking through the restaurant's gardens and orchards is an inspiring experience. The focus on plant-based elements is also reflected in the kitchen: there are two tasting menus – one entirely green, while the other, despite including animal products, also highlights vegetables as the main feature.

Name: Orwell Road
Address: 8 Orwell Road, Dublin City, D06 H2Y5, Ireland
Description: Located in the city's smart suburbs, this buzzy little restaurant is a proper neighbourhood spot. Enjoy snacks and cocktails to start, before moving onto the menu of dishes founded on quality Irish ingredients. Each one is skilfully cooked and provides ample flavour, such as lamb rump with carrot purée and cavolo nero. It's a small place with a quick turnover of tables, but the chatty and efficient service team handle it with aplomb, making their fast-paced jobs look rather easy. The wine list includes some unusual but intriguing choices.

Name: Orwells
Address: Shiplake Row, Binfield Heath, RG9 4DP, United Kingdom
Description: Named after George Orwell, who spent his childhood in the area, this 18th-century building has the appearance of a rural inn from the outside, but once indoors you'll see it for the modern place it really is. Choose between the tasting menu and the à la carte to enjoy dishes mining quality British produce and vegetables from the team's own smallholding. They make their own honey, too, which is used in the signature 'Mill Lane Honey Sponge' dessert – a real treat to end your visit on.

Name: Oryori Honjo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: The owner-chef cut his teeth in the counter kappo trade. There, he learned that a counter chef must be able to respond spontaneously to customer requests. Menus are omakase, but with plenty of flexibility to accommodate preferences. His Kyoto experience shines in his use of Kyoto vegetables and in soup stock of Rishiri kombu kelp and dried bonito flakes. Seasonal small hotpots are well worth the wait: flower of Japanese pepper in spring, pike conger in summer; Matsutake mushrooms in autumn and wild boar in winter.

Name: Oryori Horiuchi
Description: The starting point for Mrs. Sayaka Horiuchi is her early life lived amid natural beauty. Considering that ‘the mountains water the village and feed the ocean,’ the dishes are prepared with a spirit of gratitude for ingredients from land and sea. Horiuchi nurtures relations with food producers nationwide who share her vision. Local vegetables are from farmers in Nerima, clams from fishermen in Kyoto. Her famous chicken offal stew is home cooking from her native Yamanashi Prefecture.

Name: Oryori Ichiho
Description: The name is a play on ‘ho’, which could mean ‘step’, as in ‘stepping forward’ or ‘bounty, prosperity’, reflecting chef Ryusuke Yamazaki’s desire that his restaurant blossom and prosper. The soup stock gets its umami from kombu, with a light flavour reflecting his Kyoto experience. Dishes such as fish steamed with grated turnip on top and dumplings made from bamboo-shoot derive from ages past, recounting the culinary culture of the ancient capital. Pike conger in summer and eddoes in winter are eagerly awaited.

Name: Oryori Katsushi
Description: The owner-chef’s obsession with dashi soup stock was learnt from his mentor, a Kansai native. He mixes dashi of dried bonito flakes, kombu kelp and clams to impart depth and richness. This dashi is found throughout: in savoury egg custard, soup dishes, hot pots and other Japanese favourites. The chef’s choice of career is down to the influence of his brother, a sushi chef, and this brotherly bond is shown in his vinegared rice, simmered abalone liver sauce and pressed chub mackerel sushi. The menu is a stage on a fascinating journey that we’re going to keep watching.

Name: Oryori Kokoroba
Description: The name incorporates a character from the chef’s name while professing sincere devotion to gastronomy. That sincerity is on full display in the hassun appetisers. To convey the mood of the passing seasons, the chef incorporates meticulously chosen items fresh from the market. Oyakodon (chicken and egg on rice) made with freshly cooked rice is a sentimental favourite of the chef, one he’s made continuously since his apprenticeship. His dedication shines through in his painstaking attention to his work.

Name: Oryori Kotan
Description: ‘Kotan’ refers to having depth of taste in light foods. Owner-chef Masanori Mizukawa chose the name as one that chimes with the essence of Japanese cuisine. Embodying this idea is the dashi for the soup; its simple, refined flavour comes from kombu and dried tuna. He puts his experience of having worked as a cook at a ryotei to use in the elaborate vegetable takiawase as well. Accenting the menu is the beef hobayaki speciality.

Name: Oryori Maeshiro
Description: In the Kyoto dialect, ‘monmona-ryori’ means ‘as it is’. As with ‘kinari-ryori’ in Osaka, fussy over-preparation is avoided. The Osaka-apprenticed chef takes to heart the words of his mentor: ‘light, sweet and deep’, and let the ingredients do the talking. Though the custom at a Kyoto kappo is to do the cooking in the back, here the chef displays all his skills for guests to see.

Name: Oryori Matsumura
Description: Tomonori Matsumura built the foundations of his career at a ryotei before travelling to France to add Western techniques to his toolkit. His creed is ‘Make ingredients taste even more like themselves’. For example, shrimp dishes use reduced shrimp stock to enhance the star ingredient. Butter, garlic and fresh cream are sometimes used to lend subtle notes to his seasonings. Matsumura’s aim is to create recipes that will resonate a century from now; Japanese cuisine that will be talked about for generations.

Name: Oryori Nonohara
Description: The restaurant weaves the culture and traditional ceremonies of Japan into its menu. In the seventh lunar month, to celebrate Tanabata, the Star Festival, wanmono is served in lacquer bowls featuring the Milky Way in powdered precious metal. Other tableware also reflects the seasons. One wanmono item features a pairing of hamo and samatsu mushroom in a dish that recalls the tale of Hikoboshi and Orihime: the stars Altair and Vega, two lovers destined to meet but once a year. Sweets include umegae mochi, from Dazaifu Tenmangu Shrine in Fukuoka. Tea from the Yame area of Fukuoka is served in homage to the chef’s hometown.

Name: Oryx
Address: Blvd. Agua Caliente 10750, Int. 84, Tijuana, 22014, Mexico
Description: This Tijuana favorite is the domain of Chef Ruffo Ibarra. The dining room boasts a dressed-up industrial look with dark earthy colors, exposed red brick walls, wood and tiled flooring, metal beams and warm lighting.The menu is a contemporary take on Mexican cuisine and lists an extensive selection of items including chilled seafood starters and grilled steaks. Consomé de camarón con hongas is presented with chopped raw shrimp, then filled tableside with a hot, deeply flavorful shrimp broth which gently poaches the shrimp. Golden-brown, crisped striped bass shares the plate with creamy onion puree, bits of fried kale and some salsa verde. The stack of churros, served warm and accompanied by bourbon ice cream, make for a fine ending.

Name: Os Cachivaches
Description: This restaurant is run by two siblings in a residential district close to the university. It features a tapas bar with high tables for informal eating plus two dining rooms where guests can choose from an extensive à la carte which impresses thanks to its array of rice dishes (we particularly recommend the creamy rice with marine plankton). Make sure you also leave space for the exquisite desserts, especially the brioche “torrija” with vanilla ice cream, and the delicious cheesecake.

Name: Os Maristas
Address: Plaza de la Verdura 5, Pontevedra, 36002, Spain
Description: Found in the heart of Pontevedra, under the stone arcades of one of the most charming medieval squares of the city, we can say that this is a modern and informal tapería, with a dynamic proposal that combines traditional Galician snacking with more elaborate or modern dishes, where Iberian and Mediterranean flavours happily coexist with those from other latitudes. Here you will find octopus tacos, vitello tonnato panapuris, occasional Asian nods, and more). The dishes are designed for sharing!

Name: Osadía de Crear
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the province of Mendoza there’s no excuse for not visiting a winery to enjoy an authentic wine-tourism experience. And with this in mind, Susana Balbo, famous as the first female wine expert in Argentina and a leading wine reference on the South American continent, founded the family-run Susana Balbo Wines bodega, 30km or so south of Mendoza. The Osadía de Crear restaurant, which has existed on the estate since 2013 and is now under the baton of chef Flavia Amad Di Leo, aims to enhance this wine appreciation experience with modern cuisine that is highly delicate and always focuses on local and seasonal ingredients (pumpkin, string beans, beetroot, pomegranate etc). This is presented on two tasting menus (four or six courses), each with different and equally superb estate wine pairing options. Informal brunches, picnics and afternoon tea can also be arranged in the winery’s galleries and gardens.

Name: Osaka
Description: A new home for this historic restaurant, with minimalist interiors that embrace a full‑on oriental aesthetic to showcase authentic Japanese cuisine. A set menu at lunch and à la carte at dinner from which we recommend the Makimoto rolls of amberjack with shiso leaves, sesame seeds and freshly marinated wasabi. Or the festive Sukiyaki, a Japanese take on a bourguignon where meat and vegetables are cooked in a simmering broth at the table and shared among guests. The menu is extensive and rich with other succulent offerings from the Land of the Rising Sun.

Name: Osaka Concepción
Address: Concepcion Arenal 2913, Buenos Aires, C1426DGC, Argentina
Description: If you consider yourself to be a fan of Japanese cuisine, this is one of those restaurants you won’t want to miss out on. Located halfway between Palermo Hollywood and Colegiales, it is a brand with an international presence (Miami, Lima, Santiago de Chile, Quito, Bogotá, etc.) which impresses both for its size and its elegant and delightful contemporary decor, featuring a lively bar, impressive sushi bar, a plethora of wood in the dining room and an attractive terrace teeming with greenery. The cuisine on offer comes courtesy of its chef, Cindy Higa, who showcases the flavours of Peruvian-Japanese fusion cuisine built around superb ingredients. This is demonstrated on a reasonably extensive à la carte menu that includes dishes such as Wasabi Ceviche, Ebi Mentaiko (prawns, roasted rocoto cream and Parmesan) and, among the choice of desserts, a delicious Akaki Mango that plays with mango and passion fruit cream, apple sorbet with pisco and a coconut crunch. Added bonuses are highly professional service and valet parking.

Name: Osaki's
Address: 100 E. Meadow Dr., Unit 14, Vail, CO, 81657, USA
Description: Nestled within the storybook town of Vail, Osaki's is a tiny spot where just a handful of counter seats and a sprinkling of tables await diners. It's a classic sushi-ya in every way with a no-frills look but a laser-focus on the fish. After taking a seat, diners consult a whiteboard for the selections, enjoyed either as nigiri or sashimi. The quality shines through and isn't gussied up with superfluous sauces or flourishes. Indeed, their purist mentality is best seen in the selection, where offerings such as hagatsuo, not often found outside of very small regions in Japan, make an appearance. Japanese snow crab is sweet and meaty; akamutsu is silky; and buttery ankimo proves why it's given the nickname, "foie gras of the sea."

Name: Oscar
Description: Situated amid the fascinating 19C buildings in Ardenza, a district in the south of Livorno, Oscar is an excellent choice for anyone keen to enjoy simple, classic and traditional fish dishes with a focus on good quality – the sort of place where you would be more than happy to eat every day. And surely there’s no higher compliment than that!

Name: Oshikoji Okada
Description: The chef came to value the history and culture of Kyoto cuisine from a stint at a restaurant in Gion. The menu is a reflection of everyone who makes Kyoto cuisine possible: the wholesalers bringing together ingredients from the regions, the farmers growing Kyoto vegetables, the potters crafting a wide variety of tableware, and more. Combinations of food and vessels express the changing faces of nature. Dashi is made with water drawn from a spring every morning. The meal ends with handmade sweets. Guests are welcomed here with dishes prepared with great care.

Name: Osmose
Description: In Armentières, the hometown of popular French actor, Dany Boon, Osmose occupies the ground floor of a characteristic red-brick building not far from the town hall. The minimalist decor provides the perfect foil for polished cuisine that skilfully blends Northern French, Japanese and Nordic influences in a surprise menu that stars seasonal produce: crab, horseradish, aubergine, Artois trout, rhubarb…

Name: Osmosis
Description: Continuing to gain prominence, this restuarant, with an informal atmosphere and simple setup (there are more tables on the upper floor), is where chef John Ordóñez's imaginative proposal awakens a certain amount of interest, as it plays with surprising aromas and is not lacking in flavour either. He usually uses lots of ingredients, although these are kept well differentiated and without hiding their identity. You can order à la carte or opt for one of various set menus that change according to the number of courses. Don't miss their wonderful desserts!

Name: Osmossi - Maison Mavrommatis
Description: In a bright, contemporary bistro interior, upstairs from the delicatessen and wine shop, diners can feast on hot and cold mezze, pan-fried octopus with fava from Santorini or the ubiquitous moussaka. It's fresh and it’s tasty: what’s not to like?

Name: Osméra
Description: In Le Petit Bayonne neighbourhood, a couple who trained at the Ferrandi School in Bordeaux run this discreet restaurant, which they have refurbished in a pared-back style. Loïc cooks the savoury courses; Faustine, the daughter of a pastry chef, is on desserts. Together, using the finest local produce, they meticulously prepare flavoursome dishes – eg line-caught meagre and a medley of heirloom vegetables, Kintoa pork risotto and pickled chanterelles, followed by a superb apple dessert that leaves no doubt as to Faustine's talent.

Name: Osso
Address: Rua Bandeira Paulista, 520, São Paulo, 04532-001, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: An address that is much prized by meat-lovers in the Greater São Paulo area. Here, chef Renzo Garibaldi, who is known as the “Master Butcher” in his native Peru, has opened his first culinary venture in Brazil. His cuisine is based around meat sourced from sustainable producers, with the option of dry aged and different maturing times covering an array of different cuts. Beef is the star of the show here, available as ribeye, fillet mignon, picanha and short ribs, alongside special dry-aged pure Wagyu, Vaca Velha and Angus. Dishes such as ceviche, salad, Josper-grilled fish and the rice-based “arroz de costela” also feature on the menu in a modern, elegant space with an extensive and superb wine list.

Name: Ossobuco
Address: Sentral Wynwood, 62 N.W. 27th St., Miami, FL, 33127, USA
Description: Wynwood’s newest tenant is making some noise in an already-bustling zip code. From the glossy wood tables to the handsome bar, everything seems to shine under the spotlights. The dining room is anchored by a roaring, wood-burning grill, which turns out big proteins like smoked lamb chops with pistachio dukkah and charred, dry-aged steaks. Indeed, the steakhouse portion of the menu offers obvious appeal but so too do the lighter courses. Smoked baby beets with ricotta mousse is right on target, while the ossobuco empanada and sweetbreads with wagyu potato purée are the makings of a meal of their own. A stylish patio with a vibe of its own, a thoughtful cocktail list worth digging into, and a weekend DJ who knows how to work a room seal the deal.

Name: Ostaria
Address: Via Giovan Battista Perasso 10/12, Syracuse, 96100, Italy
Description: This restaurant in the centre of the modern city, yet just a stone’s throw from Ortigia, focuses exclusively on meat (local and from further afield, much of it aged on the premises), which is sourced from non-intensive farming and cooked using contemporary methods such as the Josper oven. The excellent wine list focuses mainly on Sicilian labels but also includes bottles from elsewhere in Italy, as well as from other important wine-producing countries. A typical Sicilian ambience, soft lighting in the evening and friendly yet professional service complete the picture.

Name: Ostaria da Gino
Description: This delightful family-run restaurant's enduring popularity among regulars is a testament to the unwavering dedication and passion that have been poured into its operations for the past 40 years. Authentic Italian cuisine is served in a laid-back setting with bags of charm! Staff will be happy to guide you through the options written up on the board and recommend the right wine. Tip: the moderately priced lunch deal. Delicatessen goods can be purchased to take home.

Name: Oste Scuro - Finsterwirt
Description: Run by the capable Mayr family, this long-established restaurant has occupied a narrow alleyway in the centre of Bressanone (Brixen) since the late 19C. The dining rooms are decorated in historic style, plus there’s a charming terrace for alfresco dining in summer. Dishes are presented on different tasting menus with the option of choosing traditional or Mediterranean dishes à la carte style – we highly recommend the soup made with Sylvaner wine from the Isarco valley, as well as the Tirtl (fried pie) stuffed with ricotta, spinach and cinnamon. Guestrooms are available in the nearby and recently renovated Adler Historic Guesthouse, which is run by the same owners.

Name: Osteria 1126
Description: Il Borgo di Cianciano is much more than just an osteria: it's also a farm, wine bar, and scattered hotel. The name “Osteria 1126” refers to the year of its founding; in the kitchen, a young couple offers simple, seasonal Tuscan dishes. Don't miss the pappa al pomodoro and the Chianti Classico Riserva, which is elegant and persistent. At the entrance of the borgo, a small aging cellar offers a brief but fascinating visit.

Name: Osteria 1861
Address: Via Valentino Izzo 1, Santa Maria di Castellabate, 84048, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Accessed via a narrow alleyway behind the beach, this restaurant housed in an old warehouse once used for smoking cured meats and drying Cilento figs boasts stone-vaulted ceilings, a romantic ambience and a small terrace embellished by beautiful plants. Chef Antoni Tafuri’s cuisine features on various tasting menus (including vegetarian and vegan) and an à la carte and demonstrates careful combinations that aim to showcase his regional ingredients to the full.

Name: Osteria Al GiGianca
Description: Although the out - of - town location is a slight drawback, this restaurant passionately run has a welcoming atmosphere. Seasonal, regional cuisine, plus a good choice of wine and beers.

Name: Osteria Angelina
Address: 1 Nicholls Clarke Yard, London, E1 6SH, United Kingdom
Description: Whereas the original Japanese-Italian Angelina in Dalston is centred around a kaiseki-style set menu, here at the more casual and bigger Osteria, the focus is more on grilling over binchotan and the flexibility of a sizeable à la carte. Start with the delicious Hokkaido milk bread, followed by the likes of cod cheek karaage, fazzoletti with duck ragu and grilled dishes such as Church Hill chicken. Order the house fries too, and watch the covetous looks from your fellow diners. You can face the open kitchen counter in the cool, post-industrial room or watch the chefs at work in the ‘pasta lab’.

Name: Osteria Antica
Address: 6F, The Podium, 18 ADB Avenue, Ortigas Centre, Mandaluyong - Metro Manila, The Philippines
Description: This Italian restaurant playfully experiments – think bruschetta topped with mango – to deliver a fresh yet satisfying twist on familiar dishes. In addition to pasta, seafood and meats, more traditional pizzas arrive from the open kitchen, with tasty smoky crusts. Their tiramisu, too, strays from tradition but retains that home-made feel. Exposed brick walls evoke Tuscan charm, and diners can enjoy the city views from this sixth-floor perch in the mall.

Name: Osteria Antico Brolo
Description: Situated in the upper part of the town near the Vittoriale estate, this rustic 18C building is the setting for regional cuisine prepared using seasonal ingredients. The charming small courtyard offers shade for summer dining, while the interior dining room also includes a single table on a small balcony which needs to be booked well in advance.

Name: Osteria Arborina
Description: Arborina Relais is a delightful retreat tucked away among Italy's most prestigious vineyards. Time here seems to slow down to make room for pleasure: a modern and refined location, where every detail speaks of passion and care. The cuisine takes you on a sensory journey, combining technique and creativity to deliver unique experiences. The “no waste” concept becomes a philosophy, turning every ingredient into a pure harmony of flavours. You will be surprised by two tasting menus, with 5 or 8 courses, designed to excite and amaze with every bite. Completing the picture is a wine list that celebrates Piedmont, ready to accompany every moment with elegance and character.

Name: Osteria Ardenga
Description: An authentic trattoria which is a joy to visit, where time seems to have stood still for decades. Situated on the border between two provinces, the restaurant focuses on specialities from Parma, many of which are made from home - grown produce. Homemade pickles and chutneys are also sold here.

Name: Osteria Bellavista
Address: Via Piovega 30, località Farra, Paderno del Grappa, 31017, Italy
Description: At Osteria Bellavista, the menu is recited: Paolo and Raffaele, father and son, will guide you through the dishes of the day, prepared with excellent ingredients and authentic passion. The cuisine? A tribute to tradition, between sea and land, with a contemporary touch that surprises without betraying its roots.

Name: Osteria Bertaina
Description: Overlooking the picturesque square in the city’s oldest quarter, medieval in origin, the restaurant welcomes guests through the porticoes, leading them into two intimate dining rooms of vintage charm, with frescoed ceilings dating to the early twentieth century. The cuisine delivers on every level: Piedmontese recipes are reinterpreted with a modern, lighter touch without betraying their soul. Among the must-try dishes, our inspector highlights the gobbo cardoon prepared according to grandmother’s family recipe. And if indecision takes hold, trust the advice of the young, energetic and knowledgeable dining room manager, always ready to guide you toward the ideal path.

Name: Osteria Billis
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace
Description: Almost ten years after it opened, this restaurant run by the Billis twins is moving towards what its owners describe as a “new tradition” – a personalised way of interpreting local traditions through the lens of global influences. While maintaining roots in solid Piedmontese traditions, the cuisine combines local ingredients with international techniques. Examples include “roasted rice”, a dish which is cooked in the oven and then flavoured according to the season and whim of the chef, and the “Carpaccio in Ramino”, beef which is lightly seared in a copper pan with rosemary, bay leaf, salt and pepper. The veranda’s retro ambience immediately catches the eye of passersby in the nearby park, adding to the appeal of this fascinating building dating from the early 20C.

Name: Osteria Boccolicchio
Description: Having gained experience in various restaurants throughout Europe, Tespi has now returned home to open this delightful small osteria in the historic centre, just a stone’s throw from the sea. His huge passion for fish is evident from the menu, where fish dishes feature in numerous regionally influenced recipes. The excellent wine cellar includes a good choice of sparkling wines.

Name: Osteria Borgo Ronche
Description: With only a handful of tables – all the more reason to reserve – and a contemporary, streamlined yet welcoming setting, this intimate spot showcases the chef-owner’s resolutely seafood-focused cuisine, though a couple of meat options round out the menu. Preparations and pairings remain largely classic, as seen in the gratinéed Breton scallops, while raw seafood also makes an appearance, sometimes unexpectedly atop pasta, as in the standout spaghettoni with cacio e pepe and red prawn tartare.

Name: Osteria Casale Ferrovia
Address: via Stazione 1, sulla SP 34, Carovigno, 72012, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in what was once the 20C dwelling of an old olive mill, this restaurant boasts elegant decor, including a few antique family pieces and Art Deco - style tables. The female owner - chef prepares light and modern dishes with a regional flavour, while the wine list also showcases the best of Puglia. As the name suggests, the railway lies to the rear of the property, although there’s very little noise and no disturbance at all.

Name: Osteria Cascina dei Fiori
Description: This restaurant’s warm, elegant and rustic atmosphere with wooden furniture and exposed beams provides the setting for its seasonally inspired, regional cuisine. The experienced owners are welcoming and attentive, while the menu features specialities such as frogs’ leg and courgette flower risotto.

Name: Osteria Dalie e Fagioli
Address: via Campagnola 45, Manerba del Garda, 25080, Italy
Description: One of the best restaurants in the region, where you’ll enjoy eclectic cuisine full of convincing flavours which is inspired by various regional traditions (especially those from Brescia, but also from elsewhere in Italy) which always hits the mark.

Name: Osteria Del Centro
Description: This small, very friendly restaurant offers a successful mix of tradition (the setting is an old house in the centre of Comano), minimalist furnishings and modern cuisine. In the evening, enjoy a surprise tasting menu (five or seven courses) which is almost entirely vegetarian, with the option of choosing your main course. 95% of the ingredients are organic and the owner-chef will be happy to discuss his philosophy on organic food during the course of your meal. The elegant, original dishes include options such as beef wellington with kohlrabi, chimichurri and mushrooms, accompanied by artisanal wines from Switzerland and further afield.

Name: Osteria Dell'Unione
Description: In the heart of the Langhe del Barbaresco, this osteria preserves the convivial spirit of traditional establishments from times past. The atmosphere is warm and familial, while aromas and flavors immediately evoke the home cooking of recipes handed down through generations, and prepared to order. The menu celebrates the cornerstones of authentic tradition: from free-range chicken cacciatore to the soft, celebrated spinach frittatas, dishes deceptively simple in appearance, yet revealing a precise hand respectful of Piedmontese culinary heritage. The wine list, well-structured and fairly priced, accompanies the meal in a natural manner. In warmer months, the vine-shaded pergola becomes the ideal setting for a meal of rustic, genuine charm.

Name: Osteria Erbaluce
Description: Just steps from the Leonardo-designed canal harbor, this spot takes a bold stance: it serves only meat, with a strong focus on the grill. Quality ingredients, fresh pastas, and classic house-made spoon desserts. An excellent wine list, especially strong on reds, rounds out the offering. The dining room is bright and all white; the cool, tranquil outdoor terrace is very welcoming, ideal in the warmer months. At the helm is a young couple driven by passion and professionalism.

Name: Osteria Ester
Address: 629 E. Central Blvd., Orlando, FL, 32801, USA
Description: Located in the Thornton Park neighborhood of Orlando, this stylish space offers plenty of charm. Chef Michael Cooper's Italian American menu delivers the classics (think chicken parm) albeit with some swagger. Start the meal with one of their delicious house-made breads like the gnocco fritto, an Italian fry bread, before tucking into truffle arancini in a rich fonduta sauce. Their house-made pastas are always a hit, as in the bucatini diabolo with its spicy garlic-forward sauce. Round out the meal with butterscotch budino, a classic caramel silky pudding finished with hazelnuts and whipped cream.

Name: Osteria Europa
Description: Despite its simple appearance, this restaurant housed in the hotel of the same name serves interesting, traditional cuisine which is well prepared and full of flavour.

Name: Osteria Fernanda
Address: via Crescenzo Del Monte 18/24, Rome, 00153, Italy
Description: In the district famous for its Porta Portese market, this restaurant run by two talented business partners is definitely worth a visit. Andrea oversees the minimalist-style dining room, while Luca demonstrates real passion in his creative cuisine made from locally sourced ingredients, as well as produce from further afield. Among the desserts, we highly recommended the Porter beer ice-cream with black garlic mousse, chocolate and tuber peelings.

Name: Osteria Ferrara
Description: Foodies flock here safe in the knowledge they have found sanctuary in an elegant interior that sets the stage for culinary magic. Sicilian chef Fabrizio Ferrara concocts a menu of tasty and well-crafted ingredient-led Italian recipes, such as fried courgette flowers, stuffed with mussels and parsley-spiked mussel jus, or ravioli stuffed with ewe’s milk ricotta, raw langoustines and shellfish jus. A bistro with soul and an appealing wine list to boot.

Name: Osteria Forno Ercole
Description: Hidden among the alleyways of Jesi, Osteria Forno Ercole is a former bakery (part of which can still be seen) which serves authentic cuisine in a warm, welcoming atmosphere. Local recipes and Mediterranean flavours come together on the traditional menu, with a focus on seasonal ingredients of the highest quality. Tagliatelle with porcini mushrooms, Marche-style fritto misto and steak with carrots, potatoes and radicchio are just some of the dishes on the menu here.

Name: Osteria FraSe
Address: Via Crociata 9, Piove di Sacco, 35028, Italy
Description: In this restaurant, husband Francesco takes care of the wine, while his wife Serena is at the helm in the open-view kitchen, creating dishes with a focus on fish and seafood (including raw options), fresh pasta dishes and classic recipes with the occasional imaginative twist or the addition of exotic fruit. This is a modern and welcoming osteria with a simple decor, where the female staff provide excellent service with a friendly smile.

Name: Osteria Frangipane
Address: via Maraldo da Trani 5, Trani, 76125, Italy
Description: The owners' smiling welcome immediately puts customers at their ease, in a very pleasant contemporary tavern setting with light colours and vaulted ceilings. The Inspector recommends: codfish mantecato with walnut bread, bell pepper cream and caper mayonnaise; risotto with broad beans, hairy mussels and pecorino cheese from Foggia.

Name: Osteria Funkcoolio
Address: ​La Cote B03 -R04, ​Port De La Mer, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,No alcohol served,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: When a French bistro de luxe meets itameshi (a blend of Japanese and Italian cuisine), you get this intimate spot overlooking the marina in the Port de la Mere neighbourhood. Take a seat in one of three horseshoe booths and order an array of appetisers, homemade pastas, pizzas with toppings – like veal ragu or spicy duck and sriracha – and various meats and fish dishes. End your meal with their twist on a tiramisu that comes wrapped in a cover of soft meringue. Be sure to explore their selection of alcohol-free wines and spirits to complement the experience.

Name: Osteria Giorgione da Masa
Address: Calle Larga dei Proverbi, 4582/A, Venice, 30121, Italy
Description: Just steps from Campo Santi Apostoli, Chef Masa weaves together homestyle Japanese traditions with Venetian cicchetti, transcending the classic distinction between courses: here, dishes arrive all at once, without rules. For those who prefer to be guided, there’s a tasting menu offering a wide array of bites. Desserts are a true surprise, especially the yogurt, caramel, and matcha mousse, a favorite of our inspector.

Name: Osteria Grande
Description: This restaurant overlooking the magnificent Piazza Grande and the Loggia Vasariana that takes up one whole side of the square was opened in the summer of 2022 by the enthusiastic Fatjon and Lorenzo (if you ask, they’ll happily share their knowledge of Arezzo’s history with you). The former is at the helm in the kitchen where he expresses his passion for cuisine in seasonal, contemporary-style dishes such as pigeon breast, leg and fillet (each cut is prepared in the appropriate way) served with sweet onion and cocoa nibs, while the latter oversees the wine selection and recommends suitable pairings to guests. For the chef’s pigeon speciality, he may, for example, suggest an original Maturato Tiberini 2018 (a white wine made from grapes that are left to ripen on the vine). Cocktail staff are also hand for guests keen to choose an aperitif or an after-dinner drink from the extensive cocktail list.

Name: Osteria Il Bagatto
Address: via XX Settembre 16, Limone Piemonte, 12015, Italy
Description: Nestled amid the stone houses of Limone Piemonte, this charming gourmet restaurant is situated in a typical historic passageway. Influenced by the seasons and the chef’s creative skills, the menu includes interesting dishes such as char, gnocchi with blue goat’s cheese and delicious sweetbreads in butter with cannellini beans and cavolo nero. To accompany your meal, you might like to indulge in a bottle of vintage Barolo chosen from the concise yet carefully chosen wine list. The 2013 Michele Chiarlo Barolo Cerequio, produced in a cold and rainy year, has aged well thanks to its powerful tannins.

Name: Osteria Il Cappello
Description: The outdoor terrace at this restaurant overlooks a pleasant pedestrian piazza in the historic centre, while the welcoming dining rooms are decorated in a style typical of the Trentino. The cuisine – reliable, seasonal and full of flavour – is traditionally Italian, yet with a contemporary touch. The menu also features a few regional options as well as the occasional fish dish. The quail stuffed with acacia honey, pumpkin purée and stewed radicchio is superb.

Name: Osteria Il Granaio
Address: via dei Monaci, Rapolano Terme, 53040, Italy
Description: Although it calls itself an osteria, Il Granaio is really a restaurant. It has elegant brick - arched dining rooms occupying a 17C palazzo in the historic centre of Rapolano. On the menu you will find Tuscan specialities such as pici pasta cooked with various sauces, peppery Tuscan beef stew and a selection of fish dishes.

Name: Osteria Il Maialetto
Address: via Della Repubblica 348, Monsummano Terme, 51015, Italy
Description: Next to the historic family butcher’s shop lies the vibrant tavern, which is approaching its 100th anniversary without losing any of its surprisingly youthful spirit. People come here to enjoy authentic, straightforward Tuscan cuisine: from bruschetta and crostini to pappa al pomodoro and ribollita, via platters of charcuterie and Florentine steak – which, naturally, will bump up the bill a little.The warm hospitality that characterises the place makes the experience even more enjoyable.

Name: Osteria Il Principe e Il Pirata
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: This restaurant is housed in a typical island house with rustic furniture and a large terrace with sea views. Here, the Casano family look after guests, are responsible for the impressive wine list and, of course, prepare the cuisine that focuses on top-quality ingredients and Sicilian recipes. Specialities include couscous with fresh fish and vegetables, cuttlefish “alla fiamma” and courgettes marinated in mint, as well as typical desserts such as the “bacio pantesco”.

Name: Osteria Ime
Description: In this pretty, welcoming restaurant, the female chef from Albania, who has adopted Italian culinary traditions over her many years in the country, serves a choice of tasting menus. Her dishes have distinct geographical names and are full of colour and prepared from top-quality ingredients which change with the passing seasons. There are only a few tables available, so booking ahead is always a good idea. You’ll be warmly welcomed with a friendly smile that sets the tone for what is sure to be a highly enjoyable evening.

Name: Osteria L'Abbiccì
Address: via Medici da Seregno 29, Seregno, 20831, Italy
Description: Situated in the centre of Seregno, this modern inn boasts a bright, spacious dining room with an ambience which is both friendly and yet respectful of guests’ privacy. The cuisine is overseen by Davide, who trained with Mauro Elli, the owner-chef of Il Cantuccio in Albavilla. Here, he creates dishes full of character, with a focus on top-quality ingredients and skilful presentation techniques. For a memorable dining experience, the chef’s surprise menu makes an excellent choice. Impressive wine selection and professional service overseen by Gabriele add to the appeal. The business lunch offers excellent value for money.

Name: Osteria L'Orciaia
Description: Osteria l’Orciaia is a little treasure trove of authentic flavors, where true Tuscan cuisine is celebrated in a rustic and well-crafted setting. In the summer, dining is outdoors with breathtaking views of the hills; in winter, guests retreat to a cozy room featuring exposed stone, wood, and artisanal details. The peposo is a must-try: intense, traditional, and irresistible!

Name: Osteria La Fenice
Description: A slice of Italy in Cuxhaven! Behind a rather unassuming façade on a busy shopping street, a truly welcoming osteria ambiance awaits – the decor features decorative wine racks, closely spaced marble tables and even a Vespa! Not to forget the authentic Italian cuisine made with high-quality, fresh ingredients – the sourdough bread and pasta are both made in-house. The wine list showcases Italian labels. Tip: Italian food items can be purchased to take home.

Name: Osteria La Sangiovesa
Address: piazza Beato Simone Balacchi 14, Santarcangelo di Romagna, 47822, Italy
Description: History pervades this eighteenth-century palazzo, but above all it is the soul of Romagna that fills the air, its friendly welcome, through rooms that overflow with warmth and atmosphere. The cooking is, naturally, of the local area, with cured meats, pasta, meat dishes and excellent desserts holding uncontested sway.

Name: Osteria Langhe
Address: 2824 W. Armitage Ave., Chicago, IL, 60647, USA
Description: Open since 2014, this osteria has become an area staple, thanks to its charming space and focused menu that displays a keen eye on hearty Piedmontese cuisine. The staff is as welcoming as the design, which features a garage-like glass façade, glowing bulbs that protrude from the walls, bare wood tables and metal chairs lining the floor.For starters, we’re partial to the thin slivers of poached beef arranged around a tangy tonnato, but just as tempting is the cauliflower and leek flan. Pastas are, of course, made-in house and the specialty is no doubt the tajarin, a plate of deliciously eggy noodles twirled high with a savory ragù. Other regional specialties include hand-pinched ravioli stuffed with la tur cheese as well as prosciutto-wrapped rabbit loin.

Name: Osteria Locatelli at the National Gallery
Address: Sainsbury Wing, The National Gallery, Trafalgar Square, St James’s, London, WC2N 5DN, United Kingdom
Description: You know what you’re getting just from the name: an outstanding location inside the National Gallery’s renovated Sainsbury Wing, partnered with Italian fare overseen by famed chef Giorgio Locatelli. Quite a few notches above your usual museum café, here you can pair your Botticelli with burrata and your Titian with tiramisu – all executed by an able team. Handmade pasta is a particular highlight, such as the cappellacci stuffed with peas. Downstairs, you’ll find a bar for coffee and freshly baked maritozzi.

Name: Osteria Luca
Description: Al dente spaghetti with briny clams and finely chopped parsley, fork-tender ossobuco in a knockout sauce or iconic classics of the likes of vitello tonnato or grandma’s rabbit stew: Chef Luca is a champion of down-to-earth, honest Italian nosh that he crafts with lashings of sensitivity and nuance. Mediterranean tradition sets the tone of the enticing set and à la carte menus, while a buzzy vibe and on the ball, cheerful service underscore this osteria’s warm welcome; the front is cosier than the flower-decked area near the kitchen. Buzzy Osteria Luca has added a cheerful vibrant dimension to this peaceful village.

Name: Osteria Lucio
Address: The Malting Tower, Grand Canal Dock, Clanwilliam Terrace, Dublin City, D02 DW90, Ireland
Description: Located under the railway arches, this elegant restaurant comes with a lively ambience and a roll-call of recognisable Italian dishes. You could start proceedings with bruschetta or arancini before moving onto a choice of pastas, while suckling pig cooked 'al forno' has become something of a signature. Each dish is prepared with care using quality produce and in turn delivers plenty of flavour. The food is accompanied by an all-Italian wine list and a good selection of cocktails.

Name: Osteria Lupo
Address: 4609 Magazine St., New Orleans, LA, 70115, USA
Description: Wood-fired Italian? Yes, please. This restaurant off busy Magazine Street has a sleek, yet classic elegance and a menu that pleases practically everyone. From pizza dough and pasta to ice cream, it's all made in house, every day. First up, a salad of charred corn and okra with goat cheese and honey paprika vinaigrette is layered with flavor. Then, delicate mortadella-stuffed tortellini in a savory broth or fregola studded with 'nduja, cherry tomato and arrabbiata sauce topped with scallops are vying for your attention. Why choose just one —order both.

Name: Osteria Manzoni
Description: This restaurant housed within a colourful, skilfully restored historic building with exposed stonework has a young friendly couple at the helm. The menu features delicious, refined and traditional Italian cuisine.

Name: Osteria Matto
Description: Chef Thomas Asti has Italian blood running through his veins. So, it made sense when he and his partner opened this bistro-styled trattoria. The duo draws on Italy’s glorious culinary heritage to the delight of their loyal regulars, who flock here to sample vitello tonnato, bagna cauda, veal with house-made potato gnocchi – and Sicilian lemon tart, just the way nonna used to make it. To be washed down with premium Italian wines. What’s not to like?

Name: Osteria Mercato
Description: Tucked slightly away from the city’s main tourist paths, behind the lanes of the historical center, this restaurant presents a contemporary setting with a distinctly customized décor. The cuisine moves confidently between land and sea: from ravioli filled with “farmyard” meats, nettles, and cardoncelli mushrooms to skewered octopus with mussels and a saffron broth, with room for a touch of creativity as well. Excellent attention is paid to sourcing local ingredients, and in the warmer months, the outdoor terrace is fresh and pleasant.

Name: Osteria Mercede
Description: For over ten years this welcoming trattoria has delighted its guests with a vibrant seafood cuisine steeped in Sicilian and Mediterranean character. In the dining room, a blackboard of daily specials invites guests to choose between recipes of solid local tradition and offerings that celebrate the sea with simplicity and personality. Among the house must-tries, the delicious bruschette del marinaio stand out: a trio of swordfish and aubergine caponata, marinated anchovies and amberjack carpaccio with salt and tuna bottarga, a perfect expression of the venue’s true calling. Also well worth trying is the “Caciucco Mercede”, rich and fragrant, prepared with John Dory, scorpionfish, sea bass, prawns and squid. And to close on a sweet note, room must be left for the desserts, in particular the “Scannolo”, a deconstructed and highly accomplished interpretation of the classic Sicilian cannolo.

Name: Osteria Mood
Address: Via Cesare Battisti 58, San Bartolomeo al Mare, 18016, Italy
Description: Situated just a few minutes from the seafront promenade in a quiet, residential district, this restaurant with a relaxing ambience serves delicious Ligurian cuisine with a focus on organic vegetables, fish and seafood (local whenever possible), and home-made bread, desserts and fresh pasta. In summer, meals are served by the swimming pool in the garden, while in winter, the welcoming covered veranda boasts extensive sea views.

Name: Osteria Mozza
Address: Hilton Orchard, Level 5, 333 Orchard Road, 238867, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: After a hiatus, the first Asian outpost of celebrity chef Nancy Silverton’s famed establishment Osteria Mozza reopened, now in a modern, rustic setting with a lively and inviting vibe. The small lunch menu features antipasti, salads, pizza and house-made pasta. The dinner menu steps up a gear to include her signature mozzarella dishes and other Italian specialties. The impressive wine list covers 280 labels from different regions of Italy.

Name: Osteria Numero Sette
Description: There’s been a recent change in management at this informal, friendly restaurant which serves generously portioned, carefully prepared dishes from the region and elsewhere in Italy, all at highly competitive prices. Although the cuisine might not be particularly modern, this is good solid cuisine served in a welcoming atmosphere.

Name: Osteria Orzo
Description: Osteria Orzo continues to offer an authentic taste of a casual and cozy Italian osteria at its Hannam-dong location. Signature offerings on the menu include the white ragù pasta which features home-made fresh pasta drenched in rich meat sauce with mascarpone cheese and truffles. The spicy tagliatelle and the seafood tartare are also among the restaurant's all-time favorites. Reserve a table across from the open kitchen and watch the chefs in action.

Name: Osteria Ottanta Sette
Description: Franciacorta is a sparkling wine from Italy’s Lombardy region. The couple who run this osteria used to run one back in Italy and now offer both Lombardy wines and cuisine. Dishes are faithful to tradition: risotto is made with Carnaroli rice; pasta is served al dente. The number ‘87’ in Italian is ‘ottanta sette’. This is a play on the phrase ‘ho tanta sete’, meaning ‘I’m thirsty’. Wet your whistle on some Italian bubbly.

Name: Osteria Padre Pio
Address: 97 Lake St., West Harrison, NY, 10603, USA
Description: Naming a restaurant after a saintly miracle worker is a bold move but there's a reason why locals keep coming back. Chef Andrea Ingenito is onto something, and is supremely dedicated to offering a true Campanian experience to guests. The interior is inviting and charming, matched only by the warm hospitality and carefully crafted dishes. Nearly everything is made from scratch here, where each table is given a beautiful wooden board loaded with room-temperature caponatina and plenty of house-made focaccia. It's tempting, but but don't fill up, and don't skip the specials. From the baked corvina to the silky pappardelle, come hungry to enjoy hearty portions, then order a house-made limoncello to accompany your dessert.

Name: Osteria Porta Sud
Description: Walk through the heritage Passage Zuidpoort and you will come to this fine example of Dutch interwar architecture. The first impression is enchanting: curved woodwork, the bar, the tiled floor and the colourful glass details. Yonna and Ralph keep their modern osteria intimate to preserve its Italian soul. Quality ingredients and those characteristic Mediterranean nuances are prepared with finesse and a contemporary edge. Highlights include a vibrant and unique take on vitello tonnato with the depth of a veal-jus-based vinaigrette and house-made agnolotti stuffed with mushroom, chestnut and hazelnut, finished with vegetable jus and truffle – familiar flavours which the chefs subtly inject with their own character.

Name: Osteria Ricanatti
Description: This cozy little restaurant, backed by attentive and impeccably polished service, reveals a regional cuisine that is both flavorful and thoughtfully reinterpreted, available through several tasting menus as well as à la carte. Ingredient sourcing is exacting, with all vegetables harvested from the family’s garden just a few kilometers away – a guarantee of freshness and seasonality. Among the most representative dishes: the pecorino and potato tartare dressed with chimichurri, Argentina’s signature green sauce, or the perfectly al dente paccheri with a two-tomato coulis, raw bluefin tuna, and fried capers – a plate that strikes an ideal balance of intensity and harmony.

Name: Osteria Romana
Description: Don’t even try to resist the appeal of this Osteria Romana - you will be bowled over by the romantic allure of the mansion, the cocktail bar and the immaculate tailored service. Roman specialties and tableside preparations set the scene. Delicacies include Roman-Jewish deep-fried artichoke, carbonara pasta, pasta with tuna tartare, pepperoncino, combava and ginger in a lineup whose subtlety, generosity and flavour are to die for! What more proof do you need that Italians do it better!

Name: Osteria Saint Martin
Description: In the historic centre of Zagarolo, the simple and intimate dining room hosts an excellent cuisine that draws upon certain Lazio elements in both produce and recipes, yet also embraces deliberate influences born of the chef’s wealth of experience. This is a gastronomic destination not to be missed, particularly if one wishes to experience cookery that is less traditional and incorporates more exotic ingredients, or at least those not strictly local in character. Tables are limited, so we recommend booking ahead, while in fine weather one may take a seat on the charming terrace.

Name: Osteria San Gallo
Description: This agreeably lively little osteria stands on the edge of the pedestrian precinct, with a terrace area in front of the entrance. The attractive interior is comfortable, with simple bistro chairs, polished wooden tables and an open kitchen. An ambitious team cooks up authentic Italian dishes – try, for example, the "gnocchetti di Mamma Bruna" – house-made potato gnocchetti al ragù della casa – or sea bass "alla spigola in sinfonia mediterranea". At lunchtime, options are more limited but include short set menus for a quick lunch.

Name: Osteria Savio Volpe
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Clean and contemporary, with white marble and modern light fixtures, Osteria Savio Volpe could easily fit right in on a street in Milan, Naples or Rome. Simple materials, including red-and-brown tiles and a muted palette, set a modern tone for cuisine that takes inspiration from the regions of Italy while balancing authenticity and expectations. Dig in to warm and tender garlic knots studded with black pepper and a thatch of grated pecorino. Sop up every last dot of the piquant marinara—it's worth the additional charge. Thinly sliced beef carpaccio is plated in traditional fashion, then topped with a flavorful leek-accented aioli, and creste di gallo is an ideal pasta for the richly flavored lamb ragu with zippy sage and pecorino.

Name: Osteria Scottadito
Address: Torri Ta Kenuna, Nadur, NDR 1436, Malta
Description: Scottadito is an osteria that champions Italian food culture without compromise: starters such as sardoncini scottadito, crumbed and oven-baked, and classic pasta dishes like carbonara rub shoulders with more regional specialities, including gnocchi with rabbit ragù, all designed to delight. The setting is simple and informal, lifted by the owner’s warmth and his talent for offering spot-on recommendations.

Name: Osteria Stella
Description: This osteria, just outside the town, has a long history and recently reopened its doors in 2024 thanks to a duo of young chefs who, after numerous experiences elsewhere, chose to breathe new life into it with a pleasantly contemporary atmosphere and cuisine that narrates the territory through regional recipes poised between Liguria and Piedmont, enriched by passion and modern technique. Not to be missed are the gnocco filled with pesto and pine nut sauce and the guinea fowl prepared in the Ligurian manner with triple-cooked potatoes, dishes that sincerely express their vision of updated tradition.

Name: Osteria Taviani
Address: Via del Monte Ovest 25, Bientina, 56031, Italy
Description: Housed in a small Art Nouveau-style villa, this restaurant boasts an elegant yet warm and friendly ambience. The cuisine here is modern and full of flavour, with a focus on meat dishes (although a few fish options also feature) with their roots firmly anchored in Tuscan traditions (such as the fried steak). During the hunting season, the contemporary-style game dishes are particularly delicious. The wine list includes a few French labels, plus there’s a small, attractive outdoor space in the courtyard to the rear which overlooks a beautiful garden.

Name: Osteria Terra Arsa
Description: The two Murani brothers offer compelling reason to venture into this unremarkable neighbourhood east of Foggia’s centre: their cooking. The fresh and colourful dining rooms anticipate a style that finds full expression on the plate, where fragrant and flavourful tastes reveal themselves. The recipes, sometimes inspired by family memories, take shape from Puglian and seasonal ingredients, further elevated by vegetables from their own garden. An exception is salt cod – to which an entire tasting menu is dedicated – yet it remains perfectly in keeping with local tradition: the oven-baked version is excellent, with savoury breadcrumbs, served on a cream of Carpino broad beans and sautéed chicory. The wine list is entirely regional, a coherent choice that completes the experience with authenticity.

Name: Osteria Vecchia Noce
Description: This former 18C mill, located in the centre of a tiny medieval district on the outskirts of Uliveto Terme, boasts a warm, elegant ambience full of character. Expertly run by the same family for the past 35 years, it serves honest, traditional cuisine with a focus on regional recipes and an equal balance of meat and fish.

Name: Osteria Vecchio Borgo
