Description: Described as a “meeting point between Piedmont and Liguria”, this quiet, welcoming restaurant in the historic centre of Cuneo focuses on ingredients and recipes from these two regions – the family, all of whom are involved in the restaurant (the women in the kitchen and the men front of house), are from Liguria. The generous, top-quality cuisine is prepared using seasonal produce with a personalised touch and is accompanied by a good selection of wine, also available by the glass.

Name: Osteria a "Le Due Spade"
Address: Via Don Arcangelo Rizzi 11, Trento, 38122, Italy
Description: This beautiful Stube-style restaurant in the city centre has existed since the Council of Trent, with a succession of chefs and owners serving food here ever since the 16C. Still run with skill and expertise today, the restaurant boasts a small, intimate Alpine-style dining room where Trento specialities (char, apple strudel with vanilla ice cream) are served alongside typical Italian fare (risotto with mussel power and parsley pesto). All the dishes are cooked with an imaginative touch, resulting in a perfect balance of tradition and modernity!

Name: Osteria alla Chiesa
Description: Genuine warmth in the dining room and interiors that recall the inns of old: the building is historic, and the discreet creak of the wooden staircase contributes to a d’antan atmosphere. Among the most intriguing offerings is a raviolo accompanied by fried artichokes and a sweetbread “carpaccio,” completed by an almond sauce that rounds the dish with gentle, measured succulence.

Name: Osteria alle Testiere
Address: Calle del Mondo Novo, sestiere Castello 5801, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: This restaurant, now one of the most popular bistros in Venice, started out as a typical Venetian “bacaro”. The cuisine focuses on traditional Mediterranean and Venetian dishes, including vegetables, many of which are grown in a kitchen garden on Sant'Erasmo island (Osti in Orto) – an initiative which sees a number of small restaurants coming together to grow and share produce. The menu changes in line with market availability. With just a few tables, booking well in advance is highly recommended.

Name: Osteria da Afro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An expertly run family restaurant not far from the historic centre. Warm atmosphere in the two dining rooms (especially the one with the fireplace), where the daily specials are marked on a blackboard. A real gem of restaurant, which also has a few charming guestrooms furnished in fir and cherry wood.

Name: Osteria da Cippi
Description: A corner that is simply out of this world, tucked away in a delightful chalet with a fireplace that smells of wood and warmth. The cuisine celebrates local produce in tune with the seasons: wild herbs from Valdestali in spring, vegetables from the kitchen garden in summer, and fruits from the surrounding woods in autumn. Delicacies include lasagnetta with venison ragout and chanterelle mushrooms, cjarsons and antique apple strudel with vanilla ice cream. There is only one tasting menu, and reservations must be made at least two days in advance.

Name: Osteria da Fiore
Address: calle del Scaleter, sestiere San Polo 2202/a, Venice, 30125, Italy
Description: Among a labyrinth of alleys and canals, stands the trattoria Da Fiore, elegant and with a family atmosphere. The main hall warmly welcomes guests, while a romantic terrace hosts a table for two by the canal. The cuisine, true to the land, will allow you to enjoy fried moleche [soft-shell crabs] (when in season): an experience not to be missed! Last but not least, there is the wine cellar, which has a fine selection of the most sought-after French and Italian wines (about 800 labels). Equally impressive is the selection of grappas, cognacs and whiskies.

Name: Osteria da Nando
Description: Operating since 1957 in the heart of the historic center, Nando is a go-to spot for those wanting to experience Valdostan cuisine: excellent cured meats (usually served with the famous fontina), polenta and fondue, fondue bourguignonne, rustic polenta tart with goat milk gelato... all prepared with top-quality ingredients and served in a simple yet atmospheric setting. The wine selection is excellent, focusing mainly on the Aosta Valley, with over 100 different labels, many of which are available by the glass. Among the desserts, the rothia is a must-try: white wine custard, spiced bread, and a sprinkle of cinnamon – intense, rich, and delicious.

Name: Osteria dai Coghi
Address: via Alcide De Gasperi 9/13, Albarè di Costermano, 37010, Italy
Description: This well-kept, welcoming restaurant with a colourful decor and wine bottles adorning the walls serves imaginative dishes with modern combinations – our inspector particularly enjoyed the guinea fowl supreme with smoked black tea, carrots and beluga lentils. The well-chosen wine list features labels from Italy and further afield.

Name: Osteria dai Mazzeri
Description: Once the town hall of Follina, this building dating from 1704 is now home to a restaurant run by two brothers who serve delicious regional and seasonal cuisine here (in winter, don’t miss the spit-roasted chicken, veal or pork cooked according to local tradition). A beautiful mulberry tree, the old symbol of the village that was once involved in the silk industry, graces the outdoor dining space.

Name: Osteria dalla Peppa
Description: A trattoria in the old town, with rooms filled with memories and nostalgia, offering an atmosphere that makes you feel at home, just like the traditional cuisine. The fresh-egg pasta rolled out with a rolling pin (also on sale in their nearby shop) is the main attraction here, with main courses featuring various types of meat, and fish dishes on Fridays.

Name: Osteria de l'Umbreleèr
Description: Situated in Cicognolo in the Lower Po valley, where early morning mists create an evocative atmosphere in autumn, this traditional restaurant with a rustic feel serves specialities from Lombardy with a focus on delicious starters and top-quality meat. Our inspector particularly recommends the white onion gratin soup and the Burgundy-style snails. A simpler menu is available at lunchtime and there’s a small garden for alfresco dining on summer evenings.

Name: Osteria de' Mercati
Description: Slightly set back from the bustling streets of the historic centre yet still in the heart of the town, this delightful small restaurant is a recent addition to Sassari. It boasts a modern, elegant decor, friendly staff and a menu featuring carefully prepared fresh, seasonal dishes. Our inspector particularly recommends the seafood risotto. A choice of regional wines completes the picture.

Name: Osteria degli Angeli
Description: An attractive restaurant which offers a friendly and informal welcome and service, alongside an elegant, personalised yet classic decor. The cuisine is mainly Mediterranean in flavour, emphasised by the use of local and seasonal ingredients. The self-taught chef here is passionate about his cuisine.

Name: Osteria dei Vespri
Address: piazza Croce dei Vespri 6, Palermo, 90133, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Situated in the palazzo where the famous ball scene in the “The Leopard” by Luchino Visconti was filmed, this restaurant serves cuisine that moves with the times, featuring modern dishes made from local ingredients, while a friendly welcome from the long-established owners adds to the appeal. Cocktails, tapas and simpler yet equally delicious cuisine is served in the Occhiovivo! Bistrot next door, the name of which refers to a Sicilian saying which means “Be careful!”.

Name: Osteria del 36
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The Osteria del 36 traces its roots to 1880 and owes its name to a curious tradition: wine was once sold here at 36 cents a litre. Today it presents a cuisine firmly anchored in the Emilian tradition, set alongside touches of a more contemporary flavour, as in the crispy loin of rabbit with Prosciutto di Parma, cream of onions, carrots and cardoncelli mushrooms. A deep affinity with the world of wine is reflected in a list that is well-constructed, carefully considered and of reliable quality, conceived to complement each dish to its best advantage.

Name: Osteria del Borgo
Description: Located in the heart of the historic center, this restaurant is distinguished by its warmly welcoming and attentive management. The cuisine alternates between fish and meat dishes, prepared with a personal touch yet still rooted in tradition. Among the desserts, highlights include the indulgent bunet or zabaione served with canestrelli cookies.

Name: Osteria del Borro
Address: località Borro 52, San Giustino Valdarno, 52024, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In the heart of Valdarno, Osteria del Borro is located within a thousand-hectare estate that houses an authentic medieval village. In the summer, you can dine on a terrace with breathtaking views of the countryside, while in the winter, you can settle into an elegant room with soft tones and an open kitchen. There are three tasting menus, built around local products and, most importantly, the estate's own garden.

Name: Osteria del Centenario
Description: A restaurant that has been renovated in contemporary style, in complete harmony with its attractive setting overlooking the scenic lakeside promenade. Talented chef Egon Bajardi conjures up interesting Mediterranean cuisine with a focus on creative technique and the occasional exotic touch. Don’t miss his selection of desserts, including Crema Catalana with pumpkin, orange and bay leaf gelato.

Name: Osteria del Guà
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in the “barchessa” of a Palladian villa dating from 1541, this restaurant boasts an elegant dining room with an open fireplace. The cuisine here is creative and of excellent quality, with many of the main meat courses cooked over the barbecue grill. All in all, a romantic setting and superb food that is not to be missed.

Name: Osteria del Ponte
Address: Via Vittorio Veneto 22, Trezzano sul Naviglio, 20090, Italy
Description: Housed in a majestic historic farmhouse, this small friendly restaurant boasts intimate dining rooms and attractive “shabby-chic” style furnishings. In summer, the delightful outdoor space in the internal courtyard offers an idyllic setting. Traditional Milanese cuisine is the star of the show here, including specialities such as risotto with roasted bone-marrow, mondeghili meatballs and delicious breaded veal cutlet, also available in an “imperial” version for sharing.

Name: Osteria del Posto
Address: via Calderini 15, loc. Chiugiana, Corciano, 06073, Italy
Description: Housed within an ancient mill in the village of Chiugiana, a small hamlet of Corciano, the osteria offers contemporary cuisine deeply rooted in the local area. Ingredients are carefully selected, and the wine list tells the stories of small producers, both local and national, with a special focus on artisanal and natural wines.

Name: Osteria del Tasso
Address: via Bolgherese km 3,9, località San Walfredo, Bolgheri, 57020, Italy
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the famous Viale dei Cipressi avenue in one of Italy’s best-known wine-producing areas, this restaurant occupies one of the region’s most famous wineries, namely Guado al Tasso, renowned for its excellent wines. In fine weather, guests can dine in the shade of plane trees looking out over the vineyards. Simple, delicious and well-prepared cuisine, mostly traditional in style, plus specialities such as cured hams and grilled dishes.

Name: Osteria del Teatro
Description: Enjoy traditional cuisine served in an elegant 16C dining room with a fireplace or in more informal trattoria-style rooms, all of which are decorated with the same theatrical theme. The recipes here focus on local traditions and seasonal ingredients, resulting in colourful, well-balanced and beautifully presented dishes that are full of flavour. There are just a few tables on the small terrace near the entrance overlooking the pedestrianised street, so if you want to sit outdoors make sure you book well in advance.

Name: Osteria del Tempo Perso
Description: Situated in a hidden corner of the historic centre, this small bistro-style restaurant has a friendly and welcoming atmosphere, with photos alternating with books, wine bottles and glasses on the walls (the wine list includes a few labels from elsewhere in Europe). Small tables set close together, warm, subtle lighting and an almost Parisian ambience make this a perfect choice for a romantic dinner or a meal with friends. There’s also a small outdoor space for fine weather but seats are limited, so it’s best to book ahead!

Name: Osteria del Trentino - Da Marco
Description: A historical restaurant whose name recalls the origins of one of its earliest owners. Today this venue offers simple, traditional Piacenza cooking, where guests can enjoy excellent cured meats accompanied by vegetables from the restaurant’s own garden, fresh homemade pasta dishes, and main courses that also include offal preparations. Not to be missed are the fried veal brains: crispy on the outside, ultra soft within.

Name: Osteria dell'Arco
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Wheelchair access
Description: Enjoy a warm family welcome at this centrally located restaurant with an internal courtyard, where the menu features a good choice of traditional and authentic dishes full of flavour. The restaurant is run by the same friendly managers as the renowned and popular Boccondivino in Bra, where the Slow Food concept was born. Booking ahead is always a good option.

Name: Osteria dell'Oca Bianca
Description: In the heart of a small town, right opposite the church, this typical village osteria run by a friendly family serves traditional cuisine from the Piedmont, including goose dishes. Highlights here include the rustic, welcoming ambience, an excellent wine list, a wine cellar that can be visited, and a charming glass-fronted veranda that is used throughout the year. There are also three beautiful guestrooms reserved exclusively for guests dining at the restaurant.

Name: Osteria della Chiocciola
Description: Situated in the historic centre just a stone’s throw from the elegant Via Roma, this restaurant is decorated with paintings by renowned modern artists such as Pignatelli, Andy Warhol, and Valerio Berruti. The ground floor is home to a colourful wine bar, while the first-floor restaurant serves traditional cuisine made from local ingredients with a natural focus on Piedmont. There is also a fish alternative for non-meat-eaters.

Name: Osteria della Corte
Description: This restaurant with 18C stone walls and arches boasts a small, intimate dining room and an outdoor courtyard for summer dining. The delicious yet simple cuisine focuses on fish and seafood full of rich flavours, which are a must for chef Silvia Cardelli! Just a stone’s throw from the restaurant, there’s also a champagne bar offering tastings by the glass and bottles produced by small, enthusiastic wineries – a choice of over 130 different labels in total.

Name: Osteria della Foce
Description: A lively and contemporary bistro that celebrates Mediterranean cuisine with a modern twist, offering meat and fish dishes characterised by distinct flavours and refined techniques. Highlights include yellowtail tartare with celery, rose syrup and seed crackers, and the delicious pavé of striped bass accompanied by mashed potatoes, sautéed artichokes and lemon sauce.

Name: Osteria della Tana
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Occupying the same red house as chef Alessandro Dal Degan’s gourmet restaurant, the Osteria is where this chef turns his attention to more traditional dishes (meat and fish alike), which are often typical of the Veneto. There’s one highly recommended exception, however, namely the carbonara dell’Osteria, prepared with top-quality ingredients from the region. Also popular are the baccalà alla vicentina (dried cod) and the tripe, both of which feature on a menu with a wide selection, including renowned dishes from the chef’s Michelin-starred restaurant. Full-bodied flavours that will delight the palate.

Name: Osteria dello Strecciolo
Description: Situated in the centre of the village, this popular and professionally run restaurant has an informal atmosphere. The cuisine is inspired by Mediterranean recipes and more regional traditions, with great care taken in the choice of ingredients and beautifully presented dishes. A business lunch menu is also available.

Name: Osteria il Cru
Description: Spread between the basement and the ground floor of a small hotel in the Old Town, CRU has been reborn as Osteria il Cru – and both its new name and the olive tree at the centre of the cosy room give a good indication of its new direction. Head Chef Ivari Vokk leads a newly formed kitchen team in creating Italian dishes that exhibit all the flavours you know and love, enhanced by a few personal twists. The extensive menu represents good value and offers plenty of choice, including the likes of spinach and ricotta stuffed zucchini flowers, parmigiana di melanzane and delicious homemade pastas.

Name: Osteria il Moro
Description: Overlooking the main thoroughfare of Trapani and enhanced by a pleasant outdoor area, Osteria Il Moro interprets Sicilian tradition with a contemporary outlook. The cooking of chef-patron Nicola Bandi draws its roots from the flavours of the island, before opening out into original and personal creations full of intensity and character. The sea is the chief protagonist, though forays into land-based cooking are not lacking: among these, the “Guancia Dolce Forte” stands out, enriched by an age-old chocolate-based sauce that elegantly enhances the meat. The wine selection is also carefully curated and of considerable interest, offering a generous showcase of regional excellence.

Name: Osteria la Fontanina
Address: Portichetti Fontanelle Santo Stefano 3, Verona, 37129, Italy
Description: Cross the Ponte Pietra and the enchantment of the picturesque streets of Veronetta (Verona’s historic quarter on the left bank of the Adige), continues inside this restaurant: a succession of intimate dining rooms brimming with eclectic décor. The ambiance delivers exactly what one hopes for in a romantic dinner setting, while the kitchen moves deftly between local specialties and ingredients and more creative preparations, offering both meat and fish dishes of excellent caliber.

Name: Osteria la Lanterna
Address: via Finali 1, frazione Cressogno, Valsolda, 22010, Italy
Description: Situated on the road leading to Lugano in Switzerland, this charming restaurant with elegant furnishings and a rustic decor boasts bright dining rooms and a pleasant terrace for summer dining. The dishes are prepared with a focus on locally sourced, seasonal ingredients and are inspired by traditional recipes reinterpreted in contemporary style.

Name: Osteria le Logge
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Having retained its old shop counter and glass - fronted display cabinets, this former grocer’s shop is perfect for anyone in search of old - world charm. However, the cuisine is the real draw with its focus on quality of the highest level. Wine buffs can ask to visit the wine cellar nearby, housed in a tunnel of Etruscan origin. Simpler dining room on the first floor.

Name: Osters
Address: 125 High Street, Gosforth, Newcastle Upon Tyne, NE3 1HA, United Kingdom
Description: The team behind Lovage in Jesmond have turned their attention to the fruits of the sea at this restaurant on the bustling Gosforth High Street. Despite not quite being the restaurant’s namesake, oysters are available in multiple guises to kick off proceedings, before a choice of prime fish and shellfish. The chefs are aware of the quality of their ingredients, eschewing overcomplication in favour of simple combinations – like Pink Fir potatoes, tenderstem and beurre blanc accompanying a generous helping of sea trout.

Name: Othym
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Counter dining
Description: This restaurant has moved into a larger, brighter space. True to its ecological commitments, the new establishment has used a range of recycled materials. The menu, which is written on the blackboard, includes flavorful rustic sharing plates made with seasonal ingredients supplied by small-scale Québec producers. Flavors are always the name of the game, whether you opt for the lamb bavette with kale, the onion and beet tartlet, or Arctic char with carrots. The restaurant has adopted the "Bring Your Own Wine" policy.

Name: Otok
Description: Located on the ground floor of Hotel Osam, in the heart of a picturesque seaside town, this restaurant offers a delightful cuisine inspired by island traditions, balancing land and sea with classic recipes and local ingredients. Among the specialties, standout dishes include shrimp and cherry tomato skewers with a creamy butter and lemon sauce, and flavorful chicken thighs cooked under a brick. The pleasant outdoor area, shaded by ancient olive trees, makes the experience even more relaxing. For an aperitif or after-dinner drink with a view, it’s worth heading up to the rooftop bar, which offers stunning vistas of the sea and the town of Supetar.

Name: Otora
Description: A guiding principle of the chef’s cuisine is ‘junkan’ — a philosophy that views the seasons in ten-day spans. Within each span, ingredients reach their peak expression. Each dish is at its finest in the very moment it is prepared and served. The chef cherishes every fleeting instant that, once gone, cannot return, and remains grateful for the human connections formed each day. Traditionally, a month is divided into ‘jojun’, the first ten days; ‘chujun’, the middle ten days; and ‘gejun’, the final ten days. Each span offers a precious encounter with the season and its finest ingredients from land and sea.

Name: Otoro
Description: Pajtim Bajrami makes no bones about his love of produce, as the top-drawer scallops, wagyu beef and other delicacies quickly demonstrate. His Anjou pigeon is a perfect example: he first cooks the breasts rare before adding a high-flying felicitous blend of foie gras and truffles. Polished French classics are right up his street, enhanced by gutsy sauces and the odd Asian tang. A cosy interior depicts this eatery sodden with rippling ambition. A knock-out wine list and Ardita’s friendly, professional service add the final flourish.

Name: Otoro Jukusei
Address: Fernández de la Hoz 35, Madrid, 28010, Spain
Description: Looking for Japanese cuisine at its purest? In the heart of the Chamberí neighbourhood, a stone’s throw from the Basílica de la Milagrosa, there is a restaurant that imports many of its raw ingredients and it is certainly an interesting proposal. Although it has a small dining room where wood is the star, it is the bar that takes all the limelight, as this is where the colourful chambers housing the matured fish (jukusei) can be seen. The à la carte, heavily focused on these matured fish for the preparation of nigiris, is quite comprehensive (oysters, starters, grilled fish, nori, etc.) and is well supported by three tasting menus: Umi, Tochi and Hoshi. They also offer the option of adding a caviar tasting to any of their set menus!

Name: Otsuki
Description: Do everything to the best of your ability, his mentor taught him. The chef takes those words to heart, channelling all his skills to offer fresh-from-the-grill aromas and flavours. The menu strikes a delightful balance between seasonal fare and creative cuisine. New items are constantly added, rewarding every visit with fresh sensations. Eager to satisfy expectations, the chef caters to diners’ preferences, adjusting portions to focus on customer satisfaction.

Name: Ottavi Mare
Description: In the heart of Bevagna, just steps from the picturesque Piazza Filippo Silvestri, this small, welcoming, and well-cared-for restaurant offers cuisine that blends seafood flavors with Umbrian tradition, serving balanced yet never predictable dishes. There are three tasting menus, each available in full or reduced versions, allowing for a personalized culinary journey.

Name: Otto
Description: A welcome addition to the rue Mouffetard: this bistro with a minimalist decor comprising concrete floor and ceiling is modelled on the Japanese izakaya. Otto proposes a cuisine for sharing based on a short menu that revolves around the produce, simply accompanied by a condiment or a sauce for that extra kick. Hence chimichurri, sauce vierge or diable, ponzu sauce or lemon condiment are served alongside meat and fish, often cooked over binchotan coals. Please note that they don't take bookings.

Name: Otto
Address: 375 Karangahape Road, Auckland Central, Auckland, 1010, New Zealand
Description: Gather up some mates and make a night of it here at Otto, a perfect fit for K Road – this is a fun, frantic, colourful and perpetually busy restaurant where it’s best to come in a group to make your own noise. The good value menu is ‘Italian-inspired’, so you can expect plenty of homemade pasta, alongside popular dishes like their lamb ribs – and it’s all about ordering plenty and sharing. However tempting it is to end dinner with the affogato with hokey pokey ice cream, know they also do a pretty mean panna cotta.

Name: Otto
Description: Conveniently located in the city centre, a stone's throw from the cathedral and the Rhine River, this is the second maiBeck restaurant. In a trendy and chic setting, Jan C Maier and Tobias Becker serve up modern Italian cuisine with a focus on fish and seafood, although vegetarian options are also available. The pasta dishes are highly recommended. In addition to the excellent à la carte selection, the six-course "La Sera" set menu is available in the evening. The wine list is exclusively Italian. The front-of-house team are dedicated and attentive – the chefs also help to serve the food.

Name: Otto
Description: This compact restaurant has an appealingly lively atmosphere. The friendly vibe is due in no small part to the fantastic, well-drilled team, who have a personalised touch when it comes to looking after diners. The open kitchen – overlooking which there are also a few seats at the bar – sends out seasonal, modern, pared-down dishes with Nordic influences, all made using locally sourced ingredients. You can choose between the sharing menu and à la carte dishes. Vegetarians are also catered for. There is a rather short but carefully curated wine list with a predilection for natural and orange wines. Small terrace in front of the restaurant. This very popular restaurant has limited seating, so be sure to book in advance!

Name: Ottolenghi
Description: Housed in the swanky Mandarin Oriental Geneva, this restaurant rolls out modern, vibrant food signed by Yotam Ottolenghi, acknowledged guru of Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cuisines. The menu, devised to be shared, features dishes like a cardamon-flavoured melt-in-the-mouth shoulder of lamb or crunchy Mammole artichoke served with velvety hummus and a spicy sauce. The delicacy of the food is further enhanced by exquisite plating and a contemporary decor in which a central bar sets the tone of the establishment’s relaxed mood. A first-class selection of wines and cocktails adds the final flourish to a casual dining experience with friends or colleagues in a stylish, yet refreshingly unstuffy location.

Name: Ottoman Taverna
Address: 425 I St. NW, Washington, DC, 20001, USA
Description: Ottoman Taverna is fit for royalty. From the honeycomb wall patterns and Hagia Sophia mural to the glowing blue pendant lights and whitewashed interiors, the dining room channels a polished, contemporary version of Istanbul in the heart of Mt. Vernon Triangle. The menu focuses on Turkish and Eastern Mediterranean staples with a lightly modern approach. A large assortment of hot and cold meze, including hummus, smoky moutabal, muhammara and herb-laced labneh spreads, arrives with warm house pita, while grilled items like the juicy adana kebab showcase the kitchen at its strongest. Finish with Turkish coffee alongside traditional sweets like baklava or rice pudding sutlac.

Name: Ou Jiang Nan
Address: No. 1 Guangying Ma Tou, Oujiang Road, Lucheng, Wenzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Foreign credit cards not accepted,Great view,Terrace
Description: On the banks of the River Ou, this elegant restaurant affords 180-degree river views and the nightly light show can be seen from some tables. The seafood-heavy menu focuses on modern Wenzhou cooking and state dinner recipes. Home-style braised yellow croaker uses a dense chicken broth made with Jinhua ham and dried seafood. Other deftly-crafted, Wenzhou favourites include raw marinated crab and braised fish skin with garlic cloves.

Name: Ou Ju Hai
Address: 2F, Banquet Center, Hilton Wenzhou City Center, 969 Ouhai Avenue, Ouhai, Wenzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: The modern interior features stylised Wenzhou motifs and meticulous, understated yet luxurious details. The head chef, who hails from Guangdong and has over 20 years of experience under his belt, savvily puts a new spin on the classics as he melds Cantonese and Wenzhou cuisines. The seafood is prepared in a myriad of ways. For example, yellow croaker, which can be braised home-style or cooked in scallion oil, is silky and boasts distinctive aromas however crafted.

Name: Oudeland
Description: Urban and trendy, yet warm and welcoming, Oudeland is run by an enthusiastic team who bring the place to life. Their passion shines through in the way they present their impressive selection of natural wines and express their deep connection to Texel. Any produce not grown in their own garden is sourced from local suppliers on the island. Pan-seared haddock, for example, is served with pasta made of locally milled flour, a brunoise of kohlrabi and a shellfish emulsion packed with character. The chefs showcase their terroir in creative dishes, keeping diners on their toes with a new set menu every month.

Name: Oukan
Description: It's worth seeking out this restaurant, the entrance of which is a bit hidden. A long, mirrored corridor leads you to an interior characterised by distinctive architecture and a clean-lined, minimalist, Far Eastern design. The food is no less interesting: The Japanese-inspired cuisine is completely vegan, with fermented food playing a major role – hence having built their own Fermentation Lab. The creative seven-course set menu can be extended by an additional course. The dishes seem pleasingly pared back, although a lot of effort has gone into them. An individual signature is evident, for example, in the delicate maitake with robust roasted aromas and a subtle note of thyme, accompanied by a sensational sauce made from mushrooms, sake, port wine, vanilla and coffee, which inspires with fantastic depth. The intriguing tea pairings are an absolute must! Top-notch teas are celebrated here and presented in depth. It is also possible to go for a mixture of tea and other drinks pairings.

Name: Ourea
Address: 72 rue de la Paix-Marcel-Paul, Marseille, 13006, France
Description: In a quiet side street just a 5-minute stroll from the Vieux Port, this dinky eatery furnished with colourful banquettes is warm and buzzy and a hit with the locals. The chef favours a hyper-local ethos: artisanal fishing boats and cherry-picked market gardeners, resulting in a Provençal-led five-course evening menu. The score, which eschews jargon or trend, is a savvy blend of balanced, spot-on seasonings, illustrated by Mediterranean red mullet, lemon-spiked gnocchi and a knockout jus, or farm-reared veal, olive oil sauce, roast celery and a coffee-laced jus. Friendly, on-the-ball front-of-house team.

Name: Ousta Maï
Description: Courgette flower soufflé, trout, sorrel from the garden and chanterelles; blue lobster roasted in its juices, white polenta with basil; verbena-infused apricots, red and black berries: Jean-Paul's seasonal cuisine wins diners over with its precision and generosity. Sandrine's solicitous welcome, the impeccable service and the hushed atmosphere in the two cosy lounges – just like home – add to the appeal of this restaurant nestled in a peaceful village a few kilometres from Uzès. Another highlight is the show cellar with its superb selection of local wines.

Name: Outro by Vito
Address: 18 Millakbondong-ro 19 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48087, South Korea
Description: Now renamed Outro by Vito, the restaurant relocated near Gwangalli Beach and revamped its exterior and decor with contemporary elegance. Despite these changes, its signature pasta dishes have remained the same—only with enhanced flavours. The house-made pasta now features higher flour content and undergoes fermentation. Its glutinous texture and seamless pairing with the sauces make the dishes even more appetising. The menu also includes salads, meat, and other well-crafted offerings. To complete the experience, diners can enjoy a glass of natural wine in a relaxed, stylish setting.

Name: Oval (by Val d'Auge)
Description: From the outside, it might look typical of northern France, with its white bricks and eaves, dinky windowpanes and black window surrounds, but this restaurant actually sports a sleek modern interior. Christophe Hagnerelle is a genuine craftsman, who conjures up indulgent seasonal fare starring local produce: fish from the North Sea, blanc bleu beef from Bondues and permaculture veg…

Name: Oven
Description: If you’d like to take your tastebuds on a journey to Asia, Oven is the perfect place. Nepalese chef Hari Chapagain promises to take you on a voyage from India to Nepal through his cooking, to which he adds an innovative and contemporary touch. Many of his dishes are prepared in the “tandoor” oven (which is part of the open kitchen here and gives its name to the restaurant). Dishes he cooks in the oven include the tasty naan bread, as well as delicious grilled ribs of lamb, duck and chicken marinaded in Nepalese herbs and spices. A word of advice: we recommend asking the staff here about the levels of spiciness of each dish.

Name: Ovillo
Description: A bright, spacious and attractive restaurant with an industrial decor in which the creative cuisine on offer and its philosophy of solidarity (the restaurant is part of the Fundación Raíces’ “Cooking with a Conscience” project that aims to involve vulnerable young people in working and social environments) have won many admirers. The cuisine on offer here is based around an à la carte and three tasting menus (Ovillo, Madeja and Tirar del Hilo), all of which impress with their extensive choice of mini appetisers. We particularly recommend the tripe with haricot beans, which won the world’s best tripe dish award in 2022.

Name: Ovio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Run by celebrity chef Panos Ioannidis, this restaurant is, without doubt, an excellent choice for those exploring the busy streets of central Athens. In this spacious setting, divided into three dining areas (one on the ground floor, a few tables upstairs, plus a pleasant terrace) the chef offers a menu based around Italian cuisine. This includes homemade pastas, such as the delicious Gnocchi with a velvety sauce, diced pear, grated walnuts and finished with gorgonzola in two textures. These are complemented by meat dishes and pizzas cooked in the wood-fired oven, plus an extensive selection of Italian wines and a balcony where guests can savour an array of impressive cocktails.

Name: Owenmore
Address: Ballynahinch Castle, Recess, Connemara, Ballynahinch, H91 F4A7, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Located inside the grand 18C Ballynahinch Castle Hotel and surrounded by a particularly picturesque part of the Wild Atlantic Way, there are few more impressive locations to dine than here. Spectacular views of the grounds and river accompany well-versed service and modern, precisely executed dishes. The West Coast larder is used to great effect and features the likes of delicious mussels and clams from Killary Fjord. Be sure to fit in a walk around the grounds or spend time on the peaceful terrace before you leave.

Name: Owl's
Address: GF, 32 Mody Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: You’ll need to wait as the homemade choux pastries are filled on order with cream and custard of different flavours but, rest assured, the wait is worth it. Check out the occasional limited time offers. Take-out only.

Name: Ox + Anchor
Address: 877 Palm St., San Luis Obispo, CA, 93401, USA
Description: Chef Ryan Fancher's modern steakhouse is on the grounds of Hotel San Luis Obispo, in a separate building connected by a walkway. The hotel's contemporary Southwest vibe lives on in the restaurant. Design details, like butterscotch leather banquettes, a stacked brick wall divider, and teal-blue tiles, enhance the X factor. Staff are well-informed, so let them steer you through the menu. Start with such comfort fare as savory goat cheese croquettes with sweet lavender honey before embarking on the main event—charred steaks and sides of creamed spinach topped with onion rings.On the same property and from the same chef, Piadina is worth a visit—for its Cal-Ital menu and that hotel classic club sandwich turned on its head with fried chicken and B&B pickles.

Name: Ox Club
Address: Bramleys Yard, The Headrow, Leeds, LS1 6PU, United Kingdom
Description: Housed in a former mill, along with a beer hall and cocktail bar, this unpretentious restaurant attracts a young and lively crowd keen to sample its wood-fired cooking using a grill imported from the US. Utilising fire and smoke to enhance quality produce is the name of the game – with the 1kg côte de boeuf on hand if you're feeling flush – but the kitchen isn't afraid of adding in bold flavours too, as evidenced by the nduja with the oysters and the gochujang glaze on the crispy pig tails. Pleasingly, there's plenty of choice for vegetarians too.

Name: Oxalis
Description: Prepare yourself to be blown away as you drive past fields full of red and white cabbages en route to this cosy little establishment housed in a former post office. Geoffrey van Melick cut his teeth at top-flight restaurants such as The Fat Duck and 't Nonnetje, and it shows in his selection of quality ingredients, the depth of his sauces and his meticulous garnishes. Take, for example, the perfectly pitched and beautifully reduced veal jus that accompanies the rich fillet of veal Rossini, with fine vegetable accompaniments that add their distinctive nuances. This chef proves that creativity need not be at odds with respect for tradition!

Name: Oxalis
Description: This ancient edifice, whose oldest stones date back to the 13C, oozes historical cachet (exposed beams and stonework, vaulted cellar that can be rented out for private events), while the open kitchen behind a glass partition and splendid rough-hewn wooden tables add a contemporary touch. The chef-owner, whose CV boasts some top Parisian establishments, conjures up tasty dishes in a bistronomic vein at lunchtime (e.g. burrata with truffle and beetroot seasoning; seabream with aubergine caviar), with a more high-flying score in the evening (white asparagus and scallops; seabass, baby artichoke and cashew nuts).

Name: Oxalis
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: This establishment, located in the Casa Velha do Palheiro hotel a few kilometres from the south coast and Funchal, enchants visitors with its two-plus centuries of history and its setting amid verdant golf courses. With classic-colonial style and a completely open kitchen, Chef Gonçalo Bita Bota proposes modern Portuguese cuisine, raising Madeiran flavours to a higher level. The use of seasonal ingredients from local farmers and fishermen shows a genuine commitment to island produce and is reflected in different menus. A dish that enchanted us? "Chão" da Ribeira's cured trout accompanied by fennel ice cream.

Name: Oyatte
Address: 125 E. 39th St., New York, NY, 10016, USA
Description: Chef Hasung Lee’s first restaurant draws heavily on the fine dining experiences that shaped him. Guests begin downstairs in a wood-clad lounge inspired by Crown Daisy Farm, the Hudson Valley farm that supplies much of the restaurant’s produce, before moving upstairs for a tasting menu that blends Korean influences with contemporary fine dining. Ingredients from the farm appear throughout the meal, often alongside techniques such as fermentation and preservation. Highlights may include the signature green porridge, as well as inventive desserts like mugwort ice cream with kiwi and fava shoots. Thoughtful sourcing, ambitious cooking and a clear commitment to seasonality define the experience.

Name: Oyster
Address: Radisson Blu Hotel, Aleja Baltic Park Molo 4, Świnoujście, 72-600, Poland
Description: The name is an easy clue that this restaurant inside the Radisson Blu hotel is all about seafood. Although there are meat dishes, fish and shellfish lead the way on a menu where you could opt for a light, wallet-friendly meal or splash out and celebrate. Oysters are available to start, of course, but the Baltic herring is a great alternative and main dishes like halibut with spaghetti show subtle creativity while still highlighting the natural flavours of the ingredients.

Name: Oyster Box
Address: La Route de la Baie, Saint Brelade, JE3 8EF, United Kingdom
Description: One of the best things about Oyster Box is that it really reminds you that you're on an island. The location looking out over St Brelade's Bay is magnificent, with the terrace in particular offering some of the finest sea views you'll find – and the food is a perfect match for the setting, with bright, fresh dishes featuring top-drawer seafood. Jersey rock oysters are an obvious must-order, but the rest of the dishes are equally enticing; it's worth keeping an eye on the fish of the day and if you order the terrific crab taglierini, you won't be disappointed.

Name: Oystera
Address: C. Benito Juarez, Ignacio Zaragoza y Santos Degollado, Todos Santos, 23300, Mexico
Description: Oystera is located in the heart of Todos Santos, in a massive and rather grand building that is built on the former site of a sugar mill. The oyster bar takes center stage, with the dining space surrounding the bar. A patio out back takes advantage of the view. Chef Poncho Cadena, a Sonoran native, oversees a seafood-focused, Mexican menu spotlighting contemporary, even ambitious, cooking. As might be expected, oysters are a must. Try the half-dozen selection, with all six sourced from Baja waters and served with their version of cocktail sauce, a mignonette and Baja-style ponzu sauce. If raw isn't to your liking, try the plump, fried oysters with habanero aïoli. Beyond the bi-valves, a marinated tuna tostada or the catch of the day would round out your meal nicely.

Name: Ozio Gastronómico
Description: In this small yet welcoming restaurant with a contemporary feel, which has developed as an offshoot of its original incarnation in Palermo, they are happy to boast that they offer Italian cooking with a Sicilian soul. In general, much of the focus here is on the cuisine of southern Italy, adapting traditional recipes and flavours to a more modern perspective, both on the à la carte and tasting menus, both with the option of a wine pairing (Amantes de la pasta and Ozio Supremo). Authentic Sicilian pottery is integrated into the restaurant’s decoration!

Name: Ošterija Debeluh
Description: Situated in inland Slovenia, just a few kilometres from the border with Croatia, this is one of the most interesting restaurants in the region. Here, highly experienced owner-chef Jure Tomič has created an excellent network of suppliers from all over Slovenia. His meat and fish dishes are prepared with a modern, precise and technical touch that is unfussy and focuses on bringing out the full flavour of his ingredients. Traditional recipes and ingredients are reinterpreted with a personal twist: examples are the plum extract served with duck and the sweet “butter, honey and milk” dish that takes the ingredients of a typical local dessert and creates something new and original. The chef’s specialities include his Cake Debeluh, a beef tartare with meat macerated in a cold nutmeg broth, goose liver and quail egg spiced with coffee. You’ll have no problem finding the right wine to accompany your meal from the extensive wine list.

Name: O’BikiniBé
Description: The name is a nod to both the "bikini" – Catalonia's iconic toasted sandwich – and the Grand Bé islet that lies off Saint-Malo across from the restaurant. Nicolas Bourdon (who previously opened Le Coude à Coude) has redesigned this stripped-back space that offsets exposed concrete with pops of colour. It is set practically on Plage du Sillon, opening up to both the kitchen and the sea. At lunchtime, the precise and unpretentious seasonal menu features expertly executed dishes (seared asparagus, pearly hake, cream puffs). In the afternoon, the venue morphs into a tearoom and pastry shop; in the evening, the menu is more ambitious. Friendly service.

Name: PACAI Restaurant
Description: The owners here claim that this 17th Century baroque property in the heart of the Old Town was once the most magnificent mansion in the Grand Duchy of Lithuania; today, it’s home to a boutique hotel complete with a spa and this stylish restaurant. Start with a drink in the large, retro-style cocktail bar, before moving on to interesting seasonal dishes with a strong Lithuanian base. The wine list is highly recommended, with some great vintages at every turn and a good selection of different wines by the glass. In the summer months, when the light lasts long into the evening, the central courtyard becomes an appealing oasis.

Name: PAI
Description: Named for the Thai village where Nuit Regular and her husband opened their first restaurant, PAI is perpetually busy. A former nurse, Nuit now soothes by cooking her family recipes and street food favorites for hungry patrons. The mod bohemian look is appealing, but it's the extensive menu that you'll spend all of your time admiring. It's full of fresh, tasty dishes sized for sharing and with varying spice levels. While they traipse across Thailand for inspiration, zero in on the North Thai plates and chef favorites, including khao soi, a noodle and coconut milk dish, or kanom jin nham ngeaw, a pork rib and tomato soup with rice vermicelli. Kung tawt, a plate of fried shrimp sided by a piquant tamarind sauce, is delicious but gaeng panang, a sweet-and-sour red curry, hits all the right notes.

Name: PASODOBRE
Address: Poznań Congress Centre, ul. Śniadeckich 25, Poznań, 60-773, Poland
Description: Just to the side of the Poznań Congress Centre is this spacious Spanish restaurant serving up the usual tapas suspects. You’ll find Padrón peppers and patatas bravas all present and correct, alongside more filling main dishes and a selection of pintxos. Strong, satisfying flavours run throughout, while the flan is a terrific incarnation of a classic dessert. A small fridge is filled with Spanish goodies to buy and take home, including olive oil and almonds.

Name: PEI FULL
Address: 2F, United Hotel, 200 Guangfu South Road, Da’an District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: After a recent refurbishment, this restaurant in a long-standing hotel now boasts a bold red-and-green colour scheme. With 40+ years of experience under his belt, the chef puts a creative spin on Jiangzhe classics in dishes like boneless eel stuffed with smoked dried plums that looks and tastes divine. Another signature, osmanthus Peking duck, needs pre-ordering three days ahead. The numerous private rooms make it perfect for business meetings.

Name: PEN KLUB Restavracija
Description: Head up to the first floor to this retro-style restaurant, where you pass a welcoming lounge bar before moving into the main dining room adorned with an attractive fresco. The “culinary journey” offered by the chef here follows the rhythm of the seasons and showcases local traditions, enhanced by the occasional international influence. Although at lunchtime you can order à la carte, in the evening the choice is between three tasting menus (four, six or eight courses) with a wine-pairing option (labels from Slovenia and further afield) or a choice of non-alcoholic drinks. The tiny summer terrace has just a few tables (book in advance).

Name: PER TE
Description: Pizza and other items are offered with this prix fixe menu of wood-fired cooking. The Marinara and Margherita pursue the essence of these classics, while more creative pizzas draw inspiration from regional Italian cuisine, exploring new possibilities. Fresh from the oven, pizzas are served one slice at a time, ensuring both portion and pacing are balanced. The course unfolds in a chic setting, offering a new vision of the pizzeria.

Name: PERIGEE
Description: Perigee means the point in the orbit of a satellite at which it is closest to the Earth. The restaurant was named in the hope of bringing diners closer to food and wine. The restaurant, which is run by chef couple Shin Ga-young and Lim Hong-keun, serves pasta that is all made fresh in-house. Diners can enjoy different types of pastas with textures and shapes rarely found in Korea, such as cavatelli, andarinos, and pici. Experience familiar yet unique combinations like vongole with pici, and lobster pasta with andarinos.

Name: PIER 6
Description: This stylish restaurant in the Havenwelten quarter delights diners with modern dishes made with locally sourced seasonal ingredients. Mouthwatering options on menu include Heligoland lobster bisque and skrei fillet with a tomato and thyme crust. Wallet-friendly lunch specials such as beef roulades or goulash also have their fans. The tables near the windows and on the terrace are especially coveted – the view of the New Harbour is beautiful. Given the popularity of this place, it's definitely best to book in advance.

Name: PINK - DAS RESTAURANT
Description: Located in the Haus für Kultur und Sport, in a quiet yet easily accessible area in Schwalbach-Hülzweiler, this restaurant is very popular. The interior with modern lines is tastefully decorated in a palette of calm, cheerful colours, and the broad, glazed façade means the space is lovely and bright. The seasonal and Mediterranean-inspired food is cooked meticulously and with attention to detail. The excellent à la carte selection ranges from beef carpaccio to truffle pasta and fried halibut. There is also a children's menu. Attentive service with a personal touch comes courtesy of the competent team.

Name: PLANTXA
Description: Under the supervision of the renowned Juan Arbelaez, the chef of this bistro signs cuisine replete with unusual South American notes. The dishes are meticulously crafted and served in a laid-back, “home from home" arty interior. Invigorating and welcoming!

Name: POF
Description: The lunchtime menu is chalked up on a slate, while in the evening, the dishes of the concise menu carry playful, tongue-in-cheek names, which do however require a certain command of the French language to be appreciated! The globetrotting partners aim for a friendly vibe, a wide range of culinary influences (cream of cauliflower with Brittany curry spices, wakame crumble; crunchy quinoa and a Mexican-inspired jus; pear, myrtle, star anis, mascarpone and matcha tea) and market-fresh ingredients in line with the zeitgeist.

Name: POLLEN
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Surrounded by the gorgeous Meuse Valley, the Naxhelet estate boasts a golf course, a luxury hotel and this cosy restaurant. The natural beauty of the area is best appreciated from the terrace. Chef François Durand strives to maximise the use of local produce, often sourced from the sustainable projects of Terres du Val. His cuisine celebrates vegetables in all their glory. For example, he roasts pumpkin, crisps up the seeds and makes oil from the leaves. The dish is finished off perfectly with a subtly spicy Brillat-Savarin cheese sauce. At POLLEN, the flavours of the seasons come alive.

Name: PONTE DEL PIATTO
Description: ‘Ponte’ means ‘bridge’, while ‘piatto’ means ‘dish’. The earnest desire of the chef is to build bridges among people through food. Prix fixe menus express the seasons of Japan, but cooking methods and flavours are Italian through and through. Ribollita is a vegetable soup from Tuscany. Tiramisu is raised to a new level. Beautiful, modern arrangements attest to the chef’s many years of honing his craft.

Name: PONTE VECCHIO
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Daisuke Yamane’s culinary goal is ‘optimal cuisine’. Cooking and composition are kept to a minimum, so that beauty flows from function. Each ingredient serves a purpose. The chef rejects needless decoration, knowing too much can be as bad as too little. Disparate elements judiciously balanced create harmony—for example, the luxury of caviar meeting the familiarity of potato.

Name: POPS
Description: Pops is the venture of two fledglings who have flown the cosy nest that is La Mare aux Oiseaux, a recognised incubator of talent. At their restaurant set slightly back from the seafront, Corentin Leverger and Océane Maisonneuve pull out all the stops to delight diners with the freshest of ingredients, such as red mullet, monkfish and scallops. Their subtly creative bistronomy rolls out a feast of textures and bold flavours. Right next door, their bistro Locco serves simpler fare.

Name: POTS
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Relaxed, chic and stylish! The eye-catching features of the Ritz-Carlton's restaurant are its striking decor and large open kitchen. The chefs put a modern spin on traditional German cuisine in dishes such as Königsberger Klopse (meatballs in a white wine sauce) with capers and yellow beetroot. There are also options for sharing. Alternatively, take a punt on the surprise menu. The lunch deal is also popular. Friendly and adept service.

Name: PRIME STEAK
Description: The attractive modern interior of this restaurant tucked away in a building complex may come as a surprise – the small glass dry-aging refrigerator at the entrance and the kitchen, visible through a large window, draw the eye. As the name makes clear, steak is the mainstay of this joint, but there are other appealing mains, starters and desserts. Fish and seafood are available only if ordered when you book. At lunchtime, additional – and some simpler – dishes such as goulash soup or bratwurst make for a quick and inexpensive meal. The quality of the meat and the side dishes is on point! N.B. Parking can be tricky.

Name: PRISMA Expérience
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Terrace
Description: Housed in the exclusive Park Hotel Vitznau, which dates back to 1903, this summer-only restaurant whisks you away on a culinary voyage. Japanese fusion cuisine is the name of the game here. There is an omakase menu (for two or more diners) and an à la carte selection including sushi, sashimi, Wagyu dishes and ramen. The vibe is casually elegant. The location overlooking the lake is a draw in itself, and it goes without saying that tables on the terrace are highly coveted.

Name: PS Ristorante
Address: via di Petriolo 7, Cerreto Guidi, 50050, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the splendid countryside of Cerreto Guidi, Villa Petriolo is a magnificent Medici residence offering luxurious rooms in a setting of great allure. Besides the beauty of the villa and its garden, onto which the restaurant’s outdoor terrace looks, the property benefits from an abundance of its own production: extra-virgin olive oil, wine, Cinta Senese pig farming, meats, poultry, a kitchen garden and ancient grain varieties. The kitchen reinterprets this exceptionally rich range of produce in a modern key, offering two tasting menus – one of them vegetarian – from which it is also possible to order à la carte. Alternatively, the Osteria di Golpaja offers genuine and intense flavours of the kind that have made Tuscany a celebrated destination for lovers of fine dining.

Name: PUCHE
Description: This restaurant, housed in an old stone and brick building that captivates visitors with its rustic charm, is run by chef Alan Puche and features an open kitchen, a small bar for four diners, two dining areas with tables and... an open grill! The humble cuisine here is centred around the ingredients and tradition, with a wide range of dishes designed for sharing and some market-led options not on the menu. What to order? Try the Palamós red prawn salad with a vinaigrette made from the prawn heads, or the delicious fish of the day, marinated and smoked, with a gribiche sauce.

Name: PULS
Description: Stylish boutique hotel Legend, right in the heart of Cologne's Old Town, is home to the restaurant-bar PULS. The atmosphere here is lively, modern and urban. You can dine at the bar, at high tables or at standard tables – or, during the summer, out on the lovely terrace. Chef Johannes Langenstück and his team serve bar food alongside dishes in sharing or individual portions. Alternatively, you can hand over the reins and go for the "Chef's Choice" surprise menu. A good selection of wines and an interesting range of cocktails, including signature creations, round off the meal.

Name: PUR Hurden
Description: The location by Lake Zurich is quite something – the terrace overlooking the water is dreamy, not least on account of the mountain views! The restaurant boasts further charms indoors: regional cachet shines through, beautifully combined with chic, modern style. The menu includes classics – beef tartare and crispy battered fish bites are a must – and contemporary dishes such as lake fish ceviche or, for dessert, "wild cacao from Bolivia".

Name: PURO
Description: The restaurant on the first floor of the Mövenpick Hotel serves interesting and ambitious cuisine. This comes in the form of a very appealing fusion concept of Asian and Latin American-inspired dishes made with plenty of regional produce, but also ingredients from around the globe. The food is down to earth, flavoursome and fresh! This is complemented by an international wine list, extremely friendly service and a stylish interior.

Name: PY Restaurant
Description: In this dinky brasserie in a smart neighbourhood, Pierre (in the kitchen) and Yuko (front of house) make the magic happen. In this contemporary decor, diners sample generous, well-crafted dishes. The à la carte menu in the evening is enriched with premium dishes such as hare pâté en croûte.

Name: Pa Noi Beef Noodles
Address: 57/8 Sisuttha Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
Description: The aroma of beef noodle soup greets diners at this popular eatery. The distinctive tamarind chilli paste pairs perfectly with deep-fried chicken skin or mixed into the noodles. The boat noodles with rich flavours are also a must-try.

Name: Pa Porn Traditional Pork Noodles
Address: 121/2 Mu 8, Soi Pa Maphrao 10, U Thong Road, Hua Ro, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: Auntie Porn has mastered pork noodle soup for over 50 years, initially on her boat at age 17, now on land. Her Tom Yum soup boasts expertly prepared noodles, rich broth, and toppings like minced pork, fish sausage, or BBQ pork, complemented by red shrimp and peanuts. She also offers tasty fish balls.

Name: Pablo
Address: GF, The Picasso Boutique Serviced Residences, 119 L.P. Leviste Street, Salcedo Village, Makati - Metro Manila, The Philippines
Description: This upbeat spot blends industrial style with colourful wooden flooring and lively music. Initially focused on classic Spanish fare when they opened in 2014, the menu now spans international influences. Don't miss the crispy croquetas with creamy jamón or goat cheese and spinach filling – we recommend ordering both, so you can sample the different flavours. The lively music brings energy, making this a popular place to unwind with wine or a cold cerveza.

Name: Pacht 26
Description: Stefaan, chef and sommelier, is an enthusiastic foodie and wine connoisseur. He regularly scours eastern Europe to enrich his wine list. The many regulars to his friendly, welcoming establishment applaud the wine formula which reveals the full scope of his creativity. Each dish is a consummate blend of character and delicacy with legible ingredients such as duck’s liver and beetroot, depicted in fresh, subtle nuances.

Name: Paco Espinosa
Description: This restaurant, located in the La Victoria district of the city, boasts a popular tapas bar by the entrance plus a dining room in which the reasonably varied à la carte stands out for its quality. On it, you’ll find delicious Iberian ham, scrambled egg dishes, home-style stews, as well as superb fish and seafood (red prawns, scallops with onions, baked sea bass with garlic etc), which is unusual given the restaurant’s distance from the sea. The extensive wine list features several international labels.

Name: Paco Meralgo
Description: A tapas bar that defines itself as a ‘high tavern’ of this culinary art. Here you will find tempting open sandwiches (montaditos) (the one they make with Steak Tartare is a must), interesting seasonal suggestions not on the menu, delicious meat, good wild fish from the fish market... and some vocally advertised rice at lunchtime. It is perfect for an informal gathering with friends, with dishes for sharing!

Name: Pacto Raíz
Description: If you enjoy street food, this restaurant overseen by Álex Marugán (of Tres por Cuatro fame) is entirely focused on just that. Here, in this informal, rustically inspired space with a bistro vibe, the duo of Rocío Martínez and André Chumbe offer a fusion that plays with the flavours of Spain, Peru and Mexico through dishes designed for sharing (half-portions are an option so you can try a little of everything). There is also an executive set menu, with a wine pairing option, available from Tuesday to Thursday. One particularly special, highly original and delicious dish that we can recommend is the menestra stew with peanuts, herbs and egg.

Name: Pades Restaurant
Description: Wolfgang Pade offers a constantly changing menu, which is based on the availability of produce and relies on regional producers. Please note that there are only two service times: 5.45pm and 8.15pm – so make your reservation in good time! The garden terrace behind the pretty patrician house is magnificent.

Name: Pae Araya
Address: Rim Khong Road, Khong Chiam, Ubon Ratchathani, 34220, Thailand
Description: Where the Mekong meets the Mun River, this floating restaurant enjoys a cooling breeze and gentle undulations from passing boats. Fresh fish is delivered each morning, and the catch of the day dictates the menu: Most of the dishes feature river fish cooked in a local Thai style with bold flavours; the spice level can be adjusted upon request. Arrive early for dinner to catch sundown views over the river and the Laotian landscape beyond.

Name: Page
Address: 4, Alley 20, Lane 595, Bei'an Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, 104, Taiwan
Description: This laid-back bistro has rich blue walls and white tiled dados; cheeky artwork adds to the fun and vibrant ambience. The chef leverages his formal training in Western cuisine to re-create familiar Taiwanese recipes using local produce. His signature roast half chicken with mushroom risotto is a hybrid of Taiwanese barrel charbroiled chicken and the Italian rice dish. Most items are designed for sharing. It is always worth checking the daily specials.

Name: Pageou
Description: Located in the CityQuartier Fünf Höfe shopping centre, the chic restaurant of renowned TV chef Ali Güngörmüs is named after his hometown in the Turkish province of Tunceli. Here, his team serves Middle Eastern cuisine that draws on classic French influences and is available as a four-course vegetarian "Levante Menu" and as a five- or six-course "Chef Menu". A starter dubbed "Meze", for example, is a great option comprising various small dishes. A number of noteworthy Turkish labels are included in the extensive wine list. The lovely sheltered terrace is delightful on summer days.

Name: Pahissa del Mas ...
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant occupies the “straw loft” of the Mas Pou, a farmhouse built in 1352 and surrounded by rice fields. Here, seven generations of the Pericay family have devoted themselves to a culinary project in which locally sourced ingredients have always taken centre stage. And if the persistent drought in the region doesn’t stop them, they even grow their own rice (Carnalori variety). Choose between an impressive à la carte of traditional dishes, where spectacular rice dishes are the standout option, a tasting menu, plus enticing daily specials.

Name: Pairedd
Address: Shop 703, 7F, UFun, 300 Jiaozi Avenue, Wuhou, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
Description: With only 12 counter seats framing the open kitchen, Pairedd offers an intimate dining experience and close interaction with the young chefs. As its name suggests, wine is at the core of its brand DNA and the set 10-course tasting menu is designed to complement the seven-glass wine flight. Dishes change with the seasons, but meat and seafood form the backbone of the menu: expect Fujian seafood in summer and local produce from Sichuan in winter.

Name: Paju Villa
Description: The suburb of Nõmme is home to this elegant art nouveau villa named after Karoline Paju, who built the house in 1931. Dining takes place over two floors, with several small, interconnecting rooms creating a stylish and intimate space. Instead of being listed under the usual headings of ‘Starters’, ‘Mains’ and ‘Desserts’, the appealing dishes are presented under the tempting-sounding sections of 'Can’t Resist', 'For a Real Gourmand' and 'Cherry on Top'. The menu may be small, but modern twists bring an extra element to the classically based recipes, ensuring there’s something to appeal to one and all.

Name: Pak Mor Robot
Address: 82/4 Benchama Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, Ubon Ratchathani, 34000, Thailand
Description: The chef owner of Pak Mor Robot has satisfied the tummies of locals for over 30 years. She prepares a variety of Vietnamese dumplings in a steamer at the front of this neat little outlet. The signature, her own invention, is the incredibly tasty Vietnamese dumpling with fried eggs.

Name: Palacio Ico
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: A restaurant with plenty of charm, a focus on select ingredients, and a chef at the helm who, despite his young age, has plenty of experience behind him. Palacio Ico occupies the hotel of the same name in a restored property that still showcases the beauty of the archipelago’s architecture. The contemporary Canary Island-inspired cuisine prides itself on the quality of its ingredients such as smoked salmon from Uga, gambas and Carabinero prawns from La Santa, octopus from Lanzarote, the famous black Canarian pig, and local cherne fish etc. Choose between two tasting menus (one short, one long) that evolve with the seasons and offer a wine pairing option. The well-stocked wine cellar is enhanced by an exclusive selection of champagnes.

Name: Palais Royal by David Martin
Description: As soon as the doorman ushers you into the luxurious Corinthia Grand Hotel, you will be entranced by its period charm. The restored stained-glass dome of the Palm Court is truly magnificent, while the dining room immerses you in a romantic Belle époque ambience. A marble fireplace, lovingly restored details and fresh flowers set the scene in the spacious, characterful restaurant, which also offers privacy and intimacy. David Martin has assembled a team that invites you to sample subtle creations enhanced by familiar Japanese flavours in a vibe that is both classy and casual. An example: juicy fillet of red mullet lacquered in a sweet-sour chorizo sauce and flanked by a rich chorizo oil, subtle vegetable sides and chunks of merguez… You can expect a culinary banquet that intelligently combines a few carefully chosen ingredients to create a genuine explosion of flavour. A banquet of royal proportions indeed!

Name: Palanga
Address: Palanga Life Balance SPA Hotel, Birutės av. 60, Palanga, 00135, Lithuania
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Giorgio Pignagnoli brings plenty of Italian flair and creativity to the kitchen of this smartly dressed restaurant at the Palanga Spa Life Balance Hotel. There are often dishes to share on the menu, such as sole or chateaubriand, while standouts include his smoked eel risotto, which is as flavoursome as it is colourful. Many of the generously sized dishes come with his own original touches, but neither is he afraid of tradition – he uses his grandmother’s special recipe for his delicious tiramisu, for example.

Name: Palazzo Branciforte
Description: Inside a late 16th-century patrician residence, which now also houses a fascinating archaeological museum, is a restaurant that is pure magic. Its elegant and secluded inner courtyard becomes the main dining room: a space that changes with the seasons thanks to its retractable roof, offering the chance to dine “en plein air” under the starry sky on the most beautiful evenings. A place where history and taste come together, creating an experience that goes beyond a simple meal.

Name: Palazzo Petrucci
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The entrance from the street does little to prepare you for the surprise that awaits once you’ve taken the lift down to this restaurant, where the dining room looks out at the beach and guests dine with the sound of the waves as a romantic backdrop. In a modern and minimalist setting, chef Lino Scarallo offers a choice of tasting menus, include a surprise option on which he has carte blanche, and others based on signature dishes that include raw fish options and meat specialities.

Name: Palazzo Petrucci Pizzeria
Address: piazza San Domenico Maggiore 5-7, Naples, 80134, Italy
Description: Situated right in the city centre, this pizzeria with the same name and owners as the gourmet restaurant has a contemporary, minimalist feel, plus an attractive outdoor space on the piazza. Among the excellent pizzas made from top-quality ingredients, you’ll find a few created by the young, skilful pizza chef, as well as one by chef Scarallo. Don’t miss the desserts!

Name: Palazzo Utini
Description: A historical palazzo in the town center has been given new life after its purchase by a local entrepreneurial family, who also bestowed their name upon it. Just steps from the heart of Italy’s famed food valley, it now serves as a refined hospitality venue: the ground floor hosts a bar and bistro, while upstairs are elegant spaces devoted to gourmet cuisine. Tasting menus are available, with dishes also offered à la carte, alongside an extensive and well-curated wine list. The upper floors feature intimate, stylish guest rooms, designed in the same reassuring style that runs throughout the building.

Name: Palette Tea House
Address: 900 N. Point St., Ste. B201A, San Francisco, CA, 94109, USA
Description: This buzzy dim sum restaurant may call the heart of Ghirardelli Square home, but it is hardly a spot just for tourists. The gorgeous space is fitted out with colorful light fixtures splashed with Chinese characters, delicate tiled murals and flickering candle tea warmers. Pork and duck puffs crafted into little black swans are Instagram-ready, followed by radish cakes, shrimp dumplings, as well as slippery rice crêpe rolls with XO. More substantial dishes like Ibérico pork char siu with cognac glaze also merit attention.

Name: Palm Court
Address: Plaza de la Lealtad 5, Madrid, 28014, Spain
Description: The Palm Court restaurant is located beneath an impressive glass dome in the elegant lobby of the Mandarín Oriental Ritz Madrid hotel. The à la carte here, which every lunchtime in winter is enhanced by delicious traditional-style dishes (on Thursdays, you can order the traditional “cocido madrileño”), includes options such as creamy rice with vegetables, glazed lamb shank with potato gratin, and a superb sole meunière.

Name: Palma
Description: Dressed head to toe in concrete and lit with candles, this narrow room in Little Havana is out to make a mark. The staff totals less than five, including Chef Juan Camilo Liscano and his sous who cook, plate and clear with impressive efficiency. The lean team, however, turns out a stylish and agreeably priced tasting menu that changes with great frequency; sit at the counter to enjoy the full experience. Grilled baby corn brushed in burnt eggplant aioli and wrapped in aged sirloin is a thrilling start, followed by delicately steamed flounder enrobed in a smooth sabayon made of mussels. Brioche made with roasted plantains is the only staple, and what a staple it is. Beautifully shaped, nicely crusted and served hot with caramelized coconut butter, it is impossible to resist.

Name: Palmier
Address: Four Seasons Private Residences Bangkok, 300/1 Charoen Krung Road, Yan Nawa, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In 2024, French chef Guillaume Galliot brought this classic yet relaxed brasserie dining experience to Bangkok. Take a seat outdoors to enjoy views of the Chao Phraya River and a menu composed of classic French dishes, signature creations and innovative offerings. The culinary delights include foie gras terrine and Boston lobster confit. A passionate sommelier is on hand with recommendations from an extensive French-focused wine list to match the food.

Name: Pammy's
Description: Chef and owners Chris and Pam Willis run this utterly charming operation in Cambridge. With its inviting space outfitted with salvaged finds, personable service and enticing menu; it's the perfect neighborhood restaurant. The prix-fixe menu offers tempting flexibility and is designed to be a three-course meal bearing product-focused inspiration. Baccala enriched with mascarpone and served with boquerones, dried sour cherries and puntarelle presents a riotous combination of flavors, while squid ink-tinted gnocchi are impressively light and tender. Dessert is additional; order the chocolate cake with sesame ice cream, or finish with a shot of the house-made Meyer lemon limoncello.

Name: Pamparigouste - Le Couvent des Minimes
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: In addition to his fine dining restaurant, chef Louis Gachet lovingly oversees this upscale bistro. The space exudes a soothing vibe, and the loggia has picture windows that can be opened fully in fine weather. Showcasing modern cuisine that gives pride of place to Provençal flavours, sun-kissed vegetables and aromatic herbs, the menu is packed with mouthwatering dishes. A prime example is his delicate prawn carpaccio with taramasalata and a citrus sauce maltaise. Blending Southern French components with classic French sauces, the chef also pays tribute to his Burgundian roots with his œufs en meurette (eggs in a red wine sauce).

Name: Pampín Bar
Address: Ruela das Fontiñas 4, Santiago de Compostela, 15703, Spain
Description: The modest façade of this restaurant in the historic quarter hides a traditional, slightly retro dining room that comes as a pleasant surprise and where guests will feel completely at home. The restaurant features a large shared table in the centre of the room and a decor of bare concrete, where the focus is on traditional home cooking full of the flavours of bygone days, which the chef likes to describe as “cocina de barrio” (neighbourhood cuisine). The menu includes homemade empanadas, numerous dishes to share, and a focus on escabeches, stews and freshly caught fish.

Name: Pan Fang Chun (Zhongshan South Road)
Address: 479-481 Zhongshan South Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: A favourite spot for breakfast among locals, Pan Fang Chun specialises in potstickers – with a nicely charred, paper-thin crust and juicy pork filling, they taste even better dipped in chilli sauce and vinegar. Cut through the richness with a bowl of sweet soymilk. For a lighter option, try the bite-size wonton soup with laver and scallions. Expect to queue at the door for service, and they close before 1pm, so come early to avoid disappointment.

Name: Panacée
Description: Panacée, or panacea, is a universal remedy to cure all ills, something akin to what the cuisine of Chef Catherine Couvet Desrosiers is accomplishing. She works behind a circular counter, welcoming some 20 guests per service, convivial atmosphere guaranteed, thanks to the good-humored staff, too. The contemporary fare is prepared using seasonal ingredients only, and these are enhanced with beautiful tangy vinaigrettes and fermented vegetables. Produce is carefully selected, for example bluefin tuna from Prince Edward Island, served with a medley of carrots; barbecued pork loin, accompanied by its jus gras pan sauce; and Beurrasse, a creamy local goat's milk cheese, served with a poached pear and a salted almond sorbet.

Name: Pancho's Takos
Address: Basilio Badillo 162, Zona Romántica, Emiliano Zapata, Puerto Vallarta, 48380, Mexico
Description: Puerto Vallarta's Zona Romántica is well known for its charming cafes and art galleries set on cobblestone streets, and while there are plenty of appealing restaurants here, Pancho's Takos is a standout. A longstanding favorite of both locals and tourists, bring patience (for the line) and cash, since credit cards are not accepted here. Once inside, the seating is tight, though there are some outdoor seats on the patio. It's all worth it after the first bite of their pastor tacos. They're the highlight of the show here, with overflowing portions of thinly sliced meat that's piled on corn tortillas and topped with cilantro and diced onion.

Name: Panorama
Description: The name says it all!
