The location at an altitude of over 1 000m makes for a fantastic panoramic view of the surrounding mountains – it would be a crime not to enjoy it from the terrace in summer. The Rindisbachers have been running their establishment since 1985 already, serving food influenced by tradition, made with quality ingredients and paired with good wines. The pasta is manufactured in their own workshop. Panoteca sells delicatessen wares.

Name: Panoramarestaurant
Description: Spoiler: this restaurant does indeed boast a magnificent panoramic view! This is, of course, best appreciated from the terrace, but you can also enjoy the sight of the mountains from inside through the floor-to-ceiling windows. The seasonal cuisine is regional Austrian. With dishes such as Wiener schnitzel and juicy goulash with sour cream, salmon trout from the Ötztal and Bregenzerwald cheese spaetzle, as well as Kaiserschmarrn (Austrian pancake dessert) – the menu promises a feast. Lila Pause, a bar with outdoor lounge, is also pleasant. As well as Panoramarestaurant, Hotel Alpenstern has another restaurant: Löffelspitze.

Name: Pantagruele
Description: Situated in the town centre just a stone’s throw from the port, this small, typical trattoria is renowned for its delicious fish and seafood, including an excellent antipasto buffet and fresh fish cooked mainly on the grill. The large outdoor area is perfect for summer dining. Informal service.

Name: Panther City BBQ
Address: 201 E. Hattie St., Fort Worth, TX, 76104, USA
Description: Named in honor of Fort Worth's nickname, Panther City BBQ began as a food truck before landing this space with both indoor and outdoor seating. This is central Texas-style barbecue with meat slow-cooked on offset pits. Here, they dole out Texan classics while also leaning into Tex-Mex offerings like brisket burritos, brisket elote, and street tacos. Arrive early to avoid long lines to savor the likes of expertly smoked, thickly sliced brisket with a pepper-heavy rub or tender, shredded pulled pork. As with any good barbecue spot, the sides are attention grabbing, and some of their hits include spicy smoked mac and cheese and potato salad with baked, smashed potato and red potatoes mixed with shredded cheese, green onion, and mayonnaise.

Name: Panurge
Description: In a cosy and comfortable setting, a mix of oval and square tables contribute to a very Parisian, retro-style decor. Old engravings on the walls reference Rabelais – a nod to the restaurant's name. Former sous-chef at L'Arcane (18th arrondissement), Tomoyuki Uchida embraces French culinary tradition with style in a personal, vibrant and unfettered interpretation of its cuisine. His attention to detail and well-balanced dishes set the tone: confit veal tongue marinated in shio koji, served with Romanesco broccoli and tonnato sauce; trout with sorrel and petits pois à la française. And the "divine bottle" is never far away.

Name: Pao by Paul Qui
Address: Faena Hotel Miami Beach, 3201 Collins Ave., Miami Beach, FL, 33140, USA
Description: Damien Hirst's giant sculpture of a gilded woolly mammoth resides famously behind the lavish Faena Hotel. Such scale and grandeur is also the norm in this restaurant, overlooking the iconic attraction. Pao’s oval room is capped with a gold-dome ceiling that's centered around yet another statue by Hirst—a golden unicorn perched on a platform looming large over the stylish guests.To be clear, this spot is more than just good looks and its short menu knits together a range of influences. Many of them are Asian, as in dishes like scallop aguachile with pineapple and black lime or a bao with smoked Wagyu short rib with XO aïoli. Roasted black bass with chili patis and ginger-garlic rice swings from sweet to savory to spicy, and comforts at every turn.

Name: Paolo Teverini
Address: via del Popolo 2, Bagno di Romagna, 47021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the charming village of Bagno di Romagna and surrounded by beautiful rolling hills, Teverini is a culinary name full of history in this area. The cuisine here demonstrates different traditions – the local region is an obvious influence (especially its mushrooms), but fish and seafood also feature along with plenty of vegetables.

Name: Papa Llama
Address: 2840 Curry Ford Rd., Orlando, FL, 32806, USA
Description: Set in an unassuming strip-mall location, this intimate dining room offers a clear view into the kitchen, where Kevin and Maria Ruiz cook a family-style Peruvian menu with contemporary touches. The atmosphere is casual and personal, with decorative flourishes that nod to Peru and a compact layout that keeps the experience close to the action. The menu leans on familiar Peruvian staples interpreted simply: dishes like grilled shrimp anticuchero, lomo saltado with skirt steak and mushrooms and arroz chaufa emphasize approachability over reinvention, and local sourcing is a clear priority. Sweet potato picarones with spiced syrup close the menu on a traditional note. The natural wine program is impressive.

Name: Papa San
Address: 501 W. 34th St., New York, NY, 10001, USA
Description: Restaurateur Juan Correa and Chef Erik Ramirez are the brains behind Llama Inn and now this New York hotspot, where Nikkei cuisine blending Japanese and Peruvian influences is given a playful twist. Papa San's menu is cheeky in tone (there’s even a “best friend” section for your favorite sides) with dishes inspired by Ramirez’s heritage as well as travel to Tokyo. Zansai, or small plates, as well as robataya (grilled items), donabes and maki comprise most of the offerings. Don't miss the ceviche, especially the fluke atop an avocado leche. Seared wagyu tri-tip is even better with a dollop of yuzu bearnaise that's so good you'll want to bottle it and take it home.

Name: Papageno
Description: Even after moving to the centre of Konstanz, Patrick Stier has remained true to his style. He serves up classic cuisine with Mediterranean influences – think sea bass grenobloise with artichokes and a saffron emulsion or saddle of venison with a sour cherry game jus, warm pointed cabbage salad, port wine cherries, macadamia nuts and Topfenknödel (curd dumplings). Diners can choose between the "Gourmet" and "Vegetarian Gourmet" set menus and à la carte dishes.

Name: Paparoto Cucina
Address: Av. Pres. Juscelino Kubitschek, 2041 - Térreo, São Paulo, 04543-011, Brazil
Description: Part of the luxury JK Iguatemi complex, this restaurant has a spacious and modern setting with a decor that includes plants and subdued lighting that accentuates the illuminated Italian phrase “Se non ora quando?” (“If not now, when”). Famous chef Dayse Paparoto, who won the first edition of Brazil’s Professional Masterchef, showcases his Italian-inspired menu with an authentic and innovative touch that is based around fresh, top-quality ingredients. The menu features an array of options, such as the excellent egg yolk ravioli with ricotta and spinach, served with a soft egg yolk. Other options include fresh pastas and risottos, although the desserts steal the show here, highlighting the extreme creativity of the chef in dishes such as tiramisu, served with a candy floss tree, which comes as a complete surprise.

Name: Papaveri e Papere
Description: Situated in the verdant setting of San Miniato, this attractive and friendly restaurant is home to chef Paolo Fraschi, who creates imaginative cuisine that is full of character with regional and Mediterranean influences (the home-made spaghettini with clams, courgettes and parmesan is particularly delicious). In season, dine alfresco in the beautiful garden.

Name: Papavero
Description: This long-established little restaurant serves a mixture of Polish and Mediterranean-inspired cooking in a stylish setting. The generous and well-executed dishes include their signature roast duck with red cabbage, alongside homemade pastas and classic desserts like tiramisu and crème brûlée. Sit overlooking the street or in the smaller, more intimate room to the rear.

Name: Papillon
Address: 129 Frabelle Corporate Plaza, Tordesillas Street, Salcedo Village, Makati - Metro Manila, The Philippines
Description: Inspired by the travels of its chef-owners, Papillon offers a refined take on Southeast Asian cuisine. In a Colonial-style space oozing tropical flair, dishes such as Thai shrimp balls wrapped in pasta sheets and Cha Ca La Vong reflect regional diversity, while Pandan desserts served hot pot-style add a playful touch. Vibrant flavours and a warm and evocative decor capture the essence of Southeast Asia down to every carefully crafted detail.

Name: Pappas Bros. Steakhouse
Description: Even after more than two decades of service, this Houston institution is as sharp as ever. The menu is focused, offering just a limited number of appetizers and salads to keep all eyes and appetites on the prime, in-house dry-aged steaks. Seasoned and seared properly, the cuts are complemented by generous, finely tuned sides like creamed spinach with ham or oversized onion rings (ask for extra crispy). Part of the genius here is the service: Veteran waiters and friendly sommeliers are effortlessly hospitable regardless of whether you order 1947 Petrus. Altogether, with white tablecloths, glossy wood paneling, and a wine list that has few equals, this restaurant captures a kind of magic that is rarely seen these days but unquestionably appreciated.

Name: Paprica
Description: In this centrally located restaurant, which promotes vegetables from small organic producers and meats from farms where animal welfare is respected, they offer traditional cuisine with modern touches and slight nods to other cultures. On the menu, rounded out with a selection of tapas and two menus, you'll find dishes such as the house hake salpicón, the chicken gyozas with balsamic and black beer or their Canelón de ropa vieja with Celtic pork, black chickpeas and green turnip top mojo. It is home to a charming patio-terrace too!

Name: Paprika Café
Description: This tiny spot is the perfect sojourn before or after a visit to the Monterey Bay Aquarium, thanks to its delectable and affordable Mediterranean food and friendly service. A diminutive and humble place, it has only six tables, but the chef/owner provides a warm welcome, recommending favorite items before he goes to work in the tiny back kitchen. Vegans and vegetarians will delight in the ample menu featuring flaky spanakopita, smoky baba ghanoush and vibrant tabbouleh with a perfect zip from fresh lemon. The tahini that accompanies the crisp, golden falafel is luscious, and a classic Greek salad is refreshingly satisfying. Don’t fill up completely though, as the homemade baklava, which just so happens to be vegan, is sure to sate and is available packaged to go.

Name: Parada de la Reina-Martina Bistró
Description: This restaurant, which started life as a typical bus station café, has evolved into what could be described as a 'gourmet concept'. Today, it is a contemporary bistro where they are committed to an international and modern cuisine, designed for sharing, which comes to life through an interesting à la carte. We especially liked, for its texture and juiciness, the grilled veal sweetbread, with tupinambo and ratatouille with oloroso. The suggestions of the day usually contain a hidden gem or two!

Name: Paradiesli
Description: The journey to the village of Betlis may not be the most straightforward (the road from Weesen is only open for five minutes at a time on the half hour or hour), but the stunning elevated location more than compensates with a view of nearby Lake Walen and the mountain landscape. There is greenery at every turn – on the terrace in particular you feel like you are in a corner of paradise. The interior is attractive and sleek, its wooden decor exuding traditional charm, fostering a pleasingly unpretentious and relaxed atmosphere. Choose between small plates such as pickled vegetables or "lettuce leaves, herb quark, popped buckwheat" and larger dishes such as "pork cheeks (organic, Uelihof), Serviettenknödel (bread dumplings), raw fennel salad". Alternatively there are three versions of the set menu: meat/fish, vegetarian or vegan. The restaurant Wirtschaft im FRANZ in Zurich belongs to the same establishment.

Name: Paradisaea
Address: 5680 La Jolla Blvd., San Diego, CA, 92037, USA
Description: Just look to its name to get a sense of what Paradisaea is all about. This La Jolla spot has an upscale tropical theme, where bar chairs are enlivened with a floral pattern and everything feels sunny and warm, especially outside on the patio. As might be expected, the mood extends to the bar, where tiki drinks take center stage. The kitchen turns out simple, contemporary cooking featuring local ingredients with Asian and tropical inflections. Case in point? A classic coconut shrimp, though here it's grilled over a robata and served with a coconut-lime dipping sauce. Northern halibut is fried to a crispy, golden brown and served over a thin slice of watermelon radish and lettuce with green curry aioli and a sweet chili sauce.

Name: Paradise Café
Address: Daleside Nurseries, Ripon Road, Killinghall, Harrogate, HG3 2AY, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A smart, spacious café behind a garden centre; if it’s sunny, grab a seat on the terrace overlooking the lake. They’re open for breakfast, brunch and lunch, and the frequently changing menu offers seasonal dishes which are fresh, unfussy and full of flavour. Book the chef’s table to watch the kitchen at work.

Name: Paradiso
Address: Yas Bay Waterfront Pier 71, Yas Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Terrace
Description: A partnership between celebrated French chef Pierre Gagnaire and Nicole Rubi of La Petite Maison in Cannes resulted in this bright and colourful restaurant. It’s the perfect backdrop to their favoured cuisine – that of the Mediterranean, so expect everything from snails and roast poussin to fritto misto, pizza and assorted pasta dishes. The terrace overlooking the water is nicely decked out and a very pleasant spot.

Name: Paradiso
Description: In good weather, you can take in breathtaking views up here at 2 181m above sea level. This down-to-earth Mountain Club restaurant appeals to diners of all ages. You can look forward to good food and a great wine selection, as well as a relaxed atmosphere, partly thanks to the music and DJs. Note: there is an entry fee for non-members. Accessible by chairlift and a short walk (10min).

Name: Paradoxon
Description: The atmosphere here is pleasantly down-to-earth, and the waitstaff laid-back and friendly. The cuisine is modern and seasonal. Along with à la carte options such as char ceviche or local ribeye steak, there is a set menu comprising four or six courses. Tip: Brunch is also served on Sat and Sun (10am-2pm). N.B. cash payments only. The restaurant also has an online shop selling home-made goods (sauces, pesto, jam etc), as well as beer and wine.

Name: Parapluie
Description: This lilliputian restaurant serves globetrotting food in the zeitgeist, with a sprinkling of spices and based on seasonal, mostly local, ingredients. The culinary offer is rolled out in a single set "mystery" menu comprised of several courses at dinner, and a reasonably priced lunchtime menu with options. Fine selection of wine, beer and spirits (whiskies, eaux de vie etc).

Name: Parcelles
Description: The quintessence of vintage Paris! In a side street of medieval Marais, this 1936 bistro would have been quite at home on the set of Woody Allen's Midnight in Paris: authentic bistro furniture, bare or beige walls, vintage floor tiles, a gilded ceiling and a copper and wooden counter. The food is similarly nostalgic: red mullet in a bisque sauce, calf’s sweetbread in beurre noisette and a dark chocolate and caramelised pecan tart to finish. Ten out of ten for this restaurant that is fully deserving of its success. (Book if you can!)

Name: Parche
Description: A festival atmosphere, advertised by a lively playlist of Latin music and colorful décor, may draw you in off the street, but the charming service and soulful, satisfying cooking seal the deal. Alongside an assortment of ceviches and empanadas, the menu proudly announces its Colombian bona fides with dishes like patacones (smashed fried plantains) and arepas, but isn’t shy about departing from tradition. The cooking embraces the country’s multicultural influences, including African and Lebanese, spotted in items like a labneh dipping sauce served with cheese-filled yuca buñuelos, or a leche de tigre with tahini. This isn’t a spot for a quiet, pensive night out, but if the volume is elevated, so too is the sense of fun.

Name: Parco Gambrinus
Address: via Capitello 18, San Polo di Piave, 31020, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A rustic and romantic setting provides the backdrop for the traditional and creative cuisine served here. It is made from typical local produce with an emphasis on ethical and sustainably produced ingredients (vegan and gluten - free options are also available). Exotic animals inhabit the park, where a stream is home to the house specialities of crayfish, eels and sturgeon. The restaurant also offers a few comfortable guestrooms nearby.

Name: Pares Pares (N. Escario Street)
Address: Unit E, Escario Building, N. Escario Street, Cebu, Cebu, The Philippines
Description: When cravings hit for local street food favourites, but you'd rather skip the heat, this bright, air-conditioned eatery is just the ticket. The star of the show is the signature beef pares, featuring tender brisket in a dark, sweet-spicy sauce, best enjoyed with steamed rice. A noodle soup version is also available. Open until midnight, it's a go-to place for late-night diners seeking bold, satisfying flavours in a cool, casual setting.

Name: Pari-
Address: 8-10 Samlarn Road, Phra Sing ,Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
Description: The cosy design and small counter foster a vibrant, relaxed dining experience. The small yet high-quality dishes combine Japanese Izakaya style with Thai ingredients, enhanced with wasabi or yuzu. The ham comes from a Yunnan village in Chiang Mai, perilla from Mae Hong Son, sashimi-grade fish from the south, and meat from organic farms. We recommend the corn-fried rice Yunnan ham and the house-made ponzu sauce, elevated by a refreshing Somsa citrus oil.

Name: Paris 1930 de Hideki Takayama
Address: 2F, The Landis, 41, Section 2, Minquan East Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, 104032, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Anchored in French cuisine, this understatedly elegant restaurant with a Japanese executive chef at the helm weaves together ingredients from Japan and Taiwan. The seafood-focused menus are built on contemporary techniques, with local teas and spices used thoughtfully to achieve balance and originality in the flavour profile. For dessert, the millefeuille layers crisp textures with flavours that change with the seasons. Refined and attentive service supported by in-house wine and tea sommeliers lends the experience a sense of ease and calm.

Name: Paris Bonheur
Description: Boasting an ideal location on Place du Maréchal Juin, this restaurant is part of the Stéphane Manigold group. Against a backdrop of Belle Époque touches and nods to Alsace, diners tuck into classic bistro dishes in a lively atmosphere (eg calf's foot cromesquis with sauce gribiche, steak with peppercorn sauce and spaetzle, pike quenelles) – or opt for one of the tempting cuts of meat for sharing displayed in the ageing cellar. Culinary bliss right in the heart of Paris.

Name: Paris House
Address: Woburn Park, Woburn, MK17 9QP, United Kingdom
Description: A beautiful mock-Tudor house built in Paris and reassembled in an idyllic parkland location; enjoy a drink on the terrace while watching the deer. The seasonal tasting menu offers sophisticated, artfully presented dishes with creative texture and flavour combinations and subtle Asian influences.

Name: Parizzi
Description: Along a street in the city centre, a colourful and welcoming dining room provides the setting for a culinary offering that oscillates between local tradition and contemporary touches. The menu moves between local dishes and a selection divided between meat and seafood, providing a balanced and versatile choice. The dishes impress above all for the quality of the raw materials and for the precision of their cooking: exemplary in this respect is the charcoal-grilled sea bass, accompanied by roasted potatoes and cherry tomatoes, which expresses simplicity and flavour at their very best.

Name: Park
Description: At Westmount, Chef-owner Antonio Park serves up vibrant and balanced Japanese/South American fusion cuisine. To the sound of 80s pop, diners tuck into dishes such as precisely cooked suzuki accompanied by fragrant chimichurri and maitake mushrooms, or a selection of tuna sushi with specialty condiments: bluefin tuna with daikon steeped in yuzu, marinated jalapeño albacore, longfin tuna with ginger flower... This is an extensive and mouthwatering menu, that is also available as an omakase experience in the evening, for a culinary voyage with stopovers in Japan and Argentina.

Name: Park Fora Balık ve Deniz Ürünleri Restoranı
Address: Muallim Naci Caddesi No:54/A, Cemil Topuzlu Parkı İçi, Kuruçeşme/Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34347, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Grilled, meunière, steamed, tandoori – however you like your fish, Park Fora has it covered. At this traditional seafood restaurant, the produce is always in season and super fresh. As you enter, you will see crates of the day's catch stacked and waiting and numerous aquariums filled with king crabs, lobsters and other creatures. Specify your cooking preferences – for us, it was sole à la meunière – and then savour! It will be cooked to perfection and accompanied by carefully prepared accoutrements. Factor in the waterfront location, with views of the boats coming and going on the Bosphorus, and you will really feel like you are on holiday!

Name: Park Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Located at Parkhotel Bremen, this restaurant occupies an elegant conservatory overlooking the Bürgerpark and the lake (Hollersee). Frank Seyfried, previously at Gotthardt's in Koblenz, runs the kitchen, serving up a contemporary take on classic cuisine. Create your own three- to six-course set menu from a tempting array of dishes. The good food is complemented by friendly and adept service.

Name: Parks BBQ
Address: 955 S. Vermont Ave., Ste.G, Los Angeles, CA, 90006, USA
Description: Lauded as one of the city's most cherished destinations for Korean barbecue, Parks has been luring patrons for years, evidenced by the photo wall of famous chefs, actors and politicians right by the front door. The interior is simple, as efficient, friendly servers do most of the work managing the grills and flipping and slicing meat. From bulgogi to galbi, the meat is prime quality and often lightly marinated. Pricier American wagyu will appeal to spendy guests, and the acclaimed garlic-soy-brown sugar marinade is ace with short ribs. Crisp kimchi pancakes served hot on cast-iron skillets as well as cold noodles are proper foils for the protein. Cinnamon punch with dried persimmon is the perfect ending. Lunch specials are particularly popular and offer both good value and variety.

Name: Parma Rotta
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Here, where the Parma river once broke its banks, you’ll find an attractive trattoria with pleasant dining rooms and excellent cuisine cooked over a wood and herb fire, one of the oldest culinary techniques in the world. The main courses feature meat only, with an extensive number of dishes on the menu. Among the home-made desserts, we recommend the fior di latte ice-cream, which is served with a choice of delicious sauces.

Name: Parnham Restaurant
Address: Parnham Park, Beaminster, DT8 3LZ, United Kingdom
Description: Few restaurants come with as delightful a setting as this. You arrive via a slow drive through the majestic tree-lined Parnham Park estate, culminating at a wonderful walled garden filled with impressive objets d’art. Take your seat in either the rustic-chic dining room in full view of the open kitchen, or in the glasshouse behind with its glorious garden views. Seasonality is the name of the game in the natural, flavour-forward dishes, from the ‘Parnham Pintxos’ snacks to foraged mushrooms with Jerusalem artichokes and Cornish gouda.

Name: Parquet
Description: French bistros can be predictable, but this neighborhood corner in Harbord Village takes a wonderfully refreshing approach. One could spend all day taking in the design: The marble bar is a worthy perch for admiring the gorgeous, patterned floors, forest-green ceiling and stylish, wood-paneled walls. And that patio – it’s a summer oasis. The cooking, meanwhile, hits all the right marks, and feels unquestionably French in its richness and satisfaction. Who knew that mushroom beignets could be so light and pair so well with lime and pepper sauce? One could make a meal out of the roasted cauliflower with cumin vinaigrette and puffed chickpeas. Cassoulet with duck confit and steak frites with béarnaise are proper classics.

Name: Parrilla
Address: 7-9 Sandford Road, Ranelagh, Dublin City, D06 E2H7, Ireland
Description: Lively, loud and simply wonderful fun, Parrilla offers both a great night out in Dublin and lightning-fast transport to Mexico in one appealing package. As soon as you arrive, it gives off ‘hottest ticket in town’ energy, combining a pumping soundtrack with a room full of smiles from the team and guests alike. Start off with a margarita before choosing from a menu dominated by its taco and grill selections – although don’t miss out on the padron peppers with red pepper salsa or the generous crab tostada too. If you’re in a group, ask for one of the booths.

Name: Partage
Description: Julie and Hugo first met at Lameloise, later setting up shop in the house where Alexis Kreyder (1839-1912) – renowned for his still-life paintings of flowers and fruit – was born. The location, a traditional half-timbered inn painted pomegranate red on the outside and done out in contemporary style inside, wins diners over. As for the food, the talented chef creates nicely fragrant and balanced dishes that taste as good as they look, for example marinated and subtly smoked sea bream, bibalakas-style cream with herbs and beetroot shavings.

Name: Partage
Address: Rue des Fossés Fleuris 18, Namur, 5000, Belgium
Description: Charles Jeandrain of the starred establishment, Attablez-vous, has opened this buzzy eatery in Namur’s pedestrian centre. Diners can choose between a bargain-priced lunch menu, an enticing set menu and a few suggestions, all of which are in line with Jeandrain’s focus on authentic, unfussy flavours. Examples include a tartare of raw shrimp with finely diced celeriac and apple, a sweet curry emulsion and a crunchy salad, followed by a textbook perfect vol-au-vent. Just the ticket to share a meal with friends and family in Namur.

Name: Partage
Description: In the kitchen, a young chef nurtured on home cooking and refined through significant professional experience in France now presides over an intimate and welcoming establishment in the heart of the town. At lunch, the offer is more immediate, with a streamlined formula and a decidedly appealing price-quality ratio; in the evening, meanwhile, the spotlight shifts to a broader, more personal à la carte menu, where creativity and technique find expression in dishes of land and sea. All of this is enhanced by a carefully curated selection of natural wines, well-structured and coherent. Passion, expertise and the youthful spirit of the management complete a gastronomic picture of undoubted interest.

Name: Parva Farmhouse
Description: This 17C stone farmhouse sits on a bank of the River Wye and is run by a friendly couple. Its simple, rustic interior comprises a spacious lounge and a cosy, welcoming restaurant with an inglenook fireplace. The gutsy, modern British cooking has a classic French backbone and the odd Italian or Asian touch. Booking is essential and the menu is sent a day in advance for pre-ordering. Bedrooms are comfortable and some have river views.

Name: Parzival
Description: After years at Prism in Berlin, Gal Ben Moshe is rising to a new challenge in Prague, bringing his Levantine-inspired cuisine to the elegant restaurant of boutique hotel Bookquet. A six-course set menu has been created under his direction – it is influenced by his Israeli homeland, but Asian influences can be detected, too. The wine pairings are also of interest. Almost all of the wines on the short menu are available by the glass. Enjoy an aperitif in the chic lounge in the hotel's lobby.

Name: Pascalucci
Address: via Appia 1, San Nicola Manfredi, 82010, Italy
Description: A traditional restaurant serving regional cuisine, as well as skilfully prepared fish dishes made from fresh produce. Specialities include Beneventano beef fillet and octopus in aspic jelly.

Name: Pascua
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: In the heart of Salamanca, as the flagship of the welcoming Eunice Hotel Gastronómico, there is a restaurant with soul, as chef José Manuel Pascua constantly seeks harmonies between tradition and modernity, respecting the culinary legacy learned from his grandmother (the hotel bears her name). At the same time, he champions what he calls ‘purist cuisine’, very respectful of cooking times and focused on exalting the best seasonal products of the area. You can choose between à la carte service or one of their tasting menus: Celemín and Media Fanega.

Name: Pascual
Address: 732 Maryland Ave. NE, Washington, DC, 20002, USA
Description: Pascual may be named for the patron saint of cooks and the kitchen, but this spot from Chefs Isabel Coss and Matt Conroy doesn't need any extra blessings (and reservations are a challenge, so plan accordingly). Their casual, contemporary Mexican spot delivers on dishes more often found in Mexico City than in D.C. It's all meant for sharing, and tetelas and tlayudas are always a good idea. Other standouts include a blue corn tamal balanced on pickled onion and tomato finished with crema and charred eggplant sauce. Mains, like the lamb neck barbacoa or smoked chicken, are also intended for tucking into with tablemates. End on a sweet note with the buñuelo: a crispy rosette dusted in cinnamon sugar and served with cajeta and chocolate sauces.

Name: Pasjoli
Address: 2732 Main St., Santa Monica, CA, 90405, USA
Description: Chef Dave Beran’s Santa Monica bistro is irresistibly charming, a breezy space buzzing with activity and accented with wood beams, exposed brick and gleaming white kitchen tile. Brioche with chicken liver mousse and shallot truffle jam or bay scallops with green garlic beurre blanc reflect an unapologetically French approach. There are a number of dishes intended for two, and the pressed duck is the pinnacle of luxury. Should there be room to spare, chocolate soufflé paired with vanilla ice cream or a strawberry tart with whipped cream make for a sweet sendoff. No time for a full meal? Take to the elegant marble bar for Champagne, Osetra caviar and blinis.

Name: Pasqualina
Address: via Santi Filippo e Giacomo 12/14, Frascati, 00044, Italy
Description: In the historic centre of Frascati, this restaurant offers straightforward, traditional cooking, executed with considerable skill and often faithful to the region’s classics. From the excellent coratella (lamb offal) and other preparations celebrating nose-to-tail cooking through to the canonical Roman pastas (carbonara, gricia, amatriciana, cacio e pepe), it is a celebration of the rather robust and pleasingly rustic flavours of local cuisine.

Name: Passage Secret
Description: Tucked away in an elegant 19C shopping arcade, or passage couvert, this restaurant is aptly named. Located inside the Caviar de Neuvic boutique, it features a chic bistro-style dining room and a charming glass-roofed terrace. At the helm is unassuming chef Thomas Pasquereau, whose classically inspired cuisine is executed to perfection, a case in point being his pâté en croute façon Richelieu (ie with foie gras), which is underpinned by admirable technique. His passion for great French sauces is also clear, as is his love of vegetables (a vegetarian set menu is available).

Name: Passage Thru India
Address: 4 Jalan Delima, off Jalan Bukit Bintang, Imbi, Kuala Lumpur, 50400, Malaysia
Description: Established in 1993, Passage Thru India catches the eye with its artistic interior as much as its cooking. The owner-artist painted the murals on the walls and ceilings to create a technicoloured yet intimate cottage feel. The sizeable menu offers a good variety of traditional Indian favourites, including tandoori, naan and roti from the coal-fired oven. The aromatic biriyani rice puts you right at home and goes well with any of the tapas-sized plates.

Name: Passerini
Description: In his convivial restaurant, Giovanni Passerini treats us to tasty, carefully prepared Italian dishes, such as his trippa alla romana, which could hardly be bettered. Here, it's all about the produce and authenticity: sharing plates are a house speciality, as is Black-Headed Manech suckling lamb or whole pigeon in two courses. This place is very popular, so be sure to book!

Name: Passionné
Description: Set back from Grands Boulevards, this restaurant plays the minimalist card: a bar with midnight blue mosaics, dark walls and floor and refined lighting. A very Japanese brand of elegance, designed for this location officiated by chef Satoshi Horiuchi, originally from Hokkaido island, a few kilometres from Sapporo, a prefecture with a high concentration of small-scale producers, especially market gardeners. Horiuchi is as passionate as ever about creating a modern French cuisine characterised by his quest to find quality ingredients and cook them perfectly.

Name: Pasta Moon
Address: 845 Main St., Half Moon Bay, CA, 94019, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: One of Half Moon Bay’s most popular restaurants, Pasta Moon draws a steady crowd of locals and visitors eager for hearty Italian American fare made with quality ingredients. With vaulted ceilings, an open kitchen and multiple dining rooms, including one overlooking Pilarcitos Creek and a lush garden, the space feels lively yet comfortable. Recognized by Slow Food U.S.A., the kitchen highlights artisanal products and house-made pastas, alongside crisp thin-crust pizzas and generous classic dishes. A soppressata pizza shows off the kitchen’s particularly successful crust, while plates like eggplant Parmesan layered with mozzarella, ricotta and smoked provolone deliver satisfying richness. Desserts keep things simple and well executed, such as a classic affogato with vanilla ice cream and candied orange peel.

Name: Pastamara - Bar con Cucina
Description: Housed in the luxurious Ritz-Carlton, Vienna, this restaurant allies the hotel's classic elegance and a modern feel. The pleasingly professional team serve traditional Sicilian cuisine with a modern twist. There are no compromises when it comes to the quality of the ingredients, as shown in dishes such as vitello tonnato and spaghetti gambero e limone – the expertly prepared pasta also deserves a mention. A highlight for dessert is the cannolo siciliano. In addition to the à la carte selection, a six-course surprise menu is available in the evening. There is also an appealing, moderately priced two-course lunch deal. There is additional seating at the large open bar in the middle of the room.

Name: Paste
Address: 3F, Gaysorn Village, 999 Phloen Chit Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The food here is as intricate as the spiral silk cocoon sculpture that fills the airy dining room. Drawing inspiration from royal Thai cuisine, the kitchen also employs century-old techniques and plenty of local ingredients. The roasted duck curry with lychee, fennel seed and freshly squeezed coconut milk and the char-grilled pork, fennel seed, and smoked tomato relish are recommended and can be found on the tasting menus and à la carte. Excellent service further enhances the experience.

Name: Patachée
Description: This dinky traditional restaurant in the town centre sports a bistro vibe, while rustic touches bear witness to the establishment’s age. The veteran chef concocts a modern, hearty score based on what his suppliers bring in fresh daily and in which spices are cast in the leading role: vieille (fish) with crunchy veggies in curcuma and rouille sauce; five spice leg of lamb; upside down apple pie, creamy pistachio and orange blossom. Sensibly priced lunchtime menu.

Name: Patauner
Description: Despite its simple appearance, this restaurant on the side of the road dates from the 17C and has been run by the same family for the past century. Today, the third and fourth generations work side by side in the kitchen, preparing dishes with a strong regional flavour. Highlights include the white Terlano asparagus in season and offal dishes throughout the year.

Name: Patine
Description: A proper bistro and quintessential eastern Paris spot with its open kitchen, understated decor with retro details and exposed brickwork. The menu showcases traditional cuisine based on carefully selected ingredients and expert execution. The oyster mushrooms are grilled to perfection and served with an indulgent egg yolk, confit garlic and a boldly flavoured Parmesan cream. Beautifully seared, the crispy-skinned brill is enhanced by peas, crunchy asparagus and a glazed beurre blanc. For dessert, a warm, crispy tarte fine with caramelised apples and vanilla ice cream. The wine list leans into organic and natural wines.

Name: Patois
Address: 6078 Laurel St., New Orleans, LA, 70118, USA
Description: Located a few minutes away from Audubon Butterfly Riverview Park, Patois has been a favorite date spot for those in-the-know for years. It's a classic neighborhood restaurant set inside a cottage, and its cozy and inviting interior and welcoming staff just feel right. The food matches the mood with a French-Creole flair. There's plenty to dig in to on this menu, but deviled eggs topped with wonton noodles and furikake seasoning is the twist on a staple that you didn't know you needed. The Cuban Madame is a brunch favorite, served with ham, smoked pork, gruyère and manchego custard, plus a sunny side up egg. Order a wedge of key lime tarte for dessert.

Name: Patous
Description: Bread finishes baking the moment guests arrive. The warmth and aroma of freshly baked bread are the chef’s way of graciously welcoming you. ‘Pan-seared layered scabbard fish, potato and foie gras’ has been the speciality since the restaurant’s inception. The chef’s experience comes to the fore in his subtle manipulation of flame and texture. Patous is a common name for Great Pyrenees, a breed of dog. The white fur of this dog reflects the restaurant’s pure devotion to its craft.

Name: Patricia’s
Address: 1082 Morris Park Ave., Bronx, NY, 10461, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Italian in spirit, but far from a red sauce slinging checkered tablecloth joint, Patricia's is convivial and elegant, with high ceilings featuring exposed brick walls and a semi-open kitchen. The cocktails selection is interesting, and the succinct wine list is carefully chosen with some unexpected (and fun!) Italian varietals.That brick oven churns out pleasing pizzas with lightly charred crusts, like the Regina simply adorned with buffalo mozzarella, torn basil and a drizzle of excellent olive oil. Calamari fritti are light and crispy without a touch of grease, but don’t miss the flaky and gently poached baccalà salad. Seafood risotto is creamy-dreamy with plenty of tender mussels, clams, shrimp and squid.

Name: Patrizia
Description: Creative dynamism in the very heart of the city: this is Patrizia, a restaurant named after the chef’s mother. Here the journey is singular — available in either a complete or abbreviated form — and evolves with the turning of the seasons; alongside it, the lighting, music and dining room details transform as well, following precisely the vision of young chef Tommaso Zoboli. A continuous movement of ideas and exploration, designed to satisfy himself whilst delighting his guests.The progression of dishes reveals an exuberant kitchen, rich with references to diverse thoughts and cultures, unfettered by preconceptions in its pairings and consistently thoughtful in its presentation. The storytelling at the counter, led by the chef-patron and his young team, completes a dynamic and immersive experience.

Name: Patsy
Description: In a pared-back interior featuring distressed walls, polished concrete floors, and an open kitchen, diners tuck into generous cuisine drawing on cosmopolitan influences and plenty of character. The dishes exude energy – from a mojo picón sauce that elevates a vegetarian starter to a refreshing mint sauce that invigorates the skate wing served with excellent guanciale crisps. Thrilling!

Name: Patty O's Cafe & Bakery
Description: This is "casual" as done by the meticulous chef Patrick O'Connell (of the Inn at Little Washington) whose latest project is a cafe and bakery located in a converted 1950s garage. The setting now sports a white-painted brick exterior and al fresco dining; while inside it's all country chic with an inviting marble bar counter, cozy wood tables, beamed ceiling and walls enhanced with still life canvases - all warmed by a stone-fronted fireplace.The menu offers broad appeal and all of it is executed with finesse. A sandwich of shaved Champagne-brined ham and Comté cheese on a pillowy onion roll is a lovely midday meal; while Julia Child's beef Bourguignon is a tempting option come dinnertime. Treat yourself anytime with sweets from the bakery, like the wedge of bourbon chocolate pecan pie.

Name: Patyntje
Description: A meal in this elegant colonial-style villa is a must for any self-respecting food aficionado. A superb riverside terrace by the Lys, a bustling vibe and old-fashioned table service set the scene at Patyntje, without forgetting the extensive menu of Belgian brasserie favourites. Timeless classics such as eels in sorrel, vol-au-vent and carbonade flamande (stew) prepared with textbook skill and care. Don’t miss the sweetbread fritters – one of the Michelin inspectors’ favourites since time immemorial…

Name: Paul's Canteen
Address: 162 Sihwei 3rd Road, Linya District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Cash only
Description: The Macanese owner-chef, who has been cooking professionally for over 30 years, opened this bustling spot in 2022. The menu is based on Taiwanese fare, with occasional Cantonese twists, and he seasons his food lightly allowing the natural flavours to shout their name. His deft hand is best sampled in simple dishes like scrambled egg with spinach and tomato – the mild peppery heat, bright colours and light seasonings work together seamlessly. BYOB.

Name: Paulette
Address: 18 Formosa Street, Little Venice, London, W9 1EE, United Kingdom
Description: Named after the grandmother of one of the owners, Paulette is the sort of cosy, traditional French bistro everyone laments as no longer existing. The atmosphere is convivial – you get the feeling most customers walked here – and the menu is hugely appealing; expect everything from escargots and moules marinière to filet de boeuf and chocolate soufflé. Add in a cleverly curated all-French wine list that’s great value, along with a fridge full of produce to buy and take home, and you have the recipe for a very satisfying night out.

Name: Paulownia
Description: Opposite the spot where a paulownia tree once grew, chef Geoffrey Belin and sommelier Tess Duteil (who met while working for Alain Passard) channel their passion for vegetables and good ingredients. In the wood-panelled space featuring a large curved bar, the kitchen focuses on dishes prepared à la minute and oven-roasted whole cuts (meat and fish). This comforting cuisine strikes the perfect balance: "winter summer rolls", sweet-and-sour quince; tortellini with smoked scamorza, celery consommé; braised endive, grapefruit and cloves. Notably friendly service and a keen sense of hospitality.

Name: Paute
Address: Passage Darracq, 1 rue du Hédas, Pau, 64000, France
Description: Two friends who met at catering college have hit the jackpot with this picturesque spot hidden away in a narrow little stepped street in one of the town's oldest neighbourhoods. Aromatic herbs, spices, infused vinegars made in-house, citrus fruit and authentic jus often finished with butter – a wealth of flavours that come through in dishes brimming with original ideas and childhood memories. Often a full house, so be sure to book ahead.

Name: Pavane
Description: This buzzing bistro on Granby's main thoroughfare is run by François Côté, previously encountered at the restaurant Joe Beef. The indulgent and sincere menu revolves around hearty down-to-earth fare (calf's liver with soubise sauce, macaroni au gratin with lobster, pudding chômeur) and a smattering of Asian influences (izakaya-style mackerel, kamikaze-style salmon tartare, halibut from the Gaspé Peninsula etc). The decor of wood and leather in the long, narrow space exudes warmth; laid-back service.

Name: Pavillon Steak House
Description: This restaurant boasts a gorgeous location in a small park near the centre. Sleek and chic design, high ceilings and large windows make for an airy atmosphere. As the name suggests, the focus here is on meat and different steaks. You choose origin, cut and how you would like it cooked – the kitchen takes care of the rest. There is a variety of side dishes and sauces to accompany the meat. The menu is complemented by fish and seafood - for example, one starter might be ‘seabream, citrus, wild garlic, zucchini, honey, pistachios’. Are you coming as a group? Then the steak platters are perfect for you. In addition, there’s a curated selection of wines, and the trained and friendly service team also offers recommendations by the glass.

Name: Pavāru māja
Description: At this smart village restaurant, you are encouraged to start your meal by sitting back, listening and watching the world around you in their lovely nature observation garden. Both their raised beds and regular foraging trips provide the kitchen with vegetables and herbs, and the remainder of the produce is locally sourced, with the menus informed by what’s at its peak each day. Sauces are a real highlight in dishes such as asparagus with wild garlic cream, goat’s cheese and sorrel-infused asparagus sauce or fjord trout with pickled kohlrabi, cucumber, chive oil and rhubarb and ginger broth.

Name: Paysages
Description: Here in the former capital of the Perche region, Sylvain Parisot draws inspiration from the local terroir and masters wood-fired cooking. A dish of crispy-skinned mackerel, pink at the bone, and sabayon with vin jaune perfectly illustrates the skill, sensibility and finesse of this talented young chef, who trained at renowned establishments such as L'Astrance and La Maison Lameloise. Keiko, his wife, keeps a watchful eye over the restaurant floor. A hit with foodies.

Name: Pazo de Toubes
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace
Description: Located in the heart of the Ribeiro wine region, this restaurant bearing the name of a winery occupying an 18C manor house surrounded by vineyards, comes as a pleasant surprise, courtesy of its contemporary cuisine with a local flavour enhanced by touches from further afield. The à la carte is complemented by two tasting menus, one entitled Floración (7 courses), the other Envero (9 courses), both with a wine-pairing option. We can highly recommend the sea urchin and red prawn dish, with its focus on top-quality ingredients, as well as the more traditional combo of egg with fried pig’s ear and smoked potato parmentier.

Name: Pazzo
Description: This casual, yet stylish eatery, which sports a terrace opposite, has been a prominent feature of the Antwerp F&B scene for donkey’s years. Seasoned chef Tim Meuleneire crafts, on one side, a lineup of house specials with an Italian slant, and on the other, signature dishes that bear a distinctly Gallic touch. He pays tribute to the ingredient in recipes like pheasant, cooked rare and served with an Albufeira sauce, peppery au gratin potatoes and endive stuffed with a stew of pheasant legs. Vibrant, succulent recipes underscored by a first-rate wine list, without forgetting a jazzy wine bar packed in character upstairs.

Name: Pałac Mierzęcin – Restauracja Destylarnia
Address: Mierzęcin Palace Wellness & Wine Resort, Mierzęcin 1, Dobiegniew, 66-520, Poland
Description: At this red-brick former vodka distillery, you have the chance to dine amongst the old steam generator and the hoppers which once held fermenting potatoes. It’s a hugely characterful setting which forms part of a wider country estate and sets the scene nicely for seasonal cooking with some vibrant modern touches. The bread served with homemade flavoured oils is a highlight. To drink, the wine list is entirely made up of options from their own estate.

Name: Peaches
Description: Fruit, vegetables, grains and pulses all get their moment in the spotlight at this fully vegan restaurant with stripped-back, bistro-like interiors and an open kitchen. The menu is ideal for sharing, offering original, delicately flavoured and well-balanced dishes such as fried polenta with agave and chilli syrup. Make sure you save room for the ‘sfinci’ doughnuts and homemade jam. Attentive and efficient service keeps things running smoothly.

Name: Peak
Address: 30 Hudson Yards, New York, NY, 10001, USA
Description: Pop quiz time. Where is the highest outdoor observatory deck in the western hemisphere? If you guessed The Edge at Hudson Yards, you win. And your prize? Dinner at Peak, the next-door restaurant with jaw-dropping views over lower Manhattan and New Jersey. This spot stands above the competition in this high-end complex, and while the crowd of mostly tourists and business types is largely here for those views, the food is far from a concession. Kick things off with dishes like the hiramasa topped with Kirby cucumber and watermelon radish before a skin-on roasted chicken with roasted kabocha squash and kale pesto. Unsurprisingly, the prices skew high.

Name: Peang-Prai
Address: 101/18 Soi Namtok Bangpae, Ban Pa Khlok Road, Pa Khlok, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: In the depths of the forest at the entrance to Bang Pae waterfall, two wooden pavilions stand connected by a terrace walkway. Here, a family-run restaurant faces a lagoon and a verdant wall of forest, while diners are accompanied by the welcoming calls of birds and gibbons. The tranquil ambiance is joined by traditional Thai and Southern Thai cooking, with local Phuket dishes standing out. Seasonal local clams are delicious and can be cooked many ways, including stir-fried with chilli paste.

Name: Pearl
Description: Do you want to travel to Japan without leaving the Algarve coast? This restaurant, located in the heart of Faro and close to the Church of São Pedro, combines techniques of Japanese cuisine with the best local ingredients! Born of its creators’ desire to explore and reinterpret Japanese culture, this project invites us around a counter with capacity for 10 diners to immerse ourselves in this culinary art. The offer, presented by three chefs who share roles, revolves around the Omakase concept and turns each visit into a unique experience, adapting the offering to the fresh products available at the fish auction and also to the inspiration of the day. Ingredients such as oyster, prawn, eel, squid, turbot, bluefin tuna shine in dishes such as oyster, sardine and redbanded seabream, different kinds of Nigiri, Sashimi… Dive into this experience and let yourself be surprised by the riches of the region!

Name: Pearl 6101
Address: 6101 California St., San Francisco, CA, 94121, USA
Description: This spot in a retro drugstore still draws in a lively local crowd—not unlike neighboring sister, Pizzetta 211. The big and airy space is charming, as is the friendly staff, and a well-curated Italian-focused wine list and well-crafted cocktails are additional bonuses. The kitchen turns out a Cal-Italian menu, like rustic handkerchiefs in a creamy white Bolognese sauce, or caramelle filled with melty crescenza cheese and paired with smoked walnuts, chanterelles and brown butter. Vegetable lovers will find plenty to love on the menu, as in a roasted Japanese sweet potato paired with a miso tahini sauce and peanut salsa macha.

Name: Pebble
Description: A chef whose skills were honed in Italian restaurants works alongside an affable owner-sommelier. Delicate, seasonal dishes are paired with wines from around the world. The food is presented with evident enthusiasm, born of a desire to convey the dedication of the producers behind it. Designed by Tadao Ando, the modern exposed-concrete space looks out over the gently flowing Okawa River.

Name: Peckham Cellars
Address: 125 Queens Road, Peckham, London, SE15 2ND, United Kingdom
Description: This neighbourhood bistro and wine bar is run by three friends, who all hail from this part of South East London. Original small plates have a rustic style; they’re made for sharing, so choose three or four per person – if you’re in a group, consider ordering the whole menu. The wine list features some interesting small producers and they even have some wines on tap.

Name: Peculiare Restaurant
Description: Just steps from the Arco dell’Annunziata, in a quiet side street off Via Roma, Peculiare is the reflection of a young chef’s talent. The menu blends creativity and tradition, with dishes such as sole Wellington, tagliolini with sea urchins, and a refined Rossini-style filet with velvety purée and foie gras. The sober, elegant setting unfolds in an 18th-century palace, where an ancient arch tells the story of the place. The warm welcome and genuine smiles round out the experience.

Name: Pedra Furada
Address: Rúa Do Comandante Fontanes 6, A Coruña, 15003, Spain
Description: Located a stone’s throw from the Playa del Orzán, Pedra Furada can be viewed as a sibling of the successful Morrofino de Vigo as it shares the same culinary philosophy thanks to its fun, contemporary and meticulous dishes that also place a little more emphasis on top-quality ingredients inspired by the sea (e.g. flame-seared mackerel with cosium and a citrus jus with yellow chilli, and the grilled squid, onion sauce and delicate saffron cream). The à la carte, which is designed for sharing, is complemented by two menus entitled Pedra and Orixe, both served to the whole table.

Name: Pedro Martino
Description: On the banks of the river Nalón, approximately 4 miles southwest of Oviedo, this colourful house occupies the premises of what was once L'Alezna, a restaurant that already shone with a MICHELIN Star between 2004 and 2008. Chef Pedro Martino, who has returned to his origins and has given his own name to the renovated business, seeks to bring Asturias to our palates, which is why every day, along with the appetising menu, he presents a menu called Orígenes Tradición (Origins Tradition) and another, more extensive and modern, called Orígenes Degustación (Origins Tasting) (the latter is a sequence of small bites where the chef, with great skill and care, brings the powerful flavours of yesteryear into the modern day). Which dishes caught our attention the most? There are several, such as the Caramietcha (pork cheek cured in salt), the Caldo de Pote (this stew was the predecessor of the famous fabada), the delicate onion stuffed with tuna and liquid yolk, the grilled wild turbot... It has a pleasant terrace and panoramic dining rooms!

Name: Pegasus
Description: Pegasus is poised to take wing at the entrance to this restaurant housed in a magnificent 18C abode. While you immerse yourself in the classical interior (woodwork, old tiles), run your eye over the menu. This will reveal a wide choice of balanced dishes, all of which are made with fine produce. Lovely terrace.

Name: Peixes Bonaparte
Description: Between Place Garibaldi and the port, this offshoot of the Peixes Opéra also boasts a huge terrace that is taken by storm on sunny days! The Bonaparte deploys the same winning formula of seafood dishes (fish, tataki, sashimi, accras, oysters) and ceviche specialities. The updated blue and white seafaring bistro decor calls to mind Portugal or Greece. Behind the bar, a mixologist conjures up cocktails. The lunch menu is a steal. Open all day long, albeit with a more concise menu until 7pm.

Name: Peixes Opéra
Description: Near the town hall and the opera house is Peixes – pronounced "pesh" (i.e. "fish" in Portuguese). In a dinky bistro interior adorned in blue and white tiles, fish and seafood is served in the form of tapas-style dishes (ceviche, carpaccio, tataki fried fish, cod fritters). Mediterranean and South American accents are joyfully blended into dishes that are packed in fresh, vibrant flavours. Extremely popular, non-stop service from noon to midnight with a concise slate menu from 2-7pm, no bookings; the terrace is frequently taken by storm.

Name: Pellico 3
Description: The Park Hyatt’s small gastronomic jewel enjoys one of the most privileged positions in the city: it may be reached directly from the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, or alternatively through the cocktail bar with its street entrance. The interiors, adorned with works of contemporary art, are complemented by elegant and precise service, creating the ideal context for the cuisine of young chef Guido Paternollo. The proposal is articulated across two tasting menus: “La mia città”, a personal homage to Milan, and a freer itinerary tied to seasonality and the inspiration of the moment. Both reveal a modern, intense, and well-calibrated cuisine, capable of exploring interesting pairings without ever losing balance, as in the wild garlic risotto with morels and sea snails, finished with a delicate smoked scamorza cream. The experience is completed by an outstanding wine service, guided by sommelier Lorenzo, who leads guests with expertise through a selection of around 700 labels, with particular attention also given to wines by the glass.

Name: Penang Famous Samosa
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Pets not allowed
Description: This stall in Little India serves a delicious range of samosas, including mutton, chicken, sardine, egg and vegetable. Encased in a crispy shell, the flavoursome fillings are moderately spicy. Prices are fair, too, so no wonder customers are prepared to queue.

Name: Penati al Baretto
Address: 94 boulevard de la Tour-Maubourg, Paris, 75007, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: It is no secret that Italians have great taste. Milanese chef Alberico Penati has set up shop in this chic bistro with honey-coloured wood panelling, and bay windows overlooking the garden of the Invalides – a highly prized location indeed! Tradition is the chef's passion. With no concessions to passing fashions, his menu features a selection of Italian classics made out of carefully selected ingredients. Home-made pasta remains the forte of this place, eg ravioli del plin piemontesi with a very good roast beef jus. The 100% Italian wine list highlights Piedmontese wines, particularly Barolo and Barbaresco.

Name: Peninsula House
Address: Level 1, India House, 25B Lebuh Pantai, George Town, 10300, Malaysia
Description: The discreet entrance and stairway may appear shabby, but the lofty, retro restaurant space on the upper floor of this heritage building (1937) is nothing short of sublime. The short Australian-inspired menu features over 10 appetisers and mains, made using organic produce from local indoor farms and its own garden. The speciality is seafood, and the crayfish and prawn étouffée tagliatelle stands out for its deep umami. Reservations are a must.

Name: Penny
Address: 90 E. 10th St., New York, NY, 10003, USA
Description: Two cool marble counters stretch the length of the bar and kitchen and run parallel to mounds of ice stacked with bottles of Champagne and crisp white wines. The food is no less refreshing, celebrating mostly pristine seafood expertly sourced and astutely dressed and seasoned. Think razor clams with giardiniera, stuffed squid with fiery harissa, and wax beans dusted in katsuobushi. Dover sole set in an excellent bordelaise would satisfy a meatier appetite, but then again, how about just another round of freshly shucked oysters or maybe a vanilla bean and passionfruit ice cream sandwich? A small number of reservations are available, but most seats are reserved for walk-ins, so arrive early just before doors open.

Name: Pensionat Furuhem
Description: Båstad might be known as Sweden’s centre of tennis, but Chef Magnus Nilsson is also aiming to put it on the map as somewhere to visit for its cuisine. In the centre of the seaside resort – also famed for its Cold Bath House – sits this beautiful white building dotted with green balconies, where three simply decorated, wood-furnished rooms provide a perfect match for the unfussy cuisine. The spettekaka dessert is not to be missed – a local speciality made from traditional Scanian pastry, slowly grilled all day over beech embers, then cut to order at your table and served with daily changing accompaniments.

Name: Pentole e Provette
Description: This restaurant run by Luca Trabalzini and his partner Rossella is a real gem in the small town of Fasano. Their story, which began in Australia, adds a fascinating touch to this gastronomic project. The atmosphere here is warm and lively, making this the perfect setting in which to enjoy the chef’s innovative cuisine, which he showcases on three distinct menus dedicated to meat, fish and vegetarian dishes respectively. Luca’s cuisine is modern and elegant, with particular attention paid to flavours and textures so that each and every dish offers a fully rounded sensorial experience.

Name: People's Palace
Address: GF, Greenbelt 3, Esperanza Street, Makati - Metro Manila, 1223, The Philippines
Description: Relocated to premises beside Greenbelt Park in 2020, this Thai restaurant in a minimalist, high-ceilinged space has a resort-like feel. The Filipino chef faithfully crafts MSG-free Thai classics, with heat levels tailored to local tastes. Start with tod man pla – tasty fishcakes paired with sweet-sour cucumber chilli sauce, and finish with tako, a coconut milk and tapioca pudding. Attentive service and upbeat evening vibes are the icing on the cake.

Name: People's Park Hainanese Chicken Rice
Address: People's Park Complex Food Centre, #01-1098, 32 New Market Road, 050032, Singapore
Description: Cantonese barbecue like roast pork and duck aside, the main draws are Hainanese chicken rice and double-boiled soups. The rice is richly perfumed with garlic and the flavourful chicken with a gelatinous skin is not to be missed.

Name: Pepe Nero
Description: Overlooking the western shore of Lake Bolsena, Pepe Nero is an intimate restaurant that wins one over through its modern furnishings and a pleasing maritime character. The service, gentle and professional, discreetly accompanies a predominantly seafood gastronomic journey, conceived for an immersive and unhurried experience of flavour. Guests may opt for themed menus or entrust themselves to the carte, choosing at least two dishes. The wine list ranges across regional and national labels, while in the warmer months a small terrace at the water’s edge affords the pleasure of dining with a direct view over the lake shore.

Name: Pepenero
Address: piazza del Duomo 4, San Miniato, 56028, Italy
Description: In its new home in Piazza del Duomo, in beautiful San Miniato, in the hands of chef Gilberto Rossi Pepenero continues to serve cuisine that showcases the best ingredients (both meat and fish) from this bountiful region, with delicacies such as excellent truffles featuring on the menu throughout the year. Prepared with a light and modern touch, meals are served in a spacious dining room where the many windows offer glimpses of the town centre.

Name: Peploe's
Address: 16 St. Stephen's Green, Dublin City, D02 KF34, Ireland
Description: Named after Scottish painter Samuel J. Peploe, a favourite of the owner, this atmospheric cellar restaurant occupies a former bank vault, with the space now having a warm, clubby feel thanks to its red leather banquettes and large, colourful murals. While Irish produce is at the core of the tried-and-tested cooking, inspiration tends to come from around Europe, be that in a classic French onion soup or the signature chicken Milanese, which mines plenty of flavour from the well-seasoned meat and the simple, capably executed accompaniments.

Name: Pequeno Mundo
Description: If you’re looking for a pleasant, romantic spot with excellent service… this is a must-visit restaurant! Set in a charming Algarvian house, with outdoor courtyards filled with plants and greenery. Inside, it’s divided into different dining rooms, plus a bar area at the entrance, complete with a lovely fireplace. The concept is based on international cuisine, with strong French and Portuguese influences, highlighting the quality of the predominantly local produce. The menu features a 6-course tasting option, vegetarian choices, and off-menu dishes featuring the day’s freshest products. Our recommendations? The prawns with sautéed portobello mushrooms and, for dessert, the crispy red fruits — light and delightful on the palate!

Name: Perbacco
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A rustic restaurant offering an authentic taste of the Cilento area, both in its setting amid lush Mediterranean vegetation and in its regional cuisine. Fish and seafood dominate the antipasti selection, while the main courses focus more on meat and vegetable dishes. Good choice of regional wines, plus the option of a few pleasant guestrooms.

Name: Perception
Description: Under the helm of Korean chef Sukwon Yong, Perception rolls out a felicitous, spot-on score that wavers between France and Korea. In a subdued decor of polished concrete and soft lights, the lunch and evening tasting menus celebrate first-class, flavoursome ingredients: mandu (Korean dumplings) with a gochujang-laced KFC (Korean Fried Chicken) sauce or flame-licked mackerel, daikon radish balls, tarama ice cream and Japanese-inspired yuzu koshô. A spicy, expressive score in keeping with the house ethos.

Name: Periplo Portixol
Description: An informal restaurant that stands out for its pleasant views of Palma bay from its impressive setting in the old Molinar fisherman’s district. The highlights here, on an à la carte mainly featuring dishes designed for two sharing, are the meticulously prepared fish and seafood purchased at the market daily and cooked mainly on the open grill.

Name: Perle
Address: 43 E. Union St., Pasadena, CA, 91103, USA
Description: This quaint French bistro feels right at home in downtown Pasadena. The cozy space draws in anybody walking by, thanks to vintage frames, sturdy Mahogany tables, and a coffered wood ceiling. Whereas many restaurants are content to merely look like a French bistro, in this one Chef Dean Yasharian has the chops to cook like one too.There is no need to reinvent the wheel and he knows it, carefully preparing such sleek, straight-shot Parisian classics as Burgundy snails glistening in herbed butter; silky-smooth pork pâté wrapped in pastry; and duck à l’orange with celery root purée. Dessert is essential: the airy Gran Marnier soufflé with crème fraîche ice cream and indulgent apple tarte Tartin are exactly the kind of sweet comforts worth returning for.

Name: Pernambucco
Description: This restaurant boasts a garden setting with a pleasant outdoor dining space, plus a long, narrow interior decorated in decidedly classic style. Fish and seafood take pride of place on the menu, with a focus on local fish, including excellent tartare (usually either seabream or tuna, depending on the catch of the day) and shellfish (cooked in salt, baked or grilled). The vegetables are sourced from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden.

Name: Peron
Description: On the coast road, this building clinging to the rocks commands a breathtaking view of the bay of Marseille and its islands and the château d’If. A bracing Mediterranean breeze has refreshed the menu: roast squid, chickpea, lemon and ginger seasoning; carpaccio of grouper, cream of pinenuts, grilled capers and coriander; translucent monkfish, a reduction of fishbones, roasted spring cauliflower with seaweed. Local and wild fish of the day, without forgetting the ubiquitous bouillabaisse, are served alfresco. A landmark since 1855!

Name: Perroquet Vert
Description: This intimate, lively restaurant on the Place de la Fontaine exudes the Belle Epoque charm of the Parisian brasseries of old. A feel that chimes perfectly with the traditional, French dishes chalked up on the blackboard. Favourites include scallop risotto, entrecôte and tarte tatin.

Name: Perseid
Address: Hotel Saint Augustine, 4110 Loretto Dr., Houston, TX, 77006, USA
Description: With light streaming in from all sides, this cheery, French-inspired bistro is a cut above your typical hotel restaurant. A collaboration between Chef Aaron Bludorn and the boutique Hotel Saint Augustine, the stand-alone dining room is painted head to toe in sunflower yellow with tall windows and a spacious patio to boot. Expect familiar favorites prepared with refinement like smoked salmon dip with everything bagel seasoning and house-fried potato chips or steelhead trout with Romano beans and sauce almondine. Roast duck breast, serious steaks, and an endlessly tempting dessert selection round out the offerings. Matching the tenor of the room, attentive servers keep guests at ease. As an added bonus, breakfast is offered all week as well.

Name: Persepolis
Address: 1407 Second Ave., New York, NY, 10021, USA
Description: Silky-smooth spreads, homemade yogurt, grilled meats and fragrantly spiced stews have solidified Persepolis’ reputation as one of the city’s finest Persian restaurants. Linen-draped tables, spacious banquettes and big windows facing Second Avenue fashion a look that inspires dressing up (or not). Service is always gracious, if at times too earnest.The kitchen shines with its eggplant halim, a creamy, steaming roasted eggplant and onion dip with tender lentils and a dollop of yogurt on top. A kebab duo of saffron-tinged chicken and grilled beef are both succulent successes, served with basmati rice flecked with sour cherries. For dessert, try the tart-sweet Persian lemon ice studded with bits of rice noodles and doused in a deep red cherry syrup.

Name: Persika
Description: Persika is a name that combines Italy and Sweden: in both languages, it means "peach." In the Chia district, an Italian restaurateur collaborates with a highly experienced Swedish chef to create a gastro-bistro with a relaxed and welcoming atmosphere. The surprise menu is often chosen, but there's also an interesting and accessible à la carte option. The cuisine is contemporary, with international influences and a strong focus on local ingredients.

Name: Persona
Description: Named after the 1966 Ingmar Bergman film, this stylish restaurant creates a striking contrast between its old townhouse exterior and its elegant interior design. Before dinner you are invited down to the cellar to pick your wine; the chefs then adjust the à la carte depending on your choice. Alternatively, you can opt for the fixed tasting menu to enjoy the full breadth of the cooking. Expect bold flavours and quality ingredients, supported by relaxed service and an immersive feel.

Name: Perłowa Pijalnia Piwa
Description: Located in the heart of the city, this restaurant forms part of a wider complex that offers something for everyone, including bars, apartments, a terrace and a cinema. A brewery is at the core of it all however, with exclusive beers available in the restaurant alongside local radlers perfect for a hot summer’s day. The cooking is hearty and doesn’t skimp on flavour, in nourishing dishes such as gnocchi with roasted pumpkin or a tweaked version of tiramisu.

Name: Pescarino-Sapori di Terra e di Mare
Description: Warm and inviting atmosphere with wooden walls and ceiling. The kitchen, recently renovated alongside the terrace, remains unchanged in offering: relatively simple in some concoctions, more creative in others, aiming primarily to highlight the product quality, predominantly seafood, with Ligurian nuances but extending to other regions. Considering the isolated location, seizing the opportunity to rest in the rooms may be worthwhile.

Name: Pesceria San Martino
Description: Born as a fishmonger’s and transformed over time into a small seafood delicatessen, this venue welcomes guests into a simple yet thoughtfully appointed setting, with an intimate front room and a colourful conservatory at the rear that opens to the outdoors in summer. Here Ivan manages front of house with courtesy and expertise, while in the kitchen Bartolo selects the freshest produce with great care. Among the more distinctive offerings, the original and well-executed “seafood charcuterie” stands out, alongside fried squid that is also available for takeaway. Not to be missed is the pan-cooked baby octopus, tender and flavourful, served with a datterini tomato sauce and a crispy bruschetta that practically begs you to mop up every last drop. Strong demand makes booking essential, particularly at weekends.

Name: Pescheria
Description: The name of this restaurant between the historic centre and the seafront refers to the main item on its menu, which is dedicated almost exclusively to fish (fresh and not farmed). Fish and shellfish are displayed in a glass cabinet and aquarium respectively, both of which are situated to the rear of the long, narrow dining room near the open-view kitchen. Classic fish dishes full of flavour (served raw, baked, cooked in salt, in water or grilled) are to the fore here.

Name: Petals of a Peony
Address: 1250 N. Germantown Pkwy., #105, Cordova, TN, 38016, USA
Description: Opened in 2013, this Chinese restaurant has taken the city by storm—and rightly so. Although there are a number of offshoots around town, the original location in an unsuspecting Cordova strip center is the place to be. For those who love heat and savor spice, this is ground zero for fiery, tongue-numbing, chili-laden Sichuan cuisine. Focus on classics like the umami-packed mapo tofu, stir-fried cumin lamb, crispy chicken tossed in a mound of dried chilis and properly charred green beans. Portions are generous so bring friends and order with abandon.

Name: Peter Luger
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Peter Luger remains an unapologetic New York classic, where dry-aged Porterhouse and old-school charm are the main event. The wood-paneled rooms buzz with longtime regulars and curious newcomers, all tended by brisk, good-humored servers. Start with a house-made bratwurst or the iceberg wedge crowned with thick-cut bacon, then move on to the sizzling Porterhouse, broiled and served with its buttery jus. Simple sides like German potatoes, creamed spinach or sautéed broccoli round out the experience. Of course, there is always room for cheesecake — and schlag. Bring cash, come hungry and enjoy a slice of living history.

Name: Petersham Nurseries Restaurant
Address: Church Lane, Richmond, London, TW10 7AG, United Kingdom
Description: As you sit in the greenhouse with sand at your feet, surrounded by fresh flowers which even in the winter months perfume the air, it feels as though all is right with the world. A unique spot within the London dining scene, this restaurant forms part of the wider Petersham Nurseries complex, where you can buy plants and homeware to spruce up your abode. The cooking features some herbs and vegetables from the garden and has a clear Italian accent, from pea risotto with crispy pancetta to hake with mussels and saffron sauce.

Name: Peti 181
Description: This restaurant’s excellent location is best appreciated in summer, with tables overlooking the river and charming views of the castle lit up at night. The dining room, personally designed by the chef with taste and sensitivity, is also attractive, boasting muted tones and an elegant and intimate ambience inspired by the early 20C. The cuisine is Mediterranean in style, with a focus on fish and seafood – the shellfish are excellent, as is the delicious grilled sea bass with buttered mashed potatoes. One of the house specialities (which must be booked in advance) is the lamb cooked in the wood-fired oven and served with seasonal vegetables. The wine list focuses on Slovenian labels, which are also available by the glass.

Name: Petit Boutary
Description: Petit Boutary is certainly living up to the standard set by its Left Bank counterpart. In this refined bistro, with a black and white chequered floor, zinc-topped bar, leather-clad banquette seating and hanging light bulbs, modern, creative cuisine is served in the form of a single surprise menu with several courses. You may taste the house signature dish: “Potatoes in Boutary caviar”.

Name: Petit Comitè Gaig
Address: Passatge de la Concepció 13, Barcelona, 08008, Spain
Description: A restaurant with a contemporary look and renowned chef Carles Gaig at the helm in the kitchen which focuses on traditional cuisine that remains faithful to Catalan gastronomy. Choose between the à la carte and the set menu, but to make things easier we can recommend either the latter (Gran Ágape) or the always-interesting daily suggestions. The fish dishes here particularly stand out; in addition, some dishes are available in half portions.

Name: Petit Grill Basque
Description: Basque chef, Inaki Aizpitarte, is breathing new life into this almost centennial institution.
