They work with the finest ingredients and know how to elevate them with exuberant sauces seasoned, for example, with the perfect amount of curry. This cuisine is sophisticated and, at times, delicate. Be sure to explore the selection of wines; after dinner, an impressive whisky collection awaits you in the lounge.

Name: Restaurant Kanalen
Description: This quaint building was once the Harbour Police Office, and there's a delightful canal-side terrace from which you can watch the boats bobbing up and down as you eat. Inside it has a bistro-like feel, with long wooden benches and old plank flooring. Dishes are seasonal, unpretentious and full of flavour; some honouring Danish traditions and others bringing Mediterranean ingredients into play.

Name: Restaurant Krainer
Description: The second restaurant of the hotel of the same name lies in the centre of the village and offers an altogether classic dining experience with its tastefully designed upscale interior and Andreas Krainer's cuisine. The chef's passion for reinvented classics is evident in dishes such as "Tschantschendorf pigeon from Gerhard Methlagl, kohlrabi from Vali, cherries from our garden, brioche dumplings". He prides himself on using regional produce, most of it sourced from the immediate vicinity. The set menu comprises four or six courses and is complemented by a selection of fine wines, as well as attentive service provided by a friendly and adept front-of-house team. Alternatively, you can dine in the Wirtshaus with its conservatory-style setting.

Name: Restaurant Kurt im Gutshaus
Description: A truly idyllic location. A cobblestone drive meanders through the stunning estate to the lovingly restored historical manor that houses this restaurant. Inside, contemporary design elements have been seamlessly incorporated into the classically elegant decor. The terrace overlooking the grounds is glorious in summer! Expect clearly structured modern cuisine made primarily with regional ingredients. There are two set menus: "Nachbarschaft" ("Neighbourhood") and the vegetarian "Ackerland" ("Farmland"), each comprising four to six courses. Dishes can also be ordered individually. Friendly service and astute by-the-glass wine recommendations add the finishing touch. The wine list features labels from around the globe. Tastefully furnished guestrooms are available at Gutshaus Stolpe hotel, where patrons can also relax in a heated outdoor pool and saunas.

Name: Restaurant L'église
Description: The atmospheric L'église feels like a cosy wine bar and is instantly welcoming. You can just pop in for a glass of wine – hostess Kira has put together a list of excellent options – and a few nibbles, but we definitely recommend opting for the set menu or something from the à la carte selection. Chef Niek proves that just a few elements are enough to make a dish come alive. The food is meticulously prepared with an emphasis on zest and punch, as well as a dash of international flair. For example, he creates a ceviche dish in which sweet, fruity watermelon, sweet-and-sour pickled radish and a citrus jus elevate the fish. Just a hint of vadouvan gives the lamb rump an exotic twist. This is easy fine dining that will bring a smile to the face of even the most discerning foodie!

Name: Restaurant Lassey - Château Sainte-Sabine
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the picturesque Auxois region of Burgundy, a Renaissance château provides a historic backdrop for a plush stylish restaurant. The chef signs a gourmet lineup: artichoke and mushroom tartlet with confit egg yolk and a creamy époisses sauce; Corton pigeon roasted whole with raviole of offal, smoked beetroot and a coffee- and miso-laced jus, ending with a dark chocolate soufflé and blackcurrant sorbet extravaganza. Fine dining set menus in the evening, simpler lunchtime deal, and brunch on Saturdays. The guestrooms invite you to unwind as you take in the lake and bucolic grounds, where deer roam. Slick service.

Name: Restaurant Le Sable
Description: The charm of tranquil Zandoerle permeates this old farmhouse, where authenticity, Scandinavian design and a homely atmosphere meet. Owner Laura comes outside to give diners a warm welcome and, with her team, provides impeccable service. She draws on a wealth of experience and talent despite her young age (she also makes the delicious sweet treats served with the coffee!). The same goes for chef Chiel, whose dishes reflect that youthful playfulness. Although he draws primarily on French culinary tradition, the chef likes to add his own twist, serving dishes as a series of small plates. A dessert featuring an exotic composition of white chocolate cake, pineapple compote and a yuzu and ginger sauce demonstrates the kitchen's nuanced understanding of flavour. The palpable sense of ambition at Le Sable makes it all the more appealing.

Name: Restaurant Lepelem
Description: Ellen and Christopher have gradually turned a former tearoom into a smart restaurant. An exquisite home-from-home vibe and a wine list that will knock your socks off are among its standouts. Christopher enthusiastically offers diners the possibility of composing their own à la carte menu. He has a knack for juggling familiar flavours with complex preparations, depicted by hand-shelled shrimps with a creamy burrata, pickled watermelon and a fragrant dashi, or juicy, melt-in-the-mouth turbot flanked by a silky bearnaise sauce. Unbeatable quality-for-pleasure ratio.

Name: Restaurant MANNA
Description: MANNA blends fashion and cosmopolitan flair in a building full of character. Out front, there's a charming city terrace; inside, no fewer than five private dining rooms await, along with luxurious hotel rooms upstairs. Fish takes centre stage here, but meat lovers and vegetarians are equally well catered for. The plates presented are just as on trend as the setting. Whether you are in the mood for a bento box starter, followed by a succulent entrecôte with a balsamic-infused roasting jus, or sea bass baked in a salt crust, MANNA delivers. Alternatively, indulge in a super fresh seafood platter from the fish bar. This is your go-to spot, open daily for both lunch and dinner.

Name: Restaurant Mare
Description: Located on the island of Čiovo, just a five-minute walk from Trogir’s historic center, the restaurant is located in the Bifora Heritage Hotel, a finely restored fourteenth-century building. Chef Robert Predag Zmire offers refined, contemporary cuisine founded on quality ingredients and modern, precise technique. Fish is the star, though meat dishes and vegan options are available. The wine list, while not extensive, is well-selected, offering excellent value with numerous Croatian labels available by the glass. A welcoming and authentic address slightly off the beaten path, this restaurant offers moments of pure relaxation on its intimate stone patio, rich in charm, during warmer months.

Name: Restaurant Markant
Description: (Markant moved to Doctor Batenburglaan 111 in Breda) This cosy little establishment outside Breda city centre bears its name well. The fact that the staff take great pleasure in spoiling their diners is palpable. Decorative features such as wine crates show that Markant is driven by a passion for wine as well as food. Be sure to take a look at the wine list, which features all sorts of great finds, before perusing the extensive à la carte menu. The young chef's repertoire includes classics such as œuf en gelée, as well as vegetarian options and the occasional Asian-influenced creation. His attention to quality is evident in the generosity of flavours and depth of the sauces. Some dishes are prepared right at your table, which is a nice touch.

Name: Restaurant Mathes
Description: This restaurant, on the scenic wine road of this pretty region of Moselle and near a splendid village that boasts innumerable wine cellars and vineyards, is well known to foodies. Today, the third generation is upholding the family legacy and diners will taste textbook classics with a subtle modern spin served in an elegant dining room overlooking the Moselle or on the sun-drenched terrace. The menu is the epitome of traditional and the house signature remains zander – oven-bake, underscored by a delicate Riesling sauce and washed down with an attractive selection of Luxembourg wines. Just the spot to explore this lovely region.

Name: Restaurant Max'es
Description: A chic bistro vibe, friendly hospitality and good food are the hallmarks of the restaurant of the Hotel Wegner, a family-run business since 1957. The cuisine is modern and takes its cue from the changing seasons. The chefs like to give their dishes the finishing touch at your table when they serve, for example, cheese wheel pasta, crêpes Suzette or fillet of sole. Tip: Pre-order beef Wellington, Chateaubriand or the monthly changing set menu. In summer, be sure to secure a table on the quiet, leafy terrace! You can also come for breakfast.

Name: Restaurant Melt
Description: Jan Audenaert believes in simplicity before all else, mixing vegetables and exotic herbs to compose stunningly presented dishes. His creativity shines through in the detail he lavishes on the side dishes, illustrated by his upside-down pumpkin pie which is served with a gutsy breast of pheasant. Nothing leaves his kitchen that hasn’t been endlessly pondered and puzzled over. We recommend his lunchtime menus. The minimalist interior of this restored presbytery suits this culinary offering down to a T!

Name: Restaurant Meudon
Address: Hotel Meudon, Maenporth Road, Mawnan Smith, TR11 5HT, United Kingdom
Description: Imposing granite pillars and neatly laid tables help to bring an air of classical elegance to this restaurant inside the Hotel Meudon. The dining room overlooks impressive mature sub-tropical gardens, which also contribute to the all-round lovely setting. The concise, daily changing menu is Cornish at heart, especially when it comes to seafood. Dishes like Mylor crab filo tart are understated yet well-executed and wholly enjoyable.

Name: Restaurant Morillon
Description: Previously Le Staeffele, an institution in Saverne, this place has been taken over by a small, enthusiastic team. It has an intimate feel, with 10 tables at which diners pick from the à la carte menu or opt for the ambitious tasting menu. The name refers to morels – these mushrooms are always on the menu, prepared in different ways depending on the season for a wonderfully indulgent interlude. The lunch set menu is good value for money.

Name: Restaurant Mosaic - Château des Tesnières
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: In the lavishly restored Château des Tesnières, South African chef Chantel Dartnall has brought to life an ambitious project combining fine dining and charming accommodation. The decor – a blend of Art Nouveau wood panelling and artwork from South Africa – makes for an eclectic atmosphere. With a focus on plants and flowers, the set menus are captivating with their visual poetry and the quality of the ingredients. The wine cellar, packed with wines from around the world, with a particular focus on South Africa, is impressive. A handful of luxurious rooms on the floor above.

Name: Restaurant Moustique
Description: Located in the heart of Haarlem, Moustique boasts stylish interior design and a terrace overlooking the Grote Kerk, plus it's open every day of the week – what a treat! The chef showcases his experience through an appealing à la carte selection and a multi-course tasting menu. He is just as adept at jazzing up fish with pickled cucumber, horseradish and jalapeño as he is at putting his own spin on steak tartare. The kitchen team thrives on excitement and daring combinations, but never at the expense of harmony on the plate.

Name: Restaurant Nectar
Description: With its elegant, warm and welcoming decor, Nectar brings the historical charm of Zutphen's city centre indoors. The concept is compelling from the outset: all dishes are served in medium-sized portions and are available both in tasting menus and à la carte. From the very first bite, you can tell that Joost van Outheusden gives free rein to his creativity without lapsing into unnecessary complexity. Succulent monkfish, for instance, is glazed with XO sauce and served with fennel in a variety of textures and a beurre blanc infused with tandoori spices. This is playful cooking that looks beyond borders and allows bold flavours to speak for themselves - all in a wonderfully welcoming setting!

Name: Restaurant Nigl
Description: Upon arrival, you are greeted by a sensational backdrop – let your gaze linger on the Nigl family vineyard and the vine-covered slopes, with the castle ruins, Burgruine Senftenberg, looming above. In addition to the wine estate with its delightful courtyard, a hotel and a shop, there is a charming restaurant. Chef Bertram Nigl presents a menu featuring regional and French classics, such as "Grandma Nigl's traditional Waldviertel-style Grammelknödel (potato dumpling stuffed with greaves)" and "braised beef roulade with Schupfnudeln (potato dumplings), Brussels sprouts and carrots". Everything is carefully prepared with attention to detail, and the flavours are robust. The outdoor dining area is a truly special place, to be enjoyed in fine weather.

Name: Restaurant OY
Address: B1F, 48-12 Seolleung-ro 148-gil, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, 06064, South Korea
Description: Tucked away on a quiet residential street, Restaurant OY blends seamlessly into its surroundings with a modest, serene façade. Run by chef duo Sehun Oh, a veteran of French kitchens, and Le Cordon Bleu-trained Ah-young Yoon, the restaurant offers elegantly restrained French cuisine. Oh handles the savoury courses while Yoon crafts the desserts. Their deep understanding of ingredients and polished technique result in dishes that are simple, balanced, and refined, such as a delicate bean soup, tender pork tenderloin with a rich sauce, and a decadent fondant au chocolat.

Name: Restaurant Old Skool
Description: Old Skool is, quite literally, an old school, but today it is first and foremost a stylish restaurant with a charming retro-modern aesthetic – think atmospheric lighting, herringbone parquet flooring, warm colours and bold artwork. In his cooking, meanwhile, the chef leans decidedly towards the new school, incorporating flavours from far-flung places and placing great emphasis on vibrancy. Succulent pheasant roulade, for instance, is accompanied by a Guinness jus that brings caramelised notes, alongside mustard seeds, a refreshing quince compote and fig cream. This cuisine is full of energy, and the enticing vegetable-led tasting menu is no exception.

Name: Restaurant Olivia
Address: 290 S. Downing St., Denver, CO, 80209, USA
Description: Partners Ty Leon, Austin Carson and Heather Morrison bring their talents to bear at one of the city's hottest tables, respectively overseeing cooking, beverages and warm hospitality (Morrison's daughter is also the restaurant's namesake). House-made pasta occupies the bulk of the menu, from bronze-die extruded gemelli with Umbrian sausage and pecorino cream, or hand-shaped tortellini filled with braised duck. The offerings range from fairly traditional, like the tagliatelle Bolognese, to inventively globe-trotting, as in ricotta gnocchi paired coconut lobster bisque and black garlic, but assertive flavors are a constant throughout. Inventive cocktails serve well as aperitifs, or to sip while lingering in the relaxed, comfortable atmosphere.

Name: Restaurant Olivo
Description: Its Belle Epoque style lends this restaurant on the first floor of the Grand Casino a distinct elegance and charm that hark back to a bygone era. Under a high ceiling with moulding and chandeliers, Mediterranean-inspired cuisine is served in the form of a set menu or à la carte. The "Dinner & Casino" packages are also worth mentioning. Fabulous balcony terrace with lake and mountain views. Tip: Park in the casino garage.

Name: Restaurant Palægade
Description: Enter past the pavement terrace with sheepskin-covered chairs and you’ll find yourself in this beautiful brasserie with a striking black & whited tiled floor, unique brass light fittings and oak & walnut chairs modelled on Finn Juhl’s ‘Reading Chair’. During the day, this is the place to come for smørrebrød – both traditional and modern – from warm fried herring with caramelised onion, ramson and apple to red pickled herring with dark berries and crème fraiche. At night, the menu focuses on contemporary Danish cuisine and an impressive wine list, with the hand-crafted dessert trolley a real feature.

Name: Restaurant Pony
Description: Nestled in a small town at an elevation of 770m, this third-generation family business serves classic seasonal fare with a Mediterranean twist in an elegant light-filled extension. There are two set menus (one of them vegetarian), from which you can also order à la carte. Tempting dishes include Sigigen trout fillet with wild garlic, and timeless favourites such as "Suure Mocke" (marinated beef roast). Or why not share the Chateaubriand beef fillet for two? Friendly service. For a more rustic dining experience, head to Beizli & Sonnsyte, which also doubles as a lounge. Another option is to dine on the gorgeous terrace, where you can order from either restaurant.

Name: Restaurant Quack in der Villa Weismüller
Description: It's a treat to sit either out on the terrace overlooking the city or inside – in a tastefully decorated dining area blending elegance and trendy chic styling. The ambitious seasonal cuisine has distinct Mediterranean and regional influences. Various set menus feature dishes such as corn-fed Bresse chicken cooked with truffles and served with kohlrabi, chicory and gnocchi or Breton turbot, mashed potatoes with artichokes and baby spinach. The Chef's Table is an interesting affair: counter seating with a view into the kitchen, and a surprise menu. Good wine list. Comfortable apartments are available for a stylish stay. N.B. The property is accessed via a narrow private road.

Name: Restaurant Renilde
Description: Renilde Hammacher-van den Brande served as a curator at the Museum Boijmans van Beuningen for many years and would no doubt have been proud of the restaurant that bears her name. Located in a creatively landscaped rooftop garden on the sixth floor of what is now Depot Boijmans, this place affords stunning views over the city. In the afternoon, the restaurant is reserved for museum visitors; in the evening, it opens its doors to everyone who wishes to discover chef De Jong's surprise menu. This creative chef has a penchant for vegetables and bold combinations. His culinary audacity shines through in his sublime combination of elderflower ice cream, the subtle bitterness of Belgian endive caramel and rhubarb root. Prepare to be blown away!

Name: Restaurant Roku
Address: 6 Hobb's Hill, Croyde, EX33 1LZ, United Kingdom
Description: With a name that means 'six' in Japanese, Chef Martin Baylis’ Restaurant Roku acts as a nod to his Japanese heritage. Fittingly enough, the restaurant’s address is No. 6 and they serve a six-course dinner menu which changes every six weeks. There’s a three-course à la carte too, but the tasting option provides the full experience. The cooking subtly blends in various Japanese ingredients and flavours, such as tuna crudo with togarashi or a pineapple and shiso pre-dessert. A well-chosen wine pairing and nicely paced service enhance the experience.

Name: Restaurant Rollier
Description: Tucked away in a bend of the River Scheldt, this spacious venue overlooks a typically Flemish landscape of (often) cloudy skies, grassy meadows and water. Maurane is in charge of the attentive service, while Nicolas demonstrates his mastery of classical cuisine (à la carte) and contemporary fare (set menu). Examples include a juicy breast of black chicken, intelligently paired with a knockout poultry jus. International accents also crop up in the menus, demonstrated by a slow-cooked cutlet paired with spicy kimchi.

Name: Restaurant Roots
Address: 141 Belle Vue Road, Southbourne, BH6 3EN, United Kingdom
Description: Just around the corner from the beach, behind frosted glass, is this jovial, laid-back restaurant. The décor is bright and fresh, with pictures of crashing waves on the walls and a large mobile of tiny fish hanging from the ceiling. Chef Jan imbues his ambitious tasting menu with influences from his German heritage, including family recipes like "mamma's red cabbage". Enthusiastic service from Geza illustrates the team's overall passion.

Name: Restaurant Rootsch
Description: Restaurant Rootsch boasts an enchanting location on Zierikzee's charming Oude Haven (old harbour) and is every bit as elegant as the boutique hotel Mondragon, in which it is housed. Nods to Zeeland are woven into every detail – from the decor to the menu. Bradley Deurloo lets the wonderful quality of his ingredients shine through in unfussy dishes. Combining lightly seared scallops, gently braised leeks, a creamy sherry-infused beurre blanc and lacinato kale chips, for example, he creates a plate of pure joy. This cuisine is beautifully in tune with the times and steers clear of unnecessary complexity.

Name: Restaurant SCHLOSSBERG
Description: What a view! It would be worth coming up here if only to drink in the panoramic vista over Graz and far beyond the city limits. The tables right by the floor-to-ceiling windows are particularly popular. Seasonal dishes and classics are served. At lunchtime they have cheaper options, but you can also choose from the evening menu. If you would like to walk, you can get up here on foot via the Schlossbergsteig; alternatively the Schlossbergbahn funicular will get you to the restaurant in just a few minutes. Tip: Take a look at the clock tower or the Schlossberg Museum.

Name: Restaurant Saga
Description: A change of name in 2025 from Spontan Vinbar to Restaurant Saga placed a little more emphasis on the food side of things, but its philosophy remains the same. Striking eclectic art adorns the walls of the relaxed and trendy restaurant, while the adjoining wine bar offers an impressive array of bottles to choose from, with real depth to the list and numerous vintages from heavy hitting producers. The ten-course tasting menu offers modern, restrained cooking and original touches – like a deconstructed XO sauce – that enhance the dishes.

Name: Restaurant Scheucher
Description: The attractive location in the city centre, and the invitingly timeless atmosphere provide the perfect backdrop for the good food served here. The classics are held in high regard, from Wiener schnitzel and steak to baked porcini with tartar sauce and vitello tonnato – regional and international dishes feature on the menu. In summer, the lovely terrace to the rear beckons. Drivers have the option of parking in the Parkgarage Schönaugasse right next to the restaurant.

Name: Restaurant Sletten
Description: A relaxed former inn in a charming coastal village; most people head to the room with the sea view, although the others with their bold foodie pictures are equally as pleasant. Well-presented modern small plates make up the menu – 2-3 per person is about right. The wine list provides plenty of interest.

Name: Restaurant Sow
Address: Pensons Yard, Tenbury Wells, WR15 8RT, United Kingdom
Description: As you settle into your seat inside this beautiful 16th-century barn, you’re struck by what a stunning restaurant setting it is. Situated on the Netherwood Estate, ensure you take a look around its garden before dining, as much of the produce you see will be on your plate a little later. The kitchen is run under the auspices of experienced operator Andrew Sheridan and pairs the local produce with occasional East Asian influences, such as Japanese milk bread. Save yourself the journey home by staying over in one of the luxury bedrooms on the other side of the courtyard.

Name: Restaurant Suzie's en Van Aken
Description: Chef Tom is no stranger to the concepts of nose-to-tail eating and zero waste. With a keen sense of the zeitgeist, this is a creative chef who draws inspiration from his extensive travels, especially to Asia. For example, a beurre blanc sauce with dashi that adds depth to a salty dish based on oyster and samphire. The jovial Suzanne plays her part, serving up excellent wine and dessert recommendations. The natural vibe of this cosy establishment will make your dinner that little bit more enjoyable.

Name: Restaurant Tara
Description: This fine dining restaurant is as stylish as it is warm and welcoming. Your charming hostess is always happy to help you navigate the wine list, and the chef, who has honed his craft in top-flight kitchens, has an instinct for selecting exceptional ingredients. Restaurant Tara possesses every element to entice the discerning diner – and it also delivers. In the kitchen, Glenn Heijlands takes an approach that is perfectly in tune with the zeitgeist, emphasising global nuances and refined techniques. A standout example is the brightly seasoned veal tartare, elevated by briny pops of oyster, oyster plant, caviar and samphire. This is a chef who dares to experiment with marriages of flavours, and whose masterful plating makes every dish a feast for the eyes.

Name: Restaurant Tossal Gros
Address: Carretera de Prenafeta a L'illa, Prenafeta, 43400, Spain
Description: In Prenafeta, a district to the east of Montblanc, and as a complement to the Escoda-Sanahuja winery (a pioneer in natural wines from organic farming in Catalonia), this restaurant occupies a restored farmhouse in the heart of nature, overlooking the mountains and surrounding vineyards. In the kitchen, Russian-born chef Vladislav Degtyarev shows a clear dedication to Mediterranean tradition, based on seasonal and local organic produce, much of which is grown on the farm itself. Each dish (ordered à la carte or through the tasting menu) is designed to pair wonderfully with the wines of the winery, which accompany the experience with great character and personality. The interesting cheese menu is another highlight!

Name: Restaurant Uijttewaal
Description: Chef Sven Uijttewaal warmly welcome you into his chic and stylish establishment. A timeless interior design and a tasteful blend of warm tones combine to create a pleasant atmosphere. His fresh cuisine follows current trends, as demonstrated by the signature amuse-bouche – an ode to his grandfather, who owned a pickle company: a refreshing sweet-and-sour piccalilli sorbet served with sweet-and-sour pickle creams and a carrot coulis finished with dill oil. The menu intrigues from start to finish (they also serve lunch), with dishes such as steak tartare with ponzu or a delicate pairing of sole and morels. The excellent wine list, with plenty of options by the glass, is also worthy of your attention.

Name: Restaurant VOS
Description: Tucked away behind a tennis and padel club, VOS, bathed in natural light, sports a wall garden and a warm ambience. Chef Stijn and his youthful team craft a set menu that is in tune with the seasons and founded on Franco-Belgian classics. The kitchen’s hallmark is creative, playful cuisine depicted by fresh notes and grilled dishes. The grilled ribeye steak is coated with a punchy veal gravy that is just the right consistency and emblematic of the chef’s know-how. The lunchtime formula ticks all the boxes!

Name: Restaurant Vannu
Description: Today's culinary landscape is characterised by a shift towards plant-based, zero-waste dishes underpinned by long-established techniques such as fermentation and pickling. At Restaurant Vannu, Gijs Kemmeren gives his creativity free rein, incorporating all those elements into a multi-course set menu. With seaweed, for example, he adds nuance to the earthiness of beetroot and fresh celery. He also whisks up an intensely flavoursome chanterelle sauce to tie together al dente vegetables and a millet polenta cake. His cuisine is sophisticated, playful and certainly intriguing. The accompanying natural wines and juices underscore the ethos of this establishment. A memorable dining experience is guaranteed.

Name: Restaurant Villa Esche
Description: Built in 1903, the former coach house of Villa Esche (now the Henry van de Velde Museum) houses this bright, tastefully designed restaurant where diners can enjoy attentive service and top-notch seasonal cuisine. Opt for the four-course menu or order à la carte. At lunchtime, the options are slightly more limited but include moderately priced daily specials. Delightful terrace overlooking the grounds.

Name: Restaurant Vrå
Address: Clarion Hotel Post, Drottningtorget 10, Gothenburg, 411 03, Sweden
Description: The imposing 1920s city post office is now a hotel, and this glamorous restaurant sits within what was the central hall – the listed cashier booths still on display. A Nordic-Japanese approach sees fine Scandinavian produce meet Asian techniques, and there’s an impressive range of sake by the glass.

Name: Restaurant Wöber
Address: Wiener Straße 3, Tulln an der Donau, 3425, Austria
Description: Christian Wöber runs a thoroughly inviting restaurant in Tulln's pedestrian zone. In the semi-open kitchen, his team prepares a five- to nine-course set menu featuring dishes such as medium-rare venison saddle with hazelnut polenta, elderberry compote, porcini and parsley, or grilled octopus with sweet pepper, Hokkaido pumpkin, bacon, chilli and forest honey. The additional seasonal set menus depend on the time of year. The kitchen frequently draws on ingredients from the property's diverse garden. The wine list leans strongly toward Austria, with a few intriguing options served by the glass. The decor is chic and modern, with cheerful pops of colour, artwork on the walls and a distinctive onyx bar.

Name: Restaurant am Hochfuchs
Description: "Traditional – innovative – down-to-earth – modern" is the motto of Margit and Michael Oberreiter. It is also an apt description of the modern-inspired Austrian and regional fare served here, which ranges from Backhendl (breaded fried chicken) with potato and cucumber salad and lingonberries to sheatfish fillet with lardo, chamomile butter broth, blini and wild broccoli. The four-course "Michaels Menü" comes highly recommended, but the extensive à la carte selection of traditional dishes and tavern classics is also tempting. And on Sundays and public holidays diners can tuck into Sunday roast – oven-fresh roast pork with bread dumplings and cabbage salad. The wine list boasts a solid selection of Austrian labels. Friendly and attentive service is provided in an attractive space that blends modern design and regional charm, featuring clean lines and warm wood. And from this altitude, you have a magnificent panoramic view over the Flachgau region. In summer, the tranquil terrace beckons. Tip: They have well-kept, comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Restaurant de L'Île Benoist
Description: Run by an oyster-farming family since 1955, this fashionable restaurant celebrates the sea and all its produce with flair. Spot-on, legible recipes showcase the quality of the local fish and a knockout cast of shellfish. Poached oysters are one of the house signatures. The artful plating is fully the equal of the delicious sauces, further enhanced by sensible prices. Premium, ultra-fresh local produce is the strong suit of this esteemed establishment. Meals are served in a room whose picture windows overlook a peaceful pond and mill.

Name: Restaurant de l'Hôtel DuPeyrou
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: This lavish 18C palace in the town centre ticks all the boxes and is polished yet unconventional, classical yet quirky. Chef Edmond Bavois rustles up a traditional Gallic lineup, enhanced by subtle Asian twists in elegant creations of the likes of fillet of poached turbot and Valle Maggia risotto or verbena-flavoured pigeon from Poitou. Each dish enhances painstakingly sourced produce and meals are served in a majestic setting whose high ceilings, soft lighting and gleaming parquet floors are perfectly underscored by slick unobtrusive service. An establishment dripping in charm and ideal for connoisseurs of fine food and premium locations.

Name: Restaurant de l'ITHQ
Description: As part of the Institut de tourisme et d'hôtellerie du Québec, a hospitality industry school, the ITHQ restaurant is underpinned by a unique educational approach. Students and professionals work together, both front of house and in the kitchen, under the watchful eye of the instructors. In this bright and serene dining room overlooking Square Saint-Louis, the menu highlights local ingredients, including fish from the Gaspé Peninsula, bison from Lanaudière, and honey from the Laurentian Mountains. Based on the technical principles of French cuisine, the dishes evolve with the seasons: smoked char, semi-cooked and enhanced by a chorizo broth; braised beef tongue, bone marrow broth, root vegetables, and gribiche sauce. Dessert brings with it a surprise: crêpes Suzette flambéed tableside.

Name: Restaurant de l'Écluse 16
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant standing beside the Canal de la Sarre towpath was once a coaching inn, along which horses used to tow coal from the mines. The chef, from Morbihan in Brittany, cooks up delicious and meticulous cuisine, such as saffron risotto with chorizo served alongside premium quality poultry with wild prawns, or his truly unforgettable take on tarte Tatin. He occasionally uses ingredients from the local terroir, enhanced with condiments or home-made aromatic oils.

Name: Restaurant du Blavet
Description: This former guinguette on the quayside has been reinvented under the direction of Marine Nemesien and François Lagneaux and exudes lively charm. In a pared-back and inviting space, meticulous contemporary cuisine with international influences wins diners over. The lunchtime formule is a simple affair; in the evening, a more elaborate à la carte menu where spider crab with Paimpol beans and lobster bisque sits alongside Rossini-style beef paleron, creamy celeriac and meat jus. Precise cuissons and balanced flavours. An appealing little place!

Name: Restaurant du Champ de Mars
Address: 16 avenue de la Victoire, Meaux, 77100, France
Description: This elegant and cosy restaurant giving onto the main road was once a roadside inn and combines old features (beamed ceilings, exposed stone walls, terracotta floor tiles etc) with tasteful contemporary touches. Chef Romain Leydier cooks up a tempting menu that showcases fine ingredients in generous, carefully prepared dishes: crab with Meaux mustard mayonnaise and Brie caviar; Corrèze veal sweetbreads grenobloise style; praline millefeuille with Madagascar vanilla. The tree-lined terrace is popular in fine weather.

Name: Restaurant du Grand Hôtel Nord-Pinus
Description: Set within the renovated Grand Hôtel Nord-Pinus, a landmark in the heart of Arles, this restaurant is part of the city's legendary artistic heritage. Surrounded by tall mirrors and weathered wood panelling, in a hushed atmosphere blending heritage with contemporary elegance, chef Antonio Altamura serves up his precise, understated Italian cuisine: hake crudo, saffron and black lemon risotto, orange blossom millefeuille, strawberries and honeycomb. Well-chosen and expertly prepared ingredients feature on the concise menu. On fine days, the terrace giving onto the square makes this one of the liveliest spots in Arles.

Name: Restaurant du Musée
Address: 2 rue de la Rochette, Fréland, 68240, France
Description: In this former mill on the banks of the Ure, next to the museum of the Welche country, Alain Schmitt’s cooking, dotted with nods to the local countryside, is never at a loss for inspiration: prawns poached in a stock flavoured with Alsace saffron; Iberic pork chop paired with different textures of cabbage; a cherry-flavoured mousse and brownies of Black Forest gateau inspiration…

Name: Restaurant du Port
Description: After a walk around the headland, where the pretty beaches are too many to count, head to the little port. At the restaurant, tuck into the catch of the day, turbot fillet, oysters from Sterec, or the lovely sole meunière, which the chef, a pro who has worked under chefs Michel Trama and Stéphane Carrade, complements with a bowl of new potatoes, fine green asparagus, snow peas and confit red pepper. Pleasantly informal atmosphere.

Name: Restaurant im Parkhotel Tristachersee
Description: The romantic lakeside location is an attraction in itself – here on the shore of Tristachersee, the dedicated Kreuzer family run both the lovely hotel and the restaurant. The dining space is inviting; the winter garden extending out over the water is wonderful – in summer it gets turned into a terrace! The menu draws on good-quality, mostly local produce – char, trout, Danube salmon etc are from their own fish ponds nearby. They serve various set menus and an à la carte selection. The hotel also has its own spring water, which is offered free of charge throughout the premises.

Name: Restaurant zum Bären
Description: The Buggle family has been running this traditional restaurant in the idyllic Lahn Valley since 1827 and chef Joachim Buggle represents the eighth generation to take the helm. He has brought in an impressive concept revolving around culinary classics, serving flavour-intensive, unpretentious dishes. Appetising examples include braised venison shoulder with house-made spaetzle, wild cranberries and glazed pointed cabbage, or grilled calamaretti with lemon risoni, green asparagus and a crustacean foam. Food is served from noon to 9pm Thu-Sun. There is a three-course lunch menu Thu-Sat. On certain dates, they propose a four-course surprise menu. With its beautiful country-style interior, the restaurant has a pleasant, cosy atmosphere; the Weinstube exudes a slightly more rustic feel. And they have another ace up their sleeve in the form of a wonderful terrace in the shade of the lime trees! The front-of-house team provides charming and cordial service… and Landhotel zum Bären is an excellent overnight option.

Name: Restaurant ÖRME
Address: 218 Church Road, Urmston, M41 9DX, United Kingdom
Description: You will find a pleasantly welcoming quality at this small restaurant run by three young owners. There’s a distinct Nordic touch to proceedings – think clean, simple décor and an on-view kitchen – yet British produce is at the heart of the appealing menus, which include tasting options, an à la carte and Sunday roasts. Attractively presented dishes offer bold, vibrant flavours with a mix of the classic and the modern in their influences. Wine flights are also available, including a particularly interesting British-themed option.

Name: Restaurante 1497
Description: Part of the EcoResort Mas Salagros, the first 100% eco-hotel in Spain and an oasis of peace and tranquillity in the protected Serralada Litoral area just a few minutes from Barcelona. The restaurant, the name of which is a nod to the year of the first documents relating to the main farm building, has a contemporary feel and shares access with the more informal Cibus eatery, which specialises in grilled and rice dishes. Here, the focus is on modern cooking that is based around certified seasonal, organic ingredients, for which seasonality, proximity and purity are key tenets (many of these are sourced from the kitchen garden by the entrance to the hotel as well as from local farmers committed to practices that respect nature). The experience is centred around three tasting menus served to the entire table only: 1497, Albor and Tierra, each with their distinct narrative that reflects the landscape, the seasons and a deep respect for provenance.

Name: Restaurante Amores
Address: Av. Roque González Garza 201, Colinas del Cuchumá, Tecate, 21449, Mexico
Description: Restaurante Amores is lovingly run by Chefs Marcelo Hisaki and Reyna Venegas with their team. The cuisine here is offered as a prix-fixe and diners can choose from a few options. There is an element of surprise at play, as the items are not specifically described until they are presented on the table, with many compositions featuring the day's local product. A fish course may feature Pacific Dover sole from Ensenada, pan seared and dressed with an herb and caper pipián and bouquet of asparagus; while the meat choice can include lamb, done as barbacoa and presented as a sope with black bean puree. Dessert brings the meal to an impressive close, as in a block of warm lemon curd cake accompanied by a quenelle of berry ripple ice cream.

Name: Restaurante F
Address: Av. Tomás Cabreira - Edificio Falésia, Portimao, 8500-802, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Restaurante F is the ideal place for those seeking good food in a relaxed atmosphere with stunning views. Away from the typical seaside eateries, this welcoming spot features a glassed-in terrace that looks out over the iconic Praia da Rocha — perfect for watching the sunset. The menu is inspired by authentic Portuguese cooking, with international influences, where the key feature is the quality of ingredients sourced from local producers. All the dishes are prepared with skill, and the selection features meat, fish, fresh seafood... but be sure not to miss the octopus cataplana with sweet potato, cooked to perfection and packed with flavour. The wine list is dominated by Portuguese wines, which can also be purchased on site.

Name: Restaurante La Noria
Address: Av. 41 Pte. 2120, Reserva Territorial Atlixcáyotl, Heróica Puebla de Zaragoza, 72410, Mexico
Description: Located in what was formerly the San Miguel La Noria hacienda from the 1920s, Restaurant La Noria opened in 1993. The setting is a sprawling space with well-preserved features. Seats outside are plentiful, while the interior feels just right for celebrations with tiled flooring, a sloped, beamed ceiling and linen-draped tables. The expansive menus cover all bases, offering breakfast, lunch and dinner with everything from mole Poblano, tacos and pasta Bolognese to chicken Cordon Bleu. Despite the broad array, local specialties are impressive, as in the battered and fried parcels of huauzontles, an indigenous green, and cheese draped with a duo of luscious pipian rojo and verde.

Name: Restaurante Punta Morro
Address: Carr. Tijuana Km 106, Ensenada, Ensenada, 22860, Mexico
Description: This hotel dining room has an enviable location facing the ocean. The room is intimate in scale and boasts a wall of windows offering a gorgeous view. Time it right and you can watch the sun set while enjoying dinner.The menu offers a range of items to please various palates including vegetarian items, house-made pasta and grilled steaks. Yet this team's cuisine also has a creative streak. The empanadas Baja are a highly recommended starter; made from blue corn masa they are delicately crisped and stuffed with finely diced lobster that is seasoned chorizo-style. Seafood preparations are a specialty of Ensenada, but the grilled quail, coming from the Valle de Guadalupe, is simply grilled and accompanied by a luscious sun-dried chili and beer sauce.

Name: Restavracija 1906
Address: Hotel Triglav, Kolodvorska cesta 33, Bled, 4260, Slovenia
Description: 1906 was the inaugural year of the Hotel Triglav, which houses the restaurant, beautifully situated on the hills overlooking the picturesque Lake Bled. The view accompanies the experience both from the bright indoor dining rooms and, above all, from the magnificent summer terrace. Slovenian traditions reign supreme in the kitchen, starting with freshwater fish, accompanied by more international and seafood dishes.

Name: Restavracija CUBO
Description: Away from the historic centre, in a peripheral district little frequented by tourists, CUBO welcomes guests in a modern interior of dark, elegant tones. The kitchen, of Mediterranean orientation yet open to international influences, distinguishes itself through technique and creativity. Among the dishes, the corn-crusted tuna fillet stands out, expertly cooked and accompanied by a vibrant green curry sauce. The desserts are not to be missed, being a true strength of the house, among which are the celebrated chocolate soufflé with crème pâtissière, sorbets and artisan ice creams. The wine list is broad and well-structured, with options available by the glass.

Name: Restavracija Calypso
Description: In the Slovenian part of Gorizia, within the Perla Resort & Entertainment – a vast leisure complex encompassing hotels, a casino and restaurants – Restavracija Calypso is particularly appreciated for its seafood cooking. The dishes, often presented directly in the dining room, celebrate Adriatic fish and seafood through predominantly classical preparations, from raw dishes to oven-roasted fish. Alongside the seafood, references to the hinterland are not lacking, with various specialities from the surrounding regions.

Name: Restavracija Grad Otočec
Address: Grajska cesta 2, Otočec na Krki, 8222, Slovenia
Description: This luxury hotel and restaurant in a spectacular and tranquil location in the middle of the Krka river occupies a charming 13C castle that was demolished and then rebuilt for the purpose. Antiques, a delightful bar with a fireplace and soft comfortable sofas all combine to create the feel of bygone days in the attractive dining room. The cuisine is traditional, featuring carefully prepared dishes and fresh vegetables from the restaurant’s kitchen garden. Both the à la carte and the tasting menus evolve according to ingredient availability throughout the year. To round off your visit in truly aristocratic style, stay in one of the hotel’s luxurious guestrooms.

Name: Restavracija Hotela Marina
Description: The position is undoubtedly one of the restaurant’s greatest assets: directly facing the marina, with large windows overlooking the sea. The kitchen, firmly oriented towards seafood, is fresh, careful, and genuine, in the spirit of “from the sea to the plate.” The menu follows the availability of the day, in full respect of seasonality and the catch. Shellfish, reef fish, and pasta dishes with original dressings compose an offering that is classic yet full of taste, further elevated by the use of local extra-virgin olive oil, also from the restaurant’s own production.

Name: Restavracija Mangrt
Description: Set in a small village at the foot of the imposing Mount Mangrt, within a restored farmhouse with over two centuries of history, Chef Tomaž Sovdat’s cooking is distinguished by its apparent simplicity, which belies a remarkable ability to make the most of the ingredients, with balance and finesse. The restaurant offers two tasting menus of four or six courses, presented verbally by the dining room staff. The wine selection, focused on local labels, is thoughtfully curated and offered at particularly appealing prices.

Name: Restavracija Plesnik
Description: A welcoming mountain hotel is the setting for this bright and lively restaurant which, at lunchtime, serves local traditional dishes inspired by the recipes of grandmother Marija Plesnika, who cooked here in the 1940s. In the evening, on the other hand, guests are served a tasting menu which is available only by booking ahead for anyone not staying at the hotel. In the kitchen, experienced Janez Bratovž, renowned for his work at the JB Restavracija in Ljubljana, is here in an advisory role, while the talented young Tom Čopar who has experience both in Slovenia and abroad is the resident chef. We particularly enjoyed the Štruklji (dumplings) filled with cheese and lovage (the latter is sourced from the hotel’s own garden).

Name: Restavracija Sedem
Description: Seven, like the house number and the Slovenian expression (Sedem!) for sitting down to eat. In a modern and welcoming setting with an open kitchen, students from the town's tourism and hospitality school take their first steps, supported by experienced and consolidated staff. The result is a gastronomic offering that revisits local dishes, with occasional international influences, which can be chosen freely from the à la carte menu or as part of a tasting menu.

Name: Restavracija Shambala
Description: A “hidden oasis” of peace and harmony in the heart of Ljubljana, just steps from the lively riverfront. Shambala is an Asian restaurant of elegant and discreet atmosphere, with oriental references that never tip into excess. The gastronomic proposal ranges across Japan, Thailand and Vietnam, with meat, seafood and vegetarian options available both à la carte and as tasting menus. Among the specialities, an excellent Thai curry stands out alongside traditional preparations and others of fusion inspiration. In the desserts, more classic notes are enriched with exotic touches, as in the panna cotta with mango and date sauce. The attention given to pairing Asian cuisine with wine is also of interest.

Name: Restavracija Strelec
Description: The refined dining room of the panoramic Strelec (Sagittarius) tower of the castle, decorated with 1950s sgraffito murals inspired by local folk songs, sets the scene for Igor Jagodic's cuisine and creates the ideal atmosphere for a romantic evening. The chef offers a single nine-course tasting menu, which can be adapted to seven or five courses, with modern and creative dishes that pay tribute to Mediterranean tradition. The wine list is strongly rooted in the local area, with interesting forays into France and Italy. Don't miss a visit to the beautiful castle courtyard and, if possible, the museum exhibitions. When the weather is fine, book a table outside on the ancient ramparts to enjoy an exceptional view of the town.

Name: Resto 136
Description: Make a beeline for this peacock blue townhouse at number 136 where you will be pampered by Niels and Laura. Their elegant contemporary establishment upholds tradition and while the chef clearly enjoys mixing spicy Asian flavours with Mediterranean extravagance, he is equally capable of winning you over with a flawless piece of cod flanked by knockout beurre blanc and creamy mashed potato.

Name: Resto Dit Vin
Description: In a pedestrian street in the centre of Pau, this inviting and indulgent place complete with outdoor tables is one to keep under your hat, as it is often packed to the rafters! In his semi-open kitchen, chef Alexis Bourdrel gives pride of place to local ingredients, attracting a loyal clientele with his no-nonsense, streamlined formule of flavoursome house-made dishes. A beloved bistro, lively and authentic.

Name: Resto JETT
Description: “Just enjoying time together” is the thinking behind this small, elegant eatery. Cheerful Sarah supervises the dining room, while Dries can be seen in the open kitchen crafting dishes to be shared with friends and family. Convincing recipes that combine the rich classicism of Gallic tradition with exotic influences and a scattering of original ideas. Exceptional ingredients are the norm here, like pan-fried turbot paired with smoked eel, a beurre blanc infused with fennel pollen together with an exquisite range of delicately crafted textures. Just the ticket to just enjoy together!

Name: Resto Wald
Description: Lisa and Walter Wald are keen to maintain the “Small is beautiful” ethic of their hip eatery, which adds to the home-from-home feel. Whenever possible, the enthusiastic chef prepares everything himself using locally sourced ingredients. He draws his inspiration from his many overseas trips and enjoys mixing surprising flavours. He is equally at home with juicy pheasant in a cognac sauce as with a tartare of seabass paired with shellfish oil, vanilla, cucumber extract and goat’s yoghurt and tarragon ice cream. You can expect a flavourful meal with a modern spin in a cosy setting.

Name: Restobar Rosie
Description: Rosie is a bustling yet cosy establishment where foodies can indulge uninterrupted from noon. A love of wine pervades the place and music fills the air – the record player spins nostalgic tunes regularly. From shrimp croquettes to Jerusalem artichoke with labneh or a no-nonsense meat or fish dish: the international menu has something for everyone. This straightforward cuisine makes the most of the versatility of vegetables. Reservations are recommended!

Name: Restobar Vista
Description: Dine against the stunning backdrop of the Rotterdam skyline and the Nieuwe Maas River at Restobar Vista. On the ground floor of the De Rotterdam building, the tastefully modern restaurant is done out in muted colours. The team assembled by Henrie van der Heijden, head chef at Vista in Willemstad, creates distinctly French dishes, with the occasional nod to the Mediterranean. Think succulent roasted tournedos on a bed of caramelised onion, accompanied by a rich Madeira sauce and potato rösti. The chefs eschew complexity and delight diners with their unpretentious dishes. The extensive menu and fantastic value for money will bring a smile to your face.

Name: Restobar de Woage
Description: Set within a charming old building in Gramsbergen, this modern restobar is an inviting spot where even a glance at the extensive menu is sure to bring a smile to your face. Chef Jelle Jansen is a devotee of authentic flavours and puts his ingredients centre stage. Highlights include medium-rare grilled entrecôte with a stroganoff sauce infused with smoked sausage, served with crispy fries. The rich tiramisu is simply irresistible, right down to the last spoonful. This is a place with something for everyone, prepared by a seasoned chef who is attuned to what diners want.

Name: Restoran O2
Description: A modern redevelopment on the edge of the Old Town plays host to this contemporary restaurant with dark, moody décor. Estonian chef Martin Meikas offers a menu informed not only by his own heritage but also by his love of Nordic cuisine, and he enjoys throwing the occasional Asian touch in too. The cooking is hearty, with bold flavours and a refined edge. Lunchtime sees a great value weekly changing special for those in a hurry, while if you prefer to linger longer, there’s the curved chef’s table in front of the open kitchen where you can settle in to watch the chefs at work.

Name: Restoran Vila Rova
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view
Description: Within the eponymous hotel, the restaurant occupies an elegant contemporary dining room looking out over the sea: the gaze drifts across the tranquil and magnificent Kvarner Gulf, framed by a small private olive grove from which an excellent extra-virgin oil is produced. It is well worth booking in advance to secure one of the four front-row tables, from which the panorama may be enjoyed to the full. The kitchen offers a blind tasting menu available in versions of four or seven courses. The menu celebrates above all local ingredients through contemporary and at times decidedly creative recipes, such as the octopus salad stained a deep red by beetroot and finished with crunchy hazelnuts.

Name: Restó SCA
Description: Restó SCA occupies a listed building in Recoleta, widely considered the most elegant district in Buenos Aires, where it shares occupancy with the headquarters of the Sociedad Central de Arquitectos (SCA), founded in 1886 and one of the country’s oldest professional associations. Located at the end of the building’s former carriage entrance, the restaurant has a subdued bistro-style feel with just a few tables and a bar that is home to an enticing display of cheeses. Previous incumbents here have included renowned chefs such as María Barrutia and Guido Tassi, although it is now the turn of María Magdalena Piaggio, a chef who has an in-depth knowledge of French cuisine and whose fresh Mediterranean and international recipes are based around Argentinian ingredients. Standout dishes include the stuffed quail (the stuffing changes with the seasons), the ricotta gnocchi, and several of her fish dishes, such as the cured Bariloche trout which we particularly enjoyed.

Name: Retrobottega
Description: The fruit of a sweeping renovation by the celebrated architect Jean Nouvel, the building houses apartments and art galleries, while on the fifth floor the gastronomic soul comes to life: a single communal table, divided between an elegant interior dining room and a striking panoramic terrace offering uninterrupted views across the Palatine Hill. The cooking looks to the Mediterranean with particular attention to handmade pastas, the true hallmark of the offering. Among the iconic dishes, the tortelli with pork ribs, spring onion and cacao mass stand out with quiet authority. The same terrace is also home to a cocktail bar of enviable situation, ideally placed for raising a glass while contemplating the Roman sunset.

Name: Retrogusto
Description: Although this restaurant is slightly set back from the seafront, the high quality cuisine focusing on the flavours of the Salento makes the short walk well worthwhile. A classic ambience with simple yet tasteful furniture, soft background music and an informal atmosphere.

Name: Reunros (Yan Nawa)
Address: Bangkok Square, 762/2 Rama 3 Road, Bang Phongphang, Yan Nawa, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: When Ruenros opened 40+ years ago, its owner came from a medical background, hence the focus on herbal and medicinal braised dishes. The 3rd generation heir now runs it and he chooses all the market fresh ingredients himself every day. Specialties include spring rolls using a family recipe, stir-fried goat with celery, fried rice with salted fish and slow-cooked soup, which is packed with flavour. For dessert, try the taro purée with sticky rice.

Name: Reussenstein
Description: Everything here is "100% Swabian". All the ingredients come from Württemberg, and the menu is entirely dedicated to regional fare. If you are ordering à la carte, you pick your main dish by its key ingredient (eg beef, game or freshwater fish) and it comes served on a special ash wood tiered platter that was custom-made for the restaurant. The glass partition means there are interesting glimpses into the kitchen, plus the service is very cordial. The vaulted cellar houses a further restaurant, Wild, where a seasonal set menu featuring game is served on Friday evenings. At dinnertime Tue-Thu, this menu is available exclusively for small groups. Their novel "Spätzle Drive-in" is open throughout the day. This long-standing family business also has cosy modern guestrooms.

Name: Reveler's Hour
Address: 1775 Columbia Rd. NW, Washington, DC, 20009, USA
Description: A simple black and glass facade belies the delicious small plates available at this place. Pass a set of double doors to be greeted by a U-shaped bar, arched ceilings and a romantic dining room. Natural wines are a serious focus and pair wonderfully with the shareable plates, and seasonal wines are even accompanied by a poem. Meanwhile, the food is as delightful as the wine selection, offering approachable dishes like pappardelle with spicy roasted pork ragu and fennel breadcrumbs. Be sure to indulge in a pillowy garlic knot, then finish with a Brazilian budino made with coconut caramel and toasted coconut flakes.

Name: Reverie
Description: Stuart and Luca have been friends since hotel school and have turned their shared dream into reality with this sleek, intimate and rather minimalist restaurant. The bonsai tree in the middle of the dining space is a nod to the restaurant's fascination with Asian influences. The chefs love blending their French foundations with Asian sweetness and spice, pairing al dente green asparagus with a richly flavoured rendang sauce whose gentle heat is balanced by sweet-and-sour nuances. The patiently reduced sauce has real character, and the dish is finished with grilled Turkish bread topped with yoghurt and a green curry condiment. Those keen to taste the chefs' Indonesian influences should order à la carte; the set menu takes a more modern turn. Reverie brings all these elements together with energy and ambition.

Name: Revolver
Description: The name is a pun on how the cooking here revolves around the charcoal grill, brazier and tandoor. Whether you sit at the counter or in a booth, the chefs put on a performance that is visible from all the seats. On top of the ‘Discovery’ and ‘Experience’ tasting menus, there are also an à la carte and a vegetarian set menu. The food cleverly melds international flavours with South Asian techniques, courtesy of savvily-layered spices and high-end ingredients.

Name: Revés Bistró
Description: This restaurant's unique location may come as a surprise; and no wonder, it is located in a quiet residential area, within the Tafira Tennis Club. The name, a nod to the sport of tennis but also a statement of intent, underscores the team's philosophy and its overwhelming enthusiasm for serving up informal haute cuisine. Here, what is made abundantly clear is the desire to do things the right way, both in the kitchen (Paco Budia) and in the dining room (Héctor Suárez and Sem Suárez), in a relaxed atmosphere... although with incredibly high self-imposed standards! The menu, supported by a tasting menu, includes dishes worthy of a Grand Slam, such as squid in textures and its black ink or, for dessert, yuzu cream, lemon foam and green tea ice cream. It is sure to win you over!

Name: Reznicek
Description: All you would hope for from a contemporary-minded traditional inn! The regional and seasonal cuisine, which takes inspiration from classic Austrian fare, showcases carefully selected ingredients and impressive craftsmanship. Diners delight in dishes such as beef soup with shredded pancakes, organic char meunière, Backfleisch (breaded and fried meat) and Palatschinken (crêpes), as well as a selection of increasingly hard to find offal dishes. The extensive and well-curated wine list includes an appealing range of wines by the glass. Service comes courtesy of the friendly and attentive front-of-house team. Guests are seated at simply yet elegantly laid tables in an inviting dining space with all the charm of a Viennese tavern. Be sure to cast an eye over the well-stocked cheese display case.

Name: Rhiza
Address: 1 carrefour de la Croix-de-Pierre, Le Pré-d'Auge, 14340, France
Description: In a lovely, out-of-the-way spot in the Normandy countryside, this bright establishment also boasts a gorgeous terrace. Camille, front of house, and Tom Blain, in the kitchen, are the charming, energetic young couple at the helm. This well-crafted cuisine is a delight for the taste buds: varied textures in the starter featuring goat's cheese and slow-cooked egg, and excellent preparation of the beetroot accompanying a tasty wild boar pie. The bill, too, is sure to put a smile on your face. Tapas are served on Thu and Fri evenings.

Name: Rhizome
Description: The rhizome is an underground shoot full of energy resources that is the equivalent to a root for some plants. A name that cleverly references the return of this young Soissons couple to their Picardy roots, after stints in top establishments (Mère Brazier, Parisian Saturne, Auberge du Vert Mont). The name also depicts their lively and instinctive, market-fresh cuisine and regularly changing menu, together with the couple’s clear preference for local produce and organic and natural wines. A firm fixture on the local culinary scene and not only because of its (single) lunch set menu. We recommend booking.

Name: Rhodes w1
Address: Mezzanine Florr, Grosvenor House Hotel, Al Emreef Street, Dubai Marina, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The most recent redecoration resulted in a brighter, airier look for this restaurant in the Grosvenor House hotel. The culinary legacy of the late, great Gary Rhodes is reflected in the appealing menu of European and British dishes. The kitchen handles classics like smoked haddock with Welsh rarebit, salmon fishcake, and bread and butter pudding so well they’re sure to hit the spot. Be sure to also try the chocolate Jaffa fondant with orange jelly.

Name: Rhosyn
Address: Penally Abbey, Penally, SA70 7PY, United Kingdom
Description: Rhosyn means ‘rose’ in Welsh and there are plenty on display in the gardens of this lovingly restored country house. The gorgeous setting provides a calming atmosphere in which to dine, with a tasting menu or an à la carte to choose from. The seasonally guided cooking is modern in execution but rooted in tried-and-tested flavours we all know and love. Pembrokeshire is well-represented on the menu, so look out for delicious local lamb and some superb new potatoes.

Name: RiVi
Description: Drawing from experience in Italian and French cuisine as well as pastries, RiVi creates a genre-less cuisine. It is a dialogue between Japanese cuisine, the influence of the chef’s birth and upbringing, and the Western cultures he admires. As his craft is always evolving, he has no standard dishes. The theme of the first half of the prix fixe menu is a celebration of all things Osaka. The meal finishes with seasonal mixed rice because he wants his guests to taste it with the bowl in their hand. Crockery created by an artisan adds beauty to the presentation.

Name: Rialto
Description: Over the past few years, a streamlined selection of antipasti paired with a stronger focus on primi has become a clear trend in Seoul’s Italian dining scene. In keeping with this shift, the restaurant presents a concise menu that stays true to its northern Italian roots as well as the chef’s personal philosophy, sensibility, and style. Standout dishes include tajarin and cacio e pepe, richly flavoured and marked by a beguiling harmony of butter and cheese. The kitchen’s other pasta dishes show the same fine balance of sauces and seasonings. The pickled ponytail radish is another highlight, offering a nostalgic note that lingers on the palate.

Name: Ribarska Koliba
Description: The “Fisherman’s Hut” is a great Istrian institution with a history of over a century. The restaurant was in existence well before the eponymous resort that now hosts it, built at a later date around it. The bright veranda dining room, with one wall entirely in glass, overlooks the Marina Veruda yacht harbour, offering pleasant sea views from every table. Even more evocative is the summer terrace, as is the Lounge Bar Vertigo, open in the evenings on the building’s rooftop and perfect for a sunset aperitif. The kitchen specialises in the flavours of the sea, offering a menu that celebrates the freshness of the local catch: Kvarner langoustines are served grilled or alla busara, while the catch of the day may be prepared in the most classic ways – grilled, baked, or in a salt crust. A selection of meat dishes is also available. Vintage car enthusiasts will appreciate the 1970s Triumph Spitfire convertible on display within the restaurant.

Name: Riccio Restaurant
Address: via Molo di Baia 47, Bacoli, 80070, Italy
Description: Overlooking the port, this restaurant serves top-quality fish and seafood with interesting and personalised touches added by its young chef. We recommend starting with the excellent selection of cooked fish (although there’s also a choice of raw fish should you prefer it), following which you can choose from classic seafood dishes such as spaghetti with clams and fried fish, and a selection of original, top-quality dishes such as dry-aged, smoked and preserved fish and seafood.

Name: Ricciocapriccio
Description: This bistro is a popular spot for Belgian Italians, as evidenced by the amount of Italian that is spoken here. The chef, a fan of fine produce (sea urchins and squid are his specialties), deftly whisks up enticing dishes featuring carefully considered and, occasionally, unusual combinations. For instance, he prepares risotto with a sea bream tartare and parmesan foam, or puts a new spin on the classic tiramisu, but he always respects the essence of the dishes he prepares. The ample à la carte menu promises a Mediterranean feast!

Name: Rice Field
Address: 2F, 75-77 Ho Tung Mau Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: Spread over three storeys, this delightful venue with an open-air rooftop boasts a rustic décor inspired by local villages and rice fields and serves Vietnamese dishes from the north to the south. The stuffed snails with meat cooked with lemongrass and paired with ginger fish sauce, are succulent, while La Vong fishcakes strike the perfect balance combining vermicelli, marinated fish, fresh Vietnamese vegetables and herbs, shrimp paste sauce and rice paper sheets.

Name: Rich Table
Address: 199 Gough St., San Francisco, CA, 94102, USA
Description: This petite Hayes Valley delight is packed nightly and yet nobody seems to care about its stream of crowds. Simply decked with a light-and-dark color scheme along with distressed wood, the room features a laid-back style and rustic-chic farmhouse vibe. It books out far in advance, so arrive early to score a seat at the bar, where trendy types can be found devouring the Californian fare, infused with global ingredients and fine-dining precision.The hip staff is quick on their feet and may present diners with a salmon tostada slathered with tangy avocado purée and dots of salsa verde; or lobster chow mein garnished with charred corn and scallions. Advertised as dessert, cucumber sherbet with diced melon and watermelon granita is a perfect bite by itself.

Name: Richard Lequet
Address: 239 route d'Atur, Boulazac Isle Manoire, 24750, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Having previously garnered a MICHELIN star at L'Amphitryon in Limoges, chef Richard Lequet is now showcasing his talents in this newly renovated elegant bourgeois mansion. His cuisine is seasonal and uses local produce as much as possible. In the evening, the surprise dinner menu includes dishes such as cod steak on a bed of crunchy fennel, carrot brunoise and smoked pancetta, or supreme of Landes poultry ballotine with carrot tagliatelle and a pea purée. The chef makes his own bread from local flours. Should you wish to extend the experience, comfortable guestrooms are available.

Name: Richard Rivalee
Description: Fashion designer Richard Rivalee shares his passion for Nyonya culture and Peranakan food in this smart vintage joint, whose knickknacks and heritage premises are a nod to the Baba-Nyonya culture. Deceptively simple, homespun dishes are finessed with spot-on seasoning and loads of punch. Otak-otak, or savoury fish egg custard, combines a velvety texture with just the right amount of heat. To reduce food waste, most items are available in two portion sizes.

Name: Ricordeau
Address: 13 rue de la Libération, Loué, 72540, France
Description: Sit out on the pleasant terrace set up in the garden, on the banks of the River Vègre, and treat yourself to a fine dining interlude courtesy of the chef's cooking, which is always in touch with the seasons. The contemporary dishes, which are deliberate and meticulous, make use of the finest local ingredients, including supreme of Loué chicken stuffed with onions and morel mushrooms, first-harvest vegetables and a creamy poultry jus. La Table du Coq, the hotel's second restaurant, serves simpler fare.

Name: Ricos Tacos Toluca
Description: In more than two decades, this taqueria has moved three times. It's now situated in the Centro Histórico of Mexico City near the Mercado De San Juan. There are just a few red stools, so come early or you'll eat standing up. This taqueria specializes in handmade Toluca-style chorizo and sausages. Sample individually to appreciate the flavors and unique characters of each chorizo or mix them for an equally satisfying experience. Top with grilled or fresh onions, French fries, cilantro and various salsas. Obispo is a large pork-based sausage, seared ever so slightly for a delicate crisp, while chorizo tamarindo is diced then grilled and delivers a subtle sweetness and terrific flavor.

Name: Rifugio Col Alt
Address: Stazione monte cabinovia col alto, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: During the day this restaurant can be reached in just a few minutes by cable car, providing you with breathtaking views of the Dolomites, while in the evening (when the service is more attentive – things are faster paced at lunchtime) you have to arrange transport via snowcat. The name “refuge” refers only to the location as the cuisine is definitely that of a restaurant: although the menu features hearty mountain fare, it also includes modern options and a few fish-based recipes, including oysters. Last but not least, there’s a good selection of wines.

Name: Rifugio Fuciade
Address: località Fuciada - Soraga di Fassa, San Pellegrino, 38035, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: To give you an idea of the Alpine location of this restaurant framed by the Costabella mountain chain, suffice it to say that for centuries it was used for mountain pasture. There’s a breathtaking view of the Dolomites which extend into the distance as far as Pale di San Martino, while the menu here focuses on regional recipes such as canderli dumplings on a bed of cabbage, veal stew with polenta and chanterelle mushrooms, and polenta gnocchetti with herb pesto, smoked ricotta and lemon thyme. The wine cellar is home to more than 600 labels, plus accommodation is available in a choice of tranquil guestrooms.

Name: Riley's Fish & Steak
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Located in the heart of downtown's waterfront, Riley's Fish & Steak lures guests with stunning views and a polished nautically informed interior that pours on the glamour. Don't let the high rollers and spendy tourists turn you off; the staff's warmth and the kitchen's precise techniques will charm you in no time. Dishes that may seem tried-and-true are far from ho-hum. Take the Louie salad, for instance, with Baby Gem lettuce bested with beautiful lump crab, crunchy onion rings, creamy avocado and Thousand Island dressing—it's refreshing and satisfying. Then, fish and chips is surprisingly light yet savory, thanks to the ultra-crisp batter. Charred broccolini with an herbaceous and citrus-forward gremolata is a virtuous side dish.

Name: Rimsuan
Address: 200 Phu Khao Thong Soi 5, Pratu Chai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: The owner hails from Nakhon Sri Thammarat and has been serving quality southern Thai cuisine in the ancient capital for over 25 years. Despite its simple décor, the restaurant with its high vaulted ceilings, shady garden and lack of walls is well worth visiting. The southern Thai sour curry with fish is a family recipe and a must-try, while the fried prawns are glazed in a delectably sticky tamarind sauce. Keep an eye out for the daily specials on the white board.

Name: Rindenmühle
Description: Take a seat in the elegant yet cosy, country-style interior – or, in summer, out on the beautiful garden terrace – and choose from a seasonal menu. Vegetarians are also catered for. For overnight guests there are cosy contemporary guestrooms.

Name: Rio Bistrot
Description: Situated on the street that heads down to the port in charming Riomaggiore, this lovely, well-kept restaurant offers a small selection of dishes split between Ligurian specialities and more creative options. Dine in the rustic, elegant dining room or on the outdoor terrace.

Name: Rio by Paulo André
Address: Praça da República 8, Vila do Conde, 4480-715, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: A young and informal eatery with an open-view kitchen located at one end of Praça da República, one of Vila do Conde’s most beautiful squares thanks to its setting on the banks of the Ave river. In a nod to the name of his restaurant, chef Paulo André’s professional career is as surprising and unexpected as the meanders in a river! His cisHisontemporary-style cooking will definitely leave its mark given his passion, technical skill and a strong desire to please, plus a continual focus on using locally sourced vegetables (vegetarian dishes feature on the menu), fish and meat. If the weather’s fine, make sure you eat on the terrace.

Name: Rios O Freixo
Description: A family-run restaurant with a superb location overlooking the port, where the quality of ingredients is always to the fore, especially in terms of its shellfish (oysters of different sizes, clams, cockles etc) and superb fresh fish, meat and rice dishes (the rice with sea urchins and Cambados scallops is a delight). For the best views, make sure you book a table by the picture windows.

Name: Ris
Address: 2275 L St. NW, Washington, DC, 20037, USA
Description: Ris Lacoste helms the stove at this terrific neighborhood spot, a draw for diners in the company of family, friends, and business associates alike. The sprawling, light-filled dining room is dressed in earth tones and filled with intimate corners for an air of seductive sophistication. And the menu, with its ramped-up takes on the tried-and-true, toes the line between familiar and surprising. Loaded with butter and olive oil and jazzed up with red pepper flakes, linguine with clams is briny and delicious and chicken Milanese has a perfectly zippy tomato topping. The crab cakes are always on point, and the crown of cauliflower is both interesting and complex, thanks to an ensemble of roasted vegetables slicked with mustard cream and an army of flavors.

Name: Risbo
Description: Chef/owner Boris Ginet's all-day cafe is a perfect spot to visit before or after a visit to Prospect Park, just a stone's throw away. And while its whitewashed walls lined with artistic photos, industrial-chic cement floors and a glorious garden patio hint at its Brooklyn locale, the anchor here is the open-air, Parisian-style rotisserie, churning out a host of delectably roasted items.This menu highlights everything from bowls and platters to seasonal soups, vegetables and grains. The roasted chicken is a must. Marinated for 72 hours with a host of spices, it's a signature. The Risbo platter is another house special, underscoring the likes of well-seasoned roasted pork served with hummus, a spicy cabbage salad and plantains.

Name: Risette
Address: 81 Old Theatre Street, Valletta, VLT 1429, Malta
Description: Facing the Basilica of Our Lady of Mt. Carmel, the restaurant’s modern, elegant decor provides the perfect foil to the refined score. At the helm, chef Steve Scicluna demonstrates his high-flying technique, clearly influenced by the French school. Some dishes (like rabbit) pay homage to Malta, or to Italy, with ravioli taking the spotlight, together with a subtle sprinkling of Japanese ingredients, creating a culinary reflection of the chef’s diverse past experiences, all presented with unfailing elegance.

Name: Riso Amaro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Inspired by the famous film Bitter Rice, directed by Giuseppe De Santis, who was born in Fondi, this restaurant welcomes guests into elegant dining rooms and a lush courtyard which is perfect for summer evenings.
