The cuisine looks to the present with a well-balanced creative flair that is evident in dishes such as the cuttlefish lasagnetta, served with an intense creamy sauce made from cuttlefish ink and offal, or the intriguing sweet “pinzimonio”, a fresh and light dessert that combines sweet-and-sour vegetables with softer notes. The concise but thoughtfully curated wine list features labels from all over Italy, whilst the central location, just a stone’s throw from the castle, adds further charm to the experience.

Name: RistoFante
Description: Run by the reliable and experienced “Titta” in the kitchen and Silvia front of house, this elegant, contemporary-style restaurant serves simple, modern dishes in which fresh, seasonal ingredients take centre stage. The focus here is on fish, with a menu that includes a fine selection of raw seafood options, as well as a simple yet tasty sea bass carpaccio which cooks quickly on a bed of hot porcini mushrooms.

Name: Ristorante 1500
Address: via Pavicolo 43, funivia per raggiungere il ristorante in via Villa 3, San Vigilio, 39011, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: If you’re not a guest at the Vigilius Mountain Resort hotel where this restaurant is situated, leave your car in Lana and take the short cable-car ride to Monte San Vigilio where you’ll find the hotel at an altitude of 1 500m (remember to check the time of the last cable-car back down the mountain!). Decorated with a profusion of wood, the dining room has the same modern feel as the creative mountain cuisine prepared by the new chef who started here in 2023.

Name: Ristorante ACQUA PAZZA
Address: 2F, Passage Aoyama, 2-27-18 Minamiaoyama, Minato-ku, Tokyo, 107-0062, Japan
Description: Chef Yoshimi Hidaka has broadened the horizons of Neapolitan hometown cooking. Acqua pazza, the poached white fish dish that so thrilled him in Naples, is both the restaurant’s name and its signature dish. Prepared by fishermen, it began as fish and tomatoes simmered in seawater but here freshwater is used and Manila clams are added for saltiness. The synergy of umami from inosinic acid in the fish, glutamic acid in the tomato and succinic acid in the Manila clams is classic Yoshimi Hidaka ingenuity.

Name: Ristorante Angelo
Description: The restaurant's name, meaning ‘angel’, was inspired by an Osaka eatery whose influence guides the chef each day. He sources his ingredients from within the Kansai area with which he is familiar. Sea bream from Akashi is aged, daggertooth pike conger from Awaji served as fritters. Game is served here too, including venison and boar from Tamba-Sasayama and duck from Wakayama. White porcelain dinnerware provides a canvas for modern arrangements, innovative enough at times to impress as art.

Name: Ristorante Da Anita - Chalet Prà delle Nasse
Address: via Cavallazza 24, località Prà delle Nasse, San Martino di Castrozza, 38054, Italy
Description: This family-run restaurant is surrounded by views of the Dolomites that are particularly impressive from the outdoor terrace in summer. A historic culinary stalwart among San Martino di Castrozza restaurants, Prà delle Nasse focuses on regional mountain cuisine, although a few more personalised dishes also feature on the menu. The desserts include the grandmother’s traditional tarts alongside more contemporary options.

Name: Ristorante Engel
Description: With almost 200 years of gastronomic history to its name, this place has been in Italian hands for over 40 years. Following in his parents' footsteps, Franco Iaia now runs this ristorante with his wife Yvonne. With a tiled stove and warm wood, the inviting dining space is vibrant and charming. "La Piazza" is their lovely terrace shaded by mulberry trees. Highlights of the "cucina italiana strettamente classica" include homemade pasta, brasato and osso buco.

Name: Ristorante HONDA
Description: Seasonal foodstuffs are the theme at this modern Italian restaurant. Tetsuya Honda’s culinary creations link the traditional cuisine of Italy with the seasons of Japan. The speciality, ‘Sea Urchin Tagliolini’, uses no cream, relying instead on lashings of sea urchin to achieve a rich, satisfying flavour. Honda strives to elicit the flavour of each ingredient.

Name: Ristorante L'incontro
Description: The chef’s journey starts from the craftsmanship he encountered in an Italian village. Keen to do as much as possible in-house, cured meats such as prosciutto and salami are prepared on site. Wild plants and mushrooms are foraged from the surrounding mountains, and his hunting experience ensures the chef handles game with skill. A course dedicated to game is offered from the start of each year. The use of traditional medical herbs deepens both aroma and flavour, bringing out the meat’s distinctive wild character.

Name: Ristorante Mas-cì
Description: Situated in the charming historic centre, this hotel and restaurant are now run by the third generation of the same family. Welcoming dining rooms with a fireplace provide the setting for cuisine which makes the most of local produce while also including dishes from elsewhere in Italy. Don’t miss the black truffle specialities!

Name: Ristorante Roma
Description: Opened in 1950, Roma was the first Italian restaurant of Luxembourg, and it remains true to its founding authentic values. Seventy years on, little has changed and the venue, adorned with Venetian chandeliers, is still as vibrant and colourful as the food is wholesome. The pasta is homemade and oozes with crisp Mediterranean accents. Examples include pasta stuffed with seafood and a velvety vongole-type sauce or why not order a melt-in-the-mouth medallion of lamb, flanked by a gutsy gravy, mashed potatoes and scamorza? Themed festivals and a varied menu with something for everyone transform each meal into a feast.

Name: Ristorante Seven Lugano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated on the rooftop of the casino and accessible via a glass-sided lift, this restaurant boasts fine views of the lake. In summer, the popular seats on the terrace need to be booked well in advance, while the lounge bar on the ground floor is perfect for a post-dinner cocktail. The cuisine here is varied and wide-ranging, both on the set menus and the à la carte, plus there’s an excellent choice of wines featuring labels from around the world.

Name: Ristorante con enoteca Origini
Description: On the doorstep of the Breggia Gorges and just a few miles from the border, this former mill framed by greenery paints a picture postcard snapshot of peaceful countryside with a garden to relax and wind down and three cosy dining rooms, where the stage is set for a cast of bold, wholesome flavours to take the limelight. Traditional down to its core, the menu stars dishes like fork-tender sweetbread, served in a succulent jus and enhanced by crunchy cashew nuts and fresh scallions. The wine list pays tribute to Ticino with some 200 labels, including a traditionally crafted sparkling wine not to be missed. Ticks all the boxes for a country weekend oozing in culinary indulgence.

Name: Ristorante de LEN
Address: Via Cesare Battisti 66, Cortina d'Ampezzo, 32043, Italy
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the central and very busy Corso Italia, this restaurant has an elegant Alpine feel. Here, subtle lighting, soft background music and larch wood cladding on the walls create an ambience with an attractive blend of the modern and traditional. The cuisine takes inspiration from the local region, with specialities interpreted with a contemporary twist, including a focus on vegetable- and cheese-based dishes such as the excellent “fonduta di Saporito d'alpeggio” (fondue).

Name: Ristorante della Stazione
Description: There’s a change of guard at this Ticino dining institution where young couple Eloa Geiser and Yanick Walker have taken over the running of both the kitchen and front of house service. Eloa, the charming female half of the partnership, is also a qualified sommelier and takes very good care of her guests, while Yanick, adds his classic-French culinary stamp without neglecting his Valois roots, although he is not averse to adding some Mediterranean flair to his cuisine. In addition to its usual menu, on Tuesdays guests can order the “Stazione” veal liver, and on Saturdays the special braised beef with Merlot. The gracious building housing the restaurant with its beautiful views remains unchanged, as do the comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Rita
Address: 89 Aro Street, Aro Valley, Wellington, 6021, New Zealand
Description: The indecisive or the easily envious will be pleased to know only a three-course set menu decided by the chef is served at this homely spot – but it does change every service. What doesn’t change is the high quality of the ingredients used, whether that’s the kingfish which is grilled and could come with coconut and lemongrass, or the duck used in tortellini. The restaurant, named after the chef’s grandmother, is housed in a cute old cottage. There are two sittings in the evening – but do book well in advance.

Name: Ritz
Description: Chef Basia Ritz was the first winner of MasterChef Poland and used this as a springboard to fulfil her ambition of running her own restaurant. Her dream has been realised at this quayside spot nestled amongst numerous other eateries. Locally sourced produce provides many of the menu’s highlights, with the likes of in-season chanterelles laying a strong foundation for the unfussy modern cooking. The personable team provide keen and friendly service.

Name: Ritüel
Address: Şifne Mahallesi 5495. Sokak No:26, Çeşme, Izmir, 35000, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Head to GAIA BY THE SEA hotel, follow the path to the rear and immerse yourself in the romantic atmosphere of this outdoor restaurant. The view of the water is utterly captivating! You even make this a regular treat: Chef Tolga Kamiloğlu brings his experience to bear in a contemporary take on Turkish cuisine, which is detailed and elevated with the occasional Asian influence. Highlights include the charcoal-grilled baby calamari with cherry tomatoes in a jus of tomato, vinegar and mirin, and the orange-themed dessert with lime sorbet, yuzu sorbet and yuzu jelly – each plate delivers an experience. The wonderful à la carte selection is guaranteed to delight.

Name: Riva
Description: Perhaps the only true fish restaurant in Ascona where fish specialities are nothing short of exceptional, but meat lovers will not be disappointed either. Situated inside the Seven Boutique Hotel, Riva offers a maritime atmosphere with colourful touches that recall the blue expanse and a tasty cuisine declined in tasting or à la carte menus, from ‘I Crudi’ with oysters & co. to ‘Sogliola alla mugnaia with lettuce, capers and spring onion’. Definitely a great address!

Name: Riva
Description: In a small village with a fascinating crenellated castle, this restaurant is run by a husband and wife team. They offer a refined cuisine that is a balanced blend of local recipes and creativity.

Name: Riva
Address: Maison Bérard, 6 rue Gabriel-Péri, La Cadière-d'Azur, 83740, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: This family-run hotel and restaurant in a scenic Provençal village, boasts a warm, colourful interior (open kitchen, sanded beams, Italian tableware) and a panoramic view over the vineyards of Bandol. The regularly changing menu draws on the flavours of the Mediterranean, taking diners on a journey that hugs the coastline from Liguria to Provence: chilled red mullet à la niçoise, bouillabaisse dressing; ravioli of foie gras, cappuccino-style duck stock and seasonal mushrooms; seabream, tian of vegetables and a saffron jus. A fine dining experience to be savoured.

Name: Riva
Description: Bathed in natural light, this striking minimalist edifice boasts both a holiday vibe and a luxurious designer edge. All of which is further enhanced by the drop-dead view over the Meuse from the idyllically placed terrace. Live lobster, which can be seen in tanks as you enter, is prepared different ways ranging from a familiar pasta dish to a Thai-inspired recipe. Brasserie classics such as filet américain with fries and vol-au-vent are reworked to suit a contemporary palate without losing their original DNA. Riva upholds the best of brasserie traditions and all its trappings!

Name: Riva
Description: Riva’s tagline is ‘Where the southern sea meets the northern shore’, and this can immediately be seen on the plate, with top-notch local produce from the land and sea taking on vibrant Mediterranean colours and flavours – a great example is the pike-perch cutlet with green pea purée and bouillabaisse sauce. The room itself also pops, with its bright, blingy style, while the friendly team add a welcoming touch. The lunch menu is shorter and simpler, with the options at dinner becoming more extensive in number and more ambitious in style.

Name: Riva Lounge
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Within the luxurious adults-only Hotel Monte Mulini, whether on the sunny terrace or in the intimate dining room of Riva Lounge, a locally inspired cuisine awaits, with specialities such as pljukanci pasta and truffle alongside seafood dishes. Considerable attention is also given to food and wine pairing, with an extensive selection of local labels and sparkling wines, complemented by a carefully curated Champagne offering.

Name: Riva del Fiume
Address: LF, Four Seasons Hotel Bangkok at Chao Phraya River, 300/1 Charoen Krung Road, Yan Nawa, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The view from the terrace is of the Chao Phraya, but inside, this modern Italian restaurant in the Four Seasons Hotel feels more like Lake Como with its Euro vibes, open kitchen and wood oven. At the helm is an Italian chef who worked at several famed restaurants in Europe. Here he deftly cooks favourites like his pizza and home-made pasta with quality ingredients imported from Italy. Adding to the experience is the high level of service of the team.

Name: Rivaaj
Address: The St. Regis Doha, Al Gassar Resort, West Bay, Doha, Qatar
Description: ‘Heritage Indian Cuisine’ under the aegis of Surjan Singh, better known as ‘Chef Jolly’, is the order of the day at this elegant and moodily lit restaurant at the St Regis hotel. That means a menu offering an appealing range of dishes, from elevated street food to elegant curries and biryanis. The undecided should consider the ‘Signature Board’ offering a range of meats and seafood from the tandoor, plus salad and chutney. The service is always endearingly sweet-natured, adding to the restaurant’s appeal.

Name: Rivage
Description: Catherine and Hervé Bourdon (previously of Le Petit Hôtel du Grand Large) have entrusted the keys to their establishment to their former colleagues, Pauline and Thomas Le Morlec. Its prime location on the port of Portivy has not changed. The small seasonal menu draws on local ingredients, often from short supply chains (such as the fish). Diners can look forward to the flavour, simplicity and natural harmony of ikejime sea bream, spider crab emulsion, sweet chilli and grilled courgette. Six guestrooms upstairs with sea views.

Name: Rivas
Description: A family-run restaurant with a modern exterior and welcoming dining rooms featuring a mix of wood and cement that has been taking orders in the Salamanca countryside for over half a century. In the kitchen, the focus is very much on traditional dishes that are strongly based around local ingredients, including vegetables from its own market garden. On the menu, you’ll also find delicious stews and roasts, constant references to Iberian pork, plus a good selection of fresh fish of the day priced by weight. Traditionally caught red tuna is a favourite, hence the themed days organised here every year, which see large tuna brought directly from the port of Barbate.

Name: Rive Fish & Faible
Description: Sitting right on the port, this bistro is run by the same team as Tschebull. It serves good quality, flavoursome seafood and grilled meats alongside classic dishes such as Hamburger Pannfisch and Wiener Schnitzel. In summer the wonderful terrace is a must! Hot food served throughout the day.

Name: Rive Gauche
Address: 2F, The PuXuan Hotel and Spa, 1 Wangfujing Street, Dongcheng, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In this chic modern place inspired by Paris's Left Bank, Gallic techniques and recipes hold no secrets for the seasoned head chef from Hong Kong. Chinese influences are also apparent in the fermented tofu-flavoured butter served with the bread, and the longjing tea panna cotta. His flexible prix-fixe lets diners choose four or five items from the à la carte menu, including signatures such as foie gras mousseline in pistachio tart shell, and scampi ravioli.

Name: Rive Gauche
Description: This restaurant boasts a fantastic location on Lichtentaler Allee, right next to the Museum Frieder Burda and Museum LA8. In the clean-lined conservatory of the beautiful historic building, you can tuck into an appealing three-course lunch set menu as well as "petites bouchées" such as French onion tart or croque monsieur. In the evening, the cuisine moves up a gear, with dishes such as marinated venison loin with Waldorf salad or wild-caught monkfish with braised pointed cabbage and chorizo. Eduard Knecht, who previously cooked at Alte Baiz in Neuhausen, heads up the kitchen. In summer, the terrace is a real highlight.

Name: River Bar
Description: The maritime decor inside this striking oval pavilion is indeed enchanting, yet one of its main draws is the view of the Nieuwe Maas River. As you soak up the vibrant atmosphere and watch the cruise ships dock, you can choose from a fine selection of wines by the glass and the European-inspired menu. Eschewing any unnecessary frills, the chef comes up with some truly original dishes. His repertoire includes perfectly cooked Mediterranean-style turbot, foie gras as rich as anywhere in France – and even beef Wellington! The wide selection promises a delightful culinary journey along Europe's rivers.

Name: River Twice
Address: 1601 E. Passyunk Ave., Philadelphia, PA, 19148, USA
Description: Texan Chef-Owner Randy Rucker has called Philadelphia home since 2019 and it’s proved to be a very successful marriage. His corner restaurant is an understated space that’s not without charm, with floor-to-ceiling windows making the most of its appealing location. The small tables come with drawers for your cutlery, but it’s really a seat at the counter you want if you’d like to watch the chefs in action. On offer is a multicourse monthly-changing set menu with a distinct seafood bias – but there are always additional courses you can add on, some of which have a distinctly luxurious feel, like chawanmushi with Ossetra caviar. As that dish suggests, the main influences applied to the quality local ingredients are mostly French and Japanese, so wild halibut comes with shellfish emulsion, and squid is paired with butter beans, sake lees and miso.

Name: Riviera
Description: This long-standing brasserie has stood the test of time, and it's easy to see why. The room has a fresh, unfussy elegance and a warm Mediterranean style – and the menu is the perfect match. Good quality ingredients feature in an appealing range of classic Mediterranean dishes, with everything from oysters and tartares to fish and steaks of offer; the vitello tonnato is worth a mention, as is the tiramisu. Everything is generously sized, with well-defined flavours and textures, and the sizeable wine list (1,000+) offers some great choices from around the globe. In summer, the terrace is the place to be.

Name: Riviera
Address: Carlton Cannes, 58 boulevard de la Croisette, Cannes, 06400, France
Description: The legendary luxury hotel, which celebrated its 110th anniversary in 2023, now has its own marble-clad restaurant with a superb terrace overlooking the Croisette. In an opulent-feeling dining room where white meets black, the tables set with Gien porcelain are in line with time-honoured tradition of French table arts. The chef's table opposite the open kitchen also draws the eye. Everything else meets the standard set by your surroundings: Mediterranean cuisine made from top-quality local and seasonal ingredients, the calibre of service, with meat and fish cut at your table. You'll enjoy an excellent rack of Alpilles lamb with vegetables and jus, and a remarkable St Honoré cake with vanilla caramel and walnut pieces.

Name: Riviera by Jean Imbert
Address: The Lana - Dorchester Collection, Marasi Drive, Business Bay, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Valet parking
Description: Be transported to the iconic French Riviera in the heart of Business Bay. Ideally located on the fourth floor of The Lana hotel, overlooking a small marina of luxury yachts, this restaurant exudes chic, French allure from its style to its flavours. Ratatouille cake, signature tuna tartare (made at your table) to green risotto and Carabineros spaghetti, allow you to travel from the South of France to Italy in just a few bites. Its bright terrace is perfect for alfresco dining during cooler weather.

Name: Rizibizi
Description: Situated in an attractive location on the seafront promenade in Portorož, this restaurant boasts a classic-style interior with a profusion of wood, square tables and a traditional lay out, plus an attractive summer terrace facing the sea. The well-balanced menu offers plenty of choice, including tasting options and an à la carte, all of which showcase carefully prepared meat and fish dishes. In season, truffles add their unique flavour to various dishes – we particularly enjoyed them served with pumpkin and prawns, as well as in the Mediterranean sea bass dish. An excellent wine list completes the picture.

Name: Rizoom
Description: Rizoom blends a design-inspired, post-industrial loft vibe with a cosy feel. Take a seat in the open kitchen or at a beautifully laid table and watch Yves Kerckhoffs wield his magic as he brings his passion for produce to life, invariably courtesy of solid Japanese technique. Sustainability and the seasons guide both the menu and the establishment’s choice of suppliers. You can expect dry-ageing, koji fermentation and a single-minded quest for umami, hence the major role enjoyed by sauces and gravy. For example, brill is wrapped and aged in kombu leaves, before it is sliced into sashimi and then further underscored by a gutsy roast poultry jus. An adventurous culinary score that is enhanced by an outstanding list of wines and sakes.

Name: Ro'cha
Description: The philosophy of seasoned chef Jean-Luc Rocha, who has captained many starred restaurants and who became a Meilleur Ouvrier de France in 2007, is founded on good food and good vibes. Every dish showcases the work of a savvy, veteran chef who has quietly mastered all the tricks of his trade; this certainly applies to his delicious raviole of snails and ricotta, served with a poultry gravy. From start to finish, the cooking and seasoning are deftly executed, a case in point being the delectable saddle of veal paired with carrots in a jus and white asparagus. Soul-warming fare at reasonable prices in a bistro vein at lunchtime – more ambitious in the evening.

Name: Roam
Address: Sandridge Barton Wines, Lower Well Farm, Waddeton Road, Stoke Gabriel, TQ9 6RL, United Kingdom
Description: On Lower Well Farm, the home of Sandridge Barton wines, you’ll find this lovely converted barn serving a fresh taste of the seasons. The restaurant is in a sheltered spot tucked behind the shop and tasting room, with its own extensive terrace soundtracked by the gentle flow of a nearby stream. The daily, lunch-only menu makes the most of the local larder, from fish caught at Brixham to ceps picked on Dartmoor. There’s a wholesome element to the cooking, which ensures the true flavours of the ingredients shine through. Make sure you order a glass of their own wine.

Name: Robata
Address: The Canopy, Northern Ring Road, Hittin, Riyadh, 13512, Saudi Arabia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,No alcohol served,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: As the name suggests, the focus here is Japanese barbecue – or robatayaki, to be more precise. Expect flavourful, modern Japanese dishes paired with carefully sourced ingredients, such as a juicy Angus beef fillet, Gulf prawns with a kimchi sauce and plenty of vegetarian options like portobello mushroom in a ponzu marinade. Inside, the ambiance is always lively, as dance music plays in the background and the chefs can be seen grilling away through the glass wall.

Name: Robin's Teppanyaki
Address: 2F, Regent Hotel, 3, Lane 39, Section 2, Zhongshan North Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, 104, Taiwan
Description: One of the best known teppanyaki places in town, named after a long-serving maître d’, enjoys an enthusiastic local following. The show-stopping teppan tricks are something to behold, but they don’t outshine the perfectly cooked seafood, premium steaks from the U. S. , or the Wagyu from Japan and Australia. The six-course dinner unfolds according to your pace as experienced chefs time things just right. An excellent wine list also features.

Name: Roble by Jairo Rodríguez
Address: Robledo 21 B, Pola de Lena, 33630, Spain
Description: Run by a couple (Jairo is in the kitchen, while Paula is at the helm in the dining room), this restaurant on the outskirts of town always comes as a pleasant surprise thanks to the essence of the Asturias region that is in clear evidence here. The à la carte, offering an updated take on traditional cuisine, features superb fish sourced from the Rula de Avilés company, including red mullet cooked at low temperature and wild grouper with an orange velouté, and is complemented by an impressive tasting menu. The cheese trolley and meats carved in front of you add an extra touch.

Name: Robun
Address: 4 Princes Buildings, George Street, Bath, BA1 2ED, United Kingdom
Description: This Japanese restaurant in the historic city of Bath takes its inspiration from 19th-century author Kanagaki Robun, who is credited with introducing barbecued food to Japan. The cooking reflects his influence, with dishes from the robata grill forming the central part of a menu that is well-suited to groups as the majority of dishes are ideal for sharing. An eye-catching Japanese take on afternoon tea – including bao buns and chicken karaage – stands out amongst the vast menus.

Name: Robusk
Description: Jeroen Borglevens loves embarking his diners on a journey, particularly to Asia. His finetuned score is not averse to surprising us, but never to excess. For example, he may craft seabass as a ceviche with grapefruit, jalapeno and wasabi ice cream or pair cod aged in kombu with a yusukosho-spiked beurre blanc. Be prepared for an experience that unveils a host of unexpected treats and endless sensations. The beverage list, rich in cocktails, sakes and wine, is equally captivating. Should you fancy a close-up view of the culinary show, book a seat at the counter, which is as elegant as the zen-inspired interior is intimate.

Name: Robuust
Description: This warm and welcoming restaurant is run by two larger-than-life brothers: chef Raimon and maître d' Peter Ian. You can look forward to dishes brimming with distinctive flavours, as in the finely spiced beurre blanc that lends a touch of indulgence to a perfectly fried slice of cod. Such culinary excellence characterises their classic fare as well as the more creative set menu. Be sure to ask your expert host for his beer recommendations – he has some real gems up his sleeve!

Name: Robuust
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace
Description: The contemporary elegance of this delightful villa is more than worthy of a home decoration magazine. Even better, it is flanked by a lovely patio and boasts a small conservatory to the rear. The chef focuses on flavours which he crafts into his own versions of traditional recipes such as classic eels in green herbs and vol-au-vent. High-flying, inspired craftsmanship and lashings of flavour illustrate that Robuust is far from averse to showcasing its delicate facet.

Name: Rocacho Plaza
Address: Plaza del Marqués de Salamanca 9, Madrid, 28006, Spain
Description: Located in the heart of the city’s Salamanca district, Rocacho Plaza boasts a pleasant terrace and a menu that focuses on grilled dishes. Among its choice of meats, the selection from El Capricho, the famous farm in Jiménez de Jamuz in the province of León, are a real draw, including its premium “Selección José Gordón” ox chop and its beef chop aged for 90 days. It also offers market-inspired dishes, recipes featuring seasonal vegetables, superb grilled fish, and rice and fideuá options. It also occasionally hosts full-day food events such as those dedicated to the delicious oxtail.

Name: Rock-Fort
Description: North Sea fish and natural wines are the bedrock of this bright, elegant bistro. Chef Laurent and Eline, in charge of the front of house, who first came to our notice at Amuzee in Zeebrugge, are going from strength to strength as they settle in here. The menu overflows in the generous produce of the North Sea with a distinctive subtle, sometimes spicy edge. The fascinating culinary score is depicted by almost translucent grilled langoustines, which are paired with a dashi umami edge or raw scallops served with green apples and jalapeno. Rock-Fort is alive and kicking – in every sense!

Name: Rockfish
Address: Jumeirah Al Naseem Hotel, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud Street, Umm Suqeim 3, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This professionally run seafood restaurant, set in the Jumeirah Hotel, has a terrace overlooking the Burj Al Arab and its surrounding sea, and its light and airy interior has high ceilings, floral displays and a chic, exclusive feel. The concise menu showcases beautifully fresh fish and shellfish in precisely cooked, powerfully flavoured dishes; the Moka Tiramisu is also a must try. The wine list features a good range of Provençal rosé wines.

Name: Rocpool
Address: 1 Ness Walk, Inverness, IV3 5NE, United Kingdom
Description: Occupying a prime spot on the banks of the River Ness, this enduringly popular restaurant is to be praised for its longevity. It's a bright and colourful, brasserie-style place where the experienced team deal well with their high turnover. The extensive menu offers something for everyone and a love for Scottish produce is never far away, despite regular global influences – as evidenced by the likes of Shetland monkfish with risotto Milanese and 'nduja-roasted prawns. This is also a perfect pit-stop if you're on the North Coast 500 road trip.

Name: Rocus
Description: Housed in an attractively converted railway building dating from 1904, this restaurant proposes ambitious cuisine that takes its cue from the seasons – available à la carte or as a set menu. Dine al fresco in the courtyard or on the terrace facing the railway line. A table in the wine cellar, surrounded by Spanish red wines, comes highly recommended.

Name: Rodd & Gunn The Lodge
Description: Looking out to Lake Wakatipu and the surrounding mountains, the restaurant exudes a warm, relaxing atmosphere. Oak flooring, leather chairs and fur throws resonate with the clothing brand's timeless, refined style. Modern New Zealand fare is the mainstay of the menu and most ingredients – as well as the wines – are locally sourced. The market fish of the day and handmade pastas are standouts. In summer, get closer to nature by dining al fresco on the lawn.

Name: Rodd & Gunn The Lodge
Address: GF, Commercial Bay, 7 Queen Street, Auckland Central, Auckland, 1010, New Zealand
Description: Following on from the success of the original Queenstown restaurant, this second branch continues the theme of showcasing the best local produce by putting a spin on classic recipes, with the addition of some Mediterranean influences. Meats like lamb shoulder are a speciality and it’s worth adding the fantastic duck-fat roast potatoes to any order – if you do, then consider trying on those pants in the next-door boutique after, rather than before, your lunch. The wooden floors and sheepskin on the chairs add plenty of warmth to the bright, well-run room.

Name: Rodesand
Description: In an idyllic lakeside location by the Kellersee, this estate was made famous by the German cult film series Immenhof. Nowadays, within the pretty white walls of the manor house, diners tuck into ambitious fish and vegetarian/vegan dishes, such as "beetroot, buckwheat, calamansi, dill" or "Lofoten skrei, monk's beard, verjus, capers, chorizo". Choose between the set menu and individual dishes à la carte. The grilled fish options are sure to whet the appetite. The interior design is delightful: With seven tables, the main room has an elegant, modern feel. There are also two private dining spaces for smaller parties, and Jantzens Bar (with a cigar lounge), where sushi is served. Delightful terrace overlooking the greenery. Tip: Afternoon tea on Sat and Sun. Hotel, riding facilities and farm shop on site.

Name: Roe
Address: 5 Park Drive, Canary Wharf, London, E14 9GG, United Kingdom
Description: Launched by the team behind Fallow, this vast restaurant can house up to 500 diners in the heart of Canary Wharf, all while being run with impressive slickness. Guests are spread across several dining rooms, some with counter seating, plus a lovely wrap-around terrace that boasts commanding views of South Dock. The wide-ranging menu offers something for everyone, including playful takes on British classics like maitake Cornish pasty or market fish served with parsley liquor, that's reminiscent of an East End pie and mash.

Name: Rogues
Address: 460 Hackney Road, Hackney, London, E2 9EG, United Kingdom
Description: After a succession of pop-ups, friends Zac Whittle and Freddie Sheen found a permanent home at this rustic restaurant where bright prints enliven exposed concrete walls and the mix-and-match wooden tables fit the informal vibe. The overtly seasonal menu changes daily, but you can expect interesting and full-flavoured dishes such as grilled Bobby beans with piperade, smoked almonds and cherries, in which the flavours and textures all work together beautifully. The genial service team run things well.

Name: Rojak‧Popiah & Cockle
Address: Maxwell Food Centre, #01-56, 1 Kadayanallur Street, 069184, Singapore
Description: This clean, tidy stall is named after the three items on its menu. The rojak features pineapple, yam bean, cucumber and fried dough stick dressed in a sweet, tangy and spicy sauce. Try their made-to-order popiah, too.

Name: Roka Bahçe
Address: Hacımemiş Mahallesi, 2027. Sokak No:6, Çeşme, Izmir, 35937, Türkiye
Description: The narrow, stone-paved streets of Alacati are always buzzing with activity. Tucked away in one such lane is this alfresco restaurant, whose lively atmosphere instantly draws you in. Gökhan Safkan allows Turkish flavours to seamlessly merge with Bosnian influences, creating a heady mix in dishes such as artichokes cooked with onion and garlic in an orange-infused broth, or succulent pljeskavica (Balkan meat patties) and delicately grilled, ultra-fresh sea bass. This laid-back place puts the emphasis on fun, and the steady stream of dishes emerging from the kitchen is testament to this. You have been warned: the charm of Roka Bahçe is irresistible.

Name: Roku - Japanese Dining & Wine
Description: This is the third restaurant to be opened by Yoshizumi Nagaya in Düsseldorf. The atmosphere is trendy, modern and relaxed. The Japanese menu ranges from a variety of appealing starters and a fine selection of sushi and sashimi to tempura, fish and meat dishes – including, for example, A5 Wagyu steak. There is a good, predominantly German wine list and a selection of sake. Tip: Lunch Wed-Fri.

Name: Rola
Description: It is surprising to find such a restaurant in the countryside (located about 3 km south of Bermeo), inside the charming hotel Nafarrola, which has recovered the magnificent farmhouse of the same name. Behind the term Rola, with which they use locally to refer to a log or a piece of wood, they seek a perfect symbiosis with the environment around them, the beautiful Urdaibai Biosphere Reserve. Here, in a space of elegant rustic minimalism that fascinates with its views of the valley and the sea, chef Gaizka Goikoetxea focuses his proposal on a unique tasting menu that evolves with the seasons, inspired by the ecosystem of Urdaibai and demonstrating both the traceability of the best nearby produce (many from his own vegetable garden) and his commitment to the environment. Everything is delicious, but we recommend you try the Bermeo hake, with its citric collagen and clam pil-pil. Also, it is not a bad spot to discover the txakolis of Bizkaia, as they offer more than 30 different types!

Name: Rolf and Daughters
Description: Chef/owner Philip Krajeck's Germantown restaurant lures a well-heeled crowd of locals who flock here for great food, done well. His cooking is earnest and approachable, with a seasonal and contemporary mindset. This is a menu where you'll want everything; luckily, it's all designed for sharing. The house-made pasta program turns out impressive work in plates that speak to the season, from fresh spaghetti tinted green from the inclusion of tomato leaves to a corn agnolotti tucked with sweet corn in a beurre blanc. Main dishes like chicken or pork t-bone lean into the refined comfort appeal. A very simple dessert of house-made vanilla bean ice cream with a mashed amaretti cookie topped with a poached peach is a perfect send-off.

Name: Rolin
Description: A charming and elegant setting, extremely friendly service courtesy of attentive professional waitstaff, and dishes with Mediterranean, classic and regional influences, such as "monkfish cheeks pan-fried in a caper and lime butter, saffron risotto, fennel, tomato, artichoke" or "crisp-fried Label Rouge guinea fowl breast, raw-marinated pointed cabbage with grapes & walnuts, lukewarm mushroom salad & browned bread dumplings". The quality of the produce and the craftsmanship are as impressive as the distinctive flavours and the appealing presentation. From the well-curated à la carte selection, recommendations also comprise a three- to five-course set menu. "Rolin" is the name of the captain of the luxury express steamer Cap Polonio – the restaurant is located in the hotel of the same name.

Name: Romantyczna
Address: First Floor, Hotel SPA Dr Irena Eris Wzgórza Dylewskie, Wysoka Wieś, 14-100, Poland
Description: On the first floor of the Dr Irena Eris spa hotel, itself buried within the forest, this traditional restaurant offers an old-school kind of charm. With its fireplace, floral tablecloths and wooden parquet flooring, there’s an unashamedly classical vibe to the place. The cooking has a similar feel, with dishes such as Masurian zander and trout with beurre blanc underpinned by the kitchen’s well-honed techniques and careful composition.

Name: Romolo Mare
Description: Situated in a private beach club facing the sea, this restaurant combines a relaxed atmosphere with an elegant feel thanks to its professional owners who have worked as restaurateurs for many years. Here, they serve excellent fish and seafood cuisine with a focus on raw dishes, plus a choice of daily fish specials. A selection of interesting local wines completes the picture.

Name: Ron Gastrobar Indonesia Ouderkerk
Description: Top chef Ron Blaauw has a nose for a winning concept, as proven by this typical Indonesian restaurant with its bustling terrace by the River Amstel. The flavours are distinctively Asian, but he and his colleague Agus Hermawan also add their own twists for that extra fragrance and depth. The rijsttafel options "Agus" (15 dishes) and "Guillaume" (12 dishes) provide the perfect opportunity to share all kinds of delicious treats, such as satay kambing and udang peteh.

Name: Ronan
Address: 7315 Melrose Ave., Los Angeles, CA, 90046, USA
Description: Aim for the two-story floral mural to find this Italian favorite with a dive bar-feel and plenty of LA style. Sit in the lovely patio, or head inside to the black marble bar. Other options include booths as well as an attractive communal table crafted from a varnished wood slab. Diners can expect to see pizza dough stretched, blenders whirring and the wood-fired oven crackling, all of which contribute to Ronan's swank allure.Come for their hand-stretched Neopolitan pizza, as well as their shared plates using seasonal produce and ingredients, with appetizers like their spring arancini with pastrami-spiced maitake with English peas and garlic, or their charred broccolini with their house blend of za'atar, fresh mint, and a Meyer lemon aïoli.

Name: Rond de Carotte
Address: 50 rue de la Vignette, Saint-Gervais-les-Bains, 74170, France
Description: In the heart of the resort, this eatery shines the spotlight on seasonal, sometimes local ingredients, such as Magland snails. The chef conjures up well-crafted dishes, like free-range poached egg flanked by sweet chestnuts and creamy squash, or melt-in-the-mouth chuck beef stew that is eaten with a spoon. The chalet-inspired dining room, divided in two by a small open-plan kitchen, is the quintessence of alpine charm, in particular due to the shelves loaded in bottles (the establishment is also a wine merchant). Daily brunch from 9am-2pm.

Name: Rong Cuisine
Address: 10-2, Lane 17, Section 4, Fuxing Road, East District, Taichung, Taiwan
Description: Chef Rong opened this little gem tucked away in an alley in 2021. The room is reminiscent of a Japanese diner, with its wooden counter enclosing an open kitchen. The eclectic menu covers Taiwanese, Japanese and Western dishes in smaller portions so that guests can sample more variety. Signature items include braised pork rice with sakura shrimps – the hand-diced pork is fatty and melty, Job’s tears and rice that’s rich and creamy. Reservations are mandatory.

Name: Rong Ji Hai Xian Lao Hua (Cangshan)
Address: 161 Liaoyuan Road, Cangshan, Fuzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: Lao hua, or Fujian-style noodle soup, is usually considered frugal eats. This shop, however, champions a novel lao hua that uses luxury seafood such as live abalone and razor clam. The modern, cosy room is also worlds apart from your average lao hua stall. Just indicate your favourite toppings and noodles to the server. The kitchen team will then cook them to perfection. Also try pork head meat dressed in Sichuan pepper sauce.

Name: Rong Ju
Address: Capella, 139 Dunhua North Road, Songshan District, Taipei, 105021, Taiwan
Description: The dining room with the ceiling covered in faux red brick evokes a modern yet warm Chinese home. In 2026, under the helm of a chef with an international background, the kitchen introduced a subtle contemporary touch to the cuisine. The set menus remain anchored in Cantonese classics, but are thoughtfully updated with modern twists and premium ingredients such as lobster dim sum with truffle and stir-fried Shandong cabbage with sakura ebi. The tea selection and pairing are well curated – order a pot for a harmonious complement to the meal.

Name: Rong Rong Yuan
Address: 2F, 25, Section 4, Xinyi Road, Da'an District, Taipei, 106, Taiwan
Description: The chef here has been at the helm for 30 years and each dish is prepared exactly as it was when the shop opened back in 1965. The extensive menu highlights painstakingly prepared recipes, many of which need pre-ordering when booking. The signature steamed stinky tofu is briny, silky and juicy. For a taste of authentic Jiangzhe fare, try quick-fried rice paddy eel with yellow chives in Ningbo style that boasts deep aromas and soy umami.

Name: Rongros
Address: 392/16 Maha Rat Road, Phra Borom Maha Ratchawang, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
Description: Meaning ‘House of Flavours,’ Rongros preserves the taste of traditional Thai cuisine on the banks of the Chao Phraya River with a stunning view of Wat Arun. Highlights include the green curry with rib eye beef served with roti and the tangy glass noodle salad. The vintage décor, including the chandeliers, painted Chinese panels, and wooden furniture only add to the experience. Book a table on the terrace for dinner to take in the view at sunset. Keep in mind that this restaurant is a favorite spot for tourists, so it's a good idea to make a reservation in advance to secure your place.

Name: Ronin
Address: FIVE LUXE JBR, The Walk, Jumeirah Beach Residence, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Uninterrupted views of Ain Dubai and its surrounding sea paired with contemporary Japanese cuisine is a recipe for a great evening. Located on the ninth floor of the FIVE LUXE JBR hotel, this eatery’s interior is detailed with beautifully tiled walls and red paper lanterns. The food is fun, packed with flavour and prepared with precision and care; expect everything from raw fish to robata grilled meats, tempura to teppanyaki, made with quality ingredients. We suggest booking a seat at the counter for an exclusive omakase experience.

Name: Ronquillo
Address: Menéndez Pelayo 2, Ramales de la Victoria, 39800, Spain
Description: A restaurant with a delightfully rustic ambience that includes a profusion of exposed stone and wood, which provides the backdrop for traditionally inspired cuisine that includes a skilful contemporary touch and revolves around the sourcing of the best zero-mile ingredients. The family at the helm takes care of the meticulous service and the beautiful presentation of dishes featuring on the à la carte and three tasting menus: Cullavera, Cueva del Mirón and Cueva Covalanas. All the soups and stews we tried here, such as the pinto beans with venison, were superb.

Name: Roof Garden
Description: Make sure you ask for one of the tables next to the glass wall in this restaurant, which boasts romantic views of Bergamo’s Città Alta. The innovative, inventive cuisine is tempting and full of flavour.

Name: Rooh
Address: 333 Brannan St., San Francisco, CA, 94107, USA
Description: Amidst a slew of upscale Indian restaurants descending upon San Francisco, Rooh rises to the top, thanks to an innovative menu that fuses the subcontinent’s myriad flavors with modern restaurant staples (oysters, pork belly, burrata). The bold India-goes-industrial décor is a bit paint-by-numbers, with vivid jewel tones and an oversized mural, but the vibe is engaging and the cocktails quite unique. Rooh's cuisine is approachable, but an extra degree of care and punched-up ingredient quality are reflected in the pricing. Sharing is encouraged with an array of small and larger plates like tandoori black pepper chicken. Wrap up with unique desserts like a cashew praline cake paired with phirni mousse and thaindai ice cream.

Name: Rooselaer
Description: Lovers of traditional fare have been frequenting this elegant manor with its conservatory and alfresco terrace and garden since 1977. The chef’s generous, traditional fare has attracted a faithful crowd of regulars who appreciate both the set and à la carte menus, in which lobster and grilled meat take pride of place. The second generation is pursuing this classical heritage, albeit with the odd more modern touch, but ever true to its hallmark hearty flavours.

Name: Roosenberg
Description: Waasmunster’s discerning foodies make up the faithful clientele of this smart eatery. They come for the elegant interior, friendly vibe and top-quality produce, without forgetting the lure of the wine cellar, well stocked in Burgundy and Tuscan tipples. The à la carte lineup embodies the establishment’s devotion to quality. Chef-owner Bruno De Wilde errs towards flame-licked techniques and seasonal ingredients, together with signature dishes like vol-au-vent, tartare steak, asparagus à la flamande or local game in season. What’s not to like?

Name: Rooster
Description: After training in prestigious houses (from Passedat to Darroze), Frédéric Duca has set up shop in the more working-class part of the 17th arrondissement. In a former street corner cafe, the Marseille-born chef signs dishes which pay numerous tributes to his Mediterranean and Provençal roots. The lunchtime menu is at delicious eater-friendly prices. More ambitious in the evenings.

Name: Root 81
Description: This pleasant restaurant rolls out Mediterranean-style fare, skilfully crafted by a talented chef with a focus on local ingredients. The outdoor alfresco area sports an attractive and relaxing vibe, without forgetting an excellent selection of wines and cocktails.

Name: Roots Restaurant
Description: Ralph Kollnitzer – a familiar name in the region – cooks up a storm here in the fine dining restaurant of the small Hotel Aldershoff by the Lavant. The space has a modern decor with light wood and pops of green; the service is friendly. A surprise menu is available in a four-, six- or eight-course format. Aromatic dishes made using regional ingredients are testament to the chef's creativity and his ties to his roots in Carinthia: think smoked trout with Grantnschleck (cranberry cream). The evening menu is also served in the café. During the day, breakfast and a simpler lunch menu are up for grabs.

Name: Rory's Place
Address: 139 E. Ojai Ave., Ojai, CA, 93023, USA
Description: Sisters Rory and Meave McAuliffe run this charming Ojai spot with rustic, feel-good vibes. Wide plank wood floors lend warmth while exposed ducts keep things trendy. There is a little bit of everything here, from a local produce-driven menu and terrific raw bar offerings to a natural wine list and a provisions counter up front. Some dishes seem simple but deliver in spades. A stunning salad of avocado, baby beets and citrus served on a wide, oval plate is a riot of colors. Then, an herb-laced broth bobbing with Aleppo sausage, spring garlic, potatoes and steamed countneck clams offers a refined take on stew. Then, a classic Pavlova is topped with a citrus custard and fresh blood and cara cara oranges, grapefruit and kumquat for a bright finish.

Name: Rosa Pulver
Description: After relocating within the city centre, the restaurant still draws diners with its seasonally inspired cooking. There is a choice of a five-course "Chef's Choice" menu (with fish and meat or vegetarian) as well as appealing à la carte options such as "cured char, rapeseed", "smoked tofu tempura, chard, kimchi" or "lamb, parsnip, spring herbs". The house-baked sourdough bread served at the start of the meal is wonderful. A carefully curated selection of wines is also available. Warm, attentive service is the icing on the cake.

Name: Roscioli
Description: This restaurant is part of one of the best food outlets in Rome, which offers delicacies such as typical Roman pastas, cooked and raw fish, meat, an impressive selection of cured hams and cheeses, as well as top-quality ingredients such as anchovies and mozzarella. Excellent home-baked bread and a varied wine list complete the picture. Make sure you book ahead, as it’s hard to get a table here without a reservation.

Name: Rose Mary
Address: 932 W. Fulton Market, Chicago, IL, 60607, USA
Description: Conceived by Chef Joe Flamm, this neighborhood delight in the West Fulton Market is worth every bit of hype—from its singular menu to the airy design. Imagine a setting that evokes Croatia's konobas (akin to a rustic trattoria) featuring whitewashed walls, rustic clay, and hanging plants with seating that can easily accommodate some-100 diners.Well-versed servers are on hand to guide patrons through the menu, which draws inspiration from the Adriatic. High points include tortellini djuvec (eggplant and preserved zucchini in a red pepper cream) as well as burek with ground beef and mozzarella. The charcoal hearth is solely responsible for such sumptuous mains as lamb with blitva and potatoes. Save room for sweet treats like rosewater fritule.

Name: Rosella
Address: 137 Avenue A, New York, NY, 10009, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: This high dining, hyper-sustainable operation is proudly unbound by tradition. The intimate dining room favors warmth and personality over minimalism, with cerulean tones and a handcrafted central counter. The à la carte menu clearly reflects the restaurant's sourcing philosophy, spotlighting local, responsibly harvested seafood treated with restraint and curiosity. Contemporary, gently playful touches appear throughout, from smoked or pickled fish preparations to subtle nods to hand-roll culture and dishes like XO grits that balance comfort with precision. A thoughtfully curated wine list leans domestic, drawing from the North Fork and West Coast.

Name: Rosella
Address: 18 Majoribanks Street, Mount Victoria, Wellington, 6011, New Zealand
Description: This dining concept melds Mediterranean, North African and Middle Eastern accents in food jazzed up by exotic spices, herbs and condiments. Recipes are cleverly devised, and each dish has its own distinctive character. The smoked tomato toast with white bean purée and green olives boasts deep umami, balanced flavour and contrasting textures. Visit the bar upstairs for signature cocktails, such as negroni featuring bitters made in-house.

Name: Rosi
Address: The Beaumont Hotel, 8 Balderton Street, Brown Hart Gardens, Mayfair, London, W1K 6TF, United Kingdom
Description: Inside the luxurious art deco confines of The Beaumont Hotel, Rosi is decked out in soothing pastel shades, with eye-catching friezes from artist Luke Edward Hall lending a bold splash of colour. Here, the menu offers a roll-call of traditional British favourites with the occasional decadent touch. While the exact dishes change, expect the likes of calf's liver and bacon, cottage pie or a choice of steaks. The sundae is a fun way to finish, with a playful ‘design your own’ approach. Sundays, in classic British fashion, see roast dinners take centre stage.

Name: Rosita
Description: Decorated in the same simple and rustic style as the Hotel Rosita in which it is housed, this restaurant boasts an attractive terrace overlooking the sea and the coast (call in advance to book one of the tables with the best view), which more than compensates for the narrow, winding road that you have to follow to get here. The delicious cuisine is regional in flavour, including seafood options such as the excellent stuffed baby squid in a sauce served with mashed potatoes, and meat dishes that include a tasty rabbit casserole.

Name: Rosso di Acqua e Sole
Description: In the mood for fresh Italian cuisine that skilfully combines typical cucina casalinga with modern influences? The select ingredients are seasonal, with fish and seafood as the focal point. The ikejime dry-aged sea bass, for example, from the restaurant's own maturing cabinet, is excellent. In addition to the à la carte menu, patron Ingmar Goetzloff will talk you through the latest creations at your table. He will also be happy to advise you on drinks – they have a nicely curated wine list with around 400 labels. The modern, attractively decorated restaurant is located in a residential and office area close to the main railway station and Landestheater.

Name: Rosso di Sera
Address: via Pietro Nenni 2, Castelletto sopra Ticino, 28053, Italy
Description: Situated closed to the motorway exit, this restaurant’s rustic exterior belies its young, colourful and contemporary interior. The dishes are as modern as the decor, yet they have their roots in strong local traditions. The owner has a real passion for French and sparkling wines, including around 160 different champagnes and a wide selection of Burgundies, plus a good choice of wines by the glass, craft beers and cocktails.

Name: Rossoblu
Address: 1124 San Julian St., Los Angeles, CA, 90015, USA
Description: This standout from Chef/owner Steve Samson is a favorite among local shoppers and visitors alike. While the area teems with restaurants aplenty, cutting-edge Rossoblu won't disappoint. There’s nothing avant-garde about its food however, and thankfully so. In fact, due to delicious summers spent in Emilia-Romagna, the chef's creations are a veritable ode to the region and promise to make Italian palates proud.Quality ingredients and simple execution come to life in redeye tuna tartare with shallots, capers, and preserved lemon over an avocado puree, served with lavash bread. Pastas, like Olimpia's tagliatelle, with house-made pasta with a pork and beef ragu, are just right. Close on the heels is an irresistible brick of tiramisu crowned with candied cocoa nib cream.

Name: Rosô
Address: 1 route du Grabat, Le Perrier, 85300, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Located in a village nestled in the Marais Breton, this restaurant is run by a couple of young industry professionals: Mathieu Blanchet in the kitchen and Pauline Merceron front of house. The seasonal cuisine makes the most of high-quality local produce – think courgette panna cotta, lemon condiment, lamb's lettuce and onion pickles, or skate wing terrine, caper butter, leek maki and black sesame. In an understated, minimalist setting, the open kitchen is laid out behind a long, pale-wood counter. Friendly service with a smile. Lunchtime set menu, à la carte options and a tasting menu in the evening.

Name: Rote Bar
Description: This restaurant in the famous Hotel Sacher, a piece of the city's history, epitomises the charm of this great Viennese establishment with its striking red interior, elegant oil paintings and crystal chandeliers. The menu features dishes that draw inspiration from modern culinary trends as well as Viennese and Austrian traditional specialities, including Tafelspitz and Sachertorte. Gorgeous little veranda.

Name: Rote Wand Stuben
Description: This charming restaurant in the Rote Wand Gourmet Hotel serves traditional Austrian cuisine at its best, whether it's a perfectly souffléd Wiener schnitzel, delicious Buttermilchschmarrn (shredded, fluffy buttermilk pancake) or fabulous fondues! Diners can also look forward to cordial service and an extensive and well-curated selection of wines. At lunchtime, dishes are served à la carte, including fondue chinoise (Swiss-style hot pot) and cheese fondue. In the evening, culinary tradition is presented in appealing set menus. Compose your own two-, three-, or four-course meal from a range of options, or select one of five fondue set menus.

Name: Rotes Haus - Restaurant am Marktplatz
Description: This charming old Rhine Valley building dating back to 1639 is quite something! A Dornbirn landmark right on the Marktplatz (still the market square), it has been sensitively renovated and restored, and now boasts five really beautiful historical rooms. Delicious Austrian cuisine with Mediterranean influences is on the menu – the Wiener schnitzel and fried chicken are as appetising as the pickled char with radish and rhubarb-wild garlic vinaigrette. The spacious terrace, shaded by parasols, is also inviting.

Name: Roti Sai Mai Abeedeen-Pranom Sangaroon
Address: 32/1 Mu 4, U Thong Road, Pratu Chai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: Over 70 years have passed, but this renowned spot opposite Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya Hospital still serves the same perfect rotis with candy floss, made by the same family. Two flavours are available — the original is especially worth trying. As popular as ever, be prepared to queue.

Name: Roucou
Address: 28 Aberdeen Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: An expert cheesemaker has teamed up with French and Japanese chefs to offer Hong Kong’s first cheese omakase with 12 courses that combine French artisan cheeses with Japanese culinary art. The tasting menu juxtapose different taste profiles and textures for a genuine fine dining experience. In addition to the 8-seater omakase counter, there is a main dining room for guests ordering à la carte dishes. Check out their Japanese-inspired cocktails, wine and sake pairing options.

Name: Rouge Barre
Address: 50 rue de la Halle, Lille, 59800, France
Description: In the heart of Vieux Lille, local man Steven Ramon confirms – after his Top Chef adventure in 2014 – that we should be counting on him in the future. A Ch'ti to the core, he concocts inspired and lively dishes that make the most of fine ingredients. The restaurant has a "rouge barre" interior (red brick and white stone). Irresistible!

Name: Rousille
Description: Exit L'inaTTendu, welcome Rousille! Romane Veyrac, previously sous-chef here, has taken over this intimate bistro, which has been given an attractive makeover in the process. This chef in her thirties gives the classics a clever twist. The menu comprises simple but not simplistic dishes: sea bass fillet "grenobloise", textures of cauliflower with a caper beurre noisette; pork tenderloin with aubergines in a chorizo crumb and thyme jus; lemon and sesame choux.

Name: Roussel's Restaurant La Bonne Adresse
Description: Thierry Roussel and Jane Kölchens run this place with dedication. The elegant restaurant exudes cosiness, and the extremely friendly service, directed by your hostess, also contributes to the pleasant atmosphere. At beautifully laid tables, upscale classic cuisine is served in the form of set menus (one vegetarian) or à la carte. They are also happy to share their wine recommendations, including some from their own production. Plus: guestrooms where you will feel right at home.

Name: Routier
Address: 2801 California St., San Francisco, CA, 94115, USA
Description: Routier is a welcoming neighborhood spot serving its own take on French bistro fare, featuring a distinct Californian accent. Chef/owner JP Carmona's casual-meets-sophisticated approach can be seen in dishes like a hot-and-cold composition of crisp, buttery potato pavé topped with sweet Dungeness crab in an herby, lemony mayonnaise, or tender pork cheeks nestled on a bed of creamy lentils, topped with a salad of apples and mustard greens. Quality produce and satisfyingly rustic cooking are hallmarks year-round. Sweets are furnished by celebrated next-door neighbor, B. Patisserie, so it should go without saying, save room for dessert.

Name: Roux
Description: Every great sauce starts with a roux, and here it's very much a speciality. The trend-conscious cooking features playful combinations, engaging textures and international influences, and is underpinned by those robust sauces. Think medium-rare fillet of hare in a sweet-spice crust, elevated by a refined game jus and complemented by slices of raw foie gras and crunchy quince. The sommelier's expert wine pairings are delivered with infectious enthusiasm. One final tip: The long dining counter is our favourite spot in this elegant luxury brasserie.

Name: Roux
Description: When we think of a French bistro we all have a general idea of what to expect. This corner restaurant, complemented by small pavement terraces on each side for alfresco dining, boasts an intimate and attractively classical interior with tables set close together, a kitchen that is partially visible from the bar, whitewashed woodwork and large windows that provide plenty of natural light. Chef Martín Rebaudino who, as part of his career path, travelled to Europe and had the good fortune to share a kitchen with legendary Spanish chefs such as Martín Berasategui, Juan Mari Arzak and Pedro Subijana, offers an extensive contemporary-style à la carte with French, Spanish and Argentinian influences that includes an appetising array of hot and cold starters, delicious risottos, and top-quality red meats. If you sit out on the terrace, you’ll almost feel as though you’re dining on a Parisian boulevard!

Name: Roux 30A
Address: 114 Logan Ln., Ste. 1A, Santa Rosa Beach, FL, 32459, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted
Description: Set along Florida's Emerald Coast in Grayton Beach, Roux 30A is the kind of place that charms at first sight. Slightly quirky in style (think pot racks strung with flatware), it's an inviting space where diners are seated at communal tables or counter stools with a view of the open kitchen. The tasting menu is equally endearing. The kitchen prepares a handful of courses with contemporary American leanings, all based around the seasons. The ever-shifting menu promises creativity in dishes like pasta made with purple sweet potato powder with beech mushrooms in a Parmesan and sage sauce that's topped with a savory, seared U-10 scallop. Local cobia rolled with sweet potato threads over sautéed pumpkin and caramel apple sauce leans into the season in an especially flavorful way.

Name: Roux at Skindles
Address: Mill Lane, Taplow, SL6 0AG, United Kingdom
Description: You can't keep Alain Roux away from the banks of the Thames. Up the road from his famous Waterside Inn, he owns this contemporary brasserie in a similarly pleasant riverside setting. The skill and confidence of the chefs is evident across the menu of traditional French and other European dishes, such as the wonderfully satisfying crab bisque linguine with lemon stracciatella. If you're lucky, there might be a fruits de mer platter chalked up on the blackboard specials. Arrive early for drinks on the terrace or in the cocktail bar.

Name: Rovello
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Although it has a new venue, this restaurant has retained its attractive friendly feel in a dining room that acts as a backdrop for substantial dishes that are full of flavour. The interesting classic menu is supplemented by a selection of daily specials, with meat, fish and vegetables (some grilled) prepared in front of guests seated at the counter. There are also traditional tables available and the lively atmosphere remains that of a friendly, welcoming bistro. Interesting wine list, including a selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Rowan
Address: Rothay Manor, Borrans Road, Ambleside, LA22 0EH, United Kingdom
Description: In an understandably popular part of the picturesque Lake District, the Rothay Manor country house hotel stands proud with its Regency-era grandeur and stylish modern additions. Rowan is its restaurant, occupying an elegant dining room that features original shutters and cornicing alongside bold William Morris wallpaper and striking chandeliers. The concise à la carte is full of seasonal goodness, all executed with skill and care. Look out for bright, fresh fish dishes like roast cod with 'nduja, gremolata, broad beans and shrimp.

Name: Roxanne
Description: Restaurants could learn a thing or two from this eccentric spot. There are no long narratives or spiels once you’re seated, and the menu shows no interest in trends. The sparse room is painted in a quirky purple with Japanese tatami tables on one side. Named after her mother, Chef Alexandra Holt just wants to cook — and cook she can. Not one to shy away from seasoning, she offers a small selection of dishes that prioritize flavor over fuss. Garlic scapes arrive buried under a mountain of ripe melon with sheep’s milk cheese running down one side. Delicate ricotta gnudi are set in a fierce Sungold tomato sauce. Does roast duck really need a wedge of Stilton? How many cherries does it take to cover coffee crème brûlée? Just go with it.

Name: Royal
Address: 501 Florida Ave. NW, Washington, DC, 20001, USA
Description: This airy, quaint, and relaxed all-day spot likes to keep things low-maintenance. The price point too is agreeably lower than its fussier competitors, and the Latin American food is decidedly scrumptious. No wonder, it's a legitimate local favorite.Breakfast is a must, especially if the messy, eggy arepa is on offer. Served wrapped in a white pouch, it resembles a present crafted from seared masa and filled with a fried egg, tomato, cotjia, and avocado. At dinner, hungry fans head to the intimate second-level space—complete with original details—to try their hand at tender pork empanadas laced with aji and the heavenly scent of garlic. The masa “gnocchi” is a rare treat, tossed with braised beef, maitake mushrooms, and loads of herbs.

Name: Royal China Club
Address: 3F, Bund 5, 20 Guangdong Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: Operated by London’s Royal China Group, this Cantonese restaurant specialises in dried seafood like abalone and fish, along with other assorted seafood dishes. The quality of the seafood is good, with some of the ingredients imported from the UK, such as lobsters from Scotland. Dim sum is popular at lunch and, during Chinese festivals, handmade products like glutinous rice dumplings and mooncakes are provided.

Name: Royd
Address: 95/1 Dibuk Road, Talat Nuea, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: With seating for just 20, at tables and the counter, this intimate spot explores Southern Thai cuisine with almost exclusively local ingredients. The six- to eight-course menu highlights herbs, seafood and spice – think Krabi fish curry and frog's legs with fermented rice noodles. The torch ginger features prominently in many courses and pairs beautifully in each one. Low-intervention wines pair seamlessly with the bold flavours.

Name: Roza
Address: 3 place de la Monnaie, Nantes, 44000, France
Description: In his restaurant in the centre of Nantes, chef Jean-François Pantaleon expresses his passion for the produce of the Pays de Loire terroir. The wine list gives pride of place to hand-picked small-scale wine producers. The cosy interior and inviting, laid-back atmosphere further add to this delightful dining experience.

Name: Rozdział
Address: Sava Boutique Hotel, ul. Wybrzeże Kościuszkowskie 43, Warsaw, 00-347, Poland
Description: There’s a minimalistic kind of elegance to this intimate restaurant inside the Sava Boutique Hotel on the banks of the Vistula river – think whitewashed walls, dimmed lights and neatly dressed tables. High-quality ingredients are at the bedrock of the cooking, which shine brightest in uncluttered, subtle dishes such as mackerel with horseradish, dill and caviar. While there is an à la carte, go for one of the two tasting menus for the full experience.

Name: Rozewied
Description: Rozewied, "poppy" in Zeelandic, is the joint venture of Ferdy and Noëmie. The two of them do everything themselves in this centuries-old building, into which they have breathed new life, while taking care to preserve its historical character. In the kitchen, classical combinations are given a modern twist. Lamb, for example, is paired with garlic, but with the lightness and playfulness expected by today's diners. The chefs give pride of place to European produce, and have a penchant for fish dishes and delicate sauces.

Name: Ruba's Bakery
Address: Morelos 8, San José del Cabo, 23406, Mexico
Description: There's sure to be a crowd at this Arts District charmer, housed in a casita dating back to the 1940s. The space is fronted by umbrella-shaded tables facing a papel picado-strewn street. Inside and out back, it's all quite comfortable.This casual bistro serves throughout the day, and there is a coffee counter and display case of conchas, croissants and donuts, among other treats. More substantial offerings include cheese and charcuterie, salads, sandwiches and wood-fired pizza. At brunch, order the chilaquiles (available only Friday-Sunday), served in a skillet with crisp yellow corn tortilla chips soaked in a morita chile sauce, accompanied by diced bits of roasted lamb and a Valle de Guadalupe-style consommé. The freshly baked bolillo is great for dipping in the broth.

Name: Rubaiyat Madrid
Description: Discover the authentic flavours of São Paulo by visiting this cosy establishment, dressed with a profusion of wood and decorative details that evoke the great South American haciendas. Here, as you would expect, everything revolves around the embers and the grill, which is the thread that runs through the entire proposal, with high-quality meats (especially Angus and Wagyu) that conquer guests by playing with Brazilian, Argentine and European cuts (Bife de chorizo, Picaña, Tomahawk, T-Bone, etc.). Fantastic terrace with trees and vegetation!

Name: Rubaiyat Rio
Address: Rua Jardim Botânico 971, Rio de Janeiro, 22470-051, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Located in the Jockey Club Brasileiro within the boundaries of the city’s botanical gardens, this restaurant boasts breathtaking views where you can enjoy a meal on the terrace to a picture-postcard backdrop that features the horse-racing track as well as the statue of Christ the Redeemer. Inside, there is a large dining room with a counter that is home to the kitchen, where a large glass window provides views of the churrasco grill. Renowned for its array of premium meats and for managing its own production, the restaurant offers more than ten different cuts, although fish, seafood, rice and a variety of sides also feature on the menu. On Saturdays, don't miss the chance to try the traditional feijoada stew, made with prime cuts of meat, along with milkshakes and an incredible dessert buffet!

Name: Rubens
Description: This pretty restaurant owned by friendly hosts Cornelia Stolzer and Ruben Baumgart – she is Austrian and he is German-Austrian – is something of an Alpine hot spot. Accordingly, classics such as Backhendl (breaded fried chicken), Alt-Wiener Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) or Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake), as well as modern dishes feature on the menu. Charming, well-trained waitstaff and a decent selection of Austrian wines. Incidentally, the pumpkin seed oil comes from the proprietress's village.

Name: Rubino Kitchen
Address: Kelvedon Road, Inworth, CO5 9SP, United Kingdom
Description: A red-brick former pub provides the new home for this restaurant, which has long been a feature of the local dining scene. A large array of menus is available and the fixed price lunch is a steal. The experienced chef knows how to get the best out of his ingredients and dishes burst with flavour from the effective combinations. They even run regular cookery classes for kids.

Name: Ruby
Address: Yıldız Mahallesi, Ortaköy Salhanesi Sokak No:5, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34349, Türkiye
Description: With stunning views over the Bosphorus, a roof that can be fully opened when the weather is fine, and a terrace that turns into a DJs' playground at weekends: Ruby is one of the hot spots in Ortaköy. The menu comprises dishes for sharing, traditional Turkish fare and a tempting range of pasta and risotto options. And whether you opt for the penne puttanesca or the grilled sea bass with spinach and orzo in a cream sauce, rest assured that your meal will be indulgent and brimming with rich flavours.

Name: Ruca Malen
Address: Ruta Nacional 7 km. 1059, Bodega Ruca Malen, Mendoza, M5507, Argentina
Description: At the Ruca Malen winery, situated in Agrelo (in the department of Luján de Cuyo) just over half an hour to the south of Mendoza, guests can enjoy a dining experience that will live long in the memory. Its eponymous restaurant (the name comes from a Mapuche legend in which women walked with their heads bowed to avoid meeting the gaze of a handsome young god) is located on a beautiful estate with stunning views of the Andes mountains. The attentive staff encourage diners to sit back and relax and, if they wish, enjoy a glass of wine or freshly baked empanadas at the outdoor tables. The multi-course tasting menu balances creativity with accessibility and reflects the best of each season. Our recommendation? The grilled steak with potatoes, tomatoes and lettuce, a classic and comforting main course.

Name: Rudä
Address: Rua Garcia D'Ávila, 118, Rio de Janeiro, 22421-010, Brazil
Description: At Rudä, chef Danilo Parah champions what he calls “emotional and creative cuisine” in a contemporary bistro-style setting featuring different ambiences and a private room on the first floor. His dishes are colourful, generous and highly flavourful with little fear when it comes to combining lots of ingredients. It’s hard to beat the octopus with jambu fruit (a dish with a profusion of colours and textures that includes pasta cooked in a moqueca sauce) or the delicious cheesecake with an almond tuile, guava syrup and strawberry compote, all of which will linger long in the memory. The hospitality is on a par with the food, the latter presented on a varied à la carte that showcases local ingredients in addition to an “executive” menu.

Name: Rue Poh
Address: 8 Soi Srinagarindra 56, Nong Bon, Prawet, Bangkok, 10250, Thailand
Description: Open for over nine years, this family-run seafood restaurant has its roots in the Saen Sombun legacy. Fresh catch is cooked to order and sent out swiftly, in generous portions made for sharing. There are three dining areas, indoors and out, making it a good choice in Bang Na for families. Do not miss their signature stir-fry from a 50-year-old secret recipe – less sweet than many Chon Buri styles, it is prized for its aromas and balanced flavours.

Name: Rue Saint Marc
Address: 2103 San Marco Blvd., Jacksonville, FL, 32207, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted
Description: Located at the entrance to the historic San Marco Square in Jacksonville, this charming space featuring an open kitchen offers some of the best seasonal French-style cooking from husband and wife Scott and Gabrielle Alters. This dinner-only spot, having both à la carte and tasting menus, guarantees to satisfy with beautifully presented and skillfully cooked dishes. Start with the unagi tartlets, filled with a chilled koji "potato salad," topped with sweet glazed freshwater eel. Next, try the warm, savory gougères filled with black walnut béchamel. Outstanding main courses include Mediterranean sea bass, pan seared with fried mussels, matsutake mushrooms, grapes, gnocchi and a verjus vinaigrette. Complete your meal with the pleasing spiced apple crisp with vanilla ice cream and caramel drizzle.

Name: Rue de la Plume
Description: Everything about this inviting restaurant makes it clear that Luella and Madelene are passionate about what they do. Luella likes nothing better than to amaze her guests with her contemporary surprise menu. Her dishes revolve around a main ingredient of the finest quality, elaborate garnishes and velvety sauces that bring it all together. The wines recommended by Madelene complement the intense flavours beautifully. This duo's enthusiasm is infectious!

Name: Rueda Gaucha
