Lunch has its benefits too: The spring onion and goat gouda quiche is peerless, plus there’s a superb burger and a towering stack of French fries. All the while, sun beams through the skylight of a bistro that seems well on its way to becoming a neighborhood classic.

Name: Sails
Address: 103-113 Westhaven Drive, Saint Marys Bay, Auckland, 1011, New Zealand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list
Description: Now run by the third generation, this family business has been celebrated for its quality cooking and warm hospitality since 1991. Panoramic views of Westhaven Marina and Auckland Harbour Bridge are visual cues for the oceanic theme that permeates its menu. Regulars find comfort in the freshest seafood prepared consistently well by the kitchen. Be sure to check out the wine list: it includes some great Kiwi choices and rare vintages.

Name: Sain
Description: This restaurant is a café, canteen and grocery shop all in one, combining a relaxed atmosphere with respect for both the produce and the planet when it comes to the food: a stall for organic vegetables from the family farm in Guérande, a shelf of mostly natural wines (to take away) and laid-back service provided by Samuel Huitric. His brother Josselin cooks honest, delicious market-fresh fare that is on point, without beating around the bush: celeriac cream, duck gravlax and walnuts; hake, cauliflower and wild garlic.

Name: Saint Georges Premier
Description: Standing in the king’s old pheasant grounds in Monza’s picturesque park just a stone’s throw from the famous racetrack, this restaurant has a refined and elegant feel. Here, the menu features Mediterranean fish recipes alongside regionally inspired dishes such as the excellent Milanese-style chop with mashed potatoes and sweet-and-sour shallots, as well as the occasional French-influenced recipe in a nod to the history of the park itself. The restaurant comes into its own in summer, when its attractive terrace looking out at the lush surroundings adds to the appeal.

Name: Saint Julivert Fisherie
Description: This long-time neighborhood favorite comes courtesy of Chefs Alex Raij and Eder Montero, who also run next-door La Vara. The narrow space does not at all match the kitchen’s outsized talents and imaginative plates, which put seafood front and center. Consider starting with a plate of tempura-battered delicata squash with black garlic-infused labneh or golden-brown fried hamachi and shrimp boudin with Thai chili mayo before diving into the likes of Ibérico pork steak. Tamarind-glazed and grilled, it's served over a bed of coconut creamed spinach and okra and sided by a bowl of roasted potatoes with sauce choron.A generous selection of regional wines highlights small producers to match the cooking.

Name: Saint-Christophe
Description: Wholehearted and talented, virtuoso chef Olivier Dewulf has taken up abode in this handsome town house, which boasts a classical interior depicted by high ceilings, soft lighting and a delightful terrace. Saint Christophe is the epitome of character and sophistication. The menu reveals a classical bent, crafted indulgently and carefully and strewn in subtle creative notes. You may taste a velvety foie gras laced with cognac, or melt-in-the-mouth cod enhanced by a beurre blanc to die for. We heartily recommend the establishment’s signature set menu.

Name: Saint-Malo
Description: As its name suggests, this modern bistro deluxe brings a little bit of France to Vilnius. The large rear terrace is the place to be in warmer weather, but the interior is just as appealing with its sleek, clean-lined style, large vases, oversized wooden figurines and monochrome prints. The menu draws its influences from the north to the south, and the roll-call of Gallic classics is sure to make any Francophile happy. Seafood leads the way, with the likes of bouillabaisse and lobster, but you’ll also find galettes, entrecôte de bœuf and crêpes Suzette. The superb all-French wine list boasts over 400 bins.

Name: Saison
Description: In Dijon's Antiquaires neighbourhood, this French-Italian restaurant welcomes diners in a pleasant space decorated in a palette of light colours. Milanese chef Riccardo Maiello, who trained in MICHELIN-starred establishments, is at the helm: he delights diners with modern cuisine that alternates French recipes with nods to local produce, such as a starter of slow-cooked egg, broad beans from nearby Arc-sur-Tille, shiitake, emulsion with garlic and farmhouse Cancoillotte cheese, and 100% Italian dishes, eg al dente paccheri alla carbonara, home-made pasta straight from Italy made with Pecorino and guanciale.

Name: Saison
Description: This converted pub has retained its unpolished, pared-down decor in a space that has lots of character and a long counter. Local produce takes centre stage on the menu: rainbow trout, creamy white wine sauce, celery and Granny Smith apple; beef fillet with a gastrique and fried shallots... Attentive staff, rock music and a fine selection of cocktails, plus a wine list showcasing exclusively Quebec picks, curated by an enthusiastic sommelier. Book for one of two sittings. N.B. Tips are included.

Name: Saisons - Cave à Manger
Address: 2 place Massenet, à La Madeleine, Lille, 59110, France
Description: Antoine Dacquin and Pierre Bleuzé, Lille-born chefs and partners here, first became friends in the kitchens at Bloempot, Florent Layden's restaurant. During service, one of the pair oversees the restaurant floor, the other cooks. Through their surprise menus, at lunchtime and in the evening, they are making waves with dishes cooked up using quality farm produce – seasonal, of course! Roasted aubergine, rouille sauce, samphire and bouillabaisse broth; confit cod, roasted leeks, Swiss chard, marjoram béarnaise: a meal replete with indulgence and joy.

Name: Sait
Address: Yalıkavak Marina, Çökertme Caddesi No:2 D:06 Blok, Yalıkavak, Bodrum, 48990, Türkiye
Description: The luxury yachts and chic boutiques may call to mind Saint Tropez, but you are in fact sitting on a terrace on Yalikavak's marina. The restaurant's maritime decor leaves no doubt that fish and seafood are the speciality of the house. The day's catch is displayed on ice, and you are handed an extensive menu of irresistible options. Begin, for example, with dolmas filled with aromatic rice and meat, then move on to the prawn ceviche infused with orange, lime and dill. Each plate bursts with colour, fragrance and generous flavours. Home cooking is at the heart of this family-run place – and the key to its success.

Name: Saiti
Description: An attractive restaurant with a bistro ambience and rustic-contemporary decor. On its menus (L'Eixample, Na Germana and Lo Rat Penat), all of which are available with a wine pairing, chef Vicente Patiño takes us on a gastronomic journey via Mediterranean cooking that is rooted in tradition but approached from a more modern perspective. Dishes on the menu here range from the local “all I pebre” of white prawns and cacao, to blue crab, and signature dishes such as the celery meringue.

Name: Saittavini
Description: Combining a bistro, wine bar and delicatessen, this friendly restaurant serves Italian food (including a lovely small antipasto counter). They also sell over a 1 000 different wines in the wine shop and a range of Italian specialities in the delicatessen.

Name: Saka
Address: 7, Alley 9, Zhongshan Road, Daya District, Taichung, Taiwan
Description: This quaint shop with over 40 years of history stands at the end of a winding alley. The second generation of the family prides itself on its signature dish – chicken braised in rice wine with Chinese herbs. No water is added and the broth bursts with deep umami. The chicken tastes especially good after being dipped in chilli soy sauce and ground pepper. For a complete meal, pair with blanched noodles to soak up the broth.

Name: Sakaimachi Kamokura
Description: The menu is written in the husband’s own hand, in light, supple brush strokes. Flavours of the season are prepared as you like them—grilled, steamed or deep-fried. Simmered dishes are his forte, with time taken to craft seasonal flavours in creations such as bamboo shoots with wakame, summer daikon, ebi-imo taro, and kaburamushi, steamed fish topped with grated turnip. ‘Kamokura’ is an amalgam of the couple’s family names; they welcome you together, offering a two-part harmony of service.

Name: Saketokoro Tanaka
Description: The seafood-focused menu traces the path the chef has taken. He once worked at a fishmonger's to learn the nature of fish and now gets his seafood from that same shop. The meal begins with a soup and tsukuri, after which guests may add dishes to their liking. Octopus is served simmered in a sweet soy-based broth or as karaage, while tilefish is prepared as agedashi or matsukasa-yaki, each prepared in the style best suited to the fish. Items like tekka-maki or squid ink yakisoba bring the meal to a close, allowing guests to enjoy seafood to the very end.

Name: Sakeya
Address: Via Cesare Da Sesto 1, Milan, 20123, Italy
Description: A Kyoto-born chef, a yakitori grill on full display from the entrance, and pared-back interiors evoking Japanese bistros: the tone is set before you sit down. One wall is devoted entirely to sake – over 150 labels, with new arrivals each week. The kitchen takes an unmistakably Eastern approach in both ingredients and technique, ranging from creative forays such as Gindara 2.0, cod with ginger and yuzu, to classics such as wagyu fillet, cooked tableside over charcoal by the guest. The true specialty, however, remains the kushiyaki: skewers of various cuts grilled over the open flame near the entrance. Service is gracious and well-prepared; let the sommelier guide you through the list, he’s always eager to share the stories and craft behind each sake.

Name: Saklı Konak Cappadocia
Address: Tekelli Mahallesi, 2. Karlık Sokak No:3, Uçhisar, Nevşehir, 50000, Türkiye
Description: Located just outside Nevşehir's tourist hub, this convivial and inviting restaurant is the perfect place to take a break and delve into the region's cuisine. They take pride here in their testi kebabs and unique versions of kofta, but be sure to sample the manti, too – made with grilled aubergine, butter and tomato sauce, and topped with a yoghurt dressing and a sprinkling of dried herbs, they are simply divine! The combination of local produce and traditional recipes ensures that each dish is a joy. Consider extending your experience with a stay in one of the guestrooms.

Name: Saku Restaurant
Description: Saku is the nickname of the chef of this establishment tucked away behind a nondescript façade. He and his wife, both of whom are Japanese, prepare jubilant Gallic cuisine in keeping with today’s tastebuds. The produce is fresh, the dishes are meticulously prepared, at common-sense prices, and the service is friendly; an enjoyable experience.

Name: Sakuragi
Description: The ‘counter kappo’ format was adopted to serve food as fresh as possible from the kitchen. Dried bonito is shaved and dashi is made for the soup right before your eyes. Fish is char-grilled and roasted on straw. Keeping a watchful eye over his kitchen, the chef serves each dish at just the right temperature and with an alluring aroma. Fresh-cooked rice can be savoured topped with raw egg or seasoned minced chicken. Though presentations range widely, each one conveys a desire to satisfy and delight guests.

Name: Sal Gastronomia
Address: Rua Bela Cintra 1958, São Paulo, 01415-006, Brazil
Description: There are very few Brazilians who are not familiar with chef Henrique Fogaça, who is extremely popular thanks to his role as a judge on MasterChef as well being the lead singer for the hardcore band Oitão. Behind Sal Gastronomia’s unique pirate-inspired logo (a skull with a knife and fork) is a contemporary-style restaurant featuring industrial decorative decor, which provides the backdrop for modern Brazilian cuisine on an à la carte and two tasting menus. The sort of dishes you’ll find here include scallops with a chestnut cream and pupunha heart of palm; fish of the day with a plantain moqueca stew; and beef ribs with cassava purée, watercress pesto and cheese curd.

Name: Sala
Address: L.V. Locsin Building, Podium Level, 6752 Ayala Avenue, Makati - Metro Manila, 1223, The Philippines
Description: Opened in 1997 by Scottish-born chef Colin Mackay, this intimate restaurant continues to charm with linen tablecloths and chic, understated decor. The concise modern European menu includes two set courses, with your chosen main determining the final price. French techniques underpin dishes that showcase classic refined flavours, allowing premium ingredients to shine. This quietly confident spot proves that timelessness and quality never go out of style.

Name: Sala of Tokyo
Description: Classic Japanese cuisine made from top-notch ingredients is the name of the game here. The sushi and sashimi, tempura, and robata grill specialities, as well as the sukiyaki and shabu shabu stews all come highly recommended. Another draw of this place is its inviting interior, which is sleek and simple, yet cosy at the same time. You can watch the sushi master at work at a small counter.

Name: Salabka
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: On the outskirts of the city, this restaurant is located in a vineyard with a wine-growing tradition dating back to the 13C. A combination of exposed old wooden beams, quarry stone walls and sleek modern furnishings creates an atmospheric setting. The view of the vines is best enjoyed from the tables at the windows on the first floor, which is actually a gallery constructed under the open gable roof. In summer, tables on the terrace are coveted. Chef Petr Kunc presents an ambitious three- to six-course tasting menu - a vegetarian version is also available. Dishes such as ‘Beluga sturgeon, beluga caviar, stuffed morels, herb purée, pommes soufflées, Vin Jaune sabayon’ are meticulously prepared with great technical precision - they are visually stunning and feature very good produce. The menu is accompanied by a wine pairing or a non-alcoholic alternative. Tip: Book a wine tasting or tour of the estate. For overnight stays there are six cosy, tastefully furnished apartments.

Name: Salamensa
Address: via Monsignor Oscar Romero 69, Montichiari, 25018, Italy
Description: A multi-function open space, with a bar for breakfasts and a classic restaurant serving pizzas made from naturally fermented dough. Although the ambience is modern, friendly and minimalist, the attention paid to the choice of ingredients and preparation of dishes is of the highest quality.

Name: Sale
Address: Via dell'Amore 23, Licinella-Torre di Paestum, 84047, Italy
Description: Housed within the Sogaris hotel, this restaurant boasts a spacious glass-fronted dining room overlooking a garden with swimming pool and furnished in a contemporary style that gives it an elegant yet relaxed look. The cuisine focuses on fish and seafood served in regional recipes reinterpreted with a light, modern touch. Don’t miss the daily raw seafood specials which are listed separately on the menu.

Name: Sale Grosso
Description: This restaurant describes its cuisine as Mediterranean and it’s true that fish and seafood dominate the menu. However, other dishes also feature and during our visit we particularly enjoyed the carefully prepared fried artichoke heart accompanied by a fresh white Tuscan Montecarlo wine. Friendly, informal service in a simple dining room with a distinctive bistro feel.

Name: SaleGrosso
Address: piazza della Vittoria 14, Marciana Marina, 57033, Italy
Description: On the waterfront of Marciana Marina, just steps from Il Cotone, the old fishing village, the setting itself suggests a cuisine focused mainly on the sea, combining fish traditions with a few creative offerings. Dishes are of excellent quality, making this one of the island’s best restaurants.

Name: SaleGrosso
Address: viale II Giugno 15, Milano Marittima, 48015, Italy
Description: One of the town’s authentic favourites, this fish restaurant has a pleasant, light - coloured decor inspired by the sea. The eclectic cuisine includes tapas and raw fish dishes.

Name: Salicornia
Description: A bright and airy restaurant situated slightly away from the centre, where a couple of well-established professionals (Jan front of house and Vjekoslav in the kitchen) serve fresh fish and seafood dishes sourced daily from the fish market. The menu features colourful, generously portioned dishes accompanied by a wine list which focuses on Slovenia, yet also includes labels from Italy, Croatia and France (with champagne from the latter).

Name: Salitre
Address: Paseo Marítimo Alcalde Francisco Vázquez 25, A Coruña, 15002, Spain
Description: In this bright restaurant, which stands out for its huge windows overlooking the Paseo Marítimo and the mouth of the estuary, the menu is built around magnificent Galician ingredients, with an emphasis on traditional flavours and à la carte dishes. The dish we liked best was the sea bass seasoned with citrus and herbs, although one of their rice dishes or famous fish stews go down a treat as well.

Name: Salle Climatisée
Description: With only about 20 spots, this bistro installed in Little Italy is nothing if not convivial. Its atypical and somewhat surreal name—meaning "air-conditioned room"—is a nod to French signage and a reflection of its distinctive character. Brendan, the charming owner, creates a happy and laid-back atmosphere. The menu, presented on a slate board, changes with the seasons. It generally comprises a choice of seven mains and two desserts, all of them delicious (consider the chicken with clams and beans, or cabbage with browned butter and goat's cheese). From the seats at the bar, facing the kitchen, you get a prime view of these rustic and indulgent dishes being prepared.

Name: Salmen
Description: A delightful place with a lively atmosphere! This elegant 19C townhouse opposite the Church of St Martin houses a charming brasserie with decorative details such as old photos, a striking chandelier and attractive parquet flooring. There is also a heritage-protected dining room with stuccoed ceilings. Chef-patron Daniel Bitterli cooks classic, traditional dishes that take their cue from the seasons and draw on Mediterranean influences. Dishes such as the sole fillets with two kinds of asparagus and hollandaise sauce exemplify the restaurant's commitment to fresh, high-quality ingredients and flavoursome cuisine. The waitstaff are very attentive, friendly and adept.

Name: Salon 1905
Description: Located on the first floor of the grandiose 19C Geozavod edifice, this opulent, aristocratic restaurant occupies one of Belgrade’s most eye-catching, iconic landmarks, whose marble, stucco, brass and gilt decor creates a glitzy special occasion vibe. In this sumptuous setting, the young chef crafts a high-flying culinary repertory, depicted by consummate execution and exquisite plating. The goal is to highlight top-drawer Serbian produce and thoroughbred recipes, all of which viewed through a contemporary lens. There is no à la carte menu; instead, guests are invited to enjoy a surprise tasting menu, with the only choice being the number of courses.

Name: Salpoente
Address: Cais de São Roque 83, Aveiro, 3800-256, Portugal
Description: Its wooden construction and reddish hue show that it once operated as one of the many salt warehouses facing the São Roque canal (the only one that still preserves its essence today). This setting, not without sophistication, offers a cuisine based on Portuguese gastronomy, incorporating ingredients from the estuary, presented in a modern format with signature touches. Among them, the smoked eel stands out, served with fresh notes and beetroot emulsion, the sea fish accompanied by bivalves from the estuary, and the classic Portuguese style egg nog presented in various textures. The menu features à la carte choices, a 6-course tasting menu, a vegetarian menu, and the “Nas mãos do chef” (“Chef’s Choice”), as well as an executive menu for weekdays!

Name: Salsedine367
Address: Via Marradi 11, Lido di Savio, 48125, Italy
Description: Meals are served outdoors at this beach restaurant, which is also a private beach club. Here, the cuisine focuses on imaginative and personalised dishes that stand out for their excellent ingredients, among other things! The “blind” tasting menu is based around the chef’s inspiration, while the varied à la carte offers dishes with generous portions.

Name: Salt
Address: The Ritz-Carlton, Amelia Island, 4750 Amelia Island Pkwy., Amelia Island, FL, 32034, USA
Description: Nestled inside the plush Ritz-Carlton on Amelia Island and blessed with a wall of windows fronting the Atlantic Ocean, Salt could coast on looks alone. It doesn't. A measured tasting menu is the best way to see how this contemporary kitchen threads European and Asian influences to deliver a broadly appealing menu that includes tuna tartare in a dashi emulsion, butter-baked halibut with a tableside pour of saffron tomato consommé, and wagyu ribeye cap finished with truffle hollandaise. An ace service team keeps close watch, ever sincere in their interactions and keen to remember the many diners who frequent this destination regularly. An early dinner time guarantees prime sunset views.

Name: Salt & Silver
Description: "Wanderlust cuisine" is the theme at this St Pauli restaurant with views of the Elbe. Diners choose from a regularly changing à la carte menu that features dishes that draw on seasonal and regional ingredients, Mediterranean influences and international twists. Examples include "shiitake wonton, enoki, dashi, Szechuan oil" or "butterflied Arctic char, salsa verde, new potatoes". There is also a surprise menu for sharing and a carefully curated wine list. The pleasingly relaxed atmosphere is enhanced by polished and highly professional service, which is provided by a cheerfully charming and laid-back front-of-house team.

Name: Salt & Silver am Meer
Address: Zum Böhler Strand, Sankt Peter-Ording, 25826, Germany
Description: This restaurant is housed in an 8m-high building on stilts right by the beach, within spitting distance of the sea – an impressive location in which to enjoy fresh cuisine featuring produce from the region. At this "Fish Grill & Beach Bar", the tempting menu includes dishes such as grilled turbot and "fish fingers royal". Good to know: The chicken nuggets on the children's menu are made from regional organic poultry. Wine connoisseurs are bound to find something to their liking on the well-selected wine list. The atmosphere is nice and lively both inside and out on the fabulous terrace. Another Salt & Silver in addition to the two Hamburg restaurants. During the high season and on weekends, be sure to make a reservation. Tip: Park behind the dunes and enjoy the lovely 15min walk to the restaurant.

Name: Salt Road
Address: Andaz Doha Hotel, 23 Diplomatic Street, Zone 61, West Bay, Doha, Qatar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: As the name suggests, the owners hail from South Africa as does the cuisine of their restaurant located in the Andaz Doha hotel. The space has shelves stacked with salt from around the world, as it’s used for curing and pickling, which is how they used to preserve food back in the day. The menu has a variety of sharing options – the 5 cured brisket is delicious as are the Josper roasted mushrooms – but the steaks are particularly notable here. If you’re unsure what to order, the well-informed team’s advice is a good guide. Try some of their South African wines, offered by the glass or bottle.

Name: Salt Smokehouse
Address: 1300 Meridian St., D-104, Huntsville, AL, 35801, USA
Description: In the sparkling Lincoln Mill district, this family-owned barbecue spot is out to satisfy. High ceilings, white walls and ample seating make for a Spartan vibe. The menu, by contrast, is full of personality, as it pulls global inspiration from all over, starting with a roster of hearty appetizers like brisket fritters with chihuahua cheese or fried soft-shell crab bao sliders. Sandwiches and burgers also tempt, but for the purists among us, stick with the fundamentals. A fatty slice of prime-grade smoked brisket cooked overnight cuts like custard and doesn’t need a lick of sauce. Soft, tender pulled pork is another winning order, along with creative sides like ginger serrano coleslaw or fried Brussel sprouts with hot honey and yuzu.

Name: Salta
Address: Rua Rodrigo da Fonseca 82A, Lisbon, 1250-193, Portugal
Description: A few minutes from Praça Marquês de Pombal, you’ll find Salta, a restaurant that blends Asian cuisine with Central American flavours in an informal setting. Spread across three areas decorated in dark tones, the main floor looks onto the kitchen and a counter where creative cocktails are served. At the stoves is chef Tomaz Salema Reis who, after extensive international experience, returned to his homeland to showcase the flavours and techniques he picked up in the kitchens he passed through. Packed with bold, well-balanced flavours, the menu offers à la carte dishes to share, or three tasting menus: Vegan Experience, Chef’s Experience and Chef’s Experience “+”. One not to miss? The Soft shell crab Taco, combining the sweetness of pineapple chutney with the gently spicy kick of gochujang mayonnaise.

Name: Salto!
Description: At this hip urban bistro, ingredient quality is paramount. As far as chef Duys is concerned, that goes as much for the Brussels sprouts as for the sea bass. He is also not averse to working with traditionally overlooked produce, such as pig's head. Whether he is rustling up a vegetable dish based on winter leeks, or pan-searing pheasant to be paired with a fine champagne sauce: generosity is key. His creations are not unnecessarily complicated, but they are brimming with flavour. Diners can also look forward to an expertly curated selection of wines and beers.

Name: Salty Monk
Address: Church Street, Sidford, EX10 9QP, United Kingdom
Description: Set in an old 16th-century salt house, this long-standing, proudly run restaurant is a pleasant blend of the old and the new – and is the type of place that’s always evolving. Dine in either the Abbots Den or the Garden Room, and start with a small plates selection, followed by a hearty, classically based main course that will come with minimal fuss but plenty of flavour. Alternatively, just come down for a spot of afternoon tea. If you're looking to explore the area, then extend your visit by booking one of the bedrooms.

Name: Salty Seafood Restaurant
Description: As the name of their restaurant implies, chef Nino and hostess Aysen are dedicated to serving up fish and seafood in their charming restaurant, which feels like an upgraded fisherman's hut. Their principal supplier is sustainable fisherman Hendrik Kramer from Urk, whose catch largely dictates the menu, which also features vegetables from their own garden. Their emphasis on local sourcing yields ingredients of remarkable quality. The chef knows how to build depth into his sauces, and his accompaniments reveal a fondness for intricate preparation. Whether he is transforming fish trimmings into an outstanding fish soup or dry-ageing sea bream before pairing it with a warm bisque emulsion, his cooking is delicate and pays fitting tribute to its surroundings. Do bear in mind that à la carte dining is only possible at lunchtime; a set menu is served in the evenings.

Name: Salutation Inn
Address: 68 Fore Street, Topsham, EX3 0HL, United Kingdom
Description: This characterful 1720s coaching inn has a surprisingly contemporary interior, which is matched by its understated bedrooms. Take your seat in either the intimate dining room or in the airy, glass-covered historic courtyard – the perfect spot for a sunny afternoon. In the evening, choose between a tasting menu and a seasonally themed à la carte, where the colourful modern dishes are well-judged and nicely balanced, such as a deconstructed take on rhubarb cheesecake. Be sure to pick up some goodies from their deli and wet fish shop on your way out.

Name: Salvo
Description: Situated opposite the Villa Comunale gardens, this restaurant serves some of the best pizzas in Naples (classic Neapolitan-style pizza which is soft and so big that it spills over the plate) as well as a selection of delicious appetisers, such as superb pasta fritters with various toppings. Welcoming ambience, with a more elegant feel than that of a typical pizzeria.

Name: Salvo Cacciatori
Description: Since 1906, when distant forebears established a simple osteria with wine counter, this establishment has travelled a remarkable path. Today it presents itself as a welcoming and well-appointed restaurant, distinguished by elegant and contemporary furnishings. The cooking offers an à la carte selection of fish and meat dishes, complemented by tasting menus that allow guests to place themselves entirely in the hands of the chef. The well-structured wine list encompasses not only Ligurian labels but also selections from other regions. The terrace overlooking the pedestrian thoroughfare is most pleasant, and should be reserved well in advance.

Name: Salão Nobre
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Valet parking
Description: It is located in the luxurious Vidago Palace hotel, built in 1910 by King Carlos due to its proximity to the famous Vidago thermal spring waters. It is no surprise that the restaurant boasts a majestic décor, with high ceilings and a huge handmade carpet covering the floor that once served as the palace’s ballroom. Consultant chef Vítor Matos provides traditional Northern Portuguese cuisine combined with modern creativity, showcased in an à la carte menu and two tasting menus: Essência (“Essence”) and Cumplicidades (“Alliances”). Standout dishes? The scallops accompanied by prawn ravioli and a delicate beurre blanc sauce, the sea bass with scarlet prawn served with roasted cauliflower cream, and the moist apple cake, drizzled with cinnamon chutney, nestled inside crispy puff pastry.

Name: Salón Mezcalli
Address: C. 8 Sur 501, Barrio de Analco, Heróica Puebla de Zaragoza, 72505, Mexico
Description: Everything you need to know about this restaurant is in the name. Boasting one of the largest mezcal collections in the region, this bright salon puts its bottles front and center at the bar and offers a multitude of flights and finely mixed cocktails. The kitchen, meanwhile, works in traditional flavors. Chile en nogada is a seasonal highlight, along with neatly stacked chalupas smeared in delicate salsas and hearty enchiladas covered in flavorful, classic moles like monchamantelas, pipian verde and poblano. For dessert, the local specialty, cremita poblana, arrives dusted in cinnamon powder and dotted with peppermint leaves for an herby twist.

Name: Sam's Riverside
Address: 1 Crisp Walk, Hammersmith, London, W6 9DN, United Kingdom
Description: Experienced restaurateur Sam Harrison is behind this modern riverside brasserie beside Hammersmith Bridge. It's an enduringly popular place and you can see why from the appealing, pleasingly varied menu that might incorporate a range of influences but doesn't lose sight of the flavour gained by using quality produce. British ingredients from land and sea are cooked with precision and there's a whole section of the menu for oysters and other shellfish. Stock up on provisions at Sam’s Larder before you leave.

Name: Sambal
Description: Located on a buzzy, vibrant street, Sambal serves a tantalising mix of Asian and European flavours. There’s a unique twist to the beloved Lap Mei Fun, with fragrant rice, Chinese sausage, char siew (honey BBQ pork) and crispy pork lard. The Udang Entangled claypot boasts a rich, creamy broth infused with Chinese wine, served with glass noodles and succulent prawns. The standout dessert is taro purée, a modern adaption of creamy Teochew yam.

Name: Sammarco
Address: 4 Front St. E., Toronto, M5E 1G4, Canada
Description: Gold accents, marble finishes and a dining room that is at once luxurious and welcoming—this sleek spot in St. Lawrence has all of the polish one would expect of a modern Italian steakhouse (with prices to match). Just like the setting, which marries traditional inspiration with contemporary flair, the dishes reflect a blend of old and new. Grilled calamari with burnt orange and pangrattato is at once simple and refined. Main dishes, whether the 24-ounce contrafiletto or the Nova Scotia lobster finished with a vermouth and tarragon butter, are impressive. Finally, torta di cioccolato with dark chocolate ganache in an espresso crème anglaise is decadence defined.

Name: Samouraï
Description: Samouraï has been a culinary landmark of Brussels since 1974. Since moving to Avenue Louise, the uncluttered interior sports three dining areas adorned in Asian art, a large bonsai and a pastel terracotta colour scheme. Razor-sharp precision and rich flavours embody the authentic Japanese fare, depicted by a varied menu of sushi and sashimi, together with tableside preparations like sukiyaki. The chef crafts gyoza, which can be crispy or velvety, with a fork-tender prawn stuffing, home-made dashi and a scattering of sweet-sour sides to further underscore the subtle flavours. Popular lunchtime bento boxes; set menus in the evening as well as an à la carte lineup.

Name: Sampa
Address: 67 Warwick Street, Manchester, M1 1EH, United Kingdom
Description: In Manchester’s artsy Northern Quarter, Sampa is quite literally hidden away, with the exact address of this 12-seater chef’s counter only provided to guests 24 hours prior to dining, and a sign hung outside the door just 20 minutes before service. This sense of intrigue is fitting for an immersive experience where Chef Caroline Martins hosts her guests in a gregarious manner and treats them to a surprise menu of Brazilian cuisine. From the traditional ‘pão de queijo’ cheese bread to the showstopping ‘Dormouse’ dessert, these are fun, flavourful dishes packed with personality.

Name: Samphire
Address: 7-11 Don Street, Saint Helier, JE2 4TQ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This buzzy all-day brasserie deluxe has a striking colour scheme which takes in blue velour banquettes and yellow leather chairs. Cooking adopts a modern approach and there’s a distinct Mediterranean influence. Island ingredients are to the fore and the oysters are something of a feature.

Name: Samut
Address: 14/119 Mu 1, Rawai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83100, Thailand
Description: (The restaurant is temporarily closed.) Samut (or ocean) is set in a traditional Thai-Chinese building decorated in an Oriental style, with dark teak wood. Previously the lobby of the adjacent hotel, it’s now a gastronomic destination. The set menu, with more than 10 dishes, tours the island’s coastline, offering seafood caught by local fishermen. The chef respects the traditions of the island, selecting flavours and fruits inspired by local creativity, including a reinterpretation of Phuket dim sum.

Name: Samwon Garden
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: For several decades, Samwon Garden has transformed Korean barbecue culture and enjoyed a reputation for its intricate balance between comfort and haute cuisine. Diverse cuts of prime Korean beef meet the staff’s seasoned grilling skills, creating a delightful gastronomic experience. What's more, a gorgeously landscaped outdoor garden, coupled with high ceilings and glass walls infused with the Korean aesthetics, adds a feeling of spaciousness. Visit this culinary landmark and enjoy a meal loaded with great flavours.

Name: San Baylon
Description: Just a short distance from Piazza del Popolo, within the elegant Palazzo Ripetta, San Baylon presents itself as a refined yet informal venue, perfectly at ease in the heart of Rome. The spaces marry the architectural charm of the historic building with a contemporary and measured atmosphere, giving rise to surroundings that are welcoming and equally suited to an unhurried lunch or a more elegant dinner. In the warmer months, service extends to the delightful internal garden, a kind of secluded green retreat that adds a note of tranquillity to the experience. The cooking is distinguished by precision and balance, with careful attention to seasonality and the selection of ingredients. It is the produce itself, of evident quality, that occupies centre stage, drawn out by a modern and restrained approach that keeps the flavours clean, recognisable and direct. Technique, never worn on its sleeve, and a measured creativity lend the dishes both finesse and coherence, giving shape to a style that is elegant and immediately legible. The service, attentive and discreet, accompanies the meal with natural and unhurried rhythm.

Name: San Daniele
Description: San Daniele, now housed in a stylish cottage on the village square of Sint-Martens-Bodegem, has been delivering fine food for many a year. The interior combines a spacious impression with unpretentious elegance, without forgetting an exquisite terrace for fine weather. Chef Spinelli continues to uphold the house hallmark: Italian authenticity, outstanding produce and heartwarming portions. An example: al dente squid ink ravioli stuffed with lobster and courgette, melded with a parmesan sauce and a rich unctuous bisque. The crusted seabass is filleted tableside and the handsome wine list is a treasure trove of enticing gems. The quintessence of a feel-good establishment.

Name: San Domenico
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Perched high on the tufa cliffs overlooking the Costa degli Dei, this contemporary-style restaurant boasts superb views from its dining room and especially from its panoramic summer terrace. The cuisine served by the young owner-chef is as modern as the setting – dishes are light and almost exclusively focused on local fish.

Name: San Fen Su Chi
Address: 8, Lane 49, Guoguang Road, Yonghe District, New Taipei, Taiwan
Description: This long-standing joint used to be a speakeasy-style establishment. Now the room is decorated with ink paintings and calligraphy against a soundtrack of classical music. The concise menu is mostly Jiangzhe in origin, focusing on natural, fuss-free flavours. Local emerald chillies are stuffed with ground pork, deep-fried and dressed in a sweet sauce. Well-layered flavours make them the perfect companion to steamed rice.

Name: San Genesio
Address: Via Francesco Viano 1, San Genesio, 10090, Italy
Description: Commanding a dominant position in the heart of this small hamlet, this historic restaurant — lovingly maintained through the years — has found renewed vigour since 2017 under a passionate and accomplished stewardship (here, fittingly, sommelier Simone’s christening was once celebrated). From the dining room and expansive terrace, one’s gaze sweeps across the surrounding landscape, and on the clearest days the vista extends even further, offering a panorama of considerable enchantment.The kitchen remains faithful to tradition, yet interpreted with contemporary freshness in its presentations and through certain pairings that lend character to the offering. The wine list, too, is of excellent calibre, intelligently structured and rich in both breadth and depth, spanning Piedmont, Italy and beyond.

Name: San Huberto
Description: A restaurant-asador with a classic feel where you can enjoy meticulously prepared traditional cuisine. It features a pleasant summer terrace, bar space (note the impressive glass-fronted bodega and fresh fish and seafood display counter) and dining room. The à la carte, which specialises in dishes roasted in a wood-fired oven (baby lamb, Castillian-style suckling pig etc), also features enticing starters, stews and superb fish (including Cantabrian hake, “estuary” sea bass, and red tuna tataki).

Name: San Laurel
Address: Conrad Los Angeles, 100 S. Grand Ave., Los Angeles, CA, 90012, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: San Laurel is at the top of its game—quite literally, since this tenth-floor dazzler affords unobstructed views of Walt Disney Concert Hall from its polished perch. With soothing earth tones, lush greenery, a bustling bar and a breezy vibe courtesy of a fully opened facade, it looks and feels like an urban oasis. Expect modern Californian dishes with Spanish leanings from a talented team put together by visionary chef, José Andrés. A tartare turns tradition on its head when "beefsteak" is actually tomatoes in a perfect disc, topped with a "yolk" made of gelatinous tomato water. A rack of lamb, cut into four, is plated around a circle of red mole sauce and a half baby eggplant, roasted and topped with pea tendrils and puffed rice. Desserts really shine, as in an ethereal pistachio cake with fragrant lime zest and sweet strawberries matched by a tart mascarpone sorbet.

Name: San Lorenzo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated within the Clitunno hotel, this well-managed family-run restaurant serves classic, seasonal meat and fish dishes, including generous portions of black truffles in some dishes. Recently refurbished, the intimate, elegant dining room also occasionally features live music at weekends, while the outdoor terrace on the small square offers pleasant alfresco dining. Guests are advised to park outside the ZTL (restricted traffic zone) and make their way on foot, via a short walk through the beautiful historic centre.

Name: San Lorenzo
Description: Chef Massimo Fabbri, who long ruled the kitchen at DC’s beloved Tosca, has traded in those white tablecloths for this neighborhood charmer, named after his son (Lorenzo is the “patron saint of cooks”). Photos of the chef's Tuscan hometown adorn the exposed brick walls and painted tiles line the floor, hinting at the delicious regional specialties that await.A dinner in this chef's hands might begin with tender squash blossoms stuffed with truffled goat cheese and fried to perfection. Pasta is a must: try crown-shaped tortelli with robiola and black truffle, pooled in a porcini mushroom sauce; or splurge on the parmesan risotto, dusted with freshly shaved white truffles. Maple panna cotta with caramelized apples and oat streusel is a refreshing finale.

Name: San Mamés Jatetxea
Description: A restaurant with a unique location inside the Los Leones football stadium, which makes it the perfect way to end a visit to the Tour San Mamés and its beautiful museum as you can enjoy your meal overlooking the pitch. The cuisine focuses on traditional Basque recipes, with some dishes to share and three tempting set menus (Especial, Gastronomía Vasca, and Degustación). On match days, the restaurant also serves guests in the VIP section of the stadium.

Name: San Marco
Description: This long-established restaurant in the Asti region has been open for over 70 years and is still renowned for its regional cuisine served in a classic-style dining room. Dishes include cardoons with Raschera cheese fondue, the famous agnolottini del plin (a type of ravioli), and the Piedmontese bunet which is part of a trio of desserts that includes hazelnut tart and zabaglione with Canelli muscat wine.

Name: San Martino 26
Address: Via San Martino 26, San Gimignano, 53037, Italy
Description: Occupying the wine cellars of an old palazzo in the historic centre, this restaurant has a fashionable feel with just a few tables and a selection of contemporary - style dishes inspired by classic recipes (from Tuscany and elsewhere) on the menu.

Name: San Michele
Address: via Castello di Fagagna 33, Fagagna, 33034, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated next to the ruins of the old castle and the small church of San Michele, this 13C building, thought to have once housed a guardroom, is now home to a small restaurant serving regional, seasonal cuisine with a modern twist. During the week, the restaurant offers a lunchtime menu of top-quality snacks (the Venetian “cicchetti”), as well as a few “primi” and desserts.

Name: San Quintino Resort
Description: Once you have crossed the plain and climbed up into the San Quintino hills, you come to this restored farmhouse surrounded by an attractive garden. The restaurant is divided into a brick - walled dining room and a winter garden, while the charming guestrooms make this a romantic place to stay. Creative dishes with a focus on local ingredients and a few fish specialities feature on the menu.

Name: San Remo
Description: Behind its simple, somewhat old-fashioned façade lies a restaurant that lives and breathes gastronomy with a heated passion. Chef Alberto Villegas, who after studying at the Basque Culinary Centre took over the family business where he grew up, wants the restaurant to be seen today as ‘a haven for the senses’. He focuses on seasonal produce, offering a contemporary menu with dishes such as smoked eel with salsa verde and Palencia peas, red prawns and bisque made from their heads, and, for dessert, the surprising ricotta and mascarpone flan.

Name: San Rocco
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: In a typical Istrian village a few kilometres from the sea, this hotel restaurant with a romantic atmosphere occupies an elegant stone building, run with passion by the Fernetich family. The dining room, with stone walls and wooden ceiling, is elegant and full of character, while in the summertime the outdoor terrace is an option. The owners have entrusted the kitchen to chef Floriana Ružić, discovered and mentored by them, who navigates a modern cuisine crafted from seasonal and territorial produce. Hers is a contemporary telling of the flavours of Istria, from the hinterland to the sea. Alongside the house-baked bread, a tasting of their four extra-virgin olive oils, of excellent quality, is naturally offered.

Name: San Shu Gong
Description: The owner named the restaurant after her late father and serves Cantonese and Teochew cuisines – her father's favourites. The two chefs, each with over 30 years of professional experience, excel at seafood dishes that accentuate the natural umami of seasonal produce. Some specialities have to be pre-ordered, such as the steamed and chilled fourfinger threadfin with tender flesh and generous fish oil.

Name: San Tommaso 10
Description: It was here, in 1895, that Luigi Lavazza opened a grocer’s shop and immediately began blending coffee. Today, the same establishment is home to a modern restaurant serving excellent cuisine, led by a chef from Le Marche who offers one of the city’s most convincing interpretations of Piedmontese gastronomy, often revisited with a creative touch. Among the dishes, the carousel of starters is truly not to be missed, as is the white truffle (when in season). The wine list is also highly interesting, organised according to a chromatic system that identifies the various styles: from “voluptuous” to “purpureal”, from “luminous” to “veiled”. A refined game that invites guests to indulge in the choice of the perfect bottle for every palate and occasion.

Name: San Xiang Rou Cuo Mian
Address: ABC Brickworks Market & Food Centre, #01-132, Blk 6 Jalan Bukit Merah, 150006, Singapore
Description: Its bak chor mee can be made with your choice of noodles – mee pok being the most popular. Bouncy noodles are dressed in sambal and topped with sliced pork and meatballs. Also try the noodle soup with fish balls or pork liver.

Name: Sancerre Rive Gauche
Description: In this upmarket neighbourhood, Sancerre denotes a hill, a wine and even a great little Parisian restaurant – a location once run by the great Sancerre winegrower, Alphonse Mellot. In a modern bistro atmosphere, Anne-Cécile Faye, no stranger to the art of hospitality, extends an exuberant welcome. As for chef Éric Lecerf, he cooks up humble dishes from French popular tradition and the effect is as remarkable as it is cheering: different pâtés, offal and other filling foods, plus stuffed cabbage – the house specialty. Everything is presented on the counter; whole pies and cakes are cut to order by the waiter.

Name: Sand & Koal
Address: Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental Hotel, West Corniche Road, Al Ras Al Akhdar, Abu Dhabi
Description: It’s not every day that you get to sit in a luxurious beachside gazebo overlooking a grand Presidential Palace and a glistening Arabian Gulf, but this is exactly the appeal of this modern restaurant. Catch the sunset with a drink before enjoying tasty woodfire cooking. Take your pick of mouthwatering steaks, ‘Reef and Beef’ – their version of a surf and turf – or seafood platters if you plan to share. Finish off with a smoked chocolate mousse or fig tart. This is where to come for a romantic evening out.

Name: Sandikala
Address: 9 rue de la Barsogue, Galan, 65330, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Australian-born chef Luke MacLeod welcomes guests to this old farmstead, which has been done up in a tasteful country chic vein. He concocts generous seasonal cuisine that allies local produce with Asian ingredients, in a nod to his travels: pan-fried foie gras and kimchi; spaghetti squash tempura and fresh wasabi. The ingredients are firmly rooted in the terroir, and the seasonings are a blend of tangy, sweet and spicy flavours.

Name: Sandpiper Inn
Address: Railway Street, Market Place, Leyburn, DL8 5AT, United Kingdom
Description: You’ll receive a cheery Yorkshire welcome from the friendly owners of this characterful stone pub, which has been impressing locals and visitors alike for over 25 years in this pretty market town. They refer to their three dining rooms as 'snugs' and rightly so, as there's a delightfully cosy vibe throughout. The menus are overtly seasonal and reflect the location with ingredients like Dales lamb, and the chef's experience shines through in carefully prepared, tried-and-tested dishes. Two ‘country-chic’ bedrooms offer excellent comforts for those wishing to stay over.

Name: Sandro's
Address: 2 Drakes Way, Lyme Regis, DT7 3QP, United Kingdom
Description: The kind of heartfelt and enthusiastically run restaurant that guarantees you’ll leave feeling better than when you arrived, Sandro’s is a hometown return for the titular chef, who has taken over the premises his father once ran. In an intimate 16-cover space, he cooks fuss-free and flavour-packed dishes such as spatchcock quail with Montbéliard sausage and coco de Paimpol, while adding occasional touches from his Italian heritage. Sandro’s partner Vicky looks after the service with skill, and they are both relaxed, welcoming hosts.

Name: Sang Ka Si
Address: 262/8 Yaowarat Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: This outlet with a red-brown zinc roof offers a menu of both individual and sharing dishes, with nicely balanced flavours. Despite its humble guise, Sang Ka Sri attracts a crowd, so be prepared to wait for a table before enjoying the fresh squid with herbs and tangy dressing.

Name: Sang Thatien
Address: 75 Maha Rat Road, Phra Borom Maha Ratchawang, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
Description: Formerly an ice factory, this small eatery retains some of the interior structure and incorporates vintage décor in a dining room decorated with basic wooden furniture and collectibles. The chef embraces seasonal Thai ingredients, especially fruit, to produce unique, signature dishes in a home-cooking style, such as strawberry salad with shrimp paste and caramelised pork and spicy plum mango salad. The crab meat with fresh herbs and spicy sauce is unmissable.

Name: Sangiovese
Address: Muralla de Sant Llorenç 32, Mataró, 08302, Spain
Description: Located in the heart of Mataró and boasting an intriguing interior décor, this restaurant features design details and curious aesthetic nods to Art Deco. Chef Pepi Sánchez, visible from the dining room thanks to the glass-walled kitchen, serves up a traditional yet updated menu that is full of creative touches and nods to other cuisines. The à la carte service is complemented by several set menus: Weekly (lunch), Sangiovese Nights (dinner only) and the Festival Tasting Menu.

Name: Sanjuhachi
Description: Toshikazu Kamei is a ‘chef of the soil and water’. As an agriculture student, he researched vegetable growing and water quality. He grows the vegetables himself and uses the right water for each dish. Having prepared data on the water that goes best with each ingredient, he blends different kinds to achieve the right hardness and pH. Kamei applies a variety of cooking methods to each ingredient, creating variations and revealing new aspects. His vegetable soup, prepared with only water and salt, also follows this idea, letting even delicate vegetable flavours come through.

Name: Sankt Annæ
Address: Sankt Annæ Plads 12, Copenhagen, 1250 K, Denmark
Description: An attractive terraced building with a traditional, rather quaint interior. There's a seasonal à la carte and a daily blackboard menu: prices can vary so check before ordering. The lobster and shrimp – fresh from local fjords – are a hit.

Name: Sanro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Valet parking
Description: Chef Sung-yup Yoo’s dedication to washoku cuisine shines through at Sanro. The nuanced, chic objets d’art that adorn the space are in harmony with the chef’s sensibilities expressed through both his menu and the dining environment. When seasonal ingredients meet his refined technique and passion for culinary craft, a succession of subtle flavours unfolds, gently pleasing the palate throughout the meal. To complete the experience, the service is as polished as the clean, elegant flavours that define his washoku cuisine.

Name: Sansan Bistro
Address: 170, Section 2, Dunhua South Road, Da'an District, Taipei, 106033, Taiwan
Description: The modern room, done up in burgundy red with wood and metal trim, is both refined and trendy at the same time. The chef champions a concept that melds neo-Sichuan cooking with unusual cocktails and alcoholic beverages. His chicken with fresh Sichuan peppercorns is a poultry version of the classic Shuizhu beef, layering meaty flavours with mild tingling heat. Spices and sauces imported from Sichuan add unrivalled oomph.

Name: Sansho
Description: The atmosphere here is trendy and lively with a friendly neighbourhood vibe. You'll enjoy an Asian-inspired cuisine, served by friendly staff – the "Beef smoked red curry: homemade sausage, pastrami & braised shin, spiced potatoes & fried shallots" is a tempting option, for example. Importance is placed on regional and seasonal ingredients, organic whenever possible. You can choose dishes à la carte or go for one of the set menus, which come in classic or vegetarian options. The affordable lunch set menu is particularly enticing.

Name: Sansibar
Description: A restaurant with cult status! This smart beach cabin is a much sought-after place to eat. It takes five minutes to reach it on foot through the dunes – or you can use the shuttle service. Fancy a Sansibar classic such as rice pudding with red fruit jelly? Or perhaps you'd prefer something more sophisticated? Superb wine list. No reservations taken at lunchtime. There is a playground for children next to the restaurant.

Name: Santa Joana
Address: Rua de Santa Marta 61B, Lisbon, 1059-002, Portugal
Description: Inside the Locke de Santa Joana hotel, a 17th-century convent that now blends past and present, you will find a restaurant you simply must visit, with premises full of personality. The menu, signed by chef Nuno Mendes, seeks to honour the city’s distinct cultural influences in order to tell stories with soul, both of yesterday and of today; always, however, with a contemporary touch and international nuances that speak of the cook’s journey. A recommendation? Try his Berbigão da costa (coastal cockles), caldo Bulhão-Pato (Bulhão Pato broth), croutons and sea herbs, because… it comes with a sauce that is truly addictive!

Name: Santa Mariana
Address: Camí de Loreto s/n, Alaior, 07730, Spain
Description: This restaurant occupies a Menorcan-style country house with plenty of typical charm (including a delightful terrace) that has been converted into a small rural hotel. The cuisine here is based around an à la carte service (with specific sections dedicated to vegetables, seafood, rice dishes, pasta... and a special one, available upon reservation, where lobster is the star of the show) and a choice of two set menus: ‘Ecos de la finca’ (Echoes of the Farm) and ‘Esencia menorquina’ (Menorcan Essence) (one expertly uses the honey produced by its bees, and the other, their homemade olive oil). Here, they are constantly experimenting with culinary techniques and regional ingredients to rustle up locally sourced delicacies, with plenty of Mediterranean touches. The estate has its own organic vegetable garden, olive trees, chickens, and lambs!

Name: Santa Teresa
Address: via di Porta Soprana 55 r, Genoa, 16123, Italy
Description: Just a stone's throw from the alleged home of Christopher Columbus and Piazza De Ferrari, you will find cosy rooms and lounges, as well as a handy outdoor area in the pedestrian zone. Here, the expert hand of the Scala family, which also runs the renowned San Giorgio, will make you appreciate market and regional cuisine, especially seafood. You will often find the famous Genoese cappon magro, but there is no shortage of good meat-based alternatives, revisited in a slightly contemporary key and carefully plated. It will be easy to find a good match, even by the glass, thanks to a fine selection of wines.

Name: Santamonica
Description: Head down a small street along Corso Italia in the Albaro neighborhood toward the beach, where both the interior dining room and summer terrace offer sweeping sea views. The majority of the menu’s ingredients come directly from those waters (half a page is dedicated to raw preparations). The chef ventures into modern recipes with an emphasis on striking final presentations.

Name: Santi
Address: 11 E. 53rd St., New York, NY, 10022, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Santi is Chef Michael White's paen to the Mediterranean in the heart of Midtown. There may be multiple spaces within, but this stunning spot feels intimate, making it a perfect date-night reservation. The menu draws on White's experience in the South of France and the Amalfi Coast with crudités di mare like prawns with pistachio, antipasti like butternut squash soup, primi including gnocchi and risotto, and secondi ranging from grilled steak to sea bass. Orecchiette tossed with blue crab and sea urchin is a highlight, as is the pan-roasted veal chop plated with pancetta-wrapped, charred radicchio. In a final bow, Delizie al Limone pays tribute to the Italian coast with white chocolate-covered sponge cake filled with limoncello cream and basil whipped cream.

Name: Santi
Address: 101-107 Chawala Nok Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, Ubon Ratchathani, 34000, Thailand
Description: Diners can sit inside or roadside in this simple, open-air restaurant. Thai-Chinese is the fare and dishes are prepared at the front. The sound of the wok and sight of the flames make an impressive spectacle. The stir-fried minced pork with olives is a must for its smoky, intense flavours. The deep-fried seabass with sweet fish sauce takes a little longer to prepare but the result is a fantastically crispy skin that goes well with the homemade spicy sauce.

Name: Santo
Description: Chef Hosea Rosenberg draws inspiration from his hometown of Taos, in northern New Mexico, to deliver a menu of satisfying, rustic cooking. Guests can stop in at all times of day to satisfy a craving for southwestern fare. In the morning, grab-and-go breakfast burritos are the mainstay, while at lunch, casual counter service encompasses a broader array of options from pozole to tortas. Finally, at dinner, full table service accommodates a livelier crowd where margaritas flow with the full menu in play, featuring specialties like roasted chicken mole with red pepper polenta.

Name: Santo Remedio
Address: 152 Tooley Street, Southwark, London, SE1 2TU, United Kingdom
Description: A colourful, lively and happy place, Santo Remedio takes inspiration from its owner’s time spent in Mexico City, Yucatán and Oaxaca. As soon as you enter, the buzz hits you, with plenty of excited diners enjoying what the kitchen has to offer – namely bright and flavoursome dishes drawing together a selection of tacos, tostadas and flautas (rolled tacos), alongside regional specialities like barbacoa lamb shank from Oaxaca. There’s a wide cocktail selection, too, and the bottomless brunch is a hit on weekends.

Name: Santu Pultru
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Just a few kilometres from Sartène, this equestrian centre and restaurant set deep in the maquis promises an authentic foray into the mountainous side of Corsica. In a rustic-style interior blending wood and stone, the establishment has no shortage of charm and also boasts a country garden. The generous, flavoursome cuisine showcases local produce, eg veal reared by the owner, charcuterie made in-house, fish from the small port of Tizzano, and fruit and vegetables from growers in the surrounding area.

Name: Sant’Agostino
Description: Tucked beside the deconsecrated church of Sant’Agostino, a beautifully kept cloister ushers guests into the culinary world of chef Mauro Brina, a young talent with a stated preference for meat, yet one who truly comes into his own with seafood. Little wonder, then, that we recommend his marine preparations: the pisarei with shellfish or the fish soup brimming with tomato, crustaceans, mussels, cuttlefish, and the day’s catch. In fine weather, make a point of securing a table on the terrace, an evocative setting steeped in history and the timeless charm of the ancient convent.

Name: Sanwa
Description: ‘Sanwa’ means ‘three-part harmony’: between producers, chefs and guests. The menu lists producers by name, linking them to guests through the chef. Prix fixe service begins with dry-cured ham and gnocco fritto. Meat dishes include venison and beef, both char-grilled. The meal ends with a pasta dish, as per convention. Sanwa exerts special effort to make each dish impressive, so the number of main ingredients is limited to three—a three-part harmony on the plate.

Name: Sanyod (Bang Rak)
Address: 89 Soi Charat Wiang, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: With a history spanning more than half a century, what started as a food stall located in a small alley has since grown into a popular and bustling neighbourhood restaurant. They specialise in Cantonese cuisine, and their roast duck and signature sauces are highly recommended, especially paired with Cantonese-style noodles. The menu also features a deliciously tender clay pot-braised beef.

Name: Sanzaru
Description: Behind the Cubist-inspired façade lies a pleasant, airy, colourful establishment devoted to creativity. The chef reverently respects the season in dishes that subtly draw on influences from all four corners of the earth. An example: a characteristic caprese salad to start is given a crisp modern perspective courtesy of surprising textures, while pollock cooked in butter is served with mashed potato and leek-flavoured ice cream. The contents of the various surprise menus (including vegetarian) are pleasantly true to their names and there is an attractive lunchtime formula. You can expect a score in the zeitgeist that is both surprising and balanced, and guaranteed to set your tastebuds tingling!

Name: Sao
Description: On the quayside of the River Odet in Quimper city centre, Sao is the brainchild of talented young chef Kevin Gourret, formerly of the restaurant Le Goyen in Audierne. In an inviting contemporary setting, he serves up his original recipes inspired by regional ingredients (langoustine, local fish, seaweed, buckwheat, buttermilk) and Asian influences (such as ponzu, gomasio, sesame and ginger). The more ambitious evening menu reveals the full extent of his technical prowess, particularly his robust sauces and jus. The desserts are on a par – for example, a creation bringing together vanilla, chestnut and yuzu.

Name: Sapa İstanbul
Address: Küçükbakkalköy Mahallesi, Rüya Sokak No:12/18A, Ataşehir, Istanbul, 34750, Türkiye
Description: Stylish and spacious, Sapa is located in a predominantly corporate neighbourhood and caters to breakfast, lunch and dinner crowds. We especially recommend the set menu, available from 2pm. (N.B. The 12-course menu is for a minimum of two people.) The chef has a penchant for open-flame cooking and a knack for balancing robust flavours with contemporary culinary lightness. He accompanies succulent grilled rockfish with a salmon cream paired with chestnut and capers for a touch of fresh acidity. A drizzle of syrup adds a hint of sweetness – a refreshing spin on Turkish cuisine!

Name: Sapereta
Address: via Provinciale Ovest 73, località Mola, Porto Azzurro, 57036, Italy
Description: A working farm (producing wine and olive oil) that features charming interiors, though the real highlight is outdoor dining beneath a pergola draped with fragola grapes, overlooking a meadow. The menu features both meat and seafood, rooted in Tuscan tradition but often elevated with creative flair.

Name: Saperlipopette !
Description: In a quiet street of Puteaux, this airy restaurant boasts a large peaceful terrace. You can expect well-crafted, indulgent helpings of food presented in sensibly priced menus. Examples include a crunchy Caesar salad packed in flavour. Cheerful service – ideal for a friendly lunch with friends or a more relaxed meal in the evening.

Name: Sapori
Description: This restaurant's stylish historical setting alone, in the hotel Victoria-Jungfrau, is worth a visit: wonderful hardwood floors beneath your feet, impressively lofty painted ceilings complete with mouldings overhead. When the sun is shining, you should definitely dine on the terrace and take in the magnificent view of the mountains. The cuisine is Italian – the pizzas are a must!

Name: Sapori
Address: 40 Stadon Road, Anstey, LE7 7AY, United Kingdom
Description: 'Sapori' means 'flavours' and that's exactly what this charmingly run Italian restaurant delivers. Located inside a substantial Victorian building in a Leicester suburb, the interior is sleek and modern, even a little glitzy, with an open kitchen pass so you can get a good look at the chefs. A passionate Italian family are in charge, drawing on influences from their native Naples, as well as well-known staples like carbonara, zucchini fritti and tiramisu. Sweet, endearing service makes a visit all the more appealing.

Name: Sapristi
Description: Located on a large square in Rueil-Malmaison, this bistro matches its culinary standards with an equally impressive decor: hardwood floors, painted walls, floral wallpaper and quirky paintings of historical figures sporting modern accessories. The large terrace is a definite highlight! The concise and appealing menu features dishes that are well executed using top-notch ingredients, eg asparagus mimosa, vol-au-vent, floating island. Pleasant service.

Name: Sardis
Description: Tiziano Cappai welcomes diners warmly into this stylish red-brick terraced house, which boasts a cosy interior, sensual artwork on the walls and a blissfully peaceful patio at the rear. Chef Eveline Cappai deftly updates a pure-bred lineup of Italian classics. For example, she might pair bigoli pasta with a subtle stock, to which she adds white wine, parsley, savoury vongole and a hint of umami thanks to kombu. The tiramisu manages to underscore authentic flavours with an amusing new spin thanks to a play on textures. Attention to detail is the watchword here.

Name: Sarmiento Brasa Andaluza
Address: Carretera de Casares km 12,5, Casares, 29690, Spain
Description: Fancy a visit to a typical 'white village'? Casares, in the province of Malaga, is a great option and this restaurant, located at the top of a hill, boasts wonderful terraces, with the best views to contemplate while you enjoy good traditional cuisine. The brothers at the helm, Juan Diego and Miguel, have updated the charming family home to offer a menu that is varied but not lacking identity, as the focus here is clearly on grilled meats (especially young Malaga goat, although they also have a variety of matured cuts). Ask for the daily specials!

Name: Saroa
Description: Enthusiasm, passion, youth... the couple at the helm (with Salvador in charge of savoury and Aroa in charge of sweet) champion an innovative take on traditional cuisine in the centre of Lleida, which is reflected in both the à la carte and set menus: Degustación Aroa (lunchtime only, Monday to Friday, except bank holidays) and Degustación Salvador. Recommendations? Always keep an eye out for their off-menu dishes and don't miss the Lleida snails stewed with slow-cooked tomato and onion, as they have an exquisite flavour.

Name: Sartoria
Description: Sartoria, with its terrace outside and its industrial-chic interior, is always buzzing with a crowd of young diners and couples, here to enjoy a night out. The kitchen turns out typical Italian offerings, ranging from antipasti and pasta to entrees. The menu may not be large, but there's something for everyone. Great care is taken with the presentation in dishes like tortellacci with a creamy burrata that tastes as good as it looks, and entrees highlight quality products. To finish, you'll never go wrong with a classic tiramisu.

Name: Sartoria by Paulo Airaudo
Address: 56F, The Empire, 1 South Sathon Road, Yan Nawa, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: With panoramic views of Bangkok's skyline, this warm, elegant wood-panelled space has mosaic floors inspired by Florence. In a meticulous and modern take on Tuscan dining, Thai produce meets select Japanese and European ingredients from handmade pasta and dry-aged meats to fresh seafood. Choose the larger tasting menu so you can pick your main. The parsley carabinero risotto and dry-aged pigeon cooked rare stand out. There is also an à la carte menu.

Name: Saru Sushi Bar
Description: Hilly Noe Valley is the perfect setting for this jewel of a sushi restaurant, so make your way inside to discover a bustling (read: energetic) vibe. The menu is thoroughly Japanese with a few Californian touches—think grilled shishito peppers tossed with crunchy daikon in a ponzu dressing.Begin with the signature tempura-fried seaweed cracker topped with spicy tuna and avocado. Then, perfectly sized tasting spoons of seared ankimo with scallions, as well as halibut tartare with yuzu make for delightful quick bites. Though rolls are available, regulars opt for the nigiri, which might include kampachi, baby snapper and snow crab. Several omakase (including an all-salmon variation) are also on offer. Since Saru doesn't take reservations, arrive early to avoid a line.

Name: Sasa
Address: 6, Lane 42, Section 2, Zhongshan North Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, 104, Taiwan
Description: Tucked away in a busy shopping and dining area, Sasa welcomes customers with its massive cypress counter and seats ergonomically designed for unbeatable comfort. Omakase menus at different price points feature both cooked dishes and raw fish flown straight from Tokyo's Toyosu market. The fish, mostly white, is aged for different lengths of time to enhance taste and texture. Tuna belly smoked with cherry wood seduces with its unique fragrance.

Name: Sate House
Address: 15 Leli Road, Da'an District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: Since 1993, the Sino-Indonesian owner has been serving authentic Indonesian classics fit for visiting dignitaries, like rendang beef, satay, and ayam goreng Kalasan. Pair with fried tempeh (fermented soybean cake) or tofu for a filling meal. For special occasions, pre-order nasi tumpeng – a festive rice tower with sides and garnishes. The simple room is decorated with Indonesian knickknacks and ornaments that impart ethnic charm.

Name: Sato Omakase
Address: 1122 Post St., San Francisco, CA, 94109, USA
Description: This stylish operation runs as smooth as silk, but more importantly, it serves up an indulgent tasting that highlights excellent ingredients with skill and flair. The menu draws upon both tradition and invention, as in a dish of butter-poached lobster with dashi. Though the cooking does flaunt luxury ingredients with a certain abandon, it's the more understated elements that most impress, like the soy-marinated tuna sashimi with a silky, meaty texture, dotted with freshly grated wasabi; or a nigiri of buttery hamachi belly, lifted with yuzu zest.Next door, livelier sibling Sushi Sato serves more affordable sushi and sashimi, assorted small plates, as well as a beverage program that highlights fine Japanese whisky.

Name: Satori
Address: 2C St. Mary's Row, Wake Green Road, Moseley, Birmingham, B13 9EZ, United Kingdom
Description: An array of both classic and contemporary Japanese dishes are available at this on-trend restaurant, whose bustling atmosphere suggests it’s a hit with the local diners. The wide-ranging à la carte covers all your Japanese favourites, from sushi and sashimi to super-fine tempura and a choice of cuts from the robata grill. If you want a taste of it all, the well-priced tasting menu is the best option. To finish, ‘Mount Fuji’ is their take on a Mont Blanc, set alight at the table for added volcanic flair.

Name: Satricvm
Description: Creative cuisine with a modern twist for a restaurant that places the Agropontino region and its extraordinary produce at the heart of its culinary creations. The tasting menu, which is seasonal and built around a theme, allows Chef Cotilli to fully express his vision. Proposals include carefully crafted dishes that respect the local terroir and are beautifully presented: from black rice with mussels and beurre blanc to Lara Peri’s pigeon, roasted to perfection and served with castagnaccio and an excellent jus. The outdoor area also serves as a winter garden, filled with plants, bamboo and soft lighting that create a pleasant atmosphere. And, weather permitting, it is well worth visiting the archaeological site of the same name, just a few metres away.

Name: Sattlerhof - Wirtshaus
Description: This renowned winery and hotel enjoys a sensational location amid the vineyards – the terrace overlooking the region beckons in summer! With Wirtshaus, siblings Anna and Markus Sattler propose a charming alternative to their fine dining restaurant. Popular classics and seasonal dishes can be ordered à la carte, and there is also a daily set menu. To complement the dishes, they serve wines from their own estate. Besides the delicious food, the warm hospitality ensures a wonderful dining experience.

Name: Sauce
Address: The Painswick Hotel, Kemps Lane, Painswick, GL6 6YB, United Kingdom
Description: Something of a hidden gem, this inviting brasserie-style restaurant is situated within a Palladian country house hotel, itself secreted down the narrow lane of an attractive Cotswolds town. The chefs put their skill and experience to use on straightforward yet refined dishes where each plate is pleasingly uncluttered. A superb beef Wellington shows the kitchen at its best, accompanied by a pot of deep, rich and glossy Madeira reduction. When execution is skilled and ingredients are strong, there’s little need for anything else.

Name: Sauf Imprévu
Description: Félix Gagnaire extends a warm welcome in this bistro whose hearty, buzzy vibe sports the ubiquitous bistro chairs, worn tiles and mismatched wooden tables. His wallet-friendly patriotic score stars seasonal produce: salmon tartare with sesame and ginger; flank steak with turnips, baby potatoes and a peppercorn sauce; roasted apricots and peaches, tonka bean ice cream. The next-door wine bar goes by the same name.

Name: Sauge
Description: Amandine Chaignot has breathed new life into this inn, in which centuries-old beams meet modern concrete. While the bistro has energised this village deep in the Perche region, the fine dining restaurant unveils a personal style of cooking marked by remarkable finesse. The restaurant's name, meaning "sage", is particularly apt, as herbs are ever-present in and set the tone for the dishes: sorrel or nettle in the starters, complemented by bay leaf oil or an infusion of verbena, rosemary and sage. Locally sourced produce, from neighbouring farmers, lies at the heart of the plant-forward menu.

Name: Saur
Description: An unexpected restaurant hidden among the fields of a small hamlet in the Bassa Bresciana region. Although the menu features a few regional dishes, the focus here is on creative cuisine with an emphasis on herbs and vegetables, some of which are grown in the restaurant’s own kitchen garden.

Name: Sauska 48
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Find a table on the spacious terrace of this modern winery to enjoy wonderful views out across the vineyard and the hills; on a warm summer’s day, it doesn’t get much better than this. The well-curated wine list covers Hungary and Europe, and includes reds and rosés from the vines you see in front of you, as well as whites from the owners’ other winery in Tokaj. The concise selection of contemporary dishes take their inspiration from the Hungarian kitchen but exhibit a level of refined creativity. The passionate team will share their knowledge to help you find the perfect wine match.

Name: Sauska Padi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: If wine’s your thing, you can’t go wrong with a visit to this striking hillside building in the heart of wine country. You must open, of course, with one of their own Sauska wines in the smart bar, before heading through to the sleek restaurant whose wonderful terrace offers views over the vines below. There’s a small à la carte of refined, eye-catching dishes as well as two tasting menus on offer, one themed around Tokaj itself – choose this option along with their local wine recommendations to fully immerse yourself in the region. To really complete the experience, ask for a peek into their winery below.

Name: Sauvage
Description: This place has been dedicated to hospitality for over 500 years. Not only does the long-standing Hotel Wilden Mann have charming, individually styled guestrooms, it is also a bastion of fine dining.
