The tastefully elegant Sauvage serves classic and traditional dishes made with select, exceedingly fresh ingredients. In addition to the à la carte selection – featuring, for example, flam-seared Brüggli char or sautéed veal liver – a set menu is available. At lunchtime, the options are slightly more streamlined but include dishes from the evening menu. Tip for motorists: the Kesselturm multi-storey car park is just a short walk away. Alternatively, you can park on the other side of the river, stroll through the beautiful old town and then cross the bridge (Reussbrücke).

Name: Savage
Address: Rue de la Paix 22, Ixelles, 1050, Belgium
Description: The fashionable natural interior of Savage is perfectly at home in the trendy Saint-Boniface neighbourhood. A seat on the pavement terrace is just the ticket to soak up the district’s bubbly vibe, without forgetting to pop into the house grocery-bakery. The single set menu unveils plant-based cuisine, depicted by fascinating combinations of herbs and vegetables. You can choose your own meat or fish from the refrigerated counter near the restroom. Chef Rammelsberg orchestrates a creative score, illustrated by a cream of radishes underscored by yuzu juice and a perfectly balanced combination of marinated carrot and confit kumquat. The deftly crafted, seasonal lineup is legible and enticing.

Name: Savelberg
Address: 136/1 Soi Yen Akat 2, Chong Nonsi, Yan Nawa, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Food and mood pair well at Dutch chef-owner Henk Savelberg’s eponymous restaurant, now in a contemporary house in Chong Nonsi. The sparkling dining room features an open kitchen, a refined wine cellar and garden views, with private group dining available. The menu boasts adventurous, modern, colourful French dishes with a classical base, made from fine international ingredients. Rounding out the experience is the professional service. Booking is essential.

Name: Savoury
Description: This spruce detached house does sport a faintly English hallmark, the menu, however, unveils a patriotic line-up of classical French cuisine. Kick off your meal with an aperitif in the wine cellar before taking a seat in the modern dining room or on the leafy patio. Subtle classicism depicts the textbook precision cooking, albeit with an occasional Mediterranean twang and a refreshing sprinkling of modernity. Pop into the delicatessen before you leave and take a few delicacies home.

Name: Savoy
Description: This local institution’s refurbishment has restored much of its original charm and its 8th floor setting boasts superb views over Esplanade Park. Sophisticated classic dishes have a Finnish-French slant and a modern edge, with the occasional Russian touch. The wine matches are first class.

Name: Savoy Grill
Address: The Savoy, Strand, London, WC2R 0EU, United Kingdom
Description: There's something undeniably decadent about dining at this iconic restaurant. From the moment you enter via the hotel's beautiful lobby, the décor is elegant and opulent in equal measure with the chandeliers setting the tone for a dining room that's unsurprisingly popular with celebratory couples. The menu follows in these luxury footsteps, offering a mix of French and British classics that put premium produce front and centre, whether that be caviar, Dover sole or excellent quality beef for the signature Wellington.

Name: Savô
Description: The reopening in 2022 of the Hotel Windsor with its romantic vintage decor, is a real bonus for Laigueglia, especially the hotel’s new gourmet restaurant Savô (which translates as “flavour” in Ligurian dialect). Here, a contemporary dining room and an outdoor space with views of the beach and the sea provide the setting for modern cuisine prepared from regional, seasonal ingredients with a focus on fish (there is also a meat option for each course). The impressive selection of wine and choice of cocktails from the elegant Windsor Bar adds to its appeal.

Name: Sawa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: This lively spot lures a crowd: by the time they unlock the doors, the line is already long. Everyone is here for the convivial ambience and the standout Middle Eastern cuisine. This is a menu thick with options, with house-made pita arriving piping hot to scoop up labneh and hummus with wagyu beef cheeks plus baba ghannouj before a round of mezze like tabbouleh, fried meat pies and kibbeh nayeh. Don't miss the rakkakat, or akkawi and halloumi cheese wrapped in filo and fried to a golden crisp. Grilled Australian lamb chop with garlic labneh and a generous coating of urfa bibir is a smoky, savory main dish. Finish with the tamriyeh, phyllo pastries filled with sweet semolina pudding.

Name: Saxlers Restaurant
Description: This restaurant is housed in the inviting Weinhotel St. Stephanus on the riverside promenade and not far from the old market square. In a refined setting, the friendly and committed hosts serve delicious food made with top-notch ingredients, vegetarian options included. The menu features classic dishes and regional specialities. Tip: Leave room for the delicious desserts! In the basement, the Braukeller serves Kloster Machern beer.

Name: Saó by Vicenç Fajardo
Description: What is most striking about this charming restaurant, in the old centre of a small village in the Baix Empordà, is its gastronomic concept, as it seeks to be a contemporary restaurant where the embers (as a technique and as a language of expression), seasonal produce that speaks of the environment and the sensitivity of the chef are perfectly balanced. You will find an à la carte with a Mediterranean-Catalan flavour that combines tradition and innovation, as well as two tasting menus. The terrace, surrounded by greenery, is a great option in summer!

Name: Scala
Description: Set in an enviable position at the entrance to Mdina, this restaurant stands out by its terrace with sweeping sea views and the rich, expressive Mediterranean cuisine of chef Sheldon, that has earned it a reputation as one of the island’s finest establishments. The staff is always at hand to help you choose between locally sourced fish and expertly prepared meats. Signature dishes include yakitori-style octopus and Rossini-style beef fillet. While in the area, make sure you visit the nearby historic attractions; we also recommend getting a taxi to Mdina, unless you are staying nearby, as parking can be scarce.

Name: Scala
Description: This modern restaurant boasts beautiful views across the lake and a delightful terrace. It also serves seasonal dishes with an emphasis on regional ingredients, and the vegetable and animal produce are used in their entirety. A smaller selection of dishes is served at lunchtime. Friendly service and fine wines.

Name: Scalottas - Terroir
Description: At this trendy Alpine-style restaurant, the kitchen works exclusively with regional ingredients, many of which they produce themselves. Seasonality and a strong sense of terroir define the cuisine – the staff will be happy to tell you more about their concept. To order, simply mix and match the dishes on the menu that pique your interest. From Vazerol char to Grisons lamb, the outstanding quality of the ingredients shines through in every course. The wines are also sourced from the region and surrounding areas. Warm and courteous service is provided by staff who are attentive to diners' needs. Be sure to reserve, as the restaurant is very popular.

Name: Scappi
Address: Alsancak, Gaziosmanpaşa Bulvarı No:1, Konak, Izmir, 35210, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Take the lift to the ninth floor of Swissôtel and immerse yourself in the elegant setting of Scappi. It's definitely worth trying to secure a spot on the terrace, where you get to take in the views of the bay and the sea – the sunsets are simply divine! But perhaps you would prefer to home in on the action in the partially open kitchen complete with pizza oven. With great skill, the chefs rustle up dishes such as a creamy risotto with barbecued squid, al dente house-made pasta with an aromatic tomato sauce, or freshly caught sea bass with a saffron-infused lime sauce. This is a popular place, so don't forget to make a reservation.

Name: Scaramouche
Description: Set in the affluent northern suburb of South Hill, Scaramouche has been a Toronto mainstay for decades, with Chef Keith Froggett at the helm since 1983. Don’t be alarmed when you arrive and head downstairs to the restaurant thinking you are off to a basement—you're not, as the superb city skyline view soon proves.Guests come for the views and stay for the traditional French cuisine. Don't expect modern twists, as dishes such as foie gras terrine with a sour cherry reduction and rabbit loin wrapped with bacon sided by a fricassee of sweet peas and fava beans, are as classic as they come. Savor the dark chocolate mousse with cherries for dessert, or take home one of their signature coconut cream pies.

Name: Scarlett
Address: 37F, Pullman Hotel G, 188 Silom Road, Suriyawong, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: For a night out with friends, this fun and lively restaurant on the top floor of the Pullman hotel may just fit the bill. A large menu of mostly European dishes, from duck confit to vongole, has something for everyone, but it’s the meats and fish cooked on the grill – which forms the focal point of the open kitchen – that diners go for. Steaks are mostly Australian, while the seafood could include octopus, sea bass or turbot. Add in cocktails, views of the city below and even a cheese counter and you have all bases covered.

Name: Scarpetta
Address: 33 Mengzi Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: This two-storey restaurant takes its name from the act of using bread to mop up the last bit of sauce left on the plate. Homemade pizza and pasta, such as pizza vongole, and other specialities like Wagyu carpaccio topped with shaved black truffle slices, mean you’ll certainly not want to waste anything. The last facelift in 2018 left the dining room with a warm and romantic ambiance, making it an ideal choice for a date.

Name: Scatto
Description: From Turin’s beautiful Piazza San Carlo, you head through an inner courtyard to this restaurant’s modern dining room with its open-view kitchen. Whether you opt for the à la carte or tasting menu, you’ll find a balance of traditional Piedmontese and more creative dishes, all of remarkable quality, in keeping with the superb wine list.

Name: Schaarschmidt's
Description: This building on a corner plot with a gorgeous leafy façade is home to a cosy restaurant that is run with great dedication. Its many regulars come in droves to enjoy specialities of Saxon cuisine – the beef roulade is a firm favourite! The friendly waitstaff will gladly talk you through the options on the menu. Head for the lovely small terrace planted with trees.

Name: Schankkuchl Pogusch
Description: A seriously cool concept! The bright and airy architecture of the space, with its floor-to-ceiling glass façade and an open kitchen as its centrepiece, is a draw in itself. Diners are seated at the long counter and watch the chefs in action. The twist: Everything is cooked over an open flame or steamed. The dishes, which are regional and take their cue from the seasons, bear creative names such as "Pearls before Swine", "Kissed by Fire" or "Chef Poisonnier". The pyrography art decorating the menu is a lovely detail. From 5-7pm, you can order à la carte or opt for the set menu "Let it Flow"; from 7pm onwards, only the set menu is served, tailored individually to each table. Choose your own bottle from the walk-in wine cellar, which is another highlight. It is definitely worth taking a moment to browse the farm shop. Wirtshaus Steirereck am POGUSCH along with some quirky, one-of-a-kind accommodation options are also on site.

Name: Schapers
Description: A family-run place where you will be treated to friendly and cordial service. As for the food, you can look forward to ambitious classic cuisine brimming with regional influences. Choose from the à la carte offering or the set menus drawn from it, which include a vegetarian set menu. The terrace is lovely. Should you wish to stay overnight, there are comfortable and convenient guestrooms available, distributed over two buildings.

Name: Schattbuch
Description: Trendy and elegant Schattbuch is a firm fixture in the Allgäu fine dining scene. The kitchen team prepares modern dishes, always staying true to the region and consistently using high-quality ingredients. In the evening, there are two menus (one of them vegetarian) and a small à la carte selection. At lunchtime, in addition to more affordable daily specials, you can also order from the evening menu. Restaurant manager Christian Marz adds his personal flair to the friendly atmosphere and service that's both casual and expertly delivered. Head for the terrace in summer.

Name: Schatteman
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This imposing villa tucked away in the woods is a real gem. Modern artwork, a log burning fire and a wine cellar set the stylish scene, further enhanced by a manicured garden and terrace, ideal for a drink in fine weather. While Marieke spoils guests in the dining room, owner-chef Gregory demonstrates his inventive flair in a modern score, courtesy of cherry-picked ingredients from the region. Seasonings and fermentation techniques add a distinctive touch to his signature cuisine and he enjoys surprising and pushing culinary boundaries, but always with a deft, subtle hand. We recommend the set tasting menu which offers a choice of number of courses (three at lunchtime).

Name: Scherp
Description: Mart Scherp's restaurant, which also offers accommodation, merges the historical charm of Middelburg's town centre with a trendy vibe. The talented chef likes to work with Zeeland's local produce and Asian seasonings. Enticing flavours and subtle spiciness are common features, so it's no surprise that he has gathered a loyal following.

Name: Schillingshof
Description: Schillingshof has been around since 1648. The family business takes pride in providing first-rate hospitality. Behind the spruce half-timbered façade, you will find an elegant interior where diners enjoy attentive and cordial service and, last but not least, classic cuisine. Made using carefully selected ingredients, the dishes are pared down to the essentials. There are various set menus and tempting à la carte options such as confit char on a bed of mussel risotto with lime foam, or veal fillet "saltimbocca" with rosemary gnocchi, vegetables and sauce divine. The wine list is also fantastic – sometimes, a Mediterranean antipasti platter and a good bottle of wine are all you need. Lovely guestrooms.

Name: Schimmel's
Description: This restaurant's striking red façade draws the eye. The smart interior is modern and stylish, and the atmosphere is welcoming – the wooden tables are a nice touch. In the open kitchen, regional dishes are prepared, occasionally incorporating influences from around the globe. Diners can choose between the two set menus or order à la carte. The soups, for example, are delicious, but so is the fresh fish! The proprietress ensures cordial and attentive service. They also offer pretty guestrooms and holiday flats.

Name: Schlegelhof
Description: The charming boutique hotel Schlegelhof boasts not only elegantly appointed rooms, but also culinary excellence courtesy of Marianne and Martin Schlegel. The cuisine is rooted in classic culinary tradition and takes its cue from the seasons. Dishes showcase the finest ingredients, often sourced locally, alongside fruit and herbs from the hotel's own garden. There are various set menus and à la carte options. Classics such as Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) and Wiener schnitzel feature, as do more sophisticated numbers such as Atlantic monkfish with beetroot, capers, and potato mousseline. The waitstaff are laid back yet attentive. Decked out in light wood, the interior is sleek and inviting. Floor-to-ceiling windows look out onto the garden and splendid summer terrace.

Name: Schloss Binningen
Description: This stylishly furnished restaurant housed in an attractive 13C castle serves contemporary international cuisine with Mediterranean and Asian influences. At lunchtime choose between the "Business Lunch" deal and the four-course "Sorpresa" set menu; in the evening, they serve a four- to six-course "Emozione" tasting menu – or you can dine à la carte, which includes a vegetarian alternative. Under the direction of the dedicated sommelier, the service is friendly and proficient. In summer, the terrace is inviting. The hotel area beautifully combines modern and historical features. Tip: There is covered parking next door; if you prefer to get here by tram, line 10 stops right by the castle grounds. The narrow River Birsig also flows past here.

Name: Schloss Farrach - Das Restaurant
Description: Behind its striking mosaic façade, this 17C castle houses a beautiful restaurant with a cross-vaulted ceiling. There is also a delightful terrace. In the evenings, diners have a choice of two set menus showcasing seasonal and regional specialities; at lunchtime, the options are more limited. Some of the ingredients come from organic farms or the restaurant's own garden. Owner Alexander Stöhr is in charge of the kitchen; his son manages the front-of-house team and expertly recommends wine pairings. Tip: Various cultural events take place on specific dates. This is also a fantastic venue for private functions.

Name: Schloss Loersfeld
Description: The centuries-old castle with its extensive grounds is a magnificent property, boasting stylish rooms and salons displaying period details behind its massive old walls. This stately backdrop makes for a fabulous setting in which to relish classic cuisine either à la carte or in the form of a three- to six-course set menu. Caviar or oysters are popular appetisers, followed by tempting dishes such as "smoked eel, eel glaze, beetroot, potato, radish" or "lobster tail, mandarin, kumquat, walnut, gin gel, bergamot beurre blanc". Friendly and attentive service. Tip: There is an interesting set menu at lunchtime. In an adjacent building, three pretty apartments accommodate overnight guests.

Name: Schloss Monaise
Description: With Hubert Scheid's cuisine, this place is nothing short of a culinary institution in the region. His signature style comprises pleasantly straightforward dishes made from excellent ingredients – served à la carte or as a set menu. The restaurant occupies stylish, high-ceilinged rooms that channel the stately flair of these premises dating back to 1783 – once a summer residence. Or you can dine on the wonderful terrace with a view of the surrounding nature and the Moselle. It's also worth taking a look at the wine list, which features many a big name.

Name: Schloss Niederweis
Description: This tasteful restaurant is housed in the converted corn barn of a magnificent Baroque castle dating from 1751. The decor is a fascinating blend of rustic cachet and modern design – the open truss roof is striking and the two historical carriages on the wall are certainly eye-catching! Sample the flavoursome dishes à la carte or as a set menu, washed down by your choice from the terrific wine list that includes rare finds, including by the glass. Charming garden, a banquet hall and a registry office. On a practical note: easy parking.

Name: Schloss Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Set in a phenomenal location, the renowned Rosewood Schloss Fuschl has many admirers, and not only among its hotel guests. With its exceptionally upscale and tastefully elegant interior, the restaurant strikes a perfect balance between grandeur and cosy comfort. The large windows offer a magnificent view of the lake. The set menu and à la carte dishes are prepared with select regional ingredients, including produce from the restaurant's own fish farm. The impressive wine list is extensive and includes some prestigious labels. In fine weather, you can also dine on the lakeside terrace one floor up.

Name: Schloss Restaurant Venus
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park
Description: Set in the "Versailles of Westphalia", this classic, distinguished restaurant has vaulted ceilings and numerous paintings by owner Franz L Lauter, an avid painter. A seasonal set menu is available in the evening (from 5pm). At lunchtime on Thursday to Saturday, there are set menus. Tip: Either before or after dinner, why not take a walk around the castle and park?

Name: Schloss Wartegg
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The elevated location between Lake Constance and the Alpstein massif is quite something! As it is in the small castle hotel, the focus in the restaurant is on all things organic and ecological. This translates into mindful produced ingredients and organic produce from local suppliers, plus vegetables and herbs from the hotel's 2 500m2garden. In the evening, diners enjoy adept service and dishes such as fillet of perch caught by professional fisherman Claudio Görtz from Altenrhein, saffron foam, leek and Parisian potatoes, or roasted lettuce, lentil vinaigrette, creamed potato and herb oil. Options are more limited at lunchtime. From the terrace there is a wonderful view of the countryside and Lake Constance.

Name: Schlossanger Alp
Description: Set against the backdrop of the Allgäu Alps, this hotel has tasteful, comfortable guestrooms and a lovely, inviting restaurant in which cosy Alpine vibes meet elegant table settings. Affording stunning views, the terrace is a wonderful spot for a meal in summer! The menu is varied: at lunchtime (from 1pm) there is a three-course set menu and à la carte dishes, including "small bites to share"; in the evening the selection includes their "Signature Menu", as well as dishes ranging from braised vegetable ravioli to lobster, and venison loin to Gröstl (pan-fried potatoes). The extensive wine list encompasses a fine selection.

Name: Schlossberg
Description: The location on the Schlossberg (castle hill) is fantastic in its own right: located right beside Vauban fortress, the business travellers' hotel that houses this restaurant towers over the city and affords a one-of-a-kind view – best enjoyed from the terrace. The interior is also delightful with its sleek contemporary design, coupled with panoramic vistas through generous windows. The menu changes with the seasons and features classic dishes with international twists. Order à la carte or opt for the set menu of the month (three or four courses).

Name: Schlosskeller
Description: When it comes to the setting, the lovingly decorated vaulted cellar is really cosy, and the terrace by the castle pond is fantastic! The seasonal cuisine is in a regional vein, ranging from classic Wiener schnitzel to roasted fillet of sea bass with a rosehip foam. They are also open at lunchtime, which is excellent news.

Name: Schlosspark Restaurant by Tristan Brandt
Description: Tristan Brandt has found a fantastic setting for his new fine dining concept here. The location right next to the castle park is wonderful – the terrace is a truly idyllic spot! Inside, mouldings are combined with modern elements to create a chic interior. The cuisine strikes a successful balance of diverse styles, with a menu that includes Flammkuchen and cake in the afternoon, as well as Tristan Brandt's specials such as truffle fries or caviar, alongside such classics as Wiener schnitzel with warm potato salad or char and beef fillet.

Name: Schlossschänke auf dem Johannisberg
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In an annexe of the centuries-old Schloss Johannisberg – the world's first Riesling wine estate – this bright, friendly restaurant has a wonderful conservatory and terrace. Thanks to its elevated location, it commands a wonderful view of the region and the Rhine. The food is fresh, classic cuisine with seasonal and regional influences served in a four- or five-course set menu format or à la carte. Appetising options include "Schloss Bouillabaisse", beef tenderloin Wellington, braised beef roulade and crêpes Suzette flambéed tableside. Various types of caviar also feature on the menu. Simple regional plates such as Spundekäs (spiced cream cheese) or "Rheingauer Schnittchen" (crusty bread with spreads) are also delicious with a glass of wine. Tip: There is also a wine shop.

Name: Schlüssel
Description: Tanja Grandits, known from Restaurant Stucki in Basel, has developed an intentionally easy-going and accessible concept. The kitchen turns out fresh, contemporary and creative dishes, including the occasional Grandits signature. Besides an appealing à la carte selection, including dishes such as "crustacean bisque, prawn dumpling, tomato compote" and "ricotta gnocchi, lemon cream, cauliflower", there is a four- or five-course evening set menu (regular or vegetarian) and a three- or four-course lunch set menu. Marten Harder's cuisine is accompanied by a carefully curated wine list featuring superb bottles, mainly from Switzerland. The service, headed up by Edi Magalhães (formerly of Casa Caminada), is polished, well organised and always attentive to diners' wishes. You are made to feel genuinely welcome. The clean-lined, contemporary interior is tastefully understated, and the small lounge by the entrance is particularly inviting. The sheltered, peaceful terrace, set away from the street, is another highlight.

Name: Schmidhofer im Palais
Description: In close proximity to the Graz Museum, this restaurant has a tasteful, modern interior and a high vaulted ceiling. The street view from the tables right by the window means you can watch the world go by as you eat. The terrace in the courtyard is wonderful in summer. International dishes such as "tuna sashimi rolls meet tuna tartare" are served, as well as Austrian dishes such as the impeccably prepared Wiener schnitzel – the salad of Graz-grown butterhead lettuce is a great accompaniment. The extremely polite and attentive service – the team is always on hand with a smile – also contributes to the pleasant atmosphere.

Name: Schmidt's
Description: This restaurant is housed in the Hellerauer Werkstätten für Handwerkskunst (a workshop founded in 1909 by Karl Schmidt). Served in a modern bistro atmosphere, the classically based food has seasonal and regional influences, and is made with carefully selected ingredients, which are prepared for maximum flavour and minimum fuss. Having difficulty deciding? Then go for the surprise menu ("Schmidt's Karte rauf und runter"). The affordable lunch deal goes down a treat, and the terrace is also lovely.

Name: Schmitte
Description: This is the fine dining restaurant of the long-established Hotel Schweizerhof. The small space is inviting, with an elegant and cosy feel, and service is provided by a friendly and attentive team. The dishes are rooted in classic cuisine and draw on modern influences and the seasons. The six-course set menu is predominantly made up of regional ingredients. A vegetarian version is also available upon advance request. N.B. The set menu price is to be paid in advance. In the hotel garden, there is a sun terrace and a bar.

Name: Schneider Stube
Description: Hotel Tuchmacher, ensconced in a pretty Renaissance town house with this delightfully cosy restaurant, is an institution here in Görlitz. The classic regional menu includes dishes such as Wiener schnitzel, stewed rabbit leg on Leipziger Allerlei vegetables, and stewed brook trout roll on pickled vegetables. Almost all of the wines are also available by the glass. In summer, the courtyard with its terrace is absolutely idyllic! "Bleicherstube" and "Zunftsaal" are their attractive salons. The location in the heart of the old town is charming – it is next to the church (Pfarrkirche St Peter and Paul) and not far from the Lausatian Neiße River that borders Germany, Poland and the Czech Republic.

Name: Schorre
Description: The top floor of this entirely revamped 18C salt barn is home to a fashionable, stripped-back restaurant decked in raw materials that commands a panoramic view over the Somme Bay. According to the dictionary, a schorre (or a salt marsh) refers to an “upper coastal intertidal zone of thick mud, covered by grass and regularly flooded by high tides”. Chef François-Xavier Sailly regularly renews his creative gourmet score with unexpected combinations.

Name: Schorse im Leineschloss
Description: This pleasingly down-to-earth restaurant is the second in the cube-like extension of the Leineschloss, along with Votum. The flavoursome food is made with select ingredients and draws on French influences. Delicious examples include the fish soup or the Charolais beef bourguignon. It's lovely to dine on the terrace with views onto the weir (Leinewehr) or the square, Platz der Göttinger Sieben.

Name: Schotte-Sepp-Stube / Flickflauder
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Whether you choose to dine in the cosy Schotte-Sepp-Stube, the bright Veranda or the contemporary, minimalist-style Flickflauder, you’re guaranteed good-quality, seasonally inspired cuisine and friendly service at this restaurant, which hosts an “Appenzell evening” with a buffet every Wednesday. The à la carte is available to non-resident guests from 8pm onwards.

Name: Schranners Waldhorn
Description: Maximilian and Marie-Luise Schranner's establishment is a haven of comfort and calm. They have lovingly transformed this traditional inn with a tasteful interior design concept. At the helm, Maximilian Schranner specialises in classic cuisine and proposes three set menus: the "Menü Gourmet", the "Menü vegetarisch" and the "Wirthaus-Menü" – but you can also order dishes from these à la carte. There is also a very reasonably priced set menu at lunchtime. On warm days, the gorgeous terrace on the Seebach with its views of the castle is a particular highlight.

Name: Schulhus
Description: In a building that once housed the village school, this restaurant has a history that stretches far back. Gabi and Herbert Strahammer never tire of treating their guests to a relaxed yet stylish gourmet experience – their accessible cuisine is always connected to the region. In a friendly, pared-back ambience, they serve pleasantly uncomplicated, fresh and flavourful dishes, such as ravioli with Langenegger Schottenkäse smoked cheese, herbs, spinach, lemon sauce, or pike from Lake Constance, spinach leaves, roast vegetables, ricotta gnocchi. On-point wine recommendations from the owner.

Name: Schuppen 13
Description: The Pusceddu family’s restaurant is located right on the marina and from the outside looks a little like a boathouse. The food within is classic Italian cuisine meticulously prepared using fresh produce. Try the delicious baby squid braised in tomato stock with pan-fried polenta.

Name: Schupps
Description: Regina and Markus Schupp, after whom this restaurant is named, are both professionally trained chefs. Here they rustle up seasonal dishes inspired by the cuisines of France and Germany. Delicious examples include scallops au gratin with green asparagus, Jerusalem artichoke and almond, or venison ragout with cranberries, Brussels sprout leaves and sour cream. Those who wish to savour a more extensive meal can put together their own set menu comprising three to five courses for a fixed price. At lunchtime, the inexpensive daily specials are ideal for a quick meal. This friendly little restaurant also has a terrace for sunny days. Tip: free parking available along the street.

Name: Schwane 1404
Description: In this centuries-old inn in the beautiful old town, this is a truly charming alternative to the fine dining restaurant. Both the inviting, rustic-style restaurant room and fantastic inner courtyard are appealing places to eat. In the evening, you can order modern-inspired classic dishes à la carte or opt for the "Romantik" set menu. Many of the ingredients are locally sourced; some of the vegetables are from their own garden, and they have their own wines. Hearty meals (‘Brotzeit’) are served at lunchtime.

Name: Schwanen
Description: Here, the Swabian Jura theme is writ large. The menu changes with the seasons and puts the emphasis on top-quality ingredients, most of which are sourced from the surrounding area. A huge panorama of the Swabian Jura landscape is the most striking feature of the modern yet cosy dining area – it couldn't be more apt. Tip: Given the restaurant's proximity to OUTLETCITY, keen shoppers might consider an overnight stay in one of the hotel's stylish guestrooms.

Name: Schwanen
Description: This family business has been going for three generations. The dishes served in this chic, modern restaurant are made with preference for regional produce and sing with freshness and flavour. For a bistro alternative, Karl Benz Stube has a short menu featuring traditional Swabian fare. There are also suitable spaces for special occasions available and practical guestrooms with contemporary decor. Tip: the "Kultur & Genuss" events.

Name: Schwartz's Deli
Description: This restaurant is as quintessentially Montreal as Notre-Dame Basilica or Mont Royal. As soon as you cross the threshold, you are immersed in history: covering an entire wall, photos, illustrations, and articles chart the existence of this institution, which will celebrate its centenary in 2028. To avoid the queues, aim for off-peak times, sit at the counter, or share a table. Needless to say, the menu includes steak, entrecôte, chicken, and foie gras, but it is the famous smoked meat that is the main draw. Their recipe sees beef brisket marinated in the house's own spice blend, smoked, steamed, thinly sliced, and served on rye bread smeared with mustard. If you want to stick with tradition, wash it all down with a cherry soda.

Name: Schwarzer Adler
Description: This inn dating back to 1482 is extremely cosy and serves delicious food. The appealing à la carte selection whets the appetite with traditional home-style dishes such as Wiener schnitzel, cordon bleu and game ragout, as well as classic gourmet dishes such as "medium rare venison loin, red cabbage, brioche dumplings and Brussels sprouts". In charge of this culinary offering is chef duo Marco Gatterer and Mario Naschenweng. Rustic-style tables without tablecloths; wooden benches and floorboards, as well as decorative details such as vintage pendant lamps and lots of small pictures framed on the walls make for a charming atmosphere. Attentive service.

Name: Schwarzfischer
Description: This restaurant enjoys a gorgeous location in a modern cuboid building by the monastery pond – the terrace affords stunning views of the surroundings. Inside, you can peek into the kitchen and watch freshly caught fish being grilled over an open charcoal flame. Specialities such as char tartare, teriyaki‑glazed fillet of stick‑grilled fish, or "milkmaid-style" trout all feature fish from the restaurant's own on-site fish farm – talk about local sourcing! The extensive à la carte selection caters not just to fish enthusiasts but also features vegetarian options and meat dishes. Cap off your meal with house-made Tyrolean milk soft ice cream. Tip: Located on the Inn River cycle route, this place is the perfect spot for a mid-ride pit stop.

Name: Schwarzmatt
Description: Served à la carte or as a set menu, classic cuisine made with seasonal produce is the order of the day here. The upscale interior is very comfortable, with harmonious, lovingly arranged decorative objects – it certainly does full justice to the luxurious setting of the traditional holiday hotel of the same name in which this restaurant is housed. For overnight stays, there are elegant country-house-style guestrooms – this is after all the sister hotel of Baiersbronn's Hotel Bareiss. Make a beeline for the gorgeous garden terrace in summer. A must in the afternoon: cakes made to Hermine Bareiss's old recipes!

Name: Schwarzreiter Restaurant
Description: This fine dining restaurant boasts an exclusive location in the famous Maximilianstraße, more precisely within the legendary Munich luxury hotel Vier Jahreszeiten, complete with its own entrance from the street. The atmosphere is elegant without being stuffy; indeed, the sophisticated, modern and chic interior makes for a pleasingly urban ambience. The approachable and well-trained front-of-house team, who are always attentive and courteous but by no means intrusive, is the perfect fit. Then there is the cosmopolitan cuisine of Franz-Josef Unterlechner, who uses top-notch ingredients from the region and beyond. The Balfego tuna cheek, white onion, Alba truffle, for example, showed us how successfully he brings to life his own ideas. A good all-day alternative, should you need one, is the pleasant Tagesbar, where the food is cooked by the same team. Incidentally, the name ‘Schwarzreiter’ comes from a small fish from the Königssee.

Name: Schweizer Wirt
Description: This place has been synonymous with tasty cuisine for years. The fresh, regional dishes are made with excellent ingredients. Stripped back to the essentials, they eschew any frills. The atmosphere in the restaurant is charming and the waitstaff are friendly. This beautifully situated traditional inn also has a fabulous terrace. You can park directly in front of the building.

Name: Schweizers Restaurant
Description: Originally opened in 1903 as Schweizer Hof, this restaurant is housed in a painstakingly restored listed building. In the aesthetically pleasing Jugendstil setting of this neighbourhood restaurant, the atmosphere is welcoming, thanks in no small part to the charming staff. A well-coordinated team in both the kitchen and front of house ensures a wonderful evening. Savour the five- to seven-course set menu, which also comes in a vegetarian version. The flavoursome dishes showcase precise technique and high-quality ingredients. There is a well-curated wine list, as well as pairings by the glass. The quiet shady courtyard terrace is delightful in summer.

Name: Schwitzer's PUR
Description: There have been some developments at Schwitzer's. In the newly refurbished rooms of the former fine dining restaurant with floor-to-ceiling windows affording views of the park grounds, diners are invited to embark on a culinary adventure that takes its cue from the seasons. Depending on the time of year, varying styles of cuisine are proposed – à la carte or as a three-course surprise set menu. Schwitzer's Hotel am Park has upscale guestrooms.

Name: Schéiss
Description: Schéiss sports a classy contemporary brasserie slant paired with classical culinary know-how in a match made in heaven. The seasoned front-of-house team ensures that you lack for nothing as they seamlessly provide tableside service with flair and talent. The score shines the spotlight on a cast of patriotic classics like shrimp fritters and Liège-style meatballs, all of which with a weakness for powerful sauces and delicate new spins on traditional recipes. The fillet of seabass, impeccably cooked on the skin, is paired with a frothy girolle-flavoured cream, mashed potatoes and steamed spinach. Rather than surprises, you can expect a serious lineup of family favourites that never fails to deliver.

Name: Schützen Donaueschingen
Description: Steeped in tradition, this restaurant in the town centre is mentioned as a tavern in a written record that dates back to 1724. In a warm and welcoming atmosphere, a friendly, attentive and professional team serves ambitious dishes made with excellent ingredients. Chef Marco Garofalo incorporates regional elements as well as Mediterranean influences. Take, for example, the lamb done two ways – "loin with a pecorino crust and shoulder, aubergine, bell pepper, basil gnocchi". Diners have the choice between a conventional and a vegetarian set menu, as well as à la carte dishes.

Name: Scilla
Address: 504 Panyu Road, Changning, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list
Description: Scilla is a blue-flowered Mediterranean plant, a nod to the fact that this restaurant focuses on the region's food, but with a twist – local ingredients, especially seafood, are given the Mediterranean treatment, for a unique fusion cuisine. The signature BBQ Taizhou yellow croaker with bouillabaisse and rouille boasts crispy skin, rich broth and creamy sauce. The underground wine cellar carries some rare finds from the Mediterranean coast.

Name: Scola
Description: Situated in the heart of the Ligurian hinterland, this country house is a real gem, surrounded by a garden that resembles a painting with an English-style lawn that ripples in the wind. Since 1926, the Scola family, now in the fourth generation, have offered guests a friendly welcome here, serving cuisine that is a delight for the tastebuds. In the warm dining room, where the wooden floor and exposed beams hint at the building’s history, guests enjoy traditional local dishes that have been reinterpreted with a modern twist, such as spaghetti with grapefruit, purple prawns and sea lettuce – an explosion of flavours!

Name: Scoria
Description: ‘Scoria’ refers to a type of volcanic rock, one which inspires some of the interior design at this chic modern restaurant on the banks of the Brda river. A window into the kitchen allows you to watch the chefs as they craft classic European dishes such as lobster tail with saffron risotto, alongside more Polish creations like duck leg with potato dumplings. Many of the dishes can be made extra luxurious by adding black truffle or Antonius caviar.

Name: Scorrybreac
Address: 7 Bosville Terrace, Portree, Isle of Skye, IV51 9DG, United Kingdom
Description: The rugged, rural beauty of the Isle of Skye is a wonderful accompaniment to any meal – and so it is at this sharing plates operation named after the chef's parents' house, where he ran is first pop-up. 'Scorrybreac' also means 'speckled rock', something you can glimpse on the mountains in the distance. The restaurant itself is a small and simply furnished place, with chatty and charming service adding to its appeal. The creative modern cooking makes use of the Skye larder, including meats from the hills and seafood from the harbour below.

Name: Scott's
Address: 20 Mount Street, Mayfair, London, W1K 2HE, United Kingdom
Description: Scott's is proof that a restaurant can have a long, proud history and still be fashionable, glamorous and relevant. It has a terrific clubby atmosphere and if you’re in a two then the counter is a great spot. The choice of prime quality fish and shellfish is impressive.

Name: Scratch Restaurant
Description: Disciples of the Slow Food movement, Estelle and Andreas Baehr are passionate about showcasing premium fresh, organic and local produce. Beautifully balanced and seamlessly crafted, the lunch and dinner set menus are a culinary masterclass – dishes such as pollock served with saffron-infused grenaille potatoes, cockles and emulsion of rockfish soup tick all the boxes. Good recommendations when it comes to biodynamic wines.

Name: Scrigno del Duomo
Description: In the city’s elegant drawing-room quarter, amid the striking palazzi of the historic center, the same refined atmosphere pervades the restaurant’s dining rooms. Seafood plays a minor role here; instead, the kitchen embraces regional specialties such as canederli, polenta, freshwater fish, roasted meats, and, naturally, strudel.

Name: Scuderie Sabaude
Address: via Amedeo di Savoia 5, Pollenzo, 12042, Italy
Description: Just steps from the University of Gastronomic Sciences in Pollenzo, the restaurant is reached through a timeless courtyard, enhanced by a meticulously tended garden. Within the rustic spaces of the former royal stables, a cuisine takes shape that showcases a selection of top-tier meats, cooked strictly over charcoal. Center stage is Piedmontese scottona (young heifer offered in various aging stages) alongside cuts of Chianina and Alpina beef, the result of careful sourcing and expert preparation designed to highlight texture and flavor.

Name: Scully
Address: 4 St. James's Market, St James’s, London, SW1Y 4AH, United Kingdom
Description: With a diverse heritage and having lived and worked all over the world, it's no surprise that Ramael Scully brings an array of international influences to his self-titled restaurant. From Malaysia to Sydney via India and China, you'll go on a culinary journey throughout the chef's complex and distinctive dishes. Unlike little else you'll find in the UK, the cooking has an appealing vitality thanks to its punchy flavours and the shelves laden with spices, pickles, preserves and oils. Both a tasting menu and sharing-inclined à la carte are available.

Name: Se7en Bites
Address: 617 N. Primrose Dr., Orlando, FL, 32803, USA
Description: A large sign just off the street signals the entrance to this bakery-café. Its bright green structure is hard to miss; inside, diners will discover a large space with wood paneling and a corrugated metal ceiling. Another wall decked with Bundt cake pans makes for a cool design feature. This is an undoubtedly inviting spot, with a friendly staff that churns out hearty American-Southern dishes in big portions and small prices.The chicken biscuit is a tender-fried revelation spread with cream cheese and pepper jelly. Next up, chicken pot pie available in hearty portions. Marked by a golden crust covering chunks of meat, peas and carrots, this is a forever favorite—and fittingly so. The large, mouthwatering display of sweet treats reminds you to save room.

Name: SeBE
Address: Avenida de las Islas Canarias 8, Costa Teguise, 35508, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: A must for visitors to Lanzarote! The interior, which reflects the colours and iconic architecture of the island, provides the backdrop for superb fish and seafood, although Santi’s delicious and intense rice dishes also take centre stage. Make sure you sample the spectacular prawns from La Santa!

Name: Sea Fu
Address: Four Seasons Resort Dubai Hotel, Jumeirah Beach Road, Jumeirah 2, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Watching the sun set from a table on the sumptuous terrace of this delightful and elegant beachfront restaurant, you feel the stresses of the day fade away; endearing service from keen staff also helps to ensure an extra-special dining experience. Vibrant, Asian-influenced seafood dishes are fresh and full of flavour. The sashimi, maki and nigiri selection, as well their tempura and wok-fried dishes showcase their strong Japanese techniques.

Name: Seacliff
Address: Sandy Cove Hotel, Old Coast Road, Combe Martin, Berrynarbor, EX34 9SR, United Kingdom
Description: The family-run Sandy Cove Hotel is the home for this long-standing, intimate restaurant which comes with a jewel of a terrace and commanding views of the bay. The colourful, modern dishes make use of quality seasonal ingredients, with a focus on local seafood – the mussel-stuffed sea bream shows the kitchen at its best, displaying technical precision and a good balance of flavours and textures. If you're celebrating, go for the tasting menu with accompanying wine pairings. The warm, friendly service adds to the experience.

Name: Seasonality
Address: 26 Queen Street, Maidenhead, SL6 1HZ, United Kingdom
Description: What started out as a produce shop has morphed into a bright and airy restaurant, which is run with a lovely personal touch by Wesley Smalley as he cooks at an on-view island kitchen. As its name and history suggests, seasonal ingredients are the foundation of the cooking, put front and centre in assured, colourful dishes that carry an appealing clarity of flavour. Regular supper evenings offer tasting menus inspired by the produce of the moment, while they still offer the 'dine at home' boxes they've done since day one.

Name: Seasons
Address: Grand Palace Hotel, Pils iela 12, Riga, 1050, Latvia
Description: The luxurious Grand Palace Hotel plays host to this sumptuous restaurant, as well as a supremely comfortable bar which comes packed with antiques and fine art – be sure to either start or end your night here. Seasonal dishes are themed around the world’s greatest painters, so are naturally both visually striking and full of colour. The likes of lightly smoked trout with béarnaise sauce are a joy to eat, and if you spot the toffee pudding with buttermilk sorbet, be sure to order it. The wine list contains some premium bottles, and plush bedrooms mean you don't have to far to go once fully sated.

Name: Secchu Yokota
Address: 199 E. 3rd St., New York, NY, 10009, USA
Description: This spot flies under the radar somewhat, and that’s just the way their loyal fan base likes it. Those who understand the fine art of tempura know how pristine the quality is here, where diners are treated to a mouthwatering omakase featuring succulent red shrimp, Japanese eggplant, and lightly battered anago. You probably won’t need it, but lemon, wasabi salt and seaweed salt are provided as enhancements. The man to thank for these treats is Chef Yokota, who takes his craft (and business) seriously, putting his clients first. Dining here is an intimate and deeply personal experience that highlights ingredients sourced mostly from Japan. As a bonus, his tempura is typically bookended by unique dishes that display his French culinary training.

Name: See Na Nuan Café
Address: 164/160 Mu 14, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: This 500-seat crowd pleaser close to Khon Kaen University serves flavoursome central Thai fare and Isan dishes in an industrial-style house with a huge outdoor dining area. Inside is all brick and black steel; outside, the steel continues in a birdcage-like dining area next to more seating centred around a lawn. Seafood tanks attest to the food’s freshness; the grilled snakehead fish served with spicy dip is recommended. Chill live music features nightly.

Name: See No Evil Pizza
Address: 210 W. 50th St., New York, NY, 10019, USA
Description: There are just some places that are so New York they couldn't be found anywhere else. See No Evil Pizza is just that. It could be the location in a subway station, or it could be because they're doling out an iconic New York staple—pizza—but don't be fooled by the environs, as a treasure awaits inside. It's casual with a hint of punk, with 80s classics overhead and black-and-white checkered floors. Sit back and let the commuters fly by as you snack on small plates like toast with sardines or a seasonal bowl of beautiful beans in a walnut sauce before moving on to the pizza. There are always specials, but the Hell pie, a thin crust variety topped with spicy meat, is always good. Finish with vanilla soft serve with olive oil and sea salt.

Name: Seebistro Belvédère
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The location right by Lake Lucerne is fabulous! This modern bistro shares its premises with the fine dining restaurant and benefits from the same stunning views over the water. Here, too, Fabian Interbitzin and his team are responsible for the food, serving up contemporary French cuisine with the odd Mediterranean influence. The set menu comprises two to six courses, which can also be ordered à la carte. A range of classic dishes is also available. The cuisine is pleasingly accessible without sacrificing elegance.

Name: Seed
Address: L1-04, Block E, The Five@KPD, 49 Jalan Dungun, Bukit Damansara, Kuala Lumpur, 50490, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: Splashes of earthy colours and cool neutrals adorn the inviting space and the seats at the wave-shaped counter command a fascinating view of the open kitchen. Just like at its sibling, Whitegrass, in Singapore, the Japanese chef crafts a European lineup from Japanese produce and seasonings. Seafood dishes stand out in particular with creative twists and light seasoning. Crusty and airy, their focaccia is unmissable, especially with creamy whipped butter.

Name: Seegarten
Description: For over 30 years, this elegant restaurant with a pleasant terrace has been making the most of its wonderful location on the marina. The menu is inspired by the seasons; there is also an appetising set menu, which changes on a monthly basis, but the classics are just as much in demand. Book your spot at the traditional seafood festival – Festival de Fruits de Mer – from late November to late January. Other highlights are the extensive wine list, and friendly, professional service.

Name: Seehalde
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Run by the Gruler brothers, this restaurant boasts a stunning lakeside location – tables on the terrace are much coveted in summer! The fresh and ambitious cuisine is also a major draw. The menu takes its cue from the region and the seasons with a classic bent. Fish from Lake Constance is also served and is even the focus of a three- or four-course set menu for two people. There is also a set menu based on regional classics. Alternatively, take your pick from the appealing à la carte selection. The well-curated wine list includes some gems, too. Well-drilled front-of house team. Tip: Take some homemade bouillabaisse in a jar with you to enjoy at home. There are well-kept guestrooms as well - most of them look out to the lake.

Name: Seerestaurant 1884
Description: As the name suggests, this restaurant enjoys a splendid location. Housed in the long-established See-Villa hotel, right by Lake Millstatt, it has a wonderful terrace that extends right to the water's edge! The elegant interior has floor-to-ceiling windows affording unobstructed views of the lake. The menu is rather diverse, featuring international, regional, traditional, seasonal fare – game and freshly caught fish from the lake take centre stage. The bar in the middle of the restaurant is sure to draw the eye.

Name: Seespitz
Description: An absolute highlight here is the lakeside location. The trendy, elegantly designed restaurant flows seamlessly onto the terrace – with every table affording a view of the water. Creatively inspired Slow Food cuisine is presented in an appealing à la carte selection that marries regional produce with international accents. There are plenty of vegetarian and vegan options. The predominantly Austrian wine list is supplemented by Old World and a few New World picks, alongside an array of sparkling wines. For those wishing to stay overnight, the Falkensteiner Schlosshotel Velden, connected via an underground passageway, offers stylish accommodation.

Name: Seifu
Address: 4F, Kissuisen, Bangkok Marriott Hotel The Surawongse, 262 Surawong Road, Si Phraya, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: On the fourth floor of Kissuisen at the Marriott, this intimate restaurant has two rooms, each seating nine. Veteran chef Yuichi Mitsui and chef Kazutomo Matayoshi extend the typical kaiseki omakase menu to include sushi and more, deploying an array of techniques. Thai produce – fresh crab meat and spring water sourced from Ayutthaya for the soups – meets Japanese finesse, and illustrations by Mitsui appear on the menus. Two sittings daily; book well ahead.

Name: Seir
Description: The sunny conservatory of this swish restaurant immediately catches the eye. The leather-seated lounge is ideal to sip a drink while admiring chef Thomas at work. An accomplished artist, he composes his visual masterpieces right on the counter. Intelligent combinations, precise and meticulous cooking. This youthful chef gives a free rein to his creative flair and is clearly determined to go places! A genuine treat for the senses.

Name: Seis Vecinos
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Sitting on a prominent corner at the base of an ornate yet classic NYC building is this now-well ensconced restaurant. The interior is sunny and welcoming with a gracious staff to boot; the menu is melting pot Central America featuring papusas from El Salvador, baleadas from Honduras, and fajitas from Mexico. Guacamole made tableside in a molcajete is a great way to begin the meal before a main dish like enchiladas made with tender corn tortillas stuffed with shredded, seasoned chicken, topped with a smoky red sauce, crema, and queso.Breakfast delivers hearty offerings such as picaditas verdes with carne al gusto or huevos revueltos con verduras y casamiento.

Name: Seixo by Vasco Coelho Santos
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Looking for a peaceful refuge surrounded by nature? This is the ideal spot. The restaurant is located at Quinta do Seixo, home to the iconic Sandeman Port wines, on the banks of the Douro and surrounded by century-old vineyards. Here, you can pair one of the available wine experiences with a memorable meal bearing the signature of renowned chef Vasco Coelho Santos. The menu reflects seasonality and regional produce, with fire shining both on the grill and in the wood-fired oven, turning out traditional dishes with a contemporary twist, such as Barriga de porco, pork belly, with beans and a courgette-and-pineapple salad, or the crisp Croquete de Choco, cuttlefish croquette, with prawn salad and coriander. The space is open daily, lunchtime only!

Name: Seki Restaurant
Address: Tekelli, Kayabaş Sokak No:23, Uçhisar, Nevşehir, 50240, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Seki is located on the ground floor of luxury hotel Argos, which was once a monastery built into a hillside that makes for a truly magnificent setting. Be sure to allow time for a stroll along the paths leading through the garden. Inside, you can have an aperitif in the romantic lounge and take in the breathtaking view of the valley, then move into the restaurant itself, which has that distinctively welcoming Cappadocian feel. In these splendid surroundings, diners tuck into local Anatolian dishes with a Mediterranean twist. For example, the chefs balance the sweetness of confit pumpkin with a light tahini paste, sesame seeds and chopped walnuts. The extensive menu encompasses classics such as mezze, salads and lamb specialities, as well as pasta and vegan options. Featuring some 300 labels, the wine list is certainly worth exploring.

Name: Selam
Address: 5494 Central Florida Pkwy., Orlando, FL, 32821, USA
Description: This graciously run restaurant offers a rare taste of the Horn of Africa, specifically the cuisine of Ethiopia and Eritrea. Set at the corner of a shopping center, it boasts a commanding presence with bold signage and a nicely arranged alfresco section. Inside the incense-scented space, there are tiled floors, windows draped with woven fabrics and turquoise seating for a pop of color.Boldly flavored but subtly spiced stews arrive with spongy injera for sopping. The menu is meat-focused but there are plenty of plant-based items on offer. The combination platter is a great way to sample a bevy of bites, including the beef key wot seasoned with berbere, beef alecha wot rich with turmeric; gomen, or stewed collard greens; and house-made cottage cheese.

Name: Selanne Steak Tavern
Address: 1464 S. Coast Hwy., Laguna Beach, CA, 92651, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Once a home, this historic setting on Pacific Coast Highway now houses a winning steakhouse. Inside, a variety of settings welcome guests, ranging from the upstairs Loft, the bistro-style Wine Library, the handsome Tavern, or outside on the Veranda or Sunset Terrace. The buzzy bar is also a favorite perch for a crowd that's both relaxed and regulars. Steak is revered in this place and it lives up to its promise with tender, well marbled meat, but the kitchen ratchets it up with expert cooking (and dousing it in butter never hurts). Thick seared mushrooms in a Madeira reduction are a nice touch, and creamy, buttery mashed potatoes are a must, but don't monkey around when it comes to dessert—Selanne's monkey bread can't be missed.

Name: Select Oyster Bar
Description: Long a local favorite, Chef Michael Sherpa's oyster bar is located on the ground floor of a Back Bay rowhouse, and the intimate setting, dominated by an L-shaped pewter bar, radiates good vibes. High quality seafood is the order of the day, be it the daily crudo, crab salad or honey-butter dressed Maine uni toast. The icy plateaux is a splurge-worthy indulgence, best shared with friends (or not). In true oyster bar fashion, the menu is supplemented by a daily offering of oysters and other shellfish. Hearty appetites will appreciate the Casco Bay halibut, beautifully cooked and plated with shaved cauliflower, lightly pickled onions, almonds and golden raisins for forkfuls of flavor. Not feeling like fish? The prime ribeye is for you.

Name: Sellae
Description: Sellae (‘chair’ in Latin) is the other restaurant of Thibault Sombardier, who also operates Mensae (‘table’) in the 19th. The chef rolls out nostalgic bistro fare, chalked up on a blackboard, with a distinct penchant for the South of France. In a suitably bistro-style interior, you will sample top-notch ingredients, crafted lovingly and expertly: ravioles of snails in a herb butter; confit pork cheeks, mash and parmesan. The chef’s signature dessert is warm chocolate mousse, vanilla ice cream and crumble spiked with fleur de sel. The lunchtime menu is a steal!

Name: Selvatico
Address: via Silvio Pellico 19, Rivanazzano Terme, 27055, Italy
Description: Opened in 1912 and now run by the fourth generation of the same family, this is one of the best restaurants in the Oltrepò Pavese area. If you’re looking to sample the gastronomic delights of this region, you’ll find a whole host of delicious specialities on offer, from charcuterie and stews to boiled meats and excellent fresh pasta. Attractively furnished guestrooms with the same nostalgic feel as the restaurant are also available.

Name: Sem Porta
Description: It adds the gastronomic touch to Sublime Comporta, a luxury hotel (awarded a MICHELIN Key) that delights with its location in the heart of nature, in a lush pine forest just a few kilometres from the beach. Here, as they put it, they celebrate “the fusion of tradition and innovation”, drawing on international flavours while still adapting them to the character and tastes of Portuguese cuisine. In its spacious, tranquil dining room, where the kitchen can be seen through glass windows, you’re presented with a menu that exalts Portuguese cooking in perfect harmony with European classics and Latin American-inspired dishes, always grounded in native produce and ingredients harvested from its own organic garden. Sharing this approach, Sem Porta champions “seasonal cooking, rooted in local traditions and inspired by the world”.

Name: Semilla
Description: In a street teeming with restaurants and art galleries, Semilla ("seed" in Spanish) is depicted by an exceptionally friendly vibe and a trendy, industrial-style decor. In the open kitchen, a youthful and enthusiastic team works with hand-picked fresh produce to roll out a veggie-heavy, set menu-à la carte lineup: velvety Jerusalem artichoke soup, pomegranate vinegar-laced emulsion of beurre noisette and toasted brioche with tonka butter; honey roasted endives and morel mushrooms in flaky pastry; sautéed line-caught croaker, potato cake glazed in lemon thyme and Noilly Prat sauce. Delicious virtuoso cooking that hits the spot every time!

Name: Sempre Oggi
Address: 164 W. 75th St., New York, NY, 10023, USA
Description: From its apartments to its restaurants, New York is well known for its diminutive spaces. And then there's Sempre Oggi. This Upper West Side spot is the exact opposite. Cavernous and contemporary with gold busts enhancing the space, it's Italian in every way, especially on the menu. While they have plenty of the usual suspects, these dishes are given a bit of flair (think fresh calamari with fresh herbs and crème fraîche). Order the rigatoni for a plate of house-made pasta interlaced with crispy guanciale and sauteed onion in a roasted tomato sauce, then for dessert, go classic tiramisu for an on-point iteration in all of its fluffy, creamy delight.

Name: Senda
Description: The restaurant lies near Kitano Tenmangu Shrine, renowned for its plum blossoms, so beloved of Sugawara no Michizane. As befits this heritage, as well as its location in Hakubaicho (‘White Plum town’), the house features ume on its bowls of stewed items. Unagi dishes pay homage to the restaurant run by the chef’s family in Fukui. Using the same dipping sauce as his family’s shop, the chef serves grilled unagi over rice at lunch and kabayaki for dinner. Unripe plums for frozen desserts come from a former classmate, and sake is brought in from Wakasa, showcasing the specialities of the chef’s native region.

Name: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup
Address: Kaki Bukit 511 Market & Food Centre, #01-31/32, 511 Bedok North Street 3, 460511, Singapore
Description: For over 60 years, foodies have been coming here for black chicken herbal soup. Double-boiled for at least 2 hours, it has pronounced herbal flavours. Each order is enough for two people. The pork offal noodles are also worth trying.

Name: Sennarizushi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: Until the previous generation, the shop had focused on sushi deliveries, but the current owner transformed it into a sushi restaurant. He changed the sushi, too, reflecting his training in the Edomae style. Sushi is served omakase style, but the chef also picks up on guests’ preferences and chooses pieces accordingly; if the guest likes to drink, he increases the number of small dishes that go well with sake. Seafood items from Osaka Bay, such as sea bream, sand shrimp, and egg cockle, are woven into the mix. Sushi is formed using red-vinegar rice.

Name: Sens
Description: In the Doutre neighbourhood near the River Maine, Sens is tucked away behind an unobtrusive façade – you will need to ring the bell to enter. After a dark corridor, you enter a characterful dining room where the charm of old stone vaults is mixed with contemporary lines and soft lighting. Chef Nicolas Adamopulos delivers a several-course surprise menu, including a vegetarian version, that keeps pace with the seasons and is sourced locally and organically, rolling out sophisticated modern cuisine that bears his creative stamp. A few standouts include mint, lemon balm and chamomile herbal tea, an inspired trout recipe and plant-based compositions packed in vibrant flavours.

Name: Sensato
Description: Sensato is a good choice for an Omakase dining experience while seated at a traditional Japanese counter. This small, minimalist restaurant, located in an elevated section of Barcelona, is run by a pair of chefs who combine local ingredients with Japanese-style techniques and preparation which they demonstrate in front of just six guests, in so doing showcasing their mastery with the knife. The menu includes a good selection of sashimi, nigiri, gunkan, temaki etc, which alternate with hot dishes such as black cod and miso soup. We recommend booking via WhatsApp.

Name: Sense
Address: 37F, Mandarin Oriental Tokyo, 2-1-1 Nihombashimuromachi, Chuo-ku, Tokyo, 103-8328, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Perched high above the Mandarin Oriental Tokyo, Sense commands sweeping views that immerse you in the heart of the city. While honouring Cantonese tradition, the chef also seeks a more contemporary flavour. Experience with Hong Kong’s food culture is delicately conveyed through Japanese ingredients. Lunch on weekends and public holidays is also a chance to enjoy dim sum. Shumai and dumplings prepared by the dim sum chef are beautiful to look at too.

Name: Senses
Description: The chic and artistic interior design of The Albus hotel's lounge-like restaurant is bang on trend. Get ready for an explosion of flavours as Eastern spices meet a burst of acidity and a healthy dose of creativity. Vegetables take centre stage in the chef's culinary artistry, as exemplified by the potato spaghetti with autumn truffle and katsuobushi, accompanied by a creamy maitake mushroom sauce and the tangy zest of tosazu. The fact that the chefs like to serve their dishes personally is a sign of their enthusiasm. The exquisite wine list is the icing on the cake.

Name: Senté (Nguyen Quang Bich Street)
Address: 20 Nguyen Quang Bich Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
Description: Step away from the bustling streets of the Old Quarter, down a discreet alley and into this cosy dining venue, which is strewn with green plants and champions healthy food. The artistically presented, modern Vietnamese dishes use flowers, leaves, seeds, stems and roots of the humble lotus plant to create unique, flavourful inventions. As a starter, the shrimp, pomelo and lotus root salad is refreshing and appetising. Advance reservations recommended.

Name: Seoul Dining
Address: 2F, Designhouse, 272 Dongho-ro, Jung-gu, Seoul, 04617, South Korea
Description: Guided by the vision of presenting a culinary journey that captures the essence of Seoul, the establishment combines seasonal ingredients with boundless creativity to bring brilliant, one-of-a-kind dishes to the table. The use of ingredients and sauces that deliver a wide variety of flavours adds to its appeal, reflecting the co-existence of diverse food cultures in Seoul. The contemporary and vibrant dining space also creates a sense of harmony worthy of its buoyant dishes.

Name: Seoul Salon
Address: 28 W. 33rd St., New York, NY, 10001, USA
Description: In what feels like an adult arcade, this place in Koreatown has warehouse floors, gunmetal grey finishes and neon accents. From the same group that gave us Atomix, the food here is all fun and games, a mishmash of influences pitting Korean rice cakes with basil and stracciatella or a block of cheese with shrimp fried in a thin batter. Maybe the dish that says it all is the whimsical mala pork belly, which is both puzzling to behold but also undeniably delicious. Such savory cooking is in the service of a talented bar that knows how to combine, say, peanut butter cachaça and passionfruit. At the close of the meal, banana shaved ice with banana cream, hazelnuts and orange zest makes for a brilliantly refreshing finale.

Name: Seppe Pizza Bar
Address: 3 Navy Pier Ct., Staten Island, NY, 10304, USA
Description: From the breezes blowing off the water to the natural light flooding its contemporary-chic space, this Navy Pier dining retreat is a breath of fresh air.First things first—peruse the cocktail menu, where savory and spicy drinks are a welcome alternative to too-sweet swizzles. Order a house spritz or a Negroni, then settle in to review the sprawling menu. Start with one of their fantastic pizzas with beautiful crispy bottoms, such as the unusually delicious Morty pizza, finished with a layer of pistachio-based pesto with mozzarella, and garnished with burrata and slices of mortadella. And while there are so many shareable plates, be sure to save room for their baked wings with a perfect char, or decadent pastas, like the cacio e pepe, both of which deliver on flavor.

Name: Sequenza
Description: The intimate Sequenza has won a place in the hearts of its many regulars, with a multi-course set menu rightly appreciated for its distinctive and at times inventive take on classic French cuisine. The chef's choice of top-tier ingredients reflects a deep command of the craft. Red mullet fillet with cherry tomatoes, jalapeño, crushed macadamia nuts, melon balls, a rich crab bisque emulsion and an indulgent hollandaise sauce with shaved tonka bean for a touch of spice – a dish that's likely to steal your heart, too.

Name: Seraf Mahmutbey
Address: Mahmutbey Mahallesi, Peyami Safa Caddesi No:38/D, Bağcılar, Istanbul, 34200, Türkiye
Description: Sinem Özler sets great store by goods from local producers. You can taste and see this for yourself, because they are also for sale in the shop of this spacious, modern restaurant, just outside the city centre. For example, she works with Trakya Kivircik lamb in a bid to keep traditional recipes alive. The İçli Köfte with the same lamb is an absolute must. To bring those ancient Anatolian flavours to the table, this chef likes to use a wood-fired oven, and she never loses sight of the changing seasons and her surroundings.

Name: Seraf Vadi
Address: Ayazağa, Kemerburgaz Caddesi No:7G, İç Kapı No:7, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34396, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Start your meal with the wood-fire grilled onion stuffed with rice, spices and currants – a speciality of the house. And be sure to sample the other mezze, such as the piping-hot lahmacun topped with succulent lamb, mint, parsley and a judicious squeeze of lemon. The main courses featuring various cuts of lamb are to die for. This contemporary restaurant close to Vadistanbul Shopping Mall and Galatasaray's football stadium is a celebration of Anatolian culinary heritage.

Name: Seraphine
Address: 324 Blackwell St., Ste. 402, Durham, NC, 27701, USA
Description: Seraphine is nestled in a quiet corner of the restored American Tobacco works. While the large terrace is ideal during the warmer months, the interior's moody, sultry ambience is especially intriguing. It's the kind of place where you'll want to sip one of their classic or creative cocktails at the marble-topped bar before dinner. The menu is equally inspired by its location with Southern classics like fried shrimp and broiled oysters vying for attention alongside gumbo and fried catfish. Be sure to save room for the beignets for a traditional treat.

Name: Serpillo
Address: via di Mezzo 1, località Torre del Colle, Bevagna, 06031, Italy
Description: Situated in a charming medieval village which is also home to a couple of small hotels, this attractive, rustic restaurant in an old olive mill acts as the backdrop for regional and Italian cuisine. Dishes with a touch of modern flavour are presented on a menu which, although not extensive, offers good value for money.

Name: Serẽa Coastal Cuisine
Address: Hotel del Coronado, 1500 Orange Ave., Coronado, CA, 92118, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: If the historic “Hotel Del” is the jewel of Coronado Island, then snagging a seat on Serẽa’s sprawling patio is like nestling into said jewel box. Thanks to its stunning views of the hotel's landscaped grounds and the ocean beyond, this is one of the prettiest perches in all of California. Just be sure to snag a reservation, because you’ll have competition from plenty of wedding parties and conference-goers.Deep-pocketed pescatarians will be delighted by the freshness and sustainability of the fish on offer—from inviting platters of raw oysters and cracked Maine lobster to flash-fried red snapper from Baja, offered by the pound for sharing. And even after the sun finally fades on the million-dollar view, the outdoor fireplace sets an exquisite mood.

Name: Set.
Address: 110, Section 2, Chengde Road, Datong District, Taipei, 103, Taiwan
Description: Far from being stuffy or overly formal, this fine dining spot boasts a friendly, laid-back vibe. Inspired by personal experiences, nature and the seasons, the dishes are underpinned by solid Western technique and packed with Asian flavours. The chef couple gives kitchen scraps a new lease of life as house-made condiments, such as mushroom chilli paste with pumpkin skin, in a bid for zero waste. The wine list comprises natural choices only.

Name: Seta Sushi Restaurant
Description: It was friendship and passion for Japanese cuisine that prompted two young business partners to open this quiet, welcoming restaurant in the heart of Bologna. Situated in a courtyard with medieval origins, Seta Sushi Restaurant has a modern bistro-style dining room, as well as plenty of outdoor space for summer dining. The menu features an impressive selection of traditional Japanese dishes with the occasional personalised touch, all made from top-quality ingredients. Don’t worry if you’re new to Japanese cuisine – Maurilio is front of house to offer guests friendly, expert advice on both food and beverage. The latter includes a choice of sake for those wishing to immerse themselves fully in the Japanese dining experience.

Name: Seten
Address: Aydınlı Mahallesi, Çakmaklı Sokak No:35, Göreme, Nevşehir, 50180, Türkiye
Description: Make your way from the centre of Göreme, past the charming boutiques, to the grounds of Sultan Cave Suites, home to the town's highest-altitude restaurant. The approach has a touch of magic to it – a feeling confirmed the moment you take in the magnificent view from the terrace. This is the perfect spot for watching the sunset! The menu reveals a clear devotion to traditional Anatolian cuisine: yoghurt with candied and fresh fruit or generously stuffed dolmas to start, followed by Cappadocian ravioli stuffed with minced lamb, accompanied by gently simmered chickpeas and yoghurt flavoured with dried herbs. Fruit and vegetables often come from their own garden, and even wine is made on site. Be sure to arrive early as they do not take reservations.

Name: Sette Feinbistro
Description: Somewhat tucked away in the pedestrian precinct, this gem has been run with great dedication by the Tegge family for many years. The name "Feinbistro" encompasses both a delicatessen and a restaurant serving Mediterranean and regional cuisine. Breakfast is also available. Don't forget to purchase delicacies such as jam, cheese and wine etc from the shop to enjoy at home.

Name: Seva
Address: 2F, LYH Building, 714 Jose Abad Santos Street, Barangay Little Baguio, San Juan - Metro Manila, 1500, The Philippines
Location: San Juan - Metro Manila, The Philippines
Description: As one of the trendy restaurants in Metro Manila, Seva was founded by three friends who are passionate about reimagining global dishes with flair. Try their signature dish of vodka rigatoni featuring a hot, peppery tomato sauce topped with rich and creamy burrata for a balanced flavour profile.
