Description: This iconic family-run shop has been packed with locals for more than 50 years. These days, the family’s second generation runs it, but the founder’s talent for cooking dishes like the signature claypot stewed duck with intestines, blood jelly, and feet clearly runs in the family.

Name: Tang Town
Address: BFM 17, Fountain Views, Dubai Mall, Downtown, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Slightly hidden on the mezzanine floor of Dubai Mall’s China Town is this dimly lit Chinese restaurant. An ambient mood encompasses the space, while its menu boasts myriad Cantonese and Sichuan dishes made with prime ingredients, like Wagyu beef and Peking duck paired with caviar – dim sum and freshly baked egg tart are must-tries. Diners can also enjoy Chinese dancing performances in the evening on the small centre stage as they eat. Pro tip: enter through the residence’s door to avoid the busy mall’s foot traffic.

Name: Tanglin (Bukit Damansara)
Address: 57G, Jalan Medan Setia 1, Bukit Damansara, Kuala Lumpur, 50490, Malaysia
Description: Founded in 1948, the family-owned Tanglin is now run by the second generation and the two-storey establishment is well known for its nasi lemak. This delicious family recipe is paired with either sotong (squid), daging (meat) or ayam goreng (fried chicken). Its fragrant rice has the right mix of coconut milk and its sambal tumis, the right level of spiciness. Whether dining in or taking away, the queues are long. Generous portions and prices that make sense.

Name: Tanh Tách
Address: 3 Yet Kieu Street, Cua Nam Ward, Hanoi, 112605, Vietnam
Description: Nestled in a historic French colonial villa, the restaurant occupies two storeys. The chef team exhibits a knack for seafood dishes based on textbook European techniques, thus explaining their prominence on the à la carte menu. Before trying the deftly crafted fish or shellfish, kick off your meal with nori or kimchi rice crackers and tom yum mayo dip. Black chicken consommé is another smash hit.

Name: Tanjiah
Address: Imam Saud Bin Abdulaziz Bin Mohammed Road, King Fahd, Riyadh, 12274, Saudi Arabia
Description: Set within the King Fahd neighbourhood, not too far away from the bustling Financial District, is this Moroccan restaurant with its eye-catching décor. A feeling of warmth starts from the welcome to the interior design, and continues with the service. A sea of lampshades hang from the ceiling and authentic artefacts are strewn across a spacious room, creating an intimate setting, similar to that of a Moroccan home. The menu offers some hearty and flavoursome dishes, with the pastilla and tagine being particularly memorable.

Name: Tannay
Description: The name "Tannay" is a reference to chef Thomas Demuth's birthplace. In fact, his parents still own a vineyard there, and some of their labels feature on the wine list. The French chef has set up shop on Realeneiland, in a building on a corner plot. His restaurant boasts a picturesque waterfront terrace and a romantic decor. Under Alain Caron's mentorship, he crafts familiar dishes that showcase his intimate knowledge of classic French cuisine. Options range from beetroot prepared in various ways with a rich Nantua sauce, to wild duck in puff pastry, and the time-honoured hare à la royale. The ingredients speak for themselves here.

Name: Tanner's Prime Burgers
Description: What happens when a fine dining chef leaves the white tablecloths behind? Enter Tanner's Prime Burgers, from Chef Brandon Rodgers. As expected, this place is all about the hallowed beef; single-source USDA prime, to be exact. Naturally, burgers are the go-to order, available in single or double sizes with toppings like American cheese, bacon, caramelized onions, and more in a brioche bun. Of course, fries are the perfect sidekick, and theirs are fried in beef tallow and double cooked for a perfectly crisp exterior. Still hungry? Order their vanilla tallow ice cream sandwich crafted from two chocolate chip cookies, or sip on a Dutch chocolate milkshake.

Name: Tannery
Address: 10 Quay Street, Dungarvan, X35 XN99, Ireland
Description: Close to the harbour sits this characterful 19C stone tannery that also houses a cookery school. Sit downstairs for small plates at the counter or head upstairs to the bright restaurant. The classically based dishes are generously sized and use good seasonal ingredients – don't overlook the specials either. Stylish bedrooms are spread across two nearby townhouses.

Name: Tano Passami l'Olio
Description: In an elegant residential neighbourhood, Tano Simonato's restaurant welcomes guests with modern design and a refined atmosphere, a prelude to cuisine that tantalises the senses. Italian tradition is clothed in creativity in the dishes: the famous “tirami su” made with cuttlefish and potatoes releases marine aromas and velvety notes, while the honey-glazed pigeon, baked in salt, delights the palate with contrasting sweet and savoury flavours, accompanied by spinach and savoury cherries. Tano sees food as a source of pleasure and enjoyment: the chef comes to the table, tells stories and suggests pairings, with every glass of wine becoming part of an experience that seduces all the senses.

Name: Tante Blanche
Description: Chic, on trend and cheerful, Tante Blanche is a truly inviting space – the terrace out front is always delightful. Chef Charles Ek's surprise menu (vegetarian version available) pays homage to his aunt's cherished recipes. His cuisine is thoroughly contemporary, with a judicious touch of freshness and heat. For example, puffed quinoa-crusted langoustine is beautifully paired with a curry and lemongrass sauce, shellfish oil and mayonnaise, and vadouvan-spiced carrot. Trust the friendly waitstaff to guide you through the thoughtfully curated wine list.

Name: Tante Kee
Description: Tante Kee is a firm favourite. Nestled on a scenic island accessible by ferry, its setting is picture-perfect, with small boats mooring right beside the terrace. The interior is stylish; the exterior has a magical atmosphere. The cuisine is in step with the times and enriched with subtle Asian accents. Think fresh, hand-cut veal tartare with a judicious touch of gochujang providing a spicy Korean kick and a Dutch soya jelly. Impeccable service rounds off the experience. This is one of those warmly inviting places where everything is just right.

Name: Tanzer
Description: Located beneath the belltower in a small hamlet, this restaurant has two romantic 17C Stube-style dining rooms, where Melanie and her sommelier husband Michael delight guests with regional, modern and imaginative cuisine. Most of the ingredients are sourced locally, including from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden. The home-made syrups and jams are highly recommended.

Name: Tao Gie Mie Zhou
Address: Building 9, Hunter Lane, Liede Xipu Street, Tianhe, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: This place serves all the Chaozhou classics, including marinated meats such as crunchy pig's ear or the flavourful, gelatinous pork hock. Raw marinated bivalves and crustaceans like striped prawns and mantis shrimps are not to be missed. For starch, try the creamy congee with 30-year-aged dried radish in claypot, which boasts deep umami – or have it cooked with the seafood of your choice. Check out the chef's recommendations on the blackboard, too.

Name: Tao Tao Ju · Ya Yuan
Address: 6F, Central Tower, 5 Xiancun Road, Zhujiang New Town, Tianhe, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: This upmarket room features a rose gold and olive-green palette, dotted with Lingnan architectural motifs. The kitchen is helmed by an experienced Cantonese chef. Dim sum are made fresh from scratch daily. Stir-fried rice vermicelli in Longmen style is loaded with wok hei - add sweet chilli sauce for a kick. The steamed sunflower seed-fed chicken and soy-marinated chicken impress with mild sweetness, juicy flesh and springy skin.

Name: Tao's
Description: Tao's has you covered if you are in the mood for Euro-Asian cuisine. The wide-ranging menu includes sushi and sashimi, steak tartare, poke bowls and dim sum, plus "Signature Grill" dishes such as Thai-style fillet of sea bass, lime, herbs, ginger, soy. The dishes are accompanied by a fantastic and extensive international wine list. A pleasantly relaxed yet stylishly elegant atmosphere prevails. In summer the cosy terrace is a huge draw, and there is also a bar.

Name: Taokan
Description: Come inside this pretty restaurant in the heart of St-Germain-des-Prés to enjoy light and fragrant Cantonese cuisine that also occasionally veers over to Southeast Asia: the obligatory dim sum, duck breast with hoisin sauce, soft-shell crab sautéed with pepper and fresh chilli. Lovely presentation and good ingredients: a real ambassador for Chinese food.

Name: Taozui Guan
Address: Building 10, Zone B, Zhujiang Party Pier Beer Culture & Art Zone, 118 Modisha Street, Haizhu, Guangzhou, 510200, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted
Description: Showcasing a ceramic theme, this restaurant doubles as a cultural hub for art making and exhibitions. The interior resembles an elegant tea house, whereas the food shows international influences and creative touches—emphasising MSG-free, healthful recipes. The signature surfer fish with pickled cabbage is cooked tableside, as the server pours scalding broth onto the raw fish. Tofu and sea urchin in claypot melds and balances all the great flavours.

Name: Taparelle
Description: This is a striking and eye-catching space in the progressive and equally contemporary Manarat Saadiyat – Abu Dhabi’s centre for art, culture and community events. The terrace is the perfect spot to sit and their Saturday brunches are a must. The appealing menu marries French and Italian cuisines; expect dishes like scallop Grenobloise, oxtail ragu, or crispy charred sea bass. The food is perfectly paired with a cool, light and airy space dotted with locally sourced pottery.

Name: Tapas 3.0
Description: This centrally located gastro-bar boasts an attractive dining room plus a glass-fronted wine cellar in the basement. Contemporary tapas and “raciones”, plus a takeaway and home delivery menu (Tapas 4.0).

Name: Tapori
Address: 22/2 Soi Sukhumvit 47, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Tapori is a chic and intimate Indian dining spot with warm lighting, modern yet subtly traditional decor and a cosy feel. A 200‐year‐old wooden door from Rajasthan welcomes guests into a space adorned with Warli, Bastar and Pichwai art. Inspired by India's 28 states, the chef-owner reworks the classics, fusing bold spices with innovation. For dessert, try their unique take on Benami Kheer. A hidden bar serves cocktails.

Name: Taqueria El Gran Abanico
Address: Gutiérrez Nájera S/N, Tránsito, Cuauhtémoc, 06820, Mexico
Description: You won't need to check your map to find this spot, as this bi-level space has a line that stretches down the block. Don't worry, as the line moves quickly at this locals' favorite. The large menu offers plenty of choices, but all eyes are on the tacos, especially their signature carnitas piled high on a double layer of soft corn tortillas. Other tacos to consider include the costilla de res, a tender bone-in beef rib that's packed with flavor. Portions are generous and prices are fair at this unfussy taqueria that runs on cash only.

Name: Taqueria El Paisa
Address: Joaquin Garcia Icazbalceta 36, San Rafael, Cuauhtémoc, 06470, Mexico
Description: On a corner in San Rafael, this bustling taqueria is a well-oiled machine. Everyone comes for the suadero, which is best ordered late in the evening when the meat has had hours to braise in its own fat. The al pastor is worth a try too. Whatever the order, tacos are on the small side so aim for three or four per person. Once through the queue, people eat wherever they can: sitting on the curb, leaning against a building, or on the hoods of their cars.

Name: Taqueria La Principal
Address: Principal, Valle de Guadalupe, Valle de Guadalupe, 22750, Mexico
Description: Situated in a warehouse space with plastic furniture, this quintessential no-frills roadside taqueria doesn’t get a lot of points for ambience, but happily the simple, satisfying fare speaks for itself. The compact menu doesn’t call for extensive decision-making: diners choose between three meats (thinly sliced beef asada, spice-marinated pork adobada, and, for the more adventurous, tender tripa), and their vehicle of choice (corn or flour tortilla, burrito, torta, etc.) and then watch the magic come together before their eyes. Lively, well-balanced salsas and perfectly fresh toppings combine with flavorful grill-kissed meats for love at first bite, and the late nighttime hours of operation might be a lifesaver after a busy day of wine tasting.

Name: Taqueria Los Parados
Address: Av. Monterrey 333, Roma Sur, Cuauhtémoc, 06760, Mexico
Description: Don't expect a sit-down experience at this taqueria that has been open since 1965, as there are no chairs, but metal shelving subbing in for tables does the trick. Charcoal grilled meats are their specialty, and everything is cooked to order. Finished to a medium-well, the bistec enjoys a subtle smokiness from the grill, while the costilla is equally delicious in all of its razor-thin, well-done glory. Al pastor tacos are also a sure bet.

Name: Taquería El Califa de León
Address: Av. Ribera De San Cosme 56, San Rafael, Cuauhtémoc, 06470, Mexico
Description: After more than half a century in business, this taqueria, with just enough room for a handful of diners to stand at its counter, has earned is place in Mexico City's taco pantheon. Its signature creation, the Gaonera taco features thinly sliced beef filet, seared to order and seasoned simply with salt and lime, cooked alongside fresh corn tortillas. A handful of other options, including chuleta (pork chop) and costilla (beef rib) are likewise worth considering, and a duo of excellent house-made salsas make for fine accompaniments.

Name: Taquiza
Address: The Broadmore Miami Beach, 7450 Ocean Terrace, Miami Beach, FL, 33141, USA
Description: When Steve Santana launched his humble taco stall in 2014, he probably didn’t imagine just how popular it would get. The web developer-turned-chef was one of the first in the city to nixtamalize, grind, press and griddle his tortillas in-house, and now look—the breezy location in North Beach is central command for a recognized brand that sources corn from small farms in the Midwest and supplies restaurants across the city. Signature blue corn tortillas wrap around a host of fillings, like melting lengua or fried mahi, all garnished with radish, onion and served with sharp salsas (ask for the charred jalapeño).With palm trees swaying throughout and the lure of the ocean just one block away, this beachside favorite is a Miami mainstay for good reason.

Name: Tare
Description: Found on the second floor of a North Austin professional building, Tare's odd location makes for a curious first impression. There is no signage, but an attendant is stationed out front to welcome diners before each seating. Once inside, the space is attractive with a dark granite counter. Chef Michael Carranza and his small team prepare a kappo-style experience, and the foundation of the meal is an array of embellished nigiri. Fish is sourced from Japan and dry-aged in-house, but tuna from Spain and ocean trout from New Zealand may also make an appearance. There is a creative streak with a Texas accent at work here, as in a Japanese ruby fish with salsa macha; toro tartare in a piece of chicharron; or Hokkaido scallop with shiro dashi aioli and chorizo.

Name: Taro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Since setting up shop in these new premises, brothers Giang Ta (maitre d') and Khanh Ta (chef) have been hosting diners in a trendy urban counter-restaurant. The chefs can be seen at work from the large U-shaped bar around the kitchen. A lively yet stylish atmosphere reigns, underscored by modern music selection which is personally chosen - something special these days. A nice detail: at every seat there is a small photo album that looks at story of the two owners and presents the team with a sense of humor. There is a seasonal five-course menu based on Vietnamese flavours and family recipes, influenced by the chef’s Vietnamese heritage and his life in the Czech Republic. The wine selection offers high quality and the sommelier provides expert advice. Alongside the wine pairing, you can also choose a cocktail or a non-alcoholic drink to accompany the set menu.

Name: Tartarun
Description: This elegant restaurant by the harbour of a small fishing village has been run by the Schiavone family for over 10 years. Son James treats diners to a daily changing selection of simply cooked whole fish and other, more modern, imaginative seafood dishes. In addition to fishermen, they support the local baker and a hydroponic farmer who is just a few kilometres from the restaurant. Their 150+ wine bin is renowned locally.

Name: Tasca del Puerto
Address: Avenida del Puerto 13, Castelló de la Plana, 12100, Spain
Description: A family-run restaurant, with mum in the kitchen and her son in the dining room, where the love for gastronomy is felt in every detail. They offer, through the à la carte service and their set menus (Menu of the Day and Gourmet Tasting), a product-based cuisine with a marked seafood flavour, very focused on rice dishes and stews (minimum two portions), fresh fish from the fish market and seafood (some by weight).

Name: Tasco da Ilda
Address: Rua Jaime da Mota, 34, Azambuja, 2050-333, Portugal
Description: This small restaurant, located near the railway station, is run with dedication by chef Madalena Dias, a woman who, through sheer hard work, has managed to preserve and perpetuate the culinary legacy inherited from both her mother and her great-grandmother. Here, in a colourful space with a welcoming interior, the family’s flavourful repertoire has taken a leap in quality to pay tribute to Ribatejo gastronomy; in fact, in some dishes, it even plays with pickles. Curious details? It has an adjoining cellar, where they offer tastings and promote wines from small producers.

Name: Tasogare
Description: Tasogare means ‘twilight’, and that’s when the doors open, to ensure guests an enjoyable visit. Fun is on the blackboard menu, with combinations that make visions of deliciousness dance before the eyes - foie gras with Danish pastry, for example, or asparagus with zabaglione. Vinegared fish and stew are the very essence of Japanese cuisine. Tasogare entices with layers of nuanced technique and a spirit of playfulness. Free-spirited cooking, to be enjoyed with a free spirit.

Name: Tasquinha da Linda
Address: Rua dos Mareantes A-10, Viana do Castelo, 4900-351, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: One of the best dining options in this attractive town on the Costa Verde, this contemporary restaurant located next to the Castelo de Santiago da Barra occupies a docks warehouse in which the large attractive fish and seafood tanks take pride of place. Its owners are fish wholesalers, hence the top-quality fish and seafood that is on offer here, normally sold by weight and at prices that are highly competitive. You won’t find a single meat dish on the menu here! Make sure you save space for desserts made by the owners’ daughter!

Name: Tassili
Address: Esplanade, Saint Helier, JE2 3QA, United Kingdom
Description: Overlooking St Aubin's Bay, this intimate restaurant inside the Grand Jersey Hotel offers a haven of luxury, not only in its opulent surroundings but also in the ingredients used. While you relax in the elegant room with linen-clad tables, you can expect to enjoy Jersey produce from blue lobster to Angus beef, not to mention excellent wild turbot. While their components are classically luxurious, there’s some playfully creative touches to the dishes. Bespoke wine flights are available to complement the cooking.

Name: Tast & Gust
Address: Sant Martí 92, Cerdanyola del Vallès, 08290, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: This small restaurant, which always offers a choice of seasonal dishes and several daily specials, is a temple for steak tartare, offering a superb classic interpretation of the dish along with four other personalised options (Roquefort; Calvados and red onion confit; foie gras; and red tuna), all prepared in front of guests. Highly personalised service, and given its size we recommend booking ahead.

Name: Tastavents
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Between Port Esportiu and Platja del Coco, on the third floor of the Marina Badalona hotel, you will find an open-plan restaurant dominated by white tones and offering beautiful panoramic views of the sea. From the kitchen, visible to diners and with a chef's table if you want to marvel in the cooking process, they offer a contemporary menu that is very much about mixing ingredients and experimentation, generally with rather good results. If you prefer to let your dishes be selected for you, they also offer three tasting menus: Raíces (vegan-vegetarian, by reservation only and with 48 hours' notice), Origen and Sensaciones.

Name: Tatar Bunar
Address: 152 Curtain Road, Shoreditch, London, EC2A 3AT, United Kingdom
Description: Shoreditch’s ever-buoyant and thrillingly diverse dining scene got an added boost in 2025 with the opening of this Ukrainian restaurant. Handsomely decorated to look more like a sleek showroom for Ukrainian ceramics, it comes with a long open kitchen and a great covered terrace at the back of the spacious room. You’ll need to share the dishes as they are as generous in size as they are in flavour. The deliciously sweet pickled cherry tomatoes with lemon yoghurt have quickly become a must-have dish, while the richly flavoured banoush with ox cheeks is like a warm, comforting embrace.

Name: Tati
Description: The owners of this restaurant in up-and-coming District 7 also have a farm in Biatorbágy, on the outskirts of the city, where they grow their own fruit and veg. Menus comprise a mix of meat, fish and plant-based combinations, and the use of traditional Hungarian recipes results in hearty, wholesome cooking. There’s a natural feel to both the appearance and the flavour of the dishes, as well as to the accompanying natural, biodynamic and organic wines, which are sourced from vineyards in close proximity to the city.

Name: Tatiana
Address: 10 Lincoln Center Plz., New York, NY, 10023, USA
Description: There's pre-theater dining, and then there's Tatiana. Its Lincoln Center location is a natural choice for Philharmonic ticket holders, but it's worthy of applause in its own right. Its stunning interior, crafted by Modellus Novus, swings to a stylish beat courtesy of its good looks and even better looking crowd. Chef Kwame Onwuachi draws on his West African roots and the flavors of his childhood in the Bronx and elsewhere on this menu with signature dishes like egusi dumplings, filled with crab and sea bass in a brick red sauce. The centerpiece—oxtail—arrives in a large pot with two glistening pieces resting in a thick sauce. Marinated for more than a day, and served with Thumbelina carrots and chayote squash along with rice and peas, it's a proper feast.

Name: Taulissa
Address: Maison Albar - Le Victoria, 6 avenue de Suède, Nice, 06000, France
Description: High up on the sixth floor of Maison Albar - Le Victoria hotel, this restaurant boasts a picture-postcard panoramic view, with the city on one side, the sea on the other. In this elegant, light-filled dining space dotted with maritime details, Glenn Viel and his associate Fred Grava put their own spin on Southern French cuisine, using local produce and intensely flavoured jus. Dishes such as catch of the day and confit lamb shoulder are presented tableside by the attentive and friendly team, adding theatricality to a dining experience that allows diners to savour the Mediterranean.

Name: Taupe
Address: 26th Street, The Maridien Tower 2, Bonifacio Global City, Taguig - Metro Manila, The Philippines
Description: At Taupe, Chef Tolentino draws on his New York training and Filipino heritage to craft modern dishes that are both nostalgic and inventive. Signature plates such as the playful Street Basket and elegant Scallops and Champagne are underpinned by personal memories and sure technique. Seamlessly blending East and West, the menu is a heartfelt take on borderless cuisine. For a creative tasting journey with emotional depth, be sure to book a table.

Name: Taverna & Trattoria Palio
Description: Palio offers fresh Italian fare from the open kitchen in a relaxed trattoria-style atmosphere – you simply have to try one of the pasta dishes! The seasonal set menus are also interesting. There’s also a lovely terrace in the shade of some old chestnut trees.

Name: Taverna Kus
Address: contrada Castello 14, San Zeno di Montagna, 37010, Italy
Description: An attractive restaurant situated on the western slopes of Monte Baldo overlooking Lake Garda, with a number of rustic yet elegant and welcoming dining rooms, including a bright veranda with partial views of the lake (enjoy the full vista from the outdoor terrace). Various culinary options feature on the menu, including meat, fish and vegetarian dishes, all colourful, full of flavour and beautifully cooked and prepared using mainly local and seasonal ingredients. The well-stocked and carefully chosen wine list deserves a special mention: among the 1 000 or more bottles stored in the old giasàra (underground cellar), you’re sure to find something you’ll enjoy.

Name: Taverna Kyclades
Description: This beloved Greek spot feels as essential to the neighborhood as traffic lights. It's a lively spot where the bustling kitchen is in view. Quick, straightforward servers may address you in Greek if you look the part — that's just how local it gets here. Grab a seat and get things going with a generous spinach pie, its flaky, sesame-speckled pastry wrapped around fresh spinach and feta, or a spread of classic dips like cooling tzatziki, briny taramosalata, garlicky skordalia and spicy feta, all served with warm pita. Simply prepared fish, like whole branzino, dressed with olive oil and herbs, highlights the kitchen's handling of seafood, while sides like Swiss chard or lemon potatoes round out the meal in traditional fashion.

Name: Taverna La Cialoma
Description: This restaurant housed in Marzamemi’s old tuna fishery boasts an outdoor terrace with tables overlooking one of the most picturesque squares in Sicily, as well as an indoor dining room and another terrace to the rear facing the sea. Wherever you choose to sit, you’ll find authentic Sicilian cuisine on the menu, with just a few simply prepared dishes in which the full flavours of fresh fish shine through.

Name: Taverna Rovita
Description: Situated just a few metres from the main square of old Maratea, this tavern is a historic and typical restaurant with a kitchen area that dates from the 18C and a decor featuring Vietri ceramics. The chef delights in introducing guests to local recipes, such as the “polpo murato” (stewed octopus), one of the house specialities. The wine list boasts around 400 labels, with a particular focus on France and small-scale producers from Italy and further afield. Small groups (a maximum of 6 people) can choose to dine in the wine cellar surrounded by old bottles, many of which are collector’s items.

Name: Taverna Trilussa
Description: A true bastion of Roman gastronomy, set in the city’s most quintessential neighbourhood for such an “attraction”. With a history stretching back over a century – it was founded in 1910 – the restaurant upholds tradition as its standard, served in a rustic yet surprisingly refined setting, supported by attentive and accomplished service. Among the first courses, beyond the timeless cacio e pepe, carbonara, amatriciana and gricia, stands out an award-winning speciality: Ravioli Mimosa, prepared according to a secret recipe that is neither meat nor fish. There follow all the great classics of Roman cuisine, from lamb to tripe, culminating in the house’s signature dish: beef fillet cooked over charcoal.

Name: Taverna del Castello
Description: Park in the small car park close to the village, then make your way on foot to this restaurant, admiring the village’s beautiful stone houses along the way. Inside the restaurant, the service is informal yet professional, while the cuisine served on the first floor includes emblematic local specialities such as tortelli alle erbette (stuffed pasta with herbs) and local salumi (including Parma ham). The wine list boasts a good selection of local and Italian wines – finding a label to suit your taste and budget will not be a problem!

Name: Taverna dello Spuntino
Description: This Roman trattoria has a particularly striking interior. From its old tufa passageways converted into a wine cellar in the basement, to its charming dining rooms with brick - vaulted arches where hams, flasks of wine, fruit and antipasti all form an attractive display.

Name: Taverna e' Mare
Address: Via Principal Marina, 16, Torre del Greco, 80059, Italy
Description: In an elegant setting facing the harbour and the sea, the dining room at this restaurant is a terrace with large picture windows boasting beautiful views that also include Capri. The sea takes pride of place on the menu, which features fresh fish and plenty of local produce in the cuisine served here. Don’t miss the raw fish options, which include a selection of oysters, tartares and ceviche. Our inspector particularly enjoyed the roll of sea bass stuffed with spinach, fior di latte, beurre blanc sauce, parsley oil and onions.

Name: Taverne du Passage
Address: Galerie de la Reine 30, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
Description: This emblematic Art deco brasserie, which is housed in the exclusive Galerie du roi, just a stone’s throw from the iconic Grand Place, takes you back in time to the Roaring Twenties. Its vintage charm is enhanced by a host of elegant details like the flock of golden origami birds hanging from the ceiling. The equally nostalgic menu features a splendid lineup of Belgian family favourites together with a few more modern recipes. Start with crunchy shrimp fritters, before moving onto veal kidneys in a creamy mustard sauce, to finish with a warm chocolate mousse and butterscotch ice cream. Living proof that tradition and generosity are timeless values!

Name: Taverne zur Krone
Description: In this stately, exquisitely restored historical building – documented as a tavern belonging to Wettingen Monastery as early as 1259 – there are two dining options: an elegant wood-panelled restaurant and a modern brasserie. In summer, the terrace is especially charming. The menu features a nicely curated selection of traditional and classic dishes. Service is exceedingly friendly and adept.

Name: Tavline
Description: Between Saint-Paul and Hôtel de Ville, a slice of Tel Aviv, a taste of Morocco, a hint of Lebanon – such is the formula of Tavline. Spices supplied by Shuk Ha'Carmel, the largest market in Tel Aviv, adorn the fine cuisine served here, including ksitsot daguim – grilled fish balls with herbs and spices on a bed of lentils with yoghurt and candied lemon, or the memorable memoulam (onions stuffed with lamb), a recipe passed down to the chef from his mother.

Name: Tavola MoS - Stefano Zanini
Address: via Ugo da Como 8, Lonato del Garda, 25017, Italy
Description: Accomplished chef Stefano Zanini showcases his considerable talent in the evocative setting of the Rocca di Lonato. His recently opened establishment occupies the spaces of the former apartment of the librarian to Senator Ugo da Como, to whom the Foundation owes its name: a luminous and carefully appointed room, almost a veranda-like dining space suspended above the gardens, where history and elegance converse in natural harmony. The kitchen presents creative Italian cuisine, consistently well-presented and guided by a refined hand. The sea bass, rapidly cooked on the skin side and finished with a sauce of anchovy essence and extra virgin olive oil, accompanied by seasonal vegetables interpreted with intelligence, is particularly convincing; the pigeon too merits attention. At lunch, in addition to the à la carte menu, a lighter formula is available.

Name: Tavolo
Description: Enter through the huge wooden doors of this old military stable and you’ll find yourself in a large and stunningly converted room with a truly buzzing atmosphere. A huge horse’s head – a copy of Leonardo's Cavallo di Forcione and a reminder of the building’s former life – takes centre stage in the bar, which is a popular spot for a cocktail and some nibbles. When it comes to the food, it’s all about Italy, with the fresh, flavoursome dishes prepared on-view in the open kitchen. From homemade pizzas and pastas to traditional meat dishes, there’s something for everyone here.

Name: Taylor Grocery
Description: In a region where fried catfish is practically a religion, Taylor Grocery stands tall as one of the great stewards of this culinary tradition. Since 1977, crowds have lingered on the front porch waiting for a seat in a rudimentary dining room where scratched walls are covered in scribble and old class photos. There’s no reason to look at a menu. You could dabble in gumbo or poke at a salad, but nothing should distract or deter from ordering a righteous mountain of cornmeal-dusted, golden-fried catfish flanked by an avalanche of hushpuppies. Tartare sauce and ketchup on the table complete the picture.

Name: Taúlla
Description: This highly unusual restaurant occupies an old paprika mill in the Espinardo district of Murcia, where the basement is home to an attractive private dining space and a themed museum dedicated to paprika (the fascinating and colourful collection of old containers is particularly impressive). The cooking here has its roots in tradition and the local region, albeit with a fun, imaginative and modern makeover, with no little technical skill. Head chef Rodi Fernández showcases his cuisine on an à la carte (the “panigiri” of red tuna and guacamole with a citrus and guacamole cream presented on an hourglass of sand was a complete surprise) and two extensive tasting menus: Molino and Taúlla. The selection of cheeses can be ordered at additional cost before dessert.

Name: Tač
Description: The restaurant stands on Vrhovec hill, a quiet residential area a short distance from the center. More akin to a private home than a conventional restaurant, it evokes an intimate, welcoming atmosphere, run with warmth by the Miletić family. They offer generous traditional recipes of land and sea, hearty in flavor and portion size. Lovers of offal will appreciate a dedicated section featuring dishes inspired by local recipes. Sharing is the norm here, contributing to a convivial experience. The wine list, focused on Croatian and neighboring regional labels, is presented and narrated directly by the dining room staff. At the entrance, beyond a meat-aging refrigerator, stands a small but carefully curated display of fresh fish of the day.

Name: Tchaikovsky
Description: Set within the well-known Hotel Telegraaf, in the heart of the Old Town, this glass-roofed restaurant has something of a celebratory feel, courtesy of a beautiful chandelier and walls hung with gilt-framed pictures. To the side of the hotel is its large summer terrace, while at the head of the room a living wall, set behind glass, brings the outside inside year-round. Refined cooking has a classical French base with Russian influences and modern overtones – the Siberian dumplings, which come with the likes of horseradish beurre blanc, are a must-try.

Name: Tean
Address: Jumeirah Saadiyat Island, Al Saadiyat Island, Abu Dhabi
Description: The first thing you’ll be tempted by will be a quick dip as you wander past the pool of the Jumeirah Saadiyat Island. The smiling service team will make you feel instantly at home, while the open kitchen prepares an assortment of Lebanese, Greek, Turkish and Middle Eastern dishes, all designed for sharing. There are excellent freshly baked breads aplenty; just be sure to order something from the charcoal grill and finish with Umm Ali.

Name: Tei-An
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted,Notable sake list,Valet parking
Description: The Arts District and Tei-An are a perfect fit, as this Japanese restaurant provides an elegant and cultured experience in an aesthetically striking environment. Opened back in 2008, it has also played an important role in nurturing the city’s love affair with Japanese cuisine. The menu is varied and extensive, allowing diners to decide their own level of expense and experimentation. There’s everything from tonkatsu to tempura, as well as dishes like grilled freshwater eel (which comes with its crisped spine as you’d get in Japan), but its house-made soba and udon noodles—served cold or hot—are the house specialties. They come with an array of seasonal toppings and dipping sauces, many traditional and some, like Bolognese, more original.

Name: Tekka
Description: Located outside the historic center in a lively commercial area, this intimate Japanese restaurant welcomes guests in a modern setting with views of the chefs at work behind the counter. Leave room for dessert, where the irresistible Chocolate Ganache stands out. An interesting and extensive wine selection, available by the glass, rounds out the experience.

Name: Tekka by Lone
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: One passes through the entrance of the thoroughly modern Hotel Lone to reach this accomplished restaurant dedicated to Japanese cuisine. The interiors are minimalist and pleasant, but the true highlight is the delightful outdoor service in the summer garden surrounded by pine forest. Here the encounter between Istria and the Orient is expressed not so much through fusion cooking – the menu offers great Japanese classics such as sushi, sashimi, nigiri, gunkan, uramaki and hosomaki, alongside gyoza, soups and other warm dishes – as through the use of predominantly Istrian ingredients. This synthesis finds its finest expression in dishes such as the seafood salad – with raw and marinated fish that may include scallops, Pacific yellowtail amberjack, and baby cuttlefish – accompanied by olive leaf tea, seaweed and crab mayonnaise, or in the rabbit loin with teriyaki sauce. The cocktail list is also well developed.

Name: Tekés
Description: One of the establishments owned by chef Assaf Granit, Tekés is summed up by its name, which is Hebrew for "ceremony". More than a restaurant, it's also a veritable musical extravaganza. The kitchen team puts on a thrilling show, cooking vegetables over an open fire, while the well-drilled waitstaff stand by, ready to spring into action. Flame-grilled leeks with potato and feta purée, fattoush salad with labneh and za'atar, fried gnocchi with yellow curry and yoghurt – just some of the delicious dishes on offer! This culinary journey taking in Levantine tradition and influences from the Middle East embraces intense flavours and carefully selected spices. The options on the mainly vegetarian (although not vegan) menu take the form of dishes to share – which is very much in keeping with the convivial atmosphere!

Name: Temaki Den
Address: The Source Hotel, 3350 Brighton Blvd., Ste. 100, Denver, CO, 80216, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: Temaki Den is nestled within The Source Hotel + Market Hall. It's an open space, tucked among other vendors, and a dark color palette lends a modern, if moody, feel to this spot. As the name suggests, it is all about temaki, or handrolls, though they do feature aburi (flame-seared) nigiri as well. Begin with broccolini goma-ae, a nicely balanced dish of blanched bright green broccolini dressed in a sesame dressing, before moving on to temaki, available à la carte or as a set. Rolled for guests, one at a time, the Scottish salmon belly with yuzu kosho and crispy shallots is a standout. Don't skip the eggplant nigiri, seared and caramelized with miso to deliver a buttery, rich and slightly sweet knockout flavor.

Name: Temmabashi Fujikawa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Shoes must be removed
Description: The uniquely elegant counter of Yoshino cedar reflects the taste of the chef. Kaiseki meals showcase the chef’s original vision. In the middle stage of his prix fixe menu, the chef offers tempura, with each piece individually deep-fried. At lunchtime, appetisers delight the eye as well as the palate; in the evening, offerings increase in number, with sharpened focus on the ingredients. As the tempo of the menu gradually rises, the diversity of skills on display in the open kitchen piques interest.

Name: Temperature Studio
Address: 50 Gongyuan East Road, Gangshan District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
Description: The owner-chef has over 10 years of experience in haute cuisine. He opened this 6-seater in 2021 because he believes temperature is at the core of all good food. The down-to-earth multi-course omakase menu uses European, Japanese and Taiwanese techniques to create dishes that are homely but layered with flavours and textures. Highlights include stuffed Portobello mushroom, and marinated milkfish on koshihikari rice.

Name: Tempi Fà
Description: Welcome to "bygone days" (tempi fà

Name: Temple Street Beef Offal
Address: 18 Arthur Street, Yau Ma Tei, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: This long-standing shop is popular with locals. Tripe, intestine, pancreas or lung can be ordered individually or as an assortment, on a skewer or in a bowl. The offal soaks up the broth nicely, with three sauces on the side.

Name: Tempo
Address: 5 place de la République, Rouen, 76000, France
Description: Between the River Seine and the cathedral, this restaurant sports a black and red geometrical design. The son of a market gardener with a passion for veg, the chef infuses his cuisine with flavours in the zeitgeist. He gives free rein to his imagination and creativity in a carte blanche menu: beetroot, hibiscus and smoked cream; seabass, Pontoise cabbage and a spicy hollandaise.

Name: Tempura Aratamikawa
Description: A warm light envelops an interior appointed in the stately Taisho Romanticist style. The shop’s name and the certificate of mastery are in the handwriting of the chef’s mentor. The chef studied theories and techniques from one of the world’s foremost practitioners of tempura. Tempura pieces, such as the irreplaceable Edomae standards of shrimp, sillago and conger eel, seem almost grilled rather than fried in hot oil. While obsessively following his mentor’s teachings, the chef is pursuing ‘a new way of tempura’ with innovations he learned as an apprentice, such as serving some fish that are not deep-fried.

Name: Tempura Endo
Address: 9777 S. Santa Monica Blvd., Beverly Hills, CA, 90210, USA
Description: There are few restaurants in the country dedicated solely to tempura, a Japanese style of cooking that is so much more than just “frying.” Tempura Endo in Beverly Hills is one such rare breed. Though there are tables woven throughout the restaurant, aim for a seat at the counter in front of the handmade copper cauldron. The tasting menus are on the pricey side, but such is the cost for a parade of vegetables and seafood dipped and fried delicately and served one at a time by the chef himself. Ribs of sweet corn, scallops from Hokkaido, broccolini, and snapper wrapped in shiso are all carefully placed in hot cottonseed oil and emerge with a lacy, almost transparent coating. At the meal’s end, opt for the tempura rice bowl over the soba noodles.

Name: Tempura Fukana
Description: Helping his mother with the cooking as a little boy was the chef’s gateway into the world of Japanese cuisine. He learned the craft at a hotel, where he was entrusted with tempura; later he went independent, fulfilling his dream. The sign was written by his mother, a calligraphy instructor. The chef’s aim is to serve tempura so light, you wouldn’t know it’s deep-fried. Pieces are lightly coated and aromatic when fried. Points of pride include tempura using sea urchin and nori, as well as wagyu beef fillet wrapped in perilla leaf.

Name: Tempura Hashimoto
Description: Light tempura fried in cottonseed oil. Commonly used fish are interspersed with inventive ingredients. Sea bream is wrapped in oba (perilla) leaves to infuse their aroma. Inspired by cutlet sandwiches, beef fillet tempura is served as a sandwich. Novelty and flexible thinking broaden the ways to enjoy the dining experience. Displayed on the wall is a calligraphy of the character for 'dragon', representing the passion to soar like an ascending dragon.

Name: Tempura Hattori
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: A chef who honed his skills at a ryotei now applies those skills to tempura. The omakase prix fixe meal begins with an assortment of appetisers. Tempura is fried in cottonseed oil for a light and airy texture. The chef’s craftsmanship shines in works such as matsukasa-age, or crispy-scaled fried sea bream, and items cured with kombu. Service alternates between seafood and vegetables, bringing variety to the flow of dishes. Unusual items such as eel and venison are born from the chef’s passion for exploring new flavours. Tencha, tempura on rice with the first brewing of broth poured over, wraps up the meal.

Name: Tempura Kawaharasaki
Description: Kansai’s Kamigata-style tempura lives on here. The selection centres on white-fleshed fish from Osaka Bay and the Seto Inland Sea, along with vegetables from across the Kansai region. Fried in lightly scented cottonseed oil, the tempura is cloaked in a pale batter, with salt bringing out the ingredients. The meal finishes with the restaurant’s original salt-seasoned tendon, inspired by tenbara, rice topped with bite-sized tempura. Its salt-seasoned kakiage combines shrimp with seasonal vegetables, bringing a sense of the season to the dish.

Name: Tempura Kitagawa
Description: The chef taught himself tempura by travelling and sampling various styles. His keen eye for fish derives from once being a sushi chef. From his native Shizuoka, farmers send him produce and fishermen send seafood from Suruga Bay. Lightness and freedom are the qualities he strives for. Lightness he achieves by trapping bubbles in the tempura batter and frying in fresh-pressed sesame oil. The first piece is an unconventional choice: largehead hairtail, also known as scabbard fish. Tempura dipping sauce is warmed to release the aroma. A cup of Kakegawa tea is served after the meal.

Name: Tempura Mizuki
Address: B1F, The Ritz-Carlton, Kyoto, 543 Hokodencho, Nakagyo-ku, Kyoto, 604-0902, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Ingredients are presented before frying begins: vegetables from Takagamine and Shūgakuin, seafood from Awaji and Shizuoka. Safflower oil is used to achieve a light tempura coating. While some items, such as shrimp and conger eel, are fried on their own, other items are ingeniously paired, such as sesame tofu with sea urchin, wagyu with perilla leaf, and egg yolk with caviar. Gracious hospitality accompanies.

Name: Tempura Nakagawa
Description: The chef learned his tempura from a master versed in the old ways. The first tiger prawn is fried at just the right heat to bring out its aroma; the second is served rare to elicit sweetness. Conger eel is fragrantly fried with minimum sesame oil. Nakagawa’s trademark theory is that ‘tempura is a process of drying-out’, by which he means ingredients are steamed and grilled in their batter to remove moisture, bringing their flavour to the fore.

Name: Tempura Otsuka
Description: The owner-chef, born and raised in Iriya, is an artisan through and through. Proceedings are by the book, starting with milder flavours like tiger prawn, squid and sillago before proceeding to bolder tastes. Edomae toppings are favoured, such as tidepool gunnel and big-eyed flathead. Decorating the walls are senshagaku, wooden tablets typically posted on the pillars of shrines, inscribed with local supporters’ names. The characters suffuse the restaurant with the atmosphere of old neighbourhoods.

Name: Tempura Shimomura
Description: The menu is extensive to cater to diners’ tastes but has strong regional roots. Fish and vegetables are fried in alternation, with the accent on shrimp, sillago and conger eel. Recently, few tempura places offer tendon only, but here, tendon of vegetable tempura and kakiage (all-in-one seafood and vegetable tempura blend) are available at lunchtime. Feel free to add seafood items to the vegetable set menu. Woodblock prints and an icebox vaguely recreate the atmosphere of working-class Edo.

Name: Tempura Sugimura
Address: 2F, Marriott Midtown,199 Lequn 2nd Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: An outpost of its namesake in Japan, this restaurant makes tempura the same way as its Japanese sibling. Its tempura boasts an ethereal batter made with extra fine cake flour imported from Japan. It is deep-fried in a blend of corn oil and sesame oil for a nutty undertone, and served with tentsuyu, nori salt and curry salt on the side. From May to June, live ayu sweetfish are kept in a fish tank and fried to order.

Name: Tempura Taku
Description: Tempura is required to be light. The flour is aerated as it is mixed with water to form a thin coating. Tempura pieces are fried in cold-pressed sesame oil to bring the flavour to the fore. Service alternates seafood with vegetable items, so flavours are constantly changing. In addition to favourites such as shrimp and conger eel, the menu includes a few novel tempura items. Sea urchin is served rare, so is wrapped in nori seaweed; asparagus tips and stalks are fried at different temperatures for the best texture.

Name: Tempura Urakami
Description: In his tempura creations, Dai Urakami prizes lightness above all. Frying in light safflower oil brings the flavour of each piece to the fore. The meal begins with two tiger prawns. To ensure that the sweetness of the flesh makes an impression, fragrant prawn legs are served afterward. Tempura items such as abalone and milt are imaginatively paired with vinegared rice stuffed with sea urchin. The painting of Mount Fuji on the wall reminds Urakami always to seek greater heights.

Name: Ten's
Address: Avenida Marqués de l'Argentera 11, Barcelona, 08003, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A minimalist gastro-bar overseen by famous chef Jordi Cruz. Here, where they say they ‘reinterpret classic tapas with creativity, precision and a rebellious touch’, you will find individual tapas, a good number of portions designed for sharing, elaborate desserts... and, of course, a tapas tasting menu called Ten's, which is only served to the whole table and is the perfect option to get a true insight into the cuisine here. One dish that bowled us over was the Japanese-style tiradito with cured gilthead bream, gazpachuelo, grapes, kumquat and seaweed.

Name: Ten-you
Description: The clean-lined interior was created by a tea-house craftsman. The ground floor has private rooms in a modern Japanese style; the upper floor features counter seating with the chef holding court. Tempura is fried in cottonseed oil for a light texture. The prix fixe menu alternates between seafood and vegetables, ensuring constant variation. In a creative touch, tilefish is wrapped in perilla leaf. The restaurant is managed by a ryokan; in hope that guests will return to dine here even after their stay is over, tendon is offered at lunchtime.

Name: Tendril
Address: 5 Princes Street, Mayfair, London, W1B 2LQ, United Kingdom
Description: There are a range of global influences to be found across the vegetable-led dishes at this ‘mostly vegan’ restaurant, from the massaman sauce with pak choi to the ‘Chinatown’ purple potatoes. There’s technical skill on display too and a strong understanding of textures in particular. It’s a smart place, with the feel of a neighbourhood restaurant; the front room, with plenty of natural light, is best for lunch, while the slightly moodier rear makes for a more intimate dinner.

Name: Tenmasa
Address: Unit 3.3 (annexe), 2F, Tower 1, Platinum Park, 11 Persiaran KLCC, Kuala Lumpur, 50088, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: Watch the chefs work their magic from the 10-seater counter but be sure to book in advance. The omakase menus include dishes ranging from appetisers to tempura and seasonal specials made with top-notch Japanese produce. Seafood and vegetables are lightly battered on the spot and deep fried in a blend of sesame and rice bran oil for an ethereal, crisp crust. The signature dish comprises fresh, sweet uni from Hokkaido on a tempura shiso leaf.

Name: Tenne
Description: Your welcoming hosts run this long-standing family business with great dedication. Done out in a contemporary take on Alpine style, the cosy interior is very pleasing. The menu takes its cue from the seasons and includes some exquisite game dishes – the chef himself is a hunter! In the evening, you can choose between two set menus – one of which is vegetarian – or order à la carte. At lunchtime, the selection is a little smaller, but there is also a set menu. The appealing wine list showcases the best of the Valais region. For overnight stays, there are well-kept, modern guestrooms.

Name: Tenne Lodges
Description: Situated near the ski slopes in the Gourmethotel Tenne Lodges, this restaurant is decorated with a profusion of wood. The large dining room is the backdrop for delicious modern cuisine which is regional in focus yet also influenced by the chef’s professional experience around the world. Excellent wine list offering plenty of choice, plus a stone wine cellar which makes a charming setting for a pre-dinner drink.

Name: Tentenkyokyo Umean
Description: ‘Tentenkyokyo’ carries the heartfelt wish that guests will enjoy tempura and soba to their heart’s content. Shiba shrimp, skewered and deep-fried, is a standard of soba-shop tempura beloved since the Edo period. Although the sea from which shiba shrimp were once harvested has been reclaimed as land, the tradition lives on. Shiba-shrimp tempura embodies the spirit of Edo, and the food culture resonates even today. For your omakase set menu, you can choose whether to include small dishes in the bill of fare or focus solely on tempura.

Name: Tenuta Casa Virginia
Address: via Cascina Violo 1, Villa d'Almè, 24018, Italy
Description: Surrounded by the property’s own vineyards, this restaurant nestlings at the bottom of a gentle hill features an elegant dining room and a beautiful terrace for outdoor dining in fine weather. The cuisine is contemporary (yet not excessively so), with a few freshwater fish also featuring on the menu, while the wine list showcases a good selection of wines. The property’s own wines are available for purchase in the shop.

Name: Tenuta del Gallo
Description: Whether you dine indoors in the charming, romantic dining room or outdoors with views of the surrounding countryside, you’ll enjoy traditional local cuisine and classic Italian favourites at this restaurant. Our inspectors particularly enjoyed the excellent beef carpaccio with truffles and the local guinea fowl with chickpeas. Comfortable guestrooms are also available.

Name: Teochew Lao Er
Address: 6 Jalan Brunei, Pudu, Kuala Lumpur, 55100, Malaysia
Description: In 1984, Lao Er started out as a street stall. In 2011, the third generation opened a restaurant and established itself as a household name in Pudu district. Teochew classics are given a slight tweak to cater to the local palate. The signature dish, meat marinated in spiced soy, is a great hit – try the assorted platter. Teochew congee with pomfret, mackerel, and traditional kueh are also popular.

Name: Teocintle-Tika'aya
Address: Av. de la Independencia 12, Oaxaca, 69600, Mexico
Description: Just south of the Mercado de La Merced, this tiny little nook of a restaurant is a surprise in every way. With just a handful of tables and no menu in sight, the tasting pulls inspiration from Oaxaca’s Mixteca region. The young chef Toño García cooks with the maturity of someone much older, as he brings refined flair to indigenous preparations. His colorful, accomplished dishes wouldn’t be out of place in far ritzier settings, starting with the avocado croquette crowned with nopales. Fish and plantain wrapped in hoja santa in an aguachile pulls flavors from Mexico and beyond.Reservations made through Facebook should be guaranteed before arrival to avoid disappointment, and don't forget to bring cash, as credit cards are not accepted.

Name: Teppanyaki Mihara Goten
Address: 3F, Cubus, 1 Hoi Ping Road, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: This 14-seater is hidden behind a sukiyaki joint and a cocktail bar. As always, chef Mihara champions a kappo-style teppanyaki experience using the freshest produce flown in from Japan. In addition to teppanyaki staples such as seafood and beef, his tasting menus include less commonly seen griddle items – silky, umami-laden chawanmushi, and donabe with foie gras, crab, fish or eel.

Name: Teppanyaki WAJO
Address: 12F, The St. Regis Osaka, 3-6-12 Hommachi, Chuo-ku, Osaka, 541-0053, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: This is teppanyaki mixed with the essence of French cuisine and refined. Appetisers showcase modern creations, prepared with seasonal mood in mind. A double sauce of soy sauce and red wine transforms wagyu steak into an evolution of flavour. Overseeing the kitchen is Ryuta Izuka, the chef back when Joël Robuchon introduced teppanyaki dishes here. Enjoy the action in the kitchen, the sounds, the aromas, and the conversation.

Name: Ter:Govw
Description: Let's first clarify the meaning of Ter:Govw – it refers to Tergouw, which is the city of Gouda's historical name. This warm and welcoming restaurant is located close to the city centre, by a canal. The chefs present a set menu that, from amuse-bouche to dessert, resonates with today's culinary zeitgeist. This translates to a reverence for the classics combined with an appreciation for zesty flavours and Asian seasonings. The menu could open with a creative take on tuna nigiri, paired with a leek-infused beurre blanc, followed by succulent tournedos Rossini encircled by a glossy Madeira jus. As for what to drink, simply rely on the fine wine pairings recommended by the house.

Name: Terakki
Address: Alaçatı, 12000. Sokak No:21, Çeşme, Izmir, 35930, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Rustic yet refined, warm and welcoming – Terakki is a gem. Nab a table on the terrace by the well and observe how the chefs skilfully balance authenticity and modern influences in their own take on generous Aegean cuisine. Think crispy fried veal liver seasoned with thyme, garlic and parsley, or succulent wild sea bass fillet with cherries for a hint of fruity vivacity and accompanied by a velvety cauliflower purée. The exceptional ingredients speak for themselves, requiring no embellishment. The hospitality of the service team comes as a delightful bonus.

Name: Teresa dal 1968
Address: piazza Lido di Pegli 5 r, Pegli, 16156, Italy
Description: Over half a century has passed since this restaurant was opened in 1968 by “mamma” Teresa and “papa” Giuseppe – and it’s still going strong! And although the staff here are proud of the restaurant’s long history and sense of tradition, they are not bound by it, as demonstrated by dishes that have successfully moved with the times, incorporating modern touches to the classic recipes, while always retaining a focus on fresh, high-quality ingredients (especially when it comes to choosing fish).

Name: Terminal #1
Address: 1408 avenue de la Mer, Montpellier, 34000, France
Description: The Pourcel brothers have upcycled this former wine storehouse into a vast space where stone, steel and wood are blended in a smart neo-industrial vein. The dishes, which draw on locally sourced ingredients at their height of their maturity, are infused with inspirations from far and wide. As you peruse the menu ranging from super-fresh seabream, red mullet and seabass to fried potato cakes, rockfish soup or roast squid with tempura of squid head, houmous cream and lemon confit dressing, you will get an excellent foretaste of the “gastronomic bistro” spirit of this terminal.

Name: Terra
Address: Paseo de la Pau 27, Berga, 08600, Spain
Description: A restaurant that goes beyond an enjoyable experience by also focusing on a sense of place. Here, the chef serves traditional Catalan and seasonal cuisine, including several interesting menus.

Name: Terra
Description: Johann Schmuck runs his chic modern restaurant in the basement of a historical mill that dates back to 1581 – tables on the terrace overlooking the Stainzbach River are coveted in summer. He and Maximilian Grandtner are jointly in charge of the kitchen. They devise two seasonal surprise menus: one comprising four courses and the seven-course "Terra" set menu. Most of the ingredients used are sourced from the region. The friendly and professional service team includes sommelier Joachim Retz, who specialises in wines from Styria and Burgenland. Tip: Enjoy an aperitif in the bar lounge. There is also a menu of small snacks – ideal if you just want to drop in for a glass of wine.

Name: Terra
Description: A long corridor takes you through a classical Parisian edifice into a glazed conservatory-cum-courtyard, whose vibe is part winter garden, part neo-industrial. The chef cherry-picks his ingredients to forge a feast that is honest and on point. The main courses are designed to be shared: barbecued monkfish, Black Angus chuck flap, pigeon, sweetbread and foie gras pie… Expertly curated mainly organic and natural wine list. FYI: the house operates a pizzeria and a wine bar in the same street.

Name: Terra
Description: A short walk from the city centre, in the suburbs of Chartres, the husband-and-wife team behind Terra (he is an Italian chef and she is a South African pastry chef) extend an invitation to join them on a culinary journey. The excellent and quintessentially Italian cuisine is served in a friendly atmosphere – the fiorentina-style cannelloni stuffed with veal and spinach and the house parmesan sauce is delicious!

Name: Terra
Description: This restaurant in the attractive Ritz-Carlton hotel boasts a bright and elegantly modern interior with captivating views of the VW works and the harbour basin afforded by floor-to-ceiling windows. The cuisine takes its cue from the seasons and showcases quality produce from the region and elsewhere in the country. One of their signature dishes is braised veal cheek with mustard jus. Good vegetarian options.

Name: Terra Cotta
Description: (Temporarily closed) This enchanting little restaurant boasts an amazing terrace that unfolds along the quayside of the port. Chef Thomas Duval works with the catch supplied by his fisherman brother, which he brilliantly combines with other ingredients to create dishes throbbing with contrasting flavours. Examples include crunchy wild prawns, panko breadcrumbs, fregola of veggies, herbs, sweet-sour sauce or low-temperature fillet of umbrine in a lemony sauce of capers and parsley with courgette fritters. Consider us smitten!

Name: Terra Restaurant by Maslina Resort
Description: Housed in the luxurious Maslina Resort, overlooking the sea, with its rooms of refined essentiality, the restaurant is perfectly in harmony with its surroundings. His cuisine blends French techniques with local and Mediterranean elements, primarily herbs and vegetables grown directly in his own garden. Sea and land dishes on an à la carte menu served in the indoor dining room or on the poolside terrace. Take advantage of the always excellent catch of the day. The wine list is well stocked and in addition to regional labels offers a good selection of French wines.

Name: Terracotta
Description: Situated in the old town, this small, cosy restaurant serves delicious cuisine, with dishes sometimes inspired by Italian and international recipes, but often revisited in a unique way. In summer, you can dine on the terrace under a beautiful wisteria tree.

Name: Terradimare
Description: Overlooking a broad piazza that faces the evocative harbour basin of Trani, and a short distance from the magnificent cathedral, a masterpiece of Apulian Romanesque and enduring symbol of the city, this restaurant, modest in size yet possessed of considerable grace, has the talented Domenico Di Tondo in the kitchen. The gastronomic offering expresses clean, assured flavours and an elegant personality, favouring the catch of the day and a seafood-led kitchen that follows the arrivals closely, while not forgoing – in a nod to the restaurant’s name – some interesting meat alternatives. In the dining room, an entirely female front-of-house team, attentive and solicitous, completes what is a harmonious and carefully considered experience.

Name: Terrae
Address: Verge del Carme 28, Port de Pollença, 07470, Spain
Description: A restaurant with a relaxed ambience and a sustainable ethos where the menu changes almost daily depending on what’s available from the island’s small-scale producers. The cuisine here is prepared without chemicals or additives, and is based around zero-mile ingredients and zero waste. Chef David Rivas, who enjoys explaining and adding the finishing touches to dishes at your table, champions market-inspired cuisine with a strong focus on the grill on an à la carte and two tasting menus (Omakase and 1/2 Omakase). A small selection of daily specials is also an option.

Name: Terrae
Address: 7 avenue de la Mairie, Cambo-les-Bains, 64250, France
Description: A former fishmongers has been savvily repurposed into a charming pocket handkerchief restaurant. Lucile Voisin and Grégory Ménard (Choko-Ona and Grand Hôtel de Saint-Jean-de Luz) have left nothing to chance from the terracotta walls, linen-coloured banquettes and pale wooden tables to the exquisite tableware: silverware, hand-crafted Basque ceramics and cutlery. The menu is inspired by the availability of fresh local produce and the chef’s boundless creativity. Barbecued venison steak, shoulder as fritters and variations on the butternut; citrus fruits in a meringue nest with a yuzu-laced house-made lemonade: hard work, impeccable taste, colour and creativity.

Name: Terraforte
Address: Via Bagnoli Terriccio 12, Castellina Marittima, 56040, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Within the vast and evocative Tenuta Il Terriccio estate, extending across 1,500 hectares of horse breeding, olive groves and celebrated vineyards – from which the famous Lupicaia is produced, offered alongside the other estate wines also by the glass – a Tuscan landscape of rare beauty and tranquillity unfolds. The restaurant occupies the estate’s former joinery, today transformed into an elegant country house. The cuisine, developed in collaboration with chef Tomei, is rooted in authentic farm-to-table produce: the recipes celebrate the resources of the estate – from farm-reared meats to game, from poultry to vegetables, through to aromatic herbs and honey (seafood alone being an exception). The experience is freely composed by choosing the number of courses, giving way to a sequence of creative and balanced dishes that always maintain a clear identity in the raw materials. In the warmer months, a table on the evocative outdoor terrace is not to be missed and, for those wishing to extend their stay, accommodation is available at La Marrana, within the estate.

Name: Terrapin Creek
Address: 1580 Eastshore Rd., Bodega Bay, CA, 94923, USA
Description: Terrapin Creek radiates warmth, whether from the ochre-colored walls, bold artwork or softly glowing fireplace. Chef/owners Liya Lin and Andrew Truong continue to create a welcoming retreat where locals and visitors alike settle in for thoughtful, ingredient-driven cooking shaped by the Northern California coast. The concise, seasonal menu balances comfort with refinement, beginning with dishes like hamachi crudo brightened with basil and sesame oil or pan-roasted Hokkaido scallops paired with sunchoke purée and pickled shiitakes. House-made pasta remains a strong suit, like campanelle tossed with lamb sausage, English peas, mint, spinach and feta. Larger plates, including olive oil-poached halibut or a deeply comforting Mediterranean fish stew, maintain the restaurant’s understated but polished style. Desserts keep things classic and satisfying, from crème fraîche cheesecake to sourdough bread pudding with roasted pears and caramel sauce.

Name: Terraza Martinez
Address: GF, Shangri-La The Fort Hotel, 30th Street corner 5th Avenue, Bonifacio Global City, Taguig - Metro Manila, The Philippines
Description: On the ground floor of Shangri-La at the Fort, with Spanish chef at the helm, Terraza Martinez presents a sun-kissed taste of Spain. We recommend the tapas – tacos, croquetas or the chilled gazpacho – followed by Iberian pork, bacalao or one of the house paellas. Cooked in wide pans and perfect for sharing, these hearty rice dishes reflect the chef's Valencian roots. The terracotta-toned interior brings a breezy Mediterranean warmth to bustling BGC.

Name: Terrazza Bartolini
Address: via A. Boito 30, Milano Marittima, 48015, Italy
Description: Following its reopening in 2020, this seafront restaurant overlooking the beach and small harbour now offers its guests a choice between its indoor dining room or the panoramic terrace in fine weather (if you prefer the latter, it’s best to book ahead due to its popularity). The cuisine here focuses entirely on simple, unfussy fish dishes, with raw options and cooked dishes which make much use of the local Cervia salt. Daily, market-fresh specials are announced at your table.

Name: Terrazza Costantino
Description: In just a few years, young owner-chef Giuseppe Costantino has turned what was once the family trattoria into an elegant restaurant serving delicious reinterpretations of local specialities. There is just one tasting menu which features either meat or fish (although this can be discussed when you make your booking, which is essential). Given the excellent quality of the food here, this menu offers exceptional value for money.

Name: Terrazza Fiorella
Address: via Vincenzo Maggio 5, Massa Lubrense, 80061, Italy
Description: Housed in the Villa Fiorella Art Hotel, this restaurant boasts a stunningly located terrace with spectacular views of the Bay of Naples and its islands. The cuisine pays tribute to Campania and its top-quality ingredients which the chef uses to create imaginative dishes reinterpreted with his own personal twist.

Name: Terrazza Gallia
Description: On the seventh floor of Hotel Gallia, with panoramic views of the square and Central Station, the restaurant’s limited seating is arranged in a room with modern furnishings and features a cuisine inspired by products and recipes from throughout Italy. A rewarding gastronomic destination in a refined setting.

Name: Terrazza Italia
Address: Levazım, Zorlu Center, Koru Sokak No:2, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34340, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: Eataly is a world-renowned concept that celebrates the finest Italian foods. It always includes a large speciality market alongside superb dining options, such as this chic restaurant with its expansive terrace overlooking the cityscape. It should come as no surprise that authentic Italian cuisine takes centre stage. Think vitello tonnato with its delicate harmony of veal and tuna, al dente tagliatelle with pistachio pesto and red prawn tartare, or a creative take on tiramisu – the chefs pay tribute to traditional flavours while introducing a touch of flair. The extensive menu will definitely leave you spoilt for choice!

Name: Terrazza Tiberio
Description: Housed on the first floor of the Tiberio hotel, this elegant restaurant boasts a terrace overlooking the rooftops of Capri. The regional and island specialities on the menu leave a lasting memory, such as the “montanara” (fried pizza), “casatiello” (a savoury bread from Naples) and the caprese-style ravioli, although more creative options also feature, especially among the desserts. All in all, an elegant dining experience.

Name: Terraço NOTIÊ
Description: Although only recently opened, this restaurant is already being talked about by the city’s foodie community. Located on the rooftop of the Shopping Light building, its design comes as a pleasant surprise as soon as you walk through the door thanks to its decor of yellow tones, glass-fronted kitchen enabling guests to watch the chefs hard at work and, first and foremost, the 18m panel on the ceiling depicting images of nature. At the helm in the kitchen is Paraíba-born chef Onildo Rocha who impresses with his use of typical Brazilian ingredients and combinations that result in intense and striking dishes. His recipes are based around his journeys to different Brazilian regions every season, and are showcased on 5-, 8- and 11-course tasting menus. The name of the restaurant is a fusion between one of the country’s most colourful birds, the tanager (tiê in Portuguese) and the Portuguese word for night (noite).

Name: Terre Alte
Address: via Olmadella 11, località Balignano, Longiano, 47020, Italy
Description: One of the best-known addresses in this region for fish enthusiasts, this restaurant serves freshly caught fish prepared in simple, traditional dishes that allow the quality of the flavour to shine through. A good wine list (particularly champagnes) and a panoramic terrace add to the appeal.

Name: Terroir
Description: Situated in a picturesque square with an old fountain, this 16C building boasts period brick walls and a rustic, romantic ambience – the cosy dining room is on the first floor and there is even a small table on the balcony (make sure you book this ahead). The cuisine focuses on local and Mediterranean ingredients, with highlights such as ricotta gnocchi with a Maltese sausage ragù, while the wine list stars a few international estates.

Name: Terroir
Description: Now at a new address, within the Madalena Beautique Hotel and just a few metres from several of the city’s tourist spots, this restaurant reasserts the character of Portuguese cooking enriched with subtle international touches. The kitchen, led by chef Guilherme Sousa, who has worked with teams at renowned restaurants in Portugal such as Fifty Seconds, Fortaleza do Guincho and Ocean, bases its concept on seasonal produce and memories of his childhood. Here, the offering comes as two surprise tasting menus (5 or 8 moments), both also available in a vegetarian version.

Name: Terrone
Address: Fort St. Angelo, Birgu Waterfront, Birgu, BRG 1734, Malta
Description: Tucked away at the tip of the small town of Vittoriosa and abutting the walls of Fort St. Angelo, Maltese-Australian chef-owner Adrian Hili has been at the helm here for over ten years. His cooking celebrates Mediterranean, Italian and Maltese traditions: the sole, for instance, is perfectly baked in a wood-fired oven and served with Castelluccio lentils from Italy, jazzed up with samphire, and paired with a small pan of homemade fries. Due to ongoing restoration work, the entrance is currently to the rear of the building (not particularly attractive), but once inside the elegant decor and alfresco dining area, which offers a partial yet captivating view of the yachts and Valletta beyond, more than compensate.

Name: Terry Black’s BBQ
Address: 1003 Barton Springs Rd., Austin, TX, 78704, USA
Description: Scions of the legendary Black barbecue clan (whose original Lockhart location has spawned multiple outlets), left the fold to forge their own path, naming Terry Black's BBQ in honor of their father. As is expected for central Texas barbeque, beef takes the pride of place: the slow-smoked prime sliced brisket and behemoth bone-in beef ribs are the main events here, but all of their meat offerings, like pork ribs and sausage, demonstrate the team's dedication to their craft. You'll also find respectable sides, like tangy potato salad or fresh green beans. Seating is first-come, first-served, but don't fret, as the sizeable building, decked out like a well-worn roadhouse, offers plenty of space, both indoors and out.

Name: Tess de Mar
Description: A restaurant occupying a small boutique hotel which stands out for its attractive, contemporary-style interior and exuberant terrace-garden. The cuisine here is contemporary Mediterranean in feel, including Mallorcan dishes and various rice options. The focus at lunchtime is on a daily menu (complemented by the chef’s suggestions), while in the evening attention turns to a much more extensive tasting menu.

Name: Testamatta Ristorante Enoteca
Description: You would probably walk right past this cosy ristorante, were it not for the vibrant energy emanating from it. The atmospheric decor, the bustle of the open kitchen at the back and the congenial service team immediately put you in the right mood. The chef demonstrates a deft hand with traditional fare, from house-made pasta with a bold lamb ragù to a fresh take on tiramisu bursting with those familiar rich flavours. A few surprises, like Dutch cheese or katsuobushi, give things a modern and international twist. Chef Roberto Borelli definitely puts his own stamp on Italian cooking.

Name: Tetsu
Description: What is most striking about this restaurant, which could be defined as a western teppanyaki (the griddle is the gastronomic epicentre of everything), are the two very young chefs behind the proposal (Miguel de Aguilar and João Kather), both under the tutelage of the MOM Culinary Institute but with incredible skills for their age. The restaurant, which is full every day for diners to enjoy its menu (which changes weekly) or the accompanying omakase menu, has a good Japanese-style bar and is clearly committed to market cuisine, often fusing Spanish and Asian flavours. Interesting dishes? We particularly liked their scallop, corn soup and black garlic combination.

Name: Tetsu Sushi Bar
Address: Times Square Suites Hotel, 775 Denman St., Vancouver, V6G 2L6, Canada
