Great service comes courtesy of a friendly and well-trained front-of-house team. The idyllic location in a village surrounded by vineyards, at the foothills of the Palatinate Forest, offers endless possibilities for excursions.

Name: Tivano
Address: LG1 Level, Upper House, 81 Bitieshi Street, Jinjiang, Chengdu, 610021, Chinese Mainland
Description: With a floor-to-ceiling wine wall as the centrepiece, the room is elegantly furnished but without feeling too formal. Diners’ eyes are also drawn to the glitzy bar by the entrance and the semi-open kitchen where pizzas are baked and food is prepared. Apart from the traditional Italian varieties, pizzas also come in Sichaunese twists and in smaller portions. House-made pasta dishes are not to be missed. Round out the meal with torrone semifreddo.

Name: Tiya
Address: 3213 Scott St., San Francisco, CA, 94123, USA
Description: At the edge of Cow Hollow, seasonal produce like squash blossoms, artichokes, and ramps bring a Californian edge to an intriguing contemporary take on Indian cuisine. Both à la carte and tasting options give equal billing to winners like a keema-style jackfruit with crunchy potato, or an eggless take on a bhurji roll, made with paneer and crispy kataifi. The elegant room adds an additional layer of sophistication, down to a well-appointed bar, which offers unique cocktails named in honor of San Francisco neighborhoods.

Name: Tkacka 7
Description: Named after its address down a cobbled side street hidden away in the city centre, this bright and colourful spot welcomes you in with open arms. Start with a drink in the cocktail bar before taking a seat near the semi-open kitchen and enjoying seasonal dishes with a modern, restrained style that puts the focus on just a few skilfully cooked ingredients. The fish dumplings with a rich, creamy shellfish sauce are a prime example of the chefs’ talents.

Name: Tlustá Kachna
Description: This inviting restaurant is located directly on the market square next to the small church. The two inviting dining rooms are done out in white with light wood furnishings and lovely cross-vaulted ceilings. There are also a few tables on the terrace in front of the building. The menu features flavoursome home-style regional fare such as braised rabbit leg with red cabbage and dumplings. Attentive service. The reasonably priced lunch deals are especially popular – reservations are recommended. In the evening, the cuisine is a little more upscale. Tip: Factor in enough time for a stroll through the pretty old town.

Name: Tmun
Address: Martino Garces Street, Mġarr Harbour, Gozo, Għajnsielem, GSM 2413, Malta
Description: This restaurant serves delicious Mediterranean food which is often inspired by fish caught fresh on the day. The vibe is informal with friendly, welcoming staff and there’s an attractive sunny terrace for alfresco summer dining.

Name: Toa Payoh 93 Soon Kueh
Address: Geylang Bahru Market & Food Centre, #01-68, 69 Geylang Bahru, 330069, Singapore
Description: The stall carries three kinds of handmade dumplings – soon kueh stuffed with jicama, rice kueh and kuchai kueh with chives. All varieties boast elastic skin and generous filling.

Name: Toast & Oak
Description: Wood tones, beige textured walls and moss green tiles create a European bistro vibe that’s intimate and vibrant. The menu changes frequently and showcases European-style fusion cooking made with seasonal ingredients. Examples include expertly crafted and big-boned pappardella & fungi. Go for the 5- or 7-course tasting menu for an insight into the chef’s outlook. The New Zealand wine list with 60 by-the-glass choices is truly spectacular.

Name: Tobalá
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: Tobalá brings Oaxacan-inspired cooking and a focused mezcal and cocktail program to Riverdale. The dining room is modern and dimly lit, with clay masks, pottery and design elements that nod to Oaxaca without overt theming. House-made blue and yellow corn tortillas are served with salsa verde and chile de arbol, anchoring a menu built around regional dishes. Tacos de barbacoa feature lamb served simply on corn tortillas, while enmoladas de pato are finished with a dark mole negro incorporating fruit, chiles and spice, reflecting a more traditional expression of the cuisine.

Name: Tobi Masa
Address: The Chancery Rosewood Hotel, 30 Grosvenor Square, Mayfair, London, W1K 6AN, United Kingdom
Description: What was once the US Embassy overlooking Grosvenor Square is now The Chancery Rosewood hotel, and among its restaurants is this London outpost from revered sushi master Masayoshi Takayama. The original modernist style of architect Eero Saarinen has been retained, resulting in a stylish, relaxing space; sit at the seven-seat sushi counter for an omakase experience or at one of the many tables, where you can choose from an extensive menu of contemporary Japanese dishes. Luxury abounds in the ingredients, including the signature toro with caviar.

Name: Toc Toc
Description: Chef Dae-chun Kim’s unwavering dedication to culinary excellence and his insistence on using only the finest ingredients are clearly reflected in the cuisine of Toc Toc. Chef Kim emphasises precision in technique to bring out the pure, natural flavours of each ingredient, highlighting his deep respect for the value of quality produce. His distinctive dishes are a testament to the care and creativity infused into every plate. In addition to his course menus, Toc Toc offers a thoughtfully curated selection of à la carte dishes, allowing guests to experience the full spectrum of flavours the restaurant has to offer.

Name: Toc al Mar
Description: A restaurant right on the beach? Originally a simple fishermen's hut, this restaurant is practically on the sand and has the feel of a traditional beach bar, with fantastic views of the sea and sunbathers enjoying the sun. The menu offers a fine selection of Catalan seafood dishes, rice dishes for two and wild fish by weight, which are usually grilled over holm oak wood. In season, given the large number of visitors due to its exceptional location, we recommend you book in advance.

Name: Toe Drûe
Address: via Corsi 44 r, Sestri Ponente, 16154, Italy
Description: Opened at the beginning of the 20th century to feed shipyard workers, this historic establishment still retains the authentic flavour of its origins. The name “Toe Drue”, which means “thick tables”, refers to the sturdy tables of the old inn. Today, the restaurant continues to celebrate Genoese tradition in an informal and welcoming atmosphere, with iconic dishes such as “cappon magro”, stockfish and other Ligurian specialities that tell a story of sincere and timeless cuisine.

Name: Toet Amsterdam
Description: On a corner plot directly opposite the RAI conference centre, this establishment has a vintage feel with a contemporary edge. The atmosphere is lively and easygoing, with coveted spots right by the open kitchen, from where you can watch the chefs bring a fresh twist to Mediterranean classics. From their signature take on vitello tonnato featuring roast beef and a refined anchovy espuma, to red mullet fillets accompanied by a rich caponata, an intense lobster sauce and fragrant basil oil, exuberance and spicy nuances shine through in every dish. Served à la carte, seven nights a week.

Name: Tofareya
Address: Anas Ibn Malik Road, Al Malqa, Riyadh, 13522, Saudi Arabia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,No alcohol served,Valet parking
Description: Regional cooking of Saudi Arabia is celebrated here at this neighbourhood restaurant. The space is decorated with brightly coloured kilims around the pillars and an array of basketwork shades hanging from the ceiling. Pick up an Arabic coffee infused with cardamom from the cart as you enter. The menu includes Hasawi meat kebabs from the eastern Al-Ahsa region, the well-known Mandi rice dishes from the Aseer and Al Bahah regions in the south, and Marqooq, which is recognised as the official dish of Riyadh. Desserts, like Om Ali, are a must have.

Name: Toh Lim
Address: 37F, Lotte Hotel, 30 Eulji-ro, Jung-gu, Seoul, 04533, South Korea
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Located on the 37th floor of the Lotte Hotel, this Chinese restaurant offers a panoramic city view in a refined, East-inspired setting. The menu spans from dim sum to regional Chinese dishes, with a particular focus on seafood to accommodate a wide range of preferences. A signature highlight is the braised dish of matsutake mushrooms, abalone, and minced pork—a harmonious combination in which the mushroom’s subtle aroma and the abalone’s deep umami enrich the savory pork. Elegant private dining rooms of various sizes make it a fitting choice for family gatherings or business occasions.

Name: Toi Sihng Lauh Yuht
Address: Shop 517, 5F, LuOne CapitaLand Plaza, 268 Xujiahui Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: This restaurant specialises in cuisine from Taishan City, Guangdong. One of their signatures is guo bian, a noodle soup made by pouring rice batter along the rim of a very hot wok – the broad noodles are silky and bouncy; the milky broth is deeply flavoured by radish, oysters and dried shrimps. Choose between crab and beef toppings. Swamp eel rice is another staple on the menu. For dessert, try the herbal jelly made with Chinese pond turtle shells.

Name: Toit
Description: The Boulemberg firm has opened this unusual restaurant on the roof of its manufacturing showroom. Floor to ceiling windows (their stock in trade!) and a terrace command splendid views of the lush green countryside, while a Mediterranean-inspired interior provides the perfect foil to extravagant, full-bodied Sardinian recipes underscored by French technique. Hence the contrast between steamed seabass and cooked sweetbread, paired with a lemon confit beurre blanc. The menu (renewed every six weeks) is rich in big-boned Mediterranean flavours and aromas.

Name: Tok Tok Mee Bamboo Noodle
Description: “Tok Tok” is an onomatopoeia of the sound made by a chef when kneading noodle dough with a bamboo pole, a tradition still practised at the entrance of this shop. Cantonese wonton noodle soup is a must-try for its bouncy noodles and flavoursome shrimp filling. Blanched noodles tossed with dried shrimp roe, and Cantonese barbecue meats are also popular. Also try their Chinese pastry – both BBQ pork pie and pandan kaya dumplings are terrific.

Name: Toki
Address: Leylaty, Al Malik Road, Al Khalidiyyah, Jeddah, 23422, Saudi Arabia
Description: The sultry vibe of this art deco-Shanghai inspired space is the first thing you notice as you walk in. The mocktail bar, soft lighting and pumping music add to the ambiance. The super attentive and very friendly team will guide through their extensive menu that features Peking and Cantonese classics alongside some dim sum specialities. Their lunch menu is also great value, with their mocktails crafted with equal pride. A great spot for a romantic evening.

Name: Tokihami
Description: A kappo izakaya bursting with creativity. The extensive menu captures your attention with its blend of Japanese and Western styles. Sansho pepper simmered in oil becomes ajillo à la Japonaise with seafood and unripe pepper. Popular items are lavished with delicacies: monaka wafers stuffed with foie gras, for example, or truffle omelette. Tsufuhan (‘Gout Rice’) is an ensemble of salmon roe, salted and dried grey mullet roe, sea urchin and caviar. Opulence that piques one’s curiosity.

Name: Tokkotai
Address: Rua do Comércio do Porto, 144, Porto, 4050 209, Portugal
Description: Technique, flavour, fusion and connectivity are the words that spring to mind on entering this restaurant. Here, the Brazilian chef Paulo César works with East Asian techniques and fresh ingredients that deliver maximum flavour to the palate. The offering appears as an à la carte menu and two tasting menus: Chef’s Experience (created with seasonal produce) and Tokkotai Experience (a selection of the chef’s favourite dishes). Don’t miss the cocktails—they’re works of art in their own right!

Name: Toklas
Address: 1 Surrey Street, Strand, London, WC2R 2ND, United Kingdom
Description: Owned by the people behind the Frieze art magazine, this brutalist canteen hasn’t got an uncool bone in its body. From the artwork on its walls to the timeless elegance of its Mediterranean menu, it feels like a thoroughly fashionable place. Works by Wolfgang Tillmans and Ragna Bley adorn the walls, while art posters from the last four decades are up behind the bar; grab a seat on the super terrace to catch a glimpse of the Thames. The cooking is fresh and unfussy, from vibrant bruschetta to Dover sole with fennel and anchovy. The friendly team run the place brilliantly.

Name: Tokumaru
Description: À la carte fare is the star here, to ensure that diners can taste whatever takes their fancy. To convey the passing of the seasons through food, the chef updates the menu every day. A full range of wanmono spoils diners for choice. Potato salad swaps ham for beef; isobe-age is topped with aosa nori, a laver seaweed, to bring out the scent of the sea. Nonchalant twists such as these form lasting impressions.

Name: Tokuo
Description: To usher in the next generation in kappo culture, Tokuo goes all in on à la carte items. Blanquillo, a staple of Kyoto cuisine, is served year-round: at times flame-grilled, at others deep-fried or as sakamushi (seasoned with sake and salt, then steamed). Duck meat dumplings, a heritage from the chef’s apprenticeship days, are lovingly prepared in homage to his culinary mentor. Rice enveloped in grated yam and bean curd skin has been devised as a treat that goes down easy in the summer months.

Name: Tokyo Chinese Ichirin
Description: Sichuan cuisine that strives for a mellow spiciness. The evening prix fixe offering, which combines steamed spicy chicken with liver paté, is highly original. We recommend adding some of the distinctive à la carte items, such as shrimp chili sauce made with whole large shrimp, or fried egg and crab as airy as a soufflé. Weekday lunches are a set menu of twice-cooked pork and dandan noodles. A popular place, so queues form at times.

Name: Tola Rasa
Description: This elegant, minimalist-style restaurant serves two tasting menus (Classici and Contemporanei – the names tell you all you need to know!) from which dishes can also be chosen à la carte style. When we ate there in late autumn, we particularly enjoyed the rabbit with saffron and porcini mushrooms prepared in the open-air kitchen. There are just a few beautifully laid tables, plus a wine list that includes a selection of labels from Italy and France.

Name: Tolcarne Inn
Address: Tolcarne Terrace, Newlyn, TR18 5PR, United Kingdom
Description: 18th-century beams and a wood-burning stove contribute towards the cosy atmosphere at this unassuming pub set beside the sea wall in the heart of Newlyn. As its location would suggest, the menu is centred around fresh fish and shellfish, much of which is landed at the adjacent harbour. The appealing menu doesn't reinvent the wheel but uses tried-and-tested combinations to provide bags of satisfying flavour, in dishes such as brill with asparagus and hollandaise or whole grilled lemon sole with Grenoble-style beurre noisette.

Name: Toledo
Address: Disney's Coronado Springs Resort, 1001 W. Buena Vista Dr., Orlando, FL, 32830, USA
Description: Situated on the 16th floor of Disney's Coronado Springs Resort, Toledo is quite the looker with lofty ceilings in bold colors and geometric tiled floors. Nab a table by the glass wall and you'll have a bird's eye view of the Epcot fireworks. Meanwhile, on the tables Spanish cuisine takes center stage. Tapas kick things off, and pan con tomate is a natural choice. Meat-forward mains include several steak options, as well as a ribeye for two, but the Rioja-braised chicken makes a compelling argument for choosing a different route. End on a sweet note with café con leche, a chocolate choux pastry filled with chocolate and coffee cream.Though certainly not inexpensive, Toledo packs less of a punch to the wallet than other Disney restaurants. -

Name: Tollbua
Description: Set within the Brattøra waterside development, this large brasserie provides exactly the buzzing atmosphere you would hope for. Banquettes and a central bar fit the bill décor-wise, while visible ducting and terrazzo flooring lend an industrial edge. Choose from a set menu of either four or six courses, where a signature dish of scallops can be added as an extra – the accompaniments depend on the season, but could include the likes of sea buckthorn, XO and celeriac. It’s beautiful Norwegian seafood like this including, when available, skrei cod of course, that will be among the highlights of your meal.

Name: Tollius
Description: With its sleek decor done out in burgundy and white and contemporary artwork on the walls, Tollius has an inviting feel. This is also down to chef Barry's expertise in producing hearty classics such as his wonderfully crispy pithivier filled with a rich combination of quail, foie gras and morels. But he is just as adept at whipping up a surprisingly zesty modern dessert involving wasabi and a lemon gel. If the extensive wine list is anything to go by, this place is certainly run by people with excellent taste.

Name: Tom Lawson at the Psalter
Address: The Psalter Hotel, 178-180 Psalter Lane, Sheffield, S11 8US, United Kingdom
Description: For his latest venture, experienced chef Tom Lawson has taken over the titular boutique hotel, and within it sits this welcoming restaurant. Bright, funky wallpaper adds a splash of colour to the room, while a large bureau is filled with Lawson’s own favourite cookery books. His set seasonal menu changes regularly but will likely include his version of cauliflower cheese that nods to his ‘Grandma B’. Elsewhere, look out for high-quality produce such as snow-white Cornish plaice with a terrific beurre blanc. Service comes from a friendly and confident team.

Name: Tomat
Address: 6261 W. 87th St., Los Angeles, CA, 90045, USA
Description: Working with local farmers and suppliers to highlight seasonality along with California's bounty, Tomat features all-day dining, but it's in the evenings when the cooking turns more serious. The design feels as farm fresh as the ingredients, with red-orange leather seat cushions set against a pale green backsplash. Kick things off with their barbari bread with roasted tomato powder-dusted butter before savoring appetizers like charred seasonal vegetables over a smooth ajo blanco. Main dishes are meant for sharing, and the half Liberty Farms duck is a perfect choice. Deftly cooked with crispy skin, it's enhanced with a pomegranate and walnut mole. Sticky toffee pudding with a butterscotch sauce and a scoop of burnt milk gelato is the perfect finale.

Name: Tomatissimo
Description: This popular restaurant with a friendly atmosphere lies slightly outside the city, in a small village. In summer you can make the most of the wonderful terrace by the village fountain, in the shade of the chestnut trees. Bernhard Grubmüller and his kitchen team serve up a conventional and a vegetarian set menu, as well as à la carte dishes, including charcoal-grilled dry-aged beef from their own maturing cabinet. The surprise menu comprising new small courses gives a good overview of the cuisine. Tip: Bernhards Küchentisch for smaller groups (on prior reservation).

Name: Tomidokoro
Description: A place to feed on sushi to your heart’s content. The owner-chef, a man of few words, focuses strictly on sushi to maintain the proper tempo. True to his Obihiro roots, he cooks ancient varieties of Hokkaido rice in a broad-brimmed hagama pot. Fish is cut thick, so guests can enjoy the flavour to the fullest, and vinegared rice servings are generous to match. Standard lunchtime items are a bargain. The chef is generous both in sushi and in spirit.

Name: Tomita
Description: The dining room, unified in white, exudes purity. As if reflecting the owner-chef’s sincere and steadfast character, the majority of his serving vessels were passed down to him by his former mentor. He strives for honest, straightforward cooking, while applying creativity to ingredient combinations. A menu standout that showcases his individuality is the seasonal tempura rice, inspired by tenbara—crispy, bite-sized tempura mixed into rice. For second helpings, dried nori and bonito dashi are added, transforming the dish into a bowl of chazuke.

Name: Tomo
Address: 3630 Peachtree Rd. NE, Ste. 140, Atlanta, GA, 30326, USA
Description: This spot, at the bottom of the chic and modern Ritz-Carlton Residences, is a contemporary space where floor-to-ceiling windows make a big impression. In addition to tables and a sushi bar, there are four seats reserved exclusively for the omakase, arranged well in advance of your visit. Slightly Americanized, the chef's tasting menu offers eight plated courses before progressing into sushi. One dish, chu-toro nuta, presents three pieces of lightly seared tuna in a miso and rice vinegar sauce, balsamic reduction, crumbled pistachio and seared scallions for a rich and satisfying plate. Sushi, such as the decadent and flavorful kawahagi, is equally impressive.

Name: TonTon
Description: The first thing that catches the eye in this restaurant in the Chamberí neighbourhood, which defines itself as a ‘playful space with a little interventionist mentality’, is its eclectic and industrial aesthetic, dominated by the presence of large wooden beams and exposed brick walls. Here, they are open to controlled evolution, which is why they have welcomed the opportunity to put themselves in the hands of chef Nico García Mingo, a chef who brings a wealth of ideas with him after working at restaurants such as Carousel (London) and Meroma (Mexico City). The concept, which will gradually incorporate these new ideas, aims to build on TonTon’s core principle: a commitment to local, seasonal produce, presented with a contemporary twist, allowing it to take centre stage.

Name: Tong
Description: One of the first questions a server here will ask is whether you like spicy food. Answer truthfully because this Thai kitchen does not hold back when it comes to those fiery chilies, which seem to find their way into every corner of the menu. It’s all part of the allure at this sleek dining room, built out of concrete warehouse floors and rustic metal walls accented with flecks of gold.The space is indeed a welcome hangout, where friends can crowd their table with a host of small plates, or kub klaem. Highlights like fried banana blossoms with cucumber relish, or crispy rice with fermented pork sausage and shallots deliver a whirl of textures and sharp flavors. The thinly sliced grilled pork jowl and warming khao soi win over many fans.

Name: Tong Chun Yuan
Address: Shiyue Building, 14A Xinjiekouwai Street, Xicheng, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
Description: Founded in 1930, this state-owned restaurant specialises in Jiangzhe cooking, especially river fish cooked in myriad ways. Diners pick their own catch from the huge live fish tanks. The menu also features roast duck and regional cuisines. The Zhenjiang pork trotter aspic has the perfect ratio of fatty and lean meat; the stir-fried swamp eel in brown sauce is flavoursome and velvety. Reservations are only accepted for bookings before noon.

Name: Tong Fu She
Address: 29 Jiaochangba West Street, Jinjiang, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
Description: This hole-in-the-wall eatery in a residential district may be stuck in the 1990s, but its delicious Sichuan home cooking transcends time. It prides itself on eel dishes – wild onion eel is a seasonal delicacy; Tongfu eel is spicy and aromatic, whereas red-braised eel imparts a mild zing. You can expect heirloom recipes rarely found elsewhere like pork liver curd soup with bamboo fungus and potsticker duck squares, but which must be pre-ordered.

Name: Tong Yin
Description: Green and red drapes and tables covered in white tablecloths lend a cozy, comfortable vibe at this Thai restaurant where sharing is paramount. The menu pulls inspiration from across the region; classics like miang kham, drunken noodles with mussels and curries like khao soi with impressively tender hunks of beef short rib are some of the hits. Servers will always ask for spice preference. Be brave, as courageous diners who embrace the heat will be rewarded with cooking at its most kinetic.

Name: Tongtown
Address: 4F, R&F Center, 10 Huaxia Road, Tianhe, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: Traditional Cantonese fare gets a hip, fresh update at this eatery. As you enter, two stations grab your attention – ho fun rice noodles are made at one, roast goose at the other. As you can imagine, these are the must-tries! The noodles can be fried with sliced beef, served plain with a dip or dressed in a flavoursome roast goose jus. For larger parties, consider pre-ordering the roast goose stuffed with gourmet dried seafood.

Name: Tony García Espacio Gastronómico
Description: This restaurant, on the ground floor of the Avenida Hotel, has a rather informal character, presenting itself as a gastrobar that attracts attention by being decorated, at the entrance, with colourful vegetables that remind guests of the excellent produce of Almeria. In its dining room, with a completely open kitchen, you can discover a fusion between the traditional and the modern, through the à la carte service or any of its set menus, one executive (Miniature Cuisine) and two tasting menus: Fortuny and Jara (the latter 100% plant-based).

Name: Tony's Seafood
Description: You’ll be hard pressed to find more picturesque views than the ones at this charming, sun-lit nook perched right on the edge of Tomales Bay. Under the ownership of Hog Island Oyster Co., the restaurant offers a casual foray into ace seafood that's often been caught or harvested in local waters. Regulars swing by for trays and trays of freshly shucked oysters sourced from California to Washington. Grilled oysters dressed in miso nori butter or chipotle bourbon butter also tempt. Other highlights include mussels steamed in a spicy tomato broth, as well as a signature clam chowder. Seats fill up fast on weekends so consider making a reservation before taking the trek through rolling hills and along the edge of the California coastline.

Name: Tooru
Address: Unit 203, Kyungdong Leen View 2nd Apartment, 1 Gunam-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48095, South Korea
Description: The chef crafts the omakase around daily-sourced seafood, highlighting a spectrum of nuanced flavours. Staying true to the seasonality central to Japanese cuisine, he incorporates Korean ingredients at their peak. Local seafood takes centre stage in dishes rooted in simple, authentic recipes. Among the chef’s signatures are somen dishes, served either in the surinagashi style or with sauces made from seasonal ingredients. Despite its compact size, the bar-centred layout creates a comfortable, relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Topaz
Address: Ömer Avni Mahallesi, İnönü Caddesi, No:42, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34427, Türkiye
Description: Take the lift to the seventh floor of The Artisan İstanbul MGallery hotel and marvel at the breathtaking views over the city, which this elegant rooftop restaurant proudly showcases. At Topaz, a favourite among Istanbul’s food connoisseurs, Mediterranean dishes are given a distinctly Turkish twist, and bold flavours abound. For example, the chef slowly braises lamb shoulder so that the meat is meltingly tender and deeply aromatic. He then serves the succulent meat with a robust sauce made from the cooking juices, along with barley risotto prepared with plenty of cream and chives, black trumpet mushrooms and salted lemon. After your meal, savour the experience a little longer with a drink at the cocktail bar.

Name: Topsoil Restaurant
Address: 13 S. Main St., Travelers Rest, SC, 29690, USA
Description: The name isn't just a playful nod to their inspiration; this restaurant just north of Greenville in Travelers Rest is a veritable showpiece for products sourced from their own 16-acre farm and other nearby farms. There is a relaxed elegance here, with hardwood floors, tall ceilings set with wood beams and wood tables with cushioned chairs. Offering three courses that naturally change with the seasons, guests choose from dishes like seared, meltingly tender pork belly with wild ramp oil and watermelon ponzu sauce to house-made ricotta cavatelli with braised short rib and butter bean in a roasted tomato jus. For the final course, savor a sweetcorn brûlée topped with a madeleine and caramel corn.

Name: Toqué!
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: A classic address that has been a mainstay on Montreal's restaurant scene for over 30 years. Chef-owner Normand Laprise and his team take full advantage of Québec's seasonal terroir to put together their generous dishes. Their solidly traditional cuisine looks primarily to French gastronomy, with the occasional foray into Italian territory. Dinner takes the form of a seven-course tasting menu; at lunchtime, the varied menu features classics such as oyster gratin, beef tartare, and duck leg. The attractive glass-paned wine cellar sets the tone: the establishment has more than 700 wines ready to be uncorked. Attentive welcome and service.

Name: Tora
Description: A contemporary restaurant spread across two floors, each of which has its own sushi bar (the one upstairs is a private space). Here, chef José Osuna showcases his contemporary take on Japanese cuisine on an à la carte (among the hot starters, the trio of Carabinero prawns in three textures stands out) and a Omakase menu (with 10 courses, available at lunchtime only, the other with 17), while using Spanish ingredients as the basis for his cooking. An interesting decorative feature here is the use of a tiger motif (“tora” in Japanese) on the crockery and uniforms.

Name: Torafuku
Description: The main influences on the cooking at Torafuku come from countries like Korea, Japan and Taiwan, so it seems entirely apt that this restaurant is located close to, but not in Chinatown. Lunch is quick and easy and all about rice bowls featuring kakuni-style braised meats, but at dinner the kitchen’s more adventurous side comes out to play. This is when you’ll discover more European elements to the dishes, like tuna tataki with Niçoise salad or Brome Lake duck rillette; and if there’s a dish you simply must order it’s their wonderful Basque cheesecake. The open kitchen is the focus of the understated room, which makes use of plenty of concrete for that ersatz-industrial look. Those of a more sociable bent will enjoy the communal table.

Name: Torero
Description: In Zagreb’s liveliest and most visited quarter, this compact and well-managed restaurant makes an immediate statement upon entry: a wall entirely clad in plants and foliage, evoking Medvednica, the mountain massif to the north of the capital that inspires the cuisine within. Centred on local produce, predominantly organic, the offering is colourful and creative, designed to awaken the senses by exploring the full range of flavour – sweet, acidic, bitter and beyond. Two tasting menus of varying length are available; among the dishes not to be missed is the beef Wellington accompanied by a composition of seasonal local mushrooms. The sommelier is well placed to suggest interesting pairings with Croatian wines.

Name: Tori Tori
Address: 720 N. Mills Ave., Orlando, FL, 32803, USA
Description: Founded by Sean “Sonny” Nguyen, this Mills District concept is a classic izakaya offering bar bites, yakitori, as well as sake and creative libations. The menu is varied and the trendy space is especially cutting-edge. Its name is painted on the side of the building and there's parking behind the restaurant. If that doesn't draw crowds from afar, the eclectic vibe and focused dishes certainly will. Start with skewers before moving on to chicken karaage served with garlic-confit mayo and lemon. A mound of fragrant fried rice may then show up mixed with sweet crab, notes of savory garlic and lemon essence. Reservations are not accepted, so arrive early or risk waiting in line.

Name: Tori-Key
Address: Plaza del Descubridor Diego de Ordás 2, Madrid, 28003, Spain
Description: A Japanese restaurant with a difference where the standard cold sushi is abandoned in favour of Yakitori-style cuisine, with a particular focus on grilled chicken kebabs. However, on the menu you’ll also find options such as chicken wings, superb scallops, and surprisingly good Avila beef tongue. Chef Hiroshi Kobayashi, who is always highly attentive towards his guests, also offers an à la carte option with a choice of 5 or 10 dishes. For an more extensive dining experience, we can recommend the Omakase menu (short and long options).

Name: Torien Yakitori
Address: 48 Zhongming South Road, West District, Taichung, Taiwan
Description: The owner-chef used to run an izakaya and honed his yakitori skills in Japan. Local chickens are prepared fresh daily and grilled with salt to highlight the natural flavour and unique texture of each cut. Check out the oyster meat cut, which boasts a crisp skin and springy, juicy flesh. Dining follows a set menu, to which other rare cuts can be added. A dinky Japanese garden leads to a dining room with table and counter seating, with the latter offering a perfect view of the kitchen team in action. Call to pre-order chicken sashimi, squab or Silkie chicken.

Name: Torikaze
Address: Unit 102, Block 3, M+ Blackstone Apartments, 1331 Middle Fuxing Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: Japanese minimalism meets moody modernism in this joint venture between a local F&B group and yakitori master, Yoshiteru Ikegawa. The head chef, who honed his skills under the master of the Tokyo flagship, has perfected the art of chargrilling. Capons from Shaoxing are grilled over red hot bincho charcoal which seals in the juices and imparts smokiness. Set menus offer yakitori with or without alcohol and otoshi; à la carte skewers only after 8pm.

Name: Torisawa 22
Address: Unit 119, Marriott Executive Apartments Town Hall, 88/8 Soi Sukhumvit 49, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: Behind a non-descript black door numbered 22, charcoal-scented secrets unfold. Diners sit around an L-shaped black counter, watching the grill master as he cooks chicken to yakitori perfection over binchotan charcoal. The menu includes a full range of hormone-free chicken parts – thigh, hatsumoto, wing, liver and gizzard, which are flavoured in one of four tare sauces and seasoned with tri-region salt. The final bite, a grilled chochin, is a real highlight.

Name: Torisho sai
Description: Both charcoal and wood flames are in this restaurant’s arsenal. These ancient heat sources draw out the deliciousness of the free-range Hinai-jidori chicken. The meat is rested in a curing house, judiciously draining moisture to concentrate the flavour. Service begins with a single skewer of breast meat, the better to showcase the poultry’s delicious taste. The chef’s credo is ‘A lifetime in skewering, a lifetime in grilling’. Skewers are built in an inverted triangle, a form that pleases the eye and crystallises knowledge and skill.

Name: Toritama
Address: GF, Greenville, 2 Glenealy, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Tokyo restaurants keep opening branches in Hong Kong and this time it’s all about yakitori. Seats are limited so it’s worth booking ahead and asking for the counter to watch the expert preparation in the kitchen. 40-day-old chickens are used, and 28 different parts of the birds are offered – rare cuts such as sweetbread may need pre-ordering. Pickles made with different produce according to the season make the perfect side dish for the skewers.

Name: Toriyaki Ohana
Description: A menu that is all about chicken in the traditional kaiseki multi-course meal style, from a chef accomplished in Japanese cuisine. Start with an appetiser of chicken breast wrapped with nori seaweed or spring roll of minced chicken with miso. Soup dishes are stocked with chicken wonton. Grilled chicken and duck are not skewered but char-grilled on a wire net, pungently scorched on the surface by broiling close to a hot flame. Chicken bone soup over rice brings down the curtain. Nothing is wasted, proving that every part is delicious.

Name: Torkel
Description: The Stoppel family serve not only cuisine underpinned by Mediterranean and classic influences, but also plenty of regional dishes. If you are having trouble choosing, a failsafe option is the short "Fine Dining Menü". It's also well worth perusing the wine list. Sit back and enjoy your meal in the inviting dining space or out on the pretty terrace. The hotel of the same name has lovely cosy guestrooms.

Name: Torno Subito
Description: A nod to the heyday of Italian cinema, the interior takes you back to the Adriatic Riviera circa 1960s. The red-yellow-blue colour scheme is carried through from the walls to the tableware. The concept by celebrity chef Massimo Bottura involves whimsically and creatively harnessing Italian produce in signature dishes like artisan tortellini in a silky sauce made with parmigiano reggiano aged for 36 months. Stone-baked pizzas are delicious.

Name: Torno Subito Miami
Description: The name translates from Italian to "I'll be right back," and return in short order this restaurant has; having relocated to the Design District. Chef Massimo Bottura's Torno Subito can be found in a stunning space, housed in The Moore, and hotel and private club. Warm and vibrant, it's flooded with natural light and punctuated by pops of color. Playful design aside, this is a serious kitchen that honors Chef Bottura's signature vision for modern Italian cuisine. While the tortellini drawn from his childhood favorite is on offer, swing for one of the dishes with a local twist, such as the cacio e pepe in Miami, where a twirl of bucatini is topped with candied Florida citrus zest for a unique touch of sweetness. Their classic Oops, I dropped the lemon tart has been refashioned with a distinctly South Florida stamp with Oops, I burned the Key lime pie for a whimsical finale.

Name: Toro
Description: Toro has been a mainstay of Boston’s South End for well over 20 years and its longevity is easy to explain: it’s fun, well run and who doesn’t need some tapas in their life every now and then? Round up some friends for a night out, then start with a glass of manzanilla and some pintxos like caña de cabra or matrimonio while you decide what to share. Highlights of the menu include crisp croquetas with creamy bacalao and roasted bone marrow with oxtail – or you can choose one of the paellas. Good cocktails and an all-Spanish wine add to the appeal, while the music plays in tune with the rustic, laid back feel of the place.

Name: Torralbenc Menorca
Address: Carretera Maó-Cala en Porter, Cala en Porter, 07730, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This attractive restaurant, where the cuisine is overseen by renowned chef Gorka Txapartegui (Alameda restaurant in Hondarribia), occupies a farmhouse surrounded by vineyards and boasting a tranquil terrace, all of which comes as a pleasant surprise. It also provides the dining service for the hotel of the same name (awarded one Michelin key) and will delight guests with its tranquil terraces, contemporary Mediterranean and internationally inspired cuisine, and a constant nod to local flavours and native ingredients.

Name: Torre Simón
Description: A restaurant with a historic feel, occupying a delightful colonial-inspired villa on the outskirts of Tona. Choose between the contemporary-inspired à la carte and an impressive gastronomic menu with a pre-determined array of interesting and different starters but with the freedom to choose the main course and dessert from the à la carte.

Name: Torre de Sande
Description: You can enjoy the more casual concept of Atrio’s cuisine in this restaurant occupying a 15th-century mansion located in the heart of the town’s old quarter, just a stone's throw from its famous big brother with its three Michelin stars. In this informal setting, take advantage of the à la carte service or tasting menu to savour dishes with a more traditional and regional flavour, including Iberian sausage, local cheeses, delicious stews, grilled meats, a few fusion-inspired dishes as well as enticing desserts. If the weather's good, it’s well worth booking a table on the attractive terrace.

Name: Torschänke
Description: Right next to the Obertor (the historical city gate), Torschänke is a really inviting restaurant. The atmosphere inside is cosy and pleasingly down to earth, and outside there is a lovely, leafy terrace. Dishes with French and Mediterranean influences are prepared using top-notch fresh produce and served by a friendly, attentive and proficient front-of-house team.

Name: Tosca
Description: Tosca takes its name from the local stone that is an integral part of its interior decor. This eatery surprises with a pleasant terrace, overlooking the canal and the moored pleasure boats! The Mediterranean cuisine served here is delicately brought up to date and the restaurant offers an à la carte service and two tasting menus: Luna and Eclipse (the latter with a wine-pairing option and only for a full table, with a minimum of two diners). We especially liked their veal sweetbread, shiso, carrot, cumin, honey and sesame taco!

Name: Tosca
Description: Set within the ancient Castello di Casole, Tosca establishes itself as a venue of great character, where warm and refined atmospheres take shape among exposed stone, sumptuous fabrics, and elegantly crafted furnishings. In the kitchen, the tasting menus reinterpret the Mediterranean tradition with a contemporary sensitivity, celebrating the seasonality and quality of the ingredients. Complementing this vision is the Territori project, which expresses a deep connection with the property’s agricultural surroundings: the Orti del Castello kitchen gardens, expanded with fruit trees and plants, nourish a cuisine ever more rooted in the land and in the concept of local sourcing. All of this unfolds within an estate of 1,300 hectares certified organic, where the farm-to-table approach finds its most authentic expression. In the warmer months, service moves to the open courtyard, offering an immersive experience in direct communion with the landscape.

Name: Toshokan
Description: Omakase counters can often be a hushed affair but Toshokan strays from the pack. Their location inside Holey Moley, an adult recreation center home to indoor mini golf and a bar with tiki drinks, is the first sign to expect something slightly irreverent. Discover this counter helmed by Chef Saine Wong hidden behind a wall lined with books. Inside, the small, soundproof boîte has room for just a handful of guests.It's far from traditional nigiri; instead find whimsically embellished, playful pieces, as in a spicy margarita-inspired Japanese hamachi topped with finely diced jalapeno, grated lime zest, and sea salt; or the wagyu embellished with grated egg yolk evoking "steak and eggs."

Name: Totoyoshi
Description: A kappo consisting of a counter in an atrium. The chef pours his skill into creations using seafood sourced from and carefully selected by his family’s fish shop. The menu offers a huge selection of dishes, encouraging you to try a variety of flavours. Portions are just right for enjoying with a tipple. Fried items are served lovingly one by one, as in a tempura restaurant. Onigiri and miso soup close out the meal, to warm you up on your way out.

Name: Tow Kwar Pop
Address: Tiong Bahru Market, #02-06, 30 Seng Poh Road, 168898, Singapore
Description: Here, the rojak is made with sliced cucumber, apple and bean sprouts, topped with either crispy tofu puffs or fried dough sticks. The syrupy dressing is rich and tangy, and the ground peanuts give the salad a lovely crunch.

Name: Towa
Description: Japanese chef Shin Okusa is at the helm of the Towa, close to the bustling Aligre market. A champion of old-school French culinary traditions and a true disciple of Escoffier, he not only whisks up the great classics (French lamb stew, breast of duck in flaky pastry), but also sauces, hot terrines and pies, with superlative skill and flair.

Name: Toy
Description: Located in one of the streets surrounding the walled access to the city's castle, this restaurant is easy to find. Behind its curious name, a small tribute to the building’s past (it was previously a toy factory), hides much more than a nod to the past, as chef Massimo Arienti seeks to surprise diners with a proposal that, never better said, plays with flavours, appearance, and textures, making the Italian cuisine that lives in his blood merge with the best local produce of the Marina Alta. There are three elaborate tasting menus (Inizio, Toy maker and Brianza), with dishes as appetising as the Calamarata frutti di mare or, when it’s time fort dessert, the Bacio di Pantelleria.

Name: Tra Di Noi
Description: Decked out with crimson walls and red-checkered tablecloths, this is the kind of place where diners feel like they’re in on a delicious secret—and that’s no coincidence, as the name is Italian for “between us.”Responsible for this Bronx gem's success is Chef/owner Marco Coletta, who runs this dining room, just off Arthur Avenue, with the precision of an air traffic controller and the passion of an Italian direttore. Refer to the wall-mounted blackboard to ascertain the night's offerings; such as the spaghetti alla chitarra that is made in-house and topped with two luscious meatballs and lots of pomodoro sauce. Only a few desserts are on offer, but we recommend a classic finish by way of the ricotta cheesecake.

Name: Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
Address: Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre, #01-12, Blk 505, Jurong West Street 52, 640505, Singapore
Description: Hakkanese Lui Cha is a soupy rice dish in which chicken, cabbage and pickles meet the nuttiness of sesame and peanuts plus a hint of herbs. Order the fish cake, stuffed tofu or fried egg toppings.

Name: Tragatá Málaga
Description: Located in the heart of Malaga, a stone’s throw from the popular Plaza de la Marina, this restaurant has become a must-visit in the city as it reflects the more casual cuisine of famous chef Benito Gómez, a gastronomic gem in Ronda. Here, you can savour dishes such as his award-winning Russian salad, the popular squid sandwich with aioli and salsa brava, and the delicious grilled bone marrow with beef tartare. It offers a change from the more creative proposals because it goes all in on traditional cuisine.

Name: Tragatá Ronda
Description: Discover the more affordably priced and informal cuisine of famous chef Benito Gómez (who also runs the two-starred Bardal), who showcases his culinary repertoire here through an array of small plates and tapas designed for sharing. A traditional proposal with modern touches and a hint of fusion, including dishes such as Mollete de panceta confit (confit pork belly sandwich), cabbage, chipotle mayo and coriander or, in the main courses, a delicious fried sea bass in adobo, with pico de gallo lettuce and adobo mayonnaise. The quality of the raw ingredients is top-notch!

Name: Tralia
Description: Find one of the city’s best pizzas buried in an assuming strip center. The team uses a sourdough base for two very different results: Artisan round is crispy and crackly, while Detroit square has the rise of a layer cake and the fluffiness and lightness of a cloud. Both eat as well as they look; the MVP featuring marinara and dueling vodka and pesto sauces is a winner. Though the menu offers a number of apps and sandwiches, a satisfying Caesar salad blanketed in parmesan and black garlic breadcrumbs is all you need before diving into the main event.

Name: Tram-Tram
Description: A classically furnished, family-run restaurant with a name inspired by this old form of transport in the city. Enjoy traditional cuisine with a contemporary touch, including the occasional international dish and a tasting menu option. The high quality of ingredients it works with is clearly evident in the fish served here (purchased daily at auction), and dishes such as Galician razor clams with a glaze of Manzanilla sherry (from Sanlúcar) and hazelnuts.

Name: Tramo
Description: One of those restaurants that flies the flag for sustainability, a commitment that is behind its decision to prioritise the recycling of materials and bioconstruction building methods. In this setting occupying one of the legendary concert rooms of the Movida Madrileña movement (the space was previously home to the El Garaje Hermético bar), its natural resources are put to effective commercial use through this socially inclusive project with an honest approach and a desire to help people who have difficulty accessing the jobs market. On the menu here you’ll find contemporary dishes prepared using ingredients from small-scale Spanish producers, farmers and local breeders.

Name: Transparence - La Table de Patrick Fréchin
Description: At Transparence, just a short walk from Place Stanislas in a busy pedestrian street, transparency is more than just a name – you can see chef Patrick Fréchin working his magic through the glass partition! His various set menus (including one dedicated to lobster) feature beautifully presented dishes that showcase excellent seasonal produce. There is a quiet terrace to the rear.

Name: Trasteo
Address: María Luisa 24, Zahara de los Atunes, 11393, Spain
Description: A gastro-bar with a pleasant and informal ambiance enhanced by the décor of unusual recycled objects and furniture from the world of fashion, art and surfing that tell us a little about the chef's other interests. Here they concentrate on fusion cuisine, with à la carte service only, combining the flavours of Asia and Latin America, usually based around local produce. Looking for recommendations? Try the Vietnamese-style fried shrimp omelette, accompanied by sweet and sour red peppers, or their original chickpea socarrat with scarlet shrimp tartare and aioli.

Name: Trattoria 'petito
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Located on the outskirts of Forlì’s charming historic centre, this simple, modern yet attractive restaurant serves eclectic and varied cuisine. More traditional fare on offer includes an excellent selection of hams and grilled meats, as well as delicious tagliatelle al ragù, while the menu also features a few more creative options including a few fish dishes.

Name: Trattoria Al Passo
Description: Successive generations of the same family have run this pleasant restaurant just outside the city for over 70 years. Enjoy a selection of fish and seafood dishes (raw, grilled or fried with numerous condiments to accompany your starters) in a maritime themed dining room or on the light and airy veranda. There is a good selection of desserts to round off your meal.

Name: Trattoria Battibecco
Description: Although it calls itself a trattoria, this restaurant situated in a narrow street in the city centre has an elegant ambience, welcoming guests with friendly service and serving an equal balance of meat and fish dishes. Our inspector particularly enjoyed the foie gras sautéed with Lambrusco blueberries and pan brioche, and the “finché c’è bottarga c’è speranza” (“while there’s bottarga, there’s hope”) spaghetti served with tuna tartare, mullet roe, lime and pistachios.

Name: Trattoria Ceriati
Address: Località Cangelasio Ceriati 18, Salsomaggiore Terme, 43039, Italy
Description: Situated in attractive countryside where the plains give way to rolling hills (a perfect destination for a Sunday outing), this simple yet well-kept trattoria serves all the usual traditional local specialities. The typical fresh pasta and the desserts are all home-made.

Name: Trattoria Da Giulio
Description: Giulio keeps the traditions of his native Sardinia alive in this cheerful trattoria. He makes his own pasta and bread every day, and the orata (gilt-head bream) in a salt crust is even filleted at the table. Here the Italian art of simplicity is at its most exuberant. House-made pappardelle with a creamy duck sauce, an aromatic panna cotta topped with a subtly flavoured juniper jam... Da Giulio is undeniably the best Italian in Arnhem!

Name: Trattoria Da Lorenzo
Address: via Fra' Gerardo Sasso 8, Scala, 84010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Slightly off the beaten track in the lesser-known village of Scala opposite Ravello, this authentic family trattoria offers an informal change from the many Michelin-starred luxury restaurants dotted along the Amalfi Coast. Da Lorenzo has been serving simple yet excellent fish and seafood cuisine for decades, with a wonderful and highly recommended array of fresh fish on display. A popular panoramic terrace adds to its appeal.

Name: Trattoria Felino
Address: Shop 3&4, GF, Pao Yip Building, 1-7 Ship Street, Wan Chai, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: The chef hails from Naples and his trattoria serves culinary gems from the Italian city, including his grandma's recipes. Start with the carbonara egg, aerated egg yolk with guanciale and pecorino in an eggcup on a bed of corn kernels. Then move on to the house-made pasta, which embodies the ethos of the trattoria. The tagliatelle with Wagyu beef ragout strikes the perfect balance between meaty and tangy. Book well ahead to secure a table.

Name: Trattoria Glisenti
Description: Situated on the lakefront with some tables set out on a panoramic terrace, this restaurant has been run by the same family since 1890 and is renowned for its typical lake cuisine. Fish and shellfish such as trout, char, shrimp and perch take pride of place on the menu, which also features a few meat dishes and vegetarian options.

Name: Trattoria Guallina
Address: via Molino Faenza 19, località Guallina, Mortara, 27036, Italy
Description: Situated in a small house in an outlying village in the countryside, this is a simple, inviting restaurant where you can enjoy seasonal local cuisine. Excellent wines.

Name: Trattoria I Masenini
Description: In a beautiful part of Verona, right opposite the famous Castelvecchio, this restaurant offers a very relaxing ambience with wood ceilings and informal classic furnishings, subtle lighting and soft background music. The menu features both regional and Italian dishes, with specialities including spit-roast meat and fish. Alfresco dining is offered in summer.

Name: Trattoria La Barca
Description: Run by the Virgilio family since 1967, this popular restaurant pays tribute to historic Bari with its delicious fish dishes and specialities from Puglia. Don’t miss the grilled fish and the reinterpreted cannolo dessert made with sheep’s milk ricotta, pear sauce and pistachio waffles.

Name: Trattoria La Strega
Description: Run by passionate, charming owners, this lively little trattoria is nestled within a quiet residential area, and serves the kind of authentic Northern Italian food that you would find in a good trattoria in Piemonte or Triveneto. Boldly flavoured dishes are best enjoyed from the 'Menu Degustazione', accompanied by a candlelit table and a glass of wine from the extensive Italian selection.

Name: Trattoria Le Viole
Address: strada nuova di Castelnuovo 60/a, Castelnovo di Baganzola, 43126, Italy
Description: Regionally based cuisine with the occasional hint of creativity and a good choice of à la carte dishes are the highlights at this friendly restaurant on the outskirts of Parma. An authentic, genuine welcome, with an attractive lounge near the entrance and the warm ambience of a private home.

Name: Trattoria Leoni
Description: Nestled among the hills of Felino, amid the lush greenery of the Parma countryside, this trattoria in Barbiano has long been a point of reference for those in search of authenticity and the flavours of another age. The cooking of the Leoni family celebrates local tradition, drawing upon recipes handed down from grandmother Erminia and interpreted with care and deep respect. Among the most iconic dishes stands the delicious rabbit alla cacciatora: already boned, enveloped in a tomato sauce fragrant with aromatic herbs, it represents at its finest the substance and richness of Parma cuisine. Not to be missed either is a taste of the Felino salame, aged at length in the family cellar, which speaks with honesty and conviction of the soul of the territory.

Name: Trattoria Margherita
Description: Don’t be fooled by the relatively simple ambience of this trattoria which is situated in the centre of a town with an interesting history linked to the reclamation of the marshes and the dairy industry. Dedicated to the owner’s two grandmothers, the restaurant serves some of Sardinia’s best-known meat and fish specialities.

Name: Trattoria Martinelli
Description: Nestled in the courtyard of the splendid Baroque Palais Harrach, this restaurant has been run by the Barbaro family for 40 years. They champion authentic southern Italian cuisine prepared with ingredients they import directly from Italy. The menu spans handmade pasta, ultra-fresh seafood and time-honoured family recipes. The house speciality is branzino, either baked in a salt crust or grilled – for one or two diners. The inviting interior has a lovely vaulted ceiling; outside, there's a charming courtyard terrace. Practical for motorists: You can park at Garage Freyung, just a short walk from the restaurant.

Name: Trattoria Pomposa - Al Re gras
Description: It’s not just the competitive prices that will bring you back, but above all the fragrant authenticity of Emilian cooking. Among the first courses, the “golden” specialties stand out, namely the fresh egg pastas: tortellini with 24-month Parmigiano cream and traditional lasagne verdi. The main courses are dominated by the indulgent cotechino with stewed beans and an impeccable bollito misto, while the ideal finale is entrusted to the celebrated zuppa inglese. In warmer months, tables in the intimate Piazza della Pomposa lend an even more charming atmosphere.

Name: Trattoria Toscana al Vecchio Forno
Address: Via Poliziano 18, San Quirico d'Orcia, 53027, Italy
Description: In the heart of San Quirico d’Orcia, an intimate trattoria welcomes guests with two small rooms on the upper floor, a main dining room animated by the warmth of the fireplace and an elegant pergola garden that opens during the warmer months. The setting, rustic and genuine, provides the backdrop for cooking deeply rooted in tradition: meats and game, the aromas of truffle and hand-rolled pasta tell the story of the territory with authenticity. Completing the experience, a well-constructed wine list, rich in local labels, accompanies the gastronomic journey with understated expertise.

Name: Trattoria al Pompiere
Description: Founded by a firefighter over a century ago, this venue delivers all the warmth and character of a quintessential Italian trattoria. Wine bottles, wood paneling, checkered tablecloths, cured meats, cheeses, and vintage photographs lining the walls: everything in the dining room creates an informal, relaxing atmosphere. Unsurprisingly, the menu draws inspiration from Venetian classics.

Name: Trattoria al Ponte
Address: via Bertolda 27, località Bornio, Lusia, 45020, Italy
Description: Recognized as the only “Historic Establishment of Italy” in the province of Rovigo, this inviting, family-run trattoria offers traditional cooking with a strong emphasis on meat dishes, served in typically generous portions. The menu is enhanced by daily specials, shared verbally, which can be enjoyed in the warm, welcoming dining rooms or on the charming terrace at the entrance. A park with a natural pond and swimming pool provides an ideal setting also for events.

Name: Trattoria alla Pergola
Description: An old-fashioned trattoria with a simple, homely atmosphere which attracts guests from all over the province who are drawn here by the classic, unfussy regional cuisine. Although the menu is concise, it includes specialities such as tortelli, tortellini, the region’s famous risottos (this is rice-growing country) and renowned boiled meats. Make sure you leave room for the tempting dessert trolley.

Name: Trattoria da Me
Description: Lively and much frequented, this trattoria guided by the energetic Elisa owes its success to a well-judged balance between dishes of the tradition – with fresh pastas prepared by the sfogline and also available for purchase in the adjoining shop – and offerings that draw upon more contemporary techniques. Among the specialities not to be missed are the tagliolini with friggione and squacquerone cream: a thoroughly satisfying and well-balanced dish. For those drawn to the flavours of another age, Sunday is the day to seek out the classic lasagne alla bolognese on the menu, prepared according to time-honoured tradition. The terrace, available even in winter, lends a further note of pleasure to the experience.

Name: Trattoria dall'Antonia
Description: Situated just outside Venice in a quiet area dotted with splendid private villas, this historic restaurant occupies a delightful 19C mansion overlooking the Brenta canal. In the fully renovated, simple and welcoming dining room, fish and seafood reign supreme, with dishes such as raw pink or red Sicilian prawns, Adriatic scampi and tender, lightly seared octopus on the menu. The first courses include classic fish and seafood options, while delicious mixed fried fish from the Adriatic and local turbot are among the stand-out main courses.

Name: Trattoria del Bivio
Description: Situated in the Alta Langa region, this old restored farmhouse is now home to an elegant restaurant with a contemporary rural feel. The cuisine has strong regional roots, although the menu also offers a few fishes dishes. Excellent food, as well as attractive guestrooms and a warm, family welcome.

Name: Trattoria del Bollito
Address: Via Don Giacomo Alberione 3/e, Alba, 12051, Italy
Description: This trattoria in the heart of Alba welcomes guests into a warm, family atmosphere, where wood panelling and smiling staff create a sense of intimacy. The service is dynamic and polite, while aromas from the kitchen evoke Piedmontese tradition. The carefully curated wine list celebrates local labels from throughout the Langhe, inviting guests to discover authentic flavours. One of the most popular dishes is tajarin with rabbit and hazelnuts: thin strands of pasta paired with delicate meat and crunchy hazelnuts, creating a delicious and comforting balance.

Name: Trattoria del Cimino dal 1895
Description: A long, uphill straight runs through the historic centre of Caprarola and leads to the extraordinary Palazzo Farnese. Before reaching it, on the left, lies a stop no less famed, at least gastronomically speaking. The figures alone are impressive: housed in a building dating back to 1370, run by the same family since 1895 and now in its fifth generation, this is a temple of Tuscia cuisine, northern Lazio, albeit with some Tuscan influence. Here one finds dishes so full of flavour that one would happily eat them every day. No less significant is the wine service: around 900 labels, with a wide choice also available by the glass, expertly managed by Samuele Calistri, the cook’s son, who returned to the family after significant international experience in starred restaurants to carry on the legend of this extraordinary trattoria.

Name: Trattoria del Nuovo Macello
Description: Named after the slaughterhouse opened opposite the premises in 1927, this restaurant was taken over 30 years later by the grandfather of one of the current partners, as he was convinced that the restaurant’s busy location would contribute to its success – and he wasn’t wrong! The traditional, regional cuisine served here is reinterpreted with a contemporary flavour and includes delicious specialities such as cotoletta alla milanese made from meat matured for 40 days.

Name: Trattoria del Pesce
Description: A good selection of fresh and raw fish dishes served in a welcoming, vaguely bistro-style restaurant with young and competent staff. Parking can be difficult, but your patience is definitely rewarded!

Name: Trattoria del Vicolo
Description: Overlooking the piazza for almost 50 years, this restaurant has been modernised but has nonetheless managed to retain its friendly ambience, especially in the outdoor space facing the narrow alleyway. The owner-chef serves regional specialities reinterpreted with his own individual twist, such as his famous swordfish rolls served in a type of pie.

Name: Trattoria della Posta
Description: Standing in open countryside, this country restaurant is decorated with elegant and romantic touches, such as silverware and candles. The menu features regional cuisine, including an excellent selection of the best local cheeses. Friendly welcome and experienced service.

Name: Trattoria di Campagna
Description: This famous trattoria, now run by the third generation of the same family, serves traditional, seasonal cuisine from the Aosta valley, enhanced by the occasional imaginative and personalised touch. The new well-stocked wine cellar includes a table for a dozen guests, while sommelier Beatrice is on hand to assist guests with their choice of bottle. Excellent array of delicacies from the dessert trolley.

Name: Trattoria di Coronate
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in a splendid 16C farmhouse just a few minutes from the beautiful Morimondo abbey, this restaurant has an elegant and friendly ambience. The wooden ceiling and furniture in the dining room gives it a warm and welcoming feel, while the cuisine, deeply rooted in the region, is reinterpreted with a contemporary twist. The delicious options on the menu include highlights such as quail breast with a thigh-meat “lollipop” and ravioli stuffed with braised beef.

Name: Trattoria la Colonna
Address: Via Emilia Est 6, località San Nicolò, Rottofreno, 29010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: This classic-style restaurant with a recently renovated dining room is situated on the street that runs through the village of San Nicolò. Although the menu features some meat dishes (on Sundays in winter, this includes specialities such as boiled meats, preceded by anolini pasta in broth and ending with typical desserts such as ciambella cake with zabaione), it is particularly renowned for its wide selection of fish dishes. At lunchtime during the week, there’s a choice of simpler recipes, but if you ask, staff will be happy to offer you the longer evening menu.

Name: Trattoria la Rosa 1908
Address: via del Bosco 2, ang. via Facchini, Sant'Agostino, 44047, Italy
Description: On the outskirts of Ferrara, this classic-style restaurant, run reliably by the same family for five generations, serves cuisine based mainly around local ingredients. Highlights include homemade fresh pasta (their tortellini in broth or served with a delicious creamy Parmigiano Reggiano sauce are excellent) and truffles, served mainly on fresh-egg pasta and risottos but also on some main courses such as foil-baked guinea fowl with fried cream and roast potatoes.

Name: Travieso
Description: Located in a residential district of the city where the chef at the helm, Dani Muñoz, conjures up contemporary cuisine with hints of creativity that is usually centred around seasonal and locally sourced ingredients. The à la carte, which starts with a section dedicated to informal tapas-style small plates, includes enticing options such as “Joselito” Iberian pork sashimi, red mullet, and glazed Iberian ribs. They also offer a tasting menu, subject to booking only.

Name: Tre Galline
Description: A bastion of traditional Piedmontese cuisine, the main dining room at this restaurant boasts a profusion of wood from its parquet flooring to the wood panelling and exposed roofbeams. The warm, hearty cuisine features local specialities such as vitello tonnato, agnolotti pasta with roast meat sauce and a selection of mixed boiled meats, as well as a cheese trolley.

Name: Tre Noci
Description: Situated in the centre of a village in the Bassa Bergamasca area, this long-established, family-run restaurant has a rustic decor softened by the owners’ female touch. The overall feel is that of an elegant trattoria, which provides a pleasant backdrop for delicious specialities from this lowland region, including meat cooked over the large grill in the dining room. There’s also a gazebo for alfresco dining in summer.

Name: Tre Scalini
Description: The menu at this restaurant features meat and seasonal ingredients served in personalised recipes and contemporary-style dishes. There are also three tasting menus: the main one consists of eight courses prepared by the talented chef. The restaurant brings to mind a modern bistro with its warm ambience and attentive service.

Name: Tredecim by Monika Jans und Thomas Huber
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Thomas Huber, representing the 13th generation of his family, and Monika Jans run the long-established Krone with great dedication. She is responsible for the cordial and professional service, and he takes care of things in the kitchen, cooking up seasonal, traditionally influenced dishes. Tableside preparation features prominently, particularly for larger cuts of meat or whole fish for two or more diners. They will also prepare a creatively inspired set menu if you order in advance, and a children's menu is available as well. Anticipation builds from the moment you arrive: freshly baked bread and plaited brioche loaves are displayed in the entrance area, and the magnificent cheese trolley is a feast for the eyes. In addition to the extensive wine list, there is a remarkable sake selection. The wood-panelled interior exudes charm and contributes to the delightful atmosphere, with its rustic dining area and many lovely details such as floral decorations and crown-shaped napkin holders. Should you wish to stay overnight, there are attractive, individually decorated guestrooms.

Name: Treetop
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view
Description: This elegant wooden cabin with panoramic windows sits amongst the trees in the middle of Munkebjerg Forest. An open fire burns in one corner of the room and the well-spaced tables make for an intimate dining experience. Not only is the setting at one with nature but the menu is too, bringing the outside inside via the herbs, berries and flowers that grace the plates and the shelves. The chefs and the service team work together to tell their story – which is centred around honesty, nature and craftsmanship – through dishes such as grilled scallop with beurre blanc and creamed celeriac.

Name: Treibgut
Description: As a sophisticated alternative to Seestern, Treibgut adds to the gourmet credentials of the Lago hotel. Modern cuisine is served in a trendy and exceedingly stylish setting. There are also dishes designed for sharing, such as steaks, whole fish or traditional grazing board. A fine selection of products from the in-house bakery, butchery and ice creamery is available. In summer, the lakeside setting is best enjoyed on the terrace.

Name: Treintaitrés
Description: A leading name in plant-based cuisine in Spain! This famous restaurant, where we are told of a family tradition of hospitality that dates back to 1952, is presented with a refurbished interior in the main room (where there is even a small olive tree), two reserved areas on the upper floor and an attractive terrace. The à la carte, offering a good deal of variety, including traditional dishes, such as stewed snails, as well as a good selection of meat and fish, is supported by two set menus: Business and Degustación de Verduras.

Name: Tremolare
Description: Located on the first basement level, the dining space features an industrial interior crafted from stone and earth, where dramatic lighting accentuates the counter. The menu boasts an extensive selection of appetisers and pasta dishes. Sharing is a great way to sample a variety of flavours, or you can opt for full portions to ensure each plate leaves a lasting impression. The predominantly à la carte offerings evolve according to what is sourced each day, and the kitchen stays open late. Versatile and welcoming, and in the prime locale of Nishi-Azabu.

Name: Trequarti
Address: piazza del Donatore 3/4, Val Liona, 36044, Italy
Description: This modern and minimalist-style restaurant with three small dining rooms full of character provides the backdrop for contemporary-style cuisine which is constantly evolving. The menu includes a few snack options for those in a hurry or looking to sample a variety of dishes in smaller portions. Open at lunchtime by prior reservation.

Name: Tres
Description: Descending into Michael and Emy's intriguing cellar is the start of a special adventure. Tres is raw and pure, vintage and warm. As soon as you enter, you are presented with products from local artisans, mostly sourced from within a 30-kilometre radius. At the expansive dining counter, you will be fascinated by the inventiveness of the self-taught chef. The freshness of fermentations, the depth of garums, the complexity of maturations, the creativity with which products are used in their entirety, processing with the latest techniques... For example, the chef glazes dry-aged turbot with yeast and combines it with pickled wasabi and a dashi with horseradish and garum. A tribute to the seasons that will surprise you more than once!

Name: Triad
Description: Drawing on their experience at renowned restaurants and hotels, Veronika and Uwe Machreich run this idyllic establishment in a quiet, rural village setting. They have a lovingly tended garden that provides herbs and vegetables for the kitchen. The cuisine strikes a good balance between traditional and innovative elements. A shorter version of the evening menu is available at lunchtime – it features modern dishes with a twist, such as Waldviertel organic chicken, pepper and corn pancake and pimientos de Padrón. At lunchtime, delicious options on the "Wirtshauskarte" menu include Kalbsrahmbeuschl (veal lights ragout) or Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy). Or why not take a punt on the surprise menu? There is also a small farm shop selling delicatessen and house-made items. Overnight accommodation available.

Name: Tribeca
Description: A stone's throw from the historic Buhaira Gardens and taking its name from the famous district in New York, Tribeca can now be considered a classic culinary haunt in Seville after more than two decades in business. Here, everything revolves around seasonal produce, working with high-quality meat and, in particular, fish caught that day (much of it sold by the slice and mostly sourced from the Gulf of Cádiz). The proposal? A tasting menu that changes according to what’s available at the market, with 12 savoury courses (including appetisers) and three sweet ones (featuring a sorbet).

Name: Trichards
Description: This chic and modern restaurant-cum-wine bar is located in Munich's Lehel neighbourhood. The owner comes from France, which is reflected in the cooking style. Tip: The "Bouillabaisse-style noble fish and gamba with rouille" is a year-round speciality. The seasonal dishes can be accompanied by your choice from the comprehensive wine list. Ideal for those who like to eat al fresco – the terrace and garden are covered and as such protected from the elements.

Name: Triciclo
Description: This essential restaurant in the Las Letras district, now run by chef Javier Goya, was born with the idea of answering the question: what type of restaurant would we like to eat in? The result is this modest, minimalist-style eatery with a strong focus on top-quality ingredients and sustainability, featuring relaxed dishes that showcase the very best seasonal produce. Their aim is to recreate pure and traditional flavours without closing the door on the culinary cultures of countries such as Peru and Japan. Alongside its set menus (Festival of Classics, Seasonal Tasting, Bar, Weekly etc), it offers an à la carte that is also enticing thanks to the option of ordering half and even one-third portions to enable guests to sample lots of different dishes. An interesting selection of artisanal cheeses is also available.

Name: Trillium
Address: 1 Snow Hill Queensway, Birmingham, B4 6GH, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Glynn Purnell brings all of his experience to bear on this restaurant in a newer part of the city surrounded by gleaming skyscrapers. The fluid menu is overflowing with appealing snacks, small plates and sharing platters, starting with the signature Trillium milk loaf with malt vinegar and chicken fat, followed by the likes of juicy Tamworth pork chop with a light salsa verde and full-toned manchego. The well-versed team are happy to make recommendations, while the impressive wine list offers variety and depth of quality.

Name: Trine
Address: 4F, Building 1, Surpass Court, 570 Yongjia Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: In astrology, "Trine" connotes balance and harmony, in line with the chef's culinary vision. Her dishes seduce with well-matched flavours, subtle creative twists and meticulous plating – think Boston lobster ravioli or cloud brioche. Boasting juicy, pinkish flesh, the jujube wood-smoked baby pigeon goes perfectly with the red wine Sichuan peppercorn sauce. The cosy space feels inviting with its warm hues, solid wood furniture and a suspended fireplace.

Name: Trippi
Address: via Stelvio 297, loc. Montagna in Valtellina, Sondrio, 23020, Italy
Description: This long-established restaurant just outside Sondrio has been run for the past decade by Gianluca, whose experience injects new life into traditional dishes from the local region, as well as introducing the occasional Mediterranean twist. There’s a simpler menu at lunchtime, plus a good selection of local wines and cheeses on sale at takeaway prices near the restaurant entrance.

Name: Trippini
Address: via Italia 14, Civitella del Lago, 05023, Italy
Description: Just a few tables and spectacular views of Lake Corbara characterise this restaurant, which has been run by the same family since 1964. The delicious cuisine is regional in flavour, showcasing home-cooked recipes and typical Sunday favourites yet with a contemporary twist that incorporates plenty of intense flavours.

Name: Trippolt Zum Bären
