The dining room is overseen by his wife, Christine Parodi, who devotes herself to providing exquisite service as well as managing the enticing wine cellar, featuring an extensive choice of French labels.

Name: VEST
Description: Take a seat in this modern, elegant restaurant by the ramparts and you may hear the moving ‘Last Post’ ceremony that takes place at the nearby Menin Gate every evening at 8pm… Local Westhoek delicacies, cooked creatively and playfully, are rich in the distinctive, crisp flavours that depict the spontaneous, market-fresh cuisine of chef Jeroen. Gracious Séverine can be relied upon for her insightful wine-food pairing tips. Book a room at the B&B, ideal to explore the fascinating heritage of Ypres.

Name: VIA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant occupies the ‘piano nobile’ of the Casa Fontcuberta, an aristocratic property in the centre of town with a striking 19th-century decor and scenes of local life and customs depicted on 18th-century frescoes on its walls. The chef at the helm, Nicolau Roger, opts for a contemporary signature cuisine, with strong Catalan roots, which extols the local seasonal produce, bringing its dishes to diners through a complete à la carte where the fish section and rice dishes for two stand out and several menus (Fontcuberta, El pica-pica del VIA and Degustación del Nico).

Name: VIDA
Description: This place has it all: a stylish, upscale decor, enthusiastic, professional and friendly service, and creative international cuisine incorporating both Asian and Mediterranean influences. Diners are offered a choice between the "VIDA" set menu – with meat or vegetarian – and a range of à la carte dishes. The attentive and well-drilled service team is also on hand to offer expert wine recommendations – there is an attractive selection to choose from. Wine pairings to complement the set menu are also available. Tip: Enjoy an aperitif or digestif at the VIDA bar.

Name: VINOTHEK by Geisel
Description: Housed in the luxurious EXCELSIOR by Geisel hotel in the centre of Munich, not far from Stachus, Vinothek is a relaxed establishment done out in a cosy rustic style. The high cross-vaulted ceiling certainly has the wow factor, as does the array of decorative wine bottles. As you might expect from the name of this restaurant, delicious dishes that are inspired by the region and the Mediterranean – such as octopus carpaccio with fennel salad, potato, tomato and basil, or glazed veal cheek with truffle sauce, celeriac and mashed potato – are accompanied by a terrific selection of international wines. Comprising around 800 items, the list is dominated by German, French and Austrian labels. Tip: Check out their reasonably priced lunchtime set menu, which includes coffee and water. Cookery courses and "kitchen parties" are also organised.

Name: VIRTU
Address: MOL Campus, Dombóvári utca 28, Budapest, 1117, Hungary
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Located on the 28th floor of the tallest building in Budapest, the MOL Campus, VIRTU affords stunning views out over this historic city and the River Danube. Start with cocktails in the smart bar, then head through to the spacious, two-roomed restaurant. The menu offers something for everyone, with a pleasing mix of modern and classical dishes. If it’s available, the Keszthely sturgeon with orda cheese gnocchi and champagne sauce is delicious – and ensure you finish with the strikingly modern somlói trifle. A fine selection of wines and professional service from a caring team complete the picture.

Name: VIVE, Maison Mer
Description: Alsace-born restaurateur Adrien Rech opened this institution dedicated to seafood in 1925. After Ducasse, it is now the turn of David and Stéphanie Le Quellec, whose Breton name alone smacks of the ocean, to celebrate fish and shellfish cuisine. The decor is sumptuous, with its huge bar, dining area on the first floor and long banquette seating. David Le Quellec serves food that is good for sharing and made with excellent, ultra-fresh ingredients from fish markets spanning France, from the Atlantic to the Mediterranean. The ceviche of sea bream with coconut milk, lime and coriander is already a house classic – not to mention the dishes prepared from fish matured on site in the maturing cellar.

Name: VIVO Gourmet
Description: Found next to the Plaza Vieja, where the Town Hall and the Monument to the Martyrs of Liberty (Pingurucho de Los Coloraos) are located. This contemporary restaurant offers simple but honest and well-prepared cuisine, with a good selection of starters in the form of pinchos (such as the foie gras, goat's cheese and caramelised apple bar), options for sharing and more substantial fish and meat dishes (among the latter, the 60-day matured Friesian steaks are particularly noteworthy).

Name: VOX Restaurant
Description: Housed in Berlin's Grand Hyatt, very close to Potsdamer Platz, this is a modern and spacious restaurant with an open layout. Diners can enjoy an interesting fusion of authentic Japanese sushi and contemporary cuisine, either à la carte or as a five-course set menu. Friendly service completes the experience. Seats at the sushi counter are particularly popular. Tip: Alongside a fine selection of wines, there are creative cocktails, mocktails and a truly impressive array of whiskies from across the globe – the fabulous bar is not to be missed.

Name: Va et Vient
Description: A sweeping view of the Lys River and the Broel Towers thanks to the establishment’s huge windows and riverside terrace awaits diners. A “rough and refined” (their words) décor provides the perfect foil to Matthias Speybrouck’s creativity, which shines through in recipes that star local veggies and fish from the North Sea, jazzed up with fresh acidic, even quirky (their words again) notes, while exotic ingredients are crafted into punchy sauces. Subtle cuisine throbbing with character.

Name: Vaaghals
Description: One of the city’s modern ‘barcode’ buildings plays host to this bright, relaxed restaurant, where an open kitchen affords views of the chefs, and a terrace is on-hand to make the most of the warmer weather. Three set menus allow you to choose between four, five or eight courses, with optional extras including cheeses and a sharing dessert platter. Cooking is underpinned by Norwegian produce, with their speciality being the in-house aged and cured hams, which are sliced at your table for an additional dash of theatre. Come on a Saturday for a leisurely sharing brunch.

Name: Vaca
Address: 695 Town Center Dr., Ste. 170, Costa Mesa, CA, 92626, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Courtesy of Chef Amar Santana, this cool and rustic tapas bar offers consistently pleasing food and an extensive list of sherries and Spanish wines amid a quirky setting (the banquettes are decorated with jokes). In addition to the beautiful bar area, guests may sit in two outdoor areas or the main dining room with views into the semi-open kitchen. The lunchtime prix fixe is a great deal, though it would mean skipping their wonderful array of tapas and paellas. Standouts include the bikini sandwich, layering cured Jamón Ibérico, Manchego cheese, and a bit of truffle oil into pretty little piping-hot grilled sandwiches. Croquettas de pollo tucked with shredded white meat are perfectly seasoned and fried to a golden crisp.

Name: Vada
Address: 30 Brunswick Street North, Stoneybatter, Dublin City, D07 TP64, Ireland
Description: You can’t help but fall for this rustic little restaurant and its warm, welcoming young team. Dark green walls and dried flowers are indicative of the nature-focused approach, with seasonal produce and a low-waste ethos key to its charms. In the day it’s a simple café serving particularly good coffee and viennoiserie, before the kitchen steps up a gear in the evening with cooking that is a feast for the eyes and the taste buds. Influences from across the globe are poured into the flavour-packed dishes, like an original venison fattoush salad with baba ganoush.

Name: Vairo del Volturno
Address: Via IV Novembre 58, Vairano Patenora, 81058, Italy
Description: Situated in the beautiful Volturno valley, this excellent restaurant boasts classic decor and a relaxed atmosphere. Here, owner-chef Renato Martino succeeds in expressing his love for the region in his dishes, which include the famous Black Casertano suckling pig, duck, lamb and the renowned buffalo mozzarella. The fish is also excellent, with mullet, John Dory and bream all featuring on the menu.

Name: Valentin
Description: Tucked away in a small side street of the island's historic centre, this restaurant is housed in a lovely vaulted cellar. In an attractive, modern setting, you can enjoy seasonally inspired cuisine made from high-quality ingredients, presented as an appealing, concise à la carte selection. Service is provided by a friendly team. The intimate courtyard terrace is a pleasant spot, and the wine bar is also a great draw. The nearby sister boutique hotel, Das Ludwig, is home to Das Ludwig x ae restaurant, which serves a modern, French-inspired set menu.

Name: Valette
Description: Housed in the former Zin space, this contemporary darling is actually a full-circle comeback for Chef Dustin Valette and his brother/General Manager Aaron Garzini, whose grandfather owned the building in the 1940s. Its current look offers plenty of charm, thanks to dandelion-like light fixtures, concrete walls and horseshoe-shaped banquettes. The bill of fare is modern American with a few French twists. Scallops arrive beneath squid ink puff pastry, into which a server pours caviar-flecked champagne-beurre blanc. Then, Peking-spiced duck breast set atop hearty forbidden rice is taken to the next level with a touch of tamarind sauce. For an appetizing end, dig into the smooth block of chocolate mousse with a luscious salted caramel center.

Name: Valhalla
Address: 2020 W. Division St., Chicago, IL, 60622, USA
Description: Ever affable and welcoming, Chef Stephen Gillanders is right at home in this intimate Wicker Park space. A single chef’s counter stretches the length of the dark, polished dining room, offering guests a front-row seat to the kitchen. The tasting menu draws inspiration from a range of global traditions while remaining rooted in quality seasonal ingredients. Seafood is a particular strength, with thoughtfully composed dishes such as a crystal prawn noodle course delicately dressed with lemon oil and an elegant trio featuring kampachi hand roll, oyster and clam ceviche. Beverage pairings, from cocktails to wine, are equally well considered, making this an engaging and polished tasting-menu experience.

Name: Valiente Kitchen Bar
Address: Av. 8 Ote. 230, Centro, Cholula de Rivadavia, 72760, Mexico
Description: On the outskirts of Puebla in the town of Cholula, this restaurant looks to chart its own path in a region rich with traditional recipes. The setting is the first surprise: a sleek warehouse with moody lighting, exposed brick, flickering candles and metal beams. Chef Eduardo Luna’s contemporary Mexican tasting menu matches the lofty space, and he makes a striking impression with smart ideas and refined presentations. Think beef tartare with serrano on brioche, puffy tortilla with mushrooms and mole poblano or a particularly satisfying strawberry salad with vanilla cream and lemon ice cream. Sharp servers keep close watch, while a bartender in the back shakes up refreshing cocktails.

Name: Valle
Address: Mission Pacific Beach Resort, 222 N. Pacific St., Oceanside, CA, 92056, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Roberto Alcocer brings his vision of modern Mexican cuisine to this handsome space in the Mission Pacific Hotel overlooking the scenic Oceanside Pier. The name is a nod to the Valle de Guadalupe in Baja California, Mexico’s premier viticultural region, and the source of a plethora of interesting options on the wine list. The elaborate tasting menu is imaginative, and the likes of mushroom and goat cheese tetela or, say, corn chowder ice cream with trout roe strike a fine balance of creative and flavorful. A roaring fireplace anchors the main dining room run by an attentive team.

Name: Valli di Lanzo
Description: The sign outside this restaurant in the centre of the typical village of Céres bears the words “Ristourànt Valàdess at Lanss con Oubèrgi”. Enjoy regional cuisine with a personalised twist, with local products from the valley featuring in many of the specialities served here, all accompanied by a good selection of regional, Italian and international wines. Outdoor dining area available in summer.

Name: Vallmo
Description: An exceedingly inviting atmosphere awaits you in this restaurant tucked away in a small side street in Prague's New Town. The decor features light natural tones, modern furnishings and wall art. The kitchen team serves up seasonal Czech cuisine, combining traditional and contemporary influences. They also make a point of using locally sourced produce. In the evening, a tasting menu comprising five or eight courses is available. The sommelier recommends the perfect wine to accompany your meal - there is a beautifully curated selection. Shorter menu at lunchtime.

Name: Valuas
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The stunning view of the Maas River from the terrace here is something you won't soon forget. The same goes for the warm welcome you will receive and the genuine hospitality that is so characteristic of the Limburg region. At this restaurant, they aim to please, as you will see from Eric Swaghoven's extensive menu. The range of delectable options includes a rich North Sea crab remoulade with textures of potato and an exquisite shrimp bisque, a guinea fowl and rabbit paté en croûte, mackerel sashimi, as well as a Mediterranean-style risotto. The experienced chef's versatility shines through, and the value for money is exceptional. Oenophiles will delight in the extraordinarily extensive wine list.

Name: Vamos!
Description: The flavours of the Mediterranean lead the way at this energetic bistro with a relaxed vibe. The dishes are designed for sharing and take their cues from Italy in particular, be it in the homemade focaccia, the duck fillet with arrabbiata lentils or the signature tiramisu, which nails all the key components of the classic dessert. The welcoming service team are brimming with enthusiasm, offering genuine hospitality with a smile on their face.

Name: VanOost
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list
Description: Part of Pillows Grand Boutique Hotel Maurits at the Park, VanOost Restaurant is housed in a lavishly converted university building dating back to 1908. Period features including authentic wood finishes and high ceilings harmonise elegantly with the fully open kitchen. From a seat at the counter you can watch Floris van Straalen channel both international influences and regional produce into intricate and imaginative cuisine. His delicate touch with flavour contrasts is demonstrated by his dish featuring langoustines cooked to perfection and glazed with katjang pedis and sambal, accompanied by a curry foam and sweet-and-sour vegetables. Before (or after) dinner, head to Fitz's Bar on the lower ground floor for an expertly mixed cocktail in a setting that transports you back to the Roaring Twenties.

Name: Vanderlyle
Address: 38 - 40 Mill Road, Cambridge, CB1 2AD, United Kingdom
Description: A large, open-plan kitchen takes centre stage at Vanderlyle, which blends shabby chic styling with designer comfort. The well-balanced tasting menu is all about showing off the power of vegetables with imagination and creativity, along with a passion for seasonal produce – all evident in dishes like roasted wild mushrooms with Roscoff onion and Bordelaise sauce. The friendly service team run the restaurant well and the wine or soft drinks pairings enhance the experience. It’s a popular spot, so book in plenty of time.

Name: Vanille
Description: The Crousens are writing a new chapter in the story of this beloved culinary landmark. The period tiled floor and elegant decor are still as charming as ever. With her radiant smile and attentive service, hostess Veronique sets the tone, and chef Jules demonstrates a seamless fusion of classical cooking and influences from around the globe in his set menus. Using a savory foam of asparagus, bumbu and tom kha kai in an original take on asperges à la flamande, the chef brings liveliness to langoustine and pork belly in cuisine that is both refined and inspired. No wonder Vanille is a favourite with the people of Limburg!

Name: Vanne Yakiniku
Address: 2F, 235, Section 1, Dunhua South Road, Da'an District, Taipei, 106, Taiwan
Description: The elegant interior is the brainchild of a team of Japanese designers and floral artists. A sister restaurant of Yoroniku in Japan, it specialises in rare and premium Wagyu cuts. The perfectly grilled chuck flap dipped in organic egg yolk boasts a mellow taste and texture; the tender beef tongue in dashi has a robust meaty flavour. There are plenty of set menu and à la carte options. Consider pre-ordering the hidden menu of sandwich, rice and noodles.

Name: Vantador
Address: 38 Jalan 25/70A, Desa Sri Hartamas, Kuala Lumpur, 50480, Malaysia
Description: Vantador’s vintage yet modern interiors are drenched in soft lighting. Aussie and Spanish beef is either dry-aged for up to 30 days in unsalted butter, or vacuum-sealed and wet-aged in its own juices for 14 days. Steaks are precisely grilled over charcoal and wood to desired doneness, striking a fine balance between smoky and full-bodied, meaty flavours. Non-steak dishes are also available, together with meticulously prepared desserts.

Name: Vantre
Address: 19 rue de la Fontaine-au-Roi, Paris, 75011, France
Description: In France in the Middle Ages, a vantre was a "place of enjoyment", and this neo-bistro devoted to culinary pleasure certainly lives up to the name. A former sommelier (at Le Bristol, Le Taillevent) and his chef serve fine dining cuisine prepared using carefully selected ingredients. Every dish delivers on both flavour and presentation, a case in point being the free-range pork filet mignon with a beetroot medley, lemon balm and wholegrain mustard sauce. There are also over 3 000 wines on the list to choose from. A well-deserved success.

Name: Vapor
Address: Hotel Bellevue, Pera Čingrije 7, Dubrovnik, 20000, Croatia
Description: Within the luxurious Bellevue Hotel, Vapor impresses above all through its spectacular sea views, visible from the broad windows of the dining room and from the terrace overlooking the Adriatic. The interiors, recently renovated, unite contemporary design with an elegance of nautical inspiration. In the kitchen, the chef offers a refined interpretation of Mediterranean cuisine, based on local ingredients, herbs and spices, and enriched by international influences.

Name: Varemottaket
Description: Pumping music and a relaxed, friendly team ensure there’s always a fun vibe at this tiny restaurant situated behind the Annis Pølsemakeri butchery and farm shop. You enter via the shop’s deliveries door, hence the name ‘Varemottaket’, which translates as ‘The Goods Reception’. The narrow, intimate space is filled with high tables and stools, where diners can enjoy a tasting menu with a strong element of charcoal grilling. Unsurprisingly, the fabulous dry-aged meats from the butcher’s make an appearance, such as entrecôte of Norwegian beef.

Name: Varier
Address: 2F, Nakanoshima Daibiru, 3-3-23 Nakanoshima, Kita-ku, Osaka, 530-6102, Japan
Description: Tables sparkling in the light of opulent chandeliers. Taking ‘classic modern’ as his theme, the chef jealously guards traditional techniques while incorporating Japanese ingredients: French cuisine, but à la japonaise. Thus, he also uses a Japanese-style dashi made from kombu and katsuo. ‘Varier’ is French for ‘to change’, expressing how ingredients shift with the seasons, and the changes to the aroma and flavour of each dish. Crockery, much of which is Mino ware, is richly varied.

Name: Varoulko Seaside
Description: If you’re looking for a restaurant with an authentic maritime flavour, this eatery overlooking the small yet attractive port of Mikrolimano will come as a pleasant surprise. Here, the relaxing ambience is in perfect harmony with superb views of the fishing boats moored out front. Traditionally, Piraeus is known as the port of Athens, hence the plethora of tavernas and restaurants specialising in fish and seafood located here. Varoulko Seaside follows the same influence, although chef Lefteris Lazarou takes his maritime cuisine to another level. The freshest ingredients are key to his cuisine which is based around the catch of the day (sea bass, red mullet, grouper, tuna, shrimp, prawns etc) and presented on an à la carte and two tasting menus.

Name: Vato
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: From the same team behind Corima, this casual, daytime tortilleria in Park Slope is all about house-made flour tortilla burritos. Order at the counter and find a table inside or out (when the weather is nice), then settle in and watch the team at work as they assemble orders. One bite in and you'll know what makes this place stand out — it's those precise and pliable tortillas, of course. Try the breakfast-style burnt ends burrito filled with tender pulled meat, scrambled eggs and cheddar cheese or the verde burrito featuring braised pork shoulder tossed with salsa verde and diced potatoes. Finish with one of their house-made cinnamon rolls, generously coated in cream cheese frosting finished with a sprinkling of sea salt.

Name: Vaughan's Anchor Inn
Address: Main Street, Liscannor, V95 FN5R, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Now being run by the third generation of the Vaughan family, this characterful pub has become something of an institution in the coastal village of Liscannor. Its Atlantic-adjacent location, impressive fish tank and walls filled with nautical memorabilia all give clues as to the focus of the menu, where locally sourced seafood underpins the cooking. The dinner dishes are more elaborate than at lunchtime, but quality produce and classically based combinations run throughout, ensuring a satisfying experience. Bright, stylish bedrooms are hung with photos of local sights.

Name: VeRo - Venetian Roots
Description: Within the elegant Ca’ di Dio, in the beating heart of the Biennale, VeRo is an exclusive restaurant with contemporary flair. The cuisine reflects the chef’s soul: essential, personal, never predictable. Two tasting journeys, with freedom to choose between dishes and desserts, complete the experience.

Name: Vecchia Osteria Seseglio
Description: Chef Ambrogio Stefanetti presents a menu of traditional recipes, flavorful and well-crafted, using local and seasonal ingredients. Among his offerings, the pike with crispy skin à la meunière, carrots and green asparagus, or the savarin soaked in yuzu limoncello, lightly sweetened white chocolate ice cream, and finished with raspberry flakes. This place has a genuine soul – it’s impossible not to fall in love with the region in summer! – and the wine list (featuring Italian and regional selections) is truly appealing!

Name: Vecchia Sorni
Description: Situated in the northern wine-producing area of Trento, this trattoria is a real highlight, thanks to its delicious, beautifully presented cuisine which is always full of flavour. The menu includes regional dishes as well as more modern specialities (plus a few fish-based options) which can be enjoyed either in the typical dining room or out on the veranda (also open in winter) with its stunning views of the Adige valley.

Name: Vecio Macello
Description: A former early 20th-century slaughterhouse, today you’ll find a restaurant with a pleasantly classic atmosphere and a kitchen that, despite the building’s original purpose, serves predominantly seafood dishes, though with some meat classics.

Name: Vedge
Description: A stalwart of the city’s dining scene since 2011, Vedge is the creation of husband-and-wife team Richard Landau and Kate Jacoby and is housed in a charming Center City brownstone. It’s not unlike stepping into someone’s house; but someone who clearly has taste and considerable means as it’s a surprisingly large and elegant space divided up into different rooms. The vegan menu offers plenty of choice, with dishes designed for sharing. Judicious use of international flavors ensures the seasonal, plant-based dishes have a vibrancy and vitality that makes them as satisfying as they are memorable. The dan dan noodles with black vinegar-glazed trumpet mushrooms is just one of the standout dishes. Add in seasonal cocktails, warm and flattering lighting, and charming, helpful service and you have all the ingredients for a great night out.

Name: Veerays
Address: 213 E. 45th St., New York, NY, 10017, USA
Description: If the red velvet banquettes, dark brown wooden walls, and decorative accents didn't quite give it away, the menu's "swanky starters," "showstoppers," and "jazzy breads," certainly will. This place exudes that classic 1920s speakeasy vibe, albeit with a twist, as the menu spotlights contemporary Indian cuisine. Bollywood hits and jazz play in the background as you peruse the cocktail list for nods to bootlegging gangsters like Diamond Joe, a slightly sweet gin-champagne cocktail. Rogan Josh, a braised lamb shank with Kashmiri chilis that add subtle heat, is spot on. Fluffy basmati rice with yellow lentils and black mustard seeds is enhanced with coconut for a savory-sweet treat, and don't miss the creamy daal makhani with black lentils and a hint of heat.

Name: Veiramar Arcade
Description: As soon as you walk through the door of Veiramar Arcade, the display cabinet gives you a clear idea of the quality of fish here, while the live tank attests to the freshness of its seafood (langoustines, lobster etc). The simply constructed dishes featuring on the menu are based around top-notch ingredients and a strong focus on the sea, although high-quality meat and rice dishes are also available. The dining room is completely surrounded by glass, hence the stunning views of the mouth of the Verdugo river.

Name: Vendémiaire
Address: 54 boulevard de la Tour-Maubourg, Paris, 75007, France
Description: Just a short walk from Napoleon's tomb, this restaurant takes its name from the month of the French Revolutionary calendar related to the grape harvest. Done out in blue and orange tones, the interior sports a chic, friendly brasserie vibe courtesy of a marble bar and silky-soft banquette seats. The score, made with fresh, premium produce, slaloms between revolutionary and classical as pedigree favourites are given a new spin (egg mayonnaise, beef bourguignon, gratin dauphinois, crème brûlée, etc). A local lad, the owner works with neighbourhood friends and shopkeepers. Good value for money at lunchtime.

Name: Veneur
Description: Veneur has an old-school vibe. The nostalgic charm of this building, with its wooden panelling and beautiful mouldings, has been subtly rejuvenated with details such as modern lighting. The terrace? It could easily be in Paris. The menu also has a bold edge. Yoran Jacobi and Moriaan Koeleman's product-driven kitchen gives pride of place to meat, grilled dishes and fire. For example, you start with a canapé of black pudding with grey shrimp, while briefly grilled rabbit is accompanied by morels and a creamy gravy with cognac. And how about pigeon with a cherry glaze and a gravy thickened with the giblets? Lovers of strong flavours will want to try everything on the menu! Be sure to check out the wine list, which has been expertly compiled.

Name: Vent Debout - Hôtel Les Hautes Mers
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Just imagine: the Île d'Yeu, a pretty little hotel overlooking the sea, a chic, laid-back restaurant, a terrace and a dining area decorated with models of old sailing ships... All in all, a truly charming spot for food lovers who can expect a deliciously fishy regional menu.

Name: Venta de Ulzama
Description: One of the best dining and accommodation options in the Ulzama valley, this tranquil family-run business with over a century of history behind it is guaranteed to please its guests. It occupies a typical mountain-style property in a delightful natural setting, with the unusual sight of a deer farm next door! It features an attractive bar, a room with an open fireplace, a classically furnished dining room with a profusion of wood, plus a traditional menu accompanied by a good selection of suggestions that change according to the availability of seasonal ingredients (vegetables, mushrooms, grilled fish, game etc). The views from the dining room and terrace are superb!

Name: Ventuno.1
Description: Major refurbishment at this renowned restaurant has given it the feel of an informal, welcoming contemporary bistro. Don’t miss the “Napule” tasting menu, which offers just four courses that include anchovies, cavatelli pasta and Neapolitan meatballs in a nod to the owner’s origins. Over time, the wine list has been extended and improved, with wines now stored in a new cellar. Some of the ingredients used in the dishes can also be purchased to take home.

Name: Veranda
Description: Alberto Faccani, the chef at the Magnolia restaurant in the hills inland from Cesenatico, oversees the cuisine at this restaurant, which occupies an elegant veranda on the town’s main avenue – a busy promenade in summer. Fish takes centre stage here, in unfussy dishes that faithfully reflect the maritime traditions of the Adriatic. The menu, alongside daily specials announced at your table, features dishes that include raw fish and seafood, gratins, seafood salads, pasta and risotto, while the main courses feature a selection of grilled, baked and fried fish.

Name: Veratus
Address: Finca los Parrales, Jarandilla de la Vera, 10450, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: A restaurant with a rustic atmosphere that boasts a beautiful green setting, as it is located next to the beautiful stone bridge that spans the river and facing some natural pools that attract lots of visitors during the summer season. The chef-owner, Ángel Sánchez, champions an updated traditional cuisine that always tries to extol the seasonal products of the area. The menu is complemented by two tasting menus, both with the option of food and wine pairings, which require prior reservation: Roble and Quercus.

Name: Verbano
Address: via Ugo Ara 2, Isola dei Pescatori, Stresa, 28838, Italy
Description: Within the confines of the small, charming Verbano hotel on the beautiful island of Pescatori, chef Marco Sacco serves top-quality cuisine in what can only be described as a stunning setting. The contemporary-style dining room boasts panoramic windows, while the outdoor terrace with its views of Palazzo Borromeo and Isola Bella is the perfect setting for dinner in fine weather.

Name: Verdi-Einkehr
Description: This is the second restaurant run by the Lukas family, and here, too, the cooking can be described as ambitious. The modern, seasonal cuisine has a regional bent and also draws on international influences – for instance, "tuna mango, miso, lime" or "braised veal cheeks chanterelles, creamed potato, Barolo red wine". As for the division of labour, owner Erich Lukas and his son Philipp work their magic in the kitchen, while maître d' Helga and her dedicated front-of-house team provide cordial service. Finally, there is the gorgeous location on a leafy estate at the edge of a forest overlooking Linz – in summer, you can take in stunning views from the terrace.

Name: Verjus
Address: 550 Washington St., San Francisco, CA, 94111, USA
Description: In the shadow of the Transamerica Pyramid, Chef Michael Tusk's stylish little wine bar-cum-French bistro returns for its second act as popular as ever. Reservations are a hot commodity, but walk-in guests can angle to snag a seat at the crowded bar or counters. The hubbub makes more sense after considering the appealingly simple, skillfully prepared cuisine, which highlights top-notch seafood and peak produce, as in sweet razor clams anointed with celery brunoise and Meyer lemon. Seasonal offerings change frequently, but you can count on delicious staples like the duck-based pâté en croûte, studded with vibrant green pistachios; as well as a variety of house-made sausages. To finish, a caramelized brioche pain perdu is always in vogue.

Name: Vermeer
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Sebastian Baquero Garces has taken over the reins at this intimate designer restaurant, which is every bit as upmarket as the NH Collection Amsterdam Barbizon Palace, where it is located. A champion of the farm-to-table movement, the chef is passionate about using the freshest locally sourced ingredients, and his creativity shines through in every dish. Think thinly sliced ​​hamachi and zolderspek (aged smoky bacon) with a subtly smoky bacon jus infused with dashi and soy. His cooking is intricate and sometimes complex. And if you would rather not commit to the set menu, you can simply dine à la carte.

Name: Vernick Food & Drink
Description: The eponymous chef-owner is an alumnus of Jean-Georges Vongerichten, so you can expect a cooking style underpinned by a strong, classical base and a kitchen wholly familiar with seasonal, luxury ingredients. There are few things more appealing than spying a section of a menu called “On toast”; try the fritto misto or the blue crab. The choice of raw dishes includes more than just oysters and there’s a mix of small and large plates that you can share, should you be so inclined. Creamy scallops are paired with nutty morels, while spiced lamb chops are turbocharged with eggplant chutney. This longstanding restaurant occupies an attractive brownstone and is spread over two floors but still feels quite intimate; it’s run smoothly and efficiently and there’s a small counter in front of the kitchen if you want to watch the action. If you’re looking for a restaurant aimed at grown-ups, this is it.

Name: Vernáculo
Address: Av. Cto. Frida Kahlo 303, Valle Oriente, San Pedro Garza García, 66260, Mexico
Description: Chef Hugo Guajardo showcases Noreste Mexican cuisine here, with local ingredients bolstering traditional recipes cooked over a live fire. Tortillas are made in-house, so take a seat and have some freshly made tostadas and salsa brought to your table as you peruse the seasonally minded menu. Tacos filled with adobo-marinated and fire-roasted pork belly are a sure thing, especially when accompanied by the spicy red salsa and a kicky piquin chile. Carne zaraza is a dry-brined skirt steak that is enlivened with charred onion atop fresh corn tortillas. The accompanying watercress and cilantro salad is as refreshing as the steak is juicy. End the meal with a pastry, like their tarta de nuez, that's served warm with a scoop of piñón ice cream on top.

Name: Verode
Address: Lepanto 23, Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, 35010, Spain
Location: Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Spain
Description: Halfway between Plaza del Pilar and the magnificent Las Canteras beach, this curious establishment, a kind of bistro inspired by the different landscapes of the Canary Islands (taking its name from a plant endemic to the islands), is a more informal approach from acclaimed chef Abraham Ortega (Tabaiba, with a Michelin star). Here he sets his creativity to one side in favour of good regional cuisine, brought up to date with light touches of fusion. On the menu, which is designed for sharing (half portions are available at the bar and on the terrace), we particularly liked the combination of grilled octopus, corn and green mojo sauce.

Name: Verre Pickl’
Description: Born and bred in Guadalajara, Alexandra Romero has an impressive command of traditional Mexican cooking. Jérôme Gilpin, meanwhile, originally from Portneuf, brings to the table his French flair for making jus and sauces. In their small house in Sillery, which they have converted into a table d'hôte, guests all sit at the same table in the name of conviviality. Quebec produce meets Mexican condiments and European techniques in colourful, perfectly seasoned dishes. Showcasing vegetables from organic market gardeners, the menu is updated every month, adapting its Mexican-inspired fare to the changing seasons. Jérôme provides warm and informative service.

Name: Verschil
Description: Verschil is clearly a champion of the farm-to-table concept, as you will see when you look at the estate’s farmland that is managed by your hostess and which supplies the restaurant in a cornucopia of delicacies. The chef slaloms between classics like saddle of hare, served medium rare and paired with a powerful sauce and modern recipes of the likes of kohlrabi and smoked eel with tomatoes and a subtle tomato gazpacho. We recommend the à la carte lineup, but at lunchtime, you can’t go wrong if you decide to order the delicious soup and dish of the day.

Name: Vert Frais
Address: 43-10 Crescent St., Long Island City, NY, 11101, USA
Description: This sunny, white-walled café in Long Island City feels more like a relaxed neighborhood hangout than a destination dining room, with communal tables and an easygoing daytime energy. Backed by the longstanding chef of Kanoyama, the kitchen delivers well-executed Japanese comfort food rather than high drama. The classic shio ramen is a reliable choice, built on a clean, lightly fatty broth and topped with nicely charred slices of cha-shu, while warm rice bowls layered with tender pork or sushi-grade salmon offer simple, satisfying appeal. Desserts lean playful and crowd-pleasing, with tall, jiggly soufflé pancakes that are light, airy and easy to finish.

Name: Vertigo
Description: Impressive dragons, imaginary beings from the subconscious and striking clouds of colour provide the backdrop in this highly original, aesthetically focused restaurant. Here, chef Javier Moreno has created a restaurant that is able to reflect his dreamlike world, in so doing fuelling his creativity to the full. His highly personalised cuisine is uncomplicated and without any single culinary attachment, hence the mix of ingredients sourced from far and wide.

Name: Vertueux
Description: A stone's throw from Canal St-Martin, this chic and contemporary restaurant showcases the cuisine of Raul Meza, a young chef of Ecuadorian origin, who trained in some of Paris's finest establishments. His fusion dishes strike a subtle balance between French produce and South American influences, navigating between two continents. Try his crispy tacos topped with pulled beef bourguignon, onion condiment and guacamole, or his perfectly cooked cod encocado enhanced with a coconut, coriander and chilli emulsion and accompanied by golden patacones (fried plantain slices). For dessert, an apple served as jelly, granita, confit and vanilla ice cream on Breton sablé.

Name: Verve
Description: A former textile factory has been transformed into a modern brasserie and event space, creating an attractive new destination. The exposed concrete and ventilation pipes give the space an industrial feel; minimalist design and decorative art create a modern and stylish look. The floor-to-ceiling windows can be opened up in the warmer months – there's a small terrace out front. Fresh and flavoursome dishes drawing on regional and international influences are served à la carte or as a set menu named "Herzstück". The rooftop bar is great in summer (Thu-Sat).

Name: Ververt
Description: In a former residential house, now converted into this restaurant, the charm of the local architecture blends perfectly with more contemporary elements. Romain Butet crafts cuisine that embraces tradition and incorporates just the right dose of modernity: confit pork belly, butternut squash and satay; poultry pressé, concentrated jus and local vegetables; Montsoreau apple baba, rosebuds. A good choice of wines at reasonable prices and a pleasant courtyard terrace at the rear.

Name: Verwallstube
Address: Kandaharweg 9, Sankt Anton am Arlberg, 6580, Austria
Description: At an elevation of 2 085m, the gondola ride up here (free with your reservation) is even worthwhile for non-skiers. In addition to the breathtaking view, you can expect ambitious cuisine made from high-quality ingredients that doesn't limit itself to a specific style – rather it showcases traditional, regional, Mediterranean and even Asian influences. Appetising options include yellowfin tuna sashimi, Wiener schnitzel and risotto alla carbonara. The exceedingly friendly and charming waitstaff will be happy to recommend the right wine from the extensive list.

Name: Very Good Vegan Gua Bao
Address: 129 Linsen Road, East District, Hsinchu City, Taiwan
Description: A descendant of a century-old Chinese herbal shop, the owner came up with a plant-based gua bao recipe for his vegan wife. The fluffy bun is stuffed with assorted herbs, veggies and mushrooms. Rather than rich pork belly gua bao, you will taste intriguing layers of herbal flavours and textures. The menu is concise and everything comes with herbal ingredients. Also try the fragrant Chinese angelica soup and the nourishing yam and lily bulb soup.

Name: Vescovo Moro
Description: Situated 50 metres from the basilica of San Zeno (the patron saint of Verona), this restaurant housed in a renovated workshop boasts plenty of outdoor space for summer dining. Here, enjoy eclectic cuisine with an equal balance of Mediterranean and traditional flavours, including an excellent array of raw fish dishes and a small selection of Italian caviar.

Name: Vesta Versilia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Within Twiga beach establishment, in a setting where glamour reigns supreme, multifunctional and equipped with a fully-fledged cocktail bar, the cuisine favours classic recipes and cooking methods, but equally dedicates substantial attention to raw seafood and pizza. From our last visit, the seafood salad—boasting excellent varied citronette-dressed products—and the roast turbot with lemon potato cream and asparagus stand particularly memorable.

Name: Vestibül
Description: With a penchant for seasonal and regional produce, this restaurant serves flavoursome dishes including freshwater fish specialities or classics like Wiener schnitzel. The food and drink are Viennese in style. The imposing historical building, which also houses the famous Burgtheater, makes for a unique location with a stylish interior that has a typically Viennese feel with its striking columns and gorgeous stuccowork. There is also a bar area, where small plates are served. Incidentally, the restaurant premises were once a private carriage entrance for Emperor Franz Joseph I and Empress Elisabeth when they attended the theatre.

Name: Vestige
Address: 715 Washington Ave., Ocean Springs, MS, 39564, USA
Description: On the edge of the Mississippi Gulf Coast in downtown Ocean Springs, Vestige stands firm as one of the most ambitious restaurants in the region. Open since 2013, husband-and-wife team Alex Perry and Kumi Omori pivoted after COVID to a contemporary tasting menu influenced heavily by Japanese ingredients and flavors. Glimmering plates feature the likes of bafun uni, matsutake mushrooms, and koji presented with great care. Guinea hen grilled yakitori style and paired with black truffles and charred eggplant puree was one past highlight. Modern art hangs on the walls, tables are generously spaced, and however complex the cooking may be, the friendly staff and quaint dining room put everyone at ease without a hair of pretension.

Name: Vetch
Address: 29a Hope Street, Liverpool, L1 9BQ, United Kingdom
Description: Located on Hope Street alongside numerous other eateries, there’s a homely feel to this personably and knowledgably run restaurant. The décor is all about understatement, with minimalist furnishings and neutral tones. The modern, well-versed cooking successfully incorporates a range of East Asian influences including shokupan milk bread, Korean chicken wings and char siu pork belly. At dinner, it’s a tasting menu affair which shows the full breadth of the cooking, but keep an eye out for the great value offering at lunch and early evening.

Name: Vetri Cucina
Description: First timers looking for this charming restaurant will probably walk past it a couple of times as the sign is as discreet as the townhouse that hosts it. Inside it’s equally tasteful and traditional in its décor and, as this restaurant has been a feature in the city since 1998, you can expect service that’s impeccably well-organized and attentive. The set price Italian specialties offer plenty of choice, although there’s also a set multicourse menu with wine pairings for those for whom decision making is best avoided. The antipasti could include flavorsome chargrilled octopus; if you can’t choose between the pasta dishes consider the "classic split," which could be spinach gnocchi on one side of your dish and almond tortellini on the other. The Secondi section often sees less-common offerings like baby goat or delicious suckling pig; coffee to finish is a must because they have a magnificent espresso machine dating from the 1950s. If you want somewhere to impress a date or the in-laws, this is the restaurant.

Name: Vezené
Description: If you’re a fan of wood-fired cuisine, we recommend a visit to Vezené (located next to the Evangelismos metro station), a bistro-style restaurant with plenty of elegant decorative touches and an impressive glass porch. The menu is based around traditional Greek cuisine, in which fire plays a key role and via which the majority of the ingredients are prepared, endowing dishes with their unique flavour. It also includes various types of seafood sourced from local producers, as well as aged meats and impressive pastas. At the weekend, the generously portioned Sunday roast is available, which can be enjoyed with all the family, along with the restaurant’s famous signature dessert and a real must: Ari's Deal Closer!

Name: ViEr
Description: Concrete, black and turquoise set the unusual scene in this imposing, yet nonetheless cosy venue. Fine produce such as cottage garden veggies and black chicken from Burgundy takes pride of place in the cooking of chef Bas. Natural, simple and seasonal sum up his ethos, all of which flanked by knockout sauces and at prices that make sense in the heart of Kortrijk!

Name: Via Aurelia
Address: 300 Toni Stone Xing, San Francisco, CA, 94158, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Named after the ancient road connecting Rome to Pisa, guests here can expect contemporary Italian cuisine that draws inspiration from the flavors of Tuscany. The sunny, elegant space boasts a striking backdrop of Oracle Park, located just a stone's (or baseball's) throw away, and adroit service underscores the upscale ambiance. Diners choose between a set multicourse "degustazione," or opt for à la carte offerings; in either case, house-made pastas, like the tortelli Mugellani, filled with a silky potato puree, sauced with a hearty ragù Toscana and topped with an airy Parmigiano espuma, are a must. For dessert, a soft serve swirl of toasted almond gelato and blood orange sorbetto, flanked by a crunchy anise seed pizzella, offers a sophisticated take on a creamsicle.

Name: Via Carota
Address: 51 Grove St., New York, NY, 10014, USA
Description: Occasionally, predictability can be a beautiful thing, especially when it comes to rave-worthy Italian cooking. Via Carota is not so much robotically perfect as it is pleasing—in fact it’s the kind of place where dishes can (and should) be piled on. Italian style and artistry combine in this homey space that features bare wood farm tables, sideboards and whitewashed brick. Plan ahead, since reservations fill quickly at this popular spot. Diners may start nibbling on deep-fried olives that are plump, piping-hot and stuffed with pork sausage. Then, a luscious (and unmissable) risotto cacio e pepe arrives loaded with pecorino and fresh pepper. For dessert, the simple-sounding flourless chocolate cake is downright excellent.

Name: Via Emilia
Address: 1040 Soi Naradhiwas Rajanagarindra 17 Lane 5, Thung Maha Mek, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list
Description: (The restaurant is temporarily closed.) Opened in 2021, Via Emilia brings the soul of Emilia‐Romagna to Bangkok, with authentic home‐style Italian fare. Occupying what was once an old house, the restaurant is adorned with hand‐painted murals echoing Roman architecture. The handmade pastas, freshly baked pizza and classics such as tagliatelle al ragù go down a treat with Italian wines from a well-curated selection; seasonal menus are another option. This pet‐friendly eatery is ideal for both casual meals and intimate gatherings.

Name: Via del Campo
Description: Authentic Italian cuisine is not as easy to come by in France as one might expect. Thankfully there is this contemporary trattoria, which also boasts a few tables on the verdant pavement terrace in fine weather. Chef Enrico Masia whisks diners off on a culinary voyage that takes in every region of Italy; the traditional fare of Sardinia, his birthplace, inspires the lion's share of dishes. Regulars eagerly consult the daily menu, which is devised in line with the food markets and the chef's inspiration on the day. You can expect dishes such as crunchy puntarella finished with an anchovy sauce, Venetian-style calf liver, and clam paccheri with fresh artichokes and shredded bottarga. Tatiana, the chef's partner, runs the show front of house, providing discreet and efficient service that includes astute recommendations when it comes to their selection of Italian wines.

Name: Viaggio
Address: 1727 Dundas St. W., Toronto, M6K 1V4, Canada
Description: You might consider dropping by even if it means you can only order dessert. A novel effort that feels part soufflé, part pancake, the signature tiramisu finished with espresso maple syrup and whipped mascarpone may very well be one of the best desserts in the city. Many dishes, in fact, feel unique to this neighborhood charmer, which could have very easily played it safe with standard Italian dishes. However, this is a kitchen that chooses to top pizzas with smoked pastrami and sauerkraut and chooses to toss tagliolini with charred octopus glossed in smoked dashi butter. Refreshingly creative, such moves pay off in delicious ways.The historic building boasts a handsome dining room as well as an inviting deck lit with strung garden lights.

Name: Vianda
Address: C. Guerrero 2, San José el Mogote, Guadalupe Etla, 68256, Mexico
Description: Drive 30 minutes north of Oaxaca to the village of San Jose del Mogote to find this gem. Vianda is a charming and welcoming spot, set within a house that belongs to Chef Teutli’s parents. It's simple but inviting, with wood tables arranged on a pleasing patio. Meanwhile, the menu is a celebration of the area's agricultural heritage, celebrating local products prepared in creative, untraditional ways. Order croquetas de calabaza (pumpkin croquettes flecked with chapulines) or costilla glaseada (roasted pork rib with cooked agave, green tomato marmalade and mole costeño). Bring cash, as the Internet service is spotty.

Name: ViceVersa
Address: The Elser Hotel, 398 N.E. 5th St., Miami, FL, 33132, USA
Description: Outside it may be sunny and bright, but step inside ViceVersa, just off the lobby in the Elser Hotel, and it's a different mood entirely. Dark wood and rich green walls enhanced with pops of color from framed art lend a sultry moodiness to a room that's buzzing with activity. Most are here for the crispy, thin Neapolitan-style pizza, which is a focus of the tightly edited menu, but raw bar selections like royal red shrimp with a punchy cherry bomb relish and a smattering of appetizers (think salads and meatballs) with a bold Italian-minded approach are equally worthy of attention. All good things must come to an end, but when they're met with gelato, it's so much better. For the best of both worlds, order an affogato martini.

Name: Vicinity
Address: 368 Village Ln., Los Gatos, CA, 95030, USA
Description: Located in an intimate room at the back of Tasting House, a relaxed wine bar, diners at Vicinity will find themselves in an exclusive realm of invention and storytelling. Chef Julian Silvera oversees an intricate modern tasting menu that draws from his life, from a Lower East Side upbringing to foraging in the coastal wilds of California, brought together with vivid creativity and visual flair. Although at times presentation and narrative can eclipse simpler pleasures, the meal is anything but boring, and excellent ingredients keep things aloft. From a tiny everything bagel filled with salmon and cream cheese rillettes, to tender Californian lamb with spring vegetables and an intriguing jus accented with mole and black garlic, passion and dedication are apparent throughout.

Name: Vico Astemio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the village centre surrounded by narrow alleyways, this attractive restaurant is housed in an old barrel warehouse. Here, self-taught chef Massimiliano Vasta serves colourful cuisine that is full of delicious flavours, showcased on two tasting menus and an impressive à la carte with an equal emphasis on meat and fish (despite the port being just a stone’s throw away). We focused on the main course and particularly enjoyed the Zuppa di Pietro, an updated version of the chef’s father’s favourite dish, as well as the tempting array of tasty welcome snacks. There’s an impressive wine list, while the family farm ensures that the extra-virgin olive oil is also of the highest quality.

Name: Vicus
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: This is the successful story of an old family business that initially started life as a café. Located along one of the main streets in Pals, it features a dining room with high ceilings that combines a pleasant contemporary look with more traditional decorative details that link it with its past (bar, floors, furniture etc). The chef, who has trained in a number of leading restaurants, creates elaborate traditional cuisine with an imaginative touch that never fails to please guests and includes several interesting seasonal dishes and a few rice options (such as black rice with squid and a pear aioli). They also offer a tempting lunch menu (all dishes are designed to be shared, for a minimum of two people)!

Name: Vidocq
Address: Avenida Huesca, Sallent de Gállego, 22640, Spain
Description: Named after the Frenchman considered to be the world’s first private detective way back in the early 19C, Vidocq is a superb option for those who prefer not to venture too far from the nearby ski slopes. The contemporary, fusion-style cuisine here toys continually with flavour, incorporating interesting Asian nuances (particularly from Thai cooking) into typical Aragonese mountain recipes (the vast majority of its ingredients are sourced from small-scale local producers). A single seasonal set menu (La Montaña Nómada) is the mainstay here, inviting guests on an evocative gastronomic journey though this region. Don't miss his unique Cheesecake!

Name: Vien Dining
Address: 3 Ba Trieu Alley, Hai Ba Trung Ward, Hanoi, 11606, Vietnam
Description: Vien, meaning "harmonious circle", celebrates happiness, abundance and the roots of traditional Vietnamese culture. Made with local ingredients, regional specialities are given a modern twist by a creative young team of chefs. Diners can observe the open kitchen on the ground floor or relax in one of the intimate private rooms upstairs. Choose à la carte or opt for the seasonal set menu (pre-booking required), and don't miss the refreshing house-made Junbucha.

Name: Vietnam House
Address: 93-97 Dong Khoi Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: This elegant French Colonial-style building stands in the middle of a well-heeled central district of this vibrant city. Led by Vietnamese-Australian celebrity chef Luke Nguyen, the team elevates traditional Vietnamese cooking with modern twists, in tasty dishes such as duck noodle soup, juicy char-grilled chicken, and truly delicious silken bean curd dessert. The generous portion sizes are ideal for groups; the lunch set menu is perfect for solo diners.

Name: Vieux-Bois
Address: Avenue de la Paix 12, Geneva, 1202, Switzerland
Description: Just behind the United Nations, Geneva's hotel management school (EHG) invites the general public to step into its restaurant, which is devoted to upholding traditions of excellence. In an elegant, historical setting and under the eagle eye of their teachers, students craft a seasonal lineup that combines respect for the ingredient with textbook technique. Examples include a cappuccino of celeriac with crunchy hazelnuts and brioche bread, or a roast breast of duck flanked by a gutsy gravy and melt-in-the-mouth carrots. On the dessert side, an explosive chocolate bar and pear sorbet add a decadent final flourish to your meal. The perfect place to sample pedigree recipes of flawlessly cooked traditional fare at extremely attractive prices for Geneva.

Name: View Mun
Address: 289 Mu 7, Mu Ban Thap Thai, Chaeramae, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, Ubon Ratchathani, 34000, Thailand
Description: This riverside restaurant is decorated in a dark regal style – black painted wood with red and gold trim – from the era of the former Lan Chang province. It serves a grand selection of local fish, deboned, in a quintessentially Isan style. The terrace seats are made from dark tree stumps set around rugged wooden tables. The vegetables are grown by the owner in their garden, and the pickled vegetables are made in-house using a unique recipe featuring fresh coconut water. It’s best to arrive before sunset to enjoy the stunning view of the Mun River.

Name: Vik's Chaat
Description: This bright orange and yellow building looks big enough to be a warehouse, which makes sense as the inside is not only a counter-service restaurant but also a market. Its namesake chaat may be the star here, but lunch specials are a fantastic bargain. For $15, you can get perfectly tender tandoori chicken with a mouthwatering smoky char, served alongside basmati rice, dal, raita and papadum. Family-friendly and casual, this Indo canteen seems to attract everyone with its excellent chaat, authentic flavors and breads—especially the fried and puffy bhature ideal for sopping up spicy chole. A glass case filled with colorful sweets reminds everyone to save room for dessert.The kitchen closes early at dinner, so unless you’re an early bird, go for lunch.

Name: Vila Planinka
Description: The fine alpine house that is home to the restaurant stands at the end of the Jezersko valley, just steps from the Austrian border. Here one breathes fully the Central European atmosphere that draws visitors to places of such character: imposing mountains and limpid streams frame a landscape of great appeal. In the kitchen, a young chef offers straightforward cuisine inspired by the ingredients and culinary traditions of the region. Trout and venison are constant presences, alongside excellent local beef, at times served with a delicate sweet-and-sour beetroot rose. Guests can choose from the à la carte menu or entrust the evening to one of the chef’s tasting menus. The remarkable cellar also merits a visit: a selection devoted almost entirely to Slovenian wines and, a genuine rarity, around 250 labels available by the glass. A well-deserved compliment to the accomplished sommelier Vanesa.

Name: Vila Podvin
Description: Vila Podvin is a country hotel and restaurant set amid the countryside surrounding Radovljica. Its greatest asset is the magnificent garden, an ideal setting for a cuisine that is fresh and intense, conceived to celebrate the local and seasonal produce of Upper Carniola, a region poised between Italian, Slavic and Germanic influences. The interior dining room is presented in a classic style, but for a more intimate and romantic experience the secluded tables in the alcove are particularly recommended. Among the most accomplished dishes, the agnolotti with morels and walnut sour milk stand out, as does the house signature: pheasant with rhubarb and buttermilk. All of this is accompanied by a carefully curated selection of Slovenian and international wines, with distinguished labels and notable vintages. The service is of an excellent standard, perfectly attuned to the spirit of the place through a well-judged balance of warmth and professionalism.

Name: Vila do Peixe
Address: Rua Doutor João Abel de Freitas 30-A, Câmara de Lobos, 9300-048, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An ideal lunch or dinner option for visitors given its location in the upper section of the old town (opposite the municipal market) and its huge windows boasting superb views of both the bay and the ocean. If you’re looking for authentic maritime-inspired cooking and fresh fish caught the same day you won’t find a better option, as guests can choose the piece of fish they want to eat as if they were in the market; the fish is then weighed in front of you and cooked immediately on the grill. Typical dishes well worth sampling, if available, are the popular limpets and sea snails.

Name: Vilagut
Address: Bisbe Estalella 15, Vilafranca del Penedès, 08720, Spain
Description: The name of the spacious restaurant (with a minimalist elegance and laid out on two floors) pays homage to chef Julià Bernet’s maternal grandfather. Her traditional cuisine comes courtesy of an à la carte (we particularly enjoyed the pigs’ trotters with langoustine tartare and stuffed morel mushrooms) and through a two tasting menus (Tradición and Territorio). As we’re in a region with a great wine tradition, its unsurprising that the choice of wines has been meticulously curated.

Name: Vilas
Address: Unit E103, B1F, Velaa Sindhorn Village, 87 Lang Suan Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: Revitalised in a vibrant new setting, Vilas pops with colour, energy and personality; the staff's pink and neon-green uniforms echo the playful mood. Rare regional Thai produce is paired with premium imports such as Japanese seafood and Spanish shrimp, creating dishes that marry Thai and European techniques with thoughtful precision. The move to an à-la-carte format offers greater flexibility and the commitment to modern Thai cuisine feels sharper than ever.

Name: Villa Arcadio
Address: via Palazzina 2, località Villa di Salò, Salò, 25087, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: The new chef at this restaurant prioritises beautiful presentation in his modern interpretations of Italian dishes, which are even more enjoyable in summer when meals are served outdoors, surrounded by greenery and with fine views of the southern part of Lake Garda and its shoreline.

Name: Villa Ariston
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Housed in a magnificent late-nineteenth-century villa in perfect preservation, overlooking a garden with an enchanting view of the Kvarner Gulf, Villa Ariston is a gastronomic destination not to be missed in Opatija. While the façade retains the elegance of Austro-Hungarian style, the dining spaces, also known as Gallo Nero, are distinguished by a classic and refined elegance distributed across three interior rooms and, above all, a captivating terrace that extends towards the sea, affording views of unforgettable beauty. The kitchen makes the most of excellent produce, predominantly from the sea, though with sound meat options also present. Alongside the main menu, interesting off-menu dishes are not lacking, while the recipes strike a pleasing balance between tradition and discrete contemporary touches.

Name: Villa Augusta
Description: This villa in Drôme Provençale houses a spacious, simply furnished restaurant. The rotunda section has large bay windows looking onto a terrace, which is a delightful spot in summer. In the kitchen, the chef ensures a smooth transition with modern dishes that honour past traditions. The menu is based on seasonal produce and local ingredients: Ventoux pork, Ardèche bacon, cod au gratin with aioli, flavoursome beef cheek confit with red wine and corn espuma. In the evening, there is a choice of two set menus, with each dish also available à la carte. Indulgent desserts and comfortable guestrooms are the icing on the cake.

Name: Villa Baroni
Description: This romantic restaurant on the lakeshore has a welcoming, elegant ambience and a delightful terrace for summer dining. The cuisine pays particular attention to top-quality, seasonal ingredients prepared in traditional recipes with a focus on fish. Cosy, Provençal-style guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: Villa Busch
Description: This beautiful, lavishly refurbished villa in an elevated location not only boasts a lovely terrace for summer, but the interior of the restaurant is also tasteful with its stuccoed ceilings, wooden floorboards and modern designer chairs. The chef-patron's kitchen team creates dishes with Mediterranean and Asian influences, including many fish specialities. Plus, you are waited on by a warm and charming front-of-house team.

Name: Villa Coucou
Address: Laan Van Meerdervoort 6, The Hague, 2517 AJ, Netherlands
Description: Villa Coucou radiates sophistication: hardwood floors, marble tables, artwork on the walls and an abundance of natural light create a luxurious setting. Start with an aperitif at the bar or in the wine cellar (with its own pétanque court!) before heading upstairs to admire the garden vista. The chef champions sun-drenched French cuisine enhanced by Mediterranean touches and a confident command of modern techniques. Red mullet, for example, is briefly pan-fried on the skin before being paired with a millefeuille of confit celeriac and a subtly spicy hollandaise sauce. An appealing lunch menu is available during the day and, in the evening, you can choose between à la carte dishes and a tasting menu. This chic spot might just become your new favourite.

Name: Villa De Winckels
Address: via Sorio 30, località Marcemigo, Tregnago, 37039, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This 16C villa, a period residence with many intimate dining rooms, boasts a picture-postcard setting. The cuisine is typical of the Veneto region, with dishes such as home-made pasta (with or without stuffing) and home-produced charcuterie on the menu. Named after General De Winckels who once lived here, the Cantina del Generale offers a wide selection of the best vintages which include local wines and labels from further field, with a focus on Amarone wines.

Name: Villa Feer
Description: Owner Kathrin Bucher has been running this restaurant in an attractive old villa near Lörrach exhibition centre since 2012. Dine in the cosy, bright interior or, in summer, out on the wonderful terrace. They serve lunch only: until 3pm you can order the set menu or from a small menu compiled from favourite dishes of the last decade. After that, there are desserts and ice creams/sorbets until 5pm.

Name: Villa Fiordaliso
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Villa Fiordaliso is one of the beautiful early 20C villas that line the lake front. Surrounded by verdant grounds and extending out into the lake on a pontoon, the restaurant serves creative, modern cuisine. The chef is equally at ease with fish and meat dishes, while the extensive wine list suggests that you’ll have no problem finding your favourite wine here.

Name: Villa Giulia - Al Terrazzo
Description: Housed within an elegant late-19C hotel overlooking the lake, this romantic restaurant offers stunning views from its outdoor terrace. The cuisine is mainly Italian, with the occasional modern and imaginative twist. Add in a charming stone wine cellar stocked with top-quality labels, plus modern guestrooms for anyone wanting to prolong their stay.

Name: Villa Greta
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: This collection of former farm buildings is named after the grandmother of the current generation of owners and incorporates a pottery workshop, shop, characterful bedrooms and this homely bistro. The vaulted red-brick ceiling and wood-burning stove give it a rustic feel, while the lovely garden and terrace allow you to soak up the rural peace and quiet. The cooking offers hearty classics such as a full-flavoured bigos with deer and rye bread.

Name: Villa Hammerschmiede
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in a charming villa dating back to 1893, this is a thoroughly inviting destination. Whether seated in one of the comfortable dining areas or the light and airy pavilion, you can look forward to ambitious, classic and regional cuisine, presented in the appealing "Villa Lunch" set menu or in the evening the three- to five-course "Feinschmecker-Menü". There is also an à la carte selection featuring dishes such as farm-raised duck with red cabbage and creamed chestnuts, or Dover sole for two. The terrace is especially lovely in summer, and comfortable accommodation is available as well.

Name: Villa K
Address: 32 rue de la Libération, Oberlauterbach, 67160, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Zacharie Kraemer chose his native village as the location for his first venture, after cutting his teeth in prestigious establishments such as L'Arnsbourg in Baerenthal. Where the family vegetable garden once stood, this brand-new, timber-clad building now looks out onto northern Alsace's magnificent landscape of hills and meadows, with the blue line of the Vosges in the distance. Served in a sleek, contemporary dining room with an open kitchen, the chef's dishes are characterised by aesthetic and technical precision. Hints of Japanese or Scandinavian influences shine through, and the flavours are also perfectly balanced, thanks in particular to the judicious use of punchy condiments that always add a welcome twist to the dishes. What is more, prices are wallet-friendly! Four lovely guestrooms are available for overnight stays.

Name: Villa Kabala
Description: Perched high up the hillside in the Badacsony region, with far reaching views of Lake Balaton, this period villa was once home to artist István Farkas. Now under the ownership of an ambitious and enthusiastic couple, the team here are establishing it as something of a destination restaurant. A concise lunch offering is followed by a well-balanced tasting menu – you won’t get much more local than this, with the cheese, salami, sausages, beers and wines all family made. They even have their own coffee roaster and pottery workshop too. Book a bedroom with a terrace and look forward to a fantastic breakfast.

Name: Villa Mamas
Address: Muroor Road, Eastern Road, Al Rawdah, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,No alcohol served,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Bahraini chef Roaya Saleh leaves her mark in Abu Dhabi with this elegant Khaleeji restaurant. The interior is a little like a conservatory, with plants all around, colourful artifacts, fresh fruits on display, and shelves of homemade spices, syrups and chefs’ cookbooks. The menu showcases flavours and dishes loved in the region, such as chicken machbous and hummus topped with lamb cubes.

Name: Villa Mamas
Address: Al Bujairi Terrace, Diriyah, Riyadh, 13711, Saudi Arabia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,No alcohol served,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Chef Roaya Saleh brings her own style of Khaleeji cooking from her native Bahrain to this restaurant overlooking the UNESCO World Heritage site of At-Turaif. The room has a calm, chic feel with neutral tones and subtle bursts of colour. Even on a warm evening, the air-conditioned terrace is the place to be. The menu mixes a few Mediterranean dishes with wider Middle Eastern selections. Share some dumplings and koftas, followed with lamb mozat – a typical Bahraini dish of lamb served on vermicelli rice and pine kernels. End with the muhallabia for dessert, a comforting and creamy rice and milk pudding with rose water.

Name: Villa Marinette
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This former inn has a modern interior, completely redesigned in black and yellow tones, with light parquet flooring and plant motifs; in the pretty enclosed garden the pleasant terrace remains. The contemporary food is devised to reflect the seasons by a young chef who respects the ingredients.

Name: Villa Medici
Description: This spruce villa enjoys a delightful location in a quiet residential area on the outskirts of the city. Diners here are pampered with friendly service, Mediterranean flavours and Italian wines in a chic and inviting atmosphere. In addition to à la carte options, there are daily specials and a tasting menu. A charming terrace is laid out to the side. Plus, there are five attractive guestrooms.

Name: Villa Mon Rêve
Address: 2 levée de la Divatte, Basse-Goulaine, 44115, France
Description: On the banks of the Loire, this restaurant is set in a pretty townhouse dating back to the late 19C. It has been proudly serving its guests delicious food in an elegant, cosy decor for 75 years – so you could say it's an institution. The current chef uses the finest local produce in traditional regional cuisine: frogs' legs with parsley butter or a herb sauce; local fish (pike, pike-perch and sea bass) with beurre blanc; golden-brown calf sweetbreads with a morel cream. A smiling welcome awaits you, as does a large shady terrace surrounded by a bucolic garden planted with colourful flowerbeds. Mon Rêve really is a dream!

Name: Villa Más
Address: Passeig de Sant Pol 95, Sant Feliu de Guíxols, 17220, Spain
Description: This restaurant occupies an impressive setting in an old Modernist-style villa overlooking Sant Pol beach, as well as boasting a pleasant terrace that gets very busy in the evening. The traditional, maritime-inspired à la carte features top-notch fresh fish straight from the auction (sea bream, John Dory, grouper, sea bass etc), a few rice dishes and fideuàs. The extensive wine list has a particular penchant for wines from Burgundy.

Name: Villa Paramesa
Address: Plaza Martí y Monsó 4, Valladolid, 47001, Spain
Description: A longstanding family-run restaurant that has grown in size and comfort since its move to the bustling Plaza de Martí y Monsó, one of the main tapas areas in this provincial capital. It now boasts a terrace, tapas bar where there is never a lack of atmosphere (in both spaces you can enjoy a selection of individual small snacks, such as the baby squid roll in its own ink, with lemon and piparra chilli pepper, and the “three little pigs” featuring suckling pig with ajoblanco, ponzu and pibil), and a glass-fronted kitchen that is immediately visible on the way to the contemporary-style dining room. The contemporary-inspired menu includes dishes such as Ravioli with snail bolognese, basil and ham velouté, and the tasty “carrillera de ibérico” with pear, cardamom, fresh herbs and mustard.

Name: Villa Patrizia
Description: For many years, Patrizia and Nico Bodean have been running this tasteful establishment with dedication and Italian charm. She is part of the kitchen team, and he is in charge of service – with a kind word for every diner, he brings a personal touch – "molto gentile"! You can choose from an à la carte menu as well as various set menus – tempting options include "basil gnocchi, salsiccia, morels" or "Label Rouge guinea fowl breast, leaf spinach, Parmigiano cream". In summer, the pavilion of the classically elegant villa is a particularly delightful spot: the floor-to-ceiling windows can be opened completely, so you feel as if you are on a terrace as you savour the Italian cuisine.

Name: Villa Pignano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: A veritable Garden of Eden just 15km from Volterra, this 300ha estate is home to a restaurant with a strong zero-mile philosophy. This is backed up by its careful use of ingredients grown or produced on the estate itself, such as vegetables, olives and grains, as well as chicken, pork and honey – a sustainable approach that results in delicious, contemporary cuisine. The dishes here are fresh and full of flavour yet elaborate and modern in style (note the simpler menu at lunchtime). The interesting wine list explores Tuscany through its choice of top-quality organic labels as well as including wines produced from the estate’s own vines.

Name: Villa Rothschild Grill & Health
Address: Im Rothschildpark 1, Königstein im Taunus, 61462, Germany
Description: Located in a park, this smart bankers' villa dating from 1894 is home to a stylish boutique hotel as well as this chic, modern and elegant restaurant. Patrick Bittner, who previously made a name for himself at Frankfurt's Français, where he was head chef for many years, is now at the helm here. The classic cuisine has international influences, and the dishes are served à la carte. Good news for oyster enthusiasts: There are always three varieties to choose from. The modern and elegant interior is tastefully decorated, with a striking open fireplace in the centre of the room serving as the focal point and creating a wonderful atmosphere in winter. In summer, the lovely terrace beckons. Tip: Head to Titian's Bar for a digestif. Lunch is also available on Sundays – ideal for day trippers.

Name: Villa Saint-Antoine
Description: In a former textile mill on the banks of the Sèvre Nantaise, diners can enjoy a smart brasserie interior (red velvour banquette seating, bay windows) and the chef's delicious repertoire of dishes, which are full of flavour and lovingly prepared. Last but not least, service courtesy of a young and dynamic team.

Name: Villa Salina
