She is in charge of the friendly and attentive service and also presents the regional wines; he takes care of the cooking. His creative Mediterranean cuisine with international influences includes exciting combinations, for example, "Skrei, red lentils, purple curry, dates, pak choi" or "Pork cheek and thick flank (from an organic farm, Biohof May), spelt, broccoli, mustard, lychee". There is also the option of picking dishes from the small à la carte menu to put together a three- or four-course set menu. Lunchtime revolves around a simpler daily menu.

Name: Weinhaus Neuner
Description: With its cross-vaulted ceiling, herringbone parquet and wood panelling, this old restaurant has lost nothing of its traditional charm. The food is just what you would expect from an upmarket Munich inn – try the flaky pastry crust chicken fricassee pie. The Kaiserschmarrn for two is also a firm favourite! Nice wine list with a good selection of champagnes.

Name: Weinlaube
Description: A wonderful place where hospitality is truly a way of life. With its family feel and warm-hearted service, Weinlaube exudes a cosy, welcoming charm. In this converted farmhouse nestled in a quiet hamlet near the Austrian border, diners take their seats in cosy Stube-style dining rooms or out on the gorgeous terrace and tuck into honest, seasonal fare with the odd international twist. The menu features dishes such as pan-fried char from Brüggli fish farm, Béarnaise sauce, peas and potatoes, or tajarin, agretti, cured egg and bottarga. Open-fire cooking also plays a key role – a barbecue, fire ring and smoker are set up outside the kitchen. The wine list boasts an impressive selection.

Name: Weinrestaurant Turmschänke
Description: In this restaurant in the Nicolaiturm, the lovely historical details, such as paintings and original furniture dating from 1912, foster a rustic yet elegant feel. The waitstaff are pleasingly laid-back and down-to-earth. Meticulously prepared seasonal dishes are served as a set menu or à la carte; mouthwatering options from the barbecue are also available. Complete with helpful descriptions, the wine list comprises some 140 items – most are from the region, but international labels also feature. Special wine evenings are also hosted here.

Name: Weinstube Baldreit
Description: This lovely wine tavern may be somewhat hidden away in its pleasantly quiet location, but it is well worth seeking out – especially in summer, when the charming secluded courtyard terrace comes into its own. Along with a relaxed atmosphere with rustic charm and friendly service, diners can look forward to an array of different flammkuchen, speciality mussel dishes and regional classics. The seasonal specials of the day are written up on a wooden board or presented verbally. The restaurant has plenty of regulars and is always busy, so it's advisable to make a reservation!

Name: Weinstube Sibylla
Description: A good place to come for unpretentious cuisine. The menu ranges from classics such as Wiener schnitzel or Berlin-style calf's liver to a "Gourmet Tradition" section featuring dishes such as saddle and shoulder of venison in pasta sheets, with tenderstem broccoli and an elderberry jus. There is also a selection of vegetarian dishes and a range of delicious desserts. Lovely old wooden floors, wood-panelled walls and pretty decorations make for a charming atmosphere. The verdant terrace is also inviting. Guestrooms are available in the adjoining Erbprinz hotel.

Name: Weinstube am Brühl
Description: These former stables have been converted into a delightful restaurant, in which terracotta tiles, warm colours and an old brick ceiling lend a real country feel. The international cuisine on offer follows the seasons closely. The six-course "Weinstuben-Menü" (with vegan/vegetarian alternatives) comes with optional wine pairings. À la carte dining is also possible. Attentive service comes courtesy of a friendly and adept front-of-house team. Tip: Summer barbecue evenings (Jun-Aug) – booking recommended. Charming and elegant guestrooms are available in the Hotel Am Brühl.

Name: Weinwirtschaft Kleines Jacob
Description: As soon as you enter this restaurant, you fall into the embrace of its inviting atmosphere: Charming tavern-style decor, soft candlelight and warm, attentive service make for a delightful setting – no wonder so many locals flock here as regulars. The Austrian cuisine is a hit – the "Schmankerl Brett" (snack platter) and stone-baked flammkuchen, as well as Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) and Wiener schnitzel are crowds-pleasers, not forgetting the caramelised Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake) with stewed plums. There is also an appealing three- or four-course set menu dubbed "Lütten Jacob Genusstafel". The wine list is exclusively Austrian, and some labels are available by the glass. No wonder this place has become a favourite of so many foodies!

Name: Weisser Bock
Description: Pretty details such as wood panelling and historical photos contribute to the cosy atmosphere in this traditional establishment. The kitchen serves up a fine selection of dishes made from regional and international ingredients, from which you can choose a three- to six-course menu. The à la carte menu includes appetising dishes such as "beef tartare, anchovies, brioche, caviar" and "turbot, wild cauliflower, capers". The hotel of the same name has comfortable and tastefully decorated guestrooms. The central location is another trump card.

Name: Weisses Rössli
Description: At Weisses Rössli, good-quality ingredients are transformed into dishes inspired by regional and Mediterranean cuisine, always prepared with a modern approach and a creative twist, including some appealing vegetarian and vegan options. Diners can compile their own set menu, selecting two to five courses – one standout is "Giulia's Ravioli Del Plin". The atmosphere is invitingly down-to-earth, and the service team is very friendly and dedicated. A terrace in the rear courtyard makes for a peaceful retreat from the street. Tip for motorists: Hürlimannareal and Sihlcity car parks are nearby.

Name: Weitmoser Schlössl
Description: In the setting of this picturesque centuries-old castle, you can savour classic cuisine with an Austrian twist. The dishes are meticulously crafted from first-rate ingredients including organic beef from the restaurant's own on-site farm. Be sure to try the Wiener schnitzel and the Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) – the side dishes are also excellent, such as the exquisite creamed spinach. Adept service comes courtesy of a friendly front-of-house team. Delightful terrace.

Name: Weißes Roß
Description: This restaurant serves as a delightful alternative to the fine dining restaurant at the long-established Weißes Roß spa hotel. The flavoursome regional fare is made with fresh seasonal produce – the meat is from the hotel's own butchery. As well as the classic Wiener schnitzel, the menu features appealing dishes such as "lake trout, salsify, fig, quinoa". You can choose à la carte or, in the evening, take a punt on the four-course surprise set menu. As for the decor, it runs the gamut from charming and traditional, to stylish and chic, to modern and elegant. Attentive and extremely cordial service ensures a seamless dining experience.

Name: Wellington Arms
Address: Baughurst Road, Baughurst, RG26 5LP, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: At this smart cream pub they have their own herb and vegetable beds, keep sheep, pigs, chickens and bees, and source the rest of their meats from within 20 miles. Menus feature 6 dishes per course – supplemented by a selection of specials – and cooking is generous and satisfying. Smart, rustic bedrooms come with slate floors, sheepskin rugs and big, comfy beds.

Name: Wen Tao
Address: 191, Section 3, Taiyuan Road, Beitun District, Taichung, 406, Taiwan
Description: Meaning ‘my home’, this single-storey courtyard house circa 1950s set amid tall residential buildings will instantly teleport guests back to grandma’s home in the countryside. The menu is mostly Taiwanese from a bygone era, with occasional Hunan and Xinjiang offerings. Old-time steamed river perch with fermented chillies has complex savoury umami with a mild kick. Barrel chicken is chargrilled in the courtyard and needs pre-ordering.

Name: Wenjian Hainan Cuisine
Address: Shop 502, 5F, K11 Art Mall, 6 Zhujiang East Road, Tianhe, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: This restaurant, which doubles as an immersive gallery housing some of China’s best-known art, is the brainchild of a Hainan-born owner and a French curator. The signature poached chicken is made with free-range, antibiotic-free, coconut-fed Wenchang birds about 180 days old. Pair with chicken oil rice perfumed by shallot and sand ginger. Hainan-style stir-fries, and eight-treasure chicken soup, steamed in a whole coconut for six hours, are also recommended.

Name: Wenpapa Goose
Address: 274, Section 3, Simen Road, North District, Tainan, 70444, Taiwan
Description: The goose-themed menu is the handiwork of an owner-chef who has over 20 years of experience with the bird. He opened his own joint in 2008 and moved to this location in 2018. His signature saltwater goose uses 90- to 100-day-old birds, precisely blanched in brine, left to cool and boasting juicy flesh. Classic goose meat rice is paired with braised bamboo shoots and scallion goose oil sauce for a lovely crispy crunch and deep aromas.

Name: Wenwen
Description: Chef Eric Sze and partner Andy Chuang bring the vibrant flavors of Taiwanese cooking to Greenpoint with Wenwen. The façade is unmissable with its tall and narrow wood-framed windows allowing for a full view of the clean, airy interior. Menu highlights include the sacha hot honey popcorn chicken garnished with Taiwan dust, a sugar-spice combination that ratchets up the flavor, as well as whole striped bass stuffed with fish paste and glistening in a pool of black sugar-yuzu vinaigrette and fermented black beans. The 16-hour oxtail broth and tender braised beef share the spotlight in the beef noodle soup that nourishes body and soul.

Name: Wenzhou Said
Address: Unit 3, 2F, Building 4, PAC, 718 Wuding Road, Jing'an, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: This restaurant entices with authentic Wenzhou fare, especially seafood from the Zhejiang coast. A banquet of cold appetisers, claypot dishes and seafood is displayed in three areas, making the ordering process interactive and fun. The must-try sautéed pounded fish and shrimp is the Chinese version of paillards in a savoury glaze with a subtle peppery kick. For a sweet finale, try fried sticky rice balls in brown sugar syrup.

Name: Westerndorfer Stube
Description: Housed in Landgasthof Karner, this cosy eatery makes for a lovely down-to-earth alternative to the adjacent fine dining restaurant. The outstanding chef, Hannes Fussel, proves that he is also a master of home-style cooking, turning seemingly simple dishes into a delight for the palate! Think lamb lights, Wiener schnitzel or the classic Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) – diners are bowled over by the depth of flavour and presentation. Regional ingredients take centre stage, and the decor complements this perfectly: rustic charm and subtle modern elements make for a harmonious whole.

Name: Westphalenhof
Description: This stylish and sophisticated restaurant is somewhat tucked away in a residential area. Here, the Westphal brothers – one is the chef, the other the sommelier – delight diners with delicious food and excellent wine recommendations. The menu features international dishes that take their cue from the seasons, such as confit halibut fillet in nut butter, potato scales, cauliflower cream, dried tomatoes and Sardinian pasta. The walk-in wine cellar accommodates 120 different labels. The restaurant is also open for lunch on Saturdays and Sundays.

Name: Westwood
Address: New Walk, Beverley, HU17 7AE, United Kingdom
Description: This smart, modern restaurant occupies one wing of an impressive Grade II listed former courthouse and has a sheltered courtyard terrace for warmer days. It’s run with passion by twins Michele and Matthew, whose menus mix traditional dishes with some more modern, creative choices.

Name: Wettsteins Restaurant
Description: This beautiful property is a little out of the way – on summer days, diners can enjoy sitting out on the terrace. The restaurant has been around for many years. In addition to cordial hosts and friendly service, the programme here includes regionally influenced cuisine, which you can choose to sample as a set menu or à la carte. The menu also features barbecued meat, such as rump steak, and classics like schnitzel and roast joint.

Name: Weyerhof
Description: On the outskirts of Weyer, this farmstead, the presence of which was first documented in 1130, lies at the start of the Habach Valley. It has been owned by the Meilinger family since 1832, and today the hotel and restaurant are in the capable hands of siblings Elisabeth and Franz Meilinger Jr. The chef and his team cook up traditional regional cuisine with seasonal influences, served either à la carte or as a tasting menu, and accompanied by an all-Austrian wine list. A five- or seven-course surprise menu is available Fri-Mon by pre-booking (one day in advance). The cosy space with a beautiful vaulted ceiling has a rustic feel; the terrace commands a view of the Hohe Tauern mountains.

Name: Weyringer Wallersee
Description: The restaurant is somewhat hidden away, in a beautiful location overlooking the lake, Wallersee – the view from the terrace to the rear of the building is magnificent, but you can also enjoy the view from some of the tables inside. Eclectic design details such as furniture, figurines and pictures, as well as strikingly colourful Murano glass chandeliers, create decorative accents in the tasteful interior. The cuisine is international, so the menu features dishes such as "oysters, artichokes, lemon marmalade" and dim sum with various fillings. Friendly and attentive service.

Name: Whale Chicken Noodles
Address: 156 Sri Chant Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: The secret to the popularity of this eatery is its tender chicken and flavoursome broth – made with chicken bones and vegetables, it has a rich, meaty and naturally sweet flavour. Enjoy the breeze as you dine on the sidewalk, just like a local.

Name: Whampoa Soya Bean & Grass Jelly Drinks
Address: Whampoa Makan Place, #01-52, 90/91 Whampoa Drive 91, 320091, Singapore
Description: Tofu pudding is freshly made on the spot – just add toppings such as grass jelly, red beans or lotus seeds. Or try their drinkable versions, in which the soybean flavour is complemented by the velvety texture of a smoothie.

Name: WhatSaeb Boat Noodles
Description: Come here to get your fix for boat noodles. The owner hires a kitchen team from Thailand to make sure it’s made properly. There are many toppings and noodles to choose from, but pork rice noodle soup with extra pork cracklings will be your best bet. In addition to the noodle soup, the menu also features an array of Thai classics, such as curry, som tum salads and desserts. On weekends, make sure to try their mango sticky rice.

Name: Where The Light Gets In
Address: 7 Rostron Brow, Stockport, SK1 7JY, United Kingdom
Description: This large, loft-style restaurant is located on the top floor of a Victorian coffee warehouse and its open kitchen truly feels like part of the room. The set sharing menu is based on seasonal British produce and often incorporates foraged ingredients; this combines with a low-waste ethos that involves using a range of pickles and ferments. Walk-ins are available at the kitchen counter, where you can enjoy low-intervention wines and bar snacks. The same team run Yellowhammer, a bakery and pottery studio just around the corner, which provides both excellent sourdough and tableware for the restaurant.

Name: Where there's Smoke
Address: 7 Silver Street, Masham, HG4 4DX, United Kingdom
Description: As the name suggests, this well-run restaurant is all about cooking over coals, and a lovely smoky aroma will hit you the moment you enter. Sitting within a delightful market town, it has a chef-owner who’s also a potter, so the good-looking, brightly decorated space comes with plenty of bespoke creations to admire – he even made the wooden tabletops as a side project too! The seasonal set menu is based around whatever prime produce is available at the time, be that monkfish cheeks or saddleback pork, with the ember-based cooking resulting in comforting, satisfying dishes.

Name: Whiskyplaza
Description: By the Nikolaifleet canal, one of the oldest buildings in Hamburg, which is located in the city's oldest street, is home to this appealing bar-cum-restaurant. Spanning a few floors, the space capitalises on the historical charm of the original structure (1697): Crystal chandeliers, wooden beams and modern furnishings as well as shelves lined with decorative bottles all come together to create a genuinely warm ambiance. The kitchen serves its modern take on classic cuisine as a sophisticated set menu or à la carte. Highlights include scallop with barley, salt marsh herbs, apple, seaweed caviar and beurre blanc, or flat iron steak with pumpkin seed dumplings, kalette, mushrooms, apple and cheese. Given the restaurant's name, it might come as no surprise that the extensive selection of spirits includes around 1 100 whiskies.

Name: White Bull
Address: 166 New Lane, Oswaldtwistle, BB5 3QW, United Kingdom
Description: This neighbourhood pub’s menus cover everything from bar nibbles to pub classics; they offer lunch, afternoon tea and dinner – and even serve breakfast on Sundays. The endearing team take care in everything they do, portions are generous, and dishes not only look good but taste good too. The traditional Lancashire cheese, onion and ale pie is a must-try.

Name: White Elephant
Description: This restaurant at the Zurich Marriott Hotel is a must for fans of authentic Thai cuisine. Made with market fresh produce, the food is authentic and authentically spicy! Whatever you do, don’t miss the curries.

Name: White Hart at Fyfield
Address: Main Road, Fyfield, OX13 5LW, United Kingdom
Description: There’s a lot to love about this imposing 15th-century chantry house. There’s the three-storey, vaulted dining room for starters, joined by a cosy open-fired bar and a minstrels’ gallery, while outside you’ll find a terrace, a vegetable garden and an outdoor kitchen with wood-fired oven. The cooking is guided by their own seasonal produce, with both British and Mediterranean influences on the flavoursome, carefully prepared dishes. The friendly service team run the restaurant well.

Name: White Pillars
Description: The husband-and-wife team of Chef Austin Sumrall and Tresse Sumrall opened White Pillars almost a decade ago. Guided by the seasons, Sumrall's cooking is inspired solely by locally sourced ingredients. This is a farm to table, nose to tail spot where the menu shifts accordingly. It's not overly fancy or fussy, but it is skillful. Dinner may offer items like tender pork bourguignon with creamy rosemary mashed potatoes before a dessert of peach cobbler with house-made sweet corn ice cream.

Name: Whitehouse
Address: Vermane Park, Terbatas iela 2, Riga, 1050, Latvia
Description: Whitehouse's dining terrace is one of the most sought after in the city thanks to its views over the colourful flower displays of Vērmanes Garden, but its signature cocktails ensure that the place really comes alive too. It’s a sizeable spot, with a long, narrow room, stylish décor and even a living wall. Menus blend influences from across the globe with a range of fermentation techniques, and there’s a touch of theatre to the presentation. The seasonal tasting menus reflect the locality – as do the smaller local producers on their wine list – and desserts are a particular highlight.This restaurant is temporarily closed until September 2026.

Name: Whitstable Oyster Company
Address: Royal Native Oyster Stores, Horsebridge, Whitstable, CT5 1BU, United Kingdom
Description: One of those wonderful restaurants that 'does what it says on the tin', this family-run spot does indeed specialise in Whitstable Oysters, produced right outside the restaurant in the family's own oyster farm. Fresh and pure, they are a must-order and are available in a number of ways including natural, 'Royale' and 'Rockefeller'. The rest of the menu is as seafood-centric as you'd expect, with minimal adornment applied to the latest catch, be that gilthead bream or Dover sole. A large terrace and tremendous views over the estuary are the icing on the cake.

Name: Wicca
Address: LaSpa Hotel, Puhkekodu tee 4, Laulasmaa, 76702, Estonia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Angelica Udeküll is not only a well-known TV chef but also a torchbearer for Estonian cuisine. Her elegant restaurant at the LaSpa hotel sits in a beautifully tranquil spot overlooking the pine trees and the sea – the perfect location to showcase her ethical cuisine. Cooking is original, ranging from interpretations of her grandmother's recipes to dishes which incorporate elements from her travels. The drinks menu is split in two to offer the choice of either international beverages or local flavours that celebrate the region's heritage.

Name: Wicky's Innovative Japanese Cuisine
Description: Although the contemporary, minimalist-style decor is typical of Japanese restaurants, the cuisine will come as more of a surprise, with its magical blend of classic Japanese dishes made from Mediterranean ingredients, beautifully presented and full of flavour. There are two dining rooms: one overlooking the road, and the other with an open-view kitchen and sushi bar, where the chef serves an evening tasting menu for guests happy to put their faith in his imaginative improvisational skills.

Name: Wieland-Stuben
Description: This restaurant has become something of an institution in the region. The Wieland-Stuben has been a byword for classic cuisine since 1965. The elegant, tastefully decorated dining area makes for a really appealing setting, as does the gorgeous garden terrace. In their classic French cuisine, Lukas Erfurth and his team use only selected ingredients that impress with their freshness and quality. You can opt for the set menu or dine à la carte. The excellent service comes courtesy of a team headed up by sommelier Ronja Diedrich. On Sundays, there is a three-course set menu (no à la carte dishes).

Name: Wielinga
Description: Housed in a historical building, this charming restaurant has more of an intimate feel at the front than at the back, thanks to the natural light. However, the best spot is the canal-side terrace – perfect for soaking up Leiden's vibrant atmosphere. The chef proposes an appealing set menu with options for each course (priced higher in the evening than at lunch) alongside an à la carte selection that showcases premium ingredients. From sole fried in butter to skrei topped with a Taggiasca olive crumble and accompanied by a bright sauce vierge, lobster tartare and a rich lobster bisque, her dishes highlight classical technique at its best. She cooks with precision and is unafraid to add subtle modern twists. Be sure to peruse the expertly curated wine list.

Name: Wierzbowa 15 by Juanlu Fernández
Address: Hotel Altus Palace, Wierzbowa 15, Wrocław, 50-056, Poland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The basement of the Altus Palace Hotel – a beautifully restored building from the 19th century – makes a wonderful setting for this elegant restaurant with atmospheric red-brick walls and a vaulted ceiling. The well-travelled chef crafts dishes combining the classic with the subtly creative, leading to the likes of Jersualem artichoke foam with mushrooms and egg yolk or beef rib with potato and truffle. When available, the 'Duende' tasting menu provides the full experience.

Name: Wijnhuis De Blauwe Camer
Description: The medieval site of Sint-Catharinadal convent is an oasis of charm. The coach house has been turned into a modern restaurant bathed in natural light and with a rustic vibe. There is also a kitchen garden and several hectares of vineyards (hence the wine barrels at the entrance). The chef always starts with quality ingredients, often from his own garden, and distinguishes himself through expressive flavours, bold combinations and cosmopolitan influences. Expect dishes such as charred sea bass with marinated green apple and smoked feta ravioli, or lamb shoulder in red curry with coconut milk and mint. The experience ends with a mignardise bearing a QR code underneath that recaps your entire tasting journey.

Name: Wild
Address: 105 Burford High Street, Burford, OX18 4RG, United Kingdom
Description: Doing something different for this pretty Cotswolds town, Wild offers an interactive dining experience in the uber-stylish Bull hotel, where Banksys and Damien Hirsts adorn the walls. The restaurant occupies a purpose-built marquee in the courtyard, with guests sat around a copper-topped counter and fire pit. The personable chef cooks over the flames in front of you while demonstrating an understanding that less is often more. That means dishes where finely balanced accompaniments marry well with their prime central ingredients, such as Indonesian butter with Orkney scallops.

Name: Wild
Address: Boca Paila Carretera Tulum Km. 10, Tulum, 77780, Mexico
Description: In a world where uniformity is seemingly around every corner, Wild stands out from the pack. Nestled within the jungle of Tulum, this setting blends striking modern and rustic elements with lush nature. American Chef Norman Fenton is the brains behind the contemporary dishes, offered à la carte or as tasting menus. Begin with an appetizing vegetarian dish such as the crispy avocado with sikil pak, pico de gallo and oxalis before moving on to main dishes where quality ingredients shine. Excellent fish is seen in seafood plates like Campeche prawns or sea bass wrapped in hoja santa leaf. For dessert, a coconut granita with passionfruit, almond coco-crunch, lime and fresh mango is as refreshing as the open-air setting.

Name: Wild Atelier
Description: Jonathan Zandbergen is a dedicated craftsman who interprets "wild" in the broadest sense. Naturally, this encompasses game from the forests of the Veluwe – you can see pheasants and ducks hanging in the ageing cabinet – but he is also mindful of overfishing in the North Sea and Wadden Sea, and champions regenerative agriculture. His reverence for his ingredients is evident in his skilful technique and the way he allows them to shine in carefully considered, elegant preparations. His cooking is precise and well defined, characterised by aromatic depth. The red mullet, grilled to succulent perfection over an open fire, paired with flash-seared squid and Wadden shrimp, all bolstered by the intensity of a jus made from heads and bones and a sakura-infused beurre blanc, is simply outstanding. The concept is coherent, encompassing everything from his personal interpretation of hare à la royale to the forested surroundings brought into the modern dining room. For those looking to truly embrace the wild, a stay at De Echoput is ideal.

Name: Wild Cherry
Address: 38 Commerce St., New York, NY, 10014, USA
Description: Hiding inside the Cherry Lane Theatre, find this small bijou where dimmed globe lights cast an amber veil across a curved bar, tiled flooring and handsome green banquettes. As one might expect from the team behind Frenchette, the roving menu tempts in several directions. A pristine raw bar selection leads into appetizers like steak tartare, croque monsieur and a particularly impressive fried frog legs with garlic butter. Some tables go right for the cheeseburger. Either way, end with a handsome swirl of frozen custard or perhaps another round of cocktails. Be warned that seating is limited and reservations are scarce.

Name: Wild Flor
Address: 42 Church Road, Brighton and Hove, BN3 2FN, United Kingdom
Description: A group of lifelong friends own this relaxed neighbourhood restaurant, and they lead the service with obvious pride. The room takes on a modern bistro style and there’s a pleasingly unpretentious feel to the place. Well-prepared, seasonally changing dishes – try the goose rillettes with redcurrants in the winter – have a similarly unfussy style and good depth of flavour.

Name: Wild Shropshire
Address: 25-27 Green End, Whitchurch, SY13 1AD, United Kingdom
Description: Self-taught chef James Sherwin’s dream came true when he opened this endearing restaurant that’s the epitome of field-to-fork dining. Micro-seasonal produce is grown on their Wild Shropshire farm before being fashioned into a daily changing surprise menu for a maximum of 14 guests. There’s a Japanese influence throughout the harmoniously flavoured dishes, including ingredients like furikake, koji and yuzu, as well as a sake pairing. The passionate, welcoming team offer lovely, personable service.

Name: Wild Tavern
Address: 2 Elystan Street, Chelsea, London, SW3 3NS, United Kingdom
Description: Set overlooking the tiny Chelsea Green, this homely neighbourhood restaurant has the enticing feel of a warm Tuscan trattoria, with its waxed wooden floors and terracotta hues. True to the ethos of Italian cuisine, the dishes are ingredient-led and rely on the natural flavours of the produce – an approach extended to the raw bar of oysters, tartares and carpaccios. Alongside the prime cuts of meat and fish cooked over the grill, there are some terrific homemade pastas you'd be a fool to miss, especially the 'Tavern Tortelli' with Wagyu oxtail.

Name: Wild by Tart
Address: 3-4 Eccleston Yards, Belgravia, London, SW1W 9AZ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This laid-back brasserie is located in a former power station and coal store; the lofty glass roof ensures it’s light and airy, and the open kitchen gives it a real buzz. The rustic, Mediterranean-influenced dishes are hearty and satisfying, such as wood-fired monkfish with peas, crème fraîche and trout roe. Make sure you start with one of the flame-licked flatbreads too, which come with a choice of toppings. Tucked within the restaurant, The Wild Store sells a mix of snacks, seasonings, homeware and kitchen essentials.

Name: Wilde Triebe
Description: Set in refurbished former railway buildings dating back over 150 years, Wilde Triebe offers a minimalist, imaginative and fashionable mix of art and food. The flavoursome, seasonal, regional fare is served in an upmarket brick, concrete, steel and wood interior on the restaurant’s own tableware. Great garden.

Name: Wildenmann
Description: This gorgeous building, which started out as an inn in 1708, boasts an idyllic location just a few metres from the shore of Zugersee. Run by a mother-and-son team, the restaurant serves classic cuisine, with fish from the lake playing an important role, for example. A fine dining menu is also available, and in summer the charcoal barbecue is put to work. The service is charming and professional, and the atmosphere in the dining area is cosy. The fantastic terrace is understandably popular – it's wonderful to sit in the shade of the large trees and drink in the view of the lake!

Name: Wilder
Address: Market Street, Nailsworth, GL6 0BX, United Kingdom
Description: Everyone is asked to arrive at this well-run restaurant at 7pm – and that usually includes a loyal band of locals. The 3-hour menu takes on a surprise tasting format and there’s the option of matching wines or non-alcoholic options. Humble ingredients are used in ambitious, sometimes rather unusual combinations, which are precisely prepared. Service is structured and passionate, with dishes delivered by the chefs themselves.

Name: Wilder Mann
Description: The history of this old inn stretches back to the 16C, and the Schatz family has run it with great dedication since 1985. The Tyrolean influence is evident both in the interior design and on the menu. Flavoursome traditional dishes prepared using excellent, mostly local produce are served in various cosy dining rooms. Among the dishes to try are the Tyrolean veal liver with a creamy caper sauce, wine soup with toasted white bread croutons, or the delectable spinach ravioli with melted butter and chives. And be sure to sample the wonderful Sachertorte. Friendly and adept service.

Name: Wildflower
Description: Tucked inside the Gravity Haus hotel in the LoHi district, step past two sets of doors to find this moody-eclectic spot with a vintage vibe and a contemporary, plant-forward menu. Whether you order a la carte or choose a customizable tasting menu, expect bold and creative dishes with plenty of personality and character. Take the butternut squash soup that's far from a typical bowl. Here, butter-poached Dungeness crab takes center stage in a bowl with a ginger and pepita crumble and sunchoke chips, plus a tableside pour of soup. Salmon is sided by a crispy fennel cake with sunchoke puree and roasted fennel slices for a beautiful, tempting plate. Dessert impresses with honey semifreddo, Marsala foam, toasted oats and honeycomb brittle for a distinctive finish.

Name: Wildflowers
Address: 57 Pimlico Road, Pimlico, London, SW1W 8NE, United Kingdom
Description: It’s easy to miss this bright, modern restaurant located within Newson's Yard, a stylish development just off Pimlico Road with plenty of high-end inhabitants. Choose between an à la carte and a set sharing menu, both of which have a Mediterranean heart, with the produce-driven and attractive dishes from the open kitchen proving to be both comforting and full-flavoured. Go for the sharing dishes like ‘cuttlefish arroz al horno’, while desserts such as baked rice pudding with zabaglione will ensure any meal here ends on a high note. Try Bar Flor upstairs for a pre-dinner drink.

Name: Wildlight Kitchen + Bar
Address: 5380 University Blvd., Ste. 107, Vancouver, V6T 0C9, Canada
Description: Wildlight Kitchen + Bar is at the center of the quickly growing community of leləm̓ Village. This light-filled space is enhanced with natural and organic decorative elements, but the relaxed sophistication belies the serious nature of Chef Warren Chow's kitchen, where sourcing is paramount. Begin with a stunning charcuterie board that substitutes seafood for the ubiquitous meat to snack on everything from house-made salmon pastrami, marinated Salt Spring Island mussels, and pickled sea asparagus to tataki of smoked albacore tuna and cod rillette topped with cured ikura. A thick fillet of Gindara sablefish rests over soba noodles with baby bok choy for a main dish that is deeply satisfying. Finally, go for broke and order both the caramelized honey cheesecake with cardamom granola crust and the lemon tart.

Name: Wilford T
Description: The industrial sobriety of Wilford T is underscored by the artwork in the adjoining Wilford X exhibition gallery. Meals are served in an arty ambience steeped in serenity, which provides the perfect foil to a banquet of unadulterated purity. Chef Vermeiren, who doesn’t hesitate to add the finishing touch right in front of diners, is committed to highlighting the ingredient with unusual combinations, that are sometimes complex, but always flavoursome. Should you order venison, for example, it is flanked by an intense spicy sauce and succulent fritters that are still handmade by mum herself.

Name: Wilhelminapark
Description: Utrecht's city park is an ideal spot to unwind, and where better to do that than in this stylish restaurant with its authentic thatched roof and idyllic terrace overlooking the magnificent lake? Wilhelminapark has been a fixture since 1926, and you'll notice that right away. The chef wins diners over with both a rather classic fish dish accompanied by a rich beurre blanc and a steak tartare with an Asian twist. The wine pairings are equally impressive. Or just drop in to enjoy a drink and some delicious oysters.

Name: Willa Biała
Description: The ‘White Villa’ is so called because it occupies a listed neoclassical house from the early 20th century, whose white exterior fits well with the smartly kept dining room. The Ukrainian chef focuses on Eastern European specialities that are brought up to date with careful presentation and subtle creative touches. High-quality produce lies at the bedrock of their success, seen in the likes of the full-flavoured seasonal rabbit dumplings.

Name: Willett's
Address: The Cadogan, A Belmond Hotel, 75 Sloane Street, Chelsea, London, SW1X 9SG, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: Situated inside the storied Cadogan Hotel in the heart of Chelsea, this restaurant and bar is named after the Willett family who built the original townhouse in 1887. There’s a modern, clubby feel to the bar and two salon dining rooms, where you can choose from a menu that flies the flag for British ingredients, recipes and even wines. Topped crumpet snacks signal the kitchen’s intent, followed up by the likes of lamb faggots, day-boat fish and a host of nostalgic puddings – think Eton mess, jam roly-poly and a sherry trifle inspired by the chef’s grandmother.

Name: Williams ButchersTable am Bellevue
Description: This is the second Williams ButchersTable in Zurich, complementing their restaurant on Hegibachplatz. Located on Hechtplatz in the old town, this establishment also has a butcher's shop and restaurant under one roof. Top-quality steaks are the order of the day here. A cosy brasserie atmosphere reigns throughout, with tables on both the ground floor and upstairs, as well as on the small terrace out front. Diners hand-pick their preferred cuts from the meat counter at the entrance – Swiss LUMA beef rib eye, US bison fillet steak or Wagyu beef tenderloin from Japan or Australia? Or perhaps an Appenzeller Ribelmais chicken is more to your liking? The selection is varied; the quality of the meat is exceptional. The "specials" and "dailies" are also popular at lunchtime. Tip: At the butcher's counter you can purchase meat to cook at home. If you're coming by car, Parkhaus Hohe Promenade is within easy walking distance.

Name: Williams ButchersTable am Hegibachplatz
Description: If it's high-quality meat you're after, look no further than this steakhouse located just outside the old town. The butcher's counter is sure to whet your appetite – here you can hand-pick your preferred high-quality cuts. The fantastic national and international selection includes US Prime Black Angus Beef, Swiss LUMA Pork and pata negra bellota, as well as New Zealand lamb or bison and Japanese Wagyu beef. There are also "specials" and "dailies" available at lunchtime. Diners can bask in the nostalgia of the charming brasserie setting. To the front of the restaurant, the terrace with shady trees is appealing, too. Tip: Take the bus or train directly to the door. If coming by car, park in Parkhaus Feldegg, just a few minutes' walk away. It's worth noting that even non-diners like to buy their meat here. A second Williams ButchersTable can be found in the city centre near the Limmat River.

Name: Willie Mae's Nola
Address: 898 Baronne St., New Orleans, LA, 70113, USA
Description: In the realm of fried chicken excellence, few do it better than the Seaton family. With history dating back to 1957, this institution has found a way to maintain quality and spirit while moving ahead with expansion and even relocation. The sunny, spacious dining room in downtown is miles from the original in Treme, but the fried chicken is as superb as ever. The menu offers more, but first timers need to stay focused. A cup of finely spiced gumbo with shrimp and blue crab is the only start you need before the main event. Sides like butter beans and rice or spiced cabbage round out a hearty meal that is visceral and rewarding in all the right ways.

Name: Willie's
Address: Rua do Brasil 2 - Vilamoura, Quarteira, 8125-479, Portugal
Description: Located near the Pinhal Golf Course, a quiet, residential area of the upscale town of Vilamoura. It occupies a classic house, tastefully decorated and surrounded by a pleasant outdoor terrace — ideal for summer days. Here, German chef Willie Wurger offers classic international cuisine with modern twists. The freshness of the lobster tail, served with a delicate avocado cream, mango cubes, bisque, and a crunchy sesame tuile, stands out among the selection based on excellent quality products. The veal rib-eye with pistachio tagliatelle, and the crisp millefeuille with white chocolate mousse perfectly offset by the acidity of fresh raspberries, are also on the enticing menu.

Name: Windsor
Description: This restaurant, with its updated classic decor, is enhanced by an exquisite terrace and several dining rooms that allow for different configurations. Contemporary Catalan cuisine including a good choice of set menus.

Name: Wine & Dine
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: In the center of Canazei, this restaurant within the Croce Bianca hotel occupies wood-paneled rooms that foster a relaxed, informal atmosphere, with a few charming alcoves for more intimate seating. Meat reigns supreme, notably a dedicated selection of grilled main courses. A good assortment of wines by the glass.

Name: Wing
Address: 29F, The Wellington, 198 Wellington Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: The second venture from owner-chef Vicky Cheng who runs the well-acclaimed Vea upstairs, Wing is named after his Chinese name, meaning eternity. The tasting menu features contemporary Chinese courses made with quality global ingredients but underpinned by European techniques. He reinterprets classic recipes and familiar flavours with creative twists and playful food combinations. Online reservations open at midnight for up to 28 days ahead.

Name: Wing Lee Restaurant (Yuexiu)
Address: 2-3F, Xianjian Building, 259 Yanjiang Zhonglu, Yuexiu, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Since 1981, Wing Lee has been a household name famous for its nostalgic Cantonese fare and handcrafted traditional dim sum – some of which are rarely found elsewhere. The founder’s son took over the helm in 2018 and has been reviving old-time favourites. Crispy skinned chicken stuffed with minced shrimp boasts an interesting mix of textures and deep umami. Dim sum-like eggy doughnuts in icing sugar are served at breakfast and lunch only.

Name: Winkler
Description: This fish and snail restaurant stands out for its intriguing and uncommon concept. The menu ranges from grilled pike-perch with mustard sauce and crayfish in white wine broth to fresh mussels sautéed in garlic butter and chilli, and snails with herbs or pepper. For dessert, the pastries are practically a must. As well as the appealing à la carte choices, the four-course set menu is well worth trying. The tranquil lakeside location by Wallersee, complete with a bathing area, is delightful – the terrace is, of course, the place to be in summer. The interior is also attractive with its upscale, modern design, and striking maritime-themed artwork providing decorative accents. Tip: Go for a stroll by Wallersee and take in the fabulous panoramic view. Well-appointed guestrooms are available for overnight stays.

Name: Winkler Bräu
Description: The culinary tradition of this building dates back to 1428. Cosy traditional parlours are testament to its long history – heavy timber ceilings, dark wood-panelled walls, lovely hardwood floors and old paintings create a charmingly rustic setting. The old-world feel of the interior is complemented by a modern conservatory and a terrace. The regional, seasonal cuisine is based on carefully selected ingredients, with dishes such as Schneemühl char with garden herbs and potato salad, or the classic roast Swabian-Hall pork with crackling and potato dumplings. Diners can either opt for the four-course "Gutshof Menu" or order à la carte. A reduced menu is served at lunchtime and in the afternoon. The property also has its own brewery (showcased in the exhibition "TraditionsReich Kupfer") and a brewery shop. Comfortable accommodation is offered in the adjoining hotel, which includes spa facilities.

Name: Winsome
Address: 74 Princess Street, Manchester, M1 6JD, United Kingdom
Description: Manchester’s industrial history feels like it’s had an overt influence on this buzzing brasserie with a large kitchen counter and a stripped-back look. The cooking has an admirably gutsy, straightforward quality to it, with hints of nostalgia. Think cold cuts, whole fish, hearty homemade pies and a mixed grill. It’s all executed with skill and the ingredients are of obvious quality, resulting in no shortage of flavour. The young and enthusiastic service team are a perfect fit for such a fun place.

Name: Winstub Arnold
Description: Dive headlong into Alsace traditions at this winstub featuring numerous elsässische Spezialitäten, including kougelhopf, sauerkraut, black pudding, apple purée, baeckeoffe hotpot or specials such as "Marie Leczinsca vol-au-vent"… Choose a wine from the family estate to accompany your food, then sit back and enjoy in a setting that couldn't be more characteristic of the region.

Name: Winter Garden Florence
Description: Once entered by carriages, the ancient courtyard of the St. Regis – generous in scale and dramatic in its proportions – has today been transformed into a refined winter garden. Among the sofas and armchairs embracing the cocktail bar – where the aperitivo is an almost indispensable ritual – this venue preserves a charm of another era, with precious marbles, carpets, plants and Murano glass chandeliers, while at the centre a pianist provides an elegant accompaniment to the atmosphere. In the kitchen, the chef navigates a line that balances contemporary ambition with classic reassurance, drawing on the Mediterranean tradition of both land and sea. The dishes stand out for their simplicity and attention to seasonality, with few ingredients elevated through precise technique and measured flavour.

Name: Wintergarten
Description: The tastefully designed conservatory restaurant of the long-established Brenners Park-Hotel & Spa is a light and airy space with floor-to-ceiling glazing that affords a splendid view of the leafy gardens – and the terrace is, of course, especially inviting. In the evening, the classic and seasonal dishes can be enjoyed as a set menu or ordered à la carte. Vegetarian options are also available. A three-course set menu is served at lunchtime from Monday to Friday.

Name: Winterstellgut
Description: It is worth making the journey here for the stunning views of the surrounding mountains from the sun-drenched plateau some 1 000m above Annaberg – and they are even better from the terrace. At this 16C farm building, dine in cosy, rustic-style nooks or on the light-filled veranda. The kitchen is open all day, serving traditional regional and seasonal cuisine that draws on the odd international influence, such as Kalbsrahmbeuscherl mit Semmelknöde (veal offal ragout with bread dumplings) and lobster gyoza with an Asian-style bisque. Alternatively, opt for the set menu. Everything is made with good-quality, fresh ingredients, including preserves. Tip: House-made goods can be purchased to enjoy at home. For overnight stays, there are a few attractive guestrooms and suites, plus a natural pond for bathing.

Name: Winzerhaus Rebstock
Description: Following stints at various MICHELIN-starred establishments, Konstantin Keller has taken over this much-loved traditional inn. He is the youngest son of the Keller family, who run Schwarzer Adler across the road. "Down-to-earth, regionally inspired cuisine: the best of the simple things" – that's the promise here, and it could hardly be more apt. Eschewing superfluous creative flourishes, the cuisine is all about quality ingredients, meticulous craftsmanship and full, authentic flavours. In short: The food is just fantastic! This holds true for the exceedingly succulent, classically rolled cordon bleu served with lingonberries and potato salad, as well as the flame-seared Black Forest char with cauliflower and carrot sauce or the pâté de campagne. If steak is more your thing, the dry-aged saddle of Black Forest herb-fed pork is a particular standout. There are also daily specials and a short afternoon menu. The wine list features a selection from the family's own estate (Franz Keller) along with other German and international labels. In fine weather, be sure to make the most of the charming courtyard terrace.

Name: Wirt z'Zell Gasthaus Langwallner
Description: Adjacent to the church in this tranquil little village, this inn was established in 1616 and is now run by Barbara Langwallner, who is carrying on the family tradition. Food is served in well-kept, charmingly rustic dining rooms or, in fine weather, on the lovely terrace. With the family's own butcher's shop on site, the menu includes classics such as tartare, Viennese goulash, schnitzel and Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef), as well as locally caught fish, vegetarian options and – in the form of an ever-changing set menu – more creative dishes, which can also be ordered individually.

Name: Wirtschaft Traube
Description: Tanja and Tobias Schöpf's establishment is pleasingly informal. She provides cordial and proficient service in the inviting wood-panelled dining space, occasionally taking a seat alongside diners at their table. Her husband, meanwhile, prepares five flavoursome dishes using regional ingredients, for you to select à la carte or as a set menu. Tantalising examples include Riebelmais (dry-milled corn), onion, Vorarlberg mountain cheese, or chicken leg, Savoy cabbage, leek, parsley root. He likes to keep things natural and seasonal – he goes hunting and forages for mushrooms, buds and herbs. The wine pairings, too, are carefully selected – an alcohol-free alternative is also available.

Name: Wirtschaft am Schlössli
Description: Christian Kuchler from Taverne zum Schäfli in Wilgoltingen is also behind this culinary hotspot here in nearby Bottighofen, in a lovely location by the marina. Under the direction of head chef Monika Huber (formerly sous-chef to Christian Kuchler), the food is ambitious. The menu is divided into "France", "Italy", "Iberian Peninsula" and "Classics". Your Mediterranean journey ranges from "rabbit roulade, raw ham, sage, courgette" to "scampi, fregola sarda, lemon, pepperoncini" and "Ibérico pork Alenttejana" to "tortelloni, tomato, burrata, Taggiasca olive". Accompanied by a well-curated wine list with a fine selection from Switzerland and Europe. Enjoy your meal inside in a relaxed bistro atmosphere or out on the gorgeous terrace on the shores of Lake Constance. Tip: Tapas are also served all day on a separate terrace – Lästermeile – on the marina promenade.

Name: Wirtschaft von Johann Gerner
Description: The journey out here to the countryside is well worth it, because Detlef Gerner and his wife Tanja live and breathe hospitality par excellence in their cosy restaurant. The hand-written menu features flavoursome dishes based on seasonal and predominantly regional produce – incidentally, they bake their own bread. In summer, you can sit on the terrace out front. Overnight accommodation in the pretty "Häusla" (for two to seven people).

Name: Wirtschaft zum Frieden
Description: This centuries-old inn enjoys a prime location right on Marktplatz, and its charming ambiance, redolent of a bygone era, will have you yearning to return. The dedication of your hosts is also infectious. While maître d' Heidi Bischoff graciously attends to diners in the cosy wood-panelled dining areas, chef-patron Fabrice Bischoff cooks up classic, home-style fare using fresh, high-quality ingredients. Some dishes also incorporate a Mediterranean twist. On the menu you will find beef fillet Stroganoff, as well as Swiss salmon steak with accras. A simpler set menu of the day is also available at lunchtime. The verdant terrace is a delightful spot in the summertime!

Name: Wirtschaft zur Rosenburg
Description: Wherever you look, there's history – the old fortified tower is magnificent! After 33 years, the business has changed hands, but new owners Lukas and Evelyn Christen are committed to keeping the tradition alive. The menu continues to feature both regional and international dishes. Look out for the label "Guets vo hie" on the menu, which indicates the local specialities such as topside beef carpaccio with horseradish, red onions and fried mushrooms. The courtyard terrace is especially pleasant. Tip: This pretty restaurant also makes an ideal venue for weddings and other celebrations.

Name: Wirtshaus Huberwirt
Description: With chef-patron Alexander Huber and hostess Sandra Huber at the helm, this long-standing family business is now run by the 11th generation. Regional cuisine is served either à la carte or as a three- to five-course "Wirtshausmenü", with optional wine pairings. Highlights include jellied catfish and sturgeon with herb sauce, cabbage and root vegetables, or boiled beef shoulder and bone marrow with roast potatoes, apple and horseradish sauce, and spinach. A children's menu is also available. The restaurant consists of two inviting dining rooms, their striking old wooden ceilings testament to over 400 years of history. Open for lunch at weekends – booking recommended. For a more elevated dining experience, the separate Restaurant Alexander Huber is located at the rear of the property.

Name: Wirtshaus Hörnlingen
Description: At this restaurant in a beautiful historical house on the road leading to the imposing Basilika Rankweil, the culinary focus is firmly on the region. Young and ambitious Dominic Mayer and his team serve surprise menus only – diners decide on the number of courses. Fresh seasonal ingredients go into dishes prepared with a personal touch. Traditional and modern combine to form the basis of the cuisine, which adheres to "leaf to root" and "nose to tail" principles. Other plus points are the extremely friendly service and a well-curated wine list – all of the Vinothek wines are also available for purchase. The aesthetic is attractive with its blend of rustic charm and modern features. It is a joy to sit out on the terrace with its shady plane trees when the weather is good. The Tapas Bar in the historical vault is also open Thu-Sat. Another interesting option is the "Brasserie Pop-Up" on Mondays, when changing à la carte dishes are served.

Name: Wirtshaus Kogel 3
Description: Against the backdrop of vineyards and the rolling hills that surround Leibnitz, the setting is almost heavenly. The marvellous tiered terrace and a lounge area beneath the arcade are, of course, extremely inviting in summer. The interior is equally delightful, with its stylish modern design and floor-to-ceiling windows affording stunning views. Here, you can look forward to contemporary seasonal cuisine paired with exceptionally friendly, attentive service and an excellent wine list - nice the viewable wine cellar in the basement.

Name: Wirtshaus Post
Address: Speckbacherstrasse 1, Sankt Johann in Tirol, 6380, Austria
Description: It's easy to see why this traditional spot in the very centre of town is so popular. Its classic tavern cooking is a major draw – favourites such as Frittatensuppe (pancake strips in broth), beef goulash with bread dumplings, or Wiener schnitzel are staples here. The lovely modern Alpine-style dining rooms with light wood panelling and the friendly service add to the appeal.

Name: Wirtshaus by Stefan Glantschnig
Description: In addition to gorgeous hotel rooms and the upscale second restaurant, Rouge Noir, Neusacherhof is also home to Wirtshaus, where chef Stefan Glantschnig and his team put a contemporary spin on classic regional dishes. Their traditional character is deliberately retained while being cleverly enhanced with flavourful and visually appealing touches. In addition to the à la carte selection, there are daily specials – for those who find it difficult to choose, a surprise menu compiled from those options is available. The good food is complemented by a relaxed atmosphere in a modern Alpine-style setting. In front of the building, there is an inviting terrace overlooking the lake.

Name: Wirtshaus zum Herrmannsdorfer Schweinsbräu
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: "Dishes that can't be pigeonholed" – such is the name of the game for chef Olimpia Cario. In her surprise set menu, she gives free rein to her creativity, cooking up unusual combinations such as chicken, trout, egg, cucumber, corn and redcurrants. She uses seasonal produce and high-quality ingredients, often grown on her own farm. The interior itself has an eye-catching design, with a large, high-ceilinged space reminiscent of a modern rustic barn on account of the beam construction climbing up into the roof.

Name: Wirtshaus zur Sonne
Description: This restaurant has been in the same family for over 300 years. Diners can sit inside in the wonderful, wood-panelled dining room or outside on the pretty garden terrace to enjoy the flavoursome fare. This includes tafelspitz (boiled topside of beef) galantine with radish carpaccio or pan-fried skrei cod with tomatoes and herbs.

Name: Wistub Brenner
Description: In this authentic winstub in the heart of Little Venice, the cuisine is – of course – regional: salad with Comté cheese and cervelas, "Papi Lucien's onion tart", sauerkraut and braised pork knuckle, Pinot Noir sauce. Local produce, a friendly atmosphere and a pleasant terrace.

Name: Withee Laab
Address: 94-120 Charoen Muang Road, Wat Ket, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50000, Thailand
Description: This charming wooden building down a narrow alley has been serving delicious lap for years. The spicy minced buffalo meat and zesty cooked minced pork are sure to impress. With surprisingly affordable prices, this is a gem worth seeking out.

Name: Witlof
Description: The view of the Waal River, the ever-cheerful hostess, glimpses of the chef at work as you pass by the kitchen on your way to use the facilities, plus the moss-covered wall and numerous paintings of fish all contribute to the welcoming atmosphere at this cosy establishment. Jurgen Eikholt lovingly prepares classic cuisine with his trademark sophisticated, often Asian-inspired touches. One example is his use of mirin in a hollandaise sauce to lend salmon and al dente vegetables a rich, subtly sweet note. Witlof only serves surprise menus, and they are definitely worthy of your confidence.

Name: Witwenball
Description: What makes this deluxe bistro in Hamburg's bustling Schanzenviertel so beloved? A perfect blend of cuisine, service and atmosphere. Once a dance hall, this place now exudes a laid-back yet lively energy, and feels at once trendy and chic with its decorative wine racks – the white marble counter in the middle of the space is a striking feature. The delicious contemporary food incorporates regional, seasonal, and international influences. Order à la carte or compile your own four-course "Your Choice" set menu, with a fish, a meat or vegetarian option for the main course. Wiener schnitzel is also always available on Sundays. The impressive wine list comprises over 500 items, and the staff provide expert guidance. Alternatively, you could have a cocktail. Lovely pavement terrace.

Name: Wolf Atelier
Description: Michael Wolf likes to experiment with sophisticated flavours and surprising ideas, giving diners the opportunity to test them out and then refining them to retain their best features. He is just as happy to cook up a turnip-based vegetarian take on Beef Wellington as he is to concoct surf and turf combinations that put a new spin on familiar flavours. The name Atelier is therefore particularly appropriate in this trendy, industrial-style restaurant, which is located on an old railway bridge with a beautiful view of the IJ.

Name: Wolfgang's Steakhouse (Gongrentiyuchang North Road)
Address: 1F, Space 8, Pacific Century Place, 2A Gongrentiyuchang North Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
Description: This outpost of the namesake institution in New York City is furnished in classic American-style with burgundy leather chairs and dim, warm lighting. The menu and recipes are essentially the same as its Manhattan flagship, where the chefs and manager were trained to ensure the same standard of service across the board. USDA prime Angus steaks are dry-aged for at least 28 days and its signature crab cake will send your palate into overdrive.

Name: Wonderful Baba Bak Kut Teh King Of King
Address: 18-1 Juguang Road, Banqiao District, New Taipei, Taiwan
Description: Wallpaper of Malaysian street scenes and herbal aromas immediately transport diners to the home country of this father-and-son team. For over 10 years, the son has been presiding in the kitchen, the father front of house. Made with over 10 different Chinese herbs, as well as peppercorns from Sarawak, their signature Fujian-style bak kut teh reveals many layers. Try the special minced pork and shrimp rice, too, and enjoy its rustic flavours.

Name: Woo Nam Jeong
Address: 5953 Buford Hwy. NE, Doraville, GA, 30340, USA
Description: Anchoring the corner of a shopping center along Buford Highway, this busy spot features an expansive Korean menu. With so many options, it may be difficult to pick just one but start with a seafood or kimchi pancake or their seared mandu and you won't go wrong. Then, plenty of specialties tempt but you're here for one in particular: the house specialty "stone bowl" bibimbap. Take a peek at the neighboring tables and nearly everyone is tucking into one of these signature dishes. Bulgogi, or tender beef, is the classic order, and it arrives in the stone bowl sizzling long after it is set atop the table. Rice that has been crisped sits at the base, with beef, vegetables, and a sunny side up egg on top for a delicious one-pot dish that will make you a regular in no time.

Name: Wood Tavern
Description: It's a classic neighborhood standby, where friends, families and chic couples congregate for drinks at the copper-topped bar. Flanked by organic groceries, indie bookstores and antique shops, its environs speak of peace, weaving a bohemian spell that captivates both regulars and rookies alike.Seasonal Californian cooking with an Italian bent dominates this tavern's menu, and a "butcher block" of well-prepared charcuterie — pork rillettes seasoned with Aleppo pepper, sumac, and lime — is a prudent way to start your meal. Bucatini with a beef and pork ragu bolognese or pan-roasted half chicken with fingerling potatoes are comforting choices. End with crème brûlée cheesecake with yuzu curd.

Name: Woodend
Address: Maroma, A Belmond Hotel, Carr. Cancún - Tulum Km. 51, Playa del Carmen, 77710, Mexico
Description: Acclaimed Chef Curtis Stone lends his name and refined culinary sensibilities to this seaside retreat, and though he’s unlikely to be present in the flesh, rest assured that you are in good hands regardless. As the first step into the smoke-perfumed room will give away, the cooking here centers around live fire, with a charcoal oven and wood-fired grill lending their aroma to a small menu that leans to bold simplicity. Local seafood and well-marbled steaks from Oklahoma make up the mains, while sides like crunchy potato pavé with jocoque and buttery Parisian gnocchi with endive and poblano are tasty enough to stand on their own. For dessert, a twist on tarte tatin with pineapple, mezcal-tinged caramel, and toasted vanilla ice cream hits just the right mark.

Name: Woods
Description: The view of the Oude Rijn and the authentic sawmill charms you as soon as you walk into this characterful restaurant (that terrace!), but chef Van der Pluijm's cuisine also deserves attention. His style is modern and restrained, with subtle cosmopolitan accents. For example, he cooks bavette to a beautiful pink and serves it with a creamy parsnip purée, mushroom duxelles, pommes dauphine and a slice of fried goose liver. The plates are beautifully presented and combine classic touches with refined creativity, without excess.

Name: Woods Hill Pier 4
Description: When the sun is out and the garage doors are up, it can feel as if the entire city is angling for a prime table here in the Boston Seaport District. Sitting right on the harbor and armed with a wrap-around patio, this bustling restaurant is not content to rely solely on its good looks. Chef Charlie Foster and his team deliver a hearty, global cuisine, with many ingredients sourced from their own farm in New Hampshire. Start with a Thai-inspired striped bass crudo or the signature smoked ham hock croquettes lashed in a honey and Aleppo gastrique. Grilled pork loin or perhaps smoked lamb shoulder and a side of charred broccoli finished in a cheddar and smoked garlic aioli make for a proper feast.

Name: Woodstockholm
Description: A compact bistro owned by a group of friends, who set up a furniture making business and now use the bistro to showcase their products. Cooking follows a theme which changes every two months – perhaps a country, a style of food or a famous chef – and the rustic small plates are simple yet full of flavour.

Name: Woogu House
Address: 72, Lane 247, Section 1, Zhongshan North Road, Tamsui District, New Taipei, Taiwan
Description: Behind sky blue doors, the dining rooms exude retro chic thanks to vintage furniture and assorted memorabilia. After training formally, the chef honed his skills for over three decades before opening Woogu House. He offers two omakase-style menus, creatively blending a healthy eating philosophy with Taiwanese culinary traditions. His sea bass in red wine lees sauce is served with seasonal greens, creating a unique ensemble of colours and flavours.

Name: Workshop Kitchen & Bar
Address: 800 N. Palm Canyon Dr., Ste. G, Palm Springs, CA, 92262, USA
Description: Farm-to-table food may seem like an impossibility in the middle of the desert, but nearby Coachella Valley is actually one of the nation’s most productive regions. Here you’ll find that bounty on full display. A dedicated garden in Rancho Mirage, along with a sizeable herb planter behind the kitchen, furnishes peak-season produce for wood-fired dishes like a flat iron au poivre, and even a simple yuzu tart is prettied up with farm-fresh raspberries and wood sorrel. The setting is a Spanish-style building from the 1920s, while the interior is a modernist temple of polished concrete—a mist-cooled courtyard provides additional seating. Special touches like house-made ginger beer distinguish an exemplary bar program, with cocktails both classic and creative.

Name: Written By The Seasons
Description: You don’t need to be a genius to work out the philosophy behind this likeable restaurant that is a perfect fit for the Bishop Arts District. Local ingredients in season are used here to create fresh tasting, colorful, and rewarding dishes. Vegetables are often given star billing rather than mere supporting roles and the kitchen isn’t afraid of incorporating a little international flavor here and there. So, carrots may come with dukkah, branzino with harissa, and pork ribs with miso; and be sure to start off with some of their delicious focaccia. The time of year not only informs their menu but also their cocktail list, so it’s worth exploring. The space is bright and contemporary and the atmosphere, warm and energetic.

Name: Wu Ming Mian Guan
Address: 17-1 Youdian Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, 310006, Chinese Mainland
Description: The shop has no name because the owner believes his noodles are good enough to keep guests coming back regardless. In over 30 years, the place has not changed – with just six tables set up in the tiny space. But the huge portions of tasty noodles at bargain prices have amassed a loyal fan base. The fall-off-the-bone pork ribs with strong scallion aromas in particular tend to sell out early. The pork liver and kidney are also popular.

Name: Wu Yue Gong
Address: Inside CD Courtyard, 28 Wuyuegong Street, Qingyang, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
Description: Inside a historic courtyard house-turned hotel, this private dining concept opened its doors in 2018. It only accepts reservations for parties of 2 to 10 diners and menus are tailor-made according to guests’ preferences. Novel Sichuanese fusion dishes are underpinned by solid skills and exquisite plating, complemented by Cantonese, Guanfu, Huaiyang and even Western items. Try kung pao prawns and chargrilled beef ribs in black pepper sauce.

Name: Wulin
Description: Tucked away in a small alley, Wulin has been serving authentic, reasonably priced Hangzhou food since 2008. The drunken prawns marinated in a wine sauce have a sweet aftertaste; the braised yellow croaker with sticky rice cakes is cooked with chilli bean paste and sliced pork for an umami extravaganza. Lamb, especially popular in winter, is prepared in myriad ways. The main restaurant area isn't huge, but there are a few private rooms available to book.

Name: Wunderkammer - Herbarium
Description: Located near the Schlegelkopf piste, the luxurious Almhof Schneider hotel, built in 1929, is home to this fine dining restaurant, which is only open during the winter. At lunchtime and in the evening, you can enjoy Austrian cuisine with international influences: the menu includes Fiaker goulash, Wagyu steak, Riesling Beuschel (offal ragout) with bread dumplings and, for dessert, Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake). The wine list, comprising over 1 200 labels, is superb. Meals are served in two tastefully decorated dining spaces: Wunderkammer, designed by artist Paul Renner, and Herbarium, featuring beautiful woodcuts by Christian Thanhäuser.

Name: Wurzel
Description: An appealing dining option at spa hotel Weißes Roß, which is located in the centre of the village, beside the church. Warm colours and a modern design create a very tasteful and stylish yet cosy interior. In the kitchen, Christian Fleischmann shows a deft touch with vegan cuisine, transforming high-quality ingredients into modern dishes inspired by the seasons – think "potato, chestnut, radicchio, truffle" or "gyoza, Chinese cabbage, shiso, dashi". Diners can opt for a four-course set menu, which can be extended with an optional surprise course, and individual dishes can also be ordered à la carte. To accompany the set menu, wine pairings or alcohol-free alternatives are available. Service is highly attentive and adept.

Name: WurzelWerk
Description: This restaurant lives up to its name: Wurzel, meaning "root", signifies a dedication to the local terroir, Werk, meaning "craft", highlights a commitment to artisanal cooking techniques – chef-patron Benjamin Bendzko puts both into practice in his market-fresh cuisine. Exceptional and almost exclusively regional ingredients are used to create flavoursome and pleasingly down-to-earth dishes. Two buildings, built in 1875 as a farmstead, now house a guesthouse (with a café at weekends) and this restaurant, whose rustic charm and pretty decor make for a cosy atmosphere. In summer, the garden terrace is the place to be.

Name: Wälder Stube 1840
Description: This restaurant is named after the year in which Das Schiff, the tasteful hotel that houses it, was founded. Done out in an abundance of wood and featuring delightful decorative details such as pictures and lamps, the dining nooks with their classically laid tables are the epitome of cosiness. In his set menu, chef Bernd Reimer places great emphasis on regionality, but also incorporates international flavours. The quality of the produce is exquisite – as exemplified by Black cod with miso, salicornia, chanterelles and wild garlic gnocchi. Dominated by labels from the tri-border region, the wine list boasts plenty of tempting options. Service with a personal touch adds to the charm of the overall experience.

Name: Würzhaus
Description: This really is an appealing restaurant. At lunchtime, things are toned down a little, with reasonably priced options (à la carte or a small set menu). In the evening, there is an ambitious set menu that comes in four to six flavourful courses. Head chef Diana Burkel is committed to using locally sourced ingredients. The wine list is dominated by organic, biodynamic and natural wines. The service is friendly and attentive, and the atmosphere is welcoming.

Name: XO Seafoodbar
Description: As well as haebel, just across the street, Fabio Haebel runs this trendy, laid-back establishment in the heart of St Pauli. Occupying two floors, the restaurant has an agreeably lively atmosphere. Upstairs there are also a few seats at a counter facing the open kitchen. The food is modern and seasonal, with a focus on seafood specialties, including oysters, monkfish schnitzel and grilled prawns, and of course the famous "Pasta Krabbe". Alternatively, you could opt for "Chef's Choice" – a selection of items picked from the menu by the kitchen team. Tip: Treat yourself to a cocktail at the small bar. In summer, head for the terrace and soak up the buzzy atmosphere.

Name: XU Dubai
Address: Kempinski Hotel, 2nd floor, Mall of the Emirates, Sheikh Zayed Road, Al Barsha 1, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Credit cards not accepted,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: This chic Chinese restaurant brings authentic Cantonese cuisine made modern to the second floor of the Kempinski Hotel Mall of the Emirates. The creative chef prepares the dishes with quality, fresh ingredients while respecting traditional cooking techniques. Delicious homemade condiments are bold in flavour and elevate every dish. Come here in a group as all the plates, such as the delicious Peking duck and the excellent dim sum, are meant to be shared.

Name: Xavier Pellicer
Description: In this centrally located restaurant just a few metres from the city’s emblematic La Pedrera-Casa Milà building designed by Gaudí, the focus is on “healthy” cuisine that is centred around seasonal vegetables and the sourcing of its ingredients exclusively from small-scale local producers. The backdrop is an elegant interior with a rustic simplicity that includes a modern dining room with an industrial vibe and a completely open kitchen behind the bar counter, enabling guests to interact with the chefs (there’s also another more multi-functional dining room called El Menjador designed for private events). You will find à la carte service (only at lunchtime, Wednesday through Sunday) and two tasting options (one with 5 courses, the other 8), each featuring three different options: vegan, vegetarian and omnivore. The interesting wine list includes lots of little-known labels.

Name: Xerta
Description: If you’re still unfamiliar with the culinary delights of the Ebro Delta, a visit to this restaurant in Barcelona is a must to savour the flavours of a region that has been declared a World Biosphere Reserve. Accessed via the lobby of the Ohla Eixample hotel, Xerta boasts a contemporary dining room with views of the kitchen. Chef José Guadalupe Couoh Pomol, hailing from Yucatán, is passionate about Mediterranean cuisine and offers expert insight into the specific cuisine of the Ebro Delta, giving us the opportunity to discover its authentic gastronomy (elvers, oysters, rice... 90% of the products come from there) from a creative point of view. What’s on offer? The à la carte menu, which always features an array of delicious rice dishes and showcases seasonal ingredients (sea cucumbers, spot-tail mantis shrimp, blue crab, wild mushrooms, etc.), is complemented by three set menus: Temporada (lunchtime, not available on bank holidays, Tuesday to Friday), Delta and Producto.

Name: Xi Bei Qiao Tou La Mian Da Wang (Gulou)
Description: The sign may say "ramen king" but this shop is routinely packed with fans of beef potstickers – just queue at the machine to order yours, then present the ticket to collect them. These potstickers have crispy golden bottoms and a soupy filling redolent of scallion. Those in the know dip them in vinegar and chilli oil for an extra kick. The menu also includes staples typically served in halal noodle shops, such as lamb dishes and cold appetisers.

Name: Xi Jiu
Address: Shop 218, Building No.2, Casa de Numero 9, 5 Xiaoheyan, Zhonglou, Changzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: An upmarket brand of a local F&B group, Xi Jiu packs tons of wow factors in its design-centric venue – from an authentic royal Qing Dynasty embroidered robe to light fixtures that impart a futuristic glow. The menu is mostly Cantonese with some Changzhou and Huai Yang twists. Double-boiled soups are their strong suit, including geoduck and laver soup made tableside in a siphon pot. Golden deep-fried hairtail fish is a new take on a classic Changzhou recipe.

Name: Xi Xi Liang Chen
Address: 8 Wujiawan Street, Xixi National Wetland Park, Fangxi Road, Yuhang, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: A serene place in a wetland park with a manicured Chinese garden. With just eight private rooms, privacy is guaranteed. Menus are tailor-made to diners' liking in advance, without à la carte options. The kitchen puts a sophisticated spin on authentic Chaozhou and Swatow dishes, with produce such as pickled mustard greens and baby mussels from Chaozhou. Try the soy-marinated goose webs and liver, and sticky rice balls in peanut sesame sugar.

Name: Xi'an Gourmet House
Address: 955 Spring St. NW, #C, Atlanta, GA, 30309, USA
Description: You won't get a lot of fuss at this Midtown spot, an offshoot of the original in Duluth. You'll order at the counter and then pick up a paper plate, but what they may lack in niceties, they make up for with dialed-in cooking. Spotlighting the Xi'an region of China, the menu focuses on biang biang noodles and as well as boiled dumplings and dishes featuring plenty of cumin and other spices. Richly flavored noodles are the way to go, though it’s never a bad idea to supplement with the boldly flavorful cucumber salad, and there must be dumplings, of course. Here, they are available on their own or with spicy and sour soup. Choose from pork and lamb and then tuck in to a baker's dozen of simply boiled treats served with a house-made dipping sauce that brings them alive.

Name: Xia
Address: 1F, Lohkah Hotel & Spa, 277 Penang Road, Huli, Xiamen, Chinese Mainland
Description: Since 2018, Chef Yang hailing from Jiangsu has been helming the kitchen with a menu that is half Cantonese and half Minnan. Chilled peanut sweet soup is a modified version of the Fujian classic, with a velvety peanut custard over a bed of toothsome algae. The west-facing views over Wuyuan Bay make Xia the perfect spot for a romantic dinner at sunset.

Name: Xiang Se
Address: 1-2 Hukou Street, Zhongzheng District, Taipei, 100, Taiwan
Description: Vintage furniture, terracotta tile flooring and exposed wooden beams make for a cosy European cottage feel.
