Description: The signature kolo mee set menu is a tour de force starring everything the stall has to offer – braised spareribs, wontons, char siew and curly, bouncy kolo noodles dressed in lard and shallot oil. Ipoh hor fun is also available.

Name: Yun House
Address: 5B, Four Seasons Hotel, 145 Jalan Ampang, Kuala Lumpur, Kuala Lumpur, 50450, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Set under high ceilings, this remarkable dining room with nice views is a great choice for both casual and formal gatherings. A specialist in Cantonese cuisine, the chef has lived in Southeast Asia for many years. His concise menu is pork free with a quality selection of seafood and dim sum. Don’t miss the daily Inspirational Soup or fresh prawns simmered with glass noodles. Wrap up your meal with a crispy red bean pancake. The signature duck must be ordered in advance.

Name: Yun Pavilion
Address: 5F, Conrad Hotel, 222 Xingmin Road, Zhujiang New Town, Tianhe, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: This lavish interior is inspired by the eight categories of Chinese musical instruments, while the Longquan celadon teacups add a touch of refinement. The experienced kitchen team focuses on traditional Cantonese fare, spiced up by the clever use of gourmet ingredients, such as the signature deep-fried honeycomb taro puff stuffed with seared scallop. In addition, the menu includes regional specialties that cater to all tastes.

Name: Yung Khao
Address: 111 Mu 4, Thanaratch Road, Nong Nam Daeng, Pak Chong, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30130, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: This lively spot, opened in Khao Yai over a decade ago, serves up bold Southern Thai flavours in a welcoming setting with both open-air and air-conditioned areas. The kitchen works with house-made curry pastes, delivering punchy dishes such as stir-fried petai with kapi, minced pork and shrimp – each is intense, fragrant and satisfying. Expect generous portions, quick service and made-to-order cooking that keeps the pace brisk, especially during peak season.

Name: Yunomi Handroll
Address: 806 E. 3rd St., Ste. 100, Los Angeles, CA, 90013, USA
Description: Chef David Movsisian's Yunomi Handroll is located on a stretch of East 3rd Street that has become a hotbed of terrific restaurants and nightlife, and this cool, inviting spot is certainly keeping up with its neighbors. Inside, it's moody and dark with a pared-down design while the counter is the heartbeat of the operation. It's always buzzing—likely due to its unique offerings. There's nothing cookie cutter about this experience where you'll savor the likes of crispy Brussel sprouts with sweet soy sauce, sesame seeds and Ichimi pepper or rock shrimp tempura tossed in spicy mayo seasoned with shichimi togarashi. A signature for a reason, the Yunomi special handroll marries spicy albacore, shrimp tempura, crunchy onions and truffle soy.

Name: Yushan Soup (Liede Xipu Street)
Address: Shop 103, 10 Liede Xipu Street, Tianhe, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: This quaint restaurant stands in a restored 900-year-old village. It says “soup” on the sign and its double-boiled soups that take six hours to prepare are must-tries. However, the season-driven menu offers much more than soups. Scrambled egg with brisket deckle and wild chilli imparts big flavours and mild heat. Diners in private rooms may try the chef’s secret menu. Make sure you book your table and pre-order your favourite seafood.

Name: Yushin
Description: In a residential neighbourhood of well-heeled Neuilly, this Japanese restaurant hosts a pedigree lineup of sushi, bento, omakase. The fish is of the freshest quality and meticulously crafted as one would expect, as are the exquisite, artistically presented desserts. Pale wooden fixtures and white walls depict the classic pared-back interior.

Name: Yut Fei
Address: 3F, Sino International Plaza, 137 Wusi Road, Gulou, Fuzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: This smart restaurant comes complete with a manicured garden, a main dining room and lavish private rooms. The Cantonese head chef, well versed in Cantonese barbecue, sizzling claypot dishes, and dim sum, has been practising his art for over 20 years. He prides himself on his double-boiled soups, slow-cooked for four hours to allow flavours to mingle. Stewed Silkie chicken soup in coconut uses coconut juice instead of water for a nutty-sweetness.

Name: Yuu
Address: 15, Alley 33, Lane 216, Section 4, Zhongxiao East Road, Da'an District, Taipei, 106, Taiwan
Description: A recent renovation has created more contrast and now sports a black counter against wooden panelling. With years of training in Japan, the head chef cooks mostly over an open flame, encompassing eclectic influences from around the world. Only the freshest produce acquired on the day makes it onto the two set menus, with aged and unaged beef from the U.S. and Australia, and Saga and Omi Wagyu from Japan being the main event.

Name: Yuwa
Description: Yuwa's chic interior may lean European, but just one bite of Chef Masahiro Omori's creations and you'll be firmly planted in Japan. This is not fusion cuisine; instead, the chef adheres to the classics. External influences may not come into play, but freshness does—the menu shifts daily to take advantage of the best products available. His nigiri selection features a masterful presentation with a nest of radish threads, fragrant shiso leaf and crushed ice. Buttery chutoro melts in your mouth, and the other offerings might include snappy, clean-tasting nodoguro, premium kinmedai, delicious sayori and local bluefin tuna, but it's the sockeye salmon that will be etched in your memory forever.

Name: Yuxiu
Address: 2F, Zhongwu Hotel, 1899 Zhongwu Road, Zhonglou, Changzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: This hotel restaurant combines Chinese architectural motifs with Jiangnan-themed art and landscaping for a relaxed, serene feel. The menu is based on Jiangsu traditions, with uniquely Changzhou DNA and a few Cantonese dishes. Their rich, buttery Zhaiqiao braised goose has a robust meaty flavour; the steamed buns filled with pork, crab roe and crabmeat explode with umami. For starch, try the dried radish fried rice with shepherd's purse.

Name: Yuyu
Description: The shop’s name recalls the phrase ‘yuyu-jiteki’, ‘a life of leisure, free of worldly cares’. True to this proposition, Yuyu offers dining à la carte in the evening, so guests can relax and dine at their own pace. Sashimi plates are accompanied not with soy sauce but with Daitokuji natto. Beef tongue is dressed with white miso, resembling a stew. Yuyu respects the boundaries of Japanese cuisine while mixing in creativity for a distinctive spin. For the final item, flexibility is the order of the day, as guests can choose from rice with toppings, noodles, curry or a wide range of other options.

Name: Yuè (Causeway Bay)
Address: Shop 1301, Food Forum, Time Square, 1 Matheson Street, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Having worked in some prestigious kitchens in Japan and Macau for over 40 years, the chef designed a menu of refined Cantonese dishes using top-notch ingredients from around the world, such as Alaskan king crab, Japanese chillies and Taiwanese bird’s-nest fern. The classic sweet and sour pork is given a new spin with aged vinegar and dried plums, plus an option of plant-based ‘meat’. Private rooms in various sizes are perfect for parties.

Name: Yuè (Gold Coast)
Address: LG, Gold Coast Hotel, 1 Castle Peak Road, Gold Coast, Tuen Mun, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: It’s not often one can enjoy Cantonese food surrounded by verdant scenery but here on the ground floor of the Gold Coast hotel that’s exactly what you get as this comfortable restaurant looks out onto a delightful garden. The menu includes both traditional and more contemporary dishes and it’s worth seeking out the chef’s specialities such as barbecued pork and double boiled pork lung soup with almond milk and fish maw, and deep-fried chicken with shrimp paste.

Name: Yè Shanghai
Address: 3F, Infinitus Mall, 168 Hubin Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: Though moved into a shopping mall, the grey-brick façade is reminiscent of Shikumen architecture style. In stark contrast, the interior sports velvet sofas in gold and modern art for a touch of glamour. Start your night with creative cocktails from the bar. Then sample their Shanghainese classics like braised pork belly, sautéed shrimps with wild garlic, or xiao long bao. Try also hairy crab dishes such as stuffed crab shell when available.

Name: Yì By Jereme Leung
Address: Raffles Arcade, #03-02, 328 North Bridge Road, 188719, Singapore
Description: The chef honed his remarkable skills while working in China for many years. He returned to Singapore and opened Yi – the Chinese word for art and craftsmanship, hence the fancy dining room adorned in exquisite paper art and the food that reflects eclectic influences from all over China. Steamed free range chicken in herbal broth impresses by its umami and mild herbal aftertaste. Also check out the seasonal menu bursting with creative twists.

Name: Yùn: La Cuisine
Address: 10-13 Fengle Road, Beitun District, Taichung, Taiwan
Description: It may look like a hipster café from the outside, but the warm, relaxing interior boasts some 10 counter seats around an open kitchen. The Taichungese-born, Singapore-trained chef fashions a tasting menu in omakase style that blends Taiwanese traditions with subtle influences from various Chinese regions. The modern, creative score is shrewd and restrained, while still feeling familiar and comforting.

Name: YŪGIN
Description: Perched high above Central Park, YŪGIN is the first restaurant from Chef Eugeniu Zubco. The intimate 12-seat counter blends traditional omakase with influences drawn from the chef’s travels and professional experiences. The experience begins with a series of composed seasonal dishes that showcase Zubco's broader culinary perspective before transitioning into a classical nigiri progression. Throughout the meal, pristine seafood, carefully sourced ingredients and restrained seasoning take center stage, while subtle European influences occasionally emerge alongside traditional Japanese techniques. Custom ceramics and sweeping views over Manhattan complete the highly polished experience.

Name: ZELO
Description: The elegant ZELO restaurant enjoys a beautiful setting in the garden of a 15C inner courtyard, which also boasts an attractive summer terrace. The cuisine is modern in style, created by a chef who uses the best Italian ingredients to prepare creative and contemporary dishes, as well as a few Italian classic favourites such as vitello tonnato and breaded veal. Some dishes are not available at lunchtime, when they are replaced by salads, while in the evening raw fish and seafood options take centre stage.

Name: ZEN Japanese Restaurant
Description: Located in a residential area, this restaurant is a firm favourite with fans of Japanese cuisine. In a pared-back Far Eastern-style setting, diners can look forward to a pleasantly lively atmosphere, as well as friendly and professional service with an authentic Japanese touch. It is clear that a well-coordinated team is at work here. Your options include gyoza, tempura, grilled and pan-fried dishes, udon, sushi and sashimi, plus a large omakase set menu. Wine, sake and Japanese whisky to go with it.

Name: ZOI
Address: Obala Hrvatskog Narodnog Preporoda 23, Split, 21000, Croatia
Description: Located at the edge of Diocletian’s Palace, overlooking the harbor and in the heart of the old town, this restaurant is recognized by its discreet, unmarked entrance that conceals a splendid panoramic terrace on the top floor. The young, vibrant cuisine offers a successful blend of Mediterranean flavors and traditional recipes, interpreted with balance and taste. The wine list, though not extensive, is carefully selected; it’s worth relying on the staff’s recommendations to discover interesting local labels.

Name: ZUM HIRSCHEN beim stöckeler
Description: This family-run restaurant is firmly established in the village and surrounding area. The cosy, rustic dining rooms and pretty terrace in the shadow of the church making an ideal setting for its seasonal, regional cuisine. There is also a good selection of gluten-free dishes. The matching wines are offered. Overnight guests can look forward to pretty, modern Alpine rooms and a good breakfast – taken on the balcony terrace perhaps?

Name: Zaap
Address: 6, Lane 345, Wuxing Street, Xinyi District, Taipei, 110, Taiwan
Description: With 10-plus years of experience in Thai cooking, the owner-chef insists on making all sauces and condiments from scratch. He doesn't hold back on the chillies, so taste first before dousing your food with sauces! Certain items, including the signature chargrilled Thai river prawns, and banana roti, need to be pre-ordered. The prawns are bursting with rich, creamy roe; the flesh is springy and savoury. The house-made dip is the icing on the cake.

Name: Zab Bite - Thai E-Sarn Cuisine
Description: Focusing on the cuisine of northeastern Thailand, this cheery operation has quickly become one of Vancouver's favorites for casual Thai. The sizable menu makes the typical concessions to crowd-pleasing mainstays like pad Thai and pad see ew, which are prepared diligently, but it's the regional specialties on offer that will leave the strongest impression. Think boat noodles, featuring funky, aromatic beef broth loaded with bouncy meatballs and tripe, or crunchy, succulent grilled pork jowl with toasted rice and a punchy nam jaew dipping sauce. Although there are options for all tastes, diners seeking to break a sweat are not likely to be disappointed when requesting spice.

Name: Zacry's
Address: Watergate Bay Hotel, Sea Lane, Watergate Bay, TR8 4AA, United Kingdom
Description: Forming part of the Watergate Bay Hotel but occupying a separate building on the sea wall, this relaxed restaurant comes with one of the best views you’ll find in all of Cornwall. Ensure you ask for a window table, so you can sit back and enjoy the stunning vistas over Watergate Bay, while the chefs work calmly in their open kitchen on a concise, original menu that reflects its surroundings with plenty of seafood, such as Cornish turbot or BBQ monkfish tail. The service team run their restaurant with great care and pride in their work.

Name: Zahav
Address: 237 St. James Pl., Philadelphia, PA, 19106, USA
Description: Tell anyone you’re from Philadelphia, and chances are they’ll ask you about Zahav. This Society Hill institution is as busy now as it was when it opened its doors back in 2008 – and it’s easy to see why. The concept is simple but highly effective: everyone has the same salatim and mezze but you then decide to go either for the Al Ha’esh option, where you get charcoal-grilled skewers, or Mesibah, which means the lamb shoulder (or one of a couple of other specialties). Along with the delicious laffa bread and hummus, the lamb has rightly gained legendary status; it is brined and then smoked over hardwood for a few hours before being braised with pomegranate molasses. It comes with delicious chickpeas and crispy Persian rice and is so soft and yielding, you won’t need your knife. The whole place is run like the well-oiled machine it has become; you just need to be ready when they release reservations weeks in advance.

Name: Zahter
Address: 30-32 Foubert’s Place, Soho, London, W1F 7PS, United Kingdom
Description: If you’ve just returned from Istanbul and want to keep that holiday spirit alive, then get along to this colourful Turkish restaurant just off Carnaby Street and sit at the counter for extra atmosphere. The chargrill and wood-burning oven are used to good effect, whether it's the potatoes with red onions or the prawns with chilli and garlic. Hummus comes with crispy fried chickpeas and is a great way to kick off, while the chicken thighs with peppers and tomato are succulent and flavoursome.

Name: Zaika
Address: 1 Kensington High Street, Kensington, London, W8 5NP, United Kingdom
Description: This long-standing member of London's Indian dining scene is located in a Grade II-listed former banking hall, with all the ornate splendour that would imply – imagine high ceilings, elegant wood panelling and neo-Gothic sculpted detailing. The cooking offers an overview of different Indian regions, with a slight leaning towards northern cuisine, in dishes that use well-judged spicing to enhance the flavours of the central ingredients. Original cocktails can be sipped at the large central bar and the window tables come with views of Hyde Park and Kensington High Street.

Name: Zak The Baker
Description: Look for the color-splashed facade to find this all-day operation which is the brainchild of baker Zak Stern. He grew up in Miami, then apprenticed at a number of organic farms in Sweden, France and Israel before returning to his hometown to fulfill his culinary dreams. The crux of his kosher menu is baked, as in breads and pastries, along with sandwiches, soups and salads. The likes of avocado toast, a frittata sandwich and crispy local fish on brioche sate the legion of ravenous fans who descend upon this Wynwood favorite. Save room for something sweet, say the seasonal concha.

Name: Zalacaín
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: A major icon of Madrid’s restaurant scene, after more than half a century in operation, this restaurant has seen countless personalities of the national and international elite sit at its tables. However, beyond all that, it boasts a historic milestone: It was the first restaurant in Spain to earn three MICHELIN Stars (between 1987 and 1995, both editions included). Today, with that halo of elegance and distinction still firmly in place, it showcases a totally contemporary space, with a beautiful glass-fronted wine cellar and a classic-international menu with a section dedicated exclusively to its most legendary dishes (Búcaro ‘Don Pío’, mushroom and foie gras lasagne, Tellagorri cod, Sirloin Wellington, etc.), alongside a tasting menu.

Name: Zaldiarán
Description: Situated on one of the main avenues that crosses the capital of Álava province, Zaldiarán is one of the town’s long-standing classic restaurants. The updated dining room serves as a backdrop for reinterpreted traditional cuisine, as well as a superb selection of grilled specialities (tuna belly, wild turbot, premium beef chop, Duroc rib etc) and the option of a tasting menu. Take time to admire the photos on display, where you’ll see restaurant owner Gonzalo Antón standing alongside various renowned chefs from Spain and further afield.

Name: Zamek Topacz - Dom Wierzynka
Address: Zamek Topacz Resort & Art Spa, ul. Templariszy 1, Ślęza, 55-040, Poland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: The surroundings are an event in themselves at this restaurant situated on the estate of the same name, which has a 14th-century castle at its heart and now hosts bedrooms, a spa and even a motor museum across its various buildings and parkland. Dining takes place across several castle rooms and focuses on carefully executed dishes with heart and soul, such as comforting homemade blood pudding or generous duck breast with a rich, full-flavoured sauce.

Name: Zamù
Description: This restaurant’s name comes from the initial syllables of the two restaurants that once stood here, which were combined and refurbished a few years ago. Now in the style of a modern bistro, Zamù serves traditional and generously portioned cuisine, plus a reasonably priced business menu at lunchtime. There’s an equal emphasis on meat and fish on the menu, while the clearly displayed blackboard lists the daily specials available.

Name: Zandunga
Address: 41 Dongcheon-ro 108 beon-gil, Busanjin-gu, Busan, 47247, South Korea
Description: Tucked away in a quiet alley, this spot combines an industrial, chic interior with lively music for a relaxed, inviting atmosphere. Inspired by his passion for Mexican cuisine, the chef started this restaurant. Everything from tortillas to fillings and sauces is made in-house. Fresh tortillas are prepared every morning, with colourful variations crafted from different corn varieties. The pork taco is a must-try. Warm, attentive service completes the dining experience.

Name: Zandunga
Address: Manuel García Vigil 512 E., Oaxaca, 68000, Mexico
Description: Sunlight beams down through an open roof and into this colorful, spacious courtyard set with handsome wooden tables. Pottery, textiles and paintings by local artists adorn every wall in sight. Truly, this restaurant captures the vibrant spirit of downtown Oaxaca. It’s a lovely scene to take in while exploring a curated menu focused on traditional regional flavors. Start with the garnachas, the masa carefully fried and topped with tender, shredded beef and pickled cabbage, before moving on to the crispy plantains stuffed with queso and crema that are both tropical and savory. Tamales come prepared with mole negro, sweet corn or raisins. A generous platter featuring many of these standout dishes offers diners an efficient way to sample everything.

Name: Zanze XVI
Address: fondamenta dei Tolentini, sestiere Santa Croce 231, Venice, 30135, Italy
Description: Although the setting and convivial atmosphere in this restaurant recall that of a typical Venetian bàcaro , the cuisine is completely different in feel. The ingredients are sourced from the best markets and local producers, resulting in unique dishes that reflect the culinary traditions of the lagoon and its surrounding area. The few tables arranged outdoors with views of the tranquil canal add to the appeal, while the professional yet friendly service helps to put guests completely at ease.

Name: Zao
Address: 4 Ngo Hue Street, Hai Ba Trung Ward, Hanoi, 113000, Vietnam
Description: This lively, laid-back restaurant combines global flair and Vietnamese roots, as the Hanoi-born chef is a returnee from a career abroad. The elegant setting is conducive to quiet dinners and larger gatherings, with cosy corners or counter seats for kitchen views. Dishes such as tomato bingsu – heirloom cherry tomatoes, buffalo cheese and lime-basil granita – set the tone, alongside razor clam pâté or salmon with baby sprouts for a zingy, refreshing start.

Name: Zapirain
Description: A restaurant with a long history that has finally arrived in Bilbao after half a century and more in Lekeitio! Here, high-quality traditional cuisine is to the fore, specialising in fish and seafood in particular, which the team prepares with as little fuss as possible in order to respect its true essence (we thoroughly enjoyed the grilled white prawns, clams in green sauce and the hake “kokotxas”). Meat does feature, however, including a mouthwatering T-bone steak. For dessert, the home-made tarts are a must!

Name: Zappaz
Description: From the artwork by Peter Wellens and Charlotte De Baere that adorns the bar area to the spacious Scandinavian inspired dining room, Zappaz is a treat for the eye. In the kitchen, chef Seppe demonstrates that contemporary fine dining can be both polished and playful. Creative touches and international flavours like dashi and ponzu are perfectly at home in his inventive score. The menu of three to five courses shines the spotlight on creative recipes, like venison, served medium rare, with prunes and red beetroot, an emulsion of curly kale, churros and a punchy gravy. A banquet of surprises awaits the diner!

Name: Zarza
Description: Zarza, an authentic cosy bolthole with a pretty town garden, is the type of place that inspires loyalty. Chef Cordemans pampers his diners with flawlessly sourced ingredients. The patriotic line-up of Belgian fare is jazzed up by the occasional dash of creativity, illustrated by masterfully cooked langoustine, paired with a gutsy shellfish jus and crunchy courgettes. Sophisticated yet full-bodied flavours. The lunchtime menus are always a safe bet!

Name: Zauberberg
Description: The name translates as "magic mountain", and the name is fitting for a number of reasons. For one, dedicated host Claudia Kimbacher, who adds a pleasantly personal touch to the service with her remarkably warm manner and is also happy to assist you in choosing your wines. Then there is Sven Gerlach's cuisine, which comes in the form of a surprise menu comprising five to six modern and creative courses. If you would like a vegetarian option, please indicate this when making your reservation. From January to November, a three-course "Work Day Supper" set menu is also available Tue-Thu by advance booking. As for the restaurant itself, inside the atmosphere is friendly with an elegant feel to the decor; outside there is a lovely terrace that is very popular on warm summer evenings.

Name: Zayton Courtyard (Licheng)
Address: 10-1 Lanqiao Lane, Licheng, Quanzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Foreign credit cards not accepted,Terrace
Description: The red-brick façade is matched by the retro mosaic flooring and dark peach wood furniture inside. The menu, too, pays tribute to the culinary heritage of the Minnan region – it features standout dishes such as ginger duck stew, which boasts tender meat and deep aromas. The braised taro in meat gravy is starchy, creamy and flavoursome. On a balmy day, request a table on the terrace overlooking the Confucius Temple next door and take in the scenery.

Name: Zazie Bistro
Address: MOL Campus, Dombóvári utca 28, Budapest, 1117, Hungary
Description: Zazie Bistro sits within the tallest skyscraper in Budapest, the MOL Campus, and offers some great views out over the city. It’s a spacious place that incorporates a large open restaurant, a terrace and even a café. The chef brings with him plenty of experience, which shines through in the well-executed, classically inspired, rustic dishes. These could include chilled fruit soups in the summer, or a top-class schnitzel with deliciously creamy potato salad – with the potatoes supplied by the chef’s brother-in-law. There’s also a great value business lunch on offer.

Name: Zeffirino
Address: 11 rue du Portier, Monaco, 98000, Principality of Monaco
Description: Just a stone's throw from the Japanese Garden, this relaxed place, with its warm retro Italian chic (lamps on tables, almond green walls, cane benches and chairs) is dedicated to pasta. The central kitchen and its fresh pasta-making station take pride of place in the restaurant. The authentic Genoese pesto (basil, pine nuts, Pecorino, Parmesan, olive oil and a hint of garlic) is made here according to time-honoured tradition. The quality of every ingredient is top-notch. Here, Riccardo Giraudi, also the creator of the Beefbar brand, pays tribute to Genoese chef Zeffirino Belloni, renowned for his pesto…

Name: Zeffirino
Description: Riccardo Giraudi, founder of the Beefbar concept, opened this establishment, which pays tribute to Genoese chef Zeffirino Belloni, renowned for his pesto, as does its Monaco counterpart. Established in a swanky neighbourhood of the capital, it delivers flawlessly crafted, family-style Italian cuisine, throbbing with flavour: a selection of antipasti, an enticing lineup of fresh house-made pasta, escalopes of veal, Amalfi lemon and almond sauce; a majestic tagliata of chateaubriand, roast potatoes in rosemary; grilled squid tentacles, romesco sauce and a superb millefeuille for dessert. The decor in the style of "Italy in the Roaring Twenties" will not disappoint neo-vintage fans.

Name: Zehntkeller
Description: Located in the middle of the village, this traditional establishment serves good regional and seasonal cuisine. The menu features mouth-watering dishes such as braised beef cheek in a Pinot noir sauce. Opt for a four-course set menu or order à la carte. The house proposes its own organic wines. Very friendly and well-drilled service, a cosy interior, and a lovely terrace laid out under the wisteria. The hotel of the same name has stylish, classic guestrooms.

Name: Zelai Txiki
Address: Travesía del Rodil 79, Donostia / San Sebastián, 20013, Spain
Description: Zelai Txiki boasts a superb location on the slopes of Mt Ulía (hence the impressive views from its panoramic terrace) and even its own vegetable garden. On the extensive à la carte, with its strong focus on dishes inspired by the traditions of Basque cuisine (hake in a salsa verde with clams, Donostia-style spider crab in its shell, hake cheeks in batter or with a pil-pil sauce, etc), you can easily appreciate the importance given to the use of fresh, locally sourced ingredients of the highest quality. You’ll also find interesting daily suggestions plus an extensive tasting menu. The restaurant also makes its own bread every day with organic flour.

Name: Zelna Bisztró
Description: A smart, modern wine bar in the livelier part of this seasonal town, Zelna is named after the wine company whose biodynamic wines it serves – and also offers for purchase. This is a place to kick back and relax, and the small menu mixes light bites with more substantial Hungarian dishes so you can tailor-make your own experience – the beef cheeks are a hit and be sure to save room for the golden walnut dumplings for dessert! Every table is located on the large terrace, which stays open until 2am.

Name: Zen
Description: Value is something of a tricky term when it comes to sushi, which can cost almost as much as a ticket to Japan these days. But in an unassuming Markham strip center dominated by an auto repair shop, those looking to scratch the omakase itch without breaking the bank are in for a treat. The space is true to its name, a calming, tasteful blend of wood slats and attractive lighting with a chef’s counter as well as tables further back. Fish from Japan arrives multiple times a week; the rice is warm and finely vinegared; and chefs work with precision and diligence. They keep the toppings fairly traditional, limited mostly to a keen swipe of soy. Recent highlights include scallops and Murasaki uni from Hokkaido as well as some of the best nori in town.

Name: Zen
Description: This succulent restaurant combines a pleasantly traditional interior with authentic Japanese fare. The extensive menu stars a lineup of staples: sushi, grilled dishes and tempura, together with the house signatures of gyoza and chirashi - even the mochi are made in house. A word of warning: no bookings possible at lunchtime (more concise menu) and it fills up quickly – so come early!

Name: Zen On
Description: It’s easy to see why this restaurant styled on Japanese izakaya is one of the city’s hotspots. Simple, fresh and fun, it boasts bright décor and a buzzing atmosphere that reverberates around the split-level dining room. The menu offers all manner of delights, from dim sum and bao buns to daily made udon noodles and standout ramen crafted using flour delivered direct from Japan. The two-course lunch menu is a steal and the sake list is worth checking out.

Name: Zen Tea
Address: on the side of main entrance of Xiaogang Park, 146 Qianjin Road, Haizhu, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: Styled after a Zen theme, this space provides only private rooms to ensure a serene dining experience. Soybean products made with spring water are exceptional, as are specialities such as faux sea cucumber made with agar-agar and yam starch in a creamy cashew pumpkin sauce. For ovo-vegetarians, stir-fried lily bulbs with olive nuts and egg white is the must-try – the half-set egg white works magic with the crunchy lily bulbs and olive nuts.

Name: ZenA
Address: 75, Section 2, Jiafeng 2nd Street, Zhubei City, Hsinchu County, Taiwan
Description: After honing his skills in Europe for a few years, the head chef has returned to his hometown and opened ZenA, championing a single tasting menu, heavily based on seafood and vegetables. The showstopper fish Wellington is layered with salmon and monk fish fillet and stuffed with monk fish liver, boasting oily richness and deep umami. The counter seats encourage interaction with the chef – ask him to recommend a wine to pair with your food.

Name: Zenzakan
Address: Taunusanlage 15, Frankfurt on the Main, 60325, Germany
Description: Since opening in 2009, this has been a go-to classic in the city's financial hub. Somewhat hidden away, this elegant and stylish restaurant is accessible via a courtyard. The interior, done out in dark tones with dimmed lighting, smacks of the Far East (the terracotta warriors are eye-catching). The atmosphere is lively, and contemporary music provides the acoustic backdrop. The menu includes a wide selection of pan-Asian dishes ranging from sushi and sashimi to classic curries and robata grill specialities. Dishes such as velveted black pepper beef or char siu chicken are especially tempting.

Name: Zero Base
Address: 2F, 17 Millak-ro 33 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48285, South Korea
Description: The chef at Zero Base offers reimaginations of traditional Japanese cuisine. Each visit brings new delights, with dishes that vary depending on the seafood available that day. The chef pushes the boundaries of Japanese cuisine and shares his achievements with the diners. The meticulous balance of dashi and katsuobushi, along with rice cooked from grains grown by the chef’s father, reflects the restaurant’s distinct ive philosophy. The clean, modern interior contrasts with the classic dishes, creating an intriguing ambiance, while the easy conversation with the chef adds to the enjoyable experience.

Name: Zero Milano
Description: “Zero” compromises when it comes to care and quality: the cuisine here is built on exceptional ingredients and rigorous Japanese technique. Under the guidance of Hide Shinohara, the crew presents pure Japanese gastronomy, centered on the highest quality products and the art of form. Beyond the à la carte, the Omakase tasting menu is highly recommended, where the chefs construct a blind journey of great interest and refinement. The dining room features white onyx panels, elegant minimalism, and soft lighting; at the traditional counter, in addition to observing the chefs’ dexterity up close, you can opt for a tasting prepared in the moment, further elevating the sensory experience.

Name: Zest
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Situated within the luxury Grand Hotel La Favorita in the centre of Sorrento, this restaurant has the traditional, opulent style of a grand hotel, while the outdoor terrace boasts the romantic charm that is typical of Sorrento. In the kitchen, the chef creates top-quality cuisine influenced by Campania and enhanced by his own creative touches, resulting in dishes such as marinated tuna with tonka beans, lemon gel and ginger mousse. There’s also a vegetarian tasting menu. A recently opened restaurant that is growing in popularity.

Name: Zest
Address: 25 St. George's Road, St. Julian's, STJ 3208, Malta
Description: Set in a chic hotel in the bustling St Julian’s district, enthusiasts of Asian cuisine will find plenty to explore in this modern and elegant restaurant. The extensive menu covers the classics of Far Eastern cuisine: from sushi and noodles to curry-based dishes, Peking duck and bao buns - you will be spoilt for choice…

Name: Zest
Address: 32 cours de la Vilaine, Cesson-Sévigné, 35510, France
Description: The secret to Zest's success is its market-fresh cuisine, original dishes elevated by creative touches, spices and seasonings, a convivial atmosphere and, in fine weather, a riverside terrace on the banks of the Vilaine. Efficient service and unbeatable value at lunchtime.

Name: Zezilionea
Address: Plaza de San Juan 3, Olaberria, 20212, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: The duo of Ugutz Rubio in the kitchen and his sister Izaro overseeing the front of house have taken over the reins of this beautiful large property in the centre of Olaberria, which is also known as the Balcony of the Goierri region. The traditional Basque cuisine served here features excellent grilled fish and meats, including specialities that you won’t want to pass up on, such as peppers stuffed with cod and the famous mushrooms baked in the oven.

Name: Zhan Bi Lou
Address: 38 Yanggong Causeway, Xihu, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: Sitting on a lotus pond at the north end of West Lake, this restaurant commands lovely views. It serves exquisitely crafted Zhejiang cuisine that befits its iconic location, including dishes named after scenic spots in Hangzhou, such as "wind and lotus by a curvy courtyard": lily bulb, sugar snap peas, and bamboo fungus shaped into a lotus flower, seed pod and root in a light chicken stock. Try the buns and pastry filled with salted mustard greens, too.

Name: Zhang Ji Fish Ball
Address: 25 Jishan Street, Ruifang District, New Taipei, Taiwan
Description: Located in the bustling Jiufen Old Street area, this place isn't very spacious, nor is it conducive to quiet conversation. But this household name has stood the test of time, turning out its famous Fuzhou fish ball soup since 1946! The bouncy texture of the fish contrasts nicely with the juicy minced pork filling. For starch, try the braised pork rice or noodles tossed in pork sauce. Super-fast service means it is a good choice for a quick bite.

Name: Zhang Ji Shanghai La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Address: Alexandra Village Food Centre, #01-56, Blk 120 Bukit Merah Lane 1, 150120, Singapore
Description: Besides xiao long bao, this busy stall offers an array of Shanghainese food, such as pan fried dumplings, sour and spicy soup. Their pork and chives potstickers are filled to the brim and nicely browned on the bottom.

Name: Zheng
Description: Zheng takes you back to the banquets of Imperial China. Through a parade of small dishes, often served on three plates, you will discover the traditions of the four main branches of Chinese cuisine. The succulent Peking duck, with its crispy skin, is deservedly a signature dish – it is heavenly when paired with hoisin sauce and the house-made sambal! The typical tableware and objets d'art (also for sale) add to this unique dining experience. Subtle cuisine which nonetheless offers a wealth of flavours.

Name: Zheng Zhi Wen Ji Pig's Organ Soup
Address: Clementi 448 Food Centre, #01-26, 448 Clementi Ave 3, 120448, Singapore
Description: As well as pork offal, the menu features marinated pork trotter, kway chap and bak kut teh. But the noodle soup with pork liver and kidney stands out – the offal is cooked perfectly and the broth loaded with herbal aromas.

Name: Zhengyalov Hatz
Description: How many leafy greens and herbs can you name? At this simple, no-frills Armenian bakery in Glendale, watch seasoned chefs knead, roll out and griddle a specialty flatbread stuffed with more than a dozen chopped varietals. It’s as if they’ve been doing this their entire lives, working with the likes of sorrel, spinach, scallions and beet leaves to make a tight, forest-green lining that is at once sweet, sour, sharp and refreshing. It’s easy enough to eat one for a snack and several for a meal.

Name: Zhi Wei Cafe
Description: On a quiet street in the Leather District, this friendly Chinese restaurant specializes in Lanzhou-style hand-pulled noodles. A constant whack and thud rings out from the kitchen, as chefs make the noodles all throughout the day. The signature beef noodle soup delivers handsomely with a deep, soulful broth, tender slices of beef and daikon, and a slick layer of chili oil for bittersweet heat. Stir-fried noodles are also worth an order.

Name: Zhonghuafuchun Salon
Description: Zhonghuafuchun Salon is a fascinating establishment where traditional Chinese recipes, combined with local twists, translate into a richly flavourful feast. A cuisine that transforms and responds to changing times must be founded on the chef's clear and accurate understanding of the culinary tradition. Chef Bok-chun Nam’s dedication to reforming Chinese cuisine is unmistakable in his culinary creations. To promote a gradual evolution in his native cuisine, he pays particular attention to selecting quality ingredients while engaging in active exchanges with chefs in Mainland China.

Name: Zhu Xin Ju
Address: 69 Sinyi Street, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
Description: This quaint red-brick mansion, built circa 1846, has housed an omakase restaurant serving traditional Taiwanese banquet dishes since 2015. The room has been carefully restored to its former glory, befitting the old-time recipes the head chef is devoted to. The set meal, offered at a fixed price per person with three tiers to choose from at the time of reservation, comprises seven dishes and one soup. The food highlights local seasonal ingredients, such as savoury milkfish belly with Taiwanese pickled cucumber.

Name: Zhudong Fried Sparerib Noodle (Zhudong)
Address: 8, Section 2, Beixing Road, Zhudong Town, Hsinchu County, Taiwan
Description: This noodle shop started in a wet market in 2003. It moved to its current address near a train station in 2021, while growing in size. As the name suggests, it prides itself on its fried sparerib noodles served with crisp bean sprouts and starchy taro in a broth rich in scallion aromas. The choice of noodles is almost head-spinning; try the locally made ribbon noodles which are springy in texture and are ideal to soak up the flavourful broth.

Name: Zhulin Chicken (Yonghe)
Address: 13, Lane 39, Zhulin Road, Yonghe District, New Taipei, 234002, Taiwan
Description: Long queues at meal times are testament to just how good this tiny gem is. Customers come in droves for its silky, succulent Taiwanese-style poached chicken on steamed rice or noodles. The meat bursts with natural flavour, and well-balanced dips elevate the umami. You can also ask for the chicken leg. The menu also includes other home-style sides and soup for a wholesome meal. Wallet-friendly prices also explain its popularity.

Name: Zhuo Yan · Zhuo Mian
Address: Building No. 19, Ligongdi Phase 4, Suzhou Industrial Park, Suzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: Behind the name – a nod to Suzhou's famous Zhuozheng Garden – an eclectic decor melds traditional Chinese and bold modern aesthetics. At lunchtime, it's all about Suzhou noodles: the soy-based broth is packed with deep flavours, thanks to the condensed base of chicken and pork bone. At dinner, prix-fixe menus, tailored in advance, feature cuisine that fuses Jiangzhe, Suzhou and Cantonese styles, and may include the signature crispy-skin squab.

Name: Zi Jing Cheng Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice
Address: Alexandra Village Food Centre, #01-15, Blk 120 Bukit Merah Lane 1, 150120, Singapore
Description: There is only one thing on the menu – Hainanese boneless chicken rice. Set menus are available for one to three guests, all served with steamed chicken, rice and soup. The bird is tender and flavoursome. Expect to queue any time.

Name: Zi Wei Hall
Address: Building 8, West Lake State Guesthouse, 18 Yanggong Causeway, Xihu, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: Set in a manicured Chinese garden by the lake, the traditionally furnished restaurant makes an impression with its grand and airy space. The smart Chinese attire of the service team is also part of the appeal. On the menu: nicely made Jiangzhe and Hangzhou fare. Try the fried shrimp cake with crunchy water chestnut and diced Chinese celery. The Hangzhou crisp fish is a cold appetiser of deep-fried fish braised in sweet soy – delicious.

Name: Zicht
Description: Bull’s eye: you can enjoy the knockout view over the Flemish Ardennes as much as you like thanks to Zicht’s immense picture windows. The experience is even better on the terrace. Get ready to be pampered by a veteran couple: Hélène graciously supervises the dining room, while Kwinten crafts a subtle Franco-Belgian score that unveils his talent and craftsmanship. An example: ballotine of pheasant, salsifies and endives, flanked by an amazing sauce made out of the bones and enhanced with cognac and cranberries. There is also a vegetarian version of his seasonal set menu with several courses.

Name: Zincenco Kitchen
Description: Offering something a little different, this restaurant is located within a residential apartment, but there’s certainly nothing amateurish or domestic about it; it's even licensed. There are six tables – for a maximum of 14 diners – and all guests are asked to arrive at 7pm, which helps contribute to the supper party atmosphere. You ring doorbell 31 and are greeted by your host Igor Zincenco and his team, who go on to fully explain each well-balanced, satisfying dish which features on a modern surprise menu inspired by Hungarian classics. Do opt for one of the two well-chosen wine pairings.

Name: Zinco Zentido
Address: Ronda del Cañillo 30, Talavera de la Reina, 45600, Spain
Description: Offering traditional cuisine brought up to date that draws from the recipes of Castile-La Mancha and Andalusia, in this cosy restaurant in Talavera, next to the Parque del Cañillo, chef Piedad Sánchez concocts a menu with nods to both La Mancha and her native Malaga, giving us the option of a journey through the flavours of both regions through its set menus: the one called Ejecutivo (only available at lunchtime from Tuesday to Friday) and another one called Gastronómico. You'll find dishes such as semi-liquid mushroom and truffle croquettes, candied and grilled artichokes with seasonal vegetables and foie gras, tuna tataki, juicy venison from the mountains of Toledo... They also boast a large private dining room!

Name: Zinfandel Food & Wine bistro
Description: Situated in a narrow street in the old town, this busy, welcoming restaurant is open from breakfast to dinner, when live music adds to the atmosphere. The menu is focused on Dalmatian cuisine with seasonal and fresh ingredients. The well-curated wine list covers the whole of Croatia, with around 15 wines also available by the glass.

Name: Zinfandel's
Description: Within the Hotel Esplanade, a historic luxury establishment in the capital that was inaugurated in 1925, Zinfandel’s has been guided since 2012 by chef Ana Grgić, whose kitchen delivers a personal and creative reinterpretation of the Mediterranean and continental tradition, celebrating local and seasonal ingredients. The elegant dining room recalls the hotel’s art deco style, with carefully considered furnishings and a sophisticated atmosphere. Among the most interesting dishes, the “Frozen foie gras powder, celery cooked in Port, dense Port and tonka cream with cocoa crumble” merits special attention. The cellar is equally impressive, with over 200 labels and a generous selection available by the glass.

Name: Zintziri Errota
Description: This restaurant occupies a bucolic country house dating from 1650 that was originally used as a blacksmith’s (it is said that, in addition to anchors, weapons and farm implements, they also made high-quality shackles for prisoners similar to those referred to by Shakespeare in the pages of Hamlet), and later as a mill for grinding maize. The beautiful rustic interior comes as a pleasant surprise (an old wood-fired oven is nowadays used as a counter, with a second providing heat in the dining room). The home-style cooking has a contemporary feel and features the occasional creative detail. Check out the daily fish specials and start by ordering the spectacularly flavoured baked octopus on a parmentier of Ratte potato.

Name: Zipang
Description: Zipang translates to "kingdom of the rising sun" – everything about this restaurant, from the modern minimalist decor to the menu, is a celebration of the Far East. The food is definitely something to get excited about – with meticulous attention to detail, the finest ingredients are prepared using authentic Japanese techniques. At lunchtime, excellent value for money; in the evening, the mood is more upscale, with a six- or eight-course tasting menu featuring dishes such as hamachi with mackerel, yuba, Japanese mayonnaise and summer vegetables, or tuna with shungiku wasabi sauce and shrimp croquette. Great selection of top-shelf sake! Friendly service.

Name: Zira Uzbek Kitchen
Address: 7422 Melrose Ave., Los Angeles, CA, 90046, USA
Description: Owner Azim Rahmatov brings the flavors of his native Uzbekistan to Los Angeles with Zira Uzbek Kitchen. Located in the Fairfax District, this restaurant has an engaging ambience complete with tile floors, pale stucco walls and wood furnishings decorated with ikat fabrics and pillows. Zira highlights the unique cuisine of this former Soviet republic that sits at the crossroads of China and Europe, and the name, which translates to cumin, harkens back to the spice trade of the Silk Road in the 15th century. Serving lunch and dinner daily, the menu spotlights traditional cooking with salads, savory pastries, breads, hearty soup (lagman with hand-pulled noodles), grilled skewered meats (shashlik) and dumplings (manti, pelmeni).

Name: Zirbelstube
Description: The journey to this friendly family-run establishment on the outskirts of Nuremberg is well worthwhile. Set in a smart sandstone building (1860), Zirbelstube boasts an attractive main dining space and a separate room with a vaulted ceiling. They serve good regional and seasonal cuisine with classical and international influences in the form of two set menus featuring dishes you can mix and match, such as pan-fried octopus with fennel and beans, labneh and olive tapenade, or Franconian Sauerbraten (marinated pot roast), red cabbage and cranberry salad, dried fruit and bread dumplings. Delightful terrace. Attractive guestrooms.

Name: Zivieri
Description: The produce of the hills come down into the city: this, in essence, is the restaurant. Within the mediaeval Torre Alberici, in the heart of the historic centre, the simple dining room furnished in a contemporary style showcases the produce that the Zivieri farm itself rears and cultivates in the Apennines. Regional cookery, therefore, of an excellent standard, with charcuterie and meats as the jewel in the crown, which moreover can also be purchased, along with cheeses and other foods, from their adjacent butcher’s shop.

Name: Zlatne Gorice
Description: Nestled in the heart of a winery, this restaurant captivates with the natural beauty of its setting, amid rolling hills and verdant vineyards. The culinary offerings are deeply rooted in local products and traditions, with numerous cuts of meat finding their ideal expression on the grill. Don’t miss the celebrated “Hussar’s Steak,” served with house-made bacon, smoked ham, onion, and red chili. In warmer months, dining under the large outdoor gazebo, with its evocative views of the surrounding landscape, is almost mandatory.

Name: Zoe Ma Ma
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: This humble operation wears its charms on its sleeves: a mother-and-son collaboration between businessman Edwin Zoe and Chef Anna Zoe, who cooks up her take on traditional from-scratch recipes using high-quality ingredients, resulting in soul-satisfying, homey dishes — the appeal is not hard to find. The pint-sized space is counter service only — you’ll seat yourself and bus your own table — but the exceedingly reasonable prices make this an easy value proposition. Staples like dan dan noodles and potstickers are top-notch but look out for rotating daily specials like Sichuan braised beef soup noodles.

Name: Zoilo
Address: 9 Duke Street, Marylebone, London, W1U 3EG, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: The menus at this lively grill restaurant explore seasonal ingredients and regional specialities from across Argentina. The wood-panelled room is dominated by a U-shaped bar counter and bright red studded banquettes, which provide a striking contrast to the checkerboard floor. Typical dishes include sea bream ceviche, steaks from the grill and slow-cooked shoulder of lamb. The all-Argentinian wine list offers a great range, with many wines available by the glass and carafe.

Name: Zola
Address: 585 Bryant St., Palo Alto, CA, 94301, USA
Description: A Palo Alto mainstay, Zola charms its way into diners’ hearts via an upscale French bistro menu with Californian flair. Whether you’re using grilled levain to soak up the vermouth cream sauce from a bowl of PEI mussels dotted with pancetta and Fresno chili, breaking the yolk of a soft-cooked egg in a plate of pillowy Parisian gnocchi with wild mushrooms and Brussels sprouts, or indulging in filet mignon with luscious pommes purées and sauce Périgueux, the cuisine offers no shortage of pleasure. Whether seated in the more relaxed, intimate restaurant space, or the bustling adjacent bar, the cocktails are top-notch, and a well-chosen wine list is equal parts Gallic and Golden State. Crème caramel for dessert may be traditional, but it’s also perfectly executed and decadently rich.

Name: Zoltners
Description: You'll find the Zoltners Brewery in the heart of the glorious Zemgale countryside, along with this slick, modern restaurant and an attractively restored period house that’s now a small hotel boasting modern bedrooms; make a weekend of it by dining, staying the night and visiting the Tērvete Nature Park. Menus showcase local produce in an appealing mix of flavoursome northern European dishes, and the simple starters go perfectly with their home-brewed beers and local spirits.

Name: Zomm
Address: Leutascher Straße 485, Seefeld in Tirol, 6100, Austria
Description: This friendly restaurant done out in a modern style is to be found in a small boutique hotel. Depending on your table, you may be able to see into the open kitchen. The menu is built on classic foundations, with a new spin on classic dishes, eg "Winter edition bouillabaisse – Alpine prawns & premium local fish, Jerusalem artichoke, winter vegetables & sourdough toast" or "Confit char – cauliflower, potatoes, chives, beurre blanc & herring caviar". There are three menus to choose from, as well as à la carte dishes. Front-of-house staff ensure diners receive attentive service, with the chefs also lending a hand. The wine recommendations are also spot on; Austrian wines enjoy pride of place.

Name: Zorn - La Petite Auberge
Description: Carnaroli risotto, pan-fried mushrooms and truffle emulsion; quasi de veau, tarragon sauce and celeriac purée; coffee crème brûlée and mascarpone ice cream… Experienced chef Willy-Marc Zorn serves market-fresh cuisine and a "carte blanche" menu at this restaurant near Laon train station. Excellent wine selection. A safe bet.

Name: Zoutra
Description: Opposite its big sister Adraba, Zoutra (meaning "little one" in Aramaic) is a Levantine wine bar-cum-eatery curated by chef Elior Benaroche. This more intimate venue fêtes the Eastern Mediterranean through small sharing plates of fragrant, generous and sun-drenched fare: prawns with bacon, labneh and roasted chilli; braised lamb arayes wrapped in mofletta; burnt lemon tart. The inviting setting blends stone, concrete and hardwood floors, with an open kitchen and a laid-back lounge atmosphere.

Name: Zrno Soli
Description: Located on the first floor of the ACI Marina, this restaurant boasts an ideal setting with a panoramic terrace offering magnificent views of the marina and the old town. The culinary offering is vibrant, creative, and well-executed, with fish as the absolute star, available for selection directly from the display case. Don’t miss the desserts, all strictly homemade.

Name: Zu den drei Linden - Lindenblüte
Description: Tanja and Thomas Siemes run their family business with great dedication, and the food here is exceptional. He cooks up international cuisine that takes its cue from the seasons and incorporates Mediterranean and regional influences; she provides charming service. You can opt for the set menu or order dishes à la carte, such as the mouthwatering crispy fried loup de mer with spinach and Carmague rice. The atmosphere is friendly and the decor has an elegant Mediterranean feel.

Name: Zucchero
Description: As a seafood wholesaler, Zucchero offers seafood dishes in abundance and having worked in both markets and kappo, the chef has learned the skills of handling fish. The menu changes daily, with an impressive lineup of seafood in season. Dishes are simple, including fare such as carpaccio, fritters and stewed tomatoes. A point of pride is that dishes arrive piping hot. Oven-baked veggies served in the pot and steaming plates of pasta testify to the chef’s passion for his craft.

Name: Zucker
Description: The name sort of gives it away if you have any German: This attractive modern brasserie is housed in a former sugar factory, now a listed building. Exposed red brick walls and high ceilings give the setting an appealing industrial feel. In summer, the terrace is shaded by awnings. Flavoursome seasonally inspired dishes are served à la carte, with an additional set menu available. The waitstaff are pleasantly down-to-earth, very friendly and well organised.

Name: Zuid by Adrian Zarzo
Description: Adrian Zarzo brings the world to your plate in this trendy, chic establishment. For example, you start with dim sum, then move on to an intense bouillabaisse and continue your journey with a Mediterranean take on sea bass. Zuid advocates a relaxed approach to gastronomy and is run by a chef who knows how to win over the modern diner. Be sure to drop by the bodega next door for some delicious snacks and a good glass of wine.

Name: Zum Ackerbürger Can Basar
Description: This long-standing inn in Stuttgart's Bad Cannstatt district is in one of the area's oldest half-timbered buildings, dating back to the 15C. The setting is cosy and rustic, with lots of aged wood creating a charming, old-world atmosphere. The kitchen is headed by Can Basar, who previously worked at several renowned establishments. The menu includes seasonal and international cuisine alongside timeless classics – the roast beef is a favourite. In addition to an à la carte selection, there is also a four- or five-course set menu.

Name: Zum Adler
Description: Bearing its name of old, this modern restaurant carries on the tradition of the original 19C Zum Adler inn. Today it is lovely and light inside, with a smart and minimalist decor. The focus lies squarely on high-quality meat, such as Wagyu beef steak. Fish and vegan options also available. At lunchtime there is a smaller offer with a reasonably priced lunch menu - but you can also choose from the steak menu.

Name: Zum Buberl Gut
Description: More than just a pretty face, this gorgeous 17C country estate, located on the outskirts of the city, is also a delightful setting for a delicious meal. The cosy interior marries classic elegance with charming regional touches, creating a welcoming atmosphere. In the summer, the lovely garden beckons. The cuisine is a flavoursome blend of Austrian and Mediterranean influences. The wine list, too, is definitely worth a look. Tip: Come at lunchtime for the small, moderately priced menu available.

Name: Zum Gogosch
Description: Incorporated into the Bio-Landgut Esterhazy, an estate with its own farm, this restaurant has a laser-like focus on regional and seasonal ingredients. Local produce, some of it organic, is used in pleasingly uncomplicated yet sophisticated dishes, for example wild cheese sausage, baked schnitzel, organic Angus beef steak and venison carpaccio. In addition to the well-curated à la carte menu, a five-course set menu (dubbed "Hofmenü") is available on Fri and Sat evenings. Tables are arranged in a converted stable that has been beautifully modernised – the ceiling with beams is lovely. The terrace is wonderful! In case you were wondering, Gogosch is a colloquial term in these parts for a rooster, reflecting the close ties this place has to the region. Access to the restaurant is via Markthalle Kulinarium Burgenland, where you can buy selected products.

Name: Zum Goldenen Anker
Description: Not only does this 18C hotel offer a comfortable stay (opt for one of the newer guestrooms), it is also a popular modern take on a rural restaurant. Diners are waited on by a friendly front-of-house team in an attractive modern setting with a rustic touch. The food is flavoursome, fresh and seasonal. The main courses are also available in smaller portions. In summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous terrace to the rear of the building.

Name: Zum Goldenen Engel
Description: This traditional 16C inn right next to the church has been rebuilt in a way that is absolutely true to the original. You will feel completely at home in the lovingly decorated restaurant, thanks not only to the atmosphere and the competent, charming front-of-house team, but also of course to the high-quality food. Many ingredients come from the region. Plus they have cosy guestrooms.

Name: Zum Goldenen Hirschen - Hirschenstube
Description: Dating back to 1624, this venerable old building in the centre of Gmunden used to be an inn and is now a boutique hotel and restaurant. Chef Christoph Parzer expertly transforms fresh ingredients into flavoursome dishes that range from regional specialities to modern international cuisine. This interesting mix is presented in the form of an appealing à la carte selection including steaks and Alpine sushi, and the "AURUM" fine dining menu served in the evening. The interior impresses with its attractive blend of traditional elements – such as a tiled oven, a timber ceiling and brick vaulting – and modern touches (artwork and clean lines). Pretty terrace in the courtyard. Austria is particularly well represented when it comes to the wines.

Name: Zum Goldenen Pflug
Description: In one of the oldest inns in the region, tradition is celebrated, but not at the expense of progress. There are a number of charming dining areas in which to enjoy dishes such as Rindertafelspitz aus dem Kupferpfandl (boiled beef fillet from the copper pot), apple horseradish, chive sauce, creamed spinach and sautéed potatoes and, for dessert, Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake) with plum compote and whipped cream. Order à la carte or opt for the "Signature Menu" for two or more diners.

Name: Zum Goldenen Schäfli
Description: Dating back to 1484, this place has a palpable sense of history. It is the city's last surviving guild house and is brimming with charm, not least due to the wood-panelled interiors. One quirk of the Zunftstube (guild room) is its sloping floor – you might find yourself sitting at a bit of a tilt! The kitchen follows a classic approach, emphasising regional and seasonal fare. Be sure to sample the hand-cut beef tartare, available mild, medium or hot to suit your taste. Or perhaps the St Gallen veal sausage with red wine onion sauce is more your thing. Service is attentive and genuinely warm.

Name: Zum Hirsch
Description: Familiar faces in the region, Markus and Britta Nagy are known as ambitious restaurateurs. Here, in their charming half-timbered inn dating back to 1688, they serve regional and Mediterranean-inspired fare. In addition to an à la carte menu, there is a three- to five-course set menu in the evening and the reasonably priced three-course "Eat & Talk" set menu at lunchtime (Tue-Fri). On Friday and Saturday, for dinner, diners choose between two set menus (no à la carte). In winter, the room with a fireplace is cosy; in summer, the lovely terrace beckons. Well-kept overnight accommodation available.

Name: Zum Krug
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This place has a long history that stretches back to 1720, and the Laufer family has now been at the helm for three generations. Behind the gorgeous historical façade, the cosy dining spaces exude traditional charm. Theregional and international cuisine takes its cue from the seasons, and the menu includes dishes such as a Sauerbraten (marinated pot roast) of organic pasture-fed beef with potato dumplings and cranberries. The friendly and professional waitstaff will be happy to recommend fine Rheingau wines from the estate to accompany your meal. Delightful courtyard terrace. Smart guestrooms – some are especially modern.

Name: Zum Loejelgucker
Description: In a wine-growing village at the foot of the Vosges, this 18C Alsace farmhouse has bags of charm: tasty regional dishes, plus some more modern options, dark wood panelling, frescoes and a flower-decked courtyard in summer. Warm, friendly service and a family vibe.

Name: Zum Löwen
Description: The elegance and warmth of this restaurant remain unchanged, like a timeless signature. The cuisine, always attentive and in tune with contemporary tastes, offers more essential and straightforward dishes that convey local flavors with refined simplicity in the new "Wine & Dine" concept by Elisabeth. The charming interiors result from the skillful renovation of an old farmhouse, from the barn to the old stables, incorporating what was once outside; everything has been restored and enhanced with modern touches. A commendable service and an excellent wine cellar, built over the years, complete the delightful experience.

Name: Zum Ochsen
Description: It is not without good reason that this 300-year-old restaurant has so many regulars. Here, they honour tradition while managing to keep up with the times – and that goes for both the decor and the food, which is not only beautifully presented but also of the highest quality. The Swabian cuisine follows the seasons and draws on international influences. The emphasis is on regional ingredients, including meat and sausage products made on site in their own butcher's shop. As well as à la carte dishes, a three- or four-course set menu is available.

Name: Zum Ochsen
Description: The atmosphere is really cosy in this restaurant, which is charmingly done out in the traditional style typical of the region. The kitchen serves up flavoursome, ambitious dishes with a regional and seasonal focus, as well as the occasional international twist. For overnight guests, this long-standing family-run establishment offers comfortable guestrooms and a spa with a range of facilities and treatments and a swimming pool.

Name: Zum Riesen
Description: The Wenz family put their heart and soul into running this place, and quality is also a top priority in the kitchen. Good-quality regional and seasonal ingredients are used to rustle up modern-inspired dishes, which are also served in the form of a set menu. Choose a regional wine to go with your food. In summer, the terrace in the courtyard is a secluded spot. There are lovely individually decorated guestrooms too.

Name: Zum Rössl
Description: This long-standing family-run establishment is housed in a former coaching inn dating back to 1642. In the charming, traditionally styled restaurant, you can choose between regional classics and seasonal dishes, some with a Mediterranean twist. Menu highlights include boiled beef brisket with sweet-and-sour fruits, horseradish sauce and potatoes, or French bouillabaisse with toasted bread and rouille sauce. A surprise menu can also be pre-ordered. The lunch options are particularly appealing. Tip: In good weather, make a beeline for the idyllic terrace!

Name: Zum See
Description: For over 30 years, the Mennig family has welcomed guests to their cosy chalet, which enjoys an idyllic location in a little old mountain hamlet – the terrace is truly one of a kind! The menu features regional cuisine, with the Cremeschnitte (vanilla slice) as the undisputed classic. Exceptionally warm and efficient service is the icing on the cake. In winter, the property sits right by the ski slope. The 45min walk from the town centre is more than worth it.

Name: Zum Simonbräu
Description: A down-to-earth pub, just the way we like them! Part of the Bitburger Brewery, this place has an attractive decor of solid wooden tables (no tablecloths here!), walls decorated with pictures, and modern details that foster a pleasantly lively atmosphere. The charming team serves home-style regional dishes, as well as more sophisticated options. Cordon bleu with Eifelschwein pork and "Ōra King salmon – tartare & fried" whet the appetite. The inexpensive dish of the day is popular with the lunchtime crowd. You can also spend the night in one of the spruce guestrooms.

Name: Zum Storchen
Description: This establishment is run by the Trienen family in a beautifully renovated old townhouse. The food here is exceptional; the cuisine is seasonal and regional, drawing on modern and international influences. Tip: Try the daily specials as a set menu. There are two pleasant terraces: one out on the pavement, and one in the courtyard to the rear of the building, which is quieter. Comfortable modern guestrooms.

Name: Zum Verwalter
Description: Its origins dating back to the 17C, this site is steeped in history. Today the building houses pretty hotel rooms and an extremely tasteful restaurant with authentic charm – plenty of wood and low ceilings make for a really cosy atmosphere. In summer, the terrace, too, is very inviting. When it comes to the food, the kitchen draws on what the market has to offer. Top-notch ingredients are used to create classic veal tartare with pan-fried sweetbreads, for example. The marvellous selection of 600 wines, including top wines from Austria, Italy and France, is a must for wine lovers. The service is friendly and proficient – while always on hand, the staff's presence is by no means intrusive.

Name: Zum weissen Rauchfangkehrer
Description: This cosy restaurant is divided into four traditionally decorated rooms – in one of them, gentle piano music provides the soundtrack to your evening meal. Delicious Austrian cuisine is the order of the day, including house specialities such as "Rauchfangkehrers Wiener Schnitzel". The wine list is exclusively Austrian and organised according to grape variety.

Name: Zuma
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Notable sake list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The Dubai outpost of this global brand is set over three floors and comes with trendy, contemporary styling, several sushi counters and a lively atmosphere. Super-fresh, high quality ingredients are prepared with dexterity. Flavours are superb and the charming staff provide friendly, efficient service.

Name: Zuma
Address: Abu Dhabi Global Market, The Galleria Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Gliding down the softly lit staircase allows everyone to feel like they’re about to arrive at the best party in town – this really is Fun Central, with the music to prove it. As with all other Zuma branches around the globe, the menu covers a multitude of Japanese bases, with seafood from the robata grill being the standout, although the signature corn-fed baby chicken rightly has many admirers too.

Name: Zuma
Address: Al Maha Island, Lusail, Doha, Qatar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: With Winter Wonderland theme park opposite, this branch of the international group has always been popular with families at certain times of the year; its weekend DJ, large terrace, island bar and on-view kitchen also make it a favourite with groups of friends looking for a fun night out. The menu offers an extensive selection of contemporary Japanese dishes, which are all designed to be shared; this includes a range of options from the robata grill like marinated lamb chops and salmon teriyaki.

Name: Zuma
Address: 5 Raphael Street, Knightsbridge, London, SW7 1DL, United Kingdom
Description: Zuma may now be a global brand, but this long-standing Knightsbridge restaurant was the originator of its informal, izakaya-inspired Japanese cuisine. Managing to still feel fresh over 20 years after opening, its home to a glamorous clientele who fit right in with the striking surroundings and bustling atmosphere. Sharing is a great way to experience as much of the extensive menu as possible – but if you have to prioritise, make sure you try the array of produce cooked on the robata grill, from tofu to chicken wings.

Name: Zuma
Description: Here you will find an international concept that has already made a name for itself in London, Bangkok, Las Vegas, Doha and Capri… Stylish, sleek design, dimmed lighting and subtle music create a lounge-like atmosphere; the large bar in the centre is an invitation you can't refuse – to have a cocktail. The extremely courteous English-speaking waitstaff bring you the extensive menu, which offers something for everyone. There is sushi, meat and vegetables from the robata grill (eg aubergine with aka miso is a great side dish) or modern dishes such as crispy fried squid, green chilli and lime. The restaurant is housed in the tasteful and history-laden Weisses Rössl hotel, very close to the charming old town.

Name: Zuma Bodrum
Address: Cökertme Caddesi No:36, Yalıkavak Marina, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
Description: Zuma is not at all out of place among the impressive yachts and luxury boutiques. This izakaya has a sophisticated feel with its phenomenal sea views, clubby vibe and laid-back atmosphere. From May to October, this is the place to discover a trendy take on Japanese cuisine, in which the robata grill and sushi take centre stage. They serve a variety of nigiri, succulent grilled tiger prawns or teriyaki-marinated grilled salmon with pickled cucumber. Meat lovers might prefer the 700g dry-aged ribeye. The extensive menu is full of irresistible options! Prolong your experience at this hip establishment with a refreshing cocktail at the bar.

Name: Zuma İstanbul
Address: İstinye Park No:461, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34460, Türkiye
Description: The Istanbul branch of this chic Japanese restaurant is on a par with its London, Dubai and other outposts. That means top-notch ingredients that are showcased by a contemporary approach to authentic Japanese cuisine. On the menu: sushi (you can watch the chef meticulously preparing it at the counter), tempura, fish from the robata grill, vegetarian options… There's so much to choose from! Replete with subtle East Asian nuances, the ingredient-led, intensely flavoursome dishes never fail to hit the mark. The gyoza, filled with minced beef and lamb and seasoned with paprika, chilli, sesame and lemongrass, are simply irresistible. Rest assured: The cosmopolitan Zuma feels right at home amid the most exclusive fashion boutiques of Istinye Park shopping centre.

Name: Zuni Café
Address: 1658 Market St., San Francisco, CA, 94102, USA
Description: Famous for its laid-back California vibe and great, locally sourced eats, this San Francisco institution’s iconic space embraces its unique shape, and is styled with bold artwork-covered walls, a copper bar and wood-burning oven sending out delightful pizzas that fill the room with mouthwatering aromas.Zuni makes for a divine anytime destination — and proof is in the many business folk, trendy ladies-who-lunch and tourists who fill its tables. Lunch may be time for the Caesar salad or slow-cooked kale and onion soup with croutons; while dinner should include oysters to start, the chicken for two roasted in the wood-fired brick oven and a wedge of the gâteau Victoire for dessert.

Name: Zur Dankbarkeit
Description: Steeped in tradition, this restaurant in the centre of Podersdorf has been run by the same family for four generations. Their ties to the region are reflected in delicious dishes made with ingredients from the owner's native Burgenland. The handwritten menu features classics such as veal liver and schnitzel, as well as options including pan-fried Arctic char fillet with pak choi and celeriac cream. In summer, the courtyard behind the house is especially inviting, with a spacious gravel terrace shaded by trees. The estate's own wines are well represented on the menu. The establishment also runs a wine tavern nearby (open Fri, Sat and Sun), and has five cosy and inviting double rooms.

Name: Zur Glocke
Address: Friedrich-von-Teck-Straße 12, Höchstädt an der Donau, 89420, Germany
Description: The Stoiber family put their heart and soul into running this modern restaurant. Their commitment is particularly evident in the excellent cuisine, which follows the seasons and draws on quality ingredients. There are three set menus, one of them vegetarian, and all courses can also be ordered à la carte. Mouthwatering creations include beetroot with porcini ice cream, quail and mushrooms, or cream of sweetcorn soup with wild prawn, polenta and popcorn. Diners are treated to attentive service in an inviting setting: Pale wood, clean lines, exposed concrete and restrained decorative details create a refined, minimalist feel. The terrace in the front garden is ideal for warm summer days. For overnight stays, there are two categories of contemporary guestrooms: "Design" (in a new building) and "Classic" (in the original building).

Name: Zur Iphöfer Kammer
Description: This picture-perfect Gasthaus is located on Marktplatz, in the centre of this quaint wine-growing town. The lovely little terrace is as inviting as the elegantly charming interior. Your dedicated hosts, Heidrun Kaufmann and Markus Lösch, really know how to create a warm and welcoming atmosphere: she provides cordial service with a personal touch; he cooks up ambitious dishes brimming with bold flavours – venison ragout fin with rye bread gnocchi, or sea bass with artichokes and lemon polenta. Excellent wines from Wirsing wine estate.

Name: Zur Kaiserkron
Description: In the heart of Bolzano, on the ground floor of the refined Palazzo Pock which grandly overlooks the piazza, Zur Kaiserkron (The Imperial Crown) welcomes guests in elegant, contemporary surroundings enhanced by striking vaulted ceilings that lend a touch of theatricality to the experience. Since 2025, chef Sinisgalli’s vision unfolds along two distinct paths, designed to suit different guests and moments of the day. The first offers a light, dynamic cuisine firmly anchored to the territory, where traditional flavors are reinterpreted with contemporary spirit, ideal for a city in constant motion. The second, housed in a gilded dining room with an almost suspended charm, represents the chef’s deeper, more creative soul: a gastronomic journey that delves into research, technique, and imagination, delivering an immersive experience of great intensity.

Name: Zur Krone
Description: The Isele family has been cultivating the art of hospitality in this traditional building since 1854. The interior boasts a pleasant atmosphere in which to enjoy classic German cuisine that is seasonal, carefully prepared and based on a range of regional ingredients. The home-made terrines and desserts are definitely worth trying – the diet will have to wait! The wine list also has a very regional slant.
