In addition, there are comfortable, tastefully decorated guestrooms in which you will be tempted to stay for more than one night!

Name: Zur Linde
Description: The fifth generation is now in charge of this family-run establishment. Sandra and Marco Linden are committed to creating a charming atmosphere and serving good food here. She courteously and competently oversees the service; he cooks up tasty regional and seasonal dishes, which are always modern in inspiration – served as a set menu or À la carte.

Name: Zur Linde
Description: The Trautwein brothers run this former coaching inn with great dedication. Some 300 years old, it features a charming blend of historical and modern decor. The menu includes Swabian classics such as Gaisburger Marsch (traditional beef stew), Maultaschen and Zwiebelrostbraten (beef and onions in gravy), alongside seasonal dishes such as pink-roasted lamb rump with beans done two ways and polenta with herbs, as well as vegetarian options. A lovely leafy terrace lies to the rear of the building. A rustic vaulted cellar can be booked for private functions. Tip: The shop sells soups, sauces, Maultaschen and spaetzle to take away.

Name: Zur Mühle
Description: In their well-established restaurant – it’s been in the same family since 1895 – Hermann and Kerstin Berger prepare internationally inspired cuisine such as sliced salmon in a rocket and pesto crust with teriyaki beans, mashed potato and sweet mustard. The interior is cosy with a modern note.

Name: Zur Palme
Address: Marktplatz 6, Neuhofen an der Ybbs, 3364, Austria
Description: After completing stints at renowned establishments, Theresia Palmetzhofer returned home, and she has been running this charming restaurant with her dedicated team since 2016. Modernisation work saw the historical walls and structures of the 500-year-old building carefully preserved and given an inviting, upscale look. In addition, the property boasts a gorgeous terrace. The boss herself heads up the kitchen and presents a pleasingly concise seasonal menu featuring classic and regional dishes with a modern twist, such as celeriac with a cheese foam, apple and buckwheat, or saddle of venison served rare with Brussels sprouts, red cabbage and potato pillows. The emphasis is firmly on locally sourced ingredients. Heavily centred on Austria, the excellent wine list also showcases French and Italian labels. A range of natural wines is additionally available.

Name: Zur Schlupp
Description: Isabelle and Michael Ehrhardt devote themselves with great enthusiasm to running their charming little restaurant in this house dating from 1608. The atmosphere is cosy and casual, with the building's original character beautifully preserved and enhanced by tasteful modern touches. The chef-patron's cooking is defined by freshness and seasonality – there are two set menus (one vegetarian) that change on a monthly basis as well as à la carte dishes. The hostess provides attentive service and recommends good wines, with the Rheingau Riesling selection being a highlight. Don't forget to book. Tip: The courtyard is a romantic spot in summer!

Name: Zur Sonne
Description: Hanspeter Rombach attaches great importance to organic ingredients in his cheerful and inviting restaurant. At lunchtime and in the evening, local cuisine is served à la carte; the evening features more elevated fare – diners can choose between two set menus or an additional à la carte selection. Tempting highlights include "red cabbage baked in a salt crust, marinated with linseed oil and red onions, a fine bitter-orange sauce, and toasted sourdough" or "St Peter kid goat from from Ernst's farm, served in its own jus with mushrooms, fig compote, baby vegetables and Schniederspätzle (Black Forest spaetzle)". The on-site shop, Heimatladen, sells delicious treats such as organic vegetables, bread, honey, wine and more for you to take home. For overnight guests, this long-established family business has cosy guestrooms and a lovely sauna area. Tip: Pay a visit to the monastery with its Baroque church.

Name: Zur Sonne
Description: Run by the Glück family, this place serves fantastic seasonal dishes and regional classics. From game to Altmühltal lamb and their unique "Sauerbraten 2.0", the menu is packed with delicious options. With a clear preference for local produce, the kitchen team serves up dishes that are beautifully balanced in flavour. The bright, modern conservatory is a delightful space, as is the splendid terrace in summer. Comfortable and attractive guestrooms.

Name: Zur Waage M.E.B.
Description: This long-established restaurant enjoys a charming location in the town centre, directly on the Leda River – in summer, the lovely terrace with a view of the museum harbour beckons! Inside, you can expect all the trappings of a traditional inn with the odd rustic maritime touch. Mario E. Brüggemann, who began his culinary career here as an apprentice, prepares fresh, flavoursome cuisine rooted in regional traditions and seasonal produce. The menu features items such as shrimp soup, North Sea plaice fillets or a duo of venison. Lunch options are a little more limited.

Name: Zuzori
Description: A welcoming and informal atmosphere characterises this small restaurant in the very heart of the medieval walls. The menu draws inspiration from Mediterranean tradition while opening to international influences. A selection of Croatian tapas – prosciutto, local cheeses, tartare and tempura – provides the opening, followed by fish, meat and vegetarian dishes, each interpreted with an agreeable contemporary touch. The outdoor seating in a narrow lane of the old town is particularly evocative, perfect for immersing oneself in the magic of Dubrovnik.

Name: ZweiSinn Meiers | Bistro
Description: If a really nice bistro in Nuremberg is what you are looking for, then this is the place for you! A pleasant, refined atmosphere, friendly service, and good food await you here. The modern and Mediterranean-inspired à la carte selection is appealing, and there is also a caviar menu. At lunchtime, the reasonably priced daily special is always in demand. Tip: On Wednesday and Thursday evenings, selected dishes from the menu of the fine dining restaurant, which is located in the same building, go into a three-course business menu (sparkling wine included). They also offer fine wines by the glass and top-drawer alcohol-free alternatives.

Name: Zwo20
Description: The name of this restaurant refers to the year 2020, in which Andrea von Csiszer (head chef) and Sophie Herzog (the cordial and highly adept maître d') set up shop. Diners are drawn here not only by the somewhat unusual setting in a historical chapel with striking features such as vaults and ceiling paintings, but also the trendy and laid-back atmosphere, as well as the intriguing culinary concept: Asian sharing cuisine with a European twist. You can put together an assortment of several small, cleverly devised dishes to share, such as "Peking pork 24hr sous vide" with fried onion, soya and honey, or cauliflower wings with red cabbage, sweet chilli, fennel and potato. The location in the centre of the old town, caught between the Danube and the Inn, near the Dreiflüsseeck (three-river confluence), is also delightful. Tip: Römerplatz multi-storey car park just a few minutes' walk away.

Name: Zàghara Restaurant
Description: Housed in the elegant Relais Villa Flora, this restaurant occupies a natural terrace with breathtaking views of the Nissene hills. The dishes are predominantly regional in style yet reinterpreted with a modern twist. There’s also a good wine selection with a focus on Sicilian and Italian labels.

Name: Zéphirine
Description: This urban inn, sporting a bistro vibe and fronted by a delicatessen, is blessed with a quaint, old-fashioned name! It is also a family story that unites three veterans who’ve knocked around a bit. Each dish bears the chef’s distinctive hallmark (special mention for the side dishes and the starters, to share). The accent is on classic Gallic nosh with a modern twist in terms of presentation; the menu is more elaborate in the evening.

Name: Zócalo
Description: Set right in Capitol Mall, this upscale spot (which also has outposts in University Village, Roseville and Folsom) greets guests with heavy wooden doors, dark metal chandeliers and plenty of lush greenery. The sprawling outdoor patio offers prime people-watching, while the menu draws inspiration from regional Mexican cooking.Freshness is a clear focus, whether in bright ceviches layered with avocado, cucumber and serrano or in a range of tacos served on house tortillas. Options run from crisp Baja-style fish to marinated steak and braised chicken, paired with lively salsas and classic garnishes. Tequila enthusiasts will appreciate the deep selection, though there’s no shame in sticking with a margarita — the “mango fresco” with its tajín rim remains a popular choice.

Name: Zöllner's Weinstube
Description: Surrounded by splendid gardens, this 18C half-timbered sandstone building is as charming on the outside as it is on the inside. Sitting beneath a striking vaulted ceiling, diners can enjoy regional as well as Mediterranean-inspired cuisine made from first-rate produce. There is also an excellent selection of Franconian wines. In summer, the terrace is a must!

Name: Złoty Groń
Address: Złoty Groń Resort & Spa, Istebna 593, Istebna, 43-470, Poland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated within the alpine resort of the same name, the views at this charmingly run restaurant are a serious draw. Whether seen from the terrace or the dining room, the sweeping countryside vistas are a treat. The cooking provides a worthy accompaniment to the setting with both an à la carte featuring aged Polish meats and a tasting menu showcasing the chef’s love of the region, via complex, occasionally nostalgic dishes based around prime local produce.

Name: [bu:r]
Description: Eugenio Boer offers a 100% Italian menu which focuses on local ingredients, with the aim of showcasing some of Italy’s favourite dishes while at the same time supporting small-scale producers. However, this philosophy is in no way limited to respecting traditions – on the contrary, it offers the chef the freedom to express his own creativity via a selection of dishes which combine past and present. As a result, guests can choose between a concise à la carte and two different tasting menus: “I Classici” (meat-based dishes) and “Le Aromatiche”, which changes perspective by placing aromatic plants centre stage. In short, a flexible approach which offers guests a culinary experience that will certainly make an impression!

Name: [w]einklang
Description: A cosy atmosphere reigns in this chic little restaurant in the northwest of Nuremberg, with wine racks adding a nice decorative touch. In this setting, chef-owner Tomas Spanu serves a four- or five-course set menu, of which a vegetarian version is also an option, and an à la carte menu. The chef – who, as it happens, is of Sardinian-French heritage – cooks in a pleasingly streamlined and ingredient-led style. The friendly and attentive service is the icing on the cake. You'll definitely want to keep coming back for more! NIAN BISTRO is also part of the establishment.

Name: a food affair
Description: As soon as you set foot in this eatery of oriental inspiration, you will feel the serene vibe, further enhanced by the exquisite terrace to the rear. Chef Locquet shares his passion for Thailand and Vietnam. Traditional recipes made with first-class ingredients and dishes that shout the talent and deft touch of their chef. An Asian excursion steeped in subtlety and enthusiasm.

Name: a.lea
Description: a.lea is the quintessence of appetising bistronomy fare: slow-cooked egg, creamy peas and smoked haddock; duckling fillet, sweet potato, blood orange, mild curry sauce and meat jus. The dishes are spot on and have that "fresh from the market" quality. At lunchtime, including at weekends, a meal here is excellent value for money. Dishes are more elaborate and refined in the evening.

Name: abcV
Address: 38 E. 19th St., New York, NY, 10003, USA
Description: Tucked inside ABC Carpet & Home, this restaurant offers elevated vegetarian food in a beautiful, minimalist space. A clean aesthetic dominates the space, with mismatched chandeliers and bursts of bright colors. There is a buzzy energy here, luring everyone from the business crowd to ladies who lunch and like their green juice poured into a wine glass, The menu is detailed and clever, offering vibrant dishes for breakfast, lunch, and brunch alongside pressed juice, smoothies, and kombuchas. An egg and cheese dosas delights, then bergamot-scented spaghetti is tossed with rainbow chard for an umami-packed dish.

Name: acquafarina
Address: 425 W. Georgia St., Vancouver, V6B 5A1, Canada
Description: This downtown Italian restaurant's lofty ceilings match its equally lofty ambitions. This wasn’t always the plan: it originally meant to open as a pizzeria, which explains the large wood-burning ovens perched up above the room. But this pivot to fine dining is less severe than it seems. Friendly, uniformed servers hardly enforce the rules, and diners can still order a la carte, including pizzas at lunch. The kitchen shines brightest at more straightforward preparations, like a wonderful, chilled tomato soup with Spanish ham or delicate pasta dressed simply. The enclosed patio offers the best mix of formality and fun.

Name: ad lib
Description: Dietmar and Nicole Sawyere have moved on from Dallenwil, where they enjoyed great success with two restaurants at Gasthaus zum Kreuz. Since December 2025, the dedicated couple, along with their daughter and son and the Dallenwil team, have been running this compact restaurant in the charming Hotel Welschen. The cuisine, rooted in classical traditions and inspired by the seasons, is presented as a five-course menu, with optional dishes to add on or swap in. A fine example of the bold and technically precise cooking is the tender Alpine Angus beef served with aromatic white asparagus tips and a freshly whipped béarnaise sauce enhanced with pine nuts and wild garlic. Well-matched wine recommendations come courtesy of the charming and attentive proprietress. Large windows in the tasteful, upscale modern interior overlook the village and mountains, and there is a lovely terrace facing the Matterhorn. Welschen Bar & Stübli is an alternative dining option on the premises.

Name: aerde
Description: Housed within the imposing building designed by architectural firm Robertneun in the Lokdepot development, this compact restaurant is well worth seeking out. In the kitchen, set on a mezzanine above the dining space, the chefs create modern dishes designed for sharing. Seasonal ingredients take centre stage, with fermentation playing a key role – a theme echoed by the decorative jars displayed throughout the pared-back interior, which features clean lines, wood finishings and earthy hues. Capacity is limited to a few small tables, a communal table in the middle and the bar counter. The atmosphere is neighbourly and personal; service is friendly and adept. The team are happy to provide drinks recommendations, drawing from an exciting selection.

Name: al kostat
Description: Occupying the former Moritz beer brewery where al kostat shares its dining spaces and kitchen with the gastronomic Alkimia restaurant. Here, you can enjoy the more informal and less expensive cuisine of award-winning chef Jordi Vilà on a Catalan-inspired à la carte designed for sharing. We can highly recommend the “kokotxas” (cheek) of hake pil-pil with white Ganxet beans.

Name: al lago
Description: Housed in a type of winter garden with a charming terrace (the jewel in the crown!), this restaurant serves dishes that combine modern influences with more classic touches, all prepared using ingredients of the best quality. Make sure you try the risotto made from Carnaroli rice with red pepper, green sauce and Cantabrian anchovies, as well as the Guanaja chocolate mousse and ice cream with mixed berries. An excellent selection of wine and young, friendly service complete the picture.

Name: alewino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Spread across various rooms, this starkly decorated bistro started life as a wine shop. There’s still a range of bottles for sale, along with a wine list that offers plenty of younger and lesser-known producers. The menu allows guests to order a few plates to share, sometimes showing off seasonal fruits and vegetables, and packing plenty of intense flavour into the generous dishes. Look out for the signpost by the gates when arriving, as the entrance is tucked away off the main street.

Name: alexxanders
Description: Located in a residential area, this restaurant boasts a stylish interior and a courtyard terrace with a beautifully landscaped little garden. The flavoursome dishes draw inspiration from around the globe and incorporate Mediterranean and seasonal influences. Why not enjoy an aperitif at the bar before your meal? The wine list is also worth a look. Guestrooms with modern interior design are available in the hotel of the same name.

Name: allta
Address: 1 Three Locks Square, Grand Canal Dock, Dublin City, DO2 A5W7, Ireland
Description: After years of moving around Dublin at festivals and pop-ups, the talented team behind allta finally have a permanent home in this spacious dockside building in a swish area of the city. The space is split into two parts: an industrial-chic cocktail bar complete with a DJ and a separate dining room with an open kitchen where guests can sit at the counter. The cooking takes the form of a tasting menu and has a strong Irish base, with quality seafood from native blue lobster to day-boat sole making an appearance.

Name: alto
Description: This restaurant in the Atlantic Grand Hotel has a tastefully sleek interior, with dark wood panelling, large modern fixtures, as well as designer upholstered chairs in red and brown. The conservatory extension is also a lovely spot, as is the courtyard garden in fine weather – an Alpine-style hut is erected here every winter. The menu features classic dishes with a modern twist, plus classics such as schnitzel. Incidentally, the crockery is custom-made in Bremen. The location in the old town is ideal, with all the main attractions – the Weser River, Schnoor, Rathaus, Kunsthalle – just a short walk away.

Name: am kai | restaurant. seafood. drinks. elbblick
Description: This pleasant restaurant right on the waterfront is trendy, hip and relaxed, and offers a super view of the container port – especially from the terrace in summer! The kitchen serves modern seafood dishes such as "prawn tempura, kimchi, nuoc cham, passion fruit" and "monkfish BBQ, grilled corn, plum, tarragon". Meat eaters, too, are bound to find something to their liking; there are also vegetarian/vegan options. In addition to a varied à la carte selection, the restaurant offers a seasonal menu and a sharing menu (for two or more people).

Name: anico
Description: Located in this resort in the Hautes Vosges, you come across this appealing contemporary restaurant named after its two owners: Anita, who works front of house, and Nicolas, who presides in the kitchen. In a warm decor featuring stone and wood, the chef, who hails from Moselle, delivers his own personal take on fine dining cuisine, combining high-quality local produce (Wagyu beef, trout, snails, chickpeas and lentils) with techniques and flavours picked up during his many travels.

Name: anu
Description: Adding fun to good taste makes the experience of cooking all the more fulfilling. For example, a chef who explains his cuisine with humour brings smiles to diners’ faces. The name, French for ‘as it is’, reflects the restaurant’s philosophy. There are no fences or borders between cuisines here. Ingredients are expressed as they are, service flows with a calm, natural grace. Let go of preconceptions and enjoy everything as it is.

Name: arte
Address: Blow up Hall Hotel, ul. Kościuszki 42, Poznań, 61-891, Poland
Description: The imposing former Stary Browar brewery was once filled with boiling hops and fermenting yeast, but today houses shops, an art gallery space and the sleekly modern Blow Up Hall hotel. Within the latter, arte lives up to its name with a creative streak running through dishes that take pride in Polish ingredients. Lunch is a lighter offering so come in the evening for the full experience, which culminates in imaginative desserts like their version of a crème brûlée.

Name: arthur
Description: You could easily walk right past arthur, where the "Laundromat" sign from the previous business remains, but this Greenpoint gem demands to be seen. Brick walls and vintage furniture remind of earlier days, while Chef Kevin Finch and co-owner/wife Alexa Finch showcase a modern French bistro menu that puts a spotlight on ingredients sourced from the Northeast. Small plates, including escargot and tuna crudo, are intended for sharing, while larger main courses like New York strip steak and tilefish are memorable. The dessert options are light and are designed to pair well with dessert wines.

Name: aster
Description: The faux industrial décor feels like an appropriate fit for this restaurant housed in a former warehouse, in an area once home to the city's shipyards. The kitchen forms part of the room, bringing a certain energy to proceedings, and the friendly team also help to create an enjoyable atmosphere. The short menu offers dishes with a rustic edge, where distinct flavours are nicely balanced – such as minty salsa verde with grilled lamb loin, or sharp apple cutting through a rich chocolate dessert.

Name: austa
Address: Rua Cristovão Pires Norte - Edificio Dunas Living, Almancil, 8135-117, Portugal
Description: Behind the name “austa”, a Latin term meaning “south wind”, lies, poetically, a veiled homage to the Algarve region and, above all, the intention to be a breath of fresh air in Almancil’s gastronomic landscape. In this restaurant with an alternative spirit (seen in its music, ambience and the terrace - which can even feel like a chill-out space, set in a rural-residential setting, you will find an appealing contemporary proposal. The exclusively à la carte menu encourages sharing and offers a more relaxed lunchtime dining experience.

Name: ava
Description: Lured by the atmosphere of the ancient capital, the chef moved here from Tokyo. At his counter kitchen, in a renovated merchant’s house that blends Japanese and Western aesthetics, the chef wields skills he honed at restaurants in Sicily. Cherished flavours from the food stalls and kitchen tables of Sicilian villages are arranged with modern stylings. Through its ingredients, such as olive oil, cheese and pistachios, the chef showcases the delights of Sicily.

Name: avec
Address: 615 W. Randolph St., Chicago, IL, 60661, USA
Description: This West Randolph mainstay has been a smash hit for more than two decades – and for good reason. All day long, fans crowd the long counter and close-knit tables that stretch down the length of a restaurant encased head to toe in wood planks. The Mediterranean menu runs with the seasons, and it’s no trouble finding favor in the bold, colorful plates that come out of this smooth-running kitchen. Dishes like roasted asparagus with za’atar buttermilk or chickpea hummus with oyster mushrooms arrive crowned with all manner of vibrant herbs, sauces, and crunchy garnishes. Generously portioned salads and tartines feature prominently at lunch. A second, more spacious location in River North is better suited for larger groups.

Name: bellasLOKAL
Address: Langstraße 15, Bad Soden am Taunus, 65812, Germany
Description: In a narrow village lane in the Altenhain district, chef-owner Isabelle Pering welcomes you to her restaurant done out in a tasteful, clean-lined style. With her set menu, which also comes in a vegetarian version, she demonstrates a knack for creating harmonious flavour combinations – this is where her experience gained at top-flight establishments shines through. Pleasingly minimalist dishes such as "Beef - Carrot - Hay" or "Asparagus - Tomato - Pimentos" also whet the appetite. The majority of the ingredients come from the region and most are certified organic. There is a well-curated wine list, as well as a lovely selection of wines by the glass and alcohol-free pairings to go with the set menu. Pretty terrace.

Name: bhoga
Description: Following a 20-month closure for essential city groundworks, Bhoga is back. Set steps away from one of the most picture-perfect canals in the city, it’s a popular spot, and the team will make you feel truly welcome. For dinner, choose the length of your menu – five, seven or nine courses – and the rest is up to the talented chefs; that could include a lamb chop and cabbage-wrapped lamb meatball, with a classic stock poured at the table. On Thursdays and Fridays they also serve lunch: choose one of three main dishes – meat, fish or vegetarian – and they’ll fill the tables with sides to match.

Name: bistro in der remise
Description: The magnificent estate of Schloss Hugenpoet, which dates back to 1647, is a truly remarkable location. Here – in the converted coach house, to be precise – the atmosphere is relaxed and casual, yet the decor is stylish; listed elements of the former stables lend a special touch. From your table you can see into the open kitchen, where dishes are prepared with traditional, international and seasonal influences – from beef Bourguignon to flambéed salmon sashimi and mushroom and buckwheat risotto. In the afternoon, there is a selection of light snacks and cakes. The terrace in the courtyard with a view of the castle is lovely in summer. Planted with mature trees, the grounds are perfect for a stroll.

Name: bistro simba
Description: The concept is a ‘neo-bistro’, which was in vogue when the chef apprenticed in Paris. Casual bistro fare gets a leg up, thanks to the chef’s gastronomic skills, complimented by organic wine. The name ‘simba’ is an anagram suggesting the words simple, saveur (flavour) and simpatico. Everything is natural here—the food, the wine, the people—filling the belly and satisfying the soul.

Name: bistronauten
Description: A word to the wise: make sure you book, as this really appealing restaurant is always busy! Housed in an old railway station dating from 1903, the atmosphere is laid-back, the decor modern with industrial charm and the food excellent. On the blackboard there is a seasonal set menu – choose between meat, fish and vegetarian for the main course. They also have a selection of German wines. Dine at the counter to watch the chefs at work in the open kitchen.

Name: blooms
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Set in a beautiful terraced garden on the third floor of a modern annexe, this outdoor restaurant is a highlight of The Dolder Grand luxury hotel. It is truly idyllic to sit on the little individual terraces on the edge of the forest, surrounded by vegetable beds, fruit bushes, herbs and blooming flowers. A striking red sculpture by artist Keith Haring stands out against this backdrop of greenery. This intriguing concept is the brainchild of Heiko Nieder, who, alongside a dedicated team led by sous-chef Robin Briner, serves up vegan cuisine with a modern, seasonal twist – think tomato and strawberry salad with peperoncini and pumpkin seeds, or cabbage roulade with herbs and a shallot and caraway jus. Order à la carte, or opt for the "Chef's Choice" set menu, which comprises four to six courses. N.B. The restaurant is open from May to September and only in good weather – your booking will be cancelled if it rains.

Name: bonélan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Tucked adjacent to its sister restaurant l’élan, Bonélan offers a relaxed dining experience, where the theme is ‘classic cuisine, casual style’. Prix fixe offerings centre on modern preparations such as vegetable terrine, seafood poêle and duck confit. Offcuts are used to make consommé, sending a message about food loss. The allure of traditional cuisine, passed through a modern filter.

Name: brut.
Address: 16 rue des Prés-Garniers, à Saillé, Guérande, 44350, France
Description: In a traditional salt workers' village in the heart of the salt marshes, this picturesque white house with snug, cosy dining rooms is open for business. Japanese chef Takashi Aoki crafts a creatively subdued Gallic line-up that showcases the season. The wine list is extremely well curated and the vast majority of the wines are available by the glass.

Name: buffet Kull bar
Description: A word to the wise: Book ahead to avoid disappointment at this trendy restaurant in the centre of Munich! The "French bistro meets New York steakhouse" concept is a hit. The atmosphere is lively, the tables are close together, and the service is both lively and attentive. But above all, it's the cuisine that impresses: Here, the focus is clearly on taste and ingredients – no visual frills needed. The cooking is precise and unpretentious. Mouth-watering options include the NY-style fillet steak with maître d'hôtel butter. For dessert, why not try the tarte Tatin served with vanilla ice cream and crème fraîche?

Name: būccan
Address: 350 S. County Rd., Palm Beach, FL, 33480, USA
Description: This Palm Beach mainstay is beloved by locals who flock here for Chef Clay Conley's expansive contemporary American menu. From crudos and shared small plates to pastas, there's plenty to choose from here, where several dishes are staples but most rotate with the seasons. Begin the short rib empanada, one of buccan's staples. Drizzled with aji amarillo sauce and finished with salsa criolla, it's a perfect beginning. Pasta always suits, especially when half-orders facilitate enjoying more than one, but don't skip dessert. The Bananas Foster butter cake takes a standard finale and infuses it with a dash of creativity (think deconstructed, with a mini Bundt cake, banana with a brûléed sugar shell, and banana rum ice cream) for a total hit. Looking for a casual lunch? Pick up a beef carpaccio sandwich from their counter.

Name: canade
Description: The Pinocchio doll on the shelf is a souvenir from the couple’s time in Italy. The chef studied cooking there, while his wife studied wine. Macallè-style risotto is a simple farmer’s dish, made more elegant with seasonings; Tokachi beef, from cows that have calved raised for this restaurant, is grilled over straw for aroma. The restaurant’s name is from the Japanese kanaderu, ‘to play an instrument’, and indeed the couple’s cuisine and wines make a beautiful harmony.

Name: cucina regionale YANAGAWA
Description: Mami Yanagawa managed a restaurant in her hometown out of love for the produce brought forth by nature’s bounty. Encountering regional cooking in a northern Italian restaurant and studying the cuisine of mountain and inland regions made her aware of the attractions of Nara. She prepares simple, modern fare using ingredients sourced from producers she works closely with, reimagining hometown cooking with a contemporary sensibility. Italian cuisine presented in a uniquely Nara style.

Name: d'Afspanning
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Dark floor tiles and bare brick walls set the scene in this historic edifice of Beernem, albeit elegantly paired with modern fixtures and fittings. Diners can choose between cosy nooks or the spacious glazed extension. The varied menu appeals both to fans of classical fare and to those keen to try out world cuisine. The veteran chef is equally at home with the ubiquitous shrimp fritter as with an Asian take on steak tartare. Honest, wholesome fare.

Name: d'Artagnan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Epicureans will be delighted by the elegant, refined interior and charming rear terrace. Diners can choose between a classical or a more creative menu, both equally precise and flavoursome. Private parking by reservation.

Name: d'Oude Schuur
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Wine takes front stage in this pretty farmstead with a courtyard patio and warm lights twinkling indoors. In addition to adorning the walls, it is above all the passion with which the wine is served that sets the scene. Burgundy takes pride of place on the wine list, a genuine bible. The chef adds subtle, modern twists to traditional recipes, underscoring tuna tartare with Asian accents, for example, while the sole meunière is quite simply the summum of textbook perfection.

Name: da Frappa
Description: Fabio Imparato, who hails from the Italian province of Salerno, is the head chef at this restaurant not far from the lake. After working in various fine dining restaurants, he now devotes himself to Italian and Mediterranean cuisine. The seasonal surprise menu comes in a four- or five-course format. The wine list, too, draws on labels from the chef's homeland. Service is friendly and professional, and the aesthetic is appealing, refined and upscale. Conveniently, there is a public car park nearby.

Name: da Omar
Address: via Dante Alighieri 21, Lido di Jesolo, 30016, Italy
Description: Passion and enthusiasm overcome all obstacles and lead to the best results: this summarises the professional journey of the chef at this restaurant. He prepares fish dishes inspired by classic Italian cuisine, sometimes with a modern twist, but always using the best quality produce.

Name: dario&
Description: Dario Breuer, the chef-patron behind the name, serves modern French dishes featuring international and Far Eastern influences and with a focus on seasonal produce. The "&" in the name deliberately leaves plenty of room for interpretation, because everyone should feel at home here, whether you go in for laid-back or ambitious cuisine – perfectly in step with its "casual fine dining" byline. The four- to seven-course set menu also has a vegetarian counterpart. Alternatively, you can pick à la carte. The well-curated wine list featuring 265 different labels encompasses big names as well as new finds and a fine champagne selection. The set menu can be accompanied by wine pairings served by the glass – "Élémentaire", "Par Excellence" or "Noble & Vieux" – or an alcohol-free equivalent. Service is pleasant, cordial and knowledgeable. The interior has a trendy, urban feel and, in summer, a handful of tables are laid out on the pavement in front of the restaurant. Being close to Synagogenplatz and not far from Elisenbrunnen, the cathedral and the town hall, the location is also of interest.

Name: das Schrei
Description: Hosts Jakob Schmid and Daniel Reifecker form an owner-and-chef duo who clearly take great pleasure in their work. They serve a creative surprise menu comprising four to seven courses, with a vegetarian version available by pre-order. The ingredients, which are of outstanding quality, are sourced primarily from the region. Friendly, adept service includes personal presentations of some dishes by the kitchen team. For pairings, there are wines, non-alcoholic options or a combination of both. The excellent wine list highlights bottles from Austria, Germany and France. The interior is stylish and chic, combining clean modern lines with warm, soothing tones. The focal point is the open kitchen in the middle of the room, where the chef's table is set up to offer a special up-close experience. In good weather, they also set up tables on the terrace.

Name: das grander
Description: Diners come here to enjoy the friendly and vibrant atmosphere and delicious food. In the evening, you can compose your own seven-course set menu from the featured dishes or order à la carte. Alternatively, there is a surprise menu comprising three to five courses as well as a set menu of Japanese cuisine. At lunchtime, they serve a reasonably priced set menu that changes on a daily basis, the "weekly gourmet set menu" and a range of à la carte classics such as beef carpaccio, Kalbsrahmbeuschel (calf lights ragout) or Wiener schnitzel, as well as modern fare such as sea bass with saffron foam. In summer, you can sit on the terrace facing a small square laid out like a park. Tip: Your best bet for parking is the underground car park Am Kirchplatz.

Name: das weinberg
Description: Since the beginning of 2024, Sandra Apflauer and Marcus Doller have operated their restaurant as a hub for foodies, wine lovers and art enthusiasts, pulling out all the stops for their guests. The cuisine is modern and seasonally inspired; the menu features dishes such as salmon trout from Oberwasser fish farm, white wine, kohlrabi, hazelnut and suave chilli, or crispy straw-fed pork roast with beer jus, bacon and cabbage salad, and bread dumpling. Main courses can be ordered as Tapas Schmankerl (small tasting servings) or in standard portions. In addition to the à la carte selection, there is the five-course "DINE Winzer Menü". The sleek, modern interior is decorated with artwork, and the idyllic, verdant garden terrace is a true city highlight. At the small Speak Easy Bar, you can enjoy classic or trendy cocktails, as well as their signature drinks.

Name: de Molenaar
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: The charm of the converted Hunsingo windmill (1855) is as captivating as this picturesque village, and it houses a really special restaurant. Chef Kooijker works only with a surprise menu in which he brings to bear all his creativity, paying special attention to the presentation, creating elaborate garnishes and giving a new perspective on familiar flavours. Rest assured, you are in good hands here. And why not treat yourself to an overnight stay in the mill or granary?

Name: de Wanne
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Part of the elegant Parkhotel de Wiemsel, De Wanne boasts a splendid terrace overlooking the grounds. Inside, the linen, silver and attentive front-of-house team lend the setting a classically elegant feel. Chef Jan Huiskes serves dishes that are rooted in French culinary tradition and incorporate international influences. Think classic beef tartare with Twickel cheese and truffle cream, or saddle of lamb with a shallot and lamb sauce and crispy pommes dauphine. A dependable choice for those who enjoy refined dining in peace and comfort.

Name: der allerKrug
Description: Here at der allerKrug with its friendly hosts Sven Hütten and Petra Tiecke-Hütten, you can look forward to carefully and skilfully prepared dishes. The dishes are based on country cuisine with international influences, plus there’s an attractive terrace to the rear of the restaurant.

Name: die kleine Linde
Description: This compact restaurant started out in autumn 2024 as a pop-up serving dishes à la carte. Today, it opens its doors in the evenings to present modern and creative cuisine in the form of two five- or seven-course set menus: "Eine Rundreise" and the vegetarian "Botanischer Garten". At the helm in the kitchen, Valentin Thesing (previously at Aqua in Wolfsburg) delivers expressive, harmonious flavour combinations in dishes such as "scallop, water spinach, coconut", complete with robust sauces and stocks. The restaurant is housed in the stately, lovingly renovated Jugendstil building of the Lindenhof. Historical details such as high ceilings and striking pillars, wood panelling, impressive old windows and lovely herringbone hardwood flooring have been tastefully incorporated into sleek, modern interior design. The atmosphere is pleasingly informal, and the service is attentive and professional.

Name: dinette
Description: Operating as both a coffee shop and restaurant, this is one of those appealing something-for-everyone places. Occupying part of a former 1930s department store, its modern bistro feel is infused with subtle art deco touches that tie in with the building’s history. Brunch is served in the day, before the dinner à la carte kicks in with its clean, fresh and seasonal dishes taking inspiration from around Europe. Pastries from the café are sometimes available for dessert.

Name: doc
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: It occupies a modern-style building that stands out due to its riverside location on the Douro and boasts an appealing terrace overlooking the water. This venue combines a superb setting with a cuisine that needs no introduction, since the menu is by the renowned Chef Rui Paula and overseen daily by chef Joel Paiva. Here, the chef offers a style of cooking that reflects his Trás-os-Montes roots, drawing on past memories and fused with products from the riverside, delivering intense, surprising flavours. The à la carte offering is supplemented by a 14-course tasting menus, which can be reduced to 11 or 6 courses, as well as a vegetarian section. To round out the experience, there is an extensive wine selection — well worth a look!

Name: dr Egge - das restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Located in Muttenz's old town, this compact restaurant delights diners with its stylish and charming decor, warm hospitality and Italian-inspired cuisine. They propose a seasonal set menu made using regional produce wherever possible; the "Piedmontese Autumn Menu", featuring Alba white truffles, is also a popular choice. Astute wine recommendations come courtesy of the maître d'.

Name: east
Description: This restaurant, housed in the stylish hotel of the same name, is quite striking on account of the fantastic industrial architecture of the former iron foundry and the slick, chic interior. The centrepiece here in what was once the factory hall is the sushi counter. The menu features modern international dishes. A tip for meat lovers: fine steaks from the Southbend Grill.

Name: echt JAN AIGNER
Description: Housed in forumKLOSTER, a seminar and events centre, this is a modern and trendy restaurant with artistic decor that would be right at home in a city such as Graz or Vienna. Jan Aigner serves up dishes that draw on international influences and showcase regional and seasonal produce – you can order à la carte or take a punt on the surprise menu. Friendly and attentive service. There is also a bar and a terrace. Tip for motorists: There is a public car park next door (charges apply until 6pm).

Name: eins44
Description: This restaurant tucked away in the third courtyard of the Otto-Reichel-Höfe hits the mark. Inside, the converted distillery exudes a casual, trendy urban loft atmosphere with an industrial feel. At beautiful solid old beechwood tables, diners tuck into ingredient-led seasonal cuisine. The modern, creative dishes are served in the form of a five- or seven-course set menu – either with meat/fish or vegetarian. Dishes such as "spring salad, brawn & peanut" or "Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef), wild garlic & coffee", are rich in flavour and represent excellent value for money. Service is provided by a dedicated, friendly and well-organised team.

Name: elda
Address: Mill Road, Stoke Mill, Stoke Holy Cross, NR14 8PA, United Kingdom
Description: Nestled inside the Stoke Mill Restaurant – itself located in a beautiful ancient mill – this intimate and personal experience sees the chefs serving just 14 diners. As they proudly explain each well-honed dish, you feel like you’ve been welcomed into a private home. The consistently impressive tasting menu makes great use of top-quality ingredients, often enhanced with delicate yet deeply flavoured sauces – a prime example could be monkfish rubbed with Baharat spice mix and finished with a beurre blanc based on tomato water reduction.

Name: eleanore
Address: 30-31 Albert Place, Edinburgh, EH7 5HN, United Kingdom
Description: With its cosy atmosphere and French-rooted menu, the true spirit of the bistro is strong in this pleasantly relaxed spot from the team behind The Little Chartroom. Make sure you order the the English muffin with miso honey butter to start, alongside other sharing plates that swing between Gallic classics and British reinterpretations, such as the nostalgia-tinged banoffee cremeux for dessert. The super friendly service team put a smile on your face and add to the feel of a proper neighbourhood restaurant for all occasions.

Name: elfbuchen
Description: The appeal of the Waldhotel Elfbuchen goes beyond its superb tranquil location in a forest clearing at 536m above sea level – its restaurant draws visitors with fine cooking too. The kitchen presents modern dishes inspired by the seasons and the region, with game sourced from the hotel's own hunting grounds. Precisely prepared dishes packed with flavour are served either à la carte or as a set menu by an attentive and professional front-of-house team. Choose to dine in the cheerful modern interior or out on the lovely terrace. On Sundays, the café serves cakes and tortes from the family's own patisserie. Tip: The UNESCO World Heritage Site Bergpark Wilhelmshöhe and the famous Hercules Monument, both about a 20min walk away, are well worth exploring.

Name: elven
Description: Sister to Nüman in Kaunas, the name of this restaurant means ‘river’ in Norwegian, with the language being a clue both to the design of the room and the style of the food here. The traditional creamwashed façade of the heritage building is certainly in complete contrast to the sleek interior, which is an elegant space with a design-led style. The menu delivers a good range of creative, pared-back dishes with bold flavours, a blend of textures and eye-catching presentation, with sharing dishes for two also a feature. In summer, head for the rear terrace.

Name: eman
Description: Drawing inspiration from Japan’s four seasons, the chef fuses ingredients with the cuisines of various regions of Spain. His choice to take the path of Spanish cuisine was set when he tried paella as a student. Obsessed with reproducing this epiphany for his guests, the chef offers Spanish and Japanese rice cuisine in tandem. Clams on rice is a Basque recipe, arranged in Fukagawa-meshi style. A deep dive into the hometown cuisines of Spain and Japan, in the heart of Kiyosumi Shirakawa.

Name: ember at No. 5
Address: 5 Romilly Crescent, Pontcanna, Cardiff, CF11 9NP, United Kingdom
Description: There’s a welcome brightness to this neighbourhood restaurant in one of Cardiff’s foodie suburbs. The simple décor includes light-wood furnishings and a white-topped counter, ensuring a clean, uncluttered feel. The cooking has a similarly straightforward ethos, looking fairly pared-back on the plate, but packing a punch in its flavours. Seasonal British ingredients and a notable Italian influence guide the menu, leading to daily made focaccia and a choice of pasta dishes – such as spaghetti topped with lovely red mullet.

Name: eme
Description: This intimate restaurant is run by a Uruguayan couple who earned their stripes at leading establishments around the world. In the kitchen, the chef – who has worked at Astrid y Gastón, Mauro Colagreco and David Toutain – devises pared-back blind tasting menus inspired by his travels, and occasionally with a Uruguayan component. Acidity, vinegars and condiments punctuate the dishes, which are unfussy, but full of character, for example in the combination of white asparagus, wild garlic and coriander, or the cod with yeast and fermented milk. Mara herself designed the minimalist green-hued decor with a cosy atmosphere.

Name: en
Description: His father was an artist specialising in maki-e, gold and silver decorations on lacquer; his mother the latest in a long line of tea-ceremony instructors. Overseas, he spread the word about the virtues of shojin-ryori. ‘En’ means ‘swallow’; the chef named his restaurant for this migratory bird in reference to himself, a man who had lived away from Japan but had come home to Kyoto. The menu is broad in scope and includes some dishes incorporating Western elements. The swallow is said to bring good fortune, and the chef’s personality and the reputation of his cooking bring customers flocking to him.

Name: enPure
Address: 33, Alley 7, Lane 86, Jiangxing Road, North District, Taichung, Taiwan
Description: Tucked away in a quiet alley, enPure ushers diners through a lush garden and into a minimalist space decked out in muted tones of brick red and cool grey. The interior designer-turned-chef unveils a tasting menu marked by delicate elegance and modern finesse. Using locally sourced produce, each dish brings out the authentic flavours of the land. For instance, the claypot-cooked Taiwanese rice tossed with tea seed oil from a partner tea farm features a lingering nutty aroma. For a more complete experience, add the tea pairing.

Name: enotèca
Address: Charing Cross, Saint Aubin, JE3 8AA, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Jersey meets Italy at this wine bar serving hearty, full-flavoured dishes in what was once a delicatessen. The owners run a business called Wild Wine, which imports natural wines from small producers – and a fabulous choice of these bottles is available to enjoy while dining. The pasta and gelato are both made in-house, and all the cooking is executed with such care. Keep an eye out for the blackboard specials.

Name: es/pacìo
Address: 201 nouveau port des Lecques, Saint-Cyr-sur-Mer, 83270, France
Description: Local seasonal veg and fruit, freshly caught wild fish, an on-the-ball team (including the former sous-chef from La Chassagnette), a concise, savvily curated list of local natural wines: the scene is set for lip-smacking, heroic fare in which everything tastes of something. Examples: red tuna, raspberry and coriander harissa; line-fished dentex, borlotti beans, tomatoes, pilpil and combava; duckling, caillette, broccoli rabe and blackberry juice. The picture windows of this seafront bistro, appointed in a lowkey vein, overlook a terrace and the marina.

Name: ess.
Description: Prix fixe presentations seem to be ascendant these days, but this Italian restaurant boasts an unstinting menu of à la carte offerings. The list of pastas is so extensive that you can find a new one every time you visit, while gelato comes in plenty of flavours. Staff provide attentive service, ensuring that guests can always enjoy delicious items when they want them without hesitation. The name ‘ess.’ is short for ‘essential’, and that’s the experience this restaurant brings you.

Name: esskunst
Description: The former hall of a bank is now a smart and sophisticated restaurant serving ambitious cuisine. Here, culinary tradition is tastefully combined with modern trends. On the menu, for example: char fillet, strudel dough, celery, turnips, kohlrabi. Tip: try the home-made pralines with your coffee. Charming, attentive and experienced service.

Name: estiatorio Milos
Address: Atlantis The Royal, Crescent Road, The Palm, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: It’s not just the wonderful bounty from the sea displayed on ice that’s the attraction at this smart and impeccably run restaurant in the grounds of Atlantis The Royal; the Hellenic menu offers up plenty of other choices, like a terrific tomato and aged feta salad, along with some special Greek wines. At lunch there’s a great value Business Lunch menu.

Name: etch. by Steven Edwards
Address: 216 Church Road, Brighton and Hove, BN3 2DJ, United Kingdom
Description: An attractive former bank plays host to this lively modern restaurant, where an open kitchen and bar take centre stage in the dining room. Tersely described tasting menus deliver ambitious, technique-driven dishes with bold flavours and intriguing textures; Steven's signatures include a marmite brioche and his take on 'dippy egg'. The wine list offers a good selection from Sussex and cocktails are available in the basement Ink Bar, so-called because the premises was once a tattoo parlour.

Name: eòrna
Address: 68 Hamilton Place, Edinburgh, EH3 5AZ, United Kingdom
Description: There's a plush quality to this smart counter restaurant in the suburb of Stockbridge. Small "chef’s table" operations like this allow for a much greater intimacy to your dining experience and, indeed, there are just two people working here: Brian in the kitchen and Glen looking after service and wines. Following a warm welcome, you can enjoy a highly seasonal tasting menu that has a strong Scottish heart, from the Orkney beef to the fantastic Perthshire strawberries.

Name: fago
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: This restaurant is situated in Marvão, a village at the highest point of the Serra de São Mamede, just a few kilometres from the Spanish border. It occupies a small house that has been completely remodelled by Diogo Branco, a chef from Porto, and Daniel Boto, a native of this region. The concise à la carte here changes constantly according to the seasons and availability from local producers. Three main dishes are always available: one vegetarian, one meat, and one fish or seafood.

Name: farsi largo!
Description: The Italian-trained chef runs this restaurant with his wife. A chance encounter with a fishmonger in Shizuoka Prefecture made the seafood of Suruga Bay the star of this show. One fish dish after another is served, from fried fish to soup and carpaccio. Panna cotta of black truffle comes from the chef’s experiences in Piedmont. The name of the restaurant means ‘blaze your own trail’, and the cuisine wordlessly conveys the chef’s single-minded passion.

Name: fine.wine.dine.
Description: Located in the pedestrian area, not far from the Rhine River, this modern yet cosy little restaurant serves ambitious seasonal cuisine in the evening. You can either order the set menu or choose à la carte; on Wednesday and Thursday evenings there is also an appealing sharing menu for two. Vegetarian options are also available if ordered in advance. For lunch, there are simpler, more moderately priced daily specials. Delicatessen goods and wine can be purchased to enjoy at home.

Name: finesse by Elvis Herbek
Description: First things first: it is advisable to book well in advance, as this chic, modern restaurant is small and very popular. Little wonder it draws a crowd, given the passion with which the two amiable owners run the place. In the open kitchen, owner Elvis Herbek prepares a set menu comprising four or five courses. The creative seasonal dishes are inspired by Mediterranean and international influences: think "Potage – wild garlic, scallop, preserved lemon, shiso" or "Saltimbocca – veal, sage, hollandaise, Parma ham, Beelitz asparagus". Front of house, Nicole Hieke not only ensures everything runs smoothly but also adds a charming, personal and relaxed, neighbourly touch to the whole experience. And you can certainly rely on her wine recommendations, too.

Name: fischerhaus
Description: This lovely country house is located just a stone's throw from Wörthersee. The restaurant boasts a chic, elegant interior, as well as a delightful terrace. The menu features a diverse range of dishes prepared with the finest ingredients, covering everything from Austrian classics and Asian cuisine to truffles and caviar. Regulars and newcomers alike are treated with the same warmth and professionalism by the friendly staff.

Name: fragment Azabujuban
Description: The concept is intriguing: ‘Italian cuisine from all over Japan’, the furthest thing from traditional Edo fare. Its strength is its unique routes to obtain seafood from around the country, sourced from intermediate tuna wholesalers. The chef’s speciality, tuna, is served as carpaccio, tuna salad, roast cheek of tuna and more. To encourage drop-in trade, the restaurant offers a selection of pasta at lunchtime and an extensive à la carte menu in the evening.

Name: freistil.
Description: In addition to an appealing modern decor featuring sleek design and warm wooden fittings, diners can look forward to a selection of regional and seasonal dishes (including vegetarian and vegan options) that can be put together to create a set menu or ordered à la carte. For overnight stays, the boutique hotel has attractive, comfortable guestrooms.

Name: freyja
Description: Head straight for the roof terrace to kick off your visit with a cocktail and 360° views of Stockholm and, once inside, opt for a seat by the curved window to capitalise on the 13th floor location. The menu includes modernised yet comforting Swedish classics like Kroppkaka, executed with care and confidence, yielding well-balanced flavours. This is a place where you'll feel equally at home dining in a couple or as a group, as it delivers something for everyone.

Name: fumée
Address: B3, Regent Hotel, 3, Lane 39, Section 2, Zhongshan North Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: The sister restaurant of the Osakan yakitori institution Ichimatsu sports a dark colour scheme, reminiscent of an opera house. The young Japanese chef sources local poultry such as Hsinchu free-range chicken, and Wenchang chicken for his kebabs along with local herbs like prickly ash and maqaw. The set menu with 10+ courses showcases an array of textures and flavours. Consider paying extra for rare cuts such as shiro reba and kinkan.

Name: genso
Description: The venue, a remodelled ironworks, exudes an industrial vibe. Guests are greeted with cuisine styled on the concept of the four elements of fire, earth, wind and water, represented on the menu by elemental symbols of ancient Greece. A platter of vegetables, each grilled with a variety of techniques, represents cuisine of the earth; soup redolent with herbs and other ingredients expresses water; and so on, with each item conceptually linked to a classical element.

Name: gentil H
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: The aim here is to offer refinement through the flavour of excellent ingredients. Placing harmony of flavours above all, it focuses on temperature, fragrance and texture. The menu lists producing regions and producers, conveying gratitude for the ingredients that make the restaurant’s cuisine possible. The chef personally serves the dishes, ensuring that the recipe’s intention and passion shine through. Name-brand tea and bread baked by a friend from the same graduating class are both from the chef’s native Shizuoka.

Name: girotondo
Description: Regional cuisine from the Emilia-Romagna region of Italy is faithfully recreated here. Especially prized are the meatballs and ragu the chef learned from a nonna during his apprenticeship. ‘Cappelletti‘, a kind of ravioli whose name means ‘little hats’, have a charming appearance and a rustic, home-style taste; enjoy them with a wine chosen by the proprietor, and it will conjure up images of an Italian dinner table.

Name: goldener Adler
Description: Everyone would love to have a cosy and buzzing restaurant like this in their neighbourhood! The contemporary decor strikes a rustic note; the traditional regional cuisine is based on fresh produce. The menu ranges from classics such as cordon bleu with potato salad to internationally inspired dishes such as pan-fried prawns with shellfish noodles. Vegetarian options are also available. The beautiful large terrace (you can park here in winter) is a stand-out feature in this city-centre location.

Name: hakubi
Description: Chinese cuisine with a modern interpretation. Lifting a page from the lavish entertainment of the imperial court, hakubi populates its prix fixe menus with multiple courses of small dishes. Rice vermicelli paired with caviar and chicken wing tips wrapped in foie gras signify cuisine unafraid of incorporating Western elements. Dressings of chilli sauce and mayonnaise for shrimp set up an interesting taste comparison. A whimsical spirit pervades the fare, setting the heart racing.

Name: handicap.
Description: There is temporarily a change of concept here, with an amended menu, "Restaurant Würzburger Bau", being served until the end of June. From July onwards, fine dining cuisine will be back. As its name suggests, this tastefully decorated restaurant in a side wing of Hotel Anne-Sophie employs differently abled people, and the success of the initiative is clear to see in the great team. In the stylish decor, clean lines meet artwork, including a celestial painting by Markus Schmidgall on the high ceiling. The small terrace in the courtyard is delightful on a fine summer's day.

Name: hatsune
Description: The chef works alone in this tiny restaurant. At lunchtime the predominant theme is noodle dishes, such as dandan noodles and hot-and-sour ramen. In the evening, both à la carte and set menu dining are available. Be sure to order the appetiser platter, as it’s packed with variety and the time and effort taken to prepare it are apparent. The spring rolls, a finger food, are also recommended. The ‘Yellow Mapo Tofu with Seafood’ intrigues with its unusual name and distinctive yellow colour.

Name: henne
Address: High Street, Moreton-in-Marsh, GL56 0AT, United Kingdom
Description: ‘henne’ refers to Marsh Henne, the original name of the Cotswolds market town which has this likeable restaurant at its heart. Run by two friends, it's a place filled with passion and enthusiasm, with plenty of care put into dishes that are well described by the service team. Local produce is showcased on the surprise tasting menu, where the best courses have an appealing simplicity about them, like hand-dived scallops enhanced by pickled celery, apple and yuzu oil. Go for the wine pairing to complete the experience.

Name: hom
Address: InterContinental Phuket Resort, 333, 333/3 Mu 3, Kamala Beach, Kamala, Kathu, Phuket, 83150, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets not allowed
Description: After a stroll through a serene garden walkway, you will find this restaurant inside the InterContinental Resort. The Portuguese chef showcases a fermentation-heavy concept on the menu, highlighting new sides to local produce. Leeks, betel leaves and pandan are just some of the ingredients that are given the fermentation treatment, in delicately executed dishes. The natural wine list is in keeping with the restaurant’s ethos, and the intimate atmosphere makes it ideal for a romantic dinner.

Name: huist
Address: 3, Lane 22, Shengping Street, West District, Taichung, 403, Taiwan
Description: After graduating from culinary school, the owner-chef honed his skills in different places before opening huist (Dutch for "home") in 2023. His prix-fixe menu is inspired by Taiwanese cooking, finessed by Western techniques and has lots of home-style touches: appetising raw scallops marinated in chilli garlic kombu soy; smoked marlin in sugar rub with sliced chicken comb sandwiched between the silky fish for contrasting textures.

Name: i-Fame
Description: A delightful journey into the future: modern, bright rooms featuring a play of white, mirrors, and glass. The cuisine also looks forward without forgetting the past: the chef from Rimini starts with mostly local ingredients (a lot of Adriatic fish on the menu, but also some meat) to create modern recipes, always rich in flavor and substance. The dessert “i-CLOUD” is very good and refreshing: a cloud of soft and delicious yogurt foam covering a yogurt and vanilla panna cotta, accompanied by various sorbets. The outdoor space with greenery is also attractive.

Name: iPalici
Address: Via Antonello da Messina 3, Viagrande, 95029, Italy
Description: Situated behind Acireale at the foot of Mount Etna National Park, this restaurant is located within the Relais San Giuliano. Deceptively uninteresting from the outside, this historic building and its inner courtyards boast a charm and grandeur that will take your breath away. A huge 16C wine press provides the backdrop for fine cuisine that is more than equal to its impressive setting. Here, the menu makes full use of vegetables and other Sicilian ingredients in dishes that are influenced by the island’s culinary traditions yet reinterpreted with a skilful contemporary twist by the chef.

Name: ice Q
Description: Beyond its sleek design, this large glass cube delights with a spectacular panoramic view of the mountains. The restaurant is located on the ground floor and proposes a modern tasting menu (vegetarian version available) as well as an à la carte selection of more classic dishes such as beef consommé, Wiener schnitzel and rib-eye steak. The service is friendly and attentive. Alternatively, tapas are served in the lounge on the top floor. Diners can also head outside to the lovely terraces. When it comes to wine, the PINO 3000 is attention worthy – it is aged at this altitude, over 3 000m above sea level! The well-curated wine list includes a decent selection of picks available by the glass. This incredible site also served as a filming location for the James Bond film Spectre. 007 Elements cinematic installation is right next to the restaurant – well worth a visit!

Name: iggy's
Address: 609 Merritt Ave., Ste. 101, Nashville, TN, 37203, USA
Description: Curious what this spot from brothers Ryan and Matthew Poli is all about? Take one look at the mural outside and you'll soon realize. This Wedgewood-Houston restaurant with a sleek, modern industrial look (and a glass-enclosed pasta room!) is all about Italian food.The concise menu keeps things simple with a few small plates like crispy arancini in warm goat cheese fondue or Village Bakery brioche stuffed with whipped cream cheese before a tempting array of house-made pastas like little shells with Maine peekytoe crab in a sea urchin butter. Soft serve sundaes are nonnegotiable. Lemon huckleberry with cubes of brown butter cake, lemon curd and huckleberry sauce over vanilla ice cream is a sure thing.

Name: il Centrino
Description: The name is a diminutive of ‘Il Centro’, in tribute to Ristorante Il Centro in Piedmont, Italy, where the chef apprenticed. What he learned was how to express hometown flavours in a modern style, taking pride in farm produce with deep roots in the land. He overlays regional cuisines with the flavours of the Japanese seasons, refining them both. The handmade pasta he learned in northern Italy especially conveys his passion. Savour flavours born of the chef’s feelings and the climates of Japan and Italy.

Name: il Gigante
Description: Tucked away in Ridgewood, Queens, this neighborhood gem has quickly become a local favorite for its Italian dishes served in a cozy setting. The offerings are simple but hit all the right notes, with daily specials, appetizers like cured meats and cheeses, fried calamari, and salads like arugula with pears, goat cheese, and caramelized walnuts dressed with balsamic, plus pastas like Bolognese and cacio e pepe. Main dishes include branzino and breaded pork cutlet. One dish not to miss? Lasagna alla Bolognese, a perfect rendition of a classic that's sided by a small mug filled with grated parm for sprinkling on top. End with tiramisu, of course.

Name: illata
Address: 2241 Grays Ferry Ave., Philadelphia, PA, 19146, USA
Description: With room for about 20 guests, illata isn't a big spot, but this neighborhood gem makes a big impression. This neighborhood BYOB shares a hit list of under a dozen small plates, emphasizing seafood and local produce while throwing in a few fun meat dishes. It all rotates with the seasons with approachable but thoughtful options that highlight familiar ingredients in creative ways (think carrots paired with crab and brown butter). Chilled mussels paired with pickled turnips are set over a miso dressing hit with chili oil for subtle heat, while grilled lamb skewers, glazed and finished with a small bundle of cilantro leaves and a few cherries, are sided by a dollop of black sesame sauce. Chocolate cake soaked with caramel and finished with crushed peanuts is a decadent finale.

Name: in between days
Address: 2340 1st Ave. S., St. Petersburg, FL, 33712, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Notable sake list
Description: In Between Days bills itself as Florida’s first Tokyo-style sake bar and vinyl house. The space feels intentionally intimate where the lights stay low, the records spin slowly and the food comes in a tight little lineup of dishes that include gyoza, hamachi, oysters and a single rotating noodle dish. This is very much a place you settle into. The team leans into sake-based cocktails, the vibe feels warm and effortless and the food hits a sweet spot between comfort and quiet technical skill.Dive into some bouncy, chewy noodles by trying the chef's choice ramen consisting of a rich, silky bone marrow broth base with enoki mushrooms, thinly sliced scallions, a runny soy egg and nicely torched pork. Finish with a slice of nutty, slightly burnt subtly spiced pumpkin Basque cheesecake with toasted pepitas, miso caramel and whipped cream.

Name: isolata
Description: The restaurant, named after the Italian word for ‘outbuilding’, is housed in a refurbished storehouse, once a dressmaking room at a girls’ finishing school, beside a retro-style building. The original ceiling and beams lend the space a stately ambience. The chef, who honed his skills in several regions of Italy, pays special reverence to local cuisines. Using techniques suited to the climate of each season, he interprets Italian culinary lore with a modern sensibility.

Name: ita
Description: (Temporarily closed) “Ita” is the affectionate nickname by which grandmother Isabel was known by those that knew her, and through it chef Mariela Fernández pays her own small tribute to her personal memories and to family recipes. In this small restaurant in the Salamanca district, the hallmarks are simplicity and honesty, visible via a concise à la carte that changes with the seasons and which features a predominance of locally sourced organic vegetables, plus a few meat or fish options.

Name: jezz Alm Resort Ellmau
Description: The location above Ellmau is spectacular! Whether in winter or summer, the unobstructed view of the valley and mountains is simply magnificent – take it in from the terrace or from inside the semi-circular dining room, through floor-to-ceiling windows. In the comfort of the chic Alpine decor, choose from an appetising modern-meets-regional à la carte menu – Austrian classics such as Wiener schnitzel and Kaiserschmarrn (torn pancake dessert) can be as heartily recommended as "salmon trout, quince, blood orange, ponzu" or "jezz emperor goose, red cabbage, chestnuts, potato dumplings", for example. The atmosphere is pleasant and unpretentious, the service well organised, accessible and very friendly – guests are addressed informally. The nicely curated wine list also features a few rarities.

Name: jfk.
Description: In a side room of Tim Mälzer's bustling Bullerei, the two hosts, Jule-Fee Poll and Kevin Bürmann – both previously employed at Haebel – bring their relaxed, modern concept to life. Jule-Fee Poll looks after diners in a laid-back manner, combining professionalism with a charming, personal touch. Meanwhile, the chef-patron prepares the surprise omakase menu, which comprises five courses and can be extended to include the classic "Toast Hawaii" – this nostalgic dish, presented with a humorous wink, is hugely popular. He is also happy to jump in and help serve dishes and talk diners through them. Fun fact: The restaurant is named after the owners, "jfk" being the initials of their first names (Jule-Fee and Kevin).

Name: jiü
Description: Wood-fired French cuisine defines the theme here, a marriage of classical French technique and wood flame. Meat and fish are enveloped in fire, while vegetables are gently smoked. Even the red wine sauce for meat dishes reflects this devotion to wood fire: the aromatic vegetables used in the stock are first charred over flame. The name ‘jiü’ refers to the ‘blessed rain’ that nourishes the fields, and it is with the hope that this restaurant may gently nourish the hearts of its guests.

Name: jjii
Description: Exposed stone walls, visible electric cables and streamed music in the long, narrow dining space, and, at work in the open kitchen, Korean chef Jaywook Hur. Going solo in the kitchen, he can be seen cooking up modern, creative French cuisine with a few Asian touches (on this particular evening, they include tempura, sesame, kimchi), as his mystery menu unfolds: a surprising and beautifully fresh starter such as sea bass, kimchi and avocado, accompanied by raspberries and a quenelle of smoked herring roe; or the oh-so-tender matured Simmental sirloin, fennel, beetroot and its bold jus.

Name: joujouka
Description: The restaurant’s name comes from an album recorded by a former guitarist of The Rolling Stones in the 1960s. The chef is not one to be swayed by fads, as his cooking attests. He pursues his own ideals in flavour, yet never strays far from the foundations of French cuisine. In roasting meats, vegetables and fish the chef prizes heat and aroma. No-nonsense, simple preparations make the results all the more impressive.

Name: jū-ni
Address: 1335 Fulton St., San Francisco, CA, 94117, USA
Description: jū-ni remains one of the city’s most intimate omakase counters, tucked off the busy Divisadero corridor with a compact dining room centered entirely around the chef-to-guest interaction. Chef Geoffrey Lee and his team guide diners through a seasonal progression of nigiri and small bites. The meal shifts constantly with availability, but signatures remain, including house-cured ikura finished with a snowy grating of frozen monkfish liver. Other memorable bites may include New Zealand king salmon accented with pickled cherry blossom leaf, buttery Hokkaido scallop or lightly torched fish brightened with yuzu kosho and citrus. The experience concludes traditionally, often with mochi and sweet red bean.

Name: kochZIMMER in der Gaststätte zur Ratswaage
Description: Located right in the centre, on Neuer Markt, the 18C Ratswaage oozes style! On the outside you have the historical façade; inside, a minimalist interior with chic details such as silvery walls, 1950s-style chandeliers and burnt-orange designer chairs. The Frankenhäuser family and their team have dubbed their culinary style "new Prussian cuisine". Head chef Nico Werner, previously sous-chef, presides in the kitchen, cooking up two five-course set menus (with the option of an "upgrade" in the form of additional dishes); the vegetarian version of the set menu should be ordered at the time of booking. The select ingredients are sourced from producers in Brandenburg. Be sure to consult owner Jörg Frankenhäuser when it comes to selecting your wine. Tip for the summer: Try to bag a table in the gorgeous courtyard – places are limited!

Name: kodō
Address: 710 S. Santa Fe Ave., Los Angeles, CA, 90021, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Notable sake list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Note: Temporarily closedIt may be tucked inside a former firehouse, but kodō is more calm and cool than fiery. It's the kind of place where a boulder doubles as a desk and the abundant use of natural materials sets a serene tone. Choose from breezy, outdoor dining on the patio or come indoors for a menu that celebrates Kyoto cuisine, from robata to sushi, albeit with a California influence. The sushi and nigiri are so good that you won't even notice the trendy crowd snapping photos for their Instagram feed. Off-menu specials, such as the Japanese sea snail, are especially memorable, while sea bream and octopus are impeccable. A steaming bowl of little neck clams garlic and butter is dreamy. Up for something sweet? Cheesecake with passion fruit sauce and kinako crumble is a favorite.

Name: ku:de kiyo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only - lunch,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: ‘Kuude’ is ‘let’s eat’ in Osaka dialect, the chef’s nickname is Kiyo, and the whole name has a French sound to it. A colour scheme of bright blue and green declares the shop’s freedom from convention. The theme is ‘unforgettable cuisine’: each dish features no more than three items, arrangements are minimal, and portions are generous. At lunchtime, set meals of Western items paired with rice and miso soup make ku:de kiyo a local favourite.

Name: l' Ciocio - Osteria di Suvereto
Description: Situated in the historic centre of the picturesque village of Suvereto, this restaurant boasts a traditional decor of wood and stone. The menu includes dishes made from the restaurant’s own grains, as well as a selection of meat and fish specialities.

Name: l'Amitié
Description: L’Amitié is depicted by a warm bistro feel and sports a huge street art-inspired fish mural. The focus is on laid-back cuisine oozing with flavour. Quality produce is revered and lovingly presented in small plates free of fripperies and designed to be shared. Delicious cured meats, vintage sardines straight from the tin, slightly seared prawns in a kimchi and pineapple sauce and an extravaganza of passion fruit, bananas and chocolate to finish. If you close your eyes, your tastebuds may well take you on a culinary world tour courtesy of fascinating blends. A place of sanctuary for fans of fine food and friendship.

Name: l'Odorante par Minoru Nakijin
Description: The chef sharpened his gastronomical senses in Grasse, a city in the south of France known as the ‘capital of perfumes’. Recalling his apprentice days, the chef named his restaurant ‘l’Odorante’, meaning ‘the pungent’ or ‘the aromatic’. Refined fragrance is the name of the culinary game here. Matching classic French techniques with Japanese ingredients, he fuses the two into a Franco-Japanese esprit, ensuring each dish is unique and brimming with flavour. He revels in explaining the background to his cuisine, leaving the memories of the culinary journey in all five senses.

Name: la forme d'éternité
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: In the French countryside, the chef absorbed the love of hometown; in Paris, he learned the importance of the classics. The chef has built relationships of trust with producers and uses local ingredients to convey the richness of Nara’s natural bounty. He sets great store by sauces, from his respect for the classics. His speciality is poached Gojo eggs in red wine sauce. His wife, his constant companion since his apprenticeship, will suggest wine pairings.

Name: la p'tite maison
Description: This ‘dinky’ house in Savièse seats fifteen in a warm setting that blends bare stone walls with contemporary lines. Since 2021, Margaux, in the kitchen, and Jeremy, front-of-house, have been conjuring up a five-course seasonal surprise menu that changes monthly.
